issues.title: Provide a system-wide Windows installer for enterprise deployment

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

In our environment, GitHub Copilot CLI installs into the user profile and also attempts to execute files from `%LOCALAPPDATA%\copilot`.  This conflicts with our corporate security requirements, which restrict execution from user-writable directories. Installing the main executable centrally is therefore insufficient if the CLI still extracts or runs supporting executables from the user profile.  We need a supported deployment option that works without weakening these restrictions.

### Proposed solution

Provide an official system-wide Windows installer, preferably MSI, with the following capabilities:

- **Machine-wide installation** into an administrator-controlled location such as `%ProgramFiles%\GitHub Copilot CLI`.
- **All bundled executables and runtime dependencies installed centrally**, without extracting or executing them from `%LOCALAPPDATA%`, `%APPDATA%`, or other user-writable locations.
- **Silent installation, upgrade, and uninstallation** for centralized software deployment.
- **Operation without local administrator privileges** after installation.
- **Administrator-controlled updates**, including an option to disable automatic updates and prevent per-user executable downloads.
- **Clear separation between application binaries and user data**. Configuration, authentication information, logs, and session history may remain in the user profile, but application executables should not.
- **Documentation of executable locations and update behavior** so administrators can configure application-control policies appropriately.

## Acceptance criteria

An administrator can deploy GitHub Copilot CLI once for all users. A standard user can then use it without the CLI installing, extracting, updating, or executing its own bundled binaries in user-writable directories.

This should work in an environment where execution from `%LOCALAPPDATA%\copilot` and other user-profile directories is blocked.

## Business value

This would make GitHub Copilot CLI deployable in managed corporate environments without requiring security-policy exceptions or unsupported packaging workarounds.

### Example prompts or workflows

issues.title: SDK with BYOK providers: short model names aren't matched to the provider's models (custom agents fail; a short session model fails with a misleading "No GitHub OAuth token" error)

labels.name: area:non-interactive
labels.description: Non-interactive mode (-p), CI/CD, ACP protocol, and headless automation

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

issues.body:
### Describe the bug


When an SDK session configures BYOK `providers` and `models`, its models are only known as
provider-qualified ids such as `copilot/gpt-5.4-mini`. Any model given by its **short name** is not
matched to them, even when exactly one configured provider serves that model:

1. **Custom agents.** An agent whose `model` is a short name fails when the main agent starts it.
   The tool call returns
   `Model 'gpt-5.4-mini' is not available. Available models: copilot/gpt-5.6-sol, copilot/gpt-5.6-luna, copilot/gpt-5.4-mini, copilot/gpt-5.6-sol, copilot/gpt-5.6-luna, copilot/gpt-5.4-mini`.
   The list itself names the model, and also lists every model twice. This happens for agents
   passed as `customAgents` and for `.github/agents/*.agent.md` files loaded with
   `enableConfigDiscovery: true`.
2. **Session model.** `createSession` accepts a short `model` (`session.start` reports
   `selectedModel: "gpt-5.6-sol"`), but the first turn fails with
   `Execution failed: InvalidArg, No GitHub OAuth token or Copilot HMAC key provided`. The debug log
   shows the turn quietly switched to `claude-sonnet-4`, a model that isn't configured, on GitHub's
   own inference:

   ```text
   [WARNING] model resolution before the turn did not commit a new selection {"error":"No model available. Check policy enablement under GitHub Settings > Copilot"}
   [WARNING] turn model is in neither the picker nor the unfiltered catalog, ...; falling back to default capabilities and the chat-completions wire {"model":"claude-sonnet-4",...}
   ```

   The error points at authentication, not at the model name. When the user is also signed in to
   GitHub, the request would presumably go to GitHub's own inference instead of the configured
   provider, without any error.

**Why it matters.** Agent files are shared between Copilot CLI and SDK sessions. In CLI BYOK mode
the same `.agent.md` must use the short name, and a file can't know which provider name an SDK host
chose. With discovery on, the main agent sometimes recovers by retrying with the qualified name. That
costs a failed tool call, depends on the model noticing, and in our runs a retry sometimes picked a
different model instead. GitHub Agentic Workflows currently rewrites every agent's model to a
qualified name before creating the session; we'd rather not keep that workaround.

This short-name matching is probably also the SDK-mode cause of #5126 (built-in agents' default
models never match).


### Affected version

`@github/copilot-sdk` 1.0.19 against `copilot --headless` from Copilot CLI 1.0.96. Also seen with SDK 1.0.16 and CLI 1.0.90.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior


Start `copilot --headless --port <port>` with no GitHub sign-in, and use one BYOK provider:

```json
{
  "providers": [{ "name": "copilot", "type": "openai", "wireApi": "responses",
                  "baseUrl": "https://api.githubcopilot.com", "bearerToken": "<token>",
                  "headers": { "Copilot-Integration-Id": "copilot-developer-cli" } }],
  "models": [{ "id": "gpt-5.6-sol", "provider": "copilot" },
             { "id": "gpt-5.6-luna", "provider": "copilot" },
             { "id": "gpt-5.4-mini", "provider": "copilot" }]
}
```

All models are on the same wire API, so #5103 doesn't apply.

1. **Custom agent with a short model:** session `model: "copilot/gpt-5.6-sol"`, plus
   `customAgents: [{ "name": "quick-checker", "description": "Finds where a function is defined", "prompt": "...", "model": "gpt-5.4-mini" }]`.
   Prompt: `Use the task tool with agent_type "quick-checker" to find which file defines add_numbers.`
   Observed: the first task call fails with `Model 'gpt-5.4-mini' is not available. Available models: ...copilot/gpt-5.4-mini...`.
2. **Same agent from a file:** no `customAgents`, `enableConfigDiscovery: true`, and
   `.github/agents/quick-checker.agent.md` with `model: gpt-5.4-mini` in its front matter. Observed:
   the same error.
3. **Control:** the same agent with `"model": "copilot/gpt-5.4-mini"` runs on mini
   (`modelSelectionSource: "agent_definition_default"`).
4. **Short session model:** `model: "gpt-5.6-sol"` and prompt `Reply with the single word OK.`
   Observed: `session.error` `Execution failed: InvalidArg, No GitHub OAuth token or Copilot HMAC key provided`,
   with the `claude-sonnet-4` warnings above in the debug log.

### Expected behavior


1. A short model name resolves to the configured provider model with that id when exactly one
   provider serves it: `gpt-5.4-mini` → `copilot/gpt-5.4-mini`. This applies to the session model,
   custom agents from `customAgents` or discovered files, and built-in agent defaults (#5126).
2. If several providers serve the id, pick deterministically (for example, the provider whose wire
   API the model supports), or report the ambiguity and list the qualified choices.
3. A session model that can't be resolved fails at `createSession` with an error that names the
   model and the available ids. It isn't silently replaced by another model, and the error doesn't
   point at authentication.

### Additional context

- Related: #5126 (built-in agents ignore their default models under BYOK) and #5103 (one wire
  API per BYOK session in CLI mode).
- Environment: Linux ARM64 (Ubuntu 24.04), Node 22. Also seen on GitHub Actions Linux x64 runners
  through GitHub Agentic Workflows' AWF API proxy as the BYOK provider.

issues.title: BYOK: built-in agents (explore, task, research) never use their default models and silently run on the session model

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

issues.body:
### Describe the bug


Copilot CLI's built-in agents declare their own models in their definitions (unchanged from 1.0.90
to 1.0.96):

| Agent | Default models, in order | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| `explore` | `gpt-5.6-luna`, `gpt-5.4-mini` | `low` |
| `task` | `gpt-5.6-luna`, `gpt-5.4-mini`, `claude-haiku-4.5` | - |
| `research` | `claude-sonnet-5` | - |

In a normal signed-in session these models are used, so a quick `explore` search runs on a small
model. **In a BYOK session they are never used.** Every built-in agent runs on the session's
model, even when the BYOK provider serves the default model and the session lists it.

As far as we can tell, the cause is the check that a definition's model is "available" in the
session. Under BYOK it never passes:

- **CLI with provider environment variables** (`COPILOT_OFFLINE=true`, `COPILOT_PROVIDER_*`,
  `COPILOT_MODEL`): the only available model is `COPILOT_MODEL`.
- **SDK with `providers` and `models`:** the session's models are provider-qualified
  (`copilot/gpt-5.6-luna`), while the definitions use short names (`gpt-5.6-luna`), so they never
  match. Issue #5127 describes the same short-name matching problem for models the user
  configures.

**The fallback is silent and misreported.** It isn't logged at the default log level, and the
`subagent.started` and `subagent.completed` events report
`"modelSelectionSource": "agent_definition_default"` with `model` set to the session model. That
reads as if the definition chose that model.

**Why it matters.** A BYOK session on an expensive model makes every built-in agent expensive too.
GitHub Agentic Workflows (`github/gh-aw`) runs Copilot through a proxy configured as a BYOK provider
and picks the session model per task. On runs on Claude Opus, `explore` and `research` used 49–58%
of the run's AI credits, all on Opus, although their definitions ask for Luna, mini and Sonnet.
`explore` is also slower on a large model.

**The provider does serve the default model.** As a diagnostic, setting
`subagents.agents.explore.model` in `~/.copilot/settings.json` makes `explore` run on Luna through
the same provider (`modelSelectionSource: "configured_preference"`). We don't want to rely on that
setting as a fix: it skips the cost guard (a Sol preference in a Luna session ran on Sol), so every
integrator would have to re-implement the runtime's model choice and cost rule.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.96, and `@github/copilot-sdk` 1.0.19 against `copilot --headless` 1.0.96. Also seen on 1.0.90 and 1.0.95.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior


**CLI mode** (BYOK straight to the Copilot API, no proxy):

```bash
mkdir demo && cd demo
printf 'def add_numbers(a, b):\n    return a + b\n' > math_utils.py
export COPILOT_OFFLINE=true \
  COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL=https://api.githubcopilot.com \
  COPILOT_PROVIDER_TYPE=openai \
  COPILOT_PROVIDER_WIRE_API=responses \
  COPILOT_PROVIDER_BEARER_TOKEN="$(gh auth token)" \
  COPILOT_MODEL=gpt-5.6-sol
copilot --allow-all-tools --no-ask-user --log-level all --log-dir ./logs -p \
  'Use the task tool with agent_type "explore" to find which file defines add_numbers. Do not search yourself.'
```

Observed: the output shows `● Explore (model: gpt-5.6-sol)`, and the log's `subagent.started`
event has `"model":"gpt-5.6-sol","taskModelSource":"unset","modelSelectionSource":"agent_definition_default"`.

**SDK mode:** start `copilot --headless --port <port>` and create a session with these options:

```json
{
  "model": "copilot/gpt-5.6-sol",
  "providers": [{ "name": "copilot", "type": "openai", "wireApi": "responses",
                  "baseUrl": "https://api.githubcopilot.com", "bearerToken": "<token>",
                  "headers": { "Copilot-Integration-Id": "copilot-developer-cli" } }],
  "models": [{ "id": "gpt-5.6-sol", "provider": "copilot" },
             { "id": "gpt-5.6-luna", "provider": "copilot" },
             { "id": "gpt-5.4-mini", "provider": "copilot" }]
}
```

Send the same prompt.

Observed: `subagent.started` has `"model":"copilot/gpt-5.6-sol","modelSelectionSource":"agent_definition_default"`,
and every request goes to `gpt-5.6-sol`. This happens although `copilot/gpt-5.6-luna` is one of the
session's models.

**Control** (shows the provider serves Luna): add
`{"subagents":{"agents":{"explore":{"model":"gpt-5.6-luna"}}}}` to `~/.copilot/settings.json` and
rerun the CLI steps. `● Explore (model: gpt-5.6-luna)`, with
`"modelSelectionSource":"configured_preference"`.

### Expected behavior


1. Under BYOK, a built-in agent uses its definition's model when the session can serve it, just as
   in a signed-in session:
   - **SDK mode:** match the definition's short name to the session's provider-qualified model
     (`gpt-5.6-luna` → `copilot/gpt-5.6-luna`).
   - **CLI mode:** don't treat `COPILOT_MODEL` as the only available model. The session needs a way
     to know the provider's other models; #3795 (BYOK model discovery) would provide one.
2. The existing cost guard keeps applying, so a default that costs more than the session model
   (`research` → Sonnet under Luna) is still skipped. It should also work under BYOK, where pricing
   may have to come from the model id.
3. A default the session can't reach is skipped, not tried and failed. For example, in CLI mode a
   Claude default under a GPT session model is on the other wire API (#5103).
4. When the agent does fall back to the session model, the fallback is visible: logged at info or
   warning level, and reported in `subagent.started` with its own `modelSelectionSource` value or a
   fallback reason, not as `agent_definition_default`.

### Additional context

- Related: #5103 (one wire API per BYOK session) and #3795 (BYOK model discovery). This issue
  doesn't depend on #5103 for same-family defaults: `explore`'s defaults are GPT models, which a
  GPT session can reach today.
- `code-review` and `general-purpose` have no default model and inherit the session model, which is
  expected.
- GitHub Agentic Workflows confirmed the same behaviour on GitHub Actions (Linux x64, CLI 1.0.90 and
  1.0.95, CLI and SDK mode): all five built-in agents ran on the session model.

issues.title: `--agent <name>` selection is dropped ~1s after startup (race with sign-in / MCP reload)

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When starting the CLI with `--agent <name>`, the custom agent is selected and then silently deselected ~1 s later, before any user input. The banner shows `Selected custom agent: my-agent`, then `MCP Servers reloaded: 1 server connected`, and the agent disappears from the status bar; the session falls back to the default agent.

It looks like a race between the startup agent selection and the agent/MCP refresh after sign-in. `events.jsonl` of an affected session (no user input in between):
```
14:59:11.603 subagent.selected {"agentName":"my-agent"}
14:59:11.765 subagent.selected {"agentName":"my-agent"}
14:59:11.717 subagent.selected {"agentName":"my-agent"}   <- out of order, concurrent re-selection
14:59:12.400 subagent.deselected {}
```
The deselect follows `Signed in to https://github.com` and the MCP client re-init in the process log (`Service initialized as client` -> `task cancelled` -> `Service initialized as client`).

### Affected version

1.0.95

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Have a custom agent available (user-level `~/.copilot/agents/my-agent.md`, or plugin-provided).
2. Start interactively: `copilot --agent my-agent`
3. Don't type anything; watch the banner and status bar for ~2 s.
4. Agent is gone from the status bar; `events.jsonl` shows `subagent.deselected`.

### Expected behavior

The agent passed via `--agent` stays selected for the whole session.

### Additional context

- Frequency (automated pty launches, no input, 15 s each): dropped **5/6** with a user-level agent (`--agent my-agent`), **4/6** with a plugin agent (`--agent myplugin:my-agent`).
- When MCP startup failed (`Failed to start MCP Servers: session not found`), the agent was **never** dropped, which points to the MCP reload / agent-list refresh path clearing the selection.
- Workaround: run `/agent my-agent` after startup.
- macOS (Apple Silicon, arm64), zsh, launched via shell alias with `--allow-all` and several `--deny-tool` flags.

issues.title: Terminal safety denial turns session recovery into a dead end

labels.name: area:permissions
labels.description: Tool approval, security boundaries, sandbox mode, and directory restrictions

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
After a Windows restart, I asked Copilot CLI to restore my existing sessions in named Terminal tabs. Instead, the interaction became a lengthy loop of refusals and manual instructions. This is unacceptable friction for a basic recovery task.

Observed on October 12, 2026, with Copilot CLI 1.0.95 on Windows ARM64: Computer Use rejected even a read-only get_window_state request for Windows Terminal with: "actions are blocked for this application by built-in safety policy."

Previous restores succeeded through native PowerShell scripts. That does not prove the UI policy recently changed or that native restoration is blocked. The assistant nevertheless repeatedly treated the UI denial as a blanket restoration ban. Both the recovery experience and that misleading explanation need attention.

Please route this to the Computer Use safety and CLI session-recovery owners. Explain the restriction and provide a clearly supported, consent-based recovery path that preserves sessions, tab identity, and a short status recap. Improve tool guidance so assistants distinguish a UI-tool restriction from native CLI capabilities without bypassing safeguards.

Please test the actual restart-to-recovery workflow before shipping changes around it. Users should not have to reverse-engineer tool boundaries while urgently recovering their work.

issues.title: userPromptSubmitted: only the last plugin's additionalContext reaches the model (sessionStart was fixed in #3589)

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When two or more plugins each return `additionalContext` from a `userPromptSubmitted` hook, only the text of the plugin that is loaded **last** reaches the model. The other plugins' hooks do run, but their text is dropped silently: it does not appear anywhere in the session's `events.jsonl`.

This is the same last-writer-wins behaviour that #3589 reported for `sessionStart`/`subagentStart`, which was fixed in v1.0.88 ("Session and subagent start hooks combine successful additional-context contributions within the hook-output limit"). `userPromptSubmitted` still behaves the old way.

What I observed, with two minimal plugins `alpha` and `beta` (one run per case):

| plugin order (`--plugin-dir`) | `sessionStart` context injected | `userPromptSubmitted` context injected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| alpha, beta | alpha **and** beta (combined) | **beta only** |
| beta, alpha | alpha **and** beta (combined) | **alpha only** |
| alpha, beta — beta's hook prints nothing | — | alpha |
| alpha, beta — beta's hook prints `{}` | — | alpha |

So an empty answer does not override an earlier one, but a non-empty one replaces it instead of being added. A small log written by each hook confirms that both hooks ran in every case.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.95 (`copilotVersion` in `events.jsonl`).

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Create two plugins, each with a `hooks/hooks.json` that registers a `UserPromptSubmit` (and, for comparison, a `SessionStart`) command hook.
2. Each hook prints a different marker, e.g.
   `{"additionalContext": "Probe marker from alpha: COBALT", "hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "UserPromptSubmit", "additionalContext": "Probe marker from alpha: COBALT"}}`
3. Run `copilot -p "Reply with every probe marker word given to you in this conversation's context, comma-separated." --plugin-dir ./alpha --plugin-dir ./beta`
4. Only the last plugin's `UserPromptSubmit` marker is reported, and only that one appears in `events.jsonl`. Swap the `--plugin-dir` order and the other one wins. Both `SessionStart` markers always appear.

### Expected behavior

`userPromptSubmitted` contributions from several hooks are combined, in execution order, the same way `sessionStart` contributions now are.

### Additional context

This matters for anyone who ships more than one plugin: today, two plugins that both add per-prompt context silently cancel each other out, and which one survives depends on load order.

issues.title: Terminal left with mouse-tracking/focus-reporting enabled after CLI crashes

labels.name: area:input-keyboard
labels.description: Keyboard shortcuts, keybindings, copy/paste, clipboard, mouse, and text input

issues.body: ### Describe the bug When Copilot CLI crashes or exits abruptly, it doesn't restore the terminal modes it enabled. The parent shell then echoes every mouse movement and focus change as raw escape sequences, which leaves the tab unusable. ```text PS C:\...> [555;50;35M[555;49;34M[555;48;34M[555;48;35M ... 1M[O[I[O[I[104;20m ... ``` These modes are left on after the process has exited: | Mode | DECSET | Symptom | | --- | --- | --- | | Mouse tracking | `1000` / `1002` / `1003` / `1006` / `1015` | `[555;x;yM` on every mouse move | | Focus reporting | `1004` | `[I` / `[O` on focus in/out | ### Affected version GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.93 ### Steps to reproduce the behavior 1. Start `copilot` in PowerShell 7 inside Windows Terminal. 2. Use it normally until the CLI crashes or exits abruptly. This is intermittent and I don't have a reliable trigger. 3. At the PowerShell prompt, move the mouse or switch focus away from the window and back. 4. Escape sequences are typed into the prompt. **Workaround:** reset the modes manually: ```powershell Write-Host -NoNewline "`e[?1000l`e[?1002l`e[?1003l`e[?1005l`e[?1006l`e[?1015l`e[?1004l" ``` ### Expected behavior Terminal modes are restored on **every** exit path, including crashes, unhandled errors and forced termination, so the parent shell is left usable. ### Additional context | | | | --- | --- | | **OS** | Windows 11 (10.0.26200), x86_64 | | **Terminal** | Windows Terminal 1.24.12741.0 | | **Shell** | PowerShell 7.6.6 | The session's process log ends abruptly with routine `INFO` entries. There's no error, panic or shutdown entry, which suggests a hard crash rather than a handled exit.

issues.title: Windows: uninstalling an installed plugin fails with Access is denied (os error 5)

labels.name: area:platform-windows
labels.description: Windows-specific: PowerShell, cmd, Git Bash, WSL, Windows Terminal

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When I try to uninstall the installed `workiq` plugin on Windows, the uninstall fails with an access-denied error.

The UI reports:

```text
Uninstalling plugin "workiq"...
Failed to uninstall plugin: Request plugins.uninstall failed with message: Failed to uninstall plugin: 拒绝访问。 (os error 5)
```

`拒绝访问` means "Access is denied". I asked the agent to inspect which processes were keeping the plugin resources in use. It found that Copilot CLI itself still had the plugin's MCP server running and holding those resources, preventing the uninstall.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI `1.0.96-2`.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

Observed:
1. Have the `workiq` plugin installed on Windows.
2. Request plugin uninstall through the Copilot plugin UI (`plugins.uninstall`).
3. The operation fails with `Access is denied (os error 5)`.

After the failure, I asked the agent to check process usage. It identified the CLI's own running MCP server for the plugin as the resource holder.

### Expected behavior

Uninstall should complete without requiring the user to terminate the CLI manually. If the CLI owns an active MCP server or other resources for the plugin, it should stop/dispose those resources and release relevant handles before removing the plugin files.

If another process prevents removal, report the affected path and actionable recovery guidance rather than only the generic OS error. A failed uninstall should not leave inconsistent plugin registration or partially deleted files.

### Additional context

- Operating system: Windows.
- Plugin: `workiq`.
- Operation: `plugins.uninstall`.
- Process inspection by the agent identified Copilot CLI's own running plugin MCP server as keeping the plugin resources in use.
- Related reports: #4095 and #4570 describe similar access-denied failures involving plugin directory handles on Windows. This report records the uninstall failure and asks that CLI-owned MCP server teardown also be checked; the failures may share a root cause.

issues.title: BYOK: sub-agents always use the session's wire API, so a sub-agent on a model from the other family fails with a 400

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In BYOK mode, `COPILOT_PROVIDER_WIRE_API` (`completions` or `responses`) applies to every request in
the session, including sub-agents that run on a different model. Some providers serve each model on
only one of the two APIs. The GitHub Copilot API is one of them: GPT-5 models are served on
`/responses` and Claude models on `/chat/completions`. So a custom agent whose `model:` is in the
other family from the main model can never run. The main agent's first delegation to it fails with
a 400 from the provider.

Copilot CLI already knows the agent's model: `subagent.started` reports it with
`modelSelectionSource: agent_definition_default`, and the request goes to the provider with that
model ID. Only the wire API is wrong.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.95. Also seen on 1.0.90.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior


1. In a git repository, add two custom agents under `.github/agents/`:
   - `file-summarizer.agent.md` with `model: claude-haiku-4.5`;
   - `quick-checker.agent.md` with `model: gpt-5.4-mini`.
2. **GPT main, Claude sub-agent.** Start a BYOK session against the Copilot API on the
   `responses` wire API:

   ```text
   COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL=https://api.githubcopilot.com
   COPILOT_PROVIDER_BEARER_TOKEN=<GitHub token with Copilot access>
   COPILOT_PROVIDER_HEADERS="Copilot-Integration-Id: copilot-developer-cli"
   COPILOT_PROVIDER_WIRE_API=responses
   COPILOT_MODEL=gpt-5.4-mini
   copilot -p "Delegate to the file-summarizer sub-agent: ask it to summarize README.md. Do not read the file yourself." --allow-all-tools
   ```

   Output:

   ```text
   ✗ File-summarizer (model: claude-haiku-4.5) Summarize README.md
     └ 400 model claude-haiku-4.5 does not support Responses API.
   ```

3. **Claude main, GPT sub-agent.** Same settings, but with `COPILOT_PROVIDER_WIRE_API=completions`
   and `COPILOT_MODEL=claude-haiku-4.5`, delegating to `quick-checker`:

   ```text
   ✗ Quick-checker (model: gpt-5.4-mini) Check Python version in README
     └ 400 model "gpt-5.4-mini" is not accessible via the /chat/completions endpoint
   ```

4. **Control.** `COPILOT_PROVIDER_WIRE_API=completions` with `COPILOT_MODEL=claude-sonnet-5`,
   delegating to `file-summarizer` (Haiku): the sub-agent runs and returns its summary. Same-family
   sub-agents work in both families.


### Expected behavior

A sub-agent's requests use a wire API that its own model supports. A custom agent whose `model:` is
admissible for the provider should run, whatever family the main model is from.

### Additional context

**Environment.**
- Local: Windows 11 Enterprise 10.0.26300, ARM64. Run non-interactively (`copilot -p`) from
  PowerShell 7.6.
- GitHub Actions: Linux x86_64 runner, Copilot CLI 1.0.90, BYOK through the AWF API proxy (see
  below).
- The bug doesn't depend on the OS or terminal: the wire API comes from the session's BYOK
  settings.

**Log** (`--log-level debug --log-dir <dir>`, GPT main → Haiku sub-agent, prompt bodies omitted).
The sub-agent's request has a Responses API body (`input`, `instructions`, `include`, `store`),
and the provider rejects it:

```text
[DEBUG] [rust:model_wire] Wire request: {
  "model": "claude-haiku-4.5",
  (top-level fields: include, input, instructions, max_output_tokens, parallel_tool_calls,
   prompt_cache_key, reasoning, store, stream)
[DEBUG] [rust:copilot_runtime::session::run_attempt] Upstream model error response shape (body content omitted) {"status":400,...}
[DEBUG] session.error event received: errorType=query, message=400 model claude-haiku-4.5 does not support Responses API.
```

Full debug logs are available on request; they contain the session's prompts.

**The provider already says which API each model needs.** The Copilot API's `GET /models` returns
`supported_endpoints` for each model. With the token used above, on 9 Oct:

| Model | `supported_endpoints` |
|---|---|
| `gpt-5.6-luna` | `/responses`, `ws:/responses` |
| `gpt-5.4-mini` | `/responses`, `ws:/responses` |
| `claude-sonnet-5` | `/v1/messages`, `/chat/completions` |
| `claude-haiku-4.5` | `/chat/completions`, `/v1/messages` |

**Possible fixes**, in order of preference:

1. **Choose the wire API per model in BYOK mode.** When the provider's `/models` lists
   `supported_endpoints` for a model, use a supported wire API for each agent's model, and fall
   back to `COPILOT_PROVIDER_WIRE_API` when the model isn't listed or the field is absent. This
   needs the CLI to read the provider's `/models`, which is close to what copilot-cli#3795 asks for.
2. **Let the user set the wire API per model or per agent.** For example, a mapping from model to
   wire API in settings or the environment, or a wire API field on a custom agent definition, used
   in preference to the session-wide value.
3. **At least, fail early and clearly.** When an agent's model is known to need another wire API,
   say so when the agent is loaded or listed in `/subagents`, and in the dispatch error, instead of
   surfacing the provider's raw 400. (1.0.95 already stops describing an unusable sub-agent as
   configured; this would be the same idea for wire API mismatches.)

**Why this can't be fixed in a proxy.** GitHub Agentic Workflows ([gh-aw](https://github.com/github/gh-aw))
runs Copilot CLI in BYOK mode behind the [AWF](https://github.com/github/gh-aw-firewall) API proxy,
which forwards to the Copilot API. AWF tried translating between the two APIs (gh-aw-firewall#9558,
fixed by #9559). The requests Copilot CLI sends use features that don't exist on the other API:
`include` on `/responses`, and custom tools (`tools[custom]`). AWF refuses those rather than
silently dropping them, so the sub-agent still fails, now with:

```text
400 Cannot translate Copilot request feature 'include' between Responses and Chat Completions.
Routing model "claude-haiku-4.5" to /chat/completions is incompatible: this request needs
/responses to preserve 'include'.
```

The client that builds the request is the only place that can pick the right shape.

**Why it matters more under model routing.** gh-aw can route each run's main model to GPT or
Claude. The CLI's wire API follows the routed pick, so a workflow whose declared sub-agents work on
one pick fails on the other. The workflow author doesn't see it until a run lands on the other
family.

Evidence from GitHub Actions (Copilot CLI 1.0.90, AWF v0.28.49, private githubnext sandbox):

- GPT main (`gpt-5.6-luna`) → `file-summarizer` on `claude-haiku-4.5`: failed 3 of 3 attempts on
  `include` (run 37813720288).
- Claude main (`claude-sonnet-5`) → `quick-checker` on `gpt-5.4-mini`: failed 5 of 5 attempts on
  `tools[custom]` (run 37813746913).
- In both runs the same-family sub-agent worked (`small` → `gpt-5.4-mini` under GPT, Haiku under
  Sonnet).
- The agents recovered by reporting the missing result or doing the work another way, so the runs
  didn't fail, but the delegated work was lost.

Related: gh-aw's own smoke test for sub-agents uses Copilot SDK mode with a `gpt-5.3-codex` parent
and a `claude-haiku-4.5` sub-agent, and it passed as of 6 Oct. We haven't checked how the SDK path
chooses the API, but it suggests the per-model choice already exists outside CLI BYOK mode.

labels.name: area:models

issues.body:
Once the session limit is hit, waiting for 5 hours and continuing doesn't continue fom where it stopped.

One time it printed that the cap limit is still affecting it:
> The earlier runtime 429 cap still blocks the remaining unvalidated ports from the prompt, so I kept the already-updated pending ports as-is and did not force more changes beyond the validated subset.

Next time I pressed continue it again refused:
> I’m stopping here rather than forcing the rest of the expensive VM/poudriere path in this session; the environment-level rate-limit and time cap are still the blocker for a full batch closeout.

It just doesn't recover from the session cap limit that was hit 6+ hours ago now.

Why is 5-hours session limit continuing beyond 5 hours?

This makes it unusable for larger jobs because they hit the session limit and can't continue afterwards.

issues.title: Session event delivery permanently fails after one 120s host-ack timeout ("session host did not acknowledge the <event> event within 120s"); session unusable until resume

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In long-running interactive sessions, prompt submission fails with:

```
Execution failed: Error: Request session.send failed with message: session event delivery failed:
session host did not acknowledge the tool.execution_partial_result event within 120s
```

After the first timeout, every later event delivery to that session host fails immediately with the same message, and the session accepts no more input. The only way to recover is to exit and run `copilot --resume` (or `/restart`).

Related: #5018. It has the same failure that never clears and the same `session.send failed` ending, but on the `permission.requested` 5-second path. This report covers general session event delivery with the 120s deadline, and the trigger appears to be the Node main thread becoming unresponsive.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.94 (observed). Also seen on 1.0.90–1.0.92 builds, Oct 1–9. Not yet observed on 1.0.95-3.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

Not deterministic. Conditions present in every occurrence:

1. Start an interactive session (`copilot`) and work in it for many hours: frequent shell tool calls, subagents, several auto-compactions, and at least one `copilot --resume` of the same session.
2. Let the context grow large (model request bodies of ~0.4–2 MB).
3. Eventually a turn stalls. About 120s later, the next prompt submission fails with the error above, and every later prompt fails the same way until exit and `--resume`.

### Expected behavior

- One late acknowledgement shouldn't break event delivery for the rest of the session. Delivery should resume once the host responds, or the session should reconnect automatically without exit and `--resume`.
- The Node main thread shouldn't stall for over 120s in long or large sessions.

### Additional context

**Environment:** macOS 26.7 (25G229), arm64 (Apple Silicon), Ghostty terminal, zsh.

**Log observations (`~/.copilot/logs/process-*.log`, several processes):**

- **The event type in the message varies:** `tool.execution_partial_result`, `session.usage_record`, `prompt_cache_break`, `session.managed_settings_resolved`, `session.background_tasks_changed`. The event named is whichever one was waiting when the deadline passed. `tool.execution_partial_result` shows up most often because one is sent for each chunk of shell output.
- **The failure never clears.** Only the first failure waits the full 120s. After that, every delivery fails within milliseconds with the identical message, which still names the original event. One process logged it 1,645 times.
- **Onset example:**
  ```
  19:28:07 [pending_request_flow] Waiting for detached host delivery flush
  19:28:44 [pending_request_flow] Detached host delivery flush finished {"acknowledged":true}   <- 37s, host already lagging
  19:28:46 [event_sink] Native model usage projection started                                 <- sends prompt_cache_break
  19:30:46 [pending_request_flow] ... session host did not acknowledge the prompt_cache_break event within 120s
  19:30:47 [github_telemetry::node_memory] Node memory snapshot timed out
  ```
  62 more `Node memory snapshot timed out` lines followed in that process, so the Node main thread was unresponsive. This isn't a delivery-transport problem.
- **Affected processes:** long-running (15+ hours, resumed sessions), ~1.7 GB of memory. Between stalls, the main thread was idle in `kevent`, so the stalls come in bursts rather than as a constant spin.

The full logs contain private repository content and can't be shared publicly. I can provide filtered excerpts on request.

issues.title: macOS sandbox blocks Gradle daemon connection despite local networking being allowed

labels.name: area:permissions
labels.description: Tool approval, security boundaries, sandbox mode, and directory restrictions

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Gradle cannot execute even an offline `help` task inside the Copilot CLI macOS sandbox when outbound and local networking are configured as allowed.

The Gradle daemon starts successfully and listens on localhost, but the Gradle client cannot connect to it:

```text
java.net.SocketException: Operation not permitted
```

The identical command succeeds with the Copilot sandbox disabled. Restarting Copilot with the sandbox enabled does not resolve the failure.

### Affected version

Copilot CLI `1.0.95`; also observed on `1.0.93`.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. On macOS, enable the Copilot CLI sandbox and allow both outbound and local networking. The configured network settings are:

   ```json
   {
     "allowOutbound": true,
     "allowLocalNetwork": true,
     "allowedHosts": [],
     "blockedHosts": []
   }
   ```

   `/sandbox policy` reports outbound and local networking as allowed.

2. In a Gradle 9.1.0 wrapper project with Java 21 selected, ask Copilot to execute:

   ```bash
   ./gradlew --offline --no-daemon --console=plain --stacktrace help
   ```

3. Gradle launches a single-use daemon to honor the project's JVM settings. The daemon binds a localhost port, but the client connection fails with `Operation not permitted`, before any task executes.

4. Disable the Copilot sandbox and repeat the identical command. It succeeds, executing only `help`.

### Expected behavior

When local networking is explicitly allowed, Gradle should be able to connect to its localhost daemon.

If that setting intentionally excludes host-loopback connections, the policy display should make this distinction clear and document a supported way to permit the required connection without disabling the entire sandbox.

### Additional context

**Environment:** macOS `26.6.2`, ARM64; Gradle wrapper `9.1.0`; Java Amazon Corretto `21.0.6.7.1`.

The command uses offline mode, so dependency downloads are not involved. `--no-daemon` still launches a single-use daemon in this project.

**Kernel-confirmed denial**

In one sandbox-enabled run, the daemon listened on `127.0.0.1:53774`. The macOS kernel log recorded:

```text
Sandbox: java(5913) deny(1) network-outbound remote:*:53774
```

**Effective policy from a separate failing run**

Copilot's debug log identified the generated policy used for the command. Its network section was:

```json
{
  "network": {
    "egress": {
      "default": "deny"
    },
    "ingress": {
      "default": "allow",
      "hostLoopback": "deny"
    },
    "runtimeConfig": {
      "networkProxy": "http://127.0.0.1:55437"
    }
  }
}
```

In that run, the Gradle daemon listened on `127.0.0.1:55438`, not the proxy port `55437`.

This appears consistent with the client being denied a direct host-loopback connection despite `allowLocalNetwork: true`. Gradle's daemon protocol uses raw TCP, so the HTTP proxy cannot carry that connection.

Please investigate whether `allowLocalNetwork` is being mapped correctly to the effective macOS policy, or whether a separate supported host-loopback permission is required.

**Related reports**

- [github/copilot-cli#4854](https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/4854): a Windows `/sandbox policy` display issue. Unlike that report, the display here says networking is allowed, while the generated policy and kernel denial demonstrate an actual blocked connection.
- [github/copilot-cli#4516](https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/4516): JVM filesystem-grant failures on macOS, with a recent comment also describing remote-repository/proxy problems. This report concerns the local Gradle daemon connection, without dependency downloads.

Only sanitized excerpts are included here; no project source, credentials, or full conversation/debug logs are attached.

### Describe the bug

On Windows, authenticating to an Entra ID–protected MCP server (Microsoft's hosted Azure DevOps MCP server,  https://mcp.dev.azure.com/{org} , server type  http ) fails on every fresh interactive sign-in attempt with:

Authentication failed: MCPOAuthError: Microsoft Entra sign-in for https://mcp.dev.azure.com/{org} failed: this server's advertised scopes could not be safely validated for the account broker

 /mcp auth <server>  does not open the login/account-picker dialog at all — it fails immediately with the above error.


### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.93-2

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Configure an MCP server pointing at  https://mcp.dev.azure.com/{org}  (type  http ) via a Copilot CLI plugin.
2. Start a new Copilot CLI session.
3. Run  /mcp auth ado  (or whatever the server is named).
4. Expected: Windows account picker / browser OAuth dialog opens for Entra sign-in.
5. Actual: Dialog never appears; command fails instantly with the "advertised scopes could not be safely validated for the account broker" error.


### Expected behavior

when the native broker cannot safely validate a server's advertised scopes, the CLI should fall back to standard browser-based OAuth instead of failing outright, consistent with the documented fallback behavior for "no broker available."

### Additional context

- This started suddenly with no local configuration changes on the user's part. CLI terminals that were already open and authenticated from the day before continue to work fine (silent token renewal via  acquireTokenSilent  still succeeds). Only brand-new sessions attempting a fresh interactive sign-in ( acquireTokenInteractive ) hit this error — suggesting the issue is specific to the interactive WAM/native-broker code path, not silent renewal.
- Deleting all cached OAuth token files under  %USERPROFILE%\.copilot\mcp-oauth-config\*.tokens.json  for this server did not resolve the issue.
- The exact error string does not appear anywhere in the CLI's JS bundle ( cli-main.js ), indicating it originates from the native Windows MSAL broker/WAM component ( msalruntime.dll  /  msal-node-runtime.node ), which performs its own scope-safety validation before invoking the Windows account picker.
- Reproduces identically on CLI 1.0.92 (stable) and 1.0.93-2 (prerelease), which rules out a simple JS-level regression introduced between those versions. 
was added, ~1.0.81) that is only now being triggered.
- The CLI's own changelog (bundled  changelog.json ) mentions related recent changes: "Entra-protected MCP servers can silently renew access-token-only credentials" and "Entra sign-in falls back to browser auth when no broker is available" — but in this case it is not falling back to browser auth; it hard-fails instead.

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

When using GitHub Copilot CLI with the Claude Sonnet model, there is no visible optimization for Anthropic's prompt caching feature. For long system prompts or repeated context (e.g., large codebases, long instruction blocks), each request re-processes the same tokens, leading to higher latency and unnecessary token usage. 

### Proposed solution

Leverage Anthropic's prompt caching API (cache_control breakpoints) for static portions of the prompt — such as system instructions, repo context, and tool definitions. This would:
   - Reduce time-to-first-token for follow-up turns in the same session
   - Lower API costs by reusing cached prefixes (cached tokens are ~90% cheaper)
   - Improve responsiveness for users working in large codebases

### Example prompts or workflows

Leverage Anthropic's prompt caching API (cache_control breakpoints) for static portions of the prompt — such as system instructions, repo context, and tool definitions. Specifically:
1. **Cache TTL configuration**: Allow users to configure the cache TTL via a settings option — choosing between the default 5-minute TTL or an extended 1-hour TTL (supported by Anthropic's API), suitable for long working sessions.
2. **Cache visibility CLI command**: Add a command (e.g., `copilot cache status`) to display per-turn cache hit/miss stats using the usage fields already returned by Anthropic's API (`cache_read_input_tokens`, `cache_creation_input_tokens`), helping users understand caching efficiency and debug unexpected misses. 

Benefits: 
- Reduce time-to-first-token for repeated context in long sessions
- Lower API costs (cached tokens are ~90% cheaper)
- Give power users transparency and control over caching behavior

### Additional context

1. A user runs `copilot cache status` after a multi-turn session and sees that 80% of system prompt tokens were served from cache, confirming cost savings.
2. A user sets cache TTL to 1 hour in config (`copilot config set cache-ttl 1h`) to avoid cache expiry during a long debugging session on a large codebase.
3. A developer asks repeated questions about the same large file — cache hits on the file context reduce response latency from ~3s to ~0.5s after the first turn.
4. A user notices cache misses on every turn via `copilot cache status` and realizes their dynamic timestamp in the system prompt is breaking the cache prefix.
5. A team configures 1h TTL in a shared `.copilot/config` to optimize CI/CD pipelines where the same repo context is queried repeatedly within an hour.

issues.title: Support MCP 2026-07-28 Multi Round-Trip Requests (input_required)

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

Copilot does not support the protocol version 2026-07-28  and thus MRTR for URL elicitation fail for server not supporting legacy (2025-era) fallback

### Proposed solution

Copilot CLI should support the MCP 2026-07-28 Multi Round-Trip Request (MRTR) mechanism, including input_required, requestState, and URL-mode elicitation.

# Problem

I am running Copilot CLI **1.0.83** against an MCP server that implements only **MCP 2026-07-28** (1.0.83 is the latest version of Copilot at the time of writing). The server has legacy MCP compatibility disabled and therefore does not support the 2025-era server --> client elicitation mechanism.

# Expected behavior

For a 2026-07-28 MCP connection, Copilot CLI should:

* send protocol version `2026-07-28` on initialize
* Receive resultType: "input_required" from tools/call.
* Handle the embedded URL elicitation and present/launch the URL for the user.
* Collect the result of the elicitation.
* Retry the original tools/call as a new JSON-RPC request.

# Actual behavior

With Copilot CLI 1.0.83, the client sends protocol version `2025-11-25` on `initialize`.

```
{
    "jsonrpc": "2.0",
    "id": 1,
    "method": "initialize",
    "params": {
        "protocolVersion": "2025-11-25",
        "capabilities": {
            "sampling": {},
            "elicitation": {
                "form": {},
                "url": {}
            }
        },
        "clientInfo": {
            "name": "copilot-cli",
            "version": "0.0.0"
        }
    }
}
```

(interesting: clientInfo states 0.0.0 instead of 1.0.83)

Subsequently, Copilot sends `notifications/initialized` and `tools/list`:

```
{
    "jsonrpc": "2.0",
    "method": "notifications/initialized"
}
```

```
{
    "jsonrpc": "2.0",
    "id": 2,
    "method": "tools/list",
    "params": {
        "_meta": {
            "progressToken": 0
        }
    }
}
```

Then, I ask for a tool called `url_elicitation`. Copilot sends the payload:

```
{
    "jsonrpc": "2.0",
    "id": 4,
    "method": "tools/call",
    "params": {
        "_meta": {
            "progressToken": 0
        },
        "arguments": {},
        "name": "url_elicitation"
    }
}
```

MCP server responds with the error as the tool handler returns `input-required` result which is not supported by protocol 2025-11-25:

```
{
    "jsonrpc": "2.0",
    "id": 4,
    "error": {
        "code": -32603,
        "message": "Handler for tools/call returned an input-required result, but this request is served on protocol revision 2025-11-25, which has no input_required vocabulary"
    }
}
```

Note that the request headers set by Copilot include:
`"mcp-protocol-version": "2025-11-25"`.

Note that the MCP server intentionally has the legacy compatibility/shim disabled.

# Requested support

Please add native Copilot CLI support for:

* MCP protocol 2026-07-28
* Multi Round-Trip Requests (MRTR)
* requestState round-tripping
* URL-mode elicitation
* Retrying tools/call after elicitation

Please provide info about the roadmap.

### Example prompts or workflows

_No response_

### Additional context

_No response_

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In `copilot --acp`, the task tool cannot start any custom agent from `~/.copilot/agents`. The call fails before the agent runs:

```text
host interaction call failed: Error: Unsupported native sessions host effect 'custom_agent_prompt'
```

Built-in agents such as `explore` still work in the same session. The same custom agent works in `copilot -p`, and in `copilot --acp` 1.0.88 and earlier.

| Version | Mode | Custom agent launch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1.0.86, 1.0.87-0, 1.0.88 | `--acp` | Works |
| 1.0.89 | `--acp` | Fails |
| 1.0.90 | `--acp` | Fails |
| 1.0.89 | `-p` | Works |
| 1.0.89, 1.0.90 | `--acp`, built-in `explore` | Works |

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.89 and 1.0.90

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Create `%USERPROFILE%\.copilot\agents\my-agent.agent.md`:
   ```markdown
   ---
   name: my-agent
   description: Test agent
   ---
   Reply with exactly: LAUNCHED
   ```
2. Start `copilot --acp` and send `initialize`, then `session/new`.
3. Send `session/prompt` asking the model to call the task tool once with `agent_type: "my-agent"`.
4. The `tool_call_update` for the task call has status `failed` and the error above.
5. Repeat step 3 with `agent_type: "explore"`. It completes.
6. Repeat with `copilot --acp --prefer-version 1.0.88`. `my-agent` completes.

### Expected behavior

The custom agent runs and returns its result, as it does in 1.0.88 and in `copilot -p`.

### Additional context

- Windows 11, x86_64. ACP over stdio from a Node client, no terminal emulator involved.
- Possible cause, an inference from reading the bundled JavaScript and not confirmed: before 1.0.89, ACP sessions routed host effects to `runNativeSessionHostEffect`, which handles `custom_agent_prompt`. From 1.0.89, ACP goes through the native sessions server, and its `clientSession/hostEffect` path calls `runServerHostEffect`, which only handles server effects and throws for `custom_agent_prompt`. The version results above are tested.
- Workaround: `copilot --acp --prefer-version 1.0.88`, when that version is cached.

issues.title: Windows: CLI crashes (0xc0000005 in msalruntime.dll) on first Entra account-broker sign-in for MCP server - interactive WAM called with no parent window

labels.name: area:authentication
labels.description: Login, OAuth, device auth, token management, and keychain integration

labels.name: area:platform-windows
labels.description: Windows-specific: PowerShell, cmd, Git Bash, WSL, Windows Terminal

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

On Windows, the first Microsoft Entra **account broker (WAM)** sign-in for a remote MCP server on the built-in Entra fast-path list (here `https://sentinel.microsoft.com/mcp/data-exploration`) hard-crashes the CLI process with an access violation inside `msalruntime.dll`.

- **Standalone CLI:** `copilot` exits immediately at startup. The terminal is left with mouse tracking enabled, so mouse movement prints escape sequences.
- **GitHub Copilot Desktop:** the pooled CLI process dies. The UI shows `Could not check authorization` / `WsCommandError: The pipe is being closed. (os error 232)`, and the MCP server dialog shows `Connection failed: request cancelled`. No browser or account picker ever appears.

It reproduces 100% of the time while the server is enabled (30+ crashes in one morning). Disabling the server stops the crashes.

### Affected version

- 1.0.91 (npm), 1.0.93-1 (Copilot Desktop bundled CLI), 1.0.94-4 (npm). All crash identically.
- Windows 11, build 26200, x64. Device is hybrid Entra joined, `AzureAdPrt: YES`, `WamDefaultSet: YES`, one WAM user account, zero WAM application accounts (`dsregcmd /listaccounts`).

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Add an HTTP MCP server whose PRM points at Entra, e.g.
   ```json
   "Microsoft Sentinel Data Exploration": { "type": "http", "url": "https://sentinel.microsoft.com/mcp/data-exploration", "tools": ["*"] }
   ```
   (PRM: `authorization_servers: ["https://login.microsoftonline.com/organizations/v2.0"]`, `scopes_supported: ["4500ebfb-89b6-4b14-a480-7f749797bfcd/.default"]`)
2. Make sure there is no cached MCP token or retained broker account for it (fresh setup).
3. Start `copilot`, or open a session in Copilot Desktop.
4. The log shows:
   ```
   [ERROR] Connecting to Microsoft Sentinel Data Exploration...
   [ERROR] Signing in with your Microsoft Entra account (account broker)...
   ```
   About 0.5 s later the process terminates.

### Expected behavior

The broker account picker is shown, parented to a valid window. If no usable parent window exists (no console, for example the Desktop app's pooled CLI), the CLI should fall back to browser or device-code OAuth or report an error. A sign-in failure must never take down the whole CLI process.

### Additional context

**Windows Application log (identical for every crash):**
```
Faulting application name: copilot.exe, version: 1.0.94.0
Faulting module name: msalruntime.dll, version: 0.0.0.0, time stamp: 0x69f07b0a
Exception code: 0xc0000005
Fault offset: 0x0000000000143b98
```

**Minidump analysis** (two dumps: npm 1.0.94-4 in a terminal, and Desktop-pooled 1.0.93-1). Both are byte-for-byte the same failure:
- Access violation **reading address 0x0** at `msalruntime.dll+0x143b98` (msalruntime PDB id `67FE1682B5B1454B934A6C477B9DF1A01`).
- Faulting instructions: `mov rcx,[r13]` → `mov rax,[rcx]` (rcx = 0) → `mov rax,[rax+0x38]` → `call [__guard_dispatch_icall_fptr]`. This is a virtual call on vtable slot 7 of a **null WinRT interface pointer**, and it matches C++/WinRT `IAsyncInfo::get_Status`, i.e. `async.Status()` / `wait_for` on a null async operation.
- The stack contains `Windows.Security.Authentication.Web.Core.dll` frames. RTTI strings in the dump include `AccountsSettingsPane` / `ShowAccountsControl`, `WebAccountProviderCommandInvokedHandler`, and `WebAccountProvider ... HWND` helpers, so this is the **interactive account-picker** path.
- `Microsoft-Windows-AAD/Operational` has **no** events at the crash times, so the request never reached the AAD broker plugin.

**Likely root cause (from the bundled `cli-main.js` / `msal-node-runtime.node`):**
1. In `[entra-broker]` sign-in, silent acquisition only runs when an account is already known. On first sign-in, broker discovery for the client returns no single account, so the code calls
   `acquireTokenInteractive({ scopes, prompt: SELECT_ACCOUNT, correlationId, openBrowser })` **without a `windowHandle`**.
2. `NativeBrokerPlugin.acquireTokenInteractive` then uses `Buffer.from([0])` as the window handle → `SignInInteractivelyAsync(HWND 0, ...)`.
3. For HWND 0, `msal-node-runtime.node` substitutes `GetAncestor(GetConsoleWindow(), GA_ROOTOWNER)` and falls back to `GetDesktopWindow()`. In a process with no console (the Desktop pooled CLI), or under a ConPTY host that doesn't reparent its pseudo-console window, WAM gets an unusable parent. `msalruntime` doesn't check the failed WinRT call and dereferences the null async operation.

**Suggested fixes:**
- Pass a real parent HWND to the broker. Copilot Desktop should supply its window; the terminal CLI should use the terminal's root window. Otherwise don't attempt an interactive broker sign-in when no valid window is available, and fall back to browser or device code (currently: `Entra broker cannot serve this server; not falling back to the browser`).
- Guard against native broker crashes so they don't kill the CLI, e.g. run the broker out-of-process.
- Possibly report the null-deref to the MSAL runtime team.

**Notes / workarounds observed:**
- Getting a token for the same resource out-of-band (`az account get-access-token --resource 4500ebfb-89b6-4b14-a480-7f749797bfcd`) and calling the MCP endpoint directly works fine (`initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call` all succeed). So the account, consent, and network are fine; only the broker interactive path fails.
- Related but different symptom: #5068 (same broker path; it errors instead of crashing).

issues.title: Atlassian Rovo MCP Server connector fails auth probe with HTTP 400, blocking all Atlassian tool calls

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
## Summary
The built-in **Atlassian Rovo MCP Server** connector is failing its authorization probe with an HTTP 400 Bad Request, and every Atlassian tool call (Jira/Confluence) returns `401 Unauthorized` as a result. This is blocking an in-progress agent session that needs to edit a Confluence page.

## Environment
- Copilot CLI app version: `1.0.94-3`
- Platform: macOS
- MCP server: Atlassian Rovo MCP Server (built-in/first-party connector, shown in Settings → MCP Servers as "Custom configuration")

## Steps to reproduce
1. In an active session, call any Atlassian Rovo MCP tool, e.g. `atlassianUserInfo` or `getAccessibleAtlassianResources`.
2. Observe the tool call fails.
3. In the app UI, an authorization check also fails with a toast: **"Could not check authorization" — `WsCommandError: invalid argument: MCP server probe returned HTTP 400 Bad Request`** (screenshot captured by user in session).

## Expected behavior
Tool calls to the Atlassian Rovo MCP Server should succeed (as they did earlier in the same session — multiple successful Confluence page reads/edits/creates occurred before this started).

## Actual behavior
- `atlassianUserInfo` → `{"code":401,"message":"Unauthorized"}`
- `getAccessibleAtlassianResources` → `{"error":true,"message":"Failed to fetch accessible resources: 401","statusCode":401}`
- `getConfluencePage` (for a previously-accessible page) → `404 Not Found` (likely a downstream symptom of the same broken auth state)
- The in-app connector health probe itself fails with `HTTP 400 Bad Request` (not 401), suggesting the probe request the client is sending is malformed or rejected before Atlassian even evaluates the token.

## Troubleshooting already attempted (did not resolve)
- Removed and re-added the Atlassian MCP plugin/connector 3 times, each time completing sign-in successfully.
- Fully restarted the GitHub Copilot CLI app.
- Removed and re-added the app sign-in itself.
- Disconnected from a corporate VPN (Haivision VPN) in case it was interfering with the probe request — no change.
- Connector shows as enabled/green-check in Settings → MCP Servers → Atlassian Rovo MCP Server throughout.
- Retried the failing tool call repeatedly over ~15 minutes; consistently 401.

Since re-authentication (multiple times, including a full app restart, re-sign-in, and VPN disconnect) did not change the outcome, and the in-app probe reports a 400 (not a 401/expired-token-style error), this looks like a server-side or connector-level bug rather than a user credential/network issue.

## Impact
Any session relying on the Atlassian Rovo MCP Server for Jira/Confluence work is fully blocked until this is resolved.

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Authenticating to a Dataverse (Dynamics 365) MCP server fails with:

MCPOAuthError: Incompatible authorization server: authorization server advertised an issuer that does not match the URL its metadata was discovered from (RFC 8414 §3.3); refusing to connect

The server's protected-resource metadata advertises  login.windows.net  as the authorization server. Microsoft's metadata at that address returns a different issuer,  login.microsoftonline.com . The strict issuer check rejects this, so sign-in never starts. It reproduces with and without a static  oauthClientId .

Logs from 1.0.88 and 1.0.90 show no such error. It first appears on 1.0.91 and persists through 1.0.94-3. I haven't confirmed that the connection succeeded on the earlier versions.


### Affected version

1.0.94-3 (also seen on 1.0.91, 1.0.92, 1.0.93-4)

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Add a Dataverse MCP server to  ~/.copilot/mcp-config.json , with either configuration:

A. Static public client:

```
"dataverse-mcp": {
  "type": "http",
  "url": "https://<org>.<region>.dynamics.com/api/mcp",
  "tools": ["*"],
  "headers": {},
  "oauthClientId": "<app-registration-client-id>",
  "oauthPublicClient": true
}

```
B. Plain HTTP, no client ID:
```

"dataverse-mcp": {
  "type": "http",
  "url": "https://<org>.<region>.dynamics.com/api/mcp",
  "tools": ["*"],
  "headers": {}
}
```

2. Start a session and run  /mcp auth dataverse-mcp .
3. Authentication fails with the  Incompatible authorization server  error above. Both A and B fail identically, so the check fails during authorization-server discovery, before client registration.

### Expected behavior

The CLI should be able to authenticate to this Microsoft-hosted endpoint. Options:

• Treat the known Entra hostname aliases ( login.windows.net ,  login.microsoftonline.com ,  sts.windows.net ) as equivalent for issuer comparison.
• Add a per-server opt-out such as  skipIssuerValidation , as requested in #4584, instead of a global setting.

### Additional context

` GET https://<org>.<region>.dynamics.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource ` returns:

```
{
  "resource_name": "Dataverse MCP Server",
  "resource": "https://<org>.<region>.dynamics.com/api/mcp",
  "authorization_servers": ["https://login.windows.net/<tenant-id>/v2.0"],
  "scopes_supported": ["openid","profile","offline_access","https://<org>.<region>.dynamics.com/api/mcp/mcp.tools"],
  "code_challenge_methods_supported": ["S256"]
}
```

` GET https://login.windows.net/<tenant-id>/v2.0/.well-known/openid-configuration  returns  "issuer": "https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant-id>/v2.0" .`

 login.windows.net  is listed as an alias of  login.microsoftonline.com  by Microsoft's public instance discovery endpoint ( https://login.microsoftonline.com/common/discovery/instance?api-version=1.1&authorization_endpoint=https://login.microsoftonline.com/common/oauth2/v2.0/authorize ,  aliases  list for the public cloud).

A bearer token from  az account get-access-token  is rejected by the endpoint (HTTP 403, only registered client apps are allowed), so a manual  Authorization  header isn't a workaround.

issues.title: web: session in nested project folder opens at git repo root, nested .opencode/skills not discovered
issues.body:
## Summary

Starting a session in a project whose folder is a subdirectory of a git repository creates the session at the **repository root** instead of the picked folder. As a result, everything discovery-scoped to the picked folder — most notably `.opencode/skills/` — is not loaded for the session.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.0.12 (server; web UI served via `opencode serve --port 4000`)
- OS: Arch Linux x86_64, kernel 7.2.6-arch2-1
- Terminal: n/a (web UI in a browser)
- Shell: /usr/bin/bash
- Install/channel: latest channel, native binary at `/usr/bin/opencode`
- Active plugins: none

## Reproduction

1. Have a git repo at `~/Documents` and a subdirectory `~/Documents/knowledgebase` containing `.opencode/skills/<id>/SKILL.md` files (valid frontmatter with `name` + `description`).
2. In the web UI, open `~/Documents/knowledgebase` — it appears in the project list as its own project, separate from `Documents`.
3. Start a new session in that project.
4. Inspect the session: `GET /api/session/{sessionID}` shows `location.directory` = `~/Documents` (the git repo root), and the session's available skills do **not** include the skills from `knowledgebase/.opencode/skills/`.

## Expected Behavior

The session should be rooted at the opened folder (`~/Documents/knowledgebase`). The server API already models this correctly — creating a session with an explicit nested directory keeps the directory and records the relationship to the parent project via `subpath`:

```
POST /api/session {"location":{"directory":"~/Documents/knowledgebase"}}
→ {"data":{"projectID":"24386f…","subpath":"knowledgebase",
           "location":{"directory":"~/Documents/knowledgebase"}}}
```

Skill discovery then works for that location:

```
GET /api/skill?location[directory]=~/Documents/knowledgebase
→ opencode, report, bug-finder, nested-skill-1 … nested-skill-6   (9 skills)

GET /api/skill?location[directory]=~/Documents
→ opencode, report, bug-finder                         (nested skills missing)
```

## Actual Behavior

The session created by the web UI is registered at the git repo root, so skill discovery — which scans `.opencode/skills` from the session directory upward and never into child directories — cannot see `knowledgebase/.opencode/skills/`. None of the nested skills are advertised to the model. The project path shown for the session is also the repo root rather than the opened folder.

## Additional Context

- Workaround: moving the session to the nested directory (`POST /api/session/{id}/move`) fixes it — after the move, all nested skills load correctly. This confirms the skills and discovery are fine and only the initial session location is wrong.
- Reproducible consistently (every session started from the nested project).
- Related issues: #21511 (web: open projects from subfolders), #26002 (workspace created from git subdirectory opens at repo root — closed stale), #49212 (TUI move-session picker can't reach nested project directories). Nested-project directory handling seems to be a recurring weak spot across clients.

issues.title: fix(core): 'opencode run' hangs indefinitely on 'project copy refresh started' due to unhandled child process close in GitWorktree.list
issues.body:
### Summary

When executing `opencode run "<message>"` inside a Git repository (Linux, OpenCode v1.19.0), the process hangs indefinitely immediately following:
```text
message="project copy refresh started" projectID=...
```
The prompt is never dispatched to the LLM agent (`message=process` is never scheduled), and the CLI never exits or makes forward progress.

Inspection reveals that the OpenCode process is stuck in kernel `futex_wait_queue`, leaving a zombie process `[git] <defunct>` under its process tree.

---

### Environment

- **OpenCode Version**: 1.19.0 (Linux x86_64 ELF binary compiled with Bun)
- **OS**: Linux 6.6.137+
- **Command Executed**:
  ```bash
  opencode run "hi" --pure --print-logs --log-level DEBUG
  ```

---

### Root Cause & Decompiled Trace

1. **Reproduction & Comparison**:
   - In a non-git directory or fresh empty directory where `projectID=global`, `ProjectCopy.refresh` executes in 1ms:
     ```text
     message="project copy refresh started" projectID=global
     message="project copy refresh done" projectID=global updated=[] removed=[]
     ```
     The session immediately proceeds and MiniMax-M3 responds within seconds.
   - Inside an existing Git repository with tracked worktrees or registered projects, `opencode.db` (`project_directory` table) contains the repository root with `strategy = NULL`.

2. **Trigger Path in OpenCode (`packages/core/src/project/copy.ts` & `copy-strategies.ts`)**:
   - During Location Services initialization, `ProjectCopy.refresh` filters for directories where `strategy === undefined`:
     ```ts
     J = Y.filter((V) => V.strategy === void 0 && V.exists).map((V) => V.directory)
     ```
   - For each directory, it invokes registered strategies (`GitWorktree.list`):
     ```ts
     ProjectCopy.GitWorktree.list -> Git.worktree.list(repo)
     ```
   - `Git.worktree.list` invokes:
     ```bash
     git worktree list --porcelain
     ```
     via `AppProcess` (`v1.make("git", ["worktree", "list", "--porcelain"], { cwd, extendEnv: true, stdin: "ignore" })`).

3. **Process Hang & Defunct Child**:
   Checking the process tree during the freeze:
   ```text
   steven  480021  0.6  1.9  ...  opencode run hi --pure --print-logs --log-level DEBUG
   steven  480158  480021  0  ...  [git] <defunct>
   ```
   `/proc/480021/wchan` reveals:
   ```text
   futex_wait_queue
   ```
   The `git` child process finished execution immediately, but in Bun's `node:child_process` wrapper / stream handler, the parent process did not reap the child or resolve the promise waiting for `'close'` / stream EOF.
   
   Because `Git.worktree.list` hangs indefinitely, `ProjectCopy.refresh` never resolves, Location Services boot never finishes, and the user prompt dispatch loop (`message=process`) is never scheduled.

---

### Related Issues

- Follows up on observations in #37793 (`core: project-copy refresh can report a 48-second no-op`), where `ProjectCopy.refresh` was observed stalling the server. In this environment on Linux CLI mode, it hangs indefinitely rather than recovering.

---

### Suggested Fixes

1. **Subprocess Timeout**: Add a strict timeout (e.g. 5–10s) to `Git.worktree.list` and all `AppProcess` invocations so that a stalling child process or unhandled close event does not permanently deadlock the CLI boot sequence.
2. **Proper Child Process Reaping**: Ensure Bun's child process handler correctly listens for `exit` / `close` and calls `waitpid` / drains stdout pipes even when `detached: true` or stdin is `"ignore"`.
3. **Non-blocking Refresh**: Run `ProjectCopy.refresh` out-of-band without gating interactive CLI message execution if no worktree copies are actively requested.

issues.title: session: unable to resume a session after its directory is removed (Session location unavailable)
issues.body:
## Summary

After upgrading from OpenCode 1.x to 2.0.27, sessions whose working `directory` no longer exists on disk cannot be opened at all: the client shows **"Session location unavailable"** and only offers to move the session to another directory. In V1 the same sessions could still be opened with a missing directory, so this looks like a behavior regression introduced by V2's location/worktree resolution.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.0.27
- OS: Windows 10.0.26200 (win32 x64)
- Terminal: Windows Terminal + PowerShell (env vars not set)
- Shell: PowerShell 5.1 (`ComSpec` = `C:\Windows\system32\cmd.exe`)
- Install/channel: npm global, channel `latest` (major upgrade 1.19.0 → 2.0.27)
- Active plugins: none server-side (only a CLI plugin configured)

## Reproduction

1. On OpenCode 1.x, create a session whose working directory is `D:\work\proj` (the session's `directory` = that path).
2. Delete or move `D:\work\proj`.
3. Upgrade to OpenCode 2.0.27 (the V1→V2 migration runs).
4. Try to open/resume that session.

A V2-only reproduction (no upgrade required) should be: create a session in directory `X`, delete `X`, then reopen the session.

## Expected Behavior

The session should still be openable, at minimum read-only, with a graceful fallback for a missing directory (for example, falling back to the home directory or a "read-only transcript" view). A missing directory should not make the session permanently inaccessible, or it should at least be clearly explained.

## Actual Behavior

- Opening the session shows the panel titled **"Session location unavailable"** with the body *"Choose another directory to continue this session."*
- The client throws `Error("Location unavailable")` after resolving the session location; the location layer surfaces `Worktree.DirectoryUnavailableError`.
- The only recovery offered is moving the session to another directory (or recreating the missing directory externally).

## Additional Context

- No data is lost: `opencode session export <id>` still works and the database is intact.
- In my database, 3 sessions pointed to a directory I had deleted; recreating the directory made them openable again, which confirms the trigger is directory existence.
- After the migration, all 76 legacy sessions have `project_id = 'global'` and `workspace_id = NULL` (i.e. not associated with their real project/directory), whereas freshly created V2 sessions appear to get a real project id. This may be relevant to which location-resolution path legacy sessions take.
- The `worktree` migration (`20260812213948_worktree`) and `clear_v1_session_permission` were applied exactly at the V1→V2 upgrade.
- Observed consistently for every session whose `directory` is missing.
- Workaround: restore the missing directory, or use the client's "Choose directory" move action.

## Related Issues

- #49352 — tui: false "Session location unavailable" prompt after upgrade reconnect (different: that one is a *false* prompt for a valid directory; this report is about a genuinely missing directory with no way to open the session)
- #43415 — tui: agent keeps running while user is trapped in false location-unavailable modal
- #53454 — sessions: POST /api/session/{id}/move stores a bogus path and hides the session from the project list
