issues.body:
### What happened?

In SDK 1.1.0, `session.abort()` called by a public `agent_settled` subscriber resolves successfully, but a continuation already queued by an extension still starts another HTTP provider request. This can start work after a host has stopped the session. Compaction is not required.

### Steps to reproduce

Run the standalone local HTTP reproduction in the comment below with `node http-repro.mjs abort-no-compact`. It loads only one inline extension (`noExtensions: true`) and uses Pi's real OpenAI-compatible streaming provider against localhost.

1. A one-time extension `agent_settled` handler queues `pi.sendMessage(..., { triggerTurn: true })`.
2. The subsequent public `session.subscribe()` callback calls `session.abort()` once.
3. Observe: `request:1 → continuation-queued → abort-requested → abort-resolved → request:2 → prompt-resolved`.

Reproduced 5/5 times, including when `clearQueue()` is called before abort. The active-request cancellation control stops after one request, also 5/5.

### Expected behavior

Abort should prevent this already-queued continuation from starting a new provider request. No new work is submitted after abort.

Related: #9340, #9783 and #10289 cover other cancellation boundaries; this case is specifically the deferred actions replayed after `agent_settled` callbacks.

### Version

`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@1.1.0`, fresh npm install; Node 26.5.0, macOS.

issues.title: Add a modelDiscovery setting so /model and /scoped-models can ignore providers enabled only by environment variables

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Add an opt-in `settings.json` option that controls which providers model discovery advertises:

```json
{ "modelDiscovery": "all" }
```

- `"all"` (default): current behavior. Every provider with usable credentials is listed, including providers enabled only by an exported environment variable.
- `"registered"`: only providers registered through `/login` (`auth.json`), `--api-key`, `models.json`, or an extension, plus providers that need no credential. `/model`, `pi --list-models`, and model cycling all honor it.

### Why?

Exported API keys silently populate the model pickers. On my machine `pi --list-models` returns 471 models: 380 from `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, 78 from a HuggingFace token, and only 6 that I actually registered. Model switching is one of the most frequent interactions in the CLI, so scrolling that list every time adds up.

`/scoped-models` does not solve it: it reads the same `ModelRuntime.getAvailableSnapshot()` as `/model`, so configuring a scope means scrolling the same 471 entries. There is currently no way to reduce the list except unexporting the keys.

This looks like the same underlying behavior as #8646 (env activates providers after logout) and #8477 (`/model` should default to configured models); both were closed no-action. What is new here: `/scoped-models` shares the source, so scoping cannot self-serve, and this is an opt-in switch rather than a change to the default.

An opt-in switch with an unchanged default is additive: users who rely on environment variables keep today's behavior. Request auth is unchanged either way, so a hidden provider still works once it is registered.

### How? (optional)

Add `modelDiscovery` to `settings.json`. In `"registered"` mode, filter `ModelRuntime.getAvailableSnapshot()` and `getAvailable()` by credential source: keep stored / runtime / `models.json` / extension providers and credential-less providers; drop providers whose only credential is an ambient environment variable.

I have this working on a fork (settings schema, `setModelDiscoveryMode()`, unit tests) and can open a PR if the direction is acceptable. If the core should stay minimal, an extension hook that lets an extension filter the available-model list would also solve it; I can implement either.

issues.title: After compaction, stale signed thinking blocks are replayed every turn; Anthropic drops them (prefix_binding_mismatch) on every request
issues.body:
## What happened?

After a manual compaction in a long session, pi prints this on every subsequent turn:

```text
Anthropic dropped 15 thinking blocks: prefix_binding_mismatch at messages.5.content.0; prefix_binding_mismatch at messages.11.content.0; ...
```

The same 15 paths, every request, for the rest of the session. The session keeps working, the warning just never stops.

Looking at my session `.jsonl`: a long turn hit ~120k tokens, I compacted manually. Compaction kept a tail of the original conversation (`firstKeptEntryId` onward), and the assistant messages in that tail still have signed thinking blocks. Those signatures were created against the pre-compaction prefix, so Anthropic now rejects them and drops the blocks. Pi keeps them in its history though, so it replays the same mismatch on every request and the warning repeats forever.

## Steps to reproduce

Happened in a real multi-hour session:

1. Long agentic session on `claude-fable-5-1` with thinking on, long enough that the context grows large.
2. Run `/compact` manually (I didn't test whether auto-compaction does the same).
3. Keep working. The `prefix_binding_mismatch` warning appears on every turn from then on, always with identical paths.

## Expected behavior

Either don't send stale thinking blocks after compaction, or at least don't warn about the same drop on every single turn.

## Version

0.85.1, provider `anthropic`, model `claude-fable-5-1`.

issues.title: Session outliving its release loses not-yet-loaded providers after pi update prunes it (Cannot find module)

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
**What happened?**

`pi update` prunes old releases without checking for running sessions. A long-running session that outlives its release keeps working only for API chunks already in memory; switching to a provider whose chunk was never loaded fails with:

```
Error: Cannot find module '.../dist/bundle/chunks/anthropic-messages-Q7SXESRX.js'
imported from '.../dist/bundle/chunks/chunk-TJXZSVTD.js'
```

No restart hint appears — `detectInstallChange` compares the startup `package.json`, and files vanishing from a still-listed release look unchanged. The provider stays broken until restart. In 1.0.2 the same family of error killed the process outright; #10439 fixed codemode's copy of this (worker pinned in memory) but provider API chunks are still `lazyApi(() => import(...))`.

Two sides to it:

- Provider APIs load on first stream call; the ESM loader cache protects only what has already loaded.
- Update pruning keeps just the new release and the replaced one (`package-manager-cli.js`), so a session living across two updates loses the directory it runs from.

**Steps to reproduce** (1.2.0, managed install)

1. Start interactive pi, send a message with e.g. an `openai-completions` model.
2. Move `dist/bundle/chunks/anthropic-messages-*.js` out of the running release (simulates the prune).
3. Switch to an `anthropic-messages` model, send a message → `Cannot find module`, no restart hint.
4. Switch back to the first model → still works (its chunk is cached in memory).

Real-world trigger: keep one session open across two `pi update` runs, then switch models.

**Expected behavior**

Model switching in a running session should not depend on files pruning may have deleted. The #10439 approach generalizes: lazy provider streams could expose an optional `preload()` (force the dynamic import), and the agent session could call it whenever a model is selected. The ESM cache then covers every provider the session switches to, so it keeps streaming after its release is pruned. Happy to send a PR along these lines.

**Version**: 1.2.0 (managed install); the 1.0.2 process exit was observed on an npm install.

issues.title: Windows: settings shellPath is non-deterministically ignored when extensions are loaded; PATH fallback executes via WSL System32 bash.exe
issues.body:
## Summary

On Windows, bash-tool shell resolution is **non-deterministic when any extensions are loaded**: a valid `shellPath` in `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` is silently ignored, and resolution falls through to the standard Git Bash locations and finally to the first `bash.exe` found on `PATH` — which on Windows with WSL enabled is `C:\Windows\System32\bash.exe`, the **WSL launcher**. Commands then execute inside a Linux environment (no `git` there), producing `git: command not found` or `No bash shell found`, depending on what happens to win the race at startup.

This is the same underlying problem as #9229 (and adjacent to #8763 / #7829), but #9229 was auto-closed as untriaged without a fix. Unlike those reports, here the failure is **fully reproducible and directly attributable to extension loading**, with a clean version-fingerprint diagnostic (below).

## Environment

- pi (pi-coding-agent) **0.85.1** (current latest), installed via Scoop on Windows 10 (es-AR locale)
- Git for Windows 2.53 installed at a non-standard path (`E:\...\Git`); a second Git Bash 2.47 (Laragon bundle)
- **No** Git Bash at `C:\Program Files\Git` (standard search location absent)
- WSL enabled; default distro has **no git** installed
- `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`:
  ```json
  {
    "shellPath": "E:\\laragon\\bin\\git\\bin\\bash.exe",
    "packages": [ "npm:pi-mcp-adapter", "... 6 packages total ..." ]
  }
  ```

## Reproduction

Prompt used for every run (forces exactly one `bash` tool call):

```
pi -p --no-session --offline "Use the bash tool to run: git --version. Reply raw output only."
```

| Configuration | Observed `git --version` | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-ne` (extensions disabled) | `2.47.1` (Laragon) **4/4 runs** | `shellPath` honored deterministically (step 1) |
| full extensions loaded | mix of `2.47.1`, `No bash shell found`, `2.49.0` (WSL distro git), `git: command not found` + `/usr/bin/bash` (WSL) | `shellPath` **lost** → fallthrough to step 2 (standard dirs, absent) → step 3 PATH finds `System32\bash.exe` = WSL |

`where.exe bash` on this machine resolves `C:\Windows\System32\bash.exe` first. `wsl -e bash -c "which git"` returns empty with `execvpe(git) failed: No such file or directory` — matching the failure output byte-for-byte.

Each extension package was also bisected individually (`-ne -e <pkg>`); no single package reproduces the drop reliably — it emerges with the full set loaded, consistent with a startup race between extension/tool registration and settings-based shell resolution. (`--no-skill-registry` did not change the outcome, so it is not specific to any one package's startup work.)

## Impact

1. **Silent wrong-environment execution**: commands that "work" run inside WSL against a different toolchain — destructive potential (e.g. `rm`, `git commit`) silently operates in the wrong environment.
2. Users without Git Bash at the standard location cannot use the bash tool at all once the race is lost, despite a correctly configured `shellPath`.
3. The error text (`No bash shell found ... Searched Git Bash in: C:\Program Files\...`) never mentions the configured `shellPath`, so it misdirects debugging (I confirmed my `shellPath` itself was valid before suspecting pi).

## Expected behavior

- `settings.shellPath` is applied **deterministically**, regardless of which or how many extensions are loaded.
- The PATH fallback **never** selects `%SystemRoot%\System32\bash.exe` (WSL launcher). @petrroll already acknowledged in #9229: *"it is true this path can select bash.exe which is backed by WSL even if wsl is disabled"*.
- When shell resolution fails, the error message includes the configured `shellPath`, whether it existed, and why it was rejected.

## Suggested root-cause area

Whatever caches the resolved shell/bash operations at startup: the resolved shell differs between the `-ne` and extension-loaded code paths in the same build, suggesting extensions re-create or re-register the bash tool through a path that does not consult `settings.shellPath` (or reads settings before load completes).

## Local mitigation applied

Created a directory junction `C:\Program Files\Git -> <actual Git install>` so step-2 discovery always resolves to a real Git Bash. This masks the race but does not fix the `shellPath` preference loss.

## Related closed issues

- #9229 — Windows: shell_path config is ignored, always prefer WSL bash (auto-closed, untriaged)
- #8763 — `getShellConfig()` ignores settings shellPath, picks WSL bash shim (closed no-action)
- #7829 — Invalid settings.json silently ignored; misleading 'bash not found' (closed)

issues.title: Hardware cursor jumps to the wrong column while a mouse selection is active (1.2.0)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

With `showHardwareCursor: true`, pi positions the terminal cursor using a
zero-width marker (`\x1b_pi:c\x07`) that the editor puts in the line. The column
is computed in `extractCursorPosition()` as the visible width of the text before
that marker.

When a mouse selection is active, `applySelection()` splits the line into
before / selected / after and rebuilds it. The slicing helper
`sliceWithWidth()` (utils.js) mishandles zero-width escape sequences:

- a sequence at or after the end of the range is dropped
- a sequence before the range is buffered and prepended to the next slice,
  so it is duplicated into a later slice

So the cursor marker can end up on the other side of the selection, and
`extractCursorPosition()` then reads the column from the wrong place.

Measured over all combinations of cursor position × selection range, for
`"ab中文def"` and `"abcdefgh"` (1406 combinations):

| Symptom | Count |
|---|---|
| Cursor placed at the wrong column | 70 (max off by 2 cells = one CJK char) |
| Text outside the selection rendered in reverse video | 175 (`showHardwareCursor: false`) |

Example: line `ab中<marker>cursor-on-文def`, selection covering columns 0-3.
The cursor should be at column 4, pi puts it at column 2.

This bug is not new in 1.2.0 - pi-tui 1.1.0 has the same 35 wrong-column cases.
What changed in 1.2.0 is that `showHardwareCursor: true` no longer draws pi's own
reverse-video cursor, so the misplaced terminal cursor is no longer covered by a
correctly positioned one.

### Steps to reproduce

Deterministic, no terminal needed:

```js
const T = await import("<pi>/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-tui/dist/tui.js");
const A = await import("<pi>/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-tui/dist/tui-alt-screen.js");

const terminal = { columns: 60, rows: 12, write(){}, start(){}, stop(){}, hideCursor(){}, showCursor(){}, on(){}, off(){}, setTitle(){} };
const tui = new A.TuiAltScreen(terminal, true, undefined, { copyOnSelect: false });

const line = `ab中${T.CURSOR_MARKER}${T.renderFakeCursor("文")}def\x1b[0m`;
let lines = tui.resolveFakeCursors([line]);           // cursor is at column 4

tui.selectionAnchor = { row: 0, col: 0, scrollView: undefined };
tui.selectionFocus  = { row: 0, col: 3, scrollView: undefined, boundary: true };
lines = tui.applySelection(lines, null);

const pos = tui.extractCursorPosition(lines, 12);
console.log(pos.col);   // prints 2, should be 4
```

Interactively: enable `showHardwareCursor`, put the cursor in the middle of the
input box, then select text with the mouse so the selection covers the cursor
position. The cursor moves to the wrong cell.

## Suggested fix

Take the cursor position before the selection highlight is applied, so the
marker is already stripped when the line is split. In `doRender()`
(tui-alt-screen.js):

```diff
-screen = this.applySelection(screen, nextLayout);
-screen = this.compositeFlashes(screen, width, height);
-const cursorPos = this.extractCursorPosition(screen, height);
+const cursorPos = this.extractCursorPosition(screen, height);
+screen = this.applySelection(screen, nextLayout);
+screen = this.compositeFlashes(screen, width, height);
```

The highlight does not change visible widths, so the column is unchanged in the
cases that already worked. With this change the 70 wrong-column cases above drop
to 0, for both `showHardwareCursor` settings, and the selection highlight is
unaffected.

The same reorder should be applied to the bundled copy in
`dist/bundle/chunks/`, which is what the pi CLI actually loads.

A more complete fix would teach `sliceWithWidth()` to keep zero-width sequences
in the slice they belong to instead of dropping or duplicating them, but that
touches every caller.


### Expected behavior

_No response_

### Version

1.2.0

issues.title: codemode models.classify: catalog advertises image-input classifiers, but System One API rejects images

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## Problem

Pi 1.2.0, codemode `models`. `models.getAvailableOfType("classifier")` returns six models whose `input` includes `"image"`:

- `openrouter/~perplexity/pplx-decider-27b-latest`
- `openrouter/cloudflare/clef`, `clef-flash`, `clef-omni`
- `openrouter/openai/gpt-6-luna-decisions`
- `openrouter/perplexity/pplx-decider-v1.1-27b`

Passing an image block (from `tools.read` of a PNG, matching the documented classify-with-images example) to **any** of them fails with:

```
stopReason: "error"
errorMessage: "System One API does not support image input"
```

So the catalog metadata (`input: ["text","image"]`) and the classifier API's actual behavior disagree: image-input classification is advertised but never works through this path.

## Reproduction

```js
const img = await tools.read({ path: "any.png" }); // returns { type: "image", data, mimeType }
const model = { provider: "openrouter", id: "cloudflare/clef-omni" };
const r = await models.classify(model, {
  state: { task: "probe" },
  images: [{ type: "image", data: img.data, mimeType: img.mimeType }],
  questions: { q: { type: "bool", instructions: "…", criteria: { true: "…", false: "…" } } },
});
// r.stopReason === "error", r.errorMessage === "System One API does not support image input"
```

Identical result for all six image-capable catalog entries; text-only classification with the same script shape works fine (e.g. `typesafe/jev-latest`).

## Question

Is image input expected to work through the System One classifier API? If yes, this is a bug in the image path. If no (yet), the catalog should stop advertising `image` in `input` for models reached through it, so `getAvailableOfType` results stay trustworthy.

issues.title: Builtin grep/bash descriptions should say when text search is the wrong tool

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## Problem

The stock builtin tool descriptions carry no routing constraint:

- `grep` description (`dist/core/tools/grep.js`): "Search file contents for a pattern. Returns matching lines with file paths and line numbers…"
- `bash` snippet (`dist/core/tools/bash.js`): "Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)" — this actively advertises grep-through-bash.

In projects that provide their own AST/parser/language-server tooling (which pi's extension and MCP ecosystem encourages), models default to grep — or bash grep — for structural questions (declarations, references, configuration keys, "where/how is X wired"), because nothing in the tool text revokes that license.

## Observed failure

During an audit of the form "how is feature X wired and used in this project", the agent ran bash `grep` for the feature name across the repo. The located text was not the answer — the answer depended on the *structural role* of each occurrence (config key, enum member, registration site, prose mention). A local guard blocked the bash grep, but only after the misclassification; the tool descriptions themselves steered toward it.

## Proposal

Add a revocation sentence to the builtin `grep` description or its `promptGuidelines`, e.g.:

> Use text search only when the located text itself answers the question. If the answer depends on an occurrence's structural role — declaration, reference, configuration key, heading — use the project's AST, parser, or language-server tooling instead.

And adjust the `bash` snippet/guidelines so it stops advertising `grep`:

> Text search runs through the grep tool, not shell grep or ripgrep.

`ToolDefinition.promptGuidelines` already exists as the per-tool channel, so this needs no new mechanism.

## Local workaround in use

We currently inject both corrections from a `before_agent_start` handler via mutable `systemPromptOptions.toolSnippets`/`toolGuidelines`. Native support would make that rewrite unnecessary.

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

Every time I press Ctrl+L, pi refreshes the model catalog. With an OpenRouter key
stored, this now makes two network calls on every refresh:

- `https://pi.dev/api/models/providers/openrouter`
- `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models/user`

Both take ~1.4s from my machine, so the refresh takes ~3s every time. In 1.1.0 the
same refresh took ~1.5s and only called pi.dev.

### Steps to reproduce

## Why

`withPersonalizedCatalog` (dist/core/remote-catalog-provider.js) calls
`requestCatalog()` and then `personalizeOpenRouterCatalog()` on every refresh.

Unlike `withRemoteCatalog`, it has:

- no freshness window (`REMOTE_CATALOG_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS`, 4h)
- no ETag / `if-none-match` revalidation

So the per-key list introduced in 1.2.0 is fetched on every Ctrl+L.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Store an OpenRouter key (`auth.json`).
2. Run pi 1.2.0, press Ctrl+L.
3. Watch connections: openrouter.ai is contacted every time.

## Measurements

Same key, warm cache, `modelRuntime.refresh()`:

| Version | Time | Hosts |
|---|---|---|
| 1.1.0 | 1.4-1.9s | pi.dev |
| 1.2.0 | 2.9-3.3s | pi.dev, openrouter.ai |

With no credentials at all: 6ms, no network.

## Suggested fix

Let `withPersonalizedCatalog` use the same `checkedAt` freshness window and ETag
revalidation as `withRemoteCatalog`, so the key's model list is only re-fetched
when the stored copy is stale.

issues.title: pi-durable: on a Durable Object, a sleeping task wakes only on the next request

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

On the [Durable Object storage](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/7bd01fb92485c06f92ecfff7ccf3197148bc16af/packages/durable/README.md?plain=1#L663), a task that calls `runtime.sleep()` doesn't wake at its deadline once the object restarts. It stays `pending` until some request happens to open the Harness and call `resume()`. Generation [retry](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/7bd01fb92485c06f92ecfff7ccf3197148bc16af/packages/durable/src/harness/generation.ts#L225) and [deferred poll](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/7bd01fb92485c06f92ecfff7ccf3197148bc16af/packages/durable/src/harness/generation.ts#L240) sleep the same way.

The deadline itself is safe; what's lost is the wake-up. [`#sleep`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/7bd01fb92485c06f92ecfff7ccf3197148bc16af/packages/durable/src/harness/scheduler.ts#L1812) is an in-memory `setTimeout`, and a Durable Object runs code only for a request or an alarm. A pending timer keeps the object alive for at most 15 minutes, and none survives a deploy or runtime restart ([lifecycle](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/concepts/durable-object-lifecycle/)). Pi never sets an alarm. The app can’t set one either, because it has no way to learn when a task wants to wake up: only the task’s own code knows the deadline.

So a sleep longer than 15 minutes misses its deadline every time, and a shorter one misses it whenever a restart lands in between.

### Steps to reproduce

Deployed to Cloudflare: a SQLite-backed Durable Object over `openDurableObjectSqliteStorage(ctx.storage)`, one task that sleeps 2 minutes, a redeploy partway through, and no further requests (UTC):

| Event | Time (UTC) |
|---|---|
| Sleep starts | 20:45:26.570 |
| Redeploy | 20:46:06 |
| Deadline (nothing runs) | 20:47:26.570 |
| Next request; task wakes (66 s late) | 20:48:32.632 |

A 20 s sleep without a redeploy woke on time.


### Expected behavior

A sleep that wakes on time in a long-running process should wake on time on a Durable Object too, with no extra app code. Waking the object is Pi’s job, not the app’s.

### Proposal

On Cloudflare that takes an alarm set for the next deadline, which should be the durable harness' not the app code's job. Should pi-durable ship a Durable Object base class, like codemode’s CodemodeSandboxDurableObject, that runs the Harness and sets that alarm? I have one working. Happy to send it.

### Version

1.1.0

issues.title: openai-responses: aborted stream keeps the premature-EOF errorMessage

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

Cancelling an `openai-responses` request mid-stream can record:

```json
{
  "stopReason": "aborted",
  "errorMessage": "OpenAI Responses stream ended before a terminal response event"
}
```

The stop reason is correct, but the message describes a provider drop rather than a cancellation. Log readers must check `stopReason` to distinguish the two.

Source path at [7bd01fb](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/7bd01fb92485c06f92ecfff7ccf3197148bc16af/packages/ai/src/api/openai-responses.ts#L192-L230): the OpenAI SDK iterator can return quietly on abort; [`processResponsesStream`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/7bd01fb92485c06f92ecfff7ccf3197148bc16af/packages/ai/src/api/openai-responses-shared.ts#L760-L762) then throws the missing-terminal-event error. That skips the subsequent `signal.aborted` check that would throw `Request was aborted`. The catch sets `stopReason` from the signal but preserves the EOF message.

Related: #8409 and #9883 concern cancellation during setup being classified as `error`; here classification is already `aborted`. #9513 and #10693 concern actual premature stream endings.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start a long response using an `openai-responses` provider.
2. Call `agent.abort()` while the response is streaming, before a terminal event arrives.
3. Inspect the final assistant message's `stopReason` and `errorMessage`.

The output above was observed in session logs on 1.1.0. This minimal repro has not yet been independently rerun with `pi -ne`; the control-flow explanation is source-verified.

### Expected behavior

An aborted request should have an abort-specific message, such as `Request was aborted`. Keep the premature-EOF message for genuine stream truncation.

### Version

1.1.0; source checked at 7bd01fb. Bundled OpenAI SDK 7.19.0.

*AI-assisted report, condensed from an existing diagnostic draft.*

issues.title: Cache-preserving reasoning effort changes for GPT-6

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

When the thinking level changes mid-session on GPT-6, send the new effort as a configuration_update input item before the next user message instead of changing the request-level reasoning.effort. This would cover both openai-responses and openai-codex-responses, behind a compat flag on the GPT-6 models.

### Why?

I switch effort levels a lot in long sessions. Right now each switch changes the request-level effort, which rewrites the prompt prefix, so the next turn misses the cache for the whole transcript. On Codex it also drops the WebSocket previous_response_id continuation, since the request body no longer matches the previous one.

This is the same problem as #9335, which was closed as no-action. I wasn’t sure if that was because of the scope or the write-up, so I wanted to propose a narrower version.

### How? (optional)

Pi already does this for Anthropic by recording providerThinkingLevel on each response (4e69b0c28). The OpenAI version would work the same way: keep the first effort at the request level, record the effort in force on each response, and replay configuration_update items where the effort changed so history stays identical between requests. A change made during a tool loop would apply at the next user message, since that’s where the API accepts it.

I have a working branch (~130 lines plus tests) and would like to open the PR if this sounds reasonable.

issues.title: packages/durable README: document post-resume aborted salvage entries
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Document the recovery-salvage entry in `@earendil-works/pi-durable`'s README recovery section: after a crash mid-generation and `resume()`, the interrupted partial is committed as a distinct assistant entry with `stopReason: "aborted"` and zero usage, before the fresh final answer.

### Why?

Kill-during-stream trials (15/15 with a real streaming provider, plus scripted-provider runs) show every post-resume transcript contains these aborted-attempt entries. The behavior looks correct — accounting stays honest (the aborted entry carries zero usage; the regenerated final bills once) — but every transcript consumer has to expect the shape: token accounting, compaction, diffing viewers, anything that assumes one assistant entry per turn. The README's recovery docs don't currently mention it, and it silently surprised our downstream tooling. One paragraph would prevent the same surprise for overnight-worker authors.

### How? (optional)

Suggested wording (adapt to house style): "After a crash during generation, resume commits the interrupted partial as an assistant entry with stopReason 'aborted' (zero usage), followed by the regenerated final answer. Consumers of recovered transcripts must tolerate these marker entries."

issues.title: Pi Durable support for client-side tool execution and tool approval

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Submitting this as a contribution proposal because there's no feature option and this isn't a bug. I initially submitted a [discussion](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/discussions/10632) but not sure if that's the right area.

Some tools require human approval before they run, or require client-side information before they run. Here's an example for each scenario.

Destructive tool that requires human approval:
1. The model calls a tool
2. The run stops before the tool executes. The pending call is persisted, and nothing is held in memory
3. The user approves, denies it, maybe hours or days later 
4. The run continues from that same tool call and the tool executes (or a denial result is written), and the agent loop continues.

For requiring client-side information for a tool result (a good example of this is WebMCP, or a `askUserQuestion` style tool):
1. The model calls a tool
2. The run stops before the tool executes (because it has no execute function in its definition). The pending call is persisted, and nothing is held in memory
3. The client receives the tool call, executes what's necessary, and sends back the tool output result
4. The run continues from that same tool call: the agent loop receives the tool result, and the agent loop continues.

It seems like something like this doesn't exist for Pi durable. There's some similar examples but they seem to wait in memory or return a terminated tool result.

Questions:
- Is there an existing solution I missed?
- Is support for something like this planned or in consideration?

If you only plan on supporting one of these, I would kindly ask for it to be the second: client-side tool execution (it doesn't have to be client side, but basically "paused" or "deferred" tool execution). I think this pattern can support the human-approval feature if need-be, it just might be a bit awkward in its implementation depending on the design.

Related:
- https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/5901 but that was for pi, not pi durable
- This could also tie-in with support of the MCP spec with tools that return with an [input required] request(https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools#input-required-tool-results), 
- Examples of how this is designed elsewhere:
  - Vercel's AI sdk has approval states for tool execution: https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/agents/tool-approvals. And for client-side tool output, if you don't define an `execute` for a tool, when that tool is called it stops the agent run, and the client can start the run again by providing the tool result (see `getLocation` tool here https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/ai-sdk-ui/chatbot-tool-usage)
  - Cloudflare think similarly has a [tool approval](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/harnesses/think/tools/#tool-approval), as well as [client side tools](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/harnesses/think/client-tools/) 

### Why?

The UX for many agent interfaces need humans to approve certain actions. There's also many situations where a tool's execution is done on the client.

### How? (optional)

_No response_

issues.title: Pi Web Code mode self-test: 10 s budget + sticky failure makes Code mode unavailable on cold Windows starts

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
**Symptom**

Pi Web (desktop) shows "Code mode's sandbox cannot run on this Pi Web server — the sandbox did not answer within 10000 ms", and server.log records:

```
[pi-web] Code mode is off: the sandbox did not answer within 10000 ms
```

on every cold launch (Windows 11, bundled Node 22.23.3, pi 1.0.1).

**Root cause**

The self-test's 10 s budget must cover, in one shot:

1. The deferred first-load of `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` — a `serverExternalPackages` entry in the Next server config, so it is evaluated lazily on first use, not at server boot. Measured in fresh idle Node processes on the reporter's machine: **5.0–5.6 s** just for the import.
2. Sandbox boot: `readFile` + `WebAssembly.compile` of the 0.6 MB `quickjs-wasi` wasm, worker-thread spawn, QuickJS VM init, and the round-trip for `return 6 * 7`. ~0.3 s when warm.

At app launch the Next server is simultaneously doing startup work (DB init, session restore, npm audit in the server dir), and Defender real-time protection can add scan time on first file reads. The result is that the first self-test attempt on a cold start frequently exceeds 10 s — even with AV exclusions in place (verified: adding `D:\tools\Pi Agent` to the exclusion list did not make it pass).

Additionally, the result is memoized process-wide (`globalThis[Symbol.for("pi-web.codemodeSandbox")] ??= m().then(…)`), so **one failed attempt disables Code mode for the entire server process lifetime with no retry path** — the failure persists across app restarts on affected machines.

Related packaging defect seen in the same log history: a nested incomplete `quickjs-wasi` under `pi-coding-agent/node_modules/` (package directory present, `quickjs.wasm` binary missing) produced:

```
[pi-web] Code mode is off: Cannot find module '…\@earendil-works\pi-coding-agent\node_modules\quickjs-wasi\quickjs.wasm'
```

until the nested copy was no longer present.

**Suggested fixes**

1. Raise the self-test budget (e.g. 60 s) or make it adaptive to process-start time; don't hardcode 10 s.
2. Don't memoize failures — allow a retry of the self-test on a later trigger.
3. Log the failing sub-phase (deferred import vs wasm load vs worker spawn) so users can diagnose.
4. Verify nested `quickjs-wasi` installs ship the `.wasm` binary.

Local workaround applied by the reporter: patched the bundled chunk to use a 120 s budget; Code mode then passes. The patch is lost on app update, hence the request.

issues.title: TUI cold start ~1.8s to first frame even with -ne: startup waits instead of computing

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
**What happened?**

Interactive TUI cold start is ~1.8–2.4s before the first usable frame on a fast machine (Mac Studio M2 Ultra, macOS, mimo-v2.6-pro). It is per-process cost: my workflow spawns several Pi panels per work session (agent panels), so every spawn pays it.

Validated with `pi -ne` as CONTRIBUTING asks (no extensions loaded):

- `pi --no-session -ne`, first frame from process start: 1773 / 1861 / 1862 ms (median 1861), version 1.1.0.

So extensions are not the cause. Decomposition of a full interactive start (medians, N=5 live pty panels per tier):

- node + bundle + CLI (`node -e ''` vs `pi --version`): 166 ms
- TUI core + user config (start in a dir without project `.pi`): 1852 ms
- project extensions: 143 ms
- git detect + status footer: 58 ms
- total to usable input: 2338 ms

The interesting part: startup **waits instead of computing**. A CPU profile of a 5s start (`NODE_OPTIONS=--cpu-prof`) shows ~4.2s idle and only ~200ms of real CPU (anonymous module init 135ms, readFileSync 70ms). Looks like sequential async init / terminal probing before the first frame, not CPU-bound work.

**Steps to reproduce**

issues.title: streamProxy rewrites an accepted done message to error when the body fails afterward

labels.name: last-read
labels.description: A marker label for triaging

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### What happened?

`streamProxy` keeps reading the HTTP body after it pushes `done`. If a later read fails, for example a connection reset after the terminal frame, its `catch` sets `stopReason: "error"` and `errorMessage` on `partial`: the same object the `done` event and `result()` already returned. The stream ignores the second terminal event, so the accepted message changes after the fact.

With `Agent`, a `toolUse` turn is accepted and its tool runs, then the transcript message becomes `error`. `transformMessages` skips errored assistant messages but keeps their tool results, so later requests carry a result without its call. This is one way an errored assistant message ends up with executed tool calls (see #7777). #8997 fixed EOF before a terminal event, not this case.

### Steps to reproduce

At upstream `441f5767c`, use the [offline repro and setup](https://gist.github.com/fitchmultz/98b4fd8b9f2f8e83815ae755619986b1), then run `node repro-proxy-terminal.mjs` from the checkout root. It stubs `fetch`: a complete tool-use response whose body errors after the tool has run, then a plain `done`. No proxy server or provider is involved.

Actual: `proxy accepted=toolUse,stop transcript=error error="synthetic HTTP tail reset" orphanToolResult=true`, then the assertion fails.

### Expected behavior

The first terminal event owns the message: stop reading, cancel the reader, and leave the accepted message unchanged. A four-line change in the read loop makes the repro pass; I can submit it with a regression if approved.

### Version

Upstream main `441f5767c4fe4eebbec6ebe9bb4a57f430871eba`; Node 24.21.0, macOS arm64. Direct library repro, no extensions.

issues.title: OSC 52 copy in fullscreen TUI is swallowed by tmux (no passthrough wrap)
issues.body:
### What happened?

Copy-on-select in the fullscreen TUI writes a raw OSC 52 (`\x1b]52;c;...`). When pi runs inside tmux, tmux consumes the incoming OSC 52 into its paste buffer and does not relay it to its client. pi flashes "Copied!" either way.

On a headless Linux host over SSH (no DISPLAY/WAYLAND), OSC 52 is the only clipboard route, so copying from the TUI silently does nothing.

### Steps to reproduce

1. tmux on a headless Linux host, SSH'd from another machine (`set-clipboard on`)
2. Run pi, drag-select text in the transcript, release
3. "Copied!" flashes but the client machine's clipboard is unchanged
4. `tmux show-buffer` on the pi host shows the selection: tmux ate it

Traced to core, not an extension. Both OSC 52 emit sites write the raw sequence: `copyToClipboard` in `packages/coding-agent/src/utils/clipboard.ts` and the TUI fallback in `packages/tui/src/tui-alt-screen.ts`.

### Expected behavior

The client terminal's clipboard updates. Wrapping the write in the tmux DCS passthrough (`\x1bPtmux;\x1b<seq>\x1b\\`) when `$TMUX` is set fixes it: tmux forwards the unwrapped sequence to its client, where a plain terminal sets the clipboard and an outer tmux picks it up. I have the change with tests ready and can send a PR.

### Version

1.0.0 (also present on current main)

---

issues.title: Concurrent pi processes race managed npm install on the shared project .pi/npm prefix (no install lock)
issues.body:
## Summary

When several pi processes run concurrently against the same project (e.g. a parent session that spawns parallel subagent child sessions), the managed-package reconciliation in `package-manager` can run `npm install --prefix <project>/.pi/npm` from multiple processes at once. The concurrent installs race on the shared install root; one process wins, the others die with a bare `failed with code N` spawn/install error.

## Environment

- Windows 11 (also reported on the same setup multiple times)
- `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` 1.0.4 (verified the same code path is unchanged in latest 1.1.0)
- Project-scoped npm package pinned to an exact version in `.pi/settings.json` `packages`

## What happened

Right after bumping the pinned version of a project package, two child pi processes were spawned concurrently in the same project. Each saw the installed copy not matching the pin (`resolvePackageSources` → `installedNpmMatchesConfiguredVersion` → false) and each executed:

```
npm install <pkg>@<version> --prefix <project>/.pi/npm --legacy-peer-deps
```

against the same install root. One finished normally; the other failed at spawn time with:

```
npm install <pkg>@<version> --prefix <project>/.pi/npm --legacy-peer-deps failed with code 190
```

Re-running the identical command manually right after reports `up to date` (exit 0) — the failure is a transient race, not a registry or pin problem.

Earlier occurrences of the same pattern on this setup: parallel subagent spawns dying with npm `ENOTEMPTY`/`EPERM` on the shared `node_modules` (Windows file locking), in one case leaving the install root corrupted.

## Root cause

`packages/coding-agent/src/core/package-manager.ts` performs managed npm installs (`installNpm` / `installNpmBatch`, and the update path via `updateNpmBatch`) with no inter-process mutual exclusion on the install root. Any N concurrent pi processes sharing a project can race reconciliation whenever an install is genuinely needed — first session after a version bump, a missing package, or an unpinned-package update. Within one process the checks are sequential, but nothing serializes across processes.

## Suggested fixes

1. **Single-flight managed installs**: take an inter-process lock on the install root (e.g. a stale-pid-aware lockfile at `<installRoot>/.pi-install.lock`) around managed npm install/update. Waiters re-check `installedNpmMatchesConfiguredVersion` after acquiring the lock and skip the install if another process already satisfied it. This also makes the reconciliation idempotent under concurrency.
2. **Surface stderr in failures**: `runCommand` currently rejects with `... failed with code N` only. Including the tail of npm's stderr would let reporters distinguish network / lock / permission failures without manual reproduction.

## Impact / workaround

Multi-agent workflows that spawn several child sessions in parallel within one project (a common code-review setup) hit this probabilistically whenever a real install is pending. Current workarounds: spawn serially, or run one session first so reconciliation completes before spawning the rest.

prs.title: fix(ai): adapt OAuth device polling margin after slow_down
prs.body:
TL;DR: WSL / Ubuntu is stupid and can easily lead to persistently a bit too fast (10 %) clock. This, in turn, can make oauth requests to COPILOT just a bit faster than "slow-down", leading to it *never* succeeding. Layers of suck.

Obv. it should be fixed in Ubuntu wsl (https://bugs.launchpad.net/ubuntuwsl/+bug/2170230) or WSL2 (https://github.com/microsoft/WSL/issues/12583) but until then, probably worth fixing it here given #1990, #6187 (some of those protections got removed). 

With this fix, we double the margin 2x on each subsequent slow down failure. That way we don't slow it down when we don't need to but do when we do. Might help other oauth other than copilot. 

---

AI summary:



Fast local clocks can keep device logins polling before the authorization server's minimum even when each slow_down response supplies a new interval. For example, a 10-second local wait takes about 9.09 seconds when the clock runs 10% fast. Increasing only the server interval never closes that gap.

Add a separate margin on slow_down: start at 250 ms, double on subsequent responses, and cap the additional wait at 5 seconds. Retain the margin on pending responses, reset it for each login, and clamp waits to the existing device-code deadline. Normal polling is unchanged until slow_down occurs. Keep the protocol interval separate so RFC 8628's 5-second increments do not compound the margin, and do not lower it on a smaller server interval.

Cover recovery with both timers and Date.now running 10% fast, the margin cap, pending responses, cancellation, expiry, per-login reset, and Copilot credential persistence. Update Copilot and xAI polling expectations.

Related WSL clock-frequency issue:
https://github.com/microsoft/WSL/issues/12583

prs.title: fix: preserve legacy model catalog route on publish
prs.body:
Fixes #9099

## Problem

Pi `0.80.8`–`0.84.4` fetch the OpenRouter catalog from pi.dev but send every OpenRouter request through `openai-completions`. Per-model OpenRouter APIs start in `0.85.0`.

The publisher labelled every catalog `minimumPiVersion: "0.80.7"` and replaced that index entry on each run. Once the generator emitted OpenRouter `anthropic-messages` entries, pi.dev served them to older clients:

```text
Pi 0.82.1 gets: api anthropic-messages, baseUrl https://openrouter.ai/api
uses openai-completions anyway -> POST https://openrouter.ai/api/chat/completions -> HTML 404
```

The `baseUrl` is correct for `anthropic-messages`, which appends `/v1/messages`. The bug is serving that entry to clients that ignore `api`.

## Change

The publisher records generated catalogs under `minimumPiVersion: "0.85.0"`, so each run updates only the `0.85.0` entry and `defaultRevision`. The existing `0.80.7` entry is left alone. The regression test runs the real publish path against a local R2 stand-in and fails on the old publisher.

pi.dev already selects catalogs by the User-Agent's Pi version and needs no change. Its released-client tests (`0.80.8`, `0.82.1`, `0.84.4`, `0.85.0`, `0.99.0`) are on pi.dev `main`.

## Production repair

Merging stops future runs from breaking older clients. The live `0.80.7` entry still points to a mixed-API catalog and must be repointed to a legacy snapshot generated by the `v0.84.4` generator. This needs write access to the `pi-artifacts` R2 bucket; the endpoint is `R2_ENDPOINT` in `.github/workflows/publish-model-catalog.yml`.

### 1. Generate the legacy snapshot

```sh
git worktree add --detach /tmp/pi-legacy v0.84.4
cd /tmp/pi-legacy
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npm run generate:model-catalog
npm run check:model-catalog   # prints "revision": "sha256-..."
```

Check that every OpenRouter model uses the legacy API:

```sh
node -e 'const m=require("./.artifacts/model-catalog/models.json").openrouter; const bad=Object.values(m).filter(x=>x.api!=="openai-completions"||x.baseUrl!=="https://openrouter.ai/api/v1"); console.log(Object.keys(m).length+" OpenRouter models, "+bad.length+" incompatible"); process.exit(bad.length?1:0)'
```

The snapshot has no typed `.all.json` files. Affected clients don't request them.

### 2. Rollout

1. Upload the snapshot. Nothing references it yet, so this is safe at any time:

   ```sh
   REV=<revision printed by check:model-catalog>
   aws s3 cp .artifacts/model-catalog/ "s3://pi-artifacts/models/v1/revisions/$REV/" \
     --recursive --exclude publication.json --endpoint-url "$R2_ENDPOINT" \
     --content-type "application/json; charset=utf-8" \
     --cache-control "public, max-age=31536000, immutable"
   ```

2. Merge this PR.
3. Make sure no publish run is queued or running (`gh run list --workflow publish-model-catalog.yml`). A run for a pre-merge commit uses the old publisher, and any run that read the index before the repair writes back its stale copy.
4. Download `models/v1/index.json`, edit it keeping existing entry metadata, and upload it with `--content-type "application/json; charset=utf-8" --cache-control no-store`:
   - `0.80.7` → `$REV`
   - `0.85.0` → the current `defaultRevision` (add the entry if missing)
   - `defaultRevision` unchanged
5. After about a minute, check that `curl -sL -A pi/0.84.4 -D - -o /dev/null https://pi.dev/api/models/providers/openrouter` reports `x-pi-model-catalog-revision: $REV`, and `pi/0.85.0` the current revision.

Clients pick up the change on their next refresh: immediately for fresh CI runs, within four hours for local installs, or right away with `pi update --models`.

### Reference validation

A snapshot generated this way on 2026-10-10 (`sha256-90b251b8df293406ca205db60a5f8b1285fef2d72e476cdd47a78c8f734effd6`, 38 providers, 1518 chat models) was loaded by released clients through their normal catalog refresh, with one intercepted request per model. Your revision will differ because upstream data changes.

| Client | OpenRouter | OpenCode, OpenCode Go, Fireworks |
|---|---|---|
| `0.80.8` | 392 → `/api/v1/chat/completions` | 130 of 136 |
| `0.82.1` | 392 → `/api/v1/chat/completions` | 136 of 136 |
| `0.84.4` | 392 → `/api/v1/chat/completions` | 136 of 136 |

The six `0.80.8` failures are OpenCode Go `openai-responses` models, supported from `0.81.0`. They fail with an explicit "no API implementation" error on `0.80.8`–`0.80.10`. This predates #9099; removing them would hide working models from `0.81.0`–`0.84.4`.

## Out of scope

The second comment on #9099 reports a separate client-side bug. Custom models in `models.json`, or registered by extensions, that omit `baseUrl` can inherit a URL meant for a different API. `0.85.0` fixed the common case. Pi can fix the remaining edge cases itself in a follow-up: inherit `baseUrl` only from a built-in model with the same `api`, otherwise fail with an error asking for it. Setting `baseUrl` explicitly avoids it on released versions.

## Validation

- `node --test scripts/publish-model-catalog.test.mjs`
- `npm run check`

prs.title: fix(durable): reject waits that close a cycle
prs.body:
Fixes #10411.

Cyclic waits are still a programming error. They now fail at the wait that closes the cycle, the way waiting on yourself or your owner already did, instead of hanging.

A task can't finish before the tasks it waits on, or before its live ordinary owned work (the [`completing` hold](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/28dcce2ba45ce4a9efeb0f5b686f0be830fd89b9/packages/durable/docs/spec.md?plain=1#L2078-L2103)). Those are the edges of a wait-for graph, and a cycle in it is a deadlock: no task on it can finish first. The old check rejected only the two shortest cycles, a task waiting on itself or on its owner chain. The issue's orchestrator → worker → reviewer cycle mixes a hold with two waits, so it got through.

The fix keeps one invariant: the wait-for graph is acyclic. In an acyclic graph, adding an edge u → v closes a cycle exactly when u is reachable from v. So `#validateWait` collects the tasks reachable from the wait's targets, following [`#waitingOn`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/28dcce2ba45ce4a9efeb0f5b686f0be830fd89b9/packages/durable/src/harness/scheduler.ts#L744-L752) and [`#ownedLive`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/28dcce2ba45ce4a9efeb0f5b686f0be830fd89b9/packages/durable/src/harness/scheduler.ts#L613-L631), and rejects the wait if the waiter is among them. Only a wait adds an edge between existing tasks, since a new task has only incoming edges, so checking each wait maintains the invariant.

Cost: a wait on your own children, including every `failFast` wait, skips the search, since the hold edge is already there. Other waits pay one `#ownedLive()` pass, like every terminal commit. One wait commit with 2,000 live tasks (memory storage), 30 samples each for main and this PR, run interleaved; the difference of medians with a bootstrap 95% CI, and a Mann–Whitney U test:

| wait on | main | this PR | difference | p |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2,000 own children | 12.7 ms | 12.1 ms | −0.5 ms [−1.6, +0.3] | 0.25 |
| one of 2,000 live tasks | 12.3 ms | 12.2 ms | −0.1 ms [−0.6, +0.6] | 0.81 |
| a held task with 2,000 live children | 5.3 ms | 5.9 ms | +0.6 ms [+0.5, +1.0] | 6×10⁻⁵ |

Only the last case, the worst one for the search, is significant: the one `#ownedLive()` pass, +0.6 ms.

One behaviour change: a background task can now wait on its conversation's owner. Background work doesn't hold its owner, so that's no cycle, but the old owner-chain check rejected it.

The spec states the cycle rule in §5.1 and §5.5. Tests: a cycle of two waits, a cycle through a held owner, and the background case.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): fall back after Bun image worker null
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #10645.

A Bun-compiled image-resize worker can successfully respond with `null` when it cannot resize/load an image. That is a valid *worker result*, but not a successful resize. Previously the Bun-specific branch returned that `null` immediately, preventing the URL-worker and in-process fallback chain from running.

This change falls through when the Bun worker returns `null`; a non-null resize result still returns immediately.

## Regression test

Adds a focused test that simulates a Bun worker returning `null` and verifies that `resizeImage()` invokes the URL-worker fallback and returns its successful result.

## Validation

```text
npm --prefix packages/coding-agent test -- image-resize.test.ts
# 1 passed

npx biome check packages/coding-agent/src/utils/image-resize.ts packages/coding-agent/test/image-resize.test.ts
# passed

git diff --check
# passed
```

`npm run check` was also run from a fresh clone after `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, but fails before this change's files with repository model-catalog TypeScript errors (for example `modelDataManifest is of type unknown` and generated provider model types resolving to `unknown`). The focused test and formatter pass.

AI assistance: I used an AI coding assistant for code inspection and implementation; I reviewed the change and test. Please apply the `llm-generated` label if appropriate.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): bound retries across successful tool turns
prs.body:
A successful `toolUse` response currently resets `retry.maxRetries`. With `maxRetries: 2` and responses `error → toolUse → error → toolUse → error`, Pi 1.1.0 still issues a sixth request. Repeating this pattern never exhausts the budget. `Internal error during token generation` reproduces it with the existing transient-error classifier.

Keep the retry budget until the automatic run settles, including its tool and queued continuations. Report success only at settlement; preserve failure and cancellation reporting. A subsequent prompt receives a fresh budget.

Validation: the two new budget/lifecycle regressions fail on unmodified v1.1.0; all 53 focused retry and boundary tests pass with this change, including the new aborted-response case. `npm run check` passed. Full repository validation remains incomplete: unrelated suites exercise destructive filesystem/Git operations prohibited in the test environment. All reproductions use the offline faux provider and synthetic messages.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): demonstrate durable filtering of degenerate output
prs.body:
Pi 1.1.0 replays successful assistant text verbatim and retains recent messages during compaction. A synthetic `toolUse` reply containing `Checking a file.\n` followed by `"*\n".repeat(1024)` therefore sends the repeated tail back on the next request.

Add an opt-in extension example using the existing `turn_end` / `context_edit` API. It removes long whitespace/asterisk tails from model context while preserving tool calls and the raw transcript. The edit also survives compaction and resume. No new core hook or default filtering policy is introduced. Fenced code and short Markdown separators remain unchanged; the example is unsuitable for tasks requesting long literal whitespace/asterisk output.

Validation: `npm run check` passed; 25 focused tests passed, including replay, summary input, retained context, resume, raw-history preservation, and normal-output controls. Full repository validation remains incomplete: unrelated suites exercise destructive filesystem/Git operations prohibited in the test environment. This draft uses only synthetic fixtures and contains no private session content.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): emit before_agent_start for runs started by custom messages
prs.body:
Runs started by pi.sendMessage(..., { triggerTurn: true }) skipped before_agent_start. After their first tool call, the next-turn refresh fell back to the base prompt options and patched away the sections handlers had added, changing the system prompt mid-run and breaking the provider prompt cache.

These runs now go through the same setup as prompt(): compaction check, before_agent_start, tool loadout, nextTurn messages, handler messages, and the system patch. BeforeAgentStartEvent is a union on messageType ("user" or "custom"); custom events carry the starting message.

The session counts as busy from the start of setup, so messages sent while handlers run go into the starting run instead of starting a second one, and an abort requested meanwhile aborts the run once it starts.

closes #10267, closes #5581, closes #10639, closes #10289
partly fixes #10606

prs.title: fix(ai): send x-opencode-session by endpoint, not provider id
prs.body:
OpenCode's zen endpoints reject requests that lack a per-conversation routing header with `400 MissingSessionID`. #9326 fixed this in pi-ai by wrapping the `opencode` and `opencode-go` provider streams, so the header was only added when the provider id was one of those two.

Any provider that names one of OpenCode's protocols is missed. Example: a custom route

```yaml
providers:
  my-route:
    api: openai-completions
    baseURL: https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1
```

uses the generic `openai-completions` implementation, so the wrapped streams never run and the request 400s.

This keys the injection off the endpoint instead of the provider id. `createProvider` now adds `x-opencode-session` for any model served by an OpenCode endpoint (host `opencode.ai`), so built-in providers and custom routes behave the same. The provider-id wrappers in `providers/opencode.ts` and `providers/opencode-go.ts` are removed since the endpoint check subsumes them.

Caller semantics are unchanged: a caller-provided session header (any case) is preserved, and no header is fabricated without a `sessionId`.

Tests: `packages/ai/test/opencode-provider-headers.test.ts` covers the endpoint predicate, the header merge, and injection through `createProvider.stream`/`streamSimple` for an OpenCode endpoint, other endpoints, and a caller override.

Follow-up to #9326.

prs.title: docs(coding-agent): use registerToolRenderer in minimal mode example
prs.body:
## Problem

The `minimal-mode` example re-registers each built-in tool with `pi.registerTool({ ...createReadToolDefinition(cwd), renderCall, renderResult })`. Re-registering replaces the whole definition, including `execute`. An extension that reroutes a built-in tool's `execute` (for example to a remote host) then has its routing clobbered by loading this example.

## Fix

Rewrite the example to override only the renderers with `pi.registerToolRenderer((toolName, next) => renderers[toolName] ?? next())`, and leave tool registration alone. Behavior (collapsed shows only the call or a count, expanded shows full output, `ctrl+o` toggles) is unchanged.

Renderer resolvers receive `unknown` args, so each entry narrows them to the tool's shape. The `edit` entry keeps an explicit `renderShell: "default"` because the built-in edit tool draws its own shell and replacing its renderers must opt back into the default boxed shell.

The file drops from 354 to 181 lines and no longer imports the `create*ToolDefinition` factories.

Verified with `tsc --noEmit` against the package types (strict, `erasableSyntaxOnly`, `verbatimModuleSyntax`, Node16) and `biome check` with the repo formatter settings.

releases.name: v1.2.0
releases.body:
### New Features

- **Per-key OpenRouter model lists**: with an OpenRouter key, Pi lists only the models that key may use, with the key's context size, max output, and prices, including regional endpoints set in `models.json`. See [OpenRouter](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.2.0/packages/coding-agent/docs/providers.md#openrouter).
- **Published configuration schemas**: add `$schema` to `settings.json`, `models.json`, keybindings, and themes for editor validation and completion. See [Settings](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.2.0/packages/coding-agent/docs/settings.md), [Models](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.2.0/packages/coding-agent/docs/models.md), [Keybindings](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.2.0/packages/coding-agent/docs/keybindings.md), and [Themes](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.2.0/packages/coding-agent/docs/themes.md).
- **Clipboard copies over remote sessions**: `PI_CLIPBOARD_OSC52=1` sends copied text to a remote client's clipboard when Pi cannot detect the remote session, such as a multiplexer attached from another machine. See [Pi Process Configuration](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.2.0/packages/coding-agent/docs/environment-variables.md#pi-process-configuration).
- **Codemode improvements**: tool declarations show input constraints such as integer, minimum/maximum, and default, and codemode rows show elapsed and total time. See [Codemode](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.2.0/packages/coding-agent/docs/codemode.md).
- **`before_agent_start` for extension-triggered runs**: runs started by `pi.sendMessage(..., { triggerTurn: true })` go through the same setup as prompts. See [Events and concurrency](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.2.0/packages/coding-agent/docs/extensions.md#events-and-concurrency).

### Breaking Changes

- Published generated configuration schemas for models, settings, keybindings, and themes at `https://pi.dev/schemas/*.schema.json`. The theme schema moved to `https://pi.dev/schemas/theme.schema.json`; themes loaded during startup now receive the same schema validation as later reloads. Update theme `$schema` references, define reusable colors under `vars`, and remove unsupported metadata ([#9880](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/9880), [#10751](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10751) by [@christianklotz](https://github.com/christianklotz))
- Changed `before_agent_start` to also fire for runs started by `pi.sendMessage(..., { triggerTurn: true })` while idle. `BeforeAgentStartEvent` is now a union on `messageType`: `"user"` events carry `prompt` and `images`, and `"custom"` events carry the starting `message` and no `prompt`. Messages returned by handlers are added to both kinds of run, and pending `deliverAs: "nextTurn"` messages are delivered with the custom-message run. Handlers that should act only on user prompts must check `event.messageType === "user"` ([#10267](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10267), [#5581](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/5581), [#10739](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10739) by [@davidbrai](https://github.com/davidbrai))
- Changed the session to count as busy while a run starts, including during `before_agent_start` handlers: `ctx.isIdle()` is false, `pi.sendMessage()` queues into the starting run instead of starting a second run that failed with "Agent is already processing", `pi.sendUserMessage()` requires `deliverAs`, and an abort requested meanwhile aborts the run once it starts ([#10739](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10739) by [@davidbrai](https://github.com/davidbrai))
- Changed `pi mcp list --json` to report `resources: true` for servers that offer resources instead of `resources` and `resourceTemplates` counts; Pi no longer lists resources when connecting ([#10526](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10526))

### Added

- Added `reachesTools` to tool definitions, so tools that reach other tools (such as `codemode` and `tool_search`) declare which tools a call may reach; the MCP extension uses it to wait for the servers a call needs and to decide whether a replacement `codemode` or `tool_search` tool can reach MCP tools
- Added `aliases` to tool namespaces; codemode's `describeNamespace()` and the `namespace` option of `searchTools()` match them, and MCP namespaces use the server name
- Added per-key OpenRouter model lists: with an OpenRouter key, Pi lists only the chat models that key may use, with the key's context size, max output, and prices, including guardrails and regional endpoints set as the base URL in `models.json`. The list is saved and used offline ([#10353](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10353), [#10672](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10672) by [@davidbrai](https://github.com/davidbrai))
- Added `PI_CLIPBOARD_OSC52=1` to send copied text to the terminal with OSC 52 after the local clipboard write, so copies reach a remote client's clipboard when Pi cannot detect the remote session, such as multiplexer attaches from another machine or remote IDE daemons ([#10826](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10826), [#10835](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10835), [#10114](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10114))
- Added elapsed time while a codemode script runs and its total time once finished to the codemode tool row, like bash rows ([#10708](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10708))

### Changed

- Changed the `showHardwareCursor` setting to use only the terminal cursor instead of also drawing Pi's reverse-video cursor
- Changed codemode tool declarations to show input constraints such as integer, minimum/maximum, length, pattern, and default as `@` tags on property comments, so scripts see them without the tool repeating them in descriptions ([#10707](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10707))
- Changed codemode declarations of MCP tools to spell out the result type (`content`, `structuredContent`, `isError`) instead of referring to `CallToolResult<T>`, which `describeTool()`, `searchTools()`, and `ALL_TOOLS` showed without defining it; the codemode description no longer includes the shared MCP types
- Changed `serializeConversation()` (compaction, branch summaries, bug reports) to omit thinking blocks; replayed thinking is often not in the live context, so including it could make a summarization request larger than the context it summarizes and fail

### Fixed

- Fixed codemode ignoring a `// @options:` line that is not the first line of the script, which ran the script without the requested `timeout_ms`; the call now fails with an error before the script runs ([#10631](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10631))
- Fixed Mistral streams being aborted mid-generation (e.g. during long thinking) after the request timeout; the timeout now applies only to waiting for response headers ([#10609](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10609))
- Fixed a symlinked `AGENTS.md` in a git worktree nested inside its main repo causing no project context file to load ([#10681](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10681))
- Fixed the code mode tool description claiming every failed tool call rejects; a tool that declares an output schema resolves with its value on failure too (e.g. `bash` with a nonzero exit)
- Fixed runs started by `pi.sendMessage(..., { triggerTurn: true })` removing system prompt sections added in `before_agent_start` after their first tool call, which changed the prompt mid-run and broke the provider prompt cache twice per run ([#10267](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10267), [#10739](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10739) by [@davidbrai](https://github.com/davidbrai))
- Fixed codemode blocking the process for seconds to minutes after scripts with many `text()` calls; joining the output items was quadratic ([#10678](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10678))
- Fixed print mode (`-p`) exiting 0 without a warning when the final response was cut off at the model's output token limit; it now prints the partial text, writes a warning to stderr, and exits 1 ([#10799](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10799))
- Fixed `pi mcp login --help` and the CLI docs describing `--timeout` as only the wait for the browser; it limits the whole sign-in ([#10636](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10636))
- Fixed `~` not being expanded in `!pattern`, `+path`, and `-path` entries of the `extensions`, `skills`, `prompts`, and `themes` settings, so entries like `!~/skills/pdf` matched nothing ([#10765](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10765))
- Fixed MCP servers with resources registering no tools until every resource was listed; Pi no longer lists resources when connecting, so `/mcp` and `pi mcp list` show that a server offers resources instead of counting them ([#10526](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10526))
- Fixed MCP tool calls failing when the server returns structured content that is not an object (an array, `null`, or a primitive, as MCP 2026-07-28 allows); codemode declarations of MCP tools without an output schema now type `structuredContent` as `unknown` instead of an object ([#10416](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10416))
- Fixed reading or writing `auth.json` on Windows failing with `EPERM` when the previous lock folder was still being deleted; Pi now retries briefly before reporting the error ([#10801](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10801))
- Fixed OpenRouter router models such as `openrouter/auto` showing a cost of -$1,000,000 per 1M tokens; OpenRouter's negative placeholder prices are now 0 ([#10672](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10672) by [@davidbrai](https://github.com/davidbrai))
- Fixed Anthropic requests failing when the provider rejects the strict tool set for grammar size, tool count, or union limits; Pi now retries once with preferred tools non-strict ([#10409](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10409))
- Fixed "The upstream provider returned an error" not being retried as a transient provider error ([#10842](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10842))
- Fixed focused fullscreen overlays blocking mouse-wheel scrolling of the transcript ([#10769](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10769))
- Fixed fragmented terminal color replies leaking hex values into the prompt and opening the external editor (related reports: [#10256](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10256), [#10657](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10657))
- Fixed inline images not rendering in Herdr since 1.1.0 ([#10774](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10774) by [@ogulcancelik](https://github.com/ogulcancelik))
- Fixed key bindings that name a shifted symbol, such as `+` or `ctrl++`, not matching under the Kitty keyboard protocol or modifyOtherKeys ([#9880](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/9880) by [@christianklotz](https://github.com/christianklotz))
- Fixed the compaction status indicator embedded in a custom editor using the default muted colors instead of the editor border or thinking-level color, as the working indicator does ([#10809](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10809), [#10810](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10810) by [@Jay-Madden](https://github.com/Jay-Madden))
- Fixed MCP tool calls that were cancelled or timed out while waiting for an OAuth refresh still being sent to the server once the refresh finished ([#10598](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10598))
- Fixed MCP OAuth sign-in accepting an authorization response with an `iss` parameter that could not be checked because no authorization server metadata was discovered; sign-in now fails with an issuer mismatch. Reported by [@AizenvoltPrime](https://github.com/AizenvoltPrime)
- Fixed codemode failing with a broken bridge error when Pi runs under `node --watch` on Node 24 or 26 ([#10725](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10725))

### Removed

- Removed the unreleased experimental server, client, and plugin stack (`src/experimental`, `src/cli/experimental`) and its source-only `./client` and `./experimental/plugin` exports; none of it was part of the published package. The `@earendil-works/pi-client`, `@earendil-works/pi-protocol`, and `@earendil-works/pi-server` packages it used are removed and no longer released
- Removed the dependency on `@earendil-works/chord`
