prs.title: fix(memory): budget the index title against the line cap
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Makes `MAX_INDEX_LINE_CHARS` a real bound on the emitted index line instead of a bound on the hook alone. `docIndexLine()` now budgets the title and the link target against the 150-char cap before rendering, so a long title is truncated with `…` rather than pushing the line past the limit that names it.

The title yields to the cap, but only down to a floor: `MIN_INDEX_TITLE_CHARS` (24, mirroring the existing `MIN_INDEX_HOOK_CHARS`) is clamped with `Math.max`, and the link target is never shortened. A path long enough to starve the title is kept whole and the line runs long — a resolving long link beats a short dead one — with the title clamped at the floor instead of collapsing to nothing.

## Why it's needed

Fixes #13910. `docIndexLine()` (`packages/core/src/memory/indexer.ts`) rendered the entry as

```js
const link = `- [${title}](${encodeIndexPathTarget(doc.relativePath)})`;
```

and then budgeted **only the hook** against `MAX_INDEX_LINE_CHARS` (150). The hook branch was safe, because `truncateIndexField(description, room)` made that line land exactly on the cap. The no-hook branch returned `link` unchanged, so the emitted line was bounded only by `MAX_INDEX_FIELD_CHARS` (120) plus the path length — up to ~197 chars for a 120-char title on a 71-char path, matching the 182/189 the issue measured on real stores. The read path then re-measures that line against its own cap, so the writer's own constant was silently not the limit it names.

The fix is to make the title share the line budget instead of escaping it:

```js
const target = encodeIndexPathTarget(doc.relativePath);
const titleLimit = Math.max(
  MIN_INDEX_TITLE_CHARS,
  MAX_INDEX_LINE_CHARS - INDEX_LINK_AFFIX_CHARS - target.length,
);
const title = truncateIndexField(sanitizeIndexField(doc.title) || doc.type, titleLimit);
const link = `- [${title}](${target})`;
```

`INDEX_LINK_AFFIX_CHARS` is the `- [`, `](` and `)` wrapper spent around title + target (6 chars), so `link.length <= MAX_INDEX_LINE_CHARS` whenever the path leaves room for `MIN_INDEX_TITLE_CHARS`.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

```
$ cd packages/core
$ npx vitest run src/memory/indexer.test.ts src/memory/prompt.test.ts
# Test Files  2 passed (2)
#   src/memory/prompt.test.ts  (45 tests)
#   src/memory/indexer.test.ts (36 tests)
```

`npx tsc --noEmit` reports no error under `src/memory/`, and `eslint` reports no new violation — the 7 pre-existing `vitest/no-conditional-expect` errors in these two test files are unchanged in count.

Local note, stated so it is not mistaken for a clean sweep: on this Windows host 4 of the 48 files in `src/memory` fail, for reasons unrelated to the change. `team-memory-sync.test.ts` hits `spawnSync git EBUSY` (Windows file locking), `recall-scan-latency.test.ts` asserts a 100 ms wall-clock ceiling the host misses, and `forget.test.ts` / `memoryLifecycle.integration.test.ts` hit hook timeouts. Running those same four files against the parent commit `4cd30565b2` fails identically (`2 failed | 2 passed` both sides), so nothing here is caused by — or masking — this change.

### Evidence (Before & After)

| case | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 120-char title, 71-char path | 197 chars | ≤ 150, target intact |
| long title + long path, no hook | over the cap | ≤ 150, title truncated with `…` |
| long title, short path | hook kept | hook kept (non-regression) |
| short title + hook | unchanged | byte-identical |

The added tests each fail if the change is reverted, rather than merely passing alongside it.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ✅   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Windows, Node.js v24.18.0, vitest run from `packages/core`. Unit tests only; macOS and Linux are left to CI.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a path longer than the whole budget still lets the line run over the cap, with the title clamped to `MIN_INDEX_TITLE_CHARS`. That is deliberate — the link target is never truncated, because a resolving long link beats a short dead one — but it does mean the cap is a bound on `- [title](target)` only when the path leaves room for the title floor.
- Not validated / out of scope: the writer/reader mismatch the issue mentions is already absent on `main`, because `prompt.ts` interpolates the writer's own `MAX_INDEX_LINE_CHARS`, so no reader-side change was needed. Because the cap is now genuinely enforced, `MAX_INDEX_LINE_CHARS` reads true as a hard limit, so the "advisory vs hard limit" naming point needs no rename.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. Only newly written entries are affected; existing stores keep the lines they already have. `packages/core/src/memory/prompt.test.ts` needed a fixture adjustment — its long-line fixture was tuned to land just over `MAX_INDEX_CHARS`, and shorter lines made it fall under, so the path's space run grew from 250 to 288 to keep exercising the truncation path.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #13910

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

让 `MAX_INDEX_LINE_CHARS` 成为对输出行真正生效的上限，而不再只是对 hook 生效。`docIndexLine()` 现在会在渲染之前，把标题与链接目标一起纳入 150 字符的预算，因此过长的标题会以 `…` 截断，而不是把整行顶过这个以它命名的上限。

标题会让位于上限，但只让到一个下限：`MIN_INDEX_TITLE_CHARS`（24，与既有的 `MIN_INDEX_HOOK_CHARS` 对应）通过 `Math.max` 进行兜底，链接目标则永不缩短。当路径长到足以挤掉标题时，路径整体保留、该行允许超出上限——可解析的长链接优于短而失效的链接——标题则被夹在下限处，而不是塌缩为空。

## 为什么需要

修复 #13910。`docIndexLine()`（`packages/core/src/memory/indexer.ts`）此前这样渲染条目：

```js
const link = `- [${title}](${encodeIndexPathTarget(doc.relativePath)})`;
```

然后**只把 hook** 纳入 `MAX_INDEX_LINE_CHARS`（150）的预算。hook 分支是安全的，因为 `truncateIndexField(description, room)` 让该行恰好落在上限上。但无 hook 分支会原样返回 `link`，因此输出行仅受 `MAX_INDEX_FIELD_CHARS`（120）加上路径长度约束——120 字符标题配 71 字符路径可达约 197 字符，与 issue 在真实存储上测到的 182/189 一致。读取路径随后又会用自身的上限重新度量该行，因此写入方自己的常量其实并非它所声称的那个限制。

修复方式是让标题共享行预算，而不是逃逸出去：

```js
const target = encodeIndexPathTarget(doc.relativePath);
const titleLimit = Math.max(
  MIN_INDEX_TITLE_CHARS,
  MAX_INDEX_LINE_CHARS - INDEX_LINK_AFFIX_CHARS - target.length,
);
const title = truncateIndexField(sanitizeIndexField(doc.title) || doc.type, titleLimit);
const link = `- [${title}](${target})`;
```

`INDEX_LINK_AFFIX_CHARS` 是包裹在标题与目标之外的 `- [`、`](` 与 `)` 共 6 个字符，因此只要路径给 `MIN_INDEX_TITLE_CHARS` 留出了空间，就有 `link.length <= MAX_INDEX_LINE_CHARS`。

## 审阅者测试计划

### 如何验证

```
$ cd packages/core
$ npx vitest run src/memory/indexer.test.ts src/memory/prompt.test.ts
# Test Files  2 passed (2)
#   src/memory/prompt.test.ts  (45 tests)
#   src/memory/indexer.test.ts (36 tests)
```

`npx tsc --noEmit` 在 `src/memory/` 下无报错；`eslint` 无新增违规——这两个测试文件中既有的 7 个 `vitest/no-conditional-expect` 错误数量不变。

本地说明，写出来以免被误读为全部通过：在本机 Windows 上，`src/memory` 的 48 个文件中有 4 个失败，原因与本次改动无关。`team-memory-sync.test.ts` 报 `spawnSync git EBUSY`（Windows 文件锁），`recall-scan-latency.test.ts` 断言的 100 ms 挂钟上限本机达不到，`forget.test.ts` 与 `memoryLifecycle.integration.test.ts` 则是 hook 超时。把这 4 个文件在父提交 `4cd30565b2` 上重跑，结果完全一致（两侧均为 `2 failed | 2 passed`），因此没有由本次改动引起、也没有被它掩盖的失败。

### 证据（改动前后）

| 场景 | 改动前 | 改动后 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 120 字符标题 + 71 字符路径 | 197 字符 | ≤ 150，目标完整 |
| 长标题 + 长路径，无 hook | 超出上限 | ≤ 150，标题以 `…` 截断 |
| 长标题 + 短路径 | 保留 hook | 保留 hook（非回归） |
| 短标题 + hook | 不变 | 逐字节一致 |

新增的测试在回退改动后都会失败，而不是仅仅与之并存通过。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ⚠️  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ✅  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ⚠️  |

### 环境（可选）

Windows，Node.js v24.18.0，在 `packages/core` 下运行 vitest。仅单元测试；macOS 与 Linux 交由 CI 把关。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：当路径长于整个预算时，该行仍会超出上限，标题被夹在 `MIN_INDEX_TITLE_CHARS` 处。这是有意为之——链接目标永不截断，因为可解析的长链接优于短而失效的链接——但这确实意味着该上限只在路径给标题下限留出空间时，才是对 `- [title](target)` 的约束。
- 未验证 / 超出范围：issue 提到的写入方/读取方不一致在 `main` 上已不存在，因为 `prompt.ts` 插值的正是写入方自己的 `MAX_INDEX_LINE_CHARS`，因此读取侧无需改动。由于该上限现在真正生效，`MAX_INDEX_LINE_CHARS` 名副其实，故"建议值 vs 硬上限"的命名问题无需改名。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。仅影响新写入的条目；既有存储保持它们已有的行。`packages/core/src/memory/prompt.test.ts` 需要一处 fixture 调整——它的长行 fixture 原本刚好落在 `MAX_INDEX_CHARS` 之上，行变短后落到了下方，因此把路径中的空格串从 250 增至 288，以继续覆盖截断路径。

## 关联 Issue

Fixes #13910

</details>

prs.title: fix(cli): carry branch points through the session load replay
prs.body:
## What this PR does

When a session is restored from disk, for example after `qwen serve` restarts, the load replay now stamps each assistant answer with its persisted branch checkpoint, the same decoration the paged transcript path already applies. Web Shell keys the Branch action off that marker, so a reopened session offers Branch on every answer that has a valid checkpoint, exactly as it did while the turn was live.

The transcript reader already indexes branch checkpoints; the restore projection just never forwarded them to the replay layer. The change plumbs them through for both the cold load and the live restore, and both replay entry points now share one stamping helper instead of only the paged path having it.

## Why it's needed

After a daemon restart, hovering any earlier answer in a restored Web Shell session shows only Copy, and no answer in the session offers Branch, even though the checkpoints on disk are still valid and branching through the RPC works. Restored sessions look read-only for no reason. #13782 has the full measurements, including that the transcript endpoint and the branch RPC both stay correct; only the load replay drops the marker.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Unit level: the new reader test asserts both restore projections (cold and live) advertise the checkpoint of an assistant record on their replay page, and the new replay tests assert the load replay stamps the checkpoint onto the answer's final visible chunk and leaves updates untouched when no branch points are passed in. The existing paged-replay tests keep pinning the stamping semantics (last visible chunk only, own-property lookup against untrusted record ids), now against the shared helper.

Real stack, the scenario from the issue: run `qwen serve`, open the Web Shell, send a prompt, wait for the answer, hover it: Branch shows. Restart `qwen serve`, reopen the same session from the sidebar, hover the same answer: Branch shows again. Before this change it did not.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A: no UI change on this side of the stack; the fix restores metadata the Web Shell client already keys on (`MessageList` shows Branch when the marker is present), and its smoke test already assumes restored replays carry it.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅    |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️    |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️    |

Unit tests, typecheck and build on macOS arm64; Windows and Linux via CI.

### Environment (optional)

N/A

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: none identified. The field is additive and optional end to end, and the stamping helper is verbatim the code the paged path already ran.
- Not validated / out of scope: the ungated read-only history dump (`qwen/session/loadUpdates`) reads through the session service rather than the transcript index, so it has no branch points to forward and is untouched; rewind at head operates on the live session and does not re-replay from disk.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Closes #13782

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 的内容

会话从磁盘恢复后（例如 `qwen serve` 重启再打开），load 回放现在会把每个助手回答对应的已持久化分支检查点标上去，和分页 transcript 路径已有的处理保持一致。Web Shell 正是依据这个标记来显示「分叉」按钮的，所以重新打开的会话里，凡是有有效检查点的回答都会重新提供分叉入口，和回合实时进行时完全一样。

transcript 读取层本来就索引了分支检查点，只是恢复投影从未把它们转发给回放层。本次修改把冷加载和热恢复两条路径都接通，并且两个回放入口现在共用一个打戳 helper，不再只有分页路径有这段逻辑。

## 为什么需要

daemon 重启之后，在恢复出来的 Web Shell 会话里把鼠标悬停到任意一条历史回答上，只会显示「复制」，整个会话没有任何回答提供「分叉」，尽管磁盘上的检查点仍然有效、通过 RPC 分叉也正常。恢复出来的会话无缘无故变得像只读一样。#13782 里有完整实测：transcript 接口和分叉 RPC 都是对的，只有 load 回放丢了标记。

## 评审验证计划

### 如何验证

单测层面：新增的 reader 测试断言冷、热两个恢复投影都会在回放页上公布助手记录对应的检查点；新增的回放测试断言 load 回放会把检查点打到回答最后一个可见分块上，并且在没有传入分支点时不做任何改动。既有分页回放测试继续钉住打戳语义（只打最后一个可见分块、对不可信记录 id 做自有属性判断），只是现在跑的是共用 helper。

真实环境，按 issue 里的场景：跑 `qwen serve`，打开 Web Shell，发一条消息等回答，悬停：能看到「分叉」。重启 `qwen serve`，从侧栏重新打开同一会话，悬停同一条回答：「分叉」重新出现。在本 PR 之前它是消失的。

### 前后对比证据

N/A：这一侧没有 UI 改动；修复只是把 Web Shell 客户端本来就依赖的元数据补回去（`MessageList` 在标记存在时显示分叉），它的冒烟测试本来就假定恢复回放携带该标记。

### 已验证平台

macOS arm64 上跑了单测、typecheck 和构建；Windows 和 Linux 走 CI。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或权衡：未识别到。该字段端到端都是新增且可选的，打戳 helper 就是分页路径原本在跑的那段代码。
- 未验证 / 不在范围内：非门控的只读历史导出（`qwen/session/loadUpdates`）走的是 session service 而不是 transcript 索引，没有分支点可转发，保持原样；rewind 在当前 head 上作用于存活会话，不会从磁盘重新回放。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。

</details>

prs.title: feat: project agent identity and Agent Team delivery onto the ACP/daemon wire (refs #13785)
prs.body:
## What this PR does Projects agent identity and Agent Team coordination onto the ACP/daemon wire, in two deliberately distinct collaboration columns. Subagent column (parent→child delegation): every projected subagent frame (thought, message, tool call, tool call update) now carries `_meta.agent = { agentName, depth, kind }` with a path-style name (`/root/general-purpose`), mirroring OpenAI Responses' per-item `agent` identity; the Web Shell shows that path on subagent panels (tooltip always, visible chip from depth ≥ 2). `agentName` is a readable role path, not a unique execution id: concurrent same-type subagents share it, and renaming the agent definition changes it. `parentToolCallId` distinguishes subagent executions; that boundary is documented on both the producer and the normalizer. Agent Team column (peer complete agents): an ACP-hosted session now attaches a leader sink (`teamSink.ts`). Before this, `TeamManager.pollLeaderInbox()` returned before consuming on this host (teammate reports stayed unread in the leader inbox) and `TEAMMATE_APPROVAL_REQUEST` was void-emitted — the coordination never reached anyone. Now teammate reports are delivered as `peer` background notifications carrying structured sender identity (`kind: 'teammate'`, minted from the inbox entry's `from`, never parsed from message text), roster joins/exits are projected as peer notifications so an already-attached client can track membership transitions (there is no current-state snapshot for late attach or reconnect), and teammate tool approvals route to the client's `requestPermission` (fail-closed: Cancel plus a `` to the leader when the host cannot answer; YOLO auto-approve only when the request carries no renderable details). ## Why it's needed #13785 records the gap: the public vocabulary names child agents and teams, but nothing a client receives says which agent produced what. Both reference protocols (OpenAI Responses multi-agent, Anthropic Managed Agents) treat agent identity as contractual. This slice delivers the identity dimension on the daemon/ACP projection and removes the "ACP host has no leader sink" failure class — the zero-signal class among the three host classes in #13785 M4 — giving M1b a reference wire shape. Peer delivery reuses core's existing `'peer'` background-notification channel (idle wake, loss accounting, kind-agnostic drain/display), so no new event types and no ACP protocol extensions were needed. ## Reviewer Test Plan ### How to verify At `df760052100d1`, bridge-client tests passed 159/159, Agent Team leader-sink cases 6/6, and team-sink tests 12/12; targeted ESLint, CLI/ACP bridge typechecks, and the ACP bridge build passed. Real-model acceptance confirmed that a writer approval survives leader background-turn completion, remains pending for host approval, and writes the file after a Web Shell vote. See the [current-head report and screenshots](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13902#issuecomment-6138227209), including outstanding CI gates. Earlier build and runtime results below belong to earlier revisions and are not current-head acceptance evidence. Real machine: boot the daemon from this branch with `QWEN_CODE_ENABLE_AGENT_TEAM=1 node scripts/dev.js serve --port

--token --workspace

`, create a session, send a team prompt (`team_create`, then spawn teammate `correctness` asking it to report one sentence ending in a marker). Expected and observed on SSE: peer notifications `teammate-roster-1` (status joined) and `teammate-message-2/3`, each carrying `_meta.agent={"agentName":"/root/correctness","depth":1,"kind":"teammate"}`, plus leader-reply frames with `source=background_notification_response`; the same capture contains zero subagent-column frames. Contrast run without a team: 47 `parentToolCallId`-chained frames carrying `kind:'subagent'` and zero peer markers — the two columns are mutually attributable at a glance. The Web Shell rendered the peer rows (`ⓘ … · peer`) and the verbatim teammate report in a real headless Chromium against the same daemon. ### Evidence (Before & After) Before: on this host an ACP session with a team delivered 0 teammate reports (retained unread in the leader inbox) and emitted 0 approval signals; no projected object carried any agent identity. After: the SSE markers and browser rendering described above. ### Tested on | OS | Status | | :--------: | :-------------: | | 🍏 macOS | ⚠️ not tested | | 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested | | 🐧 Linux | ✅ tested | ### Environment (optional) Linux host; daemon via `node scripts/dev.js serve` (no bundle step); headless Chromium (playwright) for Web Shell rendering; unit suites via vitest with `env -u QWEN_CODE_SERVE -u QWEN_RUNTIME_DIR`. ## Risk & Scope - Main risk or tradeoff: identity is additive `_meta`; older readers ignore it. Teammate identity is minted only for single-sender batches — mixed-sender batches stay unattributed rather than misattributed. Status/idle team events are deliberately not projected (each would wake the leader into an automatic turn). Join/exit notifications are incremental, so a client that attaches late still needs a non-waking roster snapshot/query before it can claim authoritative current membership. - Not validated / out of scope: managed-agent public-contract projections (#13785 M1a/M2/M3) and client intervention verbs (M4) remain design surfaces; foreground nested subagents do not project their own frames today (verified on real machine: single `parentToolCallId` layer, depth values only 1), so depth ≥ 2 identity has no wire producer yet — nested trees remain record-projection work (M1a); cross-session teammate projection is M1b/M3. - Breaking changes / migration notes: none; all fields additive, no new daemon routes, no contract-test surface changed. ## Linked Issues Refs #13785 (referenced without a closing keyword: the public-contract milestones remain open design work).
中文说明 ## 本 PR 做了什么 把 agent 身份与 Agent Team 协调投影到 ACP/daemon 的 wire 上，分为刻意保持区分的两条协作列。 subagent 列（父子委派）：每个投影出的 subagent 帧（thought、message、tool call、tool call update）现在都带 `_meta.agent = { agentName, depth, kind }`，名字为 path 风格（`/root/general-purpose`），与 OpenAI Responses 的逐 item `agent` 身份同形；Web Shell 在 subagent 面板上显示该 path（tooltip 恒显示，depth ≥ 2 显示可见 chip）。`agentName` 是可读的角色 path，并不是唯一执行 ID：同类型并发 subagent 会共享它，agent 定义改名也会改变它；`parentToolCallId` 用于区分 subagent 执行，这一边界在生产侧与 normalizer 两侧都有文档。 Agent Team 列（对等完整 agent）：ACP 托管会话现在会挂一个 leader sink（`teamSink.ts`）。在此之前，本宿主上 `TeamManager.pollLeaderInbox()` 会在消费前早退（队员报告留在 leader inbox 里未读），`TEAMMATE_APPROVAL_REQUEST` 空 emit——协调过程到不了任何人手里。现在队员报告以 `peer` 背景通知投递，带结构化发送者身份（`kind: 'teammate'`，从 inbox 条目的 `from` 铸造，绝不从消息文本解析）；roster 的加入/退出投影为 peer 通知，已挂载的客户端可跟踪成员变化（晚挂载或重连时没有当前状态快照）；队员的工具审批路由到客户端 `requestPermission`（fail-closed：宿主无法应答时 Cancel 并向 leader 注入 ``；仅当请求不带可渲染细节且处于 YOLO 时才自动批准）。 ## 为什么需要 #13785 记录了缺口：公共词表里有 child agent 与 team，但客户端收到的任何东西都不说明「哪条输出是哪个 agent 产的」。两个参照协议（OpenAI Responses multi-agent、Anthropic Managed Agents）都把 agent 身份当契约内容。本片在 daemon/ACP 投影侧交付身份维度，并消掉「ACP 宿主没有 leader sink」这一失效类——即 #13785 M4 三类宿主中的零信号类——为 M1b 给出参考 wire 形状。peer 投递复用 core 既有的 `'peer'` 背景通知通道（空闲唤醒、丢失记账、kind 无关的 drain/display），因此不需要新事件类型、不需要 ACP 协议扩展。 ## 评审测试计划 ### 如何验证 `df760052100d1` 上 bridge-client 159/159、Agent Team leader sink 6/6、team-sink 12/12、定向 ESLint、CLI/ACP bridge 类型检查和 ACP bridge 构建均通过。真实模型已验证队员审批跨 leader 后台轮次结束仍保持待审，Web Shell 单次批准后文件实际写入。见[当前提交验收报告与截图](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13902#issuecomment-6138227209)，其中也列出尚未完成的 CI gate。下方构建和真机结果属于较早版本，不作为当前提交的验收证据。 真机：从本分支起 daemon（`QWEN_CODE_ENABLE_AGENT_TEAM=1 node scripts/dev.js serve --port

--token --workspace

`），建会话，发 team prompt（`team_create`，再派 teammate `correctness` 要求其回一句以 marker 结尾的话）。SSE 上期望并实测到：peer 通知 `teammate-roster-1`（status joined）与 `teammate-message-2/3`，均带 `_meta.agent={"agentName":"/root/correctness","depth":1,"kind":"teammate"}`，以及 `source=background_notification_response` 的 leader 回话帧；同一抓帧中 subagent 列帧为零。不带 team 的对照跑：47 帧 `parentToolCallId` 链帧带 `kind:'subagent'`、peer 标记零命中——两列形状互斥、可一眼归因。Web Shell 在真 headless Chromium 中对同一 daemon 渲染出了 peer 行（`ⓘ … · peer`）与队员原话。 ### 证据（Before & After） Before：本宿主上带 team 的 ACP 会话投递 0 条队员报告（留在 leader inbox 未读）、0 个审批信号；任何投影对象都不带 agent 身份。After：上述 SSE 标记与浏览器渲染。 ### Tested on | OS | Status | | :--------: | :-------------: | | 🍏 macOS | ⚠️ 未测试 | | 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 未测试 | | 🐧 Linux | ✅ 已测试 | ### 环境（可选） Linux 宿主机；daemon 走 `node scripts/dev.js serve`（无 bundle 步骤）；Web Shell 渲染用 headless Chromium（playwright）；单测走 vitest 并加 `env -u QWEN_CODE_SERVE -u QWEN_RUNTIME_DIR`。 ## 风险与范围 - 主要风险或权衡：身份是 additive `_meta`，旧读者会忽略它。teammate 身份只为单发送者批次铸造——混合发送者批次宁可无身份也不张冠李戴。status/idle 队事件刻意不投影（每条都会唤醒 leader 起一个自动 turn）。加入/退出通知是增量流，晚挂载客户端仍需要一个不会唤醒 leader 的 roster 快照/查询，才能声称拿到了权威当前成员表。 - 未验证 / 超出范围：managed-agent 公共契约投影（#13785 M1a/M2/M3）与客户端干预动词（M4）仍是设计面；foreground 嵌套 subagent 今天不投影自身帧（真机验过：parentToolCallId 仅一层、depth 取值仅 1），故 depth ≥ 2 身份暂无 wire 生产者——嵌套树仍是记录投影工作（M1a）；跨 session 的 teammate 投影属 M1b/M3。 - 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无；全部字段 additive，无新 daemon 路由，契约测试面未变。 ## 关联 Issue Refs #13785（不用 closing 关键字引用：公共契约里程碑仍是开放的设计工作）。

prs.title: feat(managed-agent): add L4 Shell and MCP session lifecycle
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds durable close and delete for the exact `hosted-workspace-shell/1` and `hosted-workspace-mcp/1` profiles. A lifecycle operation settles prior business effects and SessionEnd/SessionDelete Hooks once, then prepares and settles the original resources before detaching the writer and stopping the original worker. Java independently checks the resource evidence before completing close or atomically committing private-output retirement and the deletion tombstone.

Cleanup can recover a fenced writer in DRAINING under the current operation claim without running SessionStart, a model, new tools, or Monitor rebuilds. Shell cleanup preserves final output and suppresses new notifications; MCP cleanup releases each connection through H1 before releasing its shared owner, with a separate trusted-stop-proof path for a worker that has already died. Unknown effects or missing output remain recovery blocked.

Keeps the files v1 protocol and existing public API, owner/read authorization, actor-scoped idempotency, archive/unarchive behavior, and child cascade policy. Lifecycle v2 advertisement is disabled by default and enabled per exact profile. After the main rebase, exact-profile admission also prevents an unsupported Shell/MCP profile from falling back to legacy close, and closed /1 Sessions reuse retention with matching capabilities. Lifecycle v2 rejects newly started model attempts in both effects and resource phases, while retaining files v1 semantics.

The public Shell deletion-to-collection fixture follows its actual inline capture resources and enables the scheduled collector through the production configuration. It requires real captured stdout, retirement, collection ledger/byte evidence and physical byte removal, while retaining the companion Session and shared Workspace marker. Exact-head `86656d109` [Linux Hosted/MySQL CI](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/38280154338/job/114915236005) passes 36/36, including the ten-case public Workspace class and public Shell deletion-to-O4 collection (123.284 s). The prior `2ef8fba0d` result remains historical evidence.

Foreground capture evidence now follows its actual storage: retained inline receipt outcomes are checked against their original journal, while published manifests, pages, segments and seals are verified against the original execution identity. Known capture failure still requires manifest evidence when resultRef is null. Object-backed publication outcomes keep the existing object/receipt verification and final-transaction publication pointer and quarantine checks. Manifest identity uses the original execution protocol: legacy runtimeProtocol 3/deferred captures compare their strict bare input digest, while deferred v3/O2 and background start captures retain the original argument digest. Missing or changed identity still blocks cleanup; whole-request hashes are not normalized into input hashes.

## Why it's needed

Files-only lifecycle settlement cannot establish that background Shells, Monitors, captures, publications, MCP connections, and Hook-shared owners have all finished. An effects receipt proves Hook completion but cannot authorize resource retirement by itself. L4 adds the resource barrier needed to close these Sessions or delete their private recovery/output state without affecting shared Workspace files or other Sessions.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. In a Linux Hosted deployment with upgraded Java/Broker consumers, enable the Shell v2 profile. An idle Session owner with current read access can close or delete through REST and WebShell. An active, cancelling, or approval-waiting foreground Turn returns `turn_active`; cleanup remains available after disabling new Shell execution.
2. Verify close runs SessionEnd only, delete runs SessionEnd followed by SessionDelete, and retry or claim takeover does not repeat either Hook. A DRAINING cold recovery accepts only the current cleanup writer and rejects stale claims without starting ordinary work.
3. Drain foreground/background Shell and Monitor resources while they still produce their final output. Completion requires sealed output or a verifiable capture-failure terminal. Missing output continues to block even if the original worker is stopped, and cleanup creates no new Monitor notification.
4. After the Shell gate, enable MCP v2. Verify all configuration revisions and Hook-shared owners: live workers release H1 connections before their owner; stopped workers require matching stop proof and known business/Hook effects. An unknown dispatched result remains blocked, and a local HTTP transport close does not claim remote Session deletion.
5. Delete a Shell Session through the public API and observe scheduled O4 collection without directly invoking retirement or collector helpers. Private retirement and the tombstone commit together; a companion Session and shared Workspace marker survive. Archive/unarchive after close leaves the Session closed.

### Evidence (Before & After)

No TUI or WebShell control changes. The installed global qwen 0.24.6 baseline could not launch the reserved Hosted profile, so it did not provide a runtime before/after comparison. On exact head `86656d109`, build/typecheck/bundle and three Java module Checkstyle checks pass. Targeted Java tests pass 597/597 (SDK 70, Broker 267, Managed Agent 260); seven related TypeScript files pass 658/658, and the two upstream-fixed files pass another 17 and 28 cases (703 total). Both prior failing assertions now pass after absorbing the official main fixes; all six L4 patches are unchanged. Local native MySQL 37 cases and ten POSIX fault scenarios remain historical results on `2ef8fba0d`; unchanged lifecycle sources and drivers support their scope, but those local gates were not freshly executed on `86656d109`. Fresh `86656d109` Linux Hosted/MySQL reports now pass 36/36, including the public Workspace class 10/10 and deletion-to-O4 collection. Remote CI is not yet green. On the first rerun cycle (1/3 for this head), the Ubuntu unit job passed: its published report has 89,825 passes, no failures and 119 skips, including all 65 child-agent cases. The initial fixed-200 ms cancellation failure and controlled delay probe remain historical diagnostic evidence. The Java 21 rerun completed its SDK/Broker test command and Broker Checkstyle successfully, but the entire job was CANCELLED after exceeding its 30-minute limit in Post Set up Java. GitHub annotations prove the timeout; unavailable job logs prevent identifying the exact post-action/cache operation or reporting fresh Java test counts. WebShell smoke is still queued. The watcher has no retry recommendation, so no further rerun was triggered. Threads remain 1/1 resolved, with no new review or source, unrelated test or CI configuration change. Exact evidence and remaining release gates are in the separate E2E report.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :--: | :-- |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ Current-head build and targeted unit verification; native MySQL/POSIX evidence is pinned to prior head `2ef8fba0d` |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ Not tested locally |
| 🐧 Linux | ✅ Exact `86656d109` public deletion-to-O4 and Hosted/MySQL 36/36 pass; complete L4 phase/original-worker/H3 and live MCP release matrix remains pending |

### Environment

macOS arm64, Node 22.14, Java 21, Maven 3.9, native MySQL 8.4.11/InnoDB, isolated fake-model fixtures. No real-model endpoint or production database was used.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: correctness depends on original Runtime identity, current claim fencing, and durable resource/output evidence across crashes and lost responses. Missing evidence intentionally leaves the operation closing/deleting and recovery blocked.
- Not validated / out of scope: full Linux original-worker/reboot and delegated cgroup-v2 H3 lifecycle faults, every L4 phase crash/lost-response cut, and the complete live MCP stdio/HTTP/SSE release matrix remain release gates. `/2`, CSI, a separate TeamLead profile, new WebShell buttons, and automatic child foreground cancellation are outside scope. Independent `/review` was unavailable; manual review and self-audits were performed.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: v0/v1 operations retain their semantics; unknown versions are refused. Upgrade every Java/Broker lifecycle consumer before advertising Shell v2, then enable MCP only after its gate. Unfinished v2 operations prevent rollback to v1-only consumers.
- Review/merge base: #13889 has merged. The L4 commits are rebased onto main `18f80f566` to absorb the upstream Shell fixture and transcript ceiling fixes, preserving the merged H3 drain, G3 recovery, asynchronous publication verification, CSI and never-started recovery interfaces. The PR targets main; validation and CI for the rebased head are recorded in the follow-up E2E report. V2 profile advertisement remains disabled by default.

Design: [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/l4-shell-mcp-lifecycle/docs/design/workspace-profile-lifecycle.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/l4-shell-mcp-lifecycle/docs/design/workspace-profile-lifecycle.zh-CN.md). Both versions are complete, linked, and synchronized.

## Linked Issues

L4 of #13164. Prerequisites #13673, #13674 and #13889 are merged. This PR does not close the entire lifecycle issue.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 的变更

为精确的 `hosted-workspace-shell/1` 和 `hosted-workspace-mcp/1` profile 增加持久化 close/delete。生命周期操作先结算已有业务效果，并执行一次 SessionEnd/SessionDelete Hook；随后准备并结算原资源，再 detach writer、停止原 worker。Java 独立检查资源证据，然后完成 close，或原子提交私有输出退役与删除 tombstone。

清理可以在 DRAINING 中由当前 operation claim 恢复受围栏保护的 writer，不运行 SessionStart、模型、新工具或 Monitor rebuild。Shell 清理保留最后输出并禁止新通知；MCP 清理先通过 H1 释放每条连接，再释放共享 owner，已死亡 worker 则走独立的可信 stop proof 路径。未知效果或缺失输出继续保持 recovery blocked。

保留 files v1 协议、现有公开 API、owner/read 授权、actor 范围的幂等、archive/unarchive 行为和子会话级联策略。生命周期 v2 能力默认不声明，按精确 profile 开启。rebase 到 main 后进一步修正精确 profile 准入，防止不支持的 Shell/MCP profile 回退到 legacy close，已关闭 /1 会话复用 retention 且 capability 保持一致。v2 在 effects 与资源阶段均拒绝新的模型尝试，保留 files v1 的原有语义。

公开 Shell 删除到回收 fixture 按实际 inline capture 资源验证，通过生产配置启用定时 collector；要求真实 stdout、退役、台账/字节证据和物理字节清空，并保留 companion 会话及共享 Workspace marker。精确 head `86656d109` 的 [Linux Hosted/MySQL CI](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/38280154338/job/114915236005) 已 36/36 通过，含公开 Workspace 类 10/10 和公开 Shell 删除到 O4 回收（123.284 秒）；旧 `2ef8fba0d` 结果保留为历史证据。

前台 capture 证据按实际存储路径校验：保留的 inline receipt outcome 与原 journal 对照，PUBLISHED manifest、page、segment 和 seal 与原执行身份核对。已知 capture 失败时，即使 resultRef 为 null，仍要求 manifest 证据。对象存储 publication outcome 沿用已有对象/receipt 验证，以及最终事务内的 publication 指针和 quarantine 复核。 manifest 身份遵循原执行协议：旧 runtimeProtocol 3/deferred capture 比较严格的裸输入摘要，deferred v3/O2 和后台 start capture 继续比较原参数摘要。身份缺失或变更继续阻塞清理，不能把完整请求摘要归一化成输入摘要。

## 为什么需要

仅针对 files 的生命周期结算无法证明后台 Shell、Monitor、capture、publication、MCP 连接以及与 Hook 共享的 owner 都已结束。effects receipt 只能证明 Hook 完成，不能单独授权资源退役。L4 增加资源屏障，使这些会话能关闭或删除其私有恢复/输出状态，同时保留共享 Workspace 文件和其他会话。

## 审阅者测试计划

### 如何验证

1. 在已升级 Java/Broker 消费者的 Linux Hosted 部署中开启 Shell v2。空闲会话的 owner 且当前可读时，可以经 REST 和 WebShell 关闭或删除。前台 Turn 运行、取消或等待审批时返回 `turn_active`；关闭新 Shell 执行后仍能清理。
2. 验证 close 仅执行 SessionEnd，delete 按顺序执行 SessionEnd、SessionDelete；重试或 claim 接管不重复 Hook。DRAINING 冷恢复仅接受当前清理 writer，拒绝旧 claim，也不启动普通工作。
3. 在前台/后台 Shell 与 Monitor 仍产生最后输出时 drain 原资源。完成必须有封口输出或可验证的 capture 失败终态。即使原 worker 停止，缺失输出仍阻塞；清理不产生新的 Monitor 通知。
4. Shell 门槛通过后再开启 MCP v2。验证全部 configuration revision 和与 Hook 共享的 owner：存活 worker 先释放 H1 连接，再释放 owner；已停止 worker 必须有匹配的 stop proof，且业务/Hook 效果已知。已 dispatch 的结果未知时继续阻塞，本地 HTTP transport 关闭不宣称远端 Session 已删除。
5. 经公开 API 删除 Shell 会话，观察计划任务执行 O4 回收，不直接调用退役或 collector helper。私有退役与 tombstone 原子提交；同 Workspace 的 companion 会话和共享 marker 保留。close 后 archive/unarchive 仍保持 closed。

### 证据（变更前后）

没有 TUI 或 WebShell 控件变更。全局 qwen 0.24.6 无法启动当时保留的 Hosted profile，未提供运行时前后对比。精确 head `86656d109` 的 build/typecheck/bundle 和三个 Java 模块 Checkstyle 通过；Java 597/597（SDK 70、Broker 267、Managed Agent 260），7 个相关 TypeScript 文件 658/658，两个上游修复文件另有 17 和 28 项通过，合计 703 项。吸收主干正式修复后，两项原失败断言均已通过；6 个 L4 patch 保持不变。本地原生 MySQL 37 项与 10 个 POSIX 故障场景仍归属历史 head `2ef8fba0d`，生命周期源码和驱动保持一致支持既有适用范围，未将本地旧结果计作新执行。`86656d109` 的新 Linux Hosted/MySQL 报告已 36/36 通过，含公开 Workspace 10/10 及公开删除到 O4 回收。新 head 远端 CI 尚未全绿。第 1 轮重试（本 head 预算 1/3）中，Ubuntu unit 任务已通过，发布报告为 89,825 通过 / 0 失败 / 119 跳过，含全部 65 项 child-agent 用例。首轮固定 200ms 取消失败与受控延迟探针保留为历史诊断。Java 21 重试的 SDK/Broker 测试命令及 Broker Checkstyle 均成功，但整个任务在 Post Set up Java 阶段超过 30 分钟上限后被取消；GitHub annotation 已证实超时，任务日志不可用，不能进一步断定具体 cache 操作或补报新 Java 测试数量。WebShell smoke 仍排队，watcher 未建议重试，本轮没有再次重跑。线程仍 1/1 已解决，无新审阅或源码、无关测试、CI 配置修改；精确证据与剩余发布门槛见独立 E2E 报告。

### 已测试平台

| OS | 状态 |
| :--: | :-- |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ 当前 head 构建与针对性单测通过；原生 MySQL/POSIX 证据归属先前 head `2ef8fba0d` |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 未在本地测试 |
| 🐧 Linux | ✅ 精确 `86656d109` 公开删除到 O4 与 Hosted/MySQL 36/36 通过；完整 L4 阶段、原 worker/H3 及 live MCP 发布矩阵待验收 |

### 环境

macOS arm64、Node 22.14、Java 21、Maven 3.9、原生 MySQL 8.4.11/InnoDB，以及隔离的 fake-model fixture。未使用真实模型 endpoint 或生产数据库。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：正确性依赖崩溃、丢回复场景下的原 Runtime 身份、当前 claim 围栏及持久资源/输出证据。缺失证据会保持 closing/deleting 与 recovery blocked。
- 未验证或范围外：完整 Linux 原 worker/reboot、委派 cgroup-v2 H3 生命周期故障、每个 L4 阶段的崩溃/丢回复切点，以及完整 live MCP stdio/HTTP/SSE 释放矩阵仍是发布门槛。`/2`、CSI、独立 TeamLead profile、新 WebShell 按钮及自动取消子会话前台 Turn 不在范围内。独立 `/review` 不可用，已执行人工审阅与自审。
- 兼容与迁移：v0/v1 操作保持原语义，拒绝未知版本。先升级全部 Java/Broker 生命周期消费者，再声明 Shell v2；MCP 门槛通过后才启用。有未完成 v2 操作时不得回滚到仅支持 v1 的消费者。
- 评审与合并基线：#13889 已合并，L4 提交已 rebase 到 main `18f80f566`，吸收主干正式的 Shell fixture 与 transcript 上限修复，保留已合并的 H3 drain、G3 恢复、异步 publication 验证、CSI 与未启动恢复接口。本 PR 的目标为 main；新 head 的验证和 CI 状态记录在后续 E2E 报告中。v2 profile 默认仍不声明。

设计：[English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/l4-shell-mcp-lifecycle/docs/design/workspace-profile-lifecycle.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/l4-shell-mcp-lifecycle/docs/design/workspace-profile-lifecycle.zh-CN.md)。两版均完整、互链并同步。

## 关联 Issue

实现 #13164 的 L4。前置 #13673、#13674 和 #13889 均已合并。本 PR 不关闭整个生命周期 issue。

prs.title: feat(extensions): load deployment-managed extensions from a directory
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds `--managed-extensions <root>` to the CLI and daemon. Qwen discovers complete extension packages in the root’s direct children and reads their contributions in place, including with a fresh user home. Deployment providers own the package files; users retain activation preferences, settings and runtime state in writable storage.

The startup root follows workspace creation and new, resumed or recreated Agent processes. Managed packages remain subject to activation controls, while package update/uninstall/replacement is guarded by ownership. After proven withdrawal, ownership can return to a user installation with preserved preferences. Status reads, including queued update checks and the Extensions dialog’s Installed/Sources loaders, and unrelated settings writes do not perform that hand-back; bulk updates retain successful results when another candidate fails. The reported `extensionSource` describes the listed package; `user` or an omitted value does not authorize mutation when managed policy is retained. Credential checks and cleanup use recorded writer locations across later processes sharing a Qwen home. A queued uninstall cannot report a replacement user package removed after the requested managed identity has changed. Explicit release preserves a surviving or uncertain user artifact's pre-managed activation; proven withdrawal also permits an already-renamed stable user identity to hand back in the same transition. Credential cleanup failures remain durably recorded for later mutating refreshes; passive reads do not drain pending cleanup. With a configured managed root, a store-only local Skills probe defers when recovery or identity migration is required rather than manufacturing enabled defaults.

The root is pinned at startup and reverified before managed loading or read-permission exemptions. A later unavailable or redirected root remains configured for ownership and state-separation checks but grants neither form of trust. Both SDKs reject reserved CLI bindings supplied through extra arguments, including leading-equals short-option groups.

macOS Seatbelt is refused when a managed source is configured, for built-in and custom profiles. This prevents launching with a deployment-readonly guarantee the current native policy cannot enforce. Users can explicitly select Docker or Podman; ordinary Seatbelt remains available without managed extensions.

## Why it's needed

Images and shared installations can deliver extension packages, but the install/link lifecycle still requires user-side registration. A separate source lets a launcher provide consistent capabilities without coupling package deployment to each user’s installation and activation state.

Implements proposal #12147; the independent skill-refresh prerequisite #12182 is merged. Launcher authorization, managed precedence, the single-root interface and default preference adoption after managed withdrawal remain explicit maintainer review decisions.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- With only managed packages and a read-only user home, test missing current activation state with valid recovery material, and stored identities that need recasing or re-keying. Local inventory must refuse to manufacture enabled Skills; truly empty stores, exact disabled policies and unrelated-name defaults should keep their intended answers. The ordinary locked lifecycle must recover or migrate while preserving disablement.
- Rename a stable user package before its retained managed ownership is reconciled. Proven clean withdrawal should release the old ownership and accept the rename in one pass; unknown or still-deployed managed ownership must continue to refuse.
- Fail credential deletion during withdrawal or explicit release, then restart with a healthy backend. The pending work and warning must survive; passive status reads should make no new deletion attempts, and a newly redeployed managed owner must prevent draining.
- Give an Agent Plugin package a manifest symlink to harmless JSON outside the package, alongside an unrelated user package named by that JSON. The unrelated user must remain visible, while the package-basename reservation and valid contained-manifest controls remain intact.

- On macOS, select Seatbelt with a managed source. Both built-in and custom profiles must refuse before native sandbox preparation/launch with a Docker/Podman migration hint. A configured source that later disappears or is relinked must still refuse. Without a managed source, ordinary profiles must retain their existing startup and write boundaries.

- Release a withdrawn managed policy while a canonical or noncanonical same-name user package survives, including an unreadable manifest. Shared preferences/settings must remain. With no user ownership, all recorded spellings must be cleaned. A same-directory redeployment before commit must refuse release and preserve state.
- Lock a present native credential backend: adoption must refuse, release must report incomplete cleanup, and independent File-backed scopes must still be attempted. An absent optional native module must retain file-only support.
- Run passive ACP MCP status, explicit workspace MCP discovery and temporary source-copy after withdrawal. Managed policy fields and credentials must remain; source-copy must still persist target metadata, and ordinary runtime initialization must still complete hand-back.
- Construct an already-pinned configuration with an offline filesystem root. Unrelated literal paths remain separate, overlap refuses, managed reads receive no exemption and fresh CLI startup validation still rejects the unavailable root.

- Run legacy and queued V2 update checks with a retained managed policy and a deployed or withdrawn package. Both must report update states without hand-back; a later actual activation operation must still reconcile ownership.
- After proven withdrawal, changing activation with the configured root should survive later reads and refreshes. Without a provable source, a returning user copy with retained managed ownership must refuse the change. While the managed package is deployed, activation changes must preserve the pre-managed user baseline. Before hand-back, CLI User/Workspace columns should match Core's loaded view without rewriting policy or credentials.
- With a withdrawn managed package and a same-name user copy, inspect extension/MCP state, reconnect MCP, browse transcripts, and open/reload the Extensions dialog’s Installed and Sources tabs. Retained managed ownership and credentials must survive these reads; the returning user should show its preserved activation. Enable/disable, uninstall, scope-change and ordinary runtime refreshes must still perform their intended ownership reconciliation.
- Disable a name before a managed episode, then perform proven hand-back and a later user installation. Restored default/workspace and legacy-path preferences must survive without permitting replacement of an existing artifact.
- Try literal symlink-plus-dot-dot read requests and leaf links whose target contains that traversal. Permission checks and execution must agree; normal managed reads should work, while managed ownership alone must not authorize outside targets.

- Start the CLI or daemon with a fresh temporary home and a read-only extension collection. Contributions should load without install/link, package files should stay unchanged, and sessions in other workspaces should inherit the startup root.
- Disable/re-enable a managed package globally and per workspace. Upgrades and root relocation should preserve preferences; disabling a managed package must not activate its shadowed user copy. A scope change should retain late legacy rules when no earlier stash exists, while an existing pre-claim snapshot remains authoritative at hand-back.
- Use a child directory whose basename differs from the declared package name, then remove only its manifest. Retained ownership and secrets must survive and destructive release must refuse. A relocated or unrelated manifestless child also delays release: retain ownership and credentials until every unattributed child is removed or completed. An empty collection should permit proven withdrawal. Status reads and unrelated ACP setting writes should retain state until the intended release or runtime refresh.
- Record credentials under several case spellings, then withdraw the managed package. Cleanup and conflict probes should cover every recorded spelling, including intermediate names. A failed update or cleanup candidate must be reported without suppressing other successful results or cleanup attempts.
- After startup, relink the root or a parent to another directory, including packages with identical manifest size and mtime. No replacement package should load as managed, no read exemption should remain, and retained ownership must not be handed back. Restoring the original root should restore discovery; a missing root must still enforce writable-state separation.
- Supply reserved flags through SDK extra arguments, including `-=y`, `-=s=v` and `-=e`; both SDKs should reject them. Check permitted-spelling controls alongside the rejected variants. Full strict CLI parsing should separately reject the leading-equals vectors as `Unknown argument: =`; parser binding alone does not establish execution or approval-mode behavior.

- Start a container sandbox with managed packages under a writable parent such as `<QWEN_HOME>/prepared`. The settings and runtime directories should remain writable, while every supported mount alias of the managed child is covered read-only. An exact writable workspace collision and any strict-descendant writable overlay must refuse startup. A readonly descendant overlay must use the corresponding canonical deployed subtree; an unrelated or missing counterpart must refuse. Compatible readonly subtrees, source aliases and writable ancestors should remain supported.

- Install ZIP and tar.gz archives containing a malformed root `plugin.json` and one wrapped valid Qwen extension: installation should succeed and preserve the carried malformed file. A malformed-only archive should fail with the supported-manifest diagnostic; valid root-Qwen precedence and unsupported Agent Plugins schema diagnostics should remain unchanged. For an explicitly selected marketplace plugin, conversion should preserve unrecognized carried metadata in its copy without modifying the original source.

### Evidence (Before & After)

<!-- R37 managed probe evidence -->
R37 follow-up: admission and unknown-id lookup no longer materialize managed Agent Plugin runtime data or stdio working directories. Full discovery/validation and normal runtime creation remain; repeated scanning is unchanged. On final head [`547cf3cf9dfe`](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/commit/547cf3cf9dfed3ab5d1ac76c5f8604a2037916fc), fresh full-Core XML confirms 272/272 across eight affected files, and independent built-Core/source witnesses each pass the four original boundaries. Built CLI refusal is correct, but its legitimate full refresh creates data and cannot isolate the probe side effect. ## Risk & Scope

The process-start option authorizes the deployment-maintained source, including later versions. “Managed” denotes ownership, not Qwen authorship or an execution sandbox. Hosts should identify their provider; trust, safe/bare mode and tool permissions retain their distinct roles.

Seatbelt with a configured managed source is unsupported, including custom profiles; use `QWEN_SANDBOX=docker` or `QWEN_SANDBOX=podman`. The environment overrides `--sandbox`, and automatic macOS selection can choose Seatbelt. No backend fallback is automatic.

Generated sandbox mounts protect the managed destination subtree and require matching canonical provenance for readonly descendants; advanced `SANDBOX_FLAGS` overrides remain outside that contract. One direct-child collection and explicit refresh are supported; no public environment variable, watcher, marketplace, author-field schema or multi-root composition is added. Package deployment is not made atomic. Any unattributed manifestless child, including assets/staging, delays retained ownership release until removed or completed; a completely empty collection still proves absence. A returning user copy cannot accept activation writes while its retained managed ownership cannot be resolved. Stage complete packages outside the collection before publishing them. Known credential conflicts and unproven withdrawal continue to block destructive ownership changes. Workspace-secret coordinates are recorded before new writes; old unindexed credentials in unknown workspaces require explicit path hints. The inventory does not add cross-home keychain isolation or serialize settings writes with ownership changes; A present but unavailable native module cannot prove credential absence and blocks adoption. Cleanup attempts independent backends/scopes before reporting incomplete cleanup; unsuccessful post-transition cleanup remains durable and is retried by later mutating refreshes. Passive reads never drain it, and a current managed owner prevents deletion. An absent optional module supports file-only operation but cannot detect historical native values.

A lock-free local Skills view that needs recovery or identity migration is temporarily unavailable unless authoritative live/cached status exists; it does not immediately launch a child or perform a repair. Credential verification uses isolated file backends and controlled failures rather than a real OS keyring. Manifest evidence uses harmless static regular files and canonical read identity; dynamic retargeting, FIFO/device behavior and external deployment atomicity are not certified.

**R3-1 — pending human maintainer confirmation:** The proposed default is that an explicit same-name installation after proven withdrawal adopts retained managed-era activation/resource preferences. The name may belong to a different publisher, so this tradeoff still needs an explicit decision in [the review](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/12183#pullrequestreview-5347007520). It is not approved; separate opt-in remains the alternative. Existing ownership, artifact and detected-credential conflicts still block adoption.

**Release-note compatibility:** Qwen-format command hooks expand `${extensionPath}`, `${/}` and `${pathSeparator}` at load time for user-installed and managed extensions, alongside `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`. Other hook types are unaffected by this expansion.

**Deferred performance follow-up:** Name-filtered refresh still discovers and loads both sources before selecting names. That optimization remains deferred. The SDK reserved-argument guard remains conservative; full parser-grammar equivalence is not asserted, and a structural parser-runtime redesign remains deferred.

Optional policy and snapshot metadata preserves observed child directories, exact managed spellings and pending cleanup without changing the state version or credential service-name format. Older records learn directory evidence on successful discovery; already-lost associations or spellings cannot be reconstructed. Managed-era writes do not replace an existing pre-managed activation snapshot.

## 风险与范围

进程启动参数授权由部署方维护的来源，包括后续版本。“Managed”表示归属，不代表 Qwen 作者身份或执行沙箱。宿主应标明提供方；trust、safe/bare 模式和工具权限各自保留原有职责。

已配置 managed 来源与 Seatbelt（包括 custom profile）的组合不受支持；使用 `QWEN_SANDBOX=docker` 或 `QWEN_SANDBOX=podman`。该环境变量优先于 `--sandbox`，macOS 自动选择可能选中 Seatbelt；不会自动降级或切换后端。

生成的 sandbox 挂载保护 managed 目标子树，并要求只读子目录来源与规范化后的对应部署源一致；高级 `SANDBOX_FLAGS` 覆盖仍在该契约之外。支持一个直接子目录集合及显式刷新，不新增公开环境变量、watcher、商店、作者字段 schema 或多根目录组合。包部署不会因此成为原子操作。任何无法归属的无清单子目录（包括资源/staging）都会暂缓释放保留归属，需移除或补全后恢复；完全空的集合仍证明缺席。用户副本保留的 managed 归属无法确认时，不能接受启停写入。应在集合外暂存完整包后再发布。已知凭据冲突及尚未证实的撤回继续阻止销毁性归属变更。 新的工作区密钥写入前先记录位置；旧版未记录且位置未知的凭据仍需显式路径提示。索引不新增跨 home 的 keychain 隔离，也不将设置写入与归属变更串行化，原生模块可加载而后端不可用时无法证明凭据缺席，会阻止接管。清理继续尝试独立后端及范围，再报告未完成；归属转换后未完成的清理持久保留，并由后续可写刷新重试。被动读取不清理，当前 managed 归属阻止删除。缺少可选模块时支持文件后端，但无法检测历史原生值。

无锁本地 Skills 视图需要恢复或身份迁移时，如果没有权威实时/缓存状态，会暂时不可用；不会立即启动子进程或修复。凭据验证使用隔离文件后端及可控错误，没有验证真实 OS keyring。清单证据使用无害静态普通文件及规范读取身份，不声称动态换链、FIFO/设备或外部部署原子性已验证。

**R3-1 — 待人工维护者确认：** 提议的默认行为是：确认撤回后显式安装同名包时，接管保留的 managed 期间启用/资源偏好。相同名称可能属于不同发布方，因此这一取舍仍需在[审查中](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/12183#pullrequestreview-5347007520)明确决定；它尚未获批，单独 opt-in 仍是备选。既有归属、文件及检测到的凭据冲突仍会阻止接管。

**发布说明兼容性：** Qwen 格式命令 hook 在加载时为用户安装及 managed 扩展展开 `${extensionPath}`、`${/}`、`${pathSeparator}`，与 `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` 一并处理。其他 hook 类型不受此展开影响。

**延后性能跟进：** 按名称筛选的刷新仍会先发现并加载两个来源，再选择名称；该优化继续延后。SDK 保留参数守卫仍采取保守策略，不声称完整解析文法等价，结构性的解析器运行时重构继续延后。

可选策略及 snapshot 元数据保存观察到的子目录、managed 精确拼写和待清理记录，不改变状态版本或凭据服务名格式。旧记录在成功发现时学习目录证据，已丢失的关联或拼写无法重建。managed 期间的写入不会替换已有的 managed 之前启用状态快照。

设计及验收标准：[English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/managed-extension-directory/docs/design/managed-extension-directory.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/managed-extension-directory/docs/design/managed-extension-directory.zh-CN.md)。

#12147。独立 skill 刷新前置修复已在 #12182 合并。

prs.title: fix(cli): report terminal model errors in headless JSON output
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Treats terminal model error events as failures in every headless output format. JSON and stream-json now use the existing failure result path instead of falling through to success, and pending tools from the failed turn are not executed. Notification cleanup propagates its rejected promise correctly, and SDK monitor turns avoid emitting a second terminal result when the runner already emitted one.

## Why it's needed

An Anthropic-compatible HTTP 200 SSE response containing invalid_request_error currently prints the provider error but exits 0 with subtype=success and is_error=false in structured output. Automation therefore treats a failed model request as a successful run. This is the same underlying output-format gate described for OpenAI in #8920; the fix is provider-independent and separate from SSE rate-limit retry changes.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Serve the deterministic Anthropic SSE error in #11217 from a localhost endpoint with a dummy key. Run a one-shot prompt using text, json, and stream-json output. Each error scenario should exit nonzero; each structured format should emit exactly one terminal error result retaining the provider message. Return a valid success stream and confirm success remains unchanged. In both main and notification-drain turns, a tool request followed by a terminal error must not execute. An SDK monitor failure should emit one result whether the runner reported the error before throwing or failed before it could report.

### Evidence (Before & After)

- Before: built CLI text errors exit 1; JSON and stream-json errors exit 0 with a success result. All three success controls exit 0. Four structured-output unit regressions fail; the SDK monitor regression reproduces a duplicate result.
- After: built CLI errors exit 1 in all three formats; JSON and stream-json emit exactly one error_during_execution result with is_error=true. All three successful-response controls still exit 0. Every scenario makes one localhost request.
- Automated validation: 428 tests passed, one existing test skipped, with unhandled errors explicitly treated as failures. Full build, bundle, repository typecheck, changed-file ESLint, Prettier and diff checks are recorded in the verification comment.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :---: | :---: |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ tested |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ not tested |

### Environment (optional)

macOS 27.0 arm64, Node.js v24.18.0, Qwen Code 0.23.0, Anthropic SDK 0.36.3. Built CLI with isolated configuration, localhost mock endpoint and dummy credentials; no live model calls.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: consumers that previously accepted false-success results now receive an error result and a nonzero one-shot exit. Existing text formatting and successful results are preserved.
- Not validated / out of scope: Windows/Linux runtime, live-provider behavior, and changing the lifetime or aggregate process-exit policy of long-lived SDK sessions. Such sessions retain their existing continuation behavior while reporting each failed turn once. Rate-limit recognition belongs to #11216.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: no configuration or schema migration; this corrects the existing error-result contract.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #11217. Related to #8920. Independent of #11216.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 此 PR 的改动

让所有 headless 输出格式都把模型终止错误作为失败处理。JSON 和 stream-json 改走现有失败结果路径，不再进入成功分支，失败轮次中待处理的工具也不会执行。通知清理正确传播被拒绝的 Promise；如果运行器已经输出结果，SDK monitor 轮次不会再重复输出终结结果。

## 为什么需要

Anthropic 兼容接口在 HTTP 200 SSE 中返回 invalid_request_error 时，结构化输出目前会打印服务商错误，却以退出码 0、subtype=success 和 is_error=false 结束，导致自动化把失败的模型请求当成成功。这与 #8920 报告的 OpenAI 问题来自同一个输出格式判断条件；修复不依赖具体服务商，也与 SSE 限流重试改动独立。

## Reviewer Test Plan

### 如何验证

使用 localhost 接口和假 key 返回 #11217 中的确定性 Anthropic SSE 错误。分别使用 text、json 和 stream-json 运行单次提示词：错误场景均应以非零码退出，结构化格式均应只输出一个保留服务商原始消息的终结错误结果。再返回合法成功流，确认成功行为不变。在主请求和通知处理轮次中，工具请求后若出现终止错误，不应执行该工具。SDK monitor 失败时，无论运行器在抛错前已报告错误，还是在报告前就失败，都应只产生一个结果。

### 修复前后证据

- 修复前：打包 CLI 的 text 错误退出码为 1；JSON 和 stream-json 错误退出码为 0，并输出成功结果。三个成功对照均退出 0。四个结构化输出回归测试失败；SDK monitor 回归复现了重复结果。
- 修复后：打包 CLI 在三种格式中遇错均退出 1；JSON 和 stream-json 恰好输出一个 error_during_execution、is_error=true 的结果。三个成功响应对照仍退出 0，每个场景仅发送一次 localhost 请求。
- 自动化验证：428 项测试通过，一个已有测试跳过，明确将未处理异常视为失败。完整构建、打包、仓库类型检查、改动文件 ESLint、Prettier 和 diff 检查结果记录在验证评论中。

### 测试平台

| OS | 状态 |
| :---: | :---: |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ 已测试 |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 未测试 |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ 未测试 |

### 环境

macOS 27.0 arm64、Node.js v24.18.0、Qwen Code 0.23.0、Anthropic SDK 0.36.3。使用隔离配置、localhost 模拟接口和假凭据运行打包 CLI，未调用真实模型。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：过去接受错误成功结果的调用方，现在会收到错误结果和单次运行的非零退出码。原有文本格式与成功结果保持不变。
- 未验证或不在范围内：Windows/Linux 运行、真实服务商行为，以及常驻 SDK 会话的存活周期和整体进程退出策略。此类会话保留原有继续处理行为，同时每个失败轮次只报告一次。限流识别由 #11216 处理。
- 破坏性变更或迁移：无需配置或 schema 迁移；这是对既有错误结果契约的修正。

## 关联 Issue

修复 #11217，关联 #8920，与 #11216 独立。

</details>

prs.title: feat: add hybrid code mode
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds a Codex-aligned `tools.mode` enum with `direct`, `code_mode`, and `code_mode_only`. `code_mode` keeps ordinary tools directly callable while also exposing the isolated `exec` JavaScript tool; each visible ordinary tool carries its nested JavaScript declaration, while `exec` retains compact `ALL_TOOLS` metadata. `code_mode_only` preserves the strict exec-only ordinary-tool surface, and `direct` remains the default.

Updates filtered subagent tool surfaces so direct declarations and nested exec bindings honor the same allowlists, exposes the enum in Settings as Default / Code Mode / Code Mode Only, regenerates the settings JSON schema, and removes the former `tools.codeModeOnly` boolean setting entirely.

Adds synchronized [English](docs/design/code-mode.md) and [Chinese](docs/design/code-mode.zh-CN.md) design documents, and brings the existing CodeModeOnly design up to the repository's bilingual documentation standard ([English](docs/design/code-mode-only.md), [Chinese](docs/design/code-mode-only.zh-CN.md)).

## Why it's needed

Qwen Code previously offered only the default direct tool surface or the strict CodeModeOnly surface. Models could not combine direct calls for simple operations with `exec` orchestration for multi-tool workflows. A three-value enum matches Codex's `ToolMode` naming and gives users one explicit setting for all supported exposure modes.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Leave `tools.mode` unset or set it to `direct`, restart Qwen Code, and confirm ordinary tools remain available while `exec` is absent.
2. Set `tools.mode` to `code_mode`, restart, and confirm both ordinary tools and `exec` are available. Confirm ordinary tool descriptions include their `tools.<name>(args)` declaration and deferred tools remain discoverable through `tool_search`.
3. Set `tools.mode` to `code_mode_only`, restart, and confirm ordinary tools are available through `exec` rather than as top-level calls, while direct control tools remain available.
4. Open Settings and confirm Tool Mode cycles among Default, Code Mode, and Code Mode Only. Confirm `tools.codeModeOnly` is no longer present in the settings schema.
5. Start with `--safe-mode` or `--bare` while either code mode is configured and confirm the effective mode is `direct`.

Automated verification completed: focused Core tests (121 tests), focused CLI tests (585 tests), a repeated settings-schema regression run (60 tests), full build, full typecheck, full lint, and both installed and branch-built CLI version smoke checks.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: Settings exposed `Code Mode Only (Experimental)` as a boolean with `false` / `true`.

After: Settings exposes `Tool Mode (Experimental)` as an enum displaying Default / Code Mode / Code Mode Only. Updated TUI snapshots cover the default display.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

macOS, Node.js v24.18.0; local source build and package-level Vitest suites.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: Hybrid mode adds a short nested-call declaration to each ordinary tool description, increasing prompt size slightly; complete schemas are not duplicated in the `exec` description.
- Not validated / out of scope: Live-provider interactive runs and Windows/Linux local execution were not tested; CI covers supported platforms.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: `tools.codeModeOnly` is removed. Replace `{ "tools": { "codeModeOnly": true } }` with `{ "tools": { "mode": "code_mode_only" } }`.

## Linked Issues

Related to #10377.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

新增与 Codex 对齐的 `tools.mode` 枚举，支持 `direct`、`code_mode` 和 `code_mode_only`。`code_mode` 在保留普通工具直接调用能力的同时提供隔离的 `exec` JavaScript 工具；每个可见普通工具会携带自己的嵌套 JavaScript 声明，而 `exec` 保留精简的 `ALL_TOOLS` 元数据。`code_mode_only` 保持严格的普通工具仅经 `exec` 调用模式，`direct` 仍为默认值。

更新经过过滤的子智能体工具面，使直接声明和 `exec` 嵌套 binding 遵守同一组 allowlist；在设置界面中将该枚举显示为 Default / Code Mode / Code Mode Only；重新生成 settings JSON schema；并彻底移除原来的 `tools.codeModeOnly` 布尔设置。

新增同步的[英文](docs/design/code-mode.md)和[中文](docs/design/code-mode.zh-CN.md)设计文档，并将现有 CodeModeOnly 设计补齐为仓库要求的双语文档（[英文](docs/design/code-mode-only.md)、[中文](docs/design/code-mode-only.zh-CN.md)）。

## 为什么需要

Qwen Code 此前只提供默认的直接工具面或严格的 CodeModeOnly 工具面。模型无法在简单操作中使用直接调用，同时在多工具工作流中使用 `exec` 编排。三值枚举与 Codex 的 `ToolMode` 命名一致，并为所有支持的暴露模式提供一个明确的统一设置项。

## Reviewer 测试计划

### 如何验证

1. 不设置 `tools.mode` 或将其设为 `direct`，重启 Qwen Code，确认普通工具仍可用且不存在 `exec`。
2. 将 `tools.mode` 设为 `code_mode` 并重启，确认普通工具和 `exec` 同时可用；确认普通工具描述包含各自的 `tools.<name>(args)` 声明，延迟工具仍可通过 `tool_search` 发现。
3. 将 `tools.mode` 设为 `code_mode_only` 并重启，确认普通工具通过 `exec` 而不是顶层调用使用，同时直接控制工具仍然可用。
4. 打开设置界面，确认 Tool Mode 可在 Default、Code Mode 和 Code Mode Only 之间切换，并确认 settings schema 中不再存在 `tools.codeModeOnly`。
5. 配置任一 code mode 后用 `--safe-mode` 或 `--bare` 启动，确认有效模式为 `direct`。

已完成自动化验证：Core 相关测试（121 个）、CLI 相关测试（585 个）、再次运行的 settings schema 回归测试（60 个）、完整 build、完整 typecheck、完整 lint，以及已安装版本和分支构建版本的 CLI 版本 smoke 检查。

### 前后对比证据

之前：设置界面以 `false` / `true` 布尔值展示 `Code Mode Only (Experimental)`。

之后：设置界面以枚举展示 `Tool Mode (Experimental)`，可选 Default / Code Mode / Code Mode Only。更新后的 TUI snapshot 覆盖默认显示。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ✅  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ⚠️  |

### 环境（可选）

macOS、Node.js v24.18.0；本地源码构建和 package 级 Vitest 测试套件。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：混合模式会在每个普通工具描述中增加一段简短的嵌套调用声明，使 prompt 略微增大；完整 schema 不会在 `exec` 描述中重复。
- 未验证 / 范围外：未进行真实 provider 的交互式运行，也未在 Windows/Linux 本地执行；支持平台由 CI 覆盖。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：`tools.codeModeOnly` 已移除。请将 `{ "tools": { "codeModeOnly": true } }` 替换为 `{ "tools": { "mode": "code_mode_only" } }`。

## 关联 Issue

关联 #10377。

</details>

prs.title: feat(web-shell): Reuse standard UI for Managed Agents
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Managed Agent creation and conversations reuse the standard Web Shell welcome page, composer, message layout and native Workspace/model controls. Java Workspace creation admits the Session and first input in one existing API request, while response-loss retries preserve the chosen AgentDefinition, Workspace, directory, input and idempotency key. Existing Sessions retain their binding and model identity, and the shared composer clears only the owning draft after admission.

## Why it's needed

The separate Managed forms make users relearn basic chat interaction and obscure Workspace/model selection. Reusing the established UI provides a consistent creation and conversation flow while keeping Java authorization, pinned AgentDefinitions, approvals, cwd changes, cancellation and tool results authoritative. The standalone component also supplies the standard scoped frame/theme variables, so its composer has usable width without host-specific CSS setup.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

With a Java deployment that already authorizes Workspaces, enable Workspace binding and supply host-published model presets. Open a new task, explicitly select a Workspace and model, optionally choose a relative directory, then send the first input. Confirm one bound Session/initial Turn is admitted, no extra input submit occurs, and the selected identity appears in the conversation. Choosing another model or Workspace requires a new Session.

Simulate a lost creation response and reload: retry must preserve the original payload and key. Once the Session identity is accepted, a failed read-back retry must only reread it. Confirm successful admission clears its owning draft, including after switching A → B → A following a lost response, and a retained request for another Session does not erase the current draft. Retrying A from the B view, including after a reload, must also clear the admitted A draft before returning to A. Check text with leading/trailing spaces and confirm a newer different saved draft survives. Retrying an accepted input must leave the current editor empty; pressing Enter then must not create another submission. Bang/question-mark text stays literal; daemon Shell, attachments and slash commands are unavailable in Managed.

After a lost first-input creation response, confirm Abandon warns that the Session/input may already be running and that a new send can repeat effects. Abandon preserves the draft and refreshes the Session list without cancelling or creating another Session; recovery controls must not appear while the request is still in flight. Empty-only providers keep their empty-Session warning.

Check desktop and narrow layouts, the standalone component, and a long conversation inside ordinary Web Shell. The composer, progress and cancel controls must remain visible; cancellation must settle before continuation. Ordinary Web Shell keeps its existing composer defaults, and empty-only providers retain their previous creation contract.

Local validation passed: 491 focused Vitest cases across eight files plus 28 build-artifact cases, nine Chromium browser cases with deterministic Java transport, repository build/typecheck/bundle, changed-file ESLint/Prettier and two self-audit passes. The independent browser report and source review are posted separately. Browser transport evidence is mocked; historical demo Java/model runs are not counted as exact-head verification.

Before: separate Workspace creation form and conversation textarea from main e9789d091133d9753decfc139df64c935a1866e6. prs.title: fix(web-shell): bound pending edit diffs to nearby context
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Pending and in-progress whole-file edit previews show each change with up to three surrounding lines and file-relative hunk coordinates. Common file ends are trimmed before comparing. Oversized previews explicitly report omission; LF and CRLF final-newline-only edits show a localized notice. Replacement-fragment arguments retain their headerless preview, and supplied patches and completed previews retain their existing behavior.

Diff previews visibly mark invisible characters instead of rendering them as indistinguishable source text. Both raw patches and full-content artifact views use the same visible escapes; the underlying CodeMirror document retains its original bytes. Call details apply their 4,000-character content limit after escaping. Uniform CRLF previews remain clean when their final line is unterminated, while actual ending conversions remain visible.

## Why it's needed

A one-line edit near line 100 of a 200-line file previously rendered 201 rows. Whole-file previews now render nine rows with correct coordinates. This keeps approval readable without changing the permission protocol or tool execution.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- Edit line 100 of a 200-line file: the approval dialog and pending/in-progress whole-file card should show lines 97–103 and +1/-1.
- Supply replacement fragments through the edit tool's real arguments: expect the existing headerless preview, without a claim about the fragment's file offset.
- Check a large insertion and distant edits that exceed the preview budget: expect an omitted notice rather than a fabricated whole-file rewrite.
- Add or remove only the final LF or CRLF terminator: expect the localized notice and no +1/-1 badge. Adding/removing a sole blank line and converting LF to CRLF remain real content changes.
- Review a CRLF file without a final newline: a content edit should not add terminator noise.
- Compare real invisible characters with literal escape text and mixed full-content/raw-patch artifact entries: only real characters receive a visible decoration, with matching display in both renderers. CodeMirror retains the original document.
- Expand a call whose escaped output exceeds 4,000 characters: content remains within the bound and a truncation notice appears. Embedded notice-like patch rows remain literal.
- Check supplied patches, completed previews and failed calls: preserve their existing behavior.

### Evidence (Before & After)

The five round-5 review findings were reproduced at the exact reviewed head `e6e31c40`: seven independent component witnesses failed before the fix and passed afterwards. Six deliberate fix reversions each fail their corresponding regression.

On 2026-10-13 the branch was synchronized with upstream main `6373fc4e` in signed merge commit `e1b302e4`. The only textual conflict was the transcript bundle budget; the upstream Excel preview assertions and all round-5 fixes are retained. The transcript JS remainder measures 1,332,856 UTF-16 units, below the existing PR ceiling of 1,336,000. No additional budget increase was needed.

Frozen-lockfile installation, the complete workspace build and CLI bundle, Web Shell TypeScript, related ESLint, and the normal staged-file Prettier/ESLint commit hook pass. The six focused rendering/diff suites pass 426 tests, and the build-artifact suite passes all 30 tests.

The full Web Shell unit run reports 11,520 passed, 83 failed, and three unhandled errors. Failures were confined to the session-provider suite (82) and the settings-route development-server test (one, default 5-second timeout). A separate run of those exact files at the default timeout passes all 420 session-provider tests and 20 of the 21 settings-route tests. A further settings-file run with a command-line 15-second ceiling passes all 21 tests; no repository timeout configuration was changed. The session-provider source, its tests and the settings test are identical to upstream main. An exact-main runtime failure is not claimed, and the complete default-timeout suite is not reported green. Whole-workspace tests and live daemon/model/native Desktop E2E were not run in this synchronization.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :--: | :-- |
| Windows | Actual React/CodeMirror jsdom regressions, package build and static checks; full unit result disclosed above |
| macOS | Not tested locally |
| Linux | Awaiting upstream CI |

### Environment (optional)

Windows, Node.js 24.20.0, pnpm workspace dependencies and Vitest/jsdom. The workspace CLI was built and bundled during frozen-lockfile installation. No live daemon, live model or native Desktop E2E is claimed.

## Risk & Scope

Compact whole-file previews omit distant unchanged lines; oversized input yields an explicit omitted notice. Invisible characters are represented visibly, so displayed escapes differ from the underlying bytes. Already escaped adapter text stays literal because its original character provenance is unavailable. No permission protocol, tool execution or core-package changes; no dependency changes beyond upstream main synchronization. The current-head CI requires maintainer authorization.

AI assistance: implemented and verified with AI coding assistants, including OpenAI Codex.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #13766

prs.title: feat(managed-agent): H4 workflow child runtime
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Issue #13803 (stage H of the Managed Agent proposal #12380) delivers the managed workflow child runtime — the "Workflow runtime" follow-up the H4c design deferred. A managed Session can now launch a `workflow` child through a new Workflow tool declaration that mirrors the Agent tool's admission: inline deterministic workflow source, bounded structured args, foreground or background. The control plane's child result relay discovers the pending launch and creates exactly one child Session under retry, at the parent's precise Workspace binding, with lineage stamped in one transaction; the child's first Turn runs the workflow deterministically in-process (node:vm sandbox, in-process AgentHeadless subagents under ordinary per-run caps — not nested managed grandchildren), and its settled result flows back through the relay, acceptance, and consumption pipeline unchanged. Closing a parent cancels its non-terminal workflow children through the same funnel as child agents. Every launch pins its definition from revision 1 — the sha256 of the exact script bytes — and the child re-verifies the digest before spending anything, so a tampered copy can never execute.

This slice required one change outside the managed surface: a workflow launch block is the first prompt ever to carry fractional `args` across the daemon's `sha256(JSON.stringify(prompt))` admission digest, and the SDK's fastjson2 substrate renders fractional numbers in Java's scientific form where ECMAScript uses plain notation, so any fractional arg would wedge the child's first Turn with a deterministic `invalid_hosted_prompt`. The SDK's JSON digest substrate is now canonicalized to byte-fidelity with `JSON.stringify`, pinned by golden vectors derived from Node.

No Flyway migration, no OpenAPI or contract change, no legacy Workflow tool behavior change (managed admission is a separate declaration, inline-source only; saved/referenced workflows, script-level resume, and nested managed grandchildren are explicitly deferred).

## Why it's needed

The kind gate on `managed-child_run` fires on every revision commitment, so the four issue exit checks can only land together: widening the relay/cascade queries (K2) without lifting the gate (K4) would make every relay verb on a workflow row answer 409, while lifting the gate without widening the queries would leave workflow runs invisible to exactly the machinery that creates, settles, and cancels them — the isolation failure the issue forbids. With this slice the managed Agent and Workflow tools share the full child Session pipeline instead of the Workflow tool existing only outside the managed runtime.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Unit and integration: all suites touched by the change are green — core `managed-runtime` suites (290/290 in the five changed files; full suite green except one pre-existing timer flake that also fails on main), CLI serve suites including the new funnel/witness files (420/420 across the six workflow-adjacent files; full `hosted-harness-session` green at 344 tests), `managed-agent-server` surefire (all 71 tests in the five touched classes green; the only module failure is a pre-existing environment-dependent worktree-git test that fails identically on main), `qwencode` suite green including the new golden-vector digest tests. A physical acceptance run in the shape of #13532 drove the packaged stack (managed-agent-server + MariaDB + bundled daemon) on a real host: a foreground workflow launch completed end to end with exactly one child Session under retry; a background launch delivered and consumed its notification; a store-tampered pin refused execution with `Workflow launch pin does not match its script`; the packaged build admits workflow records by construction while a baseline build refuses the same commits. Parent-close cancellation of a workflow child is recorded blocked-with-reason (this macOS host cannot admit workspace close — capability refusal, re-confirmed on the final tree), and the mid-interruption re-claim behavior is partially observed with the boundary finding filed as issue #13838. The full behavior table with commands and outputs is in a follow-up comment.

Mutation discipline per project convention: every new guard was individually disabled and its named witness went red (digest encoder, kind gate, route gate, wake and close-drain predicates, batch exclusion, key derivation).

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A (no user-visible surface; the managed workflow tool is declared only on private Hosted profiles — production enablement is its own gated follow-up)

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   N/A  |
|  🐧 Linux  |   N/A  |

(Windows and Linux not exercised locally; the acceptance run notes a Linux re-run belongs to the production-enablement slice, as #13532 recorded for H3.)

### Environment (optional)

Unit/integration: `npm run build` + vitest per package; `mvn test` under JDK 21. Acceptance: packaged `dist/cli.js` daemon + built `managed-agent-server` jar + fresh MariaDB instance, driven by `.qwen/scripts/workflow-child-acceptance.mjs`.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the managed Workflow tool admits inline script source only for v1 — saved workflows, `scriptPath`, `resumeFromRunId`, and `sourceRef` refuse with a named follow-up error rather than executing, keeping the launch pin honest (the digest binds the exact bytes that run). A script's `agent()` calls run in-process inside the workflow child under ordinary caps and are not managed grandchild Sessions.
- Not validated / out of scope: workspace-close cancellation of a workflow child is blocked on this macOS host's capability refusal (verified blocked-with-reason, Linux re-run deferred to the production-enablement slice); the relay's mid-interruption re-claim settles the run once but the restarted connector's load re-attachment answers 409 on non-durable host profiles (filed as issue #13838); Windows unexercised.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none — no schema migration, no public contract change; production AgentBundle enablement is not part of this slice.
