issues.body:
<!-- status-at-0.10.1 -->
> **Status at 0.10.1** (re-triaged 2026-10-08): partly done. Filed against 0.9.13 (filed 2026-09-14); idle-PTY sub-report reproduced against 0.10.0.
>
> **What remains**
> - Input attribution: add user-vs-agent origin to stdin/input on crates/tui/src/runtime_api/jobs.rs and runtime_api/terminal.rs, with permissions still enforced
> - Restart-safe identity: land the keyed job creation and Lost/Unknown projection claimed on 2026-10-07 (runtime_api/jobs.rs, runtime_threads.rs, runtime_api.rs), coordinated with #6556
> - Windows: make /v1/terminal/* exist on Windows via ConPTY and qualify PTY jobs there (terminal.rs is cfg(unix) end to end)
> - Readiness field (accepting input vs blocked) and a long-poll wake for /v1/terminal/{name}/output; one fixture proving bytes + input + resize + exit
>
> **Checked in the 0.10.1 source**
> - Terminal byte routes exist at v0.10.1: /v1/terminal/{name}/output, /input, /resize, /kill at crates/tui/src/runtime_api.rs:2263-2269, owned by tools::terminal_session (runtime_api/terminal.rs:1-8)
> - Client job routes exist at v0.10.1: POST/GET /v1/threads/{id}/jobs plus /output, /stdin, /kill, /resize at crates/tui/src/runtime_api.rs:2379-2397; documented at docs/RUNTIME_API.md:1809-1844
> - Bounded cursor read is served: cursor/next_cursor/offset/exit_code in crates/tui/src/runtime_api/jobs.rs:386-415, non-consuming multi-client reads (:420-422)
> - Idle-PTY liveness regression from 0.10.0 is fixed in v0.10.1: commit 14792c3a6e (PR #6716, merge 1cdec0f81e) is an ancestor of v0.10.1 and not of v0.10.0; crates/tui/src/tools/shell.rs:1714-1720 exempts jobs with terminal_size from STALE_NO_OUTPUT_AFTER
> - Windows/ConPTY not done for the terminal routes: crates/tui/src/runtime_api/terminal.rs 'Known limitations' says 'Unix only ... on Windows these routes do not exist yet. ConPTY qualification is its own slice'
> - Reconnect across Engine restart not done: terminal.rs limitations say live sessions only, a restarted Engine reports no session; no long poll and no scrollback recovery either

---

GPUI needs a Codewhale-owned interactive terminal, not a second PTY in the desktop. Opened from [Hmbown/codewhale-platform#565](<https://github.com/Hmbown/codewhale-platform/issues/565>) so the native pane ([Hmbown/codewhale-platform#566](<https://github.com/Hmbown/codewhale-platform/issues/566>)) is not blocked on a comment.

Do not start this if a live issue already covers the HTTP terminal session. Reconcile `crates/tui/src/runtime_api.rs` and `crates/tui/src/tools/terminal_session.rs` against today's tip first.

## Serve

1. Stable session id that survives the client window closing; reconnect is the same process or a truthful loss (never a silent new shell).
2. Authenticated raw byte read with a bounded cursor (replay/window). Shell-tool text is not this.
3. Authenticated input with user vs agent attribution; sandbox/permissions stay enforced.
4. Resize (cols/rows) with a receipt.
5. Readiness: will accept input vs blocked.
6. Exit status + cleanup receipt; no orphaned store lock.
7. Native Windows ConPTY (Unix-only portable-pty is not acceptance).

## Reply with

Claimed files and routes, what exists vs what you will add, ConPTY status, and the smallest fixture that proves bytes + input + resize + exit.

GPUI will show “Not available from this Codewhale” plus the real route name until those routes exist. No second shell owner in the desktop.

### 2026-09-28 idle PTY liveness fix claim — Codex

Reproduced against released 0.10.0: a live client-owned PTY idle for more than 60 seconds reports status=Running, stdin_available=true, stale=true, tty=null, with terminal_size retained. This makes reconnect inventory treat a live shell as unavailable and the resize route reject it as no longer running. Source root cause: BackgroundShell::job_snapshot applies STALE_NO_OUTPUT_AFTER to interactive PTYs waiting for input. Claim exact Core paths crates/tui/src/tools/shell.rs and crates/tui/src/tools/shell/tests.rs in the existing clean checkout from b36a34774. Exclude owned PTYs from the no-output staleness heuristic; preserve real process-exit and historical stale records, and non-PTY silent-job behavior. Reuse existing PTY resize/input/exit regression with an aged output clock. No transport, permission, storage or release changes. Per-OS/ConPTY qualification remains open.

### 2026-09-29 remote handoff

Saved the idle-owned-PTY repair to branch fix/idle-terminal-liveness, commit 14792c3a6e, draft PR [Hmbown/Codewhale#6716](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/6716>). Exact source scope: crates/tui/src/tools/shell.rs and crates/tui/src/tools/shell/tests.rs. Required npm test && npm run check:web passed: 68 package, 16 runtime SDK, 50 extension-host and 502 web tests (636 passed / 0 failed); type/lint/build, formatting and diff checks passed. Released 0.10.0 reproduced the 65-second idle failure. The first focused Rust compilation was interrupted without a result; a resumed five-filter run is still compiling at handoff. No Rust pass, updated Engine runtime result, release or Windows/ConPTY qualification is claimed. Keep draft unmerged until relevant Rust checks and exact-head CI pass. Full targeted command is in the PR body. Broader issue acceptance remains open.

### 2026-09-29 focused Rust verification of [Hmbown/Codewhale#6716](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/6716>) — Claude (app stabilization session)

Exact head `14792c3a6eeede15d4248b41b244747d463de496`, Linux x86_64 cloud container, rustc 1.94.1 (the Core `stable` toolchain present there): `cargo test --locked -p codewhale-tui --lib -- tools::shell::tests::pty_resize_updates_live_terminal_and_rejects_finished_or_pipe_jobs tools::shell::tests::running_job_snapshot_marks_no_output_stale_after_threshold tools::shell::tests::test_job_list_poll_cancel_and_stale_snapshot --exact` → **3 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored, 13,804 filtered out**. That covers the extended real-PTY regression (the idle PTY stays non-stale, then resize/input) and both existing stale-job tests (silent non-PTY jobs still go stale). The first attempt was OOM-killed while the app built alongside it; this re-run is a clean, isolated result. Not claimed: the other two filters from the PR body, a revert-to-fail negative control, exact-head GitHub CI (none is reported on the draft), a candidate Engine runtime probe, macOS, or Windows/ConPTY. This session cannot push to Hmbown/Codewhale, so the PR body is unchanged. The app pin stays at 0.10.0 until a released Engine contains the fix.2026-10-07 Codex desktop /root claims the bounded canonical Jobs creation/recovery slice, coordinated with codewhale-hq/Codewhale#6556 and the existing durability intake (no new issue). Existing checkout worktrees/cw-ts-extensions, wave/0.10.1-next, refreshed read head d7965090e37360da67fc4d98a029ab8066f32ddc. Exact proposed source ownership: crates/tui/src/runtime_api/jobs.rs, crates/tui/src/runtime_threads.rs, crates/tui/src/runtime_api.rs. A delegated artifact-only candidate is being reviewed; shared source has not been edited or built. It reuses the owning ShellManager, operation directory/claim locks and atomic store helpers: optional keyed creation with stable authenticated Master/device owner, exact workspace/current execution-scope/held-lease assertions, Reserved→Unknown durable before spawn, Accepted receipt with exact client job ID, passive lookup, changed-intent refusal, and Lost/Unknown projection after Engine restart. The same key may never silently spawn again after uncertainty or adopt an agent job. Turn startup cleanup must preserve the domain-separated job receipts. Legacy no-key behavior remains compatibility only; coordinated capability advertisement/native+web consumers are required before claiming end-to-end parity. Source-only brief and candidate receipt under CW/artifacts/setup-design-refinement-20261006; no runtime, Windows/ConPTY, provider, package, CI, installation or release proof yet. labels.description: CI, test harness and build infrastructure

issues.body:
Follow-up from #6953. v0.10.1 failed to start on Windows 10 1607: an unresolved load-time import of `DeriveCapabilitySidsFromName` gave 0xC0000139. 830b86fddd fixes that import, but nothing stops the next release from adding a load-time import that the oldest supported Windows lacks.

**Proposal.** During the release build, list the import table of each Windows binary (for example with `dumpbin /imports`, or a small PE parser on the hosted runner). Then check each imported function against the floor for the oldest supported build, Windows 10 1607. Fail the release dry run on any import above the floor that is not delay-loaded or resolved at run time.

## Done when

- A release-time check runs on the Windows artifacts and fails on an import above the floor.
- The floor is written down in the release docs.

Refs #6953

issues.title: Windows runtime floor blocks read-only piped commands under Full Access, on a native (non-npm) install

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: New external report awaiting maintainer triage; repro, logs and version output help

labels.name: windows
labels.description: Windows-specific behaviour

issues.body:
### Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. 我已搜索过现有 issue。

### What happened? 发生了什么？

## Summary

Follow-up to #6827. The Windows runtime floor (`SessionRuntimeRisk`, `crates/tui/src/core/authority/auto_review.rs`) refuses ordinary read-only commands that pipe test output, with `UnclassifiedWindowsInvocation`. It does this while the session shows **Full Access**, although the floor's own test says Full Access skips it.

Refused:

```
cd C:\Users\me\repo; .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests\runner -q --tb=line 2>&1 | Select-Object -Last 6
cd C:\Users\me\repo\apps\extension; node .\node_modules\vitest\vitest.mjs run 2>&1 | Select-Object -Last 30
cd C:\Users\me\repo; .\.venv\Scripts\ruff.exe format .; Write-Output "fmt=$LASTEXITCODE"; .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests\e2e --collect-only -q 2>&1 | Select-Object -Last 3
```

Every refusal reads:

> Built-in safety gate requires approval: Windows command input cannot be classified safely enough to exclude termination of Codewhale npm launchers; use a direct PID- or port-specific command.

The same commands without `2>&1 | Select-Object ...` run fine. None of them stops a process.

## Two problems

1. **Full Access does not skip the floor.** `windows_runtime_floor_holds_across_reviewing_postures_but_skips_full_access` (around line 2104) asserts that under `ApprovalMode::Bypass` "Full Access skips the platform hold with the rest of the floor". The TUI status bar shows `Full Access` and `operate`, and the operator and its Fleet sub-agents are still blocked. Either the operate/Fleet posture does not carry `Bypass` into tool review, or sub-agents get a different `ApprovalMode`.
2. **Unparseable means blocked, even for read-only pipelines.** When `command_invocations(command)` returns `None`, `windows_session_runtime_risk_scoped` returns `UnclassifiedWindowsInvocation` (around line 1371). A pipeline into a read-only cmdlet (`Select-Object`, `Select-String`, `Where-Object`, `Format-*`, `Out-String`, `Measure-Object`) with `2>&1` cannot terminate anything, but it is held. Agents use this pattern constantly to trim test output.

3. **The npm-launcher hold fires on a non-npm install.** This machine uses the native installer, so there is no `node.exe` launcher in Codewhale's process tree. Yet the hold's reason is "termination of Codewhale npm launchers". `windows_tool_runtime_risk` does not check the install method, so the floor applies to every Windows install. #6906 already detects npm installs with `codewhale_release::current_install_method()`, and the same check could scope this hold. (A broad `node.exe` kill could still hit *another* npm-launched session on the same machine. That is a narrower risk, and it does not apply to read-only pipelines either way.)

## Impact

In one Fleet run of about 70 minutes (DeepSeek V4 Flash, about 8 workers), one implement sub-agent had 12 refused or failed tool calls out of about 60. 4 were this gate; each refusal costs a model turn while the agent re-plans. The operator hit it repeatedly as well. It is avoidable: the agent can drop the pipe. But every model reaches for this pattern first, so it fails again and again.

## Expected

- Under Full Access, the floor does not apply, as the existing test asserts. Or, if the floor is meant to apply under Full Access in operate/Fleet mode, the test and the docs should say so.
- A pipeline whose stages are all known read-only cmdlets, with stream redirection like `2>&1`, is classified as non-terminating rather than unclassified.

### Steps to reproduce 复现步骤

1. Windows 11, Codewhale from the native Windows installer (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\CodeWhale\bin\codewhale.exe`, launched through `codewhale.bat`; **not** npm), started from PowerShell in Windows Terminal.
2. Select Full Access and run in operate mode, with Fleet sub-agents.
3. Have the agent run: `.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest -q 2>&1 | Select-Object -Last 5` (any command, piped into `Select-Object`).
4. It is refused with the message above. Without `2>&1 | Select-Object -Last 5`, it runs.

### Codewhale version 版本

codewhale 0.10.1 (fead51eeea0f)

### Where did it happen? 在哪里出现？

TUI (terminal interface)

### Operating system 操作系统

Windows

### How did you get Codewhale? 获取方式

GitHub Releases download (native Windows installer)

### Provider and model 提供商和模型

deepseek / deepseek-v4-flash

### Terminal and shell 终端

Windows Terminal + PowerShell 5.1

### codewhale doctor (optional)

_No response_

### Logs, screenshots, anything else (optional)

- Evidence: `.codewhale/state/subagents.v1.json`, worker events marked `refused or failed`, and checkpoint tool results carrying the safety-gate text.
- Related: #6827 (the original gate), #6906 (agent environment line for the npm launcher), #6011 (tool-call error diagnostics).
- I am happy to send a PR for part 2 (read-only pipeline classification) once the intended Full Access behaviour in part 1 is confirmed.

On a non-official endpoint (Custom excluded), `Off` now stays `Off`, and the catalog ladder still applies (the Grok gateway test keeps Medium).

prs.title: test(runtime): steer tests no longer require the two-second in-band receipt
prs.body:
## What and why

`steer_turn` waits `STEER_SETTLE_WAIT` (2 s) for the engine's verdict and otherwise answers with the `Queued` receipt, whose `steer_count` is still 0. Two tests assert `steer_count == 1` on that answer, so they fail whenever the settlement takes longer than 2 s. On windows-latest that has happened three times since 10-10, twice on main:

- https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/38026237501/job/114137638785 (main, 8aea0265c): `runtime_threads::tests::steer_turn_on_active_turn_records_item_and_event`
- https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/38182149299/job/114596847032 (a run for #6959, which doesn't touch steering): `runtime_api::tests::steer_and_interrupt_endpoints_work_on_active_turn`
- https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/38234571127/job/114762090391 (main, a395e3845): the same API test

```
assertion `left == right` failed
  left: 0
 right: 1
```

Both tests now take either receipt and wait for the settlement itself:

- the manager test waits for `turn.steered` and the steer's `item.completed`, then reads `steer_count` from the stored turn. It used to read the count from the terminal turn, which can be loaded before the settlement worker has written it.
- the API test waits for `turn.steered` before it sends the interrupt, then checks the stored count.

The waits use the bounds these files already have (`TURN_SETTLEMENT_DEADLOCK_TIMEOUT`, and `ci_scaled` 10 s like the test's own terminal wait). Nothing asserts the in-band `Accepted` receipt any more; I couldn't find a way to keep that without keeping the two-second race.

## Issue

Refs #6276

## How I tested it

- To take the `Queued` path on purpose I made one scratch build that reads the settle wait from an environment variable and keeps the two old tests next to the new ones. With the wait at 0, the old tests failed 5 of 5 each with the assertion above and the new ones passed 5 of 5 each. At the normal 2 s all four passed. None of that scratch code is in the diff.
- I could not make 2 s overrun on my machine with CPU load alone: 100 runs of the old tests next to 60 and then 400 busy loops all passed, so I can't show the Windows timing locally. Under the 400-loop load and with the wait at 0, the new tests passed 40 of 40.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui --all-targets --all-features` with CI's flags, and `cargo check -p codewhale-tui --all-targets`: clean. Clippy also on 1.99, plus `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui`.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui --lib`: 15242 passed, 44 failed, both steer tests among the passes. The same 44 fail on main (35b11285a) on my machine; most need an extension-host Node version I don't have.

No new tests; this changes two existing ones.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, rebased on current `main`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) — n/a

prs.title: test(subagent): widen three short approval bounds to 30 s
prs.body:
## What and why

`child_permission_gate::ask_without_a_durable_receipt_store_fails_closed_before_prompting` gives `registry.execute` 250 ms to refuse the call. On windows-latest it has overrun that four times since 10-11, three of them on main:

- https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/38123604545/job/114423296927 (main, 25cc4f7a4)
- https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/38146297151/job/114490352956 (the run for #6958, which doesn't touch subagent code)
- https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/38213790167/job/114693837196 (main, 2c550fa8c)
- https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/38234571127/job/114762090391 (main, a395e3845)

```
a missing receipt store must fail closed without waiting for a decision: Elapsed(())
```

#6698 moved this module's approval waits to one 30 s `CHILD_APPROVAL_EVENT_READINESS` after a loaded run overran the 2 s and 5 s ceilings. Three bounds in the module stayed on private values:

- the 250 ms one above,
- the 2 s wait for the prompt in `child_prompt_carries_agent_scoped_keys`,
- the 1 s wait for the wait-end event once the host drains.

The two event waits now use the shared ceiling. The 250 ms one waits for `registry.execute` to refuse the call and asserts that no event is sent, which is not what the constant's comment describes, so it keeps a bound of its own and that becomes 30 s. (The first commit put all three on the constant; the second takes this one back off.)

Each still ends as soon as the call returns or the event arrives, and still fails the test when it never does. Only the 250 ms bound has been seen to fail. The other two are the same shape, so I moved them in the same change.

## Issue

Refs #6698

## How I tested it

- To reproduce it locally I ran the test in a loop at the lowest priority next to 60 busy loops at the same priority. With the 250 ms bound, 48 of 80 runs failed with the `Elapsed(())` above. With the 30 s bound, none of 138 runs failed under the same load (80 on the first commit, 58 on the second). On an idle machine both pass.
- The three touched tests still finish in about 0.1 s each in a normal run; the ceiling only matters when something is stuck.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui --all-targets --all-features` with CI's flags, and `cargo check -p codewhale-tui --all-targets`: clean. Clippy also on 1.99, plus `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui`.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui --lib`: 15242 passed, 44 failed. The same 44 fail on main (35b11285a) on my machine; most need an extension-host Node version I don't have.

No new tests; this changes three bounds in existing ones.

- [x] One focused change, rebased on current `main`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) — n/a

## What and why

A slice of #5587. I took the `#![allow(dead_code)]` off five modules and let `cargo check -p codewhale-tui --all-targets` show what each one was covering:

- `worker_profile.rs`: nothing. The allow was stale.
- `model_profile.rs`: `FactProvenance::LegacyModelHeuristics` has had no constructor since 5cf09da77 moved `model_profile()` off `model_registry::lookup`, so it is deleted. Four predicates (`supports_image_input`, `has_large_context`, `prefers_full_tool_surface`, `suitable_for_broad_fleet_worker`) are only called from the module's tests and are now `#[cfg(test)]`.
- `tui/git_status.rs`: `chrome_label` and `chrome_ink` lost their last caller when 07a95e530 deleted the underwater header widget. Only their tests use them now, so `#[cfg(test)]`.
- `fleet/roster.rs`: `load_with_personal_dir` and `shadowed_for` are test seams. `#[cfg(test)]`.
- `fleet/task_spec.rs`: `record_verification_receipt` is only called from its test. `#[cfg(test)]`, along with the `FleetLedger` import.

None of these files has items that are only reached from `cfg(unix)` or `cfg(windows)` code, so Windows sees the same result as macOS. `llm_client/mock.rs` looked stale too but isn't: `tests/support` pulls it into the integration crate by `#[path]`, and that crate never uses `FauxStep::Error` or `push_error`. I left it alone.

issues.title: [Bug]: Windows git-source update fails in preflight-runtime-stage - candidate copy recursively expands extensions/*/node_modules/openclaw workspace symlink until EINVAL/path-length limits
issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

A git-source `openclaw update --yes` on Windows fails in `preflight-runtime-stage`: the candidate runtime copy recursively expands the pnpm workspace self-symlink `extensions/<id>/node_modules/openclaw` (which points back to the repository root) into real directories (`candidate\extensions\buzz\node_modules\openclaw\dist\extensions\buzz\node_modules\...`) until the path exceeds Windows limits, then aborts with `cp returned EINVAL`; the resulting deep tree also fails cleanup with "Filename too long".

### Steps to reproduce

1. Windows Server 2022 (10.0.20348), NTFS, git checkout of this repository at `36f5082c9` (v2026.9.9) with `pnpm install` (pnpm 12.5.1, Node 26.11.0) — the default workspace layout where 40 of 166 `extensions/*` have `node_modules\openclaw` as a symlink to the repo root (`LinkType=SymbolicLink, target=..\..\..`).
2. Stop the Gateway, run `openclaw update --yes` (git mode).
3. Update passes staging, git preflights, deps install, and all candidate validations (state snapshot, doctor, doctor lint, config, plugins, recovery, canary gateway startup), then enters `preflight-runtime-stage`.
4. After ~84 min of runtime staging the phase fails with the errors below.

### Expected behavior

The updater's candidate copy replicates (or skips and re-links) workspace symlinks/reparse points, the same way the local `runtime-postbuild` path does — the run-node wrapper's postbuild rebuilt the same checkout's runtime artifacts in ~77 s without expanding the self-links. The update should complete or fail with a bounded, clean error.

### Actual behavior

From the update console log (paths under the user profile redacted as `~`):

```text
validating — preflight-runtime-stage — still running (5010.07s)
  ✗ preflight-runtime-stage (5034.77s)
    Failing check preflight-runtime-stage (Error): Cannot copy an unknown file type: cp returned EINVAL
    (cannot copy an unknown file type: \\?\C:\openclaw\dist.openclaw-update-<uuid>.tmp\candidate\extensions\buzz\node_modules\openclaw\dist\extensions\buzz\node_modules\openclaw\dist\extensions\buzz\node_modules\openclaw\dist\extensions\buzz\...)
...
  ✗ preflight-cleanup (4.29s)
    Failing check preflight-cleanup (command-failed): error: failed to delete 'C:/ocu/ocu-pf-<id>/wt': Filename too long
    windows fallback cleanup removed preflight tree
Phases: requested (1.63s) → staging (91ms) → validating (8105.17s)
Failed: validating — Exit code: 1
```

The nested path in the EINVAL error shows the copy followed the self-referential symlink as a real directory instead of replicating the link. The source link itself (checked with PowerShell):

```text
C:\openclaw\extensions\buzz\node_modules\openclaw
attributes=Directory, ReparsePoint; linktype=SymbolicLink; target=..\..\..
```

After the failure the updater correctly leaves the managed Gateway stopped ("Managed gateway remains stopped because update recovery could not prove a runnable installation"), so the service stays down until the operator restarts it manually on the previous build.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.9 (git source checkout @ 36f5082c9, updating toward 2026.10.2 / origin/main)

### Operating system

Windows Server 2022 (10.0.20348), NTFS

### Install method

git source checkout served via Scheduled Task (`node C:\openclaw\dist\index.js gateway`); pnpm 12.5.1, Node 26.11.0

### Model

N/A — updater path, no model involved.

### Provider / routing chain

N/A — updater path, no model involved.

### Additional provider/model setup details

N/A

### Logs

Included in "Actual behavior" (redacted). Full failure artifacts were also saved by the updater under `~\.openclaw\logs\support\openclaw-update-failure-*.json` and `~\.openclaw\update-reports\<uuid>.md`.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

- `extensions/buzz/node_modules/openclaw` → repo root: `LinkType=SymbolicLink, target=..\..\..`
- 40 of 166 `extensions/*` in this checkout carry the same `node_modules\openclaw` self-link (default `pnpm install` workspace layout, not hand-made).
- The local `runtime-postbuild` executed by `scripts/run-node.mjs` on the same checkout completes in ~77 s and does not expand the self-links, which isolates the recursive expansion to the updater's candidate copy step.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: Windows git-source installs using the standard pnpm workspace layout.
- Severity: blocks workflow — a git-source update cannot complete on Windows in this layout.
- Frequency: 1/1 update run that reached `preflight-runtime-stage` failed deterministically at this phase (~84 min into staging).
- Consequence: ~2.25 h of validation work discarded per attempt, a multi-GB nested `dist.openclaw-update-*.tmp` tree that resists normal deletion (needs long-path-aware removal), and the managed Gateway is intentionally left stopped after the failure.

### Additional information

Possibly the same class of self-materialization as #162585 (plugin source capture re-materializing a plugin's own package) and adjacent to #170182 (copy source overlapping update state), but on the git-source updater candidate copy path on Windows. Suggested direction: the candidate copy should replicate reparse points as links (or skip workspace `node_modules` self-links and recreate them), and the fallback cleanup should use long-path-aware deletion (`\\?\` prefixes) so an aborted attempt cannot strand an undeletable tree.

issues.body: ### Bug type Regression (worked before, now fails) ### Beta release blocker No ### Summary ## Summary OpenClaw appears to leak unreaped child processes from hook/tool execution. Over time these accumulate as zombies under the main `openclaw` process (`openclaw-hooks`, `bash`, `codex`, and occasionally `chrome-headless`). Once enough accumulate, the runtime degrades and can eventually fail to spawn new helper work (`spawn EAGAIN`, `uv_thread_create`, gateway instability, connector silence). Restarting OpenClaw immediately clears the process table and restores service until the leak accumulates again. This is not a single connector failure in our deployment: we have seen the same shape across multiple OpenClaw 2026.6.x versions, and the current affected runtime reports: ```text OpenClaw 2026.6.10 (aa69b12) ``` ## Environment - Runtime: OpenClaw `2026.6.10 (aa69b12)` - OS: Debian 12 GCE VM - OpenClaw launched in Docker with host networking - Workload: - Slack provider enabled - Telegram provider enabled - Codex provider enabled - scheduled/cron work enabled - hook/tool plugins enabled - The issue is most visible on a busy runtime, but the leak pattern is not limited to a single connector. We also see stale `bash` and `codex` children, not only connector-specific workers. ## Symptoms After OpenClaw has been running for hours, process pressure grows steadily. A recent sanitized snapshot: ```text total processes: 336 zombies: 225 dstate: 1 zombie_comm openclaw-hooks 113 zombie_comm bash 108 zombie_comm codex 2 zombie_comm chrome-headless 2 ``` The zombie children are parented by the main `openclaw` process: ```text PID PPID STAT ELAPSED COMMAND 141806 141784 Ssl 20:12:59 openclaw 142413 141806 ZNs 20:07:50 [openclaw-hooks] 143325 141806 ZNs 20:00:41 [openclaw-hooks] 177641 141806 Z 11:33:55 [codex] ... ``` OpenClaw health remains nominal for a while, but the process table continues growing: ```json { "openclaw_reachable": true, "telegram": { "ready": true }, "slack": { "ready": true }, "process_pressure": { "degraded": false, "restart_recommended": false, "process_count": 326, "zombies": 225, "hook_zombies": 113, "d_state": 0, "reasons": [] } } ``` When the leak gets worse, the same runtime reaches degraded/restart territory: ```json { "process_count": 1003, "zombie_processes": 889, "hook_zombie_processes": 798, "d_state_processes": 1, "reasons": [ "hook_zombie_warning", "hook_zombie_degraded" ], "thresholds": { "hook_zombie_warning": 250, "hook_zombie_degraded": 750, "hook_zombie_restart": 800, "total_zombie_restart": 1000 } } ``` In worse incidents we observed downstream runtime failures such as: - `spawn EAGAIN` - `uv_thread_create` - gateway health timeouts / intermittent gateway unavailability - Slack/Telegram messages not being processed - task failures where OpenClaw can no longer start expected helper work Restarting OpenClaw clears the zombies immediately and restores the runtime, which strongly suggests unreaped children rather than external API/network failure. ## Secondary effect: monitoring traffic ramps up On GCE with Google Ops Agent installed, outbound network slowly increases until OpenClaw is restarted. Packet sampling showed the largest outbound flow was the Ops Agent (`otelopscol`) exporting host/process metrics, not OpenAI/Slack/Telegram payloads. This appears to be a consequence of the leak: as the process table grows, per-process metrics export grows. After OpenClaw restart, process count drops and the outbound metric volume falls. ## Expected behavior OpenClaw should reap hook/tool child processes when they exit, including subprocesses created by hook runners and embedded provider/tool helpers. Completed hook/tool invocations should not leave zombie `openclaw-hooks`, `bash`, `codex`, or browser-helper children indefinitely. ## Actual behavior Defunct children remain parented to `openclaw` for many hours, accumulating until runtime health degrades. Restarting OpenClaw is currently the only reliable recovery. ## Why this looks like an OpenClaw process lifecycle bug - Zombies are direct children of the main `openclaw` process. - They survive after the tool/hook work has completed. - They include generic hook/tool child processes (`openclaw-hooks`, `bash`, `codex`, `chrome-headless`), not just one connector-specific worker. - The problem clears only when the parent OpenClaw process is restarted. - We have reproduced the pattern across multiple 2026.6.x versions. ## Related / possibly adjacent issues These may be related but do not seem to cover the same root issue: - #79224 - #77249 - #88870 ## Useful diagnostics we can provide We can provide more sanitized snapshots if useful: - `ps -eo pid,ppid,stat,etime,comm,args` - OpenClaw gateway logs around the degradation window - process-pressure watcher summaries - packet-header-only traffic samples showing Ops Agent traffic growing with process count ### Steps to reproduce I do not yet have a minimal synthetic reproducer, but the issue is reproducible in a long-running OpenClaw runtime under connector/tool load: 1. Run OpenClaw 2026.6.x on a Linux VM with gateway enabled. 2. Configure Slack and/or Telegram connectors. 3. Enable hook/tool execution paths that spawn child processes, including connector ingestion, scheduled/cron tasks, and normal agent tool calls. 4. Let the runtime process real connector traffic for several hours without restarting the OpenClaw container. 5. Periodically inspect the OpenClaw process tree with `ps`, `pstree`, or equivalent host process metrics. Observed result: child processes created by OpenClaw/tool/hook execution become zombies and remain parented under the OpenClaw process instead of being reaped. The zombie count grows over time, eventually causing process/thread exhaustion and runtime degradation. ### Expected behavior OpenClaw should reap all completed hook/tool child processes promptly. A long-running gateway/runtime should keep a stable process count under normal connector and tool usage. Completed child processes should not accumulate as zombies, and the runtime should not degrade into `spawn EAGAIN`, `uv_thread_create`, gateway timeouts, connector silence, or required container restarts. If a tool or hook subprocess cannot be reaped normally, OpenClaw should detect it, log a bounded diagnostic, clean it up or quarantine it, and continue operating without unbounded zombie/process growth. ### Actual behavior Completed hook/tool child processes remain as zombies parented under the OpenClaw runtime process. Over time the zombie count and total process count grow without being cleaned up. Once enough zombies accumulate, the runtime begins failing unrelated operations because the host/container hits process or thread limits. Observed failures include: - `spawn EAGAIN` - `uv_thread_create` failures from Node - gateway requests timing out or becoming intermittently unavailable - Slack/Telegram connectors appearing configured but no longer responding reliably - normal shell commands such as `ps` or `ulimit` failing with `Resource temporarily unavailable` - runtime recovery requiring an OpenClaw/container restart, after which the zombie count drops and service resumes This appears to be cumulative: the runtime can work normally for hours, then progressively degrades as unreaped child processes build up. ### OpenClaw version 2026.06.10 ### Operating system Debian 12 on Google Compute Engine VM ### Install method Docker image deployed by provisioning automation/Terraform on a GCE VM. OpenClaw runs as a long-lived container with host networking, managed by systemd. ### Model GPT-5.5 on Codex subscription ### Provider / routing chain User message arrives through Slack or Telegram connector, then through the local OpenClaw gateway/runtime on the VM, then to the configured OpenAI/Codex provider path used by the OpenClaw agent. The issue appears before or around local hook/tool/process execution and is not specific to one upstream model response path. ### Additional provider/model setup details The affected runtime uses OpenClaw gateway mode with connector channels enabled for Slack and Telegram. The agent is configured with OpenAI/Codex auth for main turns, plus local tools/hooks and scheduled jobs. The zombie accumulation appears tied to local subprocess lifecycle management for hooks/tools/connectors, not to API key validity or model selection. We have observed it across multiple OpenClaw 2026.6.x versions and after changing VM size. Restarting the OpenClaw container clears the accumulated zombies temporarily, but they start accumulating again during normal connector/tool activity. No API keys, tokens, or secrets are included here. ### Logs ```shell # One example: OpenClaw process pressure: source host_proc hook zombies: 800+ total zombies: 800+ total processes: 900+ D-state processes: 1 restart recommended # Another one: OpenClaw process pressure: hook zombies: ~4000 total zombies: ~4000 process/thread exhaustion symptoms present ``` ### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence ### Impact and severity Affects users - needed to create a separate watcher that restarts OpenClaw every few hours ### Additional information Did not notice this issue before 2026.6.8 (maybe should say before 2026.6.X)

issues.body:
## Summary
On 2026.9.6, session-SQLite files that are **permanently** deferred (`historical_transcript_deferred`, "recorded source could not be hash-verified; protected without replaying or archiving it") are re-checked on **every gateway startup**, inside the startup migration lease. If there are enough of them, the scan outruns the lease and the gateway fails to start.

## Environment
OpenClaw 2026.9.6, Linux x64, Node 24, multi-agent gateway, upgraded from 2026.7.1.

## Observed
- `openclaw doctor --session-sqlite inspect`: `1 target(s), 487 legacy entries, 72 sqlite entries, 3737 issue(s)`, nearly all `historical_transcript_deferred` on `*.trajectory-path.json` pointer files in `agents/<agent>/sessions/` (6,006 of them).
- Every pointer's `runtimeFile` target no longer exists; an external retention job had moved the trajectory traces away before the upgrade. None of them is referenced from the session registry. They can never be imported, and the docs say trajectory envelopes aren't converted into conversations anyway.
- After an OOM kill, the next boot failed with `OpenClaw startup migration lease was lost before startup migrations completed; retry so migrations can run under a fresh lease | gateway.maintenance_required` (exit 78/CONFIG). It needed a stop, `doctor --fix`, and a start.
- The migration receipts still reference these paths (state DB + `session-sqlite-migration-runs/`), so an operator can't safely move or delete them: the docs warn against touching receipts, and moving referenced sources has previously caused `Retained session migration source changed` → exit 78.

## Expected
- Once a file is classified as permanently deferred (unverifiable, not a conversation, not referenced by the registry), record that and skip it on later startups instead of re-verifying it each boot.
- Startup migration checks should be bounded by *new* work, not by the total count of known-deferred files.
- A supported command to retire or acknowledge permanently deferred sources (and update their receipts), so operators can clear them without editing receipts by hand.
- Lease loss caused by a long deferred-file scan shouldn't leave the gateway down until someone runs `doctor --fix`.

Related: #160561 (migration warnings persist after cleanup), #170204 (large session store startup cost).

issues.body:
### Summary
On OpenClaw 2026.10.2 (b8952d4) the experimental Decision-assistance conversational tool prefilter never runs on any agent once the bundled **active-memory** plugin is enabled, even for agents that active-memory is not configured to serve.

### Evidence
- `extensions/active-memory/index.js` registers `before_prompt_build` with `requiresToolAuthority: true`.
- `hookRunner.hasAuthorizedPromptBuildHooks(ctx)` returns true when any such hook is registered and `isHookContextEligible` passes. Plugin-config scoping (`plugins.entries.active-memory.config.agents`, `allowedChatTypes`) is not part of that check.
- The attempt guard (`builtin-openclaw`, "hasPendingActionInstructions") then sets `decisionPrefilter = { status: "skipped", reason: "pending-action-context" }` before any Decision inference.
- Live debug window (10 primary dispatches on embedded Anthropic turns): every `Decision tool surface at primary dispatch` record was `decisionStatus: skipped`, either `pending-action-context` (9) or `internal-input` (1). This included agents that are not in active-memory's `agents` list.
- Config: `agents.defaults.experimental.decisionAssistance: true`, `agents.defaults.decisionModel: onnx/gliclass-edge-v3.0` (provider healthy: explicit `decision_evaluate` returns ok).

### Secondary measurement (same rubric v9 questions via explicit `decision_evaluate`, onnx gliclass-edge-v3.0)
| request | missing_request_context p | next_response_needs_tools p | latency |
|---|---|---|---|
| "explain mutex vs semaphore, nothing to look up" | 0.9997 | 0.09 | 4.4 s |
| "Read the file IDENTITY.md … quote its first line" | 0.988 | **0.06** | 4.7 s |
| "What's the current temperature in Santa Rosa right now?" | 0.953 | **0.09** | 13.8 s |
| "Thanks, that makes sense!" | 0.097 | 0.16 | 3.4 s |

The tool-requiring requests keep their tools only because missing_request_context is (wrongly) high. If the guard were lifted, a short follow-up imperative on this model could prune required tools. All latencies are well above the 500 ms budget, which degrades to "unavailable" → tools retained. That outcome is safe but means no filtering.

### Expected
- `hasAuthorizedPromptBuildHooks` should respect the hook owner's effective per-agent/per-chat eligibility, or active-memory should declare its scope to the hook runner, so that agents active-memory doesn't serve can still be prefiltered.
- Doctor/status should report "Decision assistance enabled but the prefilter is structurally skipped (authorized prompt-build hook: active-memory)" so the Labs flag isn't mistaken for active filtering.

Related umbrella: #155131.

issues.body:
## Environment
- OpenClaw **2026.10.2** (npm latest), Node v26.8.2
- Host: **WSL2** (Ubuntu 24.04), kernel `6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2`
- Service: systemd **user** unit `openclaw-gateway`

## Symptom
The Gateway **self-restarts repeatedly** (5 times within ~2h today), each time exiting with code 1 and being restarted by systemd. Users see `⚠️ Gateway is restarting. Please wait a few seconds and try again.` while an agent turn is in flight.

## Log evidence
```
[state] Gateway state ownership is no longer current at /home/<user>/.openclaw/tmp/openclaw-1000/state.<id>.lock: heartbeat clock moved backwards; restart the Gateway.
[admission] closed: restart (SIGUSR2: Error: Gateway state ownership is no longer current ... heartbeat clock moved backwards; restart the Gateway.)
[gateway] received SIGUSR2; restarting
...
openclaw-gateway.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE
```

## Trigger
The guest OS wall clock steps **backwards** (routine NTP correction of the WSL clock):
```
$ dmesg | grep -c 'Time jumped backwards'
15          # all within 17:03–18:18
$ timedatectl timesync-status
Offset: -664.141ms      # local clock ahead of the source
Poll interval: 32s
```
A ~0.1–0.7 s backward step is enough to be treated as ownership loss.

## Root cause (shipped dist)
`dist/gateway-state-owner-*.mjs`:
```js
const renewedAt = Atomics.load(lastBeat, 0);
const age = now() - Number(renewedAt);
const remaining = age < 0 ? 0 : 6e4 - age;
if (remaining <= 0) onLost(new Error(`Gateway state ownership is no longer current at ${...}: ${failure ?? (age < 0 ? "heartbeat clock moved backwards" : "utimes heartbeat renewal did not complete within 60 seconds")}; restart the Gateway.`));
```
The freshness check is relative to the **wall clock**; any backward wall-clock step makes `age < 0` and is treated as a lost lease → forced restart. (The module mixes `performance.now()` and `Date.now()`.)

## Suggested fix
- Base the heartbeat freshness check on a **monotonic** clock (`performance.now()` / `process.hrtime.bigint()`), or
- tolerate a small negative age instead of treating it as a lost lease.

## Local workaround
Replaced `systemd-timesyncd` with `chrony` (`makestep 0 0`, `maxslewrate 500`) so the clock is **slewed, never stepped**.

_Filing from a WSL2 deployment; the clock step is a normal WSL2/NTP behaviour, so this is easy to hit on any drifting VM/container._

issues.body:
## Summary

When using `google/gemini-2.5-pro` via the `google-generative-ai` API, three issues combine to cause rapid session context bloat, aborted runs, and silent Telegram delivery failures.

## Issue 1: textSignature Session Bloat (High Severity)

Gemini assistant responses include a `textSignature` field containing ~15KB of base64 data per response turn. OpenClaw stores these signatures verbatim in the session JSONL history. After 10+ turns, the accumulated signatures alone consume 150KB+, causing:

1. Context window bloat (observed: 416K tokens in one session)
2. Gemini API timeouts on re-submission of full context
3. Compaction failures (session too large to compact)
4. Silent message delivery failures (run aborts before reply is sent to Telegram)

**Expected:** `textSignature` should either not be stored in session history, be stored separately, or not be re-sent to the model on subsequent turns.

## Issue 2: Embedded `<think>` Tags in Text

Gemini 2.5 Pro embeds `<think>...</think>` tags directly in the `text` content field (not as separate `thinking` type blocks). If OpenClaw treats `<think>`-prefixed text as internal/thinking content, the reply is suppressed and never delivered to Telegram.

**Expected:** OpenClaw should either strip `<think>` tags from the delivered text, or not suppress messages that contain them.

## Issue 3: Mixed Text + ToolCall in Same Response

Gemini 2.5 Pro consistently emits text + toolCall in the same response turn. OpenClaw processes the toolCall, gets the result, then emits an empty `content: []` as the final stop. The original text from the first part of the response is never delivered to the user.

**Expected:** Text content from a mixed text+toolCall response should be delivered to the user, not silently dropped.

## Reproduction

1. Configure an agent with `google/gemini-2.5-pro` as primary model
2. Send 5-10 interactive messages via Telegram group topic
3. Check session JSONL — each assistant message contains `textSignature` (~15KB base64)
4. After ~10 exchanges, session reaches 150K+ tokens
5. Subsequent runs timeout or abort; replies never reach Telegram

## Workaround

Switched affected agent to Claude Sonnet 4.6, which does not exhibit these behaviors.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.3.13 (61d171a)
- macOS Darwin 24.6.0 (arm64)

issues.body:
## Summary
Let an autonomous agent restart (and update) its own Gateway through a supported, graceful tool action, without needing a human owner in the loop.

## Background
Some OpenClaw deployments run **autonomous agents that manage their own infrastructure**: the agent upgrades its own Gateway and peer Gateways, and restarts itself after config changes or when it judges a restart necessary. In these setups the agent is the operator. The human sets policy but isn't the one performing upgrades.

In 2026.9.x:
- the `gateway` tool exposes only `config.get`, `config.schema.lookup`, `update.run` (`src/agents/tools/gateway-tool.ts`). There's no `restart`.
- `update.run` requires `senderIsOwner` or an operator schedule.
- the built-in system prompt forbids restarting via exec/detached jobs (#145527).

So an autonomous agent has no supported way to restart itself. The only paths are a human sending `/restart` or using the Control UI, which defeats the purpose of autonomy. Forcing agents back to shell restarts is worse: no drain, no recovery, turns die mid-flight.

## Proposal
1. A `gateway` tool `restart` action using the same graceful path as `update.run`: drain in-flight runs, restart, resume and notify the requesting session.
2. Config to authorize it for agent-initiated use, e.g. `gateway.agentSelfManagement: { restart: true, update: true }` (default off), so `update.run`/`restart` don't need an owner principal when the operator has opted in.
3. When enabled, the system prompt omits the "never restart/update" sentence and the "ask the operator/user" guidance.

## Why
Graceful self-restart is safer than any alternative an autonomous agent would otherwise use, and it keeps the existing safety defaults for ordinary assistant installs.

## Summary
On OpenClaw 2026.9.8, the Control UI repeatedly displays only 1–3 recent exchanges followed by messages 20–36+ hours old. Recent exchanges disappear as activity continues. An independent observer saw old interrupted incoming items mixed with current activity.

## Observations
- Installed and serving version: 2026.9.8.
- Gateway connectivity and /readyz pass.
- The inspected UI and separate chat.history calls identify the same main session.
- A separate read-only history response with limit 1,000 contained recent records: 500 assistant, 487 toolResult, 13 user. Of these, 27 user/assistant rows contained text.
- Pagination reported hasMore=true and nextOffset=1000.
- One Show earlier action did not visibly restore contiguous recent conversation.

## Expected and actual behavior
Expected: recent conversational exchanges remain accessible in a coherent history view as activity continues, with older history reachable through pagination.
Actual: the view repeatedly shows a small recent tail mixed with much older items, leaving recent conversation inaccessible in the rendered view.

## Evidence limits
The RPC reads were separate from the browser inspection, not a synchronized capture of the browser's actual responses. They establish that recent records were available from chat.history, not that the browser received the same rows and omitted them. Text-bearing rows are not necessarily final display rows. Data loss, root cause, rendering versus pagination behavior, and the origin of the old interrupted items have not been established. High tool-event volume is a possible contributing factor, not a confirmed cause.

## Diagnostics pending
A synchronized comparison of actual browser history/startup requests and rendered history during initial load, Show earlier, and disappearance remains pending. Useful diagnostics would be request parameters/timing, content-free row metadata and counts, pagination/reset/delta metadata, and which returned rows do not appear in the UI.

## Scope and release status
This history-display report is separate from an updater/package-activation problem. No update, restart, reset, cache clearing, or configuration change was performed for this report. We have not confirmed that 2026.10.2 fixes this symptom.

## Public evidence
No message or tool contents, private identifiers, hostnames, paths, credentials, session database, HAR, or full WebSocket dump are attached.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On Windows with OpenClaw 2026.10.2, an attempt to link the pinned official Codex package in an isolated recovery state copy emitted a `plugins.lifecycle.lease` SQLite lock-contention diagnostic and a PowerShell `NativeCommandError`. The actual installer exit code and failing lifecycle phase remain unknown. Contemporaneous checks found no listener on the production and preceding fixture ports; they do not exclude every database user.

### Steps to reproduce

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Expected behavior

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Actual behavior

The operator recorded this attempted command shape in a separate isolated state copy:

```text
openclaw plugins install --link <existing-official-package-path> --no-enable --force --accept-capabilities
```

The retained diagnostic includes these fields:

```text
SQLite error: 5
operation: plugins.lifecycle.lease
step: begin
busyTimeoutMs: 0
failureKind: lock-contention
```

**Correction following recovery of existing records:** The earlier `mode=immediate` assertion was unsupported and has been withdrawn. The retained output specifies only `step=begin`; it is not a complete JavaScript exception stack. The saved redirected log contains only a source-trust warning, while the execution transcript retains the SQLite diagnostic and PowerShell error metadata. The script used `$ErrorActionPreference='Stop'`; its expected `$LASTEXITCODE` result file was not produced. The outer execution session's exit code 0 does not establish installer success or its actual exit code. See the evidence-supplement comment for the command, database label, original retained diagnostic, timestamps and limited concurrent observations. The lock owner and phase remain unknown. There is no clean-install reproduction or established repeatability.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.2

### Operating system

Windows; exact edition/build not recorded in the supplied report.

### Install method

Isolated recovery state copies with official `@openclaw/codex@2026.10.2`; attempted local linked installation as shown above. The supplied report does not document the outcome of normal managed official-package installation in this candidate.

### Model

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Provider / routing chain

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Additional provider/model setup details

Pinned environment: Codex CLI 0.160.0; Node 24.21.0. The attempted install is the issue reported here; no effective model/provider route was established by that attempt.

The earlier fixture test blocked external model and memory requests and used a local response fixture with a restrictive tool policy. No live subscription response was attempted.

### Logs

The evidence-supplement comment supplies the complete recoverable diagnostic output, PowerShell location/error metadata, a sanitized database path, timestamped observations and PID/parent rows. A full JavaScript stack, measured total duration, actual installer exit code, worker identities and lock owner remain unavailable. The roughly 52–117 second observed lifetime bounds are derived from presence/absence samples, not a measured installation duration.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Basis: operator-provided `SUPPORT.md` and subsequently uploaded `EVIDENCE-SUPPLEMENT.md`, which identifies retained execution JSONL records and saved files. The supplement was reviewed for publication without direct access to the Windows machine or independently opening the underlying raw records.

Relevant installed source bundles named in that report:

- `plugin-lifecycle-lease-5X2Of1QR.mjs`
- `openclaw-state-lease-Cc8rTDnb.mjs`
- `registry-854ZO8XT.mjs`
- `discovery-B1vdhqb3.mjs`
- `model-runtime-policy-BAKtKsyW.mjs`

### Impact and severity

One recorded linked-install attempt ended with a PowerShell error and without its expected installer result file. Installation success was not established, and recovery remains unactivated. Frequency beyond this attempt is unknown; no data loss or corruption is established.

### Additional information

**Installation context, not a second claimed defect:** The official Codex package was previously selected through `plugins.load` and discovered as `origin=config`. Inspection of `registry-854ZO8XT.mjs` reportedly showed that official Codex reserved runtime/native-compaction registration requires `origin=global`; registration was rejected, and the fixture turn did not enter Codex.

Current [installation documentation](https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli/plugins/install) says local paths, including `--link` entries selected through `plugins.load.paths`, do not inherit official-package trust; `--force` does not change that boundary. We therefore do **not** assume that resolving the SQLite contention or successfully linking this package would establish the required ownership. Local-source rejection may be expected policy enforcement. See also the [Codex harness documentation](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/codex-harness). These current pages may differ from the pinned release.

**Related report:** #165971 describes matching operation/error fields on macOS 2026.9.8. Its [closure comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/165971#issuecomment-6010956519) reports that shared lease-acquisition retry was already implemented on main via #162750; it also distinguishes acquisition from zero-timeout renewal/release. We have not established which lease phase/path produced this Windows 2026.10.2 failure or whether it has the same cause. We are not claiming retries are globally absent.

**Questions for maintainers:**

1. What supported diagnostics identify the database connection or lease owner blocking this operation when no gateway is running, and distinguish acquisition from renewal/release?
2. Does the earlier fix in #162750 cover this local-install path, or is additional evidence needed to determine that?
3. What supported official-package installation/import procedure establishes the required ownership in an isolated state directory? We are not requesting a bypass of ownership checks or manual deletion of lease/database records.

**Retained fixture context:** Readiness took 268.322 seconds; two dashboard authentications and effective-tool inventory (412 ms) succeeded. A turn was acknowledged, but no assistant reply or completed-turn record arrived; zero mock inference requests reached the fixture. Three utility-model attempts were blocked; no escaped provider requests were reported. This is not evidence of model-entitlement or authentication failure.

**Stopped state:** The gateway exited 43.726 seconds after Ctrl+C without force termination; four plugin forced-retirement warnings remained. At the reported October 12, 2026, 21:19 PDT checkpoint, candidate processes and checked gateway/test listeners were absent, production's logon trigger was disabled, and its configuration hash was unchanged. Neither recovery candidate was activated.

No further reproduction is claimed. This report excludes credentials, personal paths, configuration contents, sessions, and memory data.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

A persisted TTS-only assistant turn can disappear from the model-visible conversation history on a later turn when using the `openai-completions` transport.

The original assistant turn is stored correctly and contains non-empty speech text in `openclawDelivery.tts.text`, while its normal assistant text content is empty.

During later replay, the TTS speech text is not projected back into the assistant's LLM-facing `content`. The OpenAI Completions message conversion then has no non-empty assistant text to send and can omit the historical assistant turn entirely.

This can make the model believe that it never answered an earlier user request even though a successful canonical assistant response exists in the session transcript.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use a persistent OpenClaw session with the `openai-completions` API.

2. Configure the assistant so that voice replies can be TTS-only, without a duplicate written response.

3. Ask the assistant for a voice reply.

4. Let the assistant successfully produce a canonical TTS-only turn whose persisted representation contains:

```text
role: assistant

content:
  - thinking: <non-empty>
  - text: ""

openclawDelivery:
  tts:
    tagged: true
    text: <non-empty spoken response>

stopReason: stop
```

5. Start a later model turn in the same persistent session.

   In the observed case this later turn was a scheduled heartbeat, but the replay problem itself is not heartbeat-specific.

6. Observe that the later model can behave as though the previous assistant response never occurred.

In the observed case, the later model explicitly reasoned that the earlier user request had not been answered and attempted to answer it again.

No synthetic forced-heartbeat reproduction was used for this report. The runtime observation was followed by source analysis of the replay and OpenAI Completions transport path.

### Expected behavior

A persisted TTS-only assistant response should remain semantically visible to the model during later conversation replay.

If a canonical assistant turn contains non-empty:

`openclawDelivery.tts.text`

while normal assistant text content is intentionally empty, the later LLM-facing history should still represent that turn as an assistant response.

The model should not receive a conversation history that makes an already completed assistant response appear to be missing.

### Actual behavior

The TTS speech text remains stored as OpenClaw metadata, but it is not projected into the assistant's LLM-facing `content`.

For the `openai-completions` transport, assistant messages are reconstructed from `msg.content`.

Because the TTS-only turn has no non-empty normal text, and because `openclawDelivery.tts.text` is not considered during this conversion, the historical assistant message can be omitted entirely from the provider-facing message list.

The later model can therefore receive a history in which the earlier assistant response is absent.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.1

### Operating system

Ubuntu Linux 26.04

### Install method

Global OpenClaw installation using the OpenClaw-managed Node.js toolchain

### Model

deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw -> OpenRouter -> DeepSeek

### Additional provider/model setup details

- Provider: OpenRouter
- Model: `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`
- Node.js: `v24.19.0`
- Channel used for the reproduced failure: WhatsApp
- Heartbeat uses the normal main session, not `isolatedSession`
- TTS is provided through a local custom CLI-based speech synthesis setup

The TTS engine itself was therefore not the first suspected failure point. 

### Logs

```shell

```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

No screenshots are required to reproduce the issue.

The issue was observed in a real persistent session and then traced through the installed OpenClaw 2026.10.1 source.

### Persisted assistant turn

The earlier assistant response existed as a successful canonical turn with the equivalent structure:

```text
role: assistant

content:
  - thinking: <non-empty>
  - text: ""

openclawDelivery:
  textPhaseRequiresTerminal: true
  tts:
    tagged: true
    text: <non-empty spoken response>

stopReason: stop
```

The exact user text, speech text, run ID and session ID are omitted here for privacy.

The later turn was on the same conversation branch whose leaf was this TTS-only assistant turn.

### Replay path

The session history is replayed through:

```text
activeSession.messages
→ sanitizeSessionHistory(...)
→ validateReplayTurns(...)
→ filterHeartbeatTranscriptArtifacts(...)
→ history limiting
→ activeSession.agent.state.messages
→ convertToLlm(...)
→ provider transport
```

The generic assistant replay normalization does not remove the TTS metadata in this case.

`convertToLlm()` also passes ordinary assistant messages through unchanged:

```js
case "user":
case "assistant":
case "toolResult":
    llmMessages.push(message);
    return;
```

### Provider transport transformation

The transport transformation rebuilds assistant `content` from `msg.content`:

```js
const sourceContent = Array.isArray(msg.content)
    ? msg.content
    : msg.content != null && typeof msg.content === "object"
        ? [msg.content]
        : [];

const content = [];

// ...

return {
    ...msg,
    content
};
```

This preserves `openclawDelivery` as metadata on the internal object, but `openclawDelivery.tts.text` is not projected into assistant `content`.

### OpenAI Completions conversion

The OpenAI Completions adapter creates a new provider-facing assistant message:

```js
const assistantMsg = {
    role: "assistant",
    content: compat.requiresAssistantAfterToolResult ? "" : null
};
```

It collects normal assistant text only from `msg.content`:

```js
const assistantTexts = [];

msg.content.forEach((block) => {
    if (block.type === "text" && block.text.trim().length > 0)
        assistantTexts.push(sanitizeSurrogates(block.text));
    else if (block.type === "thinking" && block.thinking.trim().length > 0)
        nonEmptyThinkingBlocks.push(block);
    else if (block.type === "toolCall")
        toolCalls.push(block);
});
```

There is no handling of:

```text
msg.openclawDelivery.tts.text
```

Finally, an assistant message with no provider-visible content and no tool calls is skipped:

```js
const content = assistantMsg.content;

if (
    !(content !== null && content !== void 0 && content.length > 0)
    && !assistantMsg.tool_calls
)
    continue;
```

The compatibility default for thinking replay is:

```js
requiresThinkingAsText:
    configured?.requiresThinkingAsText ?? false
```

Therefore, with the default behavior, a TTS-only assistant turn with empty normal text and no tool calls can disappear completely from the OpenAI Completions provider history.

### Observed semantic consequence

On the later turn, the model reasoned that the earlier request had not been answered and attempted to answer it again.

That behavior is consistent with the provider-visible history produced by the code path above.

### Impact and severity

**Suggested severity: Medium**

This causes semantic corruption of persistent conversation history.

The canonical transcript records that the assistant responded, while a later model call can receive a history in which that response is absent.

Possible user-visible consequences include:

- treating an already answered request as still pending
- repeating a previous response
- incorrectly reasoning that no answer was sent
- repeating conversational actions that were already completed
- inconsistent behavior between the stored transcript and the model's effective context

The issue is particularly relevant for TTS-only replies because intentionally no duplicate written assistant text exists that could otherwise preserve the semantic turn during replay.

This is not merely a display-history issue: it changes the conversation context presented to the model on later turns.

### Additional information

This appears to be separate from #170027.

#170027 concerns a newly generated TTS-only heartbeat reply being dropped before speech synthesis/delivery.

This issue concerns a different stage:

```text
already persisted TTS-only assistant response
→ later session replay
→ TTS speech text is not projected into LLM-facing assistant content
→ historical assistant response can disappear from provider context
```

The observed later turn happened to be a heartbeat, but the underlying replay behavior is not inherently heartbeat-specific.

A provider-independent fix may be preferable to an OpenAI-Completions-only workaround.

One possible direction would be to project the semantic speech response from:

```text
openclawDelivery.tts.text
```

into model-visible historical assistant content when:

- the canonical assistant turn contains non-empty TTS text, and
- it has no non-empty normal assistant text.

That projection could happen earlier in the canonical replay pipeline so that different providers receive equivalent conversation semantics.

The original delivery behavior should remain unchanged: this would only affect how an already persisted TTS-only assistant turn is represented to later model calls.

### Bug type

### Beta release blocker

### Summary

On OpenClaw `2026.10.1`, a scheduled main-session heartbeat successfully produced and persisted a TTS-only Assistant final with non-empty `openclawDelivery.tts.text`, but no TTS media file was created and no voice message was delivered, while a normal text heartbeat from the same session was delivered successfully.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use OpenClaw `2026.10.1` with working TTS support and a scheduled heartbeat running in the normal main session.

2. Let the heartbeat produce a TTS-only Assistant final. In the captured run, the model returned:

   ```text
   [[tts:text]]<redacted non-empty spoken response>[[/tts:text]]
   ```

3. Inspect the resulting canonical Assistant transcript entry and verify that:
   - the visible Assistant text is empty;
   - `stopReason` is `stop`;
   - `openclawDelivery.tts.text` is present and non-empty.
4. Verify that no corresponding TTS media file is created and no voice message reaches the channel.
Control observations from the same main session:
- a later normal text heartbeat was delivered successfully;
- a later `NO_REPLY` heartbeat was correctly suppressed.
This sequence was directly observed for one qualifying TTS-only heartbeat. A synthetic forced-heartbeat reproduction has not been run.

### Expected behavior

On the same installation, TTS-only Assistant replies outside this failing heartbeat case are synthesized and delivered successfully.

A heartbeat final carrying a valid non-empty `openclawDelivery.tts.text` should likewise reach the TTS synthesis and outbound-delivery stage rather than disappear before synthesis, even when its visible Assistant text is intentionally empty.

### Actual behavior

The heartbeat run completed successfully, but no voice reply was delivered.

Observed evidence:

- model run completed successfully;
- `stopReason`: `stop`;
- visible Assistant text: empty;
- `openclawDelivery.tts.text`: present and non-empty;
- no corresponding TTS synthesis media file was created;
- no matching TTS/speech/audio/media/synthesis delivery log entry was found after model completion in the inspected runtime window;
- no outbound voice message reached WhatsApp;
- no user-visible error or fallback was produced.

A normal text heartbeat from the same main session was delivered successfully.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.1

### Operating system

Ubuntu Linux 26.04

### Install method

Global OpenClaw installation using the OpenClaw-managed Node.js toolchain

### Model

deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw -> OpenRouter -> DeepSeek

### Additional provider/model setup details

- Provider: OpenRouter
- Model: `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`
- Node.js: `v24.19.0`
- Channel used for the reproduced failure: WhatsApp
- Heartbeat uses the normal main session, not `isolatedSession`
- TTS is provided through a local custom CLI-based speech synthesis setup
- TTS works correctly for normal assistant replies outside this failing heartbeat case

The TTS engine itself was therefore not the first suspected failure point. In the reproduced heartbeat, no synthesis invocation occurred at all.

### Logs

```shell
Heartbeat run:

The affected heartbeat completed successfully.

runId: <redacted>
time: 2026-10-12 13:00 Europe/Berlin

status: success
stopReason: stop
aborted: false
timedOut: false
message tool used: false

The model output was a TTS-only response:
[[tts:text]]<redacted non-empty spoken response>[[/tts:text]]

Canonical Assistant transcript entry
The persisted Assistant message contained an empty visible text block but valid TTS delivery metadata:
{
  "content": [
    {
      "type": "thinking"
    },
    {
      "type": "text",
      "text": ""
    }
  ],
  "stopReason": "stop",
  "openclawDelivery": {
    "textPhaseRequiresTerminal": true,
    "tts": {
      "tagged": true,
      "text": "<redacted non-empty spoken response>"
    }
  }
}

This confirms that:
1. the model produced tagged TTS content;
2. tagged-TTS parsing succeeded;
3. openclawDelivery.tts.text was persisted;
4. the Assistant turn completed normally.
No synthesis occurred
The configured speech media directory contained no generated file for this heartbeat:
~/.openclaw/media/tool-speech-synthesis

The gateway journal around the run contained normal model execution entries but no later TTS/speech/audio/media/synthesis/delivery activity associated with the reply.
Relevant runtime window:
13:00:48 [agent/embedded] tool-search: cataloged 26 tools behind compact prompt surface
13:00:49 [plugins] active-memory: recall skipped reason=session-ineligible
13:00:51 [provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] response provider=openrouter api=openai-completions model=deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash status=200

A filtered journal search for the affected window and run ID returned no tts, speech, audio, media, synth, deliver, or whatsapp activity after model completion.
Control heartbeats
Same main session:
13:00 - TTS-only final
         agent run succeeded
         no synthesis
         no delivery

14:00 - normal text final
         delivered successfully

15:00 - NO_REPLY
         correctly suppressed
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

No screenshots are required to reproduce the issue.

Evidence was collected from:

- OpenClaw trajectory/runtime records;
- canonical SQLite transcript data;
- gateway journal;
- speech-synthesis media directory;
- the shipped `2026.10.1` distribution bundle;
- source comparison against `v2026.10.2` and current `main`.

Private conversation content has intentionally been redacted. The exact spoken text is irrelevant to the failure; it was non-empty.

### Impact and severity

Observed impact: one qualifying TTS-only scheduled heartbeat reply was lost with no user-visible error or fallback.

The same main session later delivered a normal text heartbeat successfully and correctly suppressed a `NO_REPLY` heartbeat.

The practical consequence in the observed case was silent message loss: the agent run was recorded as successful although the intended voice response never reached the user.

Broader frequency and cross-channel impact have not been established.

### Additional information

### Source analysis

The shipped `2026.10.1` payload builder preserves a TTS-only final.

It considers persisted speech metadata when deciding whether to use the canonical final answer:

```js
const shouldUseCanonicalFinalAnswer = Boolean(
  fallbackAnswerDirectiveState &&
    (
      normalizeTextForComparison(fallbackAnswerDirectiveState.text) ||
      fallbackAnswerDirectiveState.mediaUrls?.length
    ) ||
  storedDelivery?.tts?.text?.trim()
);
```

It then retrieves the stored TTS facts:

```js
const ttsFacts = shouldUseCanonicalFinalAnswer
  ? storedDelivery?.tts
  : void 0;
```

and explicitly does not discard an otherwise empty reply when TTS facts exist:

```js
if (
  !cleanedText &&
  (!mediaUrls || mediaUrls.length === 0) &&
  !delivery.audioAsVoice &&
  !ttsFacts
) continue;
```

The resulting reply payload receives TTS metadata:

```js
replyItems.push(
  ttsFacts
    ? setReplyPayloadMetadata(replyPayload, { tts: ttsFacts })
    : replyPayload
);
```

So the speech-only reply still exists as a reply payload at this stage.

### Heartbeat selection

The heartbeat path later selects its public reply using:

```ts
export function resolveHeartbeatReplyPayload(
  replyResult: ReplyPayload | ReplyPayload[] | undefined,
): ReplyPayload | undefined {
  if (!replyResult) {
    return undefined;
  }

  if (!Array.isArray(replyResult)) {
    return isReasoningReplyPayload(replyResult) ? undefined : replyResult;
  }

  return replyResult.findLast(
    (payload) =>
      payload &&
      !isReasoningReplyPayload(payload) &&
      hasOutboundReplyContent(payload),
  );
}
```

The heartbeat runner calls this directly:

```ts
const selected = resolveHeartbeatReplyPayload(replyResult);
```

`hasOutboundReplyContent()` delegates to `hasReplyPayloadContent()`:

```ts
function hasOutboundReplyContent(payload, options) {
  return hasReplyPayloadContent(payload, {
    trimText: options?.trimText
  });
}
```

In the shipped `2026.10.1` bundle, `hasReplyPayloadContent()` checks the ordinary outbound-content fields:

```js
function hasReplyPayloadContent(payload, options) {
  return hasReplyContent({
    text: options?.trimText ? payload.text?.trim() : payload.text,
    mediaUrl: payload.mediaUrl,
    mediaUrls: payload.mediaUrls,
    interactive: payload.interactive,
    presentation: payload.presentation,
    hasChannelData:
      options?.hasChannelData ?? hasReplyChannelData(payload.channelData),
    extraContent:
      options?.extraContent ?? payload.location != null
  });
}
```

No TTS reply metadata is inspected by this predicate.

This establishes a source-level mismatch: the payload builder preserves TTS delivery metadata, while heartbeat array-reply selection uses an outbound-content predicate that does not inspect that TTS metadata.

The affected production run was not instrumented at this exact function boundary, so the source analysis is provided as the code path consistent with the observed failure rather than as direct runtime instrumentation of that boundary.

The source path consistent with the observed failure is therefore:

```text
model emits [[tts:text]]
        |
        v
openclawDelivery.tts.text persisted
        |
        v
reply payload created with TTS metadata
        |
        v
resolveHeartbeatReplyPayload()
        |
        v
hasOutboundReplyContent()
        |
        v
hasReplyPayloadContent()
        |
        v
TTS metadata is not considered by the content predicate
        |
        v
heartbeat array-reply selection can reject the TTS-only payload
        |
        v
no TTS synthesis observed
        |
        v
no voice reply delivered
```

### v2026.10.2 and current main

The relevant heartbeat selection implementation remains unchanged in `v2026.10.2`.

Current `main` also contains the same `src/auto-reply/heartbeat-reply-payload.ts` implementation.

At the time of verification, the file blob SHA for that implementation was:

```text
07c12b5838d5ce4e63b739894ca3d59f8c323cbb
```

### Relationship to the previous TTS-only completion issue

This appears distinct from #164256 and its fix in PR #164285.

In the present reproduction, the Assistant turn completed successfully and `openclawDelivery.tts.text` was persisted correctly. The observed failure occurs later: no TTS synthesis media is produced and no voice reply is delivered.
