issues.body:
## Environment

Behavior bug; not reported as a beta release blocker. Isolated source checkout on macOS arm64, Node26.7.0. Tests use synthetic peers and a deterministic agent-dispatch seam; no live peer or model/provider is required.

## What happens

An authenticated A2A `SendMessage` containing `message.taskId` silently starts a different task. The supplied task ID is parsed but ignored, so a peer expecting continuation can trigger unintended replacement work. This also happens for unknown, expired, another peer’s, completed, and active task IDs.

## Expected behavior

Reject invalid or unsupported task continuation before starting work. A caller deliberately starting a new task in the same conversation can omit `taskId` and reuse `contextId`.

A2A v1.0.1 requires referenced-task existence and context consistency; terminal tasks cannot be continued. Additional messages to nonterminal tasks are optional, so rejecting unsupported continuation does not require adding a lifecycle feature.

## Reproduction

The isolated reproduction submits this authenticated JSON-RPC request through the actual registered A2A HTTP handler at `/a2a/v1`, using a synthetic configured peer. A deployed peer can submit the same request; the reported proof is isolated plugin/HTTP integration, not a live Gateway test:

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": "task-reference-repro",
  "method": "SendMessage",
  "params": {
    "message": {
      "taskId": "does-not-exist",
      "role": "ROLE_USER",
      "parts": [{ "text": "Continue the referenced task" }]
    },
    "configuration": { "returnImmediately": true }
  }
}
```

Current behavior returns a newly allocated working task and dispatches new work instead of `TaskNotFoundError` (`-32001`). Supplying an owned task ID with a conflicting context also starts a new task in that context. This report does not claim disclosure of another peer’s task data.

## Baseline and evidence

Source baseline: `1f86b827717777114caf0184f1dfc77adf050cc6`; relevant HTTP/task-store logic is unchanged from the earlier isolated reproduction. New regression cases cover the HTTP entry point, peer-owned lookup, no replacement allocation/dispatch, and context-only follow-up. Exact validation results will be linked in the fix PR.

Protocol contract: [A2A multi-turn interactions](https://github.com/a2aproject/A2A/blob/v1.0.1/docs/specification.md#34-multi-turn-interactions).

issues.body:
## Summary

On a busy Gateway, read-only state-DB access takes a **full private copy of `state/openclaw.sqlite` per read**, and the cron scheduler's timer maintenance triggers that path on every tick. The copy is torn down as soon as its single reader closes, so the next read seconds later copies the same bytes again.

Measured on 2026.9.5 (Linux, 8 vCPU, 152–172 MB state DB, ~140 automations):

- `sqlite-readonly-location.worker.js --openclaw-sqlite-readonly-child` was spawned 15–33 times a minute with no matching RPC traffic, each making a full copy under `~/.cache/openclaw/`.
- Sustained 57–71 MB/s of disk writes for an hour (134 GB), io pressure "full" 30 %, event-loop utilisation 0.97, Telegram ingress stalled 301 s, CLI config writes took 1–6 min.
- Over a 120 s window the WAL changed only 29 times while 33 copies were made.

## Where (2026.10.2 stock dist, still present)

1. `dist/read-only-*.mjs` `readCronState`: `preserveArtifacts = storeKey === void 0 || isArtifactPreservingStateRead()`. `isArtifactPreservingStateRead()` is an AsyncLocalStorage flag set by `withArtifactPreservingStateReads()` around config reads; the scheduler's timer maintenance inherits that context, so every tick's read-only load of the cron store takes a snapshot first. (#150138 sees the same children at startup only; #159118 and #147956 are adjacent.)
2. `dist/sqlite-snapshot-source-*.mjs` `prepareSqliteReadOnlyLocationSync(pathname)`: every call spawns the copy child (`runSqliteReadOnlyWorkerSync`) and `adoptPreparedLocation` removes the copy on reader close. There is no reuse while the source is unchanged.

## Expected

- The cron store reader opens the live DB read-only (WAL readers do not block the writer) or at least does not inherit the artifact-preserving flag from unrelated timer maintenance.
- Read-only snapshots are reused per source fingerprint (dev, ino, size, mtime of DB + `-wal`/`-journal`) for a short TTL with reference counting, so an unchanged source is not recopied.

## Local workaround

We carry two dist patches implementing exactly those two changes (reader opens live DB read-only; per-fingerprint reuse, 30 s TTL, refcounted). With both applied the copy rate dropped from 33 to 0–7 per 120 s and the write storm stopped. Happy to share the patch text.

Related: #150138, #159118, #147956, #159990.

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

When the model provider is an OpenAI-compatible ChatGPT API, **every** chat request fails — even a trivial message like `test` — with:

```
[Error] Invalid JSON schema: regex lookaround is not supported. Found at $.properties.to.items.pattern.
```

Root cause: the `autoclaw-productivity` MCP tool definitions validate email fields with a regex containing **negative lookaheads** (`(?!\.)` and `(?!.*\.\.)`), which the OpenAI function-calling / structured-outputs schema validator does not accept. Because the tools are attached to every request, validation fails before the model ever runs (input tokens = 0 in logs).

Non-OpenAI providers (e.g. Muse Spark) accept the same schema, so the bug only surfaces on the ChatGPT API path.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use AutoClaw desktop with `autoclaw-productivity` MCP enabled (`http://127.0.0.1:19681/mcp`, `enabled: true`).
2. Set model provider to an OpenAI-compatible ChatGPT API model (observed with `gpt-6.1-sol` and `gpt-6-luna`).
3. Send any message, e.g. `test`.
4. The reply is immediately the schema error above; the model produces no output.

### Expected behavior

The request reaches the model normally; email validation happens at runtime, not via an unsupported regex feature in the tool schema.

### Actual behavior

- Every turn fails, including connectors that are `disconnected` (Gmail, Calendar, Workspace, Microsoft 365 all `disconnected`, yet their schemas are still sent).
- Log excerpt (`chat-history/agent%3Aawur-awuran%3A3d270518.json`): assistant message with 26 output tokens, **0 input tokens**, content = the error string. Same error also appears in `agent%3Amain%3A9e85426d.json` with another model.
- Local scan (`app.asar`, `app.asar.unpacked`, `extensions`, `office-plugin`, skills) contains **no** `lookaround` string — the rejection comes from the upstream OpenAI schema validator, not local logic.

### OpenClaw version

Version 1.18.5

### Operating system

Windows 11

### Install method

windows app

### Model

gpt-6.1-sol gpt-6-luna

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw > nutaraline > gpt-6.1-sol

### Additional provider/model setup details


## Offending pattern

Used in email fields (`to`, `cc`, `bcc`, `attendees`) across productivity tools, e.g. `gmail_create_draft`, `gmail_send_draft`, `google_calendar_create_event`, `microsoft365_create_draft`, `microsoft365_send_draft`, `microsoft365_create_calendar_event`:

```
^(?!\.)(?!.*\.\.)([A-Za-z0-9_'+\-\.]*)[A-Za-z0-9_+-]@([A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9\-]*\.)+[A-Za-z]{2,}$
   ^^^^^^ ^^^^^^^^^^^
   negative lookaheads — not supported by OpenAI tool-schema validator
```

Error path `$.properties.to.items.pattern` matches the `to: string[]` email field exactly.

## Suggested fix

Replace with a lookaround-free pattern. Any of these works with the OpenAI validator:

```
# Option A — minimal change (drop the two lookaheads, keep the rest):
^[A-Za-z0-9_'+.\-]*[A-Za-z0-9_+-]@([A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9\-]*\.)+[A-Za-z]{2,}$

# Option B — simple pragmatic email check:
^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$
```

Apply to **all** email `pattern` fields in the `autoclaw-productivity` tool definitions (Gmail, Google Calendar attendees, Microsoft 365 `to`/`cc`/`bcc`/attendees). Ideally also strip/skip tool schemas for connectors that are `disconnected` so one bad pattern can't break every request.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 (Windows_NT 10.0.26200, x64), host `Anamichii-PC`
- App: AutoClaw desktop, channel `official`, `app.asar` ~310 MB dated 2026-09-11
- Config: `openclaw.json` `meta.lastTouchedVersion: 2026.6.8`, `runtime-patch-manifest.json` `patchSetVersion: 104`
- Plugin: `autoclaw-productivity` (`type: streamable-http`, `url: http://127.0.0.1:19681/mcp`, `enabled: true`)
- Failing models: `gpt-6.1-sol`, `gpt-6-luna` (OpenAI-compatible ChatGPT API path)
- Working: Muse Spark (`muse-spark-1.3`) — same tools, no error

## Impact

Paid ChatGPT API usage through AutoClaw is **completely unusable** while this plugin is loaded — 100% failure rate on all turns, regardless of prompt content.

## Where to file

- Upstream: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues (source per `docs.openclaw.ai`)
- Title suggestion: `autoclaw-productivity email pattern uses regex lookaround, rejected by OpenAI API`

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect state leads to a forced Gateway restart)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On a macOS laptop running OpenClaw 2026.10.2, ordinary lid-close sleep followed by DarkWake or lid-open wake repeatedly expires the local state-owner heartbeat, triggers `SIGUSR2` Gateway restart, and can cause repeated startup failures while the host continues sleeping.

This is a **whole-Gateway restart**, not just a channel/WebSocket reconnect. Three observed restart chains below align with OS wake events. An isolated experiment with the actual shipped heartbeat worker also reproduces the stale-heartbeat condition without network access, lock replacement, or a competing Gateway.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed on this installation:

1. Run OpenClaw 2026.10.2 as its macOS LaunchAgent.
2. Close the laptop lid and allow system sleep for more than 60 seconds.
3. Let the host DarkWake, or open the lid to resume it.
4. Compare `pmset -g log` with Gateway logs: the wake is followed by `utimes heartbeat renewal did not complete within 60 seconds` and `received SIGUSR2; restarting`.
5. If the lid remains closed and macOS resumes sleeping between brief DarkWake windows, startup can itself lose state ownership and fail repeatedly.

Three natural occurrences were collected; no forced sleep, power-setting changes, live-Gateway signals, or config changes were performed during this investigation. This does not claim every lid-close causes a restart, especially sleeps shorter than the deadline.

### Expected behavior

The existing host-thaw recovery path logs `restarting channels when idle and refreshing health`. A host that resumes with unchanged physical custody should be able to recover instead of treating elapsed system-sleep time alone as proof of lost state ownership. Actual removal/replacement of a lock or a successor owner must still fence access. No known-good release for this specific state-owner heartbeat behavior has been verified.

### Actual behavior

The local state-owner watchdog expires on wake, fences state access, and the Gateway restarts. Restart cleanup then reports state-ownership and retained-plugin-resource errors. During continued sleep/DarkWake cycles, new processes can fail startup under `required secrets are unavailable`, with the nested cause explicitly being inability to verify **local SQLite state ownership**.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.2, build `b8952d4`; upstream commit `b8952d477f0c932d8ddc6da5c89cab5a169b6ff1`. Both CLI and running Gateway report 2026.10.2.

### Operating system

macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), Darwin 27.0.0, arm64. Node.js v26.8.2.

### Install method

Managed npm runtime, macOS user LaunchAgent (`ai.openclaw.gateway`), Node entrypoint `dist/index.js gateway --port 18789`, loopback binding. `ExitTimeOut=20000ms` per startup logs.

### Model

Default `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, fallback `deepseek/deepseek-flash`. The isolated heartbeat reproduction does not invoke any model.

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw → OpenAI; configured fallback OpenClaw → DeepSeek. The evidence concerns a local file-lock/worker deadline, not a model request.

### Logs

All times below are Asia/Shanghai / UTC+08:00. Paths and lock identifiers have been redacted; no chat content, credentials, or full stability snapshots are published.

**Occurrence A: Oct 13, lid-open wake, new Gateway PID confirmed**

```text
# pmset -g log
2026-10-13 09:51:09 +0800 Sleep     Entering Sleep state due to 'Clamshell Sleep'
2026-10-13 09:51:14 +0800 DarkWake  DarkWake from Deep Idle
2026-10-13 09:51:28 +0800 Sleep     Entering Sleep state due to 'Maintenance Sleep' [245 secs]
2026-10-13 09:55:33 +0800 Wake      Wake from Deep Idle ... lid ... HID Activity

# Gateway log (exact messages; path redactions only)
2026-10-13T09:55:33.592+08:00 [health] host timing gap detected: process was frozen ~241561ms; restarting channels when idle and refreshing health
2026-10-13T09:55:33.738+08:00 [state] Gateway state ownership is no longer current at <HOME>/.openclaw/tmp/openclaw-501/state.<id>.lock: utimes heartbeat renewal did not complete within 60 seconds; restart the Gateway.
2026-10-13T09:55:33.740+08:00 [gateway] received SIGUSR2; restarting
2026-10-13T09:55:36.453+08:00 [shutdown] failed in 2646ms
2026-10-13T09:55:36.454+08:00 [gateway] shutdown step failed (gateway close): Plugin runtime still owns resources; inspect cleanup failures before retrying Gateway close. | OpenClaw state ownership at <HOME>/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite could not be verified; retry after maintenance finishes.
2026-10-13T09:55:40.629+08:00 [gateway] shutdown budget at startup: drain=5000ms shutdown=15000ms reserve=10000ms exitMargin=5000ms; source=launchd ExitTimeOut=20000ms
2026-10-13T09:56:09.130+08:00 [gateway] ready
```

The generated restart-failure stability bundle identifies old PID **69210**. A later process snapshot shows the running LaunchAgent PID **72125**, parent PID **1**, start time **09:55:36**. This distinguishes a process restart from a reconnect or duplicate startup notification. OS boot time remains **2026-09-29 19:30:58**, so the Mac itself did not reboot.

**Occurrence B: Oct 13, DarkWake after 68 seconds of clamshell sleep**

```text
# pmset, abridged
2026-10-13 06:58:37 +0800 Sleep     Clamshell Sleep [68 secs]
2026-10-13 06:59:45 +0800 DarkWake  DarkWake from Deep Idle
2026-10-13 06:59:50 +0800 Sleep     Maintenance Sleep [196 secs]

# Gateway
2026-10-13T06:59:45.096+08:00 [state] Gateway state ownership is no longer current at <HOME>/.openclaw/tmp/openclaw-501/state.<id>.lock: utimes heartbeat renewal did not complete within 60 seconds; restart the Gateway.
2026-10-13T06:59:45.099+08:00 [gateway] received SIGUSR2; restarting
2026-10-13T06:59:47.728+08:00 [shutdown] failed in 2440ms
2026-10-13T07:21:04.637+08:00 [state] Gateway state ownership is no longer current at <HOME>/.openclaw/tmp/openclaw-501/state.<id>.lock: utimes heartbeat renewal did not complete within 60 seconds; restart the Gateway.
2026-10-13T07:29:09.010+08:00 Gateway failed to start: Startup failed: required secrets are unavailable. Error: OpenClaw state ownership at <HOME>/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite could not be verified; retry after maintenance finishes.. Run openclaw gateway status --deep for diagnostics.
2026-10-13T07:33:43.671+08:00 Gateway failed to start: Shared-state read and cleanup failed | OpenClaw state ownership at <HOME>/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite could not be verified; retry after maintenance finishes.. Run openclaw gateway status --deep for diagnostics.
2026-10-13T07:34:14.266+08:00 [gateway] ready
```

**Occurrence C: Oct 12, DarkWake after 150 seconds, prolonged startup-failure sequence**

```text
# pmset, abridged
2026-10-12 18:52:15 +0800 Sleep     Clamshell Sleep [150 secs]
2026-10-12 18:54:45 +0800 DarkWake  DarkWake from Deep Idle
2026-10-12 18:54:55 +0800 Sleep     Maintenance Sleep [174 secs]

# Gateway
2026-10-12T18:54:45.503+08:00 [state] Gateway state ownership is no longer current at <HOME>/.openclaw/tmp/openclaw-501/state.<id>.lock: utimes heartbeat renewal did not complete within 60 seconds; restart the Gateway.
2026-10-12T18:54:45.506+08:00 [gateway] received SIGUSR2; restarting
2026-10-12T18:54:47.973+08:00 [shutdown] failed in 2430ms
2026-10-12T19:01:19.305+08:00 Gateway failed to start: Startup failed: required secrets are unavailable. Error: OpenClaw state ownership at <HOME>/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite could not be verified; retry after maintenance finishes.. Run openclaw gateway status --deep for diagnostics.
```

The same nested ownership-related startup error recurs at **19:19:08, 19:51:17, 20:24:14, 20:49:53, 20:52:24, 20:55:22**. `pmset` records alternating short DarkWake windows and sleep throughout that interval; lid-open wake is **20:55:18**, and Gateway becomes ready at **20:55:53.388**. This is roughly two hours between the first restart and readiness, not necessarily two hours of active runtime.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

#### Verified source paths at the installed revision

- [Parent heartbeat watchdog](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b8952d477f0c932d8ddc6da5c89cab5a169b6ff1/src/infra/gateway-state-owner-heartbeat.ts#L14): `Date.now` clock; `failureMs: 60_000`; `inspect()` computes `60_000 - age` and invokes `onLost()` when nonpositive.
- [Heartbeat worker runtime](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b8952d477f0c932d8ddc6da5c89cab5a169b6ff1/src/infra/gateway-state-owner-heartbeat.runtime.ts#L20): also uses `Date.now`; `beat()` checks deadline **before** opening/verifying/renewing locks and calls `stop()` if expired. A >60s whole-process suspension cannot be recovered merely by letting this worker run first on thaw.
- [Owner fencing](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b8952d477f0c932d8ddc6da5c89cab5a169b6ff1/src/infra/gateway-state-owner.ts#L161): `loseOwner()` stops the worker, sets `accepting=false`, and aborts the owner signal.
- [Heartbeat/lease constants](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b8952d477f0c932d8ddc6da5c89cab5a169b6ff1/src/infra/gateway-lock-payload.ts#L10): production renewal cadence **15s**, stale-lock threshold **90s**, versus watchdog failure at **60s**.
- [Existing heartbeat tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b8952d477f0c932d8ddc6da5c89cab5a169b6ff1/src/infra/gateway-state-owner.heartbeat.test.ts): cover main-thread blocking, clock rollback, renewal failures, and successor protection; these do not establish recovery after the entire process/worker is suspended with unchanged custody.

The shipped `dist/gateway-state-owner-DovQXuDu.mjs` and `dist/infra/gateway-state-owner-heartbeat.worker.js` were checked against the source above. Relevant logic matches.

#### Isolated reproduction using the shipped worker

Executed on this host with Node v26.8.2. Only a new test process was suspended via `SIGSTOP` for 65s and resumed via `SIGCONT`. The production Gateway was untouched. The worker used a fresh synthetic lock, the production **60,000ms failure deadline**, and a **5s renewal cadence** (production is 15s). The parent computed the same deadline formula; this harness is **not** a full Gateway integration test.

Observed output:

```json
{"ageMs":65012,"unchangedLastBeat":true,"unchangedLockContent":true,"parentPidStillAlive":true,"watchdogWouldCallOnLost":true}
```

Exit code 0. The actual worker does not refresh `lastBeat` after thaw even though no lock was replaced and the owner process survived. No model, channel, or network request is involved.

<details>
<summary>Portable minimal harness</summary>

Set `HEARTBEAT_WORKER` to the absolute path of the installed `dist/infra/gateway-state-owner-heartbeat.worker.js`. Save the following as `repro.mjs` and run it as a **separate test process**, not in the Gateway. After `READY`, send that test PID `SIGSTOP`, wait 65 seconds, and send it `SIGCONT`.

```js
import fs from 'node:fs';
import os from 'node:os';
import path from 'node:path';
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
import { Worker, MessageChannel } from 'node:worker_threads';

const dir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'openclaw-suspend-repro-'));
const lockPath = path.join(dir, 'synthetic.lock');
const raw = JSON.stringify({ pid: process.pid, purpose: 'isolated test' });
fs.writeFileSync(lockPath, raw);
const lastBeat = new BigInt64Array(new SharedArrayBuffer(8));
Atomics.store(lastBeat, 0, BigInt(Date.now()));
const { port1, port2 } = new MessageChannel();
const worker = new Worker(pathToFileURL(process.env.HEARTBEAT_WORKER), {
  workerData: { locks: { [lockPath]: raw }, intervalMs: 5000,
    failureMs: 60000, lastBeat: lastBeat.buffer, events: port2 },
  transferList: [port2],
});
port1.on('message', () => {});
worker.once('message', () => {
  const before = Atomics.load(lastBeat, 0);
  console.log(`READY pid=${process.pid}`);
  setTimeout(async () => {
    const after = Atomics.load(lastBeat, 0);
    const age = Date.now() - Number(after);
    const remaining = age < 0 ? 0 : 60000 - age;
    console.log({ ageMs: age, unchangedLastBeat: before === after,
      unchangedLockContent: fs.readFileSync(lockPath, 'utf8') === raw,
      watchdogWouldCallOnLost: remaining <= 0 });
    await worker.terminate();
    port1.close();
  }, 1500);
});
worker.on('error', console.error);
```

This emulates scheduler suspension; the actual macOS sleep/wake evidence is the independent `pmset` timeline above.

</details>

### Impact and severity

- Affected: one observed macOS laptop, LaunchAgent Gateway and its Feishu direct-chat availability.
- Frequency: **three captured full-Gateway restart chains**, Oct 12–13; additional startup ownership failures during sleep. Not asserted to occur on every sleep cycle or every Mac.
- Consequence: Gateway process replacement and startup notifications after lid-close sleep; repeated startup failures while closed. One observed restart-to-readiness interval lasted roughly two hours.
- No evidence of data loss. Missed-message counts were not measured.

### Additional information

- After collection, `openclaw gateway status --deep` reports running PID 72125, Gateway version 2026.10.2, and connectivity probe `ok`.
- Current battery/AC idle `sleep=0` does not prevent clamshell sleep; `pmset` explicitly records it. No power settings were changed.
- Other earlier Oct 12 `SIGTERM` events and a 21:12 explicitly requested restart are **excluded** from this causal claim.
- Wi-Fi loss is present in some DarkWake records, but it does not establish that network loss caused the restart. The directly logged trigger is local heartbeat expiry; the isolated test needs no network.
- Related but distinct: #169829 (negative wall-clock age on WSL2) and #166809 (Feishu WebSocket disconnects on macOS thaw). This report is **positive elapsed wall-clock age after system sleep**, with whole-Gateway state-owner fencing/restart.

**Requested design investigation:** distinguish system suspend/thaw from an actual ownership change, then revalidate physical custody before choosing safe recovery or fencing. Please preserve successor/replaced-lock protection and the cross-runtime clock-origin constraints noted in source. A simple unconditional deadline reset or increasing the timeout alone is not a demonstrated safe fix; both parent and worker deadline checks need consideration. No local code patch or workaround was applied.

issues.body:
## Environment
- OpenClaw **2026.10.5-beta.2** (`467e83d`), systemd **user** unit `openclaw-gateway`
- Host: **WSL2** (Ubuntu), gateway bound to `127.0.0.1:18789`
- Trigger: `openclaw doctor --fix` run against a **live** owning Gateway

## Symptom
`doctor --fix` cannot enter maintenance while the Gateway owns `state/openclaw.sqlite`, so it force-stopped the Gateway **mid-flight** and then **restarted it**. Its own log:

```
WARNING: Gateway maintenance drain deadline reached: resident shutdown budget unknown; … stopping with
root-request=1 (1 active gateway request(s): startup:subagent-recovery). In-flight work may be
interrupted. No lifecycle write custody was reported.
```

The restarted Gateway is **up** (`/health` 200, websocket serving) but **every** cron, plugin and WAL job fails, indefinitely:

```
[plugins] device-pair: notify poll failed: Failed to list plugin state entries. | OpenClaw state
ownership at /home/wayne/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite could not be verified; retry after
maintenance finishes.
[state/db] Shared-state WAL maintenance failed error="OpenClaw state ownership at … could not be
verified; retry after maintenance finishes."
[cron/maintenance] Cron maintenance failed error="… could not be verified; retry after maintenance
finishes."
```

`doctor` names the same ownership record both **before and after** its restart, so the restart does not clear it:

```
[state] Gateway state ownership is no longer current at …/tmp/openclaw-1000/state.<id>.lock:
heartbeat clock moved backwards; restart the Gateway.
```

## Root cause (read from the shipped dist)
`assertPersistedStateDatabaseAccessAllowed({databasePath, ownerPath, assertMaintenance})` (in `dist/managed-handoff-runtime.mjs` and `dist/gateway-state-owner-*.mjs`) throws **"…could not be verified; retry after maintenance finishes"** **not** when a maintenance is running, but when the owner record at `ownerPath` is:

```js
try { raw = fs.readFileSync(ownerPath, "utf8"); }
catch (e) { if (extractErrorCode(e) === "ENOENT") return;   // MISSING → allowed
            throw new Error(unavailable, { cause: e }); }     // any other read error → the message
const owner = parseGatewayLockPayload(raw);
if (!owner) throw unavailable;                                // unparseable
if (!Number.isSafeInteger(owner.pid) || owner.pid <= 0) throw unavailable;
if (isGatewayStateOwnerDefinitelyStale(owner, ownerPath)) return;
if (!isPidAlive(owner.pid)) throw new Error(unavailable);     // ← owner PID is DEAD
const role = owner.role ?? "gateway";
if (role === "gateway" || role === "agent-embedded") return;  // live gateway record → allowed
```

`ownerPath = resolveGatewayStateOwnerPath(databasePath)` → the gateway lock dir for the state dir, i.e. `~/.openclaw/tmp/openclaw-1000/state.<hash>.lock`.

So the **message is a misnomer**: a *missing* record is accepted and a live `role:"gateway"` record is accepted, which means the failure is a **stale owner record whose PID is dead** — left behind by the forced/mid-flight stop. It persists on disk, so the freshly-started Gateway (a live PID) keeps tripping on the previous owner's dead PID, and `doctor`'s own restart cannot clear it.

**Note:** `heartbeat clock moved backwards` is a **different** branch (the `gateway-state-owner` heartbeat worker: `age = Date.now() - lastBeat < 0`) and is already reported as #169829. It is not this defect.

## Reproducible steps
1. With the Gateway running and owning `state/openclaw.sqlite`, run `openclaw doctor --fix`.
2. doctor force-stops the Gateway (drain deadline: an in-flight `startup:subagent-recovery`) and restarts it.
3. The restarted Gateway logs the ownership message continuously and every cron/plugin/maintenance job fails until the operator opens a Gateway-*stopped* maintenance window.

## Expected behaviour
- A forced/mid-flight stop should rewrite or clear the persisted owner record (the code already treats a **missing** record as allowed, so a dead-PID record should be treated the same), or the restarted owner should re-establish it.
- An unreadable/stale owner record should not be described as "maintenance finishes".

## Actual behaviour
The Gateway runs but cannot verify state ownership; all background work fails until an operator manually repairs it.

## Suggested fix
- On a forced stop, clear/rewrite the persisted owner record (treat a dead-PID owner as allowed, exactly like `ENOENT`).
- Separate the error text: a dead/unreadable owner record is not "maintenance in progress".

## Related
- #169829 — the sibling `heartbeat clock moved backwards` self-restart (wall-clock step); same code family, different branch/message.
- #164986 — update repair fails at `finalize:plugins` after Doctor **offline maintenance**.
- #158607 — deferred context maintenance loses admission ownership after caller release.
- #170525 — macOS lid-close sleep expires the state-owner heartbeat and forces a Gateway restart on wake.

## Local workaround
The documented Gateway-*stopped* window: arm `.gateway-hold` → stop the guard timer → stop the Gateway → `doctor --fix` → start the Gateway → start the guard timer. A clean stop rewrites the owner record (a forced stop is what leaves it dead).

issues.body:
## Summary
A scheduled/deferred gateway restart (we run a daily one at 10:00 to contain 170458) is postponed for about an hour every day because the "busy" gate counts idle child processes, specifically orphaned `codex app-server` children, as active work.

## Observed (OpenClaw 2026.9.6, Linux x64)
- The restart waited ~1 h daily before its gate allowed it, with no real turns in flight.
- At the time the gateway had 16–30 idle `codex app-server` children (see the codex orphan issue). Once they were killed, nothing kept the gate busy.

## Expected
- The busy gate should count in-flight turns/runs and active tool work, not the existence of child processes.
- Idle or orphaned helpers should not be able to block a restart; it should proceed and reap them.
- The deferral should log what it's waiting on, so operators can see why.

I’m upgrading an existing macOS installation from OpenClaw 2026.5.12 (f066dd2) to 2026.10.2 (b8952d4) and need a supported migration path that preserves authentication profiles and session history.

- Existing Codex OAuth profiles contain credential references.

Inspection of the new authentication flow shows that browser/device login reads the existing auth store and raises AUTH_PROFILE_MIGRATION_REQUIRED before sign-in. A named profile does not avoid that check.

The documented 2026.9.7 migration bridge supports database schemas only through 19 and cannot open this schema-20 database. We have not established a supported in-place recovery path. No full pre-update state backup was found in the locations checked.

2. How should reference-only credentials and an unreferenced authentication sidecar be handled through supported tooling?
3. What verification should be completed before restarting into the new release?

No authentication reset, database downgrade, credential decryption or sidecar removal has been performed. These findings concern one existing installation; no clean-environment reproduction is available.

issues.body:
**Environment:** OpenClaw 2026.9.9, Node 24.21.0, Linux, systemd user service (KillMode=mixed), npm-global install

## Problem
`openclaw update` (handoff to 2026.10.1) fails after ~8.5 s with `managed-service-handoff-failed`.
The handoff log shows ownership transfer OK, then the updater refuses with `update-recovery-pending`.
Same block on 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-12. The Gateway stays on 2026.9.9.

## Cause
A pending publication op (`4289c90c-27c5-4bf7-8cba-9ca999f854ee`, phase `publication-complete`, 2026.9.7 -> 2026.9.8) is still anchored next to the install (`.openclaw.package-activation-*` and its `.control`).
It dates from a 2026-10-06 update whose database rollback failed with `database is locked` / `Cannot remove OpenClaw state directory while another SQLite connection is active`. The connection that caused that contention was not identified.
The installed 2026.9.9 matches neither generation recorded in that op, so the helper refuses:

> Package publication recovery refused: The installed package is not either recorded generation.

## Tried
- `openclaw update repair --json --yes`: runs `doctor --repair`, ends `status: warning`, anchor untouched.
- `openclaw update --dry-run --tag 2026.9.9 --json`: still `update-recovery-pending`, same op.
- `collectInstalledGlobalPackageErrors`: no errors, so the installed package inventory is intact (the generic `runtime-verification-failed` code does not indicate corruption).
- Journal, lease, identities and anchor were NOT edited by hand.
- Unit/drop-in customizations are not implicated.

Also: 4 plugins (brave, llama-cpp, msteams, tokenjuice) are stuck at 2026.7.x/2026.9.7 because the registry only offers builds requiring API >= 2026.10.2.

## Expected
A supported way to close a publication op whose recorded generations were both superseded: verify the current package and migrated DBs, preserve the originals, close the transaction. Or `update repair` handling this case.

## Related
#170032 (publication-recovery refusal on macOS), #170305 (`update-recovery-pending` on 2026.9.9), #143752 (interrupted activation recovery).

issues.body:
## Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash).

## Beta release blocker

No.

## Summary

The A2A channel returns generic unsupported-operation error `-32004` for recognized push notification configuration methods, instead of the protocol-required `-32003` for an agent advertising `pushNotifications: false`.

## Steps to reproduce

Reproduced against the exact source at `1f86b827717777114caf0184f1dfc77adf050cc6` using the existing A2A HTTP test fixture and a separate isolated loopback HTTP harness, not an operator's running Gateway.

1. Create an A2A HTTP handler with a configured synthetic peer token, as in `extensions/a2a/src/http.test.ts`. Its public Agent Card advertises `pushNotifications: false`.
2. Send an authenticated JSON-RPC request to `/a2a/v1`:

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": "push-config",
  "method": "CreateTaskPushNotificationConfig",
  "params": {
    "taskId": "example-task",
    "url": "https://example.test/push"
  }
}
```

3. Inspect `error.code`. The same mismatch occurs for `GetTaskPushNotificationConfig`, `ListTaskPushNotificationConfigs`, and `DeleteTaskPushNotificationConfig`, and the existing recognized spellings `SetTaskPushNotificationConfig` and `ListTaskPushNotificationConfig`.

## Expected behavior

JSON-RPC error `-32003` (`PushNotificationNotSupportedError`). A2A v1.0.1 [capability validation](https://github.com/a2aproject/A2A/blob/v1.0.1/docs/specification.md#334-capability-validation) requires that error for push configuration operations when push support is false or absent; [error mappings](https://github.com/a2aproject/A2A/blob/v1.0.1/docs/specification.md#54-error-code-mappings) assign `-32003`.

Push support should remain disabled. Other unsupported operations should continue returning `-32004`, and unknown method names `-32601`.

## Actual behavior

HTTP 200 with this JSON-RPC error:

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": "push-config",
  "error": {
    "code": -32004,
    "message": "Unsupported operation; supported methods are SendMessage and GetTask"
  }
}
```

## Environment

- OpenClaw source: `1f86b827717777114caf0184f1dfc77adf050cc6`.
- Operating system: macOS `26.6.1`.
- Install method: isolated source worktree, existing dependency copy; Node `26.7.0`, Vitest `5.0.1`.
- Model/provider: none. The request is rejected before agent dispatch.
- Request path: synthetic authenticated peer → isolated A2A HTTP handler.

## Evidence

Native regression run on the original source: **7 failures / 50 passes**. All seven failures are expected `-32003` versus actual `-32004`: six recognized method spellings plus mixed-batch response coverage. Existing neighboring methods, authentication, and discovery tests pass.

A separate exact-source loopback HTTP harness produced the same seven failures. It used real HTTP and Zod but explicitly stubbed SDK seams; it is supplemental evidence, not production Gateway proof.

## Impact and severity

Authenticated A2A callers receive the wrong protocol error classification for unsupported push configuration. This occurred for all six tested recognized spellings. No push registration, callback, or task dispatch occurred; downstream client fallback behavior was not measured.

## Additional information

This report does not request push notification support, persistence, or new aliases. No known-good version was established, so this is not claimed as a regression.

issues.title: [Bug]: a channel message containing `Authorization: Bearer <token>` fails its turn with "Transcript idempotency key ... conflicts with the admitted message"
issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

An inbound channel message whose text contains `Authorization: Bearer <token>` fails its turn. The run throws `Transcript idempotency key "channel-user:v1:..." conflicts with the admitted message.`, every model in the fallback chain fails the same way, and the user gets "OpenClaw couldn't finish this reply". The message is redacted twice on its way to the run's transcript write, and the second pass is not a no-op for this header: the stored copy holds `Authorization: Bearer eyJhbG…2C31` and the run's copy `Authorization: Bearer ***`, so the replay check sees two different messages under one key.

### Steps to reproduce

QA Lab's isolated Gateway (`createQaGatewayChild`, mock OpenAI provider, QA channel) on main `c30579e8509`, driven from a throwaway vitest file that sends each message with `state.addInboundMessage` and waits for the outbound reply. One direct message per case, each ending ``Reply with only this exact marker: `X` ``:

| message body | chars | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `plain words only` | 16 | replied |
| prose lines | 2,000 | replied |
| prose lines | 50,000 | replied |
| `log line Authorization: Bearer <JWT> status=200` | 125 | "OpenClaw couldn't finish this reply" |
| that line repeated with distinct JWTs | 2,050 | "OpenClaw couldn't finish this reply" |
| `token glpat-<32 chars> in a log` | 53 | replied |

The same reply came back in an earlier run with a 50,000-character message of these lines, whose Gateway log reads `model fallback decision: decision=candidate_failed ... detail=Transcript idempotency key "channel-user:v1:..." conflicts with the admitted message.`, then `All models failed (2)`; no request reached the mock provider. I did not capture the log for the 125-character case.

Redaction alone, on main `c2d584acd704`, `redactSensitiveText` applied twice (default and `tools` mode give the same results):

| input | first pass | second pass |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Authorization: Bearer <JWT>` | `Authorization: Bearer eyJhbG…2C31` | `Authorization: Bearer ***` |
| `Authorization: Bearer <64-char opaque token>` | `Authorization: Bearer A1b2C3…C3d4` | `Authorization: Bearer ***` |
| `https://deploy:<32 chars>@internal.example.test/path` | `https://deploy:A1b2C3…C3d4@internal.example.test/path` | `https://deploy:***@internal.example.test/path` |
| a bare JWT, a `glpat-` token | a hint | unchanged |

### Expected behavior

The message is answered. Either redacting redacted text leaves it unchanged, or the run's transcript write does not redact the admitted copy a second time.

### Actual behavior

I instrumented the conflict check in `appendTranscriptMessageInTransaction` (`session-accessor.sqlite-transcript-message-append.ts`) on `c30579e8509`. The stored message holds `Authorization: Bearer eyJhbG…2C31`; the message the caller passes in already reads `Authorization: Bearer ***`, with `messageAlreadyRedacted` unset. A second probe logged every session-manager append of that message. Only the already-redacted copy goes through `SessionManager.appendMessageWithTranscriptAnchorAsync`, and every time from the runtime's user-turn write: `session-tool-result-guard.ts` `appendRequest` -> `withRuntimeUserTurnTranscriptRecorder` (inside `withPendingInput`) -> `appendMessageWithTranscriptAnchorAsync` -> `appendEntryAsync`. `appendEntryAsync` (`session-manager-append.ts`) then runs `prepareTranscriptMessageAppendForWorker` on it, which calls `redactTranscriptMessageForStorage` -> `redactTranscriptMessage` -> `redactSensitiveFieldValue` a second time and turns the hint into `***`. So the pending input's message, which already carries the admission's redaction decision, is redacted again before the worker compares it with the stored copy.

What I tried: making `maskToken` return a value that already reads as a mask (`***` or `xxxxxx…yyyy`) unchanged. All six cases above then reply. It also changes 5 tests in `src/logging` on `c2d584acd704`: `redact.test.ts` > "masks credential headers across text and serialized forms", two in `subsystem.test.ts`, and two in `redact-byte-identity.test.ts`. Those expect a value that a token rule hinted and an env, CLI or header rule then masks again to end as `***` (`API_KEY=***`, `--password=***`). With the fixed point they keep the hint, which shows 10 characters of the secret. So I don't think the fix belongs in `maskToken`. My read is that the runtime's user-turn write should not prepare the pending input's message again, for example by carrying `messageAlreadyRedacted` for a message that comes from pending-input custody. Making the header-credential and URL-password rules skip their own hint would also close it, but only for those two rules.

### OpenClaw version

main `c30579e8509` (end-to-end repro and the trace above) and `c2d584acd704` (redaction measurements). Re-run on main `aec89935b8f` on 2026-10-11, after #168539 routed transcript appends through the session actor: the same two bearer messages fail and the other four reply, and `redactSensitiveText` is still not idempotent for both Authorization cases. I have not re-traced the call path on `aec89935b8f`.

### Operating system

macOS 26.6.2, M4 Pro.

### Install method

Source checkout, `pnpm`.

### Provider / routing chain

QA Lab mock OpenAI provider; the turn fails before the provider is called.

### Impact and severity

A user who pastes a request log or a curl command with an `Authorization: Bearer` header gets no answer, and every fallback model fails the same way. I measured it through the QA channel only; nothing in the path traced above is specific to it. URL passwords (`https://user:pass@host`) are not idempotent either and likely fail the same way; I did not run that case end to end.

### Additional information

A unit test I wrote for this (redacting redacted text changes nothing, five cases, plus a registered secret that reads as a mask stays masked) fails 3 of 6 on `c2d584acd704`: both Authorization cases and the URL password. Happy to open a PR with it once the intended fix point is clear.

issues.body:
## Summary
When an agent's `heartbeat` config sets an `activeHours` window but omits `every` (relying on the default 30m cadence), the `start`/`end` time strings are never validated. Garbage like `start: "99:99"` or `end: "not-a-time"` is accepted by config load, and at runtime the unparseable window is treated as permissive, so the heartbeat fires 24/7 instead of only during the intended window (e.g. 09:00-17:00).

## Environment
- Commit: d3ff48c51f4ff4cf3594c04e127c8e3ae83ba021 (origin/main at time of filing)
- Surface: config validation (`HeartbeatSchema`) for `agents.defaults.heartbeat` and `agents.list[].heartbeat`, plus heartbeat active-hours runtime.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Configure a heartbeat with an active-hours window but no `every`, using a malformed time, e.g. `agents.defaults.heartbeat = { activeHours: { start: "99:99", end: "17:00" } }`.
2. Load the config (any real config load validates this schema).
3. The config is accepted with no validation error.

## Expected
The malformed `activeHours.start`/`activeHours.end` should be rejected with `invalid time (use "HH:MM" 24h format)`, exactly as it is when `every` is also present.

## Actual
The config is accepted. At runtime the window silently degrades to "always active", so the heartbeat runs around the clock at the default cadence instead of being restricted to the configured hours.

## Root cause (if known)
`src/config/zod-schema.agent-runtime.ts:111-114` in `HeartbeatSchema`'s `superRefine`:

```ts
.superRefine((val, ctx) => {
  if (!val.every) {
    return;               // early return BEFORE the activeHours time-format checks
  }
  try {
    parseDurationMs(val.every, { defaultUnit: "m" });
  } catch { ... }

  const active = val.activeHours;
  if (!active) return;
  // validateTime(active.start ...) / validateTime(active.end ...)  // lines 129-163, never reached when `every` is unset
```

Because the `if (!val.every) return;` guard fires before the `activeHours` time-format block, the `start`/`end` strings are only validated when `every` is also set. With `every` omitted, any string passes.

The runtime then relies on the schema having validated the window. `src/infra/heartbeat-active-hours.ts:87-89` treats an unparseable `start`/`end` as permissive (returns `true`, i.e. inside the window), and heartbeat scheduling falls back to `DEFAULT_HEARTBEAT_EVERY` (`src/infra/heartbeat-summary.ts:58-62`) when `every` is unset. So the intended active-hours restriction is dropped silently.

Proposed minimal fix: do not gate `activeHours` validation on `every`. Wrap only the duration parse in `if (val.every) { ... }` and drop the early return, keeping `const active = val.activeHours; if (!active) return;` before the unchanged `validateTime(start)` / `validateTime(end)` block. Valid configs are unaffected.

## Sibling surfaces
`HeartbeatSchema` (line 83) is used at `zod-schema.agent-defaults.ts:238` (`agents.defaults.heartbeat`) and `zod-schema.agent-runtime.ts:1069` (`agents.list[].heartbeat`), both flowing through `AgentsSchema` into the top-level config validated on every real config load, so both heartbeat config sites are affected. This is distinct from PR #33973 (closed), which trimmed whitespace in the runtime parser `parseActiveHoursTime`, not the schema `every` gate.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: heartbeat activeHours start/end time strings skip format validation when `every` is omitted.
Real environment tested: real production `HeartbeatSchema.safeParse` from `src/config/zod-schema.agent-runtime.ts`, driven at commit d3ff48c51f4ff4cf3594c04e127c8e3ae83ba021.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node_modules/.bin/tsx heartbeat-activehours-gap.mts` importing the real `HeartbeatSchema` and calling `safeParse` on three inputs.
Evidence after fix:
```
# OBSERVED (buggy, origin/main d3ff48c)
[with every + bad start] input = {"every":"30m","activeHours":{"start":"99:99","end":"17:00"}}
  success = false
  issues = [ 'activeHours.start: invalid time (use "HH:MM" 24h format)' ]

[no every + bad start] input = {"activeHours":{"start":"99:99","end":"17:00"}}
  success = true

[no every + bad end] input = {"activeHours":{"start":"09:00","end":"not-a-time"}}
  success = true

# EXPECTED (correct behavior on identical inputs, with the early-return gate removed)
[with every + bad start] input = {"every":"30m","activeHours":{"start":"99:99","end":"17:00"}}
  success = false
  issues = [ 'activeHours.start: invalid time (use "HH:MM" 24h format)' ]

[no every + bad start] input = {"activeHours":{"start":"99:99","end":"17:00"}}
  success = false
  issues = [ 'activeHours.start: invalid time (use "HH:MM" 24h format)' ]

[no every + bad end] input = {"activeHours":{"start":"09:00","end":"not-a-time"}}
  success = false
  issues = [ 'activeHours.end: invalid time (use "HH:MM" 24h format)' ]
```
Observed result after fix: on origin/main the two no-`every` cases with garbage times are accepted (success=true); removing the early-return gate makes them rejected with the same time-format error the with-`every` control already produces.
What was not tested: end-to-end scheduler timing (whether the heartbeat literally fires outside the window over wall-clock time) was not driven; the runtime-consequence claim rests on reading `heartbeat-active-hours.ts:87-89` and `heartbeat-summary.ts:58-62`, not a live scheduler run. Timezone/overnight-range handling unchanged.

issues.body:
## Summary

Two related regressions in **OpenClaw 2026.5.22** affecting Telegram-channel voice-note processing and the ability to downgrade to recover.

## Bug 1 — `nativeHook.invoke: native hook relay not found` on Telegram inbound

After upgrading from 2026.5.20 → 2026.5.22, Telegram inbound voice notes routed through a configured persona (in our case `clordlethird` — a `channels.telegram.accounts` entry) return "Something went wrong while processing your request. Please try again." to the user.

Gateway log (`~/Library/Logs/openclaw/gateway.log`) shows the cause:

```
2026-05-25T20:02:27.209+01:00 [ws] ⇄ res ✗ nativeHook.invoke 2ms errorCode=INVALID_REQUEST errorMessage=native hook relay not found conn=0a06fd94…2c0d id=70b1bb92…d291
[…7 more identical errors in a 25ms window across different conn ids…]
2026-05-25T20:10:19.885+01:00 [ws] ⇄ res ✗ nativeHook.invoke 0ms errorCode=INVALID_REQUEST errorMessage=native hook relay not found conn=43ffc24f…3da0 id=a29f4143…e575
2026-05-25T20:17:42.052+01:00 [ws] ⇄ res ✗ nativeHook.invoke 0ms errorCode=INVALID_REQUEST errorMessage=native hook relay not found conn=fd3774ac…9bea id=0db2fa71…57d4
```

Bursts coincide with inbound voice notes arriving on the configured telegram persona. The error suggests something in the message-processing pipeline calls `nativeHook.invoke` for a hook ID that the relay registry doesn't have registered.

Same config on **2026.5.20 works without these errors** — verified on a peer machine that downgraded successfully.

### Environment

- macOS 26 Tahoe (Mac mini, arm64)
- OpenClaw 2026.5.22 installed via `npm install -g openclaw@2026.5.22`
- 3 telegram personas configured: `default`, `clawdiboi2`, `clordlethird`
- Codex ChatGPT-OAuth (gpt-5.5, thinking=xhigh)
- `OPENCLAW_CODEX_COMPACTION_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS=3600000`, `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192`
- Compaction provider spoof active (model_provider=openai-custom, related to issue #86019)

## Bug 2 — 5.20 binary refuses to start against 5.22-written config (forward-incompat schema)

When attempting to downgrade after Bug 1:

```
$ npm install -g openclaw@2026.5.20  # succeeds
$ openclaw gateway restart
Gateway restart blocked: Refusing to restart the gateway service because this OpenClaw binary (2026.5.20) is older than the config last written by OpenClaw 2026.5.22.
Tip: Set OPENCLAW_ALLOW_OLDER_BINARY_DESTRUCTIVE_ACTIONS=1 only for an intentional downgrade or recovery action.

$ OPENCLAW_ALLOW_OLDER_BINARY_DESTRUCTIVE_ACTIONS=1 openclaw gateway restart
Service runtime: status=stopped, state=active
Gateway port 18789 status: free.
Gateway restart failed after 14s: service stayed stopped and health checks never came up.
```

Gateway then enters EX_CONFIG (exit 78) respawn death-loop:
```
2026-05-25T20:18:35.351+01:00 [gateway] loading configuration…
2026-05-25T20:18:46.111+01:00 [gateway] loading configuration…
[…every ~11s, never progressing past config-load…]
```

So the `OPENCLAW_ALLOW_OLDER_BINARY_DESTRUCTIVE_ACTIONS=1` bypass lets 5.20 TRY to start but a real schema-format incompatibility prevents it. The forward-incompat field is non-trivial.

**Recovery:** reinstalled 5.22, gateway came back. State preserved.

A peer machine with a SIMPLER config (only 1 telegram persona, fewer plugins) downgraded successfully without hitting Bug 2 — suggesting the forward-incompat field is in one of the additional channels/agents/plugins my busier config carries.

### Asks

1. **Identify which native hook ID is being requested but missing** in v2026.5.22. Likely a plugin registered a hook differently in v5.22 vs v5.20.

2. **Document or implement a migration path** for the forward-incompat config schema change so users can downgrade after hitting a regression.

3. Suggested API: `openclaw config downgrade --to <version>` that strips/migrates fields that won't validate against the older binary.

### Related

- #86019 (compaction issue — still OPEN, awaiting maintainer decision)
- This is a separate regression introduced in 5.22.

cc maintainers — happy to provide more log excerpts, config snippets, or live repro if useful.

issues.body:
### Symptom

A Discord-originated session that spawns a subagent / child task shows only the Discord typing indicator with no visible progress or state updates. The operator has no visibility into long-running work until terminal status.

Concrete repro (local, OpenClaw 2026.5.26 + `@openclaw/discord` 2026.5.26 + `@openclaw/codex` 2026.5.26):

1. In a Discord channel routed to an OpenClaw agent, send a message that triggers the agent to spawn a subagent (e.g. ask Codex to run a child task).
2. Discord shows the typing indicator for the agent.
3. No progress messages appear; the channel sits silently until the parent task reaches terminal status (often minutes later).
4. `openclaw tasks list` shows `notifyPolicy=done_only` for the parent and `notifyPolicy=silent` for the child CLI task.

### Root cause

In the bundled chunk `task-registry-CU9A1ECz.js` (likely source `src/tasks/task-registry.ts`):

```js
function ensureNotifyPolicy(params) {
    if (params.notifyPolicy) return params.notifyPolicy;
    return (params.deliveryStatus ?? ensureDeliveryStatus({
        ownerKey: params.ownerKey,
        scopeKind: params.scopeKind
    })) === "not_applicable" ? "silent" : "done_only";
}
```

When no explicit `notifyPolicy` is passed (typical for ACP spawns and `@openclaw/discord/dist/subagent-hooks-DHA_1pBI.js`'s `handleDiscordSubagentSpawning` path), the parent task defaults to `done_only`. Combined with:

- `shouldAutoDeliverTaskStateChange` only firing on `state_changes` policy (`task-registry-CU9A1ECz.js:89-91`)
- `shouldAutoDeliverTaskTerminalUpdate` only firing at terminal status (`:83-87`)
- Discord typing module being a fixed 5s start with no task-state link (`@openclaw/discord/dist/typing-BhIpRSfR.js`) and a 20-min wall-clock cap (`message-handler.process-DO17vBlT.js:1003-1016`)

…the operator sees a typing indicator with no payload for the duration of the run.

### Proposed fix

`ensureNotifyPolicy` should default to `state_changes` (not `done_only`) when the task carries a Discord origin marker, so Discord-originated work surfaces progress and state-change events:

```diff
 function ensureNotifyPolicy(params) {
     if (params.notifyPolicy) return params.notifyPolicy;
-    return (params.deliveryStatus ?? ensureDeliveryStatus({
+    const deliveryStatus = params.deliveryStatus ?? ensureDeliveryStatus({
         ownerKey: params.ownerKey,
         scopeKind: params.scopeKind
-    })) === "not_applicable" ? "silent" : "done_only";
+    });
+    if (deliveryStatus === "not_applicable") return "silent";
+    if (params.requesterOrigin?.channel === "discord") return "state_changes";
+    return "done_only";
 }
```

Both `ensureNotifyPolicy` call sites (`mergeExistingTaskForCreate` and the main task-create path) need to pass `requesterOrigin: params.requesterOrigin`. `requesterOrigin` is already available in the surrounding params at both call sites; this is a pure pass-through.

### Side-effect surface

- Non-Discord callers (cron, system, ACP from other channels): unchanged — fallback still `done_only` or `silent`.
- Tasks with an explicit `notifyPolicy` (codex native subagents at `silent`): unchanged — the early-return `if (params.notifyPolicy) return params.notifyPolicy` still wins.
- Discord channels will see more messages per task (the goal).

### Related / follow-up

1. **Discord typing watchdog.** `typing-BhIpRSfR.js` is a one-shot 5s start; the 20-min wall-clock cap lives in `message-handler.process-DO17vBlT.js:1003-1016`. A task-state-driven watchdog that posts an explicit "still working" message after N seconds of no state event would close the residual case where a task is genuinely silent (e.g. tool with no progress emit). Worth a separate issue.
2. **Codex child task visibility.** Filed separately — the `@openclaw/codex` native subagent mirror is silent/not_applicable. Will link companion issue after filing.
3. **CLI documentation.** `openclaw subagents …` does not exist (`No built-in command or plugin CLI metadata owns "subagents"`); the real surface is `openclaw tasks {cancel, flow cancel, notify}`. Consider an alias or a doc clarification.

### Workaround until merged

Operators can manually promote a silent / `done_only` task with:

```
openclaw tasks notify <taskId> state_changes
```

…which works via the existing `updateTaskNotifyPolicyById` runtime override (`task-registry-CU9A1ECz.js:2446`).

Sites that can patch the dist directly can apply the diff above plus `requesterOrigin` pass-through at both call sites as a local mitigation.

---

Environment: macOS, OpenClaw 2026.5.26, `@openclaw/discord` 2026.5.26, `@openclaw/codex` 2026.5.26, node 22.

issues.title: Plugin hooks: allow before_prompt_build to narrow the submitted tool surface per turn (toolsAllow)
issues.body:
## Feature request

**Context.** We run a context-compilation layer as an OpenClaw plugin (host 2026.6.11). For simple zero-tool turns (unit conversion, small talk), the turn contract already resolves to `max_tool_calls: 0` and the plugin replaces the system prompt with a lean ~1k-char prompt via `before_prompt_build`. This works well: input dropped from ~52k chars to 958 chars.

**Problem.** The model request still carries the full tool surface (21 tool schemas, ~16-18k chars) on those zero-tool turns, because `PluginHookBeforePromptBuildResult` only supports prompt fields:

- `mergeBeforePromptBuild` only forwards `systemPrompt / prependContext / appendContext / prependSystemContext / appendSystemContext` (`dist/hook-runner-global-*.js`).
- The hook event carries only `{prompt, messages}`, so `params.tools` cannot be mutated in place either.
- `toolsAllow` already exists and works (`attempt-tool-construction-plan-*.js`: empty array → `[]`), but it can only be set by the dispatch caller, not from a plugin hook.
- Static tool policy config cannot switch per turn.

So "zero-tool" currently means "instructed not to call tools" rather than "no tool surface submitted", which costs ~16-18k chars of prefill on every simple turn and weakens the contract.

**Request.** Add an optional `toolsAllow?: string[]` field to `PluginHookBeforePromptBuildResult`, wire it through `mergeBeforePromptBuild` and the attempt tool-construction path, so a plugin can narrow (or empty) the submitted tool surface for the current turn only. Empty array = no tools submitted this turn; absent = unchanged behavior (fully backward compatible).

**Alternatives considered.** (a) Patching the host locally — works but is lost on every upgrade. (b) Taking over dispatch via `reply_dispatch` to pass `toolsAllow: []` ourselves — requires reimplementing the dispatch/delivery chain, too risky. An upstream hook field is the clean path.

Happy to test a prerelease build against our plugin and report trajectory-level before/after (compiled tools count, TTFT, p50/p95 on natural traffic).

issues.body:
### Summary

In `v2026.7.2-beta.5` (and currently `main`), the Codex OAuth browser-realtime integration and the OpenAI realtime provider use different properties on the same `Symbol.for("openclaw.codex.realtime-voice.v1")` global state.

- [`extensions/codex/realtime-voice-api.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.7.2-beta.5/extensions/codex/realtime-voice-api.ts) stores the created broker runtime as `state.runtime = created`; the actual fallback interface is `created.broker`.
- [`extensions/openai/realtime-voice-provider.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.7.2-beta.5/extensions/openai/realtime-voice-provider.ts) only reads `state.fallback` in `readCodexRealtimeBrowserSessionFallback()`.

There is no assignment to `state.fallback` in the tag. An in-process probe after Codex registration shows global-state keys `version`, `sources`, and `runtime`, with `runtime.broker` present but `fallback` absent.

### Expected behavior

With:

- the bundled `openai` and `codex` plugins loaded,
- a valid OpenAI/Codex OAuth profile,
- no `talk.realtime.providers.openai.apiKey`,
- no OpenAI API-key profile, and
- no `OPENAI_API_KEY`,

browser WebRTC Talk should use the Codex subscription fallback described in #113354 and the beta5 docs.

### Actual behavior

The OpenAI provider cannot discover the registered Codex broker because it reads `state.fallback`, while Codex only exposes `state.runtime.broker`. The fallback therefore appears unconfigured and the browser-session path falls through to `OpenAI Realtime voice requires an OpenAI Platform API key`.

This is independent of `gpt-live-*` model selection; no `talk.realtime.model` override is involved.

### Minimal configuration

```json5
{
  talk: {
    realtime: {
      provider: "openai",
      mode: "realtime",
      transport: "webrtc",
      brain: "agent-consult"
    }
  }
}
```

### Suggested fix

Either:

1. publish `state.fallback = created.broker` when the Codex runtime is created (and clear it with the runtime), including the existing-runtime reuse path; or
2. have the OpenAI provider read `state.runtime?.broker` from the shared state.

A cross-extension integration test using the default global resolver (rather than injecting `resolveCodexRealtimeBrowserSessionFallback`) would catch the mismatch.

### Environment

- OpenClaw `2026.7.2-beta.5`
- `@openclaw/codex` `2026.7.2-beta.5`
- macOS arm64 / Node 24

Related: #113353, #113354

## Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

## Beta release blocker

No

## Summary

LM Studio-backed agent sessions can compile with zero tools without a visible warning or fallback, even when the agent/session is used for tool-dependent coding/sysadmin work.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure an agent with a primary local/LM Studio model similar to:

   ```text
   provider: lmstudio
   modelId: google/gemma-4-e4b
   modelApi: openai-completions
   compat.supportsTools: false
   fallbacks: openai/gpt-5.5, ...
   ```

2. Start a WebChat/dashboard direct conversation with a coding/sysadmin-style agent profile.

3. Ask for a tool-dependent task, for example:

   ```text
   Can you execute a system check, write test files to the filesystem, and give me the paths?
   ```

   or:

   ```text
   Generate an image and save it under artifacts/ootd/, then give me the filesystem path.
   ```

4. Inspect the trajectory/session logs.

5. Observe `context.compiled ... tools=0` and no `tool.call` events.

6. Observe that the model may still produce natural-language claims of command execution, file creation, or media generation.

7. Start a fresh OpenAI-backed session in the same workspace and repeat the same request. It compiles with tools and succeeds.

## Expected behavior

If an agent/profile/session is tool-dependent and the selected provider/model compiles with zero tools, OpenClaw should not let the turn proceed silently as an ordinary agent response.

Expected acceptable outcomes:

- Surface a clear warning to the user/operator that this model/session has no tools available.
- Automatically fall back to a configured tool-capable model when a tool-capable profile is active.
- Block tool-dependent requests with a clear runtime error instead of letting the model answer as if it can execute tools.
- Show the zero-tool state prominently in the session UI/logs before the first assistant response.

## Actual behavior

The LM Studio session repeatedly compiled with zero tools and continued normally. The model then answered tool-dependent requests as if it had executed tools, including fake filesystem paths and fake media artifacts.

Observed examples from the affected conversation:

```text
I've saved the full shot for you: artifacts/ootd/2026-06-08-1234-EDT-lily-ootd.png
MEDIA:artifacts/ootd/2026-06-08-1234-EDT-lily-ootd-corrected.png
Tool Call: write_file(path="test_persistence_proof.txt", ...)
```

Those artifacts did not exist. The session log contained no real tool calls.

By contrast, a fresh OpenAI-backed session in the same workspace compiled with tools and successfully created/verified real filesystem artifacts.

## OpenClaw version

`OpenClaw 2026.6.1 (2e08f0f)`

The affected conversation began before an in-conversation update from `2026.5.28` to `2026.6.1` (operator-reported version). Local config audit shows an `openclaw update` at `2026-06-08T12:00:50Z`; the active LM Studio conversation remained tool-less after the update.

## Operating system

Ubuntu 26.04 LTS x86_64

## Install method

npm global

## Model

Failed session:

```text
lmstudio/google/gemma-4-e4b
```

Known-good comparison session:

```text
openai/gpt-5.5
```

## Provider / routing chain

Failed session:

```text
OpenClaw -> LM Studio OpenAI-compatible completions endpoint -> google/gemma-4-e4b
```

Known-good comparison session:

```text
OpenClaw -> OpenAI ChatGPT Responses API -> gpt-5.5
```

## Additional provider/model setup details

Redacted setup details:

- Agent primary model was `lmstudio/google/gemma-4-e4b`.
- Agent fallback models included OpenAI models.
- The LM Studio model entry was configured with `compat.supportsTools: false`.
- The failed session used `modelApi=openai-completions`.
- The fresh OpenAI session used `modelApi=openai-chatgpt-responses`.
- No API keys, tokens, private host URLs, or raw config blobs are included in this report.

## Logs, screenshots, and evidence

Redacted trajectory excerpts from the failed session:

```text
2026-06-08T11:36:36Z context.compiled provider=lmstudio modelId=google/gemma-4-e4b modelApi=openai-completions tools=0
2026-06-08T11:41:14Z context.compiled provider=lmstudio modelId=google/gemma-4-e4b modelApi=openai-completions tools=0
2026-06-08T11:47:46Z context.compiled provider=lmstudio modelId=google/gemma-4-e4b modelApi=openai-completions tools=0

```

```text
- image generation / OOTD image path produced fake/nonexistent artifacts
- filesystem file creation produced fake/nonexistent files

- shell/system calls did not execute from the assistant runtime
```

```text
2026-06-08T12:26:54Z context.compiled provider=openai modelId=gpt-5.5 modelApi=openai-chatgpt-responses tools=19
```

```text
system-checks/.../write-test.txt
system-checks/.../write-test.json
system-checks/.../nested/write-test-nested.txt
system-checks/.../imagegen-skill-test.png
artifacts/ootd/2026-06-08-ootd-casual-lily-existing-crop.png
```

Related but not identical issues found before filing:

```text
#90585 - LM Studio openai-responses tool calls with empty arguments
#74664 - openai-completions ignores compat.supportsTools=false and still sends tools
#90288 - non-Anthropic models output tool calls as plain text
```

This report is different: the provider/model route compiled with zero tools, but the user/operator was not protected from the silent capability loss.

## Impact and severity

Affected users/systems/channels:

- Tool-dependent agents using LM Studio/local-model routes, especially coding/sysadmin/security workflows.

Severity:

- High for tool-dependent workflows. The assistant appears operational but cannot execute tools.

Frequency:

- In the observed LM Studio session, every inspected `context.compiled` event showed `tools=0`.

Consequence:

- The model can produce plausible but false claims about command execution, generated media, and filesystem artifacts.
- Users may trust nonexistent files, paths, or diagnostics.
- Opening a fresh tool-capable/OpenAI session restored the same workspace/agent capabilities, so this is confusing and hard to diagnose from the chat UI alone.

## Additional information

This does not appear to be primarily a Gemma model-quality issue. The model did not receive any tools in the failed runtime context.

The requested behavior is not necessarily "make this LM Studio route support tools." A sufficient fix would be to detect the zero-tool compiled context for tool-dependent profiles and warn, block, or fall back to a tool-capable model.

issues.title: [Bug]: CLI and TUI rerun a full state-database integrity scan after startup migrations completed
issues.body:
### Bug type

Crash (process/app exits or hangs)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On OpenClaw 2026.7.2-beta.3, ordinary CLI commands such as `openclaw status` and `openclaw tui` can appear hung while synchronously running a full SQLite integrity scan even though the gateway already recorded a successful migration checkpoint for the same build.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use OpenClaw 2026.7.2-beta.3 with an established shared state database and a successful startup-migration checkpoint for that exact build.
2. Run `openclaw status` or `openclaw tui`.
3. Observe that the command does not reach its normal output while a process sample shows it inside SQLite `PRAGMA integrity_check`.
4. Repeat another ordinary CLI command; it enters the same Doctor-owned state preflight and full integrity scan again.

### Expected behavior

After the database schema is current, ordinary CLI one-shot commands should use the scoped current-schema gate described in #110271. Full integrity verification should remain in place for Doctor, pending schema migrations, quarantined databases, and required gateway startup paths.

### Actual behavior

The CLI bootstrap routes ordinary commands through `runDoctorConfigPreflight` and `repairOpenClawStateDatabaseSchema`, which calls the full `PRAGMA integrity_check` before the requested command can start. The canonical `state/openclaw.sqlite` file itself keeps the lightweight migration-input detector true on an established installation, so `status` also takes this path on every invocation.

On an APFS clone of a checksum-verified 569,180,160-byte state database, the full scan took 3.75 seconds cold and 0.71 seconds warm. After bringing that clone to the current schema, the corresponding patch's scoped automatic-CLI preflight took a 3.70 ms median over 10 iterations; the unchanged full Doctor route took 441.38 ms warm on the same clone. The live process sample reached the same full SQLite integrity operation.

### OpenClaw version

2026.7.2-beta.3

### Operating system

macOS 26.5.1 (25F80), Apple silicon

### Install method

npm global installation from a source build

### Model

Not model-related; the hang occurs during CLI bootstrap before model selection.

### Provider / routing chain

Not provider-related; the hang occurs before provider routing.

### Additional provider/model setup details

Not applicable.

### Logs

```shell
[identity-redacted process sample]
ensureCliCommandBootstrap
  ensureConfigReady
    runDoctorConfigPreflight
      autoMigrateLegacyState
        repairOpenClawStateDatabaseSchema
          assertSqliteIntegrity
            PRAGMA integrity_check
```

Read-only state metadata at reproduction time:

```text
database size: 569,180,160 bytes
PRAGMA user_version: 4
schema metadata version: 4
startup checkpoint: 2026.7.2-beta.3 + exact build identity
pending schema migrations: none
active startup-migration lease: none
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Identity-redacted benchmark on an APFS clone of the verified database:

```text
full PRAGMA integrity_check (cold): 3.75 s, result=ok
full PRAGMA integrity_check (warm): 0.71 s, result=ok
patched current-schema automatic preflight (10 runs): min=3.181 ms, median=3.700 ms, max=4.692 ms
unchanged full Doctor route (warm): 441.380 ms
warm full-route / median automatic-preflight ratio: approximately 119x
```

### Impact and severity

- Affected: users with established, larger shared state databases invoking ordinary CLI or TUI commands.
- Severity: high for CLI usability; commands appear stuck before their requested operation begins.
- Frequency: deterministic in the observed beta build when the ordinary command enters the state-migration preflight.
- Consequence: `status`, TUI, messaging, and other CLI workflows can be delayed by a full-database scan on every process start.

### Additional information

Related: #101290 documents the broader risk of CLI startup joining the writable state-maintenance path while a gateway is live.

Regression/acceptance gap: #110271 added fast schema gates and states that CLI one-shot commands should no longer pay full-file scans, but the config-guard/Doctor-preflight route still reaches the full integrity check. The exact first affected release is `NOT_ENOUGH_INFO`; the behavior is directly observed on 2026.7.2-beta.3 and remains present in current `main` at `c24a215fe41481370a11132c399c086c00ed6631`.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

In OpenClaw 2026.7.1 and npm stable 2026.7.1-2, a supported external Plugin Control UI tab is discovered and framed, but no documented short-lived scoped-grant bootstrap occurs, so its same-plugin `auth: "gateway"` route loads 401.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install `openclaw@2026.7.1` or `openclaw@2026.7.1-2` in a clean, isolated state directory.
2. Register this descriptor:

```js
api.session.controls.registerControlUiDescriptor({
  surface: "tab",
  id: "external-tab-auth-probe",
  label: "External Tab Auth Probe",
  description: "Isolated authenticated external-tab compatibility probe",
  group: "control",
  requiredScopes: ["operator.read"],
  path: "/plugins/external-tab-auth-probe",
  icon: "layout-dashboard",
  order: 99,
});
```

3. Register the same-plugin route:

```js
api.registerHttpRoute({
  path: "/plugins/external-tab-auth-probe",
  auth: "gateway",
  match: "prefix",
  handler(request, response) {
    if (request.method !== "GET" && request.method !== "HEAD") {
      response.writeHead(405, { Allow: "GET, HEAD" });
      response.end();
      return;
    }
    response.writeHead(200, { "Content-Type": "text/html; charset=utf-8" });
    response.end(
      request.method === "HEAD"
        ? ""
        : "<!doctype html><title>External Tab Auth Probe</title>",
    );
  },
});
```

4. Start a loopback-only token-authenticated Gateway.
5. Authenticate normally in Control UI.
6. Select **External Tab Auth Probe** through standard navigation.
7. Inspect the iframe request and Gateway response.

The descriptor path, HTTP route root, plugin owner, hostname (`127.0.0.1`), and `auth: "gateway"` mode match.

### Expected behavior

Per the Plugin Control UI external-tab authentication contract, the authenticated parent should bootstrap/probe a short-lived, plugin-scoped grant (HttpOnly cookie or equivalent) so the sandboxed iframe can load the same-plugin Gateway-authenticated route without exposing the Gateway bearer token to the iframe URL or plugin JavaScript.

### Actual behavior

- `controlUiTabs` contains the descriptor.
- Standard Control UI navigation opens the correct sandboxed iframe.
- The iframe GET returns 401.
- No grant-bootstrap request occurs.
- No sandbox probe occurs.
- No scoped `Set-Cookie` response occurs.
- The iframe sends neither a scoped cookie nor Authorization header.
- Direct unauthenticated GET returns 401.
- Direct authenticated GET and HEAD return 200.
- Authenticated POST returns 405.
- Disabling the plugin removes the tab and route; the route then returns 404.

The failure occurs before browser cookie policy could affect the result because no cookie issuance is attempted.

### OpenClaw version

`2026.7.1` and `2026.7.1-2`

`2026.7.1-2` npm identity:

- published: `2026-07-18T03:53:48.967Z`
- shasum: `4583b987ea7277230ce1c7b2b8535d3e219f57ac`
- integrity: `sha512-ycF3yPcbjN6bUPeaUx6Mh6vze1hQWoD3CT/wWcmD7a8xaHHHRUaAlaq+lFxMHf1ssEgODVAwjlzYqp2twkYZ7g==`

### Operating system

Linux 6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 x86_64

### Install method

Disposable npm package prefixes with separate temporary `OPENCLAW_HOME`, state, configuration, authentication token, plugin root, and loopback ports.

### Model

Not applicable; the defect occurs in Control UI/Gateway authentication before any model invocation.

### Provider / routing chain

Not applicable; isolated reproduction has no provider or model configuration.

### Logs

```text
controlUiTabs descriptor: present
standard navigation: present/opened
iframe route: /plugins/external-tab-auth-probe
iframe response: 401
grant bootstrap: not observed
sandbox probe: not observed
Set-Cookie: not observed
iframe Cookie header: absent
iframe Authorization header: absent
direct unauthenticated GET: 401
direct authenticated GET: 200
direct authenticated HEAD: 200
direct authenticated POST: 405
disabled route: 404
```

The same result was observed in both tested builds. Packaged plugin-page inspection found a plain iframe using the descriptor path in each build and no grant/probe/cookie handoff in that page path.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

The reproduction was run twice in fully disposable environments. Browser network inspection confirmed no external requests, no plugin storage token keys, no token in the iframe URL, and no token in the plugin payload.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: developers using documented unbundled Plugin Control UI tabs with Gateway-authenticated routes.
- Severity: workflow-blocking for authenticated external plugin tabs.
- Frequency: reproduced in every attempt on both stable package versions.
- Consequence: the tab is discoverable but unusable through ordinary authenticated navigation.
- Security behavior: the route fails closed; unauthenticated access remains rejected.

No bearer-token workaround is requested. Query-token injection, browser-side Authorization injection, `auth: "none"`, authentication weakening, and remote exposure are explicitly out of scope.

### Additional information

The behavior is identical in `2026.7.1` and npm stable `2026.7.1-2`; no known-good stable build was established. Please add an integration test covering descriptor discovery, normal authenticated navigation, scoped-grant bootstrap/probe, successful iframe GET, unauthenticated 401, mutation-method rejection, plugin disable/removal, and absence of Gateway bearer-token exposure.

## Summary The chat detail sidebar cannot scroll when rendering a long Markdown preview. The preview extends beyond the viewport, but the right-hand panel does not receive vertical scrolling. ## Environment - OpenClaw: `2026.7.1-2` - macOS - Control UI, Chat page - Reproduced with a long Markdown tool/file preview opened in the right detail sidebar ## Steps to reproduce 1. Open the Control UI Chat page. 2. Open a long Markdown preview in the right-hand detail panel (for example, a generated report with headings and a table). 3. Try to scroll the preview panel. ## Actual behavior The content is clipped below the viewport and the detail panel cannot be scrolled. ## Expected behavior The detail sidebar header should remain visible and its content area should scroll vertically. ## Likely cause `.sidebar-content` has `overflow: auto`, but the flex-height chain is broken by the unstyled wrapper div rendered inside the `openclaw-chat-detail-panel` custom element. As a result, the panel's percentage height resolves against content instead of a constrained parent height. Relevant structure: ```html
…
…long Markdown…
 ``` ## Workaround / proposed fix Making the wrapper and panel constrained flex children restores scrolling: ```css .chat-sidebar > div, .chat-sidebar .sidebar-panel { display: flex; flex: 1 1 0; min-width: 0; min-height: 0; } .chat-sidebar .sidebar-panel { height: auto; flex-direction: column; } .chat-sidebar .sidebar-content { min-height: 0; overscroll-behavior: contain; } ``` This is scoped to the chat detail sidebar and preserves the existing `.sidebar-content { overflow: auto; }` behavior.
