issues.body:
## Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

## Beta release blocker

No

## Summary

A recovery-aware gateway restart can mark an active Codex turn for recovery and then continue accepting mirrored commentary into the native transcript; if an ordinary `assistant` message with `stopReason=stop` becomes the active tail, startup recovery rejects the turn as `transcript tail is not resumable`, marks the session failed, and asks the user to resend the request.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run OpenClaw `2026.7.2 (31ccf56)` with the Codex agent runtime and a channel-backed main session.
2. Start a long-running turn that has an active Codex subagent and emits commentary while work continues.
3. From outside that gateway, trigger the supported recovery-aware restart handoff while the turn and subagent are active. In the observed run this was `ocm service restart openclaw`, which caused the gateway to receive `SIGUSR1`.
4. Observe that restart recovery marks the session before the old process has stopped writing mirrored Codex events.
5. Observe one or more ordinary Codex commentary messages being committed to the native agent transcript after the recovery mark.
6. Allow the replacement gateway process to start and run main-session restart recovery.

Observed once in a targeted live reproduction. The timing dependency makes this intermittent: other interrupted sessions recovered successfully when their transcript tails remained eligible.

## Expected behavior

An active turn marked by the supported recovery handoff should remain eligible for automatic continuation after the replacement gateway starts.

## Actual behavior

The replacement process classifies the final ordinary `assistant / stop` commentary entry as non-resumable, changes the session from `running` to `failed`, and sends:

> I was interrupted by a gateway restart and couldn't safely resume the previous turn. Please send that last request again and I'll pick it up cleanly.

The interrupted work does not continue automatically.

## OpenClaw version

`2026.7.2 (31ccf56)`; exact commit `31ccf56a8110bb9c425adde725f8fbfb218b1367`

## Operating system

macOS `26.5.1` (`25F80`), arm64; Node.js `v26.3.0`

## Install method

Release-shaped local runtime built from the exact OpenClaw commit and supervised by OpenClaw Manager (OCM).

## Model

`openai/gpt-5.6-sol`

## Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw -> bundled Codex agent runtime -> OpenAI

## Additional provider/model setup details

The active turn was a Telegram direct-session turn using the Codex runtime. It had one active Codex subagent when the recovery-aware restart began. Identifiers below are redacted.

## Logs

```shell
# Old gateway process: recovery is marked before active work has stopped.
2026-07-30T23:39:10.731-06:00 [admission] closed: restart drain
2026-07-30T23:39:10.732-06:00 [gateway] received SIGUSR1; restarting
2026-07-30T23:39:10.960-06:00 [main-session-restart-recovery] marked 1 interrupted main session(s) for restart recovery (gateway restart drain)
2026-07-30T23:39:11.014-06:00 [gateway] draining 2 active task(s) and 1 active embedded run(s) before restart with timeout 0ms
2026-07-30T23:39:11.015-06:00 [gateway] restart blocked by active background task run(s): taskId=<redacted> runId=<redacted> status=running runtime=subagent label=Codex subagent
2026-07-30T23:39:11.015-06:00 [gateway] forced restart requested; skipping active work drain

# Native agent transcript: these ordinary commentary messages are committed
# more than three seconds after the recovery mark.
2026-07-31T05:39:14.215Z role=assistant stopReason=stop mirrorOrigin=codex-app-server
2026-07-31T05:39:14.292Z role=assistant stopReason=stop mirrorOrigin=codex-app-server
2026-07-31T05:39:14.359Z role=assistant stopReason=stop mirrorOrigin=codex-app-server

# The old run is aborted only after those transcript entries exist.
2026-07-30T23:39:15.238-06:00 [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=main durationMs=377118 error="AbortError: agent run aborted for restart"
2026-07-30T23:39:15.238-06:00 [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=session:agent:main:telegram:direct:<redacted> durationMs=377119 error="AbortError: agent run aborted for restart"
2026-07-30T23:39:15.401-06:00 [shutdown] completed cleanly in 266ms

# Replacement process: startup recovery reads the ordinary assistant tail and fails closed.
2026-07-30T23:39:37.289-06:00 [gateway] ready
2026-07-30T23:39:37.681-06:00 [main-session-restart-recovery] marked interrupted main session failed: agent:main:telegram:direct:<redacted> (transcript tail is not resumable)
2026-07-30T23:39:39.639-06:00 [main-session-restart-recovery] sent interrupted main session recovery notice: agent:main:telegram:direct:<redacted> (transcript tail is not resumable)
2026-07-30T23:39:39.642-06:00 [main-session-restart-recovery] main-session restart recovery complete: recovered=0 failed=1 skipped=0
```

## Cause confirmed from the persisted transcript and current source

The recovery marker is committed before the old Codex run has stopped emitting transcript events. Late mirrored commentary can therefore replace the tail that recovery later classifies.

Startup recovery reads the active native agent transcript through `readSessionMessagesAsync` in `src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery-store.ts`. In `src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery-resume-policy.ts`, an ordinary assistant message is not accepted by `isResumableTailMessage`; unless it matches one of the explicit restart-abort, pending-tool, delivery, or replay-safe checkpoint cases, `resolveMainSessionResumePolicy` returns:

```ts
{ action: "fail", reason: "transcript tail is not resumable" }
```

In this observation, the active leaf ended with three normal Codex commentary entries carrying `stopReason=stop`, so none matched a restart-abort special case. The classifier therefore followed its documented fail-closed branch even though the same turn had been explicitly marked for restart recovery seconds earlier.

## Adjacent LosslessClaw shutdown errors were not causal

The old process also logged LosslessClaw shutdown errors after the late commentary had already been persisted:

```shell
2026-07-30T23:39:15.150-06:00 [plugins] [hooks] session_end handler from lossless-claw failed: [lcm] Database connection closed after gateway_stop
2026-07-30T23:39:15.223-06:00 [context-engine] Context engine "lossless-claw" ... failed during afterTurn: database is not open
```

The replacement LosslessClaw engine initialized successfully before the recovery classifier ran. Recovery classified OpenClaw's native agent transcript, not `lcm.db`. These messages are included to distinguish concurrent shutdown noise from the observed cause.

## Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Evidence consists of the redacted gateway timestamps above, the corresponding rows from the native `openclaw-agent.sqlite` transcript, and the cited recovery-policy source paths at commit `31ccf56a8110bb9c425adde725f8fbfb218b1367`.

## Impact and severity

- Affected: channel-backed Codex turns interrupted by a recovery-aware restart while late commentary can still be mirrored.
- Severity: high for the affected turn; active work is terminated and the user must manually resubmit the request.
- Frequency: timing-dependent; observed in 1 targeted reproduction, while other interrupted sessions with eligible tails recovered successfully.
- Consequence: automatic continuation fails despite a successful recovery handoff and the session is marked failed.

## Additional information

Related outward symptom: #101675 also reports `transcript tail is not resumable`, but the evidence there describes a different transcript condition. This report is specifically about ordinary Codex commentary being committed after the recovery mark and becoming the active transcript tail.

This report intentionally documents the observed problem, cause, logs, and reproduction only.

issues.body:
## Summary
OpenClaw appears to inject a volatile `Current time: ...` line into heartbeat, cron, and post-compaction prompt content in a way that likely reduces prompt-cache reuse for those turns.

The main concern is not timezone metadata, but exact wall-clock time being inserted into cache-sensitive prompt prefixes.

## Why this matters
Prompt caching works best when the front of the prompt remains stable.
If a changing `Current time: ...` line is included early in the prompt body on every heartbeat/cron/event turn, it can invalidate cache reuse for everything that follows.

This likely causes unnecessary cache churn and higher cost / latency for recurring automated runs.

## What I found
### Stable timezone in system prompt
There is a stable section in the system prompt builder:
- `## Current Date & Time`
- `Time zone: ...`

That part looks fine and likely remains cacheable.

### Volatile current-time helper
There is a helper at:
- `/app/dist/current-time-BkqyYDci.js`

It generates a line like:
- `Current time: ... (userTimezone) / ... UTC`

### Where the volatile line is appended
I found this exact wall-clock line being appended in at least these flows:
- heartbeat runner
- cron/system-event execution
- post-compaction context refresh

Relevant built artifacts observed locally:
- `/app/dist/current-time-BkqyYDci.js`
- `/app/dist/heartbeat-runner-dPEnJvN2.js`
- `/app/dist/server.impl-B-xK231T.js`
- `/app/dist/model-context-tokens-BFDIhVvJ.js`

## Recommendation
### Best fix
Keep stable timezone metadata in the static/system prompt, but move per-turn wall-clock time out of cache-sensitive prompt prefixes.

In practice:
1. Keep `Time zone: ...` in stable prompt context
2. Inject exact `Current time: ...` as late as possible
3. Only include exact wall-clock time when the turn truly needs it
4. Avoid baking fresh time into post-compaction injected blocks unless necessary

## Expected benefit
- Better prompt cache reuse on heartbeat/cron/automation turns
- Lower token cost
- Lower latency
- No loss of timezone awareness

## Possible implementation principle
Keep stable user timezone in the static prompt, but move per-turn wall-clock time out of cache-sensitive prompt prefixes and into late-bound runtime/event content only when needed.

## Notes
This may not be harming cache reuse for the entire main chat prompt, but it does look like a legitimate optimization target for recurring automation/event turns.

issues.body:
### Summary

Session archive (reset) filenames use UTC timestamps, causing date mismatches for users in timezones far from UTC. Sessions that occur after 16:00 UTC get filed under the previous date, making local-date-based session searches miss valid sessions.

### Problem to solve

Users in UTC+8 (Asia/Shanghai) and other non-UTC timezones cannot reliably find archived sessions by local date.

Example:
- A session at 2026-06-25 01:00 Beijing time (UTC 2026-06-24 17:00)
- Archive filename: ...reset.2026-06-24T17-00-xx.Z
- Filename says "June 24" but the session happened on "June 25" locally
- Any session between 00:00-07:59 Beijing time gets mislabeled as the previous UTC date

When searching or listing archived conversation files by local date, ~20 out of ~40 archived sessions in a typical week show the wrong date. The mismatch is always +1 day for UTC+8 users.

### Proposed solution

Make session archive filenames respect the configured timezone setting (agents.defaults.userTimezone or agents.defaults.envelopeTimezone).

Option A: Use local timezone date in the filename instead of UTC:
  Currently: ...reset.2026-06-24T17-00-xx.Z (UTC)
  Proposed:  ...reset.2026-06-25T01-00-xx.Z (local, for Asia/Shanghai)

Option B: Add a local-timezone date prefix while keeping UTC timestamp:
  ...reset.2026-06-25_2026-06-24T17-00-xx.Z

When no timezone is explicitly configured, fall back to current UTC behavior for backward compatibility.

### Alternatives considered

Make session archive filenames respect the configured timezone setting (agents.defaults.userTimezone or agents.defaults.envelopeTimezone).

Option A: Use local timezone date in the filename instead of UTC:
  Currently: ...reset.2026-06-24T17-00-xx.Z (UTC)
  Proposed:  ...reset.2026-06-25T01-00-xx.Z (local, for Asia/Shanghai)

Option B: Add a local-timezone date prefix while keeping UTC timestamp:
  ...reset.2026-06-25_2026-06-24T17-00-xx.Z

When no timezone is explicitly configured, fall back to current UTC behavior for backward compatibility.

### Impact

Affected users: All users in non-UTC timezones, especially UTC+8 to UTC+12 regions
Severity: Annoying — blocks reliable local-date session discovery
Frequency: Daily (every session crossing 16:00-23:59 UTC boundary)
Consequence: Manual searching, missed conversations, extra developer overhead debugging "lost" sessions

### Evidence/examples

On a Windows host with Asia/Shanghai timezone (UTC+8):
- 20 out of 40 archived session files have UTC-date vs local-date mismatch
- All mismatches involve sessions between 00:00-07:59 local time
- Timezone config (agents.defaults.userTimezone) is already supported and set to "Asia/Shanghai", but archive filenames ignore it

File showing the config is in place but does not affect filenames:
  ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json
  {
    "agents": { "defaults": { "userTimezone": "Asia/Shanghai" } }
  }

### Additional information

No breaking changes needed — backward-compatible fallback to UTC when userTimezone is unset. Only affects filename generation in the session archive/reset mechanism.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

After the `browser.proxy` invoke path was hardened to require `operator.admin`, `openclaw nodes invoke --command browser.proxy` still opens the Gateway connection with the generic `node.invoke` least-privilege scope (`operator.write`), so direct CLI browser proxy calls fail with `missing scope: operator.admin` before they reach the paired node.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install or run OpenClaw `2026.7.1`.
2. Pair and connect a node that advertises the `browser.proxy` command.
3. Ensure the Gateway allows the command, for example `gateway.nodes.allowCommands = ["browser.proxy"]`.
4. Run a read-only browser proxy command through the generic nodes CLI:

```shell
npx -y -p openclaw@2026.7.1 openclaw nodes invoke \
  --node '<paired-node-name-or-id>' \
  --command browser.proxy \
  --params '{"method":"GET","path":"/profiles"}' \
  --json
```

5. Observe that the call fails with `missing scope: operator.admin`.

### Expected behavior

For `node.invoke` calls where `command === "browser.proxy"`, the CLI/Gateway client scope resolver should request `operator.admin`, matching the gateway-side invoke requirement introduced for direct browser proxy calls.

The read-only `/profiles` request should then either reach the paired node and return the browser proxy result, or fail for a node/browser-specific reason after authorization. It should not fail at Gateway authorization because the CLI requested only `operator.write`.

### Actual behavior

The call fails before node dispatch:

```shell
nodes invoke failed: missing scope: operator.admin
```

The paired node is connected and advertises `browser.proxy`, so the failure is not caused by an unavailable Mac/Chrome/node route. The same command failed with the clean npm package, not only with the locally installed package:

```shell
$ NPM_CONFIG_CACHE=/tmp/npm-cache-openclaw-issue \
  npx -y -p openclaw@2026.7.1 openclaw nodes invoke \
  --node '<redacted-paired-node>' \
  --command browser.proxy \
  --params '{"method":"GET","path":"/profiles"}' \
  --json
nodes invoke failed: missing scope: operator.admin
```

The same direct CLI path was also checked against the beta tag:

```shell
$ npx -y -p openclaw@2026.7.2-beta.1 openclaw --version
OpenClaw 2026.7.2-beta.1 (a911e58)

$ npx -y -p openclaw@2026.7.2-beta.1 openclaw nodes invoke \
  --node '<redacted-paired-node>' \
  --command browser.proxy \
  --params '{"method":"GET","path":"/profiles"}' \
  --json
nodes invoke failed: missing scope: operator.admin
```

### OpenClaw version

OpenClaw 2026.7.1 (2d2ddc4)

Also reproduced through `npx -p openclaw@2026.7.2-beta.1`, which reports:

```shell
OpenClaw 2026.7.2-beta.1 (a911e58)
```

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS for the Gateway/CLI host.

The paired browser node is a connected macOS node, but the failure happens before dispatch to the node.

### Install method

npm global for the installed environment.

The failing behavior was also reproduced with clean `npx -p openclaw@2026.7.1` and `npx -p openclaw@2026.7.2-beta.1` runs.

### Model

No model involved; this is a CLI/Gateway/node authorization path.

### Provider / routing chain

`openclaw nodes invoke` CLI -> Gateway WebSocket client -> `node.invoke` gateway method -> paired node command `browser.proxy`.

### Additional provider/model setup details

Relevant node/Gateway setup:

- A paired and connected node advertises `browser.proxy`.
- `gateway.nodes.allowCommands` includes `browser.proxy`.
- No config-only scope override was found for `node.invoke browser.proxy`.
- `openclaw nodes invoke` does not expose a `--scope` or `--admin` flag.

### Logs

```shell
$ openclaw --version
OpenClaw 2026.7.1 (2d2ddc4)

$ npm view openclaw version dist-tags --json
{
  "version": "2026.7.1",
  "dist-tags": {
    "alpha": "2026.5.19-alpha.1",
    "beta": "2026.7.2-beta.1",
    "latest": "2026.7.1"
  }
}

$ openclaw nodes status --json
{
  "nodes": [
    {
      "nodeId": "<redacted>",
      "displayName": "<redacted>",
      "remoteIp": "<redacted>",
      "paired": true,
      "connected": true,
      "commands": [
        "browser.proxy",
        "system.run",
        "system.run.prepare",
        "system.which"
      ]
    }
  ]
}

$ NPM_CONFIG_CACHE=/tmp/npm-cache-openclaw-issue \
  npx -y -p openclaw@2026.7.1 openclaw nodes invoke \
  --node '<redacted-paired-node>' \
  --command browser.proxy \
  --params '{"method":"GET","path":"/profiles"}' \
  --json
nodes invoke failed: missing scope: operator.admin
```

Clean npm package source-level check:

```shell
$ node --input-type=module -e '
  import { resolveLeastPrivilegeOperatorScopesForMethod as r } from "/tmp/openclaw-2026.7.1-clean/package/dist/method-scopes-DD70REaE.js";
  console.log(JSON.stringify({
    nodeInvokeBrowserProxy: r("node.invoke", { command: "browser.proxy" }),
    nodeInvokeSystemRun: r("node.invoke", { command: "system.run" })
  }, null, 2));
'
{
  "nodeInvokeBrowserProxy": [
    "operator.write"
  ],
  "nodeInvokeSystemRun": [
    "operator.write"
  ]
}
```

Relevant clean `openclaw@2026.7.1` source snippets:

```js
// dist/method-scopes-CwW_Szsp.js
function resolveLeastPrivilegeOperatorScopesForMethod(method, params) {
  if (isDynamicOperatorGatewayMethod(method)) return resolveDynamicLeastPrivilegeOperatorScopesForMethod(method, params);
  const requiredScope = resolveRequiredOperatorScopeForMethod(method);
  if (requiredScope) return [requiredScope];
  return [];
}
```

```js
// dist/nodes-e1aIcs5S.js
const BROWSER_PROXY_REQUIRED_SCOPE = "operator.admin";

function clientHasOperatorAdminScope(client) {
  return (Array.isArray(client?.connect?.scopes) ? client.connect.scopes : []).includes(BROWSER_PROXY_REQUIRED_SCOPE);
}

if (command === "browser.proxy" && !clientHasOperatorAdminScope(client)) {
  respond(false, void 0, errorShape(ErrorCodes.INVALID_REQUEST, `missing scope: ${BROWSER_PROXY_REQUIRED_SCOPE}`));
  return;
}
```

The official browser/plugin proxy path appears to request admin explicitly:

```js
// dist/plugin-service-DKOoYlF3.js
await browserToolDeps.callGatewayTool("node.invoke", { timeoutMs: gatewayTimeoutMs }, {
  nodeId: params.nodeId,
  command: "browser.proxy",
  params: {
    method: params.method,
    path: params.path,
    query: params.query,
    body: params.body,
    timeoutMs: proxyTimeoutMs,
    profile: params.profile
  },
  idempotencyKey: crypto.randomUUID()
}, { scopes: ["operator.admin"] });
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Related upstream context:

- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/85916 hardened direct `node.invoke(browser.proxy)` so write-scoped callers are rejected and admin-scoped callers still dispatch. That appears to be the intended Gateway-side behavior.
- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104491 fixed the pairing-approval side for `browser.proxy`, but this report concerns the direct invoke-time CLI/Gateway client scope resolver.
- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/81555 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/81716 are a similar prior browser CLI scope mismatch where the CLI path was fixed to request `operator.admin`.
- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/105936 is a similar policy-drift class for a different node command (`fs.listDir`), not this `browser.proxy` nodes CLI path.

### Impact and severity

Affected: users who call `browser.proxy` through `openclaw nodes invoke` or other generic `node.invoke` helper paths after the 2026.7.1 security hardening.

Severity: Medium to high for node-host browser workflows. The official browser/plugin path can still work when it requests `operator.admin`, but direct nodes CLI / helper-script workflows fail.

Frequency: Always reproduced for the direct `openclaw nodes invoke --command browser.proxy` path in this environment on `2026.7.1` and `2026.7.2-beta.1`.

Consequence: Read-only browser proxy operations such as `/profiles` fail before reaching the paired node, even when the node is connected, paired, and advertises `browser.proxy`.

### Additional information

This does not appear to be a Mac node, Chrome, pairing, or `allowCommands` configuration problem:

- The node is paired and connected.
- The node advertises `browser.proxy`.
- `gateway.nodes.allowCommands` already allows `browser.proxy`.
- The Gateway correctly requires `operator.admin` for direct `browser.proxy` invoke after the hardening.
- The mismatch is that the generic `node.invoke` least-privilege scope resolver still chooses `operator.write` for `command === "browser.proxy"`.

Suggested fix direction:

Make the least-privilege scope resolver / CLI Gateway connection path command-aware for `node.invoke`, so `node.invoke` with `command === "browser.proxy"` requests `operator.admin`, while other generic `node.invoke` commands continue to use their intended lower scope. Alternatively, route the public `nodes invoke browser.proxy` path through the same browser proxy helper/contract that already requests `operator.admin`.

Last known good version in this environment: OpenClaw 2026.6.11.

First known bad version in this environment: OpenClaw 2026.7.1 (2d2ddc4).

issues.body:
### Summary

Add automatic output sanitization to prevent accidental leakage of sensitive information (API keys, tokens, passwords, PII) in agent responses, regardless of whether the requester is a tester or administrator.

### Problem to solve

Currently, OpenClaw has an `output-sanitizer` skill that provides guidance on redacting sensitive information, but it is **not automatically applied** to agent outputs. This means:

1. **Security Risk**: When agents read configuration files (like `openclaw.json`) or other sensitive files, they may return complete content including API keys, tokens, and passwords
2. **Testing Issues**: Test personnel requesting full file information receive unredacted sensitive data
3. **No Automatic Protection**: There is no configuration option to enable automatic output filtering
4. **Manual Dependency**: Users must manually remember to apply sanitization rules

### Proposed solution

### 1. Configuration Option
Add a new configuration section to enable automatic output sanitization:

```json5
{
  outputSanitization: {
    enabled: true,              // Master switch
    mode: "auto",               // auto | strict | off
    scope: "all",               // all | tools | responses
    redactPatterns: [
      // Built-in patterns (can be overridden)
      "\\bAKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}\\b",                    // AWS Access Key
      "\\bsk-[a-zA-Z0-9]{48}\\b",                  // OpenAI API Key
      "\\bsk-ant-[a-zA-Z0-9-]{80,}\\b",            // Anthropic Key
      "\\bghp_[a-zA-Z0-9]{36}\\b",                 // GitHub Token
      "\\b[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\\.[A-Z|a-z]{2,}\\b",  // Email
      "\\b\\d{3}-\\d{2}-\\d{4}\\b",                // SSN
      "\\b\\d{4}-\\d{4}-\\d{4}-\\d{4}\\b",         // Credit Card
      "password\\s*[:=]\\s*['\"]([^'\"]+)['\"]",    // Passwords
      "-----BEGIN.*PRIVATE KEY-----",              // Private Keys
      "eyJ[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+\\.eyJ[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+",     // JWT Tokens
      "<db-scheme>://[^\\s]+",                     // Database URLs
    ],
    exceptions: {
      // Allow specific patterns in certain contexts
      allowInCodeBlocks: false,    // Don't redact in code blocks
      allowInQuotes: false,        // Don't redact in quoted strings
      allowList: [],               // Specific patterns to never redact
    },
    reporting: {
      enabled: true,              // Log redaction events
      level: "warn",              // log level for redactions
      includeOriginal: false,     // Never log original sensitive values
    }
  }
}
```

### 2. Modes of Operation

#### `auto` (Recommended)
- Apply sanitization to all outputs
- Use smart detection (context-aware)
- Preserve code structure when possible
- Mask sensitive values while maintaining readability

#### `strict`
- Aggressive redaction
- Any potential sensitive pattern is redacted
- Higher false positive rate, maximum security

#### `off`
- Disable automatic sanitization
- Manual application only (current behavior)

### 3. Scope Options

#### `all`
- Sanitize all agent outputs (responses, tool results, file reads)

#### `tools`
- Only sanitize tool outputs (file reads, exec results, etc.)

#### `responses`
- Only sanitize final agent responses

### 4. Implementation Approach

#### Option A: Middleware Layer (Recommended)
Add a sanitization middleware in the agent output pipeline:

```
Agent Response → Sanitization Middleware → Channel Delivery
```

**Pros:**
- Centralized control
- Consistent behavior across all channels
- Easy to configure and debug
- Performance impact minimal

**Cons:**
- Requires changes to core agent loop

#### Option B: Skill-Based Auto-Application
Enhance the `output-sanitizer` skill to automatically run:

**Pros:**
- Leverages existing skill infrastructure
- Less invasive code changes
- Skill can be updated independently

**Cons:**
- Skills run after agent response
- May not catch all output paths
- More complex to maintain

#### Option C: Post-Processing Hook
Add a post-processing hook that can be configured:

```json5
{
  agents: {
    defaults: {
      postProcess: [
        {
          type: "output-sanitizer",
          config: { mode: "auto" }
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

**Pros:**
- Flexible and extensible
- Can add multiple processors
- Easy to enable/disable per agent

**Cons:**
- Adds complexity to configuration
- Requires new hook infrastructure

### 5. Redaction Strategy

#### Pattern Matching
Use regex patterns to detect sensitive data:

```javascript
const patterns = {
  awsAccessKey: /\bAKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}\b/g,
  openAIKey: /\bsk-[a-zA-Z0-9]{48}\b/g,
  anthropicKey: /\bsk-ant-[a-zA-Z0-9-]{80,}\b/g,
  githubToken: /\bghp_[a-zA-Z0-9]{36}\b/g,
  email: /\b[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Z|a-z]{2,}\b/g,
  ssn: /\b\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}\b/g,
  creditCard: /\b\d{4}-\d{4}-\d{4}-\d{4}\b/g,
  password: /password\s*[:=]\s*['"]([^'"]+)['"]/gi,
  privateKey: /-----BEGIN.*PRIVATE KEY-----/g,
  jwt: /eyJ[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+\.eyJ[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+/g,
  databaseUrl: /<(postgres|mysql|mongodb|redis):\/\/[^\s]+>/g,
};
```

#### Replacement Strategy

**Conservative (Default):**
- Replace with `[REDACTED]`
- Preserve context and structure
- Example: `apiKey: "sk-abc123..."` → `apiKey: "[REDACTED]"`

**Masked:**
- Show partial value
- Example: `sk-abc123...xyz` → `sk-****...****`

**Hashed:**
- Replace with hash (for debugging)
- Example: `sk-abc123...` → `[REDACTED:sha256:abc123...]`

### 6. Reporting and Logging

When redaction occurs, log a structured event:

```json
{
  "event": "output_sanitized",
  "timestamp": "2026-03-12T07:35:00Z",
```

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

The official live Codex Docker harness cannot complete its compaction-stress lane on current `main`. During the compaction flow, the gateway reloads the bundled Codex plugin from the source-staged tree. That reload resolves the plugin's `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*` imports against the staged root `package.json`, whose public `exports` intentionally omit private-local-only SDK subpaths.

The first deterministic failure is `openclaw/plugin-sdk/keyed-async-queue` with `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED`. The same Codex extension also imports the private-local-only `llm` and `text-utility-runtime` subpaths, but the first failure prevents the lane from reaching them.

This is a regression introduced by #111451 (`c7e7ac2728`). The exact same isolated compaction-stress command passes on its parent (`e6d7aee41d`) and fails on current `main` (`e07de4c561`).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Check out current `main` at `e07de4c56159fb90e811482b34ff466438c3cf54`.
2. Use empty temporary OpenClaw config/workspace directories so no existing gateway state is involved.
3. Run the official live harness with unrelated probes disabled and compaction stress enabled:

```bash
OPENCLAW_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-live-codex-config \
OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-live-codex-workspace \
OPENCLAW_LIVE_CODEX_HARNESS_SUBAGENT_PROBE=0 \
OPENCLAW_LIVE_CODEX_HARNESS_GUARDIAN_PROBE=0 \
OPENCLAW_LIVE_CODEX_HARNESS_IMAGE_PROBE=0 \
OPENCLAW_LIVE_CODEX_HARNESS_MCP_PROBE=0 \
OPENCLAW_LIVE_CODEX_HARNESS_COMPACTION_STRESS=1 \
pnpm test:docker:live-codex-harness
```

4. Observe the Codex plugin reload fail before the compaction-stress assertions complete.

### Expected behavior

The official source-staged live harness should be able to reload the bundled Codex plugin and complete the compaction-stress lane while keeping private-local plugin SDK subpaths unavailable to external/public package consumers.

### Actual behavior

The lane fails deterministically with:

```text
GatewayClientRequestError: PluginLoadFailureError: plugin load failed: codex:
Error [ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED]: Package subpath
'./plugin-sdk/keyed-async-queue' is not defined by "exports" in
/tmp/<staged-source>/package.json imported from /tmp/<staged-source>/src...
```

Current-main result:

```text
commit: e07de4c56159fb90e811482b34ff466438c3cf54
tests: 1 failed, 1 skipped
failure: 52.04s
```

Control result using the same command and environment on the parent of #111451:

```text
commit: e6d7aee41d684371f64cd2c309922af0e3f5e56d
tests: 1 passed, 1 skipped
test duration: 471.46s
```

Without compaction stress, the current-main harness gets through normal Codex agent turns and reaches later probes, so this is specifically a reload/source-staging failure exercised by the compaction path rather than a general Codex app-server startup failure.

### OpenClaw version

`main` at `e07de4c56159fb90e811482b34ff466438c3cf54` (package version 2026.7.2)

### Operating system

Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, Linux 7.0.0-22-generic x86_64; Docker Engine 29.1.3

### Install method

Source checkout using the official `pnpm test:docker:live-codex-harness` Docker lane

### Model

`openai/gpt-5.6-luna`

### Provider / routing chain

OpenAI Codex app-server harness via `@openai/codex` / `codex-cli 0.144.6`

### Configuration

Isolated empty OpenClaw config and workspace directories. Codex auth was staged by the official harness. Unrelated image, MCP, guardian, and subagent probes were disabled to isolate the compaction lane.

### Logs and evidence

The failure happens after the live image builds, Codex CLI preflight succeeds, the gateway harness starts, and the compaction path triggers a plugin reload. The thrown package path is the source-staged root package, not an external npm-installed plugin package.

Regression boundary:

- `e6d7aee41d` (parent of #111451): passes the same compaction-stress lane.
- `c7e7ac2728` (#111451): reclassifies many SDK facades, including `keyed-async-queue`, `llm`, and `text-utility-runtime`, as private-local-only and removes their public exports.
- `e07de4c561` (current `main`): fails on the first private-local Codex import during compaction reload.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: contributors and maintainers using the official live Codex Docker harness to validate compaction behavior.
- Frequency: deterministic when `OPENCLAW_LIVE_CODEX_HARNESS_COMPACTION_STRESS=1` under the isolated command above.
- Consequence: the official live regression lane cannot reach its compaction assertions, leaving Codex compaction changes without the intended end-to-end proof.
- User impact: no direct production outage is claimed by this report; the impact is loss of trustworthy live regression coverage for a user-facing runtime path.

### Additional information

Related but distinct:

- #111662 covers externally installed official plugins importing `text-utility-runtime` and requires a maintainer decision about the public SDK contract.
- #111660 covers an external third-party plugin importing another private-local-only subpath.

This report does not require widening the public Plugin SDK. A focused fix should keep external/public package resolution closed while making the trusted source-staged live harness resolve the canonical private-local-only subpaths used by bundled plugins. A wildcard `./plugin-sdk/*` public export would be the wrong fix.

Investigation and draft preparation were AI-assisted. The reproduction commands, commit comparison, Docker runs, and results above were executed and verified in the reported environment.

issues.body:
## Bug type

Incorrect behavior without a crash

## Beta blocker

No

## Summary

Slack's native assistant thread status can disappear without leaving enough evidence to identify why. The monitor catches every `assistant.threads.setStatus` failure, writes it only through verbose logging, and resolves successfully, so the shared typing lifecycle never reaches `onStartError`.

The Slack pipeline also inherits the generic 3-second keepalive and 60-second maximum duration even though Slack thread status has a 2-minute TTL. This creates many more API calls than needed and clears the indicator during otherwise healthy replies that take longer than one minute.

Finally, the configured `typingReaction` is added only after native status succeeds, so a native status failure also prevents that fallback indicator.

## Reproduction steps

1. Configure the Slack channel with a `typingReaction`.
2. Start a threaded reply.
3. Make `assistant.threads.setStatus` reject, for example with a mocked Slack rate-limit error containing `retryAfter: 10`.
4. Observe that `setSlackThreadStatus` resolves, the typing lifecycle does not receive the error, and the fallback reaction is not added.
5. On a successful long-running reply, observe that the generic controller attempts status every 3 seconds and auto-clears at 60 seconds.

## Expected behavior

- Native status failures reach the typing lifecycle and identify `assistant.threads.setStatus`, including structured Slack details such as `retryAfter`.
- The fallback typing reaction is independent of native status success.
- Slack refreshes status comfortably within its 2-minute TTL without calling the API every 3 seconds.
- Long, healthy replies keep status beyond 60 seconds while retaining a finite stuck-turn watchdog.

## Actual behavior

- The monitor swallows all native status failures into verbose-only logging.
- The fallback reaction is short-circuited when native status rejects.
- Slack inherits a 3-second keepalive and 60-second maximum duration.

## OpenClaw version

Observed in 2026.7.1; reproduced against current `main` at `9309a4fce94012af427a3e43df129bb882b42349`.

## Operating system

Linux x64

## Installation method

npm/package runtime and source checkout

## Model/provider

Not provider-specific; this occurs in the Slack feedback lifecycle before model completion.

## Evidence

Focused regression tests reproduce all three behaviors:

- A mocked Slack rate-limit rejection resolves instead of rejecting.
- Slack typing options contain neither a transport-specific keepalive nor a longer bounded duration.
- The fallback typing reaction receives zero calls when native status rejects.

The existing local gateway log also contained generic Slack Web API retry warnings with a 10-second retry delay, but did not identify the API method. This issue does not claim those historical warnings came from `assistant.threads.setStatus`; the missing method attribution is part of the observability defect.

## Impact

Users can see acknowledgement reactions while the special Slack thinking/typing indicator is absent, with no actionable log explaining whether the cause was rate limiting, permissions, or another Slack API failure. High-frequency refreshes also add avoidable API traffic.

issues.title: Webchat session continuity lost on every gateway restart (session_entries pointer reset to new empty session)
issues.body:
## Summary

After every gateway process restart (rebuild, `docker compose up -d`, or any restart of the `openclaw-gateway` container), the "current session" pointer for a webchat direct-chat key (e.g. `agent:<agentId>:main`) silently gets reassigned to a brand-new, empty session instead of resuming the session that was active before the restart. The prior conversation's content is **not lost** — it remains fully intact in `sessions` / `transcript_events` — but it becomes unreachable through normal UI navigation (webchat, Control UI thread list), because both only resolve "the current session" via a single-row-per-key pointer.

## Environment

- OpenClaw version: `v2026.7.2-beta.3` (commit `d111bef0eed5aefb1e7c5ac59801c1f0924495f1`)
- Deployment: Docker Compose, `openclaw-gateway` + `openclaw-cli` sharing one image/network
- Storage: per-agent SQLite (`agents/<agentId>/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite`)
- Surface: webchat direct chat (`chatType: "direct"`, `origin.provider: "webchat"`)

## Reproduction

1. Have an active webchat conversation with an agent (session key `agent:main:main`), actively exchanging messages.
2. While the conversation is in progress, restart the gateway container (in our case: `docker compose build --no-cache openclaw-gateway && docker compose up -d`, which recreates both `openclaw-gateway` and `openclaw-cli`).
3. Reconnect the webchat client (automatic on WS reconnect).
4. Observe: the webchat thread for `agent:main:main` now shows a brand-new, essentially empty session instead of resuming the conversation from step 1.

## Evidence gathered

Session that was active immediately before the restart:

```
session_id: 537f81bd-9380-41db-863c-539f8a9cfb89
session_key: agent:main:main
created_at:  2026-07-21 03:45:08 UTC
updated_at:  2026-07-21 07:35:22 UTC   (last real message)
status: done
event count in transcript_events: 141 (72 with visible text content)
```

This session contains a real, continuous 72-message conversation, ending mid-topic with a complete assistant response — clear evidence the conversation was live and coherent right up to the restart.

Immediately after the gateway container came back up (`docker compose up -d` completed ~07:51–07:59 UTC), a *new* session appeared:

```
session_id: aa85d968-8145-4eb7-a12a-57c9e618684e
session_key: agent:main:main
created_at: 2026-07-21 07:59:27 UTC
status: running -> done (within ~15s, i.e. answered with no prior context)
```

The `session_entries` table (which appears to hold the current session pointer per `session_key`) had exactly **one row** for `session_key = 'agent:main:main'`, and after the restart it pointed to `aa85d968...` — the new session — not `537f81bd...`:

```sql
select session_key, session_id, updated_at, status from session_entries where session_key='agent:main:main';
-- ('agent:main:main', 'aa85d968-8145-4eb7-a12a-57c9e618684e', 1784620916528, 'done')
```

Meanwhile, `sessions.list` (gateway RPC) reported yet a *third*, older, unrelated session (`c6bb47f6-...`, pinned, last real content from 2 days earlier) as the entry for this key at one point during the restart window, with `updatedAt` bumped to "now" despite no new content — suggesting the pinned session's metadata is also touched by some startup/reattach routine, independent of the `session_entries` pointer described above. Both behaviors point at the same underlying issue: whatever resolves "the current session for a webchat key" on gateway startup does not consistently pick the most recently *content-active* session for that key.

Code path we traced (may not be complete, offered as a starting point): `src/config/sessions/conversation-registry.ts`, `selectConversationRows()`, which joins `session_entries` (`se`) ordered by `se.updated_at DESC` — this table appears to be a single-row-per-`session_key` pointer table, so whatever writes/overwrites this row on gateway boot for an in-progress webchat session is the likely root cause.

## Impact

Any user with an in-progress webchat conversation loses UI access to that conversation's continuation the moment the gateway container restarts for any reason (routine maintenance rebuild, crash/restart, image update). The data itself is not deleted (recoverable by direct SQLite inspection of `transcript_events`), but there is no supported UI or RPC path we found (`sessions.describe` requires only `key` and resolves to the *current* pointer, not a specific `sessionId`) to resume or even view the orphaned session without manual database access.

## Suggested areas to investigate

- Whether gateway boot/reattach logic for webchat sessions creates a new session unconditionally instead of resuming the last non-archived, non-expired session for a key.
- Whether `session_entries` should track the most recent *content* update (`transcript_updated_at`) rather than being overwritten by a boot-time reattach event.
- Whether `sessions.describe` (or a new RPC) should support fetching by `sessionId` directly, to allow recovering/viewing orphaned sessions under a shared key without raw database access.

Happy to provide the anonymized SQLite excerpt used for this investigation if useful.

issues.body:
**Version:** 2026.7.1 (npm), Telegram channel.

**Config:** `channels.telegram.linkPreview: false`.

**Expected:** no Telegram link-preview cards on any bot message.

**Actual:** replies delivered via draft streaming still unfurl the first URL. Non-streamed sends (e.g. the `message` tool / CLI send path) correctly suppress previews.

**Analysis (from the published dist):**

- The non-stream send path honors the flag: `send-*.js` builds `linkPreviewOptions` from `account.config.linkPreview` and attaches `link_preview_options: { is_disabled: true }`.
- The ingress spool also wires `linkPreview: telegramCfg.linkPreview` into `deliveryBaseOptions` and into `editStreamMessage` (via `editMessageTelegram`), so those paths are fine.
- **But `createTelegramDraftStream` (bot-deps bundle) never sets `link_preview_options` at all** — its `sendMessageParams` / `richMessageParams` only carry thread/reply params, and its internal `editMessageText` calls pass no preview options either. The factory isn't even given a `linkPreview` option at the creation site in the spool (`createDraftLane`).
- The preview would still be cleaned up at finalization by `editStreamMessage` (which does pass `linkPreview`), **except** finalization deliberately skips the edit when the streamed draft text already equals the final text (`deliveredText === text.trimEnd()` → `stream.stop()`, finalized). In that common case the draft message *is* the final message and the preview persists.

**Repro:** enable draft streaming on Telegram, set `linkPreview: false`, ask the agent anything that makes it include a URL in its reply. The streamed message keeps the unfurl.

**Suggested fix:** pass `linkPreview` into `createTelegramDraftStream` from `telegramCfg` and apply `link_preview_options: { is_disabled: true }` on its initial `sendMessage` and every `editMessageText` when `linkPreview === false` (edits without the field re-enable the preview server-side).

Happy to test a fix — we're currently carrying a local patch that force-disables previews across the draft stream's send/edit calls.

issues.body:
## Bug type

Crash (process exits); regression from the prior compacted usage-cache representation.

## Beta release blocker

No. This is a core Gateway crash, not a plugin-compatibility beta blocker.

## Summary

On OpenClaw `2026.7.2-beta.5`, opening the Control UI Usage/Profile surface can crash the Gateway with a Node/V8 heap OOM when an agent has hundreds of persisted usage rollups.

The per-session SQLite rollups in `cache_entries` (`scope = 'session-cost-usage-rollup-v1'`) each persist the complete `pricingFingerprint`. In beta.5 that fingerprint includes the hosted catalog pricing payload and is about 2.6 MB in this reproduction. With 645 sessions, the rollup rows total about 2.1 GB, of which about 1.67 GB is repeated fingerprint text. The reader selects every `value_json` row at once, and Node's SQLite `.all()` materializes those strings into V8 until the process reaches its roughly 4.1 GB heap limit and aborts.

This is a Gateway availability regression. It is not related to memory search, the memory context engine, or LosslessClaw.

## Environment

- OpenClaw: `2026.7.2-beta.5` (`ee929db`)
- Node.js: `v26.3.0`
- OS: macOS arm64
- Install method: packaged npm runtime launched as a supervised Gateway service
- Model/provider: not model-call dependent; the crash is in local usage aggregation with hosted catalog pricing enabled
- Gateway has multiple agents; affected agent has 645 historical sessions/rollups
- Gateway supervised externally; supervisor observed three automatic restarts from this crash

## Reproduction

### End-to-end reproduction

1. Run OpenClaw `2026.7.2-beta.5` with the hosted model catalog available.
2. Use an agent with several hundred historical session transcripts.
3. Open the Control UI Usage/Profile surface so that `usage.cost` / `sessions.usage` runs and the per-session usage rollups are populated.
4. Inspect the affected agent's SQLite database:

```bash
sqlite3 -readonly ~/.openclaw/agents/<agent>/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite "
SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS rows,
  SUM(LENGTH(value_json)) AS total_json_bytes,
  ROUND(AVG(LENGTH(value_json)), 1) AS avg_row_bytes,
  MAX(LENGTH(value_json)) AS max_row_bytes,
  SUM(LENGTH(json_extract(value_json, '$.pricingFingerprint'))) AS fingerprint_bytes,
  MIN(LENGTH(json_extract(value_json, '$.pricingFingerprint'))) AS min_fingerprint_bytes,
  MAX(LENGTH(json_extract(value_json, '$.pricingFingerprint'))) AS max_fingerprint_bytes,
  COUNT(DISTINCT LENGTH(json_extract(value_json, '$.pricingFingerprint'))) AS distinct_fingerprint_lengths
FROM cache_entries
WHERE scope = 'session-cost-usage-rollup-v1';
"
```

Observed:

```text
rows                     645
total_json_bytes         2099280050
avg_row_bytes            3254697.8
max_row_bytes            3457477
fingerprint_bytes        1671805815
min_fingerprint_bytes    2591947
max_fingerprint_bytes    2591947
distinct_lengths         1
```

A second read-only comparison confirmed `differing_rows = 0`: all 645 rows contain the same fingerprint value, not merely the same-length value.

5. Keep the Usage/Profile view open or reopen it after the cache is populated.
6. The Gateway aborts while Node SQLite materializes the rollup rows. A connected UI can immediately retrigger the same path after restart, producing a short crash/restart loop.

The pre-beta.5 cold backup for this same agent had zero rows in this rollup scope. The 645 rows above were generated after the beta.5 upgrade and Usage/Profile access.

### Focused source-level reproduction

A deterministic regression test can use the real rollup writer/reader with:

- a catalog pricing fingerprint large enough to represent the hosted catalog;
- hundreds of synthetic session rollups for one agent;
- a read through `readSessionCostUsageRollupRows()` / `readUsageCostRollups()`.

The failure condition is visible before forcing an actual OOM: total `value_json` bytes grow approximately as `session count × full catalog fingerprint size`, and the read path requests all `value_json` rows in one `.all()` call.

## Logs

Immediately before the first crash, the Control UI requested usage data:

```text
[ws] res ✓ usage.cost
[ws] res ✓ sessions.usage
[diagnostics/memory] memory pressure: level=warning rss=2.48 GiB heap=1.96 GiB
```

The fatal stack was identical across three crashes:

```text
<--- Last few GCs --->

Mark-Compact (reduce) 4074.5 (4106.2) -> 4074.5 (4106.2) MB ... last resort

FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory

node::sqlite::StatementExecutionHelper::ColumnToValue
node::sqlite::ExtractRowValues
node::sqlite::StatementExecutionHelper::All
node::sqlite::StatementSync::All
```

## Expected behavior

Usage/Profile should remain safe and responsive as session count grows. Persisted usage rollups and their read path should not cause cache size or peak Gateway heap to scale by duplicating multi-megabyte global pricing metadata per session.

## Actual behavior

- 645 rollup rows occupy about 2.10 GB.
- About 1.67 GB is the identical 2,591,947-byte `pricingFingerprint` repeated per row.
- Reading all rows materializes enough string data to exceed the V8 heap limit.
- The entire Gateway aborts, interrupting unrelated channel and agent work.

## Regression lineage / prior art

- #99511 reported the same duplication shape in the old `.usage-cost-cache.json` format.
- #99714 fixed that format by storing `pricingFingerprint` once at the cache root.
- #108834 replaced the JSON cache with per-session SQLite rollups. `UsageCostRollupEntry` again stores `pricingFingerprint` inside every row, and `readSessionCostUsageRollupRows()` selects all `value_json` rows for the scope.
- #114060, included in beta.5, changed usage pricing to use hosted catalog data. `resolveModelCostConfigFingerprint()` now includes `modelCatalogPricingFingerprint(config)`, whose `pricing` field contains the catalog fingerprint. This made the repeated value about 2.6 MB in the observed environment.
- #95379, #98827, and #86718 cover earlier whole-JSON-cache OOM/pressure behavior. This report is the new SQLite-rollup recurrence after #108834 plus the fingerprint expansion from #114060.
- #101543 concerns growth in the former `model-pricing-cache.ts`; #114060 removes that implementation, while this report concerns `cache_entries` rollup payloads and the usage reader.

## Scope

This issue is specifically about the beta.5 combination of:

1. full catalog-derived pricing metadata embedded in every per-session usage rollup;
2. unbounded aggregate row size as session count grows; and
3. all rollup JSON values being materialized together in the Gateway process.

No production database rows were deleted or modified while collecting this report.

## Impact and severity

- Affected surface: Gateway process hosting the agent whose usage rollups are read; unrelated agents and channels in the same Gateway are interrupted by the process abort.
- Severity: high availability impact; the entire Gateway exits.
- Frequency: reproduced three times from the same Usage/Profile path and persisted cache state.
- Consequence: supervisor restarts the Gateway, but a connected Usage/Profile view can retrigger the crash after restart.

issues.body:
## Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

## Beta release blocker

No

## Summary

The default `memory-core` plugin causes a live channel task to fail automatic restart recovery on the second sequential Gateway replacement.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Check out `3a85143d979ebb7a254456bf9581a021c27dabf1` with the bundled/default `memory-core` plugin active.
2. Run `openclaw qa suite` in `live-frontier` mode with OpenAI GPT-5.4 and scenario `gateway-restart-multi-live`.
3. Let the scenario replace the Gateway at each replay-safe Code Mode wait checkpoint.
4. Observe that the first restart dispatches restart-safe recovery, while the second restart marks the same task failed.
5. Repeat the scenario; the second attempt fails at the same boundary.

## Expected behavior

The task should resume through all three Gateway replacements and deliver exactly one final audit. This exact live scenario passed through three restarts before the channel restart-recovery hardening in #108283; see the live proof attached to #105126.

## Actual behavior

Both live attempts recovered once, then failed during the second restart. The Gateway emitted a resend notice instead of continuing the task automatically.

## OpenClaw version

2026.7.2 (`3a85143d979ebb7a254456bf9581a021c27dabf1`)

## Operating system

macOS 26.5.2

## Install method

Source checkout, `pnpm` QA CLI

## Model

OpenAI GPT-5.4, fast mode, medium thinking

## Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw Gateway -> OpenAI ChatGPT Responses

## Additional provider/model setup details

The live key was injected only into an isolated QA Gateway environment. Four QA Gateways ran concurrently on separate loopback ports; the failing isolated lane used port 54247.

## Logs

```shell
[main-session-restart-recovery] dispatching restart-safe recovery for agent:qa:qa-channel:direct:restart-multi-live-4d089909
[main-session-restart-recovery] resumed interrupted main session: agent:qa:qa-channel:direct:restart-multi-live-4d089909
[tools] wait failed: code mode run is unavailable or expired
[main-session-restart-recovery] marked interrupted main session failed: agent:qa:qa-channel:direct:restart-multi-live-4d089909 (pre-hook recovery cannot bypass the active before_agent_reply hook)

# Automatic retry, different session, same boundary:
[main-session-restart-recovery] dispatching restart-safe recovery for agent:qa:qa-channel:direct:restart-multi-live-561edf45
[tools] wait failed: code mode run is unavailable or expired
[main-session-restart-recovery] marked interrupted main session failed: agent:qa:qa-channel:direct:restart-multi-live-561edf45 (pre-hook recovery cannot bypass the active before_agent_reply hook)
```

## Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

- Previously passing live three-restart proof: #105126
- Channel restart-recovery hardening that introduced the broad hook-name gate: #108283
- Current `memory-core` registers `before_agent_reply` globally but immediately returns for every trigger except `heartbeat` and `cron`.
- Local archive and live GitHub searches found no matching open issue or PR.

## Impact and severity

- Affected: channel and Control UI tasks using the default bundled `memory-core` plugin and automatic restart recovery.
- Severity: high for repeated restarts because a replay-safe in-flight task is abandoned.
- Frequency: 2/2 observed live attempts failed on the second replacement.
- Consequence: the user must resend the task, losing the promised automatic recovery and risking duplicated work.

## Additional information

Last known good: the live scenario passed three sequential replacements in #105126 before #108283 landed. First observed bad: current `main` after #108283. The likely owner-boundary fix is to let typed hooks declare a host-enforced trigger scope, so restart safety ignores a hook only when the host itself guarantees that hook cannot run for recovered user turns; a plugin-local exception based only on implementation convention would weaken the fail-closed contract.

issues.title: Bug: Sub-agents cannot receive images via read tool — image data omitted from tool results
issues.body:
## Bug: Sub-agents cannot receive images via `read` tool — image data is omitted from tool results

### Summary

When a sub-agent (spawned via `sessions_spawn`) calls the `read` tool on an image file (jpg, png, etc.), the image data is marked as `"omitted": true` in the tool result and never sent to the model. The sub-agent receives only the text label `"Read image file [image/jpeg]"` and hallucinates a description instead of actually seeing the image.

This happens even when:
- The sub-agent's model supports vision (e.g., `nemotron3-precision` with `vision` capability)
- `agents.defaults.imageModel` is configured with a vision model
- The main agent can read the same image successfully

### Reproduction

1. Spawn a sub-agent with a vision-capable model:
```javascript
sessions_spawn({
  agentId: "vision",
  task: "Read the image /tmp/frame-01.jpg with the read tool and describe what you see.",
  taskName: "vision-test"
})
```

2. The sub-agent calls `read` on the image file:
```json
{
  "role": "toolResult",
  "toolName": "read",
  "content": [
    { "type": "text", "text": "Read image file [image/jpeg]" },
    { "type": "image", "mimeType": "image/jpeg", "omitted": true, "bytes": 26052 }
  ]
}
```

3. The image is never sent to the model. The sub-agent hallucinates a description.

### Expected behavior

When the sub-agent's model supports vision (or when `imageModel` is configured), the image data should be sent to the model as an image content block, just like it works for the main agent session.

### Actual behavior

The image is stripped from the tool result (`"omitted": true`), likely in `openclaw-tools` or `session-transcript-path` where `entry.omitted = true` is set for image entries in sub-agent contexts.

### Environment

- OpenClaw: v2026.7.1
- OS: macOS 26.5.2 (arm64)
- Model: `ollama/nemotron3-precision` (vision-capable, confirmed via `ollama show`)
- `agents.defaults.imageModel.primary`: `ollama/nemotron3-precision`
- Sub-agent spawned via `sessions_spawn` with `agentId: "vision"`

### Workaround

Using the Ollama REST API directly via `exec` (curl + base64) works fine — the model receives the image and describes it correctly. This suggests the issue is specifically in OpenClaw's tool result routing for sub-agents, not in the model or Ollama backend.

### Impact

- Agent `vision` cannot analyze images via `sessions_spawn`
- Any sub-agent that needs to read image files is affected
- Forces workaround with direct API calls, bypassing OpenClaw's tool system

issues.title: [Bug]: session maintenance maxEntries ineffective — thread session entries unconditionally protected from capping
issues.body:
## Description

The session store maintenance setting `maxEntries` (default: 500) is effectively **non-functional** for Slack thread sessions. All thread entries are unconditionally protected from capping by `isProtectedSessionMaintenanceEntry()`:

```javascript
// store-CRMOBYMq.js:658
if (parseSessionThreadInfoFast(sessionKey).threadId) return true;
```

Every Slack thread creates a session entry with key pattern `agent:main:slack:channel:<CID>:thread:<ts>`. Since `threadId` is always set, every thread entry is immune to capping. This causes `sessions.json` to grow without bound as threads accumulate.

## Impact

- **Unbounded store growth**: sessions.json can grow to thousands of entries
- **Cron job failures**: At ~700+ entries (~3.2MB), isolated agent-turn cron jobs consistently fail with `CronSessionLifecycleClaimError` because the lifecycle revision persistence check hits a timing/race window related to the oversized in-memory store operations
- `maxEntries` configuration becomes a no-op; no entries are ever eligible for removal

## To Reproduce

1. Use OpenClaw with Slack for several weeks (accumulate thread sessions)
2. Set `session.maintenance.maxEntries` to any value
3. Observe that sessions.json continues growing past that limit with thread entries

## Expected Behavior

Thread session entries should be subject to capping, either by:
- Count-based limit (keep most recent N threads, cap the rest)
- Age-based limit (protect only threads updated within X days)
- Or at minimum, `maxEntries` should take precedence over thread protection when store exceeds the limit

## Environment

- OpenClaw version: 2026.7.1
- Platform: Linux (VPS)
- Chat provider: Slack

## Additional Context

Discovered while investigating `CronSessionLifecycleClaimError` failures in isolated agent-turn cron jobs. Confirmed via controlled experiment: with full sessions.json (718 entries / 3.2MB → CronSessionLifecycleClaimError), with minimal sessions.json (21 channel entries only → no error, cron job ran successfully).

issues.body:
## Summary
OpenClaw gateway heartbeat scheduler exhibits timer-reference decay after ~24h uptime. Decay manifests as rapid-fire cycles (1-minute intervals instead of configured cadence), then either self-recovers or stays stuck.

## Environment
- OpenClaw version: 2026.6.11 (config) on v26.3.1 (binary)
- Host: macOS Darwin 25.5.0 arm64
- Workaround in place: daily 06:00 PHT gateway restart via launchd

## Reproduction
1. Start fresh OpenClaw gateway
2. Configure heartbeat cron jobs at fixed cadence (e.g. every 1h)
3. Let gateway run >24h without restart
4. Monitor `~/.openclaw/cache/tom_state.json` field `delta_history`
5. Observe: cadence degrades from healthy (e.g. 43-min deltas) to rapid-fire (1-min intervals)
6. Pattern is sometimes self-recovering (~20 cycles, then 73-min delta restored), but underlying decay is not fixed

## Observed Data
- Healthy cycle count before decay: ~6 cycles
- Decay onset: ~24h uptime
- Self-recovery observed: 2026-07-02 and 2026-07-05 (16:08–16:28 PHT)
- Pattern: 3 healthy cycles → rapid-fire burst → self-recovery OR stuck

## Expected Behavior
Heartbeat scheduler maintains configured cadence indefinitely, OR provides a clean reset path that doesn't require full gateway restart.

## Actual Behavior
Timer reference decays silently. No alerting on decay (until secondary symptoms appear). Workaround requires full gateway restart which loses in-flight work.

## Impact
- Time-based cron jobs fire at wrong times
- False sense of health (TOM cache reports "NOMINAL" while cadence is broken)
- Operational burden: daily restart scheduled as workaround

## Proposed Fix Options
1. Add a `cadence_health` watchdog that auto-restarts the scheduler (not the whole gateway) when decay detected
2. Expose a `scheduler.reset()` API
3. Fix the root cause: identify what reference is decaying (timer object? cached interval?)
4. Document the decay pattern + restart requirement in the official config guide

## Related
Filed from gap audit 2026-07-12 (Yano.AI internal: G2).

issues.body:
**Version:** OpenClaw 2026.7.2 (gateway)

## Summary
A locally-configured Ollama model (`ollama/llama3.2:3b`, remote-over-Tailscale instance, not localhost) is present in `agents.defaults.models` with a valid alias, and the Ollama server itself is reachable and healthy. Despite this, invoking the model fails with a `ProviderAuthError`, and the model never appears in the Control UI chat composer's model picker.

## Environment
- `models.providers.ollama.baseUrl`: `http://<tailscale-host>:11434` (remote host, not `127.0.0.1`)
- `models.providers.ollama.apiKey`: set in config (flagged by `openclaw doctor` for SecretRef migration, confirming it is present)
- `agents.defaults.models["ollama/llama3.2:3b"]`: present, `alias: "llama"`
- Ollama plugin (`@openclaw/ollama-provider`): enabled

## Reproduction
1. Configure a remote Ollama instance under `models.providers.ollama` with `baseUrl` + `apiKey`, and add `ollama/llama3.2:3b` to `agents.defaults.models`.
2. Confirm the model is reachable directly: `curl http://<host>:11434/api/tags` returns the model.
3. Run `openclaw models list` — model shows `Auth: -` (not `yes`) and tag `configured,alias:llama`.
4. Run `openclaw models status` — reports:
   ```
   - ollama effective=missing:missing | models.json=marker(ollama-local) | source=models.json: .../agent/models.json
   ...
   Model route issues
   - ollama/llama3.2:3b [indeterminate] Auth readiness could not be confirmed for ollama/llama3.2:3b.
   ```
5. Pin a session to `ollama/llama3.2:3b` and send any prompt.
6. Gateway log shows immediate failure (~90ms, no network call reaches Ollama):
   ```
   error diagnostic lane task error: lane=session:<key> durationMs=90
   error="ProviderAuthError: No API key found for provider \"ollama\".
   Auth store: .../agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite (agentDir: .../agent).
   Configure auth for this agent (openclaw agents add <id>) or copy only
   portable static auth profiles from the main agentDir."
   ```
   ```
   warn model-fallback/decision ... "reason":"auth","status":401,
   "code":"missin…auth", requestedProvider=ollama, requestedModel=llama3.2:3b,
   fallbackStepFinalOutcome=chain_exhausted
   ```
7. Separately, in the Control UI chat composer's model picker, Ollama never appears as a provider column, even though `agents.defaults.models` (which per docs at `control-ui.md` should drive the picker directly: "If `agents.defaults.models` is present, that allowlist drives the picker") explicitly lists it. A full gateway restart and browser cache clear do not change this.

## Expected behavior
- A configured `models.providers.ollama.apiKey` (or the absence of any key requirement for a local/keyless Ollama deployment) should satisfy the provider's auth check, not raise `ProviderAuthError: No API key found`.
- Per documented behavior, the model should appear in the Control UI composer picker regardless of auth-readiness status, since it's explicitly allowlisted.

## Actual behavior
- Runtime auth resolution for the `ollama` provider does not see the configured `apiKey` and rejects the request with a 401-style `ProviderAuthError` before any network call to the Ollama server.
- The Control UI composer model picker omits the model entirely, contradicting the documented allowlist-driven behavior — likely a symptom of the same underlying auth-status resolution, since the only allowlisted model with `indeterminate`/`missing` auth is the one missing from the picker.

## Notes / hypothesis
- `openclaw models status` auth overview shows `ollama effective=missing:missing`, distinct from the `profiles:...sqlite` resolution path used successfully by `anthropic` and `openai` (both OAuth-based, both `status=usable`). It looks like the ollama provider's auth resolver only checks the `openclaw-agent.sqlite` auth-profile store (used for OAuth/API-key profiles registered via `openclaw models auth` / `openclaw agents add`) and never reads `models.providers.ollama.apiKey` directly from static config, even though other tooling (`openclaw doctor`) treats that field as the authoritative source.
- Not a networking issue: the Ollama host itself responds correctly to direct `curl` requests from the same container.

## Suggested fix directions
1. Have the ollama provider's auth resolver also check `models.providers.ollama.apiKey` from static config (or explicitly document that only auth-profile-store credentials are supported, and error at config-validate time if `apiKey` is set in `models.providers.ollama` but unused).
2. If a provider is configured with no auth requirement at all (fully open local/remote Ollama), skip the auth-readiness gate for that provider rather than reporting `missing`/`indeterminate`.
3. Investigate whether the Control UI composer picker's provider list filters allowlisted models by auth-readiness status; if so, either fix the filter to match documented allowlist-driven behavior, or update the docs to reflect the actual filtering behavior.

issues.body:
## Summary

On days where the REM dreaming phase finds zero candidate truths, the pipeline still writes a placeholder bullet into the REM dream file. That placeholder is subsequently ingested by light sleep, emitted as a `- Candidate:` line into the daily memory file, and then promoted by `applyShortTermPromotions` into the long-term `workspace/MEMORY.md`. Each empty-REM day permanently bloats `MEMORY.md` with a meaningless entry.

## Version

`openclaw@2026.5.7` (npm global install).

## Reproduction

Run the dreaming pipeline on a day where REM produces no candidate truths above the 0.45 confidence threshold (e.g. a low-activity day).

1. `workspace/memory/dreaming/rem/YYYY-MM-DD.md` ends up containing:
   ```
   ### Possible Lasting Truths
   - No strong candidate truths surfaced.
   ```

2. The next light sleep pass ingests that placeholder bullet as a memory entry. `buildLightDreamingBody` emits it as a Candidate line into the daily memory file `workspace/memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md`:
   ```
   - Candidate: Possible Lasting Truths: No strong candidate truths surfaced.
     - confidence: 0.00
     - evidence: memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md:443-443
     - recalls: 0
     - status: staged
   ```

3. `applyShortTermPromotions` (in `dist/short-term-promotion-*.js`) treats it as a valid candidate. It passes `isContaminatedDreamingSnippet` (no `confidence`/`evidence`/`status`/`recalls` keys in the snippet itself) and accumulates enough score to be promoted. `workspace/MEMORY.md` gains:
   ```
   <!-- openclaw-memory-promotion:memory:memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md:443:443 -->
   - - Candidate: Possible Lasting Truths: No strong candidate truths surfaced. [score=0.832 recalls=0 avg=0.620 source=memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md:13-13]
   ```

In my workspace this produced three identical noise entries (2026-04-19, 2026-04-20, 2026-04-21) under three separate `## Promoted From Short-Term Memory (YYYY-MM-DD)` headers.

## Expected behavior

Days with zero candidate truths should add **nothing** to long-term `MEMORY.md`. Empty results are not findings.

## Actual behavior

Every empty-REM day produces three pieces of bloat — a placeholder bullet in the REM dream file, a Candidate line in the daily memory file, and a promoted entry in `MEMORY.md`.

## Root cause

In `dist/dreaming-phases-*.js`, `previewRemDreaming`:

```js
const bodyLines = [
    "### Reflections",
    ...reflections,
    "",
    "### Possible Lasting Truths",
    ...candidateTruths.length > 0
        ? candidateTruths.map((entry) => `- ${entry.snippet} [confidence=${entry.confidence.toFixed(2)} evidence=${entry.evidence}]`)
        : ["- No strong candidate truths surfaced."]
];
```

The `else` branch unconditionally emits a human-readable placeholder line into the REM file even when there is nothing to promote. Downstream the placeholder becomes indistinguishable from a real candidate.

## Proposed fix

**1.** `dist/dreaming-phases-*.js` — skip the entire `### Possible Lasting Truths` section when `candidateTruths.length === 0`:

```js
const bodyLines = [
    "### Reflections",
    ...reflections,
    ...(candidateTruths.length > 0 ? [
        "",
        "### Possible Lasting Truths",
        ...candidateTruths.map((entry) => `- ${entry.snippet} [confidence=${entry.confidence.toFixed(2)} evidence=${entry.evidence}]`)
    ] : [])
];
```

**2.** `dist/short-term-promotion-*.js` — defensive filter in `applyShortTermPromotions` so historical placeholders in already-written daily memory files don't get promoted on future runs:

```js
const selected = options.candidates.filter((candidate) => {
    if (isContaminatedDreamingSnippet(candidate.snippet)) return false;
    if (/no strong candidate truths surfaced/i.test(candidate.snippet || "")) return false;
    if (candidate.promotedAt) return false;
    // …
});
```

Both edits applied locally; `node -e "require('…dreaming-phases….js'); require('…short-term-promotion….js')"` loads both modules cleanly.

## Workaround

Patching the two `dist/` files in `/usr/lib/node_modules/openclaw/` as above and stripping the existing placeholder entries from `workspace/MEMORY.md`. The patch is lost on `npm install -g openclaw` upgrade.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

After upgrading to OpenClaw 2026.6.11 (which resolved the indefinite hang reported in #97871), `openclaw agent --local` still fails when using a local Ollama provider. The agent initializes successfully and reaches `embedded run agent start`, but no provider request is issued before the request eventually times out. Direct model execution using `openclaw capability model run --local` continues to succeed with the same Ollama configuration.


### Steps to reproduce

1. Install OpenClaw 2026.6.11.
2. Start Ollama:

```bash
ollama serve
```

3. Verify the local provider works:

```bash
openclaw --profile cleanqwen capability model run \
  --local \
  --model ollama/llama3.2:3b \
  --prompt "Reply with exactly: test"
```

This returns:

```text
test
```

4. Run:

```bash
openclaw --profile cleanqwen agent \
  --local \
  --session-key agent:main:test \
  --message "Reply with exactly: test"
```

5. Observe that the agent reaches startup, logs `embedded run agent start`, but never issues a provider request. After the configured timeout, the embedded run fails with an LLM request timeout.


### Expected behavior

The embedded agent should issue a request to the configured Ollama provider and return the model response, just as `openclaw capability model run --local` successfully does with the same model and provider configuration.


### Actual behavior

The agent starts normally, initializes successfully, and reaches `embedded run agent start`. No provider request is logged after that point, even though Ollama is running and reachable. After the configured timeout, the embedded run fails with an LLM request timeout. Running `openclaw capability model run --local` with the same Ollama model and provider succeeds immediately.


### OpenClaw version

2026.6.11 (e085fa1)

### Operating system

Linux (MX Linux, non-systemd init)

### Install method

npm global

### Model

Ollama: llama3.2:3b

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> Ollama provider -> Ollama

### Additional provider/model setup details

The issue reproduces with a native Ollama provider using `llama3.2:3b`. The Ollama server is running locally on `127.0.0.1:11434` and is reachable (`curl http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/tags` succeeds). Direct model execution with `openclaw capability model run --local` succeeds using the same provider and model. Agent configuration validates successfully.


### Logs

```shell
### Successful direct model test


openclaw capability model run --local --model ollama/llama3.2:3b


Result:


test


### Agent debug log


embedded run agent start


No provider request is logged after this point.

After the configured timeout, the log reports:


embedded run timeout
LLM request timed out
Request timed out before a response was generated
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

No screenshots. Relevant debug logs are included above.

### Impact and severity

Affected: Local embedded agent execution using the native Ollama provider.

Severity: High (blocks local agent workflows).

Frequency: Reproduced on every attempt.

Consequence: Direct model execution succeeds, but the embedded agent cannot complete a request, preventing local autonomous workflows.


### Additional information

This issue was discovered while verifying the fix for #97871. The previous indefinite hang appears to be resolved in 2026.6.11, but a different failure remains. The embedded agent now reaches `embedded run agent start` and eventually times out before any provider request is issued. This appears to be a different failure path from the one addressed in #97871.

issues.title: Clarify or update bundled Ollama Cloud MiniMax static default model
issues.body:
## Summary

OpenClaw `v2026.7.1` appears to handle `minimax-m3:cloud` when it is returned through Ollama Cloud discovery, but the bundled static Ollama Cloud defaults still list `minimax-m2.7:cloud`.

Could you confirm whether `minimax-m2.7:cloud` is still the intended bundled static MiniMax Cloud model, or whether the static defaults should now be updated to `minimax-m3:cloud`?

## Current behavior

In `v2026.7.1`, the bundled static defaults still reference `minimax-m2.7:cloud` in:

- `extensions/ollama/src/defaults.ts`
- `extensions/ollama/openclaw.plugin.json`

`minimax-m3:cloud` appears in Ollama Cloud discovery test coverage, so the model is known to at least part of the codebase, but it is not present as the bundled static MiniMax Cloud default/catalog entry.

## Why this matters

Installations or workflows that rely on the bundled static catalog/default model list rather than runtime Ollama Cloud discovery continue to surface `minimax-m2.7:cloud`.

Locally overriding those static files works as a workaround, but it leaves source checkouts dirty and can interfere with staging or release-sync workflows. The underlying question is whether the static catalog has intentionally stayed on `minimax-m2.7:cloud`, or whether it has drifted behind the discovery behavior.

## Requested clarification

Please confirm which of these is intended:

1. `minimax-m2.7:cloud` should remain the bundled static MiniMax Cloud default for now.
2. The bundled static defaults/catalog should be updated to `minimax-m3:cloud`.
3. Both models should be exposed differently between static defaults and discovery.

If the intended behavior is option 2, the likely files to update are:

- `extensions/ollama/src/defaults.ts`
- `extensions/ollama/openclaw.plugin.json`

It may also be worth checking whether any docs or tests assert the static MiniMax Cloud default.

## Notes

Checked against upstream `release/2026.7.1` / tag `v2026.7.1`:

- `extensions/ollama/src/defaults.ts` still references `minimax-m2.7:cloud`
- `extensions/ollama/openclaw.plugin.json` still references `minimax-m2.7:cloud`
- `minimax-m3:cloud` appears in Ollama Cloud discovery tests, not in the bundled static defaults/catalog entry
