issues.body:
## Summary

All three memory paths broken simultaneously on OpenClaw 2026.6.8 with Ollama/bge-m3 on Linux:

1. **FTS-only** (`provider: none`) — `memory search` hangs indefinitely, killed by timeout
2. **Ollama/bge-m3 with `--force`** — meta corrupted, index identity missing (#91497)
3. **Ollama/bge-m3 without `--force`** — search hangs at "batch start", never completes (#93312)

## Environment

- OpenClaw: 2026.6.8 (844f405)
- OS: Linux 5.15.0-181-generic (x64)
- Provider: Ollama bge-m3 (768-dim vectors)
- Vector store: sqlite-vec (vec0.so)
- Node: v24.16.0
- 9 agents, 250+ memory files

## Reproduction

### Case 1: FTS-only hangs
```bash
openclaw config patch --stdin <<< '{"agents":{"defaults":{"memorySearch":{"provider":"none"}}}}'
systemctl restart openclaw-gateway
openclaw memory search --query "test"
# Hangs indefinitely, killed by SIGTERM
```

### Case 2: --force corrupts meta
```bash
openclaw memory index --agent main --force
openclaw memory search --query "test"
# Returns: "index metadata is missing"
```

### Case 3: Without --force, batch hangs
```bash
openclaw memory index --agent main
# Stuck at "[memory] embeddings: batch start"
# Never reaches "batch completed"
# Killed by timeout after 0/249 files indexed
```

## Root Cause Analysis

8 confirmed bugs in memory subsystem (#91592, #91183, #90787, #51782, #91497, #92018, #93312, #80476). The combination of all three broken paths means there is **no working configuration** for memory search.

## Expected Behavior

At least one of the three paths should work:
- FTS-only should return keyword results
- Embeddings without --force should complete batch processing
- --force should produce valid meta

## Actual Behavior

All three paths fail. Memory search is completely non-functional.

## Workaround

None. `memory_get` works for direct file reads, but semantic/keyword search is dead.

## Related Issues

- #91592: scopeHash mismatch after --force rebuild
- #93312: openai-compatible embedding batch hangs on "batch start"
- #91497: meta not written during --force reindex
- #90787: provider silently resets to "openai" after upgrade
- #51782: FTS-only returns 0 results (closed but not fixed for hangs)
- #91183: index metadata lost after upgrade
- #92018: meta row lost after live memory_search
- #80476: feature request for bundled openai-compatible provider

issues.title: ensurePrivateDirectory corrupts system /tmp permissions (chmod 0700)

labels.name: stale
labels.description: Marked as stale due to inactivity

labels.name: impact:other

issues.body:
## Version
2026.6.11

## Severity
High — breaks MySQL, MariaDB, Postgres, tmux, X11, etc.

## Description

When performing ClawHub skill downloads or other temp-file operations, `ensurePrivateDirectory` in `private-temp-workspace.js` unconditionally runs `chmod(path, 0o700)` on whatever directory is passed as `rootDir`. When that is `os.tmpdir()` → `/tmp`, it changes `/tmp` from `drwxrwxrwt (1777)` to `drwx------ (0700)`, immediately breaking all other processes that write to `/tmp`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install a skill from ClawHub: `openclaw skills install <any-ClawHub-skill>`
2. Check `/tmp` permissions before and after: `stat -c "%a" /tmp`

## Actual behavior

`/tmp` is changed from `drwxrwxrwt (1777)` to `drwx------ (0700)` after the operation. MySQL fails with: "Can't create/write to file '/tmp/#sql_...' (Errcode: 13 - Permission denied)". Other services relying on world-writable `/tmp` are also broken.

## Call chain

```
downloadClawHubSkillArchive()
  → createTempDownloadTarget({ prefix: "openclaw-clawhub-skill", tmpDir: os.tmpdir() })
    → tempWorkspace({rootDir: "/tmp"})
      → createTempWorkspace({rootDir: "/tmp"})
        → ensurePrivateDirectory("/tmp", 0o700)
          → chmod("/tmp", 0o700)        ← BUG
```

## Root cause

1. `ensurePrivateDirectory` runs `chmod(dir, mode)` even when the directory already existed. No check for system directories or sticky-bit.

2. `tryRepairWritableBits` (in both `secure-temp-dir.js` and `tmp-openclaw-dir.js`) checks `(st.mode & 0o22) !== 0` to detect "leaky" permissions. For `/tmp` (mode `0o1777`), `0o1777 & 0o22 = 0o22 ≠ 0`, so `/tmp` is misclassified as "insecure" and tightened to `0o700`. The sticky bit (`0o1000`) is not recognized as a safety mechanism.

## Affected code locations

| File | Function | Issue |
|---|---|---|
| `private-temp-workspace.js` | `ensurePrivateDirectory` | Always chmod's the root dir |
| `secure-temp-dir.js` | `tryRepairWritableBits` | Sticky-bit not recognized |
| `tmp-openclaw-dir.js` | `tryRepairWritableBits` | Sticky-bit not recognized |
| `clawhub-CzhGuc1t.js` | download functions | Passes `tmpDir: os.tmpdir()` |
| `temp-download.js` | `createTempDownloadTarget` | Forwards rootDir to tempWorkspace |
| `install-source-utils.js` | `withTempDir` | Also uses `os.tmpdir()` as rootDir |

## Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (Noble Numbat)

## Install method

npm install -g openclaw, launched as systemd --user service

## Model

N/A — code-level bug, model-independent

## Provider / routing chain

N/A

## Suggested fix

In `ensurePrivateDirectory`, skip chmod when the directory has the sticky bit:

```diff
 async function ensurePrivateDirectory(dir, mode) {
     await fs$1.mkdir(dir, { recursive: true, mode });
+    const st = await fs$1.stat(dir);
+    if ((st.mode & 0o1000) !== 0) return;
     await fs$1.chmod(dir, mode).catch(() => void 0);
 }
```

In `tryRepairWritableBits`, recognize sticky-bit as safe:

```diff
 const isSecureDirForUser = (st) => {
     if (uid === void 0) return true;
     if (typeof st.uid === "number" && st.uid !== uid) return false;
+    if (typeof st.mode === "number" && (st.mode & 0o1000) !== 0) return true;
     if (typeof st.mode === "number" && (st.mode & 18) !== 0) return false;
     return true;
 };
```

## Workaround

Set `TMPDIR=/tmp/openclaw` in the gateway service environment.

```
[Service]
Environment=TMPDIR=/tmp/openclaw
```

The WebSocket manager closes cached connections older than a specific age limit (connection_age_limit). However, if the socket is closed while a stream transaction is active or about to start, it results in unexpected connection abort errors for the user.

Proposed Solution:
Implement a soft age limit where connections are flagged as deprecated but kept open to drain active transactions, and raise warning hooks or allow a grace period for pending streams before initiating the forced socket closure.

issues.title: [Bug]: gateway call runs the full local state-migration preflight for a pure remote RPC command
issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

`openclaw gateway call <method>` is a pure remote RPC client: its action resolves connection options and invokes `callGateway` over the gateway WebSocket (`src/cli/gateway-cli/call.ts`, `src/cli/gateway-cli/register.ts`). It reads local config only to find the URL/token, is already tolerated with an *invalid* local config (`ALLOWED_INVALID_GATEWAY_SUBCOMMANDS` in `src/cli/program/config-guard.ts`), and touches no local state.

Yet CLI bootstrap routes it through the full local state-migration preflight on every invocation:

- `shouldMigrateStateFromPath` (`src/cli/argv.ts`) exempts only `health`, `sessions`, `update status`, and `config get|unset`; `["gateway", "call"]` returns `true`.
- In `ensureConfigReady` (`src/cli/program/config-guard.ts`), `gateway call` is also not in `shouldRunStateMigrationOnlyWithLegacyInputs` (that set is `agent`/`status`/`plugins list`/`tasks`), so `runDoctorConfigPreflight({ migrateState: true, ... })` runs **unconditionally** — not even gated on legacy inputs existing.

So a command whose only job is to ask a *running* gateway something (`gateway call health --json` is the canonical liveness probe for monitoring/watchdog crons) executes local migration detection — and, when legacy inputs exist, the migration move/archive paths — as a bootstrap side effect, concurrently with the gateway that owns that state.

### Steps to reproduce

Deterministic on current `main` (b0ccaa6eec):

1. Unit level: `shouldMigrateStateFromPath(getCommandPathWithRootOptions(["node", "openclaw", "gateway", "call", "health"], 2))` returns `true` (`src/cli/argv.ts`).
2. Behavior level, using the existing `src/cli/program/config-guard.test.ts` harness (mocked `runDoctorConfigPreflight`): `ensureConfigReady({ commandPath: ["gateway", "call"] })` invokes the preflight with `{ migrateState: true, migrateLegacyConfig: false, invalidConfigNote: false }` — with a pristine temp `OPENCLAW_HOME`, no legacy inputs at all.
3. End-to-end: with any legacy state marker present (e.g. `~/.openclaw/tasks/runs.sqlite`), run `openclaw gateway call health --json` — doctor migration output/actions precede the RPC (or the connection error if no gateway is running).

### Expected behavior

`gateway call` bootstrap reads config for connection parameters and performs the RPC. It never runs local state migrations; migrations stay owned by gateway startup, `openclaw doctor --fix`, and commands that actually operate on local state.

### Actual behavior

Every `gateway call` invocation runs the doctor state-migration preflight (`runDoctorConfigPreflight` with `migrateState: true`) during CLI bootstrap, unconditionally. High-frequency monitoring probes repeatedly execute migration scanning; when legacy inputs are present, a read-only remote probe can take local migration actions (move/archive) on state dirs the running gateway owns. With version skew (older/newer CLI probing a gateway of a different version — routine during upgrades) the probing CLI applies *its* idea of migrations to state it does not serve.

### OpenClaw version

Current `main` (b0ccaa6eec); the same predicate ships in 2026.7.1-2.

### Operating system

Linux (Ubuntu 24.04, Node 22) — mechanism is platform-independent.

### Install method

npm (global) in production; source checkout for the repro.

### Model

N/A (CLI bootstrap path, model-independent).

### Provider / routing chain

N/A.

### Additional provider/model setup details

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Logs

Production observation (multi-agent Telegram gateway): a systemd watchdog probes `openclaw gateway call health --json` continuously. Each probe walked the full migration preflight of the CLI build that happened to invoke it. On 2026-07-16 we had a state-schema incident on this host where CLI invocations of a different build against the live `$HOME` advanced SQLite state schemas under a serving gateway (restored from backup); the always-on `gateway call` probe surface is the highest-frequency entry into exactly that class, which is what led us to patch it locally.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

- Predicate: table tests in `src/cli/argv.test.ts` (`decides when to migrate state`) extended with `gateway call` expectations fail on `main` (returns `true`) and pass with the exemption.
- Behavior: a `config-guard.test.ts` case shows `runDoctorConfigPreflight` is invoked for `["gateway", "call"]` on `main` even with a pristine state dir, and — with the fix — is not invoked even when legacy state markers exist.
- Production: the equivalent one-line exemption has been running as a dist-level patch on our production gateway since 2026-07-19; watchdog probes stopped entering migration paths, no regressions.

### Impact and severity

P2 correctness/ops-safety: monitoring and automation probes (the documented way to check a gateway) mutate-scan local state they do not own, on every invocation, with real mutation when legacy inputs exist and with version-skew hazards during upgrades. Also a small constant latency/IO tax on the most frequent CLI invocation in monitored deployments.

### Additional information

The exemption pattern is established: `shouldMigrateStateFromPath` already special-cases `update status` and `config get|unset` as read-only surfaces, and `gateway call` is already in `ALLOWED_INVALID_GATEWAY_SUBCOMMANDS` (it must work when local config is broken — a fortiori it should not *migrate* local state). Adjacent maintainer direction: #112072 (stage migrations instead of applying them implicitly during onboarding) points the same way — migrations should be deliberate, not bootstrap side effects of unrelated commands; #111498 shows the user-visible cost when a persistent migration error blocks unrelated CLI surfaces. Scope note: other `gateway` subcommands (`health`, `probe`, `status`, `discover`) are also largely remote-client surfaces, but this issue and the follow-up PR keep to the `call` surface we have production evidence for; widening can be a follow-up decision. PR with the one-line exemption plus regression tests follows.

issues.body:
### Summary

 Add an outbound_payloads_sending hook that fires before a message is delivered. Needs to read the message text, access the session's tool call history, annotate or block.

### Problem to solve

Why: LLM's lie their pants off. I built two deterministic verification scripts (zero LLM) that catch it after the fact. Caught 19% fabrication rate with a tool call auditor and a scanner for commit language 'done' 'running' etc.  Missing piece is real-time interception before delivery.

Note: message:sent is already in the planned events in the hooks docs. This asks for it to ship with the context needed for verification.


### Proposed solution

Proposed API: A message:sending event with outbound text, channel, recipient, and the session's tool calls/results in context. Cancel flag to block and retry.


### Alternatives considered

Manual prefixing in prompts is inconsistent and hard to enforce. System prompt instructions ("always verify before saying done") don't work — the model skips them, which is the exact problem. A post-send cron audit catches issues but only after the user has already read and acted on false information.

### Impact

Affected: Any user running an agent for ongoing operations (not one-shot Q&A)
Severity: High — decisions get made on unverified claims
Frequency: Every session. Measured 19% phantom rate across 41 sessions in 24 hours
Consequence: False confidence in agent output. User acts on "done" that wasn't done. Compounds over days/weeks into systemic trust breakdown. No current workaround catches it before delivery.


### Evidence/examples

Built and ran two verification scripts against real production sessions:

• Tool Call Auditor: 198 lines, parses session JSONL, checks file existence/edit content/script outcomes. Found 4 failures in 100 checks.
• Claim Scanner: 200 lines, regex extracts commitment language, cross-refs against nearby tool calls. 76 claims scanned, 11 phantom (no backing tool call), 19% phantom rate.
• Specific example: agent said "Strety write access: live" with no tool call within 5 messages. Agent said "tested Python" as a promise but scanner flagged it as a claim with no exec nearby.

### Additional information

• Discord thread confirming feasibility and suggested API framing.

issues.body:
# [BUG] gog skill.md in OpenClaw bundle is significantly out of date vs the official gogcli

**Summary:** The `gog` SKILL.md bundled inside OpenClaw (at `~/.npm-global/lib/node_modules/openclaw/skills/gog/SKILL.md`) is incomplete and missing large sections of the official gogcli command surface. The skill bundled in OpenClaw is not being kept in sync with the rapidly evolving gogcli project.

---

## Evidence

### Size discrepancy

| Source | Size |
|--------|------|
| OpenClaw bundled skill (`~/.npm-global/.../skills/gog/SKILL.md`) | 8,862 bytes |
| GitHub source (`openclaw/openclaw/main/skills/gog/SKILL.md`) | 4,574 bytes |
| Official gogcli repo README (`openclaw/gogcli`) | Much larger — comprehensive reference |

The npm-global bundle is larger than the GitHub source, suggesting the GitHub source was trimmed at some point but the npm bundle was not updated.

### Missing from current skill vs official gogcli

The official gogcli (`github.com/openclaw/gogcli`) covers significantly more services than either skill version documents:

**Services the skill does NOT document but gogcli supports:**
- **YouTube Data API** — channel data, search
- **Google Maps/Places** — places search, details, directions, geocoding, reverse geocoding
- **Google Forms** — form creation, responses
- **Google Meet** — Meet attachment/auth setup for calendar events
- **Drive Audits** — tree, disk usage, sharing audits, bulk public removal, Drive Labels
- **Drive Changes** — change tracking, polling, revision history, activity logs
- **Raw API access** — `gog drive raw` for lossless API JSON dumps
- **gog gmail filters export** — export filters in Gmail web UI import format
- **gog calendar create-calendar / delete-calendar** — calendar management
- **gog calendar subscribe / unsubscribe** — calendar subscription management
- **gog calendar move** — move events between calendars
- **gog zoom auth setup** — Zoom OAuth setup for calendar events
- **gog maps** — full Maps/Places API coverage
- **MCP server** — typed MCP server for agent clients (read-only by default)

**Expanded coverage that exists in npm bundle but NOT in GitHub source:**
- Full Classroom command set (courses, roster, coursework, materials, submissions, announcements, topics, invitations, guardians, guardian invitations, profiles)
- Full Chat command set (spaces, messages, threads, direct messages)
- Extended Gmail options (filters export, autoforward, sendas, delegates)
- Extended Calendar options (focus-time, out-of-office, working-location, propose-time, team calendars)
- Full auth-services scope matrix
- Integration test documentation
- Shell completions for Bash, Zsh, Fish, PowerShell

### Additional context

- gogcli is actively maintained — the repo is at `github.com/openclaw/gogcli`
- Full rendered docs are at `https://gogcli.sh/`
- Generated command reference is at `github.com/openclaw/gogcli/blob/main/docs/commands/README.md`
- The skill system should be pulling from an authoritative, up-to-date source rather than a static file that can drift

---

## Impact

Agents using the gog skill are unaware of large portions of gogcli's functionality. This means:

1. Agents cannot effectively use gogcli commands that aren't documented in the skill
2. When gogcli adds new features, the OpenClaw skill becomes stale by default
3. Users relying on the bundled skill miss productivity improvements shipped in gogcli

## Implications for OpenClaw updates

**When OpenClaw is updated**, the npm-global skill reverts to the version currently in the OpenClaw repo (GitHub source = 4,574 bytes). This means:

- Classroom, Chat, and extended Gmail/Calendar coverage are **silently lost** with every OpenClaw update
- Agents relying on the skill for command syntax become unaware of features they previously had access to
- There is no warning during update that the skill has been downgraded

**When the skill should be updated:**

1. **Before every OpenClaw release** — the `skills/gog/SKILL.md` in the OpenClaw repo must be regenerated from the current gogcli source before shipping
2. **On every gogcli release** — if gogcli ships significant new commands, OpenClaw should update its bundled skill in parallel
3. **Automated approach** — the skill should ideally be generated programmatically from `github.com/openclaw/gogcli/docs/commands/README.md` rather than manually maintained, so it cannot drift

---

## Suggested fix

**Option 1 (preferred):** The `skills/gog/SKILL.md` in the OpenClaw repo should be regenerated/synced from the current gogcli source (`github.com/openclaw/gogcli`). The skill should pull from the official gogcli command reference (`docs/commands/README.md`) rather than being manually maintained.

**Option 2:** Add a note in the skill directing agents to use `gog --help` and `gog <command> --help` for the most current command reference, since the skill file will always lag behind the actively-developed gogcli.

**Option 3:** Add a CI check or automation that validates the bundled skill.md against the latest gogcli command index on each release.

---

## Labels

`bug`, `area:skills`, `gog`, `documentation`

---

issues.body:
## Bug Report

**Re-filing per maintainer bot guidance on locked #62102 (closed as stale). See also: duplicate #72313.**

### Summary

`AgentParamsSchema` in the OpenClaw gateway protocol uses `{ additionalProperties: false }` and does not include a `paperclip` field. The Paperclip adapter (`@paperclipai/adapter-openclaw-gateway`) injects a root-level `paperclip` metadata object in every agent dispatch payload, causing the gateway to reject every heartbeat run.

### Current Behaviour

Every Paperclip heartbeat dispatch via the `openclaw_gateway` adapter fails immediately:

```
[openclaw-gateway] connected protocol=3
[openclaw-gateway] request failed: invalid agent params: at root: unexpected property 'paperclip'
```

The `AgentParamsSchema` is declared in `dist/src-S72EdpgG.js` (as of `2026.5.28`) as:

```js
const AgentParamsSchema = Type.Object({
    message: NonEmptyString,
    agentId: Type.Optional(NonEmptyString),
    // ... many optional fields ...
    label: Type.Optional(SessionLabelString)
}, { additionalProperties: false });  // ← rejects 'paperclip'
```

### Expected Behaviour

The schema should either:
- Accept a `paperclip` field (`Type.Optional(Type.Unknown())`), or  
- Use `additionalProperties: true` to tolerate orchestrator-injected metadata

### Affected Versions

Confirmed byte-identical broken schema across: `2026.4.22`, `2026.4.24`, `2026.4.29`, `2026.5.2`, **`2026.5.28`** (latest as of 2026-07-03).

### Impact

- All agents using the `openclaw_gateway` adapter fail to start on every heartbeat dispatch
- Silent failure: tasks queue and stall with no partial output
- Documented internal impact: 3 run failures on 2026-05-01; integration broken since ~2026-04-03 before diagnosis
- Affects any Paperclip deployment using OpenClaw as a relay

### Workaround

Manual patch after every `openclaw update`:

```bash
PROTOCOL_FILE=$(grep -rl --include='*.js' 'AgentParamsSchema' /usr/local/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/ | head -1)
sed -i '' 's/}, { additionalProperties: false });/}, { additionalProperties: true });/g' "$PROTOCOL_FILE"
```

This is overwritten by every update, requiring repeated manual intervention.

### Prior Art

- **#62102** — Canonical report, closed as stale (locked); confirmed still reproduces
- **#72313** — Duplicate, closed by ClawSweeper bot
- **PR #69139** — Added `paperclip: Type.Optional(Type.Unknown())` to schema; closed without merge
- **PR #74974** — Generic `adapterMeta` namespace + `paperclip` alias; closed as duplicate/superseded

### Proposed Fix

Option A (minimal): Add `paperclip: Type.Optional(Type.Unknown())` to `AgentParamsSchema` in `src/gateway/protocol/schema/agent.ts`.

Option B (extensible, per PR #74974): Introduce a generic `adapterMeta` namespace for vendor-injected metadata, with a `paperclip` compat alias.

Either fix unblocks production use of the Paperclip → OpenClaw gateway integration.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

When using OpenClaw with AWS Bedrock via session-based credentials  (`AWS_PROFILE`, temporary STS credentials, IAM roles with assumed sessions, etc.),  the compaction feature systematically fails with the following safeguard message:

```
[compaction-safeguard] Compaction safeguard: no request credentials available;
cancelling compaction to preserve history.
```

Compaction is entirely skipped, causing the context window to grow unbounded  without any fallback or warning beyond this log line.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure OpenClaw to use AWS Bedrock as the model provider
2. Authenticate via `AWS_PROFILE` pointing to a profile with session/temporary  credentials (e.g. SSO, `aws sts assume-role`, IAM Identity Center)
3. Start a long conversation that triggers compaction
4. Observe the log output

### Expected behavior

Compaction should work correctly when valid AWS session credentials are present  in the environment. The credential check performed by the compaction safeguard  should be compatible with session-based authentication, not just static  long-lived credentials.

### Actual behavior

The compaction safeguard incorrectly determines that "no request credentials  are available" even though:

- AWS Bedrock API calls work perfectly throughout the session
- All other model interactions (completions, tool use, etc.) succeed without any credential errors
- The credentials are clearly valid and properly resolved by the AWS SDK

This strongly suggests the compaction safeguard is performing a credential  check via a different code path or mechanism that does not correctly handle  session/profile-based credential resolution (e.g. not going through the  standard AWS SDK credential chain).

### OpenClaw version

2026.5.28 (e932160)

### Operating system

Linux / Debian GNU/Linux 12

### Install method

docker

### Model

amazon-bedrock/eu.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> telegram

### Additional provider/model setup details

- **AWS authentication method:** Session-based credentials via `AWS_PROFILE` 
  (temporary STS/assumed role credentials — `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, 
  `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN`)

### Logs, screenshots, and evidence

```shell
[compaction-safeguard] Compaction safeguard: no request credentials available;
cancelling compaction to preserve history.
```

### Impact and severity

_No response_

### Additional information

Session-based credentials are the standard in enterprise/regulated environments (SSO, IAM roles, least-privilege setups). Blocking compaction silently in these  contexts is a significant usability regression, especially since the rest of the  Bedrock integration works flawlessly.

A potential fix would be to ensure the credential validation step in the  compaction safeguard uses the same AWS SDK credential resolution chain as the  rest of the application, rather than a separate or simplified check.

---

### Workaround

None known. Compaction cannot be manually triggered or bypassed.

issues.body:
## Summary
Each user message delivered via Telegram is prefixed with 400-500 bytes of JSON metadata (Conversation info + Sender blocks) embedded directly in the message text. This metadata-to-content ratio makes it harder for models — especially weaker fallback models — to locate and process actual user text.

## Observed Behavior
Each user message contains:
```
Conversation info (untrusted metadata):
\```json
{"chat_id": "...", "message_id": "...", "sender_id": "...", "sender": "...", "timestamp": "..."}
\```

Sender (untrusted metadata):
\```json
{"label": "...", "id": "...", "name": "...", "username": "..."}
\```

[actual user text here — often much shorter than the metadata]
```

- Metadata is ~450 bytes per message
- Actual user text is often ~100-200 bytes
- Models must parse through "do not treat as instructions" headers to find real content
- MiniMax-M2.7 (fallback model) spends thinking cycles on metadata instead of user text

## Impact
- Weaker models fail to comprehend user messages
- Token budget consumed by repetitive metadata
- Confusing "untrusted" framing may interfere with instruction-following

## Environment
- OpenClaw 2026.4.23
- Channel: Telegram
- Affects all models, critical impact on weaker fallback models

## Suggested Improvement
Deliver metadata as structured fields (e.g., OpenAI-compatible `name`, `metadata` fields) rather than inline text in the message content. Or provide a compact single-line header format.

issues.body:
### Summary

Keep the skill match OpenClaw already computes for a tool call (the public `skill.used` identity: skill name, source, activation) with that call's tool result, so `chat.history` and other transcript readers can show it after a reload or restart.

### Problem to solve

When an agent reads a catalog skill (a `read` of its `SKILL.md`, or `skills_read`), the `before_tool_call` wrapper matches the call to the skill in `findSkillUsageMatch` and records it through `recordSkillUsed`. That record goes to three places, and none of them is tied to the transcript entry:

- the `skill.used` diagnostic event: optional, asynchronous, and not replayable after a restart;
- the per-run usage receipt (`skillUsageByRun`): in memory, consumed when the run ends;
- the `skill_usage` table (repopulated by #129769 for #127742): a per-skill counter with no session, run, or tool-call identity.

The stored tool result keeps only the tool's own output. A client that renders a session later (the Control UI, a native app, or a third-party Gateway client) cannot tell that a `read` call loaded a skill, or which one. Re-deriving it from the file path in the client would duplicate the native matcher, which already handles workspace, home-compacted, node, and sandbox paths.

### Proposed solution

Keep the public skill identity on the tool result's `details` as `openclawSkillUsage`: `{ skillName, skillSource, activation }`, the same fields `skill.used` reports and without the skill file path.

- Attach it where each harness has its final transcript result, through one shared helper. That is the embedded `tool_result` handler after result middleware; `runAgentHarnessToolInvocation` after the adapter's middleware and legacy result extensions (Codex, Agents API); and the nested-tool activity entry for Tool Search / Code Mode calls. A middleware failure replaces only the presentation of a successful read, so it keeps the field. A failed read never gets one.
- Do not add it to the tool's own return value. Catalog calls validate that value against the tool's output schema, and `read`'s schema is closed (`additionalProperties: false`). Code Mode guests also receive `details` directly.
- Keep the field when persistence summarizes oversized `details`. Both `read` and `skills_read` store the whole `SKILL.md` text in `details`, so any skill over about 8 KB trips the cap.
- Project the field in `chat.history`, with a strict shape check.

### Alternatives considered

- **Add the field in the `before_tool_call` wrapper's return value.** This is the smallest diff, but it breaks catalog calls to `read`, which fail the output-contract check. It also puts the field in front of Code Mode guest code.
- **A durable audit record (open PR #141004).** That is an operator audit ledger, with its own table, retention, and permissions. It is useful for audits. A chat client rendering history would still need a second read path that is not tied to the transcript's lifetime or branches.
- **Clients subscribe to `skill.used`.** It is optional and not replayable after a restart.
- **Clients match `SKILL.md` paths.** This duplicates the native matcher and breaks for sandbox, node, and home-compacted paths.

### Impact

- Affected: Gateway clients that render or audit session history (custom UIs, native apps, operator tooling). The Control UI does not render skill attribution today. This change makes the data available; rendering it would be a separate change.
- Severity: low to medium. Attribution is missing; no data is lost.
- Frequency: every successful skill read through `read` or `skills_read` in embedded, Codex, and Agents API runs, including nested Tool Search / Code Mode calls in embedded runs, whenever the session is viewed after the live run ends.
- Consequence: clients show a bare `read` of a file instead of "used skill X", or carry local patches to get it.

### Evidence/examples

- Matcher and diagnostic: `src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.diagnostics.ts` (`findSkillUsageMatch`, `recordSkillUsed`).
- `chat.history` keeps only allowlisted `details` fields: `src/gateway/chat-display-projection.canvas.ts` (`projectToolResultDetails`).
- Oversized `details` are reduced to a fixed summary-field list: `src/agents/session-tool-result-guard.payload.ts`.
- Catalog output validation of `details`: `src/agents/tool-search-runtime.ts` (`assertCatalogOutputMatchesSchema`). The closed `read` schema is in `src/agents/sessions/tools/tool-schemas.ts`.
- We run a local patch with this behavior in a deployment whose web client renders skill use from reloaded history. The upstream version differs: it is attached after output validation instead of on the raw tool result.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself

### Additional information

Storage decision requested. Per `docs/reference/database-schemas/storage-changes.md`, this proposal needs maintainer acceptance; the prepared PR waits for it.

- **Owner:** the existing skill matcher produces the value, and harness transcript finalization writes it into the tool result's `details`, which transcripts already store. It is derived display attribution, not audit evidence. `skill.used` and `skill_usage` remain the accounting owners.
- **Capture:** only on transcript entries written after the change. There is no backfill.
- **Lifecycle:** the field lives inside the transcript entry, so it has the same permissions, reset, deletion, compaction, and export behavior. There is no new table, index, or retention rule.
- **Size:** three short strings (skill name, source, activation) and no file path. It is kept when oversized `details` are summarized, which stay within the existing 8 KB cap.
- **Compatibility:** old clients ignore the unknown key. A schema-compatible Gateway without this change reads the stored entries and its `chat.history` omits the field, so the field needs no migration. Rolling back to an older release across main's own schema migrations is refused as usual and needs a pre-upgrade backup; this change adds no schema.
- **Not captured:** skill command dispatch (it writes no tool result), nested activity results over 32 KB (replaced by a placeholder), `skill_workshop` views (no tool call id), and failed reads.

Related: #127742, #129769, #141004.

### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

sessions.list rows report the provider's full thinking-effort list for a model whose catalog entry has reasoning: false. For the same session and model, models.list and agents.list correctly report only off and ultra. Clients that read the session row first offer efforts the model doesn't support.

The likely cause is b46c38cfa (#147994, first released in v2026.9.5). resolveGatewaySessionThinkingProjectionInternal (src/gateway/session-utils-model.ts) swaps the merged catalog entry for a raw route-variant row from selectModelCatalogRuntimeEntry and resolves thinking from runtimeCatalog = [catalogEntry]. That row lacks config overrides such as reasoning: false. models.list re-projects its variant with projectModelCatalogEntryForRoute, and agents.list uses the merged entry, so both are correct. The code is unchanged on v2026.10.2, v2026.10.5-beta.2 and main.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a reasoning: false model on a provider with more than one route. Here that's opencode-go/muse-spark-1.3-contributor, which has openai-responses and openai-completions rows (see #135858 and #138268).
2. Have an agent on the openclaw runtime use that model, and create a session with it.
3. Call sessions.list and read the session row's thinkingLevels.
4. Call models.list {sessionKey} and read that model's thinkingLevels.
5. Call agents.list and read the agent's thinkingLevels.

### Expected behavior

The sessions.list row reports the same thinkingLevels as models.list for the session's model, here: off and ultra.

### Actual behavior

For the same session and model (gateway 2026.10.1, `opencode-go/muse-spark-1.3-contributor`), the RPCs disagree on `thinkingLevels`:

| RPC | `thinkingLevels` |
| --- | --- |
| `sessions.list` row | off, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, ultra |
| `models.list {sessionKey}` entry | off, ultra |
| `agents.list` agent | off, ultra |
| `chat.history` `sessionInfo` / `defaults` | absent |

The row's `thinkingDefault` is `off`. Its levels match what `resolveModelThinkingProfile` returns when `reasoning` isn't `false`: the opencode-go effort list from `compat.supportedReasoningEfforts`, with `ultra` added by `resolveThinkingProfile`.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.1

### Operating system

Linux 6.12.107+deb13-amd64

### Install method

npm global

### Model

opencode-go/muse-spark-1.3-contributor

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> opencode-go -> muse-spark-1.3-contributor

### Additional provider/model setup details

• The model is treated as reasoning: false: models.list and agents.list both report only off and ultra.
• [fill in: where reasoning: false comes from. It's most likely a models.providers.opencode-go.models[] entry in your gateway config, which may relate to #165414. Check that file.]
• Seen through a custom client that reads sessions.list rows. OpenClawKit's OpenClawChatThinkingProfile.resolve also reads session.thinkingLevels first, so its picker would be affected the same way. I haven't run OpenClawKit to confirm.
• A possible fix is to re-project the selected route variant with projectModelCatalogEntryForRoute, as models.list does, or to pass configuredReasoning from the logical entry into resolveGatewayModelThinkingFacts.

Client-side dump of the decoded RPC responses. `sessionInfo`/`defaults` come from `chat.history`, `sessions.list` is the session's row, `agent` is from `agents.list`, and `models.list` was called with the session key and with the agent id for a new-session draft:

issues.body:
### Summary
On 2026.10.2 (b8952d4), `before_tool_call` hooks receive no `ctx.requester` for tool calls that a `claude-cli` session makes through the OpenClaw MCP loopback (for example the OpenClaw `exec` tool). Embedded-runtime tools and Claude Code native-tool relays do receive it. Sender-aware tool policy therefore cannot recognise the owner on the claude-cli MCP route, and has to fail closed there.

### Evidence (source, 2026.10.2 dist)
- MCP loopback: `dist/mcp-http-*.mjs` builds `hookContext` for `handleMcpJsonRpc` with agentId, config, workspaceDir, sessionKey, sessionId, runId, approvalReviewerDeviceId, channelId, turnSource* and loopDetection, but no `requester` (around line 453). The context then goes into the hook (`dist/mcp-http.handlers-*.mjs`, around line 103).
- Embedded agent tools: `dist/agent-tools-*.mjs` (around line 727) builds `requester` from channel, accountId, senderId and senderIsOwner.
- Claude Code native relay: `dist/execute.runtime-*.mjs` (around line 1421) builds the same `requester` and passes it to `runBeforeToolCallHook`.
- The docs (`plugins/hooks/tool-policy.md`, "Sender-aware policy in one file") present `ctx.requester` as the way to write owner-aware policy, and say that missing fields are "unproven" and should fail closed.

### Expected
MCP-loopback tool calls from a claude-cli run carry the same host-derived `requester` (channel, accountId, senderId, senderIsOwner) as embedded and native-relay calls. Owner-aware plugins (for example ones that request a payload-bound `requireApproval` only for the owner's own chat turn) would then behave the same on every runtime.

### Impact
A plugin that asks the owner for a native approval on sensitive operations works on the embedded runtime, but on claude-cli sessions it can only block.

## Problem

Discord threads often keep a generic creation-time name even after several user and agent messages make the topic clear. Users must rename them manually or ask the agent to do it in the conversation.

## Proposal

Add opt-in `channels.discord.thread.autoName`: `false` or `0` disables it, `true` uses five messages, and a positive integer sets the user/agent message threshold. Allow `channels.discord.accounts.<id>.thread.autoName` to override the threshold per account.

At the threshold, generate a concise title from a bounded recent thread transcript in an isolated model run and rename the thread once. Respect Discord's 100-character name limit, Manage Threads permission, and the two-renames-per-parent ten-minute limit. Persist the one-time claim across Gateway restarts.

This is distinct from #17954, which concerns the initial name of OpenClaw-created auto-threads.

issues.body:
## Summary

After a gateway restart, the message bridge redelivered 12 already-processed user messages within the same second (2026-09-28 09:56 local), causing the agent to process duplicates. Separately, in the same session a formatting skill entered a tool-call loop (50+ consecutive identical calls, one run of 144 identical `read` calls), which — combined with a full context window (250k/262k) — degraded the session into producing a false "task executed" report.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.7.1-2 (0790d9f), macOS, homebrew install
- Model: kimi-for-coding (anthropic-messages API)

## Problem 1: Bridge redelivery is not idempotent

**Observed**: 12 identical user messages delivered at the same second after gateway restart. The session log shows each message processed as new.

**Expected**: At-least-once delivery is fine, but the bridge/conversation layer should dedupe on a stable `event_id` before enqueuing to the agent loop. Processed events must not be redelivered; backlog should be coalesced or dropped, never replayed in order.

**Suggested acceptance criteria** (happy to help test):
- Every inbound message carries a persistent `event_id`
- Delivery layer keeps a processed-id ledger and drops duplicates
- Restart replay is idempotent: same `event_id` → no new agent turn

## Problem 2: No circuit breaker for repeated identical tool calls

**Observed**: A skill calling a formatter/read tool with identical arguments 50+ times consecutively (peak run: 144 identical calls). Nothing in the runtime intervened; the loop only stopped when the context window filled up.

**Expected**: A runtime-level (not prompt-level) circuit breaker: same tool + identical arguments ≥ N consecutive calls (e.g. N=3) → interrupt the loop, return an error to the model, and log the incident. Natural-language instructions in prompts demonstrably do not prevent this class of failure.

## Local mitigations we built (in case they inform design)

- A session-log scanner that flags same-tool+same-args runs ≥3 and repeated call cycles (found both incidents retroactively)
- A write-claim auditor that verifies "I saved/executed" claims against actual tool calls (caught the false report)
- A context-pressure meter reading `usage.contextUsage.promptTokens` (the overflowing session peaked at 304,101 prompt tokens vs 262,144 limit — 116%)

Happy to share the session JSONL excerpts privately if useful.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

The native Codex parent-local inference relay rejects an image-heavy request above its 32 MiB decoded-body limit, but converts the deterministic size error into a generic HTTP 502; Codex and OpenClaw repeatedly retry the oversized conversation before the agent fails without a model reply.

### Steps to reproduce

Two evidence levels are available: an observed real-provider conversation failure and an executed, isolated reproduction of the installed decoder boundary. No private conversation payload is attached.

**Observed conversation path:**

1. Use OpenClaw 2026.9.9 with `@openclaw/codex` 2026.9.9, managed Codex 0.160.0, ChatGPT OAuth, and `openai/gpt-6-astra` through the native Codex app-server.
2. The affected native conversation accumulated eight inline PNG data URLs in four `exec` tool-result records.
3. Continue that conversation. Codex logs a request of **33,599,844 uncompressed bytes** and approximately **20,639,399 compressed bytes**, then receives the local relay's generic 502. Further attempts keep replaying oversized requests.
4. OpenClaw logs three same-model retries, exhausts its transient retry window, and surfaces the final transport error. This agent has no configured model fallbacks.

The image-producing workflow itself is not included as a portable reproduction. The following boundary reproduction is deterministic and was executed against the installed dispatch implementation:

```sh
node --input-type=module -e '
import { readdirSync } from "node:fs";
import { pathToFileURL } from "node:url";
import { zstdCompressSync } from "node:zlib";
const dir = process.env.HOME + "/.openclaw/extensions/codex/dist/.setup/";
const file = readdirSync(dir).find(name => /^inference-dispatch-.*\.mjs$/.test(name));
if (!file) throw new Error("Installed Codex inference-dispatch module not found");
const { createCodexInferenceDispatch } = await import(pathToFileURL(dir + file).href);
const dispatch = createCodexInferenceDispatch({ context: {}, assertCurrent() {} });
for (const size of [33554432, 33599844]) {
  const wire = zstdCompressSync(Buffer.alloc(size, 32));
  const req = {
    headers: { "content-encoding": "zstd" },
    async *[Symbol.asyncIterator]() { yield wire; }
  };
  try {
    const upload = await dispatch.prepareHttp(
      req, false, "/responses", new AbortController().signal, () => {}
    );
    upload.settle();
    upload.releaseModelExecution();
    console.log(JSON.stringify({ decodedBytes: size, compressedBytes: wire.length, result: "accepted" }));
  } catch (error) {
    console.log(JSON.stringify({ decodedBytes: size, compressedBytes: wire.length, result: "rejected", code: error.code, message: error.message }));
  }
}'
```

This intentionally bypasses sampling/authorization preparation to isolate the actual decoder. It uses synthetic bytes, sends nothing upstream, and does **not** claim to reproduce a full provider turn. The `prepareHttp` signature above is for the installed 2026.9.9 build; current main has a different signature.

Observed output:

```json
{"decodedBytes":33554432,"compressedBytes":1043,"result":"accepted"}
{"decodedBytes":33599844,"compressedBytes":1047,"result":"rejected","code":"ERR_BUFFER_TOO_LARGE","message":"Cannot create a Buffer larger than 33554432 bytes"}
```

### Expected behavior

Keep bounded request admission, but identify an oversized decoded request as a deterministic size failure rather than a transient connection failure. Surface an actionable size-specific error without repeatedly resending the same oversized history. Do not silently discard conversation content or unconditionally remove the memory bound.

Known-good controls: the installed decoder accepts exactly 33,554,432 bytes; a fresh one-shot Gateway request with the same agent credentials and `openai/gpt-6-astra` returns the requested `OPENCLAW_TRANSPORT_OK` marker successfully.

### Actual behavior

The compressed request is below 32 MiB, but its decoded body is **45,412 bytes over** the limit. zstd decompression throws `ERR_BUFFER_TOO_LARGE` before forwarding. The HTTP proxy catches the local exception and returns the same sanitized 502 used for transient transport failures. Native Codex retries internally; OpenClaw subsequently retries the model turn as `server_error`.

The affected run terminates after about **147 seconds**, with three outer retries and no model reply. A fresh connection cannot make this unchanged oversized body fit.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.9 (bcfc888); `@openclaw/codex` 2026.9.9; managed `@openai/codex` 0.160.0.

### Operating system

Linux 7.2.9-1-cachyos, x64; Node v26.8.2.

### Install method

npm global OpenClaw, installed Codex plugin.

### Model

openai/gpt-6-astra

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw Gateway -> native Codex app-server (stdio) -> private loopback parent-local inference relay -> ChatGPT/Codex backend.

### Additional provider/model setup details

ChatGPT OAuth. Agent primary explicitly selects `openai/gpt-6-astra` with no agent-specific fallbacks. Credentials are usable, and a fresh same-model request succeeds.

The last successful inference reported 85,638 input tokens; the native effective context window at failure was 258,400 tokens. Rejected requests have no provider-reported token count because they fail locally. The measured violation is the relay's **byte** limit, not a demonstrated token-context overflow. No compaction records were found in the affected native conversation.

### Logs

Sanitized Gateway excerpts, October 11, 2026, UTC:

```text
01:09:10 [agent/embedded] transient same-model retry 1/8 for openai/gpt-6-astra reason=server_error: delayMs=599
01:09:42 [agent/embedded] transient same-model retry 2/8 for openai/gpt-6-astra reason=server_error: delayMs=1239
01:10:16 [agent/embedded] transient same-model retry 3/8 for openai/gpt-6-astra reason=server_error: delayMs=4447
01:10:52 [agent/embedded] transient retry window elapsed for openai/gpt-6-astra after 3/8 retries; stopping same-model retries
01:10:52 Embedded agent failed before reply: unexpected status 502 Bad Gateway: Codex parent-local inference transport failed; retry on a fresh connection., url: http://127.0.0.1:<port>/<redacted>/backend-api/codex/responses
```

Native Codex request log fields:

```text
Compressed request body with zstd pre_compression_bytes=33599844 post_compression_bytes=20639399
Request completed method=POST url=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/<redacted>/backend-api/codex/responses status=502 Bad Gateway
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Only sizes/types were inspected for the large tool results; no image or transcript content is included:

| Measurement | Bytes |
| --- | ---: |
| Relay decoded-body limit | 33,554,432 |
| Initial failed request before compression | 33,599,844 |
| Amount over the limit | 45,412 |
| Eight inline PNG data URLs in native history | 33,247,720 |

Inline image data is 98.95% of the initial failed request size.

**Latest-release and current-main source inspection:**

The latest GitHub release checked was [v2026.10.1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.10.1), published October 10. This is a source comparison, **not** a claim that the newer release was installed or the full conversation reproduced on it.

- [v2026.10.1 inference-upload.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.10.1/extensions/codex/src/app-server/inference-upload.ts#L4): `MAX_BODY_BYTES = 32 * 1024 * 1024`.
- [v2026.10.1 inference-dispatch.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.10.1/extensions/codex/src/app-server/inference-dispatch.ts): zstd decoding uses `maxOutputLength: MAX_BODY_BYTES`; rewritten payloads are bounded too.
- [v2026.10.1 inference-proxy.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.10.1/extensions/codex/src/app-server/inference-proxy.ts): non-authorization local exceptions before response headers become a generic 502.
- Current main was also inspected and retains these bounds and error mapping. The checked main revision was [6b13e9e4142d](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6b13e9e4142d02427949b5ffbb10db574997686e).

### Impact and severity

Affected: one observed native Codex-backed Telegram conversation with large inline tool images.

Severity: blocks model replies in that conversation. The Gateway remains running and fresh same-model requests succeed.

Frequency: four failed runs across October 10-11 have the same terminal relay error; retained request-size logs confirm oversized bodies for the latest two. The decoder rejects the measured above-limit body deterministically.

Consequence: futile native and outer retries, about 147 seconds of delay on the quoted run, and terminal failure without a model reply. No data loss or additional billing impact is established.

### Additional information

This is distinct from these related items:

- [#150940](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/150940): image-heavy native history and storage-retention gap; related, but not this decoded relay limit and retry classification.
- [#125308](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/125308): long-session byte-budget and compaction recovery problems; related, but not this exact decoder boundary.
- [#142823](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/142823): merged omitted-`instructions` fix for Responses Lite requests. The same public 502 string can represent different causes; the installed build already accepts omitted instructions.
- [#155987](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155987): merged request-byte reuse optimization explicitly preserves the 32 MiB body limit.

Last known good/first known bad release: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO. This report does not establish a regression.

Temporary operational workaround: start a fresh conversation and carry forward text rather than the old inline images. Only the fresh same-model inference control was exercised; resetting the affected production conversation was not performed.

A useful repair would preserve memory/admission bounds while distinguishing decoded-size failures from transient transport failures, and define a supported path for oversized image-bearing replay context. No production code was patched during this investigation.

prs.title: fix(auth): publish synchronous SDK credential mutations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Shared and agent credential authority cannot safely replace the final SQL read while released synchronous SDK writers and generic machine-state writes can change credentials outside the Gateway's publication lifecycle. This change closes those writer paths through the existing credential owner introduced in #170583. This PR builds on that owner change. The final bearer-fetch guard remains in place for the subsequent reader cutover.

### Writer coverage

| Writer family | Entry and custody | Credential publication |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Released synchronous SDK save/upsert and provider-auth helpers | `agent-runtime.saveAuthProfileStore`, `provider-auth.upsertAuthProfile`, and native provider helpers reach `runAuthProfileWriteTransaction`; supplied connections enter custody before loading or saving rows. Standalone callers acquire the existing exclusive offline lease; a live foreign Gateway refuses the write. | Shared/agent JSON cell sinks enter `withAuthProfileCredentialWrite` synchronously before SQL. |
| Native `AuthStorage` | `SqliteAuthStorageBackend.withLock` uses the same managed transaction and prepared save; `updateAsync` uses the existing auth-store worker operation. | Native saves use the canonical cell publication; async saves use the existing host admission and commit receipt. |
| Login, import, provider setup, logout, OAuth claim/replace/fail/restore, and peer updates | Profile/upsert APIs, `store-update`, and candidate-store updates retain their existing owner routes. | `store-update-kernel` supplies credential facts before the host grants COMMIT; committed receipts install before denial is released. |
| External CLI synchronization, exact snapshot restore, secrets apply and rollback | Native store save/restore paths enter the same transaction custody and canonical cell sinks. | The existing credential publication sees the exact replacement or deletion; metadata-only changes remain outside credential revocation. |
| Model-catalog native/plugin writes | The existing request work scope binds synchronous writes to its captured shared root and rejects calls after closure. | The host starts its credential batch before dispatch; the worker collects committed receipts, drains admitted work, and returns facts before host release. |
| Generic machine-state write/update/delete/import | Only normalized `authProfiles.store` enters credential custody/publication. Other keys retain their existing behavior. | Native writes publish through the canonical owner; async `machineState.write` starts host denial and delivers the existing native receipt before release. |
| TUI and onboarding recommendation commands | Workers construct fixed namespaces from `scopeKey` or `workspaceKey`, rather than accepting an arbitrary machine-state key. | These commands cannot reach `authProfiles.store`; direct worker regressions cover the former escape routes. |
| Doctor and relocation/import maintenance | Existing exact-path maintenance admission or exclusive offline ownership remains required. | Runtime writes use the same sinks; stopped-owner relocation is the explicit maintenance exception. |

The empty agent-store anchor created by inline usage remains an audited absence-to-empty mutation. It contains no credentials and cannot replace existing credential bytes. Other generic callers use fixed keys or owner-generated namespaces. The writer-entry ratchet rejects new credential sink callers and alternate generic worker dispatches without an owner audit.

### Custody and settlement

This reuses Gateway ownership, offline schema leases, managed transaction settlement, and the existing credential authority. Agent open records its shared owner root once, including agents stored outside the state directory. An ordinary worker must have active operation admission for the captured physical root; an unrelated worker admission is insufficient. Already-admitted path aliases use the existing in-memory identity registry, so symlinked state directories remain supported without another filesystem or SQL lookup. Catalog writes reuse their request's existing work scope. There is no new owner, durable generation, polling read, or cross-thread handshake.

Credential changes deny synchronously before native mutation. Known COMMIT installs all committed facts before releasing denial; confirmed rollback restores the committed view. A supplied SDK connection retains its offline lease through its outer managed transaction. Unknown native outcomes discard release observers, leave credential authority denied, and retain exclusive custody until owner restart. A caught native write error cannot silently certify a later outer commit. Order, cooldown, and usage-only changes do not revoke credentials.

Supplied-connection and ordinary SDK saves can share a managed outer transaction; shared-state transactions enter through `runOpenClawStateWriteTransaction`, and nested supplied-connection saves continue to use the released SDK transaction helper. A later ordinary save recovers that transaction's retained custody from the existing connection cache before normal preparation and admission. This lookup reads connection identity only; it performs no SQL and adds no authority registry. Only the actual mutation connection is enrolled for settlement, so a cold ownership lookup cannot attach an unrelated database transaction to the lease.

Released SDK exports, signatures, immediate return values, and synchronous completion timing remain unchanged. Standalone SDK writes remain supported under exclusive offline custody. Writes against a live foreign Gateway must use the Gateway owner; raw unmanaged transactions remain refused because their settlement cannot publish safely. No public signature, schema, or config change is introduced.

### Scope and accepted edges

No final security check is removed here. The duplicate raw-transaction check moves into the shared custody entry; arbitrary TUI/onboarding key dispatch is deleted. The existing SQL final read remains until the covered writer graph and the subsequent memory-only guard are proved together. An external request already initiated before credential denial may finish; new effects remain denied during pending or unknown changes.

## Evidence

Candidate: `c9bd14ae4174ffca46b31f041bf5cafebfadea3a`, including landed parent #170583 (`5822af67c6da`) and the shared-transaction fixture correction. The squash-parent integration preserves the tested SDK changes; the five conflicted files were identical between the reviewed PR1 head and its squash commit, so their PR2 versions were retained exactly. Final-head [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38352370038) completed with 101 successful and 25 skipped jobs. Two test jobs and the aggregate CI gate failed only for the evidenced inherited failures below. Build, production/test types, lint, ratchets, architecture, source contracts, additional/package boundaries and security checks passed. The inherited-failure landing exception is used; the aggregate gate is not described as green.

Two Codex P0/P1 review rounds are complete. The second found an uncertain-commit bug in standalone SDK custody: the outer cleanup could release its offline lease after an unknown COMMIT. The fix attaches that lease to the existing managed transaction settlement. A negative control reproduced the four shared/agent × save/upsert failures while eight confirmed-settlement controls passed. The local candidate run was stopped under the compute-conservation rule and is not claimed as a pass. No third review is requested.

The initial [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38346907753), at `5ec9a5e04da2f2c693929b740b17806485ee0874`, passed production types, lint, source contracts, package boundaries, and 133 changed-boundary tests. It also exposed native-writer fixtures in thread pools, raw handles missing captured identity, a fixture accidentally claiming maintenance rather than Gateway ownership, an omitted writer edge, and the wrapper import inventory. These were repaired in subsequent commits; those passes are prior-head evidence.

The next [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38348394787), at `2b474bb5292ce760795c9d2ac5b0c69f039966a5`, exposed a real SDK composition regression introduced by retaining the offline lease: supplied and ordinary saves in one outer transaction could reject their own custody. The candidate fixes connection-bound reentry as described above and extends the existing commit, rollback, and unknown-settlement regressions through the released SDK transaction export. It also gives the catalog-worker fixture the production owner's admitted work scope and drain-before-receipt ordering, updates a stale test-routing probe to a genuinely isolated fixture, and integrates main's fix for a removed test import. The final-head run completed after these repairs; its remaining failures are identified below. The next CI run caught a fixture error in the new shared-state cases: they placed an ordinary shared save inside a raw SDK outer transaction, which the shared-state owner has always rejected. The fixture now enters the existing shared-state transaction owner while preserving the nested released SDK call, ordinary save, and every commit/rollback/custody assertion; no production behavior or SDK contract changes for this correction.

The account-only Codex route QA failure is inherited. The [PR failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38346907753/job/115130732426) matches an executed clean main checkout at `43584d99e8a15c9cbb1280e19be098ba9ca7e6b7`: the account-only model is refused because its Codex route compatibility is not declared. That main run recorded 1 failed / 2 passed, 107.57 seconds wall time (101.61 seconds Vitest); its content-pinned receipt is retained with the campaign evidence. The main SHA predates this lane's original base, and this PR does not change the implicated route policy.

The auth-email QA failure is also inherited. The [PR failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38346907753/job/115130732432) was reproduced on the actual lane base `592b7e4aea9386e05912e6df2d3ba5493e629aaa`: Doctor and the selected-account turn completed, but successful status output omitted the expected synthetic email and reported OpenAI `windows: []`, `error: "Token expired"`, and `collection.source: "gateway"`. To reach the unchanged assertion under host load, the diagnostic fixture used the verified Codex version constant `0.160.0` instead of the broad version-lookup import, raised that test's limit from 180 to 900 seconds, and raised Doctor/status fixture command limits from 120 to 600 seconds. All assertions and product source stayed unchanged, including status's `--timeout 60000`; the temporary fixture edits were restored afterward. The test took 196.211 seconds (286.33 seconds total Vitest), exited 1, and matched the CI failure. The relevant status, usage, Codex request, and fixture files have no base-to-candidate changes.

The final-head consent-test failure is inherited: [candidate job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38352370038/job/115147795115) and [scheduled main job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38352378612/job/115147565692), at main `4e3b11bf`, both fail `chat.native-runtime-consent.test.ts` at line 372 with an unexpected retained session row after database replacement. The later consent/rejection assertion is not reached; this is not evidence that a consent grant was accepted. The central main-repair lane already owns the exact failure. The final-head auth-email failure also matches the base reproduction above.

| Metric | Base | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Retained final-guard T1 sites in this lane | 2 | 2; reader cutover is a separate PR |
| Warmed-path SQL / request claim | No reduction claimed in this writer-custody slice | No harness pair under compute conservation |
| Auth subsystem SQL / request delta | Existing native statements and worker operations | No added SQL or worker requests by source inspection; not a measured per-turn result |

Regressions cover actual released SDK save/upsert, foreign-Gateway refusal, deny-before-COMMIT, publish-before-release, nested supplied/ordinary connection commit and rollback, unknown settlement, metadata-only writes, cold parity, wrong/missing worker-root facts, admitted state-directory aliases, generic machine-state mutation, and TUI/onboarding namespace confinement. Prior-head ratchet proof passed 43 synthetic cases and the actual-source snapshot; renaming a covered SDK writer entry produced one violation. Final-head CI passed its selected behavioral shards and T1/dialect/custody ratchets. Its generic changed-boundary job passed 11 files / 133 tests in 50.40 seconds; those are not counted as credential-specific tests. Dependency/Knip and SDK evidence are detailed below. No local broad suite was run after the compute-conservation notice.

The [SDK API report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38350388345/job/115141659330) completed and its JSON artifact was inspected. It compares parent `ed1123f89241df9212a7fc3e4dcafe5eea0e6685` against PR merge ref `61731af17d439904f9b222224a27b684ad6b7b7a`, from workflow head `cbb3812a9ee0c54bd833ebfdc4423f66d424d022`. There are zero added/removed entrypoints or exports and zero direct signature changes. All 157 entries are reachable-type changes; the six internal declaration changes cover narrowed worker inputs, optional custody context, and the no-I/O cache lookup. The released credential save/upsert and provider-auth signatures are unchanged. This is prior-head evidence reused after the test-only correction and parent integration; it is not a new-head execution claim. Report digest: `b982b8d24d12b95b4c30624f0d3edf9befdda217f73a488badcc424e40af9422`.

The earlier static/API run passed its runtime topology/architecture check and reported inherited Knip findings in unchanged UI, memory and session exports. Exact source/config identities matched main; the central cleanup landed as #170660 (`bda83ac9f1688ba1eb91a75afbaaaa44291c9792`) and is included by the parent integration. Final-head architecture job `115147794245` explicitly ran Madge and reported zero import cycles; runtime import cycles were also zero and Kysely guardrails passed. No local broad scan was repeated.

The older qualification run also reported two `agents.delete` RPC timeouts. A focused main attempt exceeded the fixture startup deadline and did not reach that RPC; it is inconclusive, not inherited-failure evidence or a repair claim. The final-head CI has no such failed job; the exact file outcome remains unlocated in its compressed shards. The original diagnostics remain recorded for the central deletion owner.

Review follow-up: shorthand worker-command discriminants can evade this intermediate ratchet, although no production bypass was found. The expanded ratchet in the subsequent reader-cutover PR handles shorthand properties before the native guard is retired.

The released synchronous SDK reader still reaches the same native primitives, so static T1 may remain after the subsequent Codex guard cutover. This writer PR claims no warmed-turn reduction. No update/Doctor/schema/plugin-loading/service-lifecycle behavior is changed; the published-driver update cell is not triggered by this custody-only change.

LOC versus the integrated parent PR: 29 files, +1222/−135. Production is +436/−119 (net +317); writer-custody ratchet tooling is +47/−1, making production including the ratchet +483/−120 (net +363). Tests, test helpers, and test routing account for +693/−15; the wrapper inventory accounts for +46/−0.

prs.title: fix(telegram): keep follow-up text behind pending photo albums
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Telegram answers a text follow-up without the just-sent photos when that text arrives while earlier photo albums are still downloading.

## User Impact

User impact: follow-up text waits for earlier albums in the same conversation to enter the session, so the model can see their images. Text without a pending album has no added wait; `/stop`, inspection commands, and `/btw` keep their independent bypasses. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Albums already reserve a per-conversation queue slot, but ordinary messages use a separate buffer. Reuse that queue's tail as the admission barrier, with the existing ingress heartbeat while waiting. The barrier releases at album adoption or claim release, not final reply completion. This adds no queue manager, timeout, or configuration surface.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

## Evidence

Built baseline `92ef706779d` and candidate `822b028c28e` through the repository Telegram Test Server userbot runner, using Convex-leased credentials, a DM, streaming off, and the same 10-photo album → 2-photo album → text scenario. Times below are seconds from scenario start; the follow-up text was sent at about 30.2 s in both runs.

| Observed reply | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| First album | 33.699 s | 33.097 s |
| Second album | 34.693 s | 33.780 s |
| Later text | **31.843 s (first)** | **34.780 s (last)** |
| Images in the later text's model request, including history | **0** | **12** |

Controls on the candidate:
- Text alone: reply 4.113 s after send confirmation; a later normal text reply took 1.563 s.
- A single two-photo album reached the model with both images and produced its reply.
- With an album downloading and ordinary follow-up text waiting, `/stop` replied in 1.265 s, before the album and follow-up replies. This checks bypass responsiveness, not a change to cancellation policy.
- Real OpenAI `gpt-5-mini`, low reasoning: HTTP 200 and the requested `ALBUM_LIVE_OK` reply after a two-image album.
- All four completed Test Server runs removed their messages with absent-on-readback receipts, removed credential scratch, and stopped their listeners.
- Focused tests: 33 passed across durable ingress coalescing and media/topic E2E files; 14 passed in the channel-post media policy file. Changed-file Oxfmt and Oxlint passed.

Simplification: reuse the existing keyed-queue owner; retain the existing error, cancellation, retry, and topic isolation tests. Against the merge base: production +56/-20 (net +36); tests/support +17/-16 (net +1). The growth is the existing queue-tail access and ordinary-claim liveness, not another queue implementation.

Merge danger: **two-way door**; a revert fully restores the old behavior, with no state or schema changes. Blast radius is Telegram conversations with pending media albums; control-lane commands and conversations without an album retain their existing admission path.

prs.title: fix(ci): share setup for central scripts lint
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Full hybrid PR checks allocate a separate 16-class runner for formatting and scripts lint even when an existing core-lint runner can execute the same work sequentially.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. Eligible plans remove one CI job, checkout, and dependency setup. Coverage, runners, worker limits, and the 15-minute core-lint deadline stay unchanged. UI, root-test, wrapper guards, targeted core rows, other runner profiles, and plans requiring the last central check row retain their existing allocation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the unchanged central selection onto core lint stripe 1 only when the complete command plan contains formatting and scripts lint. The shared step still runs after core lint fails and propagates its own failure. Keep another central check row so existing gate admission remains intact.

## Evidence

Blacksmith and GitHub observations from [run 38317345868](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38317345868): core lint stripe 1 completed in 182 seconds; separate central lint took 87 seconds, including 49 seconds of checkout/setup and 32 seconds of checks. These observations identify avoidable setup; they are not a measured post-change saving.

Focused planner and workflow regression tests: 20 passed, 4.54 seconds overall. The new admission cases fail on the original planner for the retained duplicate row. Targeted lint, scripts and all four root-test type partitions, workflow validation, TypeScript erasability, formatting and diff checks passed. Independent P2 reviews found no actionable issues.

The first CI run exposed a stale manifest fixture export. The fixture now re-exports the canonical changed-check planner and lane detector; all seven affected integration cases and all 605 planning tests pass. [Exact-head CI run 38352701238](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38352701238) and the required gate passed for `574644d913f4601d5eb32947b7a9bb39fae94232`.

Local capacity qualification completed both core stripes plus central formatting/scripts lint in 436.93 seconds on four available CPUs with a 15-GiB memory cap, 10.76-GiB peak usage, and zero OOM events. It used the existing GitHub Actions lint policy; the initial local-only replay stopped on pre-existing file-length limits. This is workload-capacity evidence, not a measured Blacksmith billing saving.

prs.title: fix(state): move Gateway state consumers through existing workers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway state consumers reached synchronous SQLite through shared-state and SDK owners although worker operations already existed. Config and machine-state operations now use the shared-state worker; profile policy uses its admitted catalog; personal GitHub connections use facts invalidated by write receipts. Authentication prepares its owner asynchronously. Deletion bookkeeping consumes the live lease and journal/provenance receipts. Canonical validation runs at admission; metadata writes use a conditional upsert without a preliminary SELECT. Bundled callers migrate together and private superseded readers are removed. Whole-store auth saves and cold discovery remain deferred to #169763.

## User Impact

Gateway state access moves off the main thread while preserving its authorization, persistence and deletion behavior.

Credential, publication and filesystem-effect checks remain with their effect owners. Failed GitHub writes invalidate requested and commit-reported owners so a lost receipt cannot preserve old credentials. Explicit local-store and environment-only reads avoid ambient shared-owner preparation. Released synchronous SDK APIs remain deprecated compatibility paths. No lane schema, retention, stored-format, dependency or permission change is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Existing workers own the database operations and publish committed facts. Callers can reuse those facts without opening synchronous handles or rereading internal bookkeeping.

## T1 and scope

| Inventory | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Source-aware lane baseline `63a034f` | 33 | 26 |
| Original census, including 21 classification corrections | 54 | 26 |

Seven actual cuts cover four final-guard primitives, lifecycle facts, canonical-receipt runtime admission and publication lifecycle reads. The remaining 26 expressions are 25 original-file calls and one relocated reader. Worker use, deprecated released SDK/native compatibility, boot admission, migrations, Doctor/CLI one-shots, lock primitives and real credential/user-data/effect guards remain. Classification is not query savings; zero literal T1 or whole-Gateway MAIN SQL is not claimed. Native incognito removal remains intact.

## Evidence

The latest integration includes main through `32437d9f414d5`, including the engine-store `inspectSqlite` contract, lexical boot admission, and session-worker consolidation. Conflict resolution retains main's thread/provenance lifetime fixtures plus the explicit writable provenance setup. The final integration resolves one auth-profile test import conflict by retaining both helpers used by the combined tests; production code merged automatically. The readiness test now matches main exactly, preserving its three shared-Gateway cases and concurrent-delete assertions while removing superseded diagnostic scaffolding. Main's `58664264d18d5` auth-policy fixture fix is retained: both session targets are discovered in workers, avoiding synchronous creation after a worker captured absence. Counted lane T1 files are byte-identical to the previously audited integration; the actual reduction remains 33→26.
