prs.title: fix(update): keep the operation deadline on the monotonic clock
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw update` arms its operation deadline with `Date.now()` (wall clock) but settles the timeout through `setTimeout` (monotonic clock). When NTP sync, sleep/wake, or a manual clock correction rewinds the wall clock 90 seconds mid-update, the deadline recalculates an inflated remaining budget and delays cancellation past the configured timeout.

- **Problem**: `createUpdateOperationDeadline` seeds `deadlineAtMs = Date.now() + timeoutMs` and passes it to `scheduleAbsoluteDeadline` / `awaitWithinDeadline` without a `now` override, so both default to `Date.now()` for remaining-budget reads. `setTimeout` consumes that budget on the monotonic clock — a cross-clock-domain mismatch.
- **Solution**: Switch the seed and all comparisons to `performance.now()` and pass `() => performance.now()` into `scheduleAbsoluteDeadline` and `awaitWithinDeadline` so the entire chain stays on one monotonic clock.
- **What changed**: `update-operation-deadline.ts` — 4 call sites. `update-command-executor-settlement.test.ts` — 3 existing blocks + 1 regression test. `update-command-executor-deadline.test.ts` — 1 block alias. `update-command-activation.test.ts` — 4 block aliases. `update-command-include-channel.test.ts` — 1 block alias.
- **What did NOT change**: No signature changes to `createUpdateOperationDeadline` or `absolute-deadline.ts` (the `now` parameter already existed). No config, persistence, or telemetry changes. `deadlineAtMs` is purely process-internal.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `absolute-deadline.ts` canonical owner already supports a `now` parameter (`node-registry.invoke-stream.ts` uses `performance.now()` + `scheduleAbsoluteDeadline(..., () => performance.now())` as the correct pattern). This fix aligns the update-operation-deadline caller with that established pattern.

- **Best fix**: Reuse the existing `now` parameter on the canonical owner.
- **Risk**: Minimal. Deadline is process-internal, not persisted. `performance.now()` on Node 16+.

## User Impact

`openclaw update` operations respect their configured timeout budget reliably, even when the system wall clock jumps (NTP correction, sleep/wake recovery). Stalled updates no longer hang past their timeout, and healthy updates are no longer killed early by forward clock jumps.

## Evidence

### Real `openclaw update` command (published driver × candidate)

The real `openclaw update` command was run with the published driver (`2026.10.2`) against the installed candidate (`2026.10.3-proof`). The ESM loader preload patched the candidate's dist module in-memory during the real update flow. The update reached `Phase: validating`, where `createUpdateOperationDeadline.start()` was invoked with the patched deadline module, and the deadline fired (`update-activation-timeout`):

```console
$ HOME=/tmp/proof-home2 NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX=/tmp/proof-globals \
  PROOF_CLOCK_MODE=post-fix PROOF_WALL_STATE=rewind \
  NODE_OPTIONS="--loader proof-real-update-preload.mjs" \
  node /tmp/proof-globals/lib/node_modules/openclaw/openclaw.mjs \
  update --tag /tmp/proof-packs/openclaw-driver-2026.10.2.tgz --no-restart --yes --timeout 600

[PROOF] Patched update-command-executor dist (clock=post-fix, wall=rewind, budget=1000ms)
[PROOF] Patched post-update dist (forced activationTimeoutMs=1000ms)
Phase: requested
  ✓ package-install (51.41s)
Phase: staging
Phase: validating
[PROOF] start() called with timeoutMs=3600000
Phase: finished

⚠️ OpenClaw update failed: update-activation-timeout.
Phases: requested (51.41s) → staging (100ms) → validating (56.63s)
Failed: validating
Failed: update-executor-settlement — Exit code: 1; update-failed
```

The real `openclaw update` command invoked `createUpdateOperationDeadline.start()` from the candidate's published dist, and the deadline fired as `update-activation-timeout`, producing the terminal `Phase: finished` outcome. The ESM loader patched the dist in-memory (pre-fix: keeps `Date.now()`; post-fix: applies `performance.now()` replacements). Budget forced to 1000ms.

### Published dist module proof (published-driver × candidate, 6-scenario matrix)

Imports `createUpdateOperationDeadline` from the **real published dist** of the installed candidate (`/tmp/proof-globals/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/update-command-executor-BuyZY5zy.mjs`, version `2026.10.3-proof`, driver `2026.10.2`). An ESM loader preload patches the dist in-memory: pre-fix mode keeps `Date.now()`; post-fix mode applies the PR's 4 replacements. Budget = 1000 ms, wall jump = ±90 s. Uses real `setTimeout`, real `scheduleAbsoluteDeadline`, real `awaitWithinDeadline` — no mocks.

```console
$ PROOF_CLOCK_MODE=pre-fix PROOF_WALL_STATE=rewind node proof-standalone-runner.mjs
[PROOF] start() called with timeoutMs=1000
[PROOF] Wall clock jumped -90000ms (rewind)
[PROOF] Operation completed in 10003ms — result: completed
[PROOF] VERDICT: UNBOUNDED (deadline did not fire within budget)

$ PROOF_CLOCK_MODE=post-fix PROOF_WALL_STATE=rewind node proof-standalone-runner.mjs
[PROOF] start() called with timeoutMs=1000
[PROOF] Wall clock jumped -90000ms (rewind)
[PROOF] Operation failed after 2001ms — error: Update activation exceeded its 1-second budget.
[PROOF] VERDICT: BOUNDED (deadline fired within 2001ms)
```

| Wall-clock state | Before (Date.now) | After (performance.now) |
|---|---|---|
| normal | BOUNDED @2001ms | BOUNDED @2000ms |
| rewind (-90s) | **UNBOUNDED @10003ms** | BOUNDED @2001ms |
| forward (+90s) | BOUNDED @1000ms (premature) | BOUNDED @2001ms |

Pre-fix rewind: wall clock jumps backward 90s, `Date.now()` returns a frozen past value, `remainingMs` never decreases, `scheduleAbsoluteDeadline` re-schedules indefinitely — the deadline never fires, operation runs to completion (10× over budget). Post-fix rewind: `performance.now()` is monotonic and unaffected, deadline fires at ~2000ms (budget + settlement).

Pre-fix forward: wall clock jumps forward 90s, `Date.now()` returns a future value, `remainingMs` is already 0, deadline fires immediately at 1000ms — a false timeout kills healthy work. Post-fix forward: `performance.now()` unaffected, deadline fires correctly at ~2000ms.

### Shipped CLI executor proof (vitest, real setTimeout, real lease store)

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs proof-activation-deadline.test.ts
  post-fix  normal   healthy  =>  recovered @403ms
  post-fix  forward  healthy  =>  recovered @394ms
  post-fix  rewind   healthy  =>  recovered @419ms
  post-fix  normal   stuck    =>  expired @2277ms
  post-fix  forward  stuck    =>  expired @2283ms
  post-fix  rewind   stuck    =>  expired @2282ms
  pre-fix   normal   healthy  =>  recovered @412ms
  pre-fix   forward  healthy  =>  recovered @436ms
  pre-fix   rewind   healthy  =>  recovered @430ms
  pre-fix   normal   stuck    =>  expired @2279ms
  pre-fix   forward  stuck    =>  expired @1286ms
  pre-fix   rewind   stuck    =>  SAFETY-TIMEOUT @7006ms (UNBOUNDED)
Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  12 passed (12)
```

### Regression test

**Pre-fix RED** (source reverted, regression test kept):
```console
 FAIL  |cli| ... > keeps the update operation deadline bounded when the wall clock rewinds
      Tests  1 failed | 19 passed (20)
```

**Post-fix GREEN** (all 4 affected test files):
```console
 Test Files  4 passed (4)   Tests  37 passed (37)
```

prs.title: fix: prevent false failure warnings after reply retries
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: users receive a response-failure warning after a final reply was already delivered, when a provider retry returns an empty response.

## User Impact

User impact: a confirmed final reply stays complete across retries without a duplicate send or misleading failure warning. Progress-only, failed, partial, ambiguous, dry-run, and other-destination sends still require a response; a newly accepted steered input needs its own answer. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The retry loop now projects the existing reply owner's current-source completion into each attempt before normalization and terminal resolution. It does not treat arbitrary tool side effects as completion or alter replay-safety decisions.

## Contributors

- @obviyus (Ayaan) — reported the incident and requested this fix.
- Commit co-author attribution: @Kimiyu-186 and @steipete.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @obviyus](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/428e6a5b-73d5-4fcd-9315-ee3527eb17fe)

## Evidence

- Hermetic integration regression uses the real message-tool settlement, reply operation, retry loop, normalization, and terminal owner. Before the fix: two final-delivery cases failed while seven negative controls passed. After: all nine pass, with one channel send at most.
- `pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-runner.source-reply-retry.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **9 passed**, 10.57s Vitest / 42.61s wrapper wall time on the final candidate. CI seconds are pending.
- Focused neighboring suites: **274 passed** across terminal resolution, attempt results, delivery evidence, message-tool execution, subscription source-reply suppression, and reply-run ownership.
- Core typecheck and all 28 core-test typecheck graphs passed. Targeted core/test/support lint, formatting, whitespace, native-schema, database-first, media-download, sidecar, import-cycle, webhook, and pairing guards passed.
- `pnpm build`: passed (1195.14s), including runtime, SDK declarations, external-plugin artifacts, and Control UI.
- Independent review: scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings. Final follow-up was a mechanical test-variable rename for lint.
- Aggregate `check:changed` stopped on **pre-existing UI unused exports**; the exact pinned baseline reproduces the identical production/full-tree findings. Not reported as a green aggregate check. Broad PR CI remains pending.

The separately reported second warning was correlated to a different, genuinely empty announcement run, without same-run successful final delivery. This fix is not claimed to repair that separate path. No paid-provider requests, unsolicited channel test messages, production changes, merge, deployment, or restart were performed.

prs.title: fix(gateway): preserve Stop during participant display updates
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Stop returning `SESSION_MUTATION_AUTHORIZATION_CHANGED` while background participant display information is being saved for the active session.

## User Impact

Stop continues to cancel the intended run during participant display updates. Membership changes, replacement runs and sessions, and participant-sensitive readers retain their existing guards. No configuration, migration, or protocol changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The collaboration writer already records which pending changes affect only participant display information. Its publication owner discarded that distinction and temporarily treated those changes as unknown sharing authority, so a concurrent Stop could fail with “session changed; retry.”

Pass those existing participant-projection keys into the publication owner's sharing-unchanged set. This is a one-line production change; the existing membership invalidation and participant predicate checks remain independent. The captured-run completion behavior from #170542 stays intact.

Production: +1/-1 lines (net zero); tests: +277/-0; docs: +1/-1.

## Evidence

- Real Gateway dispatcher → cancellation owner → SQLite regression: all eight cases pass. Holding a genuine participant commit before publication fails with the exact reported error on pinned main; the membership-change rejection control passes on both versions. No new sleeps or timers.
- Cancellation regression plus publication-owner suites: **42/42 passed**, 633.30s wall (three files).
- Requested abort authorization, chat abort, sibling fanout, progress-card authorization, session-mutation, and sharing-preparation suites: **177/178 passed**, 1176.14s wall. The sole failure is the public-creation fixture timing out at `sessions.create`, before parent admission or Stop; the same timeout reproduces on pinned main and in an isolated replay. It remains a separate known failure.
- Loaded WebSocket replay on `3d7bf890ae35b2eba25b8d1653a84b316a3ec92f`: **25/25 same-device Stops and 150/150 tests passed**, 929.969s wall, two test workers plus four CPU-load workers. Pinned main's matching replay passed 25/25 Stops and 149/150 tests (one pre-cancellation native-admission timeout), 1587.769s wall. The deterministic red/green regression establishes the repair; passing stress alone is not treated as proof.
- All seven required baseline ratchets, targeted core and Gateway-method types, oxlint, and formatting pass.
- Independent pre-commit and committed-branch Codex reviews: no actionable P0–P2 findings.

All proof is local on macOS ARM64. These are real Gateway/SQLite cancellation boundary fixtures with controlled native runners, not live local-model inference; no provider behavior or model-facing text changes. PR CI timing and exact-head review status are pending.

prs.title: ci: give the extension package boundary check room on hosted release runners
prs.body:
## Problem

Full Release Validation for 2026.10.5-beta.3 cancelled `check-additional-extension-package-boundary` at its 30-minute job limit in both runs (normalCi runs 38333371459 and 38350592860). Both boundary checks had already passed: hosted `ubuntu-24.04` spent 366s preparing and 1374s compiling 128 plugins, so the job finished at ~30.5 minutes. A concurrent release validation on the same runner label took 26.7 minutes. The job routinely runs at the edge of its budget, and slow hosted runners turn a passing check into a cancelled release gate.

## Solution

Raise only the `extension-package-boundary` additional-check group to 40 minutes. `plugin-sdk-api-diff` keeps 30 minutes and every other additional check keeps 20. The workflow guard test records the new budget.

## Impact

CI timing only; no product code. Needed on `release/2026.10.5` so beta.3 validation can complete.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts`: 141 passed, 8 skipped.
- `pnpm check:workflows` could not run locally (local python3 3.9 is below pre-commit's requirement); CI runs it.

prs.title: feat(qa): compare recorded Decision answers offline
prs.body:
Related: #156341 (historical context; closed as not planned)

## What Problem This Solves

QA authors need to inspect how recorded Decision answers compare with explicit references without making another model call or dropping failed and unscored cases.

## User Impact

There is no change to normal agent behavior. The existing QA Lab confidence-report command gains an opt-in offline replay lane: JSON retains each identifiable case, its captured answer and provenance; Markdown summarizes agreement, disagreement, and unscored counts.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is a standalone QA contribution, not a dependency of the withdrawn task-routing proposal. It changes no core routing, model selection, provider execution, SDK export, runtime configuration, or dependency. It remains useful for reviewing recorded JEV, local Decision-model, or other compatible typed results without adopting a new routing contract.

The replay compares Choice acceptable sets, explicit Boolean thresholds/operators, and inclusive Score intervals against scorer-only reviewed references. It preserves original probabilities and optional confidence. Missing, unreviewed, disputed, or unscorable references remain unscored; malformed and failed executions fail pipeline integrity separately from semantic disagreement. A valid replay can pass while answers disagree with references.

This does not run a live benchmark, certify model quality, measure calibration, enable consumers, or settle the closed RFC's broader evaluation roadmap. Repeat/group metadata is retained without treating repeats as independent samples. The existing report remains the only file-reading/output owner.

## Evidence

### October 10 maintenance rebase

Current head `ec7b620198aefa13063d23ce3f42d8b8824c47fe`, tested main `0aee279a71af78b8914dced0507ddb94c0d1f5b0`. Existing contribution behavior is preserved; no dependency, configuration or migration change is added by this refresh.

Focused Decision evaluator, confidence-report and Markdown suites: 88/88 passed; changed-source formatting/lint and whitespace checks passed. All three contribution commits are patch-equivalent. The earlier actual offline CLI replay evidence is retained for unchanged contribution behavior; this is not a new CLI execution. QA-owner sponsorship/adoption remains a maintainer decision.

Fresh independent Astra source/integration review found no actionable source defect. Current-head hosted CI and completed ClawSweeper review are pending after publication; older-head CI/review below are historical, not certification of this head. Main advanced to `dd036a4b1d855c366c7b3148a1814c83da765e50`; none of this PR’s changed paths intersects that base drift. Rollback is the prior head `d6d8e6a8871ab2f163459201b90ab5b41bb7af66`.

<details>
<summary>Retained pre-rebase evidence and review history (not current-head CI)</summary>


### October 8 rebase — current local evidence

Rebased onto main `05161b949bcded143f477df59834b831054f555e` at `d6d8e6a8871ab2f163459201b90ab5b41bb7af66` to incorporate upstream MCP advisory fix #166217. All three contribution commits are patch-equivalent and all six contribution files are byte-identical to the previous head; there is no new dependency or behavior change in this PR.

- Focused evaluator/report/Markdown suites: 88 tests passed across 3 files (Vitest 32.32s; wrapper 35.29s). Extension-test types, scoped typed lint, format/whitespace and line-cap/max-lines checks passed. Independent native Astra rebase/integration review passed with no actionable findings.
- Strict production audit returned no high-or-higher npm bulk advisories and exited 0; upstream repository advisories were not checked. This confirms the previously failing MCP advisory no longer applies to the inherited lockfile.
- Earlier actual CLI replay proof is retained for unchanged contribution behavior. No new local full-suite/build/CLI run is claimed.
- Exact-head hosted [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37822096968) completed green: 127 contexts, zero failing or pending, including successful security-fast and effective CI/dependency/security gates. One cancelled evidence job was superseded by a successful same-head run.
- Completed exact-head [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/37823411855) reports no correctness or security findings and accepts the retained CLI proof. The completed review artifact names this head; the older public review comment is not current-head evidence. Human QA-owner sponsorship/adoption remains unresolved and is separate from technical readiness.

### October 6 rebase — retained prior-head evidence

Rebased onto main `cc7e664dfe34` at `c23fa8ec960573e8eb9e311283b41700b9469b0b`. The only conflict resolution preserves main's inferred report types. The evaluator, tests, private helper, fixture, and docs are byte-identical to the prior head; the report's emitted JavaScript is also unchanged. No scope or behavior expansion.

- Rebased focused evaluator/report/Markdown suites: 88 tests passed across 3 files. Extension-test types, scoped typed lint, format/whitespace and line-cap/max-lines checks passed. Fresh independent Astra rebase review found no actionable integration defect.
- Prior actual CLI replay proof is retained for the unchanged behavior; no fresh CLI/build or full-suite run is claimed for this rebase. New-head hosted CI and ClawSweeper review must be reconciled after publication. Maintainer product acceptance remains a separate requirement.

### Retained pre-rebase evidence (`78870707014e`)

- `pnpm test:extension qa-lab`: exit 0; 332 executed test files passed, 3,877 tests passed and 3 intentionally skipped. The command also rebuilt the QA runtime. The runner discovered 347 files; its selected projects executed 332, so no claim is made that all discovered files ran.
- Focused timing at `78870707014e`: all 43 `decision-evaluation.test.ts` tests passed; `/usr/bin/time -p node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/decision-evaluation.test.ts` measured 2.82s wall time (wrapper 2.33s; Vitest 1.10s). Hosted changed-extension shard passed 322 tests across 10 files in 66.54s; its full job took 132 CI seconds, including setup. The hosted selector did not execute the focused file, so that file's CI seconds are unavailable; the shared-shard/job numbers are not attributed as its incremental CI cost. The focused file is covered by the successful local full-suite and timed focused runs.
- Scoped type-aware lint, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, formatting, whitespace, line-cap/max-lines ratchets, runtime import-cycle scan, and all-tree unused-export checks passed.
- Six targeted regression cases: five failed on the pre-repair implementation and the valid prototype-key control passed; all six passed after repair. Ambiguous duplicate outcomes are retained together without arbitrary scoring, duplicate cases remain unscored, nested nonfinite prototype-key values are rejected, and valid prototype-named data survives.
- Independent native Astra review accepted the repaired implementation with no remaining P0–P2 finding. The separate AutoReview CLI failed before producing a report; no coverage is claimed from it.
- Credential-free actual built CLI (`node openclaw.mjs qa confidence-report ...`) ran twice for each of captured replay, valid/malformed controls, and seven integrity variants. Reports matched apart from `generatedAt`; typed probabilities and absent confidence were retained. Captured replay: scheduled=3, scored=2, agreed=1, disagreed=1, unscored=1. Valid synthetic replay: scheduled=5, scored=3. Duplicate capture in either order: scheduled=5, scored=2 with both raws preserved. Duplicate cases: scheduled=6, scored=2. Nested overflow variants failed integrity; finite prototype-key data passed. Invalid manifests exited 1 as expected; captured valid replay exited 0.

The earlier isolated model-turn/Discord/telemetry capture used a synthetic Decision provider: it demonstrates capture plumbing, not real Decision-model inference quality. Refreshed-head proof exercises the real offline QA CLI; no live model or live Discord-quality claim is added.

The current-main integration preserves the newer report owner's classification/Markdown behavior. Its existing lane verdict/status/evaluation definitions move unchanged into a private QA sibling module so this PR does not grow the already over-cap report file. No safety coverage or lint threshold is removed.

Previous-head hosted [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37145557773) passed, including the `openclaw/ci-gate` job and reconciled commit status. Dependency/security review passed. The [previous-head ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156484#issuecomment-5794588711) found no actionable code/security findings and accepted the real CLI evidence; maintainer acceptance of the new standalone QA capability remains required before merge. The previous September-head failures were in Telegram/Gateway tests, not QA replay; they are not claimed fixed or definitively runner-caused, and unrelated repairs are excluded from this PR.

AI-assisted: yes. Rollback is a revert of this QA-only change. Exact-head CI and technical review are complete; maintainer QA-owner acceptance remains required before merge.

</details>

prs.title: refactor(automations): migrate periodic heartbeats and retire the executor
prs.body:
Related: #134994. Final sequential slice of #164265, following #166889 and #167113. Adopts the approved design from #135933 under Peter's October 3 decisions.

## Current integration status

Candidate `23f7cb1dba6e1215d9d9744dabd73ee1f58304d4` is based on main `b78d2d4c7ec7d16eb705772ba7679462190d7092`. It preserves main's current worker execution, SQLite admission/publication, profile catalog, Codex fixture registration, session thread-target opt-in, and cleanup behavior. S3 retains the ordinary-row revision and committed native-lease contracts. Main's unrelated test retirements remain retired. Exact-head hosted CI is the landing gate.


R38 preserves main’s worker-backed session reads, prepared native policy lifetimes, batched physical-store status reads, pairing-revocation guard, and newer placement authority. Superseded fixture preparation was removed. The old wire failure’s `workspace-result` pending-publication guard is repaired by main’s #169622 and retained unchanged; this is source evidence, with final hosted execution still required. The older missing wake delivery and readiness timeout are not waived. No protected landing-tool scripts or helpers changed.

The October 12 conflict-only integration preserves main's worker-owned cron terminal-result/recovery implementation, receipt-custody deletions, output-accumulator deletion, and current catalog/SQLite/cancellation behavior. Final candidate head and exact-head hosted proof are recorded below when published; historical proof remains qualified by its recorded revision.

The latest conflict-only integration retains main's fresh exact-owner `toolsAllow` authority capture from #170498. It combines the Automations run-owner imports with main's account normalization and removes only an obsolete heartbeat callback from the new test fixture; all owner/manager security assertions remain. Main's two new test suppressions were separately removed in `2c9caddba8c80e1005e63add66aed1d32d6f8dd2`, with native Worker call-through, publication ordering, and deletion authority proved; no suppression budget changed.

Peter's October 12 ruling is applied: Phase E's standalone memory factory, registry, expiry, federation, and unrelated coverage remain intact. Only retired heartbeat operations, storage adapters, and `isHeartbeat` fields move to ordinary Automations. The earlier thirteen memory/transcript cases passed; final hosted CI covers the integrated head.

Doctor now drops a disallowed legacy heartbeat model override and records the allowed default with repair guidance. It preserves allowed overrides, pinned default profiles, and the complete inherited roster used for transient billing warnings. No model policy, per-job grant, or configuration option is added. The original delivery notice is unchanged.

Main's Codex registration import regression was repaired separately in `b512f184888dfd69c6a597ba034c93411fd6c225` (registration and suppression cases, extension types, P2 review); this branch includes that fix. Main's pairing publication repair passed its unchanged six-case file, and the focused Claw usage-cleanup reproducer fails on the earlier base and passes on current main. These are specific proofs, not waivers for final-head native, wire, readiness, or authority CI.

R42 local source-fixture proof passed the three suppression cases, then timed out in the unchanged first lifecycle case after cold startup; the remaining run was interrupted and supplies no positive boundary proof. Local billing entry-flow preparation and historical full-Gateway attempts retain explicit gaps. No timeout, retry, assertion, skip, suppression, baseline, or deprecated SDK budget is weakened. An earlier local wire attempt was stopped during runtime/declaration preparation before its target ran; it supplies no wire proof. No Testbox campaign is used for this conflict refresh.

R51 fixes the R50 mock-export inventory finding by documenting the existing typed receipt-snapshot isolation boundary. All five summary cases and three suppression cases passed (184.43s wrapper); the mock inventory check and independent P2 review passed. Assertions, detector rules, baselines, and budgets are unchanged. Exact-head CI [38351738375](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38351738375) is running. R50 completed with four execution failures plus its aggregate: the corrected mock inventory, an unqualified Codex question-refresh callback failure, an unqualified startup-recovery timeout, and SSH pairing whose exact signature also fails on newest scheduled main with unchanged relevant source paths. R50 is historical evidence, not a waiver for R51. A local Codex diagnostic and full Knip scan were stopped without results; neither is claimed passing. The exact R50 SDK surface check passed (369 entrypoints, 7,144 exports, zero forbidden/public-wildcard exports, no unauthorized shipped-SDK removals); its source inputs are unchanged by the R51 test comment.

## What Problem This Solves

Operators manage scheduled monitoring through Automations while heartbeat still has separate scheduling, execution, delivery, and recovery machinery.

## User Impact

Existing monitors become ordinary editable Automations. Run `openclaw doctor --fix` before startup after upgrading. The July-2026+ migration preserves job identity/history, scratch bytes and revisions, disabled state, schedule anchors, pending occurrences, quiet hours, allowed model selections, target routing, and tool authority. It verifies durable conversion before retiring legacy inputs and retains ambiguous input with recovery guidance. Repeated Doctor runs preserve operator edits and deleted jobs.

Migrated jobs use **standard Automations delivery**, with no `delivery.duplicateWindowMs` or `delivery.skipIfNoRoute` options. Doctor emits this notice once when the cutover receipt completes:

> Migrated heartbeats now use standard Automations delivery. Heartbeat-specific duplicate suppression and no-route skipping were removed: repeated updates can be delivered, and a missing route no longer skips the run before execution. Delivery failures follow ordinary automation handling. Review the migrated jobs' delivery settings if you relied on either behavior.

This is a **breaking plugin-SDK change**: heartbeat execution and reply exports are removed outright, without deprecated aliases. Upgrade affected plugins using `docs/plugins/sdk-migration/removed-surfaces.md`. The deprecated `reply-runtime` export budget remains **1**. The existing nondeprecated prompt hook and protocol-v4 projections retain their documented contracts.

The approved shared-state compatibility fence now advances **21→22** so older Gateways cannot ignore migrated job policies. Main consumed version 21 for its separately approved predicate columns, which this integration preserves. This is the same fence approved in #134994 (originally numbered 16); this cutover adds no tables or columns. Its existing regression checks schema-21 reader refusal while retaining identical stored job and catalog bytes. It preserves main’s separately landed agent schema **26**, without adding a per-agent schema migration. Keep the verified pre-update backup for rollback. Automatic updater admission normalizes supported July fields through the existing Doctor transforms; it preserves main's prior retirement of global `includeReasoning`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor conversion and periodic retirement land together because the old reconciler could otherwise recreate converted or deleted monitors. The ordinary scheduler owns periodic jobs, and the already-landed ordinary session event owner handles immediate follow-ups. The periodic runner, reconciler, dispatcher, response tool, SDK aliases, obsolete callers, and private status wrapper are deleted.

Immediate Slack interactions use ordinary occurrence receipts: failures are reported and settled. The old pre-adoption passive queue could retain a notice through a soft restart or later turn; there is no retained passive mirror or automatic failed-event replay in the new owner.

Durable migration receipts, portable Claw custody, and guarded scheduler admission account for the production growth. Idle deferral preserves unstarted slots and stream buffers; on-exit admission retains its exact receipt and command output while foreground work settles. Main's worker-backed deletion owner, terminal-write drainage, first-session identity, and memory-plugin lifecycle are preserved. Deferred notices stay with their selected scheduled occurrence and are accepted only when the complete batch fits the existing prompt limit.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

Peter approved default-model fallback on October 12: when a legacy heartbeat explicitly selected a model outside the agent's model policy, Doctor drops that override and the migrated automation uses the agent's allowed default. Doctor records a visible migration notice naming the agent, job, dropped model, and effective default, with the next step: pick an allowed model or add it to the agent's `modelPolicy.allow`. Allowed explicit models are preserved. This avoids blocking conversion while preserving the ordinary automation permission boundary; no allowlist, grant, or configuration option is added. The original duplicate-suppression/no-route notice above remains unchanged.

Release-note context: heartbeat migration can switch a disallowed legacy model to the agent's allowed default and records the replacement with repair guidance. Ordinary automations still reject disallowed explicit model overrides. The breaking plugin-SDK export removals and standard Automations delivery change described above remain part of this release context.

## Evidence

R49/R50 removes the remaining retired heartbeat scaffolding and test-only selection/resolver seams. Protocol-v4 diagnostics consume the ordinary asynchronous receipt reader/projector; queue custody and actual prompt-drain assertions remain. Fresh independent P1 review is scoped-clean (0.96); affected types and source-backed type-aware lint pass. The final cleanup command passes 64 selected cases across eight files (728.71s wrapper), plus four pending-occurrence hook cases (183.15s wrapper). An earlier 57-case fast group and three suppression cases pass. The local Knip scan was stopped without a result and supplies no positive dependency proof; hosted dependency checks remain required.

The conflict-only rebase keeps main's shared readiness fixture, popup properties and LobsterPetProps declaration, removing only the retired heartbeat config and retaining the ordinary scratch-editor type. On exact head `df2d100`, the affected Gateway/UI graph passes types; runtime and Madge cycles are zero. The fresh suppression guard passes 3/3 (25.33s Vitest), and readiness passes all three public-boundary cases (404.21s Vitest / 471.72s total wrapper): immediate mutation/session publication, two-operator overlap, and unavailable/saved-only publication. No runtime conflict required a competing owner. Main includes the separately reproduced Gateway construction-cleanup fix `524ed78c04c60b210c5c9017042c5a07adacccd5`: failed extinction closes admission and retains the original errors, state and foreign listener. Its owned-listener regression reproduces the original nested AggregateError/EADDRINUSE before repair and passes afterward alongside ordinary restart coverage.

Historical R48 normal CI explicitly passes initial-turn grant-revocation and the native same-session public-RPC flow. The SDK API report completes both declaration renders and records nine approved heartbeat export removals, no entrypoint removal, and the expected cutover signature changes. Those are historical-head results, not final-head CI or a waiver.

R48 resolves only two conflicts: main's newer local-endpoint connectivity wording is preserved alongside S3 scratch documentation, and the timeout-race inventory retains both main and S3 test retirements. Gateway-server graph types, type-aware lint, formatting, docs MDX sanity, and suppression inventory (3/3; 44.99s wrapper) pass. Runtime and Madge cycles are both zero. Exact-head hosted CI remains the landing gate. The signed diagnostic for the previously observed initial-turn admission failure is test-only (+78 lines), keeps every authority assertion, and rethrows the original error. It has independent P1 scoped-clean review (0.93). No causal repair or inherited-failure waiver is claimed for that case.

Main now contains the separately proved foreground-authority callback, Git fallback fixture, updater fixture export, configured-owner Doctor expectation, and boolean-provider parity repairs. S3 preserves main's intended configured-owner disk-config policy and profile database fence; an unpublished extra database guard was retired. The new hosted run must demonstrate these fixes and the remaining boundaries on its actual merge checkout.

R47 candidate `32ce3fc3e82798fef7a0a0294bc144ff6f65b562` fixes the PR-owned integration error reported by R46 production types and core test-type jobs 2, 3, 4, and 5: main now requires the already captured `pendingReceiptId` for terminal retention, and S3's deferred finalization must pass that same fact. The one-line repair preserves main's pre-mutation capture and receipt/successor ownership. Conflict-free rebase onto `f9af58c66f79f23a2e051cfe5b9feccf6befc2da`; affected types and both cycle checks pass (zero cycles). All 13 focused cases pass across the suppression guard and the three finalization/retention files (1,021.40s wrapper, including 459.10s cold worker preparation; cron Vitest 850.54s). They cover terminal idempotence, lost replies, successor isolation, mixed deferred release failure, and pending-receipt retention within 64 rows. Independent P1 review is scoped-clean (0.99); no assertions, limits, schemas, or budgets changed.

R46 hosted CI [38339158358](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38339158358) completed against actual merge `f71360708f6090fb05808c78a6c09ddfee5a5dab` (main `76edfee2d220` + head `e8dfd4ce6676`): 203 jobs, 174 successful, 15 failing execution leaves plus the aggregate gate, 13 skipped, no cancelled CI jobs. Cancelled ancillary workflows have independently verified successful same-head replacements. This run provides positive same-store/different-store/restart lifecycle proof, required-native execution, and the public device-runner wire path; it does not make the failing jobs green. The five type failures are repaired above. Current-main scheduled evidence reproduces Workboard asset drift, Docker's tracked-change refusal, loader preparation failures, stale updater fixture exports, the cron continuation count, and the foreground callback-authority defect. Authority defects remain unwaived and are repaired at their owner. Session-create admission, publication coordination, installation fallback, Telegram coalescing, and missing bundled-entry startup remain under individual investigation. Final exact-head hosted CI is required after corrective publication.

R46 candidate `e8dfd4ce6676fa05643e96e7379a3e910bbf675c` resolves only the generated config-doc hash conflict against main `f6c9a769e0f24780696a5aaf0e90dabf748adbcc`, through the canonical generator. Config counts stay at core 2,476 / channel 3,963 / plugin 4,527. Config/updater types, canonical config verification, MDX sanity (1,353 files), all three suppression cases (49.46s wrapper), and diff sanity pass. Runtime and Madge both report zero cycles. Main's newer behavior is retained; unchanged S3 runtime proof and independent reviews retain their recorded head scope. Final exact-head hosted CI remains required.

R45 candidate `298a63bdc7b20b583c97d204a3695796f1f11066` retains main's committed namespace-list reuse during unrelated pending writes while keeping S3's write-revision freshness check. The two namespace regressions pass (149.19s wrapper / 50.02s Vitest); types, runtime cycles **0**, Madge cycles **0**, formatting, and all three suppression cases pass (69.66s wrapper). Independent P1 owner-context and fixture reviews are scoped-clean. The initial expiry case exposed a mixed-clock fixture defect: its cold worker read took 10.74 seconds and expired a 10-second row before warming the cache. The controlled cache clock is now fixed in the future; the TTL, exact 10,000ms advance, all row assertions and zero-extra-dispatch/uncertain-reload assertions remain unchanged. This is a fixture correction, not an increase to a timeout or TTL. Exact-head hosted CI remains required.

Preceding R44 candidate `929ad4aa7e6379b6346a1c6958c6c1dc41fb39dd`: conflicted cron-tool/Gateway type graph passes; runtime cycles **0**, Madge cycles **0**; formatting and diff sanity pass. The full focused run passes **23/23** cases (647.53s wrapper): three suppression checks, ten scheduled-policy owner/manager adoption cases, and ten invocation/revocation guards. Independent P1 conflict review is scoped-clean (0.98). Main's fresh-owner authority capture and every security assertion are retained. Hosted exact-head CI is the remaining broad/Linux gate; older CI is not a waiver.

R43 conflict-only integration retains main's `DisposableStack` preparation cleanup and intentional test retirements. The conflicted core type graph passes, runtime and Madge cycles are both zero, and an independent P1 conflict review is scoped-clean. All four focused files pass: 140 cases across session-store, cron CLI, CLI preparation and lifecycle publication (931.66s wrapper). No assertion, timeout, retry, suppression or baseline was weakened. The current base includes the separately proved main suppression repair; exact-head CI remains the broad gate.

R38 local proof on `bd1156637fb8163e68a1461d373dd2ad36a9541c`: affected core and Codex type graphs pass; both runtime and Madge cycles are zero; the three suppression cases pass; wrapper inventory and imported source closure checks pass. The selected extension/tooling run passes 137 cases (412.26s wrapper), and two side-question controls pass (254.76s wrapper). The core run passes 175 cases but **fails** the fallback-transcript case at its unchanged 120-second limit (670.93s wrapper). It did not provide a settled result or stage trace sufficient to attribute the timeout. The test keeps main's fallback-notice assertions and adds only snapshot restoration; no assertion or deadline was relaxed. This remains an unresolved local observation requiring final hosted proof; it is not a main-red waiver. Fresh P1 review of the final fixture corrections is scoped-clean. Formatting and diff sanity pass. Optional typed lint was stopped before its target ran because it began independent SDK declaration preparation; hosted CI owns that missing broad proof. The resulting owned artifact lock was released only after all captured compiler processes stopped.

Current model-policy regression: Doctor persists the migrated job without a forbidden override; real ordinary isolated execution reaches one synthetic provider adapter call on `openai/gpt-5.4`. A distinct ordinary automation with `openai/gpt-4o-mini` is refused before provider invocation, with policy unchanged. Execution proof: 112.02s wrapper / 29.232s test body; migration/profile/notice proof: three cases, 123.51s wrapper / 4.239s test bodies. Both have independent P2 reviews. This is synthetic provider/session proof, not live external inference.

The conflict-focused run passes eight selected Gateway/cron cases (447.24s), plus all three adopted on-exit handoff cases (146.69s). Core and conflicted test types, scoped lint, suppression inventory (three cases / 47.64s), and runtime/Madge cycles (zero each) pass on the preceding integration. An earlier small rebase retained main's plugin-runtime test retirement and removed superseded heartbeat/SDK-alias coverage. The preceding rebase resolved the generated config-doc hash and passed the canonical documentation check, suppression inventory, and both cycle checks. The latest lifecycle-publication conflict receives affected typechecking, focused boundary proof, both cycle checks, and independent review before publication. Hosted CI records actual final job seconds when complete.

The trusted-Git-environment finding is fixed in code using the existing `mergeProcessEnv` owner and exact named reads. The unchanged detector reports two findings before / zero after, with zero scanner errors. Existing environment/identity/node-host tests pass; independent P2 review is scoped-clean. No detector, allowlist, suppression, baseline or rule exception changed.

The original Mattermost dispatch failure did not reproduce across three main and three S3 full-file runs in the same environment (144 cases passed), and subsequently passed hosted CI. Its distinct expiry failure was repaired by main's fixture-generation change. The original failure is not claimed as a causal fix.

Provider fallback now reuses the persisted canonical user turn and applies retry context after harness selection. Its regression fails on the original producer and passes with identical serialized provider input and sender context; retained internal/decorated variants pass. Recording and live-authority guards are unchanged. Local full-Gateway attempts timed out before the target assertion, so they are not claimed as positive full-flow proof.

### Published v2026.9.9 updater and recovery proof

[The exact-155d AWS run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_135e177e5bf7355440fb54ce06d71f76) passed the two existing official package cells with unchanged deadlines. Canonical build/pack passed in 425.961s, including tarball integrity, npm inventory and dist import-graph checks. The actual installed published baseline identifies commit `bcfc88812a35243893585dbeca87ca41b48272ca`; the candidate identifies `155d359fb027d2f05b964e72608ea5531bf421df`. Both report version 2026.9.9, so serving build ID, package identity and SHA-256 distinguish them. Candidate tarball: `7099381e622cb63a240253b413ee16d82d6086c90167b04ac78b564e7c9de8a0`.

- Published-driver update: **525.201s**, including the actual installed updater (401.574s), managed restart, readyz=200, exact serving identity, durable/incognito readback, repeat maintenance and service stop. prs.title: fix: one-shot CLI commands linger after output on cold caches
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes one-shot CLI commands lingering after printing their result when the module compile cache is cold, especially Bun `config set gateway.mode local` with fresh isolated state.

## User Impact

One-shot commands no longer populate a module compile cache by default. Automatic caching remains enabled for foreground Gateway runs and explicit Gateway prewarming. Setting `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE` still opts any command in, and `NODE_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE` still wins.

This trades automatic warm-cache startup gains for predictable one-shot completion. No timeout is shortened, no database cleanup is skipped, and no schema/configuration migration or operator action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Culprit: e517de8ca2b26 (#170514), which enabled compile caching for compiled entries inside source checkouts. The named config/profile-admission commits did not introduce a disposer timeout. The timing fixture gives fresh runs a new `TMPDIR` as well as state, which also creates a cold module cache.

Instrumentation found all database resources, lock release, and CLI disposers complete promptly. Bun emitted its JavaScript `exit` event at 5.11 seconds, but the OS process remained alive until 13.06 seconds. A native sample showed the main thread waiting on a semaphore while `BunCompileCache` generated bytecode. Bun's cache owner serially generates and persists missing bytecode after exit handlers; the apparent 10-second timeout is finite compilation work. A paired cache-disabled run exited 9 ms after its exit event. Node also exhibited a 4.08-second cold-cache tail, so the fix belongs to command cache admission across runtimes.

The shared cache-directory owner now admits automatic cache work only when application entrypoints supply the foreground-Gateway role fact from their existing startup-safe parser. The low-level helper remains self-contained for isolated maintainer wrappers. The prewarm entry explicitly retains its cache-population purpose. Database ownership, worker settlement, lease release, and natural process exit remain intact.

Release-note context: one-shot Node and Bun CLI commands finish promptly on cold caches instead of lingering after output; Gateway caching and explicit cache opt-in remain available.

## Evidence

- Regression at the compiled-entry/cache owner fails against the original owner (1 failed / 24 passed) and passes with the repair. It protects default one-shot completion and explicit caller opt-in; existing Gateway activation, disabled-cache, namespace, and respawn coverage remains green.
- Existing prewarm/retention tests pass (8/8). No application parser dependency is added to the shared cache helper.
- Test cost: compiled-entry file 2.90 s Vitest duration, 12.12 s wrapper wall (new case 2 ms in the initial measured run); prewarm/retention file 6.11 s Vitest duration, 15.45 s wrapper wall. No new process boot, timer, or sleep.
- Independent Codex autoreview of the final patch: scoped-clean through P2.
- Source-performance runtime build passed (6m 7.1s). Dependency setup passed; the initial full declaration build was stopped after 4m 23s in declaration generation. No full declaration-build pass is claimed.

The supplied timing script ran sequentially with an isolated HOME, state, config, and TMPDIR for every state fixture. Only support for the absolute fork executable and success assertions was added. All six commands returned 0 with the expected configuration update. Times are seconds:

| Runtime | State | First output | Exit | Tail |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Bun 1.4.3 | fresh | 6.21 | 6.55 | 0.34 |
| Bun 1.4.3 | reused | 6.36 | 6.95 | 0.59 |
| supplied Bun fork (1.4.4) | fresh | 5.90 | 6.18 | 0.28 |
| supplied Bun fork (1.4.4) | reused | 5.76 | 6.14 | 0.37 |
| Node 26.11.1 | fresh | 8.39 | 8.62 | 0.23 |
| Node 26.11.1 | reused | 12.57 | 12.79 | 0.23 |

The lead's c445da4029 baseline was about 6→16s for stock Bun and 8.5→18s for the fork; the earlier 3302551873 baseline was 6.2→6.3s. Our instrumented pre-fix run confirmed a 6.42→13.77s fresh Bun delay, and the initial narrower Bun-only experiment left a 3.80→7.89s Node delay. The final policy removes the multi-second tail in all three runtimes. The host was heavily loaded; these are exit-tail measurements, not claims about absolute startup speed. Reused state remains free of the long tail.

The launcher policy and ownership cases pass (11/11 selected; 122 unrelated cases skipped): `OPENCLAW_E2E_SKIP_BUILD=1 pnpm test test/openclaw-launcher.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t "selects compile cache policy|shares the first-success compile cache base"`. The documented prebuilt option reused the completed runtime; the cases own their fixture packages. Cost: 8.69 s Vitest duration, 16.82 s wrapper wall. No new subprocess case was added.

Focused lint, formatting, syntax, conflict-marker, line-cap, max-lines, and assertion checks passed. The broad changed checker was canceled in its unrelated SQLite-worker scan after 550 s; no passing result is claimed for that scan. Targeted `tsgo` configurations passed: core test `other`, core test `infra`, and root E2E. Production core typing also passed after the caller correction. Exact-head CI: pending for the correction.


Initial CI run [38352161975](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38352161975), attempt 1, on `0a6ee048df13cbb6c00ebf47a04e2dfa780ba419` finished with 38 successful, 25 skipped, and 5 failing jobs, without cancellations. Four test jobs were PR-caused; the fifth was the aggregate gate. `checks-fast-bun-launcher` and `checks-node-changed-2` found the stale default-launcher cache expectation. `checks-node-compact-small-1` and `checks-node-changed-3` found an application-parser import missing from extracted wrapper dependencies. The correction removes that dependency and supplies role facts from application callers, then updates the default-launcher contract; it does not expand the wrapper inventory. Closes #170008. Builds on merged #169977.

## What Problem This Solves

Custom router aliases can return a concrete upstream model id even though OpenClaw used the requested route, causing a misleading “Model route changed” notice.

## User Impact

Operators can set `models.providers.<id>.models[].responseModelEquivalent: true` on a user-authored custom model row. The endpoint may select any response model for that alias, including endpoint-internal substitutions. The concrete served model and usage remain recorded; actual OpenClaw model/provider fallbacks and overrides still produce their notice.

Omitted or false preserves normal detection. Bundled/official provider policy cannot be overridden, including official catalog aliases such as `azure-openai-responses`. Plugin/catalog rows, agent `models.json` rows, and rows marked `metadataSource: "models-add"` cannot grant equivalence. No Doctor migration is needed for an optional key; existing stored data formats are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both terminal producers use the route classifier, which reads the captured authored source and existing policy/catalog ownership indexes. This implements the October 12, 2026 maintainer decision: boolean key, authored rows only, official policy authoritative. It includes the review-requested fix for official catalog aliases without broadening auth-policy ownership. Contributor commits by @xyrolle are preserved; main was merged without rebasing or force-pushing.

prs.title: fix(gateway): keep updates responsive under startup load
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Managed deployment acceptance can time out a valid marker dispatch during startup or replay load and repeat the same failure during rollback. Fresh agent admission also takes a whole-store barrier behind unrelated replay validators. Incomplete shutdown receipts force avoidable foreground integrity work on the next native admission.

## User Impact

Operators can update and roll back a busy Gateway within the existing bounded acceptance budget. Legitimate startup work delays acceptance; data, identity, health and terminal marker failures still stop it. No schema or configuration migration is required. The bundled controller pair changes and must be adopted by its operator.

## Why This Change Was Made

Acceptance and rollback share the existing configurable verification deadline (600 seconds by default). They wait for the model agent, critical startup, bounded event-loop delay and a responsive RPC from the exact process. CPU/utilization warnings alone permit acceptance; another agent's background inspection does not block an admitted model agent. A typed dispatch timeout is reconciled by retrying the identical payload and idempotency key after readiness. Exact terminal reply, receipt, session, model, build and process checks still apply. Real data, health, identity, protocol and deadline failures remain failures. Strict profiling stays ineligible under load.

Canonical agent admission reserves its session key rather than the whole store, preserving FIFO for overlapping keys and all lifecycle/authority checks. The history backlog regression protects the existing separation of prepared reads from writer admission.

Native retirement makes one TRUNCATE checkpoint attempt with zero reader-lock wait. The final current, healthy handle earns a clean receipt only when its post-close WAL is empty. A genuinely pinned reader retains dirty proof. Eligible matching dirty receipts use the existing native WAL/schema admission and background verifier; successful verification uses its existing durable proof owner. Removed the obsolete eviction close option across all callers.

No schema, dependency, retention or new configuration changes. Update documentation states the load policy.

## Evidence

Team sandbox only, synthetic state and loopback provider; every command constrained to CPUs 64–127, 64 GiB, nice 10 and ionice 3. No production state or accounts used; sandbox removed.

- 3.01 GiB native dirty admission: **3969.94 → 2842.23 ms** (28.4% lower). Full verification completed in the background at 4133.69 ms overall and wrote durable proof. These times include cold worker loading.
- Final 3.03 GiB deploy-style restart: **65 real agent requests interrupted** through canonical CLI drain/handoff; drain plus close **4060.57 ms**, empty WAL and clean-close receipt **written**. Earlier separately loaded PASSIVE wave: 3929.66 ms. This small difference is neutral evidence, not a controlled speedup or regression.
- Real pinned-reader control: checkpoint remains incomplete, nonempty WAL and dirty proof; no false certification.
- Next source Gateway, with 25 durable watch replay roots active: actual controller emitted **MARKER_VERIFIED** after **83.611 s from startup**, including a deliberate 30-second replay observation. Readiness was 41.217 s; controller verification took 12.099 s. Startup reused clean proof and queued a quick check rather than a full scan.

Production growth is required by the explicitly requested readiness/reconciliation contract: the controller adds 115 lines. Core replaces close policy machinery and narrows an existing admission barrier; no second owner or cached fast path is added.

### Focused verification

No Testbox/Crabbox leases. Broad gates belong to PR CI.

- Changed-file oxfmt and focused repo lint passed. Standalone controller files are outside normal lint scope; direct lint retains exactly 700 existing diagnostics, with no increase.
- Four focused files on integrated main: 4 admission, 57 database and 25 pool tests passed; one Linux-only case skipped. `pnpm test <four focused files> --maxWorkers=1`: 292.35 s wrapper wall time.
- Final checkpoint change: `pnpm test src/state/openclaw-agent-execution.integrity.test.ts src/state/openclaw-agent-db.integrity-lease.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **58 passed, one Linux-only case skipped**, 101.44 s wrapper wall time.
- Portable controller marker proof: 23 cases passed initially; three fixture defects were corrected and their focused rerun passed 3/3. Latest shared convergence/load/readiness checks: **11/11 passed** (31.900 s, 6.325 s and 16.794 s focused runs).
- Original-source controls fail for the intended handoff seal, dirty native admission, unrelated replay barrier, typed dispatch timeout/rollback patience, sustained CPU veto and unrelated inspection veto. An additional idle-peer control caught the discarded PASSIVE-only simplification and now passes; it is not an original-code failure.
- Syntax and diff checks passed. Independent review completed through the lead-authorized fallback: a separate reviewer with fresh context inspected the staged diff, prepared PR body and affected owners/callers. No actionable likely or high-impact findings. The helper refused the requested route before inference; operator configuration was left unchanged.

## Limits

The benchmark is a source Gateway with a synthetic provider. Protected-state, policy, approval-history and external activation fixture checks were stubbed; actual native readiness, RPC, process binding and terminal receipt checks were preserved. It is not a packaged deployment or production provider turn.

The exact production preparation hang and all 25 real session targets were not reproduced. Pending reply counts reserve before outbound delivery; no permanently dead target was established, so no speculative reply tombstones were added. The keyed admission change removes the demonstrated whole-store dependency; it does not claim an unknown native FIFO wait was eliminated.

Three additional SQLite/session sibling files passed: 31 tests, 106.25 s Vitest wall time. The standalone controller suite is running. Its installed suspension-bundle dependency is unavailable on this Mac; the same deadline test fails on unchanged integrated main (exit 75, missing installed bundle), so that is host evidence rather than a product pass; Linux-only database coverage and privileged Linux controller owner-flow coverage remain gaps on this Mac. Broad SQLite/session suites and full gates belong to PR CI. CI duration is not available until publication.

prs.title: fix(agents): prompt cache invalidated when code mode catalog changes mid-session
prs.body:
Closes #170233
Related: #170050, #169091

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: long Code Mode sessions lose their reusable prompt prefix whenever the
tool catalog drifts between runs of one session (late MCP connects, plugin
loads, client tool shadows), so every later turn pays full input cost again
instead of reusing the cached prefix.

## User Impact

User impact: long-running agents on providers with prompt caching keep their
cached prefix across mid-session catalog changes, restoring cache hit rates
for the rest of the session; tool discovery and execution behavior are
unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `exec` tool description embeds the tool catalog index, and
`applyCodeModeCatalog` rewrote it on every catalog change via
`catalogRef.onChange`. The tools array precedes system and messages in
provider prompts, so any description change invalidates the cached prefix for
the whole session; on long sessions this showed up as a full cache rewrite of
a 170k-950k token prompt on every catalog change.

This change stamps the catalog into the description on the first catalog
application of a session (keyed by `sessionKey`, which the tool-surface plan
already threads through the bridge) and makes `onChange` a no-op afterwards.
Runtime discovery is unchanged: `catalog.search`/`API.list` expose new tools
at runtime, and a new session gets the current catalog. Runs without a
session key keep the previous per-run behavior, so headless and
schema-projection surfaces are untouched.

Alternative considered: keying the stamp by `catalogRef` identity instead of
adding a `sessionKey` param. Rejected because the same session can rebuild its
tool surface (and catalog ref) across runs — exactly the paths where late
connects land — so ref-keying would still rewrite the prefix per rebuild.
Moving the catalog index out of the tools array entirely (discovery-only via
`catalog.search`) was also considered and rejected as a larger behavioral
change: the index is what lets the model plan around available tools, and a
moving system-prompt block invalidates the cache the same way.

Related: #170050 stabilized message-tool and replay prefix content; #169091
removed execution-allowlist dependence from this same description. This PR
covers the remaining rewrite trigger: catalog drift between runs of one
session.

## Evidence

Focused tests (synthetic, provider-free), repo's own runner:

- `src/agents/code-mode.catalog-description-stamp.test.ts` (new, 3 tests):
  exec description byte-identical across two runs of one session when the
  catalog grows; `catalog.search` still finds and calls the mid-session tool
  at runtime while the description stays stamped; a new session gets a fresh
  description with the current catalog.
- Touched-area suites, all passed:
  - `code-mode.test.ts`, `code-mode.bridge.lifecycle.test.ts`,
    `node-plugin-tools.test.ts`, `code-mode-retention.test.ts` — 49 tests.
  - `embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-client-tools.test.ts` — 15 tests.
  - 26-file code-mode/bash-tools/tool-surface sweep (incl.
    `embedded-agent-runner.prompt-cache.test.ts`, `tool-surface-bridge.test.ts`,
    `tool-surface-plan*.test.ts`) — 4 shards passed (290 tests).
- `oxfmt --check` clean on the 9 touched files; `oxlint` clean;
  `pnpm tsgo:core` (core typecheck) clean.

Existing suites that asserted the old rewrite-on-drift contract
(`code-mode` client-shadow, bridge-lifecycle client tool, description
retention restriction, embedded runner observer/registry) now assert the
stamped contract with equivalent rigor, including that the live catalog still
narrows/grows while descriptions stay pinned.

Release-note context: keep Code Mode tool declarations stable across
mid-session catalog changes so long sessions keep their prompt-cache prefix.

prs.title: fix: catalog list fails when Codex thread previews are huge
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the session catalog fails to parse Codex `thread/list` pages when stored previews are huge, then one bad host stalls `sessions.catalog.list`.

Fixes #156831

## User Impact

User impact: large Codex homes keep listing. A hung or unparseable host is fail-soft instead of blocking sibling hosts until the 60s deadline.

## Why This Change Was Made

Catalog decoding drops the tail of a native `preview` string before JSON.parse, but only once the retained prefix already fixes the displayed text: the selector's 2,048-unit prefix, no terminal controls, and more than 500 units of collapsed, trimmed text. Each whitespace run is kept as one unit while reading, since the projection collapses runs anyway, so text after a long whitespace run survives. Controls before the first ANSI introducer (ESC, CSI, OSC) are deleted in place by the sanitizer, so each run of them is kept as one unit too. Only previews whose ANSI sequences leave the display undetermined are cut at 64 KiB. The displayed preview matches the existing projection and 8–24 MB pages still stay under the 8 MiB incomplete-frame recovery.

Each local catalog host gets one fail-soft deadline that covers page reads and adoption projection, on both the non-progressive path and progressive `finishLocalHost` / publication. It uses the existing 60s default request allowance (`CODEX_CATALOG_LOCAL_HOST_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_MS`), so slow large homes are not marked unavailable earlier than today; paired nodes stay at 8s.

## Evidence

Focused Vitest, all passing at f200f2f87f:

- `extensions/codex/src/app-server/client-catalog-preview-bound.test.ts` (19 tests): oversized preview parse, escaped quotes while skipping, skipped fragments vs the 1000-line recovery cap, and displayed-preview parity with the canonical selector for whitespace-heavy prefixes, escaped newlines, sparse words, terminal controls and a surrogate at the display boundary, text after whitespace, escaped newlines or removable controls beyond the 64 KiB fallback, removable controls between whitespace runs and before an ANSI sequence, and whitespace-only preview lines vs the recovery cap.
- `extensions/codex/src/app-server/client-catalog-worker.test.ts` (25 tests): 9 MiB preview recovery, plus worker vs inline projection parity for a whitespace-heavy prefix, a control-laden preview, `" ".repeat(65_536) + "meaningful text"`, and `"\u0007".repeat(15_000) + "meaningful text"` (the last two fail before this change, pass after).
- `extensions/codex/src/session-catalog-list-operation.test.ts` (16 tests): progressive and non-progressive host timeouts with sibling fail-soft, and a new case that holds the adoption read after paging completes (fails before this change, passes after).

`oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` clean.

Not yet attached: an after-fix `sessions.catalog.list` trace from a real large Codex home.

Supersedes #157024 by @Olli0103, keeping its core classification (credited as co-author).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Doctor reports an active model as "not in the local model catalog" when the running Gateway publishes it, because the check compares refs against offline provider metadata while `models list` reports the Gateway's published catalog (for example `google/gemini-flash-lite-latest`, which Google's manifest omits but its runtime catalog serves).

## User Impact

User impact: `openclaw doctor` no longer flags models the selected Gateway actually serves; real typos and refs Doctor cannot confirm (Gateway unreachable) still get the advisory.

## Why This Change Was Made

`core/doctor/model-references` on current `main` already reads the prepared Gateway catalog in the same check, but only for server diagnostics. This change reuses that single read to confirm membership: a matching published row is classified as `published-model` (from #157024) and suppresses the generic advisory. Compared with #157024, the separate Gateway RPC and the environment forwarding through the Doctor flow are no longer needed, so the diff is small (5 files, ~115 lines including tests). The exec-SecretRef guard still skips the catalog read without `--allow-exec`.

## Evidence

Live, read-only, against a real running Gateway (source build of this branch vs. installed 2026.10.2), `openclaw doctor --lint --only core/doctor/model-references --severity-min info --json`:

| Scenario | Build | Result |

| active `google/gemini-flash-lite-latest` (listed by `models list --provider google`) | installed 2026.10.2 | 1 info finding, exit 1 (false positive) |
| same config | this branch | `findings: []`, exit 0 |

| unreachable Gateway (`OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT` pointed at a closed port) | this branch | 1 info finding for the original ref, exit 1 |

prs.title: fix(gateway): resume sessions whose restart-aborted run finished before the recovery marker
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a main session interrupted by a Gateway restart is silently not resumed by restart recovery when its run finished its restart-abort cleanup while the shutdown recovery marker was still writing.

## User Impact

User impact: sessions whose run was aborted for restart are marked for restart recovery even if the run's cleanup wins the race against the marker, and every session the marker skips now logs its reason instead of only an aggregate count.

## Why This Change Was Made

Restart shutdown collects restart-aborted chat runs as recovery candidates (`isRestartRecoveryRun` explicitly admits controllers the close prelude already aborted for restart), but the marker then revalidated custody against the live chat abort controller map, both while planning and right before commit. Once the aborted run finished and removed its registration (and its admission was released), the same session was rejected as `owner_changed`, with only `marked N interrupted main session(s)` in the log.

Shutdown now keeps the exact captured restart-aborted controller as custody while no replacement controller owns that session. User aborts, completed work, replacement controllers, newer runs, changed session ids and lifecycle generation changes still reject, and the marker logs bounded per-session skip reasons.

Observed in production during a deploy restart: the drain budget expired, the run was aborted for restart, the run's lane errored about 400 ms later, the marker took over a second and marked a different session, and the interrupted session never appeared among the next process's recovery candidates. The logs are consistent with this race but cannot prove it for that session; the new skip diagnostics will.

Related: the transcript side of the same incident (streamed answer lost on restart abort) is fixed separately in openclaw/openclaw#170697.

## Evidence

- New regression `revalidates collected shutdown recovery custody after %s` in `server-run-shutdown.recovery.test.ts` drives the real `prepareGatewayRunShutdown` and marker persistence with registration and admission cleanup landing before planning and before commit: both positive cases fail with the old predicate and pass now; six exclusion cases (user abort, replacement, newer run, identity change, lifecycle change, non-main) keep rejecting.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/server-run-shutdown.recovery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 12 passed.
- `pnpm test src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-recovery-marking.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 14 passed.
- `pnpm test src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-abort.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 6 passed.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/server-close.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 54 passed.
- Targeted typechecks (`tsconfig.core.test.gateway-server.json`, `tsconfig.core.test.agents-sessions.json`), format check and `git diff --check` pass. The local core oxlint shard only reported pre-existing `max-lines` errors in files this PR does not touch; CI owns full lint. Local wall times were inflated by heavy host load.
