prs.title: fix(process): Windows claude-cli spawn picks the npm POSIX shim over claude.cmd
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #141382.

On Windows every `claude-cli` turn fails in 2026.9.2. The user sees a request timeout and the gateway logs `write EPIPE`, which is a red herring: it masks an asynchronous `ENOENT` from `spawn()`.

The real cause is PATH probe order. `resolveWindowsExecutableExtensions` returns the bare name before any PATHEXT candidate:

`src/infra/executable-path.ts`

```ts
const extensions = [...resolveWindowsExecutableExtSet(env)];
return includeExtensionless ? ["", ...extensions] : extensions;
```

and `resolveExecutableFromPathEnv` takes the first hit:

```ts
for (const entry of entries) {
  for (const ext of extensions) {
    const candidate = path.join(entry, executable + ext);
    if (isExecutableFile(candidate, { env })) {
      return candidate;
    }
```

A global npm install of `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` writes three files into a directory on PATH: `claude` (a 308 byte `/bin/sh` shim), `claude.cmd`, and `claude.ps1`. The bare shim matches first, and `CreateProcess` cannot execute it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The order is reversed so PATHEXT candidates are probed first and the extensionless entry becomes the last resort. On Windows an extensionless file is not directly executable, so it should never outrank a real `.cmd` or `.exe` of the same name.

Keeping the entry rather than dropping it preserves existing behaviour for callers that pass `includeExtensionless: true` and genuinely have only a bare file present; that case still resolves, it simply no longer wins when a PATHEXT sibling exists. Call sites that already pass `includeExtensionless: false` are untouched.

This is a one line ordering change. Nothing about acceptance, caching, or PATH parsing moves.

## User Impact

Windows installs where the CLI was installed through global npm can spawn it again, which is every `claude-cli` turn on that setup. The issue reports 2026.9.1 was unaffected because launching was delegated to the SDK.

## Evidence

Production change is +4/-1 in one file.

The regression test fails on unfixed code for the right reason. Restoring only `src/infra/executable-path.ts` from main:

```
× prefers a PATHEXT match over an extensionless shim of the same name
  → expected '…/claude' to be '…/claude.cmd'
  Tests  1 failed | 26 passed | 2 skipped (29)
```

It runs on any platform: the suite already has a `withMockedPlatform("win32", …)` helper, and under that mock `isExecutableFile` only checks the file and its extension, so no Windows host is needed.

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/executable-path.test.ts        27 passed | 2 skipped
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra src/process src/tui     47 files, 688 passed
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json                                clean
./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check <both touched files>                         clean
```

One failure in that wider run, `btw-inline-message > sanitizes the question and successful Markdown result on every update`, reproduces identically with this file restored from main, so it is pre-existing and unrelated.

The existing `keeps extensionless lookup explicit with PATHEXT` cases still pass unchanged. They cover a bare file with no sibling, which this ordering does not affect; the new case is the ambiguous one they did not cover.

Proof gap worth stating: I have no Windows host, so this is verified through the mocked-platform path rather than by spawning the real CLI on Windows. The mock covers the resolver decision that the issue identifies, not the downstream `CreateProcess` behaviour.

AI-assisted: yes. I traced the source path by hand and ran every command above myself.

prs.title: fix(gateway): reject malformed usage cost scopes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Malformed `usage.cost` scope selectors can silently normalize to the default agent and return a report for a scope the caller did not request.

## Why This Change Was Made

The canonical `usage.cost` RPC owner rejects a provided non-string `agentId`, an unsupported `agentScope`, or an agent combined with `agentScope: "all"` before resolving the default owner or loading cost data. Standalone blank `agentId` remains equivalent to omission, including the existing blank-plus-all form; the earlier proposal to reject standalone blank values has been removed.

## User Impact

Malformed direct RPC requests receive `INVALID_REQUEST`. Valid default, explicit-agent, all-agent, standalone blank, and blank-plus-all requests retain their established behavior, including usage created by the installed stable release before upgrading.

## Evidence

### October 13: actual shipped Gateway and populated stable-release upgrade

Real main integration parents: original contributor head `a43d03be3cafefcadabd5ce413be1c53f68a8919` and main `799b7a347c502912efb704b1722e117bc0a644ed`; no force-push or invented ancestry.

No CHANGELOG, temporary proof assets, dependency, config/default, protocol schema, authority, database migration or persistence format change is introduced.

prs.title: fix(doctor): context engines fail reading config
prs.body:
Related: #170445

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes: `openclaw doctor` reports `Doctor finished with plugin load errors` (exit 1 with `--non-interactive`) when the plugin selected in `plugins.slots.contextEngine` reads `api.runtime.config.current()` in `register()`.
- Doctor's config flow registers that plugin for host-compatibility inspection (preview notes, `--fix` repair sequence) before the post-flow publication from #170445.
- The read then throws `Runtime config is not prepared. Await captureRuntimeConfigAsyncReader()() first.`

## User Impact

- `openclaw doctor` completes without plugin load errors when a context-engine plugin reads runtime config during registration.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The config flow publishes the loaded runtime config right after config preflight, before its preview and repair steps register plugins, through the same `loadPinnedRuntimeConfigAsync` owner `doctor --lint` uses.
- An invalid existing config stays unpublished at that point, matching the CLI config guard and `doctor --lint`; the post-flow publication from #170445 still covers it, and a Doctor config write republishes.
- `doctor --lint` publishes `runtimeConfig`, the non-deprecated name for the same snapshot object.

## Evidence

- Head: `04ecab8fe16f9459b8f3539f3652a7ae186d1709`
- Focused suites at the head: `src/commands/doctor-config-flow.test.ts`, `src/flows/doctor-health.plugin-load.test.ts`, `src/flows/doctor-health.test.ts`, and the three `doctor-lint` suites exit 0 (61/61 tests).
- Regression cases in `src/commands/doctor-config-flow.test.ts`: a fixture plugin whose `register()` reads `api.runtime.config.current()` loads after a valid or missing config file and fails with `Runtime config is not prepared` for an invalid config.

```text
HEAD 04ecab8fe16f9459b8f3539f3652a7ae186d1709
✓ doctor config flow > lets plugin registration read a valid loaded config
✓ doctor config flow > lets plugin registration read default config when no config file exists
✓ doctor config flow > leaves an invalid loaded config unpublished for plugin registration
✓ prepares runtime config before Doctor contributions register plugins
```

prs.title: fix(ci): use PR CI for broad proof and replay failed tests locally
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

PR preparation still defaults to full local build/check/test gates, and agents lack a focused replay command after PR CI classifies failures.

## User Impact

Developers can use `pnpm test:ci-failed <pr-number|run-id|run-or-pr-url>` to inspect classified failures and replay only selected failed Vitest tests. PR CI provides broad proof by default. `OPENCLAW_PR_GATES_REMOTE=local` retains explicit full local gates; unset selector with `OPENCLAW_TESTBOX=1` retains completed hosted proof.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing job inventory and main-failure classifier through authenticated, cache-aware `gh` reads. Fetch job logs once with at most four requests in flight. Add loose failure discovery alongside the unchanged strict admission-signature parser. New/unknown failures lead the output; pre-existing failures require `--include-pre-existing` for replay. Safe short one-file selections use single-quoted literal-name filters for zsh/bash; suite/unhandled failures and larger selections replay whole files. Non-Vitest failures show failed step names and a job log URL; the CLI keeps no workflow-command map.

Align contributor docs, testing instructions, and landing guidance around CI failure → focused local repair → push once. No CI workflow or runner changes. No full local suite, CI rerun, update-branch, or merge.

## Evidence

Lead-review follow-up at `056818308289f8655758faf7b483a5c224e6acda`: removed duplicated workflow-command mappings after verifying the check planner exposes selections rather than per-check commands. JSON now includes `failedSteps` and omits `localCommand`. Displayed filters use single quotes with embedded apostrophes escaped; execution argv stays unchanged. Failed jobs are processed concurrently through the shared `pLimit(4)` API transport and sorted deterministically.

Focused follow-up proof: `pnpm test test/scripts/ci-failed-tests.test.ts test/scripts/ci-known-main-red.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed 102 tests in 12.97s wall / 2.18s Vitest (the changed pure-test file: 11 tests, 5ms). No CI rerun or merge performed.

prs.title: feat: let users choose sandboxing when creating sessions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Users whose own role does not require sandboxing could not choose it when creating a shared session for sandbox-required members.

## User Impact

Any user with session-create access can choose **Require sandbox** in the New Session page or compact launcher. For a role with `sandbox: "required"`, the control is checked and locked; otherwise it is selectable.

Selecting it permanently requires sandboxed execution for the new session. Leaving it off preserves the agent's sandbox policy; it does not override configured sandboxing. Existing ordinary sessions cannot be upgraded through this creation option.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds the creation-only `sessions.create sandbox: "required"` option with ordinary session-write access and reuses the immutable session sandbox contract. The authenticated handshake exposes the existing creator-role requirement so both creation views can enforce the checked/locked state. The create owner validates adoption atomically: retries may reuse an already sandbox-required row, but cannot stamp an ordinary existing row.

Session-write authorization still applies. There is no explicit sandbox-off option, second sandbox identity, or new cron, Talk, outbound, plugin, or recovery policy path.

prs.title: fix(heartbeat): keep flood guard correct across backward clock steps
prs.body:
Replacement for closed-unmerged #156693, addressing the proof gaps from its ClawSweeper review.

## Problem

The flood buffer is insertion-ordered, but the guard reverse-scans it as though timestamps are sorted and stops at the first out-of-window value. A backward wall-clock step can place a stale timestamp between newer in-window starts, causing the guard to under-count a real burst.

## Fix

Count every in-window start, sort those timestamps newest-first, and derive the same threshold-oldest retry instant from the filtered set.

## Proof

This revision replaces the unreachable direct fixture from #156693 with scheduler-reachable state:

- the unit regression builds the buffer exclusively through `recordRunStart`, with `lastRunStartedAtMs` equal to the final recorded start;
- the scheduler regression drives six manual wakes through the registered handler/bookkeeping path across a backward clock step, then verifies a scheduled wake is skipped as `flood` with `retryAtMs: 1005001`;
- `runOnce` remains at six calls, proving the seventh wake was actually blocked.

The prior downstream proof run measured the focused cooldown test at ~0.3s single-worker and the scheduler harness at ~2.3s; fresh CI on this rebased head should provide the current-main result.

No stored-data or scheduling-contract changes outside the flood-counting assumption.

prs.title: perf(gateway): retain boot filesystem facts in their owners
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Campaign evidence recorded a signed-in reload of a dashboard deep link passing through 14 visible states over roughly 15 seconds. After duplicate Talk discovery was removed, filesystem callbacks still accounted for about 735 inclusive Gateway samples. Boot RPCs repeatedly checked legacy auth sources, canonical file identities, and agent/workspace paths.

## Change

Retain process-owned facts in their existing owners: auth-file identity and legacy-source presence, canonical persisted auth rows, agent paths, workspace Git display facts, session-source preparation, and admitted database read receipts. Local writes publish immediately. Shared directory observations and a 30-second fallback detect external edits and retire with their owners.

Persisted source rows remain separate from resolved credential projections. Observation joins pending native publications, ignores cancelled reads, and fences late invalidation against each affected snapshot, including inherited snapshots reached through a shared source. Watchers use the existing detached async root. Ordinary logical snapshot publications retain physical readers; explicit invalidation, deletion, and shutdown close them.

Authority checks remain after awaits. Privileged writes and receiver admission retain direct physical identity checks, including a swapped file before watcher delivery. The rebase preserves main's new credential-authority capture alongside this lane's read-cancellation signal. No schema, protocol, durability, retention, configuration-option, or UI changes.

**Auth/authority owner review and independent security review are required before landing. Please route through the repository's CODEOWNERS/security-review process. The campaign lead lands this PR; do not auto-merge.**

## External writers

- Live model-auth CLI mutations route through the Gateway; other mutating model-auth commands refuse a foreign live owner (`src/cli/models-cli.ts`). Config mutations also refuse a foreign live owner (`src/cli/config-cli.ts`). `src/cli/local-state-owner.ts` owns routing or exclusive offline access.
- Doctor uses maintenance ownership (`src/flows/doctor-health.ts`, `src/commands/doctor-sqlite-maintenance-lock.ts`).
- Manual edits, older binaries, and low-level store tools can bypass those routes. Directory observations detect their changes, with coarse revalidation if events are missed. Direct admission still rejects a replaced database before the next privileged write.

## Before / after

Synthetic fixture: six agents/workspaces, 120 auth profiles per agent, 300 sessions, 240 transcript messages, one dashboard widget; plugins disabled. Five clients issue 15 boot RPCs after warmup. Final measurement on production candidate `b3e243d13288993253f3b81a14e923aef78a1576`: 225 counted and 900 profiled RPCs, zero errors. Baseline: `2927fa0b918e`. Subsequent fixture-only changes do not alter measured production. No real account, state, credentials, or private capture was used.

Counts are JavaScript filesystem API calls per RPC, not inferred kernel syscalls. Columns are synchronous existence / stat / native-realpath calls.

| RPC | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `talk.catalog` | 56 / 40 / 26 | 4 / 0 / 0 |
| `chat.startup` | 3 / 20 / 38 | 3 / 0 / 0 |
| `agents.list` | 38 / 0 / 12.8 | 2 / 0 / 0.8 |
| `models.authStatus` | 1 / 0 / 3 | 1 / 0 / 0 |
| `models.list` | 1 / 0 / 3 | 1 / 0 / 0 |
| `tools.catalog` | 0 / 0 / 1 | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| `board.get` | 0 / 7 / 4 | 0 / 5 / 2 |
| `cron.list` | 0 / 0 / 4 | 0 / 0 / 4 |
| `cron.status` | 0 / 0 / 0.8 | 0 / 0 / 0.8 |
| `agent.identity.get` | 1 / 0 / 0 | 1 / 0 / 0 |
| `sessions.list`, `sessions.subscribe`, `sessions.resolve`, `sessions.describe`, `config.get` | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 |

The 52 auth legacy-source existence calls and 16 live auth-file identity checks per `talk.catalog` are gone. Its remaining four existence calls check external shell-profile fallback locations. Remaining startup/agent existence calls come from source-runner resolution. Fractional path/read calls are shared Gateway lease guards; board admission remains direct. Async log-file operations inherit RPC traces and are excluded from the process-owned-state claim. Local artifacts retain every captured path and stack for attribution.

Main-thread sampling is **noisy** on the loaded shared Mac; inclusive categories overlap. Intervening main changes also prevent attributing timings solely to this PR.

| Samples | Before | Final candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| All main-thread samples | 4,025 | 4,146 |
| Filesystem inclusive | 1,000 | 189 |
| Auth-profile inclusive | 745 | 259 |
| Agent-directory registry inclusive | 243 | 5 |
| SQLite identity inclusive | 320 | 24 |

Process CPU across threads: 4,781 → 4,025 ms; measured burst wall time: 8,004 → 3,241 ms. Deterministic removed calls are the primary performance proof. These timings do not establish an end-to-end page-load improvement. The scratch Gateway completed clean shutdown, and its loopback port has no listener.

## Evidence

Exact-head CI: Pending on `dcc981e0938b2f8174866881a23733c317f19ef2`; [PR checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/170467/checks).

Retained focused proof: 611 passing tests across 44 files on preceding candidates, each run separately with `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`. Representative wall times: auth file state 12.71 s; external source publication 40.82 s; persisted rows 33.09 s; auth owner state 88.00 s; runtime snapshots 67.52 s; database identity 19.36 s; database validation cache 24.61 s. Transform/worker preparation dominates several files. Full prior per-file results remain in the local evidence report.

New direct production-owner probes fail on their old paths and pass after the repair: logical publication retains its reader; cancelled observation retains source provenance; late refresh preserves a newer snapshot; an unrelated publication cannot hide an external source change; shared fallback retires the stale shared snapshot while preserving the newer derived agent. Native and AsyncResource-backed watcher probes confirm first-importer authority is no longer retained. Existing regressions cover separate-process SQLite writes, symlink retargeting, stale authority, and swapped-file rejection before a queued privileged write.

Local focused Vitest attempts that requested a full worker-artifact compilation were stopped under host limits (latest attempt 18.47 s). They are not passing tests. No full local suite, typecheck, or backend build ran. Testbox/AWS/Hetzner capacity remains blocked; no leases were created. Exact-head GitHub CI is the broad gate. No UI changes, so UI e2e and visual captures are not applicable.

Prior CI exposed real observer/publication regressions: Bun bookkeeping and rollback invalidation, reader retirement during a surviving agent's recovery, auth-refresh cancellation, and stale Reset status. These were treated as regressions, not dismissed as inherited. The corrected final head is now running CI; these integration results remain unverified until it completes. Independent autoreview through P2: the integrated production changes and the staged fixture repair have no remaining actionable findings through P2. Temporary diagnostic assertions were removed after attribution.

## Size and release context

Production delta: **+1,333 LOC** (1,538 additions / 205 deletions across 25 files), measured with `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD -- ':!*.test.ts' ':!*test-support*' ':!docs/*'`. Growth pays for the requested process-owned lifetime, write-through publication, source provenance, external invalidation, and cleanup contracts. Repeated request-time probes and redundant preparation are removed; the new state stays with existing owners.

Release-note context: reduce redundant Gateway filesystem work during Control UI boot without weakening auth or database authority checks. No changelog edit.

prs.title: fix(telegram): fractional media limits appear as rounded integers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Telegram reporting a rounded, incorrect media limit when `mediaMaxMb` is fractional: a 0.5 MB cap rejected a 731,022-byte document but told both the user and the model that the limit was 1MB.

## User Impact

Oversize warnings and model context now report the same accurate limit, using the shared binary-size formatting convention (`512KB` for 0.5 MB, `307.20KB` for 0.3 MB). Integer limits keep their existing text, and file acceptance, download limits, and the Bot API cap do not change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Format the effective byte limit once with the existing shared `formatByteSize` formatter, then carry that text to both consumers instead of rounding it to whole megabytes. This uses the same style and precision as media-core; no new formatter or public SDK surface is introduced.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

## Evidence

Telegram Test Server userbot, real 731,022-byte document, built candidate `9ff57cf4318023757abaae36cd1d524cbd4bf9dc`:

| Configuration | Telegram warning | Captured model request | File attached |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Baseline, `mediaMaxMb: 0.5` | `Maximum size is 1MB.` | `[media unavailable: file exceeds 1MB limit]` | No |
| Candidate, `mediaMaxMb: 0.5` | `Maximum size is 512KB.` | `[media unavailable: file exceeds 512KB limit]` | No |
| Candidate, `mediaMaxMb: 0.3` | `Maximum size is 307.20KB.` | `[media unavailable: file exceeds 307.20KB limit]` | No |
| Candidate, `mediaMaxMb: 1` | No warning | No unavailable notice | Yes, unchanged |

Timeline excerpts: the file was sent at +15s; the candidate warning arrived at +18.269s for 0.5 and +18.255s for 0.3. The subsequent model requests contained the corresponding notices above. Recovery turns and Gateway health checks succeeded, and each run cleaned up its messages and lease.

The retained baseline was recorded at `c8c0e6fbcc77ac1f6b62e637cc030695e540e903`; all three affected production owners are byte-for-byte unchanged between that baseline and this PR's base `92ef706779d10774a361b76d5887d4abed21bc32`.

- Focused bot-handler suite: 18 tests passed, including both Bot API and configured-cap failures, fractional 0.5/0.3 limits, and integer limits.
- Changed-file oxfmt/oxlint and patch whitespace checks passed; build passed.
- Isolated real-provider check on the same head: `gpt-5-mini`, low reasoning, returned `FRACTIONAL_LIVE_OK`.

Simplification: one formatted limit replaces the rounded numeric projection; no new abstraction or test-only seam. Production delta: +14/-7; test delta: +52/-21; docs: +3/-0.

Merge danger: two-way door; a revert restores the old warning text without changing stored data or configuration. Blast radius is limited to Telegram oversize-media warning/context text.

## What Problem This Solves

Interrupted provider streams could save generated text with zero or partial token counters and present them as complete usage. A cancelled Ollama `/v1` stream reproduced `Context: 0/33k` despite saving text.

## User Impact

Interrupted or unmeasured responses report usage as unavailable in status, session metadata, accounting, and usage summaries. Complete measured-zero usage remains zero, and successful streams retain exact provider accounting. Known historical subtotals remain visible without being presented as complete totals. Compatible HTTP responses omit unavailable usage while completing their normal lifecycle.

No configuration, database migration, or protocol version change is required. The optional completeness fact preserves legacy producer and stored-transcript interpretation; it cannot reconstruct missing historical usage.

## Why This Change Was Made

The transport owns accounting completeness. The same fact flows through normalization, run aggregation, the existing session snapshot and abort-partial transaction, then reporting consumers. Terminal usage survives a later transport error. Transcript-backed status and session rows preserve authoritative zero instead of substituting an estimate.

This preserves @OWWZO's commits and credit. Main `799b7a347c502912efb704b1722e117bc0a644ed` was merged without rebasing or force-pushing. Current head: `8e8bba1f724fd10ddf5e526139f3ae2658b0f0b6`.

Against that merged base: production +858/-484 (net +374), tests/fixtures +1098/-148, docs +10/-1. The necessary growth carries one completeness fact through existing typed consumers; superseded partial handling is removed. Prompt/tool text is unchanged; token delta is zero.

## Evidence

- Real CLI → isolated Gateway → Ollama `/v1`, `llama3.2:latest`, on main `706e08c4431947585166891a60c616366c87cf64`: cancellation saved 945 characters with zero/fresh usage and `/status` showed `Context: 0/33k`. Successful control: exact 2605 input / 19 output tokens.
- Repaired generation at `87fa95081e10f082b7caa6543207b8563a3759f7` saved 4607 characters after interruption with unavailable usage. Successful `/v1` and native controls retained exact provider accounting (1809/4 and 1808/10).
- Real CLI `/status`, `chat.history`, and `sessions.list` readback at `8dd5b2bea6f9a6a8f4c43bcaa5414b8dce0e58f9` reopened that saved interruption: `Tokens: unavailable (incomplete response)`, `Context: ~4.2k/33k (13% est)`, null totals, false freshness. This is later persistence/status readback of the real generation, not a fresh-generation claim for the final head.
- Earlier fixture repair: both lane-controller suites now prepare and clear canonical runtime config, matching sibling fixtures. Their 24 Node tests pass (364.84s wrapper). The original 28-file pinned-Bun CI group passes all 493 tests (290.48s wrapper), replacing its 20 missing-config/timeout failures. No assertions, clocks, deadlines, retries, or production guards were weakened.
- Earlier storage checks: 24 tests across transcript reporting, usage readers, and yielded Stop pass (493.25s wrapper). They retain cancellation, exact corruption setup, unavailable accounting, and measured-zero assertions.
- Scoped agent and Gateway test types, lint, formatting, and all seven ratchet/config checks pass. The independent committed-branch Codex review and fresh full exact-head CI are recorded below.

## CI and review

### Main refresh

Current head `8e8bba1f724fd10ddf5e526139f3ae2658b0f0b6` is pushed. Exact-head [CI run 38347871966](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38347871966) completed with 100 successful, 21 skipped, and four failed jobs including the aggregate gate. The separate security-review gate cleared: the current diff contains no sensitive product changes.

The two conflicts were resolved at their existing owners:

- `src/cli/gateway-cli/register.ts`: retain main's extracted stability formatter and this PR's lazy usage renderer; remove the superseded inline paths.
- `src/gateway/session-utils-row.ts`: retain main's sparse resident rows and undefined-field cleanup, while carrying `usageReport` and its presentation fallback.

An automatic-merge duplicate runtime-config setup was removed from the lane-controller fixture. The smaller CLI file also made its old max-lines suppression obsolete; removing that comment fixed the only source lint diagnostic.

Focused proof on merge commit `d8c9eaa5e9481e95a15be216162ff65fcb2c7a42` passed; the final head differs only by removal of that unused lint comment:

| --- | --- | --- |
| Lane controller, Node | 36 passed | 485.899s |
| Original 28-file pinned-Bun group | 499 passed | 567.722s |
| Storage and yielded Stop | 21 passed | 995.459s |
| Session usage and derived readers | 23 passed | 714.871s |
| CLI, stability and OpenAI stream siblings | 72 passed | 368.033s |

Build/setup, scoped core/UI and agent/Gateway test types, lint, formatting and all seven ratchet/config/inventory checks passed. Wrapper times include cold compiler preparation and shared-host load. The initial Ollama lint attempt timed out in SDK declaration preparation before linting; it passed after a retry using the preparer's supported longer compiler deadline. Test deadlines and assertions were unchanged. Core lint reported only the obsolete suppression; focused lint and formatting passed after its removal.

The fresh committed-branch Codex review is scoped-clean through P2 (no findings, confidence 0.82); an independent review of the final comment-only cleanup is also scoped-clean (confidence 0.99). The current head's ClawSweeper review and CI outcome remain pending. Existing real Ollama/CLI evidence below is reused; no new generation was run for this merge refresh.

### Previous-head CI attribution

At previous head `e4fcd5aa80f14696baaa847c7874314f3cba0deb`, committed-branch Codex autoreview was scoped-clean through P2 (confidence 0.80), and ClawSweeper found no code defects. prs.title: fix(ci): report all selected failures in one PR run
prs.body:
Related: #169647

Ready head: `14ab0c9fe4e94f6cd1e0442b1c62f1026089e526` (production change plus test-only CI fixture follow-up). The lead owns final-head CI admission and landing.

## What Problem This Solves

A single PR CI run hid later failures when an earlier check failed, forcing repeated expensive runs before agents could identify all failed tests.

## User Impact

Developers get the complete selected failure inventory from one run, including forks and retries. Failing runs take longer and consume more runner time because independent checks finish. Successful runs keep the same check inventory, job count, names, routing, and concurrency.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep real setup, plan, build, and artifact dependencies. Remove ordering-only failure gates and collect independent command exits before reporting failure. `ci-gate` remains responsible for the selected results; diagnostic failures stay visible and failing.

| Stops | Change |
| --- | --- |
| Mobile protocol coverage in preflight | Move to the existing required `security-fast` job, preserving its manifest scope. |
| Global guards before check planning | Materialize first; run both required guards after setup even when planning or another guard fails. Consumers require plan outputs. |
| Node/project configs, UI and Windows | CI always drains ordinary failures; remove repository/attempt continuation switches and disable fork matrix fail-fast. |
| Static compiler/evidence groups | Collect diagnostics on every CI attempt; changed-path boundary failure still runs types; frozen paired stripes collect too. |
| Docker seed lanes | Set `OPENCLAW_DOCKER_ALL_FAIL_FAST=0`. |
| Hosted checks and SDK consumers | Remove ancestor `!failure()` gates; require actual plan/SDK artifact outputs. Publish prepared SDK despite failed canaries. |
| Candidate updater consumer | Run once its candidate artifact was uploaded, despite unrelated built-check failures. |
| Built artifacts and CLI smokes | Continue independent checks once dist was built/restored; collect both Bun smokes. |
| Static guards, lint/format, prod/test types | Shared shell collector plus runner collection; `check:changed` finishes every selected command. |
| Baseline ratchets and fast-core chains | Collect independent checks while retaining base/setup dependencies. |
| UI/WebKit and real Gateway | Continue after independent lint/test/desktop proof failures, retaining browser/build prerequisites. |
| Docs, Python skills, security, i18n | Independent steps continue after earlier checks; documentation content chains collect all seven checks. |
| macOS, iOS, Android | Native independent steps continue; Swift test profiles collect; Gradle `--continue` and collect trailing lint/benchmark checks. |
| Shared collection | One helper replaces the existing additional-checks collector and is included in trusted harness snapshots. |

Timeouts/watchdogs, explicit cancellation, newer-push cancellation, and contract envelopes' cleanup-safety stop remain deliberate stops.

Skipped: deleted-monitor names in `merge-prior-ci-cancellation.mjs` are still required to validate retained historical cancellation receipts under `docs/reference/scripts/prior-ci.md`; removing them would retire an existing maintainer admission contract, rather than fix current CI execution. Add a historical-only comment instead. No other audited item was skipped.

## Evidence

Focused tests execute the actual workflow shell or runner with synthetic first failures, assert later checks still execute, and assert a nonzero aggregate exit. Baseline probes reproduced the old static runner admitting only 1/4 root partitions, and all seven native continuation regressions fail against the original workflow specifically because later commands were absent.

The requested watcher was invoked once on production head `47e021c940d49c65cf538df30725f156773bed5b`. [CI run 38347327272](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38347327272) completed in **14m15s**: **166 jobs, 139 success, 9 workload failures plus the failing gate, 17 scope skips, zero cancellations**. It exposed stale workflow fixtures and assertions expecting the retired early stops. A test-only follow-up corrects them; production workflow and runner bytes are unchanged from this observed run. Only failed cases were rerun locally. The follow-up head has not been watched; the lead owns its final CI admission.

The first failing shard finished at 04:40:59 UTC. Later successful jobs included lint (04:42:14), docs (04:42:20), test types (04:42:52), production types (04:44:53), Docker (04:45:22), built artifacts (04:45:51), and Android native 4096 (04:50:56). The [first failed shard log](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38347327272/job/115132032205) explicitly reports all four planned groups completed despite one failed invocation:

```text
[shard:core-tooling-15-hosted-3] [test] FAILED (exit 1)
[shard:completion] {"version":1,"planned":4,"completed":4,"invocations":4,"failedInvocations":1}
```

The job list is the cross-job continuation evidence; the completion receipt is the within-shard evidence. No temporary deliberately failing commit was added: natural failures supplied this evidence, while fast synthetic fixtures cover planning and producer boundaries. No CI rerun, second watcher, update-branch, or merge was performed.

| Focused proof | Result / wall time |
| --- | --- |
| Shared collector | 7 passed, 9.85s; ordinary failures drain, timeout/signal exits stop. |
| Linux/UI workflow shell | 20 passed, 12.54s (0.167s assertions). |
| Native workflow shell | 27 passed, 13.15s (1.578s assertions); old workflow fails all 7 execution regressions. |
| Package command chains | 4 passed, 10.43s; exact unchanged check inventory after first failure. |
| PR failure-control workflow | 8 passed, 13.90s. |
| Plan and gate contracts | 33 passed in the 48.41s targeted invocation; 2 updated fixture assertions passed on focused recheck, 12.97s. |
| Existing native Swift integration | 1 passed, 42.78s; three profile invocations retain failure; build failure still admits none. |
| Startup-memory workflow ordering | 1 passed, 13.95s. |
| Node runner | 63 passed, 95.237s test time (existing native process fixtures dominate). |
| Project admission | 170 passed, 135.68s Vitest duration; final focused 16 passed, 20.38s wall. |
| Static compiler continuation | 5 passed, 20.654s test time; original root plan stopped at 1/4. |
| Static helper / lint / changed checks / cancellation | 95 passed, 289.04s combined wall; existing CLI fixtures dominate. |
| Cache warmer | 2 passed, 10.61s. |
| Trusted harness materialization | 13 passed, 94.61s; architecture environment 4 passed, 15.19s. |

These invocations use `pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=1`; existing large workflow files were narrowed with `-t` to the touched contracts. The unfiltered planning/guards invocation was stopped after unrelated slow manifest fixtures; full inventory belongs to PR CI. No new real timers or polling were added to the regression fixtures. The completed CI run took 855 wall-clock seconds; individual job times are available in the linked run. Failing runs cost more because selected checks drain; successful inventory and concurrency remain unchanged.

`pnpm check:workflows` passed with the repository-pinned actionlint fallback, zizmor, trusted checkout generator verification, and composite-input guard. Formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Scoped root-test tsgo passed. Scoped script tsgo's unchanged performance-config diagnostics are recorded below after the isolated baseline check.

Final scoped oxlint passed for every changed script and root test, using `config/tsconfig/oxlint.scripts.json` and `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.json`. An earlier attempt used the general script compiler config and unnecessarily invoked SDK declaration preparation, which timed out at its existing 300-second watchdog; the supported source-backed lint config completed normally. No watchdog or artifact lock was bypassed.

Scoped script tsgo reports only two existing diagnostics in unchanged `test/vitest/vitest.performance-config.ts`: Vite's plugin type does not declare `configureVitest`, and its callback destructuring has an implicit-any binding. A second minimal tsgo program containing only that unchanged source reproduces the identical diagnostics. Scoped root-test tsgo is clean; no changed-file type diagnostics remain.

Autoreview completed the initial isolated Codex assessment through P2 and the single permitted re-review after the test-only corrections. Neither found an actionable defect in this branch's CI changes. The first report had three P2 findings; the final report had nine P2 findings in five evidence batches. All concern unchanged upstream Meta/A2A, Slack, media, Doctor, desktop, plugin, or UI files added on `origin/main` after this branch was cut. The mandated `--base origin/main` comparison presents those later upstream changes in reverse. Every final finding path has an empty staged diff from the original branch-cut commit (`88e5ae840faa5fcb5ac80ca089f04bcd4f62b5fe`), and the first report's paths have an empty task diff. All are declined outside task scope. Both assessments returned an overall incorrect verdict because of those comparison artifacts; this is not a scoped-clean review result. No actionable CI finding remains; no third assessment was run.

A source comparison confirms all 41 CI job IDs and names are unchanged; every CI matrix now explicitly has `fail-fast: false`.


Post-CI fixture correction proof uses the same `pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=1` entry point, filtered to CI-failed cases. iOS/log fixtures: 11 passed, 41.45s wall; native launch: 3 passed, 26.66s wall; runner/report ownership: 7 passed, 149.85s wall; security/published-driver: 14 passed, 31.77s wall; hourly/WebKit: 2 passed, 4.00s Vitest phase; workflow guards: 13 passed in the initial 69.55s test-wrapper invocation and its remaining hosted-lint case passed in 14.24s wall. Four Git-owner cases remain Linux-only and were skipped on this Mac (10.85s wall); their platform guard is preserved and next-head CI must supply that proof.

Follow-up TypeScript lint and formatting pass. The modified plain-Node shell fixture reports 29 lint diagnostics; an identical-source baseline at the same module location reproduces the same 29 rule/message pairs. None belongs to the five added collector-materialization lines. The expanded scoped root-test type program imports unchanged `vitest.tooling.config.ts`, whose identical 20 declaration inference diagnostics are reproduced by a minimal program containing only that unchanged config; no changed-file type diagnostic remains.

Planning fixture follow-up: all 135 selected failure/group cases passed across two failed-case-only invocations (68 already passing cases in 373.21s wall, then remaining 67 passed in 249.67s wall; 533 unrelated cases skipped on final pass). Conditions retain producer prerequisites; failure fixtures now assert every admitted guard, type stripe, and trailing Gradle check runs. Four display-name/group collisions account for the difference from 131 failed planning cases in the CI manifest.

prs.title: feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage
prs.body:
feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can emit skill-usage diagnostics while an agent reads or invokes a skill, but that observed runtime signal is not available through the durable audit surface. Operators therefore cannot inspect which skills were actually used during a run from the audit CLI/API.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first revision inferred skill selection from prompt text after attempt completion. Review correctly called that out as the wrong boundary: prompt inference is not proof of skill use and it also risked perturbing the embedded attempt-result contract.

This revision records only observed runtime skill usage from the existing `before_tool_call` skill-usage boundary:

- Skill read/command activation is detected where `recordRunSkillUsage()` already emits runtime diagnostics.
- A metadata-only `skill_selection` audit event is emitted with `selectionSource: "observed_runtime"` and `selectionConfidence: "observed"`.
- No prompt text, tool arguments, tool output, or skill file contents are persisted.
- `skill_selection` is persisted outside run-start deduplication so it is not dropped after `agent.run.started`.
- Legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only; the versioned `audit.activity.list` surface exposes skill-selection records.
- `completeEmbeddedAttemptResult()` is restored to the production calling contract, preserving the existing truncated-stream/tool recovery behavior.

## User Impact

- `openclaw audit --kind skill_selection` can show observed skill usage for a run through the activity-list API.
- Existing `audit.list` clients keep their shipped run/tool event shape and do not receive the new record kind.
- Operators get a durable metadata trail for actual skill usage without sensitive prompt or file-content capture.

## Evidence

Current-head validation after merging `upstream/main` and removing the unrelated `USER.md` bootstrap policy change:

```bash
pnpm tsgo:core
pnpm protocol:check:swift
pnpm db:kysely:check
pnpm lint:kysely
pnpm check:architecture
pnpm test src/agents/workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts src/audit/audit-events.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.test.ts
```

Results:

- `pnpm tsgo:core` passed.
- `pnpm protocol:check:swift` passed after regenerating `GatewayModels.swift`.
- `pnpm db:kysely:check` passed after regenerating `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts`.
- `pnpm lint:kysely` passed after moving ordinary companion-table insert/read/prune queries to the sync Kysely owner.
- `pnpm check:architecture` passed, including generated Kysely verification, Kysely guardrails, and database-first legacy-store guard.
- Targeted Vitest run passed 4 shards in 22.13s.
- `audit-events.test.ts`: 54 tests passed, including companion-table storage, bounded retention, and observed runtime projection.
- `server-methods/audit.test.ts`: 34 tests passed, including explicit `skill_selection`/`observed` activity access and V1-compatible unfiltered activity.
- `audit.test.ts`: 7 protocol schema tests passed, including activity schema discrimination.
- `workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts`: 9 tests passed; shared sessions now drop only root `MEMORY.md`, leaving `USER.md` behavior unchanged.
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` passed. A full local `pnpm lint:core` was started but manually stopped after 6+ minutes with no diagnostic output; CI remains the authoritative full core-lint signal.

Published-release upgrade, older-reader, and candidate-reopen proof:

- the published `v2026.9.4` tag at `3a9d69db3` created a fresh state database and wrote legacy `agent_run` sequence `1`.
- candidate head `7d74807a5` opened that exact database, preserved the legacy row, created the additive `audit_skill_selection_events` table, and wrote observed `debug-toolkit` sequence `2`.
- `v2026.9.4` then reopened the candidate-used database without migration or schema errors, ignored the additive table, and wrote a second legacy `agent_run` at shared sequence `3`.
- the candidate reopened the same database and returned sequences `[3, 2, 1]`, including both legacy rows and the retained skill-selection row.
- physical SQLite readback reported `integrity_check: ok`, `user_version: 17`, `audit_events: 2`, and `audit_skill_selection_events: 1`.
- this proves published release → candidate upgrade → published older-reader open/use → candidate reopen while preserving the legacy table, additive companion, and shared sequence allocation.

## Changed Files

- `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.ts` — observed-only metadata marker.
- `src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.wrapper.ts` — emits `skill_selection` from the existing observed skill-usage boundary.
- `src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts` — projects observed-only skill-selection records and routes them outside run-start deduplication.
- `src/audit/audit-event-store.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-types.ts` — durable store/types for observed skill-selection metadata, with ordinary companion-table access through Kysely.
- `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` — generated Kysely declarations for the companion table.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.ts` — exposes skill-selection through `audit.activity.list` while preserving legacy `audit.list`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit-activity.ts` — versioned activity schema includes `skill_selection`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.ts` — legacy audit schema stays run/tool-only.
- `src/commands/audit.ts` — CLI uses the activity surface and renders selected skill metadata.
- `docs/gateway/audit.md` / `docs/gateway/config-observability.md` / `docs/cli/audit.md` — document the approved metadata fields, default-on collection, 30-day retention, separate 100,000-row cap, compatibility behavior, and explicit CLI filters.

## Test Plan

1. Verify observed skill reads/commands emit `skill_selection` audit events.
2. Verify `skill_selection` persists between run start and terminal events.
3. Verify `audit.activity.list` and CLI expose skill-selection records.
4. Verify legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only.
5. Verify attempt-result recovery tests still pass.
6. Verify existing SQLite state opens, creates the companion table, preserves old activity rows, and reopens with skill-selection rows intact.


## Review findings addressed (2026-10-10)

All five ClawSweeper code findings are fixed on this head:

- **Distinguishable skill identities** — the lossy hyphen sanitizer is replaced by an injective dash-escape encoding (`-` doubles to `--`, other unsafe bytes become `-hh-` hex), so `Daily Brief` persists as `Daily-20-Brief`, distinct from `Daily-Brief` → `Daily--Brief` (and `_helper` stays distinct from `helper`). The audit projector accepts the encoding. Boundary coverage in `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.test.ts`.
- **Admission-owned schema setup** — the canonical schema admission owns `audit_skill_selection_events` (`src/state/openclaw-state-schema.sql`); additive DDL now runs at most once per connection and only for pre-admission databases, instead of on every insert and prune tick.
- **Bounded write overhead** — per-connection row-count cache mirrors the canonical ledger pattern: one `COUNT(*)` per connection lifetime, advanced by inserts and maintenance deletes, invalidated on rollback.
- **Restart guidance** — `docs/gateway/audit.md` now states the recorder re-reads `logging.audit.enabled` on every event, so disabling stops new rows immediately.
- **Protocol type ownership** — `AuditActivitySkillSelectionV1` is derived from the canonical schema properties via `SchemaContract` (same pattern as adjacent variants), restoring wire-required attribution to typed consumers.

## Production-path proof

Throwaway script (not committed) driving production code on a temp state DB — marker encoder → recorder projector → production SQLite writer → `audit.activity.list` Gateway handler:

```
encoded identities: Daily-20-Brief vs Daily--Brief
projected inputs: 1 kind: skill_selection
writer stored: skill_selection Daily-20-Brief
gateway response: {"events":[{"schemaVersion":1,"sequence":1,"eventId":"<uuid>","sourceSequence":1,"occurredAt":<ts>,"redaction":"metadata_only","kind":"skill_selection","agentId":"main","sessionKey":"agent:main:<session>","sessionId":"session-<id>","runId":"run-proof-1","action":"skill.selection.observed","status":"observed","eventType":"skill_selection","actor":{"type":"agent","id":"main"},"selectedSkill":"Daily-20-Brief"}]}
worker rows: 1 first toolName: Daily-20-Brief
PROOF OK: gateway output matches the observed skill invocation
```

Tool-invocation → emission coverage lives in `src/agents/agent-tools.skill-selection-audit.e2e.test.ts`; recorder → DB → filtered readback in `src/audit/audit-events.skill-selection-hidden.test.ts`; handler shaping in `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts`.


## Round 2 (rev.199 follow-up)

Three further findings from review rev.199 are fixed on this head:

- **Token-built identities** — the encoder appends complete encoding tokens only while they fit the 128-char bound (reserving the `x-` flag prefix up front), so truncation can never cut inside an escape and valid suffixes survive (`skill-a` vs `skill-b` regression covered).
- **Single-owner expiry accounting** — the deleter returns the removed count without touching the warm cache; insert-prune and maintenance ticks each adjust exactly once, with a warm-cache expiry-to-overflow regression test (exact cap trim to 99,976 rows).
- **Tool-boundary assertion** — the wrapper e2e expects the encoded `demo--skill` identity while the run-usage receipt keeps the original `demo-skill` name.

prs.title: fix(status): prepare runtime config before resolving online usage
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`status --usage --json` can lose the selected Codex account identity and retain a generic OpenAI “Token expired” result. Passive online status reads the full config for usage arguments, but never prepares it for plugin runtime readers. Codex registration then reaches `runtime.config.current()` with no published snapshot.

The source-supported culprit is 7e48efba10479f90496438e3edf3e0d0121e34c7 (#169714), which changed cold runtime reads to require prior asynchronous preparation. This repair reuses the status owner's existing config read and awaits `setAppliedRuntimeConfigSnapshot(runtimeConfig, sourceConfig)` before resolving usage. It preserves the explicit `--usage` gate and source config; there is no second read, synchronous fallback, or plugin-loader change.

The new regression invokes the real online-usage callback from an empty runtime snapshot and checks that policy and source config are visible when usage resolution starts. It catches both missing publication and a missing `await`. The adjacent usage-routing fixtures never set `scan.collection`, so they do not enter this callback and need no changes.

## Evidence

Failure evidence: [CI run 38346907753, job 115130732432](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38346907753/job/115130732432) failed `codex-auth-product-proof.e2e.test.ts` / “repairs mixed legacy auth into SQLite and sends the selected OAuth profile to app-server”. The same missing-email assertion was reproduced on baseline 592b7e4aea9386e05912e6df2d3ba5493e629aaa after Doctor and the selected-account Gateway turn succeeded. That diagnostic run substituted the verified version constant `0.160.0` for the broad test-API version lookup, raised the fixture test limit from 180 to 900 seconds, and raised Doctor/status managed-command fixture limits from 120 to 600 seconds. All assertions and product source stayed unchanged; the product status timeout stayed `60000`. Fixtures were restored afterward. The test took 196.211 seconds, 286.33 seconds total; those loaded-host timings are not performance claims.

Proof: changed-file oxfmt and oxlint plus `git diff --check` passed. One completed isolated Codex autoreview returned `scoped-clean` at P0–P2; the earlier interrupted attempt never produced a result. No local tests or broad scans were run under the compute-conservation rule. Candidate unit-test timing and the original **unchanged** hosted product case remain pending; this PR does not yet claim the original E2E failure is fixed.

Scope: two files, production +3/−1 lines and tests +61 lines. No schema, SDK, update, or plugin-loading lifecycle changes; no removed authority checks. No warmed-path SQL/request or T1 change is claimed, so no SQL harness was run.

prs.title: refactor(ui): retire Panels and Layout submenus from the session menu
prs.body:
Related: #168845 (ClawSweeper P3 follow-up)

## What Problem This Solves

After #168845 moved every chat layout and panel action into the header **Layout** menu, the session **…** menu still carried its retired **Panels** and **Layout** submenu paths, compact drill-in views, props, and the `chat.sessionHeader.panels` string. Nothing fed them anymore, so the code was dead but still looked like a second owner for layout actions. The Solid port of the menu (#169442) carried the dead paths along, so this now applies to `chat-header-session-menu.tsx`.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. The **Panels** and **Layout** entries were already absent from the session menu because the header stopped supplying actions in #168845; the header **Layout** menu remains the only place for focus, split, swap, side-panel placement, terminal/browser/desktop, session files/changes/side chat, Subagents, Processes, and Review. Keyboard shortcuts and the panel **+** menu are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

One owner per responsibility. The session menu now renders only its plain session actions (plugin actions, stop cloud worker) plus its own **View** submenu. The shared quick-action type in `chat-quick-action.tsx` is split: the session menu takes a plain `HeaderMenuSessionAction`, while the status/checkable `HeaderMenuQuickAction` union stays with the header Layout menu that renders it. The changed-file `badge` field goes with it: the shared renderer only showed it on the non-Layout path, the controller only set it on a Layout-menu action, and the session menu never received one, so it was unreachable end to end. Its `modifiedFiles` memo key in the pane header controller is removed too, which also stops the Layout menu re-rendering on file-list churn. Two docs sentences that still pointed readers at **Panels** in the **…** menu now point at the Layout menu.

Verified that no other route (command palette, mobile compact menu, keyboard shortcuts, e2e helpers) selected `quick:panels:*`, `quick:layout:*`, `compact:open-panels`, or `compact:open-layout`; the only remaining references were in the session menu's own test, which now exercises the surviving session-actions group in both compact modes instead.

Generated locale artifacts under `ui/src/i18n/.i18n` are intentionally not touched: `pnpm ui:i18n:sync` currently asks to commit only `locales/en.ts` and let the locale-refresh workflow translate after merge, because main already has untranslated new keys.

## Evidence

Behavior-only cleanup with no rendered difference, so no before/after screenshots.

On the branch merged with current main:

- `pnpm test` for `chat-header-session-menu.test.ts`, `chat-pane-header.test.ts`, `chat-pane-terminal.test.ts`, `chat-pane-session-menu.test.ts`, `dashboard-presentation-defaults.test.ts`: 5 files, 156 tests passed (~25 s).
- `pnpm --dir ui test src/pages/chat/components/chat-pane-header.browser.test.tsx`: 7 passed.
- `pnpm test:ui:e2e` for `chat-panel-layout`, `chat-header-subagents`, `mobile-chat-session-menu`: 3 files, 6 passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui` clean; oxlint over `ui/src/pages/chat` reports nothing in touched files; oxfmt and stylelint clean; `pnpm format:docs:check` clean.
- `pnpm check:control-ui-lit-ratchet` OK; `pnpm ui:i18n:baseline` produced no drift; `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` clean.
- Codex autoreview (branch mode against main, up to P2): scoped-clean, no findings.

Follow-up, not in this PR: the changed-file count badge that the old Panels submenu showed on **Show session files** has had no reachable renderer since #168845. If it is wanted back, the Layout menu's action renderer is where it belongs.

prs.title: refactor(sessions): retain membership authority at effects
prs.body:
Builds on merged #170536. The Phase E hold is lifted; this slice preserves the native incognito owner as an explicit redesign residual.

## What Problem This Solves

Session membership authorization still falls back to synchronous SQLite at final effect boundaries, and prepared sharing reads repeat physical-identity and retained-fact checks. This change makes retained membership authority belong to the existing session-entry publication owner and removes the native membership lookup from the migrated authorization paths.

## User Impact

Membership revoked while a tool waits in its before-tool hook prevents that tool from executing. Ordinary prepared authorization avoids final native membership queries. Unknown durable authority outcomes fail closed until Gateway restart. There is no schema, retention, or public SDK change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cold preparation uses the existing worker-backed sharing reader. Warm prepared guards read owner-held facts synchronously, with no SQLite statement, worker request, or filesystem identity recapture. Each domain keeps its existing visibility, owner, membership, and capability predicates.

The publication contract is:

- Deny retained sharing reads before an admitted authority-changing write commits.
- Install the committed entry/membership postimage before releasing that denial, and before notifying observers.
- Keep an unknown authority outcome denied until owner restart. Neither a fresh snapshot nor a later successful membership write clears it.
- Do not permanently poison sharing authority for unknown category, participant, or involvement bookkeeping writes that cannot change authorization.

The existing publication machinery remains the owner; this adds no schema, generation, fencing protocol, or competing cache. The existing writer-entry guard now covers `session_members`, worker add/remove operations, and the established entry-cleanup and repair writers.

The migrated callers use prepared member facts for worker grants, task-suggestion source authorization, suggestion access, actor-backed skill-library selection, and HTTP/WebSocket tool invocation. Tool invocation retains facts across the before-tool hook and checks them immediately before executing the tool, so a membership revocation during the hook denies execution. The synchronous `isSessionMember`/`hasSessionMemberInDatabase` path and synchronous `authorizeResolvedSessionMutation` entry point are removed; bundled callers use prepared facts or the existing async replacement. No public SDK export changes are included.

## Removed checks and accepted edges

- Remove final filesystem identity recapture from prepared sharing guards: unsupported external replacement of a live Gateway-owned database is outside the single-owner runtime contract; supported close/replacement still revokes retained readers.
- Remove the duplicate loop revalidating every retained sharing read before consuming the selected read: the selected source consumes its current owner-held facts once; an unrelated prepared candidate does not independently decide that source's authority.
- Remove duplicate discovery revalidation after source selection: a same-key row later created in another store does not revoke authority over the already-bound physical source; new discovery still rejects duplicate canonical rows.
- Remove the native grant branch's repeated exact-entry/member reads: retained committed facts decide the effect; cold acquisition still checks the selected worker/database identity.

## Integration boundary and remaining work

The current diff deletes `hasSessionMemberInDatabase`, but native callers of `listSessionMembersInDatabase` and `readSessionMembers` remain. Current incognito creation still writes process-held SQLite rows; the actor cannot reopen that database, and actor acquisition rejects an already native-owned namespace. Moving membership alone would lose or split those rows. The native collaboration path therefore remains an explicit owner-redesign residual until the incognito owner cutover. This is a live bundled runtime boundary, not a shipped SDK signature. Member add/remove keep their existing transaction publication: `publishSessionSharingMemberChange` stages denial, installs committed facts before releasing it, and invalidates unknown state. The custody guard enumerates only the two audited native forwarding edges in addition to the worker entry; it does not exempt a file, table, or T1 classification. Current native member/owner/suggestion/participant routes and their final authorization checks remain. The durable prepared-authority cutover is independent of Phase E.

The pending-input authority kernel retains a synchronous completion route after that integration: `UserTurnTranscriptRecorder.completeProcessing` → receipt `complete` → `nativeMutation` → `mutatePendingInput` → `readSessionPendingInputAuthorityFactsInTransaction` → `listSessionMembersInDatabase`. The `complete` mutation carries `authorityAgentId` when staged with authority, so the membership branch is reachable. The synchronous completion contract exists in v2026.10.2 and is deprecated in favor of `completeProcessingAsync`; ordinary bundled processing prefers the async method. This owner contract is preserved and is an explicit residual main-thread path. It has not been mechanically admitted as a T1 compatibility exception, so neither the membership kernel nor the authority kernel is claimed worker-only. Separately, GitHub publication's use of the same membership reader remains in the shared-state worker, including its cross-store source reservation checks. A live bundled cross-store voice path also remains: talk.client.create → createOrResumeClientVoiceSession → prepareClientVoiceSessionSourceChecks → readSessionSourceValidation → listSessionMembersInDatabase. It checks the source store while the voice metadata writer owns a different database. Its complete source predicates need owner-published authority before that final native check can be removed. The membership kernel therefore remains conservatively T1; it is neither worker-only nor exclusively deprecated SDK compatibility.

Normal Gateway event delivery supplies the initialized session-row projection. Membership-dependent internal policy callers must supply prepared facts. The existing native target fallback is outside this change; without prepared membership, a nonowner membership-dependent event check fails closed. The update canary is documented as a startup-only rehearsal and does not initialize that projection. Its fallback must not be represented as proof of ordinary member-event delivery.

Conversation final authority remains unchanged: it depends on conversation, association, window, and entry state whose complete postimages are not yet published by one owner. Goal mutation also retains its native fallback for opaque commit hooks and cross-store source authority; moving those hooks outside the owning transaction would lose real rollback behavior. These are owner-design boundaries, not line-budget deferrals.

Goal receipt capacity checking and insertion now use one conditional INSERT instead of a separate COUNT and INSERT. The expiry DELETE remains, reducing receipt persistence from three statements to two with unchanged requests, retention, fingerprint checks, and capacity. A full store still rejects the operation and rolls back its Goal, lifecycle, and transcript writes. The regression fills the last available slot, rejects the next edit, and checks unchanged retained data. The warmed-turn harness does not issue Goal operations, so this saving is reported per operation only.

CI also exposed a lost preparation wakeup in startup recovery. The recovery owner removed a pending target while awaiting its next read, so a preparation commit in that interval could leave the interrupted session stranded. Keep the target registered until the attempt is no longer preparation-blocked, and coalesce queued notifications so completed attempts consume their own write notifications without extra reads. Two deterministic regressions cover the startup and notification-triggered reads; both time out on the predecessor. This repair changes no ordinary warmed-turn operation.

## Measurements

One alternating base/candidate pair with the unchanged shared **sqlharness 2.1.0**, Node **26.11.1**, and SQLite **3.53.4**. Base: `3b75ce70f3970b616c79ea6822342159b1aa441e`; combined qualification/membership candidate: `58d5abbe40f0399a52eef9e8b6ffc076efc5a984`. The two runs used identical harness hashes. Later test fixes, main integrations, the Goal receipt consolidation, and the recovery wakeup repair are not separately measured revisions. The final integration resolved only writer-guard source changes, without changing measured SQL operations. The workload does not exercise Goal operations or pending startup recovery.

Both runs completed all 13 foreground turns, the native child, control RPCs, cron, compaction, and clean shutdown. All ten warmed turns had causal SQL/request coverage; native SQL failures were zero. Both native calibrations passed. Figures below count successful native statements across every thread/process and logical worker requests; moving a statement to a worker does not remove it from these totals.

| Metric | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Warm turn-caused SQL/turn, mean | 172.9 | 170.8 |
| Warm turn-caused SQL/turn, median [min–max] | 171 [170–194] | 170 [170–178] |
| Warm turn-caused requests/turn, mean | 42.0 | 41.3 |
| Warm turn-caused requests/turn, median [min–max] | 41.5 [41–47] | 41 [41–44] |
| Warm turn-caused MAIN SQL/turn | 0 | 0 |
| First-turn causal SQL / requests / MAIN | 372 / 77 / 33 | 375 / 81 / 31 |
| Legacy warmed-window SQL / requests per turn | 231.7 / 67.0 | 212.8 / 55.0 |
| Background SQL/min during warm windows | 531.90 | 658.70 |
| Entire workload SQL / requests / MAIN | 7,111 / 1,435 / 826 | 6,744 / 1,242 / 824 |

The medians/ranges describe the ten warmed turns in each run, not a three-run distribution. These were loaded-host count measurements, **not latency evidence**: baseline/candidate pre-run one-minute loads were 108.99/103.90 on 32 CPUs, with 0% observed idle. Warm windows lasted 66.328/38.257 seconds. Background rates and legacy-window totals remain timing-sensitive. The observed 2.1 SQL and 0.7 request reductions per warm turn are shared-owner/cache variation; this lane does not claim them as a deterministic optimization.

## Owner attribution

| Family | Entire-workload SELECTs, base → candidate | Warm SELECTs/turn, base → candidate | Warm requests/turn, base → candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Exact-entry facts | 90 → 83 | 4.2 → 4.0 | 4.2 → 4.0 |
| Actor hydration | 24 → 23 | 1.2 → 1.1 | 1.2 → 1.1 |
| Entry-cache snapshot loads | 46 → 35 | 0 → 0 | 0 → 0 |
| Row facts | 3 → 2 | 0 → 0 | 0 → 0 |
| Watermarks | 61 → 54 | 1.0 → 1.0 | 1.0 → 1.0 |

Families are matched by native owner stack, and can overlap. Request figures correlate each native statement's request ID with the recorded logical request; they are not inferred by dividing SQL counts.

The removed qualification/absence path executes **2 → 0 MAIN statements** over this workload: one cold quarantine `user_version` read and one cold quarantine-row SELECT, with **0 → 0 worker requests**. Earlier SELECT-only attribution reported one; two is the correct all-statement count. Membership remains **3 → 3 cold worker SELECTs in 3 → 3 requests**, with **0 → 0 warm SQL and requests**. The shared workload does not exercise a repeated non-owner membership authorization, so the final guard's zero-request property is established by its boundary tests rather than a claimed harness saving.

## First-turn difference

The first causal turn rises by three statements and four requests, while MAIN falls by two and entire-workload SQL/requests fall by 367/193. The complete first-turn SQL delta is:

| Existing producer/path | SQL delta | Request delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Auth-profile readonly load | +1 | +1 |
| Ordered exact-entry read | +1 | +1 |
| Sandbox exact-entry read | +1 | +1 |
| Agent-ingress deletion-status cold load | +1 | +1 |
| Active-projection watermark read within existing request | +1 | 0 |
| Removed qualification quarantine-row read | −1 MAIN | 0 |
| Removed qualification quarantine `user_version` read | −1 MAIN | 0 |
| **Total** | **+3** | **+4** |

These are existing cold/read-cache producers; no added warm operation appears in the touched owner stacks. Across the complete workload the auth readonly request stack drops 25 → 23, ordered exact-entry requests drop 41 → 40, exact-entry fact SQL drops 90 → 83, and watermark SQL drops 61 → 54. The result is a cold-work redistribution plus the removed native qualification admission; the lane makes no latency or deterministic warm-savings claim.

## Evidence

Changed-file formatting, oxlint, and `git diff --check` passed. Landed qualification/main `869ceef2c25f9c966bfb574b6f5206d1fc685039` is integrated. The sole conflict was the existing writer-custody guard: its membership and newly landed credential entries are combined, including both raw-SQL table matchers, without broadening either exception. Integrated head `6c98ae388edc90db2843597367aec8cbaf7f332b` is awaiting CI; PR CI owns types, lint, Madge, focused tests, and T1/dialect ratchets under the current compute-conservation rule. Ordinary PR CI omits the separate Knip task. The earlier full scan found an unused helper introduced by this PR (removed) and an inherited unused Board export. The Board owner fixed the latter in #170609 (`c6ee92366b568ed72868c92c7910e2d0f9395c14`), already included in the integrated main. No final integrated Knip scan is claimed under the current compute-conservation rule.

Two Codex review rounds completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings in their supplied scopes. Subsequent corrections address CI caller/type fixtures, the recovery defect, and the audited incognito custody entries; no third review round was requested. Existing review follow-up: unknown authority outcomes remain fail-closed, but their generic unavailable error should explicitly tell the operator to restart.

Head `f6f7807c7aad5ae8eca48f30660c5c98102dd420` [CI 38350746332](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38350746332) completed with 81 successful, 24 skipped, and two failed jobs (one concrete shard plus its aggregate). Its only failure was two thinking-catalog cache cases in `session-utils.metadata-perf.test.ts`. Main fixed that exact cache-key defect in #170659 (`7b871cd72f219`), whose [CI 38349551198](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38349551198) passed. This integration includes that repair; no inherited-failure exception or speculative local replay is claimed.

Previous-head [CI 38347388048](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38347388048) finished with 79 successful and 24 skipped jobs, including all production/test types, lint partitions, and architecture checks. Its two substantive failures were the native incognito custody entries (corrected here) and `sessions.patch waits for orphaned provisioning cleanup (failure=false)`. The latter returned `ok:false`; the old matcher hid its payload. One focused replay passed (30.215 seconds for the case, 130.69 seconds for Vitest). Main now contains the same improved assertion independently, so no archive-test change remains in this diff. Its intermittent cause remains unproven, and it is not labeled inherited. An earlier initial-turn execution-admission failure also passed on this CI head (6.264 seconds); temporary diagnostics are removed and no unproven repair is claimed.

The recovery repair has two deterministic failing-before regressions; all 21 cases passed in the previous-head CI (job 115132194902). The earlier focused recovery run took 285.17 seconds in Vitest (519.62 seconds including worker setup/cleanup) on the loaded host. No broad local rerun followed the compute-conservation notice. Goal capacity/rollback and the mutation-worker regression passed in [CI 38345014298](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38345014298). No SDK surface or update/Doctor/migration/plugin-loading/service-lifecycle change is included.
Boundary tests cover deny-before-commit, committed facts visible at the first observer notification, valid lost-reply settlement, unknown outcomes remaining denied after a later known write or host-handle close/reopen, cold-read parity, and no host SQL/filesystem probes during warm prepared checks. Removed external same-inode replacement, cold-registry-restore replacement, and native-consent replacement cases pinned the discarded runtime probing contract: they rename or overwrite a live database without first retiring its owner. Supported owner close/replacement and in-process revocation remain covered. Final integrated CI results will be recorded before landing.

Runtime production diff relative to integrated main `869ceef2c25f9c966bfb574b6f5206d1fc685039`: **+405 / −428 (net −23)**. Existing writer guard: **+69 / −4**. Tests: **+775 / −677**. Documentation: **+16 / −2**.

The lane's twelve named T1 sites become **9** (membership **3 → 2**, goals/receipts **5 → 4**, reads/targets **4 → 3**). Counting all primitive calls in the six mission files gives **15 → 12**. This is a bounded source count after main integration; it does not infer a whole-repository total or classify remaining kernels as worker-only. Current-head CI supplies the canonical ratchet result.
