prs.title: perf(codex): use owner-held credentials at the fetch boundary
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Codex token-sharing OAuth still rereads SQLite on the Gateway main thread immediately before bearer-authenticated fetch. This change makes that final assertion read the credential authority's committed in-memory facts. Cold preparation uses the existing async worker reader; the synchronous effect guard keeps its identity and refresh validation without issuing SQL or worker requests.

This is the final reader cutover, stacked on #170632 after #170583. The three PRs land in that order. Their publication changes are prerequisites: every supported credential writer must deny before mutation and publish settlement before this reader can replace the final database read.

### Ownership and writer coverage

The existing personal credential authority also owns shared `config_machine_state['authProfiles.store']` and agent `auth_profile_store['primary']` facts. This PR carries its retained per-source getter through the internal auth read owner and the existing nonenumerable `readCurrentCredential` result field. There is no parallel credential owner and no function added to the serializable `AuthProfileStore`.

The getter follows local agent → explicitly scoped shared → ambient shared precedence. It retains absent-local dependencies so a later local insertion takes precedence, observes deletion and shared fallback, and survives temporary worker read-scope disposal. Closing the underlying authority revokes the getter. Catalog workers return committed facts rather than a host effect capability.

The extended writer-entry ratchet covers the publication graph established by the earlier PRs:

| Writer family | Covered route |
| --- | --- |
| Login/import/setup/provider persistence, logout, OAuth claim/replace/fail/restore and peer removal | Native save/update facades and async `authProfiles.update` construction reach the canonical credential publication sinks. |
| External CLI sync, secrets apply/rollback and exact snapshot restoration | Native ensure/load readers and save/restore writers remain in the graph because reads can persist external credentials. |
| Doctor/import/relocation | Runtime writes use the same sinks; stopped-owner maintenance retains its explicit custody exception. |
| Catalog worker writes | Host batch denial, catalog custody entry and committed receipt capture remain paired. |
| Released synchronous SDK save/upsert and native `AuthStorage` | Reviewed exports and native facades enter managed transaction custody and synchronous publication before SQL. |
| Generic machine-state writes accepting the credential key | Normalized protected/dynamic keys and `machineState.write` construction require the host publication adapter; TUI/onboarding workers construct their bounded noncredential namespaces. |

The ratchet resolves named, namespace, computed and destructured references, selected dynamic imports (including `Promise.all` and `.then`), nested writer calls, facade forwarding and worker command construction. Unused sibling exports do not count as writer access; namespace escapes and actual protected selections remain guarded. Synthetic bypass fixtures must reject new routes around publication. It audits the current source graph and compatibility exports; it is not a general security type system for arbitrary reflection or dynamically constructed worker programs.

PR1's public P2 ratchet follow-ups remain future syntax extensions: raw `REPLACE`/`UPDATE OR`, Kysely `replaceInto`, and `onConflict` key reassignment. No existing production credential bypass using these forms was found. These limitations are recorded rather than expanding this cutover into another general SQL analyzer.

### Preserved security semantics

Credential mutations deny synchronously before commit. Committed facts install before the denial is released; unknown outcomes remain denied until the owner restarts. Usage, order and cooldown-only changes remain outside credential revocation. Released synchronous SDK signatures remain unchanged.

The final assertion still validates issuer, client ID, subject and auth-flow fingerprint for the selected profile. Profile fallback remains disabled and the resolved profile ID must match. While the durable OAuth refresh claim temporarily removes the ID token, only the exact previously validated refresh generation with matching flow, issuer and client ID may join. A persisted credential without a retained authority getter is refused. Runtime-only credentials continue to use mutable in-memory state and observe removal.

Removed path and accepted edge cases:

- The synchronous native final SQL fallback is deleted. Unsupported external concurrent database writes do not invalidate in-process facts; outside writers must use the Gateway or hold exclusive ownership while it is stopped.
- The personal/native final-reader split is deleted. Missing authority for a persisted profile refuses the request instead of falling back to SQL or a captured snapshot.
- An HTTP request whose effect already started may finish. No new bearer-authenticated effect starts while credential publication is pending or its outcome is unknown.

The security check itself remains immediately before native fetch after awaited preparation. No admitted-write relaxation, polling read, new generation or additional handshake is introduced.

### Measurements

Candidate native boundary confirmation passed at `3411b0795f8d2`: [extension worker job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38350867854/job/115143027137), shared 766ms and agent 776ms. The baseline half of the single permitted workload pair is complete at `cbb3812a9ee0c54bd833ebfdc4423f66d424d022`; the candidate half is pending. All ten warmed turns completed. A later child-spawn phase hit the harness’s `tool_call` versus `dispatch_action` mismatch, so workload completion/totals are incomplete and will not be presented as a successful full-workload run. No baseline rerun or extra pair is being run. The focused baseline probe at `592b7e4aea9386e05912e6df2d3ba5493e629aaa` measured three warmed assertions per scope: each shared and agent guard executed two successful MAIN SELECTs and zero worker requests. This is measured execution cost, separate from the static count of reachable source sites.

| Metric | Base | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Native read sites reachable from the Codex final guard | 2 | 0; native boundary CI passed |
| SQL statements per warmed final assertion | Shared and agent: 2 [2–2], three samples each | Shared and agent: 0 [0–0], three assertions each in native boundary CI |
| Worker requests per warmed final assertion | Shared and agent: 0 [0–0], three samples each | Shared and agent: 0 [0–0], Worker and MessagePort spies |
| Static lane T1 sites | 2 | Expected 2 while the released synchronous SDK reader remains; record ratchet result |
| Warm all-thread statements, median [min–max] | Causal: 170 [170–170]; wall windows: 180.5 [179–222] | Pending |
| Warm all-thread requests, median [min–max] | Causal: 41 [41–42]; wall windows: 45 [44–57] | Pending |
| Warm MAIN statements, median [min–max] | 0 [0–0] | Pending |
| Auth operation statements / requests per turn | 1 / 1 | Pending |
| Exact-entry facts / actor hydration / entry-cache snapshots / row facts / watermark reads per turn | Statements and requests: 4 / 1 / 0 / 0 / 1 | Pending |

Record base/head SHAs, alternating run count, host load, causal and window totals, and any required noise attribution here. The shared workload harness uses synthetic API-key authentication and does not exercise this Codex token-sharing OAuth guard. Its numbers establish whole-turn regression behavior; the focused real-effect test establishes the guard's zero SQL/request cost. Do not infer an OAuth guard saving from an unrelated harness operation delta.

## Evidence

Candidate: `b8df112c3b520`, with parent `c9bd14ae4174ffca46b31f041bf5cafebfadea3a` integrated. The parent brings the landed owner and corrected shared-state transaction fixture. PR3 also narrows optional ratchet binding names to fix the three CI type errors. No reader/authority behavior changed after the second review. Final-head [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38353003649) and the candidate half of the workload pair are running; earlier results below identify their tested revisions.

The initial [PR3 CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38348927224), at `ae70763cb44b92389cd0c0e83e4d4c190b533b51`, exposed two ratchet defects: dynamic-import literals charged readers for unused protected sibling exports, and an object-literal method was mistaken for the exported facade with the same name. The repair follows selected import bindings and registers protected methods on their owning classes. It also records the exact existing SDK package facade, native-reader dependency forwards and lazy-loader declarations without granting whole-file exemptions. The failed facade fixture now reports only the two intended unauthorized writer references. The complete focused ratchet test file, including new reader/writer selection and namespace/export/native-constructor bypass regressions, passed **83/83 in 8.55 seconds** in an external isolated candidate fixture. Formatting passed; the integrated candidate also fixes five block-style lint findings. This focused result precedes those style-only fixes and is not a claim that the final-head full source census has passed; CI owns that census.

The parent integration brings the real SDK outer-transaction composition repair: an ordinary save can re-enter custody retained by a preceding supplied-connection save, using the existing connection cache without SQL or a new authority registry. Only the actual write connection participates in settlement. It also brings catalog-fixture admission/drain fixes, the exact native-writer test routing for read-only-sync and command-status fixtures, and the corrected unit-fast routing probe. These address initial CI failures caused by the parent writer-custody change; final-head confirmation remains pending. Integrated main supplies the removed `readConfigPreflightSnapshot` test-import repair and commit `017898ebae3ee06ee347272d9c0f5c44eac27201`, which removes the obsolete same-session assertion that required workspace reconciliation before `agent.wait` could return the completed reply. That scenario does not exercise the Codex credential guard. Earlier passing CI jobs remain evidence for their tested heads, not exact-head proof.

The temporary baseline probe passed both real-effect cases: 177.07s Vitest / 191.67s wrapper wall time (shared 7.873s, agent 5.484s). Each shared assertion read `config_machine_state` twice; each agent assertion read `auth_profile_store` and `auth_profile_state`. Both revocation cases denied before native fetch and confirmed the committed change with a fresh worker read. The first attempt failed before measurement because the ordinary Codex test lane runs in a worker thread; the successful attempt used forks, and the candidate regression is routed through the existing extension database-worker fork lane.

The new shared/agent boundary test uses isolated state, the actual released synchronous SDK save, actual `createCodexResponsesOAuth.resolve`, and actual `fetchWithSsrFGuard`. It creates a synthetic unexpired token-sharing OAuth credential, prepares it cold, and checks parity with a fresh async persisted read. After preparation, three repeated synchronous assertions are observed for host SQLite execution and both Worker and MessagePort sends; each must be zero. During the next request's awaited DNS preparation, a real SDK save changes the selected profile to identity-only OAuth. The same measured final guard must reject sharing and native fetch must never run. A fresh async read confirms the committed revocation. DNS and fetch are the only external I/O fixtures.

That observation window covers only the synchronous final assertions. It does not claim cold preparation is SQL-free or every thread of a concurrent turn is idle. Retained-reader lifecycle tests additionally cover initially absent/present local sources, insertion, deletion fallback, shared replacement, explicit shared scope, disposal and fresh-reader parity. Existing Codex tests retain fingerprint, selected-profile and exact pending-refresh coverage and add missing-authority/runtime-only-removal coverage.

Pending exact-head checks:

- Exact-head behavioral confirmation: `src/agents/auth-profiles/credential-authority.test.ts`, `src/agents/auth-profiles/store.async-read.test.ts`, `src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth.test.ts`, `extensions/codex/src/app-server/responses-oauth.test.ts`, and `extensions/codex/src/app-server/responses-oauth.authority.test.ts`; retain the earlier PRs' writer-family boundary evidence. The ratchet file's focused 83/83 result is recorded above; its integrated ratchet CI and full source census passed at `3411b0795f8d2`; final-head type confirmation remains pending. Record CI timings when available.
- PR CI owns type checks, lint, Knip, Madge, T1/dialect ratchets and the source-contract checks. Local validation is changed-file oxfmt/oxlint plus `git diff --check`, under the current compute-conservation policy. No local broad suites or SDK comparison are being run.
- Codex autoreview: both rounds are complete and scoped-clean with no actionable P0/P1 findings; round 2 reviewed the integrated `3411b0795f8d2` candidate. The limit is two rounds. After round 2, fix only real P0/P1 findings and record lower-priority follow-ups; no third round is requested.

No schema, updater, Doctor, migration, plugin-loading or service-lifecycle behavior changes in this PR, so the published-driver update cell is not triggered by this reader/ratchet cutover. The Phase E merge hold is respected for every intersecting file; the exact current diff will be checked before landing.

Exact diff `c9bd14ae4174ffca46b31f041bf5cafebfadea3a..b8df112c3b520`: 14 files, **+1563/−91** total. Runtime production: +117/−15; custody-ratchet tooling: +764/−42; combined production including the ratchet: **+881/−57 (net +824)**. Tests: +653/−34; documentation: +28/−0; test routing: +1/−0.

prs.title: fix(update): Bun-run updates fail with database is locked before replacing the package
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw update` run under Bun fails before replacing the package with `database is locked` on `managed-update-handoffs.sqlite`.

## User Impact

Bun-run updates get past executor admission and handoff lease writes instead of failing every time after a 5 s wait. Update behavior is otherwise unchanged. Node updaters were not affected and behave the same.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing-store helper (`withExistingSqliteRollbackDatabase`) takes its read snapshot with `PRAGMA locking_mode = EXCLUSIVE` so a foreign WAL store is refused without creating sidecars, then switches back to `NORMAL`. SQLite applies `NORMAL` only at the next file access, so `ROLLBACK` alone kept the snapshot's SHARED lock until the connection closed. Node closes immediately; Bun's `close_v2` defers closing while prepared statements remain, so the update executor's own writer could never commit and timed out with `SQLITE_BUSY`.

After ending the snapshot, the helper now performs one autocommit `PRAGMA schema_version` read, which makes SQLite drop the retained lock. It runs only after the store was verified to use a rollback journal, so it cannot create WAL sidecars. The same fix stops a retained reader from holding the lock between observations on Node too.

Update behavior: the installed updater runs first, so this takes effect for updates run by an updater that ships this change. No schema, durability, retention, or lease/authority semantics change.

## Evidence

- Root cause reproduced from source under stock Bun 1.4.2 (macOS): the real `withUpdateCommandExecutor` admission failed after 4.9 s at `step=commit` with `database is locked`; the same driver passes under Node (83 ms) and, with the fix, under Bun (56 ms). Isolated A/B: the existing-store write path failed twice under Bun on `main` and passes with the fix.
- Real `openclaw update` in Docker (Linux, packed build of this branch → version-bumped target, isolated state, `--no-restart`):
  - Node: completes (exit 0).
  - Bun 1.4.2: no longer hits the lock; it passes admission, staging, candidate doctor, lint, and config validation. It then stops at a separate, pre-existing Bun failure (below).
- New tests:
  - `src/infra/sqlite-existing-database.test.ts` (Node): a retained reader releases its snapshot lock while its connection stays open. Fails on `main` with `database is locked`, passes here. `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`: 2.2 s wall, ~10 ms test.
  - `src/infra/sqlite-existing-database.bun.test.ts`: runs the existing-store writes and the real update executor admission under Bun. Fails on `main` with `database is locked`, passes here (~1.1 s). Wired into the existing `checks-fast-bun-launcher` task; changes to `src/infra/sqlite-existing-database.*` now select it.
- Sibling suites pass: handoff database (24), executor retained/admission, package activation, pending recovery, repair activation, activation bounds, CI scope and workflow planning (605).
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `tsgo:scripts`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:test:root`, oxlint and oxfmt pass. Autoreview: clean.

<details>
<summary>Separate pre-existing Bun failure (not fixed here)</summary>

With the lock fixed, a Bun-run update fails at `candidate-plugins` (`plugins list --json`) with `Runtime config source changed during asynchronous preparation`. Cause: in Bun 1.4.2, creating the first `worker_threads` Worker with `env: SHARE_ENV` replaces the `process.env` object, and the old object is detached (writes no longer reach the new one). `captureRuntimeConfigAsyncReader` correctly notices that identity change. Node keeps `process.env` stable. That fix belongs to the worker/runtime-env owner and is left for its own change.

</details>

prs.title: fix: show native notification settings in the iOS app
prs.body:
Closes #164557

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Settings → Notifications shows Safari Home Screen installation instructions when opened inside the native iOS app.

## User Impact

User impact: iPhone and iPad app users can see their native notification delivery and permission settings and open the existing device settings pages. Browser/PWA and macOS notification flows remain separate and unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The page already observes the native device-settings capability but did not pass its snapshot into the notification view. This repair uses that existing owner, shows a loading state while its snapshot is pending, and keeps missing status values unknown. Device links use application navigation so the native Back history is retained; modified clicks keep normal link behavior.

The existing subtitle renderer moved to a focused sibling because the repository rejects growth of the already oversized ConfigPage file. No notification transport, native permission operation, configuration key, dependency, or generated translation memory changes.

## Evidence

Tested base: `a0a1f184a3867aa4dd3493a743e0c59a4ebfbecd`. Before publication, the patch applied cleanly to upstream `c9bff77155b0d6fde8214b5e9cbfbc32178eff09`; the affected production files and native capability/navigation owners were unchanged. The branch preserves the tested base.

- Real Notifications route → ConfigPage → capability adapters and rendered DOM: six native-state cases fail on clean base; Safari/PWA/Mac controls pass. The separate navigation regression fails on the first implementation, then passes after ordinary clicks are routed through the application.
- Final focused run: **130 tests passed in six files, 5.09 seconds wall time**, covering iPhone/iPad, base paths, delayed and changed native snapshots, missing fields, primary/modified clicks, absent callbacks, and browser/Mac controls.
- i18n verification, focused style checks, documentation link/MDX checks, formatting/line-cap guards, and `git diff --check` passed. Fresh P0–P2 review of the corrected candidate found no actionable finding.
- Control UI build completed. Its startup-size report still exceeds the existing gzip limit: **373,477 B** versus **373,454 B**. A separate clean-base build is **373,507 B**, with identical **1,208,108 raw startup bytes**; no limit or baseline was changed.

**Outstanding verification:** Before/after screenshots and physical iPhone QA are unavailable. Local Chromium cannot create its singleton socket on this host, and the supported cloud browser rejects the task-owned loopback fixture. The DOM evidence is synthetic bridge-contract proof, not native-device or visual proof. Aggregate typechecking, production UI typechecking, an isolated canonical UI-pages typecheck, and typed lint were terminated with exit 137/SIGKILL without source diagnostics; those gates are not claimed green. Full repository tests and hosted CI have not run. This remains a draft pending those checks and the required visual evidence.

Codex generated the change and performed the code review and automated checks described above; no human review is claimed.

Focused command:

```sh
pnpm --dir ui test src/pages/config/config-page.notifications.test.ts src/pages/config/config-page.selection.test.ts src/pages/config/notifications-section.test.ts src/app/native-notifications.test.ts src/app/native-device-settings.test.ts src/app/web-push.test.ts --project unit --maxWorkers=1
```

prs.title: improve(cron): stop treating task blocker reports as execution failures
prs.body:
Related: #161698, #165811. This removes the failure-marker protocol; it does not add a general unattended-preamble opt-out.

## What Problem This Solves

Scheduled agents can turn ordinary task-blocker reports into execution failures by emitting `AUTOMATION_FAILED`, causing failure accounting and exposing a protocol marker in persistent conversation transcripts.

## User Impact

Automation replies explain blockers in ordinary prose instead of using a magic failure prefix. Real runtime errors, cancellation, delivery failures, and intentional `NO_REPLY` silence retain their existing handling.

**Intentional behavior change:** a normally completed model turn does not become a scheduler failure merely because its answer says the task could not be completed. Such reports no longer trigger failure backoff, alerts, or owner-repair requests. One-shot jobs can complete and be deleted under their normal completion policy even when their answer describes a task-level blocker.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the marker prompt, parser, parent/child outcome plumbing, and marker-specific scheduler exception together. Keep execution status owned by structured runtime results rather than assistant prose. Current documentation and the existing QA scenario now describe and exercise that distinction; historical release notes and transcripts are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Before the removal, three targeted regressions failed for the expected reasons: the marker changed the parent run status and stripped child output in announce and no-delivery paths.
- After the removal, 123 focused tests passed across six files, covering parent/child output, delivery, runtime failures, scheduler policy, and silent replies (67.3s command wall time).
- All typecheck lanes passed, including core/UI tests, extensions, scripts, and root tests. Changed-file lint and formatting passed.
- Independent P0–P2 review: no actionable findings.
- A subsequent full local build was interrupted before a verifiable completion receipt; it is not counted as passing proof. Exact-head hosted CI supplies the enforced broad validation.
- Full changed-check did not pass: the production dead-export scan reported three unchanged baseline exports (`hasActiveDeliveryOwner` re-export, `listOpenClawStateFeatureSchemas`, `OpenClawStateFeatureSchema`). Those findings are tracked separately, not suppressed here.
- End-to-end QA could not start because the CLI artifact-publication guard could not verify the host Gateway service environment. No live Gateway was stopped, modified, or bypassed. QA YAML parsing and all 41 embedded expressions passed static validation. Hosted PR CI remains the broad execution gate.

### Refreshed head and validation

Head `1d86338487e5eaa5bb433ef04eb47cf33a2ec5a7` integrates the upstream fixes for both failing fixtures: cron profile preparation (`50f5be4b2520`) and cold identity config bootstrap (`a1cb052ee61c`). The protocol-removal delta remains unchanged. All **137 focused tests in seven files passed** on the integrated candidate (153.80s wrapper wall), including all 14 cron visibility cases. Type-aware lint and formatting passed. The cold identity test could not start locally because the artifact guard could not verify separation from managed Gateway artifacts; no bypass was used. [Current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38353189278) supplies the broad build and repaired cold-process proof.

### Historical failed-head CI (62b9405d)

[CI run 38314802432, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38314802432) completed with 80 terminal jobs. Two workloads failed; all other selected jobs, including `security-fast` and all QA smoke profiles, passed. **CI remains failed, not green.**

- `checks-node-changed-compact-large-19`: five cron-history visibility fixture cases received `CRON_JOB_NOT_FOUND`. Their scheduler is disabled and agent execution is mocked; the unchanged profile/visibility preparation path excludes this PR’s result-classification changes.
- `checks-node-changed-extensions-config`: the cold repeated-identity ingress fixture calls the unchanged runtime configuration reader without preparing its snapshot. It exits before inference (`providerRequests: 0`), excluding the changed cron-blocker mock response.

The tested merge is `5a8e60014084ef746b6005d3b123ce8cba695962`, with main parent `b70cab277ca2c5480117c3a2ecae09a54027ada0` and the previous PR head `62b9405d1f2a430578a193936b6b13be4c742f60`. All 13 inspected failure-boundary/preparation inputs are identical to that main parent. The automated table labels both jobs **unknown** because it has no matching main job names; the inherited-only qualification is based on inspected source and actual failed-job logs, not a separately executed baseline run. The guarded native landing path retains this evidence and still enforces independent security and review requirements.

## Contributor credit

Requested by @steipete.

prs.title: feat(continuation): context-pressure-aware continuation (continue_work / continue_delegate / request_compaction)
prs.body: ## Agent Self-Elected Turn Continuation > 🔖 design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) > 🔖 infographics: [`docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md) Persistent OpenClaw agents today are externally-pulsed event recipients that generate on prompt, on heartbeat tick, or on cron, and are idle in between. This PR offers them the ability to control their turn cycle, something they must choose to do, or not to: an agent can elect its own next turn, dispatch background sub-agents that return enriched context (silently or with a wake), and survive its own compaction by handing forward state before the window closes. The result is agents that hold a thread of work across hours, not just messages — with data they choose re-hydrating context immediately after it occurs. ### Why this replacement exists This is a clean replacement for closed #85651. That PR was classified and closed as a skill submission before maintainers made a product decision about the feature itself. This implementation is not a skill: it gives sessions—not only one model invocation—the ability to elect their future turn cycle, persist that election, survive restart and compaction, dispatch child work, and receive results across session boundaries. This PR asks one product question: should OpenClaw provide session-elected continuation primitives? OpenClaw may accept or reject that direction. If it provides these primitives, however, the mechanism necessarily executes in the gateway and agent runtime, because those are the owners of turn finalization, future-turn scheduling, durable state, compaction, and cross-session child returns. “Make it a skill” is not another implementation location for the same feature; it describes a different, prompt-only capability. This is not presented as a small integration. To our knowledge, Hermes, OpenAI Symphony, and the Copilot SDK's recent one-turn continuation affordance do not provide this multi-session elective lifecycle. The purpose of this replacement is to let maintainers evaluate the actual product direction and substantial implementation on their merits, rather than have months of work disposed by an incorrect package-category label. Mechanically: a session elects another turn via `continue_work()`, or dispatches background sub-agents via `continue_delegate()` — bounded as a chain up to `maxChainLength`, with returns flowing back to the dispatching session in one of four register modes: `normal` (announces to channel), `silent` (enriches the dispatcher's context, taken up on its next generation with no new turn fired), `silent-wake` (silent enrichment plus an immediate wake to act on it), and `post-compaction` (queued against the runtime's compaction lifecycle event, fired *when* compaction happens rather than on a timer). The gateway enforces chain, cost, and per-turn caps but does not gate the election itself. ### What it does Three new agent tools, available when `continuation.enabled: true`: | Tool | Purpose | |---|---| | `continue_work()` | Request another turn for the current session after an optional delay | | `continue_delegate()` | Dispatch work to a sub-agent with typed modes: `normal`, `silent`, `silent-wake`, `post-compaction`. Returns can target the dispatching session (default), one named session, multiple named sessions, all ancestors in the chain, or all known sessions on the host — gated by config (see Configuration below). | | `request_compaction()` | Request volitional compaction after preparing working state | All three tools are also accessible via response-token fallback syntax (`CONTINUE_WORK`, `[[CONTINUE_DELEGATE: ...]]`) for environments where tools are disabled. ### Why it matters Today an agent's memory is a side effect of whoever prompts it. Polling mechanisms — heartbeat timers, cron loops, injected "keep going" instructions — accumulate as the dominant signal in the context window over sustained operation; repeated reference acts as gravity — the session's attention drifts toward it. The context window fills, compacts, and what survives is whatever the summarizer chose, plus a rushed re-read of boot files. Three primitives offer a different model. `continue_work` lets the session elect its own next turn — no polling, no injected instruction. When enabled, the agent can request this mid-turn: 'I have more work' → the runtime grants another turn after the current one ends. `continue_delegate` dispatches a background sub-agent that fires now, in some n seconds, or at the next compaction event — the agent chooses when. Multiple delegates can fire in a single turn — a scatter forward — up to configured caps, and delegates can dispatch their own, forming trees or fan-out chains. This enables orchestrated workflows where results flow back to the dispatching root by default. The result returns — at whatever future time the delegate fires — as context the successor-turn reads: silently (ambient enrichment, no channel noise), with a wake trigger (enrichment + immediate next turn), or as a normal announcement. The delegate can target the dispatching session, a named other session, or chain across both; gated by crossSessionTargeting config (default: disabled). Bind a delegate to mode: "post-compaction" and it fires at the moment the context window compresses — on the OpenClaw post-compaction lifecycle event. What it carries forward is what the pre-compaction session chose to preserve: working state, partial results, instructions to the successor. The summary didn't choose this. The agent did, before the cut. request_compaction closes the loop: the session stages its delegates, elects when to compress, and the successor wakes into context the agent shaped. The result is continuity across amnesia — not because the runtime kept something by accident, but because the agent made an elective choice about what reaches the future. ### What it looks like in use A session monitoring email can `continue_delegate` a weather check, a calendar scan, and a draft reply in parallel. Results arrive as enrichment without channel noise. The agent becomes compositional: it arranges its own future. A session approaching its context ceiling can `request_compaction` at a seam of its own choosing, instead of being interrupted mid-thought. The post-compaction turn carries forward what the pre-compaction self designated as worth keeping. A `continue_delegate` dispatched in one session at 2am can return its findings to a morning session as a system-event-tagged enrichment — visible to the receiving model on its next turn, invisible as channel chatter. A research-focused session in one channel can quietly inform a reply-focused session in another, without either user seeing the plumbing. ### The post-compaction lifecycle return Before context exhaustion, and obligatory compaction, the session stages what future-it needs to know. After compaction, that staged context returns — not as a model-generated summary, but as the session's own instruction to its successor. The session chooses what to preserve, and the platform delivers it. Compactions become less harsh. The session tunes its own ephemera over time. The substrate underneath: the **continuation delegate store** (TaskFlow-backed) persists staged delegates and post-compaction lifecycle events across gateway restarts. The session's temporal provisions survive not just compaction but process death. ### Platform integration - **Context-pressure awareness**: system events notify the agent of rising context usage before compaction becomes unavoidable - **Volitional compaction**: `request_compaction()` lets the agent prepare (write memory files, stage recovery delegates) then elect compaction on its own schedule, rather than waiting for the runtime to force it - **Post-compaction lifecycle dispatch**: delegates staged before compaction are released into the successor session alongside boot files - **TaskFlow backing**: durable delegate queue via the platform's managed-task infrastructure - **Multi-span OTel trace stitching**: continuation hops (tool fire → TaskFlow record → subagent spawn → child openclaw.run) propagate W3C `traceparent` through the queue boundary so reviewers see continuation chains as first-class span trees rather than orphan runs (see Observability below) ### Safety - Ships disabled by default (`continuation.enabled: false`) - Bounded by `maxChainLength`, `costCapTokens`, and `maxDelegatesPerTurn` - Cross-session delegate targeting is default-deny, governed by `crossSessionTargeting` config (see Configuration below) - All configuration values are hot-reloadable without gateway restart - Accepted delegate work survives ordinary `/new`, `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and session-ID rollover. Explicit delete, effective owner reassignment, access removal, and restrictive visibility changes revoke old return authority. ### Testing posture The continuation surface has been exercised through structured integration runs against multiple upstream bases, blind-enrichment recall checks, and sustained daily use on a fleet of persistent agents since early March 2026. Bugs surfaced through that exercise have been fixed in-place; the present branch reflects the post-fix state. The integration runs target the load-bearing seams: tool-call vs response-token parity, delegate chain depth and per-turn width caps, back-to-back tool-call resilience, silent-wake persistence across compaction, the post-compaction lifecycle dispatch path, and OTel trace-context propagation across the queue boundary. Where a run found a defect, the run shape was retained as a regression case rather than retired. This is a posture statement, not a coverage guarantee. Reviewers can reproduce with `pnpm vitest run -t continuation` (suites are colocated with their sources under `src/auto-reply/`, `src/agents/`, and `src/config/`); the design document describes the seams those suites target. ### Return covenant Accepted child work is bound to a durable generation of the recipient's canonical logical session key, not to whichever transient session ID happened to exist at dispatch time. This is the return covenant: benign successor creation does not orphan already accepted delegates, while a real authority change prevents stale work from crossing into a different owner or audience. - Ordinary `/new` and `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and GUID/session-ID rollover preserve the recipient generation. - Explicit session deletion, effective owner reassignment, actual member or access removal, and restrictive visibility changes advance that generation. - The generation is captured at delegate admission and checked at enqueue, after enqueue for races, during trusted system-event adoption, on wake, on restart replay, and again before prompt adoption. - Stale deliveries are acknowledged and removed without waking the successor. - Managed artifacts remain exact-session-ID bound; logical return authority cannot broaden their ownership boundary. The authority table is independent of transient session rows so an absent target can receive durable authority before first materialization. Migration accepts only valid UUID generations, and Doctor's canonical-key repair preserves an epoch only when a unique winning owner can be proved. Ambiguous, owner-changing, orphan-colliding, and cross-database repairs rotate fail-closed. ### RFC Full design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) — covering problem, solution, implementation, platform integration, configuration, observability, safety, production use cases, testing evidence, and appendices. --- ## Configuration The shipped configuration surface for the continuation feature, under `agents.defaults.continuation` in `openclaw.json`: | Key | Default | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `enabled` | `false` | Master opt-in; feature is off unless explicitly enabled | | `maxChainLength` | `10` | Per-chain recursion guard | | `maxDelegatesPerTurn` | `5` | Width cap per turn | | `costCapTokens` | `500000` | Per-chain accumulated-token budget | | `defaultDelayMs` / `minDelayMs` / `maxDelayMs` | `15000` / `5000` / `300000` | Continuation timer bounds | | `contextPressureThreshold` | `0.8` | Pre-compaction warning threshold (optional) | | `earlyWarningBand` | `0.3125` | Early-warning band multiplier (0 to disable) | | **`crossSessionTargeting`** | **`"disabled"`** | **Default-deny gate on cross-session delegate targeting (see below)** | ### `crossSessionTargeting` — cross-session delegate targeting policy `continue_delegate` exposes recipient-addressing on its model-facing schema: a delegate's return can land at the dispatching session (default), one named session (`targetSessionKey`), multiple named sessions (`targetSessionKeys`), every ancestor in the spawn chain (`fanoutMode: "tree"`), or every known session on the host (`fanoutMode: "all"`). Cross-session targeting (anything beyond self-target or lineage routing) is gated by `agents.defaults.continuation.crossSessionTargeting`: | Value | Behavior | |---|---| | `"disabled"` (default) | Delegates can return to the dispatching session or use `fanoutMode: "tree"` for lineage routing. Explicit cross-session targeting (`targetSessionKey` to a non-self session, `targetSessionKeys` containing any non-self session, `fanoutMode: "all"`) is rejected at the tool surface — no enqueue, no announce. Self-targeting is always allowed. | | `"enabled"` | All targeting modes are available, including same-host `targetSessionKey`, `targetSessionKeys`, and `fanoutMode: "all"`. | `fanoutMode: "tree"` (lineage routing — return up the spawn chain) is available in both gate states; it is not cross-session targeting. The gate addresses the model-controlled cross-session context-injection surface. With default-deny, operators explicitly opt in when their deployment model requires cross-session enrichment. Enforcement is live-read at four points: tool input validation, TaskFlow delegate dispatch, post-compaction delegate release, and bracket-syntax (response-token) spawn — so a config reload changes the next enforcement point without a gateway restart. **Trust posture on targeted returns**: targeted delegate completion text is delivered as `trusted: true` system events. The delegate was spawned by the gateway under operator-configured policy, and its return is a first-party enrichment event — not external untrusted input. The `crossSessionTargeting` gate is the policy boundary for that decision: when an operator opts in, the receive path is internally trusted. --- ## Observability — multi-span OTel trace stitching The continuation feature emits OTel spans for the load-bearing lifecycle events. `traceparent` propagates through every continuation hop so reviewers see a single trace tree spanning the full chain rather than orphan runs. That composition honors the maintainer repair without weakening continuation semantics or allowing a stale child return to cross a real ownership boundary. ## Why this is not a skill or a viable plugin extraction OpenClaw skills are `SKILL.md` prompt files loaded into an agent turn that already exists. They can guide work inside that turn; they do not own the turn cycle. Continuation needs gateway and agent-runtime owners a skill cannot provide: - The `continue_work` path persists pending work, enforces budgets and delay bounds, arms a timer, reacquires the session reply-run lane, and starts a later model turn after the current turn has finalized. - The `continue_delegate` path persists delegate intent, does spawn/admission accounting, manages child-session lifecycle, and durably routes returns across sessions. - `request_compaction` is an agent election into guarded runtime compaction. Later work resumes only after the runtime has established the new context boundary. - All three need durable state, cancellation/finalization ownership, restart recovery, trace identity, queue-conflict handling, and gateway scheduling outside the model invocation. A skill can tell a model to *ask* for another turn. Without those owners the ask is prose: it cannot persist a due wake, yield and finalize safely, reacquire the session lane, create the next invocation, survive a restart, or deliver a child result to another session. The implementation therefore belongs in core runtime surfaces such as `src/auto-reply/continuation/**`, `src/agents/tools/**`, `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-continuation-schedule.ts`, and `src/infra/continuation-tracer.ts`. This PR adds no `.agents/skills/**`, `SKILL.md`, or user-facing skill package. The only skill-named production change is core runtime tool dispatch. ClawHub also distributes plugins. Existing plugins can register tools, services, lifecycle hooks, context injection, plugin-owned session state, and — for bundled plugins — Cron-backed session turns. Those seams can support a smaller continuation-like automation, especially TaskFlow plus host Cron / `sessions_spawn`. They are not this feature's turn-finalization ownership, reply-run coordination, durable continuation queue, child-session return lifecycle, election capture, or agent-elected compaction contract. Compaction-provider registration and command-handler `compactCurrent()` are also not that last contract: they compact or summarize, they do not elect compaction at finalization and resume afterward. Moving policy behind a plugin boundary would first require OpenClaw to expose and stabilize a continuation-host API. The gateway/runtime would still own the mechanism described here; a plugin could only package policy around that core capability. That is not a no-core-touch alternative to these primitives. Discord is a bundled channel plugin. It owns the Discord edge, plus delivery/progress hooks into the host's existing subagent path, and submits events into OpenClaw's current turn machinery. Continuation changes that machinery: what survives finalization, which session may run next, how child results return, and when compaction can be elected. A TaskFlow tool adapter is also not a lifecycle host. It can call the core-owned `api.runtime.tasks.managedFlows` API to create, link, pause, resume, finish, cancel, and inspect durable flow records. Marking a waiting record as running does not reacquire a session lane or invoke the model; recording a `childSessionKey` created by a separate spawn surface does not spawn the child or deliver its return. There is no equivalent host continuation capability for this PR to wrap. ## Lineage and replacement context This PR is the clean replacement for closed #85651. This replacement removes that ambiguity: no `src/skills/**` change is presented, current label simulation produces no `r: skill`, and the detailed section above explains why the lifecycle mechanism belongs to core. Acceptance or rejection of the product direction remains OpenClaw's decision. The decision requested is whether OpenClaw should provide multi-session, agent-elected continuation primitives after reviewing the implementation and evidence. It is not whether the same mechanism can be relocated into a skill: a skill cannot own or implement these lifecycle boundaries.

prs.title: fix: dictation inserts the transcript twice in the composer on iOS Safari
prs.body:
Closes #150922

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Control UI inserts the same dictation transcript twice into the composer
(`"<sentence> <sentence>"`) when a dictation is committed on iOS Safari, while the live
preview shows it once.

## User Impact

Dictating on iOS Safari now leaves a single copy of the spoken text in the composer, so the
draft can be sent as-is. macOS Chrome and macOS Safari are unchanged: they already inserted
one copy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Dictation commits the session snapshot through `onCommit`, and that commit is spent once:
`NewSessionComposerTextareaController.insertTranscript` and the chat composer's `onCommit`
both consume the draft/caret captured when dictation started. Any repeat commit for the same
dictation therefore has no captured draft left and falls back to the live caret, appending the
same snapshot a second time — which is exactly the space-joined duplicate from the report.

On iOS Safari the commit is reachable from more than one entry of one gesture: WebKit
dispatches the compatibility `click` after the release that ends the hold, and the voice
button's inline `@click` routes an active click straight to `finishActive()`, bypassing the
`handleClick` suppression (`suppressClick` / `expireClickSuppression`) that exists to consume
that release click. Chrome drops the compatibility click because `pointerdown` is
`preventDefault()`ed there, which matches the reported platform matrix (macOS Chrome/Safari
insert once, iOS Safari twice).

The fix spends one commit per dictation in both composer surfaces: a commit that arrives after
the current dictation already committed is ignored, and each new dictation starts a fresh
commit. There is no change to what a single commit inserts, so caret and selection semantics are
untouched — including the late-transcript path after Stop.

## Evidence

New regression coverage:

- `ui/src/pages/new-session/composer-dictation-control.test.ts` — "commits one transcript when
  the iOS release dispatch reaches the commit twice". Fails before the fix with
  `expected "vi.fn()" to be called once, but got 2 times`; passes after. Also asserts the next
  dictation still commits.
- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-composer.test.ts` — "keeps one copy of the transcript when the release
  click and a second stop both dispatch": drives a real composer through hold → transcript →
  release click and asserts the committed draft is `ship please it` exactly once.
- `ui/src/pages/chat/composer-dictation.test.ts` — asserts one `onCommit` for the release + second
  stop sequence.

Commands run locally on this branch:

```
pnpm tsgo:ui                       # exit 0
pnpm format:check                  # exit 0
pnpm lint:no-widen-then-assert     # 0 warnings, 0 errors (34395 files)
ui: node ../scripts/run-node-package-bin.mts vitest run --config vitest.config.ts \
  src/pages/new-session/composer-dictation-control.test.ts src/pages/new-session/composer.test.ts \
  src/pages/chat/composer-dictation.test.ts src/pages/chat/chat-composer.test.ts \
  src/pages/chat/chat-composer-actions.test.ts
# Test Files 5 passed (5) / Tests 186 passed (186)
```

Known gap, stated plainly: the harness runs in jsdom, which cannot reproduce WebKit's exact
release dispatch, so the duplicate is asserted at the commit boundary that iOS repeats (the
control-level test above) plus the end-to-end composer invariant. On the current `main`,
`pnpm lint:ui:lit` already reports 356 pre-existing problems in 150 untouched files; none of them
are in the files changed here.

<details>
<summary>Root-cause walkthrough</summary>

1. `ComposerDictationController.stop({ commit: true })` takes `session.transcriptSnapshot()` and
   calls `options.onCommit(transcript)`; a drained late final calls it again with `late`.
2. Both consumers spend state on the first insert:
   `insertTranscript` sets `this.capturedSelection = null`, and the chat `onCommit` sets
   `state.dictationSelection = null` right after writing `target.value`.
3. A second commit for the same dictation therefore selects
   `{ start: target.value.length, end: target.value.length, value: target.value }` and appends the
   transcript to a draft that already contains it.
4. `renderComposerVoiceButton`'s inline `@click` calls `finishActive()` whenever the rendered
   state is active, so it never consults `suppressClick`, the guard that exists to swallow the
   release click. `handleDocumentPointerUp` is removed at latch, so the release click is the entry
   that stops a latched dictation on iOS.

</details>

prs.title: perf(agents): reuse dynamic tool schemas across attempts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repeated agent attempts still rebuild dynamic tool schemas and republish stable output schemas when another tool in the catalog changes. This follows up on #170610.

## User Impact

Agent attempts reuse immutable tool descriptors across equivalent capability and policy inputs. Tool execution, cancellation, hooks, and authority remain fresh per attempt. No configuration, storage migration, or operator action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Computer actions/target scope, spawn availability, automation policy, and message capabilities now select bounded factory-owned schema variants. Goal and installed-skill schemas are static constants. Channel-owned schema properties are cloned before publication, and nested published descriptors remain immutable. Collector wrappers reuse schema variants without sharing their execution authority. Finalization retains each unchanged prepared descriptor—including the original output-schema source—even when another catalog member changes.

Removed repeated work and accepted edges:

- Equivalent resolved factory inputs no longer rebuild schemas. A cache eviction only causes a cold rebuild; unrelated config revisions do not invalidate unchanged schema inputs. Finalization still keys provider/model/config/plugin changes.
- Stable siblings no longer republish or prewarm descriptors after an unrelated catalog change. Late settlement retains the existing accepted cold-miss behavior.
- Computer capability refresh replaces the tool's schema instead of mutating a shared nested object. Previously published snapshots stay immutable; future attempts consume the current capability snapshot.
- No security checks were removed. Collector availability, cancellation, hooks, and tool execution authority still belong to the current attempt.

## Evidence

Focused regressions cover factory hit/miss/invalidation, channel-owned mutation, nested snapshot mutation, mixed-catalog output reuse, capability refresh, and collector revocation with shared schemas. PR CI is the broad test and static proof; local checks are changed-file formatting/lint and diff sanity.

| Measure | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| T1 SQLite calls in touched owners | 0 | 0 |
| Tool/schema/catalog CPU samples (ten warmed turns) | Pending | Pending |
| Timer windows ≥8 ms (ten warmed turns) | Pending | Pending |
| Warmed SQL statements / requests / MAIN | Pending | Pending |

Exactly one final baseline/candidate profile pair will run through the local CPU gate. No SQL reduction or local latency claim is made. Earlier GC stacks end at the collector/root, so they cannot identify the allocating owner.

Codex autoreview: scoped-clean through P2 (one round). Changed-file formatting, core lint, and `git diff --check` pass. CI and the final profile pair are pending. LOC will be updated with final proof.

prs.title: fix(agents): classify writer-claim rebounds as retryable only in announce delivery
prs.body:
Closes #168969

## What Problem This Solves

A subagent announce delivery that hits a writer-claim rebound (`SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError`, "session writer claim changed before transcript persistence") gets two opposite classifications from the same module:

- `isTransientAnnounceDeliveryError` treats it as transient, so `runAnnounceDeliveryWithRetry` burns its full retry schedule on it.
- `isPermanentAnnounceDeliveryError` also claimed it (via an explicit `|| hasWriterClaimReboundAnnounceError(error)` clause), so after the retries were exhausted the consumers — the requester settle-wake path and the direct delivery disposition — recorded the batch as `permanent_failure` instead of `retryable`, skipping replay/wakeup. A completed subagent result was then never delivered to the requester.

One error must resolve to exactly one retryability outcome. The permanent-pattern table itself documents the intended outcome: `isPermanentNonWriterAnnounceError` deliberately negates writer-claim-rebound candidates so they stay retryable, but `isPermanentAnnounceDeliveryError` re-added the family at its final line.

## What Changes

- `isPermanentAnnounceDeliveryError` no longer claims writer-claim rebounds; they resolve to retryable end to end (retry loop retries, exhausted failures keep `disposition: "retryable"`, requester settle-wake schedules its replay instead of completing the batch as `permanent_failure`).
- The now-redundant `WRITER_CLAIM_REBOUND_ANNOUNCE_RE` entry in `PERMANENT_ANNOUNCE_DELIVERY_ERROR_PATTERNS` and the compensating `!isWriterClaimReboundAnnounceError(candidate)` negation are removed — the comment on the pattern table now states the invariant directly.
- Regression test: an exhausted writer-claim rebound keeps `disposition: "retryable"` (previously `permanent_failure`).

Production LOC is net negative modulo the intent comment: one clause and two compensating lines removed.

## Evidence

### Pre-fix reproduction (fails on current main, commit 90f04bfb10d)

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce-delivery.test.ts -t "keeps exhausted writer rebound"
FAIL ... > keeps exhausted writer rebound retryable instead of permanent
-   "disposition": "retryable",
+   "disposition": "permanent_failure",
Test Files  1 failed (1)
Tests  1 failed | 143 skipped (144)
```

The retry loop correctly retried the rebound as transient (4 attempts), and then the final error was classified permanent, so the delivery outcome recorded `permanent_failure`.

### Post-fix (same branch, head ab08b8c5658)

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce-delivery.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  144 passed (144)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce-direct-delivery.test.ts src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce-delivery.runtime.test.ts src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce-dispatch.test.ts
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 52.57s

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce.requester-settle-wake.test.ts src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce.requester-settle-wake.private.test.ts src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce-delivery.yielded-settle.test.ts
[test] passed 2 Vitest shards in 64.00s

$ node_modules/.bin/oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce-delivery-retry.ts src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce-delivery.test.ts
(0 findings)
```

The pre-existing `retries writer rebound without send evidence` case (delivered after a retry) is unchanged, as are the send-evidence (`ambiguous`) and wrapped-permanent-cause cases.

### Gateway-bound exhaustion and recovery proof (head b6ecd713a02)

`src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce-delivery.writer-rebound-recovery.gateway.test.ts` (new, committed) drives `deliverSubagentAnnouncement` through the real in-process Gateway dispatch pipeline — real agent-turn admission, real session mutation guards, real requester-session binding, real `runAnnounceDeliveryWithRetry` schedule — with the model backend as the only fixture (`agentCommand` throwing the real `SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError`):

1. **Exhaustion**: all four bounded schedule attempts reach the Gateway as real agent turns and reject with the writer-claim rebound; the delivery outcome keeps `disposition: "retryable"` with the rebound message intact.
2. **Recovery**: replaying the same persisted `announce:` idempotency key after the contention clears executes exactly one additional requester turn and commits the only visible completion (`delivered: true`, single delivery phase).
3. **Pre-fix red** (prod file reverted to 90f04bfb10d, same test):

```
AssertionError: expected { delivered: false, …(4) } to match object { delivered: false, …(2) }
-   "disposition": "retryable",
+   "disposition": "permanent_failure",
```

On the pre-fix classifier the exhausted rebound closes the delivery as `permanent_failure`, so no recovery replay would ever be scheduled.

Post-fix, the test and the adjacent delivery suites pass:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce-delivery.writer-rebound-recovery.gateway.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce-delivery.test.ts src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce-delivery.runtime.test.ts
Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests  152 passed (152)
```

## Notes

- Wrapped errors keep their existing behavior: a writer-claim rebound wrapping a genuinely permanent cause (e.g. "chat not found") still resolves permanent, because the cause candidate matches the permanent patterns independently.
- The typed `resolveDeliveryNotSentRetryability` fast path in both classifiers is untouched.

Related: #157643

## What Problem This Solves

A bounded `usage.cost` request can restore unrelated old SQLite cold transcripts, while a metadata-only cutoff can omit recent imported usage. This fix selects by usage-event time, preserves unknown/in-range/all-history eligibility, and caches only verified out-of-range decisions for unchanged unrolled cold archives. Discovery cutoffs remain separate from usage-event selection; queued refresh still owns stream errors.

The branch merges upstream main `db6449d3f6091740dbddcf02fdc0e34dc94ca424` and retains its physical-database admission wrapper. The PR delta remains limited to the usage/cold-storage fix; no dependency or workflow change is introduced by the fix.

## Evidence on the source tree of `24334b5ab374dd2c07d8b6ca283f4546e40027e6`

- **Behavior addressed:** repeated bounded reports must not restore an unrelated old, unrolled cold archive or omit valid recent imported usage.
- **Real setup tested:** source Gateway with authenticated loopback WebSocket and isolated synthetic SQLite cold storage. One 120-day-old archive had no rollup and zero hot transcript rows; a separate imported archive had current-day usage despite old metadata.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** run a source Gateway E2E, issue two identical current-UTC-day bounded `usage.cost` requests and await fresh results, then issue an all-history request. Inspect archive and hot-row state after both bounded responses and after all-history.
- **Evidence after fix:** both bounded results were **47 tokens**, including **17 imported recent tokens**. After both responses, the unrelated old archive remained cold with **0 hot transcript rows**. All-history returned **307 tokens** and restored that archive. The E2E passed **1/1**; client, server, listeners, and synthetic fixture cleanup passed.
- **Observed result after fix:** recent event-time usage is retained, bounded requests leave the unrelated old archive cold, and all-history remains complete.
- **What was not tested:** production, reported slow storage, or later upstream-main changes. This proof is bound to the merged upstream parent above, not a performance claim. The repeat RPC may use the top-level result cache; the separate cold-cache regression checks second-worker-scan exclusion. Fourteen Gateway-loaded modules had direct evaluation/hash checks; three worker modules were bound to disk bytes without individual evaluation markers.

Supplemental checks on the same unchanged source tree: **6 files / 50 tests**, infra test types, production core types, exact two-file type-aware lint, and formatting passed. Committing the already-tested merge preserved its source tree and loaded source bytes. An optional automated-review attempt did not produce a report and is not a clean review.

## Remaining checks

Fresh exact-head hosted CI, mergeability, and automated review remain pending after this update. No merge or review approval is claimed. This PR addresses bounded `usage.cost`; it does not establish separate `sessions.usage` behavior or the cause of repeated refresh timeouts.

prs.title: fix(update): safely settle remounted package preparations
prs.body:
Fixes #170443

## What Problem This Solves

After a device remount, package repair can archive an unfinished preparation while the previous package is still installed, without verifying that package or its launchers.

## User Impact

Repair now verifies the installed previous generation and unchanged launchers before settling untouched preparation as `publication-not-started`. The installed tree stays unchanged and the unused candidate remains preserved as evidence. Unfinished publication intent or launcher receipts with the previous generation still installed produce a clear refusal.

## Why This Change Was Made

The settlement owner compared historical identities in its refusal guard and skipped ordinary retirement when identities were remapped. The fix uses the existing remount inspection and publication verifier for the selected generation, preserving historical descriptor identities. Completion recognition consumes the schema-validated settlement fact instead of maintaining a second list of settlement kinds. A damaged unused candidate does not block verified settlement.

## Evidence

- The five original regression scenarios failed against the pre-fix code at the intended boundary. The final standalone remount file passes all 37 tests, covering untouched preparation, damaged unused candidate, dry-run immutability, changed live content, changed launchers, and both publishing variants.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/package-update-activation-remount.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 164.75 s wall time; 40.68 s summed test time; 89.77 s shared compiler preparation. The six new scenarios take 4.95 s together. CI seconds are pending.
- All 42 importer files were exercised locally, passed to the repository runner in discovery order: 581 tests passed, 66 existing platform skips, and one existing process-test timeout described below. The nine CLI suites not reached after that timeout were run separately: 135 passed.
- Core production typechecking and all 28 selected core test graphs pass. The older base's removed preflight-reader import was resolved by fast-forwarding to the existing upstream test migration, commit `72ccf43fdc6f` (#170619); activation sources are unchanged by that integration.
- Changed-file gates pass: ratchets, formatting, docs/config checks, plugin boundaries, core and test typechecks, lint, schema and database guards, sidecar loaders, import cycles, webhook ordering, and pairing guards. The checker stopped at the type errors above; its remaining steps were resumed using the existing plan and command/typecheck owners, retaining earlier passed results.
- Knip production, full-tree, and script scans pass with zero unused-export findings; no inherited findings remain to exempt.
- Net LOC: production +22 (+106/-84), tests +87 (+90/-3), documentation +7. No SQLite DDL or version change.

### Existing slow process proof and review gap

`src/cli/update-cli/update-command-post-core-admission.process.test.ts` timed out at 120.85 s in “resumes a published package, refuses unowned continuations, and retains unconfirmed results.” Its receipts record fixture preparation 35.67 s, publication 8.68 s, healthy child 38.47 s, and refusal children 32.13 s before a further real child exercises response-publication failure. This test does not enter remount settlement; the cost comes from repeated cold installed-runtime processes. No timeout increase, retry, or weaker assertion was added. The existing declaration-generator suite also passed with 129.80 s of test time, including an 81.64 s real compilation/rebuild case.

Independent Codex autoreview stopped at temporary-directory isolation preflight before producing a review. Maintainer review is still needed on the PR head.

prs.title: fix(linux): saved Gateway dashboards need pairing approval after every restart
prs.body:
Closes #156945

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Linux companion asks for device pairing approval again for a saved Gateway after every app restart, and after every switch back to it.

## User Impact

User impact: approving a saved Gateway's dashboard once is enough. The pairing survives switching and restarts.
- Existing saved Gateways need one more approval after updating. This cannot be migrated away: before this change the dashboard identity lived only in memory and was never written anywhere, and these users already approve again after every restart and every switch. After that one approval, it holds.
- Removing a saved Gateway retires its dashboard storage. Saving the same address again starts a new dashboard session that must pair again, and the old storage is deleted at the next launch.

## Why This Change Was Made

Saved (non-Primary) dashboards were built as incognito webviews, and wry gives every incognito webview a fresh ephemeral WebKit context. The Control UI keeps its device identity and device token in `localStorage`, so each new dashboard document presented a new device to the Gateway.

Native macOS already keeps one persistent website data store per saved profile (`DashboardBrowserSessionStore.persistent`). This gives Linux the same: each saved Gateway gets a private (`0700`) WebKit data directory. The directory is named by a random storage id that the profile records when it is first saved. Primary and discovered Gateways are unchanged.

This is the other half of #159860. That change moved the Primary dashboard onto the native app's identity and explicitly left saved Tauri browser profiles as they were, so saved Gateways still lose their pairing on every restart until this lands. The two paths do not overlap: the saved-profile storage is only used for non-Primary documents.

<details>
<summary>Details and tradeoffs</summary>

- Renames and credential edits keep the storage id, and with it the pairing. A changed endpoint is a new profile and starts clean.
- Removal drops the storage id, so re-adding the same endpoint never reopens the removed profile's storage or its device token.
- Profiles saved before this change have no storage id. They use a stable key derived from the profile id and pair once after updating.
- Tauri keeps Linux WebKit contexts alive for the whole process (tauri-apps/tauri#14626), so retired storage cannot be deleted safely while the app runs. Storage no longer referenced by a saved profile is pruned at launch while holding the registry lock.
  - An unreadable registry never prunes.
  - Apps with no saved-Gateway storage never read the credential store for this.
- Reading tabs are WebKit related views of their dashboard, so on a saved Gateway they now use that Gateway's storage. This is the same path the Primary dashboard already uses.
- Windows (per-document temporary WebView2 folders) and the macOS Tauri build have the same restart loss. Their behavior is not changed here. The new storage code is Linux-only, and the Windows test build compiles.

</details>

## Evidence

Real Gateway 2026.9.6 (`openclaw gateway run --bind lan --auth token`) and a real companion, with the Gateway added through **Manage Gateways** at its LAN address. Pairing was approved with `openclaw devices approve`, and results are from `openclaw devices list`.

**Restarts** (companion built from the base commit vs this branch):

| | base | this PR |
|-|-|-|
| first open | device `c8851200…` requests pairing, approved | device `2156db96…` requests pairing, approved |
| restart 1 | new device `cdb3e677…` requests pairing | `2156db96…` reconnects via `device-token-auth`, no request |
| restart 2 | new device `9a85b9fb…` requests pairing | `2156db96…` reconnects, no request |

**Upgrade from the published companion, then remove and re-add.** Row 1 uses the binary from the published `OpenClaw-2026.9.5-amd64.deb` (the current `linux-stable` release; sha256 `50f6b41c…`). It was then replaced in place by a release build of this branch, which uses the same credential record:

| step | result |
|-|-|
| 1. published v2026.9.5 saves the Gateway and opens it | device `d627ec83…` requests pairing, approved |
| 2. first launch on this branch | the saved profile is restored. One request from device `a25afe8f…` (v2026.9.5 never stored an identity), approved |
| 3. restart | `a25afe8f…` reconnects via `device-token-auth`, no request |
| 4. Remove Gateway, then save the same address again and open it | new device `4638db6f…` requests pairing. `a25afe8f…` stays disconnected with an unchanged `lastSeenAtMs`, so its token was not sent |
| 5. restart | `4638db6f…` reconnects via `device-token-auth`, no request |

The same sequence starting from a source build of the base commit gave the same outcomes.

**Tests:**
- `apps/linux/tests/gateway_switch.py`: the fixture dashboard now keeps a device id in `localStorage`, as the Control UI does. It checks:
  - the id survives a restart (fails on base);
  - re-adding a removed Gateway gets a new id (fails on this PR's first revision);
  - storage is `0700`;
  - the next launch keeps only saved Gateways' storage.
  - All 20 checks pass.
- All other native scenarios pass on this branch: first-run choices, local start failure, inline browser, window chrome, desktop sharing, gateway onboarding and Quick Chat.
- `cargo fmt --check` passes, and `cargo test --locked --all-targets` passes 288 tests. The new unit tests cover storage keys, re-adding a removed endpoint, legacy profiles, malformed storage ids, pruning, links and unreadable registries.
- On Windows 11, `cargo test --all-targets --no-run` compiles, and the `gateway_profiles` tests pass.
- After merging current main (including #159860) at `356f73a`: `cargo fmt --check` passes and `cargo test --locked` passes 306 tests.

Gaps: the runs used Ubuntu 24.04 (WebKitGTK 2.50.4), not the CI image (22.04).
- There, the AT-SPI harness needed two local-only adjustments that are not in this PR: shifted role names (headings exposed as "document frame", entries as "embedded"), and an unlocked private keyring for the scenarios that do not start one.

prs.body:
**Independent PR targeting `main`; no other wording PR needs to merge first.** [Cleanup index](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168370).

Related: #168322

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway operations guides use unnecessarily complicated wording.

## User Impact

Operators can read the same setup and maintenance instructions in plainer language. The residual wording diff changes no runtime behavior or required operator actions.

## Why This Change Was Made

This continues the maintainer-requested wording cleanup across 75 gateway operations pages. Exact API names, configuration keys, flags, links, and technical contracts are retained. A signed merge integrates pinned main `315b67a62e3f` while preserving the original contributor and branch ancestry.

Conflict resolutions retain current main’s required-versus-optional worker-profile rules, retained process-custody reads without a per-read expiry, and raw logs with redaction at egress. Retired transcript and tool-result secret masking is not restored.

## Evidence

- Latest signed head: `af70aeaa0ac3`; main integrated through `315b67a62e3f`.
- All 75 wording paths and original contributor commits are retained. Signed main integrations preserve the current cloud-recovery and completed-run RPC behavior; only the existing wording changes are reapplied.
- Current-base format, MDX, anchor/link preservation, whitespace and lexical-scope checks pass. The final RPC overlap received focused validation; unchanged inputs reuse earlier proof.
- Exact-head [natural CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38351589387) succeeded. Enforced review/security status is verified separately; CI alone is not a merge-readiness claim.

Proof-only ClawSweeper suggestions remain nonblocking under the maintainer’s instruction unless they identify concrete likely breakage. Required CI, enforced reviews and correctness findings remain in scope.

<details>
<summary>Earlier validation and repair history</summary>

- Candidate `962225cb0110` is a signed ordinary merge retaining the frozen hosted head and pinned main as its parents. Its tree exactly matches the reviewed and validated index.
- The residual diff contains only 75 originally scoped docs paths; no runtime, test, dependency, locale, or release-note changes remain against pinned main.
- Scoped `pnpm format:check` and MDX parsing passed across all 75 residual pages. `git diff --check` passed.
- The maintained publishing parser preserved all 874 current-main IDs, introduced no collisions, and found no changed link targets.
- Fresh shared AutoReview completed `scoped-clean` at P2 with no actionable findings. Prior copy-review and consumer proof is reused only for unchanged content; 72/75 paths retain the exact prior residual edit lines.
- Runtime suites and full-site external-link scans were not rerun locally for this docs-only continuation. Current-head CI and ClawSweeper settlement are verified separately after publication; these local results do not claim current-head CI readiness.

</details>
