prs.title: fix(acp): treat missing cwd as stale bound session
prs.body:
## Summary

- Problem: a bound ACP session can stay attached after its persisted runtime working directory disappears, so retries keep failing against a dead session and the conversation stays wedged.
- Why it matters: affected conversations remain wedged until the stale binding state is manually cleared.
- What changed: during ACP dispatch, treat a generic `ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED` as stale when the bound session's persisted `runtimeOptions.cwd` can no longer be resolved on disk (`ENOENT`/`ENOTDIR`), then unbind the dead conversation. The signal is folded into the existing `isStaleSessionInitError` classifier and the existing `maybeUnbindStaleBoundConversations` dispatch helper — no new module, no parallel helper.
- Scope: dispatch-only. Two files: `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.ts` and its test.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- ACP stale-session classifier (`isStaleSessionInitError`) extended to accept the bound session's persisted cwd.
- Auto-reply ACP dispatch stale-binding cleanup (`maybeUnbindStaleBoundConversations`) passes the persisted cwd at the `runTurn` catch.
- Regression tests: generic `ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED` + missing persisted cwd unbinds; generic init failure + existing cwd does not.

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related #60720
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause

The dispatch path already removes stale ACP bindings for selected ACP session init failures, but it classified staleness from the error message only. The live missing-cwd case surfaces as a generic spawn `ENOENT` wrapped as `ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED`, whose message does not match the stale-message set. The reliable signal is the bound session's persisted `runtimeOptions.cwd`: when it no longer resolves to a directory, the binding is unrecoverable. Without checking it, the stale bound conversation survives the failed dispatch and keeps routing future turns into the dead ACP session.

## Implementation Notes

- Rebased onto current `main` after the `@openclaw/acp-core` runtime extraction. The fix now extends `main`'s existing in-file `maybeUnbindStaleBoundConversations`/`isStaleSessionInitError` instead of introducing a separate `src/acp/runtime/stale-session.ts` helper (which no longer fits the post-extraction layout). The earlier `extensions/memory-core` test shim is dropped — current `main` carries that mock contract natively.
- Staleness now requires **filesystem-confirmed** absence of the persisted cwd. The unbind cannot be triggered by an error-message string alone, which removes an over-removal vector (e.g. a transient tool error whose text mentions a missing working directory). `ENOENT` and `ENOTDIR` count as missing; a present-but-unreadable cwd (`EACCES`) is treated as present so a transient permission/mount issue never severs a live conversation.

## Maintainer Decision (session-state semantics)

This removes persisted bound-conversation state when a generic `ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED` is paired with a filesystem-confirmed missing cwd — the recovery is correct for a permanently gone cwd, but it is session-state behavior worth explicit maintainer acceptance (per ClawSweeper's `merge-risk: session-state`). Two residual, deliberately out-of-scope behaviors to weigh:

- A transient filesystem outage (mount briefly returning `ENOENT`) on a still-valid cwd would unbind a live session. Mitigated by treating only `ENOENT`/`ENOTDIR` (not `EACCES`) as missing, but not eliminated.
- `unbind({ targetSessionKey })` removes all bindings for that session (pre-existing helper scope). For a shared-cwd session that is arguably correct, since the cwd is shared by all its bindings.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior or issue addressed: A bound ACP session whose persisted runtime `cwd` no longer exists should be treated as stale during dispatch cleanup, unbinding the affected conversation instead of keeping retries stuck on the same dead session.
- Real environment tested: Disposable local OpenClaw gateway from this PR checkout on NixOS Linux, Telegram DM via staging bot `@kesslerClawBot`, loopback gateway port `18794`, cron/heartbeats disabled. Gateway was stopped after the proof run.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: Started the disposable staging gateway from PR head `1ad568ba1e0db9051904eacee025ee36ec2f06ee`, sent a Telegram DM to `@kesslerClawBot` that routed through a bound ACP conversation whose persisted `runtimeOptions.cwd` pointed at `/home/art/.local/state/openclaw-staging/disposable/missing-cwd-pr68843`, let ACP dispatch fail with generic `ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED`, then inspected the post-run binding state.
- Evidence after fix (screenshot, recording, terminal capture, console output, redacted runtime log, linked artifact, or copied live output): Redacted public proof artifact: https://gist.github.com/kesslerio/dbefdac0c5d5a5849997b6bf702047c6. Follow-up proof comment: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/68843#issuecomment-4558022819.

  ```txt
  2026-05-27T12:18:57.491-07:00 telegram: routed via bound conversation 8352721935 -> agent:niemand-code:acp:binding:telegram:default:ecf1b7272077d0d1
  2026-05-27T12:18:57.520-07:00 telegram inbound: chatId=8352721935 ... preview="[...] PR68843 patched missing cwd cleanup proof"
  2026-05-27T12:19:06.365-07:00 [plugins] embedded acpx runtime backend ready
  2026-05-27T12:19:06.400-07:00 dispatch-acp: removed 1 stale bound conversation(s) for agent:niemand-code:acp:binding:telegram:default:ecf1b7272077d0d1 after ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED: Failed to spawn agent command: /run/current-system/sw/bin/codex-acp-openclaw
  2026-05-27T12:19:06.404-07:00 acp-dispatch: session=agent:niemand-code:acp:binding:telegram:default:ecf1b7272077d0d1 outcome=error code=ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED latencyMs=327 queueDepth=0 activeRuntimes=0
  ```

  Post-run binding state:

  ```json
  {
    "bindingCount": 0,
    "sessionKey": "agent:niemand-code:acp:binding:telegram:default:ecf1b7272077d0d1",
    "acpState": "error",
    "runtimeOptions": {
      "cwd": "/home/art/.local/state/openclaw-staging/disposable/missing-cwd-pr68843"
    }
  }
  ```

- Observed result after fix: the staging Telegram DM routed through the stale bound ACP conversation, ACPX reached the runtime backend, dispatch failed with generic `ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED`, and the stale bound conversation was removed because the persisted ACP cwd was missing. Post-run binding state showed `bindingCount: 0`.
- What was not tested: Production AlphaClaw was not used. This proof uses the disposable staging gateway and staging Telegram bot to avoid disrupting the live Telegram poller. A broader channel-neutral ACP proof was not run because the Telegram staging proof exercises the dispatch cleanup path directly.
- Proof limitations or environment constraints: the raw local `/home/art/...` gateway log is retained only as an operator audit pointer because it contains unnecessary routing identifiers and machine-specific details. Public proof is the redacted gist and copied transcript above.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged): current `main` only treated selected ACP init-failure messages as stale and did not inspect persisted ACP session `cwd` metadata for a generic `ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED`; ClawSweeper confirmed the source-level pre-fix path in its review comment.

## Tests and validation

Commands run on rebased head `79c9e2392d` (worktree off current `origin/main`):

```sh
pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.test.ts -t "stale|cwd"
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test.tsbuildinfo
```

Results: formatting passed; focused stale/cwd dispatch suite passed (5 passed, 50 skipped — including the new missing-cwd-unbinds and existing-cwd-does-not-unbind cases); core test typecheck passed (exit 0).

## Security Impact

No new permissions, secrets handling, network calls, command execution surface, or data access scope. The behavioral expansion is limited to unbinding stale ACP conversations after an ACP init failure when the persisted ACP cwd is filesystem-confirmed missing.

## Compatibility / Migration

No config or migration required. The change affects only stale ACP init failure recovery.

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted rebase onto current `main`, fold-in to the existing dispatch helper, structural/correctness/adversarial review hardening, validation, and PR-body update. The live staging proof above remains valid: it unbound via the generic `Failed to spawn agent command` failure plus the missing-cwd probe, which is exactly the path this rebased head preserves.

prs.title: feat: browse active device-folder session files
prs.body:
Related: #169722

> Stacked on #169722; base branch: `feat/device-existing-folder-sessions`.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Control UI Files panel cannot browse or edit an existing-folder session even while its paired-device worker is active.

## User Impact

User impact: active existing-folder sessions can list, preview, and save files through the paired device; stopped sessions show a clear start-the-session error and never fall back to Gateway-local files.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Files RPCs now use the worker's existing workspace-inspection command only when the exact session, device-folder binding, active placement, owner epoch, attached environment, and paired device remain current before and after awaited work. Saves use the session lifecycle mutation lock shared with stop, archive, and session-identity rewrites. Device folders have no Gateway checkpoint or reconciliation owner, so the repository checkpoint mutation service intentionally does not apply.

Workspace reveal remains unavailable because there is no Gateway checkout. `sessions.diff` is unchanged and still returns an unavailable/empty result for device-folder sessions rather than inspecting the paired device.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.device-folder.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 3 passed, 31.20s wall time.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.device-folder.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 44 passed, 1 existing platform skip, 42.73s wall time.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check docs/nodes/session-hosting.md src/gateway/server-methods/session-device-folder-workspace-access.ts src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.ts src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.device-folder.test.ts` — passed.
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/gateway/server-methods/session-device-folder-workspace-access.ts src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.ts src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.device-folder.test.ts` — 0 warnings/errors.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Isolated live proof through real authenticated `sessions.files.list/get/set` RPCs and the Control UI: active list/open/save passed; the device file changed, the same-named Gateway file stayed byte-identical, and reclaim restored the typed `device_folder_files_unavailable` error. Fresh synthetic Gateway/node state, system Chrome, port 18971, no provider call; all task processes stopped.

### Screenshots

Idle session (historical screenshot) — shows the explicit paired-device start requirement:

![Inactive device-folder Files panel error](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5b046cce-2eeb-4a6c-ac2f-3b80484038b6)

After — active session lists and opens `same.txt` from the paired-device folder:

![Active device-folder file opened in Files panel](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/11099420-6bc4-4b8d-9373-539a7716a4f1)

Broad typecheck and test suites were not run locally; hosted CI owns those gates.


### Exact rebased-head proof (2026-10-13)

HEAD: `70d4566ba31e9f53afc3d69805389cf75d6ae7f1`, stacked on BASE `8fc04f9ceef2d23142f295c43bddd35f84ccbbc2`.

- Five focused Files suites passed: **70 tests passed, 1 existing skip**. Scoped formatting/lint and `git diff --check` passed.
- Isolated live proof used a foreground paired session-host node, fresh synthetic Gateway/node state, and the QA loopback mock provider. BASE showed the previous explicit refusal. On this exact head, the Files panel listed both synthetic files, opened `same.txt`, and saved `DEVICE saved through Control UI`.
- Shell verification after the UI save: paired-device file SHA-256 `4e8d3de8cea4be4e9e9d0844668c682f8d51c98fb77da3e9fafe629bd2e022ae`; same-named Gateway file remained `GATEWAY original` with SHA-256 `c562e941208308e7c478414ee9f7ed993acf2a3f9baaa49f8d541a48e127574b`. Proof processes stopped and ports 18971/18972 were free after collection.

Before on BASE — active existing-folder session still refuses Gateway Files access:

![BASE active existing-folder Files refusal](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6cea2b46-5424-4459-9151-4ce4097a8b67)

After on exact STACK head — paired-device folder listed in Files:

![Exact-head active device-folder file list](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/40a81e2c-a591-40db-b20c-1fcbf856fe2c)

After UI save — device-owned file contains the saved text:

![Exact-head device-folder file saved through the UI](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f95c5d5b-8dc1-4234-bdbf-cd551e9c2b18)



### Remaining authority decision

ClawSweeper's exact-head review found no definite code defect, but blocks merge pending proof that an operator-device revocation while a remote save is already queued prevents the final device mutation. The current one-command node boundary rechecks requester/session authority before dispatch and after completion; the node can enforce transport/environment aborts during its atomic save, but it cannot independently revalidate a Gateway-side operator revocation at the final write. Guaranteeing that case requires an owner-approved authority contract across the Gateway/node boundary (for example a two-phase prepare/commit or equivalent protocol), which is outside this PR's approved schema/protocol scope. This PR remains draft.

prs.title: fix(control-ui): preferences load late on signed-in chat reloads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in reload of a dashboard deep link still fetched the full editable configuration and then the viewer’s appearance/navigation preferences before applying the right display settings. The campaign census recorded a roughly 161 KB `config.get` response, plus a separate `users.prefs.get` round trip. The original reload showed 14 visual states over about 15 seconds; this change addresses the preference/config portion of that waterfall.

## User Impact

Signed-in chat/dashboard reloads apply the authenticated viewer’s display preferences before hello and avoid two redundant boot RPCs. Full configuration edits and subsequent preference refreshes keep their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the authenticated document’s existing bootstrap payload with a read-only display projection and the authenticated viewer’s appearance/rail preferences. The Gateway uses the existing canonical preference reader, config scope policy, and cached config schema/redaction owner. Public documents receive no authenticated seed; secret-bearing MCP arguments, environment values, headers, and certificate contents are omitted. Embedded documents remain `private, no-store`.

Chat reads its queue mode, web-search toggle, MCP summaries, swarm display, public session origin, and shared UI preferences from that projection. The editable config snapshot stays absent until a settings page or write needs it. Seed the existing per-connection profile read cache only for the first matching Gateway/profile connection; existing preference events, config refreshes, and reconnect paths retain ownership of subsequent refreshes. A selected bearer identity cannot adopt a different navigation-authenticated viewer’s seed. The profile preference decoder is shared between document adoption and RPC reads. Display consumers use the admitted resolved server snapshot after refresh, never an editable config draft. The config RPC and document builder now share the runtime-schema cache owner; document preparation supplies its held config instead of depending on global runtime preparation.

Boot preference inventory: shared theme/mode/accent, locale, chat visibility/send/follow-up preferences; profile theme/mode/accent, fonts, background, tab icon, and rail shortcuts. Other sidebar presentation state continues to come from its existing browser settings owner.

## Measurement

The merged Team-scale benchmark and fixture were run against main at `4f8c8c58fc88` and the candidate. The local adapter supplies an authenticated inline bootstrap and a valid small config snapshot, because the stock benchmark’s 83-byte config stub has no config object and never exercises the profile preference read. Both variants use the same synthetic data and 35 ms RPC latency.

| Boot census | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `config.get` requests | 1 | 0 |
| `users.prefs.get` requests | 1 | 0 |
| Total RPCs | 86 | 84 |
| RPC request + response JSON bytes | 945,253 | 942,270 |
| Target RPC response bytes | 2,667 | 0 |

The reviewed patch rebased unchanged onto main at `4e3b11bf5c8d`. The display seed is carried in the document; it is not an editable snapshot or an extra request. The synthetic config is much smaller than the measured production payload. These results establish removed round trips, not a production byte or latency estimate. On the loaded Mac, nav-to-settle was 4.57→3.63 s, forced layouts 46→48, and visual groups 5→5; timings and layout differences are noisy and no CPU/latency improvement is claimed.

Production LOC delta from `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD -- ':!*.test.ts' ':!*test-support*' ':!docs/*'`: **+255** (343 additions, 88 deletions, 21 files; includes the generated boot manifest). Growth preserves the contract separating read-only display facts from complete revision-bearing editor snapshots and limits credential disclosure; the unconditional full-config boot read is removed where authenticated bootstrap coverage exists.

## Evidence

- New bootstrap regression fails on the old code: the old boot uses the system theme, empty rail, and no server locale instead of the document preferences. Candidate unit proof checks pre-hello preference selection and selected-bearer isolation.
- New bundled browser regression: preferences apply before hello, both boot RPCs remain absent, and `users.prefs.changed` invalidates the document-seeded cache and adopts a changed profile theme. Passed; 29.36 s including the bundle build, test body 2.00 s.
- Existing reconnect/cross-tab preference browser file: 8 passed; 77.06 s including the bundle build.
- Bootstrap preference unit: 2 passed, 4.60 s. Config capability: 17 passed, 4.19 s. Shell config/write lifecycle: 45 passed, 6.39 s. Profile preference lifecycle: 15 passed, 4.43 s.
- Gateway projection/redaction unit: passed; wrapper wall time 12.83 s. Authenticated/public HTTP boundary: 2 passed; wrapper wall time 201.16 s, dominated by a cold compiled-worker cache. The test verifies inline preferences, credential redaction, public document isolation, and private cache headers.
- CI repair proof: authenticated bootstrap document 2 passed (126.16 s wrapper), response authority 4 passed (202.56 s wrapper), Swarm startup 5 passed (20.22 s), progress history 14 passed (13.78 s), roster config-change fallback 1 passed (5.66 s), composer shortcuts 7 passed (41.50 s), locale/offline retry 2 passed (62.61 s), active-run follow-ups 11 passed (90.23 s). Files ran individually with one worker; browser durations include builds. Initial CI exposed display-source selection and schema-preparation regressions; both owners were repaired before this head.
- Formatting and `git diff --check`: passed. Independent Codex review: scoped clean at P0–P2. Exact-head CI: pending.

No Testbox/Crabbox lease was created: remote capacity is blocked under the campaign’s current policy. Full UI e2e and full typecheck/changed-file checks are deferred to CI; the full-UI-suite requirement is waived for this capacity-blocked period. No live Team state or private captures were used in public proof.

## Visual proof

Synthetic before/after captures hold hello pending to expose startup preference selection. Before uses the system’s dark theme; after already uses the saved light preference. Images are attached below.

Release-note context: signed-in chat/dashboard reloads apply display preferences from the authenticated document and avoid redundant config/profile preference boot RPCs; settings and live preference refresh behavior are preserved.

![Before: system theme while hello is held](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/af5cb33a-42cb-49ba-9021-ec6b347ac747)

![After: saved light preference before hello](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f3d5e7ab-b458-4a2c-ae50-f2181f8c5259)

prs.title: fix(cron): preserve CLI-backed cron topic route
prs.body:
Fixes #138316. Builds on #138406 and retains contributor ancestry. Related: #162034 (durable source authority, outside this PR).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes CLI-backed isolated cron completions losing their Telegram recipient/topic and falling back to the owner DM.

## User Impact

CLI cron runs receive the selected account and conversation/thread context, matching the embedded runner. Unthreaded targets still use the channel plugin's normalization. No new configuration or storage changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Fresh main (`db6449d3f6091740dbddcf02fdc0e34dc94ca424`, fetched October 10) still populated only channel/account for CLI runs; recipient resolution remained embedded-only. The shared runner parameters now carry the channel-native target and normalized thread into the CLI loopback grant.

Integrated main to resolve actual merge conflicts after cron runtime refactoring, then incorporated the maintainer-owned Kysely migration-witness fix `db6449d3f6` after exact-head CI exposed that inherited architecture failure. Kept upstream's lifecycle/admission changes and removed tests intact; the PR remains limited to two cron production files and two focused test files. Shared conversation-context assembly lives in the existing channel-output-policy module so the executor does not grow beyond the line-cap ratchet.

This is route propagation, not durable source-generation fencing or final transport authorization. Revocation, queue/recovery migration, and downgrade compatibility remain in #162034.

## Evidence

- On the updated candidate: 18/18 focused tests passed across `run.message-tool-policy.test.ts` and `channel-output-policy.test.ts`, including CLI grant recipient/topic/account and plugin normalization for unthreaded targets.
- Measured one-worker invocation: 324.29 seconds wall on the 4 GiB host; Vitest reported 314.20 seconds, including 217.74 seconds cold compiled-worker preparation. The new CLI regression took 30.59 seconds including first-fixture initialization. The integration file exceeds 30 seconds on this host: it exercises the real isolated-cron entry point through real CLI grant assembly; a helper-only test would miss the original missing producer fields. Existing cron integration fixtures account for the cold import/setup cost; no new Gateway/process boots or real timers were added.
- Targeted oxfmt, oxlint, diff-check, line-cap, and mock-factory ratchets passed.
- Core typecheck was bounded to 180 seconds on this 4 GiB host and timed out; no typecheck pass is claimed. Heavy extension type lanes were not run.
- Fresh independent Codex autoreview of the exact candidate tree is scoped-clean for P0–P2; no actionable defects identified. Source context covered runner assembly, channel target resolution, and real MCP grant construction. After the second main integration, all four PR files and the reviewed MCP grant source context remain byte-identical to the independently reviewed candidate.
- Prior exact-head CI [38040705236](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38040705236) at `b3f2743`: production/test types and lint passed; architecture Kysely and UI e2e failed. The real checker replayed the same 14 Kysely violations on main's `cdeb` source tree; the owning upstream fix is now integrated. prs.title: fix(compaction): surface recovery after repeated quality rejections
prs.body:
Related: #150577

## What Problem This Solves

Repeated compaction quality rejections can leave a growing session without actionable recovery guidance, even when each attempt fails for a different reason.

## User Impact

After three rejected attempts, users receive the rejection codes and guidance to retry `/compact` or select another summarization model through `agents.defaults.compaction.model`. Conversation history and strict quality validation remain intact; this does not add an automatic lossy fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

Track rejected attempts across reopened sessions using their resolved identity, and deliver a recovery notice through the existing compaction-notice channel even when routine `notifyUser` notices are disabled. Missing or failed delivery remains eligible for retry; successful delivery suppresses duplicates, and successful compaction clears the streak. Model-locked sessions receive retry guidance without a model-override suggestion.

Tracking is process-local and bounded to 1,024 recent session identities. Restart or eviction resets it. No persistent schema, configuration option, or migration is added.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the missing recovery guidance through the real session compaction/safeguard path with controlled summarizer outputs; the regression failed before the change.
- **427 focused tests passed** across safeguard, compaction hooks, reason classification, rejection tracking, overflow recovery, and reply delivery. A final six-scenario safeguard rerun passed after the typed reason-code extraction correction.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passed, including core/test typechecks, lint, formatting, dead exports, import cycles, and repository guards; `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent autoreview found a lost-notice edge case. Fixed it and verified absent callback, failed delivery, successful retry, duplicate suppression, and successful-compaction reset.
- UI captures below use synthetic Gateway history and the exact recovery message. They prove rendering, not a live-provider reproduction. No live Gateway state was changed.

### Before

![Before: rejected compaction without recovery guidance](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1df8b3b1-b037-4ba8-8a43-de37093214f6)

### After

![After: repeated rejection codes and recovery guidance](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5a6055ff-fd6a-4a3a-9df2-626b38f75ef0)

prs.title: perf(sessions): move target lookups and callers to workers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway target discovery and entry preparation could still open SQLite through synchronous lookup APIs during turn preparation, session selection, and later action checks. Durable callers now use the existing session read worker. Bundled callers await the replacement APIs, and mutations receive the selected canonical target instead of rediscovering it.

There is no new configuration or user-facing feature. Deprecated synchronous SDK methods retain their documented compatibility window; bundled callers use their async replacements.

## Design and ownership

Prepared facts stay alive through the action they authorize and are updated by the existing writer receipts. File, media, sharing, publication, Talk, and tool effects consume those facts. Real execution, revocation, replacement, and disclosure boundaries retain their current authority check. The actor entry replica does not certify live authority.

The cutover preserves full entry snapshots by default, list-only child discovery, qualified-address selection, configured-store initialization, physical source identity, and SQL-side copies of opaque retained payloads. It removes the superseded synchronous Gateway loader exports, the sharing snapshot cache, ordinary steering/cron bookkeeping rereads, and projection rebuild per-chunk ownership reads. Rebuild publication uses its final conditional UPDATE result.

Both async combined-store merge callers prepare missing-owner lineage facts through the existing async reader, including explicit parents, spawn parents, and implicit thread parents. Captured absence remains absent for that selection; merging cannot reopen a native store. The synchronous compatibility loader and explicit native-incognito worker paths retain their own named native resolver.

## T1 accounting

This PR reduces the lane's recognized sites **22→21**. Across the three-PR series, the original inventory is **27→21**, including two sites relocated into the explicit native discovery kernel. These are source-audited call-site counts, not a claim of 21 ordinary Gateway-main-thread executions. The whole-inventory ratchet is reported separately in the evidence.

| Original lane file | Original sites | Remaining recognized sites | Reachability after cutover |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `session-transcript-match.ts` | 1 | 1 | Native-incognito branch only; ordinary durable match uses history worker. |
| `session-transcript-projection-rebuild.ts` | 12 | 9 | Mixed kernel: workers, native incognito, deprecated synchronous SessionManager SDK methods, and offline migration. |
| `session-transcript-projection-writer.ts` | 2 | 2 | Ordinary durable reconciliation supplies publication worker; native branch serves incognito/maintenance. |
| `session-transcript-read-fence.ts` | 1 | 0 | Uses committed admission receipt bounds; SQL re-read removed. |
| `session-transcript-reconcile-memory.ts` | 2 | 2 | Native-incognito memory source only. |
| `session-transcript-reconcile-readiness.ts` | 1 | 1 | Ordinary durable readiness uses history worker; native branch serves incognito/maintenance. |
| `session-transcript-retained-data.ts` | 1 | 1 | Worker mutation or deprecated synchronous SessionManager suffix mutation; preserves opaque user payloads in SQL. |
| `session-transcript-search.ts` | 4 | 3 | Worker kernel and native-incognito host branch; post-query revision probe removed. |
| `targets.ts` | 2 | 0 | Discovery SQL moved into `targets-discovery.native.ts`; ordinary host callers use async inventory. |
| `transcript-payload.ts` | 1 | 0 | Encoding comes from admitted schema facts; independent encoding SELECT removed. |
| New `targets-discovery.native.ts` | — | 2 | Discovery workers; deprecated synchronous combined SDK loader; native-incognito history. |
| **Total** | **27** | **21 (19 original files + 2 relocated)** | **Not zero. No ordinary durable host path found after the combined-lineage repair.** |

The remaining sites are mixed kernels and must not be marked wholesale worker-only. Concrete retained chains are history workers; projection/publication workers; native incognito; offline Doctor/migration; and deprecated synchronous SessionManager/combined-loader SDK methods. No ordinary durable host path was found after the combined-lineage repair. Native incognito is intentionally left for its separate owner-removal work. Doctor and offline migration remain allowed synchronous exceptions.

The retained effect-authority chain is `followup-turn-execution` → `prepareGatewaySessionEntryReadOnlyInWorker` → `reply-tool-authority`, with final uses in host-private capabilities and question access. Removing it requires a publication contract for every relevant writer, so this PR does not substitute an actor snapshot for live authority. Deprecated SessionManager methods warn and name their Async replacements; they will be removed in a later release after the deprecation has shipped in a stable release.

## Live measurement (final frozen pair)

## Cold causal attribution

Cold first-turn +26 SQL includes the identical 32-SQL existing first-open admission batch moving from background into first-turn scope. Seven other cold reads are removed in this phase. No warm SQL/request/MAIN family increases. Count changes are retained; this report makes no latency or unconditional landing claim.

The structural first-turn delta is **−6 SQL / 0 requests** after excluding only the identical once-per-open admission batch and the two whole-count-neutral request moves. The 32-SQL batches are equal by normalized SQL/method multiset hash. The earlier pre-repair legacy-window pair was not an aggregate reduction: SQL mean360.1→480.2 and requests114.0→119.2. It identified 15 removed discovery/close requests per turn and an unrelated usage-cache write receipt invalidating shared session replicas. Commit `8feea29d435b1` scopes those four cache kernels to no changed session keys; the final pair above is after that repair, against an updated main baseline. No subtraction or speculative counterfactual saving is claimed.

## Removed checks and accepted edges

- Input actor cache-version expectation: unrelated metadata writes no longer reject input acceptance/adoption; the writer still checks the selected session, lifecycle, custody and live authority at commit.
- Steering terminal reread: an admitted snapshot may miss a just-completed bookkeeping transition; the live run registry still owns cancellation and execution authority.
- Cron generation/skill rereads: a concurrent internal bookkeeping change is observed by the next owner operation; current execution authority stays checked at the effect.
- Duplicate main-thread canonical-readiness lookup: a worker-admitted row is served using its physical identity and committed write receipt even when the separate main-thread validation cache is cold; offline validation remains owned by admission.
- Same-route read-lifetime recapture: prepared ownership and in-process write receipts govern the read lifetime; foreign-writer polling is not supported.
- Projection per-chunk ownership reads: reset during a queued derived rebuild may leave a stale derived index until a later rebuild; canonical transcript bytes remain intact.
- Post-selection registry currency: own/sibling admission and external alias replacement change the next selection; the selected physical source, receipt updates, and effect authority remain bound. Physical close, row replacement, and sharing changes still revoke that source.
- Duplicate agent admission reader: the next owner operation consumes intervening ordinary metadata; prepared rows and the actual COMMIT receipt govern the current run.
- Sharing snapshot cache: the duplicate cache and invalidation hooks are removed; prepared reads and the existing projection own visibility facts.
- Duplicate pre-wait authorization: an unauthorized `agent.wait` may occupy an observer until completion/timeout; the one current check before returning data prevents disclosure.
- Ambient Talk default recapture: an already-selected Talk operation keeps its selected agent if the default changes; sharing, incognito, replacement, and relay authority checks remain.
- Ordinary roster rediscovery after publication: captured absence stays absent for that selection; a fresh selection discovers the store. Security-scoped sharing leases still revoke after unknown registration settlement because the commit receipt was lost.
- Post-send session bookkeeping recheck: a confirmed built-in message send returns its receipt even when its own route write creates the session. Caller/credential checks remain; reads, dry runs, unconfirmed results, and plugin tools keep full session checks.
- Self-effect timestamp recapture: an `updatedAt`-only change does not revoke an otherwise valid selected effect; real identity, sharing, and execution authority remain checked.
- Read-only worker retirement/private snapshot cleanup: these events no longer force a blanket refresh of unrelated live database caches; owner write receipts still drive invalidation, and write-capable workers retain the default exit invalidation.
- Readiness wrapper identity: a fresh wrapper of the same admitted live receipt remains valid; missing receipts, changed physical ownership, invalid claims, and invalid execution authority are still rejected.
- Archive planning: the operation uses its captured row and receipt-updated predicate without an optional cache reread; raw updates that bypass the lifecycle owner are not adopted into that prepared plan.
- Repeated sharing-preparation activity checks: cancelled preparation may finish consuming an already admitted read; resource acquisition and the final effect still check the retained owner.
- Placement ACK and journal pending checks: a retained committed placement remains usable while its own bookkeeping receipt is pending; pending claims and revoked reads still reject execution.
- Maintenance inventory currency: turn claims, releases, ACKs, results, and journal writes keep preservation ownership unchanged. An overlapping inventory read may retain older bookkeeping metadata until the next publication; lifecycle changes and keyed execution authority still invalidate it.
- Cancelled media cleanup: a failed OS deletion may retain one transient, unbound cleanup tombstone for the existing sweeper; it remains hidden from artifact downloads and creates no conversation message.
- Accepted child cancellation: replacing its parent refuses new effects but does not undo an already accepted child interruption; if terminal bookkeeping fails, its exact durable claim remains recoverable until reconciliation publishes. A later best-effort session abort marker may be refused even after terminal cancellation is durable.
- Retention reply snapshot recheck: placement snapshot currency is validated once when dispatching the retain command; a later bookkeeping update does not discard its accepted reply. Current node/connection identity, session generation, archive state, and real claim checks remain.
- Cron recovery escalation: a partial monitor reconciliation may finish on its already-scheduled retry while the config is applied; thrown failures still use recovery restart.
- Inapplicable placement preflight: metadata-only patches do not read placement because no placement policy applies; permission changes, unarchive, and actual runtime selection still run their applicable checks.

The cold admission correction reserves the existing admission turn before entering the writer FIFO (all batch paths together), preventing a usage refresh/prune ↔ history deadlock found in CI. Cancellation races only admission waiting; accepted writes retain settlement and cancelled reservations preserve predecessor order. Media delivery joins the existing pending publication before its effect check. Shared terminal publication receipts keep session/security authority while tolerating workspace changes; pending/latest receipts still compare receipt-updated workspace metadata.

The final integration repairs preserve caller authority after accepted sends, reuse prepared Talk profile policy, and retain the worker-owned read-admission facts for cold publication reads. Detached placement setup retains the existing session authorization alongside its device hold; workspace and archive effects consume receipt-updated metadata rather than optional cache presence. Cold source capture now runs after the existing read admission and before snapshot dispatch, without another query. Recovery notice authority is captured after recovery admission and retained until dispatch settles, including runtimes without a typing adapter.

## Evidence and integration

Current head `8d86e0cf2b8499f51962cfb6ce01536ae2f4a589` integrates main `869ceef2c25f9c966bfb574b6f5206d1fc685039`. The final integration includes main’s thinking-policy and Knip repairs. Its only conflict combines the lane’s async target selection with main’s async qualified-target preparation in the freshness test; both calls are awaited and assertions are preserved. The preceding integration had one test-only conflict: both branches converted the auth-policy fixture to worker lookup; it retains explicit list/exact/writable preparation. The shared worker preserves both the transaction-authority callback and main’s error-message options. Its existing unknown-outcome helper now lives in the receipt module, resolving the intermediate type dependency cycle without changing behavior. The extracted wrapper inventory includes that receipt module; CI caught and identified the initially omitted dependency. Scoped oxfmt, oxlint and `git diff --check` pass. The frozen live pair above remains pinned to its explicit source hashes.

Final integrated-head CI is pending on `8d86e0cf2b8499f51962cfb6ce01536ae2f4a589`. Pre-integration [CI 38350977215](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38350977215) records the fake-clock repair and wrapper source-inventory correction on `bcdb67c70b1761277c0de4b1debc55d6e41d890f`; its production types, general test types, core lint, source contracts/export collisions, Madge, guards, and database ratchets passed. Exact-head security also passed. Remaining prior-head results are not presented as integrated-head CI. Previous [CI 38349840177](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38349840177) remains recorded separately. [Knip 38349900552](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38349900552) reports inherited unused UI files/exports plus validateVectorKnnRequest and SessionEntryReplacementPublication; the latter two match scheduled main 38347821426. prs.title: fix(codex): preserve terminal dynamic tool evidence
prs.body:
## Problem
Codex honors a plugin tool's `terminate: true` when releasing a turn, but the terminal metadata is not projected into `toolMetas`. Core therefore treats the released turn as incomplete and runs fallback settled-turn finalization.

## Impact
A tool that already delivered the complete channel response can trigger history-read failure logging and unwanted fallback text.

## Changes
Preserve terminal dynamic-tool metadata and exact tool-call identity through projection and native completion. Record the released terminal call only after the existing release gates pass, and suppress fallback finalization only for a matching successful synchronous terminal result. Add unit and integration coverage.

## Evidence
- Focused Codex projector, lifecycle, and settled-context tests
- Combined acceptance run: 227 tests passed
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`
- `git diff --check`

Closes #153712

## Current validation and merge blocker (October 4, 2026)

Hosted CI run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35522042538 fails two native command-output-fidelity cases (`Expected native command execution`, event-projector.output-fidelity.native.test.ts:238) and a pre-raw-response checkpoint assertion (run-attempt.checkpoint.test.ts:54, additional toolResult). Build, lint, and production/test type checks pass. The native test fails before instantiating the patched OpenClaw projector; the checkpoint owner and failed test files already exist in the parent commit. No executed baseline comparison establishes failure causality, and no passing CI rerun is claimed.

The recorded 227-test acceptance covers local boundaries; it is not live channel-delivery proof. Merge remains blocked on a redacted real Codex direct-chat run showing the terminal tool's completed channel reply, no fallback reply, and no settled-context failure. This host has no installed Codex executable or task-created authenticated channel/Gateway, and cannot create the required secretless execution isolation. The upstream Actions integration also refuses CI reruns (403). No replacement runtime proof is claimed.

prs.title: fix: backport compatible stability fixes to 2026.9.33
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: 2026.9.33 users can encounter failed or restarted agent work, incorrect update recovery, and broken node or companion reconnects despite fixes already available in October.

## User Impact

Backports **33 compatible fix groups / 38 source commits** to **extended-stable/2026.9.33**: 25 October groups, six newer core fixes, and two native-source fixes. Existing September versions, schemas, protocols, dependencies, and permission boundaries remain unchanged.

**Native fixes require rebuilt macOS/iOS companions; a Gateway/npm-only upgrade cannot deploy them.** Live certificate renewal and physical-device audio qualification remain outstanding. This PR does not publish a release or establish full release qualification.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adapt the fixes to September's existing owners and fixtures instead of importing October prerequisites. The target base is `d53dbcf7a09fccf19a041d5a93ca8589e85d1ef2`; the frozen October donor tip is `467e83dea27c0d9ade8e999d688de2ed656b2225`.

The [backport supplement](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/bd4e50d97cf1123cb30b646d7ff96d53b65c27dc/docs/releases/2026.9.33-backport-audit/october-backports-20261012.md) records every selected source and the bounded 150-row audit. The 5,099 historical ledger rows are carried forward, not requalified or promoted to a new accepted cursor.

- Held: [steering #168077](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168077), because September lacks its named/FIFO/direct-steering admission architecture.
- Only the recorded-success terminal portion of `d84dc316c584` is selected, together with its ExitError companion. The unrelated channel-warning residual is excluded.
- Learned-pin renewal retains September's loopback/Tailscale-only policy and strict configured pins. iOS retains its MainActor lifecycle, cancellation, backpressure, headset, and macOS paths.

## Evidence

- **Fresh independent review:** Codex AutoReview completed two full-delta passes through P2 with no actionable findings; all 140 staged files were covered and the source/index snapshots stayed identical (`e2aa84134937cae753d4cec1c73cc04a01f2056b`). Bundle-only review took 343.318 s; it does not claim execution or live-device qualification.
- **Owning/sibling proof:** 780 parent cases across 18 files pass in separate retained runs (563/15 + 182 reload + 35 migration/cutover). Independent newer-core proof passes 531 cases/19 files; the October tail passes 897/31, including 46 causal negative controls. These receipts overlap and are not summed as unique tests. The actual CLI MCP registration, manual/automatic compaction, pinned-DNS family behavior, approval and shutdown owners are exercised.
- **Types and static gates (production batch):** production core, all 27 core-test type graphs, UI and extension production/test graphs pass; all three Knip scans are empty. Line-cap, max-lines, assertion safety, formatting, config/docs, dependency, protocol, plugin boundaries, coercion, deprecation and UI-style gates pass without exception changes. The full core lint found one unused import, repaired and rechecked at its owning file; five unchanged file-length warnings remain.

<details>
<summary>Measured local test costs and repaired fixture failures</summary>

The 15-file parent owner run used the maintained Vitest wrapper with `--maxWorkers=1`: 460.382 s across ten project shards. The two-file migration/cutover replay took 281.160 s including transform/child-process overhead (120.34 s infra; 149.62 s CLI). Earlier integration exposed four September fixture/API mismatches; the actual September mock factories, imports and runtime contracts were repaired, retaining every assertion. The current owner replays pass. A full Knip scan found the retired private async migration receipt reader; it was removed after the consumer cutover, while the sync receipt projection and existing worker operation remain.

All 27 test type graphs took 263.170 s; production/UI/extension types took 9.924/11.234/13.171/18.258 s. These are local proof costs. The three test-only follow-ups have focused execution/lint/review evidence; all 27 core-test graphs were not rerun for those leaves. CI on `4963fe231ab` subsequently exposed the retained table fixture described below.

</details>

- **UI production and guards:** UI build/1066 finalized sidecars and hard performance budgets pass (17.321 s). Native schema, database-first storage, media helpers, sidecar loaders, import cycles, webhook, pairing-store and account-scope guards pass (428.328 s combined).

There are zero entrypoint/export additions or removals; all named export declarations/kinds are identical. The 123 reachable-only fingerprints reduce to three reviewed internal declaration changes: workspace forwarded through private session preparation, retirement of the unused private async receipt reader (sync worker operation retained), and equivalent private type-alias factoring. Final head `bd4e50d97cf1123cb30b646d7ff96d53b65c27dc` differs from the rendered `cb9b5d07f4af` source only in three excluded test fixtures: LM Studio timeout typing, September native-table metadata expectations, and retained projection-retry observations. - **Extension lint:** Full extension lint passes (211.414 s) after typing the single LM Studio timeout fixture; its three cases pass (125.712 s wrapper; 108.33 s Vitest including cold transform). The first SDK preparation attempt timed out at 300 s; the measured supported 900 s budget completed an 11,282-file emit, with no guards disabled. The maintained Bun-selected markdown run passes 72 cases/6 files (31.174 s); Telegram sibling proof passes 10 cases/1 file (5.023 s). Format and owning-file lint pass (149.724 s, including SDK preparation). The successful Bun run emitted a directory-mismatch diagnostic but no failed cases and exited 0. Fresh fixture-only Codex AutoReview is scoped-clean through P2 (69.273 s), with source/index unchanged at tree `c5bdef54b563e7932026bba120b8b318806a3aab`. - **Retained projection-retry fixture (CI follow-up):** [compact-large-22 on `667f46f9cc6`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38333998029/job/115090222935) failed an old one-wait assertion after the backport added foreground readiness before the writer claim. Formatting, the consuming `agents-other` type graph (9.6 s), owning-file lint (11.175 s), remaining guards, and all three empty Knip scans pass. Fresh staged-delta Codex AutoReview with owning production context is scoped-clean through P2 (83.736 s); it reviewed the supplied change/context, not the complete fixture or execution.

  The full local changed-check runner is **not green**: `deprecated-session-store-beta5-api` is past its `2026-10-12` removal date. The same guard fails on clean, untouched September base `d53dbcf7a09` (6.475 s), with identical registry/report inputs. No SDK retirement, date override, baseline exception, or production change was introduced. The runner's remaining planned checks were executed individually and pass. [Exact-head compact-large-22](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38348843007/job/115136720467) now passes the original 46-file selection: 835 cases pass / 2 skip, including the repaired case (632 ms in CI). The aggregate `pnpm build` passed asset preparation, ai/package declarations and runtime bundling. prs.title: feat(meta): add muse-image as a first-class image-generation provider
prs.body:
Closes #132228

## What Problem This Solves

The bundled `meta` provider ships Muse Spark text models but has no image capability, even though the Meta Model API serves muse-image on the same base URL and API key. Operators who authenticate with `MODEL_API_KEY` cannot generate or edit images through a first-class Meta path. The only workaround is pointing the `openai` image provider's `baseUrl` at `https://api.meta.ai/v1`, which takes over the OpenAI image slot, mislabels models in the catalog as `gpt-image-*`, and blocks using real OpenAI at the same time.

## Why This Change Was Made

Register a Meta image-generation provider on the existing `meta` plugin alongside the text provider, so `image_generate` can use `meta/muse-image-1.0` with the credentials already configured for Muse Spark.

- Switch `extensions/meta/index.ts` from `defineSingleProviderPluginEntry` to `definePluginEntry` (the multi-capability shape the bundled `openai` provider uses) and register the image provider via `registerImageGenerationProvider`. The text provider behavior is preserved exactly (api-key auth, live catalog, replay-family hooks, stream wrapping, thinking profile).
- Build the image provider on the shared `createOpenAiCompatibleImageGenerationProvider` factory against `POST /v1/images/generations` and `/v1/images/edits` (base64 WebP output), the same path `litellm` uses.
- Support single-reference editing. muse-image also supports conversational editing through the Responses API (`previous_response_id`), but that is a stateful session concept with no field in the stateless `image_generate` tool, so single-reference `/v1/images/edits` covers the "alter the previous image" case.
- Declare `contracts.imageGenerationProviders` and provider metadata in the manifest so the `image_generate` tool discovers it.
- `extensions/meta` was not routed by any vitest config, so its tests were not running; this adds it to the misc extension test roots.

No SQLite, config-schema, or new env-var surface is added. No CODEOWNERS-restricted paths are touched.

## User Impact

prs.title: fix(slack): render authored presentation text once across sends and edits
prs.body:
Closes #133135

## What Problem This Solves

Slack could repeat authored text already contained in a presentation, hide distinct formatting or code whitespace, and reject valid edits because text was duplicated or rendered twice. Structured replies also ignored the account's Markdown table setting even when ordinary text replies used it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Slack reply compiler renders presentation content first, then decides authored-text placement from its actual format-aware fragments. It compares both existing producer chunk plans without collapsing interior whitespace, inventing separators, or treating literal/plain-text fields as mrkdwn. Legacy separator matching respects complete formatting spans using the existing Slack tokenizer. Raw legacy metadata is used only before rendered facts exist; comparison never rewrites transport bytes.

Missing authored text is repacked through the same compiler, preserving raw-block → authored-text → presentation order, block limits, chart/table budgets, and control identifiers. Literal fallback fragments and individual context/section text objects remain separate until placement is decided; existing accessibility joins remain unchanged. Monitor and outbound delivery consume the same ordered message plan instead of duplicating assembly.

The existing channel/account Markdown policy now reaches that compiler from sends, edits, outbound presentation rendering, monitor replies, slash replies, previews, and stream eligibility/delivery tracking. Dispatch setup carries the prepared policy forward. Edits pass their prepared Slack text through private action context to the existing rendered-edit sender, so formatting and the 4,000-byte limit use exactly the bytes sent. Direct edit APIs still accept ordinary Markdown. The existing oversized-presentation fallback and native-block notification behavior are preserved.

The native scanner owns delimiter eligibility and complete formatting spans. One chunk writer keeps intended and emitted styles separate, emits transitions only with content, and reserves marker overhead plus pending whitespace. Chunk-edge spaces stay outside synthetic emphasis without losing bytes; empty native delimiters and intraword markers remain literal. A shared structured rich-text traversal records styles and link destinations for comparison while preserving prior plain table and escaped accessibility views. Native style spans must satisfy the shared content-edge/outside-flank policy and the renderer’s nesting contract. Native-only layouts/decorations, crossing or unrepresentable styles, opaque leaves, generated dates, and code containing an unrepresentable delimiter remain barriers: comparison cannot drop them or invent equivalent text. Styled link labels retain their exact whitespace. Code-styled links/references and metadata-bearing emoji are opaque comparison facts because literal tokens or aliases cannot preserve their native rendering. Ordinary alias-only emoji remains equivalent; accessibility/table fallback is unchanged. [Slack emoji contract](https://docs.slack.dev/tools/node-slack-sdk/reference/web-api/interfaces/RichTextEmoji/), [Slack link contract](https://docs.slack.dev/tools/node-slack-sdk/reference/web-api/interfaces/RichTextLink/).

Removed paths include premature raw-only materialization, a parallel edit renderer, post-render raw comparison, one-use fallback wrappers, duplicate monitor delivery assembly, duplicate rich-text readers, and the parallel plain-text native chunk path. Production: **+636/−638, net −2**. Tests and test support: **+1344/−131, net +1213** (including moved outbound test setup); assertion-safety bookkeeping is +1/−2. No new config, schema, protocol, public plugin SDK, dependency, or security-policy surface. Distinct authored text can require a second pure compilation to preserve one packing owner.

## User Impact

Structured sends and edits retain authored formatting, meaningful whitespace, and account table settings without adding duplicate visible text. Long native formatting remains balanced across transport chunks; rich-text content only suppresses authored text when its recorded formatting is equivalent.

## Evidence

- Exact candidate head: `f59c0692fa5d2ced0ff5ad3540d061711ac18645`.
- Frozen baseline: `3f1c84c706bf1e4c8bc7b2ab106ab96ff1fe6ddb`.
- Actual-sender regressions fail before the original repair. Every accepted subsequent source finding has an executed before reproduction; chunk and format failures were also reproduced through the compiled Gateway and recorded Slack HTTP boundary.
- Earlier native formatting proof: ten intended failures for long emphasis and rich-text styles, seven for opaque leaves/code delimiters/literal markers, and one mixed literal-prefix failure were captured before repair. The rich owner batch passes **163 tests across eight files**; the corresponding scanner batch passes **116 tests across three files**, with type-aware lint and the canonical assertion ratchet also green. These overlapping runs cover exact native transport bytes, rich-text style/link/layout boundaries, inbound mentions/accessibility, and data-table consumers.
- Earlier unchanged fragment-owner proof: **420 tests pass across eight files**, plus **46 action tests pass** after fixture typing corrections. Earlier account-policy proof passed **475 tests across eight files** and **111 action-runtime tests** in separate runs; moved outbound suites passed the same **64 cases** after splitting. These counts overlap and are not additive. These cover account policy, actions, actual outbound send/edit requests, compiler packing, formatting, monitor delivery, preview/stream fallback, and action admission.
- Account-policy regressions: ten intended failures across action send, direct/signed outbound, monitor, and slash delivery; five disabled-table controls. Two additional preview failures use the actual formatter. Four intended edit failures and two positive controls exercise the actual dispatcher → action runtime → `chat.update`. The repaired cases pass.
- Three monitor assembly controls now assert actual `chat.postMessage` text/blocks instead of an internal empty-text argument. They pass against both old and new assembly; media order, identity, metadata, threading, hooks, and receipts remain asserted.
- Original unescaped chart-list inputs remain negative equivalence cases: authored Markdown bullets differ from native/literal hyphens, so both remain visible. Escaped-list controls render equivalent bytes and deduplicate. Code whitespace, split formatting spans, plain-text headers/context, both long-code chunkers, and edit byte boundaries remain covered.
- Intra-block formatting regressions: four intended failures and two positive controls use the actual sender with raw context elements or section fields. Individually formatted text objects cannot be joined for equivalence; original blocks remain byte-identical while distinct authored text is preserved. [Slack text objects](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/block-kit/composition-objects/text-object/).
- Final 25-path changed-file gate: all 27 canonical stages pass in 336 seconds on this exact source, including production/test types, formatting, full plugin/script lint, dead exports, plugin boundaries, and runtime import cycles.
- Final writer regressions: four intended actual-sender failures cover empty/whitespace-edge emphasis, crossing styles, and exact link-label whitespace; a fifth covers nested intraword native styles. Empty native delimiter preservation also has three executed draft-regression failures and two literal controls. The repaired formatter/authored suites pass **103 tests**, including tiny limits and exact leading whitespace, plus scoped type-aware lint. These counts overlap earlier runs.
- Final native admission regressions: five intended actual-sender failures cover whitespace inside bold/italic/strike native spans and code styling on links/references; two further failures cover Unicode/custom-asset emoji metadata, with an ordinary alias control passing. The repaired eight-owner batch passes **186 tests** plus scoped type-aware lint. This is sender-boundary proof with dependency contract evidence, not live Slack UI rendering proof. Fresh whole-candidate autoreview and independent full-source challenge pass. The separate committed-head review is running against this exact commit.
- Canonical build and compiled 66-case Gateway `/tools/invoke` → message tool → Slack plugin → recorded mock Slack HTTP: pending final canonical build and execution; no prior artifact is counted as a pass for this head.
- Exact-head hosted CI: pending attachment to this pushed head.

**Not ready to merge:** separate committed-head review, canonical build, compiled Gateway proof, and required exact-head CI remain mandatory.

The Gateway fixture uses a mock provider and isolated state/workspace, with no live Slack credentials or operator Gateway. Crabline handles sends; a local `chat.update` extension validates the seeded channel/timestamp and records the real handler's text/blocks because the installed simulator lacks that endpoint. This is mock-Gateway proof, not a live Slack API claim. The final tool-flow cases cover default-code and account-bullets sends/edits; preview and stream decisions are exercised by the focused dispatcher suite.

A baseline source-Gateway attempt hit the strict 240-second startup cap before invoking the tool; it is not counted as a failed user action. Later source edit attempts were incomplete; a bounded loader profile identified synchronous source-import overhead. The canonical compiled flow uses the real CLI without a loader override or timeout increase. A malformed native-dialect fixture, an initial identity-chunker preview fixture, three invalid test fixture typings, and a leading-whitespace sender fixture above the existing presentation-normalization boundary were corrected; their failed artifacts are preserved separately and are not counted as product before-proof. The leading-whitespace assertion moved intact to the native chunker boundary; core normalization was not changed.

Hosted CI on an earlier head caught the same private callback type and invalid test fixtures as the local type gate; those are corrected without widening the public action context or weakening assertions.

ClawSweeper's recorded rank-ups require opaque crossing styles, exact link-label whitespace, no synthetic blank emphasis wrappers, and the final compiled send/edit trace. Those source repairs and the exact trailing-whitespace control are included; the current compiled trace and exact-head CI remain required before native preparation/merge. Introduction provenance is not inferred from shallow history.

Follow-ups: native-only rich-text layouts or decorations without a faithful mrkdwn projection remain opaque; broader semantic equivalence is not claimed. Native Block Kit edits intentionally retain authored top-level text as notification/accessibility content when it differs from visible blocks; the operator ambiguity merits separate product clarification. Slack's current table documentation allows 200 regular rows / 20,000 aggregate cell characters, while OpenClaw's conservative 100 / 10,000 limits remain unchanged. [Slack data-table contract](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/block-kit/blocks/data-table-block/).

prs.title: fix(gateway): honor plugin hardlink policy for Control UI browser assets
prs.body:
[AI-assisted]

## What Problem

Control UI plugin panels (e.g. Workboard) show "Plugin panel unavailable — Control UI assets could not be loaded. Build the plugin and reload its UI." on any host where the plugin's built browser assets are hardlinked. Every NixOS host with `nix.settings.auto-optimise-store = true` hits this, because the store dedupes identical files into hard links. Reported in #170409.

`readPluginControlUiAssets` (`src/plugins/control-ui-assets.ts`) always opened the plugin root with fs-safe `hardlinks: "reject"`. It never consulted `shouldRejectHardlinkedPluginFiles()` (`src/plugins/hardlink-policy.ts`), which since #129662 lets bundled plugins and `/nix/store` plugin roots in Nix mode load hardlinked files. The fs-safe error was then swallowed by a bare `catch {}` in `refreshBrowserCatalog`, so the panel showed the generic "Build the plugin" message even though the assets were present and built.

Reproduction (as filed): NixOS with `auto-optimise-store`, `OPENCLAW_NIX_MODE=1`, `stat -c '%h %n' <lib>/dist/extensions/workboard/dist/control-ui/*/index.js` → link count `3`; open `/workboard` → panel unavailable. A platform-independent repro also shows `plain copy: nlink=1 OK` vs `after one extra hard link outside the plugin: nlink=2 FAIL FsSafeError hardlink hardlinked path not allowed`.

## Why

The Gateway owns an authoritative plugin-provenance decision (`PluginRecord.origin` + `rootDir`), and a shared hardlink policy already exists for exactly this case. The Control UI browser-asset reader was simply not wired to it — the same class of bug as #114103 and #116594 (fixed by #129662 for other surfaces). The correct repair is to thread the owning plugin's trusted-root decision into `readPluginControlUiAssets`, keeping the strict default for every external caller.

**Security boundary (addressed).** The expanded admission is not a widening of the policy: `shouldRejectHardlinkedPluginFiles` returns `false` (allow) only for `origin === "bundled"` plugins and for `/nix/store` plugin roots when `OPENCLAW_NIX_MODE=1`. User/config/workspace roots still reject hardlinks, and the external CLI packing path (`buildPluginControlUi` via `plugins-feature-artifact.ts`) stays strict because it does not pass the option. Served bytes remain content-addressed and owner-bound: the HTTP path re-checks the live owner and authorization, and retiring the owner retires the assets (asserted below).

## User Impact

Bundled plugins and Nix-store plugin roots now load their panels when assets are hardlinked. User/config/workspace plugin roots keep rejecting hardlinks. When assets genuinely cannot be read, the underlying reason is now logged (`[control-ui] browser assets unavailable for plugin <id>: hardlink: hardlinked path not allowed`) instead of only the generic panel message.

## Evidence

`pnpm test src/gateway/control-ui-plugin-assets.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`

before the fix (reader still forces `hardlinks: "reject"`):

```text
 × |gateway-database-workers| control-ui-plugin-assets.test.ts > native Control UI browser assets > admits bundled hardlinked browser assets under the trusted-root policy
AssertionError: expected [] to deeply equal [ 'native-ui' ]
 Tests  1 failed | 19 passed (20)
```

after the fix (catalog admission + end-to-end Gateway HTTP serving + owner retirement + untrusted-root rejection):

```text
 ✓ |gateway-database-workers| control-ui-plugin-assets.test.ts > native Control UI browser assets > rejects symlink browser files outside their built owner 8ms
 ✓ |gateway-database-workers| control-ui-plugin-assets.test.ts > native Control UI browser assets > rejects hardlink browser files for untrusted plugin roots 11ms
 ✓ |gateway-database-workers| control-ui-plugin-assets.test.ts > native Control UI browser assets > admits bundled hardlinked browser assets under the trusted-root policy 8ms
 ✓ |gateway-database-workers| control-ui-plugin-assets.test.ts > native Control UI browser assets > serves hardlinked bundled browser assets end to end and retires them with the owner 16ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  21 passed (21)
```

End-to-end test specifics (`serves hardlinked bundled browser assets end to end and retires them with the owner`): builds a bundled plugin whose `dist/control-ui/index.js` is a hard link to another file in the plugin root, asserts the catalog advertises it, then starts the real authenticated Gateway HTTP server (`withGatewayServer`) and asserts the hardlinked asset is served `200` with the exact bytes, then disables the owning `PluginRecord` and asserts the same URL returns `404`.

`pnpm exec oxlint` and `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` on the touched files: 0 warnings, 0 errors, correct format.

Closes #170409.

prs.title: fix(imessage): check reply_to_guid in echo cache for paired mirror rows
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On iMessage, when Messages.app writes a paired inbound mirror row for an outbound message, the mirror carries a distinct GUID (`GUID-B`) but references the original outbound GUID (`GUID-A`) via `reply_to_guid`. The echo cache stores `GUID-A`, but `resolveInboundEchoMessageIds()` only collects the row id and `guid` — not `reply_to_guid`. The cache treats `GUID-B` vs stored `GUID-A` as conflicting identities, the marker-based reflection guard does not match ordinary text, and the mirror is dispatched as fresh inbound input — causing duplicate replies, recursive turns, and extra model usage.

Related to #135704

## Why This Change Was Made

`reply_to_guid` is already parsed and used for reply context (`describeReplyContext`), but was not consulted for echo identity. The fix adds a `replyToGuid` probe in `hasIMessageEchoMatch` that checks the echo cache with `reply_to_guid` as the lookup ID, using a new `requireMessageIdTextMatch` cache option that prevents the cache from short-circuiting on messageId equality alone. This ensures text must also match the same cached outbound entry, so legitimate inline replies with different body text are not dropped.

Key design decisions addressing ClawSweeper review findings:

1. **`requireMessageIdTextMatch` cache option** — Added to both in-memory (`DefaultSentMessageCache`) and persisted (`hasPersistedIMessageEcho`) cache layers. When set, a matching messageId is only sufficient when text also matches the same outbound entry.

2. **`guidTextCache` (keyed by `scope:guid:text`)** — Binds text to a specific outbound GUID. Without this, two outbound sends (A="Hello", B="Okay") would let an inline reply "Okay" referencing GUID-A match A's ID timestamp and B's text marker, causing a false-positive echo drop.

3. **Early echo probe before access/pairing** — Placed after basic row validation but before the access resolver, so paired mirrors from unpaired or blocked senders are suppressed as echoes rather than triggering pairing.

4. **Authored self-chat exclusion** — Early probe skips `is_from_me=true` rows; main echo probe suppresses `replyToGuid` when `isSelfChat` is true. Prevents authored self-chat rows from being misclassified as echoes.

5. **Self-chat limiter exemption** — Early probe returns `"self-chat echo"` reason (not `"echo"`) when either `isSelfChat` is true or `selfChatCache.has()` confirms a duplicate. The loop rate limiter exempts `"self-chat echo"` drops, preventing benign mirror bursts from suppressing legitimate conversation.

Changes:
1. **`extensions/imessage/src/monitor/inbound-processing.ts`** — `replyToGuid` parameter, early echo probe before access, `selfChatCache.has()` check for benign accounting, scoped cache probe with `requireMessageIdTextMatch`.
2. **`extensions/imessage/src/monitor/echo-cache.ts`** — `requireMessageIdTextMatch` option, `guidTextCache` for GUID-bound text matching.
3. **`extensions/imessage/src/monitor/persisted-echo-cache.ts`** — `requireMessageIdTextMatch` in persisted `has()`, text check on messageId match.
4. **`extensions/imessage/src/monitor/inbound-processing.reply-to-guid.test.ts`** — 5 regression tests using real `createSentMessageCache`.
5. **`scripts/proof-137834-reply-to-guid-echo.mjs`** — Real production-path proof exercising classifier + both cache layers.
6. **`scripts/proof-137834-limiter-boundary.mjs`** — Monitor boundary proof exercising limiter accounting contract.

## User Impact

iMessage deployments where Messages emits paired inbound mirror rows with `reply_to_guid` will no longer see duplicate agent replies or recursive turns from reflected outbound text. Legitimate inline replies (same parent GUID, different body text) remain unaffected and continue to dispatch normally. Mirror bursts do not trip the loop rate limiter.

## Evidence

### Changed files

- `extensions/imessage/src/monitor/inbound-processing.ts` — `replyToGuid` parameter, early echo probe, self-chat limiter exemption, scoped cache probe
- `extensions/imessage/src/monitor/echo-cache.ts` — `requireMessageIdTextMatch` option, `guidTextCache`
- `extensions/imessage/src/monitor/persisted-echo-cache.ts` — `requireMessageIdTextMatch` in persisted `has()`
- `extensions/imessage/src/monitor/inbound-processing.reply-to-guid.test.ts` — 5 regression tests
- `scripts/proof-137834-reply-to-guid-echo.mjs` — classifier + cache proof
- `scripts/proof-137834-limiter-boundary.mjs` — monitor boundary limiter proof

### Real Behavior Proof 1: Classifier + Cache (7/7 PASS)

Production-path proof exercising the real `resolveIMessageInboundDecision` with real `createSentMessageCache` (no mocks) and the real persisted echo cache (with iMessage runtime initialization). Script: `scripts/proof-137834-reply-to-guid-echo.mjs`.

## Notes

- The early `replyToGuid` echo probe runs after basic row validation (group without chat_id check) but before the access resolver, ensuring paired mirrors from unpaired or blocked senders are suppressed as echoes.
- The `requireMessageIdTextMatch` option ensures the cache does not short-circuit on messageId alone; text must be proven to come from the same outbound entry (`guidTextCache` for in-memory, `entry.text === text` for persisted).
- Self-chat limiter exemption covers both `isSelfChat=true` (with `destination_caller_id`) and `selfChatCache.has()` (without `destination_caller_id`) cases.
- This is a partial fix for the `reply_to_guid` identity gap. The reporter also mentions remembering an observed `is_from_me=true` concrete GUID when a send path did not return one — that is not addressed here and may warrant a separate change.

## Proof Limitations

The `handleMessageNow` function in `monitor-provider.ts:734` is a closure (not exported), so it cannot be called directly from a proof script. The echo cache is seeded through `createIMessageEchoCachingSend` (in `deliver.ts:123`) during outbound delivery, which requires the full agent dispatch chain (`runChannelInboundEvent` + bindings + agent runtime).

The two proof scripts exercise the real production functions that `handleMessageNow` calls:
- `resolveIMessageInboundDecision` — the real classifier with real `createSentMessageCache` and persisted echo cache
- `createLoopRateLimiter` — the real limiter with `record()` and `isRateLimited()` (the exact API used at `monitor-provider.ts:803` and `:849`)

The limiter boundary proof script (`scripts/proof-137834-limiter-boundary.mjs`) replicates the monitor's accounting contract from `monitor-provider.ts:800-804`:
```typescript
// monitor-provider.ts:800-803
const isLoopDrop = decision.reason === "echo" || decision.reason === "reflected assistant content";
if (isLoopDrop) { loopRateLimiter.record(rateLimitKey); }
// monitor-provider.ts:849
if (decision.kind === "dispatch" && loopRateLimiter.isRateLimited(rateLimitKey)) { return; }
```

This covers the limiter accounting logic without requiring the full agent dispatch chain. An e2e monitor test that seeds the echo cache through actual outbound delivery would require mocking `sendMessageIMessage`, `dispatchReplyWithBufferedBlockDispatcher`, `ensureConfiguredBindingRouteReady`, and the channel inbound debouncer — essentially the 1700-line fixture from `monitor.last-route.test.ts`.
