prs.title: fix(memory-wiki): avoid rescanning vault pages on repeated status
prs.body:
Fixes #170466

## What Problem This Solves

Repeated wiki status requests reopen every vault page even after the vault has been compiled.

## User Impact

Status reuses cached page and provenance counts. `wiki status`, `wiki doctor`, and `wiki bridge import` also accept `--timeout <ms>` and default Gateway requests to two minutes. Direct file edits become visible after `wiki compile` or the existing lifecycle refresh.

## Why This Change Was Made

This follows #170553, which already replaced full page summaries with bounded metadata parsing and closed the reported timeout issue. The remaining work is avoiding those reads on every request. Compilation seeds counts on the existing compiled-cache owner; cold activation computes missing provenance once, and a missing index gets one bounded metadata scan. Existing page writes and removals invalidate counts immediately, including when later cancellation or bookkeeping prevents compilation. Compilation, changed imports (including disabled auto-compile), and lifecycle refresh retain their invalidation behavior. Cache read errors retain vault-based counting so this optimization does not make status depend on cache availability.

No persisted cache format, database schema, RPC response, or configuration changes. Production changes are +193/-69 (net +124); count ownership, invalidation at existing page writers, and CLI timeout plumbing keep the persisted format unchanged. No unrelated cleanup was added to offset that growth.

## Evidence

PR CI is the test gate under the maintainer's 2026-10-13 proof policy. Live Gateway/Testbox proof was intentionally skipped; work already in progress was stopped when the policy changed.

Regression coverage in CI:

- `refreshes status counts when ingest is aborted after writing its page`: exercises the real ingest boundary and verifies that status counts the committed file after cancellation.
- `counts source provenance from the vault`: compares parsed and compiled counts, checks zero page reads after compilation and on repeated status, and verifies cold-reactivation provenance.
- `excludes malformed pages from status counts (#96125)`: preserves malformed-page exclusion and checks that a missing-index scan is cached.

prs.title: fix: preserve Doctor inventory links in update diagnostics
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing Doctor inventory links in failed-update diagnostics when a long detached report path and an existing error fill the diagnostic budget.

## User Impact

A rolled-back runtime can still open the complete Doctor findings and read their bounded receipt alongside the original failure. If an absolute inventory locator cannot fit at all, diagnostics retain the original cause and complete receipt and explicitly explain that the link is unavailable. The complete inventory remains on disk. Existing redaction, error, prompt, and artifact limits remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The writer appended the inventory link before the sanitizer reserved space for the Doctor receipt. The second truncation could cut into the link label. The sanitizer now reserves both together and truncates only the original error prose. An oversized locator produces a short unavailable explanation rather than aborting diagnostic publication. The released reader format and update/rollback decisions are unchanged.

## Evidence

On Linux, the original long-path regression failed on unchanged production code on both Node 24.21.0 and the pinned Bun runtime: four passing cases and the same missing-inventory-link failure per runtime. The additional oversized-locator regression failed on the preceding PR implementation on both runtimes: five passing cases and only the expected diagnostic-budget exception. With the final fix, all 16 focused cases passed on each runtime with identical case/status counts. The released-reader round trips verify readable inventories, complete receipts, original failures, redaction, size limits, retained inventory files, and copy identity.

| Complete test file | Node wall time | Pinned Bun wall time |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `triage-update-rollback.test.ts` (6 cases) | 6.34 s | 5.71 s |
| `triage-update.test.ts` (7 cases) | 4.20 s | 3.63 s |
| `update-failure-report-artifact.test.ts` (3 cases) | 5.48 s | 4.67 s |

The native runner retained two workers, four CPUs, the 8192 MiB heap limit, and existing test limits. Both runtime artifacts were hash-verified. QA preparation, formatting, and independent P2 review passed. Targeted lint passed with zero warnings or errors (14.60 seconds).

The first changed-check invocation used an outdated local baseline. The corrected staged invocation passed preliminary guards and production types, then stopped at an untouched stale import in `config-preflight-snapshot.test.ts` (TS2724). That failure was already repaired upstream in #170619, whose independent baseline reproduces it. The earlier PR-head CI passed all selected type, lint, and test jobs on a merge containing that fix (40 successful, 27 skipped jobs). That is prior-head evidence. Revised exact-head CI run 38349736893 passed with 40 successful and 27 expected skipped jobs on tested merge `2f36482336bd6eb9dfb1ed3415cc5bfd4f84caa9`, which also contains #170619. prs.title: fix(sessions): avoid redundant work during all-agent cleanup
prs.body:
Related: #170474

## What Problem This Solves

All-agent session cleanup repeatedly scans unchanged stores and starts reclamation workers, while its CLI can report a timeout even when the Gateway finishes successfully.

## User Impact

No-op cleanup does less work, and the CLI waits for the connected Gateway's cleanup result. Connection startup remains bounded. No new flags, configuration, migration, or retention changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Applied cleanup now classifies each store once, reuses its lifecycle receipt, and loads session payloads for artifact pruning only when artifacts exist. Maintenance with no explicit deletions uses the existing resident writer and commit kernel instead of a separate reclamation worker. Dry-run previews, physical-store identity checks, live authority checks, explicit deletion handling, and partial-result reporting remain covered. Offline cleanup retains a diagnostic dry-run only when a harness owner is unavailable, preserving the warning about native resources that could not be cleaned.

## Evidence

PR CI is the test gate under the current maintainer policy. Live Gateway and Testbox proof was intentionally skipped; the allocated Testbox was stopped before source upload. No final live performance claim is made.

Final exact-head [CI run 38346138644](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38346138644) passed: 47 successful jobs and 25 skipped jobs on `1a8ad505df8977e8ac7a1327059c80441ae25dbf`. The affected commands shard passed all 67 tests, including the five formerly failing unavailable-owner warning cases.

CI covers the cleanup command/client, storage maintenance, ownership, and recovery regressions, including:

- `does not materialize session payloads for a no-op cleanup in %s mode` (warn/enforce).
- `keeps maintenance without explicit mutations on the resident writer (cap=%s)` (no-op and actual cap enforcement).
- Existing offline harness-ownership tests cover disabled, globally disabled, denylisted, untrusted, and legacy owners, including their native-resource warnings.
- `lets delegated session cleanup finish beyond both passive-read deadlines` (31 seconds of fake time through the cleanup command).

Changed-file type-aware oxlint and oxfmt passed. The diff-scoped cleanup pass found no further behavior-neutral changes. Independent Codex review of the complete committed patch and the warning follow-up is clean through P2. GitHub review identified the unavailable-owner warning regression; the follow-up preserves that diagnostic and its existing regression coverage.

<details>
<summary>History and scope</summary>

The September lifecycle-projection-count round trip was introduced by #160858. Main already removed that round trip in #166822, but retained redundant apply-time previews, full payload reads, and maintenance-only reclamation handoffs. This change addresses those remaining costs and the separate CLI deadline.

The first CI run caught the warning regression and an unrelated missing-export type error in main. Both affected jobs passed on the final head after the warning fix and latest-main merge; no inherited-failure exception is used.

Production: 53 additions / 60 deletions (net -7). Tests: 184 additions / 50 deletions. Docs: 3 additions / 1 deletion. Earlier focused local checks completed before the policy override: 109 Gateway tests, 10 applied-summary tests, 16 readonly/fix-missing tests, and 23 worker/readonly tests passed. Additional local checks and live validation were stopped in favor of PR CI.

</details>

prs.title: perf(sessions): reduce observation writer requests
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session observation adds avoidable writer requests to each turn: digest and activity recap persistence prepare an entry patch and then queue a second command to commit it.

Related: #170171

## User Impact

Session observation uses fewer writer requests while retaining immediate preamble persistence, durable recap publication, and reconnect visibility. No schema, storage format, retention, SDK, or update migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move digest and recap predicates into the existing closed entry operations. Each operation reads the current row and merges its field within the existing writer transaction. Commit receipts alone mark an update accepted and publish it. FIFO ordering, input/output effect boundaries, transcript predicates, and durable acknowledgment ordering stay with the current writer owner.

Removed checks and accepted edges:

- The observer no longer rechecks run supersession after patch planning. It checks once before enqueue; an already queued same-lifecycle digest can briefly outlive its run until the next observation. Lifecycle and monotonic revision predicates still reject a reset or a newer digest.
- Recap persistence no longer sends a generic prepare request to reread the entry after model completion. The writer checks lifecycle, initialization, visibility, and transcript predicates against its current row; a rejected recap is marked stale.

## Profiling and measurements

The initial diagnostic at `d7be70250a4b2b3795ca4905ad0918447a06e156` used one 10-warmed-turn run on a 4-vCPU Testbox (99.13%/99.87% idle before/after). Session-writer service totaled 102.07 ms/turn. This selects the optimization; it is not the paired baseline.

The patch family cost 7 jobs and 25.08 ms/turn in that diagnostic, but those commands include callers beyond observation. Closed observation operations remove preparation without combining input admission and output publication. Same-row coalescing and transport overhead remain separate work.

Final paired baseline: `f9d5447c5946433d2a3fe63d299de3f93bb19fa9`. Candidate: `459659780f80bd0c19ab689e402eb2acb99ff9f5`. Main's worker reads and receipt-owned recap entries are integrated; no synchronous fallback is added.

Three alternating performance pairs (`M,C,M,C,M,C`) ran serially on the same 4-vCPU Testbox. The runner verified source trees and build receipts; every workload completed all 13 turns and 38 RPCs, including successful child, cron, compaction, shutdown, and restart checks. Pre-run host idle was 99.75–99.87%; candidate/base elapsed ratios were 0.971, 0.983, and 0.973. The post-workload idle observation was 1 second; no five-minute idle claim. Timing includes diagnostic instrumentation.

| Timing metric | Baseline | Candidate | Delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Session-writer service ms/turn, median [min–max] of three run means | 82.99 [76.21–86.75] | 75.28 [73.28–89.25] | −7.72 (−9.3%) |
| Warmed turn p50 / p95 ms, 30 turns | 276.45 / 439.57 | 275.33 / 418.32 | −1.12 / −21.25 |
| First chat delta p50 / p95 ms, 30 turns | 198.38 / 338.66 | 193.20 / 333.98 | −5.18 / −4.69 |
| `patch.prepare` jobs/turn | 3 | 2 | −1 |
| `patch.commit` jobs/turn | 4 | 4 | 0 |

Final paired command ranking, ordered by baseline median service (medians of three run means):

| Session-writer command | Jobs/turn, baseline → candidate | Service ms/turn, baseline → candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `session.actor.acceptInput` | 1 → 1 | 19.077 → 15.684 |
| `session.entry.patch.commit` | 4 → 4 | 16.343 → 16.897 |
| `session.actor.appendTranscriptEvent` | 2 → 2 | 12.401 → 11.999 |
| `session.actor.deliverySettled` | 2 → 2 | 6.397 → 6.430 |
| `session.entry.read` | 4.1 → 4.1 | 6.217 → 6.377 |
| `session.actor.completeTurn` | 1 → 1 | 5.808 → 5.964 |
| `session.lifecycle.project` | 1 → 1 | 4.678 → 4.344 |
| `session.entry.patch.prepare` | 3 → 2 | 3.706 → 2.608 |
| `session.actor.read` | 1 → 1 | 3.433 → 2.477 |
| `session.actor.adoptRun` | 1 → 1 | 3.249 → 2.813 |

Window-overlap counts can include background reads; component medians do not necessarily sum. The unchanged command timing deltas are observations, not savings attributed individually to this change.

The performance traces also contain shutdown-only failed `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` attempts: baseline `[1,1,1]`, candidate `[0,1,0]`; no warmed-window SQL failures. These existing shutdown diagnostics are not claimed fixed here.

The −40 ms service aim was not reached. Service here is diagnostic dispatch-to-reply duration, clipped to warmed windows, not SQL CPU or an equivalent wall-time saving. The third timing pair regressed; the pooled change is a modest observed improvement, not a guaranteed latency claim. Causal counts below establish the removed work independently of timing.

Three further alternating pairs used the unchanged shared SQL harness v2.1 on a second 4-vCPU Testbox at the same verified source pins. All six completed 13 turns and 37 RPCs, including child/cron/compaction and clean shutdown; pre-run idle was at least 99.625%, and elapsed candidate/base ratios were 1.004, 1.013, and 1.002. Timing and causal-count series are separate. The first causal attempt stopped before Gateway startup because the task launcher omitted the collector's routing module; the replacement included the complete collector. No product change or performance rerun was needed.

Counts below are median [min–max] of three runs; warmed rows divide each run's ten warmed turns. “Causal” follows originating turns across timing windows; “raw” includes background work occurring inside the window.

| Count metric | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Warmed causal all-thread statements/turn | 176 [176–182.6] | 175 [175–175] |
| Warmed causal requests/turn | 42 [42–42.5] | 41 [41–41] |
| Warmed raw all-thread statements/turn | 200.8 [200.8–207.5] | 199.8 [199.8–199.8] |
| Warmed raw requests/turn | 55.3 [55.3–55.9] | 54.3 [54.3–54.4] |
| Warmed MAIN statements/turn, causal and raw | 0 [0–0] | 0 [0–0] |
| First-turn causal all-thread statements | 418 [361–428] | 427 [416–430] |
| First-turn causal requests | 79 [79–80] | 78 [77–79] |
| First-turn causal MAIN statements | 37 [37–37] | 37 [36–37] |
| First-turn raw all-thread statements | 1,013 [903–1,119] | 1,104 [992–1,160] |
| First-turn raw requests | 173 [172–175] | 174 [172–179] |
| First-turn raw MAIN statements | 46 [37–46] | 45 [37–46] |
| Raw boot + connect + first statements | 2,891 [2,818–2,906] | 2,892 [2,892–2,907] |
| Raw boot + connect + first requests | 286 [285–287] | 285 [283–286] |
| Whole-workload all-thread statements | 6,545 [6,541–6,561] | 6,535 [6,534–6,547] |
| Whole-workload requests | 1,237 [1,235–1,238] | 1,223 [1,218–1,224] |
| Whole-workload MAIN statements | 829 [829–829] | 829 [827–829] |

The warmed patch family changes from 28 to 27 statements and 7 to 6 requests: prepare drops from 6 statements/3 requests to 4/2; commit changes from 22/4 to 23/4. The closed operation performs its current-row reduction inside the commit job. Whole-workload prepare drops 30 statements and 15 requests, while commit adds 15 statements and no requests; the combined patch family saves 15 statements and 15 requests by median.

First-turn counts increase in this sample and are not claimed cheaper overall. Comparing the runs supplying the raw medians, the +91 statements decompose into unchanged background memory-schema/strict admission +82, canonical-definition validation +6, other background +5, and changed entry reads −2. The memory/strict group executes exactly 635 statements across boot + connect + first and 636 across the whole workload in every one of the six runs: its first-window increase is phase placement. Combined-window totals are baseline `[2818,2891,2906]`, candidate `[2907,2892,2892]`; the median +1 is canonical validation +6, quarantine-version lookup −1, background transaction steps −2, and entry reads −2.

The causal first-turn +9 uses different median representatives: the changed patch family saves 2 statements, while an existing anchor/hydration/history chain contributes 10 more and an ingress lookup contributes 1. Native stacks identify `readAnchors`/`readSessionTranscriptAnchorFactsInDatabase` and `assertAgentIngressOpen`/`admitChatSend`; these paths also vary in the baseline. Causal first requests fall by 1. These decompositions explain the sampled median rows, not independent treatment estimates. Under the campaign's attribution rule, the consistent warmed saving, unchanged shared families, cheaper changed operation, and lower whole-workload counts support landing without another pair.

Prepare/commit send sites are directly attributed. The broader patch-wrapper classifier remains incomplete for unrelated message-rewrite/lifecycle-project requests (baseline `[43,44,44]`, candidate `[44,44,44]`); those requests remain in total counts and are not silently assigned to this patch. Shared-family attribution below is independently complete.

Shared read families, causal statements per warmed turn:

| Family | Baseline median [range] | Candidate median [range] |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Exact-entry facts | 4 [4–4.1] | 4 [4–4] |
| Actor hydration | 1 [1–1.1] | 1 [1–1] |
| Entry-cache snapshot loads | 0 [0–0] | 0 [0–0] |
| Row facts | 0 [0–0] | 0 [0–0] |
| Watermark reads | 1 [1–1] | 1 [1–1] |

All five families have complete source/stack attribution and zero MAIN calls in these warmed turns. No family rises. Legacy window counts include 0.3 background snapshot loads and 2 watermark reads per turn on both revisions.

## Evidence

After the coordinator lifted the merge hold, merged main `ae76b06c149232245f1002c34f7d8137bca75461` without conflicts into `f5f652ec9bd24f2aecd2c3ce62c5e61576a016b3`. The PR diff retains the measured patch ID (`66e34ced4d409bfcf3bd5aefb98723abde828908`); main's activity-summary entry projection is preserved. Changed-file formatting, lint, and `git diff --check` pass on this integration. [Final-head PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38351088533) passed with 62 successful jobs, 22 skipped, and no failures (618 seconds). Required aggregate and security checks also passed. The PR-context check initially required the existing validation section to be titled `Evidence`; that heading is corrected and the check passes. No measurements or local test suites were repeated under the compute-conservation rule.

[Measured-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38326944942) passed on `459659780f80bd0c19ab689e402eb2acb99ff9f5`: 61 successful jobs, 22 skipped, no failures; elapsed span 602 seconds. Production/test types, lint, source contracts/export collisions, architecture and ratchet checks passed. Both CodeQL analyses and OpenGrep also passed on that commit. The earlier HTTPS fixture and Bun agent-deletion failures did not recur; this PR does not claim to fix their causes.

Formatting, changed-file lint, and diff checks pass. Both permitted Codex review rounds found no actionable P0–P2 defects; the subsequent merge of main only resolved conflicts while preserving main's worker reads and receipt-owned recap entries. The completed earlier ClawSweeper review reported no findings.

The [remote proof run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38332271331) passed all recorded gates at the measured candidate: `check:changed` (1,838.87 s, including production/test types, type-aware changed-file lint, source contracts, Knip, and worker/dialect ratchets), Madge (16.73 s), and the explicit paired database-worker inventory (89.77 s). T1 calls are **0 → 0** in the observer/activity-summary/entry-patch owner scope and in the changed files; repository-wide T1 remains 456 → 456 on this measured base.

Each changed test ran as `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`: observer model 32.28 s, observer persistence worker 22.03 s, and row-change Gateway 26.64 s. The relevant Gateway siblings passed in 135.87 s and entry-owner siblings in 47.07 s. The timing proof ran separately in [this Testbox run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38328013395).

Both proof machines were stopped after collection. The Testbox workflow can show cancelled after explicit lease cleanup; the native run completion and recorded gate exits are successful.

New fault-injection coverage exercises queued digest revision changes, preservation of concurrent metadata, one command without a prepare request, and exactly-once publication after a lost worker reply. Existing recap regressions cover queued initialization, lifecycle, utility-model, visibility, and transcript changes.

Final scope: 14 files, +251/−199 lines; production code +19 net lines for the closed operation variants and shared predicates. No SDK surface, schema, migration, update, Doctor, plugin-loading, or service-lifecycle change; those conditional proof cells do not apply.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes rapid Matrix preview updates when more text arrives during a slow send or edit: the next background update could bypass the 1,000 ms throttle.

## User Impact

Preview updates stay paced. Final text still flushes without an added throttle delay.

## Why This Change Was Made

Enable the existing `coalesceInFlight` option in Matrix, as Discord and Slack already do.

## Evidence

Real transport replay uses the production draft adapter, OpenClaw `MatrixClient`, matrix-js-sdk, and isolated Synapse 1.162.0 with real clocks. A proxy holds genuine send responses for 2,500 ms while newer text is queued; no send helpers are mocked.

Redacted trace: elapsed milliseconds from releasing the delayed response to the next HTTP PUT. Final delivery calls `stop()` while the request is in flight.

| Mode | Delayed request | Background update | Final flush |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| partial | create | 1020.6 ms | 21.0 ms |
| partial | edit | 1025.0 ms | 8.0 ms |
| quiet | create | 1022.9 ms | 9.8 ms |
| quiet | edit | 1010.4 ms | 10.1 ms |

All eight scenarios passed. HTTP 200 responses and server event readback verified the latest text, `m.replace` targeting the original event, correct `m.text`/`m.notice`, final live-marker removal, and ignored late updates.

PR head `637689e38959` matches the tested tree `f2f7ab281d41`: 20 draft tests and 95 caller/lifecycle tests passed, alongside extension production/test typechecks, focused lint, and formatting. Four throttle cases fail without the fix. The prior-head Matrix CI also passed all 20 draft cases (job: 162.79 s). Cold local draft command: 185.53 s; transforms dominated.

## What Problem This Solves

## Why This Change Was Made

prs.title: fix: keep ordinary tests from reaching GitHub
prs.body:
Thanks for maintaining OpenClaw. This arose while running ordinary development tests in my OpenClaw fork.

Related: https://github.com/huntharo/openclaw/pull/25

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: ordinary development tests can dispatch GitHub requests through real transports or child commands and consume the developer's quota.

## User Impact

Ordinary tests block and count attempted GitHub access before dispatch, strip ambient credentials from test children, and report unexpected attempts even when a test catches the rejection. Live access requires the explicit live-test entry point; ambient live flags, real-home settings, and sourced profiles do not enable it.

**Validation is partial: the ordinary full suite did not complete or pass.** Remaining fixture incompatibilities and infrastructure failures are recorded below. Opaque native programs are outside the JavaScript guard's complete coverage; the audit also used a macOS external-IP egress fence.

## Why This Change Was Made

The guard covers fetch and redirects, HTTP/S, sockets, Undici, Chromium, and child `gh`/`git`/shell entry points. Bounded attribution separates deliberate negative controls from unexpected refusals. Repository-native execution and isolated test state are retained.

The first commit, `737d17f18f21` (originally `ca65e0809d5`), records the tripwire and partial audit before fixture repairs. The second commit, `78071a59e1c9` (originally `4542b906594`), repairs the exposed local fixtures: Node executable selection, local Git remotes, scripted release CLI placement, optional Git directories, shell admission compatibility, and the UI configuration assertion.

## Evidence

### Base alignment for the store PR stack

The two commits were rebased onto exactly `83b5f5425eab6021ff03104c9de1b4826f0c3d97`. Current head: `78071a59e1c97fa8b0573ca4cf6e540bfeeae32d`; proof-first commit: `737d17f18f21731763a7d6d749b1a4449a104fb3`. The rebase needed no conflict resolution. The only additional source edit corrects the UI configuration test to require the Node-only guard setup for Node projects and exclude it from browser projects; it is included in the second commit. The original guard and fixture changes retain identical added/deleted source lines.

| Validation on the aligned base, external-network fence retained | Result | Wall time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Four guard files and three release-fixture files | 160 passed, 4 platform skips; 0 unexpected attempts, 120 deliberate controls, 0 raw attribution omissions (5 control attributions omitted only from the bounded display) | 53.48 s |
| UI package/E2E configuration tests | Before correction: 65 passed, 1 stale setup-file assertion failed. After: 66 passed, 0 unexpected attempts | 48.02 s after correction |
| Crabbox executable selection (2), fork publication handoff, catalog performance, local submodule checkout | All 5 selected cases passed; 313 unrelated cases filtered; 0 unexpected attempts | 125.29 s |
| Native changed-file check for the UI assertion | Structural, formatting, and root-test typechecks passed; unused-export scan failed | 172.98 s |
| Direct native lint of the changed UI test | Passed | 11.91 s |
| Fresh independent P0/P1 review of the assertion delta | Complete, scoped-clean; 0 actionable findings | 20.09 s |

**The current changed-file gate is not green.** Its unused-export scan reports `captureSessionEntryMaintenanceAgeFact`, `SessionEntryMaintenanceAgeCapture`, `SqliteReclamationPreparedSource`, `GatewayApprovalEventPublisherV2`, `OpenClawAgentDatabaseWorkerCloseResult`, and (full-tree scan) `reconnectGateway`. Their defining files are byte-identical to the selected base, and none of these symbols appears in this branch's diff. A separate baseline scan was not run. The check stopped before its remaining lint steps; file-scoped lint was run separately. No unrelated exports were removed or ignored.

Dependencies were restored with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline` in this workspace under the external-network fence. No full suite or audit recovery was restarted. **All first-stage audit counts and gaps below are historical evidence from before this rebase, not full-suite results on the aligned head.**

### Historical audit and original scoped validation


The first-stage audit used native `pnpm test`, continue-on-failure, isolated state, explicit live flags unset, retained native JSON/count reports, and an external-IP fence. Separate recovery invocations are not represented as a single completed full run. Local validation used the branch based on `dd1c1354350e`. The unchanged head `4542b9065941` merges cleanly with upstream `main` at `5fac9ea90ecc`; the merged tree has not been tested. The results below are local branch evidence, not current-upstream CI results.

| First-stage evidence | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Original ordinary-suite plan | 643 invocations across 96 configurations; 569 native reports retained across the original run and separate recoveries |
| Settled UUID counters across those invocations | 20,609 non-control refusals; 119 deliberate controls; 230 omitted raw attributions remain unknown |
| Confirmed blocked GitHub-bound attempts | **4**: two Crabbox managed-release downloads, one worker origin fetch, and one fork-publication upstream fetch |
| Confirmed local fixture refusals | **17,331** pre-fix scripted release CLI refusals; the fixture relocation in the second commit resolved these, and all 44 affected release tests subsequently passed |
| Earlier interrupted attempt, counted separately | 244 non-control refusals; 52 controls; 0 omitted attributions; no confirmed incidental GitHub destination |

Counters measure refusals, not sent requests or unique tests. The four destination attempts were blocked. No GitHub API traffic or quota consumption is claimed from these test runs.

The original full invocation stopped after 65 finished plans on a resource-completion error in plan 66, which has native JSON. Recovery plan 301 has no JSON after the native watchdog; plan 569 has JSON but no final process/resource receipt. Plan 571 was stopped after the prolonged Gateway batch, and plans 572–643 were not started. The owned worker sample showed high CPU, approximately 1.2 GiB RSS, and V8 compilation/deserialization/filesystem activity; it does not establish an application deadlock. All recorded owned processes were confirmed gone after the stop. No full-suite aggregate is available.

| Scoped validation (`pnpm test … --maxWorkers=1`, guard and fence retained) | Result | Wall time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New lowercase JavaScript `env` regression against first-commit helper | Expected failure: one `unresolved-shell-environment` refusal | 12.75 s |
| Four guard test files after the shell fix | 116 passed, 4 platform skips; 0 unexpected refusals, 120 deliberate controls | 37.61 s |
| Two Crabbox download-trigger cases and fork-publication case | All 3 selected cases passed | Included in the 468.27 s destination selection |
| Worker identity/checkout case in that selection | Failed: branch and synthetic remote matched, but the expected synthetic `GH_CONFIG_DIR` profile was stripped; 2 separate shell-startup refusals remained. Local fetch succeeded with no GitHub-bound attempt reported. | Included in the 468.27 s destination selection |
| Release fixture files + catalog performance + merge outcome + retention + browser probe | 44 release tests and the catalog performance test passed; 60 merge-outcome tests still failed on shell-PATH admission. The first retention probe selected ambient mise and attempted a shell snapshot; the corrected fixture passed in the final selection below. The browser probe lost standalone mode, so that fixture change was withdrawn. | 277.05 s |
| Final retention/submodule/watcher selection | All 6 selected tests passed; 0 unexpected refusals, 0 controls, 0 omissions | 45.47 s |
| Native changed check for the second commit | Passed: structural ratchets, typechecks, three unused-export scans, core/scripts/test lint | 631.98 s |
| Fresh independent P0/P1 review of the second commit | Complete, scoped-clean; 0 actionable findings in the supplied delta and evidence | 51.08 s |

The worker identity case was moved into the existing sibling GitHub suite to satisfy the line-count rule without removing assertions. After the passing retention run, the mock was mechanically changed to preserve the real module exports as required by the mock-export rule; the two mocked functions are unchanged.

Guard snapshots retain all raw control attributions in the scoped passing run (0 raw omissions); the final reporter omitted 5 control attributions from its bounded aggregate display. These display omissions are separate from the 230 raw omissions in the first-stage audit. No CI execution or CI timing is claimed.

Remaining ordinary-suite gaps include conservative shell admission refusals, detached fixture executables under `.artifacts`, loopback HTTP Git/redirect fixtures, Chromium initial app navigation, and OS-fence restrictions affecting process inspection. These failures have not been masked or converted into expected passes. 


The fork PR's only failing hosted check was Labeler: its GitHub App private-key secret was unavailable. That is repository configuration, not a test failure; no rerun or code workaround was used.

### Upstream conflict integration — October 12

Commit `67384cb18dd9c917719e88405eec5e45469765c0` merges upstream `70bfdc2b58e42f02af5bdc4d345875a9e6ad3928` while preserving the original proof-first and fixture-second commits. The only manual conflict resolution retains `githubNetwork: "live"` in upstream's revised live-test launcher lifecycle. Dependency manifests and the lockfile match that upstream base.

Validation on the merged tree, using Node 24.21.0:

- The live-launcher tests and four guard test files passed: 128 tests passed, four platform skips, zero failures, in 15.09 seconds. The external-network fence remained active; counters recorded zero unexpected attempts, 120 intentional negative controls, and zero omitted attributions.
- The selected native changed check passed in 136.84 seconds, including structural rules, script typechecking, unused-export scans, and selected lint. The staged comparison uses the exact incoming base. Knip's pinned dependencies were prepared with network access before the fenced check.
- Fresh integration review completed with zero actionable P0/P1 findings (206.07 seconds).

This is scoped integration validation. The historical full-suite audit remains incomplete as documented above; no full-suite rerun or current-head CI success is claimed.

### Runner integration — October 13

Commit `61c17e1255dd30329950855edeef6635fb0ebfd6` merges upstream `cd32ddcdbd875c3d6a9f46ee9a926bc198719bea` without rewriting the original proof and fixture commits. The conflict resolution retains upstream's shared CLI bootstrap and infrastructure-error exit classification while preserving the GitHub guard around execution. The copied-CLI fixture now includes the guard preload and command transport in its existing runtime dependency collection; its assertions and guard policy are unchanged.

Scoped validation used Node 24.21.0 and the external-network fence for tests:

- Runner outcome tests: 64 passed. Guard tests: 116 passed, four platform skips. Counters recorded zero unexpected attempts, 120 intentional controls, and zero raw attribution omissions (five controls omitted only from the bounded display).
- The initial copied-launcher run exposed 29 fixture failures. Adding the preload exposed the missing transport in 27 cases; after both runtime entrypoints were included, all 62 bounded-launcher cases passed in 63.14 seconds, with zero unexpected attempts. No assertions were removed or relaxed.

Its findings concern 12 files byte-identical to the incoming base, including the reporter default export consumed through an unchanged computed module URL, memory/session exports, and UI exports. These findings remain unresolved and disclosed. The remaining selected checks, including lint, passed in 129.43 seconds with only that already-recorded scan omitted through the checker's advertised option. This is not an unqualified passing full check.

prs.title: fix(gateway): run CLI bridge tool calls in their own run's request scope
prs.body:
## Current disposition — October 11, 2026

The implementation in this PR has been incorporated into main by [#165432](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165432), commit `fdcbcf5c2ebd83316f411d406315f08225949c59`, which credits Amrit Chana and adapts this PR's authority-chain regression. There is no remaining production fix to merge from this branch.

Current main uses a detached process context for listener startup, retains the Gateway's worker resources, records each grant's minting request scope, and restores that scope for its tool calls. Its HTTP coverage checks starter isolation, fresh replacement scopes, allowed owner dispatch, the write-only ceiling, closed requester refusal, and revoked-grant rejection.

Fresh verification on main `cbe0b272883c68210aee33b67e4bdf66d9106587`: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/mcp-http.async-scope.test.ts` passed **6/6 tests** on macOS/Node 24.16.0. Vitest reported **221.45 s**, including cold transformation. This was HTTP/in-process authority boundary proof, not a new live Claude or channel test. No production or test changes were needed.

The v2026.10.1 tag predates the merged detached-context implementation, so the release-pinned follow-up remains relevant to that tag. The original branch's old CI/conflict state is historical; rebasing it would duplicate the implementation and weaker coverage already on main. This PR remains open and non-draft for maintainer disposition; no merge or closure was requested or performed.

---

## Original contributor proposal and historical evidence

Closes #157126

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after a Gateway restart that resumes an in-flight CLI-runtime turn (for example `claude-cli`), the owner's later chat turns fail admin-only tools with `missing scope: operator.admin` until the Gateway restarts again. The same leak also breaks a second owner turn once the first turn's connection has closed (`Gateway client authority closed before dispatching ...`).

## User Impact

User impact: owners of CLI-runtime agents keep their normal tool authority after a restart. Admin-only tools (automations with triggers, secrets, system and config tools) work from chat again. Lower-authority runs keep their own ceiling: the write-only restart-recovery run is still refused admin tools, and a run whose device was revoked mid-turn is still refused before its action. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The loopback MCP listener is process-owned but starts lazily inside whichever Gateway request first needs it. Its handlers kept that request's scope and tool-caller identity. So every bridge tool call ran with the authority of whichever run started the listener, not the run making the call. If the restart-recovery continuation (a write-only system caller) started it, every later owner call was capped at `operator.write`.

The fix has two parts:

1. **The listener no longer inherits its starter.** It starts outside the tool-caller identity (`withoutGatewayToolCallerIdentity`) and outside the request scope (`withPluginRuntimeGatewayContextResolver(..., { inheritRequestScope: false })`), keeping only the Gateway context resolver. This matches the rule already applied to follow-up and scheduled runs.
2. **Each bridge call runs in its own run's request scope.** A CLI client grant now records the Gateway request scope it was minted in (`mintMcpLoopbackClientGrant`, called while the run's request is active), and the handler re-enters that scope for the grant's tool calls. That is what in-process runtimes already get implicitly, so dispatch sees the calling run's own client: its scopes stay the ceiling, and its `hasCurrentClientAuthority` liveness still applies.

Part 1 alone would have removed the accidental ceiling without restoring the intended one. With no scope, a write-only recovery run and a revoked run both completed an admin-only call in live testing. Part 2 is why those runs are still refused (see the proof below).

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

**Setup.** This PR's branch at `3ff6fbe1d78`, built, running as an isolated foreground Gateway (`openclaw --profile <test> gateway run`, loopback, its own state dir, clean environment). macOS arm64, Node v26.8.2, OpenClaw `2026.9.6 (3ff6fbe)`. Agent `main` runs `claude-cli/claude-sonnet-5`. Owner turns come from `openclaw agent --agent main` on a local CLI device paired with `operator.admin` (`senderIsOwner: true`). The admin-only action is the `secrets` tool with `action: "list"` (`secrets.store.list`, needs `operator.admin`). Heartbeat, Bonjour, and dreaming are off, so no other system run can start the bridge first.

Steps:
1. **step0**: owner turn on a fresh Gateway calls `secrets` list.
2. **step0b**: a second owner turn in the same process.
3. **step1**: an owner turn runs a 90 s probe script, then calls `secrets` list. Mid-probe the Gateway is restarted (`gateway restart --wait 5s`). The drain runs out, the turn is marked for recovery, and the restart-recovery continuation (a write-only system caller) is the first CLI run after startup, so it starts the bridge. It then calls `secrets` list itself.
4. **step2**: after recovery settles, a new owner turn calls `secrets` list.
5. **step3** (fresh Gateway process): an owner turn runs the probe, and 5 s in the owner device's operator token is revoked (`devices revoke --role operator`, connection closed `4001 device removed`). After the probe, the run calls `secrets` list.

Results are the exact tool results the agent received, from the Claude Code stream in the Gateway log and `chat.history`. The "unpatched" column is the same checkout with `src/gateway/mcp-http.ts` reverted to `6907f58b136` (upstream main) and rebuilt. "Part 1 only" is this PR's first commit, `3b3536613b4`.

| Step | Caller | Unpatched main | Part 1 only | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| step0 | owner | `The secret store is empty.` | `The secret store is empty.` | `The secret store is empty.` |
| step0b | owner, 2nd turn | `Gateway client authority closed before dispatching secrets.store.list.` | `The secret store is empty.` | `The secret store is empty.` |
| step1 | restart recovery (system, write-only) | `missing scope: operator.admin` | `The secret store is empty.` | **`missing scope: operator.admin`** |
| step2 | owner, after recovery | `missing scope: operator.admin` | `The secret store is empty.` | **`The secret store is empty.`** |
| step3 | owner, device revoked mid-run | `Gateway client authority closed before dispatching secrets.store.list.` | `The secret store is empty.` | **`Gateway client authority closed before dispatching secrets.store.list.`** |

On unpatched main, step1 and step3 are refused only because each of those runs happened to start the bridge itself. On this PR they are refused by their own run's scope, whichever run started the listener.

Restart and recovery on this PR (Gateway log, local time, redacted):

```text
17:37:19.641 mcp loopback listening on <loopback>:<port>
17:37:56.086 [gateway] received SIGUSR2; restarting
17:38:01.088 [gateway] restart drain budget 4999.5ms exhausted; cutting short queueSize=1 embeddedRuns=1 activeTasks=1 sessionAdmissions=2 rootRequests=1
17:38:01.129 [main-session-restart-recovery] marked 1 interrupted main session(s) for restart recovery (gateway restart shutdown)
17:38:05.456 mcp loopback listening on <loopback>:<port>
17:38:05.460 [main-session-restart-recovery] started interrupted main session: agent:main:main
```

`secrets` tool results on this PR, in order (step0, step0b, recovery, step2):

```text
"tool_result","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The secret store is empty."
"tool_result","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The secret store is empty."
"tool_result","content":"missing scope: operator.admin","is_error":true
"tool_result","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The secret store is empty."
```

The refused call belongs to the recovery turn: in `chat.history` it follows the `[System] Your previous turn was interrupted by a gateway restart ...` continuation message, and step2's owner turn after it succeeds.

step3 on this PR (device revoked mid-run):

```text
17:41:27.494 [gateway] device token revoked device=<device-id> role=operator
17:41:27.495 [ws] → close code=4001 reason=device removed ... lastFrameMethod=agent
17:42:54.300 [agent/cli-backend] cli turn: provider=claude-cli model=claude-sonnet-5 durationMs=102068
"tool_result","content":"Gateway client authority closed before dispatching secrets.store.list.","is_error":true
```

**Differences from the issue's scenario.** Owner turns come from the local CLI (`openclaw agent`, a device with `operator.admin`), not Control UI webchat. The restart is the supported foreground restart (`gateway restart --wait 5s`, in-process SIGUSR2 with a 5 s drain), not a LaunchAgent handoff. The admin-only tool is `secrets` list only.

### Tests

- `src/gateway/mcp-http.async-scope.test.ts`:
  - "does not retain the Gateway caller of the request that started it": the listener started inside a write-only request scope and a tool-caller identity; a later owner-token call sees neither, and the Gateway context resolver is preserved. Fails before part 1.
  - "runs each CLI grant's tool calls in the request scope that minted it": the listener is started under a write-only recovery scope; grants minted under an owner scope, under the recovery scope, and under no scope each see exactly their own client (`[owner, recovery, undefined]`). Fails without part 2 (`[undefined, undefined, undefined]`).
- `pnpm vitest run src/gateway/mcp-http src/gateway/mcp-grant-store src/agents/cli-runner/prepare`: 275 of 276 pass. The one failure, `mcp-http.keepalive.test.ts` › "keeps a GET notification stream alive and releases it during shutdown", fails identically on unmodified `origin/main` at `6907f58`.
- `pnpm check:changed`: passes (exit 0).
- Autoreview (Codex), `--mode branch --base origin/main --max-priority P2`: `scoped-clean`, "patch is correct" (0.78). Its sandbox could not read unchanged files or run tests; the tests above ran locally.

prs.title: fix: preserve speech-only replies through heartbeat delivery and replay
prs.body:
Fixes #170027
Fixes #170062

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a speech-only heartbeat can disappear before synthesis, and a stored spoken answer can disappear from later model context, making an already answered request look unanswered.

## User Impact

Explicit speech-only heartbeat replies reach the speech synthesis and delivery path under the existing target, visibility, and TTS settings. Later OpenAI Completions turns see the actual spoken answer. No placeholder text, new configuration, protocol changes, or transcript rewrites are introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Canonical speech is kept in delivery metadata while visible text is empty. Shared payload recognition now treats that speech as pending content, heartbeat classification preserves its metadata, and final dispatch permits explicit heartbeat speech through TTS while preparation retains the known destination for channel-appropriate audio. Result classification no longer retries a valid speech-only completion as empty. Shared replay normalization projects the spoken words into the model's in-memory history when there is no written answer or tool call.

Original fix by @ericcurtin; maintainer cleanup folds the replay helper into the existing normalizer, removes the new test casts, and completes heartbeat delivery coverage. The contributor's original commits remain in this branch.

## Evidence

PR CI is the test gate per maintainer policy (Peter, 2026-10-13: “relax testing and trust PR CI, just lint”). CI covers the changed core source and test types, regression tests, affected test shards, production/test typechecks, and repository checks. No contributor runtime or test code was executed locally or remotely during this maintainer pass. Local tests, typechecks, production-only negative controls, and live Gateway/lease proof were intentionally skipped per that policy; no leases or Gateway processes were started. Local test wall times are therefore unmeasured.

Regression coverage:

- `replays speech-only assistant content without changing the transcript (empty block: %s)`: real Completions conversion with and without an empty text block, preserved transcript content, and an unchanged written answer.
- `selects and classifies speech-only heartbeat content: %j`: nonempty speech survives reasoning exclusion and classification; blank speech remains empty.
- `keeps speech-only before synthesis completions successful`: no empty-result fallback for canonical speech.
- `synthesizes and delivers a speech-only heartbeat without placeholder text`: the heartbeat runner reaches the mock speech-provider boundary and sends media with an empty caption.

Changed-file oxfmt and oxlint passed. The nested-install wrapper refused to run without local node_modules; the installed parent's oxlint used the repository core rules and core tsconfig. Only the nonmatching `ui/**/*.tsx` override was omitted from a temporary config because its Solid plugin dependency is absent; every rule applying to the changed files was retained. Deslop removed the superseded replay helper and new type-laundering casts.

Independent Codex branch autoreview and incremental repair reviews: scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings. Final head: `dcbd185c2be7d33b71fef40b07080151a182710e`, after merging current main `78410c7b949614e158c1be8bd8d64f5a6a0ec7a2`. Exact-head [PR CI run 38348073408](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38348073408) passed: 51 successful jobs, no failures. The production/test typechecks, lint, repository checks, and all planned runtime test shards passed.

Initial CI run [38345264744](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38345264744) passed 47 jobs but found a fixture failure in the new heartbeat regression (job 115125425175) and TS2724 in an untouched preflight test (job 115125779268). The fixture now runs actual speech policy and synthesis with synthetic audio persistence; it still requires exact speech, one media send, and an empty caption. Main commit `72ccf43fdc6fb` completes the stale preflight reader migration from `33a438a7624d3`; the final main merge includes it. This type failure is not labeled a matching inherited scheduled-main failure: scheduled run 38343322520 predates the API change. Final heartbeat regression cost: 1.751s; all 15 tests passed, file 12.12s Vitest / 13.62s wrapper ([job 115134326126](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38348073408/job/115134326126)). Local wall times remain unmeasured per policy.

Second CI run [38346948941](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38346948941) reached synthesis, one media delivery, and an empty caption, then failed the retained voice-note assertion (job 115130781191). The custom heartbeat dispatcher had left TTS without its known destination, so synthesis selected generic audio. Preparation now keeps the canonical route channel for heartbeat TTS without changing delivery authority or routing decisions. Job 115130780508 also required a mock-isolation explanation; the narrowly scoped persistence mock now documents its isolated live guards/audio storage.

The latest full ClawSweeper review (comment 6134219573, reviewed head `098ed0b85ae8`) reports no actionable code findings and asks only for live Gateway/Telegram proof. That proof-only request is intentionally declined under the explicit maintainer policy above: exact-head PR CI is the proof gate. The human comment about unsuccessful voice delivery is addressed by completing the delivery path and adding the synthesis/delivery regression.

LOC versus merged main: production +45/-12 (net +33), tests +128/-0, docs +9/-0. Production growth is the honest exception to the nonpositive-LOC preference: both defects span separate replay, completion, and heartbeat gates. The replay implementation is smaller than the contributor version; unrelated production code is not removed to fund a quota.

prs.title: perf(sqlite): transfer lexical maintenance authority
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Writer admission still needs host-local lexical maintenance state. This prerequisite gives lexical scope, accepted frames and resource claims canonical shared cells. Native and admission-service checks consume scope/frame lifetimes; explicit resource-claim assertions keep their existing host boundary.

## User Impact

Existing maintenance, cleanup and write-settlement behavior is preserved. Full writer admission remains on the host until all remaining authority owners transfer.

## Why This Change Was Made

Scope phases replace local admission flags. Draining rejects new outside work while the exact accepted frame may finish cleanup. Resource reassignment retires its original claim before replacement; that blocks future captured-resource calls without revoking work already accepted under a separate frame. Failed close reopens the same scope before reporting failure; completed scopes and retired claims remain closed.

The operation admission captures its original async scope/frame privately. The broker transfers it only for the matching maintenance scope, and native stages recheck it before requesting host admission and after receiving the grant. The direct service transport reads the same cells. Parent owner checks require nonclosed lifetime, preserving the existing distinction between owner validity and new admission. Explicit resource-claim callbacks stay host-required until their callers have typed operations; they are not silently attached to every accepted frame. Policy callbacks, physical read/exclusion, process/schema custody, final host COMMIT and receipt settlement retain their existing owners.

No schema, configuration, dependency, persistent-state or update migration changes. Restart creates fresh process-local authority.

## Evidence and Measurement

Exact baseline75bc9101ed4d8edeb498212cb2657a07354db0d8, candidate3b9a248393cc80291d0fdcc74ded6fac64917d14, patch SHA-2565c7ad5ea1a45aaf6a8aa83e4bf653ae949722ccaf041927f8107dc94ef36f944. Four balanced Team-sandbox blocks are running for each lane-830 writer and lane-860 ACK protocol. This explicitly requested prerequisite may be neutral; results, counts, ratios and limitations will be recorded before landing. Ordinary macro load runs outside lexical maintenance scopes, so maintenance descriptor counts are expected to be zero: these protocols measure ordinary-path overhead, not scoped-path execution. Actual scoped transfer is proven by the broker/native/service adversarial tests and negative control. Initial calibration endpoints/exits passed, but an overly strict positive-descriptor harness assertion rejected it; that attempt is preserved, no comparison leg ran, and the corrected interpretation will be frozen before the new-head campaign.

Production LOC delta: +193 (including one extraction inventory line; excluding tests/test support/docs). Growth implements the requested shared lifetime owners and private transfer contract. Superseded local closed/active flags and claim map-identity authority checks are removed; no parallel fallback authority is retained.

## Proof

Focused tests cover accepted-frame drainage, exact claim revocation without blanket cancellation, failed-close reopening, service refusal for stale descriptors and replacement lifetimes, and native rollback when scope revocation occurs after host validation but before release. A negative control omits only the transferred broker field and must allow the write, proving the new boundary is exercised.

Changed-file formatting, repository lint, export collision guard and diff checks pass. Focused final broker/service proof passed 24 tests in 62.52 seconds (17 broker, 7 service), including deterministic native rollback and service restart. The scope/lease proof passed 19 tests in 42.39 seconds; the two required closure files passed 20 tests in 53.28 seconds including the wrapper. Omitting only the broker maintenance-authority field made the guarded write resolve with one committed write; restoring the exact source made it reject and leave an empty table. Fresh-context independent review, given only the diff and architecture design under the lead-authorized substitute route, is clean through P2, including the rebase preserving upstream test-support ownership. Rebased focused scope/native/service proof passed in131.73s; six cases on the standalone final base passed in146.83s. Changed-file formatting/syntax lint pass at the final head. Execution predecessor is merged; the standalone rebase is patch-identical to the reviewed maintenance commit. First full CI38349257132 completed99 jobs in917s. Its own Madge type-cycle failure is corrected by defining the descriptor in the dependency-free authority leaf and importing it directly in the context; transport re-exports that canonical type. Fresh independent full-diff/design review is clean through P2; three focused scope/service cases passed94.59s after the fix, and export guard passed. The other failure, required-native same-session completed→cancelled, remains under investigation and is not claimed inherited. Fresh exact-head CI follows the genuine type-owner fix; no CI rerun or push solely for green. No Testbox/Crabbox lease is used; PR CI owns full gates.

Next owner: shared physical read admission and exclusion/seal generations, followed by process/schema custody. Neither pathname nor heartbeat may stand in for live physical authority.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in reload of a dashboard deep link downloads and evaluates closed sidebar surfaces before the operator uses them. The cold-load campaign's original evidence recorded 14 visual states over roughly 15 seconds; L34 still measured 53 boot JS requests after the earlier improvements.

## User Impact

The Inbox badge and sidebar remain available at boot, while the Inbox panel and sidebar popup renderers load through their existing interaction boundaries. Session-menu registration now belongs to the popup renderer that consumes it. No settings, authentication, Gateway records, or schema changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the connection-time Inbox preload, idle sidebar-popup preload, and eager sidebar session-menu registration. Regenerate the measured boot manifest with the existing generator, excluding both optional dynamic entries from route hints and the offline boot inventory. Pointer/focus Inbox prefetch and menu-opening loads remain available; optional chunks need a network connection until first loaded, like other lazy surfaces.

## Evidence

Production-bundle Team-scale fixture, one reload per candidate on the same loaded Mac, at UI source base `74c7b3d72589` (after the New Session Solid migration). The baseline temporarily substitutes the five changed production UI files from main in this lane's worktree, then restores the reviewed bytes exactly. The UI files at the sampled main revision `633acc213dae` are identical to that UI base. Byte counts sum emitted JS and shipped gzip sidecars, rather than compressed wire traffic; build identities differ and can introduce small gzip variance. All timing samples are noisy.

| Measurement | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Chat route boot JS, raw | 5,259,199 B | 5,159,516 B |
| Chat route boot JS, gzip | 1,625,349 B | 1,600,203 B |
| Chat route boot JS hints | 31 | 30 |
| Dashboard reload fetched app JS, raw | 5,405,524 B | 5,307,731 B |
| Dashboard reload fetched app JS, gzip | 1,675,643 B | 1,651,597 B |
| Dashboard reload distinct app JS assets | 47 | 47 |
| Dashboard reload all JS requests, including six synthetic plugins | 53 | 53 |
| Main-thread script/module evaluation, interval union | 19.3 ms | 24.1 ms |
| Renderer busy time | 1,457 ms | 1,605 ms |

No reliable evaluate-time or overall reload-speed improvement is claimed: another pair measured evaluation 26.8→20.1 ms, while the starting-base pair measured 21.7→24.0 ms. The demonstrated improvement is fewer boot-hint requests and fewer downloaded JS bytes. New Session also falls from 28 to 27 boot JS hints and from 1,344,712 to 1,300,899 gzip bytes.

Evaluation accounts for `EvaluateScript` and `v8.evaluateModule` on the selected renderer main thread; overlapping intervals are counted once. Iframe evaluation is excluded.

Source-map attribution found a single production copy of Solid, lit-html, and every other package in the fetched graph. Major vendor contributions before the change: TypeBox ~148 KB, Web Awesome ~126 KB, Zod ~100 KB, highlight.js ~72 KB, Solid signals ~65 KB, markdown-it ~51 KB; startup English ~150 KB. Foreign locale catalogs, Mermaid, terminal/noVNC, and settings page renderers remain lazy. No dependency overrides or runtime-resolution changes are needed. Retired boot code includes the sidebar popup renderer (~11 KB), update card (~10 KB), sidebar session menu renderers (~8.5 KB), and Inbox rendering/helpers.

Focused proof, one file at a time:

- `pnpm ui:boot-manifest:gen` and production UI builds through the merged cold-load bench.
- `pnpm ui:check-performance --dist <candidate-bundle>`: all enforced budgets pass, chat/New Session 30/27 JS hints (limit 35).

- `pnpm test ui/src/components/sidebar-attention.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 21 pass, 12.37 s command wall time. Move the existing import-settlement wait to the first opening instead of assuming mount preloads it.
- `pnpm test ui/src/components/app-sidebar.sessions.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 154 pass, 65.93 s.
- `pnpm test ui/src/e2e/sidebar-attention-scope.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 1 pass, 49.51 s; bundled Inbox opening, automation scopes, and dismissal.
- `pnpm test ui/src/e2e/mobile-sidebar-session-menu.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 6 pass, 76.83 s; actual session menus and shortcuts.
- `pnpm test ui/src/app/control-ui-chunking.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 5 pass, 12.69 s; grouped route styles and optional-code exclusion. Its fixture now uses remaining shared boot styles, and no longer requires a fully tree-shaken debug contract in the source-map inventory.

Later integrated main commits do not change the UI source. The resolved generated manifest also received scoped-clean Codex review through P2.

Configured fallbacks use the destination runtime's supported account selection. Explicit conversation and person-linked pins remain strict, including changes during preparation. SDK V1/V2 support-window acceptance and exact-head security/fixture owner approvals remain upstream decisions before merge; this maintenance selects no new deadline, persistence, permission, dependency or protocol policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Configured account provenance follows Chat/Cron admission and queued work. Destination CLI runtimes select their supported profiles, while explicit conversation and person-linked pins remain strict. V2 transports await current host admission before cold process launch or warm prompt I/O. Current account reads use worker-published facts, preserving native handle identity and avoiding main-thread SQLite. Legacy V1 signatures remain source-compatible.

The current ordinary merge preserves published `d6848bdbc549287d7a72503da2e66cee14be40c6` and official main `dd053f96aa300a82443d5ab9725f206214e9c36e` as its two parents to resolve five actual conflicts. Initialize-only model discovery keeps main's narrow context; real execution retains V2 admission. CLI forwards main's session-writer accounting. Node dispatch preserves main's connection, pairing-generation and error owners alongside the existing deferred-dispatch guards. Incognito snapshots publish the existing auth-profile projection through the canonical producer rather than restoring retired inline readers.

## Current Validation (2026-10-13)

Reviewed source head: `75e32ffcffec8fd2c14f8ea525a3f38585f7f8a9`.

- **286 distinct passing cases** through the repository wrappers: eight affected owner files, 247 cases / 419.12 seconds; the existing Chat/Cron account process fixture, 8 cases / 154.04 seconds; the two Cron forwarding/ownership files, 21 cases / 205.67 seconds; plugin Doctor contract declaration/closure tests, 10 cases / 31.391 seconds. Commands use `pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=1` (the Doctor contract gate uses its existing `pnpm test:serial` owner). Current-head CI seconds were not measured or manually dispatched.
- The two existing real incognito actor controls failed before the producer migration with `Incognito session account projection is unavailable` (user and user-link, 143.75 seconds). Both pass after publishing the auth fact at the canonical snapshot producer. The unchanged positive Chat process control also exposed a missing main-required writer callback (100.64 seconds); its bookkeeping sink correction passes the complete 8-case fixture without faking account admission or weakening assertions.
- The line-growth guard rejected the combined Cron file at 1000 → 1007 counted lines. The complete independent CLI ownership suite now lives in a coherent sibling and uses the same existing harness. All 21 cases and the final line-cap guard pass; no coverage, timeout, worker configuration or budget was removed or weakened.
- Fresh independent P0–P2 review covered the complete candidate. Its sole verified writer-fixture finding is fixed and separately reviewed; the subsequent suite extraction also has fresh scoped-clean review. All 74 final diff files were checked byte-for-byte against the reviewed capsule and remained unchanged through the real merge commit/hook.
- Core production types pass in 154.047 seconds. All 28 core consumer test graphs pass: the first 13 successful graph results were retained after an interrupted command, and only the remaining 15 were resumed (2876.605 seconds). Plugin production/test types pass in 301.834 / 440.039 seconds. Script lint and all 8 remaining schema/storage/media/sidecar/cycle/webhook/pairing guards pass; runtime value cycles are zero. The final environment-variable guard passes at 456/456 after the ordinary merge establishes its real ancestry. The earlier uncommitted-head growth diagnostic is retained; no budget or guard was changed.
- Normal `pnpm build` passes in 460.46 seconds, including CLI bootstrap imports and the plugin declaration/assets owners. UI reports inherited startup-size advisories (402.3 KiB JS versus a 366.1 KiB advisory target, and startup CSS above its advisory target); this is not a warning-free build claim.

**Retained failures:** the max-lines suppression ratchet reports `src/web-search/runtime.test.ts`; a complete fixed-main index produces the identical rejection. Knip reports 17 production and 11 full-tree unused exports, with 0 script findings. Complete fixed-main source reproduces exactly those lists. Full core lint ran all 5 stripes and reports 15 max-lines errors; every named diagnostic is reproduced byte-for-byte with the same type-aware owner on fixed main. Full plugin lint reports only `extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-provider.ts` at 710 > 700 counted lines; its source/rules are unchanged from fixed main, and the same owner reproduces that exact isolated diagnostic. These failures were neither ignored nor called green. The author diff introduced none of the named failing files or rule/budget changes.

**Current remote merge risk:** after this normal push, GitHub reports conflicts with main newer than the fixed validation baseline. The five captured d684→dd053 conflicts are resolved, but this does not claim the later main is conflict-free; further author integration remains pending.

**Remaining upstream gates:** SDK V1/V2 coexistence and its accepted support window still need SDK/security owner acceptance. Real-owner late user/user-link pin proof at V2 cold-launch and warm-prompt boundaries, a retained-settings upgrade from v2026.10.1, and the requested redacted runtime capture remain outstanding. The isolated Gateway evidence below is explicitly historical at d684; it is not new-head Gateway, vendor CLI, billing/cache or upgrade proof. No upstream merge, release or paid test resource was used. This author repair adds no schema/protocol bump or new public option.

## Isolated public Chat/Cron evidence (2026-10-11)

Measured head: `d6848bdbc549287d7a72503da2e66cee14be40c6`. With explicit human approval, an owned loopback Gateway, local synthetic HTTP402 endpoint and self-authored Google CLI protocol plugin exercised actual `chat.send` / `agent.wait` / history and `cron.add` / `run` / `runs` / `remove` boundaries. prs.title: refactor(sessions): stop rechecking qualified target absence
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Qualified chat targets repeatedly checked that competing session keys were still absent, performing synchronous SQLite reads after the target had already been selected.

## User Impact

Chat admission and replies keep their selected physical session target without repeated absence reads. Existing session generation, selected-source, lifecycle, and initial collision checks remain. No schema, storage format, retention, SDK export, or update migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Qualification now checks initial ambiguity once through the existing read worker, including retained placeholders, and returns the qualified target directly. The ordinary canonical single-source case adds no worker request. The obsolete native absence reader and assertion/release plumbing are deleted together.

Accepted edge case: a duplicate appearing later under an alternate key or in a sibling store affects future discovery; an already pinned operation continues against its originally selected physical source and key. This is discovery bookkeeping, not permission to redirect an admitted operation.

The targeted T1 site `retainSessionEntryKeyAbsence.assertCurrent` goes from **1 to 0**. The wider reads/targets family goes from **4 to 3** named sites; conversation binding and exact-read authority remain outside this slice because their cross-owner publication coverage is incomplete.

Production diff: **+251 / −378 lines**, net **-127**. Tests/support: **+140 / −231**. Most added reply-dispatch lines are unchanged code indented under the retained resource’s `try/finally`.

## Evidence

- Basic formatting, scoped oxlint, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Added regression covers worker-only initial sibling discovery, a later sibling duplicate preserving a pinned write, and fresh qualification rejecting that duplicate. Existing generation/replacement and initial same-store collision regressions remain. Removed two tests that only pinned the discarded late-ambiguity check. Terminal reply inspection retains the existing history-database owner so supported close/replacement still rejects delivery, without SQL or filesystem probes.
- Corrected-head CI run [38339937432](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38339937432) completed successfully; all 81 jobs passed or were skipped, including reply-session and global-identity regressions, types, lint, Madge, and database ratchets. That evidence applies to qualification head `a93266c7b03e6d28bcb53fbe11192d11f0c8d7f1`. Current head `2e39b3b0a20404f8df53047feee1e3bb80f7183e` merges main `7f98077b2e30d`; [integrated CI 38342268323](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38342268323) completed successfully (57 successful and 25 skipped jobs). The hold is lifted. Current head `53383c26645a579c5e0203138fbe1d4d0e5fb1eb` integrates main `3f1175be9d5e6bded571f47cf5d2d00ea2c9c7d1` without conflicts; its [CI 38350342990](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38350342990) and required security gate completed successfully. All rollup jobs are complete with no failures. Under the current compute-conservation rule, no additional local Knip scan is run; ordinary PR CI does not include that separate scan.
- Two Codex review rounds completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings in their supplied scopes. The second covered the authority-boundary corrections; mechanical CI caller/type fixes followed.

## Measurements

One alternating base/candidate pair with the unchanged shared **sqlharness 2.1.0**, Node **26.11.1**, and SQLite **3.53.4**. Base: `3b75ce70f3970b616c79ea6822342159b1aa441e`; combined qualification/membership candidate: `58d5abbe40f0399a52eef9e8b6ffc076efc5a984`. The two runs used identical harness hashes. Later test-only fixes and conflict-free main integration are not separate measured revisions. The new goal-receipt operation is not exercised by this workload.

Both runs completed all 13 foreground turns, the native child, control RPCs, cron, compaction, and clean shutdown. All ten warmed turns had causal SQL/request coverage; native SQL failures were zero. Both native calibrations passed. Figures below count successful native statements across every thread/process and logical worker requests; moving a statement to a worker does not remove it from these totals.

| Metric | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Warm turn-caused SQL/turn, mean | 172.9 | 170.8 |
| Warm turn-caused SQL/turn, median [min–max] | 171 [170–194] | 170 [170–178] |
| Warm turn-caused requests/turn, mean | 42.0 | 41.3 |
| Warm turn-caused requests/turn, median [min–max] | 41.5 [41–47] | 41 [41–44] |
| Warm turn-caused MAIN SQL/turn | 0 | 0 |
| First-turn causal SQL / requests / MAIN | 372 / 77 / 33 | 375 / 81 / 31 |
| Legacy warmed-window SQL / requests per turn | 231.7 / 67.0 | 212.8 / 55.0 |
| Background SQL/min during warm windows | 531.90 | 658.70 |
| Entire workload SQL / requests / MAIN | 7,111 / 1,435 / 826 | 6,744 / 1,242 / 824 |

The medians/ranges describe the ten warmed turns in each run, not a three-run distribution. These were loaded-host count measurements, **not latency evidence**: baseline/candidate pre-run one-minute loads were 108.99/103.90 on 32 CPUs, with 0% observed idle. Warm windows lasted 66.328/38.257 seconds. Background rates and legacy-window totals remain timing-sensitive. The observed 2.1 SQL and 0.7 request reductions per warm turn are shared-owner/cache variation; this lane does not claim them as a deterministic optimization.

## Owner attribution

| Family | Entire-workload SELECTs, base → candidate | Warm SELECTs/turn, base → candidate | Warm requests/turn, base → candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Exact-entry facts | 90 → 83 | 4.2 → 4.0 | 4.2 → 4.0 |
| Actor hydration | 24 → 23 | 1.2 → 1.1 | 1.2 → 1.1 |
| Entry-cache snapshot loads | 46 → 35 | 0 → 0 | 0 → 0 |
| Row facts | 3 → 2 | 0 → 0 | 0 → 0 |
| Watermarks | 61 → 54 | 1.0 → 1.0 | 1.0 → 1.0 |

Families are matched by native owner stack, and can overlap. Request figures correlate each native statement's request ID with the recorded logical request; they are not inferred by dividing SQL counts.

The removed qualification/absence path executes **2 → 0 MAIN statements** over this workload: one cold quarantine `user_version` read and one cold quarantine-row SELECT, with **0 → 0 worker requests**. Earlier SELECT-only attribution reported one; two is the correct all-statement count. Membership remains **3 → 3 cold worker SELECTs in 3 → 3 requests**, with **0 → 0 warm SQL and requests**. The shared workload does not exercise a repeated non-owner membership authorization, so the final guard's zero-request property is established by its boundary tests rather than a claimed harness saving.

## First-turn difference

The first causal turn rises by three statements and four requests, while MAIN falls by two and entire-workload SQL/requests fall by 367/193. The complete first-turn SQL delta is:

| Existing producer/path | SQL delta | Request delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Auth-profile readonly load | +1 | +1 |
| Ordered exact-entry read | +1 | +1 |
| Sandbox exact-entry read | +1 | +1 |
| Agent-ingress deletion-status cold load | +1 | +1 |
| Active-projection watermark read within existing request | +1 | 0 |
| Removed qualification quarantine-row read | −1 MAIN | 0 |
| Removed qualification quarantine `user_version` read | −1 MAIN | 0 |
| **Total** | **+3** | **+4** |

These are existing cold/read-cache producers; no added warm operation appears in the touched owner stacks. Across the complete workload the auth readonly request stack drops 25 → 23, ordered exact-entry requests drop 41 → 40, exact-entry fact SQL drops 90 → 83, and watermark SQL drops 61 → 54. The result is a cold-work redistribution plus the removed native qualification admission; the lane makes no latency or deterministic warm-savings claim.

The Phase E hold is lifted and current main is integrated. This qualification slice does not depend on Phase E landing; membership final-authority changes are separate.
