prs.title: fix: honor configured speech in Control UI
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes configured Gateway speech being ignored by Control UI Read aloud, microphone dictation, and `talk.realtime.mode: "stt-tts"`.

Closes #45508. Closes #113049.

## User Impact

Operators can use a local OpenAI-compatible speech endpoint for Read aloud and dictation, and split Talk can use the current chat agent, including a local model. Unconfigured speech keeps existing behavior. Escape and split-Talk Stop discard captured audio and cancel pending transcription. Providers report readiness through their credential owner before file transcription is advertised or admitted.

Split Talk pauses capture while the agent answers and audio plays. Camera input, barge-in, and realtime voice switching remain outside this mode.

## Why This Change Was Made

Read aloud uses `tts.speak`; file transcription adapts the existing Talk audio relay to the media owner; split Talk uses ordinary chat submission and configured Gateway speech. Explicit streaming selections and matching saved voice models retain precedence. Requester authority and disconnect cancellation reach retries, fallback, process execution, and HTTP dispatch.

The two additive contracts were maintainer-approved: optional `discard: true` on `talk.session.close`, and optional `MediaUnderstandingProvider.isAudioConfigured(context)`. Normal close still finalizes audio. Providers without the readiness hook keep existing behavior. OpenAI shares credential preparation between readiness and execution, resolving credentials again for the upload. Protocol types are regenerated through the canonical generator; SDK and protocol documentation cover both additions. No new configuration, dependency, or transcript store.

Retained Solid transcript roots receive the application context explicitly. Playback reuses an audio element prepared during the initiating gesture, and split Talk reuses the shared chat-result waiter. Superseded capture and cancellation paths are removed.

Thanks @mcfex and @mike-nott for reporting these workflows.

## Evidence

Candidate `c87fa3166364b3599e2221d47c00ed29511c926e` includes main `c0888b457b524d863d79035102e7f9516617caad` and passed independent Codex branch autoreview through P2 with no findings (247.42 s). Both approved contracts, startup cancellation, and the CI fixture repair are complete. Final merged build, Chromium refresh, exact-head CI, and ClawSweeper review remain pending.

The final Chromium run used an isolated Gateway, native `ollama/qwen3:8b`, a synthetic microphone file, and a loopback OpenAI-compatible speech stub. Read aloud called `tts.speak`; a nonempty STT result became the next `chat.send`, the local model answered, and split Talk called `talk.speak`. Both 32,060-byte WAV responses decoded and played to completion (0.5 s each). No `talk.client.create` occurred. Normal proof: 51.36 s wall / 35.996 s test body.

The live cancellation run exercised Escape before upload, split-Talk Stop during blocked STT, and dictation Stop followed by Escape during blocked STT. The first sent zero STT uploads. Both in-flight requests reached socket EOF before the stub released them, and neither produced a transcript, chat submission, or speech request. Cancellation proof: 32.61 s wall / 12.982 s test body.

Limits: Chromium on macOS; speech quality, Safari, latest-stable upgrade, and live requester-revocation proof are not claimed. Requester-revocation regression coverage reaches the media owner's HTTP/CLI effect boundaries.

Before, the configured UI lacked Read aloud and reported no realtime provider. After, Read aloud is available and split Talk completes the local-model round trip. The final cancellation/readiness repairs do not change appearance.

![Before: assistant reply lacks Read aloud](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5e2ec1db-65b5-418d-848a-cc1cd4113ac3)

![After: Gateway-backed Read aloud](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7a369dc0-f8af-4793-b1fc-69029927d153)

![Before: split configuration still requires a realtime provider](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2b42dca6-7100-40cd-b9b1-c176def5913d)

![After: microphone transcription and the local model reply in normal chat](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5dc0c977-fbf4-46c3-9f15-10249220fdb0)

<details>
<summary>Focused validation and scope</summary>

- Gateway RPC/relay: 33 tests passed; media authority/selection/CLI: 33 passed; OpenAI: 20 passed. Seven files, 86 tests, 534.59 s wall including compilation and runner cleanup. Vitest shards: 259.79 s, 78.97 s, 111.08 s.
- After merging main, seven focused UI suites passed all 105 tests using the repository-pinned Bun (42.84 s wall / 32.67 s Vitest), including Read aloud, dictation, split Talk, New Session, and the repaired async-question fixture. Earlier UI types passed in 55.76 s and focused lint in 127.20 s, including artifact waits; final merged checks are pending.
- Regression negative controls fail on the previous behavior: discarded audio finalizes or emits late transcripts; Escape/Stop omit discard; uncredentialed context providers are advertised ready. The readiness negative control fails two new assertions while the hookless-provider compatibility case passes. The strengthened startup-cancellation regression fails on the previous head after audio is appended and normal finalization starts; the repair sends discard before that finalization is released.
- Core and UI typechecks, targeted core lint, SDK exports/surface checks, protocol generation/native protocol check, formatting, and all seven ratchets passed. The selected OpenAI boundary emitted 12,128 SDK declarations; its matching production typecheck passed (3.77 s) and type-aware lint passed (104.75 s).
- The pre-merge full runtime/UI build passed (631.66 s wall). The merged head is rebuilding before its Chromium refresh.
- No prompt/tool text changes; token delta 0.

CI follow-up: run 38347838771 checked a merge with main `6775bd0aeccaaafd2e55950fff8e91d9acd709fa`. Its async-question suite failed during collection because a module-scoped composer registered per-test cleanup. Moving creation into `beforeEach` fixes it: the old feature head failed before collecting tests (58.11 s), exact main passed 6/6 (44.38 s), and the repair passed 6/6 (49.48 s), all with the pinned Bun. The other two UI shards reported runner shutdowns without test-failure markers.

Production: +1,664 / -715 lines (net +949). Tests: +1,821 / -43. Documentation: +63 / -1. Other: assertion-safety baseline -1. Growth implements the file-STT adapter and browser speech flows; existing capture, credential, catalog, playback, and chat-result owners are shared.

</details>

prs.title: fix(minimax): OAuth sign-in stops working about two hours after login because expired tokens are never refreshed
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/77467

## Evidence

Maintainer validation (2026-10-12)

Live-proof artifact: `6f4fea421d5301637ba9add262ff04ec7222a2ea`, preserving the contributor head and integrating main at `93bceb67948eb6ac991075ce14e66504553f98a2`.

Reviewed repair head: `2766fe9242ed9dcbdf56f5a43879d5f54452f3cc`. The sole delta from the live-proof artifact replaces the obsolete Chutes refresh-hook identity assertion with actual renewal through the registered provider hook using caller config. Production and live-proof inputs are unchanged.

- CI run 38323171759 failed only `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-1` on that identity assertion; `openclaw/ci-gate` failed downstream. The report classified it unknown (no matching main job), and source inspection directly attributes it to the Chutes adapter in this PR.
- Repair validation: 17 Chutes provider/OAuth tests pass; changed-file runner 16.02 s, renewal case 9 ms; targeted type-aware lint, format, extension test types and diff check pass. Independent P0-P2 review is clean. Exact-head [CI run 38349856484](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38349856484) completed successfully: all 72 jobs, including the previously failing extensions bundle. The renewed-credential case took 4 ms in CI (bundle job 140 s). ClawSweeper reviewed this repair head with zero actionable findings and confirmed the prior Chutes finding is resolved.

- Forward effective caller configuration through OAuth refresh; preserve existing one-argument handlers and adapt Chutes' helper-options binding.
- Recognize both current `api.minimax.cn` and legacy `api.minimaxi.com` as CN before any refresh request.
- 124 focused provider/OAuth tests across the unchanged MiniMax/runtime inputs and final Chutes adapter; final bundled-provider extension consumer types and full build passed. Independent correction reviews have no remaining actionable P0-P2 findings.
- **Real Global MiniMax OAuth and inference**, isolated Gateway/CLI: device-code sign-in, expiry-only preparation preserving the live token generation, actual issuing-endpoint POST **HTTP 200**, persisted refresh-token rotation and future expiry. MiniMax retained the still-valid access token; access-token rotation is not claimed.
- Exact final artifact served `minimax-portal/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview` at **low, medium, high, xhigh, max**, using the OAuth profile with **no fallback**. Direct image attachment returned the expected color. Text-file tool use and multi-turn replay also succeeded with identical MiniMax/runtime source before the Chutes-only binding correction.
- Qualification: forced **client** expiry, not a wait for natural server-side access expiry. CN/API-key behavior has focused tests, not live account proof. One tool-mediated color probe misidentified a red PNG; same-head bounded reproduction and direct attachment passed, with **no claimed code fix or blanket vision-quality guarantee**.
- Local changed-gate production dead-export scan remains red for three unrelated entries: `hasActiveDeliveryOwner`, `listOpenClawStateFeatureSchemas`, `OpenClawStateFeatureSchema`. All three were independently reproduced on untouched main `93bceb6`; no allowances or unrelated production code were changed. Required current-head GitHub CI/security/review gates still apply; old contributor CI is not used as current proof.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: MiniMax OAuth (`minimax-portal`) turns fail with `No credentials found for profile "minimax-portal:default"` once the access token expires, and users must sign in again, because the plugin never refreshes the stored token.

## User Impact

User impact: after signing in with MiniMax Global or CN OAuth, users keep working past access-token expiry; OpenClaw refreshes the token at the regional account endpoint that issued it and saves the rotated refresh token.

Upgrade behavior: a profile saved before this change does not record its region, so its first refresh is refused and the user is asked to run `openclaw models auth login --provider minimax-portal` once (today they already have to sign in again on every expiry). Refresh is also refused, before any request, when `models.providers.minimax-portal.baseUrl` has been moved to the other region after sign-in.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `minimax-portal` provider had no `refreshOAuth` hook, so the OAuth manager had no refresher for it. This adds the hook inside the MiniMax plugin. The maintainer correction also forwards caller config through the existing OAuth dispatcher as an optional second SDK hook argument; one-argument handlers remain supported, and Chutes uses a one-argument adapter to keep its helper test options separate. The existing opaque credential metadata records the issuing endpoint; no credential-schema migration is introduced.

The open question on the issue is which region a stored refresh token belongs to. This follows the review recommendation on this PR ("persist region for new logins and require sign-in for legacy profiles whose origin cannot be verified"):

- Login now records the regional token endpoint it used (`https://account.minimax.io/oauth2/token` or `https://account.minimaxi.com/oauth2/token`) in the credential's existing `tokenEndpoint` metadata field.
- Refresh sends the refresh token only to that recorded endpoint. It never derives the endpoint from the mutable provider URL and never falls back to Global.
- It refuses before any request when the credential has no recorded endpoint, or when the configured base URL names the other region (`api.minimax.io` vs current `api.minimax.cn` or legacy `api.minimaxi.com`). A custom proxy base URL does not change where the token goes.

Also in the token parser: a refresh response that omits `refresh_token` keeps the stored one, and a MiniMax `status: "error"` response surfaces its `base_resp.status_msg` instead of a generic message, so refresh failures are diagnosable. The MiniMax provider docs describe the refresh and the sign-in cases.

## Original contributor synthetic evidence

Tested at `e9548a49656` (base upstream/main `a68299da6a2`).

A real Gateway and the real CLI, built from each commit, with an isolated state directory on Linux. Faked: MiniMax itself. Everything runs in a private network namespace whose hosts file points the Global hosts (`api.minimax.io`, `account.minimax.io`) at one local TLS fake and the CN hosts (`api.minimaxi.com`, `account.minimaxi.com`) at a second one, both up for every run. Each fake serves device-code login, the token endpoint and Messages, and logs which region received each request. Login issues a 1-second access token, so the next turn must refresh. Tokens are synthetic.

**1. Region changed after sign-in** (the cross-region case). Steps: `openclaw models auth login --provider minimax-portal --method oauth` (Global), `openclaw config set models.providers.minimax-portal.baseUrl https://api.minimaxi.com/anthropic`, `openclaw gateway run`, `openclaw agent --agent main --message hello --json`.

Before (previous head of this PR, `f1e542e3376`, which chose the region from the base URL):

```text
requests received, in order (region, host, request):
global  account.minimax.io   POST /oauth2/device/code
global  account.minimax.io   POST /oauth2/token  grant_type=...:user_code
cn      account.minimaxi.com POST /oauth2/token  grant_type=refresh_token   <- Global refresh token sent to CN
agent: "OAuth token refresh failed for minimax-portal: MiniMax OAuth refresh failed: refresh token not issued by this region."
```

After (this PR):

```text
requests received, in order (region, host, request):
global  account.minimax.io   POST /oauth2/device/code
global  account.minimax.io   POST /oauth2/token  grant_type=...:user_code
(CN fake: 0 requests; no refresh request to either region)
gateway log: OAuth token refresh failed for minimax-portal: MiniMax OAuth credential was issued for the Global region, but models.providers.minimax-portal.baseUrl now points to https://api.minimaxi.com. Run `openclaw models auth login --provider minimax-portal` to sign in again.
```

**2. Normal refresh** (same steps without the config change), this PR:

```text
global  account.minimax.io   POST /oauth2/device/code
global  account.minimax.io   POST /oauth2/token  grant_type=...:user_code
global  account.minimax.io   POST /oauth2/token  grant_type=refresh_token
global  api.minimax.io       POST /anthropic/v1/messages  (authorized with the refreshed Global access token)
agent: exit=0, "pong from global"
(CN fake: 0 requests)
```

**3. The reported failure** (profile with an expired access token, imported with `openclaw doctor --fix`, base URL as Global login writes it). On base `a68299da6a2`: `exit=1`, `No credentials found for profile "minimax-portal:default".`, and no token request at all. On this PR the same pre-existing profile has no recorded region, so no token request is made either, and doctor reports `minimax-portal:default: re-auth required [sign in again] — Run openclaw models auth login --provider minimax-portal ...`; after that one sign-in, case 2 applies.

Observed result: the refresh token only ever reaches the account endpoint that issued it; the other region's fake received no requests in any run on this PR.

Not covered: the real MiniMax endpoints (no account); the request and response shapes follow the existing login token exchange and the refresh request shown in the issue. The CN-issued direction of the region check is covered by the focused test, not by a process-level run.

<details><summary>Focused tests and checks</summary>

- `extensions/minimax/index.test.ts`, through the registered `minimax-portal` provider: CN, Global and custom-proxy base URLs refresh at the credential's recorded endpoint and return the rotated credential; a credential without a recorded endpoint, a Global credential with a CN base URL and a CN credential with a Global base URL are all refused with no request. The two mismatch cases fail on the previous head; all refresh cases fail on the base (no `refreshOAuth`).
- `extensions/minimax/oauth.test.ts`: login returns the regional token endpoint it used.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/minimax/index.test.ts extensions/minimax/oauth.test.ts`: 59 passed.
- `pnpm check:changed --base upstream/main`: passed (typecheck, lint, dead-export scan, boundaries).

| Test file | `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` wall | CI seconds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `extensions/minimax/index.test.ts` | 19.2 s (whole file, 44 cases) | 0.87 s of case time for the whole file in `checks-node-changed-extensions-config` (run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36424723956, previous head); the refresh cases took 25 ms, 9 ms and 12 ms |
| `extensions/minimax/oauth.test.ts` | 14.3 s (whole file, one changed assertion) | no new case |

</details>

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin setting action menus now use the native Solid menu while preserving Reset value, Ask OpenClaw, keyboard dismissal, and row geometry. Escape from a focused menu trigger must close the menu before it can leave the settings editor.

## User Impact

Reset eligibility, Ask OpenClaw values, and trigger appearance are preserved. Both the plugin page and application shell defer Escape to an active native overlay, so the overlay lifecycle owns dismissal and focus restoration before ordinary field or page dismissal.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native menu registry handles Escape in a document bubble listener. The shell's older listener can run first, and the trigger is outside the menu panel. The shell now consumes the existing registry's active-overlay fact instead of trying to recognize the trigger through DOM ancestry. This adds no new startup module: the shell already reaches the registry through its tooltip imports, and it does not import Menu or the Solid bridge.

The E2E consumers use the native trigger and menuitem roles in place of retired Web Awesome selectors. Existing geometry, data, reset eligibility, and keyboard assertions remain intact.

The CI owner map now includes the shell and cron/plugin Settings consumers so these changes select the existing WebKit overlay-and-focus project on UI shard 1. This only broadens path selection; it adds no suite, runner, configuration mode, or parallelism.

## Evidence

Final head: `c628c8443d88cf00de0786b2399dd33d7dca8a50`. Its only change from `5227f83a4fc7f2f55f7f11bfc1bfcd06bc7f9584` is the two-line CI owner map, which passed managed static review without actionable P0–P2 findings, `node --check`, and `git diff --check`. The unchanged product tree reuses the following local, visual, and startup proof from `5227f83a4fc7f2f55f7f11bfc1bfcd06bc7f9584`:

- Managed review of the four-file consumer/shell repair completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings. The earlier full migration and main refresh also completed their scoped reviews.
- The three directly changed unit/browser files passed: `plugins-page.routing.test.ts`, `settings-lifecycle.test.tsx`, and `settings-editor.browser.test.tsx`, 36/36 tests, 63.36 seconds wall time with `--maxWorkers=1`.
- UI typechecking passed in 38.27 seconds.
- The exact installed-help E2E case passed through the repository wrapper: one selected case, seven skipped, 4.60 seconds test time and 103.05 seconds wall time including its private production build. This covered draft preservation, redaction, and departed-context cleanup.
- Full exact-head CI passed: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38346229236 — all 3 UI shards, 9 E2E shards, and 2 real-Gateway shards passed. The run used 10,670 executed job-seconds (7,204 for those UI-family jobs). The conditional WebKit step was skipped and supplies no WebKit proof.

The previous full run at `9fc6ed6` failed ten cases across four E2E shards. Nine failures identified retired selectors or the trigger-focused Escape bug addressed here. The separate installed-help failure timed out before the first menu selection and reported the Settings inventory route; it did not reproduce in the isolated replay. Its cause remains unresolved, and the passing replay is not claimed as a fix. The corresponding ten case names passed on the inspected scheduled-main baseline. Previous-run cost was 9,923 executed job-seconds. The repaired prior-head full run passed, including all E2E shards; it is not claimed as final-head CI.

Three local WebKit 26.6 attempts at `5227f83` failed during the initial navigation prerequisite: the first timed out waiting for `load`, the second stalled after switching to DOMContentLoaded/readiness and was interrupted, and the bounded diagnostic reached its 15-second navigation/initial-roster deadline. The diagnostic recorded no page errors, failed requests, or route observations. No scene, focus, no-write assertion, or WebKit capture was reached in any attempt. The cause remains unresolved, and this limitation also applies to the unchanged product tree at the final head.

Required shared-overlay WebKit coverage passed on final head `c628c8443d88c` in CI run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38350073286, UI shard 1 job `115140484102`: both “Install Playwright WebKit” and “Test Control UI WebKit overlays and focus” succeeded. All three UI shards and both real-Gateway shards passed. The full run completed with 8/9 E2E shards passing and one failure: `sidebar-cold-load.e2e.test.ts` — “restores the sessions view and pinned rail before hello through late counts and plugins.” Its observer saw the settled sidebar, a transient empty session list, then the restored list. This is the existing shared overlay/focus contract, while the separate local Settings WebKit navigation limitation remains recorded above.

## What Problem This Solves

Replace the lobster dismissal dropdown with the native Solid menu while retaining its pointer position, two actions, existing selectors, and lazy loading. Escape and action selection now return focus to the composer instead of the invisible menu anchor.

## Solution and User Impact

The shared menu owns keyboard navigation and dismissal. The consumer preserves composer focus on right-button pointerdown and translates the owner's hidden-trigger focus to the captured external target. Clicking or focusing outside still keeps focus at that destination. Resetting the invisible trigger's padding and border keeps its anchor 1×1 pixel, so edge-positioned menus fit the viewport.

## Evidence

Reviewed head: `7598dc2ce9404423ca464232de0f5abff901beea`. Merge base: `75bc9101ed4d8edeb498212cb2657a07354db0d8`. Integration includes the upstream native overlay simplification and Workboard manifest repair; the only textual conflict adopted main's type-only pet-contract import while preserving the lazy menu. prs.title: fix(cron): preserve implicit delivery session provenance
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An implicit `last` cron delivery can recover its route from one exact canonical session, then independently choose another session when recording post-send conversation state. The transport send succeeds, but delivery awareness and the mirror can be attributed to the wrong conversation.

## How This Solves It

- retain the exact session key that supplied recovered delivery context
- attach provenance only for an unchanged implicit `last` route owned by the same canonical agent session
- use that proven source for transcript and delivery-awareness attribution
- independently retain the resolved destination as outbound policy context, including group media-read restrictions
- preserve explicit overrides, reroutes, custom-session priority, malformed or foreign-agent fallback, and ordinary native jobs

## Evidence

- refreshed base: `98262d8b5fdaf4b1be499fc10c7426a0f2be5b6e`
- exact head: `daa38093ba024432f1c5f842824e45ab21722e3b`
- the five-commit range comparison against the prior proven head reports all five patches carried forward exactly
- exact-head native CI [run 37420196083](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37420196083) passed all 50 jobs, including selected tests, security-fast, production and test types, lint, formatting, boundaries, guards, source contracts, baseline ratchets, and the aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate`
- exact-head formatter passed on all 11 changed files
- exact-head type-aware Oxlint passed for both production and test configurations
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` passed
- exact-head Security Review, dependency review, and security-sensitive review passed
- exact-head ClawSweeper review found no actionable correctness or security issue, accepted the preserved Gateway and SQLite boundary proof, and marked the PR ready for maintainer review
- prior secretless Testbox workflow: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37400241251
- queue admission: 1 file passed, 10 tests passed
- Gateway E2E: 1 file passed, 1 test passed; scenario completed in 15.69s
- prior focused dispatch/outbound result: 2 files passed, 206 tests passed in 54.27s
- committed Gateway E2E: `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/gateway-heartbeat-session-routing.e2e.test.ts`
- the Gateway fixture creates dashboard-named `sessionTarget: "current"` cron jobs, runs mock provider turns, and crosses the real channel-plugin adapter boundary
- allowed media selects the destination group policy, reaches `sendMedia`, invokes the production-supplied bounded reader, and reads the exact workspace bytes
- denied media selects the destination group's `read` denial, records `deliveryStatus: "not-delivered"`, and produces no adapter trace or file read
- the source transcript retains the reply and its original session ID while source-bound delivery awareness remains present
- durable revocation proof uses `runGatewayConversationSend` and the real SQLite queue, waits for committed enqueue custody, mutates the persisted conversation route through `registerConversationAddresses`, then verifies production authorization rejects before `sendText`
- differential control: the identical source-attribution Gateway fixture failed on base because the source-awareness queue was empty; candidate passed
- no agent transcript, provider payload, or secret is attached

## Tracking Issue

Tracked in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/166746.

prs.title: perf(gateway): overlap readiness preparation and prewarm connections
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway startup serialized session projection preparation with independent early services after opening its listener. The first WebSocket connection could also load its message handler after readiness. Overlap those preparations, and make readiness own the process-stable connection imports. Readiness still waits for the complete projection, model facts and request preparation; the listener remains available for liveness during initialization.

Both concurrent branches settle before failure cleanup. Request-runtime failure priority and database activation ordering stay intact. The superseded post-ready message-handler prewarm is removed. No schema, SDK, state owner, admission protocol or synchronous database path is added.

`server-kernel-request-runtime.ts` already coalesces startup and transport calls through one `requestRuntimeReady` promise. Projection initialization runs once per Gateway; snapshots consume the resident projection. The earlier CONNECT census does not demonstrate repeated per-connect projection initialization.

## SQL measurement

Frozen base `96db2f6dfa4f47fd579a6d8408011950b8af53e1`, candidate `84a6fd5fb478e74523674088d1171f6bfa6c92c1`; one live alternating baseline/candidate pair, ten warmed turns each, shared SQL harness 2.1.0. Manifest/environment hashes match both heads. A private harness copy uses the supported 120-second handshake allowance after an excluded 15-second timeout under host load; shared instrumentation and operations are unchanged.

| Window | Base SQL / requests / MAIN | Candidate SQL / requests / MAIN |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Warmed causal median [range] | 180 [180–188] / 43 [43–47] / 0 | 180 [180–188] / 43 [43–47] / 0 |
| Warmed raw median [range] | 211.5 [190–235] / 54 [47–65] / 0 | 232 [192–287] / 66.5 [53–88] / 0 |
| BOOT | 950 / 80 / 756 | 951 / 79 / 756 |
| CONNECT | 100 / 22 / 10 | 1079 / 53 / 22 |
| First turn, raw | 1896 / 196 / 51 | 949 / 182 / 38 |
| First turn, causal | 383 / 81 / 38 | 420 / 80 / 38 |
| Whole workload | 6817 / 1270 / 833 | 7013 / 1403 / 840 |

CONNECT includes concurrent startup and one second after hello. BOOT+CONNECT+first is 2946 → 2979 statements; most of CONNECT's increase moves existing startup out of the first-turn window. The older census's corresponding totals were 2967/2989/2936. Do not report its 863–1253 CONNECT statements falling to this baseline's 100 as a saving from this PR.

<details><summary>CONNECT attribution by existing owner (SQL / requests)</summary>

| Owner | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `openclaw-agent-write-admission.ts:observeWriteAdmission` and its admission closure | 0 / 0 | 718 / 1 |
| `store-writer-queue.ts` writer drain | 0 / 0 | 140 / 5 |
| `session-cost-usage-cache-runtime.ts:runQueuedUsageCostRefresh` | 0 / 0 | 15 / 1 |
| `file-watcher.ts` and `manager-registry.ts` memory startup | 0 / 0 | 24 / 1 |
| `worker-task-pool-owned.ts:ready` | 0 / 0 | 12 / 2 |
| `device-pairing.ts:listDevicePairing` | 4 / 2 | 8 / 2 |

Pairing's four extra statements are one cache miss at the existing successful-pairing recovery lookup, on the same worker: BEGIN, pending SELECT, paired SELECT, COMMIT. Intervening shared-state watch/lease/config writes invalidate its database-wide receipt; the baseline recovery read follows a read-only prune. The separately landed #170594 removes that unused successful-path lookup while preserving final live authorization. Its measured saving is one request per successful handshake, not fewer SQL statements. Other unchanged admission, profile, pairing and periodic owners make up the remaining window.

</details>

Shared causal session families are unchanged: exact-entry 4.1, actor hydration 1.1, entry-cache snapshots 0, watermark 1, row facts 0 statements per warmed turn. Raw exact-entry is 4.6 → 4.9 and entry-cache 1 → 1.6; their extra reads originate from background writer-queue and memory session-sync work. One additional auth-profile UNION read occurs over ten warmed turns (11 → 12); the cache-miss predicate was not traced.

First-turn causal +37 is **not all redistribution**: +32 schema-refresh attribution (63 total refresh statements on both heads), +7 actual model-context read, −2 other. The candidate's bounded prepared cohort executes the same eleven statements as the baseline, then a same-agent memory embedding publication precedes the extra five-SELECT context read. Its database-wide write receipt can invalidate prepared context; baseline memory publications precede its cohort. The trace does not record installation or the failed reuse predicate, so this is evidence of scheduling-sensitive invalidation, not proof of deterministic causality. The extra seven statements are uncompensated and remain disclosed. The diff adds no SQL operation, but source neutrality alone does not establish zero first-turn effect.

## Evidence and limits

Latency is **unmeasured**. This 32-core host was heavily loaded (SQL start loads 100.39/108.68/115.66 and 117.45/133.17/119.32). The warmed windows lasted 28.144 and 53.589 seconds, explaining why raw background counts need causal attribution. All three immediate Testbox attempts queued and were canceled; no provider fallback was used. Local wall spans below describe instrumentation and phase placement, not a latency gain.

Two completed Codex autoreview rounds found no actionable P0–P2 issues. Readiness tests hold preparation promises open, prove liveness during initialization, block session requests until projection completion, and prove pending imports settle before startup failure. The initial CI fixture mismatch was corrected. prs.title: perf(gateway): reduce idle timer and SQLite maintenance wakeups
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An idle Gateway wakes repeatedly for monitoring, filesystem reconciliation, WAL maintenance, worker GC, and lease renewal even when there is no pending work.

## User Impact

Idle Gateways perform less timer and SQLite maintenance work while preserving lease liveness, scheduled work, and WAL size bounds. Native filesystem events remain immediate; recovery from a missed event can take five minutes, and high-resolution monitoring can resume up to ten seconds after new work.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep maintenance with its existing owners and remove redundant work:

- Publish event-loop health every ten seconds while healthy and idle, pausing the native 20 ms histogram. Callback stall attribution and overdue-deadline detection stay active; work, degradation, or diagnostic exporters restore one-second sampling at the next deadline.
- Batch due leases in the shared heartbeat worker with one conditional UPDATE RETURNING per database. The SQL heartbeat is 30 seconds: min(300-second TTL, 90-second foreign-host stale bound) / 3. The separate 15-second filesystem heartbeat is unchanged.
- Share successful checkpoint completion through the physical database admission's write receipt. Sibling handles skip frames already checkpointed, and a new write invalidates completion. Blocked checkpoints keep retrying. Cancel the parent checkpoint timer when a worker takes ownership, including either registration order.
- Avoid arming worker GC below the existing 32 MiB growth threshold. The native config watcher reconciles every five minutes; native event handling and poll-mode cadence remain unchanged.

## Preserved boundaries and accepted edges

Exact lease owner/expiry predicates, explicit verification, startup identity repair, contention recovery, WAL bounds, final checkpoints, and periodic reclamation remain. No schema/config migration or new main-thread SQLite access.

Removed redundant work and accepted edges:
- A lease joining a shared cadence may renew once early, never late.
- Concurrent first WAL completion publishers may allow one extra passive pass before admission propagation.
- A missed native filesystem event can take up to five minutes to recover; delivered events still refresh immediately.
- New work/exporters can wait up to ten seconds for high-resolution monitoring; callback stalls remain observed during idle windows.

## Evidence

T1 in touched owners: **0 → 0**. Focused regressions cover lease payload preservation, expiry/owner replacement, sibling cancellation, checkpoint completion invalidation, blocked-reader recovery, idle monitor cadence/stalls, GC threshold, and native-versus-poll watcher policy.

One alternating baseline/candidate live pair used the shared harness 2.1.0 in isolated state, with five-minute disconnected-client idle windows. Baseline `3b75ce70f397`; candidate `b97c9a5bddc3`. The private harness copy adds idle callback attribution and uses the same supported 120-second handshake timeout for both runs. Both completed all foreground turns, child completion, cron, compaction, idle, and shutdown. This follows the current one-pair proof rule.

| Five-minute idle rate | Baseline | Candidate | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| All-thread SQL statements/min | 68.6 | 29.6 | −39.0 (−56.9%) |
| Worker requests/min | 20.0 | 13.6 | −6.4 (−32.0%) |
| Timer callbacks/min | 191.6 | 92.8 | −98.8 (−51.6%) |
| MAIN statements/min | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Lease renewal SQL/min | 12.0 | 2.0 | −10.0 |
| Passive WAL checkpoints/min | 16.8 | 3.4 | −13.4 |

| Warmed turn, median [min–max] over ten turns | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Causal all-thread statements | 170 [170–191] | 170 [170–170] |
| Causal requests | 41 [41–45] | 41 [41–41] |
| Causal MAIN statements | 0 [0–0] | 0 [0–0] |
| Raw window statements | 222.5 [180–327] | 181.5 [180–222] |
| Raw window requests | 57 [44–75] | 44.5 [44–58] |
| Raw window MAIN statements | 0 [0–0] | 0 [0–0] |

Shared read families per causal warmed turn: exact-entry facts 4.1 → 4.0; actor hydration 1.2 → 1.0; entry-cache snapshots 0 → 0; row facts 0 → 0; shared row facts 0 → 0; watermark reads 1.0 → 1.0. Raw-window counterparts: 4.7 → 4.3, 1.2 → 1.0, 1.6 → 0.6, 0 → 0, 0 → 0, and 2.0 → 2.0. Causal request operations: execute 31.2 → 31.0 and task 10.4 → 10.0 per warmed turn. The changed maintenance operations add no causal warmed statements or requests.

First-turn causal counts are 358 → 377 statements and 77 → 81 requests, with MAIN unchanged at 33. The extra four requests originate in unchanged ordered-entry reads (+1), transcript reads (+2), and deletion-journal reads (+1); SQL adds cold reader TEMP-trigger setup (+13) and six existing reads. No added request originates in the changed maintenance operations. Whole-workload totals still fall: 7,092 → 6,813 statements and 1,327 → 1,288 requests, MAIN 827 → 827. Timing shifts deferred work into first-turn and compaction windows; this is the documented attribution-over-raw allowance, not a claim of first-turn improvement.

Physical timer attribution (callbacks/min): shared scheduler 115.2 → 57.0; filesystem reconciliation 24.0 → 4.2; delivered filesystem hint debouncers 22.2 → 15.0; worker GC 10.2 → 0.2; SQL lease heartbeat 4.0 → 2.0; filesystem heartbeat/watchdog 5.4 → 5.4; HTTP connection tracking 4.0 → 4.0; other deadlines/cleanup 6.6 → 5.0. Within that scheduler total, main-thread callbacks fall 97.2 → 33.0 while worker WAL callbacks rise 18.0 → 24.0. Both runs have three worker schedulers; one execution worker’s existing state/agent WAL deadlines are staggered in the candidate instead of coalescing, producing the observed +6/min. Scheduler job labels overlap these physical callbacks: event-loop health falls 60.4 → 6.8 and the duplicate main-thread WAL job 12.0 → 0. Do not add nested job counts to the physical total.

Timer owners and deadlines in the measured pair:

| Owner / source | Callback or scheduling function | Deadline |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Gateway scheduler, `src/infra/gateway-scheduler.ts` | `hostClock.arm` | Earliest owned deadline; one unreferenced timer per scheduler |
| Event-loop monitor, `src/gateway/server/event-loop-health.ts` | `scheduleSample` | 1 s active → 10 s healthy idle |
| WAL owner, `src/infra/sqlite-wal.ts` | `configureSqliteWalMaintenance` / `schedule` | 10 s checkpoint tick; 30 min reclamation; delegated parent tick removed |
| Filesystem adapter, `src/config/source-file.ts` and fs-safe `watch.js` | `createConfigFileAdapter`, `scheduleInterval`, `onHint` | Native recovery 30 s → 5 min; delivered hints debounce 25 ms |
| Worker GC, `src/infra/worker-idle-gc.ts` | `scheduleWorkerIdleGc` | One 1 s delay only above 32 MiB growth |
| SQL lease owner, `src/state/openclaw-state-lease-renewal.worker.ts` | `createStateLeaseRenewalScheduler` / `run` | Earliest due lease; Gateway cadence 30 s |
| Filesystem lease, `src/infra/gateway-state-owner-heartbeat.runtime.ts` | `runGatewayStateOwnerHeartbeat` / `beat` | 15 s; unchanged |
| Filesystem watchdog, `src/infra/gateway-state-owner-heartbeat.ts` | `startGatewayStateOwnerHeartbeat` / `watch` | Remaining expiry deadline; unchanged |
| Pairing plugin, `extensions/device-pair/notify.ts` | `startPairingNotifier` | 10 s; unchanged |
| Worker pool, `packages/worker-runtime/src/worker-task-pool-retirement.ts` | `idle` | 60 s retirement deadline; unchanged |
| HTTP transport, Node `Server.setupConnectionsTracking` | Connection tracking | 30 s; unchanged |

The ≤40 callbacks/min aim remains open. Remaining work includes worker WAL deadlines, the device-pair notifier, auth pruning, placement/environment sweeps, and existing liveness/maintenance deadlines. This PR preserves their contracts rather than stretching cron or lease deadlines. The native 20 ms histogram is paused while healthy and idle; those native wakeups are not counted as JavaScript timer callbacks above.

Host load was 118.4/128.0/127.3 before baseline and 133.1/113.4/111.8 before candidate on 32 cores. Counts are reported; CPU percentage, latency, and worker-service-time improvements are unmeasured on this loaded host. An immediately granted remote lease expired during source staging before running any workload and was stopped; no remote performance claim is made.

Two Codex autoreview rounds: scoped-clean at P0–P2. Changed-file format, basic lint, and `git diff --check` pass. The focused lease renewal regression passes (2 tests, 55.42 seconds including setup on the loaded host). The idle-monitor regression also passes (21 tests, 500.74 seconds in Vitest; 776.78 seconds including wrapper preparation/cleanup). Full tests and static gates run in PR CI. Final LOC after integration: +699 / −103 across 22 files.

The initial CI run passed types, lint, source contracts and architecture guards. Its PR-caused fixture failures are corrected: the lease proof now runs in the hosted database-worker pool, the wrapper inventory includes the new worker, and idle-monitor fake time advances without introducing synthetic stalls. The untouched `skill-library-read.test.ts` failures are also present in [main CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38334375513) at the same `sessions.create` boundary; they are recorded for the main-repair owner. The latest test-only commit also fixes a type-aware unbound-method lint diagnostic and accounts for the fake clock's own observed 20 ms step in the two new idle-monitor assertions. Main integration keeps the new skills-discovery worker unchanged and drops this PR’s obsolete native-skills-watcher interval change and test. The measurement above is pinned to the pre-integration revisions, which still had that watcher; its filesystem subtotal includes the now-retired path, so it is not an exact-head claim for current skills discovery. The retained lease, WAL, GC, config-watcher, and health-monitor paths are unchanged by integration. Integrated-head CI [38344925133](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38344925133) passed every selected behavior test, production types, the other test-type leaves, lint, source contracts, architecture guards, and ratchets. Its only failure is `check-test-types-core-4`: untouched `src/commands/config-preflight-snapshot.test.ts:41` still imports the now-private `readConfigPreflightSnapshot`. The identical TS2724 diagnostic was reproduced on main `fcb89a331a1f` in [baseline job 115124606702](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38345114058/job/115124606702); the main-repair owner is fixing it in #170619. The earlier skill-library behavioral failures did not recur in this integrated run. ClawSweeper reported no actionable introduced defect; its sole requested change, preserving main’s skills-discovery owner during conflict resolution, is complete. After the Phase E hold file was removed, main `3f1175be9d5e` was merged cleanly into head `11b43a8d4220`. The three overlapping documentation/test-routing files merged without manual resolution; the PR remains +699/−103 across the same 22 files. This also includes the preflight test repair from #170619. Changed-file oxfmt, type-aware oxlint, and `git diff --check` pass on this head. Final exact-head CI [38350353861](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38350353861) is green, including every selected behavior job, all production/test type leaves, lint, source contracts, architecture/Knip/Madge guards, and T1/dialect/worker ratchets. Required CI, dependency-review, and security-sensitive-review statuses are all successful for `11b43a8d4220`; no inherited-failure exception is needed. No additional local suites or SQL pair were run under the compute-conservation rule.

No SDK changes. No update, Doctor, schema/migration, plugin-loading, or service-lifecycle change; published-driver update cell is not applicable.

prs.title: perf(memory): batch indexing after agent idle periods
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session indexing previously coalesced transcript notifications for only five seconds. Active conversations therefore paid transcript preparation, embedding-cache lookup, and index-publication overhead roughly once per turn even after #170302 batched individual sources.

Memory Core now waits for a 30-second per-agent quiet period, with a five-minute maximum deferral under continuous transcript activity. Existing agent-run execution ownership (including queued turns) gates background passes; active turns always take precedence. A turn that starts during indexing lets the current bounded publication finish, then pending sessions resume after the next quiet period. Rejected passes restore the consumed queue, retaining later updates, and retry through the same quiet-period timer. Ordinary groups share transcript-worker preparation, source-state/cache reads, and one publication transaction. Groups are bounded to eight sources, 128 publication rows, and the existing transfer budget; an oversized single source retains its atomic streamed replacement.

The existing background transcript-worker pool keeps this work separate from foreground model-context reads. No new scheduler, persistent queue, configuration option, database schema, or synchronous fallback is added. The queued-run registry now emits the existing runtime notification for the first/last execution lease even when display metadata remains retained.

## Freshness and accepted edges

New transcript content becomes searchable after the quiet period. While the agent is idle, continuous transcript changes defer indexing for at most about five minutes, plus embedding time. Running or back-to-back turns can defer it longer: each return to idle starts a fresh quiet period because foreground work wins. The current turn already has its content in context. `memory_search` serves the published index and does not flush pending transcript changes. Shutdown does not flush the pending timer; startup catches up incrementally. Rewrites and compaction retain the existing reset-generation path.

Removed repeated work/checks:
- Per-source transcript-worker transactions and source-hash requests become bounded batch reads; all sources use their pass snapshot and later transcript notifications catch subsequent writes.
- The source-hash lookup's repeated owner-currentness assertion is removed; publication remains under the existing owner and preserves forget authority at the write boundary.
- The obsolete test matrix for per-source hash-read admission is removed with that read; batch publication, rollback, and incremental parity cover the retained contracts.
- Search-triggered session dirty flushing is removed; the documented recall delay is intentional.
- Provider fallback reuses the pass's already-read embedding cache instead of reading it again; cache entries are content-addressed.

Forget/tombstone checks remain because they protect user-requested deletion. The scoped memory publication receipt remains unchanged so memory writes do not evict unrelated session caches.

## Measurement

Pinned harness v2.1.0 pair: base `5cf2615e65ec` and candidate `9240cb4ffd08`, ten warmed turns each, identical 35-second post-turn quiet window. Both full workloads passed (including subagent, cron, compaction, and shutdown). The campaign's current proof policy permits one pair. Runs used the shared CPU gate; host 1-minute load was 88.1 before baseline and 96.3 before candidate.

| Measurement | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Warmed all-thread statements/turn, median [min–max] | 217.5 [191–352] | 194 [190–207] |
| Warmed requests/turn, median [min–max] | 57.5 [47–87] | 49 [47–54] |
| Ten-turn window statements / requests | 2,270 / 583 | 1,958 / 494 |
| Turn-caused statements / requests per turn, mean | 185.5 / 43.7 | 180.8 / 43.4 |
| Warmed MAIN statements (total and per turn) | 0 | 0 |
| Memory-index SQL / requests during ten turns | 244 / 24 | 0 / 0 |
| Transcript preparation batches during ten turns | 6 | 0 |
| Memory-index background SQL / requests per minute | 391.3 / 38.5 | 0 / 0 |
| Overall background SQL per minute | 665.5 | 224.5 |
| Loaded-host timing p50 / p95 (diagnostic only) | 416 / 736.7 ms | 478.5 / 853.2 ms |
| Full workload statements / requests | 6,912 / 1,310 | 6,560 / 1,185 |

The warmed-window reduction is 312 statements and 89 requests; indexing does no work during these active turns (−100% versus the baseline window), and overall background SQL/min falls 66.3%. The timing figures use `agent.wait`'s start/end timestamps, with linearly interpolated percentiles. Host load makes these timings unsuitable for evaluating a latency change; reliable latency remains unmeasured. The candidate's deferred pass began in the 35-second settle phase (20 statements / 2 requests), then yielded when subsequent foreground phases started. A separate live probe with ten warmed turns and a 90-second quiet window completed successfully: zero warm indexing passes, then one source publication during settle; the stopped Gateway database contains the indexed transcript and all three chunks. The probe logged 44 memory-index statements during settle. Its generic postprocessor retained the original 13-turn assertion and rejected this intentionally shortened 11-turn workload; direct evidence verification passed all eleven turns, shutdown, and durable index publication. Incremental/full-reindex search parity passes in the dedicated regression.

Within baseline warm indexing: transcript-preparation requests 6→0; source-state/hash SELECTs 12→0; embedding-cache lookup SELECTs 6→0; source/chunk/recall/provenance publication INSERTs 24→0. Those operations move into bounded quiet-period batches, not the foreground.

Shared-read attribution per turn (whole warmed window; turn-caused count in parentheses): exact-entry facts 4.8 (4.2) → 4.1 (4.1); actor hydration 1.1 (1.1) → 1.1 (1.1); entry-cache snapshots 1.6 (0) → 0.2 (0); selected row-fact SELECTs 11.1 (11.1) → 11.1 (11.1); watermarks 1 (1) → 1 (1). No shared family or warm MAIN count rises.

T1 in memory indexing: **0 → 0**. CI's database-worker and dialect ratchets passed on both measured head `9240cb4ffd08` and integrated head `7607f460ca621`.

## Evidence

- Changed-file oxfmt, basic oxlint, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Added fake-clock quiet-period/coalescing, maximum-deferral, long-running-turn, and failed-pass retry regressions. A nine-session integration regression interrupts embedding, then proves every deferred source is published after the next quiet period.
- Added execution-owner/queued-owner lifecycle coverage and multi-session incremental transcript parity.
- Extended index parity to ten queued transcript changes, settling before comparison with a full reindex.
- Group publication rollback/retry and shared-cache regressions cover the removed per-source transaction/read classes.
- Search regression proves pending sessions do not acquire a maintenance manager; explicit indexing still publishes them. Updated the former search-maintenance wait and five-second timer expectations to this contract. The batch-yield regression now observes the actual preparation/publication boundary.
- Focused source-race replay: 12/12 passed, including changed/deleted source isolation, the SQLite transaction collision, and recall/delete ordering. Custom-provider concurrency replay: 2/2 passed. Batch-yield replay: 2/2 passed. SDK runtime guardrails: 7/7 passed. Real-manager search: 11/11 passed (211.25 s total; the no-flush assertion took 4.889 s). Startup/close replay: 6/6 passed (580.71 s, including a 319 s worker build). Loaded-host setup dominates these runs; the yield assertions themselves take 52 ms and 9 ms. Incremental delta replay: 3/3 passed (245.52 s Vitest; 74.8 s worker preparation), including ten queued updates whose settled search results equal a full reindex. The parity fixture drains startup discovery before seeding its baseline so initial forced indexing cannot race that discovery.
- Codex autoreview round 1 found a stranded-failed-work bug; it is fixed with queue restoration and a regression. The second/final review found partial-shadow publication after interruption. Interrupted shadow work now takes the existing failure/retry path, retaining the previously published index; a regression covers that boundary. No further review round is planned. Two review rounds are complete; final static/API evidence is recorded below.

This does not change schema, migration, update, or plugin/service lifecycle contracts; no published-driver update cell applies.

Timer ownership: this replaces the existing memory transcript coalescing timer; other idle/background owners remain unchanged.

Diff: 43 files, +1,525 / -643 lines (including regressions and deleted obsolete coverage).

Measured-head CI (`9240cb4ffd08`): [run 38327575283](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38327575283) completed. All 25 static jobs passed, including production/test types, type-aware lint, source contracts, Madge/architecture, docs, and T1/dialect ratchets. The three memory bundles passed 56 files / 629 tests; wall times were 318, 280, and 250 seconds (test steps 256, 217, and 213 seconds). All changed tests and six affected SDK mock consumers were explicitly present in passing logs. Core activity (3 tests), session reset/batched exports (10), and SDK contract (1) also passed.

The earlier CI failure in `server.sessions.create.durability.test.ts` expected separately staged idle input after refused transcript commit. Main fixed that stale expectation in `3c63da22f046b` (atomic admission accepts neither pending input nor transcript when rejected); this fix is included by the main merge. The baseline diagnostic timed out in Gateway setup before reaching its assertion, so it is not claimed as inherited-failure reproduction. The redundant head diagnostic targeting the removed test name was stopped; final CI runs the replacement test. The previous dashboard-abort failure passed on the measured head.

Follow-up from the completed review of `5c299ee6834b` (P2; retained under the requested two-round/relaxed-landing scope): requeue a handled provider-fallback failure that resolves normally while retaining dirty source state. This can delay retry until later transcript activity or startup; the authoritative transcript remains durable. It is not a security issue or loss of source data. The other P2 finding, retaining completed vectors in the source-wide embedding array, was fixed on main and that cleanup is preserved in this integration.

Final integration: removed the two obsolete batch-source summary helpers reported by Knip, then merged current main (`5e1752da6a78e`) to include its UI export cleanup and memory WAL-reader ownership. Final source head is `7607f460ca621`. [Integrated-head CI 38331920780](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38331920780) completed: all hosted static checks and all three memory bundles passed. Two unrelated test jobs failed, with attribution below.

SDK API comparison: two additive exports, `observeAgentRunActivity(agentId, listener): () => void` and `buildSessionEntries(inputs): Promise<(SessionFileEntry | null)[]>`, with no removed exports or changed existing signatures. The latter is on the private local-only memory session surface and its memory-host barrel. The source-derived API diff was reviewed; full SDK surface check, runtime guardrails, production types, and test types passed. Two attempts at native semantic-closure rendering stalled on the baseline and were stopped; a completed native render is not claimed.


Earlier integrated-head failure attribution:
- The eight managed-abort cases in `src/worker/worker.chat-abort.test.ts` also fail on scheduled main [run 38331230273, job 115081407653](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38331230273/job/115081407653), head `2dd42a977aa9`. Seven preview cases have the same unexpected history-save warning; the no-preview case on main reaches the later event-count assertion (four events instead of three). This PR does not change that file. The existing red-main owner is tracking these failures.
- `src/plugins/install.npm-spec.e2e.test.ts` timed out in the `npm-pack` lifecycle-successor case after 120 seconds. A focused run on baseline `5cf2615e65ec` reproduced that exact test and timeout (122.307 seconds elapsed). The suite owns its npm package fixtures and ran in its supported `OPENCLAW_E2E_SKIP_BUILD=1` mode after ordinary preparation refused to rewrite potentially shared Gateway artifacts. Remaining baseline tests and the redundant candidate replay were stopped after the exact match; candidate CI is the head-side evidence. No passing whole-file replay is claimed.
- The script and production Knip scans report only findings also present on scheduled main: `literal`, `hasProviderRequestSizeCeiling`, `getResolvedSpeechProviderConfig`, `OpenClawApp`, `ApplicationShell`, and `ShellLayoutController`. Both combined and standalone full-tree scans timed out at the unchanged 600-second budget under local load. A completed local full-tree result is not claimed. The two newly obsolete memory helpers were removed. The later main cleanup #170499 is now integrated; its dedicated [Knip proof 38334569481](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38334569481) passed. The integration adds no exports beyond the already-scanned patch; no new local full-tree scan was run under compute conservation.

The coordinator removed the Phase E merge hold at 22:06 local. This branch then merged current main `3f1175be9d5e` into head `a7fb093803e9`. The single conflict preserves main's disabled-batch fallback together with the pass's prepared embedding cache. Main's provider-lifetime simplification and completed-vector cleanup are retained. Changed-file oxfmt/oxlint and `git diff --check` passed. [Final integrated-head CI 38350353218](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38350353218) passed on `a7fb093803e9`, including all three memory bundles, production/test types, type-aware lint, source contracts, architecture, and T1/dialect/worker ratchets. prs.title: improve: speed up sidebar refresh browser checks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Sidebar browser tests spend seconds waiting for real refresh collection and cooldown timers. The roster test's 250 ms pauses also no longer cross the current 4–5 second collection windows they claim to exercise.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. The same rendered sidebar workflows run faster while retaining recovery, error, keyboard, touch, filtering, and no-overlapping-refresh coverage.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing Playwright virtual-clock helper to cross complete refresh windows. The roster holds its first read across three collection windows, observes the distinct refreshed row after releasing the response, and then advances the bounded cooldown to verify one trailing read. Waiting for the rendered response is necessary: releasing a mock response alone does not mean the page has processed it.

## Evidence

The roster case dropped from 18.287 s to 7.401 s in focused runs; suspension/recovery dropped from 21.082–22.053 s to 2.317 s. The final full two-file run passed all four cases in 35.892 s including a 14.54 s production UI build (roster 8.732 s, recovery 2.576 s). All six refresh-coordinator unit cases passed in 4.301 s wrapper time.

The owning UI E2E typecheck, targeted lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. Independent P0–P2 review found no actionable issues. Lint required an equivalent object-copy syntax correction in the synthetic response fixture; no behavior or assertion changed. The first development attempt exposed the response-processing race described above; its trailing-read assertion failed until the rendered-response boundary was added. The final proof retains all original assertions and screenshots. CI supplies broad integration coverage.

prs.title: fix(gateway): align SSH pairing tests with handshake authority
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the SSH-verified node pairing test failing on `main` when approval finishes during the recovery lookup, after the handshake has already read device authority.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior changes. The test now distinguishes approval before the final authority read (immediate connection) from approval afterward (explicit retry followed by successful connection), while retaining device identity, approval provenance, and first-capability-surface assertions.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is a stale test, not a pairing regression. Commit `c86edb99b3d363c2b7e519289668f4fbab37a2c4` (#170594) intentionally moved the recovery-only pairing-list lookup after the final live authority read in `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-device-pairing.ts:399-425`. Its documented contract accepts that later approval requires reconnect; a recovery snapshot cannot authorize a rejected handshake.

The old test released SSH approval from that recovery lookup but still expected the first handshake to succeed. Cover both sides of the actual authority boundary instead: release approval before the live read and require `hello-ok`, or during recovery and require `NOT_PAIRED` with retry guidance. Both cases must subsequently connect with the real SSH-approved device and approved initial capability surface. The existing after-rejection case remains intact. No retries or timeouts were added.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

## Evidence

- Reported baseline on `main` (`c0888b457b5`): `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.node-pairing-ssh-verify.test.ts` — 6 passed, 1 failed. The “during handshake” case expected `ok: true` at line 302 but received `ok: false`.
- After: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/*pairing*.test.ts src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-device-pairing.test.ts` — **135 tests passed across 16 files**, including all **8 SSH pairing cases** and the production owner's real-WebSocket authority matrix. Runner time: 419.62 seconds (424.54 seconds wall time).
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/gateway/server.node-pairing-ssh-verify.test.ts` — passed.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/gateway/server.node-pairing-ssh-verify.test.ts` — passed.

Two-way door: reverting changes only test coverage. Blast radius is the SSH pairing test; no runtime, persisted state, configuration, or public contract changes.
