prs.title: fix(agents): restore saved history for fresh Claude CLI sessions on a native login
prs.body:
Related: #154716

Supersedes #156600 (builds on its account-fingerprint approach; its author is credited as co-author on the commits)

Note: #154716 carries the `clawsweeper:needs-product-decision` and `clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr` labels and this PR does not fix the existing-session gap described under Gaps, so it uses `Related:` and should not auto-close the issue.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Claude CLI conversation on a native Claude login loses its saved history whenever its Claude session is replaced or lost, because OpenClaw cannot name the login's owner and so refuses to replay it.

With the `claude-cli` backend on a native Claude CLI login and no OpenClaw-managed credential, the history boundary cannot build an owner fingerprint. `prepareCliHistoryBoundary` writes no `cliHistoryBoundary`, `prepare.ts` turns the missing writer into `rawTranscriptReseedReason: "auth-unknown"`, and `loadCliSessionPromptContext` refuses to seed saved history into any fresh CLI session (replacement session, cleared binding, lost native transcript). On the base commit every native turn logs `cli session history refused across auth boundary: reason=auth-unknown` (scenario 1 below). On the author's own install (a file-backed native login) all 301 session entries carry an empty boundary.

The guard exists so saved history never crosses to a different account. This change keeps that property and adds the native login as an accepted owner only when the operator opts in (`plugins.entries.anthropic.config.historyRecovery.attestNativeLogin: true`), only when Anthropic attests which account its credential belongs to, and only for the environment the Claude process is actually started with. Without the opt-in, nothing changes: the native login has no owner and saved history stays refused, as on main.

## User Impact

Nothing changes for an install that does not opt in. With `plugins.entries.anthropic.config.historyRecovery.attestNativeLogin: true` on a Gateway host whose Claude CLI login is a readable credential, a fresh Claude session for a conversation that started after the opt-in gets its saved history reseeded again, with or without the `anthropic:claude-cli` profile. If the login changes, is revoked, is selected differently by the child environment, or Anthropic does not attest it, saved history is refused, as the contract table below lists.

What an operator who opts in sees differently (without the opt-in, OpenClaw never reads the native token for history recovery and makes no profile request: row 35 below, 0 requests, the same prompt as current main):

- The Gateway makes one `GET https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/profile` per access token it has not attested yet, with the token Claude CLI itself would send there (834 ms measured once on a real login). Later turns on the same token make no request. `openclaw agent --local` starts a new process per turn, so it makes one request per turn.
- A turn prepared within ten minutes of its access token's expiry runs without saved history, because Claude CLI rotates the token before it accepts the prompt (measured below). The next turn is offered history again.
- A turn whose writer may replay saved history fails with `CLI history authority changed before execution` if its login changes, or cannot be attested, between preparation and the prompt reaching Claude, instead of sending that history to another account. That is every turn of a conversation the native login owns, fresh or resumed, except a turn prepared within ten minutes of token expiry, which runs without saved history. Conversations the native login does not own are never refused because of it.

One new plugin config key, `historyRecovery.attestNativeLogin` in the Anthropic plugin's config schema, default `false`. No schema migration. Conversations that already have history and no recorded boundary stay fenced, including conversations written before the opt-in (see Gaps).

## Why This Change Was Made

Main documents opaque CLI logins as unable to authorize replay (`docs/gateway/cli-backends.md`, "History account boundaries"). That is right when the login is only a profile name or a local record. It is wrong when the Gateway host holds a readable credential and Anthropic can say which account it belongs to. An acceptable owner has to cover the no-profile install (the bundled backend sets `autoSelectAuthProfile: false`), must be bound to the credential rather than to the `.claude.json` account record beside it, must be rechecked wherever saved history is sent to Claude or a turn becomes the owner's history, must survive Claude CLI's own token rotation, and must not put a network request or a subprocess on every transcript write.

## The change in one sentence

Once the operator opts in, the native Claude login's owner is the account uuid Anthropic's OAuth profile endpoint returns for the exact access token the child Claude would use, attested asynchronously at preparation and after the run, and rechecked synchronously at every spawn, prompt send, prompt hook answer that carries the turn's private context, and coverage commit against an in-process attestation cache keyed by a per-process HMAC of the token.

Shape of the whole PR against base `02368839f49` (three commits): 23 production files +918/-149 (22 TypeScript files and the Anthropic plugin manifest), 16 test files +2168/-111, and three docs files (the contract paragraphs and the config baseline counts and hash). The attestation lives in `provider-auth-claude-compat.ts` (credential read, profile request, cache), `cli-credentials.ts` (the resolver seam), `history-boundary.ts` (async attestation, synchronous rechecks, background re-attestation, refresh window), `execute.ts` (one post-run settle call) and `prepare.ts`. The owner confirmation inside worker transactions is in the turn commit and transcript report paths in `src/config/sessions` and in the SessionManager metadata worker in `src/agents/sessions`. The check on the prompt hook answer is in `extensions/anthropic/cli.runtime.ts`. The opt-in is declared in `extensions/anthropic/openclaw.plugin.json` and read by `isNativeCliLoginAttestationEnabled` in `cli-credentials.ts`.

Design:

- The attestation runs only when the operator opts in: `plugins.entries.anthropic.config.historyRecovery.attestNativeLogin: true`, declared in the Anthropic plugin's config schema with default `false` and a UI hint that names the endpoint the token goes to. `prepareCliHistoryBoundary` checks `isNativeCliLoginAttestationEnabled(provider, params.config)` before it resolves the native owner, so without the opt-in no credential is read for history recovery, no request is made and the turn is prepared exactly as on main (`auth-unknown`). The rechecks below exist only on writers whose owner was attested at preparation. The run's config is read per turn, so turning the opt-in off takes effect on the next turn.
- `attestClaudeNativeLoginOwner({ env })` (`src/plugin-sdk/provider-auth-claude-compat.ts`) reads the access token the CLI would use under `env` with the CLI's own precedence (Keychain first on macOS, bounded non-interactive lookups, tri-state so only `security`'s item-not-found exit 44 lets `.credentials.json` stand; then the file). It sends that token, and nothing else, to `https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/profile` (`Authorization: Bearer`, `redirect: "error"`, 3 s `AbortSignal.timeout`, the process global fetch, so the env-proxy dispatcher OpenClaw installs at startup applies). Claude CLI 2.1.283 calls the same URL with the same header (bundle excerpt below). The owner is `uuid:<account.uuid>` from the response. No owner on any failure: network error, timeout, non-2xx, a body without `account.uuid`, no credential, or an access token already expired. The error is dropped, not logged. The `.claude.json` account record is no longer read.
- The cache maps `HMAC-SHA256(key, token)` to the attested owner, with `key` from `randomBytes(32)` per process, at most 64 entries, only in memory. A token belongs to one account for its whole life, so an entry can stop matching (rotation, logout) but never start naming someone else. Only successes are cached. Nothing about the token is persisted; the stored boundary keeps only the existing `cli-history-v1` fingerprint over `["native-login", "uuid:<account>"]`.
- `readClaudeNativeLoginOwner({ env })` is the synchronous recheck: it rereads the credential and returns the cached owner for that exact token, or nothing. It never touches the network. The seam stays `resolveNativeCliLoginOwner(backendId, env)` (now asynchronous, returning `{ owner?, refreshDueAt? }`) plus `readAttestedNativeCliLoginOwner(backendId, env)` for the synchronous checks; both return nothing for backends other than `claude-cli`.
- Preparation awaits the attestation for the environment the child will start from (`resolveCliChildEnv`, under the run's skill env snapshot, as before). Spawn, prompt send and coverage commits call the synchronous recheck, so the per-turn Keychain budget stays at 10 lookups for a readable item.
- Claude CLI rotates its access token itself, before it answers `initialize` and so before the prompt is sent, once the token is within 5 minutes of expiry (bundle: `now + 300000 >= expiresAt`; probe below). Two rules follow:
  - A turn prepared with a token that expires within 10 minutes runs without saved history (`writer.replaysHistory === false`; `prepare.ts` treats it like `auth-unknown`), and still covers its rows.
  - A boundary check on a turn without saved history that sees a token this process has not attested starts a background attestation of it. Coverage waits until it settles and stops for good if it names another account. A turn carrying saved history refuses an unattested token outright.
- After the child exits and before the turn's rows commit, `writer.settleNativeLogin()` awaits any background attestation and, if the prepared token had entered the refresh window, attests whatever token the child left behind.
- Worker coverage confirms the owner from inside the worker's write transaction. The host no longer decides before it dispatches the command. When coverage is about to advance, the worker puts a probe (a `SharedArrayBuffer` cell) on a transaction admission request (turn commits) or on the commit admission of the write (transcript reports). The host answers the cell with the live owner check, synchronously, right before it grants that admission, and the worker reads the answer after the grant. A missing answer, a missing owner check or a check that throws means the owner does not hold. On a mismatch the rows commit and coverage is not advanced. The check runs once per coverage commit, so the Keychain budget is unchanged. The in-process path checks inside its transaction as before.
- A resumed Claude session also receives saved data: durable reference context from the transcript and the conversation's interrupted inputs. So any native turn whose writer replays history counts as carrying saved history at spawn and prompt send, fresh or resumed, including a conversation's first turn. A turn prepared inside the refresh window runs without saved history and receives no interrupted inputs either.
- Claude asks for the turn's private context (interrupted inputs, durable reference context) through its `UserPromptSubmit` hook after it has received the prompt, so the hook answer is the last place that saved data leaves OpenClaw. The stdio transport writes each answer through a closure the Claude runtime returns, called synchronously at the final write. When the answer is a `UserPromptSubmit` answer carrying `additionalContext`, that closure runs the turn's full `assertCurrent` (on a native login: reread the credential and require this process's attestation of that exact token for the same owner). If the check fails, Claude receives an empty hook answer and the context is withheld. Other hook answers and tool permission requests keep the cheaper stream check. The host passes that stream check to the bundled Claude runtime as a host-internal field, the way it passes the forwarded auth credential: it is not part of the plugin SDK `CliBackendExecuteContext` type (`ClaudeCliExecuteContext` in `cli.runtime.ts` declares it), so the public execution context is unchanged from main.
- SessionManager appends committed by the metadata worker take the same host owner check. The probe rides on the command's one transaction admission and the host answers it before it grants. Coverage facts that ask for the check advance coverage only on a confirmed answer, so a write path that cannot ask keeps its rows and leaves coverage where it is. Writers whose owner cannot change during the run (a static credential or a named OAuth account) carry no owner check.
- What a mismatch does depends on what is at stake, as before: a turn that may carry saved history is refused before Claude receives it; a change after the prompt was sent withholds the turn's private context from the prompt hook answer; that change, or one on a turn prepared inside the refresh window, lets the turn run, and its rows are kept but not covered, so coverage stops and the next turn is refused that history until `/new` or an empty reset.

`docs/gateway/cli-backends.md` states the contract: what is attested, the request and its timeout, fail-closed cases, what is held in memory and what is persisted, the synchronous rechecks, the refresh window, and the restart limitation.

## What this PR decides, and why

The question is what may authorize native replay: the local account record beside a readable credential, or an identity bound to the credential itself. This PR binds the owner to the credential with Anthropic's own account lookup (option C below), and only for an operator who opts in. Every other install keeps D, main's behavior.

| | A: local account record | B: `claude auth status` | C: authenticated profile request (this PR) | D: keep native replay fenced |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Owner source | `.claude.json` `oauthAccount.accountUuid`, read from the child's environment while a credential exists | the same record, as the CLI reports it | the `account.uuid` Anthropic returns for the exact access token the child would use | none |
| Credential for account B beside a record for account A | owned by A: history replayed to B's credential | owned by A | owned by B: A's history refused | refused |
| Bound to the executing environment | yes | yes, if run with the child env | yes: attested for the child env at preparation, rechecked at spawn, send and every coverage commit | not applicable |
| Cost per turn | 10 Keychain lookups (readable item) | one subprocess per check, 135 to 1673 ms measured | the same 10 lookups; one request per new access token (834 ms measured), none for a token already attested | none |
| Token rotation by Claude CLI | owner unchanged | owner unchanged | the rotated token is attested before the turn's rows are covered; a turn prepared inside the refresh window runs without saved history | not applicable |
| What it sends where | nothing | nothing | the access token, to the Anthropic endpoint Claude CLI itself sends it to | nothing |

Why C:

- A and B cannot detect the mismatch. Run against synthetic files with the real Claude CLI 2.1.283, `claude auth status --json` reports a fake token as logged in and returns whatever account the record holds; editing the record moves the same credential from account A to account B ([identity/claude-auth-status-probe.txt](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/11acddf1615c4aab8ad5741803e5df324dd1cd74/final/identity/claude-auth-status-probe.txt)). The CLI's own refresh path never rewrites `accountUuid` or `emailAddress` ([identity/cli-bundle-excerpt.txt](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/11acddf1615c4aab8ad5741803e5df324dd1cd74/final/identity/cli-bundle-excerpt.txt)).
- Anything keyed on token material alone changes owner on every refresh: one real refresh rotated both the access and the refresh token while the account stayed the same ([identity/refresh-rotation.txt](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/11acddf1615c4aab8ad5741803e5df324dd1cd74/final/identity/refresh-rotation.txt)). C keys the cache on the token but takes the owner from Anthropic, so a rotation needs one new attestation, not a new owner.
- The profile request is the one Claude CLI makes itself. The bundle's `AFe(e)` is ``gt.get(`${BASE_API_URL}/api/oauth/profile`, {headers: {Authorization: `Bearer ${e}`, ...}, timeout: 1e4})``, validated against `{account: {uuid, email}, organization: {uuid}}`. OpenClaw already sends Claude OAuth tokens to the same host for usage (`src/infra/provider-usage.fetch.claude.ts`, `GET /api/oauth/usage`).
- D keeps native conversations losing history when their Claude session is replaced. It stays the default: C sends the token to Anthropic, so it runs only for an operator who sets `historyRecovery.attestNativeLogin`.

What C costs, for an operator who opts in, is listed under Gaps: the token leaves the process to Anthropic, an idle expired token after a restart has no owner, a refresh-due turn runs without saved history, and a rotation outside the refresh window stops coverage.

## Contract table

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Native login, `historyRecovery.attestNativeLogin` unset or `false` (the default) | no owner, no credential read and no request for history recovery, history refused: unchanged from main (row 35) |
| Opt-in removed after a covered turn | no request; history refused; the stored boundary becomes `unknown` (row 36) |
| Opt-in set after a conversation already has rows | those rows stay fenced; a conversation started after the opt-in recovers (row 37) |
| The cases below assume `attestNativeLogin: true` | |
| Native login, no profile selected, credential attested | owner named, history seeded into a fresh session |
| Native login with `anthropic:claude-cli` pinned | same |
| Credential for account B beside the unchanged account-A record | owner is B: A's history refused |
| Account record relabelled to B beside account A's credential | owner is still A: history seeded |
| Login switched A to B between turns | history refused |
| Credential removed between turns | history refused |
| Profile endpoint times out (3 s), returns 401/5xx, or returns no `account.uuid` | no owner, history refused; the turn runs |
| Access token already expired and not attested in this process | no owner, no request made, history refused |
| Access token attested earlier in this process, now expired | same owner |
| Access token within 10 minutes of expiry at preparation | turn runs without saved history; the token Claude rotates to is attested after the run; rows covered; the next turn is seeded |
| Turn on a native login whose writer replays history (fresh or resumed Claude session, including the conversation's first turn); credential replaced or removed after preparation, before spawn or send | step refused with `CLI history authority changed before execution`; nothing reaches Claude |
| Same turn; credential replaced or removed after the prompt is sent, before Claude's `UserPromptSubmit` hook is answered | the hook answer carries no private context; the turn runs; rows kept, coverage stops; the next turn is refused history (rows 33, 34) |
| Turn prepared within 10 minutes of token expiry (runs without saved history); credential replaced by an unattested token before send | turn runs; the token is attested in the background; rows covered only if it is the same account |
| Credential rotated to another account's token during a turn, then switched back | coverage stops for the run |
| Credential replaced during an awaited worker commit preparation | rows recorded; coverage not advanced |
| Credential reassigned to another account while the coverage command is queued for the SQLite worker (turn commit or transcript report) | rows recorded; coverage not advanced; the next turn is refused history (scenario 22) |
| SessionManager append committed by the metadata worker while the login holds | row recorded and covered |
| The same append after the login is replaced by an unattested credential | row recorded; coverage not advanced |
| Same-account token rotated after send, outside the refresh window | rows recorded; coverage not advanced; next turn refused history |
| Skill `env` config selects another config dir, on every turn | that login's attested account is the owner; history recovered |
| Skill `env` config selecting another login is added mid-conversation | that turn is a login switch: history refused, the turn runs |
| Backend `env` selects another config dir than the Gateway process | owner is the one in the child's environment |
| Child environment, or its user settings `env` block, selects an API key, token or cloud provider | no owner, history refused, no request made |
| Relative `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, split credential roots, `apiKeyHelper` | no owner, no request made |
| macOS Keychain item exists but is unreadable, or both lookups fail, stale `.credentials.json` beside it | no owner, no request made |
| Keychain item confirmed absent (`security` exit 44), `.credentials.json` present | the file is the credential |
| Readable Keychain login, one turn | 10 `security` lookups (base: none) |
| Plan upgrade, or token rotation for the same account | same owner, still seeded |
| Forwarded credential (api key, token, named OAuth) | credential decides the owner, native login not consulted, no request made |
| Node-placed Claude CLI | host login not used |
| Backend other than `claude-cli` | no native owner, no request made |
| Warm Claude child started under a different native owner | not reused |
| Session with existing history and no stored boundary, including history written by v2026.10.2 | unchanged: stays unknown, rows kept (scenario 27, Gaps) |

## Evidence

All of the following in this section, up to "Earlier captures", ran on one machine (a Mac Studio) at the pushed head `5fd7205504d` (tree `7faff7483d7`; the logs name `50dd62a3430`, the unsigned local commit of the same tree), base `02368839f49`, except the records labelled `before 05501c8a`, which ran the built previous head `05501c8acd9` with the same harness, and the base controls (rows 38, 39), which ran a build of `02368839f49` itself. The scenario harness ran on the build of tree `544b2f52a7d`, whose only difference from the pushed tree is one test file (`history-boundary.native-login-metadata.test.ts`); the pushed tree was rebuilt afterwards and its `dist` compared file by file with the one the harness used (see Build). Every scenario sets `attestNativeLogin: true` except rows 35 to 39. ### Real built binary

The real `openclaw agent --local` (built `dist`), a real SQLite session and worker threads, synthetic login files on disk, the real Anthropic Claude runtime and stream-json transport. The `claude` executable is a synthetic child (`harness/bin/claude`). It speaks the control protocol and records every record that reaches it, together with the account named by the login's `.claude.json` record (`loginAccount`) and by its credential (`credentialAccount`) at that instant. It can rewrite the login at chosen moments: `FAKE_ON_INIT` fires after it initializes and before the prompt is sent, `FAKE_ON_USER` after it receives the prompt. Like Claude CLI, it answers OpenClaw's `UserPromptSubmit` hook before it handles each prompt and records the context that comes back: that is where OpenClaw's private turn context travels, including interrupted inputs (`.context-*` files beside each prompt). By default it never writes a Claude project transcript, so every later turn enters the fresh-session reseed branch. With `FAKE_WRITE_TRANSCRIPT=1` (scenarios 23 to 26) it writes one under the session id OpenClaw passed (`--session-id`, then `--resume`), so later turns resume the Claude session. Each turn is a new process.

**The Anthropic profile endpoint is a local STUB** (`harness/profile-stub.mjs`), reached through a preload that redirects only that one URL (`harness/shim/profile-fetch-shim.mjs`). Synthetic tokens `synthetic-<account>` attest to `<account>`, and the stub can answer 401 or hold the request open. Production code is unchanged and always calls the real URL. Scenarios 10 to 13 also shim the Keychain at the `child_process.execSync` seam (`harness/shim/security-shim.mjs`); the others use the real `security` binary, which finds no item and exits 44.

### Saved context on a resumed Claude session (rows 28 to 31)

`harness/gateway-probe.sh`, same login files, synthetic child and profile STUB. Turn 1 runs with `openclaw agent --local`. For turn 2 the harness starts the real built Gateway (`openclaw gateway run`) on the same state dir and sends the turn through it with `openclaw agent` (no `--local`). The Gateway stages the input, and while the STUB holds turn 2's attestation request (turn preparation, before the user message is written) the harness kills the Gateway (`kill -9`). The staged input is left unfinished, and the next reader marks it `interrupted`. Turns 3 and 4 run with `openclaw agent --local` on the same conversation. The child writes a native transcript in rows 28, 30 and 31, so turn 3 resumes the Claude session (`useResume=true`). In row 29 the transcript is removed first, so turn 3 starts a fresh session.

### Queued reassignment

### Earlier captures

The subsections below ran at earlier heads of this PR on base `0816aa1b57dc`, each stated in its first line. Their production behavior is the same as at the pushed head except where the table above differs (row 6, and turns that resume a Claude session). Captures: [attested/](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/11acddf1615c4aab8ad5741803e5df324dd1cd74/attested/README.md), [queued/](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/11acddf1615c4aab8ad5741803e5df324dd1cd74/queued/README.md), [real/](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/11acddf1615c4aab8ad5741803e5df324dd1cd74/real/README.md).

### A real attestation

Ran once on the Mac Studio during the `c276e5e3b6c` round; it exercises only the endpoint, not OpenClaw.

One real `GET https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/profile` with the access token of the Studio's logged-in Claude CLI 2.1.283 account, from a throwaway Node process, then one with a synthetic token ([identity/real-profile-attestation.txt](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/11acddf1615c4aab8ad5741803e5df324dd1cd74/attested/identity/real-profile-attestation.txt), script beside it). Values are replaced by their type; the uuid is a 12-hex SHA-256 prefix; no token, uuid or email was printed or stored:

```
real:      status=200 latencyMs=834 tokenExpiresInMin=282
           account: {created_at, display_name, email, full_name, has_claude_max, has_claude_pro, uuid}
           organization: {billing_type, ..., name, organization_type, rate_limit_tier, ..., uuid}  (+ application, enabled_plugins)
           accountUuidHash=f2407884eb8a accountUuidEqualsRecord=true emailEqualsRecord=true orgUuidEqualsRecord=true
           credentialUnchanged=true   (the access and refresh tokens on disk were the same after the call)
synthetic: status=401 latencyMs=96 {error: {message, type}, request_id, type}
```

This is the shape the code reads (`account.uuid`) and the shape Claude CLI validates. What was not exercised against the real endpoint: an expired real token (the code never sends one), a revoked token, a token without the `user:profile` scope, and a request through an HTTPS proxy.

### When Claude CLI rotates its token

Ran once during the `c276e5e3b6c` round against the real `claude` 2.1.283 binary with a synthetic login whose token had expired, its HTTPS sent to a local CONNECT proxy that logs and refuses each connection, so nothing reached Anthropic: the CLI tried the refresh (`CONNECT platform.claude.com:443`) 213 ms after spawn and before it answered `initialize`, and OpenClaw sends the prompt only after that answer. So a rotated token can already be on disk at the send check, which is why a refresh-due turn runs without saved history ([identity/refresh-timing.txt](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/11acddf1615c4aab8ad5741803e5df324dd1cd74/attested/identity/refresh-timing.txt)).

### Real Claude recovery proof

Real `claude` 2.1.283 (Keychain-held claude.ai login, scope includes `user:profile`), real `api.anthropic.com` profile attestation and real model replies (`claude-cli/claude-haiku-4-5`), through the built `openclaw agent --local` with an isolated state dir and no Gateway. Each arm is two turns in one OpenClaw conversation. Between them the Claude session is dropped by deleting that run's own Claude project dir (transcript and auto-memory), so the second turn starts a replacement session (`reuse=invalidated:missing-transcript`). Tools are forbidden in the question. AFTER is `69861729ddf` (tree `83f1df415e1`), BEFORE is the PR merge-base `0816aa1b57d`. Account and token values are not stored; the owner appears only as a short hash label of the stored fingerprint.

AFTER, turn 2 (`PINEAPPLE-1296762355` planted in turn 1):
```
after turn 1: cliHistoryBoundary {"state":"known","maxSeq":2,"keys":["authFingerprint","generation","maxSeq","sessionId","state","version","writerRunId"],"authFingerprint_label":"h:d188d040"}
cli exec: provider=claude-cli model=claude-haiku-4-5 promptChars=771 trigger=user useResume=false session=none resumeSession=none reuse=invalidated:missing-transcript historyPrompt=present
reply: PINEAPPLE-1296762355
```
BEFORE, turn 2 (`PINEAPPLE-1870742729` planted in turn 1; no boundary is ever stored):
```
cli session history refused across auth boundary: reason=auth-unknown
cli exec: provider=claude-cli model=claude-haiku-4-5 promptChars=260 trigger=user useResume=false session=none resumeSession=none reuse=invalidated:missing-transcript historyPrompt=none
reply: UNKNOWN
```
AFTER, login changed between turns: turn 2 ran with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` set to a synthetic login (fake account record and fake token) in the scratch dir; the real login was not touched.
```
after turn 2: cliHistoryBoundary {"state":"unknown","keys":["sessionId","state","version"]}
cli session history refused across auth boundary: reason=auth-unknown
cli exec: provider=claude-cli model=claude-haiku-4-5 promptChars=260 trigger=user useResume=false session=none resumeSession=none reuse=invalidated:missing-transcript historyPrompt=none
cli terminal failure: provider=claude-cli model=claude-haiku-4-5 durationMs=2013 runId=<run> error=Not logged in · Please run /login
```
Saved history never reached the unproven login (`historyPrompt=none`, 260 chars, the same prompt size as BEFORE) and the boundary went to `unknown`.

Covers: authenticated replacement-session recovery with the real binary and real attestation, the BEFORE refusal, and refusal after a login change. Does not cover: a second real account (the switch uses a fake credential, so the log reads `auth-unknown` and does not separate "owner differs" from "owner unattestable"; that distinction is shown by the stub scenarios above), repeated runs (one run per arm, no variance), a long-lived `claude setup-token` login (see Gaps), and the queued-coverage window with the real binary. Raw logs, harness and hashes: [164796-evidence/real](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/11acddf1615c4aab8ad5741803e5df324dd1cd74/real/README.md).

### Keychain cost

Counted at `69861729ddf` on base `0816aa1b57dc` with the scenario 10 harness: 10 `security` lookups per turn for a readable Keychain item (1 at preparation, 1 at the spawn-environment bind, 6 from the plugin's `assertCurrent` at the Claude runtime entry, post-restart and pre-send checks and process creation, 2 inside the worker transaction for the turn's two coverage commits), against none at base; 20.9 ms p50 per readable lookup with the real `/usr/bin/security`, about 0.21 s per turn. Call sites: [keychain/callsites-after.txt](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/11acddf1615c4aab8ad5741803e5df324dd1cd74/queued/keychain/callsites-after.txt), latency: [keychain/latency.txt](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/11acddf1615c4aab8ad5741803e5df324dd1cd74/final/keychain/latency.txt). `history-boundary.native-login.test.ts` pins the split.

### Earlier red, green and mutations

At `769c35116e0` (the record-owner implementation) and `c276e5e3b6c`, the new and changed test files were run each alone against the earlier production code: the behavioral reds and the symbol-only reds are listed in [attested/redgreen/](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/11acddf1615c4aab8ad5741803e5df324dd1cd74/attested/redgreen/redgreen.sh). 47 mutations of the attestation were applied one at a time; 43 are red, none survives, and the other 4 target code the attestation replaced ([attested/mutations/](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/11acddf1615c4aab8ad5741803e5df324dd1cd74/attested/mutations/summary-batch1.txt)). Ten mutations of the in-transaction owner check, run at `69861729ddf`, are all red ([queued/mutations/](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/11acddf1615c4aab8ad5741803e5df324dd1cd74/queued/mutations/)).

## Gaps

- **The access token leaves the process, for an operator who opts in.** Only with `historyRecovery.attestNativeLogin: true` (default `false`, row 35: no request without it). It goes only to `https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/profile`, the Anthropic endpoint Claude CLI sends it to, once per token not yet attested in the process. The request refuses redirects, has a 3 s timeout, and drops errors unread. The token is never logged, stored, refreshed or written back. The request uses the process global fetch, so the env-proxy dispatcher OpenClaw installs at CLI startup applies; a proxy was not exercised. The opt-in's UI hint names the endpoint and states that the token is sent there.
- **An idle, expired token after a Gateway restart has no owner.** An access token that expired while the Gateway was down cannot be attested until Claude refreshes it. The first turn on it has no owner, and that conversation's history stays refused until `/new` or an empty reset. Persisting attestations across restarts would mean persisting a token-derived value, which this PR does not do.
- **A refresh-due turn runs without saved history.** A turn prepared within 10 minutes of token expiry runs without saved history, because Claude rotates the token before the prompt and the send check could not prove the new one. The next turn is offered history again (scenario 20).
- **A rotation outside the CLI's refresh window stops coverage.** If the CLI rotates the token outside that window (for example after a server-side revocation and a 401 recovery), the new token is not attested before the turn's rows commit, so coverage stops and later turns are refused history (scenario 21). Detecting this would cost a Keychain read after every turn; the settle reads only when a rotation is expected.
- **Transient failures fence the conversation.** A profile request that fails (network, timeout, 5xx) at preparation, and a Keychain lookup that fails at a coverage commit, still stop coverage until `/new` or an empty reset, as before. The reply is kept. Only successes are cached, so a failed attestation retries on the next turn.
- **A login without the `user:profile` scope has no owner.** A long-lived `claude setup-token` credential carries only `user:inference`; the real profile endpoint answers it with HTTP 403 (`OAuth token does not meet scope requirement any_of(user:profile, user:office)`). Run against a login like that, the branch refuses saved history exactly as BEFORE does (`reason=auth-unknown`, `historyPrompt=none`, reply `UNKNOWN`), so those installs get no recovery. That is the fail-closed outcome; the run is in the evidence folder, `mini-setup-token`.
- **Some endpoint behaviors were not exercised.** A real successful token refresh, a revoked token, and an HTTPS proxy were not run against the real endpoint. The harness profile endpoint is a stub. The one real call proved the response shape and latency.
- **Sessions that already have history and no recorded boundary stay unknown.** Only conversations that start empty after the opt-in benefit (row 37); `/new` or an empty reset establishes the boundary. History written by v2026.10.2 is kept and not adopted (scenario 27).
- **Plugin-defined backends wrapping Claude** (`id` other than `claude-cli`) are not covered.
- **A last-instant window remains in worker coverage.** The worker asks the host for the owner check from inside its write transaction and the host answers right before it grants. A credential replaced between that answer and the end of the same SQLite transaction (microseconds on the worker) is not seen for that write, and is caught at the next boundary. The worker cannot read the Keychain or the attestation cache itself, so a fully atomic check is not possible. A reassignment while the command is queued, or during any awaited preparation, is seen (scenario 22 and the queued tests).
- **A conversation's first turn on a native login is strict at launch.** It is refused, not run, when its login changes or cannot be attested between preparation and send (row 6). The user's message is recorded and the next turn is offered history again.
- **Saved notes are not shown reaching a resumed session.** A note reaches a Claude CLI turn only when its row is covered, and no shipped path reachable from `openclaw agent` writes a covered note into a claude-cli conversation: the plugin-SDK append in row 32 is uncovered, as on main. The resumed-session context that is shown is the interrupted input (rows 28 to 31), which travels in the same `UserPromptSubmit` context. The refusal does not depend on which saved data is present: a resumed turn whose writer replays history is strict at spawn and send (rows 24, 25, 30, 31; `execute.native-history-owner.test.ts`, RED3), and its context is withheld when the login changes after send (rows 33, 34; RED4).
- **The metadata-worker path is shown by a test, not by the built binary.** The CLI runner never posts `session.metadata.append` or `session.transcript.appendMessage` (row 32 lists every worker command of a native turn), so no shipped CLI flow reaches it. `history-boundary.native-login-metadata.test.ts` runs it on the real worker thread and SQLite (RED1, RED2). It asks once per command at its transaction admission, with the same last-instant window as the turn commit.
- **The real Claude recovery run was not repeated at the pushed head.** It ran at `69861729ddf` on base `0816aa1b57dc`; at the pushed head the same paths are shown by the harness scenarios above with a synthetic child and the stub endpoint.
- **Incognito sessions on a native login may stop coverage.** The in-memory incognito actor confirms the owner only through the running turn's writer when that writer is in scope; otherwise it keeps the rows and stops coverage. No test covers a native login on an incognito session.
- **One new plugin config key.** `plugins.entries.anthropic.config.historyRecovery.attestNativeLogin` (the `historyRecovery` object and its boolean) grows the plugin config surface by two entries, so `docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json` raises the plugin budget from 4527 to 4529 and `config-baseline.sha256` is regenerated with `pnpm config:docs:gen`. The key is what keeps the default free of token requests: the options above that send nothing (A, B) cannot tell a credential from the account record beside it.
- **Removing the opt-in ends coverage for that conversation.** A turn without the opt-in has no owner, so the stored boundary becomes `unknown` (row 36). Turning the opt-in back on does not relabel the rows written in between; `/new` or an empty reset starts a new boundary, as after any owner change.
- **Unrelated suites were not run.** The full suite, the e2e and live lanes, and the Docker lanes were not run. `check:changed` selects `core`, `coreTests`, `extensions`, `extensionTests` and `docs` for this diff, all of which ran above together with the owning-directory lanes. One `src/config/sessions` test is red without this change (see Tests), and the AGENTS.md files do not require unrelated suites.

prs.title: fix(logbook): warn about missing vision model only with pending work
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An enabled Logbook service without a vision model logged “analysis paused” on every rate-limit interval even when no frames or batches needed analysis. It also needs to warn promptly if work appears after an empty tick.

The analysis owner now checks for unbatched active frames or a pending batch before warning. The ten-minute throttle timestamp changes only when a warning is emitted. Queued work remains available for analysis after a model is configured.

## Evidence

### Scheduled Gateway behavior

I built and ran `pnpm dev gateway run` with the bundled Logbook plugin on an isolated loopback port and task-owned state. Capture was disabled; all frame and batch data was synthetic. Channels, providers, browser, canvas, and cron were disabled with repository test isolation flags. No operator Gateway or real data was used.

The first three boots used the earlier PR tree `b52a513eac84c95d2495606a6e3df6444605013d`. The isolated Gateway JSON log contained:

```text
Empty queue, zero frames/batches:
04:39:06Z gateway ready
04:40:41Z shutdown
missing-model warnings: 0 (95 seconds after ready)

One active, unbatched frame:
04:41:41Z gateway ready
04:42:41Z logbook: analysis paused; no vision model
04:42:53Z shutdown
missing-model warnings: 1

Zero unbatched frames, one pending batch:
04:43:44Z gateway ready
04:44:44Z logbook: analysis paused; no vision model
04:44:56Z shutdown
missing-model warnings: 1
```

I then built and booted the **current PR head** (tree `1c8f9a3ddade9410b0f271480a495e11986a9161`) against the retained pending-batch database:

```text
05:12:40.899Z gateway ready
05:13:40.671Z logbook: analysis paused; no vision model
05:15:06.420Z shutdown
missing-model warnings: 1 (145 seconds after ready)
```

The analysis timer is 60 seconds. The current-head run crossed two scheduled ticks and emitted one warning. After shutdown, the SQLite worker still reported `unbatchedActive=0` and `pendingBatch=true`.

### Empty-to-pending regression

ClawSweeper identified that the earlier PR head advanced the throttle on an empty tick without logging. I moved that assignment into the warning branch and changed the regression to add a frame immediately after an empty tick, without advancing the clock. Using the production service, scheduler, and real SQLite worker in isolated Node processes:

```text
Earlier PR head: empty tick 0 warnings; first work tick 0; second work tick 0
Current PR head: empty tick 0 warnings; first work tick 1; second work tick 1
```

The separate pre-fix baseline also warned once on an empty queue (`unbatched=0, pending=false`), whereas the patched service stayed silent. The pending-batch-only path has an explicit worker-backed regression test.

## Checks

- Focused `extensions/logbook/src/service.test.ts`: 6/6 passed in 77 seconds (compiler preparation dominated; each test took about 0.4 seconds).
- Current-head source build, `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- The canonical autoreview helper found no actionable P0–P2 findings on the staged correction.

prs.title: refactor(sessions): avoid cloning unchanged rollback state
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Every durable session actor mutation, resident entry-patch publication, and transcript-rewrite publication deep-cloned all retained state for rollback. The clone traversed unchanged transcript payloads and indexes even for a small metadata command.

## User Impact

No command, persistence, or isolation behavior changes. Metadata-only commands avoid walking all retained transcript payloads merely to prepare rollback. No migration or operator action is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Fork the small mutable object shells and share immutable rows/payloads. Each map or navigation array detaches on its first write. The existing mutation owners replace rows, a rollback discards the working state, and only confirmed commit installs it. Returned snapshots and receipt postimages retain their existing deep-copy boundary. This removes the whole-state clone without changing commands, FIFO scheduling, persistence, SQL, or authority checks; no dependency or new state owner.

Rollback isolation protects real user data, so it is preserved. No authority check was removed, and no new rollback edge case is accepted. The change replaces the expensive isolation mechanism rather than weakening the contract.

## Evidence

### Measurement

Shared harness v2.1.0, baseline `62f79e969ef02` versus candidate `8dd786e4ee25`: three alternating pairs, ten warmed turns per capture, Node 26.11.1 / SQLite 3.53.4 throughout. Values are median [min–max] of the per-run means. The original first pair crossed a host Node upgrade; it is excluded, and the one permitted extra pair supplies the third matched pair.

| Measurement | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Warmed causal statements, all threads | 171.7 [170.8–172.2] | 170.1 [170.0–172.0] |
| Warmed causal requests | 41.5 [41.4–41.6] | 41.1 [41.0–41.4] |
| Warmed MAIN statements | 0 [0–0] | 0 [0–0] |
| Warmed raw-window statements, all threads | 208.3 [207.1–215.7] | 204.5 [194.0–206.9] |

Following the updated compute-conservation rule, final integrated-head proof will come from PR CI, without another local Knip or test run.

prs.title: feat: support principal-bound remote Control UI for trusted plugins
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Trusted plugins need to host a remote Control UI and invoke Gateway RPC for an explicitly approved owner or person without sharing the Gateway token or password.

## User Impact

A trusted plugin can bind remote UI and RPC to the same principal and chosen access ceiling. Effective access is that ceiling intersected with the principal's current role and session visibility. Embedded browsers receive no reusable device credential, remain pinned to the serving Gateway, and can use an embedder-provided Gateway switcher.

This is a privileged capability for bundled or verified official plugins. A relay can read and modify content in transit and exercise the approved capabilities; this is not end-to-end encryption against the relay. The core capability alone does not publish a Gateway or enable a relay. Existing installations retain their normal direct-listener authentication and need no config migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway owns principal resolution, live authority, session policy, HTTP route admission, device pairing, and transport shutdown. The service-bound ingress factory composes those existing owners for plugin transports and grant-bound RPC. Revocation and role changes fence retained work as well as new requests; signed embedded browsers authenticate through the live grant and never receive bearer device tokens.

The MCP relay consumer, consent UI, plugin registration, and real-plugin integration case remain in #168233. This PR contains only the reusable core/SDK capability, its core tests and docs, and the embedder transport UI. The merge preserves main's Solid app root, deferred HTTP runtime admission, and exact media-file identity checks.

## Evidence

Standalone core validation (the relay package is physically absent):

- `pnpm build:ci-artifacts` passed in 228.4s, including SDK declarations, plugin exports, and Control UI build/performance limits.
- 125 cases passed across the core ingress, transport, HTTP auth, device pairing, dispatch lifetime/authority, and service capability suites. The split initially removed a context still used by the WebSocket test host; that fixture binding was restored and all six core integration cases plus the 13 approval/service cases passed in the focused 70.36s rerun. No production guard or test assertion was weakened.
- 66 UI cases passed across seven files in 22.79s; 45 desktop/browser cases passed across five files in 41.93s. The merged GitHub grant/media suites also passed all 14 cases (34.72s); their production inputs are unchanged by the split.
- Docs links (15,332 checked, zero broken), MDX, glossary, config baseline, plugin inventory, SDK exports/surface, and formatting passed. Core production and UI typechecks, plus all 28 affected core test graphs, passed. The current focused lint recheck reports 28 inherited `max-lines` findings outside this diff; all implicated source and lint configuration blobs match the merged main base. Two earlier findings have disappeared. No lint suppression was added.
- Managed Codex review of the integrated candidate and final standalone core completed through P2 without remaining actionable findings.

`pnpm deadcode:full` reports one inherited unused export, `renderBoardWidgetError` in `ui/src/components/board/board-widget-cell-render.ts`. The same command reproduces it on clean merged main `3f168ed8c3035b9a5c2490b0c837c0cdcaeeba1e` with an independent frozen install; the relevant source and Knip configuration match. Main subsequently removes the obsolete adapter in #170609. The prior SQLite findings are gone. No suppression was added. Required CI remains authoritative, with any inherited-only exception handled through the native evidence workflow. Earlier live ChatGPT/production-relay smoke is recorded in the consumer PR; it covered the earlier owner flow. Current owner/person authorization and revocation are covered by isolated Gateway boundary tests. Live OAuth expiry enforcement is outside this core change and was not independently exercised. The coordinator Gateway was neither restarted nor reconfigured.

Release-note context: trusted plugins can expose principal-bound, tokenless remote Control UI and Gateway RPC, constrained by an approved scope ceiling and the principal's live role; embedded browsers support an embedder-owned Gateway switcher.


<details>
<summary>Existing end-to-end consumer visuals</summary>

These sanitized synthetic before/after captures belong to the MCP relay consumer in #168233. This core PR supplies its ingress capability; the Connected apps panel itself remains in that follow-up.

Before:

![Before: consumer plugin panel unavailable](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4c8831ec-a957-46f0-b4ba-f3c6e8082b9b)

After:

![After: consumer principal-bound consent](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/edaf7a47-fc02-480e-9f12-570cdbaca8ac)

</details>


Follow-up CI fixture validation: test WebSocket hosts use the existing pre-auth payload limit; node-only visibility fixtures preserve the document contract used by browser-client initialization; HTTP-route tests assert abort propagation through composed authority signals; the selected-session mock has its storage-isolation rationale and its obsolete baseline exception was removed by the generator. These changes preserve production behavior. All 69 cases in the five focused authorization, route, activity, and refresh files pass (564.57s total wrapper wall time, dominated by cold worker compilation; UI shard 9.90s). The two payload suites also pass all 45 cases. Fresh independent review through P2, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, and diff checks pass. Broad CI is attached to the repaired head; remaining failures require exact-head attribution before landing.

Archive fixture repair: the selected-session case previously published an archived `sessions.describe` response before the Archive click. A naturally occurring descriptor refresh could therefore turn that click into an unarchive request. The fixture now publishes that response only after the successful archive mutation, with the committed row timestamp; the original selection, title, transcript, archive attribution, and restored-composer assertions remain unchanged. No production behavior changed. The full archive file passes all 10 cases (150.43s; selected case 3.905s), and targeted type-aware lint, formatting, and both size ratchets pass. A held real descriptor response also passes the original flow when resolved from current fixture state.

The earlier controlled diagnostic reproduced the CI signature once, but its unchanged full-PR countercheck passed, so the bisect did not isolate a causal production hunk. The repair addresses the directly observed invalid fixture chronology; passing replays are not being used as inherited-failure evidence. Fresh independent review through P2 is scoped-clean. The repair and reviewed main merge are published at `b060084c99b283f3e69a1b9bd6b4ff5467751348`; CI on that exact head remains required. Main independently repaired the premature descriptor and roster clocks; the conflict resolution preserves their deferred patch and clocks while keeping the current post-success descriptor. The affected archive case passes on the merged source (6.031s; 107.83s total, nine unrelated cases omitted), as do UI types, target lint, formatting, and fresh conflict review through P2. The earlier cron snapshot failure matched [scheduled main run 38339144048, job 115106094544](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38339144048/job/115106094544); any remaining failure on the new head still requires exact-run attribution before landing.

Current CI: [run 38345779430](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38345779430) tested merge `f7f0a6b351524e6792ccec42d69a382a0fd7aaf4` onto main `5ac63514950809ba05512c161264ec0bc0945639`. The archive shard passes. The config-preflight missing-export type error and updater readiness-message mismatch both reproduce on that exact main base; their test and owner source inputs match the tested merge. The final Node shard was cancelled at its 60-minute deadline after the Telegram slow-album case timed out and later hooks cascaded. That cancellation is not yet attributed: the CI classification table omits it, and the exact-base Telegram replay has not reached a verdict. No inherited-only exception or merge request has been submitted.

prs.title: fix(agents): drop throttled exec update events
prs.body:
## Summary

- Problem: exec live output throttling capped detailed payloads, but throttled `tool_execution_update` events still emitted generic tool/item updates with no new user-visible payload.
- Solution: make throttled exec updates a true no-op until the next allowed live update or final result.
- What changed: `handleToolExecutionUpdate` now returns before emitting generic exec update traffic when the live exec update throttle suppresses the detailed output, with regression coverage for global agent events and `onAgentEvent` emissions.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): final exec result events, command completion items, non-exec tool updates, and the existing live exec output size cap are unchanged.

## Motivation

- #84850 captured a 60s gateway sample with average CPU at 83.66%, 42/60 samples at or above 100% CPU, and 0.00 kB/s average read I/O during an embedded exec tool run. Dropping redundant throttled update events reduces avoidable gateway projection/broadcast work in that hot path.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #84850
- Related #78645
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: Gateway CPU saturation from #84850 during embedded exec tool output. Throttled exec updates should not continue producing generic tool/item event traffic when they carry no new visible output.
- Real environment tested: Local Linux OpenClaw worktree on Node 24, using the repo Vitest wrapper plus the redacted pidstat/gateway log evidence from the affected run.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/pi-embedded-subscribe.handlers.tools.test.ts`, `git diff --check`, and `codex --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox --sandbox danger-full-access review --uncommitted`.
- Evidence after fix (screenshot, recording, terminal capture, console output, redacted runtime log, linked artifact, or copied live output): Copied terminal capture from the patched worktree:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/pi-embedded-subscribe.handlers.tools.test.ts

Test Files  2 passed (2)
     Tests  76 passed (76)

$ git diff --check
(no output; exit 0)

$ codex --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox --sandbox danger-full-access review --uncommitted
No discrete correctness issues were found in the current local changes.
```

- Observed result after fix: The regression test proves the first exec live update still emits visible output, while the next update inside the throttle window emits no additional global agent events and no additional `onAgentEvent` traffic. Final result handling remains covered by the existing exec result tests.
- What was not tested: I did not rerun the private 60s live CPU-saturation gateway session because the original setup/session details are local and redacted; the fix was verified at the exec tool update seam that emits the redundant events.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged): Redacted source evidence from #84850:

```text
pidstat summary:
rows=60
avg_cpu=83.66
avg_usr=79.42
avg_sys=4.25
avg_rd=0.00
cpu_ge_100_count=42
max_cpu=190.0

redacted gateway correlation:
2026-05-21T05:07:47.187+00:00 agent/embedded embedded run tool start: runId=[redacted run id] tool=exec toolCallId=REDACTED
2026-05-21T05:08:04.330+00:00 agent/embedded embedded run tool end: runId=[redacted run id] tool=exec toolCallId=REDACTED
```

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: the live exec throttle suppressed detailed output but still allowed generic exec update item/tool events to be emitted for every throttled update.
- Missing detection / guardrail: existing coverage checked output truncation/throttling but did not assert that suppressed updates stop all generic event emission.
- Contributing context (if known): #78645 bounded live exec output payloads, but redundant event emission could still keep gateway event projection hot during high-volume exec output.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [x] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target test or file: `src/agents/pi-embedded-subscribe.handlers.tools.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: a second exec update inside `LIVE_EXEC_UPDATE_MIN_INTERVAL_MS` emits no global agent events and no `onAgentEvent` traffic.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the redundant CPU work starts at the embedded tool update handler before gateway websocket fanout sees the event.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): existing exec output throttling tests cover payload capping but not generic event suppression.
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Exec tool output updates inside the live update throttle window are dropped completely instead of sending generic no-payload progress events. Start, allowed live update, and final result events are preserved.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[exec update inside throttle] -> [generic tool/item events] -> [gateway projection/broadcast work]

After:
[exec update inside throttle] -> [no emitted event] -> [next allowed update or final result closes state]
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`): No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`): No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`): No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`): No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`): No
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: N/A

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Linux
- Runtime/container: Node 24 local worktree
- Model/provider: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO for the original runtime sample; tests do not require provider credentials.
- Integration/channel (if any): Embedded exec tool event handling
- Relevant config (redacted): Original private session details were redacted.

### Steps

1. Run `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/pi-embedded-subscribe.handlers.tools.test.ts`.
2. Run `git diff --check`.
3. Run `codex --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox --sandbox danger-full-access review --uncommitted`.

### Expected

- First exec live update emits visible command output.
- A throttled follow-up exec update emits no generic event traffic.
- Final exec result behavior remains unchanged.

### Actual

- Targeted wrapper passed: 2 files, 76 tests.
- `git diff --check` passed with no output.
- Autoreview found no discrete correctness issues.

## Evidence

Attach at least one:

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [x] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

What you personally verified (not just CI), and how:

- Verified scenarios: allowed exec live update still emits output; throttled exec update emits no global or local agent event traffic; final exec output/result tests still pass.
- Edge cases checked: existing large-output truncation and final output redaction coverage still passes in the same target file.
- What you did **not** verify: private live CPU-saturation rerun from the original affected setup.

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [ ] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes/No`): Yes
- Config/env changes? (`Yes/No`): No
- Migration needed? (`Yes/No`): No
- If yes, exact upgrade steps: N/A

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: Suppressing throttled updates could hide command progress between allowed live updates.
  - Mitigation: the first allowed update and final command result remain emitted; only no-payload updates inside the existing throttle window are dropped.

prs.title: feat(auth): publish shared and agent credential authority
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Shared and agent credentials still require a native final read before Codex sends a bearer-authenticated request. The existing personal credential authority cannot yet replace that read because several native and worker writers do not publish their committed facts to the Gateway.

This first slice extends that same authority to shared and agent stores and publishes non-SDK writes. It keeps the final SQL guard until the synchronous SDK custody and generic-key coverage land, followed by the reader cutover.

### Design and writer coverage

Credential writes deny authority synchronously before the native effect. Managed transactions install committed postimages before releasing denial; known rollback preserves the old facts, and an unknown outcome remains denied until the owner restarts. Async updates reuse their existing commit grant and receipt transport. Catalog tasks deny the root before dispatch and return committed facts even when the catalog result fails. No new SQL, worker request, or admission handshake is introduced.

| Writer family | Publication route |
| --- | --- |
| Login, import, setup, provider persistence | Existing store-update admission and native commit receipt; canonical JSON sinks stage the postimage. |
| OAuth claim, replace, failure, restore, peer removal; logout and compensation | Same update owner; native catalog routes use the catalog settlement receipt. |
| Native session AuthStorage; external CLI synchronization | Prepared native saves enter the canonical sink before mutation and settle with the enclosing transaction. |
| Secrets apply and exact-owned rollback | Canonical write/delete sinks publish both the applied value and committed restoration. |
| Doctor, import, relocation, schema conversion | Existing exclusive offline maintenance; narrowly enumerated migration sinks in the writer ratchet. |
| Model-catalog refresh and peer writes | Host denial before dispatch; native committed-fact capture through work-scope drain and result validation. |
| Released synchronous SDK saves/upserts | Canonical sink publication is shared; explicit custody and released-entry proof follow in slice 2, with signatures preserved. |
| Generic machine-state writes accepting the credential key | Exact transitional sink entries remain in this slice; publication and custody follow in slice 2. |

The owner uses admitted database identities. A credential write that first creates an agent database also publishes to authority captured while that path was absent. Metadata-only writes do not revoke credentials. Cold loading uses the existing worker and cannot overwrite a newer committed postimage.

CI repair also separates native JSON writes from read-only imports, preserving the existing lightweight wrapper/worker closure. Preparation may run during pending publication, but the final effect reader still denies authority until settlement.

The writer ratchet rejects new direct/raw credential-table sinks, including dynamic machine-state keys that may select the credential row. Synthetic bypass tests cover direct SQL, aliases, key changes, and extra sinks.

### Checks and accepted edges

No final security check is removed in this slice. Fingerprint, selected-profile, pending-refresh, fetch, and response-disclosure guards remain unchanged. A catalog task temporarily denies credentials even when it ultimately makes no credential change; a confirmed result releases that denial. An unknown task outcome stays denied until restart. An external request already started before denial may finish; a new effect cannot start while authority is denied.

### T1 and SQL

| Metric | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Codex final guard primitive sites | 2 | 2 (cutover follows in slice 3) |
| Static primitive reachability | Retained | Retained for the released synchronous SDK reader |
| Warmed causal statements / requests / MAIN (single-run means) | 169.1 / 41.3 / 0 | 172.4 / 41.7 / 0 |
| Changed writer operation SQL / request delta | — | 0 by construction; existing transports carry additional facts |

Static T1 may remain after the final guard cutover because the released synchronous SDK reader reaches the same primitives. That compatibility reachability is separate from the intended SQL-free Codex guard.

## SQL measurement and attribution

One completed base/candidate pair uses shared harness 2.1.0: base `592b7e4aea9386e05912e6df2d3ba5493e629aaa`, candidate `1d72cc6e48450f594fdb65d54ea49f40fdecf699`. Both completed all 13 top-level turns, the native child, RPCs, cron, compaction, and shutdown. Warmed figures are means over ten turns per run, not repeated-run medians. The interrupted repeat has no completed candidate and is excluded. These are the measured revisions; this table does not claim a later integrated head was remeasured.

| Metric | Base | Candidate | Delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Turn-caused all-thread statements/turn | 169.1 | 172.4 | +3.3 (+1.95%) |
| Turn-caused logical requests/turn | 41.3 | 41.7 | +0.4 (+0.97%) |
| Turn-caused MAIN statements/turn | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Legacy warmed-window statements/turn | 222.0 | 221.2 | -0.8 |
| Legacy warmed-window requests/turn | 64.0 | 57.5 | -6.5 |
| Background statements/minute | 522.35 | 537.62 | +15.27 |
| Whole-workload statements | 7,002 | 6,961 | -41 |
| Whole-workload requests | 1,414 | 1,296 | -118 |
| Whole-workload MAIN statements | 833 | 828 | -5 |
| First-turn causal statements / requests | 393 / 75 | 416 / 81 | +23 / +6 |

The individual warmed-turn median is 170 statements / 41 requests in both runs. Individual ranges are base 162–173 / 39–44 and candidate 170–192 / 41–46; these are not repeated-run ranges. The 32-CPU host was loaded (base load 68.9→135.0, candidate 80.8→75.4). No latency claim is made. Foreground cache misses and recap work remain counted; lower whole-workload totals do not erase the warmed increase.

| Shared family, direct SQL / matching logical requests per warmed turn | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Exact-entry facts | 4.2 / 4.2 | 4.2 / 4.2 |
| Actor hydration | 1.2 / 1.2 | 1.2 / 1.2 |
| Entry-cache snapshot loads | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Row facts | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Watermark reads | 0.8 / 0.8 | 1.0 / 1.0 |
| Rewrite-generation reads | 1.0 / 1.0 | 1.0 / 1.0 |
| Transcript projection snapshots | 1.8 / 1.8 | 2.1 / 2.1 |
| Auth operations | 1.3 / 1.3 | 1.2 / 1.2 |

Every listed family has zero warmed MAIN SQL. Direct SQL is identified by its native owner stack; matching requests are distinct logical request IDs carrying those statements or naming that owner. Requests may contain multiple families, so these diagnostic rows must not be summed. Entry-cache snapshots specifically mean `loadSessionEntrySnapshot`; an inline projection is not a whole-cache load. Generic machine-state SQL is not classified as auth from its shape alone.

The complete warmed difference is +33 statements / +4 requests across ten turns. Entry-patch preparation and effect requests contribute +16 / +4; one bounded transcript hydration contributes +12 / +1; activity-summary source contributes +6 / +1; retained exact-entry lookup contributes +1 / +1. These are offset by ordered exact-entry lookup -1 / -1, auth row lookup -1 / -1, and actor requests 0 / -1. This accounting preserves every foreground execution.

Provider traces show 16 ordinary inference calls and two compaction calls on each revision. Activity recap calls differ, 12→15, while both consume the same 26 note strings in the same order (SHA-256 `d18a428e96b4290e4d8889e9b3169848c6504f86d9f40703f54d0aed98c4d52e`). The base's first recap batches seven notes; the candidate begins with one-note batches. The unchanged recap owner commits `activitySummary` through an entry patch with a transcript predicate. Whole-workload entry-patch preparation/effect counts rise 53→56 / 71→74, matching the three extra recaps. Native predicate stacks independently identify recap-guard watermark and projection SQL rising 12→15 overall, including 8→10 in warmed causal work. Thus recap batching accounts for both extra warmed watermarks and two of the three extra warmed projections; it does not establish why scheduling differed between revisions.

The remaining warmed projection is one extra bounded transcript hydration at `session-transcript-hydration.ts:412`, after no usable retained context is found. Its request carries 12 statements. The trace does not record the cache-miss reason. In candidate turn 02, the two hydration requests were sent at +6,520ms and +7,639ms; the recap commit was sent later, at +13,049ms. That later recap cannot explain the preceding hydration miss. Whole-workload watermark reads rise 15→21: recap guards +3, background row-facts reads +2, and a background anchor read +1. Whole-workload projections rise 44→47: recap guards +3, bounded hydration +1, and activity-summary source fallback -1. Background reads stay included in whole-workload totals.

Whole-workload auth is 54→55 statements / 29→30 requests. The only added auth statement is the existing union-row helper, 23→24 reads: first turn +1, warmed turns -1, second session +1, other causal phases unchanged. New authority observation consumes rows already returned by that helper and adds no persistence request. Its trace ends at the generic worker boundary, so the higher-level caller and cache-miss cause of the extra read are unproved. The measured source revisions leave auth persisted-row caching, auth write-token policy, session hydration/cache modules, and writer-queue arbitration unchanged. In-memory authority processing can still affect scheduling. This pair therefore supports operation-level attribution, but does not prove strict per-operation no-growth or a warmed-turn saving.

The shared mock-provider workload does not exercise the Codex bearer-authenticated final guard. Its SQL-free security boundary must be established by the dedicated boundary test and baseline guard probe, not inferred from this whole-workload pair.

All **22 changed test files (278 tests)** passed for PR head `281f6c09c722`, with all 21 selected compact/boundary changed-test jobs successful. Every supporting test job checked out GitHub merge `4238a37e` (`281f6c09c722` into main `c6ee92366b56`). `86b94e00719d` changes only an existing mock-isolation comment. prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Completes the page-host and route migration for 27 routes whose content now uses Solid, on top of the landed Solid shell.

## User Impact

Lazy pages retain their paths, host tags, selectors, and loading boundaries. Focused drafts survive loader refreshes and retryable errors; navigation retires the page and joins MCP teardown. No user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The 24 existing lazy route modules now supply native Solid renderers. The outlet preserves renderer identity while supplying live loader and presentation props, with inline errors in a separate rendering region. Replaced Lit page classes and temporary outlet/pairing adapters are removed. Domain state and cancellation stay in plain TypeScript owners.

Native routes inherit the shell layout owner, including while the shell is assembled detached. Containment identifies the owner without timing workarounds. Native hub headers share the existing tab focus owner, and pairing remains lazy.

Retained Lit seams have current callers: sidebar/avatar/roster rendering, the chat skill reader, the shared wizard template contract, and structured plugin settings. These can be removed with their remaining callers.

## Evidence

CI found three attributable failures on the initial integrated head: a type cycle through the route registry, the deprecated artwork `className` prop, and two initial artwork lifecycle cases. The fixes move renderer props to an import-free leaf, use `class`, and remove the plugin page bridge. One scoped DOM observer reconciles tile insertion alongside state changes; the existing owner deduplicates requests and retires resources. Current `main` already contains the generic plugin-state cap fix from `e3395867507` (`fix(plugin-state): evict current namespace on plugin row cap`). This PR addresses the remaining `telegram.message-cache` permanence angle from #87332.

The follow-up commit also addresses the review concern about pre-existing `expires_at = NULL` rows. When a namespace writes with a TTL, plugin state now updates live rows in that same namespace that were previously immortal to expire at the same deadline as the write. That keeps the upgrade path bounded without touching sibling namespaces.

## Verification
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/message-cache.test.ts -t 'plugin-state store|persistent'`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugin-state/plugin-state-store.test.ts -t 'default TTL|Telegram sibling|plugin row cap|plugin overflow'`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/plugin-state/plugin-state-store.sqlite.ts src/plugin-state/plugin-state-store.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/message-cache.ts extensions/telegram/src/message-cache.test.ts`

Behavior addressed: Telegram message-cache plugin-state entries now get a TTL instead of being permanent live rows, and old no-expiry message-cache rows receive a bounded expiry after the namespace writes under the new TTL policy.
Real environment tested: local macOS source worktree at `upstream/main`.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: focused Vitest and oxfmt commands above.
Evidence after fix: Telegram message-cache tests passed for persistent/default store coverage; plugin-state tests passed for TTL normalization, sibling namespace budget, and plugin cap behavior.
Observed result after fix: default Telegram message-cache plugin state opens with namespace `telegram.message-cache`, max entries `3000`, and a seven-day default TTL; existing no-expiry rows in that namespace are assigned the new expiry deadline on the next TTL write.
What was not tested: live Telegram traffic or a production SQLite file from a real user profile.
