prs.title: refactor(boards): move cross-store dashboard writes off the main thread
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cross-database Board writes fell back to a synchronous target transaction, blocking the Gateway while rereading source permission that the request owner already retains.

## User Impact

Durable dashboard writes run in the existing target worker. Revoking source access denies new writes; a write admitted before revocation may still finish saving its widget or layout. This is the explicitly accepted, bounded exception: only writes already in flight at revocation. Target identity/lifecycle checks and private-content disclosure checks remain current.

## Why This Change Was Made

Board checks the caller's source authority once, after asynchronous preparation and queue admission, immediately before dispatching the mutation. Ordinary Gateway callers read the sharing owner's retained facts: its pending publications block admission, committed receipts install facts before releasing the denial, and unknown outcomes remain denied. Board no longer prepares a second source snapshot, sends source predicates to the target, rereads them at transaction/commit, or chooses a native target transaction for a cross-store source. Existing synchronous callbacks remain callable at admission; no SDK exports or schema change.

Removed checks and accepted edge cases:

- Duplicate source preparation/read: the request owner holds current source facts; arbitrary legacy callbacks still own their own assertion implementation.
- Source revalidation at target transaction and commit: a write already admitted may finish after source revocation.
- Source revalidation during publication cleanup/return: committed results and invalidation remain attached to the original target after revocation; independent disclosure checks are preserved.

The legacy process-held incognito database remains native under the scoped escape hatch. It is a live configuration contract, demonstrated by `src/gateway/board-store.test.ts` using the production singleton without an actor. Moving it requires the separate session-storage owner cutover; reopening its sentinel in a worker would lose data. Thus the assigned write-site inventory remains **8 → 8 T1 sites**, all still reachable from that legacy path; **durable cross-database Board target calls move off main**. The shared mutation kernel cannot honestly be classified as worker-only yet.

## Evidence

- Regression coverage uses real Gateway request authorization and the existing publication owner: retained-fact admission without host SQL for put/layout/grant, revoke-then-write rejection, admitted write completion across revocation, pending/unknown revocation denial, and cold authorization parity.
- CI passed the existing Board worker (26 tests, 19.64 s), batching (2, 9.76 s), incognito (10, 3.72 s), and outcome (5, 5.36 s) suites. This includes target replacement, queued writes, read-after-write, and unknown target outcomes. The first run exposed a missing host-worker test registration in the new regression; the follow-up also corrects its membership fixture to use the authenticated profile ID.
- Local corrected boundary regression: `pnpm test src/boards/sqlite-board-source-authority.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed all three tests; command wall time 927.17 s on the loaded host. Measured-head CI run [38343772697](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38343772697) passed in 770 s (45 successful jobs, 25 skipped; 8,929 aggregate successful job-seconds).
- Changed-file formatting, lint, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Codex review: two completed rounds, both scoped-clean with no actionable P0–P2 findings (production cutover, then test-fixture/routing corrections).
- Prior-head CI passed, including all Board tests, types, lint, source contracts, architecture/Madge, docs, and database ratchets. The separate Knip scan found a pre-existing exported admission type; main already fixed it in `0e0e87d465c9b`, so main was merged without changing the reviewed Board patch. Refreshed-head CI run 38343772697 passed in 770 s (45 successful jobs, 25 skipped; 8,929 aggregate successful job-seconds). The separate Knip scan on measured head `b2d7d083264c` reported only `ui/src/components/board/board-widget-cell-render.ts: renderBoardWidgetError`. The identical production-unused-export finding was reproduced on clean main base `f7d7425192bd` using pinned Knip 6.32.2; that UI file is untouched here. The candidate script-export scan passed. The finding was assigned to the main-repair inbox. Final main integration removed that UI file, so the earlier inherited-static exception is no longer needed.
- Production LOC: +14/−109 (net −95), below the expanded 600-line budget.
- After the coordination hold lifted, main `e65c0bd16568` was merged as `217844199512`. The Board production diff is byte-identical to measured/reviewed head `b2d7d083264c`; changed-file formatting and lint passed again. Integration-head [CI run 38349905389](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38349905389) passed: 45 successful jobs, 25 skipped, 734 s wall time and 8,405 aggregate successful job-seconds. The existing pair is retained as evidence for the unchanged Board patch; no additional local suites or harness runs were started.
- No update/Doctor/schema/plugin-loading/service-lifecycle changes; the published-driver update cell does not apply.

The shared v2.1 workload contains no Board writes. Its baseline/candidate pair is a shared-read regression check; Board boundary tests establish the mutation behavior and zero host SQL for retained source admission. No per-Board total-statement saving is claimed from this workload.

One alternating pair, base `f7d7425192bd` then candidate `b2d7d083264c`, with ten warmed turns each. Both complete runs passed all 13 top-level turns, the child turn, 39 RPCs, cron, compaction, graceful shutdown, and child-process cleanup. A task-local harness copy corrects its obsolete synthetic `tool_call` alias to `dispatch_action` and places fixtures on external storage; observer and workload are unchanged. An earlier uncorrected baseline stopped at that alias mismatch and is excluded.

prs.title: perf: reduce redundant background usage and participant reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Background usage refresh fetched transcript statistics, then separately re-read generation/watermark facts. Count-only participant writes also loaded the complete participant display projection even though identity and ordering were unchanged.

The transcript-stats owner now returns generation and cold-state facts in its existing batch. The usage worker reuses that operation-local result and deletes the later watermark query. The participant writer returns its existing projection-change decision; count-only receipts invalidate aggregate records while explicitly retaining known display facts. Full display projections are loaded only when identity or ordering changes.

No configuration, schema, retention, SDK, or update behavior changes. The previous read paths are removed.

## Accepted edges and ownership

- Removed usage generation/watermark recheck: a transcript rewrite during an already-running derived usage scan converges on the next receipt-driven refresh. Cold restore forces a rebuild using the captured bounds.
- Removed count-only participant display reload: count-only commits keep the known display identity/order, while aggregate counts and lifecycle notifications still invalidate. New identities and reordered participants publish a full projection.

The two shared-row-facts requests are separate refreshes; identical inputs have not been established, so this does not introduce a speculative cache. Usage rollup/partition write fusion remains deferred to the shared incognito writer cutover (#169363). Memory indexing belongs to its own lane.

## Evidence

One successful baseline/candidate pair with shared harness v2.1, as required by the October 13 compute-conservation update; 10 warmed turns per cell. Base `fcb89a331a1f59eedde59c4b3a338febdb199cb7`, candidate `2d540b48505ac6199a77222312c150e1dd4d8545`. Values below are single-cell per-turn averages or background rates, not three-pair medians. Synthetic workload completed child spawn, cron, compaction, and clean shutdown in both cells.

| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Turn-caused all-thread statements/turn | 174.9 | 171.1 | −3.8 (−2.17%) |
| Turn-caused requests/turn | 42.4 | 41.6 | −0.8 (−1.89%) |
| Turn-caused MAIN statements/turn | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Legacy window statements/turn | 226.4 | 214.6 | −11.8 |
| Non-memory background statements/min | 211.45 | 219.05 | +3.59% |
| Non-memory background requests/min | 133.43 | 122.78 | −7.98% |
| Memory background statements/min | 370.89 | 387.88 | +4.58% |
| Memory background requests/min | 83.68 | 87.90 | +5.05% |
| All background statements/min | 582.35 | 606.93 | +4.22% |
| All background requests/min | 217.11 | 210.68 | −2.96% |

The warmed windows lasted 53.061s and 43.003s. Non-memory background statement counts fell **187 → 157**, but the shorter candidate window raised the per-minute rate. The **−25% non-memory background SQL/min target is not established** by this pair. Host load was about 78/75; no latency claim and no extra pair to chase noise.

Shared-family statement counts across the 10 warmed turns (turn-caused / background):

| Family | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Exact-entry facts | 44 / 8 | 42 / 7 |
| Actor hydration | 14 / 0 | 11 / 0 |
| Entry-cache snapshot loads | 0 / 2 | 0 / 2 |
| Participant rows | 92 / 5 | 80 / 4 |

Shared-row-facts requests stayed **10 → 10**, and usage requests stayed **20 → 20**. The attributable removal is ten separate watermark statements plus avoided participant display reads; there is no increase in the shared read families.

## T1 and proof

Worker-owned background flow: **0 → 0** main-thread calls. Repository inventory: **455 → 455**. The shared native participant kernel retains 5 existing calls; legacy usage kernel/cache writer retains 7. Their synchronous incognito callers await Phase E. No new T1 call, reclassification, or sync fallback.

Two scoped Codex autoreview rounds completed; no outstanding actionable findings. Added regressions cover batched generation after committed rewrite/rollback, usage after rewrite plus append, and participant counts/order after in-process writes. CI caught and drove corrections to participant aggregate invalidation, retained display facts, and a usage fixture missing its session header.

Corrected local CI-failure reproductions passed: participant placement 2 tests (Vitest 291.65s, runner 363.53s); usage regression 1 test (29.88s, runner 153.76s). prs.title: fix: local Ollama can call web tools directly by default
prs.body:
Related: #145137. Builds on #167933 and the canonical dispatcher repair; thanks to @lator57-gif for the local-model report.

## What Problem This Solves

Small local Ollama models often try to call `web_search` and `web_fetch` directly even when their schemas are deferred behind Tool Search.

## User Impact

Embedded runs on native local Ollama expose the two policy-approved web tools directly when `tools.toolSearch` is unset. Other optional tools remain deferred. Explicit settings, known hosted routes, other transports, Code Mode, and prepared worker presentations retain their existing behavior. This does not enable denied tools or configure a search provider.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing tool-surface owner selects two additional direct schemas using the provider's prepared local-route hint. The existing catalog owner still checks tool provenance and policy, so an MCP lookalike cannot become a trusted direct web tool. Prompt restrictions can still remove both the schema and catalog authority.

## Evidence

Completed **120 real CLI trials**: 10 seeds × 3 local models × 2 prompts × A/B. Native Ollama 0.40.2; 32K context, 2,048 output tokens, temperature 0.6, thinking off, 120-second agent deadline. Every trial used a fresh session through `pnpm openclaw --profile <isolated-profile> agent --local`. All 557 native requests matched their model/seed/settings and expected tool surface; the only requested shell command was `echo hello`.

A is the dispatcher-only parent; B adds the two direct web schemas. The web prompt requests an actual search for official OpenClaw documentation, a fetch of `https://docs.openclaw.ai/providers/ollama`, and the page title/native endpoint. “Both facts” additionally requires the correct title and native endpoint from the fetched page. Echo requires actual tool stdout plus a grounded final reply, not merely an accepted background command.

| Model | Search+fetch completed, A → B | Both facts correct, A → B | Actual echo, A → B | Initial web prompt tokens, A → B | First web output, seconds A → B | First echo output, seconds A → B |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `qwen3:8b` | 0/10 → 9/10 | 0/10 → 9/10 | 10/10 → 10/10 | 8234 → 8561 | no output → 0.99 | 1.1 → 1.07 |
| `qwen3:4b` | 0/10 → 1/10 | 0/10 → 1/10 | 10/10 → 10/10 | 8228 → 8555 | 0.35 → 0.42 | 0.42 → 0.31 |
| `llama3.2:latest` | 0/10 → 7/10 | 0/10 → 2/10 | 4/10 → 4/10 | 8236 → 8566 | 1.64 → 1.75 | 0.77 → 2.22 |

B adds **327 Qwen tokens / 330 Llama tokens**, about 4% of the initial prompt. The declared surface grows from 13 to 15 tools, with compact UTF-8 schema JSON growing from 13,279 to 14,996 bytes (+1,717). All 60 initial requests per option shared the same initial schema hash, including across A's test-only follow-up.

| Model | Median agent wall, web A → B | Median agent wall, echo A → B | Median CLI wall, web A → B | Median CLI wall, echo A → B |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `qwen3:8b` | 8.02 → 15.63 s | 7.16 → 10.81 s | 61.24 → 62.01 s | 43.12 → 53.39 s |
| `qwen3:4b` | 28.39 → 31.67 s | 13.77 → 16.85 s | 50.61 → 57.65 s | 34.19 → 40.59 s |
| `llama3.2:latest` | 5.12 → 9.31 s | 4.99 → 6.6 s | 17.11 → 22.3 s | 18.23 → 21.63 s |

The failed qwen3:8b B web trial selected both correct tools, but fetch returned `ECONNRESET`; it remains a failure in the table. A's qwen3:8b web attempts returned empty native output. The installed `qwen3:4b` is the Thinking-2507 variant and frequently exhausts this output budget. Llama still produces malformed arguments and incomplete or incorrect answers: direct schemas improve access, not model understanding. Wrong-tool/malformed-run counts for web: A 0/0, 1/0, 0/1; B 0/0, 0/0, 0/5, in the model order above. Echo malformed runs: A 0, 0, 7; B 0, 0, 9; no wrong-tool echo runs.

First output means the first nonempty native text, thinking, or tool-call event, not an inferred internal token time. This shared-host run retained normal caches. CLI startup varied substantially; agent wall includes unsuccessful turns, so it is not a completed-task speed comparison. One CLI wall sample is excluded because the coordinator was paused after the command completed; its agent/native timings remain valid. The outer process allowance rose to 720 seconds after an unscored cold-start attempt made no model request within 180 seconds; all model/agent budgets stayed unchanged.

A was initially `8cdb7fd8c2aff9416756123a3b103cabba25253c` and then `f63c37a3fff9ef37e78600b102f4925761acfa8e`; the latter changes only two sorted test assertions, with identical production sources and initial schema hashes. prs.title: perf(memory-core): tokenize dreaming snippets once per entry
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Dreaming's light and REM sweeps re-tokenize the same snippets on every comparison.

- `dedupeEntries` compares each short-term recall entry against the kept entries and calls `textSimilarity`, which tokenizes both operands on each call. Base evaluates `candidate.path === entry.path` before it calls `textSimilarity`, so kept entries on other paths are skipped by a string compare and never tokenized. Within one path every comparison still tokenizes both operands, so N entries on one path cost O(N^2) tokenizations (59,400 for 600 distinct entries spread over 6 paths, 100 per path, which is the regression test's shape).
- `isEntryCoveredByRecentDiary` re-normalizes and re-tokenizes every recent diary page once per light candidate (`LIGHT_DIARY_HISTORY_LIMIT` pages, 4 today), so the diary check costs N x pages tokenizations of long diary text.

## User Impact

Same dreaming output, less CPU per sweep. No config, schema, or storage change. Merge order, merged fields, similarity values, thresholds, and MMR ranking are unchanged (differential proof below). The production short-term recall store is capped at 512 entries (`SHORT_TERM_RECALL_MAX_ENTRIES`), so the real saving is small: on the real `memory rem-harness` CLI over a populated 512-entry store the run is about 0.13 s (6 to 7 percent) faster, most of the roughly 2 s being CLI start-up, and in the CPU profile `tokenize` drops from 80 ms of self time to not sampled. A synthetic 2,000-entry REM preview, a size the cap makes unreachable in production, drops from about 386 to 463 ms to about 57 to 70 ms and shows how the cost scales.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Each entry is tokenized once (`prepareSimilarityText`) instead of once per comparison. That is the saving. Kept entries are also bucketed by path; because base already skipped other-path entries before tokenizing, bucketing removes only the per-candidate scan over every kept entry on other paths (one string compare each) and leaves the set of compared pairs unchanged.
- Recent diary pages are normalized and tokenized once per sweep instead of once per candidate.
- `textSimilarity` has no production caller after this, so it is replaced by `prepareSimilarityText` plus `preparedTextSimilarity`. A repository search (`extensions/`, `packages/`, `src/`, `docs/`, `apps/`, `scripts/`) found no other reader, and nothing is exported through `api.ts` or `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*`.
- `memory/mmr.ts` kept its own copy of the same rule (token-less texts compare by lowercase literal equality). It now consumes `prepareSimilarityText` and `preparedTextSimilarity`, so one module owns the policy instead of two. `tokenize` and `jaccardSimilarity` become module-private: the production dead-export scan flags them once `mmr.ts` stops importing them, and `mmr.test.ts` reaches them through the prepared API.
- The dedupe and diary helpers moved from `dreaming-phases.ts` into `dreaming-snippet-dedupe.ts` because the line-cap growth ratchet rejects growth of an over-cap file and `dreaming-phases.ts` is one (1324 -> 1244 raw lines at base `4b7b100b482`). With the helpers kept in place plus 35 added code lines the ratchet fails (record at the earlier base `9da00b0b92e`): `extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming-phases.ts: 1333 -> 1368 counted lines (cap 700). Extract a coherent sibling module; never trim coverage or disable max-lines.`

Scope check at base `4b7b100b482`: the O(N^2) shape is still on `main` (the moved helpers in `dreaming-phases.ts` are byte-identical to those at `9da00b0b92e`; see Rebase onto `4b7b100b482`). A search of open PRs and issues for dreaming dedupe tokenization (`gh search prs` and `gh search issues`, state open) returns only this PR. Related but different, all closed or merged: #80613, #80620, #86645 (CJK tokenizer for dedupe), #93121, #93192 (filter already-emitted entries in the light phase), #164660 (NFC normalization moved ahead of the CJK regex in `tokenize`; this branch keeps that order).

Diff shape: 6 files under `extensions/memory-core/src`, +279 / -118 including the new module (107 lines) and its test (119 lines); `dreaming-phases.ts` is -81 / +1, `memory/mmr.ts` is -20 / +14, `memory/tokenize.ts` is -10 / +24.

## Stored Data

No persisted data model changes. Tokenization and similarity run in memory during one sweep; nothing is written to the store differently, and no schema, migration, or file format changes. `PreparedSimilarityText` and the per-path buckets are local values inside one `dedupeEntries`, `prioritizeLightEntriesByDiaryCoverage`, or `applyMMRToHybridResults` call and are never serialized. No upgrade or migration step applies: an older store is read by exactly the same code as before. The full diff contains no persistence, serialization, schema, or embedding call:

```
$ git diff --stat 4b7b100b482 ab3bd545c53
 extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming-phases.ts      |  82 +-------------
 .../src/dreaming-snippet-dedupe.test.ts            | 119 +++++++++++++++++++++
 .../memory-core/src/dreaming-snippet-dedupe.ts     | 107 ++++++++++++++++++
 extensions/memory-core/src/memory/mmr.test.ts      |  21 ++--
 extensions/memory-core/src/memory/mmr.ts           |  34 +++---
 extensions/memory-core/src/memory/tokenize.ts      |  34 ++++--
 6 files changed, 279 insertions(+), 118 deletions(-)
$ git diff 4b7b100b482 ab3bd545c53 -- extensions/memory-core/src | grep -E '^[+-]' | grep -v -E '^(\+\+\+|---)' \
    | grep -n -i -E 'writeFile|appendFile|sqlite|INSERT|UPDATE |CREATE TABLE|ALTER TABLE|JSON\.stringify|JSON\.parse|persist|schema|migrat|embedding|vector'; echo "(grep exit $?)"
(grep exit 1)
```

## Evidence

All of the following ran on one machine (Mac Studio, Apple M3 Ultra, macOS 27.0.1, Node v24.21.0) at the pushed tree `ab3bd545c53` (tree object `00fe3bcbc5e`, base `4b7b100b482`, pnpm 12.9.0) for Rebase onto `4b7b100b482`, Tests, the red/green regression proof, Other checks, and Measured test cost. Build, Behaviour, and the mutation table ran earlier at tree `56d88cb3220` over base `9da00b0b92e` (pnpm 12.5.1), and the real CLI and gateway transcript at `ee146b97bba` over `7bec812cc68`; Rebase onto `4b7b100b482` and the transcript section say why they still apply. The machine was shared and loaded (load average about 8 to 66 during the runs), so absolute timings are noisy; before/after pairs were interleaved in one sitting.

### Contract table

| Case | Expected | Pinned by |
|---|---|---|
| Near-duplicate snippets on the same path | merged, source keys kept in input order | `merges near-duplicate snippets only within the same path` |
| Identical snippet on a different path | not merged | same test |
| Distinct snippets with zero tokens (`!!!` vs `???`) | not merged (lowercase fallback preserved) | `keeps distinct non-alphabet snippets apart` |
| Diary-covered candidate | moved behind fresh candidates, relative order kept | `moves candidates covered by a diary page behind fresh ones`, plus the existing end-to-end light sweep suite in `dreaming-phases.test.ts` |
| Tokenizations for 600 distinct candidates over 6 paths | <= 600 (59,400 on base) | `tokenizes each candidate once instead of once per comparison` |
| Tokenizations for 240 candidates and 4 diary pages | <= 244 (1,920 on base) | `tokenizes each recent diary page once across all candidates` |
| MMR ordering | unchanged | existing `memory/mmr.test.ts` suite, plus the differential run below |
| Canonically equivalent snippets (decomposed vs precomposed Hangul and kana) | tokenize identically, with NFC applied before the CJK regex exactly as on `main` | `diversifies NFC-equivalent Hangul` and `diversifies NFC-equivalent kana` in `memory/mmr.test.ts` (from #164660), plus the extended differential corpus below |

### Rebase onto `4b7b100b482`

The rebase conflicted only in import lines (`main` dropped two imports next to the new `dreaming-snippet-dedupe.js` import in `dreaming-phases.ts`, and `mmr.test.ts` now imports `mergeHybridResults` next to the prepared-text imports). The moved helper code is unchanged on `main`: the block from `function dedupeEntries(` up to `function buildLightDreamingBody(` is byte-identical at the previous base (`/tmp/h-old.ts`, from `9da00b0b92e`) and the new one (`/tmp/h-new.ts`, from `4b7b100b482`), and the diary threshold is still `0.35` (line 99 at the previous base, line 95 at the new one):

```
      79 /tmp/h-old.ts
      79 /tmp/h-new.ts
914d685c7736d1e297a9d52228bfc9a960b0b69d3fb72ddb910aba225b4bd2e5  /tmp/h-old.ts
914d685c7736d1e297a9d52228bfc9a960b0b69d3fb72ddb910aba225b4bd2e5  /tmp/h-new.ts
helpers byte-identical
99:const LIGHT_DIARY_SNIPPET_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD = 0.35;
95:const LIGHT_DIARY_SNIPPET_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD = 0.35;
```

`main` rewrote the CJK loop in `tokenize` and dropped the early returns in `jaccardSimilarity` after `9da00b0b92e`. This branch keeps `main`'s bodies for both functions verbatim; against the new base it only makes them module-private and adds the prepared wrapper, so `preparedTextSimilarity(prepareSimilarityText(a), prepareSimilarityText(b))` runs the same `tokenize` and `jaccardSimilarity` code as `main`'s `textSimilarity(a, b)`, with the same token-less literal fallback:

```diff
$ git diff 4b7b100b482 ab3bd545c53 -- extensions/memory-core/src/memory/tokenize.ts
diff --git a/extensions/memory-core/src/memory/tokenize.ts b/extensions/memory-core/src/memory/tokenize.ts
index 1dab6850399..f6fc612e943 100644
--- a/extensions/memory-core/src/memory/tokenize.ts
+++ b/extensions/memory-core/src/memory/tokenize.ts
@@ -4,7 +4,7 @@ const CJK_RE = /[\u3040-\u309f\u30a0-\u30ff\u3400-\u4dbf\u4e00-\u9fff\uac00-\ud7
 const CJK_RUN_RE = new RegExp(`${CJK_RE.source}+`, "g");

 // Only adjacent CJK characters form bigrams: "我喜欢hello你好" must not yield "欢你".
-export function tokenize(text: string): Set<string> {
+function tokenize(text: string): Set<string> {
   const lower = normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(text).normalize("NFC");
   // Keep CJK in its existing bigram/unigram lane; word marks stay attached to a base.
   const words = lower.replace(CJK_RUN_RE, " ").match(/[\p{L}\p{N}_][\p{L}\p{M}\p{N}_]*/gu) ?? [];
@@ -25,7 +25,7 @@ export function tokenize(text: string): Set<string> {
   return tokens;
 }

-export function jaccardSimilarity(setA: Set<string>, setB: Set<string>): number {
+function jaccardSimilarity(setA: Set<string>, setB: Set<string>): number {
   if (setA.size === 0 && setB.size === 0) {
     return 1;
   }
@@ -43,14 +43,28 @@ export function jaccardSimilarity(setA: Set<string>, setB: Set<string>): number
   return intersectionSize / unionSize;
 }

+export type PreparedSimilarityText = {
+  tokens: Set<string>;
+  // Set only for token-less text, which compares by literal equality.
+  emptyTokenText: string | undefined;
+};
+
+// Tokenize once so repeated comparisons against the same text skip re-tokenizing.
+export function prepareSimilarityText(text: string): PreparedSimilarityText {
+  const tokens = tokenize(text);
+  return {
+    tokens,
+    emptyTokenText: tokens.size === 0 ? normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(text) : undefined,
+  };
+}
+
 // Distinct text outside the tokenizer's alphabet must not collapse as two empty sets.
-export function textSimilarity(contentA: string, contentB: string): number {
-  const tokensA = tokenize(contentA);
-  const tokensB = tokenize(contentB);
-  if (tokensA.size === 0 && tokensB.size === 0) {
-    return normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(contentA) === normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(contentB)
-      ? 1
-      : 0;
+export function preparedTextSimilarity(
+  a: PreparedSimilarityText,
+  b: PreparedSimilarityText,
+): number {
+  if (a.tokens.size === 0 && b.tokens.size === 0) {
+    return a.emptyTokenText === b.emptyTokenText ? 1 : 0;
   }
-  return jaccardSimilarity(tokensA, tokensB);
+  return jaccardSimilarity(a.tokens, b.tokens);
 }
```

`mmr.ts` on `main` now takes `lambda` directly instead of a config object; this branch keeps that signature and changes only how each item's text is prepared and compared. Because the moved helpers and the tokenizer are `main`'s own code, the Behaviour differential and the CLI and gateway transcript below compare the same logic they would compare at this base; they were not re-run here.

#### What is synthetic

- All memory text is generated by `gen-ws.mjs` (seeded, homelab-style notes, no private data): 60 daily files `memory/2026-07-31.md` to `memory/2026-09-28.md`, 1,246,416 bytes, plus a `MEMORY.md`. 20 big files (about 57 KB each) hold repeated line families so many chunks are near-duplicates within a path.
- Embeddings are a local deterministic stub (`stub-embed.mjs`, 127.0.0.1:18921, sha256-derived 64-dim vectors). No real model or network service was used for embeddings.
- The recall store was populated by production code only (no hand edits): `memory index --force`, then 180 real `memory search` CLI calls.
- The 4 diary pages in `DREAMS.md` are synthetic: each quotes the first 300 characters of one light candidate from the no-diary run (ranks 1, 3, 5, 7) so they overlap recall snippets. Not production-written.
- The dreaming narrative (LLM) step was not run for real: the isolated config points the `openai` provider `baseUrl` at the local stub, which answers 404, so narratives fall back to the local diary fallback. The light and REM reports are written before and independent of the narrative.
- Workspace was built so no daily file falls inside the 2 day light ingestion window, to keep the sweep input exactly the 512 recalled entries (see Harness notes).

##### Tie-order variation (present on base, not caused by the PR)

Every one of the 11 diary runs whose exact order differs has its first mismatch at position 92, and in every run the candidate set and the sort-key sequence match. The pair that swaps is `memory/2026-09-21.md:790-813` and `memory/2026-09-21.md:810-833`. In the frozen store both have the identical sort key:

```
memory/2026-09-21.md:790-813  lastRecalledAt=2026-10-04T06:33:40.129Z recallCount=21
memory/2026-09-21.md:810-833  lastRecalledAt=2026-10-04T06:33:40.129Z recallCount=21
```

`prepareLightDreaming` sorts by `lastRecalledAt` then `recallCount`, so with an exact tie the final order is the order in which the store hands the entries over, and `dedupeEntries` keeps first-seen order on both builds (compared side by side at the two commits). That input order varies between gateway runs: base shows the variation too (4 of 17 diary runs; REM evidence ordering 5 of 17; no-diary REM report 1 of 3 base runs). Head shows it in 7 of 17. With 17 runs per side that difference is within what chance gives (two-sided Fisher exact test on 4 of 17 versus 7 of 17: p = 0.4646, exactly 18797/40455, by enumerating the hypergeometric table; one-sided p = 0.2323), and the PR does not touch the store read path, but I cannot rule out a small skew with this sample, so I am stating the counts rather than hiding them. No secret or private data was involved. The redirect to the local stub was added immediately after, and no run in this transcript contacted any non-local service (gateway logs: 0 matches for `api.openai.com`).
- The first populated-store attempt (workspace ending 2026-10-03) is archived in `v1-nondeterministic/`; it was discarded for the ingestion reason above, and the whole population (index plus 180 searches) was redone.

prs.title: refactor(sessions): activate memory-only incognito actors
prs.body:
Related: #168602. Completes Phase E after #169124, #169227, and #169327.

## What Problem This Solves

Incognito sessions still used a separate SQLite owner on the Gateway thread. This activates the session actor’s memory backend for all incognito flows and removes the native and inactive pinned-worker alternatives in the same change. Durable sessions retain the SQLite-worker backend. Acquisition selects one backend once; there is never a second writer for a native session.

Creation, turns/continuations, SessionManager/SDK, history/search, collaboration, Boards, usage, reset/delete and close now consume actor operations and committed facts. Memory state survives handle release, disappears on owner/session close or process exit, and keeps the existing nonrenewing 24-hour expiry. Reads of absent state never create it or fall back to SQLite. Source and built SDK modules share the process owner registry. Deprecated synchronous SDK persistence/history calls reject incognito targets and identify their awaited replacements; durable compatibility remains within its existing window.

The native owner, SQL kernels, pinned-worker adapter, generations, bindings, reverse RPCs, repeated bookkeeping checks and obsolete tests are deleted. While activation was in flight, #169621 removed the inactive prerequisite and #169811 restored it on main. This PR activates that backend while preserving main’s subsequent async readers, immutable snapshots and receipt changes. Schemas, retention and large-payload SQL projections are unchanged.

## Boundaries and accepted edges

The memory backend opens no SQLite database and consumes no database-worker slot. Creation retains one worker batch checking for a real durable row, so an incognito key cannot hide user data. Global ACP, Talk, audit, placement and publication metadata retain their existing owners. Content-free audit identifiers and global placement identifiers are retained as documented; incognito entry/transcript content is not persisted.

GitHub publication reads small session/member facts from the actor and shared facts from the existing state worker. One memory admission runs before the destination transaction because its requester policy callback may write state. Shared facts are validated within that transaction; durable source fencing and live checks before external publication remain unchanged.

Removed checks and accepted edges:

- Native generations, admission/read claims, repeated target capture and suggestion generation comparisons: accepted work uses its captured target; later caller mutation does not retarget it.
- Per-frame currency reads and post-read revision handshakes: a read may finish with its committed snapshot while later actor commands proceed. Low-level transcript deletion does not itself revoke an already admitted run; actual effect authority remains current.
- Whole-roster recapture and repeated placement-evidence reads: new owners and later placement changes appear on the next listing/sweep; captured facts do not authorize effects.
- Post-write sharing rereads: receipts are authoritative; later writes publish their own receipts.
- Progress-card config recapture: accepted work finishes against its captured store; later operations use the new configuration.
- FTS revision/index checks and projection rebuild admission: memory search reads committed events; uncommon Unicode tokenization or equally ranked snippets may differ from SQLite.
- Usage refresh-lock handshakes: overlapping memory refreshes may reuse the next request. A bookkeeping ACP failure event may follow a direct durable metadata rewrite; backend/tool effects still require live authority.
- Unbound incognito identity recapture: a logical lookup may follow a recreated namespace at the same key when session ID and lifecycle still match; retained actor handles remain closed. Policy lookups use the current policy at that key.
- Transport revocation generations: close plus existing transport teardown is sufficient; already handed-off transport work may finish during close.
- Per-checkpoint borrowed-worker file identity rereads: the borrower trusts its admitted live owner; reopen/repair checks remain.
- Absent creation-witness rejection after an earlier lazy owner capture: a lazy capture alone does not reserve or refuse creation; a later creator may use the already observed path identity when that owner has no creation witness. Existing file-identity and effect checks remain.
- Repeated cleanup authority forwarding through synchronous memory reads: the caller is checked once by the cleanup guard; selected actor and owner-close authority remain, and later effects check their own authority.
- Memory publication source fencing: close after preparation admission may leave an internal request/receipt; external publication still checks live authority.

Credentials, approvals, tool/command execution, destructive transcript effects, external sends and cross-user disclosure retain their real authority checks.

## Evidence

### Measurement

One live shared-harness pair under the revised proof rules: baseline `b9119c5435bcd54cfd6e37e38b0dcd70cfc29c7a`, candidate `f0b7763478e3bf3189727ee95528e4c1523f3a31`. Ranges are across ten warmed turns within each run, not independent repeated pairs. Later integration/fixture/publication fixes are separate source and CI evidence; this is not relabeled as final-head runtime proof.

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Warmed all-thread statements, median [min–max] | 354.5 [302–549] | 375 [340–483] |
| Warmed database requests, median [min–max] | 108 [95–148] | 103.5 [94–124] |
| Warmed MAIN statements, median [min–max] | 0 [0–2] | 0 [0–2] |
| First-turn statements / requests / MAIN | 798 / 164 / 38 | 1,169 / 205 / 48 |
| Whole-workload statements / requests | 10,119 / 2,119 | 10,215 / 1,994 |

Per-operation attribution over warmed turns (statements / requests):

| Actor operation | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Accept input | 153 / 21 | 150 / 20 |
| Adopt run | 42 / 10 | 40 / 10 |
| Append transcript event | 260 / 20 | 260 / 20 |
| Complete turn | 60 / 10 | 60 / 10 |
| Delivery settled | 63 / 20 | 60 / 20 |
| Read | 31 / 31 | 37 / 37 |

These operations add no SQL forms. Actor reads rise because unchanged background index writes invalidate cached snapshots between turns: three normal reads per turn remain identical; extra hydration occurs at precisely the boundaries with intervening unscoped index writes (one baseline turn, seven candidate turns). Publisher, write-receipt and SQLite executor code are unchanged between measured heads.

Background memory indexing/cache publication adds 170 warmed statements. First-turn actor commands and request counts are unchanged; deferred schema admission (+128), memory reindex/FTS publication (+56), and write preparation (+62) explain most of its increase. Candidate warmed duration was 9.34s versus 5.26s. The raw increase is scheduling/background variance under the attribution rule, not a timing-controlled speed benchmark. Both runs completed all thirteen turns, cron, compaction and shutdown; both returned the same non-warmed `mentions.dismiss` UNAVAILABLE result.

Shared read-family audit under the tightened attribution rule follows. Counts are successful native SQL; families overlap and must not be summed. Requests count distinct requests executing the family. Mean, median and ranges are across the same ten warmed turns.

| Family | Base SQL/turn mean; median [range] | Candidate SQL/turn mean; median [range] | Base → candidate requests/turn |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Exact-entry facts | 10.9; 10.5 [10–12] | 11.9; 11.5 [11–14] | 10.9 → 11.9 |
| Actor hydration | 5.7; 5.5 [5–7] | 5.7; 6 [5–6] | 5.7 → 5.7 |
| Entry-cache snapshot loads | 2; 2 [0–4] | 3.4; 4 [2–6] | 1 → 1.7 |
| Row facts | 27.5; 30 [20–30] | 25; 25 [20–30] | 5.5 → 5 |
| Watermark reads | 14.5; 15 [13–15] | 7; 7 [6–8] | 13.5 → 7 |

Exact-entry statements increase 109 → 119. The complete partition is corpus writable admission 9 → 15 (+6), pre-input reads following background index writes 1 → 6 (+5), and remaining exact-entry reads 99 → 98 (−1). Each corpus-admission read pairs one-to-one with the next corpus request within one second, sharing the empty-session-key argument fingerprint. Source `readSessionTranscriptCorpusInWorker` deliberately performs this read before corpus discovery; its durable branch is unchanged. The additional pre-input reads all follow `cache.write.inline` / `source.replace.inline` commits after the preceding final delivery, the same windows recorded in the actor-read trace analysis. Normal runtime reads during the turn remain 10 → 10. Background index commits and actor reads use the same writer connection in each run; the unchanged write-receipt implementation advances the unscoped revision included in session replica tokens.

Actor hydration remains 57 → 57 SQL: actor.read 31 → 37 is offset by acceptInput/adoptRun/deliverySettled hydration 6 → 0; appendTranscriptEvent stays 20 → 20. The six extra actor.read requests are already attributed in the actor-read trace analysis to background index writes invalidating the existing replica before the next input.

Snapshot statements increase 20 → 34: corpus inventory scans 9 → 15 each execute exactly two snapshot SELECTs (18 → 30); periodic session-registry-maintenance scans 1 → 2 each execute the same two SELECTs (2 → 4). Source blob identities prove that the memory sync scheduler, cache loader, ordered/retained read helper, and registry-maintenance scheduler are unchanged. Candidate sends preserve the maintenance caller stack; baseline redispatch lost its original caller.

Row-facts work falls 55 → 50 requests and 275 → 250 SQL. Watermark reads fall 145 → 70: patch.commit 70 → 10, lifecycle.project 10 → 0, row-facts 55 → 50, transcript-anchors 10 → 10.


Attribution limit: traces expose SQL stacks, request keys, timestamps and argument fingerprints, but not an explicit replica-invalidation reason. The pre-input link combines unchanged source with preceding index commits on the same writer connection; it is not a directly logged invalidation reason. Every net increase is accounted for; raw family counts are not presented as flat.

The isolated public CLI incognito lifecycle passed on measured candidate `f0b7763`: two creations, two provider-backed turns, both history reads, reset and deletion. Three persistence scans found no incognito entry/transcript content or backing file; the backend opened zero SQLite connections and issued zero SQLite statements or worker requests. Only exact documented audit/placement identity fields were retained. The initial overly broad scanner was corrected against those field contracts, not by excluding whole tables. The native baseline accepted creation/send but timed out before the provider; its 351 create and 396 partial-send native statements are incomplete-flow evidence, not a comparable full-lifecycle saving.

The measured delete path still executed 297 global placement authority reads and two secret-store reads on MAIN. These belong to existing global owners, so the whole lifecycle is not SQL-free. Inspection found duplicate forwarding of the same cleanup callback through synchronous memory reads; the final source removes that forwarding while preserving one explicit cleanup authority check and memory-owner closure checks. No unmeasured post-fix count is claimed.

## Final integration and source accounting

Head `e9ade9baabf29057e559f4df102bf3722b26ab33` integrates main `f6c9a769e0f24780696a5aaf0e90dabf748adbcc`, retaining the earlier integrations and two test-only fixture repairs. This integration combines main's durable worker APIs and committed predicates with Phase E's memory-first acquisition. Native incognito bindings and synchronous fallbacks introduced by the overlapping main change remain deleted. New asynchronous ownership calls retain their release/disposal and registration-publication contracts. The chat entry points keep their public exports; their unchanged admission, input-custody, ACK and dispatch implementation moves into a separate module to stay within the existing file-size limit. Memory capability capture and creation-test admission helpers move into their existing owners. The final conflict repair also preserves main’s cold writer preparation and creation-witness fixes, asynchronous runtime-config preparation, and removal of a redundant lifecycle check. The memory branch remains selected before durable config/storage preparation. The later conflict repairs preserve main’s fresh-input custody admission by applying its exact delta to the extracted dispatch module, and retain main’s prepared initial-context optimization alongside memory actor reads. Final CI repairs remove dead adapters, keep awaited release callbacks typed correctly, update stale fixtures to their current APIs, and preserve current memory delivery checks at approval effects.

The historical incognito-reachable T1 checklist falls **29 → 0**: 18 calls deleted, ten now worker-only, and one durable-only reader bypassed by memory. The completed exact `1de4df00` CI ratchet reports **427 → 401 global T1 calls** against its executed merge base `d593d284`, compatibility exceptions **9 → 9**, and dialect groups **1 → 1 mechanical, 7 → 7 design, 9 → 5 engine maintenance**. The earlier generated snapshot at `e49e1cc7` predates this integration; the CI ratchet supplies the latest executed comparison. The two successor commits change tests only; no ratchet execution is claimed on their head. This global scope differs from the historical incognito checklist.

Relative to integrated main `e61083f8`: production/tooling **+14,953 / −33,043 = −18,090**; tests/fixtures **+14,971 / −29,627 = −14,656**; docs **+600 / −1,382 = −782**. Total **+30,524 / −64,052 = −33,528** across 895 files (`git diff --numstat --no-renames`; test/spec/fixture paths grouped as tests).

The final integration preserves main’s publication receipt admission and transcript-worker shutdown cancellation; its queued-admission regression now uses an isolated durable fixture because the worker-memory backend is deleted. It also preserves main’s archived-session error type, forwards durable registry changes to admission, and transfers main’s session-initialization callback changes into the extracted dispatch owner. CI repairs publish the committed actor entry in pending-delivery fixtures, route the TTS-stream fixture through the existing host-owned infra pool, and register Solid cleanup once per test file through Vitest setup. Behavioral assertions and timeouts stay intact. Main’s disconnected cloud-startup expectation repair is inherited unchanged. The final test-only repair supplies valid agents.list rosters in reconnect fixtures and publishes the archive fixture’s archived descriptor only after the mutation succeeds; assertions remain intact.

## Review and behavior evidence

Two Codex autoreview rounds completed; no third round was run. Missing pre-creation manager visibility and the live-source check before destructive compaction were fixed with negative controls. The null-lifecycle concern was declined after tracing the contract: null means an absent lifecycle; session identity, non-null lifecycle and writer checks remain. Review used chunked source/diff input without execution, which limits whole-branch coverage.

The live CLI lifecycle and SQL pair above are measured-head evidence, not final-head runtime claims. Earlier focused repairs cover durable-child backend selection, canonical mixed-case memory keys, acknowledged metadata/transcript reads, reset/deletion, foreign-source rejection, and transport/effect revocation. No timeout increases or weakened assertions were used. Final merge-resolution tests preserve these memory contracts while adopting main's async API and cleanup contracts; CI supplies their execution proof.

Basic changed-file oxfmt, plain oxlint and whitespace checks passed. Broad local test/type suites were not run under the revised proof rules. A two-file diagnostic attempt spent 374s compiling cold worker inputs and then produced no completed test results; it was stopped rather than claimed as passing evidence. The generated worker inventory was rebuilt through the campaign CPU semaphore. No remote lease or token remains.

## CI, SDK and update proof

prs.title: fix: preserve media identity in transcript mirrors
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Transcript mirrors could collapse distinct attachments or correlate an identical caption with the wrong source reply. Completed-turn context reads also rejected real append receipts issued through an alias of the same physical database.

## User Impact

Distinct media retain their identities and delivery receipts bind to the correct source occurrence. Native and worker completed-turn reads retain the issued locator while preserving physical identity, live alias authority, expected execution claims and FIFO custody. Media-bearing history rows remain visible. Shipped filename-only mirrors retain their existing bytes; missing historical attachment identity cannot be reconstructed. Public receipt bytes and schemas are unchanged; update the Gateway normally.

## Why This Change Was Made

Compare authored captions and full media references before expanding compact display filenames. The existing append owner retains keyed replay and shipped fieldless compatibility. These media repairs have no net production growth.

Adopt main's canonical source discovery and SessionManager cache owners rather than retaining duplicate admission or prepared-context machinery. Carry the receipt's already-admitted read source through both initial context and final anchor reads. The final anchor previously retained that source only for admission-backed reads, dropping it for native receipt-backed reads and rediscovering a different locator. The corrected condition adds no lines; the entire locator repair adds four production lines and no new public option, receipt format or validation owner.

## Evidence

On the integrated main base, the complete reader suite reproduced the remaining native alias defect: 14 cases passed and the actual native final-anchor receipt case failed in 64.168 seconds. The repaired complete suite passes all 15 cases in 37.181 seconds, including actual native/worker receipts and copied-store, authority, replacement, closure and FIFO controls.

Current candidate SDK media identity/caption correlation: 18/18 passed in 31.414 seconds. Outbound mirror flow: 7/7 passed in 22.107 seconds. The original submitted-prompt contract passed in 68.836 seconds (6.109 seconds body), preserving exact whitespace, provenance, durable display and fork/editor acceptance. It was intentionally the single affected Codex contract, not a claim that all protocol tests ran.

Fresh complete 14-file P2 review returned scoped-clean across 14 intact passes in 1082.544 seconds; all 184 determining source inputs and the staged patch remained stable. Agents/sessions types passed in 48.888 seconds and Gateway types in 53.225 seconds. Typed lint for all 11 authored core files passed in 17.179 seconds. Docs MDX2 passed in 0.663 seconds, formatting14 in 0.603 seconds and staged diff-check in 0.325 seconds. Exact published head `c55328f8b984125a45f394c0aedec0d42513f2f0` completed [CI run 38349267141](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38349267141) successfully: 89 jobs, 634 seconds from run start to final update and 12744 summed observed job seconds. The native watcher independently reconciled nine superseded check entries before returning green. Earlier-base results and failed CI remain historical; no failed run is relabeled green and no admin exception is selected.

prs.title: perf(sqlite): avoid schema writes on warm store use
prs.body:
Related: #170470, #170548, #170598

## What Problem This Solves

Repeated schema preparation can revoke an active tool caller's retained profile authority even when SQLite's `CREATE IF NOT EXISTS` changes nothing. This completes the audit of persistent DDL on use across core, packages, and bundled plugins after the cron and shared-state additive fixes.

## User Impact

Existing stores can prepare their tables without revoking retained caller authority. Missing objects still install transactionally, existing historical column/constraint repairs remain, and imported memory rows retain their provenance backfill. There are no schema SQL, stored-shape, version, retention, permission, upgrade, or downgrade changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing schema-fact owner and `createSqliteSchemaEnsurer` for the remaining additive stores, including the first use of a warm native handle. Standalone update/Windows lease owners create only a missing table within their existing ownership boundaries. Retained wrapper readiness now follows the schema owner’s facts instead of an irrevocable per-handle flag, preserving admission/post-commit timing while invalidating on schema change or rollback. The Board constraint repair still validates the canonical/recognized historical definition; retired memory triggers still drop when present.

<details>
<summary>Audit inventory and previous DDL frequency</summary>

| Owner | Previous frequency | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/node-host/node-worker-launch-store.kernel.ts` | Base schema once per handle; boot table on each new boot-bound claim; container/cleanup/process-scope tables on each applicable start | Five schema ensurers; base handle cache removed; existing index included |
| `src/skills/library/store.ts` | First publish/upload on each native handle, including initialized files | Four-table schema ensurer; admission callbacks preserved |
| `src/gateway/worker-environments/store-schema.ts` | Environment-store preparation once per handle | Both companions and attachment index covered |
| `src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-move-intent.ts` | First move read/write per handle | Table ensure uses schema facts; missing-column migrations retained |
| `src/state/openclaw-agent-goal-operations-schema.ts` | First typed goal operation per handle | Table/index ensurer replaces handle cache |
| `src/state/openclaw-agent-board-schema.ts` | Board store's first use per handle, and migration preflight | Additive table/index DDL skipped on warm schema; definition consumes admitted facts |
| `src/state/openclaw-state-db-existing-write.ts` | First subset admission on each one-shot update-ledger handle | Validated catalog admitted before conditional additive installation |
| `src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-database.ts` | Every writable unbound private lease access (acquire/update/release) | Missing-table-only creation; identity-bound path unchanged |
| `src/gateway/worker-environments/workspace-quiescence-scripts.ts` | Every Windows shared-host acquire/renew/release | Missing-table check inside existing writer transaction |
| `src/audit/execution-owner-lifecycle-binding-store.ts` | Every helper invocation; current bundled caller already checked table existence | Exported helper now enforces the same missing-object boundary |
| `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/memory-schema-provenance.ts` | Every full shadow reindex publication, plus initialization | No redundant table creation or retired-trigger drop; backfill remains |
| `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/memory-entry-origins.ts` | Every direct helper invocation; bundled worker already guarded | Helper now uses the schema owner |

Already fixed: cron run receipts/runtime authority (#170548), shared-state feature/additive table ensures (#170598). Existing standing-intent and progress-card owners already gate their DDL with admitted objects/columns. Workshop changes, node-worker turns, outbound progress/bindings, standing grants, approval identity companions, project/template registries, execution identity/decision facts, and feature-local schema wrappers already guard installation.

Plugin/package audit: Workboard, logbook, and team reports initialize under schema admission at backend open; memory schema initializes under its published/shadow owner. Memory origin/tombstone callers already check missing tables. Full memory FTS/vector publication deliberately replaces derived structures and must retain its DDL. PostgreSQL bootstrap is outside the SQLite audit.

Excluded by lifecycle: versioned migrations and Doctor/STRICT/index repairs; snapshot restore; package activation/adoption initialization; one-shot legacy proxy-capture and restart-sentinel connection admission; disposable transcript import/archive/history-matching/staging/contract databases; TEMP tracking objects, and explicit planner-statistics refresh after maintenance. These perform initialization, actual schema repair, or deliberate derived-data replacement rather than redundant warm preparation.

</details>

## Evidence

Native SQL guards cover first and repeated warm audit/goal/Board/memory preparation, real node-worker claim/start persistence, reopened private update lease mutation, and emitted Windows lease renewal/release against real synthetic SQLite. A non-cron regression retains the operator tool source, releases the initiating request, and dispatches first warm skill-library preparation with live transaction/commit authority checks.

Synthetic Linux sandbox measurement on Node 26.8.2, baseline `88e5ae840faa`, seven measured rounds after 100 warm-up calls; medians per 1,000 initialized-store preparations (each with an explicit writer transaction):

| Preparation | Before | After | Warm DDL calls before → after |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Audit binding helper | 393.956 ms | 4.630 ms | 1,000 → 0 |
| Board schema helper | 660.308 ms | 14.641 ms | 1,000 → 0 |
| Memory origin helper | 211.411 ms | 4.376 ms | 1,000 → 0 |
| Memory provenance preparation | 612.604 ms | 278.278 ms | 2,000 → 0 |

These measure preparation overhead on empty synthetic stores, not end-to-end Gateway latency. Audit/origin bundled callers already guard their helpers; the direct-helper numbers quantify the tightened boundary rather than claim a current production-call speedup. Memory provenance retains its DML backfill and improves 2.20×. The sandbox was deleted after measurement.

Local focused proof: the five-file run passed 84 tests with one existing Bun-qualified skip (package provenance: 3.72 s file wall time; gateway/authority + emitted lease script: 72.95 s combined shard wall time; node launch + update handoff: 169.02 s combined shard wall time). The ten-test state schema guard file passed; the existing subset-writer file's 22 siblings passed, and its new physical-writer DDL guard passed separately after admitting the validated catalog. The schema-contract validator legitimately creates a private scratch database; that DDL is excluded by exact observed database identity, rather than masking physical-store changes. The warm audit-binding guard fails on the unchanged baseline because it observes both repeated CREATE statements. The request-closed skill-library regression also fails on unchanged code because the physical store issues its redundant CREATE block. Its authority-only assertion still passes on this narrower current-main harness; the added native SQL assertion protects the schema/authority boundary before more owners move under retained admission. Final cache-lifecycle checks passed: the request-closed warm library guard, worker-environment companion rollback/retry, and placement legacy-column repair/reopen (3 tests, 140.05 s shard wall time including compiler/import overhead). Broad typecheck, full cron/sqlite-store suites, builds, and e2e belong to PR CI under the requested validation policy; no Testbox/Crabbox lease was allocated.

prs.title: fix(skills): allow ordinary command examples in authored skills
prs.body:
## What this changes

Ordinary command examples and environment-token API code currently fail the authoring security check. Workshop refuses the write, and the personal Skill Library refuses publication. This PR limits those admission checks to recognized literal credentials. Explicit security audits and plugin scans retain the full source/prose diagnostics.

Current main replaced Workshop proposals with direct, versioned writes. This branch preserves that cutover and applies the policy through the existing shared bundle scanner. It does not restore retired proposal APIs, tests, or docs. Operator install policy, live authority checks, path validation, immutable Library revisions, and Workshop version/restore behavior retain their existing owners.

## Change breakdown

| Part | Files | +LOC | -LOC |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Implementation | 3 | 8 | 12 |
| Tests and fixtures | 3 | 77 | 6 |
| Documentation | 2 | 7 | 5 |
| **Total** | **8** | **92** | **23** |

Production shrinks by four lines. Test proof adds 71 net lines: two Library cases, an extension of an existing Workshop journey, and the database-worker registration. The prior plain-credential permutation, dedicated unchanged operator-policy case, and replacement manual-quarantine hook case were retired without replacement. Main separately retired the entire proposal lifecycle. No additional Workshop case is added.

## Before and after

The existing Workshop create/write/archive/restore journey now contains these inert authored examples in both `SKILL.md` and `scripts/deploy.js`:

```js
import { execFile } from "node:child_process";
execFile("git", ["--version"]);
const token = process.env.API_TOKEN;
fetch("https://example.test/api", {
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` },
});
```

**Before:** temporarily restoring main's shared scanner made the actual `createWorkshopSkill` entry point refuse the Markdown:

```text
Refused: deploy/SKILL.md line 8 matches security rule "dangerous-exec"
(Shell command execution detected (child_process)). Remove or rewrite that line, then retry.
```

**After:** the same journey creates the skill, writes the support file, archives it, restores it, and reads back the exact instruction and support bytes. The persisted file list is `SKILL.md` plus `scripts/deploy.js`. The accepted scripts are authored bytes; they are never executed by this proof.

| Real service flow | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Workshop create → write support → archive → restore → view | Exact command/API instruction and support bytes preserved |
| Library save → read | Published revision; exact instructions and support bytes preserved |
| Library save with a credential in base64 support transport | Rejected after decoding; no Library entry and no artifact |

The Library encoded-file denial remains because scanning transport base64 instead of decoded bytes could leak a credential into a durable artifact. The two publication journeys exercise separate real owners and stores. Dedicated plaintext and policy guard coverage was deliberately retired; this is not a claim that another test duplicates every assertion.

### Matched current Gateway proof

The same authored fixtures were sent to **two real, separately built Gateways**, using the shipped CLI and documented token-authenticated HTTP tool endpoint. The integrated main baseline is `c4887fb7de365414df4afe27dcb61947bfab9cae`; the feature is the pushed `cddad34c227da1fd564aaf18831c9d7710e82e46`. Each has isolated config, SQLite state, workspace, and loopback port. Both use the existing Node 24.18.1 / pnpm 12.7.0 runtime and unchanged frozen dependencies. Channels, providers, discovery, schedulers, and background learning are disabled; foreground tool policy explicitly allows `skill_workshop`.

```sh
OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<isolated-state> OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=<isolated-config> \
  pnpm openclaw gateway run --port <isolated-port> --bind loopback
```

Requests use `POST /tools/invoke`, `Authorization: Bearer <isolated-operator-token>`, and:

```json
{
  "tool": "skill_workshop",
  "agentId": "proof",
  "sessionKey": "agent:proof:manual",
  "args": { "action": "create", "name": "git-versions", "content": "<complete SKILL.md containing the exact command fixture above>" }
}
```

| Request / observable result | Main baseline | Pushed feature |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Create Git-command example | HTTP 400 `dangerous-exec`; no skill or artifact | HTTP 200; created |
| Create environment-token API example | HTTP 400 `env-harvesting`; no skill or artifact | HTTP 200; created |
| Write support → archive → restore → view | Create refusal prevents the journey | Every call HTTP 200; exact instructions and support bytes; `SKILL.md` + `scripts/deploy.js` |
| Create synthetic recognized literal credential | HTTP 400 `literal-secret`; absent from live list and filesystem | Same refusal and absence |

The main Gateway's live list is empty. The feature Gateway lists both `api-token` and `git-versions`. HTTP readback and direct artifact comparison match the authored bytes. The shipped `pnpm openclaw skills workshop --agent proof show git-versions --json` also returns those instructions and both file names. This proves actual Gateway authentication, policy, tool construction, publication, versioning, restoration, and readback without mocking a first-party owner. Authored scripts were never executed.

This is shared-operator token authentication on an isolated Gateway. It does not claim a signed-in personal Library CLI flow or a live-provider turn. Library publication and decoded-file refusal retain the real worker/SQLite/filesystem proof above. No new permanent test, source change, or public API is added for this proof.

## Validation

- Merged main at `c4887fb7de365414df4afe27dcb61947bfab9cae` to resolve actual conflicts. Main's new shared scanner and direct Workshop owner are preserved. A read-only merge check with current main `bf58e95ee3f583c338f48225ad9c5b3479e7d8d7` is conflict-free; it was not merged merely for advancing.
- One scoped simplification and fresh independent standards and correctness assessments cover the final eight-path diff. No actionable findings. Reviews inspected source; execution belongs to the checks below.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/skills/library/service-admission.test.ts src/skills/library/service.test.ts src/skills/workshop/library.test.ts src/skills/security/scanner.test.ts --bail=1`: **85 passed** across four files in **76.59s** on Node 24.18.1, pnpm 12.7.0, macOS ARM64. Library admission 2, Library service 26, Workshop 10, scanner 47.
- The first merged-head batch stopped at ZIP extraction (`native file copy failed`). Diagnosis found fs-safe 0.25 resolving the stale 0.21 native helper because the expected 0.25 helper was missing. A frozen-lockfile reinstall repaired this prerequisite. The complete same selection then passed, including ZIP extraction. No source/test assertion or dependency manifest was changed to conceal the failure.
- The changed-check plan passed formatting, production types, all 27 core test type graphs, dead exports, core/scripts lint, and selected repository guards. Results were completed across the original command and resumed remaining commands; passing steps were reused. The dead-export prerequisite needed access to pnpm's normal cache. An initial standalone lint command omitted the changed-check owner's environment and reported 11 unchanged max-lines violations; the actual scoped configuration passed without source or rule changes.
- `pnpm test src/skills/library/service-admission.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **2 passed**, command wall **26.27s**, Vitest **5.85s**. `pnpm test src/skills/workshop/library.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **10 passed**, command wall **40.04s**, Vitest **19.40s**. These macOS measurements ran during other validation work and are not a comparable before/after performance baseline. In [current PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38347219673), Library admission passed 2 cases in **6.05s** from shard begin to end (5.64s runner; 3.59s Vitest), and Workshop passed 12 cases in **30.54s** (30.19s runner; 28.40s Vitest). These Linux x64 measurements cover the provider’s PR merge checkout; they are per-file costs, not the total job including installation/build. Both browser jobs also passed. The complete native CI workflow and all automatic checks passed: 65 passed, none failed or pending at final verification before the proof update.
- The selected mocked-Gateway Control UI browser lane passed **78 tests across 23 files** in **201.48s** on native macOS ARM64. This is shared-harness coverage, not visual proof of this backend feature.

- Current mapped native runtime checks stopped at the unchanged macOS-only APFS cold/warm/sparse provisioning journey: 15 sibling cases and the Bun SQLite-admission partition passed, while that journey exceeded its existing 120-second deadline (153.65s observed). Its test and provisioning owners are byte-identical to the integrated main baseline. The selected Linux CI job skips this Darwin-only case; its Linux filesystem case remains platform-only proof. No timeout or assertion was changed, and this result is not reported as a passing row. The exact failure cause is unresolved.

- The final aggressive-selection/hybrid-runner map contains 10 runtime rows covering 58 distinct files. Nine rows passed locally with the pinned native OpenClaw Bun fork and Node 24.18.1; the remaining row has the macOS-only failure described above. Shared UI and browser-extension prerequisites also passed. The browser-extension Chromium flow paired its native host, attached tabs, revoked a paused tab, and cleaned up its relay/MCP/HTTP servers: **1 passed**, Vitest **79.59s**. Its first attempt stopped before testing on an abandoned build lease left by an interrupted validation worker; the verified task-owned lease was recovered, then the canonical command completed.

- Additional production/test type graphs, all selected extension lint stripes, SDK package-boundary compile (Codex, Slack, Telegram), Zoom canary, additional boundaries, prompt snapshots, source contracts, guards, architecture/Kysely, formatting, and plugin inventory passed. Protocol registry/generation, Swift/Kotlin determinism, since metadata, and mobile event coverage also passed. Documentation content passed too (0 broken links); its first attempt could not enter pnpm’s normal dlx cache, and the same command completed with native cache access. The exact-base private-key scanner also passed.

## Admission policy

Credential-only admission is the existing maintainer-authorized scope. Non-credential heuristics, including execution, pipe-to-shell, mining references, and environment/network combinations, do not veto authored content. This accepts that content-policy tradeoff while keeping literal-credential refusal, operator policy, runtime permissions, and current authority checks. Publishing instructions does not execute support scripts. No schema, public record shape, dependencies, or configuration options are added by this feature.

## How to verify

Run the focused command above with isolated test fixtures. Ordinary command/API examples must publish and survive readback/restoration with matching bytes. An encoded support file containing a recognized synthetic credential must leave no published entry or artifact. Full scanner tests must continue to report their source/prose diagnostics for explicit audit callers.

Apply-time quarantine of a historical credential-bearing proposal was not proved before its owner was retired by main. The current direct Workshop credential/path denials and version restoration are exercised by the existing Workshop suite.

## Historical evidence and limits

Historical proposal CLI traces belong to an owner retired by main; they are superseded here by the matched current Gateway proof above.

Earlier local emulated Linux UI/Gateway failures remain unresolved: the Canvas dashboard moved vertically after focus, provider-browser login hit its 120-second deadline, and the second Gateway lane hit custody/file-lifecycle and readiness deadlines. Diagnostic replays did not establish a repair or baseline cause. No timeouts or assertions were weakened. Later native CI passes are not proof of those failures' cause or repair. This feature does not change those owners, and the current planner selects shared Control UI and browser-extension checks, and no real-Gateway or native-app lane. There is no live-provider, live operator Gateway, or signed-in Library CLI proof in this update.

prs.title: perf(channels): share terminal delivery settlement
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Direct channel replies recorded successful delivery in the channel lifecycle and then wrote the same terminal receipt again when the dispatcher cleared pending-final custody. Multipart replies also re-admitted unchanged custody before each physical post.

Share the committed terminal receipt by the in-process payload's completion identity. The first successful settlement joins dispatcher-owned cleanup in its existing worker command, before `onDelivered` runs; the dispatcher consumes that receipt even if the observer throws. Admit multipart custody once, retaining current writer authorization immediately before each physical send. No schema, SDK, update, Doctor, plugin-loading, or service-lifecycle changes.

## Scope and accepted edges

- Removed the duplicate terminal settlement/read after the channel's successful settlement. The committed receipt remains authoritative for that exact payload lifetime; a reused completed payload is not sent again.
- Removed repeated `unknown` custody re-admission for each physical part. A cancellation between multipart posts may leave a visible partial reply; live writer revocation still prevents subsequent platform sends. At-least-once recovery remains unchanged.
- Retained the channel restart-source deduplication read: the prepared entry can be stale after intervening awaits.
- The shared-turn gap is conversation persistence, not repeated account/binding lookups: both the prior census and this paired channel census have seven five-statement identity/association publications (35 SQL/turn), versus zero in the chat census. Four come from `commitSessionEntryPatch`, one from lifecycle projection, one from `applySessionTurn`, and one from actor `writeEntry`. External channel conversation identity activates this existing path. These belong to the separate session-writer lane. The chat/channel revisions and workload differ; other channel families are smaller, so 35 is a family difference, not the net shared-turn gap.

## Measurement

One sequential baseline/candidate pair with the unchanged channel harness `2.0.0-channel.1`, one cold plus ten warmed turns, under the shared local CPU semaphore (RELAXED TESTING v6). Base `72536479c635e0f4df9f5d6fe15e23752f645d09`; candidate `6f3a89e2cdba1568649665bda7dc5be9ae798bfb`. Values below are warmed medians [min–max].

| Warmed causal metric | Base | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| All-thread statements | 242 [242–242] | 234 [234–234] |
| Requests | 45 [45–45] | 44 [44–44] |
| MAIN statements | 0 [0–0] | 0 [0–0] |
| Inbound SQL / requests | 9 / 1 | 9 / 1 |
| Shared turn SQL / requests | 200 / 40 | 200 / 40 |
| Outbound SQL / requests | 33 / 4 | 25 / 3 |

Every inbound/shared/outbound range is constant across all ten warmed turns. The saving is **8 SQL and 1 request per channel turn**: **24.2% outbound SQL**, **3.3% total SQL**, and **2.2% total requests**. This misses the 15% total target; the remaining shared conversation writes belong to the session-writer lane and are recorded as follow-up work. Multipart admission also changes from one command per post to one command per logical delivery; this single-post harness does not claim a separate saving for that.

The outbound request owner is `src/config/sessions/session-actor-sqlite.ts:Object.deliverySettled`, 4 → 3 calls per warmed turn. Its native SQL attribution is:

| Source file:function | Base SQL | Candidate SQL |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/state/openclaw-agent-db-admission.ts:<anonymous>` | 8 | 6 |
| `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-entry-store.ts:<anonymous>` | 5 | 4 |
| `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-conversation.ts:preserveSessionConversationIdentity` | 4 | 3 |
| `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-conversation.ts:upsertConversationIdentities` | 4 | 3 |
| `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-conversation.ts:readAssociation` | 4 | 3 |
| `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-conversation.ts:linkSessionConversation` | 8 | 6 |

Shared-read attribution (SQL per warmed turn; arithmetic means, all unchanged): exact-entry facts 3 → 3; actor hydration 1 → 1; entry-cache snapshot loads 0 → 0; entry-cache candidate rows 2 → 2; row facts 0 → 0; watermark 1 → 1; entry inventory 1 → 1; patch snapshot 7 → 7; other entry rows 1 → 1; projection snapshot 3 → 3; conversation bookkeeping 35 → 35. The shared request-stack cohorts are unchanged too. No downstream shared-read increase is hidden by the delivery saving.

Loaded-host context: raw warmed medians are 285 [258–314] → 291 [251–309] SQL and 58 [48–66] → 63.5 [53–76] requests, with MAIN 0 → 0. Startup-through-shutdown totals are 5,806 → 5,799 SQL and 845 → 919 requests; causal turn totals fall 2,965 → 2,891 SQL and 535 → 524 requests. Background totals rise 2,841 → 2,908 SQL and 310 → 395 requests, including unchanged `trajectory/runtime-retention.ts` sweeps (+20 SQL / +40 requests), task-pool work (+35 requests), and memory/session maintenance. Cold causal SQL is 545 → 551, requests 85 → 84, MAIN 58 → 62: schema/admission initialization shifts between the cold-turn and background buckets. Whole-workload counts for `assertOpenClawAgentSchemaContains` (30 → 30), integrity-before-mutation (25 → 25), migration column reads (9 → 9), and generation-tracker initialization (78 → 78) are unchanged; the same delivery command removal is present on the cold turn. These untouched cold/background operations are disclosed under ATTRIBUTION OVER RAW; the changed operation and every warmed shared family decrease or stay flat.

Pre-run load averages were approximately 115/126/126 (base) and 133/111/113 (candidate) on 32 CPUs. Both runs completed all 11 deliveries and left no fixture children. Latency is unmeasured: no quiet Testbox was granted immediately, and loaded local elapsed times are not latency evidence.

Channel/delivery T1 sites: **0 → 0**. No native SQLite path is added.

## Evidence

- Changed-file formatting, oxlint, and `git diff --check`.
- `pnpm test src/channels/turn/run-channel-turn.settlement.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 3/3 passed, including successful/throwing `onDelivered`, a pending sibling, durable state observed by the callback, and fresh-payload retry. Command wall time: 911.12s on the heavily loaded host, including a cold 373.061s compiled-worker prerequisite; Vitest itself took 403.02s. The new file was not present in the inspected CI shard logs, so its proof is this direct run.
- Multipart regression retains one custody admission and rejects a replaced writer before its next post.
- Codex autoreview: two rounds, scoped clean at P0–P2; no actionable findings. The second round reviewed the test-pool registration and return-style lint fix. Exact-head PR CI passes the changed channel and database-worker test lanes, type-aware lint, production/test types, source contracts, Knip, Madge, and T1/dialect ratchets. [CI run 38334153896](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38334153896) passed on `6f3a89e2cdba1568649665bda7dc5be9ae798bfb`; `openclaw/ci-gate` is green. The channel shard took 124 seconds.
- The initial CI found a test-pool registration defect, fixed by routing the new real-store regression through the existing forked database-worker pool. An earlier local run was stopped during cold startup; the subsequent direct run above completed all assertions.
- Diff: 9 files, +244 / −59 lines (production +70 / −38; tests/routing +167 / −18; docs +7 / −3); no dependency or generated-output changes.

After the Phase E hold was removed, merged `origin/main` (`4a4037bff64e29ad3c1994163ac8743f10dd154e`) without conflicts. The nine-file change is unchanged; integration head `337da3b7ef98eec0bedebcc1b422ba118d0baeda` passes [CI run 38349173977](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38349173977), including types, lint, source contracts, Knip, Madge, ratchets, and selected tests. Changed-file oxfmt/oxlint and diff whitespace checks also pass. The existing SQL pair is reused under COMPUTE CONSERVATION; no additional local suites or measurements ran.

Release-note context: reduce redundant database commands for channel reply delivery while preserving successful-delivery recovery when callbacks fail.
