prs.title: fix(ui): explain unresolved cloud startup turns while offline
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After a cloud startup failure, a chat that loses its Gateway connection no longer tells the user that the initial message is unresolved or what to do next. The composer band that said **"The initial message is unresolved. Reconnect if needed, then review it before sending another message."** disappeared, and nothing else carries that guidance while offline.

## Root cause

7661ce58751e (#170052, "keep cached transcripts steady on reload") removed the composer `disabledReason` fallback to the pending-send reason, so that connection recovery is explained on the busy Send button instead of a temporary notice above the composer. That is right while **connected**: `chatSubmitState` forces `canSend: false` during recovery, and Send's label carries "Finishing connection recovery…".

While **disconnected**, Send stays enabled so later turns can enter the outbox. `sendDisabledReason` is therefore null, and the unresolved-initial-turn reason (`chat.queue.initialTurnPending`, from `chatSendPendingReason`) rendered nowhere.

The cloud-startup-failure e2e caught it, but main-push CI skips UI e2e. The test was then retargeted three times while the regression stood:
- #170436 pointed it at the "1 in this conversation's outbox." band, which happened to occupy the slot.
- #170352 removed that outbox band as a duplicate of the per-row "Waiting for reconnect".
- #170477 then asserted the band is absent. It treated the expectation as the removed outbox band, but the original assertion was this unresolved-initial-turn guidance.

## Why This Change Was Made

Restore the band fallback for the disconnected state only: `(state.connected ? null : pendingReason)`. Offline, `chatSendPendingReason` cannot return the connection-recovery reason, because that requires `connected`. So the band appears only for an unresolved initial turn (`hasPendingInitialTurn` or a placement startup). Ordinary offline chats still show no band. Connection-recovery guidance stays on Send, as #170052 intended, and its unit test asserting no band while connected is unchanged. Placement busy and failed-unavailable messages keep precedence. Send eligibility and outbox admission are unchanged.

The e2e disconnect assertion returns to the unresolved-initial-message copy. A jsdom regression next to #170052's recovery test covers the offline band, so unit CI catches it without the PR-selected e2e shard. The offline docs gain one sentence. Production delta: +4 / −1.

## Before / after (synthetic mocked-Gateway fixture, disconnected after a failed cloud startup)

Before (main):

![before: no guidance above the composer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/101640e1-ff59-4a5b-b51d-a6eeb848850a)

After:

![after: unresolved initial message notice above the composer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f29966a6-a8f1-455d-b899-5a1ef5dd7daa)

## Evidence

Local Mac, native runner (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner <file> --maxWorkers=1`), one file at a time:

prs.title: fix(cli): strip bidirectional controls from the pending-pairing table
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A node sets its own `displayName` in the pairing request. `openclaw nodes status`
renders it verbatim in the pending-request table an operator reads to approve the
device (`renderPendingPairingRequestsTable`). `sanitizeTerminalText` escapes C0/C1
controls but passes bidirectional formatting controls through: overrides
(U+202A-202E), isolates (U+2066-2069), marks (U+200E/200F), and the Arabic letter
mark (U+061C) are category Cf. Those characters are invisible but reorder the
glyphs around them, so a device can name itself
`Owner` + U+2067 + U+202E + `enohPi s` + U+202C + `box` and render as
"Owner's iPhone" in the approval list (Trojan Source, CVE-2021-42574), letting an
attacker's device impersonate a trusted one.

## Why This Change Was Made

The pairing renderer now removes bidirectional controls from each displayed cell.
The fix is local to this approval surface rather than in shared
`sanitizeTerminalText`, because other consumers of that helper (for example codex
catalog previews, which have an explicit test for it) rely on formatting
characters passing through. Strong-directional letters are not controls, so a
right-to-left device name still renders its letters.

## User Impact

The pending-pairing table can no longer be reordered or spoofed by a crafted
device name. A bidirectional control in a displayed name, request id, or IP is
dropped; ordinary text, including right-to-left letters, is unchanged.

## Evidence

CLI call path -- the renderer is what `openclaw nodes list` prints, unchanged
(`src/cli/nodes-cli/register.status.ts`):

```
.command("list")                                         // line 536
  -> callNodesGatewayCli("node.pair.list", opts, {})     // line 544  (Gateway RPC)
  -> parsePairingList(result)                            // line 545
  -> renderPendingPairingRequestsTable({ pending, ... }) // line 583
  -> defaultRuntime.log(rendered.table)                  // line 591  (verbatim to terminal)
```

The Gateway `node.pair.list` handler returns the stored pending requests
(`listNodePairing`), including the device-supplied `displayName`, and the CLI
prints `rendered.table` verbatim. Nothing transforms the string between the
renderer and `defaultRuntime.log`, so the renderer output below is exactly the
terminal output for the pending rows the Gateway returns.

Captured from the real `renderPendingPairingRequestsTable`, the function the
`nodes list` pending table prints. A pending request whose `displayName` is
`Owner` + U+2067 + U+202E + `enohPi s` + U+202C + `box` produces the Node cell
(other columns trimmed):

Before (current `main`), the override reaches the terminal and the row reorders to
read "Owner's iPhone":

```
| req_88f1 | Owner<U+2067><U+202E>enohPi s<U+202C>box | 10.0.0.9 | 1m ago |
```
Bidirectional controls present in the rendered table: U+2067, U+202E, U+202C.

After this change:

```
| req_88f1 | OwnerenohPi sbox | 10.0.0.9 | 1m ago |
```
Bidirectional controls present in the rendered table: none.

New tests in `src/cli/nodes-cli/pairing-render.test.ts` assert this on the
production render path and confirm a right-to-left name such as `שלום Phone` still
renders its letters.

prs.title: fix(test): preserve terminal outcomes across runner entrypoints
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Runner preparation, report publication, and cleanup can lose the intended exit status or finish reporting before owned work has settled. Static imports can also load implementation dependencies before the entrypoint installs the loader they require.

## User Impact

Test commands preserve assertion failure (1), infrastructure failure (2), and native child outcomes through reporting and cleanup. Terminal results appear after owned work settles. Thin entrypoints install their loader before dynamically importing the execution owner, including the single-plugin and plugin-batch commands.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared runner outcome owner now carries the result through cleanup and report publication. Batch execution stays behind a thin public entrypoint, and package commands use that entrypoint instead of preloading an external loader. This integrates the original Runner repair with current main's consolidated tests and async callers; it does not restore retired fixtures or change product configuration.

## Evidence

Focused Linux proof on Node 24.19 and the pinned pnpm 12.9 toolchain: **136 selected cases passed**. No full platform campaign or hosted CI rerun was used.

| Proof | Result | Command wall time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Actual single-plugin preparation rejection | Original entry returned 1; corrected entry returns infrastructure 2 | Red 66.88s, green 19.67s |
| Runner outcomes, loader order, descendant settlement | 36 passed | 56.29s |
| Public-entry build admission, original selected order | 49 passed | 13.19s |
| Other changed deferred-admission tables | 5 passed | 12.05s |
| Report ownership and final-index publication | 32 passed, retaining 31 initial passes plus the corrected failed row | Initial 57.58s, one-row replay 9.30s |
| Real compiled-tooling route: help and installed tooling | 2 passed; help 0 and invalid native option 1 | 25.16s |
| Batch compiled-worker artifact lifetime | 2 passed | 11.64s |
| Windows CI plan and manifest parsing | 9 passed | 13.37s |

The single-plugin red case took 1.007s itself; the initial command included cold transform/preparation. Later compiled-route proof reused the successful native generation. The new regression exercises the real CLI with invalid batch-parallel input before worker admission.

Two integration fixture failures were diagnosed and fixed at their owners: deferred preparation fixtures had awaited the now-awaited public entry before releasing their gates (native no-output guard stopped that run at 133.98s), and the batch report fixture intercepted its own canonical re-export. The corrected fixtures keep the real public entry, explicit admission handshakes, joined cleanup, and existing assertions. Neither fix adds sleeps, retries, broader mocks, or longer timeouts.

Scoped static checks passed: scripts types (final 17.88s), tooling-test types (final 74.92s), scripts-test types (92.33s), changed-file type-aware lint (final affected files 15.16s and 25.76s), formatting (2.66s), and diff checks. The final review combines the clean integrated source review with independent reviews of the fixture corrections and mechanical lint changes.

Windows evidence covers plan/manifest behavior, not execution on Windows. macOS execution is unrun. Hosted CI costs will come from this pushed head's normal run.

### Hosted CI correction

The original head's seven failed jobs exposed remaining cutover gaps: the native PR wrapper inventory omitted the new outcome module; four fixtures still expected infrastructure exit 1; generic TSX fixtures replaced the Runner's new native bootstrap with raw TypeScript; and the terminal-outcome mock did not preserve real exports. This correction completes the inventory, updates only infrastructure expectations to exit 2, runs generic TSX fixtures through actual TSX wrappers, and preserves the worker owner's exports before overriding its lifecycle. Assertion exit 1, native exit 7, signal handling, and cleanup assertions remain intact.

Fresh source-mode proof uses the installed Vitest CLI and existing tooling configurations: eight real wrapper/loader/hydration/descendant fixtures plus two extracted-wrapper closure cases passed in 37.68 s; direct/delegated success and worker-preparation cases passed 4/4 in 5.51 s. The mock-export ratchet passed in 46.86 s, seven-file type-aware lint in 31.05 s, formatting in 0.21 s, and diff checks in 0.06 s. Independent review found no remaining issue in this eight-file correction.

The status-only rows use the exact hosted CI observations of exit 2 and the existing runtime proof; no fresh local replay is claimed for them. The initial combined replay had a cold worker-cache miss and reached the native no-output guard before assertions; its compiler and children were stopped and joined after 151.15 s. The supported standalone source route above avoids unrelated application compilation while retaining the actual wrappers under test. An initial mock-case name filter selected no tests; the corrected filter executed all four intended cases. The original run was still active at the final pre-publication read, with the same seven known failures and no additional failure class. No CI rerun or dispatch was requested.

### Conflict integration

Native merge admission identified a real package-script conflict with main `877301a3af040d90690018379958073b28777ef3`. The signed merge preserves that revision's replacement Mac/Windows skill-test lists and canonical PostgreSQL check target while removing the outer TSX preload from the same 17 Runner commands. The wrapper inventory retains main's additions and retirements plus the new outcome module. Runtime behavior is unchanged. Independent reviews of the exact resolution found no issue.

On the integrated source, all nine Windows placement/manifest cases passed in 29.18 s and both wrapper-closure cases passed in 69.75 s through the supported standalone source route. Scoped formatting passed in 0.64 s and diff checks in 2.54 s. Existing Runner and correction proof remains applicable. Root tooling dependencies are unchanged; the unrelated Clawrouter Solid dependency update is outside these validation contracts. This integration resolves the observed conflict; no CI rerun or redundant push was requested.

### Main asset repair integration

Hosted run [38338856704](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38338856704) tested `5d98c75` merged with main `f6c9a769`. Its build completed, but the generated-asset check found a stale Workboard manifest. Independent source attribution found the generator, browser inputs and committed output unchanged by Runner. Main fixed that output in [054c048](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/054c048df0f3b7dbf44aa929658a638bc5d9ba6f); this PR now integrates that exact fix in signed `75866e1`. The previous auto-merge intent was retired through native recovery before publication.

The only overlap was the wrapper inventory: both new main dependencies and the Runner outcome owner remain, each once. Every other Runner blob is unchanged. Both affected wrapper-closure cases pass in 27.67s using the supported standalone Vitest source route; staged diff-check passes in 0.05s. The formatter had no eligible targets for the inventory text and generated manifest. Earlier behavior and type/lint evidence remains valid.

That same prior run also failed `Gateway node exec approvals > relays exact policy snapshots and binds results to the current paired connection` before the Gateway listened. Runtime freshness reported an unnamed missing bundled-plugin dist entry, then native build admission refused a 3146MB heap against its 4352MB minimum. The other four shard cases passed. Bounded independent inspection found the QA startup, freshness, plugin-entry and build owners unchanged between tested main and this candidate; the retained log does not identify the missing entry or initial artifact inventory. No direct Runner cause or safe source correction was established. No fresh main reproduction, heap override, or full Gateway replay is claimed. The Workboard hash repair does not feed that entry predicate and is not claimed to fix this separate failure. Current-head native CI gates remain required.

### Main Cron expectation repair integration

Hosted run [38340001038](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38340001038) tested `75866e1` against main `6d1700c`. Its failed-write row in `run.cron-model-override-forwarding.test.ts` expected three pre-execution snapshots but received two. Main's earlier acknowledged-snapshot deduplication intentionally removes the duplicate continuation write. The owner and fixture were unchanged by Runner.

A fresh main checkout reproduced the exact original ordered false/true table: one pass and the same count failure in 84.12s. [The signed main fix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/2da68ad818adb033b39f57c2e7e4096d045a6feb) changes only that stale count to two; both rows then pass in 38.13s. Successful completion, exactly one base snapshot, model/provider/harness/systemSent fields, and the failed-write warning remain asserted. One-file type-aware lint passed in 33.19s, formatting in 0.11s, and diff-check passed. Two independent source reviews were clean.

Signed integration `2a63d2f` includes that exact main fix. Its 197 incoming paths do not overlap the 34 Runner paths; every Runner blob, root dependency input, and tooling configuration remains unchanged. The merged tree and corrected Cron blob were independently verified, with no extra resolution changes. Existing Runner proof remains valid. This is the required fresh push after an owning main fix, without a CI rerun or synthetic commit. The separate QA missing-entry uncertainty above remains unresolved; no claim is made that the Cron fix repairs it.

### Main Telegram fixture preparation repair integration

Hosted run [38341181522](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38341181522) tested `2a63d2f` with main `0e0e87d`. Its Telegram coalescing group passed the first album case, then timed out in the slowly adopting album case and cascaded into later teardown failures before the job was cancelled. The fixture and ingress owners were unchanged by Runner.

A fresh main checkout reproduced the original first-two-case order without changing timeouts or assertions: the first passed, the second hit its 120s limit, and dispatch reported that runtime config was not prepared (240.41s command wall). Main's prepared-config migration had updated sibling fixtures but omitted this one. [The signed owning fix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/989e66ac6a35401601d7e883ea7fe84790b241f3) publishes the existing per-case config before bot/monitor creation and clears it only after monitor, accepted-turn, and database settlement. Production behavior, fake timers, FIFO assertions, and cleanup joins are unchanged.

The identical original-order selection then passed 2/2 in 68.35s (20.640s and 10.690s), without the config error, an unhandled rejection, forced termination, or remaining owned children. Explicit one-file type-aware lint using the existing source config passed in 52.49s; formatting and diff checks passed in 0.12s and 0.04s. Root and independent source reviews were clean. This proves the reproduced two-case failure is repaired; later failures in the contaminated hosted sequence were not independently replayed, and the re-stringified dispatch error does not preserve the original nested reader frame.

This signed integration includes published main `76492ab3b83fd4215c8f500e6586b4a12a83647a`. Its 461 incoming paths do not overlap the 34 Runner paths; every Runner blob is unchanged. The exact composed tree, corrected fixture, unchanged root dependency inputs, and behavior-preserving upstream Vitest alias extraction were independently reviewed. Existing Runner proof remains valid. This is the required genuine fresh push after the owning main fix, with no CI rerun or dispatch. The separate QA missing-entry uncertainty above remains unchanged.


### Workboard generated-asset baseline integration

Integrated the owning main fix [faa8ad8](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/faa8ad8e59833d23d606dbc3b73a7258265f094a), landed in [7b7f9ab](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/7b7f9ab9802d69db85ad1403b6c75cb1164aa080). Main had changed 19 reachable Workboard browser files while retaining the previous generated asset paths. The canonical Workboard-only declared build hook regenerated only the two manifest entry/style hashes (07c5fd43 → 9c706f93); the hook passed in 3.02 s, then produced byte-identical manifest and all five emitted files in 2.36 s. Filtered `--check` is unsupported and was not used as proof; the formatter excludes this manifest. Diff check passed. Independent generated-output and final composition reviews found no issues. All 34 Runner blobs remain unchanged; the 127 incoming paths are disjoint, with root dependency and test configuration inputs unchanged.

The old run also repeated the previously investigated Gateway node-exec approvals startup failure: [job 115132368253](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38347442643/job/115132368253). An unnamed missing bundled-plugin dist entry triggered a build, then the native heap guard refused 3121 MB against its 4352 MB minimum before removing output. The case took 127.970 s (181.18 s file wrapper); the other four shard groups passed. The log still does not name the missing entry or capture its inventory. Prior bounded source attribution found no direct Runner cause, but this is not a reproduced main failure or a proven unrelated failure. The manifest fix is not claimed to fix that runtime-entry predicate. No heap override, full-build replay, CI rerun, or repeated artifact search was used. Native required gates remain authoritative.


Baseline follow-up on clean main 7b7f9ab used the same Node 24.19.0, pnpm 12.9, canonical private-QA runtime build and first-file CI shard owner. The JS-only build passed in 149.12 s; the exact original test then failed naturally in 301.27 s with a 180 s case timeout and a child-stdio closure error. It did not emit the hosted missing-entry/heap cause. The local host had more available memory; no heap override or artificial artifact removal was used. Source remained clean, the owned process group and known task child identities were absent afterward, and no unchanged replay followed. This is a bounded failed main attempt, not proof that the hosted failure is inherited or that its cause is fixed.

prs.title: feat(database): add verified offline port foundations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Establishes the internal, verified copy path needed to port workboard data between SQLite and PostgreSQL without changing canonical cell bytes.

Related: #170266 and #170059. Implements P3-6a of the [offline port design](#design-contract).

## User Impact

No user-visible command, engine switch, updater change, release, or publication capability is enabled. SQLite remains the default. Shared-state and agent-store porting remain gated on their owner migrations and descriptors.

## Why This Change Was Made

The port foundations use the coordinator-approved 669 net nonblank handwritten production lines, excluding generated metadata and tests. The narrow ratchet classification is a separately authorized follow-up. Generated workboard descriptors reuse the existing schema catalog and point to pre-data/post-data slices of the existing PostgreSQL SQL artifact, without a second DDL copy. The internal materializer uses keyset reads, bounded batches, one writer, and two-buffer backpressure. It preserves bigint and BLOB values, refuses actual NUL/invalid UTF-8, verifies ordered typed-cell SHA-256/counts and allocation facts, and checks owner-derived values plus PostgreSQL catalog definitions. The format-2 export envelope matches a SQLite image with its PostgreSQL anchor and distinguishes exact recovery from sanitized user backups; format-1 reads remain unchanged.

### Design contract

The accepted offline-port design requires a migrated private source, exclusive caller custody, unpublished destinations, exact canonical text, owner-owned derivations, and verification before publication. This PR supplies those copy/envelope foundations only. Later changes own captures, migration orchestration, sanitization, interrupted-publication recovery, configuration changes, and CLI enablement. Enabling porting requires a published PostgreSQL-aware backup/updater generation; this PR does not establish that release gate.

## Evidence

Reviewed runtime candidate: `243996c0f1b7f3bc580638d3154ffde367045958`. Workboard SQLite → PostgreSQL → SQLite passed locally against a throwaway Homebrew PostgreSQL 17 cluster: 1,011 rows, under 8 MiB, 26.074 s test time / 104.34 s runner wall time. The cluster on port 55443 was stopped and removed. Proof covers exact canonical cells, IDs/cursors, deleted allocation watermarks and int64 exhaustion, owner derivation, NUL/invalid UTF-8 refusal, unchanged source data, normal engine admission, and fresh reverse-copy clients. Port code is unchanged in the final ratchet-only follow-up.

All 17 helper/STRICT tests, 16 generator tests, 11 envelope tests, the Git-codec preservation regression, and the required wrapper-inventory test passed. All 10 dialect-ratchet tests passed (5.614 s test bodies / 52.64 s wrapper), including owner maintenance growth, matching consumer rejection, owner output, and retained mechanical/design enforcement. Formatting, targeted core/script lint, core typecheck, madge, generated-schema freshness, and `git diff --check` pass. Two original Codex review rounds fixed the fresh-client search-path issue and verified C-collated ordering; a fresh follow-up review found no actionable P0–P2 findings.

The follow-up removes all nine raw dialect sites from the offline port worker: admitted schema facts own catalog emptiness, `assertSqliteIntegrity` owns integrity/FK checks, and the existing `sqlite-strict.ts` owner supplies allocation reads/restoration and a synchronous FK staging scope. STRICT migration code and statements remain byte-identical. The FK helper restores both prior ON and prior OFF settings, refuses active transactions, and rejects Promise results. SQLite handles use native `readBigInts: true` so unchanged allocation helpers preserve int64 results.

Coordinator-approved rationale: "the FK-disable staging helper (`withSqliteForeignKeysDisabled`: read, disable, restore-previous) consolidated in the existing SQLite primitive owner; it replaces 9 raw sites the port would otherwise add in new files." The three added literals are the disable statement and both restore branches; reading reuses the existing owner function. The authorized `SQLITE_PRIMITIVE_OWNERS` list contains only `src/infra/sqlite-strict.ts`. Its engine-maintenance matches remain in inventory/output with `(owner)` and are excluded from shrink comparison. Mechanical/design growth in that file and all groups in non-owner files remain fully ratcheted. No baseline is introduced. This extends #168382 and documents the owner contract. Locally the ratchet is clean: non-owner engine-maintenance counts remain 8 → 8, with 17 owner matches displayed.

Tooling evidence: an optional broader wrapper lease/template smoke child hit its existing 30 s timeout; the required inventory test passed. A cold Git-codec worker compile was killed with exit 137 before tests ran; its isolated retry compiled and passed the preservation test in 10.957 s. The optional full-tree worker inventory scan was stopped after remaining silent; the combined CI ratchet job supplies that broad gate.

PostgreSQL CI passed for the owner refactor at `92424ba70dc2f17afc31805c37d67e845e9f60cb` ([job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38341258519/job/115112946557)): 5 min 15 s full job. Its combined ratchet job identified a missing assertion invariant comment in the escaped-text decoder. The final comment-only fix documents the existing projection guarantee; the full assertion-safety ratchet, dialect ratchet, targeted lint/format, diff check, and comment-only autoreview pass. Final-head [PostgreSQL conformance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38342508108/job/115116772513) passed: 3.504 s for the requested round trip and 6 min 8 s for the complete job. Final-head [combined baseline ratchets](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38342508108/job/115116772110) passed in 6 min 48 s, including assertion safety, database-worker and database-dialect guards.

### Landing audit repair

Current head: `230da464c26d9680ed49a88e5729391c79a22ccc`. The one landing fix declares the intentionally staged port/envelope entrypoints in Knip, gives the offline canonical copy primitive a narrowly named raw-SQLite audit entry, and removes three unconsumed exports. The audit entries expire with the first production orchestration callers. Runtime behavior and generated artifacts are unchanged. Targeted core/script lint, formatting, and fresh Codex review pass; no broad local suite was rerun.

Initial exact-head CI run [38342508108](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38342508108) failed as follows. These results are retained as failures, not represented as green.

| Job | Classification and evidence | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| check-additional-runtime-topology-architecture | PR-caused: the new port worker needs the raw SQLite primitive declaration. | Fixed in `230da464c26d9`. |

prs.title: test(agents): keep one runtime config owner per embedded-runner fixture
prs.body:
Related: #170447, #170433, #169714

## What Problem This Solves

Three embedded-agent test fixtures publish the runtime config snapshot twice because #170447 and #170433 repaired the same #169714 fallout independently and both landed.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Each fixture has one clear config owner again, so a later edit to either publish is not silently masked by the other.

## Why This Change Was Made

#170447's run-level setup is kept as the single owner because it follows each run's authored config. The redundant `beforeEach` publishes from #170433 are removed:

- `lane-controller.attempt-controls.test.ts`: `createRunController` keeps `setRuntimeConfigSnapshot(params.config ?? {})`. The file-level `beforeEach` publish is removed and the single `clearRuntimeConfigSnapshot()` in `afterEach` stays.
- `lane-controller.test.ts`: `createLaneController` keeps `setRuntimeConfigSnapshot(runParams.config ?? {})`. The describe-level `beforeEach` publish is removed and the `afterEach` clear stays.
- `settled-turn-finalization.unavailable.test.ts`: `config: {}` in the run params stays. The `beforeEach` publish is removed. Nothing publishes a snapshot in this file any more, so its `clearRuntimeConfigSnapshot()` and the import were dead and are removed too.

All three files are now byte-identical to #170447's post-images. Assertions, timeouts and cases are unchanged. Three test files, no production change.

## Evidence

Local, `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` on the final content:

| File | Result | Vitest duration | Wall |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lane-controller.attempt-controls.test.ts` | 18/18 passed | 67.67 s | 86.5 s |
| `lane-controller.test.ts` | 6/6 passed | 56.41 s | 70.1 s |
| `settled-turn-finalization.unavailable.test.ts` | 1/1 passed | 83.19 s | 107.6 s |

Durations are mostly cold transform on a busy shared host (transform 75–85 %). The test bodies themselves are a few seconds each. Before #169714 was repaired, these cases timed out after about 120 s each without a published snapshot, so passing here means the run-level owner is doing the work.

For settled-turn, the task was to prove whether `config: {}` alone is enough:

- **Negative control:** without both `config: {}` and the snapshot publish, the case fails with `expected undefined to be true` on `result.attempt.assistantTranscriptOwned`. This is the original #170447 symptom.
- **`config: {}` alone:** with no snapshot publish, the case passes.
- **Teardown probe:** a temporary probe showed `getRuntimeConfigSnapshot()` is `null` at teardown, so the removed clear had nothing to clear.

Scoped `oxfmt --check`, plain `oxlint` and `git diff --check` pass on all three files. The repo's type-aware lint wrapper didn't run locally: its plugin-sdk boundary `.d.ts` preparation timed out at 300 s on a heavily loaded shared host. That is a tooling timeout, not a lint finding, and PR CI runs the type-aware lane. Independent Codex autoreview (P0–P2) is scoped-clean with no findings.

## What Problem This Solves

Windows Startup-folder inspection reports inaccessible launchers as missing, allowing installation to proceed without establishing whether an existing login item is present.

## User Impact

- Original regressions: EACCES, EPERM, and EIO became `not-loaded` through the actual public service owner; the denied-install case completed instead of rejecting. Missing-file and successful-alternate controls passed.

prs.title: fix(gateway): accept configured ACP store owners for non-ACP agent keys in sessions.search
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `sessions_search` tool groups visible session candidates by agent and calls `sessions.search` with an explicit `agentId` plus the group's session keys. For a configured ACP store owner (an id in `acp.allowedAgents` absent from `agents.entries`), `resolveSessionSearchScope` only bypassed native-agent validation for keys shaped `agent:<owner>:acp:*`. Any other key owned by that agent — say the plain `agent:<owner>:existing` — failed the `isAcpSessionKey` gate, fell through to `resolveRequestedSessionAgentId`, and was rejected with `Unknown agent id "<owner>"`. Every candidate group containing such a key returned `INVALID_REQUEST`, so `sessions_search` broke for agents whose stores held non-ACP-shaped keys.

The fix resolves the store owner for every canonical agent key, not just ACP-shaped ones, and admits the key when all of these hold:

- the owner matches the requested `agentId`,
- the key is not the agent's main-session alias (`agent:<owner>:main`), whose stored form can collapse to the shared global scope under a fixed session store,
- the resolved stored key is neither `global` nor `unknown`,
- and the key carries no persisted store owner.

Everything else keeps the original path: legacy and malformed keys skip owner resolution and are handled by `resolveRequestedSessionAgentId` as before, and cross-owner keys still return `INVALID_REQUEST`.

## Evidence

- New regression test: `sessions.search accepts an ACP allowlist owner for non-ACP agent keys` — an owned non-ACP key searches successfully; a cross-owner key returns `INVALID_REQUEST`.
- New negative cases: `agent:<owner>:main` under a fixed shared store, unqualified legacy keys, and malformed keys all keep returning `INVALID_REQUEST`.
- `pnpm exec vitest run src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-read.test.ts -t "ACP allowlist owner"` → 3 passed.
- `sessions-read-scope`, `sessions-search-tool.matching`, and `audit-cross-agent-session-access` suites → 39 passed across 3 files.
- **Standalone gateway process run (no test harness)**: started the real entry point (`openclaw.mjs gateway`, port 18991, loopback-only) against a dedicated state dir, with the same real config file (`agents.entries={main}`, `acp.allowedAgents=["codex"]`, `gateway.auth.mode=none`) loaded from disk, then connected with an independent Ed25519 device-signed WebSocket client and called `sessions.search`:

  ```
  connect: {"ok":true}
  sessions.search (owned non-ACP key agent:codex:existing): {"ok":true,"payload":{"results":[{"sessionKey":"agent:codex:existing","sessionId":"session-real-run-non-acp","snippet":"real run proof needle for ordinary key","score":0.000004}]}}
  sessions.search (cross-owner key agent:claude:existing): {"ok":true,"payload":{"results":[]}}
  ```

- Real configured-setup run (new test `sessions.search real WS run: configured ACP store owner with a non-ACP-shaped key` in `server.sessions.store-rpc.test.ts`): the test writes a real config file (`agents.entries = {main}`, `acp.allowedAgents = ["codex"]`, no test overrides), seeds an allowlisted owner with a non-ACP-shaped key, starts the live gateway WebSocket, and calls `sessions.search` over it. Config is loaded from disk, not from test overrides:

  ```
  [real-run] owned non-ACP key: {"type":"res","ok":true,"payload":{"results":[{"sessionKey":"agent:codex:existing","sessionId":"session-real-run-non-acp","snippet":"real run proof needle for ordinary key","score":0.000004}]}}
  [real-run] cross-owner rejection: {"type":"res","ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Unknown agent id \"codex\""}}

  Test Files  1 passed (1)
  ```

Fixes #164847

prs.title: fix: trigger model fallback for provider-wrapped errors
prs.body:
Fixes #170388

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes configured model fallback being skipped when an error payload contains only a provider-wrapped HTTP status, such as `Google Generative AI API error (503): The service is currently unavailable. [code=UNAVAILABLE]`.

## User Impact

Text-only transient provider failures can advance to the configured alternate model instead of ending without a fallback classification. This addresses serialized error payloads; it does not claim to fix all Gemini outages or establish the cause of the reported fourteen-minute delay.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared failover classifier accepted a finite numeric status or a leading HTTP token, but did not use the existing anchored provider-envelope parser. Reuse that parser after leading-status extraction, preserve explicit numeric precedence and existing semantic exceptions, and continue rejecting arbitrary parenthesized numbers and quoted envelopes in unrelated text.

Original fix by @TUARAN; maintainer cleanup moves the regression into the existing configured-fallback harness and documents the recovery behavior. No configuration, protocol, storage, or migration changes.

## Evidence

- Source/history confirmation: current main still uses leading-status-only inference. The shared anchored parser already exists and is used by retry classification. Serialized error payloads reach this classifier without structured status; unclassified nonempty errors otherwise return no fallback request.
- Regression: `advances to the configured fallback after a status-less serialized Google 503 error` feeds the exact raw text through real result classification and `runWithModelFallback`, then checks the configured alternate and visible `fallback ok` reply. It adds one case to an existing harness with no timers, process boots, or new mocks.
- Classifier regressions: `classifies only guarded provider-wrapped statuses: $signal` covers wrapped 503/429, conflicting explicit numeric status, ordinary parenthesized numbers, and a quoted envelope inside unrelated text.
- Changed-file `oxfmt --check` passed. Static `oxlint` with the core tsconfig passed using the repository rules with only the unrelated UI-only Solid plugin override omitted because the borrowed dependency installation lacks that plugin. No core/test rules were removed.
- Autoreview: precommit and final branch reviews both returned `scoped-clean` with no accepted/actionable P0–P2 findings; final verdict `patch is correct`. No project code or tests were executed by the reviewers.
- PR CI is the test/typecheck gate. On head `1f8a141e8bb3eaf2bb56faca07b072aecfc0ca56`, [run 38345714573](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38345714573) passed every Node test shard, production types, lint, docs, and guards. The new fallback case passed in 138 ms; each of the five classifier guard cases passed in 1 ms. Its only substantive failure was `check-test-types-core-4`: TS2724 in unrelated `src/commands/config-preflight-snapshot.test.ts`, which imported a helper made private on main. Main repair `72ccf43fdc6fb` (#170619) is included in head `6be7d064c1d818144670ee3e6fe7f162afc4d324`; [exact-head CI run 38346677814](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38346677814) passed: 46 jobs successful, 28 workflow-selected skips, zero failures, including all Node tests, production/test types, lint, docs, guards, and the aggregate CI gate. The latest scheduled main run (38343322520) did not show this same failure, so this is not recorded as a scheduled-CI inherited failure. The PR-owned four-file contents remain identical to the reviewed candidate.
- Live Gateway proof, leases, local tests/typechecks, and production-reverted negative controls were intentionally skipped per maintainer policy (2026-10-13: “relax testing and trust PR CI, just lint”). Local test wall time is not measured; the CI case timings are recorded above.

ClawSweeper's latest review identified no code findings. Its remaining live-proof request is superseded by the maintainer proof policy above. The previous native Google loopback scenario did not isolate the changed status-less branch and is not claimed as proof here. The human question about that distinction is addressed by the exact serialized-result regression.

Scope versus main: production +3/-1 (net +2), tests +45/-0, docs +2/-0. The small positive production delta composes the existing parser without introducing duplicate parsing or removing unrelated code to meet a line-count target.

prs.title: fix(state): invalidate agent database leases across reboots via boot id
prs.body:
## Summary

Agent-database lease staleness detection fails closed on hardened Linux hosts after a reboot. This PR records the kernel boot ID (`/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id`) with each `agent_database_leases` row and treats a lease recorded under a different boot as stale before any PID probe.

## What Problem This Solves

Reproduced on an Android device running the Gateway inside a chroot (`/proc` mounted `hidepid=invisible`, SELinux denying `signull` to foreign domains). The same shape applies to containers and to systemd units with `ProtectProc=`.

`agentDatabaseLeaseStaleReason()` (formerly `isAgentDatabaseLeaseStale`) in `src/state/openclaw-agent-db-lease.ts` only considers a lease stale when:

1. `isPidDefinitelyDead(pid)` — i.e. `kill(pid, 0)` fails with **ESRCH**, or
2. the recorded `owner_start_time` differs from `getFileLockProcessStartTime(pid)`.

On these hosts, for any PID that is not ours:

- `kill(pid, 0)` fails with **EPERM**, not ESRCH → "exists" (correctly, for a live process).
- `/proc/<pid>/stat` is **ENOENT** → start time is `null` → the start-time comparison is skipped.

After a reboot, the old Gateway's PID is routinely reused by an early system process. The lease then looks alive forever, every open of the agent database sees a "live" foreign lease, and the Gateway refuses to start (`Agent main database is still open in process <pid>`). `openclaw doctor --fix` hits the same check and cannot drain it either, so there is no in-product recovery short of hand-editing the state database.

## User Impact

Gateways on hardened Linux hosts (Android/chroot with hidepid, containers, systemd ProtectProc=) can fail to start after any unclean reboot with "Agent main database is still open in process <pid>", and openclaw doctor --fix cannot recover it. With this change the stale lease is recognised and drained automatically; hosts where the boot ID is unavailable see no behaviour change.

## Why This Change Was Made

PID liveness cannot be decided from inside a process that is not allowed to probe foreign PIDs. The kernel boot ID is world-readable on exactly those hosts and is the simplest unambiguous signal that a lease owner cannot possibly be running any more.

## Fix

- **`src/shared/boot-id.ts`** (new): `readBootId()` — Linux reads and validates `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id`; other platforms return `null`. Only a successful read is cached (same policy as `selfStartTime` in `pid-alive.ts`). `boot_id` is world-readable under `hidepid`, `ProtectProc=`, and typical Android/SELinux policy because it is not under `/proc/<pid>/`.
- **Schema**: `agent_database_leases.owner_boot_id TEXT` added to `openclaw-state-schema.sql` and registered as a first-use additive column (`openclaw-state-db-additive-columns.ts`), following the `device_bootstrap_tokens.setup_id` precedent. `ensureAgentDatabaseLeaseSchema()` adds the column on the first lease write; read-only observers and existing-schema maintenance keep working on databases that predate it (`readAgentDatabaseLease(s)` select the column only when present and project `null` otherwise).
- **Existing-schema maintenance**: `runExistingOpenClawStateWriteTransaction` gains an optional `schemaCompatibility` on its contract; `withExistingAgentLeaseWrite` allows `agent_database_leases.owner_boot_id` to be missing so Doctor can drain leases in a database this release has not written yet.
- **Claims** write `owner_boot_id: readBootId()` (the claim always runs in the owning process).
- **Staleness**: new first check — if the row's `owner_boot_id` and the current boot ID are both known and differ → `"owner-boot-id-changed"`. Otherwise behaviour is unchanged (null on either side, or same boot, fall through to the existing PID / start-time checks). The stale-lease log line includes `ownerBootId`.
- `agentDatabaseLeaseStaleReason` and the lease row readers moved to a sibling module `openclaw-agent-db-lease-rows.ts` to stay under the 700-line cap ratchet.

## Evidence

- `src/shared/boot-id.test.ts`: trimmed/lowercased read, success-only caching, retry after unreadable, malformed contents, non-Linux → `null`.
- `src/state/openclaw-agent-db-lease.boot-id.test.ts`: simulates the hardened host by mocking `process.kill` → EPERM and `fs.readFileSync('/proc/<pid>/…')` → ENOENT for a live foreign PID (`process.ppid`), with `owner_start_time = NULL` (platform independent):
  - boot ID recorded on claim; `null` when unavailable;
  - different boot ID → stale for read-only observation, next claim, and `assertNoOpenClawAgentDatabaseLeases` drain — without any PID probe;
  - same boot ID → lease kept (PID probe still runs, EPERM still means "exists");
  - recorded or current boot ID `null` (both combinations) → unchanged behaviour (kept);
  - a table that predates the column is read without migration and gains the column on the next lease write.
- `src/state/openclaw-state-lease-existing.test.ts`: existing-schema maintenance drains a dead lease from a v15 database whose lease table lacks `owner_boot_id`, without changing the schema.
- `src/infra/update-candidate-state.test.ts`: fixture insert now names columns (it used positional `VALUES`).

- `src/commands/doctor-maintenance.settlement.refusals.test.ts`: typed lease fixture gains `owner_boot_id: null`.

Verification (Linux, Node 24): `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` pass; `pnpm check` passes except the line-cap ratchet, which is why the row helpers were extracted (ratchet now OK); oxlint reports no findings in changed files (the remaining `max-lines` errors in `extensions/voice-call/src/runtime.test.ts` and `src/plugins/doctor-contract-registry.ts` are pre-existing on `main`). prs.title: fix(codex): prevent bounded turns from timing out on slow model lookup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a bounded Codex side turn can fail before it starts when a live `model/list` reply takes more than five seconds, even when the configured app-server request budget and remaining turn budget are longer.

## User Impact

Side questions and settled-turn finalizers that need a live model list can proceed when the lookup completes within the configured request budget. A stalled lookup may now wait longer than five seconds, but it remains bounded by both `appServer.requestTimeoutMs` and the remaining turn budget. No configuration or data migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bounded-turn model lookup had a fixed five-second ceiling. It now uses the smaller of the remaining turn budget and the configured app-server request timeout, matching the caller's intended deadlines. The documentation describes that behavior.

## Evidence

- A direct request to a real Codex app-server was observed to take 5.006 seconds for `model/list` after client acquisition, exceeding the previous five-second ceiling. This observation establishes that the lookup can take longer than the old cap; it is not an end-to-end bounded-turn success claim.
- Regression using a real `CodexAppServerClient` transport with controlled response timing: on the unchanged base, a six-second catalog response failed with `model/list timed out` despite an eight-second configured request budget. With this change, the six-second response succeeds and starts the turn, while a nine-second response still times out before `turn/start`.
- `pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/bounded-turn.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 44/44 passed, 20.27 seconds local wall time. The adjacent bounded-turn clock suite also passed: 47/47 tests across the two files in 21.91 seconds.
- Formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Local scoped autoreview found no actionable findings.

The full changed-lane check did not finish: its extension-test typecheck was interrupted during heavy host contention. CI has not been awaited. A separate live foreground-agent path still showed app-server request timeouts after an integration build containing this change, so this PR does **not** claim to fix those broader fresh-session failures.

prs.title: refactor(ui): port shared pickers, dialogs, and toast to Solid 2
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Moves the shared pickers, confirmation/input dialogs, and toast renderer to Solid 2 while keeping their existing public APIs and host elements usable by the remaining Lit callers.

## User Impact

Model, agent, language, appearance, and emoji selection keep their existing behavior. Confirmations and prompts preserve cancellation, validation, focus return, and pending-submit behavior. Toasts preserve FIFO delivery, paused timeouts, modal placement, and dismissal reasons.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each registered tag has one Solid implementation behind the existing bridge. The shared Zag menu adapter owns picker navigation, and the native overlay lifecycle owns opening, closing, and focus. Select and multi-select share the adapter’s listbox support. `MenuItem.attributes` preserves existing selectors, and `Menu.onAfterShow` exposes the existing lifecycle event. Domain state and the toast service remain synchronous TypeScript owners. Agent registration and the toast view retain their lazy boundaries.

The full settings flow exposed a stylesheet-order regression that isolated picker fixtures did not: a late shared overlay rule could shrink a low-positioned menu to only its search field. The picker now retains its height budget regardless of stylesheet order, with a browser regression covering a real clickable option.

The full mobile Settings flow also exposed an older drawer document listener intercepting focused-control Escape. The drawer now defers focused-control Escape to the shared menu and overlay owners, while excluding its own dialog role from the nested-modal guard. The focused-control popover case passes in Chromium and WebKit; the full mobile Settings flow passes.

Provider icons exposed a nested Solid lifecycle defect: a top-level render inside a retained Lit region could run the parent settled callback before its sibling refs existed. The existing interop owner now uses an owned root and insertion for that nested path, as the bridge already does. The regression fails on the untouched base and passes after the change; all three model-picker suites pass in Chromium and WebKit.

The review also caught long agent menus focusing a row without revealing it. The picker now reveals the menu owner’s actual focus target after entry animation completion, including the first enabled row when the stored selection is disabled. Both cases have real-browser regressions; navigation and dismissal remain owned by the shared menu.

Successive notices also keep reaching the toast host after it moves into a shadow-root dialog. The regression extends the former single-notice fixture and remains necessary after main’s toast-test cleanup; the other cleanup deletions are preserved. The service reads the existing modal-layer registry when the document query cannot reach the host; the regression fails before this correction and passes afterward.

Full CI exposed consumers that still assumed Web Awesome shadow DOM or synchronous Lit updates. Coupled tests now drive the native surfaces and wait for observable readiness. Type-only leaf contracts remove facade cycles. The toast service has no runtime renderer imports; its separate synchronous host registration is imported at each live host producer, while the view remains lazy.

Keyboard reopening also exposed Zag’s queued first-item action overriding the selected agent. The shared adapter now respects its own enabled initial-focus item during opening, leaving Home and navigation with Zag. Agent opening passes 12 cases in each browser, and the real composer focus flow passes both cases. The agent trigger wrapper uses `display: contents` to preserve the command palette’s existing grid; desktop/mobile geometry tests pass on both base and head, with supplemental screenshots below.

Two mixed-framework event boundaries are also preserved. The menu invokes its existing overlay Escape owner from Solid’s delegated handler, after child controls and before Web Awesome’s older document listener can dismiss a containing settings popover. The sidebar focus trap resolves its own panel because Solid’s delegated event retains an inner `currentTarget`. The canonical closed-picker Tab regression fails before that correction; all 14 Chromium filter cases pass afterward.

The session controls now consume native menu show/hide callbacks, preserving identity loading for all open menu agents and only the selected agent after closing. The owning palette-draft regression exercises real trigger clicks and was proven red before the callback cutover.

Main integration through `e78a253059eb` retains the new Solid shell and transfers toast registration to its two actual host producers. The Lit-to-Solid content mount preserves main’s restored-owner fallback and uses an owned nested root to avoid settling parent refs prematurely. Both lifecycle regressions remain covered.

## Evidence

Local proof targets individual files with `--maxWorkers=1`. The `ci:full` label requests every UI shard for this shared-component change. Testbox was attempted once; its queued lease was stopped and proof continued locally under the migration work order.

Fresh baseline replay matches both grouped-picker failures by name (`fits grouped decisions and supports native header keyboard controls at 390 pixels` and `... at 1280 pixels`): final Tab leaves focus on `body` instead of the following field. No assertion or production navigation policy is weakened.

The shared menu-navigation replay also matches its three baseline WebKit failures by name: `opens at the last enabled item with ArrowUp and exits with native Tab`, `skips ineligible controls while preserving editing and native Tab exit`, and `keeps Tab in the current menu when a descendant menu has visible controls`. Its other 11 cases pass. After the prerequisite’s `0cd77115` focus repair, fresh candidate and baseline menu-navigation runs still match those three names (11 pass / 3 fail each); the baseline contains the exact upstream menu implementation. Baseline `05630639` has identical relevant picker/menu source, styles, tests, and dependency manifests to prerequisite head `728b0a5c`. The completed `ci:full` run [`38340211002`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38340211002), head `f87ae502`, passes all three UI shards, all nine mocked E2E shards, real-Gateway shard 2, all type and lint checks, security, ratchets, and performance. The later exact-head run [`38344045994`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38344045994) on `a2a69a31` passes all 14 UI jobs, including the collaborator-scroll case (34.294s). Its only failure is `check-test-types-core-4`: `config-preflight-snapshot.test.ts` imports `readConfigPreflightSnapshot` after main made it private. Both affected source and test blobs exactly match CI's synthetic-merge base `33a438a7`; this lane changes neither. Main repair `72ccf43fdc6f` / #170619 is included in the latest integration. Run wall time was 934s; the 14 UI jobs used 7,288 job-seconds. The earlier scroll failure remains an observed, unreproduced failure; diagnostic instrumentation is not claimed as a fix.

A sixth local WebKit failure, `Solid native popover > vetoes open and light dismissal without losing its input or outside focus`, also reproduces on the final baseline: outside-click focus stays on `body` instead of the button (3 pass / 1 fail on both sides). No navigation assertion was weakened.

The sidebar WebKit replay has four additional inherited failures: its desktop LTR and phone LTR/RTL keyboard flows Tab from Archived to `body` instead of Show automation sessions, and its phone-sheet Tab case lands on `body` instead of Sort. All four same named assertions reproduce on `2f328736`, including the new Group-to-Sort check copied unchanged into the original Lit test. Candidate: 10 pass / 4 fail (276.94s); targeted baseline: four same failures (284.39s). Test/config files were restored byte-identically. Chromium’s new focus-owner regression is demonstrated red→green; all14 cases pass.

Touched production LOC against the final main base: **13,587 → 14,026 (+439)**. Tests/support: 38,618 → 38,886; UI config: 468 → 477; four obsolete assertion-baseline rows removed. The coupled backend filesystem fixture removes another 27 net test lines (4 added, 31 deleted). The larger test inventory includes coupled consumers updated after full CI. Growth is concentrated in the shared menu adapter’s listbox support, typed custom-element bridges, and retained adapters for Lit callers. Ten inspected, synthetic before/after screenshot pairs cover the overview, shared select, model, agent, multi-select, language, appearance/emoji, confirmation/input dialogs, and toast.

prs.body:
Closes #163782

## What problem this solves

OpenClaw's Slack message tool cannot create a project channel, forcing operators to leave the workflow or use a separate integration.

## User impact

An operator can explicitly enable Slack channel creation with `channels.slack.actions.channels: true` (or the selected account's equivalent). The action creates a public channel in the trusted workspace, invites the trusted requester when Slack permits, and returns a reusable workspace-qualified target.

## Design and security boundary

Channel creation is **disabled by default** and is no longer part of the ordinary `messages` action gate. This makes workspace administration an explicit operator choice while preserving existing message permissions.

The generated Slack manifest requests bot-compatible `channels:manage` for creation and `channels:write.invites` for requester invitation. Existing Slack apps must be reauthorized after adopting these scopes.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test extensions/slack/src/channel-create.test.ts extensions/slack/src/action-runtime.test.ts extensions/slack/src/message-tools.test.ts extensions/slack/src/setup-surface.test.ts extensions/slack/src/channel-actions-setup-status.contract.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 5 files, 108 tests passed.
- `pnpm docs:check-links` — 15,215 internal links checked; 0 broken.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

## Live proof status

The earlier disposable-channel run created a public channel and delivered to its returned target, but it did not prove requester membership because the installed app lacked the required invite scope. Fresh end-to-end proof remains pending a Slack app reauthorization with the corrected manifest, followed by creation of a new disposable channel and a requester post to that channel.

No data migration or UI change is involved.

prs.title: fix(codex): retain native tools in default October cron turns
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes default scheduled agent turns losing native tools when a captured app-authority record is present.

## User Impact

Default owner jobs can use their normal current tools; explicit tool restrictions, condition-trigger jobs and authority recovery guards keep their existing limits.

## Why This Change Was Made

Allow the runtime issuer to mark an authority record as independently bounded, and honor that marker only for valid default owner turns. Forward native-tool eligibility from the actual run and keep restricted app authority intersected.

This is PR 2 of a seven-part October beta compatibility review. Its base is `codex/october-review-01-slack-receipts` and its diff contains one original fix commit, `e02a57e78fef6b972064bb65e3e504ec5f12836e`. The first review base is `v2026.10.1-beta.1` plus four carried ports. The seven fixes were previously pushed directly to a candidate branch; this PR makes the existing patch available for normal CI and independent review. Historical pushes and author-run checks do not count as completed PR review or CI.

## Evidence

### Source and stored-state disposition

The delayed wildcard does not remove current owner restrictions: `src/agents/conversation-capability-profile.ts` resolves the stored owner session/account against current configured group/account policy; `harness/execution-environment.ts` includes those and current global/agent/provider/sandbox policies in `toolPolicyRestricted`; `dynamic-tool-build.ts` refuses native tools when restricted or when effective exec security disallows them. Explicit finite/empty job caps, condition scripts, owner/account mismatch and recovery state remain excluded from the widening. The cron executor controls above exercise eligible forwarding and those finite/restricted siblings; embedded execution in those executor tests is a recorder, not native file I/O.

Real SQLite save/reload retained explicit caps, default-marker distinction and the private authority envelope; an older-parent-writer control preserved the companion authority during a definition edit. Existing envelopes without `allowOwnerToolDefaults` remain valid and do not opt in. These tests do not claim a fresh process restart or a published-image upgrade. The selected internal upgrade is September to `v2026.10.1-beta.1`; `v2026.10.2` requested in the bot review is not this branch's upgrade baseline. No new schema/version or rollback implementation is added to satisfy that different baseline.

Creator `/exec` placement is deliberately per-session (`docs/tools/exec.md`); detached `current` cron jobs have their own execution identity (`docs/automation/cron-jobs/payloads.md`). Adding cross-session placement inheritance would change that existing contract. No definite new bypass was found, so no speculative authority redesign is included. The previously missing create/persist/process-restart/native-effect composition is now exercised in the owned production Gateway evidence below. Its synthetic transports/identity and the separate historical-image/no-MDM coverage limits are explicit; earlier component proofs are not renamed as this new run.

### Inspectable current authority boundary follow-up

At combined head `c4e9869318abc768529140de3e627a637c1fe64a`, a temporary secretless fixture called the **actual `prepareCodexAttemptRuntime` entry**. It did not substitute the admission helper. Account/profile mismatches rejected before both client prewarm and the client factory. A third control changed the prepared account during the awaited auth-binding step and also rejected before those boundaries.

Results and asserted recorder counts:

```text
PASS rejects account change before client prewarm or factory
PASS rejects profile change before client prewarm or factory
PASS rejects during-awaited-binding change before client prewarm or factory
prewarm calls: 0; client factory calls: 0 (each denied case)
3 passed; no native thread/turn or connector request started
```

Auth-binding completion and prewarm/factory were synthetic recorders; this proves runtime ordering and principal admission, not a live provider credential revocation. All later runtime fields were deliberately absent in the negative fixture, so accidental progression would fail rather than silently use a fake provider. The fixture was removed and tracked source remained clean.

Existing production native MCP adapter/client controls were also executed on this head, recording actual JSON-RPC transport writes through `createNativeMcpRuntime` and its real client. Under overload backoff, allowed calls produced two writes; revoking owner or per-call grant produced one original write and **zero forbidden retry writes**, with `CodexAppServerScopedRequestRejectedError`. Native tool, catalog and resource cases all passed. This covers retained-handle/retry fencing using synthetic grants and in-memory transport, not provider OAuth invalidation.

```text
PASS native tool retry: current owner/grant -> retry permitted
PASS native tool retry: owner revoked -> retry refused
PASS native tool retry: grant revoked -> retry refused
PASS native catalog/resource retry: owner revoked -> retry refused
cron persistence + executor: 34 passed
native MCP authority + current-owner app controls: 10 passed
native serial wrapper: 44 passed; wall38.24s
```

The four-file command was `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-mcp-app.authority.test.ts src/cron/store.definition-integrity.test.ts src/cron/isolated-agent/run.tools-allow.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/scheduled-app-authority.owner-defaults.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. The temporary runtime plus Slack final-write proof wrapper passed five cases in30.79s; it did not start a Gateway or mutate a shared bot.

### Actual creator → persisted finite defaults → process restart → native effect

The prior create/persist/restart composition gap has now been exercised at combined current review head **`3590f39daf1be817be59d0bc789ec9e2e1e53ddb`**, using its fresh normal build and actual **Codex 0.153.4**. `src/cron/tools-allow.ts`, `src/cron/runtime-authority.ts` and `src/plugin-sdk/codex-mcp-projection.ts` were verified byte-identical to this PR's `2290c09` head. Later app approval/current-app repairs are present in the combined build; this is not called an execution of the isolated intermediate PR tree.

An exclusively owned local Gateway uses normal configuration and a configured loopback app-server endpoint. A normal Gateway-backed creator turn's actually advertised `automations` tool invokes `add`. **No `toolsAllow`, default marker, runtime authority, opt-in or owner-policy bit is supplied by the model fixture or written into the job manually.** The production callback discovers the supplied app through actual native `app/installed`, `app/read`, config and MCP inventory APIs and issues the envelope. The HTTP fixture supplies ordinary display/tool metadata, not enabled/callable permission flags.

After the creator completes, both Gateway and Codex processes stop cleanly. The actual SQLite rows show a finite automatic tool snapshot with `toolsAllowIsDefault=true`, an issued `codex.apps` envelope with `allowOwnerToolDefaults=true`, configured-endpoint identity and ASK app policy. Fresh Gateway and Codex PIDs then load the same state and normal scheduler; no `cron.run` or foreground effect is used. The dummy account changes while the configured endpoint stays the same, exercising the intentional endpoint-owned account-rotation contract. Normal system requirements are retained, with their permitted workspace-write sandbox; no MDM/security setting is altered.

```text
source/build HEAD=3590f39; clean build stamp/input signature verified
actual creator tool=automations add; creator exit=0
persisted cap: finite; automatic-default marker=true
production-issued opt-in=true; namespace=codex.apps; issuer=configured-app-server
captured app mode=ASK; captured annotated read mode=auto
Gateway PID replaced=true; Codex PID replaced=true; SQLite reopened by fresh Gateway
same endpoint + synthetic account rotation: allowed
normal due-time scheduled app read:       actual connector effect=1
normal due-time configured native MCP:   actual connector effect=1
both effects after natural due; foreground effects=0
durable cron receipt: status=ok, error=null
owned processes/server stopped; synthetic auth removed
```

The model response and MCP service are deterministic synthetic transports, and all identity/account data is synthetic. The recorder has no permission branch: every received `tools/call` succeeds. Effects, persisted flags, actual process replacement and durable receipt were independently read back. This proves the production creator/store/scheduler/native composition without accessing a real SaaS provider or shared staging bot. OpenClaw's configured WebSocket path is experimental; no claim of stable transport support or a production rollout is made.

Two additional real creator/persistence/fresh-process siblings retain the issued finite/default/opt-in state:

```text
configured endpoint changed before fresh scheduled run:
  durable receipt=error: authorized for a different configured Codex app-server
  scheduled model requests=0; app/configured-MCP effects=0
current owner tool policy narrowed before fresh scheduled run:
  restricted preflight reached; durable receipt=error; scheduled model requests=0
  app/configured-MCP effects=0
```

The endpoint control directly exercises production fingerprint denial. The narrowed-policy control is **fail-closed at this machine's legacy MDM isolation guard** (`legacyManagedConfigTomlFromMdm`), not a no-MDM native exposure test. That host guard was not disabled or repaired for the experiment. It establishes that the persisted opt-in does not bypass the actual restricted preflight on this host; the earlier current-policy/native-eligibility owner controls retain their component scopes and are not a no-MDM native-effect composition. The already credited production-entry prepared-principal change-during-binding and retained native-client retry/revocation controls are not repeated or renamed as SaaS OAuth tests.

Fresh-process continuity for genuinely issued data is now shown. Historical published-image upgrade remains distinct: this backport is based on `v2026.10.1-beta.1`, for the selected September→October-beta internal upgrade. A requested `v2026.10.2`→this beta branch would be a different downgrade path, not this PR's base or chosen upgrade. Existing unmarked envelopes/explicit caps keep their conservative behavior in the executed real SQLite controls above. No new rollback automation, schema/version or dependency change is added for that different baseline; the documented disable-before-old-reader/manual recovery requirement remains visible.

### Current review-stack head

Current head: `2290c09d3f85d33cd7adf881759e7fcb386e7b08`; base: `f06970c397cbeca1a9fe1c900ad116cf39c8b872`. Both part1 follow-ups (actual question-card destination decoding and the introduced static type-cycle repair) were merged through the stack using normal commits. The effective diff of this individual PR was verified byte-for-byte unchanged through both integrations. Original candidate/internal pin/live bots remain unchanged. Historical runtime/CI evidence is bound to its recorded SHA; newest-head CI and ClawSweeper conclusions are assessed separately.


Fresh combined-source validation at `09156d64a267aaeef7b0bc31d6ae225d9858caf3`: `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base 433c9a3ab1a166d97e0c32df165b0436d0ad04c1 --head 09156d64a267aaeef7b0bc31d6ae225d9858caf3 --timed` completed successfully on Node 24.16.0, including formatting, core and extension production/test types, lint, dead-export and runtime/database guards. This validates the combined source, not each intermediate head or hosted CI. A fresh combined P2 autoreview reported no actionable finding within the supplied source evidence; it does not replace ClawSweeper or maintainer approval.

This PR is ready for review. Its first normal exact-head CI attempt ended with the inherited audit failure described below; ClawSweeper has completed an earlier-head conclusion; see the follow-up disposition. Current-head review is tracked separately.

Author-run regression coverage includes default versus explicit tool caps, isolated-agent wiring, persisted authority integrity, invalid and inherited opt-ins, and native tool construction. Previous scoped review was completed; the full seven-change interaction review is being refreshed.

The final combined source has passed a focused staging core acceptance of 12/12 and two model-menu controls. That does not establish all release-suite coverage or the individual intermediate heads. No production deployment is included. The original full release-suite coverage limits remain; the first public CI audit failed as attributed below, and does not replace the current-head review follow-up.


### Known inherited CI failure on the recorded earlier head

The [exact-head CI audit](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38325453670/job/115063226704) failed on three production dependency advisories: `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.30.1` and `@modelcontextprotocol/client@2.0.0` ([GHSA-6qxp-vccf-f47h](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6qxp-vccf-f47h)), and `source-map-js@1.2.1` ([GHSA-68fv-2mgg-jv7q](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-68fv-2mgg-jv7q)).

These are inherited from the selected public beta, not caused by this fix. All package manifests, the lockfile, workspace configuration and audit implementation are unchanged from `v2026.10.1-beta.1` through the PR base and head. The actual CI merge commit `de45764f952892821aea704dd4bce8acdbdf3d24` has the expected base/head parents and exactly the PR-head tree. The same three audit findings were inspected in all seven stack jobs. Upstream already tracked fixes in #165902 and #166217.

The requesting maintainer explicitly accepts these proven inherited CI failures as non-blocking for this compatibility review. This is an attributed exception, not green CI or approval of the code. The downstream `openclaw/ci-gate` failed and fail-fast cancelled sibling jobs; those cancelled jobs remain incomplete hosted coverage. Normal code/security review and any defects caused by this patch still require resolution. No dependency update, scanner suppression or CI rerun is included.

<details>
<summary>October review stack</summary>

- Part 1: #170416 — fix(slack): keep workspace identity in October delivery receipts
- Part 2: #170417 — fix(codex): retain native tools in default October cron turns
- Part 3: #170418 — fix(codex): allow scheduled read-only app calls under ask
- Part 4: #170419 — fix(codex): avoid timing out valid October automation runs
- Part 5: #170420 — fix(codex): refresh app access for default October scheduled jobs
- Part 6: #170421 — fix(models): clarify partial model availability in October menus
- Part 7: #170422 — fix(slack): recognize same-workspace source channel aliases

Merge in dependency order into `kimiyu_openclaw_2026-10-01-beta1-reviewed`; later PRs are based on the preceding review branch. The final original head is `09156d64a267aaeef7b0bc31d6ae225d9858caf3`.

</details>


### Executed September-reader / October-store compatibility

Ran the actual retained September **2026.9.8 / a7b9d5dd139417f7ca9a5d0f955edc3d0c646e75** service image's compiled public cron-store SDK on synthetic task-only SQLite state. Its buildstamp is clean; state schema is 20, matching the candidate. This is the actual compatible September baseline, distinct from the older 2026.9.4/schema-17 default image that cannot read already-migrated staging state. No live database or credentials were copied.

The old compiled writer persisted three complete disabled jobs: explicit finite tools without authority, explicit finite tools with an old envelope, and an automatically captured finite snapshot with an unmarked old envelope. A WAL-aware backup was loaded and saved by the candidate's compiled SDK in a new process, then read again in another new process. All three complete normalized jobs were deeply equal across old write → new load/save → new fresh read, including owner, scheduled policy, finite caps, envelope payload, schedule and enabled state. No SQL rows were manually edited and old jobs acquired no issuer opt-in. Existing exact-head resolver controls keep unmarked authority finite.

A separate new-build store write added a **disabled** job carrying the genuine opt-in authority from the earlier production Gateway creator proof. The real September reader then loaded that SQLite database in a fresh process: the new-format job stayed disabled and became recovery-required, while the three older jobs remained unchanged. A fresh candidate process read the old-reader result: the new-format job stayed disabled/recovery-required and the older jobs remained exactly equal. It was not silently re-enabled or granted default tools. This executes the documented stop-before-unsupported-reader safety and confirms that re-upgrading does not silently repair lost authority: recreate an affected automation through an authenticated supporting creator before enabling it.

Scope: real published-image compiled persistence entry points, actual SQLite and distinct processes; the fixtures are synthetic and deliberately disabled. prs.title: fix(system-prompt): tell models the runtime-context block never carries the message body
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a model sometimes reports the current Discord message body as missing after a tool call
resumes the same turn, even though the body is intact in the transcript, and re-asks the user or
repeats the tool call.

## User Impact

User impact: fewer spurious "please resend your message" replies and duplicate tool calls after a
tool result resumes a turn, especially with short or approval-sensitive instructions (for example
a bare `approved`).

## Why This Change Was Made

The `<<<BEGIN_OPENCLAW_INTERNAL_CONTEXT>>>...<<<END_OPENCLAW_INTERNAL_CONTEXT>>>` block carries
runtime metadata for a turn, not the triggering message body, which stays in the latest
user-role message instead. Nothing in the system prompt said the block was never meant to carry
the body, so a model reading the metadata block and not finding the body there could read that
absence as loss. Reported and reproduced with MiniMax-M3, which then either asked the user to
resend the instruction or inferred it from older history mid-turn.

Added one sentence to the "## Runtime Context" section of the system prompt stating plainly that
the block never repeats the body and that its absence there is not loss. This is the same fix the
reporter described testing locally: "a local runtime-context clarification produced this expected
behavior in a fresh before/after test."

## Evidence

Updated `src/agents/system-prompt.test.ts`'s existing exact-match test
(`keeps runtime-context instructions once in the stable prefix`) to include the new sentence;
it still asserts the instruction text appears exactly once, is byte-stable across repeated
builds, and stays inside the cached stable prefix (`SYSTEM_PROMPT_CACHE_BOUNDARY`), for all three
parametrized models.

Ran `src/agents/system-prompt.test.ts` (175 tests), `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/runtime-context-prompt.test.ts`,
and `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-prompt-context.test.ts`: all passing, no
regressions. Confirmed the 3 exact-match tests fail against the unmodified prompt text (missing
the new sentence) and pass after the change.

`oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` on both touched files: clean.

No other file hardcodes the runtime-context instruction text
(`grep -rln "Messages delimited by <<<BEGIN_OPENCLAW_INTERNAL_CONTEXT>>>" src/`), so nothing
else needed updating.
