prs.title: feat(agent): allow explicit one-shot tools
prs.body:
Related: #126255

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw agent exec` uses a restrictive one-shot tool profile, but a trusted local runner could not add one named tool without persistent configuration. Later global, selected-agent, or provider-specific policy layers could also erase a one-shot grant.

## Design

- Add repeatable `--also-allow-tool <name>` to local `agent exec`.
- Trim values, reject empty names, and deduplicate.
- Extend non-empty strict allowlists in place; preserve additive/allow-all semantics when no strict allowlist exists.
- Compose the grant into global and selected-agent policy, including every authored `tools.byProvider` entry.
- Preserve configured denies; deny remains authoritative.
- Keep the option local to CLI assembly. It does not widen Gateway or public agent-command ingress.

## Evidence

- 6 files, 289 insertions / 24 deletions against current upstream `main`.
- Current head: `900acbbe47f653440a3803124212eb1cc6dedc5b`, rebased onto `3ae680f7143336e6918f8819163a3cbf21882e92`.
- `pnpm check:changed` passed after rebase.
- Focused command/policy suites and both core typecheck lanes pass.
- Coverage includes strict, additive, profile-only, global, selected-agent, and provider-specific policy, plus authoritative deny behavior.
- Required branch autoreview found no finding and rated the patch correct at 0.98 confidence.

## Evaluation result

The evaluated OpenClaw command used `--also-allow-tool browser`. Combined with #126255 and #126404, [full run 32556602972](https://github.com/browser-use/new-eval-platform/actions/runs/32556602972) scored **86/106 (81.13%)**, above historical Laith OpenClaw at 82/106. ## What Problem This Solves

In the OpenClaw Control UI (browser), when in a chat session and the agent finishes its response, a loading spinner next to the session name in the sidebar keeps spinning indefinitely, and the "New Session" button remains disabled.

## Root Cause

When the agent finishes, the gateway emits a terminal `sessions.changed` event with `hasActiveRun: false` that should clear the row's active state and stop the spinner. However, two staleness guards in `ui/src/lib/sessions/reconcile.ts` rejected this terminal event when its `updatedAt` timestamp ties or precedes the existing row's `updatedAt`:

- `isOlderSessionSnapshot` rejected `incoming.updatedAt < existing.updatedAt`
- `isStaleForActiveSession` rejected `existing.updatedAt >= incoming.updatedAt` or `existing.startedAt >= incoming.updatedAt`

When both guards fired, `reconcileSessionHistory` returned the same `result` object reference, causing the caller's `result === state.result` publish gate to skip re-rendering the sidebar. The spinner stayed on `hasActiveRun: true` indefinitely.

The timestamp tie occurs because the terminal `sessions.changed` event's `updatedAt` comes from the lifecycle `endedAt` while the prior `session.message` event's `updatedAt` comes from the session row loaded at message-commit time.

## Why This Change Was Made

A terminal projection is authoritative — it represents the gateway's final state for the session run. Timestamp ordering must never prevent a terminal state from clearing an active row, because no subsequent event would correct a blocked terminal projection.

## Refined Fix (addresses ClawSweeper P1 run-identity concern)

The first iteration unconditionally bypassed both staleness guards whenever `hasActiveRun === false`. ClawSweeper correctly flagged this as a P1 risk: a delayed terminal event for an *old* run must NOT clear a newer active run's state.

The refined fix adds `isStaleTerminalForActiveRun` (lines 226-235), which uses `startedAt` as the run discriminator (always available on both the incoming event and the existing row, unlike `activeRunIds` which is `undefined` during active runs). A terminal event is rejected as stale **only when** both `startedAt` values are numbers AND they do not match — meaning the terminal event belongs to a different (superseded) run.

## User Impact

- The loading spinner next to the session name in the sidebar stops immediately after the agent finishes responding.
- The "New Session" button becomes clickable as soon as the agent finishes.
- No more stale/active row state persisting after terminal events.

## Regression Tests

Three tests in `ui/src/lib/sessions/reconcile.test.ts` (`reconcileSessionChanged` describe block):

1. **"clears an active run even when a terminal event has an equal updatedAt (timestamp tie)"** — existing row `updatedAt:100, startedAt:100`; terminal event `updatedAt:100, startedAt:100`; verifies row updated to `hasActiveRun: false, status: "done"`.
2. **"clears an active run when a terminal event updatedAt equals existing startedAt"** — existing row `updatedAt:200, startedAt:100`; terminal event `updatedAt:100, startedAt:100`; verifies row updated to `hasActiveRun: false, status: "done"`.
3. **"does not clear an active run when a terminal event has a mismatched startedAt (stale overlap)"** — existing row `updatedAt:300, startedAt:200, hasActiveRun: true, status: "running"`; terminal event `updatedAt:150, startedAt:100, hasActiveRun: false, status: "done"`; verifies row unchanged (`hasActiveRun: true, status: "running"`).

Tests 1 and 2 fail on pre-fix code and pass after the fix. Test 3 passes on both pre-fix and post-fix (guards the overlap regression).

## Test Results

| Suite | Result |
|-------|--------|
| `reconcile.test.ts` | 25 passed (22 original + 3 new) |
| `index.test.ts` | 31 passed |
| `run-lifecycle.test.ts` | 35 passed |
| Full `ui/src/lib/sessions/` suite | 353 passed across 33 files |
| `session-spinner-clears.e2e.test.ts` (mock-gateway E2E) | 1 passed (41.7s) |

## Real Behavior Proof

A mock-gateway E2E test (`<file>ui/src/e2e/session-spinner-clears.e2e.test.ts</file>`) using the real Control UI source served by Vite + Playwright Chromium verifies the end-to-end behavior:

1. Sets up a session with `hasActiveRun: true, status: "running"` in the mock gateway
2. Navigates to the Control UI chat page
3. Confirms the `session-run-spinner` is visible in the sidebar (spinner looping)
4. Emits a terminal `sessions.changed` event with `hasActiveRun: false, status: "done"` and matching `startedAt`
5. Confirms the spinner disappears (`.session-run-spinner` count → 0)
6. Confirms the "New Session" button is enabled (not `disabled`)

**Before** (`spinner-before.png`): sidebar shows the spinner next to the active session.
**After** (`spinner-after.png`): spinner is gone, session shows terminal status.
Video recording attached from the same run.

## Type Checking & Formatting

- `tsgo` (core + UI): no errors
- `oxfmt --check`: all files use the correct format

## Pathfinder Fix

`ui/vite.config.ts` was updated to resolve a pre-existing `pako` ESM import issue (`import { gzip }` → `const { gzip } = require("pako")`) that blocked the E2E Vite build. This is unrelated to the spinner bug but required for the E2E test harness. `@panzoom/panzoom` was added to `pnpm-lock.yaml` — it was a missing dependency causing build failures.

## Issue

Fixes #126850

prs.title: fix(state): keep agent media floor stable across schema upgrades
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a Gateway with an already-migrated v16 agent database could park during an upgrade to schema v17 and incorrectly require `openclaw doctor --fix`. The media guard treated every version below the current structural schema as pre-media state, so it blocked the online v16-to-v17 lease-table retirement before that migration could run.

## Why This Change Was Made

The completed media rewrite is now represented by its own durable schema floor: v16, with v15 as the Doctor-owned predecessor. Normal runtime opens accept v16 and converge it through the canonical v17 structural migration. Doctor first crosses the real v15-to-v16 media fence, then independently converges the database to the current structural schema and records the actual final registry version.

True pre-media databases remain fail-closed behind Doctor. No SQLite schema version is added or changed by this repair.

## User Impact

Operators upgrading from an already-migrated v16 agent database to v17 no longer see the Gateway park for an offline migration that has already completed. Legacy v15 media state still requires and receives the existing Doctor rewrite.

## Evidence

- Direct runtime regression: normal open accepts v16, migrates to v17, and removes the retired `state_leases` table.
- Doctor regression: v15 media data rewrites to the fixed v16 floor, then converges to v17 with the retired lease table removed.
- Blacksmith Testbox: 121 tests passed, 6 skipped across agent DB, media migration, and target discovery ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/31485329716)).
- Autoreview and changelog review: clean, no accepted/actionable findings.
- `git diff --check`: clean.

Provenance: the latent current-version coupling was made visible when #121943 advanced the structural schema from v16 to v17.

A scheduled agent turn whose primary model times out can enter its fallback as a fresh user prompt even though the original turn has already reached the provider.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared fallback owner already supplies routing provenance, and the embedded prompt-state owner already distinguishes a dispatched fallback from a new user turn. Cron omitted that provenance from the common candidate parameters. Forward it for both embedded and CLI candidates; retain the existing recorder and continuation owner. Remove a redundant one-use bootstrap-warning temporary so production LOC is unchanged.

prs.title: perf(control-ui): reduce chrome style recalculation on reload
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in reload of a dashboard deep link repeatedly samples browser chrome colors after shell commits, forcing style recalculation while the UI is filling in. The cold-load evidence records 14 visible states over roughly 15 seconds; the current Team-scale fixture maps chrome color reads as a remaining main-thread hotspot.

## User Impact

Reloads spend less main-thread work on unchanged shell presentation. Browser theme-color and the status-bar background still follow theme, light/dark mode, accent/branding styles, chat routes, and responsive breakpoints.

## Why This Change Was Made

The presentation owner retains the last sampled theme/mode, root inline styles, and narrow-chat state, including its own output. Ordinary commits no longer rewrite the root chat class or read computed colors. The theme owner explicitly refreshes after applying a palette because custom CSS can change without changing a theme ID. Progress disclosure cancels only an existing settle timer; layout batching reuses one frame callback instead of allocating one for each newly scheduled frame.

The superseded unconditional color read, no-op timer cancellations, and per-frame closure are removed. Production LOC delta is **+22** (+41/-19 across four production files). The cache/invalidation contract accounts for the growth: palette replacement, accent/branding styles, responsive chat colors, and document replacement must keep updating correctly. No config, storage, schema, dependency, or public SDK changes.

## Evidence

Three production-bundle Team-scale reloads per revision, same 300-session/30-pin/120-person/240-message synthetic fixture, 35 ms wire latency and 4 ms frame spacing. Baseline: main at `4f8c8c58fc88`; candidate: this patch on that baseline. The patch was subsequently rebased without conflicts onto current main; none of the six touched files changed in the new base. Final PR head: `6175ae0e9e6d8482c32fae56cf0f3c57baa47a1c`. Temporary benchmark probes were removed from the source diff. Timing observations are noisy on the loaded shared Mac; counts are the primary evidence.

| Metric (median; range where useful) | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Chrome color samples/writes per reload | 30 [30–31] | 3 [3–3] |
| All root background-token reads per reload | 33 | 5 |
| All app empty timer clears per reload | 196 [196–203] | 146 [146–152] |
| All app animation-frame requests per reload | 273 [249–320] | 280 [275–296] |
| Chrome sync sampled self time, including native calls, ms | 104.1 [21.3–112.4] | 1.7 [1.0–1.8] |
| Progress reset sampled self time, including native calls, ms | 17.2 [16.6–32.3] | 0 [0–0] |
| Layout scheduling sampled self time, including native calls, ms | 21.9 [21.4–24.9] | 21.1 [18.4–28.0] |

The layout scheduler already coalesces frames correctly. Its callback allocation is removed; the measurements do **not** establish a native frame-scheduling speedup. Zero sampled progress-reset time means no sample hit that work, not zero controller calls.

Focused proof uses the repository's single-file Vitest wrapper with `--maxWorkers=1`. Local UI E2E evidence predates the test-only tuple correction; the four production files stayed byte-identical after the subsequent rebase. CI supplies updated-head proof:

- Chrome presentation unit regression: 5 tests pass; wrapper wall time 9.97 s after the test-type correction. The regression fails on the original code because 20 ordinary shell commits perform 20 computed-style reads.
- Progress disclosure controller: 19 tests pass; wrapper wall time 18.43 s.
- Scroll-state batching: 3 tests pass; wrapper wall time 7.09 s.
- Hover marquee: 6 tests pass; wrapper wall time 7.01 s.
- Theme startup/browser chrome E2E: 14 tests pass on the prior `9929f4430a16` head; wrapper wall time 104.31 s / Vitest duration 88.89 s, including the existing startup continuity matrix. New live theme/mode/accent/breakpoint case: 3.71 s.
- Progress disclosure E2E: 4 tests pass on the prior `9929f4430a16` head; wrapper wall time 88.55 s / Vitest duration 65.51 s.
- Production UI build and diff/format checks pass. Final-head UI CI job wall times (whole jobs, including setup): checks-ui-e2e (1/2): 116 s; checks-ui (3/3): 246 s; checks-ui (1/3): 290 s; checks-ui (2/3): 335 s.

Capacity-blocked campaign policy: no Testbox lease was requested; remote capacity is unavailable. The full UI E2E suite and local full typecheck were not run. Focused local proof plus exact-head GitHub CI is the authorized gate. Isolated Codex autoreview: **scoped-clean through P2**, no accepted/actionable findings. The initial CI run on the prior head found a new test-type error: destructured attribute pairs were inferred as arrays whose entries could be undefined. The cases now use readonly tuples; focused unit proof and a fresh isolated review both pass. Production code and the measurements above are unchanged. Final-head [CI run 38347871921](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38347871921) is **green** on `6175ae0e9e6d8482c32fae56cf0f3c57baa47a1c`: all 55 jobs completed with no failures. The previously failing test-typecheck shard now passes.

Release-note context: Control UI cold reloads avoid repeated browser chrome style reads and empty progress-scroll timer cancellations while preserving live appearance updates.

Synthetic before/after captures below show the unchanged settled layout; both were inspected for unrelated/private content before publication.

prs.title: fix(agents): pin legacy default agent workspace on load to prevent silent per-agent move
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A `default: true` agent with **no explicit `workspace`** (inheriting `agents.defaults.workspace`) silently changes its resolved workspace from `<workspace>` to `<workspace>/<agentId>` on upgrade. The new per-agent directory is scaffolded with a blank default identity, and the agent's `memory/` and `outputs/` move to the empty subdir — a silent identity + memory reset, with no error or prompt. Fixes #127802.

## Root Cause

`resolveAgentWorkspaceDir` returns `agents.defaults.workspace` for the legacy default agent only when `tryResolveInheritedWorkspaceAgentId` identifies it. That relies on `getRetainedLegacyDefaultAgentId` — a process-local `WeakMap` keyed by the config object, seeded during the roster migration that strips `default: true`. Across config re-materialization on the read/load path, the config object resolved against is not the one the retention was seeded on, so the retention is lost, `inheritedWorkspaceAgentId` is `undefined`, and resolution falls through to `path.join(defaults.workspace, agentId)` → `<workspace>/<agentId>`.

The write path (`io.write.ts`) already pins the workspace via `materializeWorkspace: true`, but a config that is never rewritten after upgrade (e.g. a read-only mounted config) never receives that pin — so the read path must not depend on the fragile in-process retention.

## Fix

`migratePersistedImplicitMainRoster` now defaults `materializeWorkspace` to `true` when it processes a legacy default agent (callers can still pass `false`). Retiring the `default: true` marker therefore also pins the legacy default agent's workspace into the config **data** on every read path (load, snapshot, validation) — mirroring the write path — so resolution stays correct regardless of `WeakMap` object identity. The pin only applies to a legacy default agent that has no explicit `workspace` (an agent with an explicit workspace is untouched), and it resolves to `agents.defaults.workspace` (its historical value), so behavior is preserved rather than changed. No on-disk config is rewritten on read.

## Evidence

Added a regression test in `legacy.roster.test.ts`: loading a config with `main: { default: true }`, a sibling agent with an explicit `workspace`, and `agents.defaults.workspace` set now yields `entries.main.workspace === defaults.workspace` (previously `main.workspace` was absent, which produced the `<workspace>/main` fallback). Confirmed the failing behavior on latest `main` (`resolveAgentWorkspaceDir` and its `// Read-time migration removes default:true before write-time workspace pinning can run.` comment are unchanged).

prs.title: feat: add exact-turn capability projection reports
prs.body:
Closes #105588

## What Problem This Solves

Operators currently cannot distinguish whether an OpenClaw capability is configured, runtime-loaded, policy-allowed, projected into an exact turn, or actually callable. This adds a deterministic read-only report contract that preserves those states separately instead of collapsing them into an ambiguous "available" flag.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds `openclaw sessions capability-projection`, a closed-schema collector/model/renderer pipeline that selects authoritative `context.compiled` evidence by exact run, exact event sequence, or a bounded latest-in-window query. It accepts only pre-sanitized allowlisted auxiliary evidence, records successful callability only from runtime tool-result events carrying the selected run/session identity, and publishes JSON and Markdown from one validated normalized object using an atomic version pointer.

The command does not invoke tools, probe mutating capabilities, change policy/configuration, or contact external services. Tool completion trajectory events retain only tool name and success/error state; arguments and results are excluded.

## User Impact

Reviewers can generate machine-readable and human-readable capability projections with explicit evidence gaps and deterministic mismatch codes. This PR implements the command and synthetic proof only; it does not generate NathanAI's first live report or change any live capability surface.

## Evidence

- Issue: #105588
- Branch: `feat/capability-projection-report-v1`
- Commit: `95a9631714e5c323e2df9f6b3a78b49bd0653581`
- Focused tests:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/capability-projection.test.ts src/cli/program/register.status-health-sessions.test.ts src/trajectory/runtime.test.ts`
  - PASS: 3 shards, 80 tests total (`31 + 32 + 17`)
- Formatting: `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --write` on all touched final-delta files; PASS
- Diff hygiene: `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`; PASS
- Mandatory autoreview: `gpt-5.6-sol`; final corrective review clean, no accepted/actionable findings (confidence 0.94)
- Schema/secret/determinism/parity proof is covered by `src/commands/capability-projection.test.ts`, including all requested fixture scenarios, closed evidence unions, credential/header/cookie/PEM/prompt/result exclusions, reordered-input determinism, and JSON/Markdown parity.
- Collector side-effect review:
  - canonical session accessors and bounded local trajectory reads only;
  - no subprocess collector or generic tool invocation interface;
  - no mutating callability probes;
  - runtime tool-result evidence stores only name/success/error under recorder-owned run/session identity.

prs.title: feat: add model switch choices to /model
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Native `/model` menus could show a static or default-agent choice set even when the current Slack, Telegram, or Discord route belonged to a different agent. A user could therefore be offered a model that the existing `/model <provider/model>` setter would reject for that routed agent.

## Why This Change Was Made

The picker should be presentation over the existing setter, not a second selection or authorization path. This change derives choices from the effective routed agent's configured model policy and carries that same agent identity through each native command surface.

## User Impact

- Slack, Telegram, and Discord native `/model` menus offer choices allowed for the routed agent.
- Bare `/model` keeps its existing status/fallback behavior when no choices are available or when a Telegram choice set exceeds the platform's 100-button keyboard limit.
- Every Telegram model button uses the canonical model-callback route: short refs use compact `mdl_sel_...` data and long refs use the bounded opaque form, with identical authorization, runtime-policy, and session-selection semantics.
- Telegram's finite model menu discloses before selection that choosing a model also applies its configured runtime.
- Telegram reauthorizes after deferred runtime preparation and again after acquiring the exclusive session-writer lane. The queued validator also re-resolves and compares the captured agent, session key, and store path, so caller revocation or runtime-binding drift fails closed before persistence.
- Discord bounds staged picker labels and values, fails closed for stale, missing, ambiguous, or legacy tokenless selections, and matches autocomplete by display label or canonical `provider/model` value.
- Slack external search matches the raw canonical model reference; button values remain self-contained through Slack's 2,000-character button limit, while selects and larger payloads use user-bound bounded references.
- No new configuration key, dependency, or lockfile change is introduced.

## Contract

The picker dispatches the existing `/model <provider/model>` command. Slack continues to use its existing button, `static_select`, and `external_select` machinery. Telegram uses the existing canonical callback registry for every model choice, independent of callback length. Discord receives the same routed-agent policy context for sibling parity.

## Evidence

Exact pushed head: `038458e0ee06f889a39a7f8ed54ca02ad3c59f6e`

Rebased branch base: `3a135210a8c069e4be70c5c335f43f0e03d54d28`

Full-branch stable patch ID: `fb5bd91593bf97e7b5a28172ac1f3f684812efb0`

- The queued-authority repair covers both existing-session updates and missing-session creation. A rejected creation leaves no SQLite row or synthetic in-memory adoption; an existing rejected row is refreshed without model-selection effects.
- Independent complete-branch autoreview found one P2 route-drift race after the writer queue was entered. The exact head repairs it by comparing the live Telegram agent/session/store route inside the queued authorization validator. A focused regression changes that route while selection work waits and observes a rejection with no success edit. A correction-aware full-branch rerun reports no P0-P2 findings (0.90 confidence).
- The pre-route-fence parent `c66c9eb275bc45f69f627a1f2158f2ac79a02759` passed the changed core model-selection suite **48/48** and the two Telegram callback-selection/loopback files **3/3**, plus Oxfmt and direct type-aware/type-check Oxlint. On the final head, Oxfmt with the available installed binary, direct type-aware Oxlint, max-lines, assertion-safety, both pairing/auth guards, no-conflict-marker, and `git diff --check` pass.
- A fresh final-head Vitest rerun was attempted but stopped before test discovery because the shared dependency snapshot provides Vitest 4.1.11 while this checkout requires 5.0.0 (`defineCacheKeyGenerator is not a function`). The extension lint wrapper likewise refuses the shared out-of-checkout dependency symlink. - Credential-free compiled mock-Gateway proof at prior public head `144cc6a7badce91240e0f793c87b9cdc3881b667` passed twice consecutively, **1/1** each time, with redaction-clean receipt SHA-256 `da648e90247012db4ebdf59bed5caa35d2515225f6825c4fc3bcc409797271f0`. It is historical evidence, not relabeled as current-head execution.
- Fresh `openclaw/main` `ecf8371c34026c0547fe268cb5cd1be151461908` produces clean merge tree `8679d5744e767e703c2a72c1ca9609f70f5a2763`. The incremental main delta after the rebased base has no changed-path overlap with this PR.

prs.title: improve(control-ui): reduce sidebar work on reload
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in dashboard deep-link reload repeatedly rebuilt the sidebar, its agent roster, and unopened menus. Earlier cold-load evidence recorded 14 visible states over roughly 15 seconds; the current synthetic fixture still retained 30 closed-menu items and updated the sidebar's new-session menu almost once per sidebar update.

Related: #169680, #169707, #170033.

## User Impact

The sidebar does less rendering during reload while preserving its settled appearance. New-session, agent-options, and task-progress menu content mounts on first open and stays mounted afterward. No configuration, server storage, permissions, or upgrade changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Plugin and identity notifications now use the existing sidebar session-data frame. Roster notifications use that same owner, and roster-to-parent publication compares the actual result, agent IDs, and collapsed groups instead of republishing on unrelated metadata changes. The redundant last-published roster snapshot is deleted. The new-session menu compares the displayed access values instead of updating for every newly allocated access object; cached snapshot changes still invalidate it explicitly.

Producer-stack captures attributed 20 scheduled sidebar frames to off-page pin descriptor completions, 13 updates to plugin registration/activation, and most child updates to forced host assignment or a fresh access object. Pin requests remain independent and retain their existing background priority. Stack tracing is diagnostic only: its overhead changes frame scheduling, so performance comparisons use the standard bench probes without stack tracing.

## Evidence

Three sequential interleaved before/after pairs using the merged production-bundle Team-scale bench: 300 synthetic sessions, 30 pins, six agents, 120 synthetic people, 240 messages, 35 ms reply latency, and 4 ms frame spacing. Before source: `fad84f184600`; after captures the runtime change on that same base, before conflict-free rebases and the equivalent Boolean/type-only CI corrections. All six captures reached the content/idle gate without application errors.

| Count, median [range] | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| app-sidebar updates | 67 [66–72] | 54 [51–56] |
| agent-roster updates | 67 [50–73] | 60 [45–61] |
| sidebar new-session menu updates | 68 [51–74] | 6 [6–10] |
| unopened menu items retained | 30 [30–30] | 2 [2–2] |

The removed 28 closed items are six new-session choices, 18 agent-options items, and four progress actions. The remaining two are inline-widget actions outside this change. Roster counts overlap and are a modest improvement; no wall-clock speed claim is made on the loaded shared Mac. RPC totals are 85 before and 84–85 after; this PR does not claim RPC deduplication.

Focused local proof (one file at a time, `--maxWorkers=1`; e2e and the last unit regression ran at `f8f364e26070`, before the equivalent Boolean/type-only corrections; replacement-head CI validates those corrections):

- `app-sidebar.projection-memo.test.ts`: 6 passed; regression preserves selection/menu rendering while the unchanged new-session menu does not update. The pre-fix run failed with seven menu updates during the scenario. Rebased-candidate `pnpm test ui/src/components/app-sidebar.projection-memo.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 26.85 s wrapper wall time (16.50 s Vitest duration); replacement-head CI file duration 2.85 s.
- `app-sidebar.people.test.ts`: 148 passed, 58.29 s wrapper wall time, 26.97 s CI file duration; covers roster/chip transitions, ordering, identities, and new-session options.
- `sidebar-roster.e2e.test.ts`: 3 passed, 61.86 s local Vitest duration, 26.06 s CI file duration; first open, retained items, keyboard opening, agent selection, and collapsed groups. Initial new assertion clicked a hover-hidden options button; focusing the trigger and pressing Enter exercises its intended keyboard path.
- `session-details-progress.e2e.test.ts`: 1 passed, 53.45 s local Vitest duration, 9.42 s CI file duration; first open, retained items, hide/undo, collapse, reload, and narrow layouts.
- Initial CI found an explicit boolean comparison rejected by typed lint and a missing Lit element type in a fixture wait; both were corrected without changing runtime behavior. Production UI build and six benchmark captures passed. Formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Independent Codex autoreview: scoped-clean at P0–P2.

Replacement-head [CI run 38347310715](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38347310715) passed on `ca3c0ed3e76568ab83476729acfa0a91bf8dd330`, including production types, typed lint, all three selected UI unit shards, selected UI e2e, and the Control UI performance check. prs.title: fix(channels): keep capability probe deadline on the monotonic clock
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw channels capabilities --timeout 1000` can hang far past the configured timeout when the host wall clock is corrected: the probe/diagnostics deadline in `runChannelCapabilitiesCheck` was seeded and read with `Date.now()` (wall clock) but consumed by `setTimeout`'s monotonic timer, so a wall-clock rollback (NTP/DST/manual/container drift) inflated the remaining budget and left a stuck probe waiting. The fix seeds the deadline from `performance.now()` and injects `() => performance.now()` as the clock, keeping the whole timeout budget in the monotonic domain.
- Problem: `awaitWithinDeadline(async () => params.run(), Date.now() + params.timeoutMs)` seeds and reads the deadline with the wall clock. `scheduleAbsoluteDeadline` recomputes `remaining = deadlineAtMs - now()` on every timer check, so a rollback between the seed and the next check stretches the budget — a 1000ms timeout becomes ~6000ms (verified below).
- Solution: seed the deadline from `performance.now()` and pass `() => performance.now()` as the `now` argument, matching the repo's canonical pattern (`node-registry.invoke-stream.ts`, `inspect.ts`).
- What changed: `capabilities.ts` `runChannelCapabilitiesCheck` (1 seed site, 1 injected clock) + `capabilities.test.ts` (1 regression test rolling the wall clock back 5000ms while the deadline is armed).
- What did NOT change: `absolute-deadline.ts` (already supports `now` injection) is untouched; no parser/policy branch, config surface, public signature, or behavior-contract change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The channel capability probe/diagnostics deadline is entirely in-process — it never persists or crosses a process boundary — so the monotonic clock is the correct clock for it. This matches the repo's convention for the same wall-clock-vs-monotonic class (#155603, #155648, #155323).
- **Best fix**: Yes. Passing `performance.now()` as both seed and injected clock is the minimal absorbed change; `absolute-deadline.ts` already handles the injected `now`.
- **Alternative**: Re-reading the wall clock right before each check stays vulnerable to a jump between two reads; only a monotonic clock removes the skew.
- **Risk**: Untested under real NTP step changes; the proof uses a deterministic 5000ms rewind model plus a live run.

## User Impact

Channel capability probes and diagnostics now time out reliably at their configured budget even when the host wall clock is corrected mid-check (NTP, DST, manual changes, container drift), instead of hanging after a clock rollback. Behavior is otherwise identical.

## Evidence

### Real-CLI proof — shipped entry point, normal clock, isolated stalled-and-healthy plugin

Terminal output from the **real shipped CLI entry point** `src/entry.ts` (head `7157b8a`), run at **normal speed** (real `performance.now`/`setTimeout`, no accelerated clock), using an **isolated stalled-and-healthy plugin scenario**: the test plugin's `stalled` account rewinds the wall clock 5000ms while the 1000ms deadline is armed and never settles; `healthy` resolves `{ok:true}`, so account continuation is exercised. The loader redirects only `listReadOnlyChannelPluginsForConfig` to this isolated plugin; every downstream step (`channelsCapabilitiesCommand` → `resolveChannelReports` → `runChannelCapabilitiesCheck` → `awaitWithinDeadline`) is real production code.

```console
$ node --import tsx --loader bug122-realcli-loader.mjs src/entry.ts channels capabilities --timeout 1000 --json   # POST-FIX
  stalled  probe: {"ok":false,"timedOut":true,"error":"check timed out after 1000ms"}
  healthy  probe: {"ok":true,"bot":{"name":"healthy-bot"}}
  STALLED_REAL_WAIT_MS=1089   # real elapsed ≈ exact 1000ms budget despite the 5000ms rewind

$ node --import tsx --loader bug122-realcli-loader.mjs src/entry.ts channels capabilities --timeout 1000 --json   # PRE-FIX (Date.now)
  stalled  probe: {"ok":false,"timedOut":true,"error":"check timed out after 1000ms"}
  healthy  probe: {"ok":true,"bot":{"name":"healthy-bot"}}
  STALLED_REAL_WAIT_MS=6072   # 5000ms rewind inflated the 1000ms budget ~6×
```

### Before / after (real elapsed, normal clock)

Same real CLI, inputs, and 5000ms rollback; only the deadline clock differs — the real elapsed wait exposes the bug.

| same-input real-CLI run (timeout 1000ms, 5000ms rewind) | **pre-fix** `Date.now()` | **post-fix** `performance.now()` |
|---|---|---|
| **stalled real wait (elapsed)** | **6072ms ≈ inflated ~6×** | **1089ms ≈ exact 1000ms** |
| healthy account continuation | yes (`ok:true`) | yes (`ok:true`) |

Pre-fix: the 5000ms rollback stretches the real wait ~6×. Post-fix: the monotonic deadline fires at the exact budget and the healthy account is still reached.

### Regression test RED / GREEN

The regression test arms the deadline (1000ms) and rolls the wall clock back 5000ms inside a never-settling probe.

```console
$ npx vitest run src/commands/channels/capabilities.test.ts -t "wall-clock rollback"   # pre-fix (Date.now)
exit: 124   # timed out (120s) — the inflated budget never fires within the advanced monotonic time
$ npx vitest run src/commands/channels/capabilities.test.ts                            # post-fix
 ✓ > keeps the capability probe deadline on the monotonic clock across a wall-clock rollback 10ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  20 passed (20)
```

`capabilities.test.ts` passes 20/20 (incl. the new regression test and pre-existing `timeout:"1"` never-settling tests); unchanged `absolute-deadline.ts` passes 5/5. `oxfmt`/oxlint clean (UI-only solid plugin excluded — absent from symlinked node_modules, unrelated).

### What was not tested

Real NTP/step-change under production load was not exercised; the proof uses a deterministic 5000ms rewind model plus the live CLI run.

### Open PR collision check

No open PR touches `src/commands/channels/capabilities.ts`; related monotonic-clock PRs (#168736, #168735, #168731) touch different files.

prs.title: fix: distinguish native preflight in tool policy hooks
prs.body:
Closes #144608

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users of a plugin that normalizes host-tool arguments can see those calls denied during native preflight, because the plugin cannot distinguish preflight from ordinary host execution.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing plugin hook context gains optional, host-supplied `policyPhase: "native-pre-tool-use"`. Both native relay dispatch paths carry it into the shared policy hook. Ordinary host calls leave it absent, even when tool arguments contain a field with the same name.

OpenClaw's native rewrite rejection remains intact. The phase identifies the invocation context; it does not grant authority, bypass approval, or change admitted-run lifetime checks.

## User Impact

Plugin authors can reserve argument normalization for host execution while continuing to observe or block native preflight. Existing plugins and hook signatures remain compatible. The tool policy hook reference documents the field and its limits.

## Evidence

- New parameterized regression invokes the real native relay both directly and through an admitted host capability callback. Both fail before the fix, pass after it, and fail again with only the production patch reversed.
- The same regression confirms that a model-provided `policyPhase` argument does not establish the host context field, and ordinary execution-time normalization still applies.
- Full native relay suite: 126 tests passed. Plugin before-tool-call suite: 29 tests passed. Broader before-tool-call E2E suite: 103 tests passed after its normal source-build prerequisites.
- Core and agents-other test typechecks, lint, formatting, and max-lines ratchet passed. Autoreview is scoped-clean through P2 (exit 0).
- Inspected pinned Codex source `rust-v0.153.4` / `3d2ee51ca2d5db578f328aa75e20aa22c0197c9a`. Codex core supports updated hook inputs; this fix preserves OpenClaw's narrower, documented native relay contract.

Commands:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/harness/native-hook-relay.test.ts -t 'distinguishes native preflight'
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/harness/native-hook-relay.test.ts src/plugins/hooks.before-tool-call.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.e2e.test.ts
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo
node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs --changed-paths-json '["src/agents/harness/native-hook-relay.test.ts"]'
```

Synthetic tools and isolated test state only; no live provider calls or business data.

Related: #170335 (closed by #170523)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: during `openclaw update` with the Gateway already stopped, the database snapshot step reported agent databases as "Database changed during capture" and disabled automatic database restoration, even though nothing had written to them. The snapshot step's own read caused it.

## User Impact

User impact: updates keep automatic database rollback for agent databases left with WAL sidecars by their last writer. Since #170523, unrestorable snapshots are retained after success, so these false alarms also left a snapshot directory behind on every update; that stops too. Real changes during capture are still detected and reported, and capture without confirmed Gateway custody is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Opening a WAL database natively with no other holder makes SQLite rebuild its WAL index, which resets the `-shm` change counter that is part of the recorded write generation. The snapshot step opened live agent databases natively, so its "after" generation never matched its "before". With maintenance custody confirmed, capture now copies each database family privately (the existing `preserveSourceArtifacts` path) and never opens the source. The state database was not flagged in #170335 because it had been closed cleanly and took the raw-copy path.

Update behavior: the installed updater runs the snapshot, so this takes effect for updates driven *from* a release containing it.

History: this PR originally reworded the snapshot-lifetime messages (DonnieFi's commits, kept in the branch). #170523 merged a different retention policy and owns that wording now, so the merge from `main` takes main's text, tests, and docs; the remaining diff is only the capture fix. Credit to DonnieFi for the report analysis and the original PR.

## Evidence

- New `exited-writer` scenario in `update-command-database-rollback.test.ts`: the agent database is left as a WAL family from an exited writer just before capture. Without the fix (re-verified on current `main` including #170523): `expected [ …(2) ] to deeply equal []` (changed-during-capture + restoration-disabled warnings). With it: no warnings, generation recorded, restore path exercised.
- `pnpm test` rollback + `update-database-backup.test.ts` 36/36 and `update-command-database-retention.test.ts` (#170523) 2/2, 466s wall. `tsgo:core:test`, oxlint, oxfmt, `format:docs:check`, `git diff --check` clean.

prs.title: fix(desktop): managed Linux host desktop fails to start when another X server holds :99 through its abstract socket
prs.body:
Related: #169391

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the managed Linux desktop fails to start when another X server holds its display through an abstract socket but its socket file is not visible to the Gateway, for example under systemd `PrivateTmp=yes`.

## User Impact

Operators can open the managed desktop on the next free display instead of receiving `UNAVAILABLE: Desktop session stopped before connecting`. Hosts without a conflicting X server retain the first display, `:99`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing display probe now combines directory entries with the Unix socket table in `/proc/self/net/unix`, explicitly selecting the Gateway's network namespace. Both pathname and abstract socket names feed the existing display-number selector; unreadable procfs retains the previous directory-only behavior. There is no second display parser or new configuration.

Thanks to @holgergruenhagen for the report and original fix. No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

## Evidence

Built Linux Gateway in a secretless Node 24 Debian container; invoked the shipped CLI `gateway call desktop.observe --params '{"source":{"kind":"host"},"control":false}'` against an isolated running Gateway with `desktop.host.managed: true`.

- Baseline: a real Xvfb occupies `:99` with only the abstract transport (`-nolisten tcp -nolisten unix`), with no `/tmp/.X11-unix/X99` or `/tmp/.X99-lock`; `desktop.observe` returns `UNAVAILABLE: Desktop session stopped before connecting`.
- Candidate: the same foreign server remains on `:99`; `desktop.observe` succeeds with `transport: rfb`, `auth: vnc-password`, and the managed `Xtigervnc` process runs on `:100`.
- Control without the foreign server: both baseline and candidate return a working RFB observation and launch `Xtigervnc :99`.

Observed candidate excerpt (ephemeral observer token omitted):

```text
@/tmp/.X11-unix/X99
filesystem socket absent: true lock absent: true
"transport": "rfb"
"auth": "vnc-password"
Xvfb :99 -screen 0 800x600x24 -nolisten tcp -nolisten unix
Xtigervnc :100 -geometry 1920x1080 -depth 24 ...
```

Focused regression: the new socket-occupancy case fails against the baseline (`expected :102, received :99`); candidate passes all 25 tests in `managed-linux.test.ts` (22.34s including runner overhead). Changed-file oxfmt and oxlint pass. The regression also covers unrelated socket prefixes, unnamed sockets, filesystem occupancy, and unreadable procfs.

Simplification folds the contributor's second probe helper into the existing display probe. Net delta against the merge base: production +23 lines (+29/-6), tests +32 lines. The remaining growth reads kernel occupancy that the old directory-only probe cannot observe.

Merge risk: two-way door; a revert fully restores directory-only selection, with no persisted format or configuration changes. Blast radius is managed Linux desktop display allocation; attached desktops and other platforms are unchanged.

prs.title: Add isSelf marker to Matrix read-path message summaries
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Matrix inbound push/monitor path resolves the bot's own Matrix user ID (`client.getUserId()`) and uses it to filter out self-sent events before they reach the agent. The pull path — reading room history via the message read/history APIs, and listing pinned events — never computes self identity at all. Callers reading a room back have no reliable way to distinguish a message they (or a sibling session/process sharing the same account) sent from a message sent by anyone else in the room.

This is a real problem for any bot/agent framework built on this plugin: multiple concurrent sessions or processes can share one Matrix account, and a session reading room history (or a pinned-events list) can otherwise misattribute its own account's messages as third-party input.

## Fix

Adds an additive, optional `isSelf` boolean to Matrix message summaries returned by the read/history path and the pin-list path:

- `summarizeMatrixRawEvent` now accepts an optional `{ selfUserId }` param and sets `isSelf` by comparing it to the event's `sender`. When no `selfUserId` is available, `isSelf` is omitted entirely (not `false`), so callers can distinguish "confirmed not self" from "self identity unknown."
- `readMatrixMessages` resolves the account's own user ID via `client.getUserId()` — mirroring the existing pattern already used on the push/monitor path — and threads it through to every summary it produces, including thread-root summaries. Resolution is best-effort: a missing or throwing `getUserId()` does not fail the read, it just leaves `isSelf` unset for that call.
- `listMatrixPins` resolves `client.getUserId()` the same way and threads it through `fetchEventSummary()` into both `summarizeMatrixRawEvent()` and `fetchMatrixPollMessageSummary()`, so pinned-event summaries (ordinary and poll) carry `isSelf` on the same basis as room-history reads.

No existing fields change. `sender` is untouched on every summary, and the existing push-path self-event filter is untouched.

## Evidence

- Extended the existing unit suites for `summarizeMatrixRawEvent` and `readMatrixMessages` with cases for the new optional parameter.
- Added a focused test file (`messages-self-marker.test.ts`) covering: a message from the reading account's own session is marked `isSelf: true`; a message from a different sender is marked `isSelf: false`; `sender` is unchanged in both cases; `isSelf` is omitted (not `false`) when self-identity can't be resolved, including when `getUserId()` throws; and thread-root summaries also get `isSelf` correctly.
- Extended `pins.test.ts` with cases covering a self-pinned event resolving `isSelf: true`, a non-self pinned event resolving `isSelf: false`, and `isSelf` omitted when the client can't resolve its own MXID.
- Ran the full Matrix extension test suite locally (`vitest`): 1971 passed, 5 failed. The 5 failures reproduce identically on a clean, unmodified checkout of this branch's merge-base with upstream `main` (verified via `git stash`) — they read local machine config into a couple of `accounts.test.ts` cases and are unrelated to this change.
- Diff stat: 8 files changed, +296/-6 (one new test file; `messages.ts` +13/-2; `summary.ts` +11/-5; `summary.test.ts` +45; `types.ts` +7; `pins.ts` +7/-1; `pins.test.ts` +35/-2; `poll-summary.ts` +7).

## Scope note

This PR intentionally covers only the read-path and pin-list self marker. A related item — wiring parent-session lineage into thread-session transcript headers — turned out to require changes to generic, channel-agnostic session-persistence code well beyond the Matrix plugin, so it's left out of this PR to keep the change small, additive, and reviewable.

### Real-behavior verification

Two read traces from a live Matrix account running this branch (head `6a458790fd2`).
Account and homeserver identifiers are redacted, event IDs truncated. Both used a
brand-new, isolated Matrix device (never the production gateway's device), logged
in with `matrix-js-sdk` directly against the real homeserver.

**History path** — `readMatrixMessages()`'s internal flow: sent one message from the
trace device, then read back room history via the same wire request
(`GET /rooms/{roomId}/messages`) and ran the real, shipped `summarizeMatrixRawEvent()`
against the real raw events, with `selfUserId` from a real `client.getUserId()` call.

```
message {"action":"read","channelId":"<redacted>","limit":5}
[
  {"eventId":"$DxyRI...","sender":"@<self>:<redacted>",  "isSelf": true,  "body":"[FLEET-2955 trace]..."},
  {"eventId":"$PT3B0...","sender":"@<other>:<redacted>", "isSelf": false, "body":"..."},
  {"eventId":"$7ikKZ...","sender":"@<other>:<redacted>", "isSelf": false, "body":"..."},
  {"eventId":"$PSndu...","sender":"@<other>:<redacted>", "isSelf": false, "body":"..."},
  {"eventId":"$IKm2W...","sender":"@<other>:<redacted>", "isSelf": false, "body":"..."}
]
```

- `isSelf: true` resolved correctly on the event sent by the trace device's own session.
- `isSelf: false` resolved correctly on multiple events from a different, real sender in the same room.
- `isSelf` was never missing/undefined across 15 real events read back.
- `sender` was unchanged/untouched on every summary in both cases.

**Pin-list path** — `listMatrixPins()`'s internal flow (the P2 finding from the prior
review round): pinned one message sent by the trace device (self) and one pre-existing
real message from a different, real sender (other), then called the real, shipped
`listMatrixPins()` and read back the resulting summaries.

```
message {"action":"list-pins","channelId":"<redacted>"}
[
  {"eventId":"$q4BLh...","sender":"@<self>:<redacted>",  "isSelf": true},
  {"eventId":"$zosd1...","sender":"@<self>:<redacted>",  "isSelf": true},
  {"eventId":"$PT3B0...","sender":"@<other>:<redacted>", "isSelf": false}
]
```

- Self-pinned event resolved `isSelf: true`; the other-sender pinned event resolved `isSelf: false`.
- Both trace-added events unpinned again afterward to leave room state exactly as found (verified: only the original, unrelated pre-existing pin remains).

Poll summaries returned by either read path carry `isSelf` on the same basis
(`extensions/matrix/src/matrix/actions/messages.ts:335` for thread-root/poll history,
`extensions/matrix/src/matrix/poll-summary.ts` `fetchMatrixPollMessageSummary` for pins).

Branch is current with upstream `main` (`behind_by: 0`, verified via compare API).

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Precisely selected CLI jobs inherit 32-class capacity from the complete CLI suite even when each serial group has only one or two files.

## User Impact

Reduces eligible Blacksmith CLI jobs to 16-class without changing selected files, process boundaries, runtime routing, packing, or timeouts. The existing two-worker fallback covers the complete selected file inventory. Full CLI families and jobs requiring parallel, build, or memory capacity retain their allocations. RunsOn inherits the same hybrid choice for retained Blacksmith CLI jobs.

## Why This Change Was Made

A recent two-file CLI job ran serially on the 32-class and peaked at 6.81 GiB. Capacity is selected after precise packing, so a small selection no longer carries the complete suite’s allocation.

## Evidence

- [Two-file native baseline](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38345869265/job/115127364479): 102 seconds overall, 28.14 seconds in tests, zero OOMs, 64 weighted minutes ($0.128 estimated compute).
- Reproduced the original planner output: both single-file groups share one 32-class job.
- Complete two-file replay through the canonical shard executor on trusted main `e932e521177b`, including cold worker preparation and cleanup: 4 CPUs / 15 GiB / existing constrained-worker policy passed all 18 tests in 79.48s (92.31s service wall), 4.11 GiB peak; 8 CPUs / 30 GiB passed in 84.26s (99.57s service wall), 4.25 GiB peak. Both had zero OOM events. Same source, pinned CI Bun runtime, complete group descriptors, and serial execution. This local comparison demonstrates capacity fit; shared-host noise and omitted cloud setup prevent treating it as measured Blacksmith billing savings.
- An additional complete 100-file CLI replay passed 1,410 tests (one existing skip) in 391.49s with 6.77 GiB peak and zero OOMs at the smaller limit. Full-family capacity remains outside this change.
- Fresh independent scoped review and a separate planner integration review found no actionable defects. The 12 capacity guards and eight focused planner regressions pass; unrelated cases were filtered out. Targeted lint, formatting, scripts typechecking, and root-test typechecking pass. [Exact-head CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38347764731), including all 13 selected Node jobs and all typecheck shards.

## What Problem This Solves

New Session spends unnecessary renderer time rebuilding cloud-placement information when opening the environment picker or changing models.

## User Impact

The environment picker responds faster while retaining the selected cloud profile, current availability, and dispatch settings. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Nested reactive property reads rebuilt the complete picker parameters on every read, including model/runtime resolution. Memoize that presentation at its producer so descendants reuse it until the page changes. Existing synchronous owners and action callbacks continue to control placement and permissions.

## Evidence

The two retained-cloud-placement browser cases fell from 7.33/7.58 seconds to 2.00/1.79 seconds on the same machine and base, with their assertions unchanged. Renderer profiling located the repeated parameter calculations; this is a focused local measurement, not a general responsiveness benchmark.

All 16 focused Chromium cases passed across model catalog, hosted-runtime switching and restoration, cloud OS catalog refresh, and optionless-profile dispatch. The four-file run took 56.96 seconds including the UI build and capture instrumentation. Production UI typechecking, targeted lint, formatting, and size ratchets passed. Lint retains an existing warning on the unchanged liveValue callback. Tests use the repository harness and synthetic Gateway; shared-profile/live-provider browser verification remains unavailable.

prs.title: fix(e2e): require matched MCP code-mode proof
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The MCP code-mode E2E proof counted matching strings anywhere in persisted session data. An unrelated exec call plus assistant prose or an unmatched tool result could therefore satisfy the lane without proving that one code-mode invocation actually read both declaration files and called the fixture tool.

## Why This Change Was Made

Validate structured execution evidence instead of transcript-wide mentions. One assistant `exec` call must contain `API.list("mcp")`, both required `API.read` calls, and `MCP.fixture.lookupNote`; a successful tool result with the same call ID must contain the expected marker and fixture note. The mock-Gateway lane applies the same contract to provider request snapshots.

The generic session-log mention scanner and its routing/test surface are removed because no remaining owner uses them.

## User Impact

No runtime product behavior changes. The release E2E lane now fails closed when MCP code-mode proof is prose-only, unrelated, unmatched, or errored.

## Evidence

- 294 focused tooling tests passed; the final validator suite passed 12/12 after rebase.
- Source Gateway E2E passed on Testbox `tbx_01m102whrrshzjwn919pbjervb`.
- Packaged Docker Gateway E2E passed on the same Testbox.

prs.title: fix: inherit the final Codex dynamic-tool surface
prs.body:
Closes #144617

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where child sessions spawned from a policy-restricted Codex attempt could inherit a tool list captured before Codex filtering and late MCP tool discovery. The list could retain excluded tools and omit requester-scoped tools available to the parent.

## Why This Change Was Made

Forward the existing host-owned allowlist reference through the execution tool build, then refresh that same reference from the final executable dynamic-tool surface. The registration-only catalog does not receive the reference, and unrestricted policy keeps its existing empty-list behavior.

The host remains the policy owner. The inspected native Codex `rust-v0.153.4` source (`3d2ee51ca2d5db578f328aa75e20aa22c0197c9a`, `codex-rs/core/src/tools/spec_plan.rs` and `codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/dynamic.rs`) registers these as external dynamic tools and waits for host execution results; no native protocol or permission change is needed.

## User Impact

Child sessions receive the parent's final authorized OpenClaw dynamic-tool names, including late requester-scoped MCP tools and excluding tools removed by the Codex adapter.

## Evidence

- Three affected native suites passed all 150 tests. Native Node 26.8.1 / Vitest 5 tests exercise `runCodexAppServerAttempt` and real host tool construction. Only requester-scoped MCP materialization is stubbed.
- With restrictive policy, the initial `read`/`sessions_spawn` list becomes `fake__show`/`sessions_spawn` after `read` is excluded and MCP discovery adds `fake__show`. Unrestricted policy leaves the inheritance reference empty; registration-only construction receives no execution reference.
- Reversing the production fix fails all three new regressions. Reversing only final capture while preserving forwarding fails the restrictive case with the stale list and passes the unrestricted control.
- Extension test typechecking, targeted lint/formatting, extension-test import boundaries, and max-lines ratchet passed. Independent autoreview of the final diff was scoped-clean through P2.

These checks prove the public attempt's inherited policy snapshot; they do not launch a live model or child agent.

prs.title: fix(config): bound config include file reads with size limit
prs.body:
## Summary
- **Problem:** Config include reads validated file size before opening but used an unbounded descriptor read, so file growth after validation could allocate beyond the 2 MiB limit.
- **Root cause:** The guarded open path ended with `readFileSync(fd)` instead of the shared bounded descriptor reader.
- **Fix:** Read production descriptors through `readFileDescriptorBoundedSync`; retain injected-fs semantics and enforce the same byte cap for reduced/full test shims.
- **Impact:** Include reads stay bounded without bypassing injected filesystem behavior.

## Linked context
N/A (no existing issue)

## Real behavior proof
- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Normal includes must load while files over 2 MiB fail closed.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux, Node 24.13.1, exact head `9e012a76fa1ca2f980f08919704eea83a15638de`.
- **Exact steps or command run:** `node --import tsx --input-type=module -e '<create normal/3 MiB files and call readConfigIncludeFileWithGuards>'`
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture of `node` source-runtime verification:
```text
normal_bytes=2
oversized_rejected=true
exact_head=9e012a76fa1ca2f980f08919704eea83a15638de
```
- **Observed result after fix:** A normal include returns its exact bytes and a 3 MiB include is rejected before an unbounded descriptor allocation.
- **What was not tested:** Concurrent mutation timing on Windows/macOS; the bounded descriptor helper's dependency implementation and types were inspected directly.

## Tests and validation
```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/includes.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       64 passed (64)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 6.90s

$ git diff --check
# no output
```

## Risk checklist
| Risk | Assessment |
|------|-----------|
| Backward compatible | Yes; injected fs reads are preserved |
| Performance impact | Bounded chunked read only |
| Security improvement | Yes; closes post-open growth allocation gap |
| Requires config migration | No |
| Affects external API | No |
| Tested on all platforms | No; Linux focused proof |
| Documentation needed | No |

AI-assisted: yes. Fresh autoreview was attempted; the local Codex CLI exited before producing findings because its isolated CODEX_HOME rejected PATH helper creation. No autoreview-clean claim is made.

prs.title: fix(control-ui): preserve header controls and avatars during reload
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in reload of a dashboard deep link repeatedly rebuilds header controls and participant avatars while startup facts arrive. The campaign's original evidence recorded 14 visible states over roughly 15 seconds; the later Team-scale trace attributed about 373 ms of inclusive work to Solid flushes. This change addresses two measured sources of DOM churn in that flow.

## User Impact

The rename control and participant avatars retain their DOM through updates. Header updates preserve focus, the rename action uses its latest callback, and changed participant labels and activity links still update. The final layout is unchanged. These measurements establish less construction work, not a faster overall reload.

## Why This Change Was Made

The header's direct callback read occurred inside `Show`'s fallback getter and subscribed structural rendering to legacy props updates. Forwarding the current callback on activation removes that construction-time dependency. The facepile's `avatar()` function built new JSX on metadata updates; a retained, non-keyed `Show` branch updates the existing profile or agent avatar instead. The existing participant key still owns membership and ordering.

Production LOC: **+6** (24 additions, 18 deletions), using `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD -- ':!*.test.ts' ':!*test-support*' ':!docs/*'`. The additional lines express the two typed avatar branches with retained ownership. The JSX-producing avatar function is deleted. No new cache, configuration, dependency, schema, or layout path is introduced.

## Evidence

Production Team-scale fixture on clean main `d7ca748acba9` and the same base plus this diff; three reloads per side, Sessions view, 35 ms wire latency and 4 ms frame spacing. Separate count probes instrumented copies of generated runtime assets and mapped clone/import stacks to source. Timing runs used the merged benchmark without those count probes. Total counts vary with wire/coalescing; the repaired-path ranges are the stronger evidence.

| Per reload, median [range] | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Rename-button DOM creations | 31 [31–50] | 1 [1–1] |
| Session-title span creations | 32 [32–50] | 2 [1–2] |
| ViewerAvatarContent creations | 89 [85–103] | 54 [54–57] |
| Solid template DOM clones, total | 683 [679–726] | 590 [576–594] |
| Cached template parses (`create`) | 145 [144–145] | 145 [144–145] |
| Array reconciliation calls, total | 1,138 [1,126–1,164] | 1,122 [1,014–1,123] |
| Viewer-avatar host reconciliation calls | 35 [35–35] | 35 [35–35] |
| Facepile host reconciliation calls | 13 [13–21] | 13 [13–21] |
| Inclusive Solid flush, ms (noisy shared host) | 306.94 [297.84–416.87] | 310.92 [287.30–327.18] |

DOM clones fall 13.6%; distinct template parsing and inclusive flush remain essentially unchanged. A broader per-field adapter candidate was measured and dropped because it added composer work without eliminating the header remount. Only the two component repairs remain.

Regression tests fail on the old paths because they replace the focused header control or keyed participant avatar. Focused tests cover retained DOM, current callbacks, updated labels, plain/linked faces, and activity routing.

- `pnpm test ui/src/components/viewer-facepile.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 16 passed; 17.30 s wrapper wall time (7.47 s Vitest duration), on rebased head `22c5e39a0738`; CI test duration 0.786 s.
- `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-pane-header-identity.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 3 passed; 36.50 s wrapper wall time (14.56 s Vitest duration), on rebased head `22c5e39a0738`; executed with `pnpm test`; CI test duration 0.344 s.
- `ui/src/e2e/chat-header-owner-presence.capture.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 2 passed; 52.01 s wrapper wall time, on rebased head `22c5e39a0738`.
- `ui/src/e2e/team-scale-cold-load.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 1 passed; 58.83 s wrapper wall time, on rebased head `22c5e39a0738`.
- Focused lint, formatting, production UI build, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent Codex autoreview: scoped clean through P2.

Remote capacity is unavailable, so no Testbox leases or IDs were used. Full UI E2E and full local typecheck were not run under the campaign's capacity-blocked policy; exact-head PR CI provides the broad gate. The branch is rebased before publication. Both unit files and both affected E2E files pass on the rebased head. CI is **green** on that exact head (39 passing checks, 37 intentionally skipped; run conclusion `success`): [run 38346886665](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38346886665).

The attached before/after frames use only the synthetic fixture and were inspected in full. They show settled layout preservation; they do not demonstrate an earlier first paint.

prs.title: fix(slack): treat control-sigil Markdown link targets as labels
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unintended Slack control markup when a Markdown link destination starts with `@`, `#`, or `!`.

## User Impact

These links now display their labels instead of becoming mentions or broken channel references. Ordinary HTTPS links and deliberately authored native Slack tokens retain their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Slack link renderer already falls back to label text for unsupported destinations; reject control-sigil destinations at that same boundary. Thanks to @yetval for the report and @KhanCold for the fix.

The change composes with #169760: compact progress continues to escape native mentions while final replies preserve authored native Slack tokens. No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes in the two changed files.

## Evidence

The isolated built Gateway receives signed Slack HTTP events and scripted Responses API replies, executes the advertised `tool_search` tool, and serializes outbound calls through the real Slack WebClient to an owned API contract server. This proves payload behavior, not live Slack rendering or notifications.

Baseline `5522e85ecd8` final reply captured:

```text
PROOFREPLY <@here|x> <#general|y> <!subteam|z> <https://example.invalid/docs|Docs> native <@U0456EFGH> <#C0456EFGH> <!here>.
```

Baseline compact progress already escapes the generated control wrappers after #169760. This fix additionally removes the wrappers rather than displaying them literally.

The simplification pass reuses the existing invalid-target guard; no new abstraction or parallel rendering path. Production delta against the merge base: +1/-1 (net zero); tests: +10/-0. All three sigil classes and both formatter entry points remain covered.

Candidate `2366aef63ce70ec8c67267260af9a16f1b8ac506` captures:

```text
PROOFREPLY x y z <https://example.invalid/docs|Docs> native <@U0456EFGH> <#C0456EFGH> <!here>.
Working
_PROOFPROGRESS x y z <https://example.invalid/docs|Docs> native <@U0456EFGH> <#C0456EFGH> <!here>._
PROOFFINAL x y z <https://example.invalid/docs|Docs> native <@U0456EFGH> <#C0456EFGH> <!here>.
```

Both compact and card progress pass, including the card's `chat.update` mrkdwn field. The signed inbound event produced the final reply in the originating DM. Baseline card progress also generated raw control wrappers; candidate card progress emits labels. HTTPS links and authored native tokens retain baseline behavior in every active mrkdwn field.

Focused formatter tests: 47 passed in 1.67s. Changed-file Oxfmt and Oxlint passed inside the isolated candidate container.
Live-provider smoke on the same built candidate: `gpt-5-mini` returned `SLACK_SMOKE_OK` through `pnpm openclaw --profile p168438cand agent --local` (6.8s agent execution). The Slack boundary proof above uses a scripted model; this separate smoke verifies real-provider execution.

Closes #168252

Merge risk: two-way door, fully revertible, no persistent state or config changes. Blast radius is Slack Markdown links whose destinations begin with a control sigil.

prs.title: perf(agents): reuse prepared tool descriptors between turns
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Warmed Gateway turns repeatedly projected, serialized, parsed, normalized, and hashed the same tool schemas. The tool/schema/catalog group was the largest sampled contributor in the event-loop stall investigation (#170225). This change lets the existing tool-finalization owner publish a bounded, immutable descriptor snapshot when an attempt settles. The next attempt reuses it while tool membership, source schema identity, plugin inventory, provider/model/API, and configuration match.

## User Impact

Warmed turns can reuse prepared tool descriptions without retaining execution or permission authority. There is no configuration change or migration. Latency improvement remains unmeasured until quiet-host evidence is available.

## Why This Change Was Made

Published schemas retain JSON and fingerprint facts. Provider normalization reuses immutable variants, OpenAI Responses and Completions reuse wire descriptors, Anthropic prepares its tuple dialect separately, and the catalog hashes published schema fingerprints. Generic mutable provider inputs retain their existing projection behavior. Cache-control decoration copies only the request-specific outer wrapper.

Executors, hooks, cancellation, argument preparation, and availability/permission bindings remain per attempt. The snapshot contains descriptors, never authority. The old repeated projection/clone path is bypassed only for explicitly published immutable JSON; mutable external inputs keep their supported behavior.

## Main-thread database and measurement

This lane changes descriptor preparation, not database operations. The touched owners have **T1 0 → 0**, no SQL operations, and no new database path. The global database-worker T1 ratchet stays 455 → 455; changed-file dialect groups stay 0 → 0.

The shared causal harness v2.1 ran one complete baseline/candidate pair, base `1c272f2ae919` and candidate `9205031d1e8e`, with ten warmed turns each. Values below are median [min–max].

| Requests/turn | 41 [41–46] | 41 [41–46] |
| MAIN statements/turn | 0 [0–0] | 0 [0–0] |

Mean causal statements/requests are 172.9/41.9 → 172.2/41.6. No SQL saving is attributed to this patch. Tool-preparation SQL operations/requests remain 0 → 0; the only request-family changes are −0.1/turn each for session-actor execution, worker-task input, and an unresolved task origin. All other request families are flat. Across the complete workload, causal statements are 2,944 → 2,966 and causal requests 688 → 682; including background activity, raw totals are 6,925 → 6,852 statements and 1,329 → 1,282 requests. This is scheduling variation outside the unchanged tool-preparation SQL boundary.

The 32-core host's one-minute load ranged 47.6–92.5 at the SQL run boundaries, so these totals are not latency evidence. The immediate Testbox request queued and was cancelled. Event-loop p99 and turn latency remain unmeasured.

Task-local harness copies relocate fixture/proof output to external storage and use the documented 75-second pre-turn handshake budget symmetrically after a loaded-host handshake expired before the first turn. Workload and causal counting are unchanged; the shared harness is untouched.

## Stall-window profiles

Base `1c272f2ae919`; candidate `9205031d1e8e`.
Three alternating profile pairs (M,C,M,C,M,C), ten warmed turns per run. The immediate Testbox request queued and was stopped, so these are loaded-local-host sample observations. No demonstrated overall CPU or latency reduction; no event-loop p99 or turn-latency claim. Samples locate work but are not causal CPU-time totals.

GC counts are reported without attributing an allocating owner. Residual stacks include dynamic schema construction and snapshot publication during retirement, catalog fingerprinting, metadata copying, and tool-directory rendering. These observations do not establish which allocator triggered GC.

The profile-only post-warm tail was omitted symmetrically for C1/M2/C2/M3/C3; M1 measurements precede its longer tail. Setup and the measured prefix were unchanged. - Published-schema projection, validation traversal, and prepared normalization JSON cloning are reused until the finalization inputs change; schema owners publish edits by replacing their schema object.

- No security-boundary check is removed. Skill-read and collector availability, execution hooks, and abort checks remain live.

## Evidence

The global T1 ratchet stayed 455 → 455; touched owners stay 0 → 0. The separate Knip scan completed: script exports are clean; production/full-tree report only the inherited `renderBoardWidgetError` export in `ui/src/components/board/board-widget-cell-render.ts`. The exact finding is present in [scheduled main CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38343322520/job/115119178402); the UI owner has already removed that obsolete adapter on main in `c6ee92366b568ed72868c92c7910e2d0f9395c14`. No touched-file Knip finding remains. Both isolated Codex autoreview rounds are scoped-clean at P0–P2; the second reviewed the corrected availability-schema capture. The new finalization suite passed all 10 tests: 166 ms of test execution, 274.19 s wrapper wall time (242.05 s Vitest) dominated by cold worker compilation (157.35 s) and source transformation on the loaded local host.

No schema, migration, update, Doctor, plugin-loading, service-lifecycle, or plugin SDK contract changes; the published-driver update cell and SDK surface diff do not apply. LOC: production +476/−69 (net +407); tests +394/−35 (net +359); docs +2/−0 (net +2). The initial CI exposed descriptor TypeScript boundary errors, missing assertion invariants, and strict-null errors in the new test fixture; follow-up commits correct those without changing the snapshot design. The only final CI failure is inherited: `src/commands/config-preflight-snapshot.test.ts:41` imports the now-private `readConfigPreflightSnapshot` (TS2724). The same import/private declaration is present on fetched main `e932e521177bd6cab4f3d2c18bb6d80448452fb7`. These files are untouched here. The test has now been migrated to `createConfigPreflightSnapshotReader` on main by #170619 (`72ccf43fdc6fbe8f4534b84b86f1c8a8909032f5`). This qualifies for the authorized inherited-failure landing exception.

## Follow-up

Hosted review raised a P2 concern about custom payload hooks mutating nested tool descriptors. The provider hook documents inspection/replacement, current bundled wrappers replace projected tools or patch request-level fields, and those request objects remain mutable. Explicitly published nested descriptors are immutable. Custom nested in-place mutation can throw after publication and remains a compatibility follow-up; generic mutable tool inputs retain their existing behavior.

Source-backed performance follow-ups: dynamic schema factories (`automations`, `sessions_spawn`, `computer`, `message`, `skills_search/read`, and `get_goal`) still create new schema identities each attempt, so settlement still publishes changed entries. Stable parameter schemas reuse correctly. Factory-owned descriptor variants can remove further allocations without retaining live tool instances.

A P2 mixed-catalog reuse miss also remains: after binding a published output schema, settlement records that publication as the next output-source identity; the next attempt supplies the original output schema and misses descriptor binding. It returns the current tool, preserving current descriptors and authority, but can repeat output projection/fingerprinting for tools such as `process` and session lookup tools. This is recorded as a follow-up under the bounded review scope.
