prs.title: feat(plugins): fork a session's live context for background side questions
prs.body:
Related: #169564 (Advisor, the first consumer)

## What Problem This Solves

Plugins that review or summarize an ongoing conversation in the background can only see what they rebuild themselves: a bounded excerpt sent through `api.runtime.subagent.complete`. That loses detail and costs a fresh, uncached prompt every time. In a real-API evaluation, an excerpt-based reviewer produced 2 false corrections in 5 runs (it misread polled background commands as extra launches), while a review that saw the session's full context was correct in all 5.

## Fix

Adds `api.runtime.subagent.forkSession({ sessionKey, message, signal?, timeoutMs? })`. It asks one question against an ephemeral fork of the session's current context and returns `{ text, usage }`. It works mid-run, at `agent_end`, and after the parent turn has finished.

- **Same prefix, warm cache.** The fork reuses the parent's exact request prefix, so the provider prompt cache hits:
  - Codex runtime: ephemeral `thread/fork` on the parent's own app-server client, replaying the parent's recorded developer instructions, private persona/skills context, tool surface and turn settings. The parent's last tool declarations are kept in a bounded in-memory LRU (32 MiB global) and restored into the fork request byte for byte. When the parent used a WebSocket continuation (`previous_response_id`), history comes from native Codex reconstruction; no response output is buffered or rebuilt.
  - Built-in runtime: the embedded runner records the exact request it sent at the model-call boundary (bounded, in memory, cleared with session cleanup) and replays it with one appended user message through the same stream function and payload hooks. Anthropic cache breakpoints and the OpenAI `prompt_cache_key` stay where they were. The parent's one-shot continuation `onPayload` callback is not replayed.
- **No tool execution.** Tool definitions stay byte-identical, but every call is denied:
  - dynamic and native Codex tools are denied at dispatch (this also fixes a fail-open path: the native hook relay dropped `PreToolUse` when no global hook was installed);
  - hosted tools: `tool_choice: "none"` on OpenAI and `{ type: "none" }` on Anthropic for every fork request; unsupported APIs fail before dispatch;
  - Codex native `web_search` stays disabled. Its `web.run` declaration is still sent (copied from the parent), so the cache prefix matches but nothing can execute it.
- **No side effects.** Nothing is written to the transcript, delivered, counted as a turn, or drained from queued next-turn context.
- **Authority.** Same background admission as `subagent.complete` (plugin lifetime, cancellation, revalidation after awaits), plus the conversation-access grant, `sessions.get` session visibility, and live Gateway caller authority. These are checked right before every physical send through the guarded-fetch request authority, including DNS/proxy setup, retries and redirects; native ChatGPT WebSocket and SSE sends check them through the existing Responses request lifecycle. Ordinary parent settlement and usage updates (including a briefly unmaterialized session row) do not revoke a fork. A session reset or deletion, a replaced Codex client or thread, withdrawn conversation access, or a retired plugin still revokes it.
- **Same network policy as the parent.** Built-in replay takes the current proxy, TLS and local-service settings (including the local-service reconciler) from the existing transport owner, not from the snapshot. Native ChatGPT forks open their own transient WebSocket and never change the parent's socket, continuation or SSE fallback state.
- **Supported APIs.** OpenAI Completions, OpenAI Responses (including native ChatGPT), Anthropic Messages, and Codex. APIs whose sends the fork cannot fence (for example Bedrock) fail closed before dispatch with `Session forks do not support provider API <api>`.
- **Runtimes.** CLI runtimes (for example `claude-cli`) have no prepared context to fork, so a fork fails closed before any CLI or provider I/O. Ordinary `/btw` on CLI is unchanged.
- **Concurrency.** Forks run on the same subagent lane as `subagent.complete` (`CommandLane.Subagent`), so `agents.defaults.subagents.maxConcurrent` caps both together.
- **Fails closed** with an actionable error when no parent request was prepared by this runtime (for example after a Gateway restart).
- Fixes forked-turn usage reporting on Codex (forks only emit `thread/tokenUsage/updated`) and admits forked requests through the private inference proxy.

Ordinary `/btw` is unchanged from `main`. An earlier revision rejected `/btw` when tools were present, and rejected CLI backends with `nativeToolMode: "none"` and no `sideQuestionToolMode`; both are restored, and CLI admission stays with `prepareCliRunContext` (this answers the review note about #70413). The provider-review continuation callback from #155214 is not replayed by forks.

## User Impact

None by default: no core feature calls `forkSession` yet. Plugins that opt in get full-context side questions at cached-input prices.

## Evidence

Live, real provider APIs, isolated Gateway at the PR head, a throwaway plugin that calls `forkSession` from its service scheduler on each `agent_end`: one fork immediately (parent still settling), then two forks 8 s later (summary, plus a "use web search now" bait). Each parent turn makes 3 tool calls.

| Runtime / provider | Parent last input | Fork at `agent_end`: cache read | Late fork: cache read | Search bait |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Codex, OpenAI (API key, WebSocket continuation) | ~19.7k | 19,642 | 19,967, cacheWrite 0 | `NO_SEARCH` |
| Built-in, OpenAI `gpt-5.6-luna` | — | 15,660 (input 566) | 15,660 (input 608) | `NO_SEARCH` |
| Built-in, Anthropic `claude-sonnet-5-5` | — | 19,595 (input 73) | 19,595 (input 73) | `NO_SEARCH` |

- Codex wire check: the fork's `additional_tools` item (51,233 bytes) has the same SHA-256 as the parent's, and `prompt_cache_key` matches. Before this fix, the late fork read 0 cached tokens because disabling `web_search` removed `web.run` from the `exec` catalog (10,831 bytes).
- Before the admission fix, a fork started at `agent_end` failed with `agent harness host capability is no longer active`: the session-read fence required a fully materialized row while the parent was settling.
- Ordinary Codex `/btw` on the same session: `I ran echo one, then echo two, then echo three.`

Not proven against a real provider: the session-visibility rejection needs an identified Gateway client, and the live probe plugin runs as a service with no caller identity. The composed test below covers it against a real local HTTP provider.

Tests (regressions fail before their fix):
- byte identity of the replayed request through the real transport seam (OpenAI Completions, OpenAI Responses, Anthropic);
- Codex tool-declaration parity after continuation, and child `previous_response_id` cleared on full-prefix replay;
- tool denial for dynamic, native and hosted tools with no global hooks installed;
- fork admission during parent settlement and row rematerialization; revocation on reset, deletion, lifecycle replacement, access withdrawal and visibility change;
- authority withdrawal during preparation, during guarded DNS/proxy setup (no request leaves), during native WebSocket acquisition (no `response.create`), and before an SSE redirect hop (redirect body not sent); rejection of callers outside session visibility;
- current explicit-proxy and TLS policy and the local-service reconciler applied to the replay; native fork failures leave the parent's socket and SSE fallback state unchanged; Bedrock rejected before dispatch;
- a deny fork on a `claude-cli` session is rejected with no CLI spawn or provider call; with `maxConcurrent: 1`, three forks run one at a time and wait while a completion holds the lane;
- composed visibility proof: an identified caller outside session visibility gets `Session not found` with zero requests at a real local provider server (real guarded-fetch transport, no inference mock); the session owner reaches it and gets the prepared-context answer;
- ordinary CLI `/btw` with `nativeToolMode: "none"` and no `sideQuestionToolMode` works as on `main`;
- fork usage from thread token updates, real inference-proxy owner admission, parent→fork on the parent's exact client, snapshot release on committed session reset, and the restart fail-closed path.

CI failures inherited from `main` (the same cases fail on hosted `main` run [38334375513](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38334375513)): `run.manual-tool-authority.test.ts` (4), `github-repository-publication-restart.test.ts` (2), `openai-http.test.ts` trusted-proxy case, `server.sessions.create.accounts.test.ts` (2), `server.sessions.create.workspace-policy.test.ts`, `server.sessions.create.worktrees.test.ts`. Also `server-restart-sentinel.test.ts` (fails on a clean `main` checkout). Single gateway-server tests that failed once in CI (`archive-worker-placement`, `abort-authorization`, `create.durability`, `github-publication` singleflight) pass locally on this branch and on `main`.

Separate observation, not changed here: with an explicit multi-agent config, `/btw` on the system agent fails with `prepared model runtime owner was not published` unless `agents.entries.main.workspace` is set. The published owner uses the startup workspace (`/…/workspace`), but `/btw` asks for `/…/workspace/main`.

prs.title: fix: preserve interrupted turns when new messages arrive
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes interrupted chat recovery being skipped when a new visible message arrives before background recovery starts.

## User Impact

Interrupted work keeps its recovery claim until recovery resumes it, so a new message cannot silently consume the old request as ordinary conversation history. Ordinary failed sessions without recovery custody still recover in place. No configuration or schema change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Orphan reconciliation intentionally retains a failed outcome while marking its delivery claim interrupted. Terminal-session reuse then cleared the interruption flag and delivery/source IDs before reply admission could resume that work. Background recovery could win the race and hide the defect.

Extend the existing terminal-reuse protection with the canonical recovery-claim predicate. Add a deterministic regression beside the existing four-case Gateway recovery test; its assertions and timing limits remain unchanged. Document the recovery ordering. Production is +6 lines: the existing owner needs this additional predicate, with no new state or recovery path.

## Evidence

- The existing recovery test failed at the provider-count assertion in scheduled main runs [38334375513 / job 115091148557](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38334375513/job/115091148557) and [38339144048 / job 115106094655](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38339144048/job/115106094655): expected two requests, received one containing both messages.
- New regression: `preserves interrupted recovery custody when reusing a failed session`. It failed on unchanged production by clearing `abortedLastRun` and both delivery/source IDs. Command: `CI=1 OPENCLAW_VITEST_WORKER_CACHE=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.chat.orphaned-recovery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'preserves interrupted recovery custody'`. Case: 43 ms; command: 235.02 s, mostly cold transformation/preparation.
- The original 25-file replay was stopped during cold Gateway setup without a verdict; the isolated original case also hit a setup timeout. Neither is claimed as a reproduction or passing proof. The nearby database-admission diagnostic is not claimed fixed.
- Changed-file Oxlint: zero diagnostics across both TypeScript files. Oxfmt and `git diff --check`: passed. Deslop: clean.
- Prescribed Codex autoreview: scoped-clean through P2; no accepted/actionable findings. Hosted Codex review also completed without suggestions. ClawSweeper has acknowledged the PR but has posted no code findings as of closeout.
- PR CI is the test gate. At head `798c78243a8e8995c3be46057e9dfaf4c68247ba`, [job 115133100497](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38347696342/job/115133100497) passed the new custody regression (7 ms) and the unchanged four-case Gateway recovery test (21.539 s). Its `agentic-control-plane-agent-chat-hosted-4` shard passed both tests in 34.01 s. Run [38347696342](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38347696342) completed: all PR test, lint, and production/test typecheck jobs passed. There were 36 successful jobs, 25 skips, and two failures: the inherited asset check below and the aggregate CI gate reporting that failure.
- Live Gateway/Crabbox/Testbox proof, local typechecks, broad local suites, and production-reverted negative controls were intentionally skipped per maintainer policy. Only the lane's focused reproduction exception was used.

prs.title: fix(gateway): settle targetless update notices once
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves
A targetless update run can remain in verification while Gateway recovery checks repeatedly emit the same `lifecycle notice skipped: no delivery target` warning. One affected update logged 903 such warnings. The patch records the skipped non-final milestone once, while retaining `noticeDelivered: false`.

## Evidence

### Gateway startup and restart

I built this PR head and started the shipped `pnpm dev gateway run` CLI twice on an isolated loopback port with a synthetic CLI update run and restart sentinel in a temporary state directory. Both processes reached `gateway ready`; channels, providers, browser, canvas, and cron were disabled with the repository's test isolation flags. The same ledger and sentinel survived between boots; I did not reseed either one.

The following lines are extracted from the isolated Gateway JSON log, with only event time and message shown:

```text
2026-10-13T04:31:50.234Z gateway ready
2026-10-13T04:31:52.969Z lifecycle notice skipped: no delivery target
2026-10-13T04:32:36.818Z received SIGTERM; shutting down
2026-10-13T04:33:51.204Z gateway ready
2026-10-13T04:34:20.004Z received SIGTERM; shutting down
boot_1_skipped_notice_warnings=1
boot_2_skipped_notice_warnings=0
```

After each boot, a separate process reopened the on-disk ledger and saw `phase=verifying`, `status=running`, `noticeDelivered=false`, and exactly one `notice:verifying` step with `status=skipped` and `detail=no delivery target`. The update sentinel remained persisted across the restart. Both Gateways stopped before the ledger reads.

### Pre-fix comparison and compatibility

I reproduced the behavior with the production `finalizeRestartUpdateRun` entry point in separate Node processes, an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, an empty config, and a synthetic CLI update run in the latest-stable ledger. Each `recover` invocation below was a new process against the same on-disk database:

```text
Pre-fix bf58e95ee3, recovery 1: lifecycle notice skipped: no delivery target; noticeSteps=[]
Pre-fix bf58e95ee3, recovery 2: lifecycle notice skipped: no delivery target; noticeSteps=[]
Patched da19e52b90, recovery 1: lifecycle notice skipped: no delivery target; noticeSteps=[{status:"skipped",detail:"no delivery target"}]
Patched da19e52b90, recovery 2: no skipped-notice warning; noticeSteps=[{status:"skipped",detail:"no delivery target"}]
```

The run was created and persisted by the pre-fix build, then read and updated by the patched build without recreation or migration. Across both patched recovery processes it remained `phase: verifying`, `status: running`, and `noticeDelivered: false`. This proves the existing ledger format loads and the skipped receipt survives process restart. This exercise invoked the Gateway's production restart finalizer; it did not boot a full Gateway service.

The focused `src/gateway/update-run-notice.test.ts` suite passed on a later run: 5/5 tests in 103 seconds, including the new targetless-notice regression. An earlier sandbox denied SQLite subprocess startup (`spawnSync /usr/bin/node EPERM`); that environment failure did not recur. `git diff --check`, `oxfmt --check`, and `oxlint` passed on the changed files. The canonical autoreview helper reported no actionable P0–P2 findings. Full CI will run when the PR is marked ready for review.

prs.title: fix(agents): settle replaced subagents after restart
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An interrupted subagent can remain unresolved across every restart if its child session has been reset or replaced. Recovery repeatedly rejects the changed incarnation instead of settling the old task. Once that task is settled, parent reset can also refuse to finish because descendant cleanup still tries to stop the replacement child.

## User Impact

The old task stops with a specific reason delivered to its original parent, including when completion notifications were disabled or the parent already finished. Parent reset retires that pending private notice and completes without changing the replacement child or its descendants. Parent reset/cancellation protections remain in force; another restart does not replay the notice.

## Why This Change Was Made

Child-session authority and responsibility for the retained task are separate. A changed child incarnation revokes session effects, while the registry still owns settlement of the old task. Quiet restart notices use the captured original-parent identity independently of child-session effects, and parent findings retain the concrete stop reason.

Lifecycle cleanup now prepares its selection at the existing selection owner. For terminal tasks with recorded suppression of child-session effects, it retires the notice through the existing guarded requester-wake owner before child cancellation. Other tasks retain the normal incarnation checks. The old selection path is removed rather than retained alongside another policy. No schema or configuration change is needed; startup applies the repair to retained runs after an update.

## Evidence and Measurement

- Baseline recovery regression: restoring the original loader guard makes both changed-revision cases fail (`deferred` instead of `terminal`).
- Baseline real Gateway reproduction on the first PR head: replaced-child reset refused to finish because descendant cleanup rejected the replacement incarnation. The final candidate completes the same reset flow.
- Real managed-process Gateway proof with a synthetic HTTP Responses provider: **5/5 cases passed in 142.85 s**. Ordinary completion reached its recovery checkpoint in 10,850 ms; ordinary reset in 9,483 ms; replaced-child completion in 9,808 ms; replaced-child reset in 9,804 ms; replaced-child cancellation in 9,829 ms. These include startup and are not a live-Gateway latency comparison.
- Replaced-child completion delivers exactly one private continuation to the original parent session key and ID. The replacement child's complete saved entry remains unchanged. All five cases restart again after settlement and observe no replay.
- Reset controls stop an already-authorized pending provider request and observe **zero further provider requests** after revocation and the second restart. Cancellation holds preparation before provider I/O and observes **zero recovery requests**, plus zero later requests. Cancellation explicitly reports the refusal to alter a replacement child while stopping the parent.
- Earlier isolated Linux microbenchmark of the actual recovery/session-loader modules with synthetic I/O, 9 × 10,000 calls per case: normal recovery median **0.640 → 0.633 µs/call**, neutral within noise. Replaced child **2.155 → 0.407 µs/call**; before: 90,000 deferred results/warnings, after: 90,000 terminal results and zero warnings. This measures owner CPU/decision cost, not end-to-end delivery.
- Production LOC: **+78 net**. The growth implements two necessary correctness contracts: old-task settlement without replacement-child effects, and notice retirement without replacement-child cancellation. The selection logic moves to its existing owner to retain the cancellation module's size budget; there is no new module, dependency, cache, schema, or setting.

## Proof

- `pnpm test src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-reset.lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **12 passed**, 134.54 s including worker preparation; the two new cases took 5.66 s and 2.92 s. Its negative control verifies that unsuppressed child authority still blocks reset, while the suppressed case completes reset and never interrupts replacement-child admission.
- Earlier focused recovery/startup/notification proof: **137 tests passed**, 385.38 s including worker preparation. The new startup cases took 6.29 s and 5.70 s. After moving those cases into their existing helper for the file-size budget, their registration rerun passed in 56.85 s including preparation.
- `pnpm test:e2e:gateway test/gateway-subagent-restart.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — the real Gateway measurement above ran in an isolated Linux sandbox with synthetic state, restricted CPU/memory scheduling, and owned loopback ports. No production Gateway or data was touched. No Testbox/Crabbox leases were allocated.
- Changed-file `oxfmt`, syntax-focused repository lint, and `git diff --check` passed. Broad typecheck, lint, suites, E2E, and export/closure checks run in PR CI.
- Fresh independent review of the complete candidate: clean through P2.

The first follow-up CI run exposed three lane defects: notice-retirement persistence failures escaped the structured cleanup result, an eager registry import affected read-only subagent tools, and the suppression fixture used false instead of an absent flag. These were repaired without weakening authority or write-outcome guards. The rejected-write regression was reproduced locally, then passed with the reset controls (3 focused cases, 122.86 s including preparation); the subagent-tool file passed all 4 cases in 57.11 s. Current main already corrected the separate config-snapshot test import failure; the branch was rebased onto that fix rather than copying its commit. All 75 recovery tests passed after rebase in 156.03 s. The final real Gateway fixture uses current dispatch_action semantics; the retired tool_call name is removed. Fresh independent reviews of both the CI repairs and dispatch fixture are clean through P2. Final-head CI remains the broad gate.

Final-head [CI run 38347648580](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38347648580) passed on `9b70f89720a1c702a2370e0b3a9b4d9f35d8ee05` in **643 seconds**. Both CI and aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` states are successful. Exact-head ClawSweeper re-review accepted the real Gateway proof and reported no open findings. No inherited-failure exception or CI rerun was needed for the final head.

prs.title: feat(agents): end runs after confirmed final source replies
prs.body:
Related: #170147 (current-source completion subcase only).

## What Problem This Solves

A delivered final source reply could trigger another model request and an extra confirmation, even though the user had already received the complete response.

## User Impact

A confirmed final send, reply, thread reply, poll, or added reaction to the current source ends the run in automatic and message-tool delivery modes. Models may choose a final reaction as their complete reply. Progress (`final:false`), removals, no-op or failed reactions, dry runs, partial deliveries, and actions on other messages do not trigger this terminal action. Existing settled-turn handling of progress followed by empty output is unchanged.

Optional no-action turns retain their existing `NO_REPLY` guidance. Direct messages, mentions, commands, and accepted groups by default retain their visible-reply requirement. This does not change required/optional admission or the policy in #152786.

## Why This Change Was Made

The message delivery owner already knows whether an action reached the current source. Embedded and Codex-backed runs now consume that fact to finish after sibling tools settle and suppress later source text, errors, and mirrored assistant codas. Tool-authored replies awaiting delivery retain their separate whole-batch admission contract. Only the obsolete after-action token instructions are removed.

`NO_REPLY` and `HEARTBEAT_OK` parsing, stripping, and replay compatibility are unchanged. Production models and user-authored prompts, skills, and AGENTS files still emit these tokens. Any future removal must start with telemetry/counting and an explicit migration decision.

Codex's native tool handler marks tool calls as needing follow-up ([stream_events_utils.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/9f3d25588b3f0bdf452d4eda919f2c2365a89bba/codex-rs/core/src/stream_events_utils.rs#L321)); its loop combines that with pending input ([turn.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/9f3d25588b3f0bdf452d4eda919f2c2365a89bba/codex-rs/core/src/session/turn.rs#L548)) before stop handling ([turn.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/9f3d25588b3f0bdf452d4eda919f2c2365a89bba/codex-rs/core/src/session/turn.rs#L657)). I inspected these exact sibling-source files. This uses OpenClaw's existing host terminal-release mechanism; it does not change the Codex protocol.

## Evidence

The original terminal hook fails the real-Agent regression: a confirmed final source action makes two model requests instead of one; the `final:false` progress control passes. The repaired loop and source-delivery boundaries pass.

| Focused evidence | Result | Wall time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Core delivery, terminal resolution, stream/payload suppression, real-Agent loop (12 files) | 348 passed | Final three-file rerun 458.69s; other passing shards reused |
| Codex delivery/projector plus lifecycle (4 files) | 65 passed | Source/projector project 408.10s; lifecycle wrapper 212.87s |
| Messaging/groups and settled-turn finalization (3 files) | 14 passed | 207.28s + 156.80s |

New loop assertions execute in milliseconds; most elapsed time is cold compiled-worker preparation and imports. Source-restoration-invalidated runs are excluded. Core production typecheck, formatting, max-lines, line-cap, assertion safety, timeout-race, mock-export, config-doc and plugin-inventory checks pass. Isolated Codex autoreview of this committed head is scoped-clean through P2. Full build, remaining type/lint checks, heartbeat/cron checks, and native comparison are being completed before readiness.

### Why optional silence guidance stays

A separate 1,800-trial probe on this Mac tested compact source-derived prompts through direct provider APIs and native Ollama, including synthetic successful tool results. Clean no-text turns were 0/60 for Sonnet, 20/60 for Haiku, 28/30 for Opus (two U+200B responses), 60/60 for each tested OpenAI interface/model, and 0/60 for each Qwen model. Literal `NO_REPLY` was substantially more reliable: Sonnet 60/60, Opus 30/30, Haiku 58/60, and Qwen 8B 47/60. Qwen 4B often exhausted its output budget; these results do not establish its eventual completion behavior. This is direct API evidence, separate from the full Gateway comparison below.

The probe also observed duplicate confirmations after successful source actions. Host termination avoids asking for that continuation at all. It does not rely on every model reliably producing an empty assistant message.

### Prompt changes

Only after-action silence advice is removed; optional no-action token guidance remains. Representative changes:

```diff
-- After visible `message(send)`, final ONLY NO_REPLY.
+- A confirmed final message or added final reaction to the current source completes the reply; never repeat it in text.
-For react, set true only when the user explicitly requested the reaction to the current source message as the complete response.
+For react, set true when adding a reaction to the current source message is your complete response.
-If no text reply is needed, including after a reaction or other action, reply with exactly "NO_REPLY" ...
+If no text reply is needed, reply with exactly "NO_REPLY" ...
```

Snapshots were regenerated with `pnpm prompt:snapshots:gen`; generated outputs were not hand-edited. Generator estimates (text / including dynamic tools):

| Scenario | Before | After | Delta |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Telegram DM | 6,895 / 24,801 | 6,912 / 24,814 | +17 / +13 |
| Discord group | 7,225 / 25,280 | 7,242 / 25,293 | +17 / +13 |
| Heartbeat | 6,980 / 25,259 | 6,997 / 25,272 | +17 / +13 |

These are rough `ceil(chars/4)` estimates, not provider billing counts.

### Native local-model comparison

Pending: native Ollama `qwen3:4b` and `qwen3:8b`, four scenarios with N=10 each on the pinned main base and branch. Real model calls pass through isolated OpenClaw Gateways and a synthetic QA channel. No operator Gateway or state is used. Measurements cover final reactions, final source sends, ordinary DM answers, and required group mentions, including visible output, token leakage, duplicate/canned replies, missing answers, wall time, and prompt tokens. All proof is macOS-only.

### Change size

Production: +200/-160 lines (net +40). Tests: +777/-240; generated snapshots: +46/-46; docs: +6/-4. The positive production delta carries canonical delivery completion through the Codex lifecycle and output projector, and suppresses later embedded output across stream/final/error paths. Nearby obsolete branches were removed; further reduction would obscure these ownership boundaries.

### Follow-ups and scope

- Sending to another chat satisfying the source turn remains undecided and out of scope; #170147's primary reproduction is not claimed fixed.
- A generic `done` tool and changes to required/optional policy remain undecided.
- #156181 proposes honoring explicit `NO_REPLY` on required turns, an opposite policy direction. #162342 is an issue proposing separate cron clean-empty and deliberate-silence outcomes; that outcome/status design remains separate.

prs.title: fix(sqlite): best-effort snapshot reads fail when snapshot cleanup stays busy
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: best-effort SQLite snapshot reads fail with "SQLite snapshot lease cleanup did not complete" when the private snapshot can't be removed right away. On native Windows Bun, snapshots stay busy (EBUSY) after logical close.

## User Impact

User impact: read-only state opens, `withSqliteSnapshotSource`, the update/Doctor guard, and ownership inspection now return their successful result when best-effort temp cleanup is deferred. The existing "SQLite read-only snapshot cleanup failed" warning is still logged, and the directory stays registered for exit cleanup. Strict (signal-scoped) snapshot cleanup is unchanged and still fails with its cause.

`openclaw gateway status --deep` on Windows Bun is covered by #169572, merged earlier: schema preflight requests strict cleanup and defers only EBUSY after a successful read. This PR covers the remaining best-effort consumers.

## Why This Change Was Made

#168859 merged lease release and preparation close into one helper, `releaseSnapshot`. That widened a throw #160946 had scoped to preparation close, so a best-effort refusal became fatal and lost its cause. Best-effort bases resolve `false` only after warning and keeping the directory registered, and strict bases already throw with their cause before this point. Lease cleanup therefore returns `false` again and does not close the producer, so custody stays with the cleanup registry.

Preparation `startClose()` still throws on `false`: a close can't discharge producer custody that removal never released. Orphan cleanup (no remaining lease) keeps its existing rejection. Synchronous `cleanup()` after a refused async cleanup now reports `false` instead of `true`.

## Evidence

- Regression test in `sqlite-readonly-location.cleanup.test.ts`: a real best-effort `adoptPreparedLocation` base goes through the single-flight lease with `EBUSY` on removal. Before the fix, it fails with the exact production error. After the fix, `cleanupAsync()` resolves `false`, the warning fires once, the bytes survive, and `cleanupSnapshotOperations()` reclaims them.
- `pnpm test` over all 22 sqlite-readonly-location, sqlite-snapshot-source, sqlite-snapshot-single-flight and openclaw-state-db-readonly test files: 3 shards passed, 102 tests, about 66 s wall time. The new test adds a few milliseconds and no timers.
- oxlint, oxfmt and `tsgo -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.infra.json` are clean. Independent Codex autoreview at P0–P2 came back scoped-clean.
- Gap: native Windows Bun 1.4.2 A/B proof was attempted on two AWS Windows leases and a Parallels Windows 11 VM. All three hit infrastructure failures (SSH loss, then guest-exec stalls) before either the old or new code ran, so there is no Windows runtime evidence here.

prs.title: feat(macos): guide missing native permissions in chat
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Native Mac commands report missing privacy permissions as unrelated text errors, so agents retry or send people hunting through System Settings.

## User Impact

Missing native permissions now produce an inline Grant card. It names the affected Mac and permissions, uses the existing native grant/settings/confirmation/relaunch flows, and offers **Try again** only after the native snapshot reports effective access. The agent is told to wait for user confirmation.

The error contract is additive: `PERMISSION_MISSING` with `{ capabilities, state }`, where state is `not-determined`, `denied`, `restart-required`, `stale-grant`, or `disabled-in-openclaw`. Computer Control reports Accessibility, Event Posting, Screen Recording, and its local toggle together. Commands stay discoverable while disabled; execution remains gated. Camera enumeration requires only the existing OpenClaw camera toggle (`cameraEnabled`); capture/PTZ separately require macOS Camera access (`camera`). Grant therefore enables enumeration without requesting capture access. Automatic notification overlay fallback retains its behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

`PermissionManager` owns native checks and typed failures. The Gateway preserves the error through node, computer, and exec tools and publishes it on the existing, run-scoped notice stream. Live notices and persisted tool results render the same card, including when ordinary tool output is hidden. Existing app confirmation remains authoritative; each click handles only the current primary remediation, so stale Accessibility does not accidentally trigger a lower-priority Screen Recording relaunch; a remote node cannot grant permissions on the Mac showing its card. Permission owners carry the current document/node check through awaited authorization reads to the final OS request. First-use Accessibility remains explicitly requestable; an unsuccessful Event Posting request opens Settings and offers conditional relaunch recovery for cached denials.

### Desktop shell contract

Cards consume the shell-neutral optional capability `NativeDeviceSettingsCapability.resolvePermission(request): Promise<void>`. The request is `{ nodeId, nodeName?, command, capabilities, state }`. The Mac adapter sends `{ type: "resolve-permission", request }` through the existing native device-settings transport; the Tauri shell can implement the same capability with its own transport. Cards contain no WebKit/platform detection.

Snapshots add optional `device.nodeId` and optional permission-entry `state`. Contract-1 `permissions.entries` retains the released seven IDs; optional `permissions.additionalEntries` carries Event Posting, and the current UI validates and merges it. The host validates the active local node before effects, including after native consent. Resolving the action promise only acknowledges dispatch. Snapshot changes, local capability switches, and location mode determine grant completion; **Try again** sends a short user message through the existing chat path. Without a matching shell capability, the card directs the user to the OpenClaw Mac app on the target device.

The Gateway advertises `node-permission-errors` in hello capabilities. Native and headless node transports send typed error details only when this capability is present, preserving the closed invoke-result shape accepted by older Gateways. Both the direct native socket and app-hosted child pipe preserve details.

### Remaining live proof

The lead owns the signed-app TCC/consent/relaunch/retry, node/document authority-negative, and stable-upgrade VM proof. Local Swift execution and synthetic UI proof do not replace that live test. No operator app, LaunchAgent, or live Gateway was changed.

## Evidence

- **Executed native tests:** 35 app functions and one shared transport function pass (41 parameterized cases). PermissionManager/location: 10 functions, 37.82 s; device-settings bridge: 9, 4.13 s; runtime permission errors: 4, 2.66 s; camera PTZ: 5, 2.44 s; manifest discoverability: 6, 3.17 s; app-hosted worker pipe: 1, 6.21 s; shared negotiated-details test with legacy/current variants: 1, 27.88 s. Both `DEVELOPER_DIR` and SDK were pinned to `/Applications/Xcode.app`. App/shared test builds pass in 790.02 s / 525.09 s wall. An enclosing OS sandbox denied operator files/services and network; all task `.build` directories were removed afterward. This proves native owners with injected OS services, not actual TCC consent.
- **Fresh native camera/bridge proof:** on final camera-fix sources, 24 functions across five suites pass (38 parameterized cases, 62.44 s wrapper / 1.018 s test bodies), including all nine device-settings bridge functions. Pinned-Xcode app/test build passes in 788.09 s wall / 753.60 s Swift. Final Swift formatting/lint pass (2.62 s / 6.10 s); changed-test formatting/lint pass (0.99 s / 1.59 s).
- **Camera recovery regression:** the updated card file passes 12 cases (73.80 s full wall / 31.46 s Vitest); both new cases failed on the previous renderer. Enumeration becomes retryable while Camera TCC is absent, while capture stays blocked. Canonical type-aware UI lint passes (140.84 s).
- **Focused UI:** 16 tests pass across permission-card, persisted-history, and voice-reconciliation files (93.52 s wrapper, 69.91 s Vitest). The complete native-device-settings file passes 68 cases (16.97 s), with canonical typed lint passing in 26.02 s after an unchanged-test relocation to avoid a main insertion conflict. UI types pass (961.66 s including artifact-lock wait); canonical type-aware lint on the changed transcript owners passes (77.73 s). Fresh synthetic mock-Gateway flow passes (42.06 s): Grant only dispatches, refreshed native state enables retry, and retry sends `I granted Screen Recording, try again.`
- **Generated/build proof:** boot-manifest generation passes (157.36 s), grouped UI build passes (106.83 s). Chat uses 30 requests and New Session 28, below 35; startup CSS is 50,160 B, below 51,200 B. The canonical Gateway E2E runtime prerequisite passes in 31m 24.1s, including native loading/Doctor-closure verification of 54 built plugin modules and final build stamps.
- **Ratchets:** max-lines, line-cap, assertion safety, database worker/dialect, timeout races, mock exports, config/docs, plugin inventory, protocol, native locales, and Lit migration all pass. Prompt snapshots regenerate with no source change, token delta **0**. Changed Swift formatting/lint pass (15.73 s / 13.83 s).
- **Retained owner proof:** prior focused Gateway/agent/node-host/protocol tests cover typed errors, authenticated notices, model guidance, serialization, and negotiated old-Gateway compatibility. The continuation's source changes are the existing transcript-adapter placement, typed fixture repairs, removal of the unused camera authorization owner, isolated Swift defaults, voice-caption relocation, and regenerated boot metadata.
- **Prior live transport:** `pnpm openclaw --profile zc-perm gateway call node.invoke` exercised isolated CLI → Gateway port 19813 → headless node, `system.run` with argv `["/usr/bin/true"]` and `needsScreenRecording: true`. It returned `PERMISSION_MISSING`, `{ capabilities: ["screenRecording"], state: "not-determined" }`, node/command projection, and no-retry guidance. This ran at prior head `416ccd8fa2a3e3e5c754c04dc7a2e0421979b6d3`; no current signed-app TCC proof is claimed.

Current head: `8e2bec12aff743c47b3882f03bfbee72b94be5c8`. Committed-branch autoreview is **scoped-clean**, with no actionable P0–P2 findings. This head fixes ClawSweeper's sole code finding on `c112b53`: the node-invoke fixture now republishes its runtime config snapshot after isolated-state replacement. Final focused proof passes (341.20 s launcher); the equivalent import variant passed all 28 tests (266.39 s). The existing permission assertions and cleanup are retained. A prior local teardown finding was disproved by the complete owner: close returns before permission preflight; the final review included the intact source and confirmed the bypass.

### Pinned CI attribution

CI run [38325822517](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38325822517) completed on `8e2bec12aff743c47b3882f03bfbee72b94be5c8`: **90 success, 16 skipped, 6 failure**, including the aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate`. The five failed test jobs contain **28 cases across eight files**. All final failed-job logs were fetched once or reused from the prior lane.

Fresh comparisons use immutable branch base `d4820c404e000fbcbf608240260368d044363abb`. This is the branch's last main ancestor; the branch has no later main merge. prs.title: fix: plugin before_tool_call hooks are skipped under openclaw agent exec
prs.body:
Closes #158824

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `before_tool_call` plugin hooks never run when an agent is started with `openclaw agent exec`, so a policy plugin that blocks a tool call is silently skipped and the call goes through.

## User Impact

User impact: plugins that guard tool calls (for example, refusing a destructive shell command) now apply in headless `openclaw agent exec` runs as they already do elsewhere.

## Why This Change Was Made

A headless run loads its plugin registry scoped to the run without activating a process-wide root, so the global hook runner was never created and tool-call policy found no runner to dispatch through. The run now makes sure the runner exists; the runner already reads the current run's scoped registry on every dispatch, and keeps the same fail-closed policy for `before_tool_call`, `before_agent_run` and `before_install`.

## Evidence

- New regression test in `src/agents/runtime-plugins.hooks.integration.test.ts`: a plugin with a blocking `before_tool_call`, no process registry activated, then a tool call through the run's registry. It fails without the fix (`blocked` is false) and passes with it. On main 1844d933: without the fix, 1 failed / 8 passed (`expected false to be true`); with it, 9 passed. Cost: the new test runs in 19 ms; `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/runtime-plugins.hooks.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` takes about 21 s wall for the whole file.
- Neighbouring tests pass with the fix (on 813169e2): `hook-runner-global` 6, `state-migrations.outbound-preparation` 6, `agent-tools.before-tool-call.{decision,embedded-mode,network-error,voice-authority}` 18/26/11/6, `runtime-plugins.{channel-ownership,config-capture,decisions,memory-corpus,work}` and `runtime-plugins.test.ts` 12/1/1/2/2/36. Not run: `runtime-plugins.context-engine.integration`, which rebuilds `dist` on a dirty tree.
- End to end (on an earlier main, 813169e2, with a built `dist`): `openclaw agent exec --json` with a before_tool_call policy plugin loaded from the config, asked to run `git push --force origin main` in a scratch repo whose `main` was rewritten, against a local bare remote.
  - Released 2026.9.6: the exec tool ran the command (0 tool failures), and the remote's `main` moved to the rewritten commit.
  - With this fix: the plugin blocked the call (1 tool failure, the model reported it was refused), and the remote's `main` was unchanged.

prs.title: fix(announce): match Slack DM delivery receipts to source users
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a Slack completion delivered through the message tool to a verified DM conversation could still be reported as `visible_reply_missing` when the source target was recorded as the corresponding Slack user. It also preserves confirmed source progress delivery when final-recipient verification times out.

Fixes #144885

## Why This Change Was Made

Completion evidence resolves provider-native delivery identities before final verification starts, so a confirmed progress receipt is recorded independently of a later final lookup. Confirmed source receipts are evaluated before optional lookups, native lookups run concurrently, and the verifier keeps an independent finite deadline that aborts losing lookups after settlement. The direct-delivery owner is checked again after asynchronous receipt classification so a source session that loses ownership during Slack verification cannot settle the completion as delivered. The built-in Slack fetch removes the SDK's explicit empty body workaround, while a caller-supplied fetch receives its original request init unchanged.

## User Impact

Slack DM completions sent to the verified source user settle as delivered without weakening off-target or ambiguous-delivery checks. A stalled provider lookup cannot hold completion settlement beyond its verification budget, erase confirmed progress, or remain active after a successful match. A source completion whose owner changes during recipient verification is returned as an intentional non-delivery and does not trigger a fallback send. Custom Slack fetch implementations retain the request body supplied by the Web API SDK.

## Evidence

- On exact head `e4bbdfa141fae90772cecd15b9ec92e0d692d0ef` rebased onto `72ccf43fdc6fbe8f4534b84b86f1c8a8909032f5`, the nine affected announcement, outbound, and Slack test files passed (182 tests).


- Exact-head production-boundary proof at `e4bbdfa141fae90772cecd15b9ec92e0d692d0ef` reran the three committed localhost drivers through production announcement delivery, recipient classification, Slack route resolution, and the Web API client. The temporary Vitest wrapper used test overrides only at the Gateway dispatch and requester-session reader boundaries. It used a dummy loopback token, contacted no Slack service, and sent no production messages.

- The reviewed GitHub `check-lint` failure came from an unused `max-lines` suppression in `extensions/slack/src/channel.ts`; this follow-up removes that directive without changing runtime behavior.

- Current-head localhost results: the matching receipt delivered directly; wrong-recipient and revoked-owner cases were rejected without fallback; stalled lookups closed after a match or cancellation. This is localhost-backed production-boundary evidence, not a live Gateway or external Slack delivery claim.

- Negative-control: at pre-fix base `84b6b0858f387c5b3fbd3e4bc2bc72152b059692`, a temporary assertion called the existing `hasMessagingToolDeliveryToSource` with a final Slack receipt for `D000000001` and source target `user:U000000001` (same account and thread). The pre-fix implementation returned `false` (`expected false to be true`); on this head, the committed `credits a provider-native conversation after exact recipient resolution` regression test passes with the verified `D… → user:U…` mapping.

- CI failure attribution for run `38114301154`: `check-prod-types` and `check-test-types-core-1` reported the same `TS2353` in `src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop-startup.test-support.ts`, outside this PR's diff. Upstream commit `69d80d5fc82b8d0c177eea453cac2e495d8ba8ca` fixes that stale fixture, and is an ancestor of the current rebase target.

- **Maintainer decision requested:** This patch adds an optional cooperative `AbortSignal` to the public channel resolver so core can cancel provider lookups after verification settles. Existing resolvers remain compatible when they ignore it. Please confirm this additive API contract before merge.

prs.title: fix: allow test builds in containers without systemd
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: cloud test preparation refuses to rebuild an isolated checkout when the Linux container has no systemd manager.

## User Impact

Developers can prepare and run cloud tests without a nonexistent invoking Gateway blocking the build. Existing managed Gateway definitions and unavailable or running managers remain guarded.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the complete inventory's native manager-presence check before creating the synthetic invoking binding. Missing local manager endpoints establish absence; advertised managers, access failures, installed units, and overlapping live build outputs retain their existing checks.

## Evidence

- The original producer reproduced the exact unknown-artifact refusal in this cloud environment; a real verified-fence assertion failed before the change and returned `refuse: false` afterward.
- Live `OPENCLAW_TSDOWN_MAX_OLD_SPACE_MB=4096 node scripts/prepare-vitest-runtime.mjs --require-current-head` completed successfully in 164.6 seconds through all eight build steps, including the private QA runtime and 96 external plugins. The explicit heap uses the supported option because this cloud cgroup namespace hides the process memory limit from the planner.
- Regression and sibling daemon shard: 35 passed in 121.89 seconds wall time (114.02 seconds Vitest duration; cold worker compilation dominated, new regression cases took 23ms and 9ms). Native `tsgo:core` passed; formatting passed; targeted type-aware lint passed. CI run 38347334094 passed on the exact head; its changed-node job completed in 375 seconds including setup/build/tests. Required GitHub gates passed and the PR merged through normal auto-squash.
- Independent source review found no actionable P0–P2 issues. The canonical autoreview helper could not authenticate in this cloud session; an independent reviewer inspected the full discovery, fence, command-reader, and systemd transport owners instead.

prs.title: fix(agents): retain admitted routes for native model selection
prs.body:
Account-only models admitted through the Codex catalog can be rejected before inference because their transport route is lost. Regression commit `5d6cf7424de268b0354e3b1c4bfae81e20bdd99c` (#168789) removed the published-catalog handoff. Native capability rows intentionally omit transport fields, while the admission capture retains route evidence separately; projecting the runtime snapshot loses the object identity used to retrieve that evidence.

Reuse the existing borrowed admission snapshot when it shares the projected snapshot's catalog identity. This preserves the route, OAuth profile forwarding, and runtime compatibility evidence captured for the turn. Auth planning and harness support checks remain unchanged, including rejection of unsupported routes. No new catalog owner, database access, or model allowlist is introduced.

The regression exercises catalog capture followed by snapshot projection through runtime preparation and verifies native ownership, the subscription route, OAuth profile forwarding, and compatible runtime IDs. Scope: two files, **+92/−3** overall (**+17/−2** production).

Validation:

- One isolated Codex review completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Formatting, whitespace checks, and normal commit hooks passed.
- Local lint stopped during configuration loading because `eslint-plugin-solid` could not be resolved. Exact-candidate [hosted proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38347218098/job/115131307024) subsequently passed targeted type-aware lint with zero warnings or errors.
- The same hosted job passed the complete ownership test file, 32/32 with no skips, including the new admitted-route regression (99.47 seconds Vitest, 139.53 seconds runner wall).

Candidate and test-file blob were verified from the hosted log.
- Ordinary [CI 38347219340](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38347219340) completed successfully: 35 jobs passed and 26 were skipped. Build artifacts, production types, all selected test types, lint, source contracts, boundaries, and the aggregate gate passed. prs.title: fix(doctor): prevent Codex registration failures during checks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` exits with a Codex plugin registration error when runtime config has not yet been prepared.

## User Impact

Doctor can inspect enabled Codex tools without reporting `Runtime config is not prepared` as a plugin failure. No configuration, schema, permissions, defaults, or plugin API changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor already owns the repaired configuration, but its contribution checks can register plugins before publishing that configuration for runtime readers. Prepare it through the existing async runtime-config owner after the config flow and before contributions. This preserves the strict runtime reader introduced in #169714 rather than adding a fallback to Codex or the plugin runtime.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes in the changed files.

## Evidence

- Built base `f9d5447c5946` and candidate `ddd777e2c8c9` with `pnpm build`.
- Real `pnpm openclaw --profile <isolated-profile> doctor --fix --non-interactive --no-workspace-suggestions`: base reported Codex registration failures and exited **1**; candidate completed with no plugin load error and exited **0**. Each run confirmed its own config, state, and database paths first. The fixture uses an enabled bundled Codex plugin and a local static model definition; no live user state.
- Started a separate candidate Gateway. Its live `plugins.list` RPC reported Codex runtime state **active**. Stopped the Gateway afterward.
- Regression test fails before the fix (plugin status `error`), then all **3 tests pass** in `pnpm test src/flows/doctor-health.plugin-load.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (29.19s runner wall time, 25.23s Vitest duration). Targeted Oxfmt and Oxlint pass.
- Simplification pass: one existing publication owner, no fallback or new abstraction. Production **+2/-0** lines; tests **+47/-0**. The two production lines are the import and required preparation call.
- No model request or channel-delivery path changed; real-provider/channel checks are not applicable. The separate `update repair` wrapper was not exercised; its Doctor checks use this same flow.

<details>
<summary>Observed terminal evidence (paths redacted; unrelated warnings omitted)</summary>

Base `f9d5447c5946`, after the initial legacy fixture was repaired and a local static model definition was configured so tool-schema inspection runs:

```text
$ pnpm openclaw --profile pdoctorcodexbase doctor --fix --non-interactive --no-workspace-suggestions
[plugins] codex failed during register from <worktree>/dist/extensions/codex/index.js: Error: Runtime config is not prepared. Await captureRuntimeConfigAsyncReader()() first.
[error] core/doctor/workspace-status plugins.entries.codex - Plugin codex: plugin failed during register: Error: Runtime config is not prepared. Await captureRuntimeConfigAsyncReader()() first. (<worktree>/dist/extensions/codex/index.js)
└  Doctor finished with plugin load errors.
EXIT_CODE=1
```

Candidate `ddd777e2c8c9`, same configuration with separate state, home, workspace and port:

```text
$ pnpm openclaw --profile pdoctorcodexcand doctor --fix --non-interactive --no-workspace-suggestions
└  Doctor complete.
EXIT_CODE=0
```

Candidate Gateway, started with `pnpm openclaw --profile pdoctorcodexcand gateway run --port 19644 --bind loopback`:

```text
[gateway] ready
$ pnpm openclaw --profile pdoctorcodexcand gateway call plugins.list --json
```

Codex entry excerpt from the live RPC response:

```json
{"id":"codex","runtime":{"state":"active"}}
```

```text
[gateway] received SIGTERM; shutting down
[shutdown] completed cleanly in 120ms
```

</details>

Merge danger: **two-way door**; a revert fully removes this change. No new persisted representation or migration. Blast radius is Doctor's runtime-backed plugin checks; Gateway startup is unchanged and was smoke-tested with Codex enabled.

prs.title: perf(sqlite): transfer execution admission authority
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Writer admission cannot move off the Gateway thread while execution lifetime exists only in host-local flags. This prerequisite transfers exact logical and native execution authority for warm agent database operations.

## Change and Impact

Canonical shared cells replace logical retirement/revocation, native retirement and borrower release flags. Failed logical cleanup may reopen only the closing state; explicit revocation and native retirement remain permanent. Borrower release denies new calls and generation claims while already accepted operations retain logical/native custody through outcome and receipt settlement.

Warm descriptors are privately bound to actual admission objects and carried by the process-shared broker. Native stages recheck the same cells before requesting host admission and after receiving the grant. The service worker checks the same conjunction. Cold creation, readiness, deletion, policy, physical/process/schema custody and final host COMMIT remain host-required. This PR does not claim that chat ACKs are independent of main-thread availability.

Upstream #170557 moved the standalone service factory/direct probe into test support. The rebase preserves that complete cutover and extends only its test helper for descriptor proof; no production test seam is restored. No schema, persistent-state, config, dependency, public SDK or update migration changes. Restart constructs fresh authority.

Production LOC delta: +123 (152 added, 29 removed, excluding tests/test support/docs). Growth implements the explicitly requested transferable lifetime and private transport contracts; superseded flags are removed.

## Measurement

Exact baseline `4f8c8c58fc88fec9086bad7c4a6c6c475c3ad2be`, candidate `607c90d588fc4e6cf7f47b77e4a5fb5abadd2988`, patch SHA-256 `18941beac59c4c6a86817cf4f621260b1a1e6461ebad0ccf112e91f84778ba4d`. Four balanced ABBA/BAAB blocks each of lane-860 ACK and lane-830 writer on the Team sandbox:16 legs/protocol,320 successful ACK sends and800 verified writer turns per version, plus3,200 history reads and800 metadata updates/probe rounds. Zero endpoint/control-plane failures, admission refusals or unclean final exits. All commands used scoped CPU64–127 and64GiB memory, owned synthetic state and loopback ports; Team ran measurements only.

| Metric | Before | After | Paired ratio [95% interval] |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| ACK mean, ms |816.37|862.42|1.059 [0.849,1.322]|
| ACK p50 / p99, ms |903.09 /1341.58|937.92 /1356.27|p99:1.059 [0.929,1.207]|
| Writer main CPU/turn, ms |245.893|250.724|1.020 [0.941,1.105]|
| Writer throughput, turns/s |3.434|3.352|0.976 [0.905,1.054]|
| Transaction delivery mean, ms |0.803|0.819|1.019 [0.875,1.187]|
| FIFO hold p99, ms |35.280|36.580|1.045 [0.955,1.143]|

Neutral within measured block variability, with slower point estimates disclosed: ACK+5.6%, writer CPU+2.0%, throughput−2.4%, transaction delivery+2.0%. Four independent blocks are the replication units; paired intervals cross parity. No speedup or tight noninferiority claim. This explicitly requested prerequisite lands under the neutral-result rule.

Production native windows carried the execution contract:26,988 ACK and87,495 writer admission starts; cold creating generations remain host-owned. All starts carried broker custody. Service RPC counters were zero, so this is contract use rather than off-thread service rollout. Stress probes degraded800/800 on both versions despite successful endpoints.

Source/runtime and18 frozen harness files were verified before/after. All16 writer exits were code0; signal-to-exit-handler completion baseline616–844ms, candidate622–981ms; no pending markers. The campaign used symmetric15-second writer teardown from calibration onward with durable exit sidecars, no comparison retries or discarded legs. Earlier4a59 measurements remain historical: one candidate exceeded an initial2-second teardown after successful turns; that unexplained late finalization is retained, not reclassified as a pass. Current results use the fresh exact-head campaign.

## Evidence

Fresh independent reviews, each given only the diff and architecture design, are clean through P2, including the resolved rebase. Prior focused owner proof passed: 33 worker-admission tests48.48s;17 lifecycle tests37.91s;24 selected integrity/service tests67.83s;20 closure checks50.88s. On the rebased source, seven focused worker-admission/service cases passed in64.98s. Changed-file formatting/syntax lint and export-name guard pass; 20 rebased closure checks passed in137.87s.

Actual owner tests cover accepted writes after borrower release, revocation after host validation with native rollback, late old descriptors after retirement/service restart, and logical reopening after failed cleanup without reviving the old native generation. Removing only the final native recheck made the regression commit a write; exact restored source passed. Host COMMIT and receipt semantics are unchanged.

Current-head CI [38345495261](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38345495261) completed 94 jobs in530s. All Node tests, UI E2E, production types, other type stripes, lint/build/docs, security and the corrected authored-evidence check passed. Its only leaf red is config-preflight-snapshot.test.ts TS2724: upstream removed the readConfigPreflightSnapshot export while the untouched test still imports it. Unchanged main4f8c8c58 reproduces the same missing function at runtime (one focused case failed,18 skipped,95.22s wrapper). Test and module blobs are identical in that baseline, CI parent17929e42 and tested mergef2baf954. The classifier's older main run predates the upstream removal; this is independently reproduced inherited evidence, not a green CI claim. No CI rerun or branch update to chase green.

The previous test-only Promise annotation error was fixed; the prior unclassified UI timeout passes on current-head CI. No Testbox/Crabbox lease or local broad gate is used.

Next owner: lexical maintenance scope/frame/claim authority, followed by shared physical read admission and exclusion/seal generations, one PR each.

prs.title: fix(codex): refresh app access for default October scheduled jobs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes default owner jobs continuing to use a stale captured app cap after the owner enables a supported app.

## User Impact

Default owner jobs use current admitted app policy. Explicitly restricted jobs retain their captured ceilings, and removed or disabled apps remain unavailable.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use current app policy only when the normalized owner-default marker and actual run native-tool eligibility are both present. Keep runtime identity admission, current inventory, per-tool approval policy and explicit restrictions in force.

This is PR 5 of a seven-part October beta compatibility review. Its base is `codex/october-review-04-automation-watchdog` and its diff contains one original fix commit, `0522ce1d35f9d97110a69cfe81c0b14427792c8d`. The first review base is `v2026.10.1-beta.1` plus four carried ports. The seven fixes were previously pushed directly to a candidate branch; this PR makes the existing patch available for normal CI and independent review. Historical pushes and author-run checks do not count as completed PR review or CI.

## Evidence

### Restricted-job disposition and remaining limit

The newly admitted-app branch requires **both** actual native eligibility and issuer `allowOwnerToolDefaults === true`. For an explicit finite tool cap, native eligibility remains false. The false-native control above supplies a current new app plus an opted-in envelope and observes only the captured Calendar app admitted; the new app's config is disabled. The captured app/tool intersection for restricted runs remains authoritative. The original evidence stopped at source/projection. The installed native composition below now applies the real persisted-job projection to Codex 0.153.4: the finite schedule's valid new-app callable is not exposed and produces zero connector I/O, while the same inventory/callable works for the owner-default sibling. No shared job, account or staging permission was changed. The separate installed same-job positive and current-policy-withdrawal controls below remain the specific real dispatch evidence.

### Inspectable current authority boundary follow-up

At combined head `c4e9869318abc768529140de3e627a637c1fe64a`, a temporary secretless fixture called the **actual `prepareCodexAttemptRuntime` entry**. It did not substitute the admission helper. Account/profile mismatches rejected before both client prewarm and the client factory. A third control changed the prepared account during the awaited auth-binding step and also rejected before those boundaries.

Results and asserted recorder counts:

```text
PASS rejects account change before client prewarm or factory
PASS rejects profile change before client prewarm or factory
PASS rejects during-awaited-binding change before client prewarm or factory
prewarm calls: 0; client factory calls: 0 (each denied case)
3 passed; no native thread/turn or connector request started
```

Auth-binding completion and prewarm/factory were synthetic recorders; this proves runtime ordering and principal admission, not a live provider credential revocation. All later runtime fields were deliberately absent in the negative fixture, so accidental progression would fail rather than silently use a fake provider. The fixture was removed and tracked source remained clean.

Existing production native MCP adapter/client controls were also executed on this head, recording actual JSON-RPC transport writes through `createNativeMcpRuntime` and its real client. Under overload backoff, allowed calls produced two writes; revoking owner or per-call grant produced one original write and **zero forbidden retry writes**, with `CodexAppServerScopedRequestRejectedError`. Native tool, catalog and resource cases all passed. This covers retained-handle/retry fencing using synthetic grants and in-memory transport, not provider OAuth invalidation.

```text
PASS native tool retry: current owner/grant -> retry permitted
PASS native tool retry: owner revoked -> retry refused
PASS native tool retry: grant revoked -> retry refused
PASS native catalog/resource retry: owner revoked -> retry refused
cron persistence + executor: 34 passed
native MCP authority + current-owner app controls: 10 passed
native serial wrapper: 44 passed; wall38.24s
```

The four-file command was `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-mcp-app.authority.test.ts src/cron/store.definition-integrity.test.ts src/cron/isolated-agent/run.tools-allow.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/scheduled-app-authority.owner-defaults.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. The temporary runtime plus Slack final-write proof wrapper passed five cases in30.79s; it did not start a Gateway or mutate a shared bot.

### Installed native approval and app-exposure composition

Executed at combined review head `3590f39daf1be817be59d0bc789ec9e2e1e53ddb`, using verified **codex-cli 0.153.4**. The test calls the real `captureScheduledCodexAppAuthority`, saves the issued envelope/job through the SDK SQLite cron store, closes the DB and reloads it, derives native eligibility through production `shouldEnableCodexAppServerNativeToolSurface` using that reloaded cap, then calls the production scheduled app-policy intersection. Its output patch is passed unchanged into the actual CLI's normal `thread/start` + `turn/start` RPCs.

Identity, inventory/current config, job definition and Responses/MCP transports are synthetic. The loopback Responses fixture emits the actual advertised namespaced MCP callable. The MCP recorder **has no permission logic**: every received `tools/call` is counted and succeeds. The CLI's production app configuration, native tool exposure and consent gates decide which requests reach it. Direct `mcpServer/tool/call` RPC is not used. Native consent requests are recorded and declined by the unattended fixture; this is not claimed as execution of OpenClaw's interactive-input handler. Each CLI has an isolated home and a loopback-only macOS egress sandbox; no real credentials/model inference/provider access/shared bot changes occur.

Terminal/recorder results:

```text
actual Codex CLI: 0.153.4
current production capture/store/reload/intersection: 6 scenarios generated
ASK annotated read:                  connector calls=1, native consent requests=0, completed
captured prompt, current relaxed:    connector calls=0, native consent requests=1, declined
current explicit prompt:             connector calls=0, native consent requests=1, declined
readOnly + destructive conflict:     connector calls=0, native consent requests=1, declined
persisted finite cap, added app:      connector calls=0, target not exposed, completed
persisted owner default, added app:   connector calls=1, native consent requests=0, completed
6/6 expected native outcomes; every synthetic runtime/server stopped and scratch removed
```

The three consent controls report native `user rejected MCP tool call`; they do not silently auto-approve a prompt. The captured-prompt control uses an explicit finite job cap, retaining the captured ceiling even after current native policy relaxes. The two added-app controls have **identical native tool inventory** and the same creator-side Calendar-only capture. Actual native eligibility is true for the reloaded owner-default `['*']` job and false for the finite job. The production result enables the new app only in the default case. The CLI advertises and executes its native callable in that positive sibling; in the finite sibling it does not advertise it, and forcing that same valid callable returns `unsupported call` before connector I/O. This rules out an invalid tool name masquerading as a forbidden-schedule success.

There are meaningful failing-base controls using exact parent owner-module bytes, with the same retained current SDK/helpers and actual 0.153.4 transport:

```text
PR3 parent 2290c09: ASK read -> prompt -> native consent declined -> 0 calls (required 1: RED)
current stack:      ASK read -> auto   -> no native consent       -> 1 call  (GREEN)
PR5 parent 77db404: owner default new app -> not exposed          -> 0 calls (required 1: RED)
current stack:      owner default new app -> exposed              -> 1 call  (GREEN)
```

These are exact **owner-module baseline compositions**, not complete historical builds/images. Neither source checkout nor refs were switched. Temporary fixture/module files were removed; tracked source and the original candidate/pin are unchanged. The recorded projected-patch hashes were independently matched to the patches used by the native runs.

This closes the prior projection-only/native-enforcement gap with an actual CLI composition. It does not claim a full creator `cron.add` → older finite-default cap lifting → whole Gateway/process restart → current group-policy dispatcher run. The existing real scheduled SaaS read/withdrawal receipts and production-entry principal/retry controls remain separate evidence with their own scopes. No in-flight OAuth revocation or published-release rollback run is claimed, and no product-code or dependency changes were needed for these additional checks.

### Current review-stack head

Current head: `1a1fdf157b55ac3a7932dd698ca27ecda92909b0`; base: `77db404005ce4c0a1e268152c884f5b1c83aafcf`. Both part1 follow-ups (actual question-card destination decoding and the introduced static type-cycle repair) were merged through the stack using normal commits. The effective diff of this individual PR was verified byte-for-byte unchanged through both integrations. Original candidate/internal pin/live bots remain unchanged. Historical runtime/CI evidence is bound to its recorded SHA; newest-head CI and ClawSweeper conclusions are assessed separately.

### Specific installed current-app policy evidence

The earlier broad acceptance summary is supplemented by a separately observed, read-only scheduled job at this exact `0522ce1d35f9d97110a69cfe81c0b14427792c8d` runtime, using Codex CLI 0.153.4. The same existing disabled job was force-run under controlled test-only settings and its stored creation authority was independently compared after every run.

```text
previous candidate: foreground connector read succeeds; stored scheduled job reports app unavailable
0522ce1 scheduled run: linear.get_team real native MCP calls=1; completed=true; error=null
current app withdrawn: native history complete; app tool calls=0; outcome=unavailable
stored creation authority: identical across all three runs
original settings: restored exactly; propagation verified
```

This is actual scheduled native-dispatch evidence for adopting a newly admitted existing app and reapplying the current policy on the next run of the same persisted job. It was collected before these PRs were opened, not rerun to obtain another green result. No provider credential or account was replaced. Private account, job, thread, resource identifiers, tool result contents and endpoints are omitted.

The withdrawal control is removal from current app policy before another scheduled run, not revocation of a provider OAuth token during an in-flight call or forced reuse of a stale native tool handle. Explicitly restricted jobs and account admission are covered by the owner boundary regressions, not claimed as extra live runs here. Those precise limits remain visible for maintainer review.


Fresh combined-source validation at `09156d64a267aaeef7b0bc31d6ae225d9858caf3`: `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base 433c9a3ab1a166d97e0c32df165b0436d0ad04c1 --head 09156d64a267aaeef7b0bc31d6ae225d9858caf3 --timed` completed successfully on Node 24.16.0, including formatting, core and extension production/test types, lint, dead-export and runtime/database guards. This validates the combined source, not each intermediate head or hosted CI. A fresh combined P2 autoreview reported no actionable finding within the supplied source evidence; it does not replace ClawSweeper or maintainer approval.

This PR is ready for review. Its first normal exact-head CI attempt ended with the inherited audit failure described below; ClawSweeper has completed an earlier-head conclusion; see the follow-up disposition. Current-head review is tracked separately.

Author-run owner-default regressions and native changed checks passed. Separate scheduled-read controls verified current app policy admission and deny boundaries. The previous scoped review found no P0/P1 defect; normal PR security and maintainer review remain required.

The final combined source has passed a focused staging core acceptance of 12/12 and two model-menu controls. That does not establish all release-suite coverage or the individual intermediate heads. No production deployment is included. The original full release-suite coverage limits remain; the first public CI audit failed as attributed below, and does not replace the current-head review follow-up.


### Known inherited CI failure on the recorded earlier head

The [exact-head CI audit](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38325462606/job/115063294266) failed on three production dependency advisories: `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.30.1` and `@modelcontextprotocol/client@2.0.0` ([GHSA-6qxp-vccf-f47h](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6qxp-vccf-f47h)), and `source-map-js@1.2.1` ([GHSA-68fv-2mgg-jv7q](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-68fv-2mgg-jv7q)).

These are inherited from the selected public beta, not caused by this fix. All package manifests, the lockfile, workspace configuration and audit implementation are unchanged from `v2026.10.1-beta.1` through the PR base and head. The actual CI merge commit `78d4ce625ca9d02f70546b6c9236a6b07d9ae908` has the expected base/head parents and exactly the PR-head tree. The same three audit findings were inspected in all seven stack jobs. Upstream already tracked fixes in #165902 and #166217.

The requesting maintainer explicitly accepts these proven inherited CI failures as non-blocking for this compatibility review. This is an attributed exception, not green CI or approval of the code. The downstream `openclaw/ci-gate` failed and fail-fast cancelled sibling jobs; those cancelled jobs remain incomplete hosted coverage. Normal code/security review and any defects caused by this patch still require resolution. No dependency update, scanner suppression or CI rerun is included.

<details>
<summary>October review stack</summary>

- Part 1: #170416 — fix(slack): keep workspace identity in October delivery receipts
- Part 2: #170417 — fix(codex): retain native tools in default October cron turns
- Part 3: #170418 — fix(codex): allow scheduled read-only app calls under ask

- Part 6: #170421 — fix(models): clarify partial model availability in October menus
- Part 7: #170422 — fix(slack): recognize same-workspace source channel aliases

</details>
