prs.title: fix(gateway): explain archived sessions in OpenAI-compatible requests
prs.body:
Fixes #169679

## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI-compatible requests using an archived session return an opaque HTTP 500 instead of explaining how to resume the conversation.

## User Impact

Both `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/responses` return HTTP 409 with `invalid_request_error` and Control UI restoration guidance. Streaming requests report the same sanitized error through their existing SSE format. The archived session and its history stay intact; unarchive it before retrying.

## Why This Change Was Made

The work-start owner already distinguishes archived sessions, but agent admission discarded that reason before the shared HTTP mapper saw it. Preserve the typed owner error and translate the archived reason at the existing HTTP boundary.

This follows the documented explicit-unarchive contract and `chat.send` behavior. Automatic channel restoration has separate human-message and lifecycle eligibility rules. No configuration, schema, or SDK surface changes are needed.

Related work: #170029 addresses the same symptom. This implementation verifies actual command admission through both HTTP handlers and returns a fixed public message without the session key.

## Evidence

- **HTTP regression:** both real handlers execute actual command admission and preserve archived metadata plus nonempty transcript history. Main returned 500 for both. The regression passes on current head `861896bc790a8883d5201632278108c3f38a2042` in [CI job 115065582501](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38326157723/job/115065582501), 25.03 s Vitest. The isolated local run passed in 429.40 s on the contended host; existing HTTP coverage passed 260 tests.
- **Production-only negative control:** reverting only the three production files makes both regressions fail (`expected 409 / received 500`), while the archived-owner rejection assertion passes. Fresh Testbox `tbx_01m4rs26rb1s2j1cja3rgcvxdb`, [run 38297236344](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38297236344): 48.61 s Vitest / 50.86 s runner.
- **Refreshed main control:** with only the three production files replaced by main `981e312ce1a203642f06de9cbfee9b74d2451712`, the same two real HTTP regressions again failed at `expected 500 to be 409`; the archived-owner assertion passed. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/openai-compatible-archived-session.server.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 91.26 s Vitest / 107.11 s runner / 108.06 s command. The collector initially expected a different failure-report format; the two failures were verified directly from the log, and the candidate was restored and checked byte-for-byte.
- **Live real Gateway:** fresh Testbox `tbx_01m4s0eae5erypp2svcn5zapkf`, [run 38311173813](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38311173813), QA mock provider, isolated temporary state and ephemeral loopback ports. Maintenance (`mode: enforce`, `maxEntries: 1`, `preserveRecent: false`) archived the first conversation after two successful turns. The same routing key returned 500 on main and actionable 409 with the fix for both endpoints. Both streaming variants emitted the sanitized error. History was unchanged and both Gateway processes stopped cleanly.
- **Live commands:** `pnpm build qaRuntime`, then `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/.archived500-live.mts 500` against main production; restore fixed production files, rebuild, and run the probe with `409`. Build/probe wall times: main 104.66/66.75 s, fix 71.64/51.14 s. Source `2e525fc64bc3da410b4eb3d872e051ca205ffe96`, main control `4c0b8b1f2d50c224b46f79afcb0366077a8a84dd`. Later main merges preserved the fix patch, but changed surrounding admission code; the final merged head has not received a fresh remote Gateway run.
- **Current-head static checks:** `pnpm tsgo:core` passed (19.13 s); `pnpm tsgo:core:test --ci-graphs-json '["core-test-gateway-root","core-test-agents-root","core-test-commands","core-test-agents-sessions"]'` passed (73.43 s). Targeted oxlint, oxfmt (0.84 s), and `git diff --check` passed.
- **Current-head broad coverage:** [CI 38326157723](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38326157723) passed (43 successful jobs, 25 skipped, no failures). The 441-file owner/caller inventory is accounted for: 439 files passed (35 in exact-head CI, 25 completed in the serial local run, and 379 in the remaining parallel run); one existing opt-in allocation benchmark skipped; the unrelated source-fixture E2E failure is described below. Local commands used `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <explicit files> --maxWorkers=1`, then `--maxWorkers=4` with an isolated cache for the remaining 380 files. The serial run was intentionally stopped after completed-file results were retained; its incomplete file ran again in full. Wall times were 1,564.36 s for the bounded serial run and 1,063.10 s for the successful remaining run. The complete file lists and logs are retained with task evidence.
- **Review:** deslop completed; independent branch autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 findings. The patch ID remains `94b579ec8058927630067ef49a2b5b163936f17c` after the mechanical main merges. [ClawSweeper reviewed current head 861896b](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/170299#issuecomment-6133555702): no findings, complete issue scope, sufficient live proof.

### Validation limits and unrelated failures

The requested lease-based full-module rerun could not run: three Testbox acquisitions exhausted 45 minutes of actual queue time, then the authorized AWS fallback refused allocation with `cost_limit_exceeded`. No AWS machine was allocated, no budget guard was bypassed, and all owned Testbox leases were stopped and verified absent. Local checks and CI supply additional coverage, but do not replace a final-head remote Gateway run.

`src/config/sessions/session-entry-snapshots.benchmark.test.ts` is an existing allocation benchmark guarded by `it.runIf(process.env.OPENCLAW_SESSION_ENTRY_SNAPSHOTS_BENCH === "1")`; its source explicitly assigns ordinary regression coverage to the regular suites. The guard was left unchanged.

The untouched `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts` source fixture reported 81 early failures before its mocked agent ran; bounded whole-file attempts were stopped when later cases waited for that agent. It ran with the supported `OPENCLAW_E2E_SKIP_BUILD=1` because its private fixture does not consume packaged artifacts. A production-only baseline on main `981e312ce1a203642f06de9cbfee9b74d2451712` reproduced the selected `announces model fallback transitions across verbose levels` failure: expected `Model Fallback:`, received `Agent failed before reply: Runtime config is not prepared`. That case is inherited (97.14 s Vitest / 118.91 s runner). The other failures have not been individually classified. The main transcript repair `accded4b85c70` was incorporated, but did not resolve this fixture issue. No assertions or production placement checks were weakened.

An earlier CI run was cancelled after failures in the untouched Codex extension bundle. Main's prepared-policy repair `cbc53ac75eca3` was incorporated; the two previously failing cleanup cases then passed on `ae23a0e` (5.259 s and 0.388 s). That head's CI completed with 47 successful jobs and no failures; this is prior-head evidence.

The production delta is +14 lines (+41/-27). The owner error type and sanitized mapping require the growth; the same files remove the old block factory, redundant wrapping, and obsolete comments. Tests add 79 lines; docs add 10.

prs.title: refactor(database): prepare shared-state engine admission (PR2a)
prs.body:
## Problem and scope

`openEngineStore` inferred existing SQLite data from table-name prefixes, which could miss partial or legacy stores. The PostgreSQL adapter also granted every main-thread open an admission exemption that outlived boot.

This PR is **PR2a: engine prerequisites only**. It adds owner-supplied data classification, separately published PostgreSQL catalog facts, a single runtime DDL artifact per state object, and a synchronous admission scope with request-time enforcement. Workboard adopts the contract; its PostgreSQL workload fixtures now run in real workers with host-retained admission. Shared state remains SQLite in production; its physical-open cutover, lazy ensure wiring, state conformance, and type frontier are PR2b.

Builds on [#170059](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/170059), [#170017](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/170017), and [#170037](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/170037). No schema version, durability, configuration, or stored-data migration changes.

## Evidence

Raw native SQLite execution captures are byte-identical to the base, without SQL normalization: workboard 35,592 bytes (98 cold-open statements, one write, eight warm-reuse statements, one read); shared state 196,425 bytes (86 cold-open statements, three write-transaction statements, 31 restart statements, one read). The state owner source is unchanged.

Local PostgreSQL 17 proof used a throwaway cluster on port 55440, stopped and removed afterward. Catalog verification matched 134 tables, 1,386 columns, 293 CHECKs, 297 indexes, and 32 foreign keys; the two declared pending ACP indexes remain explicit. Physical-facts tests passed (3 tests; 40.68s Vitest, 555.18s including compilation). The final workboard fixture uses the existing engine worker broker. Its local PostgreSQL conformance passed (15 tests, seven native-only skips; 579.26s Vitest, 706.78s runner including 324.86s worker preparation). 

Engine-open tests passed (4); generator tests passed (15; 76.68s); guard/adapters/connection proof passed, including live refusal of post-admission main-thread SQL and successful worker reads/writes. After the final test-helper typing correction, the focused guard rerun passed (2 tests; 7.53s Vitest, 15.50s runner). Runtime build, formatting, Madge (zero cycles), wrapper inventory, and diff checks passed. Two independent Codex review rounds found no actionable P0–P2 defects. Initial source-freshness and SDK-preparation failures were tooling failures; successful frozen-source reruns are the evidence above.

Core typecheck and extension lint passed. The first draft CI PostgreSQL conformance job passed. CI exposed a SQLite dialect-classification bug (PostgreSQL-only JSONB constructors/aggregates were counted as SQLite debt), an extension-test helper bridge, and excessive SDK exports. The classifier now distinguishes the actual dialect functions with a regression; the workboard fixture uses the existing engine worker broker; physical catalog helpers remain engine-internal. The sole new public SDK name is the lexical admission scope; the existing worker-outcome predicate is also available on its narrow private-local worker subpath. The exact SDK budget increase is one export/one callable; no shipped API was removed. The PostgreSQL generator is registered as its actual executable root for dependency analysis. The two maintenance capability exports intentionally await PR2b routing; the production-only Knip exception names that module, while the full-tree test-aware export audit remains enabled.

The final fixture passed the extension typecheck and focused extension-boundary test (one assertion, 470.41s runner including shared build preparation); the direct extension-test-import checker also passed. The dialect regression suite passed (six tests, 72.07s runner), and the dialect ratchet reports no growth. Final targeted core, root-test, script, and revised-fixture lint passed; formatting and diff checks passed. SDK declaration preparation exceeded the default five-minute local budget, then passed with the repository-supported 15-minute budget (12,847 declarations); downstream checks reused the completed outputs. The exact SDK surface check passed at 3,713 public exports/2,168 callables with no shipped removals. The production dependency scan now reports only the inherited outbound re-export below. Prior-head CI: [run 38317012886](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38317012886) at `5c593e113b249758f148bd53a9697f30396a0080`. PostgreSQL conformance passed (409 tests; 262.43s across three Vitest shards), as did the baseline ratchets, additional boundaries, changed-boundary suite, and test-type job. The dependency job reports only the unchanged outbound re-export described below; its log was checked against the base. Other broad CI jobs may still be completing; this draft is not merged. The inherited unused `hasActiveDeliveryOwner` re-export in `src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-storage.ts` exists unchanged at the base and is outside this PR.

Coordinator correction: removed the superseded wrapped state/fragment DDL and the duplicate `.runtime` filenames. The manifest now names one unqualified runtime file per state object; catalog equivalence executes those same files. All retained state SQL is byte-identical to its prior runtime counterpart, and `agent.postgres.sql` remains byte-identical and wrapped. Tracked generated output falls from 87 files / 7,008 lines to 45 files / 4,090 lines. Manual application in a chosen schema is documented. The existing CI path filter already includes every retained generated file. Correction validation passed: `pnpm db:postgres:check` (15 generator tests, 58.12s Vitest / 139.57s runner, plus canonical/workboard freshness), wrapper inventory (4 assertions, 64.21s Vitest / 75.27s runner), targeted script/test type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check`. Shared SDK declaration preparation completed successfully (12,847 files). CI for correction head `2d92df3d9f8555ca039477504006f14b4a2464e4`: [run 38320942163](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38320942163). PostgreSQL conformance was skipped because preflight refused the stale synthetic PR merge head (`5c593e113b249758f148bd53a9697f30396a0080` instead of the pushed correction). GitHub reports the PR conflicts with current main. This run did not execute the PostgreSQL tests; the prior-head pass above is not new-head evidence.

Handwritten production growth: 296 net lines, below the 550-line budget; generated SQL and test fixtures are separate. No protected async-owned file changed.


## Landing validation

Rebased head: `0fbf8b960806a72dedf53b8e2ca92e52922ef93f`. The only conflict was SDK budget arithmetic; main's additions and this PR's one export/callable are preserved. PostgreSQL regeneration produced unchanged outputs, `pnpm db:postgres:check` passed all 15 generator tests, and current-head PostgreSQL conformance passed in [CI run 38322851750](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38322851750).

Maintainer-authorized native CI exception under the causal-path rule:

| Job | Classification and evidence |
| --- | --- |
| `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-19-2` | 23 QA Lab runtime-tool fixture failures: runtime config was not prepared. The entire QA Lab tree and runtime-config owner are identical to the tested main parent. |
| `checks-node-changed-extensions-config-119` | Repeated-turn child fails before any provider request because runtime config was not prepared. The same QA Lab tree and runtime-config owner are unchanged. |
| `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-28` | Two Teams poll-cleanup assertions resolve instead of rejecting. The entire Teams tree is unchanged; these SQLite state tests do not use the PR2a engine opener. |
| `checks-node-changed-2` | Telegram ingress-coalescing test/hook timeouts exhausted the one-hour deadline. The entire Telegram tree and CI workflow are identical to the tested main parent. This is deadline cancellation, not fail-fast cancellation; the unfinished coverage remains unverified. |

CI's automatic classifier reports `unknown` for the three failed jobs because scheduled main uses different job names. Independent causal inspection and matching tree/blob identities establish that the observed failing paths are disjoint from this PR. The tested merge is `5e8938315beeb2180a4d515a015dd4243bc4b80e`, with main parent `0a3231562bb3ddcb44d4ca73a65f9b62dbf46116` and the exact PR head. `security-fast` passed independently.

<details>
<summary>Approved design of record — sections 1–4 (PR2a implements the engine prerequisites; state integration is PR2b)</summary>

> ## 1. Physical-open seam and existing-data contract
>
> Keep `openOpenClawStateDatabase` → `openOpenClawStateDatabaseWithBusyTimeout` → its existing acquisition closure → `openUnpublishedStateDatabase` → `openNativeStateDatabase`. Insert `openEngineStore` inside that last function, after the tracked native anchor open, identity check, timeout setup, and native catalog admission; before exposing the selected connection to state ownership/schema callbacks. The native handle is the state file on SQLite and only the identity anchor on PostgreSQL. No alternative state-store facade, cache, or admission owner.
> Pass the tracked anchor, state schema id/version, canonical/generated DDL, caller's immutable engine input, owner-derived SQLite classification, and existing setup/admission callbacks. Refactor the rest of the current SQLite acquisition body into the existing `openSqlite` callback without changing its statement order. Its permissions, integrity, initialization history, failure recording, and cleanup stay owned by state. PostgreSQL state admission runs through a domain callback before the engine publishes successful admission; bootstrap metadata and domain seeds commit atomically.
> Extend `openEngineStore`'s local parameter contract with required `inspectSqlite(): { hasExistingData: boolean; hasEngineAnchor: boolean }`; retire the `${schema.id}_` table-prefix heuristic for every caller. Consume the callback only when resolving an unrecorded physical engine; do not probe on cached reuse. A validated engine anchor remains PostgreSQL even when its file already exists. Refuse mixed anchor/application content, and refuse an unported SQLite store before creating anchor rows or contacting PostgreSQL.
> For state, derive classification from #170017's already admitted native catalog/version facts: any application object other than the engine anchor/internal SQLite objects is existing data, including `schema_meta`, `cron_jobs`, historical/partial native startup tables, and views. Do not rerun historical migration discovery. `params.existingSchema` is a no-repair policy, NOT a data-presence flag; `initialization.kind` includes external deletion history and is NOT a substitute either. Preserve both separately. The current `assertStateDatabaseIntegrityBeforeMutation` already uses admitted versions plus general application-schema presence; reuse that information rather than inventing an id prefix.
> For workboard, its schema owner supplies the same explicit decision from admitted application objects (not just workboard-prefixed names). A recognized anchor is not application data. Update every `openEngineStore` test fixture to supply classification. On default state SQLite, `hasEngineAnchor` comes from the catalog already captured by `admitStateSchemaFacts`, replacing the generic unconditional missing-anchor SELECT with no additional SQL. A present anchor still refuses a SQLite selection with the existing recovery instruction.
>
> ## 2. Engine-neutral admitted facts and capabilities
>
> Add an engine-owned physical-facts API alongside the existing contract (do not edit the overlapping `database-engine/contract.ts`). Types distinguish SQLite native facts from PostgreSQL facts; never cast a PostgreSQL handle to `DatabaseSync`, synthesize `SqliteSchemaFacts`, or implement a fake `.location()`.
> The adapter supplies: selected SQL connection; physical identity (admitted anchor generation + store UUID + namespace); actual schema version; catalog capture; capability operations for native-file maintenance versus server transactions; and paired physical close. State decides acceptable version, canonical required/optional objects, initialization policy, and whether admission is complete. Schema identity is a process admission id/revision, not a fabricated PostgreSQL PRAGMA cookie.
> PostgreSQL reads `openclaw_schema_meta` (store/version/store_id), domain `schema_meta`, and `state.schema.contentVersion`; disagreements refuse admission. Capture real `pg_catalog` facts for tables/columns/types/defaults/constraints/indexes in one consistent read, restricted to the admitted namespace. Validate mandatory canonical objects and any present lazy fragment against the generated contract, including FK/check/index semantics and the two declared pending ACP indexes. Absent first-use tables remain valid. Reuse the pure comparison rules from generation instead of a second schema policy.
> Publish PostgreSQL facts under a separate engine/schema admission key through the existing anchor admission exchange. Never publish PG catalog entries as the anchor's `sqlite-schema` fact. Bind state version/runtime facts to that identity and schema revision; data-only commits retain them. Committed DDL publishes replacement facts, rollback restores prior facts, and unknown commit revokes affected facts through existing receipts. Reopen with live admission reuses facts; final close retires them and a new process validates anew. No foreign-writer probes or per-read catalog queries.
> Route state admission by capabilities, with dispatch centralized under `database-engine`: SQLite uses its current native version/shape/integrity path byte-for-byte; PostgreSQL uses server version/catalog admission and state ownership checks. Missing/newer/mismatched metadata refuses with “use the matching OpenClaw version or restore the matching PostgreSQL schema and anchor”; do not run historical SQLite migration/repair SQL on PG. Fresh PG starts at v21; offline SQLite migration/port remains P3-6.
> Native integrity/foreign-key PRAGMAs, WAL registration (including cache registration), checkpoint, and page reclamation/VACUUM are skipped for PG runtime lifecycle. They are not reported as successful SQLite verification; server constraints/catalog admission are different evidence. Explicit native-integrity/SQLite-repair requests refuse and direct the operator to PostgreSQL verification/recovery and a matched export+anchor restore.
> `.location()` is used only inside SQLite-capable branches; generic identity consumers use admitted physical identity. Copied-file snapshots, SQLite online backup, and artifact-preserving file readers refuse PG before copying/opening the anchor as data: “PostgreSQL state cannot use a SQLite file snapshot; stop the Gateway and back up/restore the PostgreSQL schema with its matching anchor (P3-6 export support pending).” Ordinary multi-query read snapshots use the adapter's REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY transaction. They do not produce a file or claim backup support.
> State's existing cache/resource owner retains both selected connection and anchor, closes the PG connection before the anchor, aggregates failures, and retains failed-close custody. Preserve #169983: accepted lifecycle writes finish before the shared worker is torn down. Do not change shutdown ordering, broker ownership, or state authority checks.
>
> ## 3. Lazy PostgreSQL fragments
>
> PR3 artifacts currently contain `BEGIN/COMMIT` and hard-coded `openclaw_state` qualification. They cannot be executed inside the engine's namespace/transaction unchanged. Extend the existing generator to emit runtime DDL from the same parsed objects without transaction/schema wrappers or fixed namespace, following its existing workboard rendering mode. Regenerate; no runtime regex stripping/requalification and no handwritten generated SQL.
> Use PR3's declaration/manifest ids, dependencies, and activation. Fresh bootstrap installs eager DDL and version-additive fragments, plus state metadata/content seeds. Existing same-version stores do not eagerly install missing additive features. First-use fragments are installed only when the existing feature ensure runs, dependencies first, in that owner's transaction; tables/indexes/FKs complete before publication. `user_background_images` installs its declared profile dependency then its FK. An unsuccessful ensure never publishes success.
> Wire the shared ensure module, additive-schema owner, and profile owner's two-phase ensure to the adapter operation. Keep the existing SQLite providers, statement bytes, and successful-return timing; do not bypass feature privacy/lifecycle boundaries or edit t1cut-state callers. A generated fragment being available does not make all consumers PostgreSQL-compatible; PR4 remains separate.
>
> ## 4. Worker-only PG and reachability
>
> Extend the conformance preload's existing worker environment transport with a state-specific test key, leaving workboard's key intact. Read it only in the state test seam; production config remains SQLite, registry state support remains disabled, and PR1 broker/read-worker input threading is deferred. Do not load full config or resolve secrets in the opener.
> Fix the current unconditional `purpose: "admission"` in `adapters.ts`: it presently bypasses the constructor's thread-0 guard on every open. Use a synchronous, lexical boot-admission/migration scope checked at the engine boundary; ordinary connection construction has no exemption. `PostgresSyncConnection` must also reject SQL requests on thread 0 after that scope exits, so retaining an admitted handle cannot permit warmed main-thread queries. Worker construction/queries remain allowed. Test both refused construction and refused post-admission use, plus a successful worker read/write.
> Conformance creates one worker fixture using the real state acquisition/transaction/read owners with isolated state/namespace. Cover cold open + v21/bootstrap seeds, absent lazy tables then first use, retained admission/restart reuse, committed write and read-only snapshot, and paired cleanup. Test final-close/new-process validation separately from live-facts reuse; never require stale facts to survive retired ownership.

</details>

prs.title: fix: gateway restart fails from verified external macOS terminals
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes macOS `openclaw gateway restart` failing with “Process ancestry could not be fully inspected” from a terminal that native service membership already verifies is outside the Gateway job.

## User Impact

Verified external terminals can restart the Gateway even when an ancestor cannot be inspected. In-service callers retain detached handoff protection; unknown membership and absent containment retain their existing guards. No config or migration changes. Update/maintenance callers use the same corrected membership owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native probe returned `outside`, but its caller still required the ancestor walk to reach PID 1. This redundant requirement was introduced by commit 6209f31ce9bb on September 26 and first appears in release tag v2026.9.7; it is present in the v2026.10.2 tagged source as well as the reported 5b29c85 build. Accept verified outside containment while retaining ancestry checks when containment is absent.

## Evidence

- Added a regression through `restartLaunchAgent`: it fails before the fix with the reported ServiceInspectionError and passes afterward, reaching native kickstart without a detached handoff.

prs.title: improve(ui): make colored sessions easier to scan
prs.body:
Closes #170371

## What Problem This Solves

Session color stripes are easy to miss when scanning a long sidebar.

## User Impact

Colored sessions are easier to recognize in light and dark mode without sacrificing readable titles or metadata. Pinned and imported rows share the treatment; the open conversation and multi-selected rows remain distinct. No configuration, persistence, or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use a subtle full-row wash while retaining the stronger stripe: 9% in light mode and 12% in dark mode, with a modest hover increase. Keep titles neutral, strengthen secondary text on tinted surfaces, and reserve neutral fill plus a stronger title for the open conversation. Multi-selection continues to override the tag fill, including pinned active rows.

## Evidence

- Focused Chromium regression: all eight colors, uncolored controls, light/dark, recent/pinned, hover/open/multi-select precedence, 3px stripe, and subtitle/trailing text contrast of at least 4.5:1. Two tests pass; same regression fails on the original styles because full-row tint is absent. Final parent run: 414ms test bodies, 4.02s Vitest, 5.17s wrapper. Hosted [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38322299113) passed; per-test CI timing was not separately collected.
- Existing theme token/contrast tests: 8 passed.
- UI production build, UI typecheck, targeted stylelint/oxlint/format, max-lines ratchet, and diff checks pass.
- Independent review: no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Actual Control UI captures below use synthetic data and identical app JavaScript. Before loads the three affected stylesheets from the baseline; after loads the changed stylesheets. This is not the design mockup. Desktop light/dark verified; no separate custom-theme, touch, or forced-colors claim.

### Before

![Before: narrow stripes in light and dark mode](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/643a9eb1-7f66-4859-bb87-049027329c27)

### After

![After: subtle full-row tints with neutral readable text](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a2cc7ce6-1683-40fa-86fc-e97b111d2beb)

Light is left; dark is right. The open conversation, hover, multi-selection, personally pinned session, metadata, and uncolored control are shown together.

Design and direction: @steipete.

prs.title: fix(openai): preserve text and image order in tool results
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes captions losing their positions when a tool returns interleaved text and images through OpenAI Responses.

## User Impact

Before-and-after screenshots retain their captions in the model's next request. Text-only tool results keep the same serialized bytes; no configuration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Walk image-bearing tool results in order at the existing Responses conversion owner instead of grouping all text before all images. Preserve adjacent-text joining, existing newline separators, structured-result fallback, unsupported-media behavior, and the unchanged text-only path.

Thanks to @Shenrui-Ma for the report, fix, and original request-capture regressions. The ordering and boundary cases now live in the existing Responses replay suite rather than a separate 211-line test harness. No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

## Evidence

Built, isolated `openclaw agent --local` runs invoked a configured stdio MCP tool and sent their next request to a capturing Responses-compatible loopback provider. Model replies were scripted; the tool ran through the shipped MCP and agent path. Both versions completed with one tool call and two provider requests.

| MCP result | Main converter | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Caption "Before:", image A, caption "After:", image B | One text item containing both captions, then image A, image B | Caption "Before:", image A, caption "After:", image B |
| Text-only, with leading/trailing spaces and an embedded blank line | Original string | Byte-identical original string |

The captured multimodal `function_call_output.output` item types were:

```text
Main: [input_text, input_image, input_image]
PR:   [input_text, input_image, input_text, input_image]
```

Live acceptance on `f8cdca366e4cf49f4d7d3f22be7507f95fba81f2`: GPT-5 mini called the same MCP tool through `agent --local`. A capturing proxy forwarded both requests to the real OpenAI Responses API; both returned HTTP 200. The second request contained the ordered text/image/text/image tool output, and the model completed its next answer. This proves acceptance of the changed multimodal payload, not just a text-only connectivity check.

The text-only `function_call_output` serialized identically: 89 UTF-8 bytes, SHA-256 `64a24e6b03b3eded4b3633cdb05eb983de5df1bf140eae515be46447696a1672`. The second PR caption retains the pre-existing newline separator, so flattening the text still produces the original joined text.

Focused replay regression: main fails both provider and transport ordering cases; this PR passes all 14 tests (`pnpm test packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-async-replay.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, 2.91 seconds wall time). Cases include different multi-image groupings, leading images, adjacent captions, single/image-only/multiple-image results, and whitespace-sensitive text-only output. Targeted oxfmt and oxlint pass. The assertion-safety baseline shrinks from 8 to 7 because the old array cast is removed.

Against the merge base: production +36/-17 (net +19), tests +91/-0 (net +91). The necessary production growth retains existing fallback and text-joining contracts; simplification removes the extra explicit-text scan. Relative to the contributor head, the standalone 211-line test file is removed.

Merge risk: two-way door; reverting restores the old wire ordering without migrating stored data. Blast radius is image-bearing tool-result replay on OpenAI Responses routes; text-only output and other providers are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(agents): warn once when a requester settle wake keeps hitting owner changes
prs.body:
Related: #154252, #154129, #157871, #163195 Scope: part of #154252. This PR fixes its diagnostic part: a requester settle wake that keeps failing on an owner change becomes identifiable in the log, with the retry cadence #157871 kept. A supported way to recover a settle wake already stranded on a terminal run is tracked separately in #170562. The dispatching attempt cap is not changed here (see Gaps). ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: a requester settle wake whose stored rows disagree about who owns a completion looks, in the Gateway log, exactly like a transient storage outage. Every settle attempt is rejected with `subagent completion owner changed before settlement`. That rejection is a function of the stored rows, so repeating the identical attempt does not change the answer. Today the log shows five per-attempt `requester settle wake failed` lines, then the generic `requester settle wake commit still failing; retries continue` warning, then nothing until it recovers (#157871 budgets the repeats). A locked or read-only database produces the same sequence. Nothing tells an operator that this wake is waiting on a persisted ownership divergence rather than on storage. ## User Impact After 5 identical owner-changed rejections in a row, the Gateway logs one warning that names the cause: ``` requester settle wake keeps failing on an owner change; retries continue rejection="subagent completion owner changed before settlement" failures=5 runIds=["run-154252"] ``` Nothing else changes. Retry cadence stays the 30s doubling to 120s backoff with the 120s ceiling that #157871 kept, so a wake whose divergence heals settles exactly as promptly as on main (measured below: 29s after the heal on both arms). The row, its captured result and its wake are left as stored, and no event reaches the requester. ## Why This Change Was Made The triage on #154252 asked for a bound on this loop. Earlier revisions of this branch bounded it by closing the wake, and then by slowing its retries to 30 minute probes. Both traded recovery behavior for less work: closure risked a captured result (#154129 removed its own count-based abandonment for that reason), and slow probes delayed settlement after a heal by up to 30 minutes. The merged #157871 deliberately keeps the 120s ceiling so settlement stays prompt when storage recovers. Retrying at that ceiling is also cheap: on a shipped Gateway, 100 stranded rows cost about 2.4s of process CPU per 22 minutes over an empty Gateway, about 2 ms per attempt (Retry cost below). So the cadence stays as it is, and this change only makes the stuck state identifiable. The change in one sentence: the settle path classifies the owner-changed rejection through one shared message, counts identical repeats on the in-memory retry episode, and logs one warning on the fifth, without touching cadence, rows or payloads. | Case | Expected | |---|---| | 5 identical owner-changed rejections in a row | one `requester settle wake keeps failing on an owner change; retries continue` warning; next attempt at the usual 120s ceiling | | Further identical rejections | no second warning; retries continue every 120s | | Divergence heals | settles on the next ordinary retry, episode clears | | Storage or transport error (locked, read-only, wrapped) | never counted, resets the count; no warning from this path | | Different owner-changed signature (different failing run) | resets the count, never reported for churn alone | | Paused `sessions_yield` cohort member | never reported | | Delivered outcome | never reported; it is a sent result, not a stuck wake | | Wake with no outcome (obsolete wake) | settles in one attempt, nothing to repeat | | Gateway restart | new episode: reported again after 5 fresh attempts | | Row state at any point | unchanged: wake `pending`, payload retained, no delivery event | The count lives on the in-memory retry episode and is not persisted; no schema change. ## Evidence All of the following ran on one machine (the Mac Studio), base `981e312ce1a` (tree `6e79a9adbab`). The Gateway arms ran at tree `7090c1cdb71`; the pushed tree `fbfc2f0889f` is that tree minus one test file (`git diff --stat 7090c1cdb71 fbfc2f0889f`: `1 file changed, 57 deletions(-)`, `src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce.requester-settle-owner-changed.test.ts`), so every production file is byte-identical. Tests, Red/green and the `src/agents/subagents/announce` lane and `pnpm check:changed` rows in Other checks ran at the pushed tree. ### Through the shipped Gateway The built CLI, `node openclaw.mjs --profile gateway run --port --bind loopback --auth token --allow-unconfigured`, each arm with its own `HOME` and `--profile` state directory, nothing substituted. BEFORE is a separate checkout of base `981e312ce1a`, AFTER is the pushed tree; each was built with `pnpm build` and run from its own `dist`. The two BEFORE arms ran together from 17:42 PDT and the two AFTER arms together from 18:52 PDT on 2026-10-12, on ports 19531 to 19534. No producer of this state is known on current main (see Gaps), so the divergence is written into the state database directly with `node:sqlite`, the same row shapes the controller tests seed: - First boot: the Gateway boots once to create its state and stops cleanly; one stranded row (`run-154252`, wake `pending`, `attemptCount` 5, its `batchRunIds` naming only itself, delivery `pending`, captured `resultText`) is inserted; the Gateway is started again and left running for 480s, then stopped. - Cohort that heals: row A (`run-154252`, wake `pending` for the cohort `[run-154252, run-154252-b]`, persisted `nextAttemptAt` 150s ahead) is inserted before the second boot; once the Gateway is up and has restored its registry, the stray sibling B is inserted into SQLite only, so every settle of A is rejected because an omitted cohort sibling still carries a wake of the same generation. B is deleted 15 minutes after the first rejection (the heal) and the run continues until the episode reports recovery. | | BEFORE (base `981e312ce1a`) | AFTER (this PR) | |---|---|---| | First boot, 480s | 5 rejections, at 0s, 30s, 90s, 210s and 330s after the first; on the 5th, `still failing; retries continue ... retryIntervalMs=120000`, then per-attempt logs go quiet | the same 5 rejections at the same offsets; on the 5th, `keeps failing on an owner change; retries continue rejection="subagent completion owner changed before settlement" failures=5 runIds=["run-154252"]` and the same `still failing; retries continue ... retryIntervalMs=120000` | | First boot, stored row after stop | wake `pending`, delivery `pending`, `resultText` retained, unchanged from the seed | identical | | Cohort: failed settle attempts from the first rejection to the heal (15 min) | 9 (`commit recovered failures=9 suppressedFailureLogs=4`) | 9 (`commit recovered failures=9 suppressedFailureLogs=4`) | | Cohort: heal to settlement | 29s (heal 18:00:09, `recovered` 18:00:38) | 29s (heal 19:09:52, `recovered` 19:10:21) | | Cohort: stored row of A after settlement | wake cleared; delivery `failed`, `lastError` `requester session unavailable`, `resultText` kept | identical | The settled row ends `failed` with `requester session unavailable` in both arms because these isolated profiles have no live requester session for `agent:main:main`; the settlement itself is what the arms compare. Masked values (`run-…4252`, `agent:main:…`) are the Gateway's own log masking in existing lines; the new warning records the exact run id.

prs.title: refactor(agents): simplify runtime preparation and bookkeeping
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Maintainer-requested agents cleanup removes speculative mid-operation bookkeeping and consolidates duplicate preparation, publication, serialization, and error paths.

Related: #153340, #158000, #163195, #165404, #165750, #167254, #119292.

## User Impact

Normal agent features, public contracts, transcript durability, tool and approval authority, and ordinary parallel-session behavior remain. Unusual mid-turn setting changes and same-execution metadata rewrites are best effort as described below. No configuration, protocol, schema, retention, permission, or dependency changes. The standalone Phase E session memory backend, its factory, registry, expiry/federation machinery, and its tests are untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the agents lane of the maintainer's pragmatism campaign, starting with the last three days of production growth, then the last fourteen days and larger owners. Native ownership reads and transcript append projections share one preparation/result path while retaining their released synchronous and worker adapters. Native permission hashing uses the existing streaming canonical serializer rather than a second recursive implementation. Requester delivery wrappers share one source-guard adapter.

Full question-lifecycle consolidation was deliberately rejected: harness and tool cancellation, prompt delivery, and receipt contracts differ, and a callback/flag framework would add policy rather than remove it. Coherent model rows/pricing publication and measured worktree caches remain. This pass qualifies for the campaign's 500–999-line exception after the bounded coverage pass; no feature or in-flight foundation was removed to reach a line target.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Cache-TTL in-memory revision fencing: #165404 describes restoring an empty branch during a deliberately held append, not a human actual-use report. Restoring a branch while its FIFO checkpoint append is pending may temporarily leave the old in-memory baseline; the next hydration restores the selected branch. Checkpoint/delta codecs, replay limits, uncertain-append reset, and persisted formats remain.
- Optional Decision-setting equality and first-primary-dispatch restoration: #153340 records synthetic model-switch/foreground-restoration tests. An admitted turn keeps its completed optional tool restriction if its Decision model or opt-in changes; the next turn uses the new setting. Fresh opt-out is still checked before external Decision inference. Required tools, independent hook caps, source/steering authority, cancellation, host scope-or-plain-callback authority before foreground observation, full host authority before provider dispatch, and provider/credential validity remain enforced.
- Diagnostic stream forwarding/descriptor fallbacks: #85341 supplied a structural stream contract, not a requirement to forward private provider methods. Diagnostics now exposes the declared iteration/result surface, including frozen streams. Undeclared provider implementation methods are not forwarded; final-result observation and provider cleanup remain.
- Host skill metadata publication's physical-database/admission rechecks: #167254 describes forced database-close/replacement interleavings after immutable metadata acquisition. A replacement in that narrow interval can publish the captured catalog; the next run reads fresh metadata. Host/run, read-policy, sandbox, workspace, and permission authority remain.
- Native relay teardown reentrant successor protocol and nested logger-failure compensation: #122503 does not cite a human reentrant-cleanup report, and the sole production callback releases resources rather than registering a successor. Teardown now runs before replacement. An unsupported reentrant callback cannot override the caller's replacement; a logger failure surfaces as an error. Approval cancellation, registration revocation, bridge drain, and partial-setup cleanup remain.
- Native permission fingerprint's partially sorted wide-object tail: #113675 carried a bespoke implementation with no cited incident or measured win for that strategy. The existing serializer sorts all keys of the already-bounded JSON payload. All content, command/cwd binding, SHA-256, admission bounds, and approval checks remain; ephemeral fingerprints may differ and wide bounded objects do a complete key sort.
- Completed subagent result's fourteen-field cloned fingerprint: #149223 cites human #138555 for deterministic truncation, not a same-execution metadata race. A metadata rewrite can leave the selected answer in flight; exact run/runtime replacement and source delivery authority still reject stale executions. Full archive answer coverage remains.
- Secondary terminal publication fingerprint/generations: #163195 includes a real production incident, whose FIFO, acknowledged publication, atomic terminal signals, runtime ownership, and cleanup settlement are retained. Only synthetic same-execution timestamp/reply ABA fencing is removed. A same-outcome metadata update can finish the selected callback; the point-of-effect terminal/outcome/kill/pause check, original session-effects binding, and live session/host authority still reject actual cancellation, replacement, and changed outcomes.
- Worktree picker object/config proof and post-refresh ref fence: #165750/#165513 describe synthetic cache-hit corruption/config and mutation-during-refresh fixtures. Suggestions may remain stale for at most thirty seconds after config/object damage, or briefly after a ref changes during refresh. Ref/HEAD metadata changes invalidate reuse; refresh runs native Git, and creation validates the selected ref before checkout effects. The measured cache and resource bounds remain.
- Remote-catalog repeated config/input/pending predicates and early unpublished-loan abort: #158000 records held-I/O/config-churn regressions; #167178's actual picker-drop report justifies keeping full discovery and coherent rows/pricing. Model-neutral config churn may retain the prepared catalog until a later refresh, and a retired unpublished candidate may finish preparation before failing the final owner/generation/auth/plugin check. Revision single-flight, predecessor commit, shutdown cancellation, disposal, and published-owner recovery remain.

## Evidence

Before conflict integration, local runtime build passed (8m 40.9s), all 28 selected test-type consumer graphs passed, and production core types passed (87.24s). Changed-check ratchets/boundaries, coercion/deprecated API checks, schema/legacy-store/media/sidecar guards, and webhook/pairing-auth guards passed. Corrected scoped lint, production types, and the three affected agent test-type graphs passed again after the final authority repairs. The pre-rebase focused wrapper passed all 34 files across seven shards: 784 passing tests and one existing platform skip, including generation-integrity verification.

Post-conflict proof passed: production core types, affected agent test types, scoped lint, zero runtime cycles and zero Madge cycles. The focused wrapper passed all 30 tests across three files, including the lint-suppression audit and the real admitted-run foreground regression, with final generation verification (915.00s wrapper / 904.59s runner). Its tooling, ordinary-submit and foreground shard durations were 35.67s, 343.39s and 224.81s. Exact-head hosted CI remains the broad landing gate; no hosted reruns or re-pushes merely for green are requested.

Local limitations: Knip's script-export scan passed with zero findings, but production/full-tree scans reached the existing 600-second limit (ETIMEDOUT after 605s); those scans are incomplete, not green. The unchanged Gateway remote-catalog integration test's two schema variants timed out at their existing 120-second limit on the lane and clean main `fd80f72fa0cba77784b759cc9533048fb48a9b4d`. Main's complete run took 1461.28s including its successful 10m 37s runtime build and cold compilation; test wall time was 673.62s. Lane diagnostics stopped before `startGatewayWithClient` returned; a diagnostic rerun's second case additionally encountered cleanup/shutdown fallout. No timeout, retry, skip, assertion, or baseline was changed to hide these failures. The catalog owner's seven publication cases passed, including coherent discovery, pinned runs, pricing/shutdown, and adopted-plugin recovery; full Gateway boundary proof remains subject to exact-head CI.

Production delta after conflict integration: +408/-940, **532 net lines removed**, excluding tests, test support, fixtures, generated directories, and declarations. This uses the campaign's 500–999 exception with the coverage log below.

Independent review found and corrected an ordinary terminal-effects rebinding gap; failed-media cleanup changes were fully withdrawn. Fresh review confirmed those corrections. Its sole remaining P2 requests zero-length insertions in an internal replacement helper; declined because its sole caller rejects empty normalized oldText and empty fuzzy matches before producing spans (`edit-diff.ts:294,320`), with retained external-boundary rejection tests. No public SDK surface exposes the helper.

Conflict-only integration onto main `72ccf43fdc6fbe8f4534b84b86f1c8a8909032f5` preserves main's scope-or-plain-callback assertions, full provider-dispatch check, and real admitted-run fixture. The fixture now revokes during the remaining persistence await rather than the deleted optional restoration await. A fresh integrated review completed with four findings, all investigated and declined: physical-database replacement, reentrant relay replacement, and cache-TTL branch-restore fencing are the exact accepted synthetic scenarios documented above; the Decision post-await full assertion already exists in pinned main, rather than being introduced by this change. That review is not claimed scoped-clean. No accepted/actionable finding remains; no review was rerun merely to change its verdict.

The retained runner tests later caught two additional PR-caused failures: opt-out during steering/operator preparation still dispatched external Decision inference, and post-persistence authority closure still reached a foreground observer. Both were repaired at their actual effect boundaries without restoring model-equality/restoration machinery; the tests remain unchanged and both now pass. A fresh full-candidate review after those repairs returned scoped-clean at P0–P2, confirming the retained consent, full host authority, terminal binding and media cleanup boundaries.

Terminal-effects owner suite passed 9/9, including the new duplicate-completion binding regression (37 ms initially, 27 ms in the final run): 258.71 s including cold compilation, 290.47 s initial wrapper wall time. A pre-fix mutation replay was not run; no baseline-test claim is made. The earlier additional focused shard passed 21 files / 653 tests (one existing platform skip), 3219.42s. The final corrected 34-file wrapper took 4947.52s wall time (4936.42s runner), using the repository test wrapper with maxWorkers=1 and isolated state. Its shard times were 728.27s, 697.47s, 2323.20s, 252.85s, 182.46s, 200.56s and 207.09s, including cold compilation. CI seconds are pending the exact pushed head.

prs.title: fix(agents): don't fail media completion when wake deadline expires with pending handoff
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a media generation completion is accepted into the durable session-delivery queue behind the requester's own active run, the handoff is already owned by that queue and drains when the run ends. The caller-side retry loop still threw at the 120s handoff deadline, and the scheduler recorded a blocked delivery failure plus a false "completion wake failed after successful generation" log. The queued handoff was not actually lost, but the task looked failed. Marking the turn successful at that deadline would also be wrong: queue custody is not delivery.

## Why This Change Was Made

`wakeMediaGenerationTaskCompletion` now reports `queueOwned` only when the delivery disposition is `session_queued`, and includes the durable `queueEntryId`. Until the deadline, admission retries are unchanged. If that deadline expires while the handoff is still pending:

- a queue-owned receipt is not failed and not completed as success
- later observation reads that same receipt instead of enqueueing again, so the handoff is not rewritten or dropped
- delivery finalizes the operation as success
- a permanent queue failure still records the blocked terminal result
- any other pending handoff (refused admission, transient read, unconfirmed settling) still fails closed, so retention and failure recording stay intact

## User Impact

`image_generate` / `video_generate` / `music_generate` no longer record a false delivery failure when the requester's own turn still holds a queue-owned completion past 120s. The generated media stays queued for delivery. The turn is not marked successful unless the media actually lands, and a later permanent delivery failure is still recorded as blocked.

## Evidence

Head `533a6ef485e373f8f9c3d54dfa88da50a0709bef`.

Real scheduler run (`src/agents/tools/media-generate-background-shared.queue-deadline.test.ts`):

```
{"proof":"pending handoff past wake deadline","operationStatus":"running","endedAt":null,"terminalOutcome":null,"wakeFailures":0,"wakeCalls":63}
{"proof":"handoff delivered after the deadline","operationStatus":"succeeded","terminalOutcome":null,"wakeFailures":0}
{"proof":"media never landed at the wake deadline","operationStatus":"running","endedAt":null,"terminalOutcome":null,"wakeFailures":0}
{"proof":"permanent handoff failure after the deadline","operationStatus":"succeeded","terminalOutcome":"blocked","wakeFailures":2}

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  29 passed (29)
```

Real durable-queue admission (`src/gateway/server-restart-sentinel.media-binding.test.ts`, 12 passed) now requires `queueOwned: true` and the same `queueEntryId` as the pending queue row. Unconfirmed pending handoffs still stop at the deadline with a blocked result (`stops pending handoff retries at the completion deadline`).

Fixes openclaw/openclaw#151964

prs.title: fix(webchat): stage offloaded images for file tools
prs.body:
Fixes #103198

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes file tools being unable to find large WebChat image uploads even though the model can see the image.

## User Impact

WebChat images larger than the 2,000,000-byte inline threshold are available to workspace tools as well as native vision. Small inline images retain their existing behavior; there are no new permissions or configuration settings.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pass offloaded images to the same managed inbound-media staging owner already used by inline WebChat uploads and channel attachments. The staging-only copy does not hydrate a second vision image. Canonical image-reference resolution prefers a staged file over its media-store alias, including when the transcript snapshot predates staging.

The simplification removes the separate staged-image reference wrapper and a duplicate regression case. The complete PR is +30 production lines and +206 test lines against its merge base (down from +60 production/+245 tests). The remaining image reconciliation preserves the existing sandbox boundary rather than adding a WebChat-only runner path.

Thanks to @synthalorian for the fix and @woohahahaaa for the report. No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

## Evidence

An isolated, built Gateway accepted actual `chat.send` image attachments over RPC. A scripted OpenAI Responses provider captured native vision input and called the real `exec` workspace tool. Baseline: `d7ca748acba99c758ab548943642e1156fbcbbca`; candidate: `8c2abc79feecaf0b959c94d292cee63fb567660c`. The affected baseline files are unchanged at the PR merge base.

| Input | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 3,147,780-byte PNG | One vision image; file missing | One vision image; staged file found |
| 378-byte inline PNG | One vision image; staged file found | One vision image; staged file found |

Observed tool output (generated IDs shortened):

```text
baseline / large:
find: 'media/inbound': No such file or directory
(Command exited with code 1)

candidate / large:
-rw------- 1 root root 3147780 ... media/inbound/openclaw-staged-.../input-large---....png

baseline and candidate / small:
-rw------- 1 root root 378 ... media/inbound/openclaw-staged-.../input-small---....png
```

Both candidate turns completed with `successfulToolNames: ["exec"]`; captured requests contained exactly one `input_image` each.

Live-provider check on the same candidate: `gpt-5-mini-2025-08-07` received the large image through an isolated Gateway, invoked the real `exec` tool, and reported `media/inbound/openclaw-staged-.../input-live-large---....png`. The tool output listed that file, the run completed successfully, and there were two provider requests. The test proxy selected the cheap live model instead of the mock model configured for the scripted comparison.

Focused checks in the secretless container:
- `chat-send-user-turn.test.ts`: 23 passed, 38.80 seconds including compilation.
- `images.media-refs.test.ts`: 12 passed, 5.23 seconds, including staged sandbox hydration from a path-less transcript fact.
- Reverting production files to baseline makes the offloaded-image handoff regression fail (`expected [] to deeply equal [...]`) and the staged sandbox hydration regression fail (`failedMediaCount` is 1 instead of 0).
- Changed-file Oxfmt and Oxlint passed; full runtime and Control UI build passed.

No visual UI changes; the proof uses the shipped Gateway RPC boundary.

Merge danger: two-way door; reverting restores the old attachment behavior without a schema or configuration migration. Blast radius is managed image staging and native image-reference resolution; inline-image and sandbox-hydration regressions remain covered.

prs.title: refactor(ui): use native popover for Cron job filters
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cron's advanced Jobs filter still uses a Web Awesome popup. Use the shared native Popover while preserving the filter button, filter values, sorting, reset behavior, and existing selectors.

The Popover owns visibility, expanded state, positioning, outside/Escape dismissal, and focus return. The caller only requests toggles through its handle. The consumer gives its five-field panel enough height to keep Reset visible on a narrow screen; the native owner still limits it to available viewport space. This cut changes only the Jobs filter renderer and its popup CSS.

## Evidence

Current head: `d37f99d0b1b003bbe21824a462f89374682f17a4`. Full UI CI is requested with `ci:full`. The earlier head `5b3ce17fee7169678fd167f74c5b7e0522c7da96` passed all 38 jobs in run [38342167488](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38342167488). Local before/after capture then found that the native default 420-pixel height hid Reset below the initial scroll viewport at 640 × 900. The one-line consumer height override corrects that. Corrected-head production build, paired startup check, and the two targeted screenshots pass; corrected-head full CI passed in [run 38346475404](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38346475404).

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Complete-module independent review | Completed; confirmed the height correction; sole index-only finding resolved by staging the exact reviewed blob |
| Own frozen install | Passed, 137.65 s |
| `pnpm tsgo:ui` | Passed, 32.27 s; before CSS-only correction |
| Directly changed test files | None; no local test suites run |
| Production head build | Corrected head passed, 71.46 s; literal baseline build reused after source/dependency/asset verification |
| Paired strict startup | Corrected head passed, 3.71 s: 342,347 → 342,371 B gzip (+24 B); 1 → 1 startup CSS request |
| Current startup budget | Both measured bundles pass 374,285 B gzip / 1 CSS request |
| Synthetic desktop/light and narrow/dark capture | Passed; retained 2 baseline frames + 2 corrected-head frames (16.99 s); five fields and Reset visible without scrolling |
| Full UI CI | Corrected head passed [run 38346475404](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38346475404) |

The exact retained baseline is `e78a253059eb07d70ea3f7140e1c4e9b9fadc383`, built on this machine from its own frozen install. Baseline source/tree, dependency inputs, and all retained asset hashes were verified before reuse. The 24 B startup difference is below the checker's 64 B build-variance allowance. Startup source maps contain only the existing Cron route descriptor, with no Cron renderer or stylesheet eagerly imported. Startup CSS is unchanged at 49,077 B; the existing 46,080 B advisory remains. No budgets were edited. The older checker still prints its transitional ceiling; the actual values above are assessed against the restored budget.

Production LOC: renderer 150 → 155; stylesheet 1,192 → 1,172; combined 1,342 → 1,327 (−15). No tests, dependency versions, shared primitive APIs, or domain state change.

prs.title: fix(anthropic): distinguish slow CLI auth checks from logout
prs.body:
Fixes #170503

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Claude CLI login reports a valid native login as unauthenticated when its status command takes longer than three seconds to exit.

## User Impact

Existing Claude CLI logins have ten seconds to complete verification on slow hosts. A timed-out or unreadable check gives a status-check and retry step; a confirmed logout still requires login. An unresponsive CLI can now delay discovery or setup for ten seconds instead of three.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reporter measured 3.658 seconds and verified that a ten-second deadline works. The shared probe now preserves timeout as a distinct result, including when authenticated JSON arrived before the process stopped. Interactive and non-interactive setup use the same validation and migration operation. Cancellation, output limits, and native credential ownership remain unchanged.

This overlaps with #170544; this branch also distinguishes timeout and removes the duplicated setup path. Production code decreases by two lines (23 added / 25 removed).

## Evidence

PR CI is the test gate under the maintainer's revised proof policy. It covers the changed Anthropic tests, extension typing, and repository checks. Live proof was intentionally skipped per maintainer policy; the earlier Testbox campaign was stopped and both lane leases were cleaned up.

Regression coverage:

- `distinguishes a timed-out probe even when it already printed authenticated JSON` checks timeout classification and the ten-second deadline.
- `registered %s cli auth reports a timeout with a retry step, not a logout` checks both registered setup paths through the real probe implementation.
- Logout cases cover exit codes 0 and 1; unreadable checks cover both setup paths; discovery publishes native auth only after a positive result.

Changed-file lint: direct `oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json` passed syntax/style checks. The type-aware wrapper with that core config reported unresolved SDK error types because the project excludes extension files; extension-aware checking is deferred to PR CI. Formatting: all six changed files passed `oxfmt --check`; `git diff --check` passed. Deslop removed the duplicated setup branch. The prescribed Codex branch autoreview returned `scoped-clean`, with no actionable P0–P2 findings.

Before the policy change, the real main CLI with an isolated four-second authenticated executable reproduced the false unauthenticated error, and the new timeout regressions failed on main. An earlier local full-module run had 368 passes and one transient-I/O timeout in untouched `session-catalog.test.ts`; this is unclassified and is not claimed as inherited or fixed. No further local test or typecheck runs are required by the revised policy.

Exact-head [CI run 38343590636](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38343590636) passed for `ea2c6e110b231debfa537f3d158d7739fa70c1e9`, including the changed-test lanes, production/test types, core/extension lint, docs, boundary checks, baseline checks, and `openclaw/ci-gate`. The extension/config shard passed 119 tests across 8 files, including all three changed Anthropic test files. All companion PR workflows passed. No CI failures required repair or inherited-failure exceptions.

ClawSweeper reviewed the same head, found no actionable code findings, and marked the fix scope complete. Its live-proof note is intentionally covered by the maintainer policy above: PR CI is the proof gate.

prs.title: fix: report missing node worker credentials
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A node with no usable local provider configuration was reported as needing an update. Removing an environment-backed API key could also leave its unresolved placeholder treated as an opaque credential, producing a provider 401 instead of a node setup diagnosis.

Reuse the existing node inference setup message at native launch admission. At the provider-auth owner, reject the exact configuration path when the canonical resolution facts still mark it unresolved. Already-resolved opaque credential bytes remain valid, including strings that resemble environment placeholders. Inventory-change retries and admission rules are unchanged.

Net production LOC: +5. The setup message has one lightweight shared owner; no new configuration, protocol, or credential format is introduced.

## Evidence

- Missing-provider diagnosis reproduced twice each in repository and empty sessions with the same node build.
- Real config-resolution-stage proof: unresolved auth present before fix (12.287 s), absent after fix while resolved opaque bytes remain usable (4.162 s).
- `pnpm test src/agents/model-auth-provider-config.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 8 passed, 44.131 s.
- Native launch adapter boundary suite: 43 passed, 208.13 s wrapper time / 82.96 s Vitest time.
- Independent review found no actionable P0/P1 issues. Final live replay: removed-key and missing-provider configurations each failed promptly with setup guidance twice in repository and empty sessions (8 failures total); four valid-key restoration turns succeeded. Invalid-key trials surfaced provider 401 errors promptly. Environment changes were picked up after restarting the node.

Release-note context: missing native worker credentials/configuration now produce setup guidance rather than an update warning or an attempted request using an unresolved environment reference.

## Updated validation

The worker baseline investigation found obsolete early-final timing assertions and two independent settlement defects. The transcript-authority repair is #170556; the completion notification repair is #170575. The E2E alignment is tracked in #170537. All four selected E2Es passed on the final test-only head in CI 38344788931, and #170537 is merged. Main was merged into this PR once, without conflicts, at 61992bcc9a072245f305a733e79d9960b4e9a267. The credential-diagnostics diff remains the same eight files, and all 70 introduced +/- lines match the original independently reviewed patch. Basic formatting/lint and diff checks passed. Final CI 38345859459 completed with all four repaired worker E2Es passing: native 42.02s Vitest / 43.47s runner; upgrade 161.08s / 162.72s; required same-session 111.59s / 113.72s; skill-library 65.80s / 68.19s. Two unrelated baseline failures remain and are covered by the authorized inherited-failure landing exception:

- `check-test-types-core-4`: `src/commands/config-preflight-snapshot.test.ts:41` imports the now-private `readConfigPreflightSnapshot` (TS2724), introduced by #170530. The implementation and test blobs are identical on main and this tested merge; this PR touches neither file.
- `checks-node-changed-compact-large-7-1`: `src/cli/update-cli.deferred-completion.test.ts:114`, case `finalize commits a validated downgrade without changing channels (9999.1.1, valid=false)`, expects `Gateway did not settle.` after #169280 introduced the more specific readiness guidance. A main-baseline probe changing only the suite label reproduced the exact expected/actual difference: [CI 38347391422, job 115132090422](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38347391422/job/115132090422), based on main `c7bbfd1281cd673a9a76e95acb43f33b4c7f3be6`. Probe #170643 is being closed without merging. This PR touches neither that test nor the update implementation.

All other completed CI and security checks passed. Both baseline defects are recorded with the campaign coordinator.

prs.title: improve: keep provider transports out of Doctor and session decoding
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Doctor, session import, and other non-agent paths that decode session transcripts loaded every provider transport and the provider SDKs, because the session codec imported one small helper from the broad `@openclaw/ai/transports` barrel.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. `openclaw doctor --fix` and other session-decoding paths load fewer modules: the built Doctor config flow goes from 3894 to 3618 modules and no longer loads the transports bundle or the openai SDK.

## Why This Change Was Made

`session-manager-codec.ts` only needs `stripCompactionReplayCheckpointInPlace`, which depends solely on `isCompactionReplayCheckpoint` in the existing checkpoint leaf. The helper moves into that leaf and stays re-exported from the transports barrel, so the public `@openclaw/ai/transports` exports do not change. The codec imports the leaf directly, the same shape #162609 used for the session readers.

This came out of investigating the nightly SIGTERM in `src/cli/gateway-cli/pre-bootstrap.process.test.ts` ("accepts a Doctor-repaired escaped reference and refuses later config drift"). That failure was not a code regression, and this PR does not change that test's wall time measurably; details below.

## Evidence

- Built Doctor config flow (`loadAndMaybeMigrateDoctorConfig` on a legacy-config fixture, interleaved A/B, 5 pairs; "before" reproduces the removed edge by importing the transports bundle in the same window): modules 3895 → 3618; median wall 4.71 s → 4.29 s; median CPU 3.36 s → 3.28 s. The transports bundle alone is 1014 modules when imported standalone.
- Source-mode Doctor preflight census: 5462 → 5109 modules; `state-migrations.doctor` subtree 2110 → 1778; no `@openclaw/ai/transports` importer remains in that graph.
- `pnpm test packages/ai/src/transports/provider-compaction-replay.test.ts src/agents/sessions/session-manager-codec.test.ts src/agents/sessions/session-manager.persistence-compat.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 15 + 31 + 15 passed.
- `pnpm test src/cli/gateway-cli/pre-bootstrap.process.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, alternating base/fix on a heavily loaded host: 17/17 passed every run; the Doctor-repaired case took 36.4 s / 31.9 s (base) and 38.4 s / 33.1 s (fix), which is noise.
- `pnpm build` passed, including plugin-SDK export and CLI bootstrap import checks. `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`: format, lint, core and core-test typecheck, import boundaries, and ratchets passed; the dead-export scan failed only on unrelated existing exports (`src/agents/failover-error.ts`, `src/tts/tts.ts`, `ui/src/app/*`, `scripts/lib/postgres-schema-catalog.mts`, a workboard fixture).
- Codex autoreview: scoped-clean.

<details>
<summary>Nightly pre-bootstrap process test investigation</summary>

- Failing full CI run 38292371460 (head 6112e37e00), `checks-node-agentic-cli`: the case took 60281 ms and was killed; its retry in the same job took 52996 ms. The previous full CI run on 506684822c ran the same case in 30671 ms.
- Across the 95 test files present in both jobs, the failing job was 1.69× slower overall, including in-process suites unrelated to Doctor or config (`run-loop.test.ts` 1.92×, `capability-cli.test.ts` 2.06×). The case itself was 1.97× slower. Same runner image, different hosted region.
- Paired local runs at both heads show the same Doctor step profile. The "Config unavailable" fallback and the three synchronous SQLite snapshot children appear on 506684822c too. #169622 is not in the failing head.
- The case's cost dates from #151025 (2026-09-25), when it moved from the startup repair owner to the full `runDoctorConfigPreflight({ repairPrefixedConfig: true, doctorOnlyStateMigrations: true })`. Doctor loads every migration family even for an empty state dir, so the case runs at about half of its 60 s deadline on a healthy runner. This PR leaves the deadline and the test unchanged.

</details>
