prs.title: perf(memory): evict superseded embedding cache rows first at the cap
prs.body:
Refs #114612

## What Problem This Solves

`memory_embedding_cache` is capped at 50,000 rows. When new vectors would take it past the cap (insertion-time reservation from #164083) or it is already over the cap (the post-publication prune), the cache deletes the rows with the oldest `updated_at`. It does not look at whether a published chunk still uses a row.

Editing a memory file changes its chunk hashes, so the vectors for the old text are never read again, but they keep their place in the cap. A cache that sits at the cap is mostly such rows, and plain oldest-first order deletes a vector that a live, unchanged chunk still needs whenever that vector is older than the superseded ones. The next full reindex then pays the provider to embed unchanged text again.

## User Impact

At the cap, the vectors of unchanged indexed text survive eviction while superseded vectors are available to take their place, so a forced reindex of unchanged content makes no provider request. In the real CLI run below, on a store seeded to the 50,000-row cap with superseded vectors and three new files added, the base build deleted the vector of an unchanged file and re-embedded it on the next reindex (1 request); the head build made 0 requests.

Nothing changes below the cap, and the number of rows deleted at the cap is the same as before. The database file size, schema, and row cap do not change.

## Why This Change Was Made

`docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md` describes the cache as bounded by the existing row cap. The bound stays exactly as it is; this change only decides which rows fill the deletions the cap already makes.

The eviction preference is narrow on purpose:

- Only rows of the active provider identities are preferred. Rows of any other provider, model, or provider key keep plain oldest-first order, so a fallback or previously configured provider is not singled out.
- A preferred row has no published chunk carrying its hash, and was written before the oldest published chunk. A full reindex rewrites every chunk, so after one such a row predates the index that dropped it.
- A row written at or after the oldest published chunk keeps plain oldest-first order even when nothing references it yet. It may be a vector a failed rebuild cached for its retry, or one another sync cached and has not published.
- The fence is read from `memory_index_chunks` in SQL, so it holds across processes and restarts. No new state is kept in memory.
- The deletion count is computed exactly as before. Preferred rows fill it first; if there are fewer, the remainder is taken oldest-first, as today. At or below the cap nothing is deleted.

For the review checkpoint in `docs/reference/database-schemas/storage-changes.md`, the persisted effect is this: when the cap deletes, it picks superseded vectors of the active identities before other rows. The cap, the number of rows deleted, the schema, durability, and rollback do not change. `memory-builtin.md` documented the old order ("removes the oldest entries"), and that sentence is updated. The cache is derived data. Any deleted vector can be recomputed by the provider, and the run below shows a base build reading a head-written store with no provider request. #114612 is the linked discussion for cache retention.

## The change in one sentence

Capacity eviction of `memory_embedding_cache` first takes, oldest first, active-identity rows that no published chunk references and that were written before the oldest published chunk, then falls back to plain oldest-first for the rest of the same, unchanged count.

Diff shape: 1 commit, 8 files, 559 insertions and 15 deletions. Production is 108 insertions and 12 deletions, docs 12 and 3, tests 439 and 0:

- `manager-embedding-cache.ts`: `evictMemoryEmbeddingCacheRows` and `deleteOldestUnreferencedMemoryEmbeddingCacheRows`, used by both `pruneMemoryEmbeddingCache` and `upsertMemoryEmbeddingCache`.
- `cache.prune` and the cache upsert header carry `unreferencedFirst: { identities }` to the existing publication worker (`manager-publication-task.ts`, `manager-publication.worker.ts`, `manager-database-context.ts`, `manager-embedding-cache-ops.ts`).
- In `pruneEmbeddingCache`, the return expression is now a `const` followed by `return pruned ?? false`. The behavior is the same; the change keeps `manager-database-context.ts` within its 700-line cap.
- Docs: `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`.

Tests: three unit cases in `manager-embedding-cache.test.ts` and one manager file `manager.cache-unreferenced-eviction.test.ts` with seven cases.

The identity comparison casts the TEXT key columns (`CAST(provider AS text)` and so on). This is a no-op on values. It stops SQLite from answering the identity filter through the primary key and then sorting every matching row by `updated_at`, which reads each vector. With it, SQLite walks the `updated_at` index and stops at the limit. In the benchmark below, removing only the three casts makes the median batch cost 126.04 ms with 1,000 chunks and 123.07 ms with 10,000 chunks, against 3.93 ms and 31.78 ms with them (output quoted there).

## Contract

| Case | Outcome | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Cache at or below the cap | nothing deleted | unchanged |
| Insertion or prune past the cap | same number of rows deleted as before | unchanged cap |
| Active-identity row, no published chunk carries its hash, written before the oldest published chunk | deleted first, oldest first | superseded text |
| Row a published chunk carries | deleted only when no preferred row is left, oldest first | live content |
| Active-identity unreferenced row written at or after the oldest published chunk | plain oldest-first | a retry's or another sync's unpublished vector |
| Rows of another provider, model, or provider key | plain oldest-first | a fallback or previous provider may be switched back to |
| Empty published index, or no active identities | plain oldest-first | no fence |
| Full rebuild fails before publication, including a source that fails partway | no extra deletion; the retry reuses cached vectors | unchanged failure semantics |
| Incremental sync | same rule; unchanged chunks keep their `updated_at`, so the fence is older and fewer rows qualify | the fence never moves past a live chunk |
| Schema, config keys, public API | unchanged | none added |

## Upgrade and rollback compatibility

No `.sql` file, migration, table, column, or index changes, and `PRAGMA user_version` is 26 before and after (transcript below). The only persisted effect is which rows remain after a deletion the cap already makes.

- Upgrade: the head build runs `memory index --force` on a store the base build created and filled to the cap, exit 0. The vector of the unchanged `delta.md` keeps its row and its original `updated_at`, and rows of another identity are untouched.
- Rollback: the base build runs `memory index --force` on the store the head build last wrote, with 0 provider requests and no change to rows or checksums, then answers `memory search`.

## Evidence

All of the following ran on one machine (Mac Studio, arm64, Node v24.21.0, macOS), base `e61083f8f116b50e742a64e219c6a26342e67fcd` (`origin/main` at the time), 2026-10-12 Pacific. The pushed head is `d2c812e581e352fac0afc766a652fba003e3249c`, tree `cb315397707caa408d9d255b08e191a073f1102b`.

- At that exact tree: `pnpm check:changed`, and the two changed test files.
- At tree `9b76f5c5fe6`: the red/green run, the owning directory, and the type checks. It differs from the pushed tree only in `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md` (3 insertions, 2 deletions).
- At tree `445ba525b57`: the build and the real CLI run. It differs from the pushed tree only in `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md` and in the edge-case unit test of `manager-embedding-cache.test.ts`. No production file differs.

The machine is shared with other jobs, so wall times are upper bounds.

### Build

`pnpm build` on the head and on the base, both exit 0:

```
head: [build-all] phase timings: total 21m 10.7s; slowest tsdown-packages 17m 20.4s; write-unified-entry-dts 1m 50.1s; tsdown-ai 59.2s; tsdown 27.2s; ui:build 11.8s
base: [build-all] phase timings: total 20m 51.6s; slowest tsdown-packages 17m 6.8s; write-unified-entry-dts 1m 48.2s; tsdown-ai 57.8s; tsdown 25.6s; ui:build 11.9s
```

### Type checks

```
$ pnpm tsgo:extensions && pnpm tsgo:extensions:test
tsgo exit=0
```

### Tests

The two changed test files at the pushed tree:

```
$ pnpm test extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager.cache-unreferenced-eviction.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-embedding-cache.test.ts
 ✓ manager-embedding-cache.test.ts > memory embedding cache > loads cached embeddings for the active provider key 46ms
 ✓ manager-embedding-cache.test.ts > memory embedding cache > handles legacy JSON cache storage without losing row identity 11ms
 ✓ manager-embedding-cache.test.ts > memory embedding cache > handles retired import cache storage without losing row identity 3ms
 ✓ manager-embedding-cache.test.ts > memory embedding cache > handles binary cache storage without losing row identity 9ms
 ✓ manager-embedding-cache.test.ts > memory embedding cache > reserves space before replacing cached vectors at capacity 5ms
 ✓ manager-embedding-cache.test.ts > memory embedding cache > reserves only missing capacity: below capacity 6ms

### Measured eviction cost

The benchmark uses one file-backed SQLite database and the real schema from `ensureMemoryIndexSchema`. It calls the real `pruneMemoryEmbeddingCache` with 1536-dimension vectors. The cache is at 50,000 rows. Live rows are the oldest, and the unreferenced rows predate the published chunks. Each round adds 100 rows and then times one prune, which is one 100-row eviction batch inside a transaction. There are 15 rounds per mode. It ran in the build directory of tree `445ba525b57`, whose production files are identical to the pushed tree. The benchmark file is not part of the diff.

```
chunks=1000 mode=oldest-first batch=100 rounds=15 median_ms=1.10 max_ms=2.33 cache_rows_after=50000 live_rows_after=0/1000
chunks=1000 mode=unreferenced-first batch=100 rounds=15 median_ms=3.93 max_ms=4.62 cache_rows_after=50000 live_rows_after=1000/1000
chunks=10000 mode=oldest-first batch=100 rounds=15 median_ms=1.02 max_ms=2.15 cache_rows_after=50000 live_rows_after=8500/10000
chunks=10000 mode=unreferenced-first batch=100 rounds=15 median_ms=31.78 max_ms=42.15 cache_rows_after=50000 live_rows_after=10000/10000
```

Load average (1, 5, 15 minutes) at the start was 5.16, 11.07, 12.64.

The same benchmark with only the three `eb.cast(...)` calls in `deleteOldestUnreferencedMemoryEmbeddingCacheRows` replaced by plain column references (reverted afterwards, `git checkout`), load average 6.86, 8.71, 10.86:

```
chunks=1000 mode=unreferenced-first batch=100 rounds=15 median_ms=126.04 max_ms=132.96 cache_rows_after=50000 live_rows_after=1000/1000
chunks=10000 mode=unreferenced-first batch=100 rounds=15 median_ms=123.07 max_ms=132.23 cache_rows_after=50000 live_rows_after=10000/10000
``` The added cost is two scans of `memory_index_chunks`, one for the minimum `updated_at` and one for the hash set. SQLite evaluates each scan once per statement. The cost grows with the number of chunks and is paid only when the cache is over the cap. In the same runs, oldest-first deleted every live row (1,000 of 1,000) and 1,500 of 10,000. Unreferenced-first deleted none.

### Measured test cost

The seven manager cases take 1.8 to 2.7 s each in the run above (3.3 to 4.6 s in the run at tree `9b76f5c5fe6`, under more load), which is above the per-test budget in `docs/help/testing/writing-tests.md`. They stay at the manager seam because the contract runs between the sync paths, the insertion header, the post-publication prune, and the publication worker. No cheaper layer exercises that. The ordering, fallback, and multi-identity cases are in the millisecond unit tests.

## Gaps, stated plainly

- **Which rows survive at the cap changes.** The count, cap, schema, and rollback do not change, but the documented order ("removes the oldest entries") does. A superseded vector can be deleted before a live one that is newer. If its text is restored later, that costs one re-embedding, and under plain oldest-first the same row would usually have gone anyway, because it is old.
- **The fence is the oldest published chunk across all sources and models.** After incremental syncs it can be far in the past, so fewer rows qualify, and the eviction falls back to oldest-first. Nothing extra is deleted.
- **The fence compares clocks.** Chunk and cache `updated_at` both come from `Date.now()` in the writing process. A writer whose clock runs behind can make a row look older than it is. The only effect is on order. The count is unchanged.
- **Eviction is slower when there are many chunks.** It takes about 32 ms per 100-row batch with 10,000 chunks, against about 1 ms oldest-first. It runs only above the cap, inside the existing worker write transaction.
- **Stale identities, byte budgets, and age-based retention are not addressed.** Rows of a provider the user switched away from keep plain oldest-first order. The row cap is still the only bound.
- **Real-provider proof was not run.** The CLI run uses a local stub provider. Embedding quality and real provider behavior are not exercised. No built Gateway process was run; the CLI uses the same manager and publication worker.
- **Full suite not run.** The changed lanes (extensions, extension tests, docs) and the owning directory are the suites this diff can break. CI covers the rest.

prs.title: fix(gateway): report resolved thinking level in startup banner
prs.body:
[AI-assisted]

## What Problem

On `main` (2026.10.2), the Gateway startup banner reports `thinking=medium` for a run whose resolved thinking level is actually `off`. Reported in #170180: with `agentRuntime: claude-cli`, no explicit `thinkingDefault`/`params.thinking`, and `anthropic/claude-opus-4-8` as the primary model, the startup line says `thinking=medium` while `resolveClaudeThinkingProfile` resolves `defaultLevel: "off"` for Opus 4.7/4.8 (the documented omitted-thinking default, which forces `MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=0` and adds no `--effort`). The banner therefore contradicts the real launch budget.

## Why

`formatAgentModelStartupDetails` (`src/gateway/server-startup-log.ts`) resolved the level via `resolveThinkingDefault(...)` and then rewrote it:

```ts
thinking = resolvedThinking === "off" ? "medium" : resolvedThinking;
```

That substitution was a cosmetic default, but the resolved value is authoritative: `off` is a real, intentional, user-visible level (e.g. Claude Opus 4.7/4.8 on claude-cli). Reporting `medium` while executing `off` misleads operators diagnosing reasoning behaviour and makes the banner unusable as a source of truth. Per the review on #170180, the narrow, correct repair is to display the resolved level rather than changing Claude defaults or launch-budget semantics.

## User Impact

Operators relying on the startup line to know their effective thinking level now see the truth (`thinking=off`) instead of a fabricated `medium`. No launch behaviour, defaults, or budget semantics change — this is report-only. Explicit `off`/`ultra`/configured levels already displayed correctly and are unchanged.

## Evidence

New regression test fails on unfixed `main` and passes with the fix:

before (substitution present):

```text
 FAIL  src/gateway/server-startup-log.test.ts > gateway startup log > reports the authoritative resolved level when a provider model default is off
AssertionError: expected 'thinking=medium, fast=off' to be 'thinking=off, fast=off'
```

after (fix applied):

```text
 ✓ |gateway-server (gateway-server-parallel)| src/gateway/server-startup-log.test.ts > gateway startup log > reports the authoritative resolved level when a provider model default is off 6ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  15 passed (15)
```

Closes #170180.

prs.title: fix: native-app sessions fail to resume after restart
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Authenticated native-app conversations could be marked failed after a Gateway restart despite retaining their original operator source. After fixing that admission, production recovery exposed a second failure: the missing-web-search guidance callback re-read session capability metadata after its worker preparation scope had ended, aborting tool construction before the resumed turn could execute.

Eligible native turns now resume in the same session under the original operator's current authority. The callback reuses the requester policy the turn already prepared. Already-terminal sessions still require explicit recovery. No schema, credential, role, configuration, or intentional permission change is included.

## Implementation

Recovery admits only the exact saved source run, agent, session key, session ID, and lifecycle revision, then delegates identity, device, authentication, role, grants, and revocation to the existing restoration owner. Unowned and mismatched internal input remains refused.

The merge with main `2bd6ca195418` retains #170252's browser/channel steering predicate unchanged. Follow-up `8581ef5701c1` passes `runtimeCapabilityProfile.policy` through the existing `preparedRequesterPolicy` argument in the embedded attempt's web-search callback. It adds no new policy owner, asynchronous execution replay, main-thread SQL, or guard bypass. The same omission remains in pinned main `33a438a7624d`.

## Evidence

- Unchanged `5804c062c649` reproduced the production preparation failure. A separate unchanged-build Inspector diagnostic captured the exact escape: `onWebSearchConfiguration` → native web-search routing → requester-policy resolution → unprepared lookup of the recovering session. Inspector was absent from the final proof.
- The persisted-dashboard regression fails before the fix at that exact callback: two intended failures, seven controls passing. With the repair, all nine cases pass, including native search, configured/disabled search, inherited dashboard denial, attribution cancellation, and permission rebuild/reset. Full file wrapper wall time: 41.42 seconds; approximately 2.9 seconds of test execution, with compiler/import preparation dominating. The fixture uses real SQLite metadata and worker preparation; only the existing coding-tool factory is mocked to invoke the real callback.
- All 18 native-search sibling cases pass (59.24 seconds wrapper wall time). Production types, the affected test typecheck shard, targeted typed lint, formatting, whitespace, line-growth and maximum-line checks pass.
- Fresh independent Codex autoreview is scoped-clean through P0–P2. The prior 17 combined native/browser/channel/refusal/composition cases passed at `5804c062c649`; their recovery guard is unchanged by this follow-up. These remain prior-head evidence, distinct from the exact-head production run below.
- The supported `sourcePerformance` runtime build passes in 75.18 seconds. Build identity: `2026.10.2-8581ef5701c1-2026-10-13T04-12-22.351Z`. Separate type checks cover affected production/test sources; public package declaration publication is not claimed. Exact-head CI seconds/results are pending.

## Exact-head production recovery and authority proof

Commit `8581ef5701c1ad70990a4ad5ab352312ef0a64eb`, isolated real Gateway, signed `MACOS_APP`/`UI` protocol client and its exact issued device token. Production `chat.send` captured custody for three synthetic sessions. Original Gateway PID 14537 was cold-killed (exit -9); successor PID 14668 automatically recovered eligible turns without another user turn or Resume action.

| Control | Same session | Actual production effect | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Exact retained native source | Yes | Exactly one real `write`; sentinel exists | done; no active run |
| Device revoked after recovery admission | Yes | No write result or sentinel | killed; no active run |
| Delegated input without source custody | Yes | No recovery provider request or sentinel | refused with `delegated_authority_unavailable`; failed/inactive |

The allowed continuation completed before public `device.token.revoke` revoked the original native device. The revoked sibling had already entered its recovery model request. Releasing an offered write after revocation caused production owner cancellation before the offered tool call was consumed. Strict checks observed zero production fallback attempts, zero fallback HTTP requests, zero provider errors, and six total provider requests: three originals, two allowed recovery requests (write and final text), and one revoked recovery request.

Selected redacted runtime observations, October 12, 2026, Pacific:

```text
21:14:32.495 marked 3 startup-orphaned main session(s) for restart recovery
allowed: decision=started reason=dispatch_started
revoked: decision=started reason=dispatch_started
unowned: decision=blocked reason=delegated_authority_unavailable
21:14:35.258 device token revoked device=<synthetic-native-device> role=operator
21:14:35.267 [model-fetch] aborted name=AbortError code=OPENCLAW_DIRECT_ABORT
21:14:35.287 lane task error: Restart recovery operator authority changed; start a new user turn.
```

Artifact identities:

- Callback source SHA-256: `6e7b69133aa3fbf9f2f46fce6c23998de8d99d2dbfe4df465179d1c8a7696fd3`; compiled callback `dist/builtin-openclaw-Bgs0gAjQ.mjs`: `3f68e3913525f93c36ecae91c6f5731a3a696c1a861f475e7cf01c0859068674`.
- Recovery-store source: `8f4048720a346b97759943c964580986f75b752732cf558ec50607f744f8eaae`; compiled recovery chunk: `306759f468082ba43d83a7fc93e7cbf13e06b3adbe9bff8f0eeb54e3bc0e4150`.

## Proof scope and limits

Authentication, source capture/restoration, SQLite persistence, startup recovery, embedded OpenClaw execution, provider transport, and the filesystem write tool are production code. The HTTP provider is synthetic; the signed native protocol client is not the Mac UI app. Current `chat.send` supplies external-user provenance, so stopped isolated transcripts reconstruct historical native missing-provenance data. The unowned control has delegated provenance and custody removed. Recorded before/after comparisons show all 30 capability projection facts unchanged and the allowed/revoked native source records retained exactly. No authorization or agent-service mock is involved.

Revocation cancels the admitted turn while its provider response is held; this proves cancellation prevents the offered write, not an independently paused write-specific boundary. An ordinary public profile refresh and single session-create retry was needed during fixture startup, after confirming no partial session existed; no independent profile bug is claimed. No exact-head subprocess red/green baseline is claimed beyond the separately recorded pre-fix failure and regression.

All proof-owned Gateway/client processes and temporary sleep-prevention helpers were joined and independently confirmed absent. Workboard was disabled; its build-generated asset-digest manifest is preserved locally and excluded from the PR. The operator Gateway, existing patches, UI source, config/state and external accounts were untouched by these checks. Earlier backport proof and recovery evidence remain preserved separately.

prs.title: perf(memory-wiki): resolve wiki_get path lookups without reading every page
prs.body:
Related: #145732 makes the `wiki_get` and search paths cancellable and edits the same `getMemoryWikiPage` block; its lookup still reads every page, now abortably. This PR makes a path-shaped lookup read one page instead. The two are complementary and overlap textually in one hunk (see "Relation to open PRs" below).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `wiki_get` with a basename (`p7`) or an extensionless path (`concepts/p7`) opens, reads and parses every Markdown page in the vault before returning one of them.

`getMemoryWikiPage` tried the exact `dir/page.md` path, and for any other lookup called `readQueryableWikiPages`, then `resolveQueryableWikiPageByLookup` over the whole list to pick a single page. The lookup only needs the file listing to learn which page to open, but the listing was used to read everything. On a 2,000-page vault each such lookup costs about 230 to 600 ms and 2,009 file opens on a shared Mac Studio, and the cost grows linearly with the vault. Through the shipped `openclaw wiki get` command, the same lookup costs 8,036 page reads: 2,009 for the lookup and 6,027 for the vault source sync that every entry point runs first.

## User Impact

User impact: the lookup step of `wiki_get` by basename or extensionless path reads one page instead of the whole vault (about 13 ms and 1 open instead of about 230 to 600 ms and 2,009 opens at 2,000 pages). End to end through `openclaw wiki get` on that vault, a basename or extensionless lookup drops from 8,036 to 6,028 page reads per command with byte-identical output; the remaining 6,027 come from the vault source sync, which this PR does not change. Which page is returned, its content, line slicing and the session visibility filter are unchanged. ID lookups and lookups that match nothing cost what they did before.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveQueryableWikiPageByLookup` tries four path tiers in order (path, path plus `.md`, path without extension, basename) over the sorted listing and only then the page ID. Those four tiers depend only on file names, so they can be answered from the listing and the matching candidates read one at a time, in tier then path order, stopping at the first page that parses and is visible to the session. That is the page the full read returns, because both walk the same sorted listing and the full read keeps listing order.

The ID tier cannot be answered the same way. The compiled digest lists page IDs as of the last compile, so a page added or edited since then with the same ID and an earlier path would be missed. IDs, every miss, and any lookup whose candidates are all invisible or invalid therefore keep the existing full read, which now reuses the listing already taken instead of listing the vault a second time.

The change is one function that decides how to resolve the lookup (`resolveQueryableWikiPageForLookup`) in a new `query-page-lookup.ts`, which also takes over `resolveQueryableWikiPageByLookup` unchanged. `getMemoryWikiPage` calls it with callbacks for the exact read, the listing and the page read. The split is required by the repo's line-cap ratchet, which rejects any growth of `query.ts` (cap 700, file already over); `apply.ts`, the only other caller of `resolveQueryableWikiPageByLookup`, now imports it from the new module.

Diff shape: 4 files, `query.ts` shrinks, the new module is 85 lines, the new test file is 186 lines.

<details>
<summary>Contract table</summary>

| Case | Expected |
|---|---|
| Exact `dir/page.md` path, visible | unchanged: read directly, no listing |
| Basename or extensionless path | listing plus one page read, same page as before |
| Several pages share a basename | first in sorted path order that parses and is visible; later ones are not read |
| First candidate not visible to the sandboxed session | next candidate is returned, not null |
| All candidates invisible or invalid | full read as before, listing reused |
| Exact path exists but is invisible | listing, candidates, then full read as before (that page can be read up to three times) |
| ID lookup (`concept.p7`) | full read, same page as before, same number of reads |
| Same name matches by path tier and by ID | path tier wins, as before |
| Duplicate IDs, one page added or edited after the last compile | full read: earliest sorted page wins, as before; the digest is not consulted |
| Page added or renamed since the last compile | found; the listing is live |
| No match (including a title such as `Page 5`) | null via the full read, same number of reads as before |
| Candidate swapped for a symlink outside the vault | `FsSafeError` as before (existing tests) |
| Unrelated page refused by the vault boundary | no longer fails a lookup that resolves through the path tiers, because that page is not read; ID lookups, misses and the matched page itself still throw |
| Claim id lookups | unchanged, digest claim precedence kept |

Deliberate limitations:

- A miss still reads the whole vault. A lookup that matches nothing cannot be proven absent without it.
- ID lookups are not accelerated, for the digest staleness reason above.
- A page that is both a candidate and invisible or invalid is read once by the candidate loop and once more by the fallback full read.

</details>

### Relation to open PRs

- #145732 (search timeouts and cancellation): its `getMemoryWikiPage` hunk threads an `AbortSignal` into `readExactWikiPage`, `readQueryableWikiPages` and the digest reads, and keeps the whole-vault read for non-exact lookups. It does not change how many pages a lookup reads, so this PR is not redundant with it. Whichever lands second resolves about 15 lines in that block. The signal would thread into this change through the `listFiles` and `readPages` callbacks, plus one `throwIfAborted()` at the top of the candidate loop in `findQueryableWikiPageByPathLookup`.

## Stored Data

No persisted data model changes. `wiki_get` still reads the same page files and returns the same page; the listing and page reads are in memory for one call, so there is no schema, migration, cache, or file format change and nothing to upgrade or roll back.

## Evidence

All of the following ran on one machine at the pushed tree, base `072f977edd4`, head `84f60b3fa73`. Mac Studio (Darwin 27.0.0, arm64), Node v24.21.0, shared with other jobs (load average 47 during the sitting), so absolute milliseconds vary run to run; read counts are exact.

### Build

```

Every command first runs the vault source sync (`syncMemoryWikiImportedSources`), which hashes the content of all 2,009 pages three times (`resolveMemoryWikiVaultSourceGeneration`, 4,018 plus 2,009 = 6,027 reads) and is identical in both arms. The lookup itself is the remaining line: 2,009 page reads on the base, 1 on the head. The Gateway `wiki.get` method (`extensions/memory-wiki/src/gateway.ts`) and the `wiki_get` tool (`extensions/memory-wiki/src/tool.ts`) call the same sync before the same `getMemoryWikiPage`.

<details>
<summary>Harness files (complete)</summary>

`count-md-opens.cjs`:

```js
// Counts .md file opens under WIKI_COUNT_ROOT for one CLI process; prints to stderr at exit.
const fs = require("node:fs");
const path = require("node:path");
const { syncBuiltinESMExports } = require("node:module");
const root = path.resolve(process.env.WIKI_COUNT_ROOT || "/nonexistent") + path.sep;
let opens = 0;
const hit = (p) => {
  const s = typeof p === "string" ? p : p instanceof URL ? p.pathname : Buffer.isBuffer(p) ? p.toString() : "";
  if (s.endsWith(".md") && path.resolve(s).startsWith(root)) opens++;
};
const wrap = (obj, name) => {
  const orig = obj[name];
  obj[name] = function (p, ...rest) { hit(p); return orig.call(this, p, ...rest); };
};
wrap(fs, "open"); wrap(fs, "openSync"); wrap(fs.promises, "open");
wrap(fs, "readFile"); wrap(fs, "readFileSync"); wrap(fs.promises, "readFile");
syncBuiltinESMExports();
process.on("exit", () => process.stderr.write(`[md-opens] ${opens} .md opens under ${root}\n`));
```

`make-vault.mjs`:

```js
// Writes the 2,000-page synthetic vault: 600 sources/src<i>.md, 1,400 p<i>.md across entities/concepts/syntheses.
import fs from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
const root = process.argv[2];
const dirs = [["entities", "entity"], ["concepts", "concept"], ["syntheses", "synthesis"]];
const write = (rel, type, id, title) => {
  const f = path.join(root, rel);
  fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(f), { recursive: true });
  fs.writeFileSync(f, `---\ntitle: ${title}\npageType: ${type}\nid: ${id}\n---\n\n# ${title}\n\nbody of ${rel}\n`);
};
for (let i = 0; i < 600; i++) write(`sources/src${i}.md`, "source", `source.src${i}`, `src${i}`);
for (let i = 0; i < 1400; i++) {
  const [dir, type] = dirs[i % 3];
  write(`${dir}/p${i}.md`, type, `${type}.p${i}`, `p${i}`);
}
```

`run-cli.sh`:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# usage: run-cli.sh ROUNDS LOOKUP...  runs `openclaw wiki get <lookup> --json` from the base and head builds, interleaved.
set -u
W=/Users/openclaw/work/pr-164781-run
rounds=$1; shift
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$W/state HOME=$W/home WIKI_COUNT_ROOT=$W/vault
export NODE_OPTIONS="--require /Users/openclaw/work/pr-164781-scripts/count-md-opens.cjs"
for r in $(seq 1 "$rounds"); do
  for lookup in "$@"; do
    for arm in base head; do
      dir=/Users/openclaw/work/pr-164781; [ $arm = base ] && dir=/Users/openclaw/work/pr-164781-base
      out=$W/out-$arm-${lookup//\//_}.json
      start=$(perl -MTime::HiRes=time -e 'printf "%.3f", time')
      opens=$(cd $dir && node openclaw.mjs wiki get "$lookup" --json 2>&1 >"$out" | grep -o '^\[md-opens\] [0-9]*' | awk '{print $2}')
      end=$(perl -MTime::HiRes=time -e 'printf "%.3f", time')
      ms=$(perl -e "printf '%.0f', ($end-$start)*1000")
      page=$(NODE_OPTIONS= node -e 'const r=JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync(process.argv[1],"utf8"));console.log(r?r.path:"null")' "$out")
      sha=$(shasum -a 256 "$out" | cut -c1-12)
      printf 'round %s  %-14s %-4s  md_opens=%-5s wall_ms=%-6s page=%-16s stdout_sha256=%s\n' "$r" "$lookup" "$arm" "$opens" "$ms" "$page" "$sha"
    done
  done
done
```

`callers-md-opens.cjs` is `count-md-opens.cjs` with the counter replaced by a map keyed on the memory-wiki function names found in `new Error().stack`; calls whose async stack holds none of them are reported as `outside the vault sync step`.

</details>

### Behaviour

Driven through the real seam, `getMemoryWikiPage`, on a synthetic compiled 2,000-page vault (600 `sources/src<i>.md` pages and 1,400 `p<i>.md` pages spread over `entities/`, `concepts/` and `syntheses/`, each with an ID such as `concept.p1`; same generator for both arms). Opens are `.md` opens counted through the fs-safe `beforeOpen` hook around each call. "Before" is the base with only the production change reverted (`query.ts` restored from the base commit), run in the same sitting and the same harness. Median of five calls per row, two separate runs per arm, interleaved before r1, after r1, before r2, after r2.

| Lookup | Before ms (r1 / r2) | Before opens | After ms (r1 / r2) | After opens | Page (both arms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| basename `p7` | 490.1 / 356.1 | 2,009 | 35.6 / 18.0 | 1 | `concepts/p7.md` |
| extensionless path `entities/p0` | 344.7 / 344.2 | 2,009 | 29.0 / 17.5 | 1 | `entities/p0.md` |
| ID `concept.p1` | 441.1 / 268.0 | 2,009 | 323.9 / 356.1 | 2,009 | `concepts/p1.md` |
| miss `Page 5` | 430.8 / 283.7 | 2,009 | 262.6 / 343.6 | 2,009 | null |
| miss `p1999` | 401.0 / 283.0 | 2,009 | 265.8 / 359.7 | 2,009 | null |
| miss `absent-lookup` | 888.9 / 477.2 | 2,009 | 401.6 / 420.5 | 2,009 | null |

The same page is returned before and after in every row. The ID and miss rows take the same code path in both arms and read the same 2,009 files; their milliseconds move by more between runs of one arm (for example before r1 against before r2) than between arms, which is shared-machine load. A test pins that ID and miss lookups perform exactly the number of opens of one full read.

### Tests

`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-wiki --maxWorkers=2` (the owning extension), 2 shards:

```
 Test Files  5 passed (5)
      Tests  64 passed (64)
   Duration  68.30s (tests 52%, transform 38%, import 8%, setup 2%)
 Test Files  43 passed (43)
      Tests  318 passed | 1 skipped (319)
   Duration  59.57s (tests 46%, import 26%, setup 14%, transform 13%)
[test] passed 2 Vitest shards in 132.55s
```

382 passed, 1 skipped (pre-existing), 0 failures. That includes `query.reads.test.ts`, which pins exact, basename and ID reads for large and hardlinked pages, claim precedence, ID fallback after an absent, invalid or directory candidate, and the outside-vault swap during exact, basename and search reads, and `apply.test.ts`, whose caller of `resolveQueryableWikiPageByLookup` moved to the new module.

New file `query.path-lookup.test.ts`, 9 tests: read count for basename and extensionless lookups, one read among duplicate basenames in path order, visibility skipping with the exact set of opens, path tiers ahead of ID, a duplicate ID that appears after the last compile resolving to the earlier-sorted page, pages added or renamed after compile, ID and miss lookups costing exactly one full read, and an unrelated refused page not failing a path lookup while still failing a miss.

### Regression proof (red/green)

Base `query.ts` with only the new test file added:

```
      Tests  5 failed | 4 passed (9)
AssertionError: expected [ 'p0.md', 'p1.md', 'p10.md', …(26) ] to deeply equal [ 'p7.md' ]
AssertionError: expected [ 'p0.md', 'p1.md', 'p10.md', …(28) ] to deeply equal [ 'twin.md' ]
AssertionError: expected [ 'p0.md', 'p1.md', 'p10.md', …(28) ] to deeply equal [ 'twin.md', 'twin.md' ]
AssertionError: promise rejected "FsSafeError: symlink open blocked { …(3) }" instead of resolving
```

The failing five are the basename and extensionless read counts, duplicate basenames, the visibility skip and the unrelated refused page. The four tests that pass on the base (ID and miss read count, path over ID, duplicate ID after compile, added or renamed pages) pin the unchanged behaviour on purpose. With this commit all 9 pass:

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  9 passed (9)
   Duration  19.80s (transform 64%, tests 24%, import 10%, setup 2%)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 26.38s
```

Mutation checks on `query-page-lookup.ts`, each mutant fails the new file:

| Mutant | Failing tests |
|---|---|
| Skip the session visibility check on candidates | skips pages the session cannot see (1) |
| Read candidates in reverse order | first-in-path-order duplicate basenames, visibility skip (2) |
| Disable the path lookup (always full read) | basename, extensionless, duplicate basenames, visibility skip, unrelated refused page (5) |
| Read every candidate before choosing | duplicate basenames, visibility skip (2) |

### Other checks

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm check:changed` (lanes `extensions`, `extensionTests`) | every gate ok except the dead export scan, which fails only on files outside this diff (see Gaps) |
| line-cap growth ratchet | `Line-cap ratchet OK: 4 changed source files; no new violations or over-cap growth.` |
| max-lines, assertion SAFETY, SQLite worker, SQLite dialect, test timeout race ratchets | all OK |
| first-party mock export ratchet | `Mock factory ratchet OK: 10050 grandfathered factories.` |
| `tsgo` extensions / extension tests (inside `check:changed`) | ok / ok |
| oxlint on the changed extension files | `Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.` |
| format changed files | `All matched files use the correct format.` |
| Knip script unused-export scan | `passed with 0 entries` |
| plugin boundaries, extension wildcard re-exports, extension test core imports | clean |

### Measured test cost

`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-wiki/src/query.path-lookup.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`:

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  9 passed (9)
   Duration  19.80s (transform 64%, tests 24%, import 10%, setup 2%)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 26.38s
```

Each test builds a 20-page vault and compiles it; tests account for 24% of the file's duration on this loaded machine.

### Gaps, stated plainly

The whole `pnpm test` suite was not run. `pnpm changed:lanes --json` reports this diff as `extensions, extensionTests` only; `core`, `coreTests`, `ui`, `scripts`, `testRoot`, `apps`, `docs`, `tooling` and `all` are false and `extensionImpactFromCore` is false. Root `AGENTS.md` does not mandate unrelated suites, so the targeted set is the owning extension (`extensions/memory-wiki`, 382 tests) plus the `check:changed` gates for those lanes.

The `check:changed` dead export step fails because its Knip production and full-tree scans report 68 and 51 unused-export entries, every one outside this diff: across both, 112 under `ui/src`, 3 under `src/agents`, 2 under `src/gateway`, 1 under `src/commands` and 1 under `test/helpers`; none is under `extensions/`. The CI job `checks-node-changed-boundary` fails in `test/control-ui-import-boundary.test.ts` with `Error: Unresolved source import: ui/src/components/board/board-document.tsx -> ../../lib/reactive/domain-board.ts`; neither file is in this diff, `ui/src/components/board/board-document.tsx` does not exist at the base, and on current `main` it exists while `ui/src/lib/reactive/domain-board.ts` does not, so the failure comes from `main` merged into this head.

An earlier same-process interleaved A/B at `279aaa48dc8` (same lookup code, base `f3698fa2a9f`) of `getMemoryWikiPage` against a bare read-every-page-then-resolve, twelve alternations per lookup, gave medians of 411.7 vs 392.5 ms for the ID, 397.4 vs 382.5 ms for `absent-lookup` and 385.8 vs 463.5 ms for `Page 5`; the bare arm omits vault initialisation, the digest load, the exact-path read and the visibility filter, so those deltas bound those fixed costs together with the one listing. It was not rerun at this head. CI seconds are not measured. The 2,000-page timings were taken on a shared machine; the stable signal is the open count (2,009 to 1), and the ID and miss paths are pinned to the base read count rather than to a time. No screenshots: this is a server-side read path with no UI surface. No docs or `CHANGELOG.md` change: `docs/plugins/memory-wiki.md` describes `wiki_get` as a read by id or path without a read-strategy promise, and root `AGENTS.md` makes `CHANGELOG.md` release-owned.

The vault source sync that `openclaw wiki get`, Gateway `wiki.get` and the `wiki_get` tool run before every lookup reads all 2,009 pages three times on both the base and this head; this diff does not touch it, so end to end the saving is 2,008 of 8,036 page reads per path lookup, not 2,008 of 2,009. The real CLI run was not repeated through a running Gateway; the Gateway method calls the same sync and the same `getMemoryWikiPage`.

prs.title: test(gateway): give agent readiness contracts their own deadlines
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `src/gateway/server.agents.config-readiness.test.ts` times out at 120 s on busy local machines because one test case carries a full Gateway boot, a CLI child boot and about 25 agent mutations under a single per-test deadline.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Developers and CI get a readiness suite whose contracts fail independently and stay well inside their deadlines on loaded hosts.

## Why This Change Was Made

The case grew by accretion: created in #167894, then the CLI guard section (#168417) and the two-operator overlap section (#169249) were appended to the same `it`. The Gateway is now a suite-level fixture (`beforeAll`/`afterAll` with `createOpenClawTestState`), and the body is three ordered cases:

1. `publishes agent mutations before acknowledging immediate session and roster requests` (unchanged name): retired-owner rejection, held CLI publication, first session, update, delete.
2. `publishes overlapping mutations from two operators`: the four-round overlap including the round-0 duplicate deletion.
3. `reports unavailable publication and saved-only mutations`: the fake-clock unavailable paths, then saved-only. Saved-only switches the shared Gateway to `reload: off`, so it stays last.

Every original assertion is kept verbatim (same requests, matchers, loop counts and delays). `recoveryRestart` is now asserted not-called at the end of every case instead of once at the very end. The CLI child is joined in `onTestFinished` even on early failure, the held publication is always released, and teardown tolerates partial setup. No production, config, helper or timeout changes.

## Root cause of the reported failures

There were two distinct failures. Both product defects already have fixes on main; this PR handles what's left over in the fixture.

- **Local 120 s timeout (heads 62cec18f / 96db2f6d):** phase timing on 62cec18f showed the first `sessions.create` for the freshly created agent stalling for **29,988 ms** before succeeding, twice in a row. Cherry-picking #170308 (cold-store first-write admission cycle) onto that head removed the stall (**8,301 ms** under even heavier load). The case **still timed out**, reaching overlap round 2 at 113 s, because the composition itself exceeds one deadline on a loaded host.
- **Nightly CI assertion (runs 38292371460 and 38271573116):** the concurrent duplicate `agents.delete` loser exhausted the 5 s deletion-lease wait while the winner was still cleaning up, under shard concurrency (the case took 43 s there). #170309 already accepts that typed `UNAVAILABLE` / `OPENCLAW_STATE_LEASE_HELD` outcome; this PR keeps that assertion unchanged.
- **Current main (648d4ab8) before this PR:** the single case passed but used **80.3 s, 90.6 s and 114.5 s** of its 120 s budget in three local runs (load average 60–90 on 32 cores). Per-step timing showed no remaining hang. The time is spread across a 22–30 s Gateway boot, a 10–17 s CLI child publication, and 1–8 s per agent mutation, mostly session-store purge and database reader close under CPU contention.

## Evidence

`pnpm test src/gateway/server.agents.config-readiness.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` on this branch (macOS, heavily shared host):

| Run | Load avg | Case 1 | Case 2 | Case 3 | File Duration | Wall |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A | 110–140 | 18.2 s | 21.2 s | 1.7 s | 255.8 s | 274 s |
| B | 50–78 | 15.4 s | 30.5 s | 3.5 s | 248.4 s | 282 s |

Most of the file Duration is Vitest transform and worker-bundle preparation (transform 56% in run B), not test time. Total test time is unchanged; each contract now has its own 120 s deadline instead of sharing one.

Also passed: `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` on the file, `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json` on the file, `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-server.json`, and `git diff --check`. PR CI [run 38335490139](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38335490139) passed on head `f813cf98a7fe` (`openclaw/ci-gate` green). In its [`checks-node-changed-compact-small-19` job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38335490139/job/115094861230) the three cases took **5.9 s / 10.3 s / 1.6 s**; the file's Vitest Duration was 64.6 s (tests 50%, transform 46%).

Known gap: splitting the case does not speed up the underlying per-mutation cost (session-store purge, cross-pool database reader close, per-deletion lease heartbeat worker). That is a separate performance question and isn't needed for correctness.

prs.title: refactor(plugins): consolidate lifecycle and policy paths
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reduces speculative lifecycle bookkeeping and parallel policy implementations in bundled plugins.

## User Impact

No feature, configuration, SDK, protocol or valid persisted-data shape changes. Ordinary concurrency, authorization at effects, user-data durability, payment limits and accepted-write settlement remain protected. Rare display/cache races are explicitly best effort below; a restart or subsequent observation repairs them. Teams pending uploads and the Phase E standalone session-memory backend are untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

This second extensions pass revisits every earlier KEEP against the human-report provenance bar, then inspects three-day and fourteen-day growth and the larger owners. It uses one owner for repeated feature pagination, native/worker Reef policy, Matrix decryption settlement, Workboard metadata/loading/state projections, Memory publication and provider installation, and X charge settlement.

Production reduction: **510 net lines** (967 additions, 1,477 deletions), including all new shared helpers and excluding tests, fixtures, test support, generated code and declarations. This is the campaign's honest 500–999 fallback after a deeper pass, not a gross-deletion claim or a BELOW-500 decision.

## Evidence

- Exact-head run [38345308679](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38345308679) completed: all selected product tests, full extension lint, production/test extension types and security/dependency reviews pass. The only non-aggregate failure is inherited core test-types stripe 4; its CI gate is consequently red. `TS2724` at `src/commands/config-preflight-snapshot.test.ts:41` reproduces identically in unrelated docs PR #144540, [job 115126160259](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38345422403/job/115126160259). #170530 removed that reader export without migrating the unchanged test; neither file is touched here. The gate's “new” label compares an older scheduled run predating that main regression. Landing uses the campaign's inherited-only exception, not a green-CI claim. CI elapsed 648 seconds; summed job duration 11,610 seconds including setup (not a billing figure).
- Final production and test extension typegraphs pass; runtime import cycles 0 and Madge components 0. Formatting passes across 79 files; SDK export checks pass.
- Final lint-suppressions: 3/3 pass, 232.49s Vitest / 291.70s wrapper. No new suppressions, test timeout increases, test retries or skips.
- Workboard browser: 244/244 pass in 86.89s; final loader/catalog 16/16 in 31.20s; final Sessions identity 24/24 in 26.44s. Compiled synthetic Chromium consumer renders 169 cards, filters to 12, and reports no page errors. Markup/appearance is unchanged; no screenshot-parity claim.
- Memory correction proof: 64/64 across publication-transfer, provider lifecycle/leases/fallback and memory-source races; 1,437.49s Vitest / 1,493.46s wrapper, with final compiled-source verification passing. Matrix retained snapshot/recovery/persistence assertions: 49 passed; its process-fixture observation failure was diagnosed and corrected without changing its timeout. Both unchanged Doctor rebound-owner regressions pass after correction (23.650s and 25.890s).
- Independent complete-candidate review and correction-delta reviews are scoped-clean P0–P2, with final source verification complete. Current reviewed head: `052ae22fd9a4d123435a187a5e3be787dacef9b9`.
- First hosted run `38342863166` found four owned failing jobs: extension bundles 7 and 9 retained obsolete immediate provider-close retry expectations; extension lint stripes 2 and 3 found a Matrix Promise-executor return, Reef map spread, and Workboard JSON-clone lint finding. These are corrected, not attributed to main. Memory's 16 focused tests pass in 703.81s Vitest / 758.18s wrapper; 17 selected Workboard/Reef/Matrix tests pass in 539.08s / 573.80s, with final source verification. Other tests were selected out by the name filter, not newly skipped in source. Fresh production/test types, runtime/Madge cycles 0/0, five-file formatting, the three exact lint rules and lint-suppressions 3/3 (42.40s / 58.48s) pass. Workboard retains persisted-JSON equality with omitted undefined fields, normalized -0 and key-order independence; it is not replaced with structuredClone. No full local suite was run after CI failed. Corrected-head hosted CI remains the final broad gate.
- Full local changed-check attempt passed conflict, line-cap, max-lines and assertion ratchets, then its SQLite inventory produced no result for 620.18s and was stopped through its task-owned parent. Scoped lint twice failed before lint in SDK declaration preparation at the unchanged 300,000ms limit. No further local retry or budget increase; the completed hosted full lint/ratchet checks close those explicit tool-preparation gaps.
- Earlier focused attempts failed collection because concurrently edited source invalidated the repo-wide worker build snapshot. No assertions ran, so these are neither product failures nor passing proof. Source freeze addresses that cause.
- Later obsolete batches ran many retained-behavior assertions but were canceled after corrections invalidated their global compiled snapshots; they are not complete-wrapper passes. Fresh correction/native-settlement invocations prepared successfully, then two forks stalled on IPC without active synchronous waits or test timers. Used the repository's environment/network-excluding diagnostic reports, stopped only verified task-owned invocations, and did not bypass the harness. Subsequent focused correction runs close the Matrix process and direct native-settlement gaps. The native delayed-close test passes (54.301s test, 532.60s Vitest / 569.47s wrapper, final source verification successful); it proves retiring writes cannot consume a replacement monitor's resumed assignment. Slow local time is dominated by worker preparation/import, not a new timer or longer test budget.
- All project execution uses isolated HOME, OpenClaw state/config/home and XDG directories. No real Gateway, Team deployment, live plugin provider calls, remote runner or real operator state is used.

<details>
<summary>Investigated local failures and remaining uncertainty</summary>

Two scalar Memory admission assertions were fixed by not restoring timeout before admission; two injected valid-PRAGMA restoration-retry variants were removed with that unsupported mechanism. The corrected 64-test Memory run passes without weakened normal admission/commit assertions. Two Doctor rebound-owner failures exposed the SDK's unchanged-row/no-op result contract; the minimal prepare-time refusal fact repairs both unchanged tests. Matrix's process fixture waited only for failed `fs.open`; native exclusive creation handles contention before a successful lock-inspection open. A standalone isolated diagnostic proved the same pending successor acquired after child release in 4.856s; the fixture now observes either real open outcome and keeps its original timeout.

The first unchanged command-context inspection test also hit its existing 120-second limit in the earlier batch. A bounded fresh reproduction invocation passed both Doctor cases but stalled in collection/import before reaching that inspection case. No new await was introduced on that initial path; its local timeout cause remains unproven, not attributed to main and not claimed repaired. Exact-head hosted job `115125611982` now passes the inspection case in 10.752s and all 24 assertions in its five-file shard (89.46s Vitest). Matrix's process test and the direct native delayed-close test also pass in focused correction runs. No CI dispatches, reruns or pushes merely for green are authorized.

</details>

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Codex failed-unsubscribe historical LRU reconstruction (#120740, synthetic lifecycle regressions and author live proof, no human LRU incident): a failed retained subscription becomes newest instead of restoring its precise old position; later eviction may choose a different idle thread. Exact live owner, callback retention, TTL and settlement remain.
- Codex public-policy/conversation projection rereads during inspection and hosted inventory refresh (#132158, feature/synthetic evidence, no human mid-read mutation report): the admitted context finishes once and the next command sees edits. Credential/session authority remains live at the actual request boundary.
- Codex post-success identity/harness mirrors (#101210, synthetic-only mismatch): trust the canonical atomic prepare/commit owner after retaining the callback's refusal fact. Focused tests exposed that the SDK can return an unchanged row after a declined patch; this result contract remains explicitly handled, with existing warning text preserved. Actual refused/conflict/null outcomes still retain the sidecar and warn.
- Codex 64-source display witness reconciliation (#150659, review/harness failover scenarios, no human report): latest supporting source wins. Its closure can temporarily reveal persisted/not-loaded presentation despite an earlier equivalent observer; the next native observation repairs it. Passive-reader isolation and actual action authority remain.
- Codex adoption per-row fallback/replay for error precedence (#151979, batch-performance PR and internal ordering tests, no human ordering contract): one batch path remains; a malformed later candidate can surface before an earlier binding error. Normal output ordering, skips, ownership and cleanup stay.
- Memory stacked host/worker/context physical-path probes (#165568/#168860/#170407, implementation and synthetic replacement tests, no human path-swap report): retained SDK admission owns the open handle; external replacement mid-read does not revoke that captured result. The next admission/open observes replacement. Source attachment and write authority remain checked.
- Memory repeated validation of already-captured numeric connection policy (#169251, internal worker input and synthetic validation): trust the typed producer and initial connection-policy reader; invalid internal mutation may fail clearly rather than be rechecked at every command.
- Memory PRAGMA restoration retry/receipt handling (#169251, injected valid-PRAGMA failures only, no human report): a valid-PRAGMA restoration failure propagates clearly after the durable commit; the publication owner does not replay thrown failures. No restoration is attempted when statement admission never began. Normal transaction, commit, tombstone and write-grant behavior stays.
- Memory serial private-child correlation nonce (#153832, persistent-child performance work, no human stale-response report): one admitted request per database and private pipes supply order. Framing, byte/row/SQL validation, bounded slots and cancellation still retire malformed children.
- Dreaming extra gateway-start epoch/timer certificate (#117885 fixes human #78458's actual orphan cleanup, but duplicate/reentrant start timing is synthetic): keep cleanup, ages, ownership, stop and drain; a duplicate hook may run the same bounded idempotent cleanup again.
- Memory failure cooldown configuration hash (#138136, synthetic retained-tool/config sequence; related #138114 is profiling, not an actual-use cooldown incident): a config edit can retain the previous failed initialization for the existing maximum 60 seconds, then retry normally.
- Memory immediate provider-close retry (#113471, blocked-close harness/obsolete adapter proof, no human incident or transient-close contract): report the first failure and retain the failed provider for a later explicit close. Immediate repetition is no longer treated as recovery.
- Matrix custom competing-process 120-second polling/abort protocol (#160707, synthetic process/store proof, no human report): use the existing SDK lock helper's roughly five-second bounded wait. A slower owner still causes a clear refusal; stop it and retry. First independent review identified a realistic slow-shutdown overlap because Matrix retirement bounds its caller before native teardown completes; minimal bounded handoff support is therefore retained, not classified as speculative concurrency.
- Matrix second custody FIFO and post-release/sealed-operation guards (#160707, synthetic lifecycle interleavings): lifecycle ordering already awaits arm/cancel/seal before release. Unsupported direct out-of-order reuse may fail; exclusive lock, guard fsync, seal reconciliation and native drain remain.
- Matrix blanket catches for SDK identity/boolean getters (#70401 links human verification issue #70213, but not throwing stable getters): inspected SDK getters are direct facts; a newly throwing invariant surfaces. Real throwing phase/method/pending/verifier access and every authorization identity comparison remain guarded.
- Matrix impossible Date clock fallback (2333d47a1e6 adds only an out-of-range Date.now test): an impossible clock raises RangeError instead of manufacturing a 1970 timestamp. Real timeout/resource bounds remain.
- Matrix failed JS-module import cache clearing (#99302, lazy-loader consolidation, no human transient-import report): a broken module import stays failed until restart; native dependency availability still has its existing owner.
- Reef synchronous review eviction retries/rereads (#168340, no human reentrant-writer report): one uninterrupted lookup/oldest-completed eviction/insert path remains; unsupported reentrant or foreign writers can fail insertion. Pending reviews and capacity protection remain.
- Reef private multi-phase removal/request state (#168340, closure-private states and synthetic misuse): live initial admission plus a single-use settlement remains; impossible intermediate-phase calls are not separately modeled. Ordinary accepted-write shutdown settlement stays.
- Agents API event-ID stream replay cache (#156182, activated feature plus synthetic/author proof, no human duplicate-stream report): official stream is consumed once and does not replay. An unexpected duplicate delta can briefly repeat live text until authoritative reconciliation; transcript/item and tool-execution idempotency stay.
- Agents API recursive key sorting for presentation hashes (#156182, no human key-order incident): fixed producer order supplies the digest. Reordered nested keys can cause one redundant replacement update, not another tool execution or persisted transcript row.
- Workboard nested compensation journals (#126161, synthetic reentrancy with no nested FIFO caller): one mutation owns its journal. Normal rollback, reverse order, CAS/current-state checks and aggregate failures remain.
- Workboard late service-reader replacement discard (#168215's human #167574 concerns fallback-run classification, not mid-read replacement): one admitted metadata read may finish with its captured result; subsequent hooks use the new service. The actual fallback fix and SDK access authority remain.
- Workboard three intermediate sweep generations (#168215/#126162, synthetic stop/read interleavings): already-admitted bookkeeping may complete after stop; worktree deletion/nudge effects still revalidate and stopped work does not reschedule.
- Workboard applied-refresh epoch/revision settlement (#134943, feature bookkeeping, no human incident): the pending invalidation boolean schedules the next read, and reconnect refreshes. Unsaved text, normal retry, current-client and teardown behavior stay.
- Workboard manual draft-object replacement during save (#168606, synthetic renderer scenario): the UI owner already blocks replacement/dismissal while saving; unsupported direct mutation no longer discards a completed result. Current client, disposal and effect permission checks stay.
- Workboard recursive identity retry on board generation (#162283, feature plus synthetic board switch): identity is activation/connection-scoped, so one result serves the destination board. Current receipt and reconnect/viewer invalidation still prevent stale publication.

<details>
<summary>KEEP re-audit and structural coverage ledger</summary>

Every original KEEP was checked again; an agent PR, synthetic reproduction or failing test was not treated as an actual-use human incident. Retained minimums have independent contracts:

| Owner / inspected clusters | Decisions and retained minimums |
| --- | --- |
| Codex client/runtime, installed probe, MCP preparation, subagents | Narrow exact LRU bookkeeping; share final disposal settlement. Keep private native probe storage, credential/permission effects, realistic native subscription ownership and ordinary accepted-write drain. Upstream unsubscribe, feature pagination and process-local status source inspected personally. |
| Codex commands, migrations and catalog | Narrow public inspection policy, immutable result mirrors, display witness sets and ordered-error fallback; share feature pagination. Keep account/session/credential authority, sidecar containment and atomic commit, orphan compare-before-delete, actual human historical-delivery repair #161728, bounded scan/confirmation maps, resident/heap/read-budget performance and effect-native eligibility. |
| Memory read/publication/provider, KNN, Dreaming | Narrow path/correlation/epoch/cooldown machinery; share scalar publication, state installation, batch eligibility and Light/REM publication. Keep atomic transactions, tombstones/Forget, coherent retained reads, source/write admission, realistic reader/provider leases, bounded transport/scans, watcher edits, Unicode tokenizer contract and human timeout behavior #137056. |
| Memory remaining KEEP families | Phase E and registry foundations unchanged. Intent scope/creator/privacy/prompt budgets, Dreaming artifact/parser/narrative/repair ownership, ordered imported host events, backed-up diagnostic repair and backfill rollback/continuation stay. CLI/query planner paths were inspected; more generic modes would obscure distinct behavior without meaningful shrink. |
| Matrix | Narrow process waits, redundant operation FIFO, stable getter mirrors, impossible clock and import-retry guards; share one decryption-promise owner and SAS callbacks. Keep room-key integrity/durability, real throwing SDK access, verification identity, outbound live authority/FIFO, committed binding projections, chunk checksums, optional released-host SDK reads and distinct public CLI actions. Human verification report #70213 verified. |
| Teams | Share replacement activity/acknowledgment preparation; keep Stop/FIFO/receipts and account credential inheritance. Pending uploads remain an explicit policy hold; public wizard signature remains. Human multi-account feature request #71058 does not justify unrelated races. |
| Reef | Share native/worker review, identity and delivery policies. Native adapters have actual channel/CLI/setup production callers and released-host >=2026.7.2 compatibility (#168340); open removal draft #169868 still calls Reef a migration blocker. Keep native audit crash markers/rollback, peer/auth effects, atomic mutations, capacity and accepted settlements. |
| X, llama.cpp, ClawRouter | Full X fourteen-day growth (~5,637 production lines), backend and 530-line UI inspected; latest FIFO charge receipt replaces duplicate Set bookkeeping. Keep paid limits, real guest rollover, access/GitHub authority, media confidentiality, artifact integrity/hash-cache performance, exact process identity before termination, bounded external responses and ordinary UI navigation/refresh isolation. |
| Expanded Agents API / Ollama and selected next-grown owners | Inspect activated stream/history contracts and Ollama transport/catalog. Keep real async tool/recovery/cancellation settlement, bounded untrusted input, credential isolation and prompt contracts. Selected Cloudflare/Crabbox/ClickClack owners inspected without broadening into paid-resource, storage or security policy changes. |
| Rejected generalized rewrites | Workboard eleven-table generic binder was implemented and reverted: only four lines saved, more naming machinery and changed getter failure timing. Generic form/header/controller rendering similarly added modes without worthwhile shrink. Reef native transaction imitation would weaken real crash recovery; not done. |

Only tests pinning removed synthetic mechanisms are deleted; kept behavior tests and limits remain unchanged. The local requested ledgers retain the full file:line/provenance audit. This PR is not a declaration that all future simplification opportunities are exhausted.

</details>

Built baseline `3f168ed8c3035b9a5c2490b0c837c0cdcaeeba1e` and candidate in a secretless Node 24 Docker container. Started isolated Gateways through `pnpm openclaw --profile ... gateway run`, then sent a real `chat.send` turn with the Claude CLI backend pointing at a recording fake CLI. Observed startup and actual Claude process launch:

```text
Baseline, no thinking setting:
  agent model: anthropic/claude-opus-4-7 (thinking=medium, fast=off)
  --model claude-opus-4-7; no --effort; MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=0
Candidate, no thinking setting:
  agent model: anthropic/claude-opus-4-7 (thinking=off, fast=off)

prs.title: fix(gateway): use monotonic clock for MCP loopback capture idle deadline
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Waiting for an MCP HTTP loopback tool-call capture to go idle (`waitForMcpLoopbackToolCallCaptureIdle`) seeded its wait deadline on `Date.now()` and read the remaining budget with `Date.now()`, then handed that budget to `raceWithTimeout`, whose internal `setTimeout` runs on Node's monotonic clock. A backward wall-clock jump (NTP sync, manual time change) stretched the computed remaining budget so the capture window stalled; a forward jump shrank it so a healthy capture was misjudged as timed out.

- Problem: deadline seed (`Date.now() + timeoutMs`) and remaining read (`deadline - Date.now()`) used the wall clock while the consumer (`raceWithTimeout` → `setTimeout`) used the monotonic clock — a cross-clock-domain mismatch.
- Solution: anchor both the seed and the remaining read on `performance.now()`, putting seed and consume on one monotonic clock.
- What changed: `src/gateway/mcp-http.loopback-runtime.ts` — two lines in `waitForMcpLoopbackToolCallCaptureIdle` switched from `Date.now()` to `performance.now()`. Added `src/gateway/mcp-http.loopback-deadline.test.ts` proving the deadline no longer stretches under a backward wall-clock jump.
- What did NOT change: no new parser, policy branch, or configuration surface. The deadline is a pure in-process closure variable (not serialized, not persisted, not shared across processes), so the clock swap is contained. `waitForMcpLoopbackToolCallCaptureActivity` and `raceWithTimeout` are untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

The canonical owner of this deadline is `waitForMcpLoopbackToolCallCaptureIdle` itself — it seeds the budget and reads the remaining time, then delegates waiting to `waitForMcpLoopbackToolCallCaptureActivity` → `raceWithTimeout`. Fixing the clock at the owner (two-line mechanical swap) aligns seed and consume without touching any caller. No alternative (e.g. guarding at callers) would avoid re-introducing the cross-clock-domain split.

This is the same monotonic-deadline pattern already shipped for sibling capture/wait paths (e.g. #162779 comfy workflow poll, #162828 device-code poll, #155801 attempt execution deadline).

Risk: `performance.now()` returns sub-millisecond floats, but the only consumer here is `raceWithTimeout`'s bare `setTimeout` (floats are silently floored) and the value is also used for `remainingMs <= 0` / `Math.min` comparisons (float comparison is safe), so no `Math.floor` is needed — consistent with the integer-contract rule for bare-`setTimeout` consumers. External contract (resolve `true` on idle, `false` on timeout) is unchanged.

## User Impact

Operators running on hosts whose wall clock is adjusted while a CLI MCP tool call is in flight (common on cloud VMs with NTP, or laptops with manual time changes) no longer risk the loopback capture wait either hanging far past its configured timeout or returning a spurious timeout for a capture that was still healthy. The configured `timeoutMs` is now honored as real elapsed time.

## Evidence

Real behavior proof drives the **shipped MCP HTTP capture flow**: a real loopback HTTP server (`ensureMcpLoopbackServer`) receives a real `POST /mcp` with the `x-openclaw-cli-capture-key` header, so the HTTP handler admits the request and calls `markMcpLoopbackToolCallStarted` on the shipped path. Node-exec availability is held pending so the admitted call stays in-flight (`capture.inFlight === 1`); `Date.now()` is then jumped backward 60s after the drain deadline is seeded. `timeoutMs` is 500ms; a 3s hard guard catches the baseline.

| MCP HTTP capture flow, wall-clock rewind -60s after seed (timeoutMs=500) | pre-fix `Date.now()` (main) | post-fix `performance.now()` (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| idle result | `aborted (hard guard)` — wait never expired | `false` — deadline expired |
| elapsed | 3001ms (budget inflated to ~60s, hard guard at 3s) | 501ms (bounded by elapsed time) |

Post-fix terminal output (real HTTP `/mcp` admission, real elapsed time):

```console
$ pnpm exec vitest run _proof_170495_mcp_http_flow.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts
[proof-170495] grant capture created
[proof-170495] HTTP POST /mcp sent, waiting for node-exec discovery entry...
[proof-170495] node-exec discovery entered (capture.inFlight should be 1)
[proof-170495] MCP HTTP capture flow: idle result=false elapsed=501ms (timeoutMs=500, wall-clock rewound 60s after seed, in-flight via real HTTP /mcp admission)
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
```

Pre-fix RED (source temporarily reverted to `Date.now()`, same HTTP flow):

```console
[proof-170495] MCP HTTP capture flow: idle result=aborted (hard guard) elapsed=3001ms (timeoutMs=500, wall-clock rewound 60s after seed, in-flight via real HTTP /mcp admission)
AssertionError: expected 'aborted' to be false
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
```

A second proof drives the shipped CLI delivery finalization stack via the production caller `finishDeliveryTracking` (`execute-tool-tracking.ts:565`, which calls `waitForMcpLoopbackToolCallCaptureIdle`) with an in-flight tool call and the same 60s rewind: post-fix resolves at 5005ms (drain grace 5000ms bounded), pre-fix hits the 8s hard guard at 8008ms — same before/after shape at the delivery-stack boundary.

Regression fixture (`src/gateway/mcp-http.loopback-deadline.test.ts`) uses fake timers controlling `Date`, `performance`, and `setTimeout` (AGENTS.md forbids new real-timer tests in CI). Baseline fails (`Expected: false / Received: Symbol(pending)`); fix expires at ~168ms.

Regression — existing capture/idle behavior unchanged: `execute.supervisor-capture.test.ts` 39/39 passed.

What was not tested: forward wall-clock jumps (the symmetric shrinks-the-budget case) are covered by the same monotonic-anchor reasoning; a separate forward-jump case was not added.

Open PR collision check: searched open PR topics and changed-file lists for `mcp-http.loopback-runtime.ts`; no open PR touched it. Related monotonic-deadline PRs (#155801, #162779, #162828, #168735) fix sibling files and do not overlap with this capture-idle deadline.
