prs.title: fix(update): say a missed original capture does not require a restart
prs.body:
## Summary

Original-state capture stays one best-effort attempt. The warning no longer tells the operator to retry the update. It says the update continues without this capture, and that a completed update does not need to be restarted because of this warning.

No retry is added. The install is not stopped. The shared inspection diagnostic that ends with "then retry the update." is unchanged. Only this best-effort warning rewrites that trailing sentence, and it closes the sentence before the continuation.

Related #170332

<!-- today-update-evidence:2026-10-12 -->
## Production baseline — October 12 update

Captured from the real npm-global update on October 12, 2026 (Halifax time): Debian 13, Node v24.16.0, `2026.10.5-beta.1 (f283c3c)` → `2026.10.5-beta.2 (467e83d)`, using `openclaw update --channel beta --tag 2026.10.5-beta.2 --yes`. The saved terminal capture and read-only update-run record agree that the run finished with `phase: finished`, `status: succeeded`. Private paths and capture identifiers are redacted; unrelated logs are omitted.

The same real update warned that original-state capture failed while reading the live state database, advised a retry, and then installed and finished:

Selected terminal lines, with unrelated output omitted:

```text
Warning: Original state capture is unavailable: Original update capture failed; evidence retained at $OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR.update-captures/<capture-id> | State schema inspection failed (exit): [redacted-diagnostic]; after 4.215 seconds during shared database discovery for $OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/state/openclaw.sqlite (scope: 1 source paths): SQLite file generation changed while reading: $OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/state/openclaw.sqlite. Check access to the reported source, free space, and storage performance, then retry the update.
✓ package-install (15.69s)
Gateway: restarted and verified.
✅ OpenClaw updated to 2026.10.5-beta.2 (from 2026.10.5-beta.1).
Recorded verification: service running (2026.10.5-beta.2); version verified; channels ready; HTTP ready.
```

The capture diagnostic reports a generation change after 4.215 seconds. This establishes the contradictory retry advice during an otherwise successful update and preserves the intended best-effort continuation described by the maintainer.

**Remaining proof gap:** This was the official unpatched beta update. It proves the original warning and successful continuation, but does not show the revised warning from an installed CLI containing this PR. The patched command-boundary proof below remains the after-change evidence.

## Proof

No live Gateway update was rerun. `updateCommand({ yes: true, json: true, restart: false })` ran with `captureUpdateRecoveryBaseline` rejecting the generation-changed inspection error. The command resolved. The visible warning and the completed ledger step `warning:original-state-capture:` were:

```
Warning: Original state capture is unavailable: State schema inspection failed (exit): generation changed. Check access to the reported source, free space, and storage performance. The update continues without this capture. A completed update does not need to be restarted because of this warning.
```

The admitted run finished `phase: finished`, `status: skipped`, `reason: already-current`.

## Base / head

The same boundary test against the parent initializer, which warns with the raw inspection error, failed (exit 1). That run printed:

```
Warning: Original state capture is unavailable: State schema inspection failed (exit): generation changed. Check access to the reported source, free space, and storage performance, then retry the update.
```

Head of the same test passed (exit 0) and printed the continuation warning above.

## Test

`update-command-fresh-preview.test.ts` — "continues a completed update when original-state capture fails". The helper-only wording test is removed. The boundary test requires the continuation sentence in both the visible warning and the ledger step, rejects "retry the update", and requires the run to finish already-current.



## Maintainer update (fix at the producer)

Pushed on top of this branch (merged current `main`, no history rewrite): `fix(update): report original capture failures accurately`. It replaces the post-hoc regex rewrite with a fix where the message is produced, and keeps this PR's "does not need to be restarted" sentence.

- The storage/retry advice is no longer appended for the best-effort original capture (a `retryAdvice` option on the inspection diagnostics; restore and Doctor checks keep it). `formatBestEffortOriginalCaptureWarning` is removed.
- Warning: "Original state capture is unavailable; the update continues without it. A running Gateway or another active writer changing state during capture is expected to cause this. Database rollback uses the pre-migration snapshots taken after the Gateway stops. A completed update does not need to be restarted because of this warning. Cause: …" The guidance comes first because the warning is length-bounded.
- The failing step is named correctly ("database generation verification") with its real input paths, instead of "shared database discovery … scope: 1 source paths".
- `[redacted-diagnostic]` is replaced by the fixed phrase "SQLite file generation changed while reading" (paths stay out of the public summary).
- `docs/cli/update/repair-and-recovery.md` updated.

Evidence: a real `database-generations` worker with a preload writing between its two reads reproduces the issue's message before the change; the `updateCommand` test keeps this PR's name with the new assertions. Focused runs of `update-command-fresh-preview`, `update-candidate-state.schema`, and `diagnostic-support-redaction` pass (320s). `tsgo:core:test`, oxlint, oxfmt, `git diff --check` clean.

Supersedes my duplicate #170396, now closed.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the outer dynamic-tool watchdog expiring before a requested automation run wait and its Gateway transport budget complete.

## User Impact

Automation runs can finish within the wait budget the tool advertises instead of reporting a premature failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

Give cron.run an execution-budget callback derived from its existing capped wait plus enqueue transport allowance. The harness honors tool-owned budgets and adds its existing completion grace. Argument validation and the inner ten-minute cap remain in place.

This is PR 4 of a seven-part October beta compatibility review. Its base is `codex/october-review-03-cron-readonly-ask` and its diff contains one original fix commit, `d162b3838f05ab2d766ac3198601ae0b82e942d5`. The first review base is `v2026.10.1-beta.1` plus four carried ports. The seven fixes were previously pushed directly to a candidate branch; this PR makes the existing patch available for normal CI and independent review. Historical pushes and author-run checks do not count as completed PR review or CI.

## Evidence

### Current review-stack head

Current head: `77db404005ce4c0a1e268152c884f5b1c83aafcf`; base: `db5a11659b992b2a14317be71aad2d61e7d4595a`. Both part1 follow-ups (actual question-card destination decoding and the introduced static type-cycle repair) were merged through the stack using normal commits. The effective diff of this individual PR was verified byte-for-byte unchanged through both integrations. Original candidate/internal pin/live bots remain unchanged. Historical runtime/CI evidence is bound to its recorded SHA; newest-head CI and ClawSweeper conclusions are assessed separately.


Fresh combined-source validation at `09156d64a267aaeef7b0bc31d6ae225d9858caf3`: `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base 433c9a3ab1a166d97e0c32df165b0436d0ad04c1 --head 09156d64a267aaeef7b0bc31d6ae225d9858caf3 --timed` completed successfully on Node 24.16.0, including formatting, core and extension production/test types, lint, dead-export and runtime/database guards. This validates the combined source, not each intermediate head or hosted CI. A fresh combined P2 autoreview reported no actionable finding within the supplied source evidence; it does not replace ClawSweeper or maintainer approval.

This PR is ready for review. Its first normal exact-head CI attempt ended with the inherited audit failure described below; ClawSweeper has completed an earlier-head conclusion; see the follow-up disposition. Current-head review is tracked separately.

Author-run proof: 118 focused watchdog and cron tests passed. Regression coverage checks the default and capped waits, invalid input fallback, existing node execution budgets and completion grace.

The final combined source has passed a focused staging core acceptance of 12/12 and two model-menu controls. That does not establish all release-suite coverage or the individual intermediate heads. No production deployment is included. The original full release-suite coverage limits remain; the first public CI audit failed as attributed below, and does not replace the current-head review follow-up.


### Known inherited CI failure on the recorded earlier head

The [exact-head CI audit](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38325459142/job/115063288865) failed on three production dependency advisories: `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.30.1` and `@modelcontextprotocol/client@2.0.0` ([GHSA-6qxp-vccf-f47h](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6qxp-vccf-f47h)), and `source-map-js@1.2.1` ([GHSA-68fv-2mgg-jv7q](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-68fv-2mgg-jv7q)).

These are inherited from the selected public beta, not caused by this fix. All package manifests, the lockfile, workspace configuration and audit implementation are unchanged from `v2026.10.1-beta.1` through the PR base and head. The actual CI merge commit `4658a82af8bf72ab5adc6c3ecca8a64c67ca1b22` has the expected base/head parents and exactly the PR-head tree. The same three audit findings were inspected in all seven stack jobs. Upstream already tracked fixes in #165902 and #166217.

The requesting maintainer explicitly accepts these proven inherited CI failures as non-blocking for this compatibility review. This is an attributed exception, not green CI or approval of the code. The downstream `openclaw/ci-gate` failed and fail-fast cancelled sibling jobs; those cancelled jobs remain incomplete hosted coverage. Normal code/security review and any defects caused by this patch still require resolution. No dependency update, scanner suppression or CI rerun is included.

prs.title: fix(codex): allow scheduled read-only app calls under ask
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unattended scheduled app reads unnecessarily requiring approval when the app policy uses ask for writes.

## User Impact

Explicitly read-only, non-destructive app tools can run under the normal read policy. Writes, destructive annotations, unknown hints and explicit per-tool approval requirements remain gated.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep read-only and destructive annotations in the scheduled app inventory and use them when applying the app-level ask ceiling, matching foreground policy. Captured and current explicit approval ceilings still intersect.

This is PR 3 of a seven-part October beta compatibility review. Its base is `codex/october-review-02-cron-native-tools` and its diff contains one original fix commit, `ffdbed7229c36c20d5c9ac29279ee2df607d25d3`. The first review base is `v2026.10.1-beta.1` plus four carried ports. The seven fixes were previously pushed directly to a candidate branch; this PR makes the existing patch available for normal CI and independent review. Historical pushes and author-run checks do not count as completed PR review or CI.

## Evidence

### Additional current-stack CI diagnostics

The prior synchronized-head [prompt job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38331831466/job/115083363143) reported drift in `discord-group-codex-message-tool.md.diff` and `telegram-heartbeat-codex-tool.md.diff`. The unchanged review base433 reproduces those exact two failures. All seven actual generated raw prompt/tool snapshot content hashes are identical between base433 and this PR's tested source-equivalent e16 head; generator, formatter inputs and committed snapshots are unchanged. This is attributed inherited drift, not a reason to rewrite snapshots in this permission fix.

The [architecture job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38331831466/job/115083362944) reported two static cycles. The875-member component matches the unchanged review base exactly. The additional Slack receipt type cycle was introduced in part1 and has been repaired there by f069, then merged through this PR. After repair only the exact inherited component remains. No blanket architecture exemption or unrelated graph refactor was added. These remain red inherited diagnostics with the requesting maintainer's scoped disposition; cancelled/skipped jobs are incomplete coverage. New-head CI is checked separately.

### Inspectable current authority boundary follow-up

At combined head `c4e9869318abc768529140de3e627a637c1fe64a`, a temporary secretless fixture called the **actual `prepareCodexAttemptRuntime` entry**. It did not substitute the admission helper. Account/profile mismatches rejected before both client prewarm and the client factory. A third control changed the prepared account during the awaited auth-binding step and also rejected before those boundaries.

Results and asserted recorder counts:

```text
PASS rejects account change before client prewarm or factory
PASS rejects profile change before client prewarm or factory
PASS rejects during-awaited-binding change before client prewarm or factory
prewarm calls: 0; client factory calls: 0 (each denied case)
3 passed; no native thread/turn or connector request started
```

Auth-binding completion and prewarm/factory were synthetic recorders; this proves runtime ordering and principal admission, not a live provider credential revocation. All later runtime fields were deliberately absent in the negative fixture, so accidental progression would fail rather than silently use a fake provider. The fixture was removed and tracked source remained clean.

Existing production native MCP adapter/client controls were also executed on this head, recording actual JSON-RPC transport writes through `createNativeMcpRuntime` and its real client. Under overload backoff, allowed calls produced two writes; revoking owner or per-call grant produced one original write and **zero forbidden retry writes**, with `CodexAppServerScopedRequestRejectedError`. Native tool, catalog and resource cases all passed. This covers retained-handle/retry fencing using synthetic grants and in-memory transport, not provider OAuth invalidation.

```text
PASS native tool retry: current owner/grant -> retry permitted
PASS native tool retry: owner revoked -> retry refused
PASS native tool retry: grant revoked -> retry refused
PASS native catalog/resource retry: owner revoked -> retry refused
cron persistence + executor: 34 passed
native MCP authority + current-owner app controls: 10 passed
native serial wrapper: 44 passed; wall38.24s
```

The four-file command was `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-mcp-app.authority.test.ts src/cron/store.definition-integrity.test.ts src/cron/isolated-agent/run.tools-allow.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/scheduled-app-authority.owner-defaults.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. The temporary runtime plus Slack final-write proof wrapper passed five cases in30.79s; it did not start a Gateway or mutate a shared bot.

### Installed native approval and app-exposure composition

Executed at combined review head `3590f39daf1be817be59d0bc789ec9e2e1e53ddb`, using verified **codex-cli 0.153.4**. The test calls the real `captureScheduledCodexAppAuthority`, saves the issued envelope/job through the SDK SQLite cron store, closes the DB and reloads it, derives native eligibility through production `shouldEnableCodexAppServerNativeToolSurface` using that reloaded cap, then calls the production scheduled app-policy intersection. Its output patch is passed unchanged into the actual CLI's normal `thread/start` + `turn/start` RPCs.

Identity, inventory/current config, job definition and Responses/MCP transports are synthetic. The loopback Responses fixture emits the actual advertised namespaced MCP callable. The MCP recorder **has no permission logic**: every received `tools/call` is counted and succeeds. The CLI's production app configuration, native tool exposure and consent gates decide which requests reach it. Direct `mcpServer/tool/call` RPC is not used. Native consent requests are recorded and declined by the unattended fixture; this is not claimed as execution of OpenClaw's interactive-input handler. Each CLI has an isolated home and a loopback-only macOS egress sandbox; no real credentials/model inference/provider access/shared bot changes occur.

Terminal/recorder results:

```text
actual Codex CLI: 0.153.4
current production capture/store/reload/intersection: 6 scenarios generated
ASK annotated read:                  connector calls=1, native consent requests=0, completed
captured prompt, current relaxed:    connector calls=0, native consent requests=1, declined
current explicit prompt:             connector calls=0, native consent requests=1, declined
readOnly + destructive conflict:     connector calls=0, native consent requests=1, declined
persisted finite cap, added app:      connector calls=0, target not exposed, completed
persisted owner default, added app:   connector calls=1, native consent requests=0, completed
6/6 expected native outcomes; every synthetic runtime/server stopped and scratch removed
```

The three consent controls report native `user rejected MCP tool call`; they do not silently auto-approve a prompt. The captured-prompt control uses an explicit finite job cap, retaining the captured ceiling even after current native policy relaxes. The two added-app controls have **identical native tool inventory** and the same creator-side Calendar-only capture. Actual native eligibility is true for the reloaded owner-default `['*']` job and false for the finite job. The production result enables the new app only in the default case. The CLI advertises and executes its native callable in that positive sibling; in the finite sibling it does not advertise it, and forcing that same valid callable returns `unsupported call` before connector I/O. This rules out an invalid tool name masquerading as a forbidden-schedule success.

There are meaningful failing-base controls using exact parent owner-module bytes, with the same retained current SDK/helpers and actual 0.153.4 transport:

```text
PR3 parent 2290c09: ASK read -> prompt -> native consent declined -> 0 calls (required 1: RED)
current stack:      ASK read -> auto   -> no native consent       -> 1 call  (GREEN)
PR5 parent 77db404: owner default new app -> not exposed          -> 0 calls (required 1: RED)
current stack:      owner default new app -> exposed              -> 1 call  (GREEN)
```

These are exact **owner-module baseline compositions**, not complete historical builds/images. Neither source checkout nor refs were switched. Temporary fixture/module files were removed; tracked source and the original candidate/pin are unchanged. The recorded projected-patch hashes were independently matched to the patches used by the native runs.

This closes the prior projection-only/native-enforcement gap with an actual CLI composition. It does not claim a full creator `cron.add` → older finite-default cap lifting → whole Gateway/process restart → current group-policy dispatcher run. The existing real scheduled SaaS read/withdrawal receipts and production-entry principal/retry controls remain separate evidence with their own scopes. No in-flight OAuth revocation or published-release rollback run is claimed, and no product-code or dependency changes were needed for these additional checks.

### Current review-stack head

Current head: `db5a11659b992b2a14317be71aad2d61e7d4595a`; base: `2290c09d3f85d33cd7adf881759e7fcb386e7b08`. Both part1 follow-ups (actual question-card destination decoding and the introduced static type-cycle repair) were merged through the stack using normal commits. The effective diff of this individual PR was verified byte-for-byte unchanged through both integrations. Original candidate/internal pin/live bots remain unchanged. Historical runtime/CI evidence is bound to its recorded SHA; newest-head CI and ClawSweeper conclusions are assessed separately.

### Specific scheduled native read evidence

An existing owned scheduled job on this exact `ffdbed7229c36c20d5c9ac29279ee2df607d25d3` candidate was independently mapped to its actual native Codex thread/turn using its unique test prompt; all native SDK pages and its Gateway terminal state were read. Deduplicating the repeated SDK representation of the same item gives:

```text
execution: unattended scheduled run
native tool: codex_apps / linear.get_team
readOnlyHint: true
status: completed
error: null
server approval/user-input requests: none
observer mutations: none
Gateway: done; active run=false; pending inputs=0; history complete
```

This is a real connector read dispatched by the scheduled native runtime, not the separate foreground read or the combined 12-case core acceptance. Credentials, account/job/thread/resource identifiers, result contents and private endpoints are omitted.

The receipt alone does not attest every ASK/captured-prompt policy setting or prove in-flight provider-token revocation/account replacement; the annotation-aware ASK ceiling and explicit captured/current prompts have owner regression coverage. Stored authority remains version 1 with the same serialized app/tool approval modes; the new readOnlyHint is current inventory metadata rather than a new persisted field. Existing captured prompt ceilings continue to intersect as prompt. No data schema or automatic expansion of an older stored prompt is introduced. Prepared-principal admission and retained native-request revocation controls are now shown above; the installed receipt still does not independently attest its effective ASK configuration. Explicit captured/current prompt and destructive-hint policy cases are component proofs, not live provider denial runs.


Fresh combined-source validation at `09156d64a267aaeef7b0bc31d6ae225d9858caf3`: `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base 433c9a3ab1a166d97e0c32df165b0436d0ad04c1 --head 09156d64a267aaeef7b0bc31d6ae225d9858caf3 --timed` completed successfully on Node 24.16.0, including formatting, core and extension production/test types, lint, dead-export and runtime/database guards. This validates the combined source, not each intermediate head or hosted CI. A fresh combined P2 autoreview reported no actionable finding within the supplied source evidence; it does not replace ClawSweeper or maintainer approval.

prs.title: refactor(sessions): consolidate worker reads and receipt settlement
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Recent session worker migrations accumulated parallel target capture, admission, publication, and transport scaffolding. This is Peter-requested wave-3 sessions cleanup.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible change, migration, or operator action. Security checks, FIFO ordering, transcript integrity, and accepted-write settlement remain intact; the accepted internal best-effort tradeoffs are listed below.

## Why This Change Was Made

Consolidate session worker preparation, typed history reads, and native receipt settlement under their existing owners.

This removes **572 net production lines** (+678 / −1250; tests, test support, fixtures, generated files, and declarations excluded). This is the campaign's 500–999-line honest-pass path; the coverage ledger below records both the cuts and the substantial machinery deliberately retained. No configuration, protocol, SDK surface, schema, durability, retention, permissions, or dependency changes are intended. The standalone Phase E session-memory backend, factory branch, registry/expiry/federation machinery, and its tests are untouched.

Tests/support grow by 10 net lines: one shared typed transport fixture replaces duplicated adapters, and the three synthetic wrong-command cases are removed with their mechanism. Kept-behavior assertions are unchanged.

## Coverage ledger

Recent three-day and fourteen-day history was examined first, followed by the largest owners. The scope inventory contains 697 production modules. This is an inventory plus targeted owner/history review, not a claim that every line was manually reviewed.

| Cluster | Decision and provenance |
| --- | --- |
| Pending-input history/source/store/withdrawal target capture | Share one captured-target helper; preserve pre-await inventory, alias/physical identity, absence and authority checks. #163582, #164313, #164284, #167106. |
| Pending-input history execution | Reuse `withSessionEntryWorker` for FIFO/admission/release; preserve transaction/commit custody and native settlement. #163582. |
| Pending-input receipt settlement | Share the identical native completion/receipt path across history, mutation and withdrawal. Domain validators and publication stay with callers; mutation's unknown-outcome error precedence and false withdrawal receipts are retained. #163582, #164284, #167106. |
| Six worker execution-source constructors | Share identical binding authorization/currentness/grant construction without changing their callback ordering or expiry strings. #166703, #166587, #159632, #156014, #169573, #163222. |
| Provider-review publication | Reuse canonical replacement mutation settlement and publication, including lost-reply recovery; keep exact provider errors. #169622. |
| Incognito domain workers | Share prepare/bind/execute/settle/close across side-data, transcript reports and outbox. Preserve inactive foundations and their admission rules; activation #169363 remains possible. |
| Transcript-event reads | Use the existing physical read-source owner; preserve native/incognito/memory, cold restore, full event bytes, bounded hydration, and the locked discovery lane. #167952, #169566. |
| History reader signatures and transport | Derive signatures from canonical request/result maps and preserve correlation through transport. Keep public method signatures, capture timing, budgets, cancellation and streaming integrity. #153325, #165916, #169622. |
| History operation kinds and topology transport | One kind inventory and the existing discovery transport, with all operations and checks retained. #163987, #169311. |
| Cohort reads | Remove repeated identity/open/location checks around one synchronous admitted-handle read. Admission and selected incarnation/session/lifecycle predicates stay. #166703, #169310. |
| Participant projection | KEEP original SQL projection and performance-accounting coverage after rejecting a tiny `selectAll()` simplification. #169989, #170127. Actor-hydration column lists also remain because Kysely SQLite JSON helpers prohibit `selectAll()`. |
| Phase E memory backend | KEEP in full: #169124, #169227, #169327 and Peter's explicit direction. |
| Actor replicas/canonical continuation caches | KEEP measured cache reuse and minimal real-writer invalidation. #170105, #170127, #170199, #166054, #166503. |
| Reclamation, archive eviction, lifecycle references | KEEP extract-before-delete, archive publication, preservation, retained-window and live-authority boundaries. No retention redesign. |
| First creation and patch owners | KEEP parallel-creation grouping, native settlement and authorization capture. #167257, #167515, #169622. |
| Resource retirement and pending-input drains | KEEP ordinary shutdown settlement of accepted write-capable work, native closure, host effects and bounded resources. |
| Entry store/reset/window/transcript owners | KEEP distinct append/dedupe, exact-CAS rewrite, legacy entries, public-share/sandbox provenance and retained-window semantics. No sound large parallel path established. |
| Incognito compute draft | Rejected: preserving its distinct cleanup/admission boundaries left a new command union, helper and three dispatch lists for only 14 fewer lines. Existing paths already share the cache owner. |

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

The reply checks originated with hydration work #153325 and were preserved by #165916, which added the synthetic wrong-command fixture. Neither cites a human report of a wrong-command reply. The original large-transcript/OOM evidence concerns transfer capacity; its chunking, limits, and integrity validation remain unchanged.

- Same-call cohort identity/incarnation/open/location rechecks: #166703 supplied synthetic correctness/performance proof, not a cited human production report; #169310 explicitly accepts admitted retained handles. A truly closed handle now fails through SQLite; admission and selected incarnation/lifecycle checks remain.
- Ordinary history-reader wrong-command result discriminators: #165916's forcing fixture (282f796dfa0) is synthetic, not a human report. The pool pairs each reply to its task and the runner now carries that input/result relationship. A broken internal dispatcher can fail at projection instead of the removed dedicated wrong-kind error.
- History-result allowlist: #165916 preserved this internal guard with synthetic wrong-command proof, not a human incident. Private task pairing and the canonical result map make another command's metadata reply unrealistic. An internal dispatcher defect is no longer specially classified here; real history variants remain typed.
- Hydration final-result kind check: #165916's wrong-command proof was synthetic, not a human incident. The paired hydration command produces the canonical full/bounded union. A dispatcher defect may now fail during projection; frame shape, encoding stability, event count, row sequence and complete-transfer validation remain unchanged.
- Projection-status/entry-presence boolean result checks: #165916 preserved internal result checks with synthetic proof, not a human incident. These private paired commands have boolean result contracts. An internal dispatcher defect may produce malformed internal data instead of the dedicated wrong-kind error; external/user input validation is unchanged.
- History cleanup after a confirmed write: #163582 carried a separate execution/release path without a cited human cleanup-failure incident. The shared writer still settles accepted native work before release, but adopts the canonical best-effort cleanup policy; a later cleanup failure does not turn a confirmed commit into a replayable write failure.

The history writer uses the canonical worker owner's internal grant-expiry diagnostic. Caller-revocation, domain, missing-store and normal user-facing behavior remain unchanged. Other cuts consolidate existing checks rather than removing them.

## Evidence

- Core production types, scoped lint, formatting, and diff whitespace pass. No new lint suppressions. Exact reader keys/parameter tuples/return types remain compatible with the base; the reader/runtime/test graph typecheck passes.
- Independent P2 review of the complete candidate found no actionable findings. Follow-up corrections were lint-local names, type-only generic constraints, and restoration of the rejected participant SQL change. Runtime value cycles: 0; Madge cycles: 0 (clean-main comparison also 0).
- A final isolated review of signed head `2b1ba3440905afd18d6bc41a97d52843fbc3ed1c`, including the unchanged publication/domain/read-source/queue owners, is also scoped-clean through P2 with no actionable findings.
- Lint-suppression tests: 3/3 pass, 56.99 seconds wrapper wall time (37.06 seconds Vitest). PR-wrapper import closure and eager-import inventory: 7 selected tests pass across 3 files in 102.04 seconds wrapper wall time; 16 unrelated CLI bootstrap cases were filtered, so this is not full-file proof. No skip or timeout changes.
- Corrected focused proof: **321 tests / 27 files pass**, 4,346.03 seconds wrapper wall time (310 runtime-config cases plus 11 command cases). Earlier unchanged-input Gateway 6/6 and infrastructure 32/32 proof remains valid. The changed reader test file alone passes 8/8: 397.74 seconds wrapper / 339.01 seconds Vitest, including compilation of 13,233 inputs in 296.374 seconds; individual cases take 0–5 ms. Hosted CI elapsed 768 seconds (not summed billable seconds).
- `check-changed`: all type graphs (including 28 core-test graphs), ratchets, formatting and boundary checks pass. Overall exit 1: production and full-tree Knip scans each reached the existing 600-second deadline without reporting findings; the scripts scan passes with zero entries. This is incomplete dead-export proof, not green. No deadline increase or deadcode bypass was used.
- The 364-file session-scope inventory was selected across focused and scope runs. The completed scope infrastructure shard reports 230 passed / 2 timed out in 17 files. The remaining 318-file run was stopped for a conflict-required rebase after 36 failures; it is partial, not full-scope proof. No test assertion or timeout was changed.

Local scope proof exposed two timeouts in the unchanged `session-accessor.sqlite-branches.test.ts`. Both reproduce on clean main `e78a253059eb07d70ea3f7140e1c4e9b9fadc383` with Node 26.5.0 and isolated state: process-only incognito branches took 128,256 ms against 120,000 ms (candidate 124,009 ms); the large shared graph took 15,133 ms against 15,000 ms (candidate 15,182 ms). Main's file result was 13 passed / 2 timed out, 542.04 seconds Vitest wall time. Two earlier baseline setup attempts failed before collection because borrowed workspace dependency links were missing; those are not behavior evidence. The underlying timeout cause is unresolved; heavy shared-host load was observed but is not claimed as a diagnosis. No tests, timeouts, assertions, retries, or skips were changed for either failure. Hosted exact-head CI remains the broad gate.

The remaining scope run first hit a 30-second reconcile fleet timeout and subsequent lifecycle/drainage failures, followed by active-events and creation-worker drainage failures. A clean-main reconcile lifecycle control reproduced the first timeout (30,014 ms), ending 11 failed / 1 passed; later main errors include native retirement and host-authority failures and are not identical to every candidate error. These downstream failures are not all classified as inherited.

Other unresolved scope failures include archive result-recording fault injection unexpectedly resolving; compound-worker reset-refusal/rollback assertions and error-class identity; an oversized actor timeout and reply-loss error mismatch; and an archive continuation timeout. Main's clean archive control passed all 17 cases (817.28 seconds wrapper / 766.12 seconds Vitest). The initial fresh-process candidate control was interrupted before any case result so the checkout could be rebased safely; fresh archive and compound controls are included in the post-rebase proof. Both archive and compound writes dispatch through the unchanged `withSessionEntryWorker`, not the modified mutation wrapper. The fault helper only intercepts worker creation in its current module generation, while the broker is process-global across non-isolated files; reused workers or old module closures are a concrete fixture hypothesis, not an established diagnosis or fix. The non-isolated runner explicitly retains SQLite globals after failed drainage while resetting ordinary modules. Interleaved logs do not establish same-fork causation. Original failures and uncertainty are retained, with no test weakening or passing-replay-as-fix claim.

Conflict-only rebase onto `ac8de4fd9562646ad7a41dfdec59fb35df06be4f` preserves main's new admission registry callback (#170464) and pending-input resource release (#170439). Signed head: `2b1ba3440905afd18d6bc41a97d52843fbc3ed1c`. Post-conflict types, scoped lint/format, runtime/Madge cycles (zero/zero), and **70 tests across 7 files pass** in 2,717.25 seconds wrapper wall time. The batch includes lint-suppressions (3/3), first-store reply admission (7/7), and 60 session cases across five files, including all 17 archive cases and all previously failing compound assertions. This is comparison evidence, not a proven repair of the original broad-run failures. One initial lint invocation used the wrong typecheck config and timed out in unnecessary SDK declaration preparation before scanning; the corrected canonical core-lint command passes with no bypass or timeout change. Exact-head hosted CI remains the broad gate.

## Exact-head CI attribution

CI run [38344707160](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38344707160), attempt 1, is attached to the exact signed head above. It tested merge `71d5026aa78f54ef5227e81e559251cef56a9bf0`, whose ordered parents are main `fcb89a331a1f59eedde59c4b3a338febdb199cb7` and this PR head.

The observed failure is [check-test-types-core-4, job 115123766162](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38344707160/job/115123766162): `TS2724` at `src/commands/config-preflight-snapshot.test.ts:41`, importing `readConfigPreflightSnapshot` after main's #170530 made it private without updating the test. Neither failing source file is changed by this PR, and both are byte-identical between the CI-tested merge and its main parent.

The identical error and commands graph fail in unrelated #170616, [run 38344629442 / job 115123572806](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38344629442/job/115123572806), against the same main base. This independently establishes inherited failure under the campaign's provenance bar. The scheduled main comparison predates #170530, so its classification table's “new” label is not used as causal proof. All 88 jobs are terminal; the only other failure is downstream [openclaw/ci-gate, job 115126484647](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38344707160/job/115126484647), caused solely by that shard. Security-fast passed. The full 223-check census has no active checks; superseded advisory cancellations are accounted for in the evidence comment. Native inherited-only admin admission merged exact head as `c4e496e254a203b4658557a731b470f852baf3df`, with the landing-parent audit matching `74c7b3d72589755d14ba630b85e049d671e81a48`; CI is not relabeled green. No CI rerun, dispatch, or green-seeking push was requested.

prs.title: fix(telegram): isolate private DM topic inbound buffers by thread id
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Messages in distinct private Telegram topics share one inbound debounce identity. Work waiting in one topic blocks another topic, and a text `/stop` in one topic discards buffered input from another.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared conversation serializer intentionally has no `scope: "dm"` case, so private bot topics fall back to the bare chat id. That same id is what session bindings look up. Changing it would stop existing private-chat bindings from matching, and a new delivery-target marker would not be honored by outbound thread selection.

Enqueue and cancellation both take their identity from the inbound debounce key. This change leaves shared peer ids and delivery targets alone, and adds a positive DM thread id only when building that key. A non-topic private DM (`scope: "dm"` with no positive thread id) still uses the bare chat id, so those messages stay one buffer.

## User Impact

Distinct private DM topics no longer block or cancel each other's buffered text. Ordinary private DMs without a topic keep the previous single-buffer behavior. Existing private-chat session bindings and outbound targets are unchanged.

## Evidence

Live run of `createTelegramInboundProcessing` (the real inbound debounce path) at `5d6eb9ad436030aac2eca7a7cb21bb93f5cbd0c4`. The debounce clock is advanced with Vitest fake timers, not a wall-clock sleep.

Two private DM topics in chat 7 were buffered separately and flushed as their own batches. Two messages in the same topic coalesced. A non-topic DM in the same chat still coalesced onto the bare chat id and did not mix with either topic.

```
HEAD 5d6eb9ad436030aac2eca7a7cb21bb93f5cbd0c4

DM_TOPIC_DEBOUNCE_PROOF {
  "keys": {
    "topic100": "7:dm-topic:100",
    "topic200": "7:dm-topic:200",
    "nonTopicDm": "7"
  },
  "dispositions": [
    { "kind": "buffered", "buffer": "debounce" },
    { "kind": "buffered", "buffer": "debounce" },
    { "kind": "buffered", "buffer": "debounce" },
    { "kind": "buffered", "buffer": "debounce" },
    { "kind": "buffered", "buffer": "debounce" }
  ],
  "flushed": [
    { "text": "beta", "thread": { "id": 200, "scope": "dm" } },
    { "text": "alpha-1\nalpha-2", "thread": { "id": 100, "scope": "dm" } },
    { "text": "plain-1\nplain-2", "thread": { "scope": "dm" } }
  ]
}

Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  1 passed (1)
```

Fixes #142107

prs.title: fix(sessions): keep cleared history out of active session forks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Forking a session while its first task after `/new` is still running can bring the cleared conversation back into the child's model context.

## User Impact

Forks respect the parent's reset and retained conversation history while leaving the unfinished task in the parent.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `forkFrom: "last-completed"` lookup could select a reply before the latest reset and discard the reset marker. Keep that boundary when no later reply has completed, so the existing context reader can apply the reset normally.

## Evidence

A local Gateway run completes a conversation, resets it, and forks while a real MCP call is still pending. Before the fix, the child's next model request contains the cleared question and answer. With the fix, it excludes both and the unfinished parent task. Model replies and tool data were scripted. [Captured runtime comparison](https://github.com/Shenrui-Ma/openclaw/blob/1a802430647ba42fc7655fece09d89942f9cd657/.github/pr-proof/active-reset-fork.json).

The no-reset control retains completed history, and full forks work after the parent finishes. The parent's stored messages stay unchanged during the fork; its tool completes once after release. Reset/fork and worker regressions, targeted type checks, lint, and formatting pass on the updated branch.

<details>
<summary>Runtime verification</summary>

The run uses the shipped `openclaw gateway run` and `openclaw agent` commands, a configured stdio MCP tool, and SQLite storage. Reset, fork, and history reads use authenticated Gateway RPC. A local HTTP endpoint captures the child's request without server-side continuation.

The tool remains blocked until the child turn completes. An ordinary full fork is rejected while the parent is active; `last-completed` succeeds, and the parent completes normally after release.

The Gateway regression can be rerun with:

```sh
corepack pnpm test src/gateway/server.sessions.create.reset-fork.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

</details>

prs.title: fix: tools.effective drops tool-only plugin tools when the inventory lease scopes its runtime generation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: enabled plugin tools (e.g. the workboard tool suite) disappear from `tools.effective` when the agent's model resolves through a plugin-owned dynamic model and the inventory lease scopes its prepared runtime generation to the selected runtime owners.

Closes #167365

## User Impact

User impact: with a plugin-owned dynamic model selected, `tools.effective` (and the agent tool assembly built on it) keeps surfacing every enabled tool-only plugin's tools; explicitly allowed plugin tool names no longer silently vanish or surface as unknown entries.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dynamic-model inventory lease acquires a prepared runtime whose metadata generation is deliberately scoped to runtime owners (provider and harness plugins). Tool discovery trusted that narrowed snapshot as the full manifest contract, so tool-only plugins outside the owner set had no manifest facts and never reached the owner cold-load path.

This change promotes scoped prepared snapshots to the complete manifest view (`completePluginMetadataSnapshot`) before tool discovery and hands the promoted manifest registry to the owner cold-load options, so missing tool-only owners can resolve their manifests outside the narrowed scope. The narrowed lease stays authoritative for model and runtime facts; promotion failures fall back to the scoped view and never block tool resolution.

## Evidence

### Live shipped-entry-point red/green on the exact issue scenario (Oct 12)

The issue's own reproduction command, run against real Gateway processes, with the real bundled `workboard` plugin and the issue's operator config (`tools.profile: "coding"` + all 38 `workboard_*` tools in `tools.alsoAllow` + `plugins.entries.workboard.enabled: true`; the session model resolves only via a provider plugin's `prepareDynamicModel`, which forces the `tools.effective` inventory lease to build). Full transcript, matrix, and disclosures in [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167585#issuecomment-6120940438):

```
openclaw gateway call tools.effective --params '{"sessionKey":"agent:main:main"}' --json
```

| Code under test | PR diff | Probes | workboard tools in inventory |
|---|---|---|---|
| `upstream/main` @ `2cd5dea12c8` (Oct 10) | none | 1 | **0 / 38 — red** |
| `main` tip `5f27b4e9182` (Oct 12) | none | 5 probes | **0 / 38 — red, stable** |
| **PR head `658ec18b205`** | **this PR** | 5 probes | **38 / 38 — green, stable** |

BEFORE: the inventory returns 38 core tools plus `memory_get`/`memory_search` only — every granted `workboard_*` tool is omitted (the issue symptom). AFTER: the inventory returns 76 tools including all 38 `workboard_*` tools, with no unknown-entry notices. The only variable between the red and green rows is this PR's diff; the proof harness stays out of the tree (in-tree tracked source outside dup:check scan targets fails `check-guards`), so the scenario is documented for reproduction in the linked comment.

**Live Gateway `tools.effective` RPC (real server runtime, real WebSocket protocol):**

Booted the shipped Gateway server runtime (`startGatewayServer`, the same core the `openclaw gateway` CLI launches), seeded a session whose model override resolves through a plugin-owned dynamic model (`e2e-dynamic-provider/dynamic-model`; the provider-owner plugin narrows the prepared generation to 7 manifests), enabled a tool-only plugin (`e2e-tools-plugin`, a dependency-free CJS plugin mirroring workboard's tool-only shape) with `tools.alsoAllow` grants, and called the real `tools.effective` WebSocket RPC:

```json
{
  "agentId": "main",
  "profile": "coding",
  "groups": [
    { "id": "core", "toolCount": 36 },
    { "id": "plugin", "toolCount": 2, "tools": ["e2e_echo", "e2e_ping"] }
  ],
  "notices": [
    { "id": "browser-filtered-by-profile", "severity": "info" }
  ]
}
```

Every allowed tool-only plugin tool is returned (`source="plugin"`), and the RPC response carries no unknown-entry warning.

Scope notes for this proof:

- The bundled workboard plugin itself cannot cold-load under this harness: it is TS-source and `extensions/workboard/index.ts` fails with an unrelated `unicorn-magic` export error, exactly like `ollama` and `openai` in the same gateway log. The RPC assertion therefore uses a dependency-free CJS tool-only plugin with the same manifest/runtime shape; workboard's own tool names stay covered by the focused tests below.
- On current `main`, the Gateway RPC path already returns tool-only plugin tools because #167374 taught inventory reads to borrow the Gateway's loaded registry. This PR repairs the callers that cannot borrow a Gateway registry (cron / headless / in-process inventory assembly). The red/green comparison below exercises exactly that path: on unfixed `main` the same inventory call returned 36 entries with the tool-only plugin's allowed tools missing; with this fix it returns 38 entries including both tools and no unknown-entry notices.

**Focused tests:** `src/plugins/tools.scoped-generation.test.ts` — enabled tool-only plugins are discovered from a runtime-owner-scoped generation (red before the fix, green after); disabled tool-only plugins stay excluded.

**Regression safety:** 78/78 tests across `tools.optional` and the new scoped-generation tests; `tsgo:core` clean.

## Revision 13 (f5d301668bf): reuse retained Gateway registrations

Accepts the re-review's P2 finding (registration reuse): metadata completion adds enabled tool-only plugins to `onlyPluginIds`, but the serving prepared registry stays narrowed to model owners, so those owners were cold-loaded through the discovery path on every assembly — re-importing already-admitted plugins synchronously on the Gateway thread and rebuilding their stores.

`resolvePluginToolsFromRegistry` now consults the host's retained full registry (the Gateway's startup registrations) for completion-promoted owners when the serving registry is the narrowed prepared generation (`collectRetainedToolOwners`, `src/plugins/plugin-tool-owners.ts`); the discovery-path cold load stays reserved for genuinely absent standalone owners. New regression: "reuses retained runtime registrations for completion-promoted owners" asserts the granted tools resolve from the retained registry and `loadPluginRegistryHandle` is never invoked. Focused suite 78/78 green; oxlint/oxfmt clean; `src/plugins/tools.ts` nets smaller than the reviewed head (751 → 744 lines).

## Revision 14 (b1b154a4b44): registration-reuse findings addressed

All four re-review findings on the reuse path are fixed in `collectRetainedToolOwners` (`src/plugins/plugin-tool-owners.ts`): reuse now requires matching registration inputs (prepared generation's `registrationConfigKey` + workspace vs the retained registry's recorded load-context state; stateless registries are never reused), matching disabled/error prepared outcomes are settled facts that reuse cannot override (#164594 semantics preserved and now guarding reuse), and the helper accepts optional `workspaceDir` per the runtime context type. New CLI trace on this branch (comment 6122400847): all 38 workboard tools returned across five probes with zero workboard loader/build activity in the gateway log — reuse without re-registration. Tests: 4 scoped-generation regressions including no-reuse-on-config-mismatch and no-resurrection-of-settled-owners; 80/80 focused green; oxlint/oxfmt clean.

## Revision 2 (f02978f6cc2): CI guard fixes

The first revision's CI flagged three guard failures in the changed files; all are fixed with no behavior change:

- `check-lint-core-3` (oxlint `unicorn/no-single-promise-in-promise-methods`): unwrapped a single-element `Promise.all` in the test's loader mock factory.
- `check-test-types-core-5` (tsgo TS2456/TS2577): the `TestSnapshot` alias circularly referenced `installFullManifestSnapshot`'s return type; it now uses an explicit structural type.
- `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` (assertion-safety): introduced a `promotedSnapshot` binding, which removes the two manifest-view assertions in `resolvePluginToolLoadState` outright (`completePluginMetadataSnapshot` already returns `PluginMetadataSnapshot | undefined`, assignable to the manifest view); the remaining prepared-runtime cast carries a `// SAFETY:` comment. Promotion failure, `undefined`, and identity cases keep the scoped snapshot and no promoted manifest registry, exactly as before.

Verification on this head: oxlint clean on both files; `tsgo:core` and the full `tsgo:core:test` shards pass; 78/78 focused tests pass; both e2e proofs above re-run green, including the live-Gateway `tools.effective` RPC (PASS: 38 entries, both tool-only plugin tools present, no unknown-entry notices).

Note for reviewers: `check-guards-architecture` fails on a Madge import cycle between `src/agents/prepared-model-catalog-fingerprints.ts` and `src/agents/prepared-model-catalog-worker.ts` — two files this PR does not touch (last modified on main before this branch); that failure pre-dates this PR.


## Round 5: published the in-process scoped red/green transcript

The scoped-runtime red/green run through the real resolver and the real missing-owner loader (no mocks: real snapshot owner, real production projection, real loader cold-loading the tool-only plugin from disk) is now published verbatim in [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167585#issuecomment-6096914045). Pre-fix build: resolver returns 0 tools for the scoped generation (defect reproduced, missing owner never attempted). Fixed build: both allowed tools resolved via the real missing-owner cold load. The only delta between runs is `src/plugins/tools.ts`.

prs.title: fix(a2a): reject task references instead of starting replacement work
prs.body:
Closes #167592

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an A2A `SendMessage` with `message.taskId` silently allocating unrelated replacement work instead of validating the referenced task.

## User Impact

Unknown or another peer's task IDs now return `TaskNotFoundError` (`-32001`) before allocation or dispatch. Task continuation remains unsupported and now fails explicitly with `-32004`; use a contextId-only follow-up to start a new task in the same conversation. An owned task with a conflicting context ID returns `-32602`. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin implements A2A 1.0. The [A2A 1.0.0 task identifier contract](https://a2a-protocol.org/v1.0.0/specification/#342-task-identifier-semantics) requires an existing task and `TaskNotFoundError` for unknown IDs. [Send Message](https://a2a-protocol.org/v1.0.0/specification/#311-send-message) applies that error to inaccessible tasks too; the [JSON-RPC mapping](https://a2a-protocol.org/v1.0.0/specification/#54-error-code-mappings) is `-32001`. Accepting additional messages on nonterminal tasks is a [MAY](https://a2a-protocol.org/v1.0.0/specification/#333-asynchronous-processing), not a requirement to implement continuation here.

Validate through the existing peer-owned task lookup in the HTTP protocol owner before the existing allocation path. Preserve the current context-only follow-up behavior and message-ID deduplication. Thanks to @clawSean for the report and original fix. No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

## Evidence

Built isolated Gateways on current-main baseline `3f168ed8c3035b9a5c2490b0c837c0cdcaeeba1e` and candidate `f29e228c6e548aebf8c6ec8afe6c15f284b631ce`. Sent real authenticated JSON-RPC requests over HTTP to `/a2a/v1`. A local OpenAI-compatible provider returned deterministic text; the real Gateway handled plugin loading, authentication, routing, task allocation, and replies.

| Request | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unknown taskId | New unrelated completed task, 1 provider call | `-32001`, 0 provider calls |
| Other peer's taskId | New unrelated completed task, 1 provider call | `-32001`, 0 provider calls |
| Owned taskId | New unrelated completed task, 1 provider call | `-32004`, 0 provider calls |
| contextId-only follow-up | New completed task in original context | New completed task in original context |

Candidate response excerpts (HTTP 200):

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"unknown-task","error":{"code":-32001,"message":"Task not found"}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"foreign-task","error":{"code":-32001,"message":"Task not found"}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"owned-task","error":{"code":-32004,"message":"Task continuation is not supported; omit taskId and reuse contextId to start a new task"}}
```

Both context-only follow-ups returned `TASK_STATE_COMPLETED`, `contextId: "shared-context"`, a new task ID, and the provider's `TASK_PROOF_OK` reply.

- The new regression selection on baseline: **4 failed / 1 passed**, detecting silent allocation; the context-only control passed.
- Candidate: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/a2a/src/http.test.ts extensions/a2a/src/task-store.test.ts`: **47 passed**, two files, **26.91s** wrapper wall time with a cold compiled-worker cache.
- Changed-file Oxfmt and Oxlint passed in the isolated container. Hosted CI owns broader checks.
- Simplified the contributor's 126 added test lines to one error-case table plus the context-only control. Existing task-store expiry coverage remains. Merge-base delta: production **+18/-0**, tests **+60/-0**, docs **+3/-1**. The production growth is the bounded validation before an unchanged allocation path, not a new task lifecycle.

Two-way door: a revert restores the old behavior without state or configuration migration. Blast radius is A2A clients that send `message.taskId`; supported context-only conversations and reference-free messages keep their existing behavior.

prs.title: fix(telegram): release account throttlers for retired bot tokens
prs.body:
Related: gap finding `gap-telegram-throttler-token-leak` (hot-update token rotation / repeated account add-remove, evidence level A — real Gateway process logs + unit/integration tests)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: rotating a Telegram bot token or removing a Telegram account leaks the old token's limiter — Bottleneck heartbeat timers and memory grow monotonically until the Gateway is restarted.

## User Impact

User impact: operators can now rotate bot tokens and remove Telegram accounts on a long-running Gateway without leaked Bottleneck heartbeat timers and cache entries accumulating for every retired token; the retirement runs inside the Gateway process on the config hot-reload stop, settling queued sends and not-yet-dispatched chat actions before disconnecting the old token's limiter while in-flight requests finish. A chat action sleeping in its 401 authorization backoff settles immediately at retirement — for group and DM dispatch alike — and never sends on the retired token. No config or behavior change for steady-state operation; the per-token shared throttling contract is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`getOrCreateAccountThrottler` caches one throttler per bot token in a process-global map with no eviction path, and grammY's `apiThrottler()` never exposes its Bottleneck instances, so each retired token left 3 perpetual `setInterval` timers (250 ms reservoir heartbeat + two group auto-cleanup loops) plus its object graph in memory forever. This change mirrors the upstream `apiThrottler()` defaults in an owned factory (`grammy-api-throttler.ts`) so the limiters can be disconnected, and retires the token's throttler in the process that owns the map:

- **Gateway-side retirement:** the CLI lifecycle hooks (`onAccountConfigChanged` / `onAccountRemoved`) never run inside the Gateway that holds the map. All three account lifecycle hooks (config change, removal, `gateway.stopAccount`) now release the throttler once the token is no longer configured for any account. Unchanged-token reloads and manual stops keep the limiter so flood penalty state survives restarts; a shared token used by another account is never released.
- **Settling queued work:** retirement stops admissions first (a `retired` gate rejects later calls on the captured transformer and prevents new group limiter creation), rejects queued group sends and not-yet-dispatched chat actions immediately, re-checks retirement after the action pacing sleep and again at the shared final dispatch boundary — including after the 401 authorization backoff, for DM and group actions alike — then `limiter.stop({ dropWaitingJobs: true })` — queued sends reject with a clear BottleneckError while running sends finish — and only then disconnects, clears the group auto-cleanup intervals, and drops the map entry. Disposal is idempotent. Backing-off group actions stay tracked for retirement settlement until their transport dispatch actually begins, so their callers settle right away instead of waiting out the backoff.
- **Thin channel hooks:** the rotated/removed/stopped release operations live in `account-throttler-lifecycle.ts`; `channel.ts` returns under its 700-line cap.

## Evidence

### Waiting requests settle during retirement (production client, real timers)

A production-client script (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs .openclaw/.tmp/oc-proof-settlement-169536.mjs`) drives the shipped `account-throttler` module through the real production undici transport (`resolveTelegramTransport` + `createTelegramClientFetch`, the same stack the Gateway uses) against the loopback Bot API stub, with real timers and real Bottleneck. It parks one send in flight, queues a second send behind it, arms the 401 authorization backoff with a group action, parks a second action in that backoff, and retires the token:

```
PROOF live intervals after throttler create: 3
PROOF send A dispatched and held in flight by the stub (3s)
PROOF send B queued behind the in-flight send
PROOF action C failed with 401 (backoff armed)
PROOF action D sleeping in authorization backoff
PROOF releaseAccountThrottler -> true after 1428ms (waits for the in-flight send to finish)
PROOF in-flight send A: fulfilled
PROOF waiting send B:   rejected: This limiter has been stopped.
PROOF backing-off action D: rejected: Telegram throttler for this token has been released
PROOF intervals: after create=3 before release=3 after release=0 (created=3, cleared=3)
PROOF stub sendMessage requests total: 1 (expected 1)
PROOF stub sendChatAction requests total: 1 (expected 1)
PROOF OK: waiting sends and actions settled, in-flight send preserved, intervals reclaimed

=== STUB LOG ===
stub listening on http://127.0.0.1:19877
2026-10-13T02:44:50.265Z  sendMessage      111:proof-token  held=3000ms
2026-10-13T02:44:50.332Z  sendChatAction   111:proof-token  first-action=401
```

The waiting send settles with Bottleneck's "limiter has been stopped", the backing-off action settles immediately with the released error, the in-flight send completes through the real transport after its 3 s hold, all three live intervals are reclaimed, and the stub records exactly one sendMessage and one sendChatAction — no dispatch ever reaches the retired token after retirement. Tokens are synthetic (`111:proof-token`); no credentials appear.

### Real Gateway process (built from this branch, this revision)

A full build of this branch (rebased on current upstream main) was run and the Gateway launched from that build with an isolated state directory and port (`gateway run --port 19876 --auth none`), talking to a local loopback Bot API stub (`apiRoot: http://127.0.0.1:19877`). Tokens are synthetic (`111:...`/`222:...`); no credentials appear in the logs. Both retirement paths were driven through the real config hot-reload.

**Rotation with an in-flight reply.** An unpaired DM reached the Gateway; its pairing reply `sendMessage` was held in flight by the stub (3 s). The token was rotated while the reply was still held:

```
2026-10-13T04:21:26.XXXZ  (stub) sendMessage 111:proof-token  held=3000ms
2026-10-13T12:21:04.187+08:00 [reload] config change detected; evaluating reload (channels.telegram.accounts.default.botToken)
2026-10-13T12:21:04.286+08:00 [reload] config change requires channel reload (telegram) — deferring until 1 gateway request(s) complete
2026-10-13T12:21:27.926+08:00 [gateway/channels] restarting telegram channel
2026-10-13T12:21:27.962+08:00 [telegram] [default] released retired Telegram account throttler
2026-10-13T12:21:27.966+08:00 [reload] config hot reload applied (channels.telegram.accounts.default.botToken)
2026-10-13T12:21:28.001+08:00 [telegram] [default] starting provider (@proof_bot_222)
2026-10-13T12:21:28.004+08:00 [telegram] Detected bot identity change for account "default" (was 111, now 222); discarding stale update offset 1 and starting fresh.
```

The hot reload deferred until the held `sendMessage` completed, the in-flight request succeeded (no failure logged), and only then did the retirement release the throttler — the "preserve already-running I/O" contract through the real transport client.

**Account removal.** Dropping the whole `channels.telegram` section produced the second release on the same Gateway run:

```
2026-10-13T12:21:30.596+08:00 [gateway/channels] restarting telegram channel
2026-10-13T12:21:30.612+08:00 [telegram] [default] released retired Telegram account throttler
```

**Clean token cutover (stub log).** The stub recorded every authenticated request: exactly one `sendMessage` on the retired token (completed after the hold), none on the new token, and no retired-token request after the rotation:

```
2026-10-13T04:21:27.168Z  getUpdates   111:proof-token   <- last long poll by the retired token
2026-10-13T04:21:27.984Z  getMe        222:proof-token   <- restart one second later
```

After rotation no `111:proof-token` request appears again: the retired token stops polling entirely instead of leaking a live long poll — the same leak class this PR eliminates for the throttle limiter.

Full redacted logs in this checkout: `.openclaw/.tmp/oc-proof-gateway-169536.log` and `.openclaw/.tmp/oc-proof-stub-169536.log` (driver: `.openclaw/.tmp/oc-proof-driver-169536.mjs`, stub: `.openclaw/.tmp/telegram-proof-stub.mjs`).

### Waiting actions settle and never dispatch after retirement (unit)

`account-throttler.test.ts` regressions for the action lane, covering the retirement windows:

- `settles a pacing action and never dispatches it when the account is retired` — the successor is sleeping out its one-second pacing window when the token is released; its caller settles immediately and the dispatch counter stays at 1.
- `settles actions queued behind a running predecessor when the account is retired` — retirement while the predecessor's dispatch is in flight settles the queued successor immediately; the in-flight I/O completes; the dispatch counter stays at 1.
- `settles a backing-off action immediately when the account is retired` (revised in this revision) — the successor parks in the 401 authorization backoff after pacing; releasing the token during that backoff settles its caller **at release time** (asserted before any further timer advancement), and advancing 10 minutes afterwards still produces no dispatch.
- `never dispatches a DM action whose authorization backoff outlives retirement` (new in this revision) — the DM successor parks in the 401 backoff; retiring during the backoff rejects it with the released error and the final dispatch never reaches the API.

Baseline: both new/revised regressions fail on the pre-fix source (previous commit `ba17964a2af`): the group regression reports `expected "vi.fn()" to be called once, but got 0 times` (no immediate settlement) and the DM regression reports `promise resolved "true" instead of rejecting` (the retired token dispatched). The low-value `keeps releasing other tokens independent` test was removed per review.

### Queued sends settle on release (unit)

`account-throttler.test.ts` `stops timers and settles queued sends on release`: with the default owned limiter, a second DM send queued behind a running one rejects with `This limiter has been stopped` when the token is released, the live `setInterval` handle set returns to zero (all heartbeats/cleanup timers cleared), and a later call on the captured transformer rejects with `Telegram throttler for this token has been released` without creating new limiters.

### Retire gate blocks queued group sends and fresh work (unit)

`account-throttler.test.ts` `rejects queued group sends and new work once the account is retired`: retirement settles the group sends already queued on the group limiter, rejects a later group send with a clear `BottleneckError`, clears the group engine timers, and a subsequent call on the captured transformer is rejected by the retired gate without creating a new group limiter.

### Before/after timer probe

Probe counting `setInterval`/`clearInterval` against the real code path (`getOrCreateAccountThrottler` + `releaseAccountThrottler`):

```
baseline:                          created=0  cleared=0
after create (1 token entry):      created=3  cleared=2
after 2 rotations (3 entries):     created=9  cleared=6
after releasing all 3 entries:     created=9  cleared=15   (+9 real clears, net 0 leaked timers)
```

Before the fix the same rotation sequence left all 9 timers firing until process exit. The production-client trace above re-confirms the same balance with real timers (`after create=3 … after release=0`).

Behavior parity with upstream grammY defaults is anchored by the pre-existing reservoir tests (e.g. "preserves the group message budget while sending topic actions": 30/msg-min global + 20/msg-min per group chat).

### Local verification on this revision

- `pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/account-throttler.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` 23/23; `pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/channel.gateway.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` 27/27 (includes the restored removal-hook regression `releases the removed account's throttler`); `pnpm test test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` 17/17
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`: 0 errors; oxlint clean on the changed files; `pnpm format` clean on the changed files
- Ratchets: `check:line-cap-ratchet --base upstream/main` OK (channel.ts stays under its baseline) and `check:assertion-safety --base upstream/main` OK
- Branch rebased onto current upstream `main` (`7f4197068b3` at rebase time). The previous head's `checks-node-compact-small-6` failure was an inherited red-main window (duplicate `transcript-entry-anchor.ts` wrapper-inventory entry on main between 12:04–12:36 UTC, fixed upstream by `30b2ef35d02`); the rebase clears it, and the test passes locally (17/17).

### What was not tested

- Live Telegram end-to-end (no real Bot API traffic): the change is transport-independent lifecycle plumbing; the Gateway-process proof above uses a loopback Bot API, the production-client trace uses the real undici transport, and existing HTTP-conformance suites cover the throttling contract.
- Waiting-send settlement and the chat-action lane through the Gateway transport require a model-backed turn (typing keepalives / streamed replies), so they are covered by the production-client trace and the owning-boundary unit regressions above rather than a Gateway run.
- Accepted edge case: after retirement settles a backing-off action's caller, the bounded one-shot backoff timer (≤ 5 min) can still run to completion in the dead scheduler; it finishes into the final dispatch guard and can never send on the retired token. Reaching into the caller's AbortSignal to reclaim that timer would cross the grammY/undici signal-type boundary for a timer that is bounded and harmless.
- Bottleneck running-job completion at stop: `stop({ dropWaitingJobs: true })` is Bottleneck's documented settlement (drops queued, waits for running); the pinned 2.19.5 source was read to confirm.

<details><summary>Notes for reviewers</summary>

- `grammy-api-throttler.ts` deep-imports the Bottleneck class from `@grammyjs/transformer-throttler/dist/deps.node.js` (the package has no `exports` map; the repo already deep-imports `dist/` paths in production, e.g. `extensions/slack/src/streaming.ts`). Adding `bottleneck` as a direct dependency was rejected to avoid a lockfile change.
- `dispose` clears the Bottleneck Group auto-cleanup interval through a documented private handle — Bottleneck v2 exposes no public stop API and `Group.disconnect()` only handles shared connections. The dependency is pinned at 2.19.5; a code comment flags this for any future upgrade.
- The final dispatch guard is a shared wrapper (`finalDispatch`) applied to both the DM branch and the group action branch; group actions additionally hand it a `markDispatched` hook so retirement settlement tracking ends exactly when transport I/O begins.
- Maintainer decision noted by ClawSweeper (approve the narrow disposable factory that mirrors upstream quota defaults) is still open for maintainers; this revision addresses the two P2 action-retirement findings, the test cleanup, and the real-behavior proof ask.
</details>
