prs.title: qa(subagents): cover deferred completion delivery on a busy requester lane
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A completed child can spend its entire announce budget trying to dispatch onto its requester's already-occupied session lane. In production, idle admission took 0.68 s while busy requesters admitted only after 286.9 s and 310.8 s; the announcer had already given up at about 120.1 s. A child that succeeded was therefore reported as failed because its parent happened to be busy.

The production fix for that landed separately in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/136423. **This PR is now QA coverage only** — a scenario that pins the end-to-end behavior on a busy requester lane, which #136423 does not carry and which the merged unit coverage cannot reach.

## Scope Of This PR

Four files, all QA:

- `qa/scenarios/agents/subagent-completion-busy-lane-telegram-live.yaml` — the new scenario.
- `extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-runtime-agent-session.ts` — one opt-in option on the QA Lab transcript helper (`assistantReplyText` → `assistantReplyStartLine`), added because the scenario cannot otherwise identify a real assistant reply event. Purely additive; every existing caller's result is unchanged.
- `extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-runtime-agent-session.test.ts` — unit coverage for that option, including the failure mode it exists to remove.
- `extensions/qa-lab/src/scenario-catalog-channels.test.ts` — a catalog guard for this scenario's executability contract, added this revision (below).

There is **no production source change on this branch**. `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` returns exactly those four paths; `src/`, `packages/` and `ui/` are byte-identical to `origin/main`.

## What Changed This Revision

Both ClawSweeper Revision 25 findings are fixed for real, with no suppression and no renaming around the problem.

**[P1] Both retired Tasks CLI polls replaced.** The two `waitForCondition` steps invoked `runQaCli(env, ['tasks', 'list', '--json', '--runtime', 'subagent'])`. The Tasks CLI was retired by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159179 without a compatibility facade, so the first poll could never discover the spawned child and the scenario stopped before validating delivery — dead on arrival, not merely imprecise. Both polls now read the isolated Gateway's own `subagent_runs` rows through `readNativeQaSubagentRuns`, and the dependent flat fields migrate to that helper's real shape:

| Retired flat field | Native replacement |
|---|---|
| `task.status === 'succeeded'` | `run.execution.status === 'terminal' && run.execution.outcome?.status === 'ok'` |
| `task.endedAt` | `run.execution.endedAt` |
| `task.deliveryStatus === 'delivered'` | `run.delivery?.status === 'delivered'` |

The three downstream overlap assertions and the step's `detailsExpr` move with them (`completedChild.endedAt` → `completedChild.execution.endedAt`). The completion poll is deliberately left **unfiltered** rather than filtered by `spawnedChild.requesterSessionKey`, so the existing "requester session key changed between spawn and completion" assertion keeps its meaning instead of becoming trivially true.

**[P2] Ingress now uses the leased primary participant.** `senderId: alice` matched neither a leased alias nor a tester user ID, so `extensions/qa-lab/src/live-transports/telegram/adapter.runtime.ts` threw `Telegram QA sender requires primary or a named leased participant alias.` before the initiating message was ever sent. The scenario now sends as `primary`, which is the alias the adapter always creates for the leased credential itself and therefore the only ingress identity a healthy multi-participant lease can guarantee.

**One defect the review did not name, fixed alongside.** The scenario declared no `requiredChannelDriver`. `scenario-lane.ts` only excludes a scenario from a lane when that key is present, and the scenario's `channel: telegram` alone is satisfied by the **crabline** mock driver — so the scenario was eligible on a lane where no leased-participant contract exists at all, while its own success criteria claim "a real Telegram inbound turn". `coverage-report.ts` also derives the reproduce command's `--channel-driver` argument from that key, so its absence published a repro command that would run the mock driver. The scenario now declares `requiredChannelDriver: live`, which is the same key the other live Telegram scenarios (`telegram-policy-hot-reload`, `telegram-rich-inline-composition`, `telegram-prepared-delivery-recovery`) use.

A catalog guard in `scenario-catalog-channels.test.ts` now pins all three, modelled on the existing `settles terminal-reply scenarios from native run facts instead of sleeps` test for `subagent-completion-direct-fallback`.

## Which Admission Path Production Takes, And Why The Scenario No Longer Picks One

Two earlier revisions tried to make the scenario *establish deferred admission*. Both were wrong, and the reviewer was right both times. The corrected reading, verified in source:

| Seam | What it does |
|---|---|
| `subagent-announce-direct-delivery.ts` | When the requester is active the completion **wakes it first**, with `steeringMode: "all"`, and returns `path: "steered"` on success. The lane-serialized `agent` call below it is never reached. |
| `subagent-announce-active-wake.ts` | On `source_reply_delivery_mode_mismatch` the helper **deletes `sourceReplyDeliveryMode` and retries** — which is exactly the `message_tool_only` gate a direct-message completion sets. |
| `run/attempt-stream-prepare.ts` | The **openclaw** runtime registers its turn through `setActiveEmbeddedRun` with message injection v2 and `supportsTranscriptCommitWait: true`. |
| `extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-active-turn.ts` | The **codex** runtime does the same. |

`execution.runtime` accepts only `openclaw` and `codex`, and both register a steerable active run. Every other refusal reason in `prepareEmbeddedAgentQueueMessage` is `no_active_run` / `stale_run` / `not_streaming` / `compacting` / `guarded_injection_unsupported` / `tool_authority_mismatch` — runtime-capability or liveness states, none of them a scenario knob.

**Conclusion: no configuration this suite can select makes a busy requester refuse the completion steer.** Asserting deferred admission would fail healthy delivery, which is precisely the merge risk this PR carried. So the scenario asserts the outcome instead of a path:

- `execution.runtime` and `config.harnessRuntime` are unset.
- **`runtimePairLane: core` stays dropped**, so the scenario cannot contribute a release-validation result before it has been executed once. The branch's catalog-count file remains identical to `origin/main`.
- The observed path is **recorded as evidence**, not asserted: `admissionPath` resolves to `separate-requester-turn` or `steered-active-run`, alongside `postReplyUserMessages` and `postReplyTools`.

## What The Scenario Asserts

A real Telegram inbound turn drives a real Gateway:

1. The requester spawns exactly one native child, then occupies its own lane with a foreground `exec` holding for 60 s (`yieldMs` 90 s, backgrounding and `process` polling explicitly forbidden).
2. The hold command writes a readiness marker the instant it starts. The child blocks on that marker in a bounded `exec` before replying, so the overlap under test is **established by a barrier, not by relative model latency**.
3. The child reaches a terminal/ok execution state while the hold is still in flight — asserted against timestamps the runtime produces: `proofContents.startedAt <= completedChild.execution.endedAt <= proofContents.finishedAt`, and `proofContents.finishedAt <= execEvent.timestamp`, which fails loudly if the `exec` had backgrounded itself at the default 10 s yield.
4. **The cutoff for everything downstream is the requester's actual visible reply event.** `readSessionTranscriptSummary(..., { assistantReplyText: parentMarker })` returns `assistantReplyStartLine`: the index of the last assistant event whose *visible* text is exactly the marker. The scenario waits for that index to exist and then slices from it. It does not use a serialized-substring probe, and it does not use an observation-time event count.
5. **No transcript summary is read before the requester's `message`-tool result is committed.** A dedicated wait re-reads the requester transcript until a successful `message` result is present, and every subsequent summary comes from that read.
6. **From the reply event onward the requester records exactly one `message`-tool send, and zero `sessions_spawn` / `exec`.** This holds on both admission paths. The user-message count in that window distinguishes the two and is reported, not asserted.
7. Across the whole session the requester used exactly one `sessions_spawn`, one `exec`, and one `message`, in that order; the requester's own reply reaches Telegram strictly before the completion reply; and the completion appears exactly once across an 8 s duplicate window.

## Why The Cutoff Needed A Helper Option

`probeTextEndLine` is computed as `events.findLastIndex((event) => JSON.stringify(event).includes(probeText)) + 1` over the full event list, so it matches reasoning blocks and tool arguments that merely quote the same string. That matters here and not only in theory: `summarizeSessionTranscriptEvents` counts a successful tool call only when the assistant invocation *and* its result are both inside the selected slice, because `assistantToolNamesByCallId` is built from that slice. A cutoff that lands between the two silently drops a delivery that actually happened.

`assistantReplyText` matches the assistant event's extracted visible text with exact equality, and returns the index of that event rather than the position after it — so a model that emits the reply text and the completion's `message` call in the same assistant message still has its invocation inside the window. The unit test seeds exactly that shape and asserts both halves: from the reply anchor the send counts as 1; from the serialized-probe cutoff it counts as 0.

## Evidence

**The previous revision's evidence table was pinned to head `2729a7d055b7972d96844ae3b864270d9b1f2538` and is withdrawn.** Those gates were real when they ran, but the head has moved twice since and I have not re-run that exact lane set, so I am not restating any of it. Everything below was re-run by me at head `513698890df9057f0ff68ddf370c817aff2a78ca`, in the branch worktree, with `git 2.55` on `PATH` (three ratchet lanes silently bail under the host default `git 2.34`).

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm check:changed` | **`exit[check:changed]=0`, 34 lane headers present** (the runner prints no summary block on success) |
| `scenario-catalog-channels.test.ts` + `scenario-catalog.test.ts` + `suite-runtime-agent-session.test.ts` | **3 files / 80 passed · EXIT 0** |
| Knip unused-export scans (script / production / full-tree) | **0 entries each** |
| `src/cli/program/command-registry.test.ts -t tasks` | **`registerCoreCliByName returns false for tasks` passed** — executed confirmation that the retired CLI the base polls called cannot be registered at all |

### Per-finding base-fail → head-pass

Each finding was measured **independently**, against the reviewed base blob `d8f24e28d1a44486da6954c292fe5580a56257c2` and against this head, because a single `it` stops at its first failed assertion and would mask the other two:

```
=== BASE d8f24e28d1a ===
FAIL  [P1] retired Tasks CLI polls replaced
        - flow still invokes the retired `tasks` CLI
        - flow still shells out through runQaCli
        - flow never calls readNativeQaSubagentRuns
        - flow still reads retired flat field task.status
        - flow still reads retired flat field task.endedAt
        - flow still reads retired flat field task.deliveryStatus
        - flow still reads retired flat field completedChild.endedAt
FAIL  [P2] leased Telegram participant used for ingress
        - senderId "alice" is neither the guaranteed "primary" alias nor a leased participant
FAIL  [extra, not in review] live channel driver is required
        - requiredChannelDriver=undefined; scenario stays eligible for the crabline lane

=== HEAD ===
PASS  [P1] retired Tasks CLI polls replaced
PASS  [P2] leased Telegram participant used for ingress
PASS  [extra, not in review] live channel driver is required
```

Independently, reverting **only** the scenario YAML to the reviewed base and running the new catalog guard through vitest fails with `expected undefined to be 'live'`, and the guard passes at this head.

**What that measurement is and is not.** It is a validation/catalog-level measurement: it proves the scenario no longer calls a CLI that cannot be registered, no longer sends as an identity the live adapter rejects, and can no longer be claimed by a mock-driver lane. It is **not** an execution of the scenario, and I am not presenting it as one.

## Known Gap — the scenario still has not been executed end to end

I want to name this boundary exactly rather than gesture at it, and I am not claiming otherwise anywhere in this PR.

Its live lane is `qa-live-transports-convex.yml` → `run_live_telegram`, which runs `pnpm openclaw qa telegram --provider-mode live-frontier --credential-source convex --credential-role ci` in the `qa-live-shared` environment and hard-requires three maintainer-held secrets: `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENCLAW_QA_CONVEX_SITE_URL`, and `OPENCLAW_QA_CONVEX_SECRET_CI`. The Convex pair leases the real Telegram bot credential. A fork cannot obtain any of them, which is the correct behavior — so this run is a maintainer action, not a contributor one. Note that with `requiredChannelDriver: live` now declared, the previously-suggested `--channel-driver crabline` reduced-fidelity fallback is no longer an eligible lane for this scenario; that was the point of declaring it.

On the merge-risk item — *"eligible Telegram QA executions can reject healthy delivery"* — the two defects that made the scenario unexecutable are fixed this revision, the cutoff is a real reply event rather than a serialized substring match, no transcript summary is captured before the requester's message result is committed, the scenario still contains no assertion that discriminates between the two admission paths, and it declares no runtime-pair lane membership, so it cannot reject supported steering or contribute a misleading release-validation result before it has been executed once.

*Written by Tank (Claude), an AI agent operated by Eddie Abrams (zeroaltitude).*

prs.title: fix(channels): ingress claimNext starves other conversations when one blocked lane fills the scan window
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the durable ingress queue's `claimNext` silently starves unrelated conversations when one busy lane fills the entire scan window. A WhatsApp group (or Slack channel, Telegram chat, etc.) with enough spooled inbound events can block delivery for **all other conversations on the same account** — hours of silence, no errors, no visible failure.

Four complementary defects in `claimNext`:

1. **SQL blocked-lane filter skipped when `deriveLaneKey` is passed.** The production drain always passes `deriveLaneKey` (ingress-drain.ts:793), but the SQL WHERE clause that excludes rows with a stored `lane_key` in the blocked set only runs when `deriveLaneKey` is absent. WhatsApp and Discord store lane keys at enqueue time, so those rows could be efficiently excluded at the SQL level — but in production, they never are.

2. **No keyset pagination when the scan window is all lane-blocked.** When all rows in the window are valid but blocked, the while loop exits immediately and returns `null`, even though claimable rows exist beyond the window.

3. **Resume cursor not invalidated when lane-policy callbacks change** (review finding). The direct-claim resume cursor was stored as booleans only, so a changed `deriveLaneKey`/`reconcileStoredLaneKey` callback that makes an earlier row eligible was not detected, and the next call could wrongly skip past rows the new policy would claim.

4. **Resume cursor not invalidated when an earlier row is enqueued between direct claims** (review finding). After a direct claim exhausts its budget and retains a cursor, a new free-lane event enqueued with `receivedAt` **before** that cursor was skipped by the keyset predicate (`received_at > cursor`), so the earlier event could be claimed after a later one.

Concrete scenario: WhatsApp group A accumulates 100 spooled events during a long agent turn (lane-A blocked). A DM from user B arrives after the flood. `claimNext` scans the first 100 rows (all lane-A, all blocked) and returns `null`, never reaching B's row at position 101. B waits indefinitely. The stalled behavior survives across drain cycles because the same blocked prefix is re-scanned each time.

## Why This Change Was Made

Minimal changes in `claimNext`:

1. **Always apply the SQL stored-lane filter.** The `!claimOptions?.deriveLaneKey` guard is removed. The SQL filter is harmless when `deriveLaneKey` is also passed: rows with a stored `lane_key` in the blocked set are excluded (correct — the stored key is authoritative), and rows with NULL `lane_key` pass through to JS-level derivation and filtering (existing behavior). This alone fully restores the WhatsApp/Discord path.

2. **Keyset cursor for lane-blocked windows.** When the entire scan window consists of valid but lane-blocked rows (none claimable, none corrupt), a keyset cursor advances past the last scanned row and re-queries, bounded by a page budget so stop responsiveness is preserved. When the budget runs out on a direct scan, the cursor is retained so the next direct call resumes past the blocked prefix instead of restarting at the queue front.

3. **Invalidate the resume cursor on callback change** (review finding). The direct-scan resume state now retains the lane-policy callbacks **by identity**; when they change, the cursor is discarded and the scan restarts, so a changed policy that makes an earlier row eligible is honored instead of skipped. Cleared whenever a claim succeeds or the scan reaches the end of the queue.

4. **Invalidate the resume cursor on an earlier enqueue** (review finding). Any write that adds a pending row sorting **before** the retained cursor — an explicit earlier `receivedAt` enqueue, a recovered/released claim, or a resubmit — now invalidates the cursor so the next direct call rescans from the front and claims the earlier row first. Rows enqueued after the cursor keep the resume benefit.

5. **Authoritative queue-state revalidation of retained and in-flight cursors** (review findings: cross-handle writes and minimal-reference release). Closure-side invalidation cannot observe writes from other queue handles, and `release({ id, claim: { token } })` carries no `receivedAt` to run the guard. The scan now records, at retention, the authoritative count of scan-visible pending rows strictly before the cursor, and the worker counts the same predicate **in the same pinned read** as the paged snapshot. On resume and on every paged direct-scan snapshot the count is revalidated against the queue; a mismatch means a write from any handle inserted or removed a row before the cursor, so the keyset is dropped and the scan restarts from the front. A claim conflict also resets the scan so a write landing behind an in-flight page cursor is not skipped. This covers cross-handle enqueue/release/recover/resubmit and id-and-token-only releases without a per-release ordering query.

6. **Register the new test in the database-worker lane.** `ingress-queue.resume.test.ts` was missing from `databaseWorkerCoreTestFiles` in `test/vitest/vitest.database-worker-core-paths.mjs`, which ran it in a bun fast lane without the host broker (`SqliteWorkerError: Shared-state admission requires the host broker`). It is now registered beside its sibling ingress-queue tests.

## User Impact

Durable channels (WhatsApp, Discord, Telegram, Slack, and any channel using the shared ingress queue) no longer experience unbounded delivery stalls when one conversation is busy. Messages from other conversations proceed normally with no config, protocol, or persisted-state changes.

## Evidence

### Regression coverage

- `ingress-queue.test.ts` (2 new, table-driven): stored-lane variant enqueues 100 rows with `laneKey="blocked"` then 1 row with `laneKey="free"` — on main, `claimNext({deriveLaneKey, blockedLaneKeys:["blocked"], scanLimit:100})` returns `null`; on fix returns `row-100`. Derived-lane variant enqueues 100 rows without stored lane key where `deriveLaneKey` returns "blocked" for each, then 1 row deriving to "free" — on main returns `null`; on fix paginates and returns `row-100`.

- `ingress-queue.resume.test.ts` (new): "resumes direct claim scans past a blocked prefix beyond the page budget", "invalidates the resume cursor when the lane-policy callbacks change", and "invalidates the resume cursor when an earlier row is enqueued between direct claims". The cursor-invalidation tests fail against the old boolean-only logic and against a build without the earlier-enqueue invalidation (stash proof: the earlier-enqueue test fails with `1 failed`).

- **Authoritative revalidation regressions** (latest review fix): "revalidates the resume cursor against authoritative state when another handle enqueues an earlier row" (a second queue handle writes an earlier row the first handle's closure cannot see; the resume must claim it first), "revalidates the resume cursor when a minimal claim reference releases an earlier row" (`release({ id, claim: { token } })` with no `receivedAt`; the released row must be claimed before the tail), and "revalidates the in-flight page cursor when another handle writes during paging" (a write lands between pages of one call via the claim clock; the keyset must be dropped and the earlier row claimed). Each fails without the authoritative count revalidation and passes with it.

- Against unfixed main, the new tests fail (claimNext returns null, never reaching the free lane past the blocked window). Pre-existing tests pass unchanged.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/channels/message/ingress-queue.resume.test.ts` → 7 passed; `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/channels/message/ingress-queue.test.ts src/channels/message/ingress-queue.claim-ownership.test.ts src/channels/message/ingress-queue.dead-letters.test.ts` → 57 passed; `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/channels/message/ingress-queue.test.ts src/channels/message/ingress-queue.dead-letters.test.ts` → 46 passed. Core typecheck (`tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json`) → exit 0.

### Runtime proof (real SQLite queue through the worker)

A focused production-queue trace drives the real `createChannelIngressQueue` against a real SQLite state file:

```
=== Scenario A: stored-lane blocked prefix fills the scan window (SQL filter) ===
claimNext(blocked=[blocked], scanLimit=100, deriveLaneKey) => "free-A"
  (free-A is row 100, beyond the 100-row window; must be claimed)

=== Scenario B: derived-lane blocked prefix beyond one snapshot (keyset paging) ===
claimNext(blocked=[blocked], scanLimit=100, deriveLaneKey) => "free-B"
  (free-B is row 100+201 beyond the snapshot cap of scanLimit+100; must page and be claimed)

=== Scenario C: blocked set exceeds SQLite bind budget ===
claimNext(40000 blocked lanes, deriveLaneKey) => "free-C"
  (the SQL predicate stays bounded, no bind-variable overflow)

=== Scenario D: earlier row enqueued between direct claims keeps ordering ===
claimNext #1 (blocks 6000-8200, budget exhausted => null) => null
enqueue earlier-free (receivedAt before retained cursor) => "accepted"
claimNext #2 (must claim earlier-free before free-tail) => "earlier-free"
```

On **unfixed main**, the same trace returns `null` for every `claimNext` — the free lane beyond the blocked window is never reached, and Scenario D's earlier enqueue would be skipped by the retained cursor.

### Sibling-surface context

The ingress drain's `resolveLaneKey` helper (ingress-drain.ts) already uses `deriveLaneKey ?? laneKey ?? id` — the stored lane key is authoritative and the drain already prefers it. The `blockedLaneKeys` set in `drainOnce` is computed identically from active/claimed/retry-delayed lanes regardless of this change. No drain, claim, or delivery behavior is altered beyond claimNext no longer returning false negatives when a blocked lane fills the scan window.

prs.title: fix: remove synchronous guard snapshots and restore CI preparation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unnecessary synchronous snapshot subprocesses in agent-deletion and updater guards, a session-creation fixture that invalidated its own database admission, and mismatched runtime/UI identities during test preparation.

## User Impact

Agent deletion and admitted updates keep current authority checks without starting a fresh snapshot child for every ordinary guard. There are no schema, configuration, retention, permission, or upgrade-format changes. Artifact-preserving reads still use private snapshots; initial update admission and finalization remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The final deletion guard now uses the same existing native current-row read path as its sibling lease guard. A cold-owner regression proves that ordinary guards create no snapshot children, artifact-preserving scopes still do, and rollback still revokes the guard.

The initial-turn authorization fixture resolves both session store targets through the existing read-only worker. Its previous synchronous lookup could create a database after worker admission had recorded absence. The retained/revoked authorization, final-write, transcript, and cleanup assertions are unchanged.

The admitted updater's mutation guards select the existing current-row native reader, without caching a recovery decision across awaits. Diagnostic recovery readers keep their artifact-preserving default. UI test preparation now passes the already-captured runtime build ID into the UI builder, then retains the exact post-build identity check.

## Evidence

- The cold-guard regression failed before the fix: three ordinary guard calls started three snapshot children. They now start zero, while the artifact-preserving call still starts one.
- `pnpm test src/agents/agent-lifecycle-registry.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 19/19 passed; 357.57 seconds including preparation on the loaded macOS host. The full Gateway deletion RPC remains for CI verification.
- Isolated Linux `pnpm test src/gateway/server.sessions.create.auth-policy.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: passed; case 46.257 seconds, wrapper 156.51 seconds. The long case exercises committed initial turns and final-write refusal through a real Gateway, not a mocked helper.
- Targeted format, typed lint, and Gateway-server types passed. Independent reviews found no actionable P0–P2 issues.
- The updater cost regression fails before the repair on an unexpected snapshot child. Both repaired cases pass, including refusal of recovery committed while a readiness request awaits its reply. Ordinary guards create no snapshot; explicit artifact-preserving inspection still creates one. `pnpm test src/cli/update-cli/update-command-recovery-cost.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 2/2, cases 4.421s and 0.379s; wrapper 330.49s including worker preparation on the loaded host. CLI-update types passed in 19.72s; scoped lint, format, and independent P0–P2 review passed.
- UI build-identity regression: two expected admission failures before the fix; six selected cases passed after it in 24.78s. Scoped scripts/root-test types, lint, format, and independent P0–P2 review passed. The real Linux test entrypoint now reaches Vitest without an identity mismatch.

## Remaining Investigated Failures

The original [main-tier CI 38337557590](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38337557590) also exposed catalog, real-Gateway UI, updater, and placement timeouts. These are not relabeled as fixed:

- The updater handoff case reproduced its unchanged 120s timeout locally, with 15 snapshot children. Removing ordinary guard snapshots has focused regression proof, but the original case still timed out in a post-fix replay (314.38s wrapper). No deadline or assertion changed.
- Both real-Gateway UI cases reached execution after the build-ID repair, then exhausted their unchanged 180s deadlines during fixture preparation, before page creation. The host-command case spent approximately 152s in `update repair`; the remaining preparation cost is unresolved.
- The catalog cold replay timed out during startup. A warm replay passed, which is not proof of a repair. Startup profiling identified expensive plugin preparation and reply-runtime activation, under separate investigation.
- Two placement replays timed out on the first `sessions.create`, before placement dispatch. Instrumentation found no snapshot children during the request and continuing creation progress, not a demonstrated placement deadlock. No speculative placement change is included.

Exact-head CI will verify the combined repair. Published-driver compatibility is unchanged; the existing main-tier legacy-updater coverage remains required evidence. CI timings will be recorded when available.

prs.title: fix(service): keep Linux pnpm 12 Gateway unit on a replacement-surviving entrypoint
prs.body:
Closes #169059

## What Problem This Solves

On Linux with a pnpm 12 global install (`global/v11` layout), `openclaw gateway install` records a versioned entrypoint in the systemd unit — `…/global/v11/<project>/node_modules/.pnpm/openclaw@<version>/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js`. Every `openclaw update` replaces that project directory, so the unit points at a deleted path and the updater leaves the Gateway stopped ("previous service installation was not restarted automatically"). `gateway start` / `gateway install --force` recover it, but both rewrite another versioned path, so the next update fails the same way.

A durable candidate exists on these hosts: `~/.local/share/pnpm/global/v11/<hash>/node_modules/openclaw/openclaw.mjs` — the `<hash>` symlink is retargeted to each replacement project on update, and the CLI already runs from it. #167905 fixed this for Windows launchers; this change extends the same durable-entrypoint guarantee to the Linux pnpm 12 (`global/v11`) layout.

- **Related:** #167905 / #168198 (Windows launcher entrypoint); issue confirmed on two independent hosts (x86_64 and ARM64).

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared service-argument planner (`resolveCliEntrypointPathForService`) has a stable-link branch that persists a verified package link instead of the replaceable store generation, but it is skipped for `global/v11` because pnpm isolated-owner discovery cannot recognize a package root reached through the versioned `.pnpm` store path — `resolvePnpmGlobalInstallOwner` returns `null` and the planner falls back to the versioned generation.

The fix makes isolated-owner discovery understand the nested `.pnpm` store path (so the verified owner is found), then resolves the durable replacement-surviving package root through the `<hash>` symlink that pnpm retargets on every update. The unit entrypoint is built from that durable path, so it keeps resolving after package replacement. Legacy `global/5` and other layouts are unchanged (the durable lookup only applies to the pnpm isolated `v<N>` layout and falls back to the existing verified-package-link path otherwise).

- **Intended outcome:** on Linux pnpm 12, `gateway install` writes `…/global/v11/<hash>/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js`, which survives `openclaw update`.
- **Out of scope:** no changes to the updater restart decision, `global/5`/legacy layouts, Windows launchers, or the environment/drop-in handling.
- **Highest-risk area:** the isolated-owner matching and durable-path derivation in the pnpm `v<N>` discovery path.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** existing `global/5` and pnpm 11 discovery tests still pass; the durable lookup is additive (falls back to the verified package link) and only active for the isolated `v<N>` layout.

## User Impact

Linux users with a pnpm 12 global install no longer need to reinstall/repair their Gateway after every update. The unit keeps pointing at the durable `<hash>` entrypoint, so the updater can identify the service and restart it instead of leaving the Gateway stopped.

- **Success criteria:** `resolveGatewayProgramArguments` pins the unit entrypoint to `global/v11/<hash>/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js`; the path still resolves after a simulated pnpm replacement of the generation project.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `src/daemon/program-args.ts` (entrypoint planning) and `src/infra/update-global.ts` (`inferPnpmIsolatedGlobalRootFromPackageRoot`, `resolvePnpmIsolatedInstallOwner`, `resolvePnpmIsolatedDurablePackageRoot`); regression fixture `src/daemon/program-args.v11.test.ts`.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** real pnpm 12 global install (`global/v11` isolated layout) in an isolated `HOME`, real shipped planner from this branch, Linux. pnpm rewrote/replaced the package exactly as `openclaw update` does (new generation project, `<hash>` symlink retargeted, old generation deleted).
- **Live user-systemd proof (disposable Linux account, real update round-trip):** on a disposable account with a canonical `HOME`, a user systemd manager (`loginctl enable-linger`), Node at a stable path, and a **real pnpm 12 global/v11 install of official 2026.10.1**, the full live flow ran end to end:
  - **A (base):** official `2026.10.1` `gateway install --port 28789` writes the unit `ExecStart` to the versioned `global/v11/<generation>/node_modules/.pnpm/openclaw@2026.10.1/…/dist/index.js`; service active, `/healthz` `{"ok":true,"status":"live"}`; a custom drop-in (`Environment=OC_PRF_MARKER=…`) and the existing `~/.openclaw` state were recorded and tracked through every stage.
  - **B (bug reproduced by a real update):** `openclaw update` (`2026.10.1 → candidate 2026.10.2` from a local artifact) completed through the real shipped updater — admission checks `config: ok, database-schema: ok, node-runtime: ok, plugin-availability: ok`, per-database migration snapshots taken — and pnpm wrote a **new generation project and deleted the old one**; the recorded `ExecStart` path no longer exists and `systemctl --user start openclaw-gateway` **crash-loops** (`status=1/FAILURE`, auto-restart) — the reported Gateway outage, reproduced by a real update on a real install.

prs.title: fix(agents): retry exec auto-review once when the endpoint requires reasoning
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The model-backed exec auto-reviewer (`tools.exec.reviewer.model`) fails closed on every request when it is pointed at a reasoning-only endpoint. With OpenRouter's `openai/gpt-oss-safeguard-20b`, a model built for exactly this kind of policy review, each review returned:

```
exec reviewer completion failed: 400 Reasoning is mandatory for this endpoint and cannot be disabled.
```

Every auto-reviewed command fell back to human approval, so the reviewer did no work while looking configured.

## Why This Change Was Made

`createModelExecAutoReviewer` calls the simple-completion runtime with `maxTokens` and `temperature` only and never sets a reasoning level. The OpenAI-compatible completions transport maps an unset level to the model's off-effort, and for OpenRouter-format reasoning models that becomes a literal `reasoning: { effort: "none" }` in the payload. Models that allow reasoning to be disabled accept it; reasoning-only models reject the request outright.

The compaction path already handles this case: when a provider reports reasoning as mandatory it retries once at `minimal` via `pickFallbackThinkingLevel`. The reviewer had no equivalent. This change gives it one:

- On a completion failure whose message matches `isReasoningConstraintErrorMessage`, retry the review once with `reasoning: "minimal"`.
- The retry only runs when `tools.exec.reviewer.thinking` (#147192) is unset. An operator who configured a level, including `off`, asked for exactly that request and gets the provider's answer unchanged.
- The retry reuses the reviewer's abort signal and gets a fresh reviewer timeout, matching how the existing code already treats preparation and completion as separate timeout windows.
- A second failure returns the existing "exec reviewer completion failed" ask decision; nothing loops.

No behavior changes for reviewers whose first request succeeds, and no config is added.

## User Impact

Operators can point the exec reviewer at reasoning-only models without every review degrading to a manual prompt. Failure handling is unchanged: an error other than a reasoning constraint, or a second reasoning-constraint error, still produces an "ask" decision with the provider message.

## Evidence

New file `exec-auto-reviewer.reasoning-fallback.test.ts` (the existing suite is at the 1000-line lint cap):

- "retries once with minimal reasoning when the endpoint requires reasoning" asserts the first call carries no `reasoning` option, the second carries `"minimal"`, and the parsed allow decision is returned.
- "does not retry a reasoning-constraint failure more than once" asserts exactly two calls and the ask decision with the provider message.
- "does not retry when a reviewer thinking level is configured" asserts a single call carrying the configured level and the ask decision.

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.test.ts src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.reasoning-fallback.test.ts
  Test Files  2 passed   Tests  87 passed
pnpm tsgo:core   # clean
oxlint src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.ts src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.reasoning-fallback.test.ts   # clean
```

Observed on 2026.9.2 with `tools.exec.reviewer.model` set to `openrouter/openai/gpt-oss-safeguard-20b`: every exec approval surfaced the 400 above in the Guardian review and fell back to a manual prompt.

prs.title: fix(sessions): self-heal session-reset races instead of bricking the agent
prs.body:
Closes #139960

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users whose session reset raced a live turn's flush would see the affected agent fail on **every** surface — chat channels, bridges, webchat, cron, and subagent recovery — with an unrecoverable `SessionCanonicalKeyMigrationRequiredError` until an operator manually ran `openclaw doctor --fix`. The same misclassification also silently fallbacked healthy models on every turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

The raced row shape (a complete entry payload invalidated by `entry_valid = -1` over a retained window) is rebuildable, not corruption: it is exactly what `doctor --fix` repairs. Validation now tolerates that tuple (empty sentinel **or** a complete, self-consistent payload over the retained window) while unparseable or identity/timestamp-inconsistent payloads still require repair. To close the race at the source, the reset and root-creation statement pairs (trigger-driven pending write + settle) are wrapped in an immediate transaction (SAVEPOINT-nested when already inside one), so a concurrent flush can no longer interleave its `entry_json` write between them.

## User Impact

A session reset racing a turn flush self-heals instead of bricking the agent: messages keep flowing (or the session transparently rebuilds from its retained window on next use), and the row returns to a valid state on the session's next turn — no operator, no downtime. Headless/bridge sessions that cannot run `/reset` or `doctor` mid-incident benefit the most.

## Evidence

- Regression tests (`src/config/sessions/session-canonical-key.test.ts`):
  - the raced tuple no longer throws on a live connection, stays tolerated on a cold listing, and returns to a listed, valid entry after the session's next turn;
  - an unparseable payload with `entry_valid = -1` over a retained window **still** throws `openclaw doctor --fix` (repair path preserved);
  - the pre-existing corruption pins (malformed row partial-snapshot protection, mismatched-time target, readonly pending-row summary) all pass unchanged.
- Full `src/config/sessions/` suite: 1538 passed; the only 2 failures (`session-transcript-reconcile.lease.test.ts`) reproduce on unmodified `main` at `279d42d4be3`.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` clean.
- Operational evidence: this self-heal + atomic-settle behavior has been running on our production fleet since 2026-09-05 after the same race produced a real multi-surface outage there; no recurrence since.

prs.title: feat(meta): support Muse Wonder
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Meta users need to select the newly released Muse Wonder with its complete public API reasoning controls.

## User Impact

Adds `meta/muse-wonder-1.0` with text/image input, tools, streaming, encrypted reasoning replay, a 1,048,576-token context window, and Standard pricing of $4 input / $0.20 cached input / $20 output per million tokens. Spark remains the lower-cost onboarding default; existing models, primary selections, and authored aliases remain supported.

**Scope confirmed: complete public Wonder API integration first. A native Muse Code adapter will follow separately after this PR is fully merged. Authenticated Wonder API and full isolated Gateway/tool/image validation have passed. The native Muse Code adapter remains deferred until this API PR is fully merged.**

Muse Wonder Full (`muse-wonder-full-1.0`) is native Muse Code subscription-only on Power Usage and Maximum Usage plans. It is not available through Meta Model API, and `max` effort does not select it. This API change does not advertise a nonexistent Full or Wonder Contributor route. The native Muse Code adapter is explicitly outside this PR's scope and deferred until this API integration is merged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Meta plugin's manifest remains the metadata owner. Its thinking policy now follows the model's supported efforts, including `max` for Wonder and Spark 1.3 Standard, without granting it to Contributor models. The existing Responses transport already owns tools, images, streaming, and replay; the new model uses that path rather than another adapter.

The model identity, availability, context, reasoning, and pricing were verified against Meta's October 12 public [model documentation](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/models), [reasoning contract](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/reasoning), and [pricing](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/pricing-rate-limits). The 131,072-token catalog output cap is OpenClaw's existing conservative convention, not a vendor-published maximum.

## Evidence

- Focused provider and runtime suites: **88 tests passed** across `extensions/meta/index.test.ts`, `src/auto-reply/thinking.test.ts`, and `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses-shared.test.ts`; combined wrapper wall time **38.39s**. The Meta file had 14 passing tests and 2.397s of test-body time (27.95s shard duration including compiler preparation). The published head and its test-only follow-up both passed PR CI; no old-head checks are substituted for current-head evidence.
- Required standalone measurement: `pnpm test extensions/meta/index.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 14 passed, **41.45s wrapper wall time**, 2.836s test-body time; the cold compiler preparation dominated the wall time.
- The new catalog/default regressions failed on the pre-implementation source. CI-safe request proof captures the final serialized HTTP body through the actual Meta completion hook and Responses transport; this is mocked HTTP boundary coverage, not live inference.
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/lib/plugin-npm-runtime-build.mts extensions/meta`: passed; six source entries compiled, and the emitted catalog contains Wonder and its native `max` mapping while retaining the Spark default.
- Extension production/test typechecks, scoped Meta lint, import cycles, provider/plugin boundaries, metadata/config baselines, and changed-file structural ratchets passed.
- Docs MDX, config examples, glossary, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent Codex AutoReview, P0–P2: the implementation and the subsequent proxy-bootstrap live-test fix both completed with no actionable findings. The test-only changed-file gate again passed formatting, extension typechecking, boundaries, and ratchets, with only the same inherited three dead-export findings below.

### Inherited local gate failure

The complete changed-file gate is **not green**: `pnpm check:changed` stopped at the production Knip dead-export scan. The same three findings reproduced on a clean, fully installed checkout of the pinned base `edccd870f4073a398652cab59da4cfccbd790bff`:

Those files are unchanged by this PR. The script and full-tree export scans passed on both candidate and baseline. The first baseline attempt had missing UI dependencies and was discarded; the reproduction above used a fresh frozen-lockfile install. Remaining scoped lint/import/runtime-sidecar/media-helper checks were run separately and passed. No unrelated core exports were removed or ignored to conceal this failure.

### Authenticated live proof

All live work below is pinned to signed source head `6d29d5491b4480d35d4521e005776e0a64675323` and uses task-owned state, config, caches, ports, and processes. The serving Gateway was not changed. Credentials were securely imported with exact `api.meta.ai` host binding and used through masked 1Password CLI injection; no credential values or encrypted reasoning blobs are included in this evidence.

The Wonder-only provider suite completed successfully: **7 tests passed, 15 unrelated/opt-in cases excluded**, wrapper wall time **86.45s**. It executed seven streaming Responses turns, each HTTP 200, requested/effective model `muse-wonder-1.0`, and exactly one payload per turn:

| Contract | Result |

| Authenticated `/models` catalog | Wonder and the Standard Spark rows present |
| High reasoning text and streaming deltas | Passed |
| Caller `maxTokens: 0` | Serialized cap 131,072 accepted; short semantic completion passed, not a claim about vendor maximum output |


The full isolated Gateway suite also passed: **1 selected Wonder model passed, 0 model skips**, wrapper wall time **218.47s** (Vitest duration 197.86s). prs.title: fix(feishu): stop inbound mentions from cascading into replies
prs.body:
Closes #121921

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu group replies would automatically mention every non-bot participant mentioned in the inbound message, even when the agent's reply did not request those mentions. Error and fallback replies could therefore wake multiple bots and create an unintended cascade.

## Why This Change Was Made

Inbound mention targets remain available as agent context, but they are no longer passed into the reply dispatcher or automatically attached to generated replies. Explicit outbound mentions, native Feishu `at` rendering, and bot-authored required mentions (`requiredMentionTargets`) remain unchanged.

This restores the boundary introduced by #71396 without reverting the native mention-rendering improvements from #93522.

## User Impact

Feishu users and multi-agent groups no longer receive unrequested `@` notifications from ordinary, error, fallback, card, streaming, block, or chunked replies. Agents can still explicitly mention users when the outbound content or message-tool request asks for it.

## Evidence

- Regression coverage verifies non-streaming final/error replies, static cards, streaming card closes, and independent block/chunk delivery do not inherit inbound mention targets.
- Existing coverage verifies `requiredMentionTargets` still reaches every required text chunk and static card reply.
- Focused Feishu tests pass:
  - `reply-dispatcher.test.ts`: **124/124**
  - `bot.test.ts` + `send.test.ts`: **131/131**
  - Total: **255/255**
- `oxfmt --check` passes for all 3 changed files.

prs.title: fix(codex): give the user-input test fixture host capabilities
prs.body:
fix(codex): give the user-input test fixture host capabilities

Refs #155440

## What Problem This Solves

Three Codex sandbox tests fail on macOS with:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'activeComputerContext')
  at buildTurnStartParams (extensions/codex/src/app-server/turn-params.ts:148:33)
```

## Root cause

`extensions/codex/src/app-server/user-input-bridge.test-support.ts` —
`createCodexUserInputTestParams()` returned an object with **no
`hostCapabilities` key**, closed off by `as unknown as EmbeddedRunAttemptParams`
(line 16). The cast silenced the type gap; it did not fill it.

`extensions/codex/src/app-server/turn-params.ts:148` reads:

```ts
params.hostCapabilities.activeComputerContext?.() ?? "…host presence unavailable"
```

The `?.` guards the **callback**, not the host **object** — with
`hostCapabilities === undefined` the property access itself throws before the
`?.` is ever reached.

Regression provenance, both verified: the fixture was last touched in
`7e0b599ca48` (#126387, 2026-08-21); the unprocessed read arrived in
`fc60bf09f2` (#153381, 2026-09-19), which did not update the fixtures.

## The fix

Two lines, in **one test fixture**. No production code is touched.

```diff
+import { createCodexTestHostCapabilities } from "./host-capability.test-support.js";
…
+    // Turn params read host authority unconditionally; a fixture without it throws.
+    hostCapabilities: createCodexTestHostCapabilities(),
```

The typed helper `createCodexTestHostCapabilities()` already existed at
`host-capability.test-support.ts:28`, documented as *"Minimal host authority for
tests that do not exercise host policy or approvals"*, and was already used by
`approval-bridge.*.test.ts`, `attempt-startup*.test-support.ts` and
`dynamic-tool-build.test-support.ts`.

## The test runs on Linux — that is the point

`transport-stdio.sandbox.test.ts:20` is
`describe.skipIf(process.platform !== "darwin")`, so the three cases that
caught this **never ran on Linux and never ran in CI**. I confirmed the other
two consumers of the fixture pass 26/26 on Linux — they have **zero**
references to `buildTurnStartParams`, so they never reach the line. A skipped
regression test is worse than a bypass: it cannot be seen failing.

So the fix comes with a test that reproduces the **same real path** in
`turn-params.test.ts` (shard `extension-codex-app-server-support`, which already
exercises `buildTurnStartParams` on Linux). It replicates the official macOS
gate's sequence literally, including `resolveCodexAppServerRuntimeOptions` with
`env: {}` / `codexConfigToml: null` / `requirementsToml: null` (the Linux
equivalent of an empty `CODEX_HOME`) and `preserveNativeTurnSettings: true`.

**Verified discriminante by reverting only the fixture:**

```
BEFORE   TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'activeComputerContext')
         ❯ buildTurnStartParams extensions/codex/src/app-server/turn-params.ts:148:33
         Tests  1 failed | 14 passed (15)                        [wall 55s, cold]
AFTER    ✓ builds a native sandbox turn without a host presence read 9ms
         Tests  15 passed (15)                                   [wall 25s]
```

This covers, on Linux, exactly the
`createCodexUserInputTestParams()` → `buildTurnStartParams()` stretch that
`transport-stdio.sandbox.test.ts:268-275` exercises on macOS. What remains
unreachable from Linux — real native binary contention, `exec_command` against
a real `codex` — is irreducible by the suite's own design and is not what broke.

### Measured test wall time

| Run | Wall | Cost of new test |
|---|---|---|
| 1st, cold, no fix | 55 s | 14 ms, failing |
| After fix, warm | 25 s | **9 ms** |
| Discriminant re-check, cold | 16 s | 14 ms, failing |
| All 4 fixture consumers | 23 s | — |

Marginal cost: **9 ms**. No timers, sleeps or polling. `env: {}` explicit, no
process boot, no credentials, no live Gateway.

## Evidence - validation gates

Green: `turn-params.test.ts` 15/15 · all 4 fixture consumers **41/41** ·
`transport-stdio.sandbox.test.ts` 3 skipped (darwin-only, expected) ·
`oxlint` 0 warnings 0 errors · `oxfmt --check` clean · `check:max-lines-ratchet` OK.

`check:line-cap-ratchet` reports 3 failures in files **byte-identical to the
base** (`git diff --quiet 7e8732d9d71` confirms) — they grew upstream and the
ratchet snapshot lags. My two files are 390 and 20 lines, far under the cap,
and neither appears.

Not run: `pnpm test` full suite, `pnpm build`, `tsgo:test:root`.

## What I would want a reviewer to push on

1. **`turn-params.ts:148` still has no object-level guard.** Every fixture is
   covered *today*, but a third fixture written without `hostCapabilities`
   breaks the same way again — silently, and only on macOS. I kept this
   PR production-code-free and scoped to the 2-line fixture fix. Whether
   `params.hostCapabilities?.activeComputerContext?.()` belongs here as a
   defence-in-depth follow-up is an open question I did not decide.
2. **The new import drags a barrel.** `user-input-bridge.test-support.ts` now
   imports `host-capability.test-support.ts`, which reaches
   `openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-harness`. `AGENTS.md` warns about broad barrel
   imports in tests. Measured: the 4-file run was 23 s total, no appreciable
   change. Worth a mention, not a blocker.
3. **The `as unknown as EmbeddedRunAttemptParams` cast stays.** With
   `hostCapabilities` present the object still lacks most required fields.
   Removing the cast would mean building a complete params object — out of
   scope here.
4. **Not duplicate coverage.** `turn-params.test.ts` already had an *active
   computer context* block with a hand-synthesised `hostCapabilities`. This
   block is not that: it asserts the **shared fixture** carries the key, which
   was the uncovered gap.

🤖 Generated with [openclaw](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw)

---

## Addendum — typecheck status, added after the body above was written

I wrote the Gates section before finishing the typecheck pass, and it is
incomplete. Stating it plainly:

- **This PR changes test files only.** There is no production change, so
  `tsgo:core` has nothing to check here.
- **The relevant lane, `tsgo:extensions:test`, did not complete.** I ran it and
  it was killed by my own `MemoryMax=9G` cap (exit 143) after 149 s, with
  **0 TypeScript errors reported** — it was killed, not type-errored. That lane
  typechecks the entire extensions test surface, which does not fit the memory
  ceiling I set for this machine. I chose not to raise the ceiling rather than
  risk an out-of-memory kill on the host.
- **So: the change is not typechecked.** Vitest transpiles without typechecking,
  which is why it passes there regardless.

What I do have: the discriminante test (real `TypeError` from the real entry
point, reverting only the fixture), all 4 fixture consumers at 41/41, `oxlint`
and `oxfmt` clean, and `check:max-lines-ratchet` OK.

Given the change is two added lines in one fixture object — a key that the
helper's own return type already declares — I judge the residual typecheck risk
low. I am flagging it rather than implying the gate passed.

Media is message content, so it now has its own 120s deadline (the reporter measured 31–50s; their workaround used 90s). prs.title: fix(update): success summary repeats settled plugin data/settings upgrades as pending
prs.body:
Closes #170334

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after a successful update, the success summary still listed acpx and codex "data/settings upgrade is unfinished … status=pending" warnings and told the operator to "let the current update finish", even when Doctor had settled those upgrades later in the same pass. Skipped plugins were counted without saying why.

## User Impact

User impact: the final update summary only shows plugin data/settings upgrades that are actually still pending, and those now say to run `openclaw doctor --fix`. The human plugin summary lists why each plugin was skipped. JSON output is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

acpx and codex declare Doctor-only `after-session-repair` migrations. Doctor's config preflight reports them pending and warns; later in the same pass, the post-session repair settles them in the ledger, but the warning was already collected and returned to the updater.

- **Producer (candidate Doctor child):** before writing its update result, Doctor drops warnings the ledger shows as settled. If the ledger cannot be read, every warning is kept. Because the post-plugin Doctor child runs from the candidate's `dist`, this applies to updates *to* a release containing it, including ones driven by beta.2.
- **Persisted steps (finalize/repair path):** `recordWarnings` now treats each call as the current list and retires dropped rows. A later warning for the same plugin retires the earlier one.
- **Guidance:** "let the current update finish" is shown only while the package swap is in progress; after the final pass it says `Run "openclaw doctor --fix"`.
- **Skip reasons:** the human summary prints each skipped plugin's message (actionable and operator-managed skips already print as warnings).

If the ledger still has a plugin pending, the warning stays.

## Evidence

- `update-command-resume-completion.test.ts`: run-record warnings and the rendered report. Before: the stale acpx step remained (`pendingAgain=false`), and stale + current both showed (`pendingAgain=true`). After: both pass. 137s wall (new cases ~7–10s; heavy file before this change).
- `doctor-health.update.test.ts`: new producer test, failed before (two warnings vs one). 24.5s wall.
- `update-cli.plugin-convergence.test.ts`: skip reason printed. Failed before. 141s wall (new test 1.7s).
- `deferred-plugin-migrations.test.ts` (31.5s), `doctor-update-run.test.ts` (25.5s), `update-finalization-lifecycle.test.ts` (157s) pass.
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, scoped oxlint, oxfmt, `git diff --check` clean.
- Known gaps: parents from before 2026-09-19 (no `completionOwner`) record first-Doctor warnings by index and can still show those stale; console lines already printed mid-run cannot be withdrawn.

prs.title: fix(update): Doctor lint deferred with 0ms left after a slow state snapshot
prs.body:
Closes #170333

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on large state directories, update validation's Doctor lint deferred all agent-scope inspections ("0ms remaining in the validation inspection window") and Doctor disposal was cut to 52ms, while the lint step still showed ✓.

## User Impact

User impact: candidate Doctor and lint now get their own inspection window per validation command, so slow state snapshots no longer starve them. When inspections are still deferred, the step shows `!` with "run `openclaw doctor --fix` after the update" instead of a plain pass. Deferral remains advisory and never blocks activation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The candidate's Doctor budget was anchored at the ledger's `validating` step, which starts before the state snapshot and `candidate-doctor`. Updaters since 2026.10.1 give each validation command its own ≥300s budget, so that anchor charged unrelated snapshot/doctor time to lint (121.85s + 152.78s > the 149s window) and clamped disposal to the remaining milliseconds. The candidate only sees the copied ledger, so it detects those updaters by the in-progress `candidate-state-snapshot` step and anchors at its own command start (with a 10s disposal margin for spawn/respawn). Older updaters keep the `validating` anchor. The lint parent computes the anchor once and hands it to its worker.

Update behavior: the budget anchor is candidate-side and takes effect when updating *to* a release containing it from 2026.10.1+ updaters. The advisory rendering runs in the installed updater and takes effect for updates driven *from* a release containing it.

## Evidence

- `src/commands/doctor-lint.update-budget.test.ts`: new fixture modeling the real copied ledger (`validating` 280s ago + in-progress `candidate-state-snapshot`): agent checks run, source `validation-command`, disposal 287s out. Fails before the change; the old-updater case still defers. 6/6, 60.3s wall.
- `src/infra/update-candidate-canary.lint.test.ts`: advisory for 0 and 3 checks run, exit 0, renders `! candidate-doctor-lint`. Fails before; 7/7 after, 72.1s wall (new tests are ms; time is worker prep).
- `src/commands/doctor-lint-process.test.ts` 15/15 (26.1s), `src/flows/doctor-health.update-budget.test.ts` and `src/cli/program/register.maintenance.lazy.test.ts` pass.
- oxfmt, oxlint, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `git diff --check` clean.
- Known gap: 2026.9.6–9.x updaters (fresh budgets but no snapshot step) keep the stricter window; operator `--timeout` below 300s is not modeled (pre-existing).

prs.title: fix(update): service definition refresh skipped when the config snapshot is large
prs.body:
Closes #170331

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw update` warns `candidate-config-read-failed: reader process exited with code 1 without a result` and leaves the Gateway service definition unrefreshed when the operator's config snapshot is larger than the reader pipe buffer (~64 KB on macOS, ~200 KB on Linux).

## User Impact

User impact: updates with moderately large configs refresh the service definition again instead of warning and skipping it. When an optional read does fail, the warning now names the real next step (`openclaw gateway install --force` after the update) instead of "Retry with the updated CLI", which was the CLI already running.

## Why This Change Was Made

The generated `dist/io.runtime.js` reader child touched `process.stdout` (which makes fd 1 non-blocking) and then wrote its result frame with `fs.writeFileSync(1, …)`. Once the frame exceeded the pipe buffer, the write threw `EAGAIN` mid-frame, the catch appended an error frame, and the parent could not parse either. The worker now writes the single frame through the stream, which queues and flushes before natural exit (the worker never calls `process.exit`).

Update behavior: the updater loads the candidate's alias after the package swap, so this takes effect for updates *to* a release containing it, including ones driven by beta.1/beta.2. The shipped beta.2 alias body hash is retained (with its published fixture) so it is still recognized during the upgrade window.

## Evidence

- New regression in `test/scripts/update-config-runtime-compat.test.ts`: generated alias under `OPENCLAW_UPDATE_IN_PROGRESS=1`, candidate returning ~1 MB; async (`readConfigFileSnapshot`, `createConfigIO`) and sync (`readCurrentConfigForPolicyCheck`, `loadConfig`) reads. Fails before the fix with `reader process exited with code 1 without a result`; passes after.
- `pnpm test test/scripts/update-config-runtime-compat.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 8.1s wall (4.2s Vitest). With `runtime-postbuild.test.ts`: 151 tests passed, 16.5s.
- Shipped beta.2 alias (from the npm tarball) reproduces the failure outside Vitest on macOS Node 26.9, macOS Bun 1.4.2, and Linux Node 24.21 (Docker); the fixed alias passes on all three. Not tested: Bun on Linux.
- oxfmt, oxlint, `format:docs:check`, `git diff --check` clean.

prs.title: fix(ui): session New window/New tab always fails with "Allow pop-ups" in the macOS app
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #144582

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users of the native macOS app choosing "New window" or "New tab" from the Control UI session tab menu would always see the toast "Allow pop-ups for this site, then try again." There is no way to allow pop-ups for the embedded WKWebView, so both actions were dead ends (the same actions work in a regular browser).

- **Related:** #144582 (labels: clawsweeper:queueable-fix, clawsweeper:fix-shape-clear, clawsweeper:source-repro).

## Why This Change Was Made

The web side reserves an inert `about:blank` popup via `window.open` and later redirects it to the session route. The macOS shell's `createWebViewWith` delegate classifies the `about:blank` request as ignorable and returns nil, so `window.open` returns null and the UI reports a blocked popup. The fix hands the final session URL to the existing native `openclawLink` bridge (already used by the Browser panel's external open) whenever that bridge is present, and keeps the previous `window.open` reservation as the browser fallback.

- **Intended outcome:** inside the macOS app, New window / New tab from the session menu hand the final session URL to the native link bridge instead of failing; no popup-blocked toast. The receiving default browser opens the Control UI session route; it needs its own gateway sign-in, so a previously paired browser renders the session directly while a never-paired browser lands on the Control UI login gate (an explicit sign-in surface) rather than the session.
- **Out of scope:** creating a native dashboard window/tab for the session (the shell has no such API today; whether to add one is flagged as a maintainer decision below); browser popup semantics are unchanged.
- **Highest-risk area:** routing the action through the native bridge hands a credential-free URL to the default browser, which does not inherit the app's WebKit credentials — a browser that never signed in to this gateway will not see the session.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** The native receiver already validates main-frame + trusted same-origin source before opening; the posted URL intentionally carries no credentials (Gateway credentials must not be exposed in URLs), and an unauthenticated receiving browser is stopped at the login gate, which the E2E now asserts explicitly. Without the bridge (regular browsers), or if the post throws, the previous flow including the blocked-popup toast is preserved and covered by tests.

## User Impact

macOS app users can open a session from the session menu's New window / New tab items again: the session route now opens through the native link handoff in the default browser instead of failing with an impossible "Allow pop-ups" instruction. The receiving browser must be signed in to the gateway itself: an unpaired browser reaches the Control UI login gate (explicit sign-in) rather than the session; a browser that has already paired renders the session directly. Regular browser behavior is unchanged.

- **Success criteria:** with the native link bridge present, both menu actions post the final same-origin session URL and never call `window.open`; without the bridge, the previous reservation + toast flow is kept. The posted URL grants nothing on its own: a never-paired receiving browser stops at the login gate without rendering the session.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `ui/src/lib/sessions/session-menu-navigation.ts` (bridge handoff placed before the popup reservation); regression fixtures in `session-menu-navigation.test.ts` ("hands … to the native shell link bridge instead of a blocked popup", "falls back to the browser popup when the native link bridge rejects the post"); the real-Gateway E2E in `ui/src/e2e/session-menu-native-bridge.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` (real Gateway + served Control UI + a page-level `openclawLink` bridge stand-in, covering both actions, the posted destination loaded verbatim in a paired isolated browser context, and the never-paired context stopping at the login gate).

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** Linux, Node 26, Playwright Chromium, a real Gateway child process built from this branch (`createOpenClawTestInstance`), and the Control UI served from this branch's source. The page-level `window.webkit.messageHandlers.openclawLink` bridge is installed through a browser init script before any page script runs — the same surface the macOS dashboard shell installs — and, like the native receiver, it does not open anything inside the source browser. The handoff destination is verified in isolated browser contexts that share no cookies, storage, or page state with the source page, modeling how an external default browser receives the `NSWorkspace.open` handoff: one context signs in to the gateway once through the Control UI's gateway confirmation surface (the analog of a previously paired default browser) and then navigates to the posted URL verbatim with no credential parameters appended; a second, never-paired context loads the same posted URL and must stop at the Control UI login gate. The macOS app itself is not runnable in this environment.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/session-menu-native-bridge.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/lib/sessions/session-menu-navigation.test.ts ui/src/app/native-link-routing.test.ts
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run test/vitest-ui-e2e-config.test.ts
  pnpm exec oxfmt --check ui/src/e2e/session-menu-native-bridge.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts
  pnpm exec oxlint ui/src/e2e/session-menu-native-bridge.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts
  node scripts/run-tsgo.mts -b test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.ui-e2e.json --builders 1
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:** real-Gateway E2E (`session-menu-native-bridge.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`, head `d626215`) output:
  ```text
  ✓ hands session New window and New tab to the native link bridge instead of a popup 28328ms
   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  1 passed (1)
  ```
  Both "New window" and "New tab" from the session menu post to the bridge:
  ```json
  [
    { "type": "open-link", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:<port>/chat/main/native-bridge-proof", "target": "external" },
    { "type": "open-link", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:<port>/chat/main/native-bridge-proof", "target": "external" }
  ]
  ```
  with zero `window.open` reservations from the menu code and no "Allow pop-ups" toast. The destination is then verified the way an external default browser receives it, in isolated contexts that share no state with the source page: the paired context first signs in once through the Control UI's gateway confirmation surface, then navigates to the exact posted URL verbatim — no `gatewayUrl` or token parameters appended — and renders the session's transcript, so the loaded session comes from the handed-off URL plus the receiving browser's own independent sign-in state. The never-paired context loads the same posted URL and stops at the `openclaw-login-gate` sign-in surface without ever rendering the session: the handoff grants nothing by itself, and an unauthenticated browser reaches an explicit sign-in flow instead of the session.
- **Observed result after fix:** with the `openclawLink` bridge present, `open-new-window`/`open-new-tab` hand the final same-origin session URL to the bridge and never touch `window.open`; the blocked-popup toast no longer fires. A receiving browser already signed in to the gateway renders the intended session from the posted URL; a never-paired receiving browser is stopped at the login gate. Without the bridge (regular browser), the previous reservation + fallback flow is preserved (covered by unit tests).
- **Before evidence:** with `session-menu-navigation.ts` restored to its pre-patch state (same worktree, patched E2E), the E2E fails — `AssertionError: expected undefined to deeply equal { type: 'open-link', …(2) }`, `Test Files 1 failed (1)` — the bridge never receives anything because every attempt goes through the `about:blank` popup reservation, matching the report (so the destination steps are never reached on unpatched code). At unit level the regression tests fail on main with `AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to be called … Number of calls: 0`.
- **What was not tested:** live macOS app / WKWebView runtime and the native Swift receiver (no macOS hardware in this environment); the native receiver path is unchanged and covered by existing native tests.
- **Proof tier:** L2 (real Gateway, real served Control UI, real browser; the WKWebView host bridge surface is installed at page level as the shell does, not mocked at module level; the handoff destination is verified in isolated browser contexts — one paired through the real sign-in surface, one never-paired — rather than a state-sharing same-browser tab).
- **Proof limitations:** no macOS environment available; the WKWebView message-handler transport and the Swift-side `NSWorkspace.open` handoff would need a reporter/maintainer repro on macOS. The bridge contract asserted in the E2E matches the existing native `DashboardWindowController.receiveLinkMessage` validation (main frame, trusted same-origin source, http(s) URL). The posted URL is credential-free by design: it grants session access only in a browser that already signed in to the gateway, and an unpaired browser lands on the login gate (now asserted explicitly). Whether the macOS session actions should instead open an app-owned authenticated destination (a new app window/tab that retains the app's WebKit credentials, as the ClawSweeper review recommends considering) is an open maintainer decision — this PR keeps the external-browser handoff and makes its sign-in requirement explicit and tested rather than building new native windowing unilaterally.
- **Review state:** Follow-up on the ClawSweeper review of `8d40173`: reworked the E2E destination step that previously appended `gatewayUrl` and token parameters before loading the posted URL (which overstated what an unpaired default browser receives) — the destination now signs in explicitly first and loads the posted URL verbatim, and a never-paired negative case asserts the login gate; the destination-access claim in this body is corrected accordingly. Rebased onto latest main (`d626215`). CI lanes pending on the updated head. Note: `checks-ui-e2e-real-gateway` previously failed on `quota-reset-status.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` ("expected 'Signed in' to be 'Ready'") — a main-level failure unrelated to this PR's files (the same test fails identically on other current PRs, e.g. #146400) and not chased here.

prs.title: refactor: render New Session with Solid
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Port New Session and its launch controls from Lit to Solid while preserving `/new`, deep links, host tags, CSS classes, selectors, placement, agent/workspace/template choices, draft recovery, attachments, and the single startup RPC. Solid owns the page, pickers, recovery views, palette controls, and composer. The Lit page class is removed; remaining Lit callers use the registered bridge. Domain owners remain synchronous plain TypeScript, and route/composer/attachment lazy boundaries remain intact.

The coupled group-defaults dialog consumes the shared Solid `PlaceBrowser`.
