prs.title: feat(control-ui): balance split panes, even splits by default, session-colour pane tint
prs.body:
Related: #144276

## What Problem This Solves

In the Control UI split view, opening a third or fourth pane leaves the layout uneven: each new split takes half of the pane it was opened from, so a row of four panes ends up as 50 / 25 / 12.5 / 12.5 and the only way to even them out is to drag every divider by hand. Panes also look identical apart from their titles, so with several sessions open side by side it is easy to type into the wrong one. Session colours exist in the sidebar but do not reach the panes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three small, related additions to the split view:

- **Balance panes**: a pane title-bar action, a layout menu entry and a shortcut (⌘⌥⇧B on macOS, Ctrl+Alt+Shift+B elsewhere, listed in the shortcut overview) that resets every column and every stacked pane to equal shares.
- **Even splits by default**: inserting a pane now redistributes its row or column evenly. A manual divider drag marks that container as custom, so later splits keep the user's proportions until Balance panes clears the flag. The two flags are persisted with the layout only when set, so existing stored layouts keep their shape.
- **Pane tint from the session colour**: the session colour already available in the sidebar is carried onto the pane cell as a 3 px top edge, a stronger tinted header and a faint wash on the pane surfaces (derived with `color-mix` from the theme variables, so it follows every theme). Panes without a colour are unchanged.

Non-goals: no new colour picker (it uses the existing session colour), no change to how many panes can be opened or to the divider drag itself. Only `locales/en.ts` carries the two new strings; the i18n sync tool asks for the other locales to be filled by the locale-refresh workflow after merge.

## User Impact

- One action or keystroke evens out any split layout instead of dragging each divider.
- New splits come out even by default; manual sizing is respected once the user has dragged a divider.
- Split panes are distinguishable at a glance by their session colour, on the transcript and composer surfaces as well as the header.
- Users who never assign session colours or resize panes see no change beyond the new menu entry and title-bar button.

## Evidence

- `pnpm tsgo:ui` clean; `pnpm lint` (oxlint core + extensions) passed; `oxfmt --check` clean on the changed files; `pnpm check:max-lines-ratchet` OK (`chat-page.ts` stays under the ratchet by moving the split actions into `chat-page-split-controls.ts`); `pnpm check:no-conflict-markers` clean.
- `pnpm format:docs:check` and `pnpm lint:docs` clean.
- Unit tests: `vitest run` on the split-layout, chat-page, keyboard-shortcut, app-shell and pane-header suites: 11 files, 157 tests passed. New cases cover even redistribution on insert, the custom-size flags surviving close and insert, `balanceLayout`, sparse persistence of the flags and the new shortcut catalog entry.
- Control UI startup budget: the first CI run measured 353124 B startup JS gzip for this branch, 17 B over the enforcement limit, because main had already consumed the 512 B growth allowance granted with the 2026-09-09 baseline. The branch itself adds about 200 B on the chat startup path (macOS comparison with `pnpm ui:check-performance:base`: main 353070 B, this branch 353270 B). The committed baseline is updated to the CI measurement with that explanation, as previous bumps did; the fixed 358400 B cap is unchanged.
- `pnpm ui:build` succeeds. The bundle has been in daily use as a locally served Control UI with four panes (two columns, stacked) across several themes: balance restores equal shares, new splits open even, and the tint follows the session colour on the header, transcript and composer.

## ClawSweeper Follow-Up (2026-09-11)

ClawSweeper's review (`needs-human`, all checks passing) flagged two correctness bugs, now fixed in a follow-up commit:

- **P1 — legacy layout sizing on load** (`split-layout-persistence.ts`): a layout saved before this PR has no `customColumnWeights`/`customPaneWeights` flag at all, and the loader was defaulting that to automatic sizing. A saved manual 30/70 split, split again, collapsed to even thirds instead of the expected 15/15/70. A missing flag on load is now interpreted as manual sizing (there is no way to positively distinguish "old save" from "explicitly automatic" once the flag is stripped from JSON, so defaulting to automatic silently discarded real user proportions). Fixed for both column layouts and stacked-pane layouts.
- **P2 — drop-indicator preview mismatch** (`split-layout.ts` / `split-drop-zone.ts`): `resolveDropIndicator` still derived the drag-and-drop preview rectangle from the old half-pane-split helper, while the actual insertion (this PR) redistributes the whole row/column. Dropping onto an edge of one of two equal columns actually creates three even columns, not a 50/50 split of the target pane, so the preview lied about where the pane would land. The preview is now computed from the same `insertPane` call the real drop uses, for both automatic and manually sized layouts.

Both are fixed with minimal, targeted changes; the balance/even-split/tint design is unchanged. Out of scope, left for a maintainer: the `config/control-ui-startup-budget-baseline.json` bump (unrelated policy call) and ClawSweeper's separate question about narrowing the whole-pane-tint surface.

New/updated tests: `split-layout.test.ts` (legacy column/stacked-pane migration, drop-preview/actual-insertion parity for automatic and manual sizing), plus round-trip assertions in `settings.layout.node.test.ts` and `chat-page.test.ts` updated to reflect the corrected legacy-load behavior. `pnpm tsgo:ui` and `pnpm tsgo:test:ui` clean; full `ui` vitest suite green (one pre-existing, unrelated flaky hover test in `board-view.browser.test.ts` passes on its own).

Visual proof: mocked Control UI dev server (`pnpm dev:ui:mock`) driven with Playwright, before (bug present) and after (fixed) screenshots — a legacy 30/70 layout split showing three even columns before the fix vs. 15/15/70 after, and a drop-preview on an evenly split pair showing a half-pane highlight before the fix vs. the correct ~1/3 highlight after. See `reports/pr-144562-clawsweeper-fix-2026-09-11/` in the OpenClaw workspace (not part of this repo) for the screenshots and exact pixel measurements.

Fixes an issue where users asking who sent an earlier group message would get an unknown-sender answer after OpenClaw reconstructed conversation history. Voice transcripts were particularly confusing: their text survived, but the model received only a generic `User` label.

prs.title: fix(async-work): release captured tracker after scope close
prs.body:
Related: #162318

## Summary
- make captured async-work trackers fall back to caller-owned execution once their captured scope begins closing
- prevent late cleanup callbacks from failing with `Async work scope is closed`
- add a focused regression test covering the closing-scope boundary

## Root cause
`captureAsyncWorkTracker()` captures an `AsyncWorkScope` by identity and later calls `scope.track(run)` unconditionally. Once that scope enters closing, late cleanup work can no longer be admitted to it and rejects with `Async work scope is closed`.

A captured tracker is specifically an ownership callback that can outlive its immediate caller, so once the captured owner is no longer able to accept work it should degrade to `runOutsideAsyncWorkScope` rather than reject the cleanup callback.

## Fix
The captured tracker now checks `scope.isClosing` before admission:
- open captured scope: preserve existing ownership/tracking
- closing or closed captured scope: execute outside that stale scope

This does not alter `trackAsyncWork` or `AsyncWorkScope.track()` semantics; direct admission to a closed scope remains rejected.

## Regression
The shared async-work test now verifies that a captured tracker invoked during scope close executes successfully without inheriting the closed scope or its abort signal.

This addresses the independent `Async work scope is closed` sub-defect documented in #162318; it does not claim to resolve the separate external AbortError root cause from that report.

No local test execution is claimed; CI is the validation source.

prs.title: fix(agents): reuse warm prefixes for single-chunk compaction
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes cold compaction requests when the same Anthropic Messages or OpenAI Responses route already has the conversation prefix cached. Eligible single-request summaries reuse the foreground system prompt, tool declarations, and verified native history. Invalid native summaries and genuinely changed history retain serialized fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

The embedded live scenario on the previous head completed with `paths=serialized usageRecords=1` and no cache read. A deterministic replay now drives two real embedded runs and on-demand manual compaction with mocked streams, large stable prefixes, and the same model alias and 512-token target budget.

The no-tool case captured 1 then 3 foreground messages. Prefix resolution successfully matched the 2-message summary source against the last 3-message request. A later core eligibility check then planned hypothetical safeguard chunks against the capped 512-token context and discarded the verified prefix. Core compaction actually emits one history-summary request. Removing that redundant check restores reuse without changing budgets, split-turn handling, or actual safeguard chunking.

The tool case captured 1, 3, 5, then 7 messages. Its 4-message summary source failed at assistant index 1: replay had normalized the tool-call ID from `read-1` to `read1`. Prefix resolution now reuses the captured foreground ID-normalization policy and replay tool allowlist. It first checks the original projection for same-attempt turns; either projection must match every dispatched message fingerprint exactly. No transcript fields are ignored, and no transcript bodies or executable tools are retained in the bounded session cache.

## User Impact

Matching routes can reuse warm prefixes during compaction without new configuration. Changed history, missing snapshots, split turns, actual multi-chunk summaries, and previous-summary redistillation retain fallback. Foreground tools are never executed by summarization. Native output must satisfy the existing summary heading contract; provider rejection or malformed output triggers serialization.

Per-request usage diagnostics now include a serialization reason: missing snapshot, history length, digest mismatch with index and role, changed route/source, missing heading contract, or rejected/failed prefix request. Exception text is excluded. Both completed requests are accounted for when a native response is rejected. See `docs/concepts/compaction.md`.

## Evidence

- 450 focused tests across seven files passed, including real embedded execution, core/session compaction, safeguard, format propagation, and hook/accounting behavior.
- Both full embedded regressions failed before the repairs and now require exactly one `foreground-prefix` request. Final assertions compare the entire native history prefix and tool declarations with the real foreground request.
- Fallback cases verify changed-history index/role diagnostics, overlong history, changed model, actual chunking, rejected native output, and a throwing prefix request.
- The live compaction fixture now requires a final `foreground-prefix` request and positive cache read, rather than passing on serialization alone.

Follow-up head: `69378adab6bfed3ad4152bc4f961d1dd950b9717`. `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passed, including production/test typechecks, lint, ownership/state guards, and zero runtime import cycles. Fresh P1 autoreview on the final diff is scoped-clean with no accepted/actionable findings. The five affected embedded/accounting cases also passed after moving usage collection into the existing diagnostics owner. Exact-head [CI run 34143177283](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34143177283) completed successfully. The canonical watcher exited 0 with `pending=0` and `GREEN` after reconciling six superseded checks; no workflow rerun was needed. The requested [ClawSweeper re-review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/141114#issuecomment-5573398520) was posted after pushing. No live provider calls were made for this follow-up. Mocked request reuse is proven; a warm live cache hit remains for the coordinator to verify. No OpenAI live result is claimed.

Coordinator rerun with provider credentials supplied through the existing live-test setup:

```sh
OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1 OPENCLAW_LIVE_CACHE_TEST=1 \
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.live.config.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner.cache.live.test.ts \
  -t 'preserves cache-safe shaping across compaction followup turns'
```

This PR remains open. No prepare or merge operation is requested.

prs.title: improve(skills): use low reasoning for weekly reviews
prs.body:
Closes #141005.

Related: #111943. Independent background model configuration remains a separate proposal.

## What Problem This Solves

Operators who use high reasoning for normal agent work also get that effort in the system-owned weekly Skill Workshop review. They cannot lower just the review through `cron edit`, and lowering the agent default affects unrelated work.

## Why This Change Was Made

Set `thinking: "low"` in the canonical weekly review task. The normal cron runner already owns effort selection, model capability handling, and execution; startup/config-reload reconciliation updates existing review jobs.

This is a default-policy proposal, not a new configuration surface. It follows the normal-cron architecture introduced in #136110.

## User Impact

Weekly reviews request low reasoning while retaining their normal model and fallback selection. Interactive work, ordinary cron tasks, and experience/history reviews keep their existing behavior. Scheduling, tools, delivery, and stored-data schemas are unchanged.

The fixed review policy also overrides a lower or disabled agent reasoning default. Maintainers should decide whether that policy is preferable to retaining inheritance pending #111943. Review quality and token savings have not been benchmarked.

## Evidence

The original focused proof below was recorded at `7b2d3d5cf38541531a2a27bd11c43d34a8b9df00`.

- Regression proof: removing the production line makes all three effort cases fail with inherited `off`, `high`, and `xhigh`. The existing-job reconciliation test also fails without the change.
- The final owner/sibling run passed **187 tests across five files**, covering weekly declarations, existing-job reconciliation, runtime effort forwarding, model/fallback selection, and ordinary cron behavior.
- The tests use isolated state and a mocked model runner. They do not execute a live review or edit an operator's skills.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/cron/isolated-agent/run.cron-model-override-forwarding.test.ts \
  src/cron/isolated-agent/run.cron-runtime-model-thinking.test.ts \
  src/cron/skill-collection-review-monitor.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server-cron-skill-review-jobs.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server-cron.test.ts
```

The complete `check:changed` gate passed for the four changed files, including core and test typechecking, lint, formatting, and repository guards. `git diff --check` passed. Fresh independent `autoreview` at P0–P2 completed with no actionable findings.


### CI refresh

`f10f5ad648a8ac1b7d32c2dcd81ecc5b8339f4ef` merges upstream main at `fd67ed8fbaff6c4d047e0a89c6e8267b1da65acc` to incorporate the existing update-finalization CI repair from #141137 and its subsequent upstream follow-up. This preserves the original contribution and branch history. The patch against the refreshed base remains exactly the same four-file change (stable patch ID `7b4feaad0b4c0873168ace5cb13f495787b0a264`); whitespace checks pass.

The original `checks-node-compact-small-31` failure was the existing update-finalization `phase-hang` process fixture: its prerequisite phase expired before the observed marker, and the test reached the 100-second deadlock guard. The original Workflow Sanity failure occurred while downloading a pinned action archive (HTTP 429), before actionlint started.

The refreshed [Workflow Sanity run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34140005897) passed actionlint. The exact-head [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34140005827) completed successfully, including [openclaw/ci-gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34140005827/job/101803308913). Final PR check readback: 163 passed, 43 skipped, no failures or pending checks.

- The repaired [Node shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34140005827/job/101799842615) passed all 14 update-finalization scenarios. The previously failing `phase-hang` case passed in 14.483 seconds; the containing CLI group passed 69 tests with 5 platform skips. These are observed hosted timings, not a controlled performance comparison.
- On the refreshed head, the same five focused cron/Gateway files passed again: **187 tests, 0 failures**, across two routed Vitest shards in 44.80 seconds.
- The complete four-file `check:changed` gate passed, including core and test typechecking, formatting, lint, dead-export scans, dependency/architecture guards, and storage/auth guards. `git diff --check` passed and the worktree is clean.
- Independent standards and spec reviews of the original fixed diff found no actionable implementation findings; the refreshed contribution retains that identical patch.

No live-model proof or cost/quality benchmark is claimed. Fresh and reconciled weekly jobs still need real-model execution evidence before claiming that proof gap is closed. The default-policy decision described above remains open.

prs.title: fix(compaction): keep history when summaries hit the output token limit
prs.body:
Closes #127987

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes conversations continuing with an incomplete summary when the summarizing model reaches its output token limit. Branch navigation could likewise save a truncated summary and switch branches.

## User Impact

Incomplete summaries no longer replace conversation context. Each default automatic compaction operation uses its existing single invalid-output retry; a second invalid summary fails without writing a compaction entry. Manual compaction stays one-shot. Failed branch summarization leaves session entries and the active leaf unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reject text-bearing `stopReason: "length"` output at the existing compaction and branch-summary owners. This reuses `InvalidSummaryOutputError` and its established automatic-compaction/overflow-recovery handling, without changing retry policy or how entries are stored.

Merged current main to resolve the conflicts. The distinct no-visible-text output-budget failure introduced by #160650 remains non-retryable: the new guard runs after that existing validation.

Thanks to @zhangguiping-xydt for the fix and @yetval for the report. The contributor's original commit is retained.

Maintainer intent: no overlap with Pash/Sarah changes on the affected files. #160650's empty-output behavior is preserved.

## Evidence

Production baseline: `0ac1c241fba8cb0e255a907e5f23e523ec579a43`. Candidate: `06aba7132b3c3e4ef65d86b394722b623f9c1957`.

Built both versions in a secretless Node 24 Docker container and exercised an isolated Gateway through the real `openclaw agent` CLI. Four synthetic history turns use a large-context mock model; switching the same session to a smaller-context model triggers required default compaction. The controlled OpenAI-compatible SSE provider returns nonempty summary text with either `finish_reason: "length"` or the normal `"stop"` control. Separate explicit profiles and isolated state/config/database paths were resolved and checked before each run.

Optional pre-compaction memory flushing was disabled to isolate one compaction operation. With it enabled, an earlier supplementary run exercised additional compaction operations and still wrote no truncated entry; the single-retry count below is per operation, not a new global retry cap.

| Scenario | Summary requests | Persisted compaction entries | CLI result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Baseline, nonempty truncated summary | 1 | 1, containing the truncated text | Success |
| Candidate, repeated truncated summary | 2 | 0; all preexisting transcript entries preserved | Visible failure |
| Baseline, normal summary | 1 | 1 | Success |
| Candidate, normal summary | 1 | 1, identical summary text | Success |

Candidate failure returned through the Gateway:

```text
Preflight compaction required but failed: Summarization failed: summary truncated at the output token limit
```

The owner-boundary regressions failed on baseline: automatic compaction accepted the first truncated summary instead of retrying, and branch navigation resolved with a truncated `branch_summary` instead of rejecting. Candidate suites passed **67 tests in 2 files**, including recovery after one invalid summary, failure after two, unchanged branch entries/leaf, cancellation, manual one-shot handling, and the unchanged empty-length output-budget path. Branch navigation was exercised through the real `AgentSession.navigateTree` API in the scoped suite, not a Gateway navigation endpoint.

Observed candidate test timings in the same secretless Docker container:

| Scoped suite | Passed | Vitest duration |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `src/agents/sessions/sdk.test.ts` | 38 | 8.99 s |
| `src/agents/sessions/agent-session-loop-correctness.test.ts` | 29 | 6.85 s |

The repository runner reported **31.85 s** for both shards, including compiler preparation and runner overhead. These are the measured correctness-run timings, not a separate one-worker performance benchmark.

No schema, persistence-format, provider-selection, or configuration-contract changes. No live provider credentials were used.

prs.title: fix(slack): cron command output renders italic subjects and loses angle-bracket text
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a cron job with a `command` payload announcing to a Slack channel would have its output rewritten by the outbound markdown pass: `*subject*` arrives in Slack as italic, and any angle-bracket text that is not a Slack token (a Python traceback's `in <module>`, a `<stdin>` filename) is preserved as a token and dropped by Slack. Operators who write their command output in Slack mrkdwn on purpose, with one star for bold and `<url|label>` links, cannot get it to the channel as written.

## Why This Change Was Made

Outbound delivery gains a `preRendered: "slack-mrkdwn"` formatting hint next to the existing `parseMode: "HTML"`. Cron delivery stamps it on `command` announces only; agent turns are the model's markdown and keep the pass. The Slack adapter maps the hint to its existing `textIsSlackMrkdwn` send option and, because the markdown pass no longer escapes for it, escapes `&`, `<` and `>` itself outside Slack's own `<url|label>`, `<@user>`, `<#channel|name>` and `<!here>` tokens, keeping entities the writer already wrote. Adapters for other channels ignore a hint that is not theirs. Failure alerts and agent-turn announces are unchanged.

## User Impact

Command output announced to Slack renders as the operator wrote it: bold subjects, working links, and stderr tails with their angle brackets intact. Nothing changes for Telegram, Discord or any other channel, nor for agent-turn announces on Slack.

## Evidence

Observed on a production gateway on 2026-09-06: every command-job announce in an ops channel rendered `_portfolio provenance_` (italic) for text authored as `*portfolio provenance*`, because the Slack plugin parses outbound text as CommonMark, where one star is emphasis.

Focused tests, all green in this branch:

- `extensions/slack/src/pre-rendered-text.test.ts`: the escape keeps links, mentions and existing entities, and does nothing without the hint.
- `extensions/slack/src/outbound-adapter.test.ts`: a pre-rendered send reaches `sendMessageSlack` verbatim with `textIsSlackMrkdwn: true`; a send without the hint keeps the markdown pass in charge.
- `src/cron/delivery.failure-notify.test.ts`: `sendCronAnnouncePayloadStrict` forwards the hint to delivery.
- `src/cron/delivery.test.ts`: `cronAnnounceFormatting` marks `command` only.

```
node_modules/.bin/vitest run extensions/slack/src/pre-rendered-text.test.ts extensions/slack/src/outbound-adapter.test.ts src/cron/delivery.failure-notify.test.ts src/cron/delivery.test.ts
 Test Files  4 passed (4)
      Tests  98 passed (98)
```

prs.title: perf(logging): keep routine egress and model activity at debug
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Routine successful egress requests, model responses taking at least one second, and tool catalog builds flood info logs. A busy Gateway observed 17,230 unsubstituted forwarding lines, 1,381 model-response lines, and 181 catalog summaries in its initial log window.

## User Impact

Routine forwarding without credential substitution, all successful model responses, and Code Mode/Tool Search catalog summaries now use debug. Refusals and credential substitutions stay at info; certificate warnings, transport failures, and non-2xx response visibility are preserved. Existing explicit model-transport debug flags still promote transport detail to info.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the slow-success promotion instead of adding sampling timers or another log path. Add bounded Prometheus counters for egress outcomes and catalog preparation so counting activity does not require verbose logs; existing model-call counters are unchanged. No hostname, tool-name, or request-content metric labels are added. Metric-only events are excluded from the bounded stability-history recorder. No config, permission, schema, or update migration changes.

Production LOC is **+56**: the requested independent egress/catalog counters did not exist, so their diagnostic event contracts, emissions, and exporter handling require growth. The log-level changes themselves remove the obsolete latency threshold. No cache or parallel implementation is introduced.

## Evidence

Synthetic Linux sandbox on a 128-core host, restricted to CPUs 64–127 and 64 GiB, Node 26.8.2. Five alternating before/after runs of 100 modeled minutes after 10 warmup blocks. Each block replays 475 ordinary forwards, 5 substitutions, 2 refusals, 1 certificate warning, 38 slow successful model responses, 1 non-2xx response, and 5 catalog builds. The harness extracts the actual producer branches from each revision and runs them through the real subsystem/file logger; it measures logging work, not end-to-end Gateway or network performance.

| Measurement | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Info file lines / modeled minute | 527 | 9 |
| Producer current-thread CPU / modeled minute (median) | 4.26 ms | 0.625 ms |
| Current-thread CPU including file-queue drain / modeled minute (median) | 5.10 ms | 1.20 ms |

That is **98.3% fewer info lines** and **76.4% less logging/diagnostic CPU** in this workload. Each block drains the bounded log queue and asserts the exact line count; an initial undrained stress run hit the queue cap and was discarded. A debug-level control retains all 527 lines before and after (CPU including drain: 5.06 → 5.89 ms per modeled minute, reflecting the additional metric work). The after runs counted all 48,300 egress events and 500 catalog events independently of verbosity. No production state was accessed or copied.

Local proof:

- Changed-file oxfmt and repository syntax lint passed. Typed lint attempted SDK declaration preparation and timed out after 300 seconds on the saturated host; full typed gates belong to PR CI.
- `pnpm test src/secrets/egress-proxy/runtime.test.ts src/agents/model-transport-debug.test.ts extensions/diagnostics-prometheus/src/service.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-client-tools.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 54 tests passed. Cold wall time 330.57 s, dominated by 268.53 s embedded-runner compilation. Egress file 10.47 s; model logging file 15.98 s; Prometheus file 8.11 s. Test bodies remained short.
- After moving counter handling into the existing operation-metrics helper, Prometheus tests passed again: 20 tests, 5.00 s file duration / 9.76 s wall.
- Independent autoreview: clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings, including a fresh pass on the final layout.
- The extra local import-closure/test-plan invocation was stopped when it became an expensive inventory run (the test-plan file reported 116 passing cases before shutdown; the overall invocation was cancelled). Complete guards, typecheck, sibling suites, and e2e belong to PR CI. No Testbox/Crabbox leases were allocated.

CI follow-up: the first run caught the new event variants missing from the stability recorder’s exhaustive switch, plus missing mock-isolation annotations in the new fixture. Both are corrected; the expanded projection regression was moved to a small sibling test file to keep the existing file under its line cap. The 23 recorder tests pass locally after the split (7.92 s wall). The same run also encountered `src/plugins/git-install.test.ts` → `falls back to the OpenClaw temp root when target workspace creation fails` (`result.ok` false at line 591). This reproduces exactly on unchanged main `fd80f72fa0cba77784b759cc9533048fb48a9b4d`: `pnpm test src/plugins/git-install.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` fails the same assertion, with 19 sibling cases passing (76.74 s wall). The lane branch was restored afterward; no plugin-install files are changed.


## Pre-rebase CI and attribution history

Exact head: `c31d73a7edccd9fe214754bc244b1cbce9ea80ee`; [CI run 38335117752](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38335117752). Production/test typechecks, lint, architecture/source-closure guards, ratchets, affected tests, and security review passed. Independent final-head source review also reported no actionable findings. CI is **not green**; these test jobs failed:

- `checks-node-changed-compact-small-6`: the plugin-install temp-root fallback assertion described above reproduces on unchanged main, with 19 sibling cases passing.
- `checks-ui-e2e (8/9)`: `update-run.e2e.test.ts` times out at line 225 awaiting the successful update headline. The identical test, locator, line, and timeout failed in [scheduled main run 38334375513, job 115091146620](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38334375513/job/115091146620), on `d6b01a200752e8f121bc21263c6563bee058b1b4`.
- `checks-ui-e2e (1/9)`: the archive-refresh case observes a restore request when expecting an archive request; the Unicode session case hits two exact `Refresh` buttons. These mocked-Gateway tests, their helpers, and all UI source are unchanged between the PR and that main revision. However, the same cases passed in its scheduled CI, and focused unchanged-main replays passed all 13 cases in both source-server and authentic compiled-main-artifact modes (74.05 s and 59.28 s). Those passing replays do **not** establish failing-baseline proof. A later [scheduled main run 38339144048, job 115106092089](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38339144048/job/115106092089) failed the same ambiguous Refresh locator in another parameter row of the unchanged Unicode test. The archive failure still lacks matching baseline proof. No CI rerun, assertion weakening, or unrelated UI change was used.

The benchmark sandbox and its synthetic state have been removed. No production Gateway or database was touched.


## Requested rebase validation

Rebased onto main `33a438a7624d37828e3e75973939d94a5c6153e5`; new head `6466d6e3176a138113b52f1fb8615c15785332c2`. Resolved one conflict by retaining main's default handling for events excluded from the stability-recorder subscription and adding only the two metric-event exclusions. No unrelated commits or files were copied into the lane. The logging benchmark remains valid because the producer-level changes are unchanged.

The two recorder files pass all 23 tests again (7.55 s wall); changed-file formatting and focused repository syntax lint pass. A fresh independent review of the conflict resolution is clean with no actionable P0–P2 findings. [Exact-head CI run 38344811561](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38344811561) finished: all functional jobs, all nine browser shards, production types, lint, source/architecture guards, ratchets, and security review passed. The only failed substantive job is `check-test-types-core-4` ([job 115124359568](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38344811561/job/115124359568)); aggregate CI gates are consequently red.

This remaining error is inherited from main commit [33a438a7624d](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/33a438a7624d37828e3e75973939d94a5c6153e5): it made `readConfigPreflightSnapshot` private without updating the unchanged test import. CI reports TS2724 at `src/commands/config-preflight-snapshot.test.ts:41`. Both that test and its producer are byte-identical to the unchanged main revision, outside this lane's diff.

Baseline proof on that unchanged main revision: `pnpm test src/commands/config-preflight-snapshot.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'preserves pending-plugin inputs'` fails at line 489 with `readConfigPreflightSnapshot is not a function` (one failed, 18 intentionally unselected, 50.49 s wall). The lane was restored afterward. An initial full-title filter skipped the case and is excluded from proof. Landing uses the operator-authorized inherited-failure exception; CI is not represented as fully green and was not rerun to chase green.

Closes #158165

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: with exec approvals in `allowlist` mode and `autoAllowSkills: true`, an agent whose commands run on the Gateway host is still denied (`exec denied: allowlist miss`) the binaries its own workspace skills declare in `requires.bins`. `autoAllowSkills` only took effect on node hosts.

## User Impact

User impact: Gateway-hosted agents (containers, servers, most self-hosted setups) can use `allowlist` mode with `autoAllowSkills` and have the binaries of their eligible skills allowed, without a hand-kept allowlist that duplicates skill metadata. Binaries of disabled or otherwise ineligible skills, and binaries no skill declares, stay denied. With `autoAllowSkills` off (the default), nothing changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The gateway exec host evaluated the allowlist without skill bins, while the node host passes them (`skills.bins`). When the agent's effective approvals enable `autoAllowSkills`, the gateway host now trusts only the bins declared by **the executing agent's eligible skills**: the set its prompt sees (`resolveWorkspaceSkillPromptEntries`: enabled, allowed by the bundled-skills allowlist and the agent's skill filter, requirements met). It never trusts every installed skill, so a disabled bundled skill cannot grant execution trust. Those bins go to the same allowlist evaluation the node host uses. This is the agent-scoped option recommended in the issue review. Bins are resolved on the same `PATH` the command resolves on: the Gateway's `PATH` plus operator `tools.exec.pathPrepend`. Host exec already rejects a requested `PATH` (`Custom 'PATH' variable is forbidden during host execution`), so a tool call cannot point a skill bin name at another binary; a test pins that invariant. The evaluation moves into a sibling module, so the already-over-cap gateway host file shrinks.

## Evidence

**Real Gateway, allowlist mode, before and after.** Same script for both: a fresh state dir; approvals `agents.main = { autoAllowSkills: true, allowlist: [] }`; two workspace skills, `skill-tool` (requires `skill-tool`) and `disabled-skill` (requires `disabled-tool`, with `skills.entries.disabled-skill.enabled: false`); the three executables on the Gateway's `PATH`; `openclaw gateway run`; then one `openclaw agent` turn per command. The model is a scripted local OpenAI-compatible stub (deterministic, no keys) that asks the `exec` tool to run one command and replies with the result.

```
===== BEFORE (published 2026.9.5 image)
[before] OpenClaw 2026.9.5 (ec9c1a1)
[before] approvals main: {"autoAllowSkills":true,"allowlist":[]}
[before] agent turn: the model asks exec to run: skill-tool
[before]   reply:   "error": "exec denied: allowlist miss"
[before] agent turn: the model asks exec to run: disabled-tool
[before]   reply:   "error": "exec denied: allowlist miss"
[before] agent turn: the model asks exec to run: other-tool
[before]   reply:   "error": "exec denied: allowlist miss"

===== AFTER (this PR, built from 659b5e30dc)
[after] OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (659b5e3)
[after] approvals main: {"autoAllowSkills":true,"allowlist":[]}
[after] agent turn: the model asks exec to run: skill-tool
[after]   reply: exec returned: skill-tool ran
[after] agent turn: the model asks exec to run: disabled-tool
[after]   reply:   "error": "exec denied: allowlist miss"
[after] agent turn: the model asks exec to run: other-tool
[after]   reply:   "error": "exec denied: allowlist miss"
```

Eligibility is OpenClaw's own: when the executables sit only in a `tools.exec.pathPrepend` directory, `openclaw skills check` lists `skill-tool (bins: skill-tool)` under missing requirements, so the skill is not in the agent's prompt and its bin is not trusted either. The trusted set always matches what the model is shown.

**Tests and checks**

- New `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.auto-allow-skills.test.ts` (real exec tool, gateway host, allowlist mode): an eligible skill's bin runs with `autoAllowSkills` on; denied with it off; **a bin only a disabled skill declares stays denied**; a bin no skill declares stays denied; a requested `PATH` reaching a planted skill-named binary is refused. The eligible-skill test fails with the source change removed (1 failed / 4 passed). The disabled-skill test fails against an earlier revision of this PR that collected bins from every installed skill, and passes now.
- `pnpm vitest run` over the gateway exec host, exec run, and exec allowlist test files: 7 files, 218 passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test`: clean.
- `pnpm check:changed`: all steps pass (including the line-cap ratchet) except `core tsgo graph boundary` ("agents-root: 721 test roots exceeds the advisory 720 limit"), which reports the same 721 on a clean checkout of main and is unrelated to this change.


---

## Authority-chain proof (revision 3)

Addresses the P1 finding: the resolver reloaded eligible skills from agent config
alone, ignoring the admitted session's narrowing.

Driven through the real gateway exec path — real skill loader, real PATH
resolution, real process supervisor, nothing mocked. The skill's declared bin
appends to a marker file, so a denial is observable as the absence of any I/O
rather than only as a returned error.

**Before (`659b5e30dc3`, the previously reviewed head)**

```
[1] baseline: skill eligible for the run
    outcome: status=completed exitCode=0        marker: I/O HAPPENED (1 run)
[2] session filter excludes the declaring skill
    outcome: status=completed exitCode=0        marker: I/O HAPPENED (1 run)
[3] session override turns the declaring skill off
    outcome: status=completed exitCode=0        marker: I/O HAPPENED (1 run)
[4] bin repointed after authorization, before launch
    outcome: allowed                            marker: no I/O
```

A session-excluded skill's binary reached process launch and executed.

**After (this revision)**

```
[1] baseline: skill eligible for the run
    outcome: status=completed exitCode=0        marker: I/O HAPPENED (1 run)
[2] session filter excludes the declaring skill
    outcome: DENIED: exec denied: allowlist miss        marker: no I/O
[3] session override turns the declaring skill off
    outcome: DENIED: exec denied: allowlist miss        marker: no I/O
[4] bin repointed after authorization, before launch
    authorized: deniedResult=no, revalidateBeforeExecution=function
    outcome: DENIED at spawn boundary:
      Exec denied (SYSTEM_RUN_DENIED: skill bin authorization changed
      before execution): probe-tool                    marker: no I/O
```

Case [4] covers the revocation-before-launch request. The approvals file records
the `autoAllowSkills` flag but never the executable a skill authorized, so the
committed-policy recheck cannot see that binary change while approval settles;
the bins are re-resolved at the spawn boundary instead. The trust comparison is
now shared with the allowlist evaluator (`isSegmentAuthorizedBySkillBins`) so the
granting and revalidating checks cannot drift.

Scope note: the recheck observes executable identity and the admitted scope. A
skill's on-disk source changing mid-run is picked up by the skills watcher's
version bump, not by this path.

Regression coverage added in
`src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.auto-allow-skills.test.ts`: session
filter exclusion, session override exclusion, the allowed case under an
including filter, and spawn-boundary denial on a swapped bin.


### Detached approval launch (revision 5)

Addresses the follow-on P1: the detached launch kept its own spawn gate that
rechecked only cwd and mutable-operand drift, so `revalidateBeforeExecution` —
which carries the skill check — was never consulted on that path.

All five gateway launch paths now recheck skill authority at their spawn
boundary: inline ask, ask-fallback, auto-review allow-once, detached approval,
and the direct allowlist path. The check is split into a reason-returning
resolver and the result-returning wrapper the inline paths use, so both call
shapes share one implementation.

Regression test `revalidates skill authority in the detached approval launch`
drives `ask: "always"` with a backgrounded approval, has the launch adapter
invoke `beforeSpawn` as the real runtime does, and asserts the follow-up reports
the denial and that spawn is never reached. Reverting only the `beforeSpawn`
change flips it to the bypass, which is the reported defect:

```
with the fix:      DENIED ... skill bin authorization changed before execution
without the fix:   Exec finished (gateway id=req-1, sess...)   <- launched and ran
```

`pnpm tsgo:core` clean; 137 passed across the two gateway exec test files, 907
across the exec-approvals and bash-tools exec suites.



### Rebased onto main (revision 6)

Rebased onto current main. Two things on main changed what this PR has to cover.

**A sixth launch path.** Main added a gateway launch path: a cron occurrence that consumes a standing grant. It rechecked only the grant, so a segment admitted on skill-bin trust could launch after that trust was withdrawn. It now rechecks skill authority **before the grant is consumed**, so a withdrawn skill denies the launch without spending the grant. All six launch paths now recheck at their spawn boundary: inline ask, ask-fallback, auto-review allow-once, detached approval, the direct allowlist path, and cron standing grants. New regression test: `rechecks skill authority before spending a standing grant` in `bash-tools.exec-cron-grant.test.ts`. It fails without the recheck.

**The line-cap ratchet now runs on pull requests.** The gateway host, its unit test and the infra allowlist evaluator stay at or below their size on main:

- The spawn-boundary rechecks (approval-binding drift, the denial result, chaining, the skill-authority recheck) moved to `bash-tools.exec-host-gateway-revalidation.ts`.
- Skill-bin trust matching moved to `infra/exec-approvals-skill-bins.ts`, re-exported through `exec-approvals`.

**Detached approval proof, without mocks.** The revision-5 test `revalidates skill authority in the detached approval launch` mocked the launch adapter. It is replaced by `detached approval launch …` in `bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.auto-allow-skills.test.ts`, which runs the real approval, launch adapter and spawn boundary. The command launches while skill trust holds, and is denied before spawn once the authorizing skill is uninstalled while approval is pending. The denial case fails without the detached-launch fix.

`docs/tools/exec-approvals.md` now says the recheck covers every gateway launch path.

Checks: `pnpm tsgo:core` and the changed test files typecheck clean. The autoAllowSkills suite, the gateway exec host tests, the cron-grant tests, `exec-approvals` and the node-host allowlist tests pass. The line-cap, mock-exports and import-cycle checks pass. The one red CI job on this head, `checks-node-changed`, fails only in `src/gateway/x-publication-owner-composition.e2e.test.ts` (404 vs 200), an X-publication route this PR doesn't touch. The exec e2e tests in the same job pass.


### Final-initiation recheck (revision 7)

**What was wrong.** The skill-authority recheck ran once, before launch preparation. The launch could then still await four things before the native spawn: standing-grant consumption (cron), secret-egress registration, the supervisor scope fence, and adapter preparation. The synchronous guards at the end of `runExecProcess` checked only source, operator and committed-policy/grant authority. So a skill uninstalled, or a bin repointed, during one of those waits still let the pinned command launch.

**What changed.**

- Each async re-resolution (`verifyGatewaySkillBinAuthority` in `bash-tools.exec-host-gateway-allowlist.ts`) now returns the authority it verified, and the recheck holds it. That held authority is the skill source revision (`getSkillsSourceVersion`, read before discovery), the bins that authorized the command, and the PATH they resolve on.
- A new synchronous check, `findStaleHeldGatewaySkillBinSegment`, rechecks that held authority. It denies in three cases: nothing was verified, the skill source revision moved (a skill was installed, removed or reconfigured), or an authorizing bin now resolves to a different executable. It uses the same `isSegmentAuthorizedBySkillBins` comparison as allowlist evaluation, so the single shared implementation is kept.
- `createGatewaySkillBinAuthorityRecheck` (in `bash-tools.exec-host-gateway-revalidation.ts`) exposes that check as `assertSkillBinAuthorityCurrent`. The gateway composes it into the `assertCurrent` it hands to the runtime: the committed-authorization assertion for the inline paths and detached approval, and the grant's assertion for cron standing grants.

**Where it runs.** `runExecProcess` passes that `assertCurrent` to the supervisor as `beforeSpawn`. It also wraps it into `initiateSpawn` (`createExecLaunchLifecycle().wrap`), which calls it synchronously right before `launch()`. No await sits between the check and the native spawn. All six launch paths go through it: inline ask, ask-fallback, auto-review allow-once, detached approval, direct allowlist, and cron standing grant. A refusal at initiation throws `GatewaySkillBinAuthorityWithdrawnError`, an `ExecProcessPreflightError`. The exec tool unwraps it into the usual denial result, and a detached launch reports it in its follow-up. On the cron path the grant has already been consumed when this final check refuses. That matches how the other final-initiation refusals already behave there.

**Regression tests.**

- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.skill-initiation.test.ts`, new. It runs the real gateway authorization, `runExecProcess`, supervisor, child adapter and native launch. The skill bin is a copy of `touch` that writes a marker file. Trust is withdrawn inside the secret-egress registration await, after the spawn preflight has passed. That is the only seam: the registry is wrapped through `importOriginal`.
  - `launches the skill bin while skill trust holds through initiation` is the allowed control. The marker is written.
  - `denies at native initiation when the authorizing skill is uninstalled after preflight`
  - `denies at native initiation when the trusted bin name is repointed after preflight`
- `detached approval launch denies at native initiation when trust is withdrawn after preflight`, in `bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.auto-allow-skills.test.ts`. The supervisor stand-in uninstalls the skill and then calls the real `initiateSpawn` hook. The launch callback is never invoked, and the follow-up carries the skill denial.

With the fix (3 + 12 tests across the two files, all pass):

```
✓ launches the skill bin while skill trust holds through initiation
✓ denies at native initiation when the authorizing skill is uninstalled after preflight
✓ denies at native initiation when the trusted bin name is repointed after preflight
✓ detached approval launch denies at native initiation when trust is withdrawn after preflight
```

Without the fix (the three source files reverted, tests kept), the withdrawn command launches and runs:

```
× denies at native initiation when the authorizing skill is uninstalled after preflight
  → expected { status: 'completed', …(7) } to be undefined   (exitCode 0, exitReason "exit")
× denies at native initiation when the trusted bin name is repointed after preflight
  → expected { status: 'completed', …(7) } to be undefined   (exitCode 0, exitReason "exit")
× detached approval launch denies at native initiation when trust is withdrawn after preflight
  → Received: "Exec denied (gateway id=…, spawn-failed): skill-tool"   (initiation was not refused)
```

Checks: `pnpm tsgo:core` and the core test typecheck are clean. oxfmt and scoped core oxlint pass on the changed files. `check:changed` passes the line-cap growth ratchet, the max-lines suppression ratchet, the first-party mock export ratchet, the SQLite worker ratchet and format; the import-cycle check (0 cycles) and the remaining lint guards were run separately and pass. Its one failure is the dead-export scan, on `extensions/voice-call/src/types.ts: CallBrief`, which this PR doesn't touch. The gateway exec host tests and the cron-grant suite pass, with one exception. Locally, `executes a cron occurrence via a standing grant without prompting` fails with `service child cleanup identity lost`, and it fails the same way on the unmodified revision-6 head. It passed in CI on that head, so it is a local process-tree environment issue.

Not included yet: real-Gateway traces of delayed detached and standing-grant launches, with an allowed and a withdrawn-trust case. They are pending maintainer acceptance of the Gateway `autoAllowSkills` scope.



### Executing-agent skill ownership and real Gateway traces (revision 8)

Head: `0a4297accba` (one commit on top of `e0e151ea91b`; no rebase, the branch merges cleanly with main).

**What was wrong.** Tool assembly can borrow another agent's tool policy. `agent-tools.ts` then has two ids: `agentId`, the policy owner from the capability profile (`options.policyAgentId`, or the profile a caller passes in), and `executionAgentId`, the agent that actually runs (`options.agentId`, or the agent of `runSessionKey`). Exec defaults received only `agentId`, and `resolveGatewaySkillBins` used it. So under a borrowed policy, `autoAllowSkills` loaded the **policy** agent's workspace, while the run's skill snapshot (`skillScope`) came from the executing agent. A bin declared only by the policy agent's skill was trusted, and a bin declared by the executing agent's own skill was not.

**What changed.**

- `ExecSkillScope` gains `ownerAgentId`. `agent-tools.ts` now always sets `skillScope.ownerAgentId = executionAgentId`, next to the session filter and overrides from the same run's snapshot. Before, the scope was only set when a snapshot existed.
- `resolveGatewaySkillBins` (`bash-tools.exec-host-gateway-allowlist.ts`) resolves the workspace and the eligible skills from `skillScope.ownerAgentId`. It falls back to `agentId` only for callers that don't separate the two. That one resolver feeds all three skill checks: allowlist evaluation, the async re-resolution in `verifyGatewaySkillBinAuthority`, and the authority it holds. The held authority records that agent's `workspaceDir` and skill source revision, so the synchronous `findStaleHeldGatewaySkillBinSegment` check at native initiation watches the executing agent's skills. No await was added before the spawn.
- Approval policy is unchanged and stays with `agentId`. That covers the approvals-file entry, the `autoAllowSkills` flag, ask/security, and the cron standing-grant source match.
- Node host, for comparison: `skills.bins` returns the union of bins across **every** configured agent (`agentSkillFilter: "ignore"`), so the node has no per-agent owner to disagree with. The gateway stays narrower: only the executing agent's skills that its run admitted.
- The skill owner is carried inside the existing `skillScope` instead of as a new top-level exec option. This keeps `bash-tools.exec-run.ts` at the line cap: a top-level field would have taken it from 700 to 701 counted lines.

**Regression tests.**

- New: `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.skill-owner.test.ts`. It has no mocks. It assembles exec through `createOpenClawCodingTools` with `agentId: "execution"`, `policyAgentId: "main"` and `runSessionKey: "agent:execution:main"`, the same borrow shape as the gateway-tool assembly test. Then it calls the real exec tool, which runs the gateway authorization, supervisor and native launch. The approvals entry exists only for `main`. Each agent's workspace has one skill: `main` declares `policy-tool`, `execution` declares `exec-tool`. Both bins are copies of `touch`.
  - `runs a bin declared by the executing agent's own skill`: the marker is written.
  - `denies a bin declared only by the policy agent's skill, with no I/O`: `exec denied: allowlist miss`, and there is no marker.
- `bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.skill-initiation.test.ts` (real native path) adds a borrowed-policy variant. The allowed control runs as `execution` under `main`'s policy. `denies at native initiation when the executing agent's skill is uninstalled under a borrowed policy after preflight` uninstalls the skill during the post-preflight await. The denial comes from the synchronous initiation check against the executing agent's held authority.

With the fix:

```
✓ skill-owner      > runs a bin declared by the executing agent's own skill
✓ skill-owner      > denies a bin declared only by the policy agent's skill, with no I/O
✓ skill-initiation > launches the skill bin while skill trust holds through initiation (borrowed policy: true)
✓ skill-initiation > denies at native initiation when the executing agent's skill is uninstalled under a borrowed policy after preflight
```

Without the fix (`agent-tools.ts`, `bash-tools.exec-host-gateway-allowlist.ts` and `bash-tools.exec-types.ts` reverted, tests kept), the policy agent's bin runs and the executing agent's own bin is refused:

```
× denies a bin declared only by the policy agent's skill, with no I/O
  - "denied": "Error: exec denied: allowlist miss",  "ran": false
  + "details": { "status": "completed", "exitCode": 0, "exitReason": "exit", … },  "ran": true
× runs a bin declared by the executing agent's own skill
  - "details": { "status": "completed", "exitCode": 0 },  "ran": true
  + "ran": false
× launches the skill bin while skill trust holds through initiation (borrowed policy: true)
  → exec denied: allowlist miss
× denies at native initiation when the executing agent's skill is uninstalled under a borrowed policy after preflight
  → exec denied: allowlist miss
```

The three non-borrowed `skill-initiation` cases pass both with and without the fix.

**Correction to the cron standing-grant wording (revision 6).** Revision 6 said the cron recheck means "a withdrawn skill denies the launch without spending the grant". That is too broad. The skill recheck applies only to segments the occurrence's own preflight admitted on **skill trust**. A command the operator explicitly allow-always granted runs on that grant, whether or not a skill still declares its bins. The grant was minted for the exact operation (command, cwd, env), so it authorizes the command independently of skill trust. Grant consumption in detail:

- **Not consumed:** the occurrence's preflight admitted a segment on skill trust, and the async recheck before consumption finds that trust withdrawn. The launch is denied and `useCount` is unchanged.
- **Consumed, then denied:** trust is withdrawn after consumption but before native initiation. The synchronous initiation check refuses the launch, and the use is already spent (as revision 7 noted).
- **Consumed, launched:** the skill is withdrawn before the occurrence starts. Its preflight then admits nothing on skill trust, the grant covers the whole command, and the occurrence runs on the grant. This is `occ3` below.
- **Grant not used at all:** every segment is admitted on skill or allowlist trust, so nothing asks. The command runs directly and the grant is neither checked nor consumed.

**Real Gateway traces on this head** (`OpenClaw 2026.9.8 (0a4297a)`, built from a clean detached checkout of this commit). The harness is the same as described before: an isolated state dir and HOME, `openclaw gateway run` on loopback with token auth, a scripted local OpenAI-compatible stub model (no keys), and one connected client with the `approvals` capability. Decisions are made with `openclaw approvals resolve`. Bins are native copies of `touch`, so a launch leaves a marker file. Nothing in the Gateway is mocked. The config now has two agents (`agents.ownership: "explicit"`): `main` with workspace skill `skill-tool`, and `ops` with its own workspace and skill `ops-tool`.

```
[D1] approvals main: {"security":"allowlist","ask":"always","autoAllowSkills":true,"allowlist":[]}
[D1] agent turn (source channel: webhook) -> model asks exec to run: skill-tool skill-effect.marker
[D1] approval requested: id=403cf70e…  tool result returned to the model: approval-pending (run continues)
[D1] skill trust left in place while the approval is pending
[D1] operator: openclaw approvals resolve 403cf70e… allow-once -> resolved allow-once by runtime:cli.
[D1] detached follow-up delivered to the session: Exec finished (gateway id=403cf70e-…, code 0)
[D1] marker: I/O HAPPENED (skill-effect.marker created)

[D2] agent turn (source channel: webhook) -> model asks exec to run: skill-tool skill-effect.marker
[D2] approval requested: id=c1a551df…  tool result returned to the model: approval-pending (run continues)
[D2] WITHDRAW: skill-tool skill uninstalled while the approval is pending (after preflight)
[D2] operator: openclaw approvals resolve c1a551df… allow-once -> resolved allow-once by runtime:cli.
[D2] detached follow-up delivered to the session: SYSTEM_RUN_DENIED: skill bin authorization changed before execution

[X-own]   no approval prompt
[X-own]   marker: I/O HAPPENED (own-effect.marker created)

[X-other] skill-tool is declared only by agent main's workspace skill
[X-other] agent ops turn (source channel: webhook) -> model asks exec to run: skill-tool other-effect.marker
[X-other] approval requested: id=1ebabf77… (not skill-trusted for agent ops: allowlist miss)
[X-other] operator: openclaw approvals resolve 1ebabf77… deny -> resolved deny by runtime:cli.
[X-other] model saw: … Exec denied (gateway id=1ebabf77-…, user-denied): skill-tool other-effect.marker
[X-other] marker: no I/O (no marker file)

[X-main]  agent main turn (source channel: webhook) -> model asks exec to run: skill-tool other-effect.marker
[X-main]  no approval prompt
[X-main]  marker: I/O HAPPENED (other-effect.marker created)
```

```
[C] approvals main: {"security":"allowlist","ask":"on-miss","autoAllowSkills":true,"allowlist":[]}
[C] workspace skill marker-skill declares bin: touch (/usr/bin/touch); mkdir is declared by no skill
[C] cron job 7cdb367e… (isolated agent turn) -> model asks exec to run: touch skill-effect.marker && mkdir other-effect.marker
[C/occ1-mint] approval requested: id=32e21217… (cron approval delivered to the approval surface)
[C/occ1-mint] operator: openclaw approvals resolve 32e21217… allow-always -> resolved allow-always by runtime:cli.
[C/occ1-mint] marker: I/O HAPPENED (other-effect.marker,skill-effect.marker)   grant 6d8a8412… uses=0 revoked=false
[C/occ2-held] no approval prompt (standing grant)
[C/occ2-held] marker: I/O HAPPENED (other-effect.marker,skill-effect.marker)   grant 6d8a8412… uses=1 revoked=false
[C/occ3-withdrawn] WITHDRAW: marker-skill uninstalled after the grant was minted, before this occurrence
[C/occ3-withdrawn] marker: I/O HAPPENED (other-effect.marker,skill-effect.marker)   grant 6d8a8412… uses=2 revoked=false
```

`occ3` is the "consumed, launched" case above. The operator's allow-always grant authorizes the exact command, so the occurrence runs and spends one use (`uses` 1 → 2) after the skill is gone.

**About the cross-agent trace.** The X cases are two agents, each running as itself. They show that a real Gateway takes skill trust from the running agent's own workspace: `ops` runs its own bin without a prompt, but `main`'s bin is an allowlist miss for `ops`, while `main` itself runs that bin without a prompt. They are **not** a borrowed-policy run. In this tree an embedded run's policy owner differs from its executing agent only when the run carries `sandboxAgentId` (`RunEmbeddedAgentParams`), or when a harness passes `policyAgentId` (worker-environment placement, the Copilot and Agents API harnesses, all from that same run parameter). No Gateway RPC, CLI flag or config key sets it. The only shipped producers are compaction and the CLI-backend runner's rooted-execution preparation, and neither can be driven with a stub model. So the borrowed-policy proof is the native `skill-owner` and `skill-initiation` tests above. D3 (repoint while pending) was not re-run on this head, so it is not repeated here.

| File | Result | Wall | Vitest duration |

The one local failure is still `executes a cron occurrence via a standing grant without prompting` (`service child cleanup identity lost`), the local process-tree issue noted in revisions 6 and 7. The real Gateway runs the same standing-grant occurrence successfully (`occ2` above).

Checks: `pnpm tsgo:core` passes, and so does the core test typecheck for the changed graphs (agents-tools, agents-root, agents-other; the first full run caught a tuple typing slip in the new test, now fixed). oxfmt and oxlint pass on the changed files. The line-cap ratchet (16 changed source files, no growth over cap), max-lines, mock-factory, SQLite worker, timeout-race and assertion-safety ratchets pass. The import-cycle check reports 0 cycles. The new test is registered in `vitest.database-worker-core-paths.mjs` next to the other two gateway skill suites.

### CLI-backend tool path (revision 9)

Head: `18936becef1` (one commit on top of `0a4297accba`; no rebase, the branch merges cleanly with main).

**What was left.** Revision 8 covered tool assembly that receives the executing agent as `agentId`. CLI backends take a different route. Their coding tools are minted on the Gateway and mediated over loopback (`resolveGatewayScopedTools` in `src/gateway/tool-resolution.ts`). That call passed `agentId: policyAgentId`, so in `agent-tools.ts` the derived `executionAgentId`, and with it `skillScope.ownerAgentId`, was the **policy** agent. The two agents really can differ there. The CLI runner (`cli-runner/prepare.ts`) resolves `policyAgentId` from `runtimePolicySessionKey` separately from the session's own agent, and passes both into the loopback grant (`agentId` plus `runtimePolicyAgentId`). `tool-resolution.ts` already had the executing agent as `sessionAgentId`, but it used that value only for the workspace and the sandbox lookup.

**What changed.** The fix is narrow. `OpenClawCodingToolsOptions` gains `skillOwnerAgentId`, and `agent-tools.ts` sets `skillScope.ownerAgentId = options.skillOwnerAgentId ?? executionAgentId`. The loopback path passes `skillOwnerAgentId: sessionAgentId`. `agentId` on that call is unchanged, so credentials, hooks, process scope and approval policy (approvals entry, `autoAllowSkills`, ask/security, grants) stay with the policy agent, as before. Callers that don't set the new option behave exactly as in revision 8.

**Regression test.** New: `src/gateway/tool-resolution.skill-owner.test.ts`. It has no mocks and uses the same fixture as the revision 8 `skill-owner` test, but goes through the CLI-backend entry point. It calls `resolveGatewayScopedTools` with `surface: "loopback"`, `mediatedToolNames: ["exec"]`, session `agent:execution:main` (agent `execution`) and runtime policy session `agent:main:main` (agent `main`). Then it runs the resolved exec tool through the real gateway authorization, supervisor and native launch. The approvals entry exists only for `main`. `main`'s workspace declares `policy-tool` and `execution`'s declares `exec-tool`, both copies of `touch`. The test is registered in `vitest.database-worker-core-paths.mjs` next to the other gateway skill suites.

With the fix:

```
✓ runs a bin declared by the executing agent's own skill
✓ denies a bin declared only by the policy agent's skill, with no I/O
```

Without the fix (only the `skillOwnerAgentId` line in `tool-resolution.ts` reverted, so the option plumbing and the test are kept), the policy agent's bin runs and the executing agent's own bin is refused:

```
× runs a bin declared by the executing agent's own skill
  - "details": { "status": "completed", "exitCode": 0 },  "ran": true
  + "ran": false
× denies a bin declared only by the policy agent's skill, with no I/O
  - "denied": "Error: exec denied: allowlist miss",  "ran": false
  + "details": { "status": "completed", "exitCode": 0, "exitReason": "exit", … },  "ran": true
```

| File | Result | Wall | Vitest duration |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tool-resolution.skill-owner.test.ts` (new) | 2 passed | 30.9 s | 18.0 s |

The existing `tool-resolution.exclude.test.ts` (24 tests) and the revision 8 `bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.skill-owner.test.ts` (2 tests) still pass.

Checks: `pnpm tsgo:core` passes, and so does the core test typecheck for the gateway-root graph that holds the new test. oxfmt and oxlint pass on the changed files. The line-cap ratchet (19 changed source files, no growth over cap) and the max-lines ratchet pass. The import-cycle check reports 0 cycles.
