prs.title: fix(worker): preserve reconciled files during fast-forward
prs.body:
Related: #137011
Follow-up to #137392

## What Problem This Solves

Replacement cloud workers already fetch and conservatively fast-forward a pushed session branch before each turn. This follow-up closes the remaining mixed-reset safety gaps:

- incoming file/directory shape changes must preserve dirty, untracked, ignored, case-aliased, index-flag-hidden, nested-repository, and submodule-backed local paths;
- clean tracked paths must not permanently block a valid remote file/directory replacement;
- a turn fenced while the replacement is already in progress must still finish materializing the checkout instead of stranding it;
- Git pattern characters in a real local path must be treated literally;
- large unrelated ignored trees must not exceed the bounded Git command output;
- subagent authority tests must await the lifecycle owner's Gateway root work instead of relying on a fixed polling window.

## Why This Change Was Made

The worker still inspects only components of incoming added paths. A collision is classified with literal Git pathspecs: dirty, untracked, ignored, or gitlink-backed paths skip the fast-forward and preserve local bytes; only a provably clean tracked file/directory blocker is recorded, removed after the ancestry-safe mixed reset, and then materialized from the fetched head. Gateway reconciliation remains file-only and owns no Git history recovery.

Removing a tracked blocker is only safe when the checkout proves the local bytes are reproducible from the index. Two classes of local state fail that proof, and a third issue decides whether the removal survives a fenced turn; each is a separate guard:

**Git index flags.** `git update-index --assume-unchanged <path>` and `git update-index --skip-worktree <path>` mark an entry as one Git should not consult, so later local edits to that path produce an empty status report while the working-tree bytes still differ from the index. The classifier reads the index tags with `git ls-files -v --stage` and authorizes removal only for a plain cached (`H`) entry; `h` (assume-unchanged), `S` (skip-worktree) and `s` (both) are treated as obstructions that keep the local bytes and skip the whole fast-forward.

**Nested repository metadata.** Git never reports `.git` entries, so an empty status cannot prove that a tracked directory holds no repository the worker initialized inside it. A recursive removal would delete that `.git` directory, including its commits, refs and stashes. Before authorizing removal the classifier walks the collision path and every directory that holds tracked entries under it, and rejects the path when any of them contains `.git` metadata.

**Fenced turns.** The mixed reset advances HEAD before the replacements are materialized, so the removal and materialization steps cannot be abandoned once they start. A fence that lands between two removals would otherwise return with tracked files missing, and every later turn returns before repairing them, because the local head already equals the pushed head. The classifier still honors the abort — a fenced turn never starts the credentialed fetch, never decides a collision, and never begins the move — while the bounded local move the same turn already began completes: the reset, the removals and the replacement checkout no longer observe the abort, and each step stays bounded by the turn's own timeouts.

Subagent lifecycle completion is registered as Gateway root work, and task finalization occurs before that root is released. The authority regression now waits for the canonical registry/root-work drain before asserting the terminal task projection; it does not increase a timeout or weaken the authority assertion.

The cloud-worker session lifecycle page now states that a collision skips the whole fast-forward rather than the update for a single path. It also scopes what may be replaced: the incoming path applies only where the local path is a tracked file or directory that Git reports clean and that holds no local work Git cannot see, such as an index flag or a repository created inside it, and every other obstruction keeps the local bytes.

## User Impact

A replacement worker can pick up safely pushed session history without discarding reconciled workspace bytes or getting stuck behind a clean tracked file/directory shape change. A turn that is fenced while the replacement is already underway still finishes it, so the next turn never inherits a checkout that is missing tracked files it can no longer restore. Local edits hidden by a Git index flag and repositories the worker created inside tracked directories are no longer removed. Real conflicts continue the coding turn with the existing bounded warning. Divergent history, same-path edits, local deletions and submodules remain untouched.

## Evidence

### Rebase onto current main

Rebased onto `main` at `d8bd336f64c`. The submitted diff is 4 files, +545/−15. Two merge conflicts were resolved: the checkout binder now builds on main's shared `executeGitCommand` helper while keeping the collision classifier intact, and the cloud-worker documentation keeps main's split documentation index while the lifecycle-page paragraph is retained.

Earlier revisions also carried a shared test-runner mock-drain repair and a session transcript-fixture teardown. Those hunks are no longer part of this diff, because main landed the same repairs independently: `#146508` rewrote the shared runner to join Vitest's native `pendingMockResolution` and deleted `test/non-isolated-runner.resolve-mocks.test.ts`, and the transcript fixtures moved to the `useTempSessionsFixture` / `closeOpenClawAgentDatabasesForTest` teardown. Replaying the older hunks would have re-created an owner main had already replaced, so they were dropped instead of re-implemented.

### Validation on the submitted head

```text
src/worker/github-binding.runtime.test.ts: 28 passed
src/agents/subagents/spawn/subagent-spawn.authority.test.ts: 6 passed
type-aware oxlint over the 3 changed TypeScript files: 263 rules, 0 warnings, 0 errors
docs/gateway/cloud-workers/session-lifecycle.md changed-file gate: all lanes passed
```

The repository-wide `typecheck core` lane of the same changed-file gate fails on this base with a `TS2345` in `src/infra/update-triage-resolution.ts`, which this pull request does not touch: that file is byte-identical to `main` here, the same failure reproduces in a worktree pinned to the base, and main has since repaired it in `c9b2f93dd65`. It is recorded as an unchanged-baseline limitation, not as a passing check.

### Real Git runtime proof

`runtime-proof-worker-checkout.mts` imports the production entrypoint and drives it against real bare origins, real worker checkouts and real `git` child processes — no test runner and no mocks. 10/10 scenarios matched the expected runtime behavior:

```text
dirty local file blocks incoming directory   : HEAD held at the initial commit
                                               blocked=file("local unpublished bytes"); later.txt=absent
clean tracked file blocks incoming directory : HEAD advanced to the pushed head
                                               swap=directory[inner.txt]
literal Git pattern characters in a path     : HEAD held at the initial commit
                                               a[bc]=directory[]; ab=file("tracked pathspec neighbour")
no collision                                 : HEAD advanced to the pushed head
                                               later.txt=file("remote later")
assume-unchanged file blocks directory       : status before=(clean); HEAD held at the initial commit
                                               flagged=file("local unpublished bytes")
skip-worktree file blocks directory          : status before=(clean); HEAD held at the initial commit
                                               flagged=file("local unpublished bytes")
assume-unchanged + skip-worktree             : status before=(clean); HEAD held at the initial commit
                                               flagged=file("local unpublished bytes")
nested repository at the collision path      : status before=(clean); HEAD held at the initial commit
                                               collision=directory[.git,base.txt]; nested HEAD=26f2d8c
nested repository in a tracked subdirectory  : status before=(clean); HEAD held at the initial commit
                                               collision=directory[sub]; nested HEAD=26f2d8c
fenced during the removals                   : fenced after 4 of 40 removals
                                               HEAD advanced to the pushed head; status after=(clean); restored 40/40
                                               next turn HEAD already at the pushed head with status (clean)
[worker/github] GitHub checkout fast-forward skipped: local path conflicts with openclaw/session-fixture
```

The five flag and nested-repository scenarios assert the hazardous premise directly (`status before=(clean)`) before checking that HEAD is held, the local bytes survive and the inner repository still resolves its HEAD. The fencing scenario declares forty clean tracked file-to-directory collisions, watches them disappear one by one against the real filesystem and aborts the turn as soon as some, but not all, of them are gone — so the fence provably lands inside the removal loop (`fenced after 4 of 40 removals`). It then asserts that the fenced turn itself advanced HEAD and left `git status` empty with all forty replacements restored, and that a further turn on that checkout stays clean instead of returning early on an incomplete tree. The literal-path scenario is kept deliberately empty (`directory[]`) with a clean tracked `ab` neighbour, so nothing but the pathspec scope can block it: removing `--literal-pathspecs` from the two classifier calls leaves every other scenario unchanged and makes this one replace the directory with the incoming file.

### RED → GREEN regressions

Every new regression failed against its pre-fix implementation for the intended reason:

```text
clean tracked file -> incoming directory: HEAD remained at the initial commit
clean tracked directory -> incoming file: HEAD remained at the initial commit
empty untracked a[bc] directory: directory was removed and replaced by the remote file
exact-head authority test: expected task "succeeded", received "running" after the 5-second polling window
assume-unchanged / skip-worktree / both: local file was removed and replaced by the incoming
  directory (EISDIR reading the preserved path); HEAD advanced to the pushed head
nested repository at the collision path / in a tracked subdirectory: the tracked directory was
  removed with its `.git` (ENOTDIR reading the preserved file); in the real-Git harness the
  scenario reported nested HEAD=absent and a moved HEAD
fenced during the removals (focused test): the abort threw while the replacements were still
  missing (ENOENT reading collision/remote.txt) with HEAD already advanced
fenced during the removals (real-Git harness): 9/10, only that scenario flipped — HEAD advanced
  to the pushed head, `git status` reported all forty replacements as deleted, 0/40 restored, and
  the following turn returned early on the same incomplete tree
```

The flag and nested-repository scenarios were also re-run against their pre-fix classifiers in the real-Git proof harness: 4/7 with all four preservation scenarios reporting destroyed local state, then 7/9 before the nested-repository guard, 9/9 before the cancel-safety change and 10/10 after it. Each harness flip was produced by reverting only the production file, with every other scenario staying green.

### Change size

```text
production:     +164 / -11
tests/support:  +380 / -3
docs:             +1 / -1
```

The production growth is the bounded collision classifier needed to distinguish a safe clean tracked shape replacement from local-byte conflicts while avoiding a full workspace inventory.

### Review findings

- `[P2] Cancellation can leave removed collision paths permanently unrestored`: addressed. Once the mixed reset advances HEAD, the turn completes its own bounded local move instead of honoring the abort; the classifier, the credentialed fetch and the collision decision still observe it, so a fence before the move leaves the checkout untouched. A focused test aborts during the replacement checkout and asserts the advanced HEAD, the restored file and the clean status, and the real-Git harness fences between the removals and then runs a further turn on the result.
- `[P1] Nested Git history can still be deleted`: addressed. The classifier now rejects a collision path when it, or any directory holding tracked entries beneath it, contains `.git` metadata. Two unit regressions and two real-Git scenarios assert that the inner HEAD still resolves, the outer HEAD is held and the tracked bytes survive; the harness reproduces the loss against the pre-fix code.
- `[P1] Dirty files hidden by Git index flags are classified as safe to delete`: addressed. The classifier requires the plain cached `H` index tag, so assume-unchanged, skip-worktree and combined paths are obstructions. Three regressions assert preserved bytes and an unchanged HEAD.
- `[P3] The literal-path runtime proof overstates its coverage`: addressed. That scenario is now an empty directory with a tracked `ab` neighbour, so only the pathspec scope can block it, and the differential is demonstrated by removing `--literal-pathspecs` from the two classifier calls (9/10, only that scenario flips).
- `[P3] Documentation excludes a supported replacement`: addressed. The lifecycle page now names a clean tracked file *or directory*, and describes the excluded local work as anything Git cannot see, covering both an index flag and a repository created inside the directory.
- `[P3] Disclose the recorded core typecheck failure`: addressed in the validation section above.
- `[P3] Describe conflicts as skipping the entire fast-forward`: addressed. The lifecycle page says a collision skips the whole fast-forward, and now also states the condition under which a local path may be replaced.

A configured remote cloud-worker backend was not available on this host. No operator configuration was changed to manufacture a remote claim; the proof above covers the real production Git boundary and the exact local validation gates.

prs.body:
Closes #144500

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a documentation and tool-guidance gap where `web_search` users cannot see that Perplexity rejects `freshness` together with `date_after` or `date_before`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Perplexity validator already returns an actionable conflict error before any network request. This change documents that mutual exclusion in the shared tool schema, the Perplexity provider schema, and both public web-search references so callers can choose either a relative freshness filter or an explicit date range.

## User Impact

Agents and operators receive clear parameter guidance before making a rejected Perplexity search request. Existing validation, error behavior, and provider support remain unchanged.

## Evidence

The production tool constructors were executed without mocks and printed the guidance they now emit:

```
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs <runtime proof script>

=== web_search tool (src/agents/tools/web-search.ts, production) ===
{ "description": "Search current web; normalized provider results. Supports freshness and date-range filters (freshness, date_after/date_before) and domain filtering (domain_filter). Perplexity time filters are mutually exclusive." }
{
  "freshness": "Time filter: day/week/month/year (Perplexity: choose this or a date range).",
  "date_after": "Published after YYYY-MM-DD.",
  "date_before": "Published before YYYY-MM-DD."
}

=== Perplexity provider tool (extensions/perplexity, production) ===
{
  "freshness": "Filter by time: 'day' (24h), 'week', 'month', or 'year'; choose this or a date range.",
  "date_after": "Native Perplexity Search API only. Only results published after this date (YYYY-MM-DD).",
  "date_before": "Native Perplexity Search API only. Only results published before this date (YYYY-MM-DD)."
}

=== shared validator outcome for freshness + date_after (unchanged) ===
{
  "error": "conflicting_time_filters",
  "message": "freshness and date_after/date_before cannot be used together. Use either freshness (day/week/month/year) or a date range (date_after/date_before), not both.",
  "docs": "https://docs.openclaw.ai/tools/web"
}
```

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/perplexity/src/perplexity-web-search-provider.test.ts src/agents/tools/web-search.test.ts` passed: 34 Perplexity provider tests and 30 shared web-search tests.
- `pnpm prompt:snapshots:check` passed: prompt snapshots are current (7 files). The Codex dynamic-tool snapshots were regenerated so they carry the longer `web_search` description and its updated char/token counters.
- `pnpm docs:check-mdx` passed (1,338 files).
- `pnpm docs:check-links` passed (`broken_links=0`, 14,964 internal links checked).
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` passed on the regenerated prompt fixtures.
- `pnpm check:changed` passes its changed-file format, lint, typecheck and guard lanes, with one exception that this change does not cause: the repository-wide `OPENCLAW_*` env-var count guard inside `scripts/check-max-lines-ratchet.mts` reports 456 distinct names against the 455 budget in `config/env-var-count-budget.txt` on current `main`. This branch adds no `OPENCLAW_*` reference and its name set is byte-identical to `origin/main`, so the guard fails for any PR based on this `main` revision. That budget file asks to never be raised without owner approval, so this PR leaves it untouched.

The branch was rebased onto current `main` and the three conflicted prompt-snapshot fixtures were regenerated from the production tool definitions, so the guidance and its generated counters match the new baseline.

The shared validator still returns `conflicting_time_filters` for the rejected combination, so this change only affects the guidance text. It does not alter validation, transport, or any external API contract, so no external search service call is required.

prs.title: fix(agent): finalize settled turns when harness callback is absent
prs.body:
## Summary

- route a genuinely absent settled-turn finalizer into the existing deterministic host fallback
- preserve the finalizer-available truncated-stream recovery merged in #140367
- preserve deliberate silence, terminal errors, detached isolation, cancellation authority, and no-replay semantics
- prove the persistence/delivery boundary through real SQLite and `dispatchReplyFromConfig`

## What Problem This Solves

Codex can complete a turn after tool side effects without emitting a final assistant message. Current `main` recovers this when a tool-free finalizer is available, including truncated completion streams after commentary. A distinct gap remained when the selected harness exposed no `finalizeSettledTurn` callback: OpenClaw returned `not-attempted` before reaching its existing safe host fallback.

This refresh keeps the merged available-finalizer behavior and removes only that stale availability precondition.

## Why Each Change Exists

- **Request resolution:** removes the precondition so an absent callback reaches the existing host-owned fallback; terminal assistant errors remain excluded.
- **Persistence fencing:** detached sessions never append a transcript; superseded writers and unresolved targets still fail closed.
- **Cancellation boundary:** cancellation before persistence suppresses the outcome; after a successful append, the committed idempotency key remains authoritative so durable state and delivery cannot disagree.
- **Tests:** true callback absence, not merely a throwing callback, proves durable, detached, pre-append, and post-append behavior. The integration matrix crosses real SQLite and the production reply dispatcher.
- **Documentation:** states the optional-callback and pre/post-commit contracts without suggesting tool replay.

## User Impact

A settled tool turn no longer ends silently merely because its harness omits the optional finalizer. OpenClaw emits the deterministic no-model fallback once, while preserving deliberate silence, failure-honest terminal errors, detached non-persistence, and cancellation semantics.

## Evidence

- exact head: `601c46ccf71224c6a5b20c6040009cd4e19fbc35`
- real SQLite → source dispatcher integration: 19/19
- related settled-finalization and terminal-resolution matrix: 85/85
- combined fresh local run: 123/123 across five requested test files
- `pnpm check:changed`: exit 0
- `pnpm build`: exit 0
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`: exit 0
- independent Cursor review on exact head: `NO_MATERIAL_FINDINGS`
- Codex protocol inspected directly: `item/completed` applies item-side effects separately; `turn/completed` may contain no loaded assistant items
- current-main relation: #140367 / `04081aa1361d6a4097d0b489126a737481220f53` is preserved and remains an ancestor

## Scope and Risk

- no configuration, migration, provider, or tool-execution change
- no model/tool/attempt replay
- production change remains concentrated in terminal request resolution and fallback persistence
- added test-support module only keeps the real integration harness within repository size limits

prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/139082

## Current landing status — private successor, public `86618c2b0a46`

The public head remains `86618c2b0a468a0e539f3908bb08e2d69d7203ef` (tree `6261a36e4dcd7b5d425672d97c8bf1fbe2b9680c`). [Exact-head CI run 35819683093](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35819683093) succeeded for that head; it is not CI proof for the unpublished successor. [ClawSweeper revision 26](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/148066#issuecomment-5660802475) also applies to that public head, with no new actionable code findings and the obsolete Slack-suppression finding resolved.

The signed private successor is `7d6db30dabeed6bd58c2a19960b2d3a16507226a`, tree `e7e721a5babf25a874b27e9d64224bec2e048ac7`, preserving the public head and main `92f0719c22d5064acc18fe8c6c27d8edf79bffb5` as parents. Its scoped qualification comprises 287 health/caller/service/post-update passes before the sole final assertion correction, plus 18 affected rejection passes after that correction; unchanged evidence is reused, not represented as 305 newly rerun exact-head tests. Whole-touched-file API-direct review found the Windows Crabbox fake counted the exact `run --help` probe as workload execution. The reviewed correction excludes only that probe; workload rejection assertions remain intact. Lint, formatting and core types passed. These are source/component checks, not Windows or installed-runtime acceptance.

**Publication:** source-write custody is released. Native `prepare-sync-head` was attempted and refused by the existing `NEEDS WORK` review recommendation, whose IMPORTANT finding is the still-open installed recovery acceptance below. No push occurred and no new-head CI is claimed. The signed successor is conflict-free in a merge-tree comparison against observed main `c214f1c705ea3dce5b98a15ebd3f20fcb607ff04`; its nine newer commits have no overlap with the 37-file residual or dependency-graph pins. Main does change state-database foundations, so this comparison is not blanket runtime equivalence or qualification of a newly integrated head. Native current-main/review preparation, publication and exact-resulting-head CI remain outstanding.

**Required before landing:** bind the actual emitted candidate and installed published-updater recovery caller, with genuine task-private initial-store ingress before preparation and through BOTH real executor routes. Every helper/Worker must preserve the physically verified private handoff/state/coordinator identity and real caller authority. Lint-only Doctor is not this recovery path. The installed transition must prove loaded launchd throttling through all twelve readiness probes to a healthy real-Gateway replacement, preservation of existing operator state, failure cleanup, and applicable Windows behavior. Identity/plugin/channel refusal, cancellation and stale/positive-owner-death behavior remain required. No final emitted composition or passing installed/Windows acceptance is claimed.

This is this PR's recovery acceptance criterion. Broader composed-update observer/collision qualification remains separately owned, not an unrelated whole-chain landing hold. Vincent Koc's original contribution and public ancestry are preserved. The original full-recovery and newer-write preservation goals are not reduced to package-only rollback. No live operator gateway was updated or restarted; the PR is not landed.

The following sections retain source and diagnostic history with their original commit/run scope.

## Problem and fix

A loaded macOS LaunchAgent can have a stopped process and free port while launchd throttles a restart. Recovery must keep waiting for its replacement within the existing budget rather than report premature failure.

The shared health waiter now infers loaded launchd supervision once when the caller supplied no decision. It checks cancellation and caller authority after the bounded native probe, preserves direct/wrapped cleanup errors, and retains explicit decisions, positive owner-death exits, identity/plugin/channel refusal, and the twelve-probe settlement requirement.

The current-main residual excludes already-landed recovery/finalization/canary/SQLite work. It retains only the supervision correction and necessary test fixtures. The catalog fixture joins real cron hydration and initial metadata preparation before testing browser snapshot ordering; the Corepack fixture reuses its prepared cache. No production deadline or assertion was weakened.

Vincent Koc's original contribution and public branch ancestry are preserved.

## Source qualification

Prior qualified baseline: `c14ee7115ccdfda7ce8a6d98708145d093562e59` (GitHub verified; PR remains draft).

Pinned source base: `a3bcdf75ceec869d76241bfba71687892b78b1c4`. Qualified tree: `6df476959e7e7a7d8ebd67974173d9c1d9f4ef01`.

- 189 fresh selected cases passed: 179 waiter/supervision/verification/post-update/Doctor controls, two real-health-owner recovery callers, and all eight catalog cases. Other unselected tests are not counted.
- Unchanged source-bound controls and the nine Corepack transport cases retain their prior evidence; these counts are not added to the fresh count as unique tests.
- Affected CLI, Doctor and UI type projects passed. Formatting, typed lint, patch checks and independent API-direct P0–P2 review passed, including a separate review of the final three-line metadata fixture correction.
- Catalog's initial run retained seven passes/one expected-2-received-3 failure. Event-only diagnosis observed an independent `chat.metadata.changed` refresh. Joining the real initial metadata read before browser connection passes all eight original cases in 81.29 seconds. This supports the competing-lifecycle fix without claiming uniquely observed historical timing.

## Qualified diagnostic and migrated-fence successor

Prior signed head: `740ccdd0d4d9410b899887f28c6b2f93e10b65a8` (GitHub verified). Its [run 35668359364](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35668359364) completed cancelled: 199 successful jobs, 8 skipped jobs, the SDK report cancelled, and the aggregate gate failed. It was not retried; fresh successor CI is recorded below.

The migrated-fence fixture starts no Gateway, but failed-update health verification is mandatory even with `shouldRestart: false`. It now supplies only a deterministic `stopped-free` observation through the existing real verification owner's health injection, using the repository's prepared candidate graph. The candidate processes, executor/delegation, ledger, terminal result and parent package cleanup stay real. All original assertions and budgets remain; additional assertions require the failed-health record and observation, including original-runtime refusal bypass.

- All **20** original cases pass. Full supported-wrapper wall: **77.85s**, with unchanged per-case 30s limits. This includes parent/retained ownership, legacy and original-runtime refusal, and both simulated compatibility budgets.
- Explicit SQLite path/realpath prechecks recorded **724 permitted handoff opens across nine private databases**, with zero refusals. The preloader was reinjected after the test environment's `NODE_OPTIONS` reset. The earlier incomplete child-instrumentation attempt is not counted as isolation proof.
- Build, affected CLI-update types, both changed fixture/declaration lints, formatting, patch checks and context-complete independent API-direct P0–P2 review passed. The unchanged SDK diagnostic postimages reuse their prior 10-pass suite and type/lint evidence.
- Windows acquisition now retains bounded readiness/post-ready logs; SDK API-diff emits bounded stage/resource markers that survive cancellation. These changes enable new observations; they do not establish the original Windows or SDK failure causes.
- The first new fixture startup failure and subsequent source-loader timeout remain recorded. The correction uses the existing prepared worker declarations, not a longer deadline, weaker assertion or skipped verification.

These are component/source results, **not installed-runtime acceptance**. The exact coherent source/package/runtime/launcher/import/Node/isolated-host tuple for loaded launchd throttle → replacement health, stale/owner-death and no-loss acceptance remains unselected with the existing integration/package/runtime/state owners. No live Odin or Mac app update/restart occurred.

## Remaining gates

The original baseline CI failed: [run 35659592558](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35659592558) failed `checks-windows-node-test-5` in `gateway-cron-process-identity.windows.test.ts` with `gateway connect timeout`. The cause is not established by the retained log; no retry, timeout increase, or weakened assertion has been applied. The dispatch-only SDK API-diff report was also cancelled after approximately 20 minutes without an artifact; its underlying stall/slowness cause is not established. Exact source/package/runtime/launcher/import/Node/host selection, installed/published-driver × real-Gateway throttle/progress/stale/owner-death acceptance, no-loss proof, and final landing remain open. Original failed/unknown recovery evidence and retry restrictions remain intact. Source tests are not installed-product proof. No live Odin or Mac app update/restart was performed.

Adopts only the two-file SDK declaration cycle-cache repair already landed in upstream commit `7d7b5ba1b5a9afa132ff369c3ea50cdaa870ce40`, preserving Vincent Koc's attribution. Root-local memoization bounds repeated cyclic walks without reusing partial closure results across roots. The dense-cycle regression preserves complete membership and second-root equality.

- The exact qualified postimages and unchanged base retain 23 passing tests, affected type/lint/format checks, and the original red control (3,914 printed declarations versus the bounded expectation). Recorded suite execution was 5.15 seconds; that is not a new wrapper timing.
- The exact prior base-rendering workload completed in 112.577 seconds with this delta. The original observation bound remains 180 seconds. Local Darwin versus hosted Linux, inspector overhead and process-cache differences prevent a unique historical hosted-cause claim. No timeout or assertion was weakened.
- Fresh independent API-direct P0–P2 review is clean with the complete renderer, owner, caller and test context.
- Source import closure, canonical build/declaration entrypoints, package whitelist and complete packed-content scan establish that these two paths do not change emitted runtime/package behavior. The existing immutable package remains a build of `740ccdd0d4d9410b899887f28c6b2f93e10b65a8`; it is not relabeled as this successor, and no new-head package build is claimed.

Installed-driver/isolated-host/state/process/caller admission is still incomplete. All twelve probes, real HTTP, failure-health, stale/owner-death, no-loss, terminal-before-cleanup and process-settlement gates remain open. The PR stays draft; no installed-native acceptance or landing is claimed.

## Current-main deadline and cancellation integration

Prior GitHub-verified signed head: `81a169893352153423c8fd67a2dfe26f99f8e560`; tree: `b88ce68bb40842ebbc66b4f3350bf362c1ce9f73`. Both main integrations preserve the contributor branch and prior signed ancestry. The candidate is merge-clean against observed main `4311a4ecdf96add7ae6d20b1b059ae72c875cde3`.

Fresh required CI: [run 35676181690](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35676181690), attempt 1, pending. Its hosted SDK report completed successfully in 5m23s (job 106583326957), and preflight passed in 1m14s. Other required jobs remain in progress; this is not an aggregate-gate pass or proof of a unique historical SDK cause. The synthetic merge's second parent was verified as this exact new head before dispatch. Neither consumed historical run was restarted; no successful aggregate gate is claimed.

Current main introduced a shared restart deadline. Native supervision now participates in that deadline and uses its effective cancellation signal. The independent review also identified a signal-only cancellation gap: the probe now uses the existing command-process scope, carries abort to the native command, joins retained cleanup, and preserves uncertain-cleanup failure ahead of caller cancellation. Caller authority is revalidated before health observation. Deterministic regressions fail on the original uncancelable code and pass after repair; no native LaunchAgent was acted upon.

The migrated-fence fixture also supplies an explicit absent-service observation for its relocated private state. Its real failure-health, executor/delegation, ledger, finalization, terminal-before-cleanup and original-runtime-refusal behavior remains exercised.

- Exact final tree: **85 health cases** across the deadline, supervision and waiter files pass in **22.334s supported-wrapper wall** (18.19s Vitest). The two new signal-only cleanup cases execute in 3ms and 2ms; budgets and assertions are unchanged.
- All **20 migrated-update cases** pass in **90.770s wrapper wall** (87.08s Vitest), retaining the existing per-case limits. This slower file proves prepared child-runtime/finalization and cleanup ordering that a helper-only test cannot replace.
- Services and CLI-update type projects, four-file typed lint, formatting and whitespace checks pass. Fresh complete-context API-direct P0–P2 review is clean after fixing its verified cancellation finding; prior unaffected review evidence remains bound.
- Explicit all-SQLite resolved-path prechecks record **1,464 permitted opens across 284 private paths**, zero refusals, and both guard and private lifecycle-directory injection in every opening process. No shared handoff database is used.
- The two SDK cycle-cache source blobs remain unchanged; their valid 23-pass/exact-base 112.577s evidence is reused. The original 180s bound and local-versus-hosted causal limits remain unchanged.

Unlike the SDK-only source successor, this main/runtime integration requires a **new exact-public-head package build**. The exact-head local package build and supported tarball checker passed. Artifact `openclaw-81a169893352.tgz` is 95,027,200 bytes, SHA-256 `589db49a2e7f82ad1f2f13ce6a9307a6c1ccfcde12ceffb4976ce44fe2a962b1`. Its build-info names this exact commit (version 2026.9.5); this is not a registry release or runtime selection. The complete inventory has 12,615 regular files. Combined source-closure, 1,224 canonical build-root, whitelist and 9,316 packed code/declaration-file checks preserve the two SDK paths as tooling-only. The static graph covers 8,680 modules, with no missing reachable imports or parse errors; 57 nonliteral imports and installed external dependencies still require the admitted host/driver tuple. Installed-runtime closure and acceptance are not claimed. The immutable 740 package remains labeled as 740, and existing suppliers remain bound to it until canonical reconciliation.

The PR remains draft. Installed-driver/isolated-host/all-process private-state/caller admission is still incomplete. Mandatory twelve-probe settlement, real HTTP, failure-health, stale/owner-death, no-loss, terminal-before-cleanup and process-settlement gates remain open. No live Odin or Mac update/restart, native acceptance, or landing occurred.

prs.title: fix(subagents): recovered subagent cleanup disturbed by overlapping restart-recovery sweeps
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after a Gateway restart, a recovered subagent's cleanup could be disturbed by a later recovery sweep while its result was still being delivered. The sweep logged `failed to durably finalize interrupted subagent run` and retried, or suppressed the child's session effects mid-cleanup.

## User Impact

User impact: subagent runs recovered after a restart finish cleanup and result delivery once, with their child session effects applied. The spurious finalize warnings and retry sweeps are gone. No config or data changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Restart recovery replays rows still marked `terminalOwner: "interrupted-recovery"` so that a crash-orphaned cleanup gets drained. After activation's own recovery pass had finalized a row, a later sweep (the scheduled post-activation sweep, or any sweep while delivery was in flight) replayed it while this process was still running that row's cleanup. The cleanup's writes changed the coordinator's recovery facts mid-replay, so the replay commit failed with `Subagent terminal execution changed`. A replay that did commit rebound the terminal session effects, and the live cleanup then suppressed the child's session effects.

The lifecycle controller now reports whether a run's terminal tail is active in this process: completion users, cleanup reservations, and active cleanup attempts. Completion starts cleanup synchronously, so these spans overlap without a gap. The recovery coordinator treats a terminal row with an active tail as handled. After a real restart those sets are empty, so orphaned tails still replay.

Provenance: likely made visible by #163195 (author/merger @steipete, 2026-10-02), which added the recovery-fact snapshot (including `terminalOwner`) to the coordinator's `isHostCurrent`. The replay of `interrupted-recovery` rows predates it. It surfaced as a Bun-only flake on #167966's CI (run 38259246034 attempt 1, shard `bun:agentic-agents-support-hosted-2`).

## Evidence

- **CI failure:** `preserves restart through lifecycle then wait as interrupted` threw `SubagentRegistryMutationRejectedError: Subagent terminal execution changed` from the replay's commit-time `assertCurrent`. The restart fixture rethrows the rejected root work, even though `finalizeInterruptedSubagentRun` catches it and only warns.
- **Deterministic reproduction:** pausing the replay after `prepare()` reproduced the exact error under Node. Traces showed the cleanup clearing `terminalOwner` between the replay's prepare and commit.
- **Regression test:** `leaves a recovered terminal tail to its live cleanup when a sweep overlaps delivery` holds announce delivery open and sweeps during it. On unfixed code it sees 2 terminal-completion lock acquisitions instead of 1, and a separate negative-control run showed `execution.suppressSessionEffects === true` after cleanup. The test doesn't assert end-state suppression, because sweeps after cleanup still replay the cleaned row (existing behavior, outside the live-tail window) and can flip it under load.
- **Merged with main:** resolved two conflicts with #170120/#170506 (legacy-warning moves) and added the predicate to the benchmark sweeper; the restart-integration, sweeper-recovery, restart-recovery, and child-owner-match suites pass on the merged head (4 files, 175 tests), and `pnpm tsgo:scripts` is clean.
- **Focused suites:** `pnpm test` on the restart integration file plus the sweeper-recovery, context-cleanup, pressure, and restart-recovery suites passed under Node (5 files, 176 tests). `pnpm check:changed` is green (typecheck, lint, deadcode, import cycles, ratchets).
- **Repeat runs of the whole file after the fix:** Node 8/8 passed. Bun (`OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun`) 7/8 passed. The one Bun failure is a different problem: that run was under extreme host load (load average ~45 on 16 cores, tests running 10–90× slower), and the case left the row `interrupted`, never finalized, which this change doesn't touch. It is most likely a separate load-only race between the test's explicit sweep and the 5s background sweeper tick, where `sweepOnce` is a no-op while another sweep runs. `main` has since sequenced that test with `fixture.settle()` in db5b24d008f.
- **Review:** Codex autoreview at P1 came back scoped-clean.

prs.body:
## Summary
- document the visibility-scope difference between `openclaw agents list` (config-scoped) and Gateway `agents.list` (runtime-scoped)
- describe both supported explicit roster shapes: canonical `agents.entries` and compatibility `agents.list`
- add focused regression coverage for implicit discovery and both explicit roster shapes
- keep runtime behavior unchanged (no visibility-surface expansion)

## Root cause
Chat/UI surfaces (iOS/Android/TUI) call Gateway `agents.list` through `listAgentsForGateway`, while `openclaw agents list` uses `buildAgentSummaries` from configuration.

When no explicit roster is configured, Gateway may include disk-discovered agent state directories. When an explicit roster exists through either `agents.entries` or `agents.list`, Gateway intentionally restricts visibility to that configured scope. The CLI remains configuration-scoped.

## Changes
- Updated `docs/cli/agents.md` to use the shared “explicit roster” concept.
- Documented `agents.entries` as the canonical shape and `agents.list` as a supported compatibility shape.
- Added regression coverage proving both explicit shapes exclude disk-only agents from Gateway and CLI output.
- Retained the existing test proving Gateway/CLI divergence when no explicit roster exists.

prs.title: fix(doctor): prioritize unresolved findings and explain repairs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Doctor reports that mix current failures, optional advice, and old recovery concerns, or continue showing findings after successful repair. Plugin migration backup inventories and coverage guidance landed in #169295.

## User Impact

The final report separates **Fix now**, **Recommended improvements**, and **Historical recovery notices**, with concrete next steps and documentation. Verified repairs disappear; failed or skipped repairs remain visible. Historical transcript notices share one summary with at most five examples across stores; every current transcript failure remains visible.

Healthy browser, manual setup, and uninspected extension bootstrap advice stays informational in lint and quiet in normal Doctor. Identical credential findings appear once, with store attribution when only part of the fleet is affected. Saved recovery copies explain when no action is needed.

No acknowledgement command or acknowledgement persistence is added. Existing archive, receipt, and retention owners keep their policies. When an older updater's sealed capture omits newly declared plugin files, Doctor saves a separate pre-repair copy and leaves the original capture unchanged; failure to make a required update-time copy refuses mutation with an actionable diagnostic.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each diagnostic owner supplies priority, remediation, and its existing warning receipt. Normal Doctor reports unresolved end state after repair verification; lint keeps per-store structured facts. The flow reuses already collected service and Gateway facts and preserves raw warning evidence, deferred inspections, shared credential ownership, and credential-read failure safeguards.

## Evidence

- **82 focused UX tests passed**, including shared OAuth refresh ownership, external read-only config refusal with the final summary, browser permission boundaries, current transcript identities beyond five, and a 20,353-notice history report.
- **41 capture and CLI-process cases passed**, covering the older sealed capture, separate pre-repair copy, immutable original bytes, and refusal before mutation when recovery capture fails. Wrapper wall time: 762.12s.
- Production, Doctor/other test, and browser package-boundary types passed. Configured typed lint, formatting, whitespace, line-cap/environment ratchets, and fresh independent P0–P2 review passed. The review's routine-browser and current-finding truncation findings were corrected at their producers and rechecked.
- Final changed-owner proof: 28 existing cases in 97.14s; shared-auth/read-only config siblings: seven cases in 148.28s. Workspace/browser completion: 30 cases in 48.60s. These reruns reuse the same cases; they are not additional test counts. PR CI supplies broad-suite coverage.

### Existing-data and upgrade compatibility

The actual older-driver capture case runs the bundled Canvas `migrateLegacyState` after its separate live pre-repair capture: the old document is moved, the destination and saved payload match the original text, and the admitted updater manifest bytes remain unchanged. The captured plugin SQLite payload still reads `plugin recovery`; config and skill bytes match exactly. Shared/agent source database bytes remain unchanged during disposable rehearsal, and unsafe capture preserves its source. The owning capture file passed two cases in 58.31s; its live older-driver case took 26.846s.

Existing fleet-preflight cases preserve config/capture bytes and skip repair for invalid admitted references. Schema cases load frozen-v24 `cache_entries` JSON after actual migration, retain transcript/window rows except the intended orphan removal, and preserve refused-mutation bytes, ledger, and config. Deletion recovery preserves bytes and inode. The Linux-only NOCOW case checks its SQL payload after two intended inode exchanges; that OS-specific case remains unrun locally. No database schema or stored-data format changes are introduced by this PR.

### Current-head CI fixture corrections

Hosted CI and local owning-entry reproduction exposed two fixture mismatches after the production cutover: update-mode cases supplied no installation root for required capture, and the remote-health case expected immediate stderr instead of the final warning summary. Local red evidence: installation-root case 121.71s; remote-health case 38.95s. The fix supplies the root only in the affected fixtures, preserves the shared harness's null default and production refusal, and checks the exact remote finding, visible action/docs, retained warning receipt, and every no-local-service assertion.

The combined five-file local suite was **not run**: its native runtime/package preparation was stopped after more than 15 minutes before any suite began, and its process group joined cleanly. Linux CI on the previously reviewed head `73b224dcc62` verified these five files, including the Linux-only NOCOW case. Affected Doctor and other test type graphs passed in 2.6s and 2.8s, respectively; configured five-file typed lint and formatting passed after the build released its artifact custody. Fresh independent P0–P2 review of the fixture-only delta passed with zero findings. The inspected CLI images below demonstrate rendering from source `87806fce`. Subsequent fixes preserve that rendering behavior; the later warm-reader lifecycle repair changes production state handling and is covered by its owning boundary proof below.

### Warm-reader lifecycle repair and final schema proof

The debug-schema cases first exposed missing fixture provenance (local red: 39.17s). After the fixtures recorded the actual updater driver and scoped run ID, the real flow exposed a stale owned read-admission failure (local red: 197.02s). The production reader now closes its invalidated warm resource and returns unavailable to the existing fresh-admission fallback. Other authority, source-identity, retained-lifetime, and cleanup failures still propagate; this adds no query replay, polling, schema, or durable state.

The owning nine-case proof passed: **171.68s wrapper / 148.05s routed**, including 16.595s native preparation. Both actual debug-schema flows passed (2026.9.2: 75.495s; 2026.9.3-beta.1: 59.988s). Six reader lifetime/alias/cleanup and no-probe controls passed in 0.386–0.567s; the sealed-replacement refusal passed in 19ms. These results prove the identified producer repair; they are not attributed to a passing replay alone.

Fresh production, state, Doctor, and other type graphs passed in 10.8s, 10.2s, 8.3s, and 8.9s. Configured three-file typed lint and the native staged line-cap check passed. Fresh independent P0–P2 delta review found no actionable findings. The shared legacy-E2E mock preserves the actual backup-inventory export; current-head Linux CI passed its execution and the Linux-only cases. No local full-E2E or installed-driver acceptance pass is claimed.

### Final legacy-E2E harness correction

The shared harness now preserves the actual process-module exports, including `runUtf8CommandWithTimeout`, while retaining its two intentional `runExec` and `runCommandWithTimeout` overrides. The source audit found this remaining closed mock seam; actual backup/inventory/config/SQLite paths remain in the flow. Doctor/other type graphs passed in 2.6s/1.8s, touched typed lint passed, and fresh P0–P2 delta review found zero actionable findings. Linux CI on the previously reviewed head `73b224dcc62` passed all five legacy-E2E cases, including legacy yes-mode migration (26.103s) and Anthropic profile migration (4.390s). ### Actual CLI before and after

After, the final report separates current inspection/Gateway failures from one historical summary: **five examples, nine omitted**, with retained evidence and conditional no-action guidance. Current transcript preservation beyond five is covered separately by the owning test.

The images below are **actual CLI stdout excerpts, rendered as PNG** after inspection. Only synthetic paths and the isolated port are redacted; output order and text are preserved. The before image shows its session recovery panel; the after image shows the final unresolved findings and completion.

![Before: actual CLI session recovery stdout excerpt, rendered as PNG](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3c2b91b3-269e-4798-9e54-fb46bdda2888)

![After: actual CLI prioritized findings stdout excerpt, rendered as PNG](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eb2bf967-e98b-48b2-af0f-7d1c3f656ca4)

### Update proof limits

The installed updater runs first and remains unchanged by this candidate. Published-driver × candidate acceptance remains unverified: full packaging was blocked by the inherited Solid adapter package-resolver mismatch. Native developer runtime builds and the actual Doctor runs above succeeded. No release, dependency, protocol, or schema bump is included.

Earlier remote-scope tests had unresolved 120s timeouts; those failures were recorded and are not claimed fixed by passing unrelated cases.

### Final readiness

[Prior reviewed-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38340852625) passed on `73b224dcc625af85ed6e034dc03ce299fc7e2968`: all 90 jobs completed successfully, including the aggregate gate. Merged main `17929e42d182` into this branch after the two prerequisite fixes landed. prs.title: fix: queued messages show no typing indicator while they wait behind a live run
prs.body:
Closes #162547

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a direct message that queues behind a live run shows no typing indicator for the whole wait, even though `docs/concepts/queue.md` says typing still fires on enqueue.

## User Impact

User impact: on Telegram and other channels whose turns carry an adoption lifecycle, a message queued behind a busy session keeps showing "typing…" until its own run starts and replies. Typing stops when the queued item finishes, is cancelled, or is dropped from the queue. Messages that do not queue are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The enqueue path already signals typing when a follow-up queues behind a live run, and the follow-up runner keeps the same typing controller. But the buffered dispatcher that handled the inbound message then returns. Its dispatcher idle callback and its `finally` (`markRunComplete` and `markDispatchIdle` in `src/auto-reply/dispatch.ts`) seal that controller and call the channel's `onIdle`, which closes the channel typing loop for good. So typing starts and stops within the same ~360 ms dispatch the issue's log shows (`message dispatch completed ... duration=363ms`).

Related: #92287 starts typing when a queued turn begins to execute (#92267). This change covers the wait before that, and keeps the controller that run would use from being sealed when the inbound dispatch returns.

This follows the direction in the ClawSweeper review: the queued item owns typing from enqueue to settlement.

- `createReplyDispatcherWithTyping` returns a new internal `onTypingHandoff` reply option. It lives in `InternalReplySessionOptions` next to `onReplyOperationOwned`, not in the public `GetReplyOptions`, and `publicReplyOptions` strips it from plugin-supplied options. Core builds these reply options itself in `dispatchReplyWithBufferedBlockDispatcher`, so Telegram still gets the handoff. After it is called, the dispatcher no longer completes the typing controller. When typing comes only from `typingCallbacks`, their `onIdle` (typing teardown) is deferred, and the queued item's typing cleanup runs `onCleanup` and then that `onIdle` once. The handoff state lives in `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-dispatcher-typing-handoff.ts`.
- A channel that passes its own `onIdle` gets no `onTypingHandoff`, so its whole typing lifecycle is unchanged. That `onIdle` can do more than stop typing: Feishu's (`extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.ts:1232`, `queueIdleSideEffects`) finalizes streaming delivery and closes the card preview. Deferring it made finalization wait on itself (ClawSweeper revision 3). Running it while the handed-off controller kept ticking let the next tick's `onReplyStart` reopen the closed preview (revision 5). So Feishu does not get typing through the queued wait. Channels that pass only `typingCallbacks`, such as Telegram, do.
- `runReplyAgent`, on the enqueue-behind-a-live-run path, closes typing from the queued item's `turnAdoptionLifecycle.onSettled`. Queue completion calls that for a run that finished, a cancelled item, a cleared queue, and the sources of a collected batch.
- The handoff happens only when the follow-up has an adoption lifecycle and queued typing actually started (`typing.isActive()` after `signalToolStart`). Without a lifecycle nothing would settle the typing. In `message` typing mode typing does not start before text, so the controller's `cleanup` never calls `onCleanup` and a deferred `onIdle` would never run. Both cases keep today's behavior. That keeps a dropped item from leaving a typing loop running forever.
- The dispatcher exposes `onTypingHandoff` only when the channel supplied a cleanup callback, because the deferred `onIdle` runs from that callback.
- Each queued `FollowupRun` now carries the typing controller of the dispatch that queued it (`typing`), and the follow-up runner completes that one (`queued.typing ?? defaults.typing`). The queue keeps only the latest runner per key, so before this an earlier queued message, when it finished, completed the later message's controller and sealed it before that message's own turn (ClawSweeper revision 6).

`waitForReplyDispatcherIdle` moved to `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-dispatcher-idle.ts` with main's current body (including its `abortSignal` handling), the queued item's `onSettled` wrap lives in `bindQueuedFollowupTyping` in `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-run-typing.ts`, and the two queued-typing cases moved to `agent-runner.runreplyagent.queued-typing.cases.ts`, so the line-cap ratchet holds for `reply-dispatcher.ts`, `agent-runner-run.ts`, and the runner e2e file.

## Evidence

- New `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-utils.test.ts` case drives a real `createReplyDispatcherWithTyping`, `createTypingController`, and `createTypingCallbacks` (channel TTL off, as on Telegram) through handoff, dispatcher idle, `markRunComplete`, and `markDispatchIdle`. On the test commit the channel `start` runs 0 times in the next 60 s. On the fix it runs 30 times, `stop` is not called during the wait, and `stop` runs once after the queued run settles.
- New `agent-runner.runreplyagent.queued-typing.cases.ts` case: a follow-up with a lifecycle queued behind a live run calls `onTypingHandoff` once and keeps typing open, and `completeFollowupRunLifecycle` on the queued item cleans typing up once. On the test commit `onTypingHandoff` is called 0 times.
- Channel with its own idle (ClawSweeper revisions 3 and 5, fixed in 0f720c428ae). The `reply-utils.test.ts` case with distinct `onReplyStart`, `onIdle`, and `onCleanup` callbacks uses fake timers: it calls the handoff option if offered, completes the run and the dispatcher, then advances 5 s. On 4f0fc716970 it fails: the controller never cleans up (`["idle"]` instead of `["cleanup", "idle"]`) and keeps calling `onReplyStart`, which is the call that reopens a Feishu preview. prs.title: perf(gateway): skip pairing recovery reads on approved connects
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A successfully approved fresh-device connection rereads the complete pairing list only to compute a recovery request ID used on failure. Keep that lookup in the failed-pairing branch. Successful connections skip one shared-state worker request; a list cache miss can also avoid four statements.

The final live paired-device read remains in place with public-key, role, scope, pinned metadata and bootstrap-profile validation. No schema, SDK, cache owner, synchronous database path or service lifecycle changes.

Accepted edge: an approval arriving after the final live authority read can require a reconnect; it cannot authorize the already-rejected connection. A recovery-list snapshot does not grant access.

## Measurement

One live baseline/candidate pair, ten warmed turns each, shared SQL harness 2.1.0. Base `96db2f6dfa4f47fd579a6d8408011950b8af53e1`; candidate `037b81dc386650abdc8db948750550c9fecd8bec`; manifest actualHead and environment hashes verified. The original shared harness is untouched. The private candidate copy adds only the supported 120-second handshake allowance; observer, causal classifier, provider routing and workload match the baseline.

| Window | Base SQL / requests / MAIN | Candidate SQL / requests / MAIN |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Warmed causal median [range] | 180 [180–188] / 43 [43–47] / 0 | 180 [180–194] / 43 [43–47] / 0 |
| Warmed raw median [range] | 211.5 [190–235] / 54 [47–65] / 0 | 223.5 [190–249] / 58.5 [47–67] / 0 |
| BOOT | 950 / 80 / 756 | 956 / 85 / 755 |
| CONNECT | 100 / 22 / 10 | 1243 / 63 / 22 |
| First turn, raw | 1896 / 196 / 51 | 709 / 134 / 38 |
| First turn, causal | 383 / 81 / 38 | 381 / 78 / 38 |
| Whole workload | 6817 / 1270 / 833 | 6952 / 1311 / 839 |

**Owned operation:** `device-pairing.ts:listDevicePairing` falls from two requests to one during CONNECT (4 → 4 SQL). The removed recovery lookup was a cache hit in the baseline. `getPairedDevice` remains two requests (4 → 8 SQL); its final read reloads the existing shared snapshot in this candidate. Both functions call `readCachedDevicePairingStoreSnapshot` with the same snapshot loader, so the removed list does not provide separate cache preparation. Other shared-state work interleaves with pairing in the candidate. This pair demonstrates one fewer handshake request (9 → 8), with handshake SQL 68 → 72; it does **not** demonstrate a net connection SQL saving. A separate earlier sample observed the removed list itself paying the four-statement reload.

CONNECT includes a one-second post-hello settle plus concurrent startup. Its large increase includes agent admission (718 SQL), writer-queue work (277), usage refresh (18), memory startup (24), worker preparation (13), cron/health and maintenance. These are existing owners in a different window, not new pairing requests. BOOT+CONNECT+first SQL is 2946 → 2908. The full workload rises 2.0% in SQL and 3.2% in requests; these raw totals are reported, not presented as savings.

Shared read families, mean causal statements per warmed turn: exact-entry facts 4.1 → 4.2; actor hydration 1.1 → 1.1; entry-cache loads 0 → 0; row facts 0 → 0; watermark reads 1 → 1. Raw means: exact-entry 4.6 → 4.8, entry-cache 1 → 1.1, row-facts primary SELECT 0 → 0.1 (envelope 0 → 0.5), watermark 1 → 1.1. The extra causal exact-entry read appears in existing turn-6 transcript hydration/entry-read work; no warm path, cache, receipt or worker routing is changed. Warmed causal mean SQL is 180.8 → 181.4 with identical mean requests 43.4. The median and MAIN count do not rise.

Latency is unmeasured: this 32-core host's load was 95.61/101.06/107.81 at candidate start and 92.70/106.74/109.48 at finish. No first-snapshot or ready-time gain is claimed from this loaded run.

## Evidence

The real-WebSocket security matrix retains actual approval, rejection, revocation, key replacement, role replacement, narrower scopes, pinned metadata and client-identity cases. Its approval case verifies that the recovery list is not read. The two old before/after-recovery-list timing cases collapse because the approved path no longer performs that read. No production test hook is introduced.

Local formatting, changed-file type-aware lint and diff checks pass. Codex autoreview completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings. Measured-head CI passed: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38342649270 (production/test types, lint, source contracts, Madge, database ratchets, and changed tests). The changed real-WebSocket test file passed in 39.44 seconds in CI. The initial Knip scan found obsolete UI exports already fixed on main. Main was merged without conflicts into `7884867c5617c1ff11b038a4ba3f1322108ec58a`; the pairing diff is unchanged. Integrated-head CI [38344921233](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38344921233) passed behavioral tests, lint, source contracts, Madge and database ratchets. Its sole failed leaf is `check-test-types-core-4`: `src/commands/config-preflight-snapshot.test.ts:41` imports the now-private `readConfigPreflightSnapshot` (TS2724), introduced on main by #170530. Those implementation/test blobs match main; the central config-preflight repair lane already owns the regression. This uses the inherited-failure landing exception, not a green-CI claim. The integrated Knip scan has one inherited UI finding: `ui/src/components/board/board-widget-cell-render.ts: renderBoardWidgetError`. Main scheduled run [38343322520](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38343322520/job/115119178402) reports the identical finding in both production and full-tree scans; the file and Knip configuration are unchanged by this PR. The script-export scan passes. Local core type-aware lint and formatting pass on the integrated head.

T1 inventory in CI: 455 → 455; retained compatibility exceptions 9 → 9. The changed Gateway owner has no direct main-thread SQLite calls (T1 0 → 0). Changed-file dialect groups 0 → 0. No SDK diff or update cell applies: this changes connect-time recovery metadata lookup, not update, Doctor, migration, plugin loading or service lifecycle.

Diff: two files, production +7/−6 and test +16/−15 (total +23/−21). Release-note context: avoid an unnecessary pairing-recovery read before a successfully approved device receives its first Gateway snapshot.

prs.title: fix: resolve plugin-discovered models outside the agent workspace
prs.body:
Fixes an issue where users who open a session in a folder outside the agent workspace would see "This model was not found" for plugin-discovered models that the picker still lists as available.

Closes #169205

## What Problem This Solves

A session whose working directory is outside the agent workspace fails the first turn for plugin-discovered models such as `zai` and `opencode-go`, while the Control UI picker still offers those models. Static providers in the same session continue to resolve.

## Why This Change Was Made

`acquirePreparedModelRuntimeLeaseFromOwners` copied the published catalog only when `ownerKey` matched, and `ownerKey` includes `workspaceDir`. An outside session cwd therefore kept its own empty run catalog instead of the configured agent's published discovery rows.

Gateway turns share the boot inventory already prepared for the configured agent. When that generation is current and supports the requested selection, an outside execution folder reuses that owner and its catalog. Admission does not resolve plugin metadata again, and it does not build a second generation. Agent, auth directory, environment, and selection support still have to match. Standalone hosts stay workspace-scoped: a different directory keeps its own catalog.

This follows the plugin architecture contract: a Gateway projects one immutable boot inventory for every run workspace, while direct CLI runs in another workspace keep a workspace-scoped generation. Execution cwd remains the session folder.

Main's asynchronous metadata preparation is unchanged. The earlier synchronous identity check during admission is gone.

Non-goals: no picker or chat-metadata change, no credential or config change, and no live vendor account.

## User Impact

A session opened on a folder outside the agent workspace resolves plugin-discovered models the picker already lists, and the turn still runs in that folder. The models come from the Gateway inventory prepared at startup, not from a fresh scan of the outside folder.

## Evidence

Production change versus main: `src/agents/prepared-model-runtime-lease.ts` +43 / -7. Head `eb6874ca436` does not change that file.

Admission regressions now follow the shared inventory. A covered outside-folder run keeps the configured workspace on the snapshot and does not build a second catalog. The admission input still names the execution folder. Reload recovery keeps the same split. The aggregate-failure case reaches preparation through credential-skipping admission, which is outside the shared owner, and still returns that aggregate error. Eight Gateway run owners that load plugins still retain the live registration.

Lease regression in `src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.gateway-leases.test.ts`: an outside-folder run with a covered provider reuses the published Gateway snapshot and plugin generation, and does not load the plugin registry again. An uncovered provider still builds its own generation.

The behavior proof is a built Gateway process, `node dist/index.js gateway`, driven by `node dist/index.js gateway call`. The binary was built from `9aec84f9359d3b9a1225d169f642eba2f36f3779`. `eb6874ca436` changes tests only, so that transcript still covers the production lease.

`proof-discovery/discovered-only` is published by a plugin catalog and is absent from `config.models.providers`. Static config only contains `proof-static/static-marker`. The provider stands in for `zai` / `opencode-go`. The account key is a fixture. Traffic stays on loopback: `GET /v1/catalog` and `POST /v1/responses`.

Redacted live output:

```
SHIPPED_GATEWAY_VERDICT {"entrypoint":"node dist/index.js gateway","model":"proof-discovery/discovered-only","pickerListed":true,"discoveryProviderInStaticConfig":false,"staticConfigModels":["static-marker"],"outsideTurn":{"label":"outside-folder","cwdKind":"outside-folder","spawnedCwdMatchesRequest":true,"sendStatus":"started","waitStatus":"ok","replyVisible":true},"workspaceTurn":{"label":"workspace-session","cwdKind":"configured-workspace","spawnedCwdMatchesRequest":true,"sendStatus":"started","waitStatus":"ok","replyVisible":true},"providerRequests":["GET /v1/catalog","POST /v1/responses","POST /v1/responses"],"endpoint":"loopback"}
```

The outside-folder cwd is a sibling of the configured workspace. `sessions.create` kept that cwd (`spawnedCwdMatchesRequest: true`). `chat.send` started, `agent.wait` returned `ok`, and `chat.history` contained `DISCOVERY_TURN_ANSWER`. The configured-workspace control did the same with its own cwd. Absolute paths, the gateway token, and the fixture key are omitted.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes opaque update reports when a dependency reaches OpenClaw-owned files or Gateway recovery readiness cannot be verified.

## User Impact

Operators get a stable `host-owned-plugin-link` reason, link-repair instructions and documentation, and observed service status with a `gateway status --deep` next step. Shared support reports retain the service status and command while excluding private startup text and profile arguments. Recovery guidance preserves verified-serving and unsafe-restart facts; runtime retention remains required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing retention owner records a typed refusal, and existing report/guidance consumers explain the next step. Readiness diagnostics reuse captured observations without another probe or an invented startup cause. The public redactor projects only the closed service status and a canonical read-only command; arbitrary diagnostic prose remains redacted.

The installed updater performs retention before package replacement. A corrected candidate cannot repair that older driver's first step, and an old driver cannot emit these new diagnostics. This patch does not change retention, admission, rollback, or restart policy or claim published-driver activation proof.

## Evidence
