prs.title: refactor(storage): make shared-state identities portable (v22)
prs.body:
Related: #169254, [v22 addendum](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/169254#issuecomment-6129843452), [combined-v22 sequencing](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/169254#issuecomment-6131216265), #170059, #170055, #170084.

## Prepared-selection authority regression

The failing CI run tested the PR merged with newer main, including #170470. The original PR head passed all 16 selection-authority cases locally; both reported role/alias cases also passed under Node 24. Pre-fix main `2bd6ca195418c5ff269439f02dd4b0b9b7c664b0` independently failed exactly those two cases (14 passed), reproducing CI's missing-revocation assertion.

Schema admission renewed an integrity epoch, replacing the profile authority store while native role/alias publishers retained the old store. Workshop change identity and ordering were unrelated. This branch now incorporates main's [c445da4029e17](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c445da4029e17aca9bf1288c08389dc35698d634) repair, which separates physical-owner lifetime from renewable schema integrity proof. No additional production code or Workshop change was needed. The existing role/alias cases are the regression tests.

Final head: [`649d54ac75429`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/649d54ac754290a9c5b80d61fc8dfbf31d267984), merging main through `877301a3af040`.

Final merged-head verification: all 46 cases passed across seven suites with `--maxWorkers=1`: selection authority (16), Workshop (2), v22 parity/upgrade (4), profile authority (7), and ACP writer/cache/resume (17). The existing role/alias cases fail on pre-fix main and pass with the upstream repair. Vitest times: unit 134.54s, infra 936.01s, ACP 94.68s. Compiler verification completed. Exact-head [PostgreSQL conformance passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38343100840/job/115118790978) in [run 38343100840](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38343100840), on `649d54ac754290a9c5b80d61fc8dfbf31d267984`. The broader CI run is not green; failures are recorded below.

All 15 PostgreSQL generator tests and canonical/workboard DDL freshness checks passed; `pendingPromotion` is empty. Wrapper inventory, formatting, `git diff --check`, and madge (zero cycles) passed. Core and generator lint passed. Extension lint could not start because plugin-SDK declaration preparation hit its unchanged 300-second timeout twice. Hosted extension lint subsequently passed on the same exact head in [job 115118791075](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38343100840/job/115118791075), closing the local lint verification gap. No timeout or guard was changed.

The final PR delta remains +169 production/config lines, +544 test lines, +26 documentation lines, and +10 generated lines. This repair adds no PR-specific production code; main's owner repair is +25/-5 production lines. No manual merge resolutions were needed.

## Current exact-head CI failures

The requested PostgreSQL job passed. The following failures remain; none is counted as passing proof or waived for landing:

| Job | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| `checks-node-changed-compact-large-36` | `session-row-projection.backfill.test.ts` expects an own `lastMessagePreview: undefined` property on a sparse row. Main already corrects that fixture in [c363cb3594479](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c363cb3594479). This PR changes neither that test nor its projection owner. |
| `check-lint` | UI Lit migration guard lists older UI files. This PR has no UI diff; newer main contains the Solid ports, including #169725. |
| `check-dependencies` | Knip reports unused admission, skill-refresh, metadata-origin and UI symbols outside this PR's changed files. |
| `build-artifacts` | Workboard's generated plugin asset manifest differs from committed bytes; there is no Workboard diff in this PR. |
| Real-Gateway UI shards 1/2 and 2/2 | Prebuilt/source-clean admission fails before UI cases run. |
| `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-10` | Codex native pending-command fake-timer assertion fails at `run-attempt.dynamic-tools.test.ts:78`; unresolved. |
| `checks-windows-node-test-2` | PowerShell cross-OS installer timeout; unresolved. |
| Node changed shards 14, 19, 21 | Session-reconnect, exec-approval and node-worker-launch E2E cases time out; unresolved. |
| `checks-node-changed-compact-large-19` | Plugin trust diagnostics lack prepared runtime config; matches the previously documented main failure. |

These results are from [run 38343100840](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38343100840). Remaining jobs were still running at this snapshot. The draft remains open; no merge is claimed.

## What Problem This Solves

ACP resume indexes and shared-state receipt cursors depended on SQLite JSON expressions and implicit rowid identities, preventing equivalent PostgreSQL storage.

## Behavior and Ownership

The typed ACP metadata owner uses one identity binding for runtime writes and Doctor identity rewrites. It trims only string resume IDs and writes both promoted columns in the same upsert as `identity_json`. Missing and non-string IDs become NULL. The v22 migration uses SQLite's guarded `json_type` and `json_extract`, preserving native first-duplicate-key behavior for historical rows. Resume lookup compares the indexed columns directly, without parsing identity JSON or applying a post-filter. The scalar/number parser has been deleted. JSON stays canonical; receipts and the accepted cohort-cache lifetime are unchanged.

Approvals, cron receipts, execution decision facts, and Skill Workshop changes receive unique `cursor_id` columns. Migration preserves original rowids, including gaps, and existing opaque cursor formats. Writers allocate `max(cursor_id) + 1` inside their existing transactions. Legacy approval repair recognizes a pinned pre-v22 schema and supplies the cursor column during its rebuild. One migration kind declares all five affected tables. PostgreSQL generation has an empty `pendingPromotion` list.

Existing resume results, cursors, and insertion ordering survive the v21-to-v22 upgrade. Older builds refuse v22; rollback restores the verified pre-upgrade backup with its matching build. No configuration, retention, or authorization change is introduced.

## Accepted Edges

- A lone-surrogate resume ID may not round-trip, so that session does not resume.
- `cursor_id = max(cursor_id) + 1` re-issues the cursor of a deleted top row, as implicit rowid did. A reader paging `> N` can miss a new row N. This is rare because retention prunes the oldest rows.

PostgreSQL text still cannot hold NUL; data-port preflight owns that limitation. This change proves schema conformance, not full PostgreSQL runtime support.

## Pre-rebase evidence

Current verification with `--maxWorkers=1`: all four v22 parity/upgrade tests, all three wrapper-inventory tests, both resume tests, and the selected Doctor ownership/identity rewrite regression passed. The six-suite ACP infra run passed 39 of 40 cases; the independent clear-writer child hit its unchanged 60-second process timeout after reporting imports ready and write start. It never reported write settlement. That clear branch and its test/process harness are unchanged by this reduction; its isolated replay passed with the same timeout and assertions (102.33s case, 339.35s Vitest). That passing replay does not establish a timing fix; the original timeout remains documented.

The other receipt/cohort, metadata read, memory, write, control, and reset cases passed. The full multi-project command took 1,988.29s; the resume command took 206.75s, and the selected Doctor command took 593.82s. The final parity body took 426ms, including exhaustive whitespace verification. All 14 PostgreSQL generator tests and both generated-DDL freshness checks passed. Type-aware lint, formatting, whitespace, and madge (zero cycles) passed. The dialect guard remains shrink-only (design 34→32, engine-maintenance 25→25); `pendingPromotion` remains empty.

The string parity test exercises the actual metadata writer against migration SQL for trimmed/untrimmed text, the complete whitespace set, Unicode, empty-after-trim strings, and missing/non-string fields. It checks every Unicode code point against the exact 25-character SQL whitespace set. Native migration cases cover invalid JSON and duplicate keys. The Doctor regression verifies that normalizing duplicate-key JSON refreshes the promoted resume column through the same binding. Runtime and Doctor v21 upgrade tests preserve cursor gaps, opaque cursor decoding, ordering, and resume results.

Retained proof for unchanged cursor owners: 51 tests across six suites, six legacy approval migration tests, three historical upgrade regressions, and version/refusal plus publication/restart migration enumerations passed. The prior local Doctor orphan-repair test timed out at its unchanged 120-second limit; a following repair case also failed. These earlier failures remain unresolved and are not counted as passing proof.

Pre-rebase final-head Codex autoreview was clean. The landing rebase retains that reviewed implementation.

Net production/config lines: +169; tests +549; docs +26; generated output +10. No reserved owner file changed.

<details>
<summary>Rowid inventory and schema-bump coverage</summary>

| Site | Disposition |
| --- | --- |
| `operator-approval-store.receipts.ts` / approval writer | Explicit `operator_approvals.cursor_id`; existing wire `rowId` retained. |
| `execution-owner-lifecycle-receipts.ts` / cron writer | Explicit `cron_run_receipts.cursor_id`; same timestamp/cursor ordering. |
| `execution-decision-facts.ts` | Explicit `execution_decision_facts.cursor_id`; existing receipt-key ordering and wire selectors retained. |
| `skills/workshop/changes.kernel.ts` | Explicit `skill_workshop_changes.cursor_id`; preserves insertion-order ties and pruning. |
| `openclaw-state-db-schema-v22-columns.ts`, `openclaw-state-db-operator-approval-migration.ts` | Keep rowid only as the one-time historical backfill source. |
| `openclaw-state-db-schema-additive.ts` | Keep historical diagnostic-event sequence backfill; runtime already uses explicit sequence. |
| `doctor-session-incognito-key-repair-state.ts` | Keep SQLite-only offline repair's row address within its owning transaction; no exposed cursor. |
| `openclaw-state-db-task-delivery-recovery.ts` | Keep SQLite-only preservation/export identity for orphan recovery; no runtime cursor. |
| `update-database-restore-source.ts` | Keep lossless SQLite backup restoration, including original physical rowids. |
| `openclaw-migration-witness.ts`, `snapshot/git-backup-codec.ts` | Keep SQLite physical-data witness/backup addressing; no shared-state runtime cursor. |
| SQLite infrastructure (`sqlite-integrity`, `sqlite-strict`, `sqlite-schema-contract-assembly`, `kysely-sync`) | Keep native SQLite diagnostics, physical rebuild semantics, and adapter internals. |
| Message receipt `rowId` / audit sequence | Already derives from explicit sequence/stage keys; no implicit rowid. |
| Agent transcript/FTS, session projection, and context-engine outbox owners | Agent database, outside this shared-state migration. |

No still-reserved owner files were changed. Schema-bump coverage includes the typed migration-to-tables map, runtime/Doctor migration registration, native version limit, version-constant assertions, publication/restart migration enumerations, raw-SQL migration markers, eager wrapper import inventory, generated types, and regenerated PostgreSQL fragments.

</details>

Earlier landing candidate: `754ff2fd53f6709a0808862962272c15a42baf9a`. Rebased onto main after #170266 and regenerated PostgreSQL artifacts into its single runtime DDL form. All four v22 preservation/parity/upgrade cases passed on the rebased implementation (`pnpm test src/state/openclaw-state-db-schema-v22-columns.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 422.33s command wall time, 370.91s Vitest). `pnpm db:postgres:gen` and `pnpm db:postgres:check` passed, including all 15 generator cases, canonical/workboard freshness, and `pendingPromotion: []`. The previously reviewed schema-owner reuse and Doctor migration descriptions are preserved. 

The pre-rebase head passed PostgreSQL conformance, while [CI run 38327468439](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38327468439) reported Knip/runtime-config failures and unresolved node-worker lifecycle/launch assertions. These are prior-head evidence, not passing CI for the landing head; final-head attribution remains pending.

## Landing CI classification and fixture repair

The rebased [CI run 38331192286](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38331192286) completed with four failed test jobs. The two schema-fixture failures are repaired in this head; production code is unchanged by the repair. Focused validation passed for both cases: the legacy Doctor fixture (274.89s command wall time) and the older-reader decision/reopen fixture (329.16s through the repository Node test wrapper). Targeted lint, formatting, and Codex autoreview are clean. 

| Failure | Classification and evidence |
| --- | --- |
| `openclaw-state-db.test.ts`: migrate operator approvals to system-agent records | Fixed stale fixture. It now uses the frozen pre-v22 DDL instead of synthesizing a legacy table from v22 DDL. The actual Doctor repair passes. |
| `operator-approval-store.execution-identity.test.ts`: older reader write/reopen | Fixed obsolete physical-schema assertion. The historical row reader still proves decoding, decision writes, schema-version preservation, and companion identity through the current database owner; an old binary admitting v22 is not the contract. |
| `loader.trust-diagnostics.test.ts`: runtime config not prepared | Inherited: matching cases fail on [main run 38331230273, job 115081408121](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38331230273/job/115081408121). The failing code is unchanged from main; all 22 recorded files in the PR job are disjoint from this PR. |
| `telegram-ingress-coalescing.e2e.test.ts`: test/hook and no-output timeouts | Unrelated under the authorized causal-path rule: all nine planned files in the failed job are disjoint from this PR. No timeout was raised and no production Telegram change is included. |

prs.title: fix(agents): resume startup recovery after the boot scope closes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After a gateway SIGKILL, restart recovery marks the orphaned main session and then each resume throws `AbortError` from the startup `AsyncWorkScope` that `runGatewayLoop` closes as soon as the listener is up. Three immediate failures exhaust the retry budget and tombstone the session, so `gateway-kill-restart-send` fails on main and on unrelated PRs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Startup recovery attempts used independent root admission, which keeps the caller's async-work owner. That owner is the boot scope, already aborted by `iterationStartupOperations.close()`. Embedded runs treat that signal as parent cancellation, so resume never starts.

Detached work admission gives each startup attempt its own live scope. The scheduler abort controller is still passed through, so shutdown and lifecycle rotation still cancel attempts. Exhaustion tombstones and owner-release admission are unchanged.

## User Impact

An interrupted main session can continue after a hard gateway kill instead of showing the "couldn't continue this session after a gateway restart" tombstone.

## Evidence

Head `3820d53fa6824b9ee46f7333737b8f2948848ada`.

Isolated local Gateway child, throwaway state dir. SIGKILL of pid `3553995` during an in-flight `agent:qa:main` turn, then a new child pid `3555635`.

- Log: `gateway child exited unexpectedly (exitCode=null, signal=SIGKILL)`.
- Log: `marked 1 startup-orphaned main session(s) for restart recovery`.
- Log: `dispatching restart-safe recovery for agent:qa:main`.
- Recovery candidate for session `9b6a34ea-e431-4cd8-8f60-1804255616c9`: `decision=started`, `reason=dispatch_started`, then `startup complete: started=1 settled=0 failed=0 skipped=0`.
- Terminal: `main-session restart recovery terminal: session=agent:qa:main run=37d40b68-7a02-41e3-8339-f570c3ae451d status=ok reason=completed`.
- Same session settled `status=done`. A later inbound message received its reply (`sameReplyTarget=true`). No "couldn't continue this session after a gateway restart" tombstone.
- The model endpoint was loopback mock `http://127.0.0.1:33133`. No live provider key.

Fixes openclaw/openclaw#167602

prs.title: fix(a2a): return push-specific unsupported errors
prs.body:
Closes #167591

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the generic unsupported-operation error returned when an authenticated A2A peer requests push notification configuration.

## User Impact

A2A clients receive `PushNotificationNotSupportedError` (`-32003`) instead of `UnsupportedOperationError` (`-32004`). Push notifications remain disabled. No configuration, authentication, or persistence behavior changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin advertises A2A **1.0** and already advertises `pushNotifications: false`. The [A2A 1.0.0 capability-validation contract](https://a2a-protocol.org/v1.0.0/specification/#334-capability-validation) requires the push-specific error; its [error mapping](https://a2a-protocol.org/v1.0.0/specification/#54-error-code-mappings) assigns `PushNotificationNotSupportedError` code `-32003`.

Keep that mapping in the existing protocol owner. Preserve all six already-recognized spellings, including the legacy Set and singular List names; add no aliases. One HTTP table covers push methods and neighboring unsupported/unknown methods. Existing authentication, batch, and notification tests retain those independent boundaries without duplicating them per push method.

Thanks to @clawSean for the report and original fix. No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

## Evidence

Built isolated Gateways with the bundled A2A plugin enabled, then sent authenticated JSON-RPC requests over HTTP to `/a2a/v1`. Baseline: `b1c08d51fab31699976751e3a57ade20c06d1ac1`; candidate: `217f8efcec5` (current-main merge included).

Both Agent Cards returned:

```json
{"supportedInterfaces":[{"protocolBinding":"JSONRPC","protocolVersion":"1.0"}],"capabilities":{"streaming":false,"pushNotifications":false}}
```

Observed HTTP 200 responses:

| Method | Baseline error | Candidate error |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| CreateTaskPushNotificationConfig | -32004 | -32003 |
| SetTaskPushNotificationConfig | -32004 | -32003 |
| GetTaskPushNotificationConfig | -32004 | -32003 |
| ListTaskPushNotificationConfig | -32004 | -32003 |
| ListTaskPushNotificationConfigs | -32004 | -32003 |
| DeleteTaskPushNotificationConfig | -32004 | -32003 |
| UnknownTaskPushNotificationConfig | -32601 | -32601 |
| SendStreamingMessage | -32004 | -32004 |

Candidate response excerpt:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"CreateTaskPushNotificationConfig","error":{"code":-32003,"message":"Push notifications are not supported"}}
```

- Regression table on baseline: six push cases failed with actual `-32004`; all four controls passed.
- Candidate: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/a2a/src/http.test.ts extensions/a2a/src/protocol.test.ts`: **38 passed**, two files; **24.11s** wrapper wall time (cold compiled-worker cache). Hosted CI owns broader checks.
- Changed-file Oxfmt and Oxlint passed inside the isolated container.
- Simplification removed the transport-specific branch and redundant push-specific authentication/batch tests. Against the merge base: production **+7/-1**, tests **+27/-0**, docs **+2/-0**. The small production growth separates two different protocol errors without introducing another owner.

Two-way door: reverting restores the old error code without state or config migration. Blast radius is authenticated A2A clients requesting unsupported push configuration; unknown methods and other unsupported operations retain their existing errors.

prs.title: fix(talk): add consult correlation tests for current main APIs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Browser Talk consult handoffs incorrectly treated Gateway interruption timeouts (`gateway_draining`) as successful no-text completion. When the Gateway lifecycle reset during a consult, it emits `status: timeout` with `timeoutPhase: gateway_draining`. The prior code treated this as a non-terminal timeout, allowing the 500ms empty-final fallback to fire and return "OpenClaw finished with no text" instead of propagating the proper interruption error to the voice provider.

This fix classifies `gateway_draining` as a terminal timeout metadata indicator, so the consult listener rejects the observation promptly with a timeout error, matching the intended behavior.

> **Note on branch history:** an earlier push on this branch added a root `CLAUDE.md`. Review asked for
> that guidance to be separated, so it is reverted here and this PR contains only the consult-correlation
> change. The guidance content is preserved outside the repository and is intended for its own change.

## What This Changes

### `shared.ts`
- **Restores the canonical `AgentWaitResult` import from `src/agents/run-wait.types.ts` (as `GatewayAgentWaitResult`)** — the projection was deliberately introduced by #162766 and preserves optional UI fields and open strings. This resolves the ClawSweeper P2 finding "Restore the Gateway-derived wait response projection".
- Adds `gateway_draining` as a terminal timeout metadata indicator — a Gateway lifecycle reset emits `status: timeout` with `timeoutPhase: gateway_draining`, which should be treated as an interrupted observation, not a successful no-text completion.
- Preserves the nonterminal timeout guard: bare `{status: "timeout"}` results (no metadata) do not reach the 500ms empty-final success fallback.
- Replaces the loose `message !== undefined` terminal check with `hasErrorMessage`, so an empty `error` string no longer counts as terminal evidence.
- The outer 120s consultation deadline remains the ultimate timeout.

### `consult.test.ts`
- 23 test cases (up from 14 on main) covering the terminal-timeout classes (`gateway_draining`, `post_turn`, `preflight`, `stopReason: "timeout"`), the nonterminal bare-timeout regression guard, runId matching, the `state: "aborted"` cancellation path, and the two retained behavioural cases below.
- Two of these were flagged as redundant during review and are deliberately **retained**, because each pins a contract the others cannot:
  - `prefers source-reply final text over an earlier empty Talk consult final` is the only case where the empty final and the source reply race with **zero elapsed time** — no fake timers, no deferred promise. Its three siblings all inject a delay, so it is the only proof that final-text selection keys on the message being *empty* rather than on which final arrived first.
  - `speaks status and cancel acknowledgements when requested by active consult steering` is the only unit assertion of the default speech gate (`speak === true && suppress !== true`) for a non-steer mode, in the file that owns `maybeSpeakRealtimeTalkControlResult`. The other two speech tests cover only the suppression branch and the legacy suppressed-steer disjunct.
  Both were previously deleted in a test-reduction pass and re-added by the commit that opened this branch; removing them again would drop coverage rather than consolidate setup.

### `extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-draining-consult.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`
Real-Gateway E2E proving the **wire contract** the consult listener keys on.

- Drives the Code Mode restart-wait fixture, which holds the run on a real `wait` tool call, and synchronizes on that call being in flight before interrupting. `sessions.list` is the authoritative active-run observation: it reads the row's `hasActiveRun`/`status` projection with real types (`ControlUiSessionListResult` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/control-ui`) rather than casting a raw store shape, then confirms the assistant `wait` tool call is still unfinished in the session transcript.
- The run is reached via `chat.send`, which returns the `runId` immediately with the run in flight.
- The `agent.wait` observation is opened with the same call the Browser Talk listener uses and is proven **pending** before interruption: if it settled (rejected or resolved) without the reset, the test fails instead of asserting a value the reset never produced.
- Interruption uses the supported Gateway lifecycle API, not a process kill: `gateway.restart.request` with `safe: true, skipDeferral: true`. `skipDeferral` bypasses the active-work deferral gate so the lifecycle reset actually retires the in-flight wait (`src/infra/restart.ts:118-119`); the equivalent CLI path is `openclaw gateway restart --safe --skip-deferral`.
- Asserts exactly `{status: "timeout", timeoutPhase: "gateway_draining"}`, which is what the wait owner emits for an interrupted observation (`src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-job.ts:710`). A rejected wait fails loudly rather than silently asserting `undefined`.
- Lives in `extensions/qa-lab/src` beside `gateway-kill-restart-send.e2e.test.ts`, its closest analog, because `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.ui-e2e.json` includes `ui/src/e2e/**/*.test.ts`, which makes any file there a **core** tsgo graph root that may not reach `extensions/**`. Keeping it under `ui/src/e2e` failed `check-test-types-core-{1..5}` and `check-additional-boundaries` with "Core tsgo graphs include bundled extension files".

### CI routing (corrected)

- Registered in `uiE2eRealGatewayTestFiles` (required — the shard planner filters on that array, so absence selects no lane), `uiE2ePrebuiltParallelTestFiles`, and the Control UI E2E ownership inventory at `test/scripts/ci-ui-e2e-ownership.test-support.ts`.
- **Removed from the frozen-target explicit operand list** in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. That list is a historical compatibility inventory for frozen targets that predate the prebuilt E2E config, and it is intentionally independent of the current registry: `ci-workflow-guards.test.ts` asserts it against `frozenRealGatewayFiles`, a separate constant, not against `uiE2eRealGatewayTestFiles`. Adding the new test there both wrongly expanded the frozen inventory and broke the guard. The frozen inventory itself is **not** modified.
- **Added to `RELEASE_ONLY_UI_TEST_FILES`** in `scripts/lib/ci-proof-test-inventory.mts` (this PR's head was based on an older `main`; upstream has since moved that set out of `ci-node-test-plan.mts` into `ci-proof-test-inventory.mts` and routed its entries through `resolveUiTypeScriptPath()`, and this branch was merged to follow that refactor). This is the existing release-only tier for slow Gateway-boot / browser / lifecycle compositions, per-root AGENTS.md test-cost policy. The planner keeps directly edited release-only files on PRs while dropping them from routine plans, so this PR still exercises the test:
  - routine main-shaped plan → excluded from the real-Gateway lane
  - directly changed path → still selected
- The associated release-only count assertion in `ci-workflow-guards.test.ts` now derives its expected remainder from `RELEASE_ONLY_UI_TEST_FILES` rather than a hand-counted literal, so adding or removing a composition cannot rot it again.

## What the proof establishes, and what it does not

**Established (real Gateway, no fakes):** a lifecycle reset during an unsettled run retires the pending `agent.wait` observation and resolves it as the exact wire response `{status: "timeout", timeoutPhase: "gateway_draining"}`, requested through the supported interrupting lifecycle API rather than a process kill.

**Not established here:** that the browser Talk listener forwards that response through the realtime voice transport. The 23 unit tests in `consult.test.ts` cover the classification half (the tag is terminal and rejects the consult) with a stubbed transport; they do not exercise a real browser submitting the correlated error on a real data channel.

**A full Browser Talk + real Gateway proof has not been built yet.** To drive the transport, the browser must call `talk.client.create` against the real Gateway. That resolves through `resolveConfiguredRealtimeVoiceProvider` (`src/talk/provider-resolver.ts:104`), and the only realtime voice provider implementing `createBrowserSession` is the OpenAI extension, whose `isBrowserSessionConfigured` requires real platform auth (`extensions/openai/realtime-voice-provider-factory.ts:441`) and whose browser session POSTs to a hardcoded `https://api.openai.com/v1/realtime/client_secrets` (`extensions/openai/realtime-provider-shared.ts:64`) with no configurable base URL and no test override. So the shipped provider cannot be driven offline without a live credential. To drive the transport, the browser must call `talk.client.create` against the real Gateway. That resolves through `resolveConfiguredRealtimeVoiceProvider` (`src/talk/provider-resolver.ts:104`), and the only realtime voice provider implementing `createBrowserSession` is the OpenAI extension, whose `isBrowserSessionConfigured` requires real platform auth (`extensions/openai/realtime-voice-provider-factory.ts:441`) and whose browser session POSTs to a hardcoded `https://api.openai.com/v1/realtime/client_secrets` (`extensions/openai/realtime-provider-shared.ts:64`) with no configurable base URL and no test override. So the offline path would require either a live credential or product changes to the provider surface.

The remaining gap is the provider seam, not the Gateway: provider resolution reads the plugin capability catalog (`src/talk/provider-resolver.ts:104`), and the browser takes its offer URL from that session (`ui/src/pages/chat/talk/webrtc-support.ts:173`), so a test-owned realtime voice provider answering a local offer URL would leave the rest of the path real. That is the intended follow-up; it is not implemented or run in this PR.

This is why every existing browser Talk test in the repo uses `installMockGateway`; none pairs Talk with a real Gateway. A mock-Gateway Talk test that hand-resolves `agent.wait` with a canned `gateway_draining` payload would assert a fabricated response and would not change behaviour on the base commit, so it is not claimed as proof here.

**Evidence classes are explicitly separated.**
- **Real Gateway, synthetic provider/model:** the qa-lab real-Gateway E2E. Real Gateway process, real lifecycle reset, real wire response; the model provider is the qa-lab mock OpenAI server.
- **Synthetic transport, unit level:** `consult.test.ts`. Classification logic with a stubbed browser transport.
- **No live voice-provider, microphone, or WebRTC evidence is claimed anywhere in this PR.**

## Evidence

- **Unit tests:** `pnpm test ui/src/pages/chat/talk/consult.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 23/23 pass, ~5s wall time.
- **Registration/release-only routing:** `pnpm test test/vitest-ui-e2e-prebuilt.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 13/13 pass; `test/scripts/ci-node-test-plan.test.ts -t release-only` — 3/3 pass.
- **Extension typecheck:** `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — 0 errors.
- **Frozen-target guard:** the failing CI case `selects the real-Gateway tier without retrying failures: {frozen:true,prebuilt:false,childExit:0}` was caused by the operand list drifting from the frozen inventory. With this change the `ci.yml` list matches upstream's `frozenRealGatewayFiles` exactly (35 file-for-file). This branch was based on an older `main` whose guard compared that list against the live registry instead, which reports a mismatch locally; the guard on this branch's current base compares against `frozenRealGatewayFiles`, which is what the integration keeps correct.
- **Release-only guard:** `selects the real-Gateway tier ... releaseTier:false` — 6/6 pass after the count assertion was derived from the inventory.
- **Real-Gateway E2E:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e-prebuilt.config.ts --configLoader runner extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-draining-consult.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`. This lane needs a Linux host with a built runtime and Chromium; it is skipped on Windows and was not executed on this branch's current host, so no pass is claimed for it here.
- **What ordinary PR CI has actually exercised:** unit, registration, release-only, and inventory/guard checks. The `checks-ui-e2e-real-gateway` lane is a conditional job that does not run on an ordinary `pull_request` event, so the new real-Gateway test has **not** been executed by CI on any head of this PR either — neither the passing Windows-side checks nor the CI runs reported here cover it.
- **Integration:** `upstream/main` was merged into the branch (not rebased) to resolve two inventory conflicts introduced by upstream's `resolveUiTypeScriptPath` refactor, and because a conflicting PR blocks `pull_request` CI entirely — a conflicting PR suppresses the `pull_request` workflow for later pushes, so the ordinary code-test jobs did not run for the previous head until the conflict was cleared. The merge is limited to following upstream's refactor plus this PR's registrations; `shared.ts` and `consult.test.ts` merged with no manual intervention.

## Test Cost
- 23 unit tests, ~5s wall time.
- 1 real-Gateway E2E case, 180s timeout, skipped on Windows; it boots a Gateway child and a mock provider. Routed to the release-only tier so routine main-shaped plans do not absorb the composition.
- Registration suites: `test/vitest-ui-e2e-prebuilt.test.ts` 13/13.

## Inherited upstream failure

`checks-node-compact-small-1` fails `test/scripts/type-suppression-inventory.test.ts` at the PR merge ref. This is not introduced by this PR: the `@ts-expect-error` it reports was added by upstream commit `04cfcd8e2587` ("fix(tooling): connect inherited cleanup sockets on Bun", 2026-10-12), which is on upstream `main` and is absent from this branch's head. That commit adds the suppression without adding it to the test's expected inventory, so the same check is red on upstream `main` independently of this PR. No change was made here to accommodate or weaken it.

## Issue
Partially addresses #142080 (queued adopted-run correlation remains a separate canonical issue)

prs.title: feat(plugins): let plugins steer a session's active run
prs.body:
Related: #170146 (session fork), #169564 (Advisor, the first consumer)

## What Problem This Solves

Plugins that notice a problem while an agent is still working can only queue context for the agent's next turn (`api.session.workflow.enqueueNextTurnInjection`). By then the run has already finished, so the agent spends the rest of the turn on the wasteful path. Core already lets users and `sessions_send` steer an active run; plugins have no access to it.

## Fix

Adds `api.session.workflow.steerActiveRun({ sessionKey, text, idempotencyKey? })`, returning `{ steered: true, runId? }` or `{ steered: false, reason }`.

- Uses the existing steering owner (`queueEmbeddedAgentMessageWithOutcomeAsync`) with the same call shape as `sessions_send` steer mode, so the built-in runner injects before the next model step and Codex receives native `turn/steer`.
- Plugin-authored and hidden: `internal_system` provenance with `sourceTool: "plugin:<id>"`, no sender or owner authority, never answers a pending user question.
- Requires the existing prompt-injection grant (`plugins.entries.<id>.hooks.allowPromptInjection`).
- Never throws for "no run accepts it": no active run, not streaming, backend rejection and missing grant return `steered: false` with the reason, so callers can fall back to `enqueueNextTurnInjection`.
- Respects plugin lifetime: the caller's plugin instance is revalidated after the lazy import and immediately before dispatch.

## User Impact

None by default; no core feature calls it. Plugins that opt in can correct an agent mid-run instead of after it finishes.

## Evidence

- Contract tests through the real plugin API factory and embedded steering queue: an active run receives the steer with plugin provenance and no sender/owner authority and does not answer a pending question; no active run returns `steered: false`; a plugin with `allowPromptInjection=false` is refused; an expired plugin instance cannot dispatch.
- Live (Codex runtime, real OpenAI API, isolated Gateway, via the Advisor plugin in #169564): a plugin steer issued mid-run was accepted (`steered: true`) and appears in the running turn's native rollout as a user item before the turn's next model request. Not observed live: the built-in runtime path, and whether the agent then changed course.
- Plugin revocation reaches final native admission (fix: `message-injection-target.ts` now composes the plugin lifetime assertion into the guard handed to V2 sinks; Codex already rechecks that guard after recorder persistence and right before the physical write, `attempt-steering.ts:302-304,350-359`). Real Codex client against a synthetic native app-server (`run-attempt.plugin-steering.test.ts`):
  - allowed guidance reaches the native server;
  - plugin disposed after the recorder persisted the item, before dispatch: rejected, `{ steered: false, reason: "runtime_rejected" }`, nothing written. Before the fix this returned `{ steered: true, runId: "run-1" }`;
  - an already-disabled plugin is rejected before queueing.
  - Totals: 3 native + 6 steering contract + 21 API lifecycle tests pass.
- Only source-guarded (V2) sinks accept plugin steering: `steerActiveRun` uses `queueGuardedEmbeddedAgentMessageWithOutcomeAsync`, so the plugin-lifetime assertion is checked up to native dispatch. A run whose runtime only has a legacy V1 sink (for example Copilot) returns `{ steered: false, reason: "active runtime does not support guarded steering" }` and nothing is queued; the caller can use next-turn injection instead. Regression: before the fix, a V1 run returned `{ steered: true }`. Totals: 62 tests across steering contract (7), `runs.steering` (31), API lifecycle (21), Codex plugin steering (3).
- Live at `0e6acc4`, real APIs, isolated Gateway, throwaway plugin that steers on the 2nd tool start (`"Also run 'echo STEERED' before you answer."`):

| Agent | Allowed steer | Effect | Plugin disabled mid-run (config hot reload) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Codex, OpenAI | `{ steered: true, runId }` | native rollout has the injected guidance, then `echo STEERED` and output `STEERED` | `{ steered: false, reason: 'Plugin "steer-probe" is no longer loaded' }`; no injected item in the rollout |
| Built-in, OpenAI `gpt-5.6-luna` | `{ steered: true, runId }` | transcript has hidden `internal_system` guidance from `plugin:steer-probe`, then `echo STEERED` output | same rejection; no injected item in the transcript |

prs.title: fix: name the last tool in the fallback shown when a tool run ends without a summary
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an agent turn ends after only calling tools and the tool-free summary pass returns nothing (both attempts), the user sees a fixed placeholder: "The tool run finished, but no final summary was produced. I did not repeat any completed actions." The message gives no hint of what ran last or whether the last step worked, so users and operators cannot tell a harmless silent finish from a failed final step without opening the transcript.

## User Impact

The fallback keeps its existing sentence verbatim and appends a short digest:

| Last tool result | Appended digest |
|---|---|
| `isError === false` | `Tool calls: N; last: <tool> (succeeded).` |
| `isError === true` | `Tool calls: N; last: <tool> (failed).` |
| `isError` absent or `undefined` | `Tool calls: N; last: <tool> (outcome unknown).` |

Example (interactive turn: `read`, then `exec`, then two empty summary attempts):

- Before: `The tool run finished, but no final summary was produced. I did not repeat any completed actions.`
- After: `The tool run finished, but no final summary was produced. I did not repeat any completed actions. Tool calls: 2; last: exec (succeeded).`

Unchanged: cron and other silent runs stay silent, and failed or timed-out turns keep their original outcome.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runner already holds the settled tool batch (`toolMetas`) when it builds the placeholder, so the digest is derived locally with no extra model call, no new setting and no new flag.

- Only the last tool name (truncated to 64 characters), the call count and the outcome are used. Arguments, results and tool metadata are never echoed, so the fallback cannot leak command lines or output.
- An absent `isError` is reported as "outcome unknown" and never as success. This follows the existing "outcome unknown" style and the producer contract that leaves the field absent for unknown terminal outcomes (this was the P2 finding from the automated review on the first revision, now fixed in the second commit).
- The change lives in the shared finalization owner (`settled-turn-finalization.ts`, new exported `buildSettledToolFallbackText`), so every channel that shows this fallback gets the same text.

Compatibility note: any consumer that matches the old fallback text exactly would need a prefix or substring match. I found one such assertion (`embedded-agent-runner.run-embedded-agent.finalization-scope.test.ts`) and relaxed it to `stringContaining`; the qa-lab e2e only checks `not.toContain`, and `chat.directive-tags` uses a fixture string.

## Evidence

Verified:

- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/settled-turn-finalization.test.ts`: 23 of 23 pass locally. New tests cover no tools (plain placeholder), last tool succeeded and failed with call count, an omitted `isError` and an explicit `undefined` (both "outcome unknown"), and that tool metadata is not echoed. Existing fallback assertions were updated.
- In CI the same test file passes in the shard that runs it (32 of 33 tests in that shard pass, including the new "reports an unknown outcome when isError is absent" test).
- oxfmt and oxlint are clean on the touched files.

Known CI failure, not caused by this diff:

- `settled-turn-finalization.unavailable.test.ts` ("preserves a failed cron turn and its transcript when finalization is unavailable") fails at the `assistantTranscriptOwned` assertion (`expected undefined to be true`). That test does not assert the digest text. It fails the same way locally with this PR's four original files reverted to base `a7b8ae74`, and the main run is also red across many shards. I have not root-caused it.

Not verified, stated plainly:

- Real-entry-point proof (redacted runtime output through a Gateway or channel) is not provided. I tried to reproduce the interactive fallback with the existing credential-free mock-provider harness (`test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/gateway-cron-idle-timeout-finalization.product-proof.e2e.test.ts`) on Windows; the Gateway did not become ready within the harness readiness window, so no turn reached the fallback and I am not quoting any output. The evidence above is unit level only.
- `finalization-scope.test.ts` fails 8 of 8 in my local Windows environment with and without this change ("Runtime config is not prepared"), so my one-line edit to that file is unverified locally and relies on CI.
- `pnpm check` stopped at two preflight guards unrelated to this diff, and I could not complete a full `pnpm build` locally.

Offer: if maintainers want runtime proof before deciding, I can produce it on a Linux runner and attach redacted logs, and I can commit the scenario as a test if wanted.

## Maintainer decision

The automated review marks this as a product preference that needs an owner decision: should the conservative missing-summary fallback include a tool count, last tool name and known or unknown outcome? I think it is a small, safe diagnostic gain, but I am happy to adjust wording, drop the docs sentence, or close the PR if the existing message is intentional.

AI-assisted PR (written with Claude); the author owns the change and will address review feedback.

prs.title: fix(feishu): accept the documented markdown table mode
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes gateway startup rejecting Feishu's documented `markdown.tables` option and applies the selected table mode across sends, replies, presentations, and previews.

## User Impact

Channel and account table settings are accepted, including the delivering/default account. Ordinary `off` table messages settle as authored rich-text posts. In `off`, presentations keep controls and show literal rows in card text and live previews. When idle close reuses a posted answer, missing reasoning follows it without duplicating it.

Accepted-prefix failures keep their receipts and do not replay accepted content. The unchanged post renderer still draws authored Markdown tables as grids.

## Why This Change Was Made

Feishu's strict schema gains the shared table option and keeps the legacy `markdown.mode` and `markdown.tableMode`. Formatting-aware delivery converts whole logical tables before chunking. Presentations and reasoning degrade undrawable block-mode tables to readable lists. For `off`, display-only delimiter escaping leaves authored fallback and deduplication text alone. The PR also declares `block` as Feishu's table default (see Table default).

The generated channel baseline rises from 4031 to 4033 for `channels.feishu.markdown.tables` and `channels.feishu.accounts.*.markdown.tables`. Core and plugin counts stay unchanged. [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f659a3576b1/AGENTS.md#L96) permits narrow source-verified exceptions with a reason. This exception is not maintainer approval.

## Evidence

### Upgrade proof

Published stable `2026.10.2` (`b8952d477f0c`) seeded channel `markdown.mode: native` and `markdown.tableMode: ascii`, an account's `mode: escape` and `tableMode: simple`, and two accounts without Markdown settings. The proof head (`effbf8c7a8ab`) used that state, main (`29fc232d40be`) a copy. Both used fresh detached worktrees and separately packed Feishu plugins.

| Check | Stable | Proof head | Upstream main |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Legacy config validates, keys and overrides read back unchanged | Yes | Yes, before and after migration | Yes, before and after migration |
| Feishu config object on disk | Seed | Byte-identical | Byte-identical |
| Stored session loads with the same key and ID, and a label update survives restart | Created and patched here | Yes | Yes |
| Documented `markdown.tables` at channel and account scope | Rejected, exit 1 | Accepted, all four values | Rejected, exit 1 |
| Account override wins, unset accounts inherit the channel value | Key rejected | Yes | Key rejected |

Both builds refuse the schema 24 agent database (Gateway exit 78) until `openclaw doctor --fix` migrates it to 26. Repair and shutdown then exit 1 with `ERR_SPAWN_BROKER_UNAVAILABLE`. The cause is undiagnosed and both databases stay readable. This is compatibility evidence, not a clean upgrade. Replacement was manual, not the published updater. Credentials were synthetic and Feishu accounts and transports disabled. Only the Feishu config object is byte-identical. Maintenance changed other config. The diff has no `src/state` change or database migration.

### Table default

Upgrade proof resolves `code` on stable and main and `block` on the proof head for unconfigured or legacy-only accounts. Legacy keys do not select the mode. In `auto`, stable and main route ordinary pipe-bordered tables to raw cards (`markdown.ts:25-27`, `outbound.ts:253-262`, `reply-dispatcher.ts:1289-1293` at main `29fc232d40be`, same logic at stable). Before captures show native grids. `block` retains them. Other modes convert before routing (`outbound-text-plan.ts:48-49`). Head lines use `948b2088919`.

Against main, standalone pipe-less and one-sided-pipe tables now get cards on `auto` sends and non-streamed replies. In chat text, blockquoted and list-opened tables take posts, but forced-card sends bypass that guard. Main sent these shapes to cards in streams or beside a fence or pipe table. Table messages needing multiple static cards also take posts. These posts use `code` unless fences cannot survive the cut. The five-table limit excludes streams. Direct post sends and edits still resolve `code`. Comments now convert raw rows to `code`. Explicit modes and size/fence safeguards apply.

A `code` default would fence those grids in cards (`outbound.markdown-tables.test.ts:662`). `block` also drops "Avoid Markdown tables." from Feishu group prompts, even with account `code` or `bullets`, because `src/auto-reply/reply/groups.ts:129-131` reads the plugin default. Telegram and Matrix already declare `block`. Maintainers decide the default.

### Current repair verification

CI on `30dc65e87a7` merged with main `c1579cff145` passed 80 checks. `checks-node-changed-1` and `openclaw/ci-gate` failed only on `telegram-ingress-coalescing.e2e.test.ts`, where one case passed and four hit test or hook timeouts before the no-output watchdog stopped it. This PR does not touch that file, and the first timeout also occurred on clean upstream `6d79ee9dd27`. The shard's seven other targets, six contract tests and a gateway e2e test, passed 115 tests. Local typecheck, four ratchets and five generated checks passed at `30dc65e87a7`. `333e9142906` then removes three helper tests, and `extension-feishu` passed 1255 tests there.

### Fresh Lark before/after rendering

[Comparison and limits](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147886#issuecomment-6093982920) cover four byte-identical synthetic fixture pairs through the production send, reply and streaming components with the real SDK. Captures compare plugin source `e7f29073f4dc` with rendering files published at `34f132a1bb49`, not whole deployments, and were not retaken at `effbf8c7a8ab`. Merges after `34f132a1bb49` left `presentation-card.ts`, `card-table-shapes.ts`, `markdown.ts` and `outbound.ts` unchanged, kept the off-mode projection in `streaming-update.ts`, and moved the reasoning formatter and close route into `reasoning-structure.ts` and `table-routing.ts` intact, so the three off-mode rows render through the same code. The idle row's settlement bookkeeping took upstream's latest-settlement shape, so that row rests on the proof head's regression tests, not the captures.

| State | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Off-mode presentation | ![Native table despite off mode](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ff00b807-a9e6-465b-9f63-5829ea331710) | ![Literal rows and retained button](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/96bf5ced-1f4e-4375-985f-cf0a9ab4132f) |
| Off-mode answer preview | ![Native answer-preview table](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e54aec3f-9a7c-41a7-886d-145522b8feed) | ![Literal answer-preview rows](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/02c9e642-b5dd-4203-a3cf-87be4de7f7aa) |
| Off-mode reasoning preview | ![Reasoning-table rows missing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/325f6680-67b2-4de6-99f7-a93a0eb9afb1) | ![Reasoning-table rows visible](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c07ea2c4-df53-4628-9793-8e1946bbf661) |
| Idle reuse of accepted answer | ![Reasoning disappears after idle](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4087a562-8abe-4253-8517-ac947981a16c) | ![One answer and separate reasoning](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/430c18ca-2774-45cc-9055-44da9e169007) |

Both runs exited 0. Idle settlement adds exactly one reasoning-only post and keeps two actual receipts without replaying the accepted answer. All three dispatcher cases keep byte-identical authored final-post payloads. The button is retained, not clicked. All eight images were verified in the saved comment. The captures used no Gateway, model or mainland Feishu client. Lark still joins adjacent quoted paragraphs in the reasoning preview, not addressed here.

### Historical evidence

Pinned to the commits named, not current-head proof.

- CLI at `dbb422c85a5` (before) and `08c0c469de4` (after). Before, `config validate` rejected `tables` at channel and account scope (exit 1) and `gateway run` refused to start (exit 78). After, validation passed, the Gateway reached ready and shut down with child exit 0, and `doctor --fix --non-interactive` removed no `markdown` key.
- Gateway send RPC at `314ddb95`, HTTPS Feishu stub, real SDK, `renderMode` unset. Accounts resolved `code`, `bullets` and `off` as configured across full, reply and default-account sends, all exit 0.
- Authority proof at `c311d8a5d53` ([comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147886#issuecomment-5707888042)), registered sender, production components, real SDK. Allowed sent four of four with every receipt. Revoked after one of four was accepted, kept its receipt and exact content in the partial-delivery envelope, and the claim guard refused the pending terminal rather than replay it.
- Lark client round at `9d52663f11b` and `d0f6e3a3ba0` ([comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147886#issuecomment-5689525610)), real SDK, 62 captures. Blockquote and list-opened tables became readable fenced posts, and a mixed message kept both tables.

prs.title: fix(crabbox): full Control UI E2E fails on fresh AWS leases
prs.body:
Related: #169677, #169288, #169680

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: full native Control UI E2E runs on Crabbox AWS/Hetzner leases report dozens of environment failures (missing Playwright FFmpeg, missing WebKit, group-writable runner directories) when the lease falls back from Testbox.

## User Impact

No product change. Maintainers can run `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts` on a freshly hydrated Crabbox Linux lease without manually installing FFmpeg/WebKit or fixing directory modes before the results mean anything.

## Why This Change Was Made

Crabbox prepares AWS/Hetzner leases by replaying the `hydrate` job of `.github/workflows/crabbox-hydrate.yml` on the box, but that job never ran the browser setup CI uses, and the image's SSH umask is `002` (Ubuntu user-private groups), so Crabbox's lease parent and run-time `.artifacts` directories came out group-writable and tripped the private-artifact ancestry guard. CI and Testbox never see this because their runners use umask `022` and run the setup steps.

One shared step in both Linux hydration jobs (`hydrate`, `hydrate-github`) now:

- removes group/other write from the workspace and every ancestor the runner user owns (stops at the first non-owned directory, never uses sudo) and from `.artifacts`, explicitly rather than via umask;
- installs Playwright Chromium + FFmpeg with CI's `scripts/ensure-playwright-chromium.mts --require-playwright-chromium`, then WebKit with system dependencies via CI's `pnpm --dir ui exec playwright install --with-deps webkit`.

The run env handoff also sets `umask go-w`, so directories created during later `crabbox run` commands match CI's permissions; stricter masks are preserved. Testbox, CI workflows, and the Windows hydration job are unchanged. Docs now state the complete UI E2E browser prerequisites.

## Evidence

- Fresh AWS lease probe (`cbx_c3b7be5cd74b`, c7a.8xlarge, Ubuntu 26.04, origin/main hydration): SSH umask `0002`; `/work/crabbox/cbx_<id>` `775`; `/work/crabbox` `755`; `/work` root-owned; no Playwright browser cache (Chromium only via system `google-chrome`); most WebKit system libraries absent. Playwright 1.62.1 lists Ubuntu 26.04 as an officially supported host.
- `pnpm test test/scripts/crabbox-hydrate-dependencies.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 17 passed, 39 s wall. New cases execute the real step scripts: ancestry/`.artifacts` lose group/other write under umask `0002`, the walk stops at the first non-owned ancestor and never touches `/`, the installer calls match CI's commands in order, an installer failure fails the step, and the env file turns `umask 0002` into `0022` under `sh` while leaving `0077` unchanged (both Linux jobs).
- `pnpm test test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 141 passed, 8 skipped. `pnpm check:workflows`, `pnpm tsgo:test:root`, oxlint, oxfmt, `git diff --check`: clean.
- Autoreview (Codex, P0–P2): scoped-clean, no findings.
- Not yet run: the one fresh-lease full-suite AWS proof. Lease creation was refused by the Crabbox coordinator's cost limit (`429 cost_limit_exceeded`) before any box was created. Maintainer decision: land on the focused tests above plus PR CI, and run the fresh-lease full-suite proof (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts` on a newly hydrated `--provider aws` lease, no manual runner repair, any residual failure classified against main on the same box) as soon as the limit allows; results will be posted here.

## What Problem This Solves

After #169484 delivered worker final replies before workspace reconciliation, session subscribers could observe reconciliation in progress without receiving its later completion. The claim owner installed internal row-change facts on completion, but that notification does not reach the existing WebSocket lifecycle bridge.

## Change

Publish the existing placement lifecycle event after an owned closure commits with both the turn claim and pending workspace result cleared. Subscribers receive the settled placement after its facts are installed. Retained recovery fences stay pending; ordinary local-turn receipts are excluded.

Production LOC: +9, a bounded correctness fix. Three files change; the archive assertion now includes its response for diagnostics without changing the expected result. The existing owner boundary test proves acceptance stays silent and completion publishes already-cleared claim and result authority. No new RPC, lifecycle state, timer, or polling.

## Evidence

Changed-file formatting, type-aware lint, and independent review passed with no actionable P0/P1 findings. `pnpm test src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-store.turn-claim-closure.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` was not run locally under the CI-only host constraint; local test wall time is unavailable. The integrated [CI run 38340516247](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38340516247) at 7be861c3d03d0 selected and passed all four affected E2Es with both production fixes: native-slot 36.141 test seconds, upgrade-wire 158.587, same-session 82.785, and skill-library 41.308. Native A/B claims clear, and all four same-session pairs publish the settled placement. This PR runs the focused owner regression and required static gates independently. The four E2E contract updates are tracked separately in #170537.

Release-note context: session subscriptions publish worker workspace settlement after an early final reply.

Focused CI run 38341715059 passed all 42 tests in the owner group (21.40 seconds), including the new completion-publication assertion (665 ms), abort and lifecycle closure cases. All selected static gates passed. The prior head had a separate orphaned-provisioning archive failure. This branch is refreshed against that main baseline, and the archive assertion now reports the response if it fails again.

The earlier archive failure did not recur after main integration; it is not claimed as inherited proof.

prs.title: fix(status): stop showing automatic auth profiles excluded by order
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes `/status` reporting a stale automatically selected auth profile after the agent's current provider order excludes that profile. For example, an audio API-key profile can appear as the chat credential even though the configured automatic order contains only OAuth profiles.

## User Impact

Status and model-menu auth labels respect the resolved automatic profile order while preserving explicit user pins, person-linked pins, and legacy pin provenance. This corrects diagnostics; it does not change runtime credential selection, media transcription, configuration, or persisted session state.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared label formatter previously prepended every saved session override to the resolved order. It now uses the existing canonical provenance helper to give that exception only to user-strength pins. Automatic preferences remain inside `resolveAuthProfileOrder`, which already honors the order. The model-menu input type now carries compaction provenance for legacy automatic selections.

The patch also removes the formatter's unchecked array cast and shrinks its assertion baseline accordingly. Production delta: +11/-3 (net +8); regression tests: +127; assertion baseline: -1 entry.

## Evidence

- Confirmed the same unconditional override behavior in installed OpenClaw 2026.9.4. Its formatter returned `api-key (openai:audio)` for an automatic audio preference with an agent order excluding audio.
- Before the patch, the complete status-command suite had exactly one failure: the new regression rendered `Auth: api-key (openai:audio)` instead of `oauth (openai:status)`; the other 55 tests passed.
- Before the patch, the formatter suite had three expected failures: excluded automatic profile, excluded legacy automatic profile, and automatic profile with an empty order; the other 16 tests passed.
- After the patch: **152 tests passed** across the full formatter (19), status-command and model-menu suites (133). The repository `check:changed` pipeline passed for all five changed files, including production/test typechecking, formatting, lint, assertion and other repository guards, and unused-export scans.
- Independent Auto Review through P2: scoped-clean, no accepted/actionable findings.

All regression credentials are synthetic. The status test uses an isolated agent auth store and the real status-text assembly and profile-order resolver. Those original regression tests did not use a production Gateway or live Matrix message. The installed-code verification below was added afterward.

### Installed build and persisted Matrix-state verification

The deployment uses upstream `main` commit `34c2fdd662d3d9058c5bf37d07364dbb58bcc6ca` plus this PR and #149365, producing integration commit `051a9483ebddd3a2af9bf868fba154d7fba0012d`. The installed CLI reports `OpenClaw 2026.9.4 (051a948)`; this main snapshot still declares version 2026.9.4. Build ID: `2026.9.4-051a9483ebdd-2026-09-15T20-24-07.846Z`. The production files from this PR are byte-for-byte equal to reviewed head `f7eca268a7f5f48a948857746beb1bc3d7ac57fe`.

A read-only probe invoked the actual installed `/status` auth-label formatter using Agent6's persisted Matrix session provenance and canonical auth-store loader, before and after replacing the installation:

| Observation | Original installed release | Patched installation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Persisted automatic audio preference exists | Yes | Yes |
| Resolved automatic order | 3 OAuth profiles; excludes audio | Same |
| Displayed auth mode | `api-key` | `oauth` |
| Displays `openai:audio` | Yes | No |
| Display matches first ordered profile | No | Yes |
| Audio media route preserved | Yes | Yes |

The config/session/media-input digest was identical before and after (`3e1a0a337670c9d1e368959f35190554bffb955cc547aeb1a0d4da08a84ea35a`), as was the non-secret auth-selection-structure digest (`0f296241fb9179610ee882f4afa40a928fc6b71be0326b9b1c52378b2b2bcd1c`). The probe performed **zero credential-store writes, zero session-store writes, zero model requests, and zero Matrix sends**. This proves the installed formatter's behavior on the real saved state; it is not a newly delivered Matrix `/status` command. The earlier status-command regression covers the full status-text assembly.

This evidence establishes a stale diagnostic label, not an actual audio credential being used by chat fallback. It also does not reconstruct when the old automatic preference was originally persisted. The heartbeat startup failure is separately addressed by #149365.

The managed Gateway reports the same integration build ID over RPC. `/readyz` returns HTTP 200 with `ready: true`; Matrix and Signal are running and connected, and the Gateway reports the bundled Codex plugin active.

No local CI suite was rerun for deployment; hosted CI remains on GitHub. Agent identities and private network details are omitted or replaced with stable Agent1–Agent6 aliases.

prs.title: fix(delivery): replay rich-text-only pending-final as plain text after restart
prs.body:
Closes #149325

## What Problem This Solves

A session restart between final-reply generation and delivery replaces a rich-text Telegram reply (headings + table + bold) with the generic pending-delivery notice, losing user-visible content that remains in the transcript. `buildRecoverablePendingFinalDeliveryText()` returns `undefined` for any payload carrying `presentation`, so the marker persists `kind: transport-only` and recovery can only send the notice.

## User Impact

Telegram users who receive formatted replies (tables, headings) and hit a session restart in the delivery window get "I couldn't confirm whether my previous reply reached this chat…" and must re-ask. The content exists in the transcript but never reaches the chat.

## Why This Change Was Made

`presentation` is visible formatting, not an action: stripping it loses styling but preserves the message. `interactive` (buttons), threads, media, voice/video, and delivery directives are different — stripping them would lose actions, so they stay unrecoverable and keep the notice path. This mirrors the existing precedent in `buildTtsSupplementMediaPayload()` (`reply-payload.ts:174-176`), which already strips `presentation`/`interactive`/`btw` when preserving spoken text. The fix downgrades presentation-only text payloads to plain text for durable recovery instead of returning `undefined`.

## Evidence

- `src/auto-reply/reply/pending-final-delivery.ts` — new `downgradeRichTextOnlyForRecovery()` + call-site integration
- `src/auto-reply/reply/pending-final-delivery.test.ts` — new test "recovers rich-text-only presentation as plain text instead of losing the reply" (rich-text replays, buttons still block, media+presentation still blocks, blank text still blocked)
- Local runs on fresh `upstream/main` (`6d158d08d`):
  - `vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/pending-final-delivery.test.ts` — 38/38 green
  - `vitest run src/agents/pending-final-delivery-marker.test.ts src/channels/turn/pending-delivery-notice.test.ts src/infra/heartbeat-runner.clears-pending-final-delivery.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-completion.integration.test.ts` — 22/22 green across 4 files
  - `oxlint` 0 warnings/0 errors, `oxfmt --check` clean, `git diff --check` clean
- Distinct from #141959 (429 flood-wait + `send_attempt_started` refusal): this incident has no 429 and fires the tested notice path on a clean session restart.
- Live incident forensics: session `agent:main:telegram:direct:6560919467`, user `seq 85/rawSeq 503`, generated reply `seq 94/rawSeq 517`, mirror `seq 95/rawSeq 518` with `main-session-restart-recovery:pending-final:fdcf1861…`.


## Update — both P1 findings resolved (head `d8e25ea`)

**P1-1 — interactive blocks inside presentation now reject the downgrade.** The guard previously checked only the deprecated `interactive` field. Buttons/select menus live in `presentation.blocks` now, so the normalized presentation is checked with the existing `isMessagePresentationInteractiveBlock()`: any `buttons`/`select` block keeps the payload transport-only. New test: "refuses presentation buttons/selects without the deprecated interactive field".

**P1-2 — presentation substance beyond `text` is preserved, reusing the delivery contract.** `text` is trusted as the complete rendering only when `presentationTextMode: "fallback"` marks it as the authored plain fallback. Otherwise chart/table blocks are mirrored into the record with the canonical `renderMessagePresentationChartFallbackText()` / `renderMessagePresentationTableFallbackText()` renderers — the same projection delivery uses in `resolveOutboundPayloadMirrorText()` — so e.g. text "Quarterly results" + sales table recovers as text plus the full table rows instead of the title alone. New tests: "mirrors chart/table substance into recovery without an authored fallback", "trusts text as complete with an authored fallback presentation".

**Fresh verification on this head (`d8e25ea`), full local repo:**
- `vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/pending-final-delivery.test.ts` — 41/41 green (38 existing + 3 new)
- Related regression files (`pending-final-delivery-marker`, `pending-delivery-notice`, `heartbeat-runner.clears-pending-final-delivery`, `delivery-completion.integration`) — 22/22 green
- `oxlint` 0 warnings/0 errors, `oxfmt --check` clean, `git diff --check` clean, full-project `tsc --noEmit` reports no errors in the touched files



## Update — complete presentation fallback (head `2e0b5a9`)

Addresses ClawSweeper review on `d8e25ea` (P1: titles/text/context dropped).

**Change:** `downgradeRichTextOnlyForRecovery()` now uses the shared complete fallback `renderMessagePresentationFallbackText({presentation, text})` — titles, text/context blocks, chart/table — exactly as Telegram delivery does in `extensions/telegram/src/interactive-fallback.ts`, instead of the narrower chart/table-only projection. `presentationTextMode: "fallback"` still trusts `text` as the authored complete rendering. Interactive `buttons`/`select` blocks still reject to transport-only.

**Tests:**
- Updated `mirrors chart/table substance...` to the canonical `\n\n` join (matches delivery `[currentText, fallbackText].join("\n\n")`)
- New regression `preserves presentation titles, text, and context during recovery`: `text:"Summary"` + `title:"Report"` + `text:"Actual answer"` + `context:"Context note"` recovers as all four parts, nothing silently dropped.

**Fresh verification on this head (`2e0b5a9`):**
- `vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/pending-final-delivery.test.ts` — 42/42 green
- `oxlint` 0/0, `oxfmt --check` clean
- Pushed as `2e0b5a90f4` on `fix/pending-final-rich-fallback-149325`

**Honest gap:** Telegram Test Server end-to-end restart replay (saved payload → recovered message) is still not supplied — requires Test Server env, not fabricated here. Unit + contract proof above is real; live proof remains open.


## Update — P2 findings resolved (head `2ae9fc7`)

Addresses ClawSweeper review on `2e0b5a9` (2 P2s + merge risk).

**P2-1 — dedup:** presentation is now rendered alone, then combined with `text`
with the same equality/suffix check Telegram delivery uses in
`canonicalizeTelegramPresentationPayload` (`currentText === fallback` or
`currentText.endsWith("\n\n"+fallback)` → keep `currentText`). `text:"Answer"` +
block `"Answer"` recovers as `Answer`, not `Answer\n\nAnswer`.

**P2-2 — MEDIA directives:** any `MEDIA:`-shaped line coming from presentation
blocks keeps the payload transport-only (recovery cannot preserve it literally
without directive reinterpretation).

**Fresh verification on this head (`2ae9fc7`), full local repo:**
- `vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/pending-final-delivery.test.ts` — 44/44 green (38 existing + 6 new)
- Related files (marker, notice, heartbeat-runner, delivery-completion) — 22/22 green
- `oxlint` 0/0, `oxfmt --check` clean

**Honest gap (unchanged):** Telegram Test Server end-to-end restart replay is
still not supplied — requires Test Server env, not fabricated. Unit + contract
proof above is real; live proof remains open.

prs.title: fix(chat): pending internal-system input shown as user message in Control UI
prs.body:
Fixes #133938

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Control UI rendered a pending recovery prompt as a message from "You" while the same input rendered as a system notice after promotion. Oversized history placeholders also dropped the provenance needed for that distinction, so large internal-system messages could lose attribution.

## Why This Change Was Made

The pending item builder unconditionally emitted `kind: "message"` without checking `provenance.kind === "internal_system"`. Canonical history already classified those inputs via the typed provenance registry (`resolveSystemNoticeKind`). This change reuses that registry for pending items (preserving the pending disposition and without assigning turn/reply/fork authority) and retains minimal `{kind, sourceTool}` provenance through `buildOversizedHistoryPlaceholder`. The sentinel path remains metadata-free.

## User Impact

Operators no longer see generated recovery prompts misattributed as their own messages during the pending interval. Oversized internal-system messages keep their system-notice presentation after projection. Ordinary user messages with identical text continue to render as user messages.

## Evidence

- New regression tests: `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pending-system-notices.test.ts` (6 tests) and `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-history-budget-provenance.test.ts` (5 tests) fail on base and pass after the fix.
- Existing tests: `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pending-inputs.test.ts` 30 passed, `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-history-budget.test.ts` 4 passed.
- Combined suite: 45 tests passed across 4 files.
- No change to runtime authority, deduplication, or search filtering.

Supersedes #134278（原PR分支已删，按原提交重建）

prs.title: fix(state): avoid redundant feature schema DDL during active runs
prs.body:
Refs #170548 #170470

## What Problem This Solves

Shared-state feature stores still execute additive `CREATE … IF NOT EXISTS` batches on every use, even when their tables and indexes already exist.

## User Impact

Repeated secret-store, MCP OAuth, device pairing, config-key, and prepared-workspace use now leaves an already admitted schema untouched. First-use installation, schema versions, stored data, update/rollback behavior, and genuine profile revocation remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared `ensureTable` funnel now caches one `createSqliteSchemaEnsurer` per table in a module-level `Map`. Each table's call sites fix its extraction options, so SQL, table/index names, and the ensurer are prepared only once. Database presence stays with the admitted schema owner, including rollback and missing-index restoration. The two startup tool-table ensures reuse this same funnel instead of a duplicate raw DDL batch. Production LOC: +21/-21 (net 0); test LOC: +18/-0, extending one existing regression.

Important attribution: `3b75ce70` originally coupled profile authority to renewable integrity proof. `c445da4029e1`, already on main, fixed that underlying lifetime coupling and added the feature-schema authority regression. This PR completes the requested sibling removal of redundant DDL; it does not claim that authority still fails on current main.

## Evidence

The extended regression retains local and transferred profile authority across the secret store's second use, checks that no DDL executes, and still proves that a real profile-role mutation revokes the binding. Before the production fix it fails with one redundant secret-store table/index batch; after the fix all seven authority cases pass. Initial single-file wall time: 34.12 s (29.24 s Vitest duration, approximately 0.91 s test time; shared compiler preparation dominates).

All seven files found by `rg -l 'openclaw-state-db-schema-additive' --glob '*.test.ts' src extensions packages test` pass: 102 tests across two routed shards, 85.41 s total wall time after the caching correction. These cover lazy installation, existing rows, outer rollback, migration, native commit revocation, and repository-workspace ownership. Independent Codex autoreview reports no actionable P0–P2 findings.

After the caching correction, the seven-file rerun, core typechecking, targeted lint, formatting, `git diff --check`, and fresh independent Codex autoreview pass. Earlier validation also passed all 28 core-test typecheck graphs. This is net-zero production-line hardening; `c445da4029e1` already fixed the authority coupling.

Inherited Knip finding: `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` exits 1 at the dead-export gate. Seven exports outside this patch were reported on the original base; six have canonical fixes on main, while `ui/src/components/board/board-widget-cell-render.ts: renderBoardWidgetError` remains unused on the rebased base. The maintainer accepted that inherited finding as outside this patch's scope. No unrelated cleanup or baseline exception is included. Checks after the dead-export scan were not run; PR CI timing is not yet available.

<details>
<summary>Sibling audit</summary>

At `3b75ce70`, shared-state profile authority borrowed the integrity revision invalidated by schema observation. The native classifier recognizes `CREATE`, `ALTER`, `DROP`, `REINDEX`, `VACUUM`, catalog writes to `sqlite_schema`/`sqlite_master`, and assignments to `user_version`/`schema_version`; schema rollback also notifies the integrity owner. TEMP table DDL and row-only rollback do not revoke MAIN schema authority. The repair in `c445da4029e1` makes the profile owner consume a separate physical-lifetime revision.

| Candidate | Finding |
| --- | --- |
| Execution-owner lifecycle binding store | Its production cron caller checks admitted table presence before invoking DDL. |
| Local workspace projection store | The create branch already checks table presence. |
| Managed-service handoff | One-time child database initialization using a native connection; it does not share the Gateway's in-process admission cells. |
| Shared additive-schema helper | Repeated feature-use DDL; converted once at the common funnel. Startup-only and Doctor migration DDL stay with those owners. |
| Workboard | Separate `plugins/workboard/workboard.sqlite` database; schema admission already gates initialization. |
| Team Reports | Separate `plugins/team-reports/team-reports.sqlite` database; schema admission already gates initialization. |
| Memory session tombstones | Already checks table presence and uses memory-owned storage. |
| Proxy capture | The cited DDL initializes the separate legacy v1 database. The shared-state branch does not call that initializer. |
| Agent board, progress-card, and quarantine schemas | Agent-database admission does not retire the shared-state profile lifetime; excluded from this state-database sweep. |

No plugin SDK expansion or plugin follow-up is required by the audited state-database paths.

</details>
