prs.title: fix(slack): record explicit top-level sends in source sessions
prs.body:
Related: #142037

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an explicit top-level Slack send can be treated as a different conversation when the inbound context also carries a synthesized reply anchor.

## User Impact

User impact: `message_tool_only` replies sent explicitly to the current Slack channel are recorded as delivered instead of being left as a mute terminal turn, while real thread-root sessions remain isolated.

## Why This Change Was Made

For `topLevel: true`, delivery placement now compares the receipt with the thread identity parsed from the admitted session key. This avoids treating `currentThreadTs`, which may be an auto-reply anchor, as proof that the admitted conversation itself is threaded. Bound Slack thread sessions can intentionally use an unsuffixed session key, so the classifier also preserves `sameChannelThreadRequired` as the authoritative fallback. Session preparation resolves that fact once from the admitted message-action capability (or host recovery context); both the installed terminal hook and subscription completion consume it. Callers without an admitted fact remain conservative: only an explicit `false` allows clearing a transport reply anchor, so older CLI callers cannot acquire new false source-completion evidence.

## Evidence

The original reviewed PR head fails the new unsuffixed bound-thread classifier regression (`expected false`, `received true`; 1 failed and 14 passed). A classifier-only correction also fails the bound-thread installed-hook regression (1 failed and 27 passed). The final installed-hook behavior proof checks that a standalone channel final send records delivery exactly once and returns `terminate: true`, while suffixed and unsuffixed bound thread sessions record no source delivery and do not terminate.

Revision 3's reviewed head `facfc9b6d24ba5fec7940770f6016a23fd644efb` also fails the new subscription completion regression (1 failed, 2 passed, 195 unrelated cases skipped): a settled parent-channel send from an unsuffixed bound thread incorrectly records `sourceReplyFinal: true`. The corrected completion handler preserves the send evidence without setting that final marker, the message-tool-only source-delivery state, normalized source-reply suppression text, or the shared delivered callback. A CLI lifecycle regression independently fails before the conservative unknown-fact correction and passes afterward. Session, execution-phase, and stream tests cover the admitted-fact propagation seams, including distinct policy/transcript session keys and admitted `false` overriding a recovery `true`.

The corrected candidate passes:

```text
source-reply-mirror.test.ts + message-tool-terminal.test.ts + tool-media-payloads.test.ts
message-action-execution.source-reply.test.ts + embedded-agent-message-tool-source-reply.test.ts
message-action-turn-capability.test.ts + attempt-session.test.ts
attempt-execution-phase.test.ts + attempt-stream-prepare.test.ts
embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.test.ts + cli-runner/execute-tool-tracking.test.ts
embedded-agent-subscribe.lifecycle-billing-error.test.ts + cron/isolated-agent/run.terminal-lifecycle.test.ts
428 passed across 13 files

oxfmt --check: passed
oxlint --deny-warnings: 0 warnings, 0 errors (230 rules)
pnpm tsgo:prod: passed
pnpm tsgo:test:root: passed
pnpm tsgo:core:test --stripe 1/1 --concurrency 2: passed (all 19 core-test graphs)
```

Validated candidate `7ac1347296fd5699a9bc9e227e512577ee26057a` on Linux with Node 24.16.0 and pnpm 12.3.4 against base `8cdb0d6df06bffcc4f407ad1dbf3598792814a8d`. The full 428-test replay, changed-file formatting/lint and all 19 core-test graphs pass on this candidate. Production and root-test typechecks passed on the preceding `a6b73145fa1b03f7fdbe1a43c506b25f12eafc20`; this follow-up changes only three test fixtures, with no production changes.

The two hosted core-test stripes exposed obsolete `sandboxSessionKey` arguments in the billing and cron lifecycle fixtures. Both are now removed; the admitted-fact session fixture also avoids spreading an existing `never`-typed fixture. No assertions were weakened. Revision 6 reviewed this exact candidate with no actionable code findings, while retaining the unexplained recursive-spawn CI failure and live Slack proof as merge risks.

Hosted CI is not green: the latest observed checks include 174 successes and two failures, consisting of [one recursive-spawn boundary test job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34929273844/job/104254086366?pr=148721) and the aggregate gate. The complete job log identifies Node 24.20.0 and synthetic merge `0bcd0f580a2d6d168374f20bf4bfc4e1eedd538b`, with then-main parent `fe8d383796f73e3b983198f19581af1273631e7e`; the previous Node 24.16 PR-head/base focused runs are not an equivalent CI comparison.

The repository CI wrapper replayed the complete 10-case production-boundary file in original file order on those frozen merge/main inputs. As root, merge passed 10/10 and main failed the original line-449 assertion (1 failed, 9 passed). In a separate task-owned copy as existing nonroot uid/gid 65534, merge failed that same assertion (1 failed, 9 passed) and main passed 10/10. Node 24.20, max workers 3 and an 8192 MiB heap budget were pinned; nonroot runs set both CI/GHA flags. These sequential single-run pairs reverse outcome, so the cause remains unresolved: neither an unrelated-CI claim nor a PR-introduced-defect claim is established. Scoped Git blob verification covered all merge-overlay and PR-control paths plus runner/runtime manifests (83 blobs), and candidate source was restored after each main comparison.

Exact original ordered-prefix attempts stopped in the preceding Gateway group before reaching spawn, on both inputs. Even after task-local Git/rsync extraction, both attempts reported 7 failed / 217 passed / 1 skipped files and 18 failed / 3559 passed / 2 skipped cases; this is matching aggregate statistics, not proof that every failure has the same cause. Remaining local issues include native-tool compatibility/library resolution and root-owned worker rejection. The replay host differs from GitHub's runner. No timeout, retry policy, assertion, runtime guard or unrelated source was changed; no successful complete-prefix replay or hosted CI rerun is claimed.

The earlier frozen-lockfile dependency install encountered a Matrix native-library download reset; linking was completed with lifecycle scripts disabled for those pure-logic tests. This installation limitation is separate from the hosted spawn failure.

### Real Slack transport validation — September 15

The exact candidate `7ac1347296fd5699a9bc9e227e512577ee26057a` was subsequently started through the supported CLI in task-owned Linux state, with a dedicated, explicitly authorized Slack app and test channel. A deterministic loopback Responses provider selected normal advertised tool calls; the unmodified embedded runtime and Slack transport executed them. This uses real Slack receipts, not fabricated transport results or paid inference, and is transport/lifecycle proof rather than model-quality proof.

- **Ordinary channel positive control:** a real standalone ingress with `requireMention:false` and `replyToMode:off` entered an unsuffixed channel session. A `message` send with `topLevel:true`, `final:true` visibly reached the parent channel; its real receipt matched the UI platform identity and reported `sourceReplyRoute:current-source`. Supported history and a bounded read-only query of the existing native run-outcome table paired that exact run/session/model with `tool_delivered/completed`, no active run and no pending input.
- **Genuine-thread paired control:** a real Slack thread reply entered the actual suffixed source session under per-channel `replyToMode:all`. Its first `topLevel:true`, `final:true` send visibly reached the parent channel with a receipt containing no thread identity and no current-source route marker. That successful result did **not** end the run: the same source run issued a second tool call, omitting `topLevel` and `threadId`. Normal routing inherited the original Slack thread; its real receipt and thread UI identity matched and the result reported `sourceReplyRoute:current-source`. The exact thread run/session/model subsequently recorded `tool_delivered/completed`, with no active run or pending input.

The first ordinary-input attempt uncovered only a fixture bug: the Responses adapter appends a protected internal-context user carrier after the actual user. It produced probe text without a tool send and is not counted as a pass. The live fixture now skips only that complete carrier envelope on verified version-4 sessions; its 14 secretless protocol regressions pass. The successful ordinary case and the single genuine-thread case were independently reviewed. No production source, tool schema, admission check, timeout or assertion was changed to produce the live results. Credential values, private Slack identifiers and raw platform timestamps are intentionally omitted.

**Remaining limits:** the unsuffixed runtime-bound-thread case still has deterministic classifier, installed-hook and subscription regressions, but no live transport proof. Missing current-source route markers are observed result markers, not direct captures of subscription booleans or hook exactly-once internals. Ordinary message-tool display mirrors are not asserted to be durable final delivery mirrors. The unexplained hosted spawn failure remains unresolved; these live Slack controls do not make CI green or establish an unrelated-failure diagnosis.

### Current-main update — September 24

The preceding CI and live-transport notes are historical evidence for head `7ac1347`. This branch now merges current `main` at `6c513528` in non-force commit `0b405858`. The nine merge conflicts were resolved against the refactored `agentSession` flow while preserving propagation of `sameChannelThreadRequired`. GitHub reports the current head as mergeable.

On Node 24.19.0 / pnpm 12.4.2, focused execution-phase (23/23), source/session/stream (98/98), terminal (28/28), CLI (8/8), and new Slack completion (3/3) checks pass. Core and root-test typechecks, changed-file oxfmt/oxlint, and diff whitespace check pass. The broader subscription-handler file had 215 passes and three `ask_user` start-path failures (two missed callbacks, one timeout); without a same-main control replay, their cause is not attributed. The scoped independent review found no actionable P0/P1 issue. The first hosted run on `0b405858` found a missing `sameChannelThreadRequired` field in the merged billing test fixture. Follow-up `8dd2ab04` adds `false` to that fixture; the direct agents-root typecheck and `git diff --check` pass. The same hosted run also had a canceled architecture job and a failing subagent admission test outside the changed paths; neither is attributed yet without a same-main comparison. Local Vitest and oxfmt are blocked by Windows Application Control on the native Node binding. Hosted CI on `8dd2ab04` has finished and is not green. Typechecking passed, but three test shards failed in subagent completion admission, gateway send/resume, and outbound reconnect-drain; the aggregate gate also failed. These failures are outside this PR's changed paths, but without a same-main control run I am not attributing them to infrastructure or to this PR. No unrelated assertions or production code were changed to mask them.

### Current-main maintenance — October 1

Merged current main (00f3a206302), preserving the recipient/account/physical-part checks and the extracted test fixtures. Replaced the retired thread-info wrapper with its existing loaded-plugin owner. Independent scoped review found no remaining material issue. Linux / Node 24.16 / pinned pnpm 12.5.1: 309 tests pass across six affected files; formatting and type-aware lint pass for all 19 changed files. Five-file run: 113.6s wall; handlers file: 45.7s wall (about 4s test work, most time is compiler/import setup). Windows tooling was blocked before tests, so these are Linux boundary tests, not a live Slack claim.

### CI follow-up — October 1

Fixed the two missing sameChannelThreadRequired fields in the Gateway/cron test fixtures. Both affected tsgo projects, formatting and type-aware lint pass; Linux Node 24.16 runs pass 2 Gateway + 23 cron tests (100.99s / 53.20s including setup). The hosted worker reclaim/force-abandon failures are in unchanged tests and owners; no Slack causal path was found, but a failing main reproduction has not been established. Those failures remain unexplained; no timeout relaxation or CI rerun was requested.

prs.title: fix: restore runtime and lifecycle CI coverage
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes CI failures when direct runtime fixtures run without prepared state and when the synthetic runner uses incomplete native TypeScript, database-broker, or producer-before-observer setup. It also aligns the native PR successor fixture with the already-landed drained-lock contract and removes unused UI surfaces left after the Solid migration.

## User Impact

There is no dependency-version change. CI repairs preserve authorization, lifecycle, cleanup, existing timeout contracts, and browser assertions. A separately proven scroll fix preserves automatic following when an upward layout correction is followed by a no-op end command; genuine user scrolling still takes control. Internal unused UI exports are removed; overlay registration remains the keyboard-listener owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prepare state at the fixture owner instead of restoring synchronous runtime fallbacks. Shutdown and sentinel tests now preserve the already-landed hoisted config fixtures, including both config getters. The attempted static snapshot alternative was incorrect across `vi.resetModules()` and is removed. Preserve native thread ownership assertions while allowing read-only probes. Startup assertions follow the current visible outbox and recovery-disabled Send controls while preserving delivery, retry, no-send, and draft checks. The overlapping GitHub custom-element fixture repair landed independently and is kept from main rather than maintaining a competing implementation.

The runner retains both its thread-isolation contract and its broker-owned provenance lifecycle contract in one child invocation, with compilation outside individual test deadlines. Sequencing belongs on the multi-project root: the first PR run exposed that child-level sequencing was ignored, and observers could run before producers. That PR-caused regression is corrected rather than treated as inherited. The native successor test now asserts that a drained failed operation releases its lock, retaining all signed-ancestry, source-resolution, and retained-evidence checks instead of attempting recovery of a nonexistent lock.

Configuration, storage, cancellation, profile, transcript-locator, media, Swift, custom-element, and dependency-check repairs landed on main during this work and are preserved rather than duplicated. The integrated cold-usage fix prepares the writer before scanning to break the scan/prune admission cycle; it is not treated as proof that every separate Gateway timeout is repaired. Direct main publication was refused by branch protection, so this repair follows the native PR workflow.

The scroll observer previously discarded an actual movement's maintenance receipt when a later explicit command moved no pixels. A delayed upward native event could then be misclassified as reader input and lock following. The fix removes only that invalidation; native-event retirement, mismatched offsets, user input, and disposal keep their existing cleanup ownership. The existing controller regression now includes the repeated no-op command and still proves genuine upward-wheel takeover. No new lifecycle machinery or timer is added.

## Evidence

Current published head: **9023be4832497da03527ebbff8dde92c9c637593**, with pinned main **f9af58c66f79f23a2e051cfe5b9feccf6befc2da** incorporated after native landing detected a real Stop-handler conflict. Fresh independent review through P2 is clean; the merged-source gateway-methods type graph passes in 60.79 seconds. Resolution retains main's independently landed completion fix and our stricter guard requiring both active and queued registrations to be absent. Exact-head PR CI **38340896493 passed all 44 selected jobs**, with 23 expected skips and successful security and aggregate gates.

The preceding exact head a02ffad passed PR CI 38336913114: **45 successful jobs, 23 expected skips**, including the original dashboard Stop case (631ms), four native-preparation outcomes (805/803/759/744ms), and all 11 OAuth coordination cases (the repaired case took 1,280ms; complete file wrapper 18.22 seconds). This is prior-head proof after the main integration, not a claim that the new head's CI is complete.

Broader main-tier run 38337557590 on a02ffad remains red. The incorporated main already repairs its exact Knip entrypoint/export findings and in-process worker-abort fixture isolation. Remote-catalog, agent-deletion, session-creation authority, post-core update handoff, required-placement, and two real-Gateway UI failures remain under investigation. No failed lane is labeled green or waived, and no timeout or assertion is weakened.

<details>
<summary>Earlier repairs, measurements, and retained failure evidence</summary>

Starting failure evidence: [scheduled main CI 38311154418](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38311154418).

- Runner fixture preparation: 55 passing cases in the focused owning batch; complete wrapper 690.31 seconds.
- Targeted Codex ownership/binding checks: 4 passing cases; complete wrapper 478.83 seconds.
- Corrected root sequencing and actor history: 2 focused parent cases passed with completed source verification, 631.35 seconds including cold compilation. The runner executes all four child lifecycle cells.
- Exact GitHub-i18n predecessor → menu sequence: 8/8 passed in 38.72 seconds after reproducing the shared-registry failure. Menu focus assertions remain unchanged.
- Offline startup cases: 2/2 passed in 62.08 seconds; steering and cold recovery also passed in their focused batch.
- UI cleanup: 112 cases passed across Chromium and WebKit, 34.16 seconds wall. Actual dependency, unused-file, and export checks all passed (589.65, 267.01, and 327.16 seconds respectively); typed UI lint, UI/component-test types, formatting, and line-cap checks passed. No Knip exemptions or assertion removals.
- All 28 selected core test type graphs passed on the earlier candidate. On the follow-up fixture candidate, the owning Gateway-server graph passed in 70.5 seconds and agents-root passed in 53.1 seconds; the expanded remaining graph run was intentionally stopped and is not claimed green. Scoped core/tooling lint and formatting passed.
- Native successor baseline reproduced the exact nonexistent-lock failure locally (336.67 seconds wrapper). The corrected case finished its synchronous native operations but exceeded the unchanged 120-second test deadline on this loaded Mac (594.93 seconds wrapper). This local run failed; no timeout was increased. Linux CI must prove the corrected case within its existing budget.
- Scroll regression failed before and passed after the two-file fix; 115 controller/policy cases passed (114.29 seconds wall), followed by 22 Chromium cases (23.20 seconds wall). The strengthened regression itself took 20 ms. Typed lint, production UI types, the canonical UI-chat test graph, formatting, and line-cap checks passed. The original strict real-Gateway scroll case still needs candidate CI confirmation; the saved CI checkpoints do not prove its exact event sequence.

The follow-up repairs pass 59 sentinel, shutdown, and accepted-cancellation cases (631.23 seconds wrapper); 30 plugin-trust, dashboard, and foreground-authority cases (556.44 seconds wrapper); and all eight cloud-startup browser cases after integrating main (91.94 seconds wrapper). The four owning test type graphs pass: agents-other 63.35 seconds, commands 39.95 seconds, plugins-platform 53.21 seconds, and UI E2E 76.16 seconds. Scoped lint and formatting pass. Independent reviews through P2 found no actionable issues in either follow-up batch.

The accepted-cancellation case retains exact record count, run IDs, cancelled outcomes, no runtime dispatch, and later-turn survival. It no longer assumes completion order among concurrently cancelled unadmitted turns; production cancellation and FIFO admission are unchanged. Plugin trust fixtures publish and clear their actual config. The foreground test revokes real admitted-run authority during restoration instead of an incomplete stand-in, retaining zero-reader/callback/dispatch checks. Dashboard still emits exactly one complete JSON failure envelope before exit. The unused internal TTS re-export is removed while the public SDK export remains; production and full-tree unused-export scans pass (176.69 and 323.17 seconds). The unused Mantis helper removal also landed independently and is preserved.

Local extension lint previously could not complete because its plugin-SDK declaration-build prerequisite timed out after 300 seconds; it did not report a source defect. This gap is not labeled green. A focused fixture attempt was also invalidated by an overlapping source edit during compilation; it ran no tests, and the subsequent frozen-source run passed. The shared Knip tool cache was incomplete; the same pinned checker passed using a task-local tool cache. No timeouts were raised, tests removed or disabled, or failures hidden.

The first PR run (38318939309, head b254dbb35e2b2b979891ad25869fa99ce612c951) failed four jobs: actor history lacked prepared config, child-project sequencing did not order the runner fixtures, and two Gateway shards needed catalog fixtures subsequently repaired on main. The repaired head 491d120f3d7eb4bc49e1e700317189b6ee476ec3 passed CI run 38322323643: 40 successful jobs, 24 expected skips, and a successful aggregate gate. Later head dba489709d268e64c59de65e3ff5c7858d562809 failed PR CI 38328667182: the static snapshot fixture, temporary diagnostic spy typing, and obsolete cloud status-band assertion were actual regressions and are corrected in this follow-up. The diagnostic spy is removed after capturing the underlying authorization stack. Main is integrated through 959426b776b7660d603af8c847616c370d40adcc. Conflict resolutions take main's stronger native successor assertion and equivalent heartbeat result variable; the reviewed cloud-startup test remains byte-identical. Prior green remains prior-head evidence, not current-head proof.

Broad main-tier run 38328734599 on dba489709 remains failure evidence, not green proof. Its real-Gateway scroll lane (1/2) passed. The exact heartbeat root was repaired independently in #170464: reply admission now forwards its existing committed store-registration callback to the retained request witness before public observers. Its cold-admission regression fails before the repair, both original heartbeat product cases pass afterward, and corrected-head CI 38330353532 passed all 76 jobs. That owner fix is incorporated, not duplicated. Main's #170433 also establishes fixture-owned shared state for Incognito lifetime; #170439 releases retained resources at their existing owners; #170455 repairs build publication; and the generated locale refresh #170489 is included. The idle-input durability expectation and context-engine canonical session key are also preserved from main.

Separate failures still need candidate verification or repair: config.patch and agent-deletion deadlines, an auth-publication waiter, OAuth coordination cost, and three packaged browser deadlines. The added abort/heartbeat assertion context is diagnostic, not itself a repair. Some earlier local runtime attempts were blocked by the managed-Gateway artifact safety fence; it was not bypassed. A Testbox request was ungranted and cancelled. These gaps are recorded, not hidden by longer timeouts, weaker assertions, or passing replays. Full repaired-source CI remains required for the requested all-green outcome.

PR CI 38332873458 on head 2b81a6629ca69f390fbb9d50daf18743d1bf5b79 completed with 50 successful jobs, 23 expected skips, two root failures, and the failed aggregate gate. Dependency checks, types, lint, generated locales, cloud-startup E2E, and 7,080 Bun UI cases pass. The remaining root failures are the dashboard Stop RPC rejecting after its captured run changes during cancellation preparation, and the WebKit modal close-during-opening test observing no exit animation. The failure classifier marked these unknown and new respectively; neither is described as green or automatically waived.

The OAuth coordination fixture now uses the same retained read-worker lifetime as the Gateway, acquired from the current module generation after fixture resets. Teardown first releases the refresh gate, then drains accepted work, then closes readers. All credential, fencing, durable-owner, and removal assertions and the 10-second deadline remain unchanged. The exact patch passed independent review through P2, typed lint, formatting, line-cap checks, and its agents-other type graph. On the overloaded local host, repeated reads fell from seconds to milliseconds, but the complete diagnostic still exceeded the unchanged deadline; Linux runtime proof remains outstanding.

The Stop failure is now repaired at the cancellation owner. If the captured run naturally completes while native descendant cancellation prepares, and neither its active nor queued registration remains, Stop returns the existing no-active outcome without consuming descendant or exec cancellation. Replaced, retargeted, and unrelated queued-successor registrations still refuse cancellation. The existing fallible session-snapshot helper replaces duplicate preparation logic; production code shrinks by 11 lines. No authorization check is removed.

The new four-outcome table reproduced the exact completed-run refusal before the fix (one failure, three passing rejection cases), then passed all four outcomes and the existing declined-parent sibling afterward. This exercises the real registered sessions.abort owner and native preparation boundary, not a duplicated implementation. Loaded-host wrapper wall time was 547.76 seconds before and 552.83 seconds after; the five green cases took 21.59, 16.45, 13.24, 16.43, and 15.47 seconds, including real store setup. No timers, sleeps, or larger deadlines were added. The gateway-methods type graph passes in 26.05 seconds, formatting and whitespace checks pass, and the line-cap ratchet accepts the shrinking production file. The exact dashboard replay timed out at sessions.send before reaching Stop (681.15 seconds wrapper); it remains a failed local attempt, not passing end-to-end proof.

The modal failure was investigated on the exact CI base d70a7e7300cdc0af4485d10b39f3e4986c3dd155. The selected modal source, style, lifecycle, bridge, configuration, and dependency inputs are identical to the CI merge. The focused macOS case passed, and the full Linux Docker WebKit suite passed all 473 cases across 39 files in 102.50 seconds wall. Event diagnostics confirmed that transitionrun can observe the active exit; they do not justify replacing it with transitionstart. These passing replays neither explain the original failure nor prove a repair. No modal assertion, transition duration, event, or product code is changed, and no inherited-failure waiver is claimed from this investigation.

The Stop repair passed fresh independent review through P2 with no actionable findings. Both line-cap and max-lines ratchets pass. Direct typed lint reports only the existing max-lines debt in the shrinking cancellation file (720 counted lines after the repair); no lint exception is added. New exact-head CI will verify the two follow-up commits, rather than rerunning the unchanged failed head for a passing result.

Current published head is a02ffad6122a287b52fbc2fcde01d20b286c572c. PR CI 38336913114 passed: 45 successful jobs, 23 expected skips, successful security-fast and aggregate gate. The four Stop outcome regressions took 805, 803, 759, and 744ms in CI; the exact original dashboard Stop case passed in 631ms, with all 40 cases in its file passing. prs.title: fix: delivery queue update no longer resurrects terminalized rows
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a race where a delivery queue entry that was terminalized (dead-lettered or completed) concurrently could be silently resurrected back to `pending` by an update. The entry was read as pending, then a concurrent writer moved it to `failed`/`completed` between the read and the write, and the blind overwrite wrote the stale payload back over the terminal state. This re-enqueues already-settled deliveries for retry and can drop terminal outcomes.

## Why This Change Was Made

`updateDeliveryQueueEntryInDatabase` (src/infra/delivery-queue-sqlite.kernel.ts) previously did a read-modify-write: it loaded the pending row, applied the transform, then issued a blind `upsert` with no `updatePendingOnly` guard. The `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` therefore rewrote every column unconditionally.

The fix marks the upsert `updatePendingOnly: true` and fails closed with the existing `ENOENT` contract when the row is no longer pending at write time, so the update only lands while the row is still `pending`. If a concurrent writer terminalized the row in between, the stale payload is never persisted. This matches the pattern already used by `reserveDeliveryQueueEntryAttemptInDatabase` and the platform-send transitions.

## Refresh against current main

Main moved delivery queue operations into a connection-bound kernel after this PR's original work; the fix was refreshed to apply at `updateDeliveryQueueEntryInDatabase` in `delivery-queue-sqlite.kernel.ts`, and the regression tests were refreshed to the kernel APIs. The branch is rebased onto the latest `main`.

## User Impact

Operators no longer risk dead-lettered or acknowledged deliveries being revived as pending and retried after the terminal state was recorded. Delivery queue state transitions are atomic with respect to concurrent recovery and settlement.

## Evidence

- New regression test in `src/infra/delivery-queue-sqlite-atomicity.test.ts` covers:
  - `preserves an independently committed terminal outcome`: the row is dead-lettered in its own committed transaction before a stale update; the update throws `ENOENT`, the committed `failed` status survives, and pending reads return null.
  - `fails closed when a concurrent terminalize lands inside the update window`: the update runs in autocommit mode exactly like production's `update()`, and the callback terminalizes the row through an independently committed writer on its own physical connection between the pending read and the write. The update throws `ENOENT`, and the committed `failed` outcome survives the rejection (status stays `failed`, pending reads return null). This exercises the committed-outcome preservation path rather than a rollback of an enclosing transaction.
  - `keeps a committed session delivery terminal across a real caller update`: enqueues a claimed session delivery, dead-letters it via the real settlement caller, then verifies the real recovery update caller throws `ENOENT` and the committed `failed` status survives.
- `delivery-queue-sqlite-atomicity.test.ts`: 3/3 pass.
- `delivery-queue-sqlite.test.ts` + `delivery-queue-sqlite-claim.test.ts` + `delivery-queue-terminal.test.ts`: 62/62 pass.
- `session-delivery-queue.storage.test.ts`: 12/12 pass.
- `pnpm tsgo:test:src`: all shards pass; no type errors in the changed files.

prs.title: fix(acp): let discard-close proceed past owner-repair verdicts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

#151859 reports ACP cleanup that cannot finish when the record's own owner-repair verdict blocks teardown.

A discarding close of a residue ACP record was rejected with `SESSION_OWNER_MIGRATION_REQUIRED`. The row survived, so callers could retry the same failure forever. A normal close, and a discard that keeps the row, must still fail closed: the merged ownership contract forbids rewriting retained resume identifiers to bypass repair.

## Why This Change Was Made

Owner repair is a reason to repair a record you intend to keep, not a reason to preserve a record you are explicitly deleting.

In `manager.close-session.ts`, the three discard-close bypasses now require `clearMeta === true`. When metadata is being deleted, an `ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED` owner-repair verdict no longer stops teardown, and fresh-session preparation is not allowed to block that deletion. `clearMeta: false` and omitted `clearMeta` still reject and leave the stored row unchanged. Ordinary close (`discardPersistentState` not set) still rejects.

Missing-backend and other non-repair cleanup failures stay best-effort. This does not make a missing backend fatal.

`closeAcpRuntimeForSession` keeps the same split at the Gateway boundary. `session-reset` still returns the owner-repair error and does not commit a rewritten row. `session-delete` stops further backend effects and removes the local ACP metadata.

## User Impact

- An explicit ACP metadata deletion proceeds past an owner-repair verdict and removes the row. The runtime close is not invoked on the unverifiable handle.
- A normal close, and a discard that retains metadata, still returns the repair error and leaves the original metadata in place.
- Session reset still honors owner repair. Session delete removes the local row instead of reporting failure while leaving the residue behind.

## Evidence

Regression tests:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/acp/control-plane/manager.owner.test.ts src/gateway/server.sessions.reset-acp-authority.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Both files passed (6 tests). The manager test covers retained discard, omitted `clearMeta`, ordinary close, and explicit deletion. The gateway test covers reset rejection versus delete clearing the row.

Public proof on head `58f90ced1ba4c13242167facf3f1eba77cf8f55f` used a real local Gateway (`src/entry.ts gateway run`, loopback, one loaded plugin: acpx). The seeded row had a locator the real ACPX runtime rejects.

`gateway call sessions.reset` exited 1:

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "gateway_request_error",
    "code": "UNAVAILABLE",
    "message": "AcpRuntimeError: ACP session \"agent:work:residue\" has an unqualified or unverifiable backend locator. Stop the Gateway and run \"openclaw doctor --fix\" to migrate ownership without losing history, then restart.",
    "retryable": false
  }
}
```

The local ACP row was still present (`backend: acpx`, `identityState: resolved`, `hasAcpxSessionId: true`).

`sessions delete agent:work:residue --agent work --yes --json` then exited 0:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "operation": "delete",
  "dryRun": false,
  "results": [
    {
      "key": "agent:work:residue",
      "ok": true,
      "status": "deleted",
      "archived": []
    }
  ]
}
```

The local ACP row was gone (`acp: null`). Gateway log: `sessions.reset` `errorCode=UNAVAILABLE`, then `sessions.delete` ok. The owner-decision checkbox is still open.

Fixes openclaw/openclaw#151859

prs.title: improve(control-ui): let drafts grow and resize message width from the border
prs.body:
Related: #113270

## What Problem This Solves

Long drafts stop growing after six lines, while changing message width requires leaving the conversation for Settings.

## User Impact

Chat and New Session drafts grow automatically until the visible-pane limit, then scroll internally. New Session never offers less than its current ten lines: where the composer rests at the bottom of a phone screen, the page scrolls as it does today. Users can drag the invisible left composer border to change both message and composer width.

Double-click or Enter restores the width active when the view opened; arrow keys adjust width. Width uses the existing **Message width** setting. There is no vertical resize handle, height preference, second width store, or migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

This replaces the earlier grow/cap height-grip proposal with automatic sizing. It preserves main's native typing path, 80% viewport editor ceiling, and complete-footer budget that reserves transcript space. Resize measurement runs in a settled frame, not a new input handler; the previous per-keystroke full-draft probe is gone.

The layout logic is one framework-free controller. The Solid chat composer attaches it from a small host component, and the New Session composer attaches it from its existing textarea controller, so both surfaces share one lifecycle and no new production file imports Lit. The drag hit area sits on the outer side of the border, so it never covers a control's touch target inside the composer.

## Evidence

Rebased on October 12 onto main `a7ab9fa695a` as one commit, after main ported the chat composer to Solid.

- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-composer-layout.browser.test.ts`: 7 Chromium tests pass. With every other product file of this PR reset to main, 6 of the 7 fail (no width handle exists, a ten-line draft that needs 252 px is held at 156 px, and added context is not budgeted).
- Three lifecycle regressions fail without their fix and pass with it:
  - Switching sessions mounts a new textarea inside the same composer. Without the fix the new editor was capped at 56 px; with it the cap stays 602 px.
  - Reopening New Session after a resize: double-click restored the earlier `1081px` instead of the current `1061px`.
  - Moving the controller to another surface left the handle and height limit on the first one.
- 42 Chromium composer tests pass across 6 files: layout, context, overflow, undo/redo, status, and the New Session draft body and placement controls. Main's overflow test covers the 44 px dismiss targets at 390 px in RTL with the drag handle present.
- 26 mocked-Gateway end-to-end tests pass across 7 composer files (text readability, New Session responsive layout, input measurement, redesign, picker layout, capability menu height, focus). `keeps the mobile composer within reach and lets long prompts scroll` at 320 × 568 fails when New Session takes the pane budget alone (the editor was held to 44 px) and passes with the ten-line floor.
- 2,503 unit tests pass across 198 files (New Session, chat composer, chat pane, chat view).
- UI type check, the UI chat test-project type check, oxlint, stylelint, formatting, i18n verification, and the Control UI Lit ratchet pass.
- Two independent review passes of the port; every finding is fixed and has a regression test above.

prs.title: feat(ui): render LaTeX in Control UI markdown
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI Markdown previously displayed supported LaTeX delimiters literally. This change renders bounded inline and display math while preserving code, escaped input, currency, URLs, and sanitized output.

## User Impact

Math rendering is now lazy-loaded. Ordinary messages and routes do not request the KaTeX engine, styles, or fonts. A completed mathematical expression initially remains readable as source, then updates automatically when the shared renderer and stylesheet are ready; no new message or manual refresh is required. Loading failures preserve readable source.

Original contribution by @jjjhenriksen; repair work requested by @RomneyDa. Contributor ancestry is preserved and Allow edits from maintainers remains enabled.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @RomneyDa](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/clawtributor-review-pr-144324)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/41d889a9-23c8-4603-889b-a35ad86acfb6)

## Why This Change Was Made

The eager implementation added a material startup payload. The current implementation defers that cost until math is actually displayed, shares the loading promise across consumers, and applies styles before typesetting. It retains the reviewed delimiter/parser bounds, sanitizer and MathML semantics, 4096-character scan limit, and 200-expression rendering budget. Author-supplied HTML remains escaped.

This is still built-in math behavior, not an opt-in plugin. Dependency authorization is recorded below; it does not by itself claim the related issue owner's acceptance of the earlier product-direction deferral in #125222 / #127859. No footnote implementation or unrelated dependency replacement is included.

## Evidence

### Current revision

- Published head: `6ae6cdcb50ce1c5aba9ba2c3202c918c7c440507`.
- Tested tree: `3d2fe439e4b5af5cab0d54ecb16ab8c8054e3089`.
- Matched eager comparison: `83e74ca9aff78ff2b3fac5fcdc584e67b89d37fd`.
- [Current-head real Control UI loading/ready screenshots, runtime observations, and performance proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/144324#issuecomment-5884479906).
- [Exact-head dependency authorization](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/144324#issuecomment-5884479339), accepted by the current dependency-review guard. The lazy-loading revision does not change dependency manifests or the lockfile versus the eager revision; the existing direct UI dependency is KaTeX 0.16.47.

### Verification

- 179 focused tests passed; UI types, lint, production build, generated boot manifest, and performance budgets passed.
- Independent P0–P2 autoreview was scoped-clean.
- Production-browser proof exercised connected completed messages, shared Markdown consumers, cached content, streaming, concurrent equations, failure fallback, stale/disconnected lifecycle, and stylesheet readiness. No-math routes requested no KaTeX runtime, stylesheet, or fonts. Concurrent math and subsequent streaming reused one runtime request and one request per required font.
- [Final browser/runtime and measurement receipt](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_10b407ab658c3e3e29cff5441be71ed1).
- [Eager comparison and safe import-trimming receipt](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_0f808048eb17c28d8829cd3d0ac94ff5).
- [Focused tests and committed-tree proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_e9897c4172a987dffcace6d53c65d54e).

### Payload and runtime costs

Matched eager/lazy production builds on the same runner; three fresh browser contexts per route, no cache or service worker, loopback without network throttling. Values below are measured, not an extrapolation from the entry-chunk budget.

| Measurement | Eager | Lazy | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Cold /chat JavaScript + CSS, gzip bytes | 1,683,477 | 1,599,409 | −84,068 (−4.99%) |
| Cold /new JavaScript + CSS, gzip bytes | 1,739,274 | 1,655,194 | −84,080 (−4.83%) |
| Ordinary fresh Markdown, median | 1.3 ms | 1.3 ms | unchanged |
| Observed first-math readiness, median | 67.6 ms | 86.6 ms | +19.0 ms in this local harness |

The first math loads an 84,821-gzip-byte runtime including styles, plus 47,920 font bytes for the measured examples. This is mainly **deferral, not removal**: cumulative JavaScript + CSS after first math is 753 bytes larger than the eager implementation. Switching to the named renderer export safely removed 289 gzip bytes from the engine plus 18 from its caller; no larger obvious safe trim was found without reducing functionality, glyph coverage, or MathML.

Dense input remains expensive. For 205 input expressions with 200 rendered, eager synchronous HTML generation measured 80.1/95.1 ms median/p95 versus lazy 1.9/2.6 ms, but work moved into enhancement: eager DOM/layout was 136.8/195.4 ms versus lazy mount-through-enhancement 237.6/280.4 ms. These are different phases, not an equivalent speedup claim. Lazy loading does not eliminate dense-math CPU cost or potential jank. First-math latency on slow networks can be higher than this loopback result. No browser-memory or paint-performance improvement is claimed.

### Readiness and remaining gates

The PR is open and non-draft; the latest GitHub mergeability observation is unknown. No merge or auto-merge has been requested or performed.

[Current-head hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36513397977): all three UI shards, all nine mocked E2E shards, both real-Gateway UI E2E jobs, build, Control UI performance, types, lint, and security-fast passed. The failed Gateway job, [checks-node-changed-compact-large-21](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36513397977/job/109230691899), tested merge `f1d7cfcc9cfb` against main `35263bd17ad`. It reported SQLite pathname/actor-identity failures in session deletion, title generation and deleted-agent startup, plus an unidentified outstanding root-work assertion. Its `src/`, `test/`, `scripts/` and root runtime/workflow inputs match that main parent; source tracing found no import path into the changed math renderer. No PR-specific defect or justified patch was identified.

A fresh isolated, Node 24.19.0 focused replay on main `46f62aa5070` passed all three originally failing files: **20/20 tests in 136.49 seconds** ([receipt](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_7a6b14a42fbf22ab0295d591c47d2502)). An earlier full-plan replay was confounded by temporary-storage exhaustion and SIGKILL; it is not clean proof. Later main commit [`1475b6f8358`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/1475b6f8358a95d2d5f5741d69bff8d9d3592c17) repairs subagent-sweeper retirement before SQLite cleanup, but the historical failing schedule was not captured. These results neither reproduce a matching current-main failure nor prove every original failure fixed. **The original CI gate remains red; no rerun or waiver was applied.**

The exact-head [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/144324#issuecomment-5624419136) completed September 29 at 06:25 UTC and rates this diamond lobster (5/6), with no actionable code or security findings and sufficient current-head browser proof. It still requests the related issue owner’s decision on built-in default math and acceptance of the measured dense-math cost. Dependency approval is complete; the separate gateway/SQLite CI failure remains unresolved. No merge or auto-merge is authorized.

prs.title: fix(windows): keep process-start probe budget monotonic
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where a Windows system clock step during a lock-owner / PID-reuse identity probe breaks the probe's shared time budget.

The Windows start-time probe runs two synchronous probes (PowerShell, then a WMIC fallback) against one deadline measured on the wall clock. When the system clock is stepped while the PowerShell probe runs:

- **Rollback** (NTP adjustment, manual set-back, VM clock sync): the WMIC fallback timeout inflates by the full rollback, so the probe blocks the synchronous caller far longer than its end-to-end budget — a 60s step adds ~60s to every such probe (a 1s budget probe returns a ~61s timeout).
- **Jump forward** past the remaining budget: the WMIC fallback is silently skipped and the probe returns "unknown" even though real time remains, losing the stronger process-start-time identity check that guards against recycled-PID misidentification of the running Gateway.

These checks run on Windows whenever OpenClaw verifies that a process/lock it owns is still the same process (gateway lock ownership, process-tree kill verification).

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared budget is now measured as elapsed monotonic time (`performance.now()` since the probe started) instead of a wall-clock delta, so a clock step can neither inflate the WMIC timeout nor drop the fallback. This mirrors the systemd service budgets, which already keep their deadlines monotonic across wall-clock steps.

The two-probe PowerShell-then-WMIC structure, the 5s/10s attempt bounds, the caller's end-to-end budget, and the function's `number | null` contract are all preserved; only the clock used to measure the shared budget changed.

## User Impact

Windows operators no longer see multi-second-to-minute stalls on gateway lock-owner or process identity checks after their system clock is stepped (NTP sync, manual change, VM clock jump), and the stronger process-start-time identity check is no longer silently dropped during a clock jump forward. Behavior is unchanged when the clock does not step.

## Evidence

- Qualified as a merge with current main while preserving the original contributor commits and the native ancestry implementation. The minimal test-fixup publication reproduces the complete tested merge tree exactly.
- Four deterministic wall-clock-step cases on unchanged production: three reproduced failures and one stable exhausted-budget control. The same complete candidate fixture passes **19/19** after the fix.
- Native Windows / Node 24.16.0: real PowerShell identity, repeated identity and baseline equality, owned-child identity/CIM ancestry, invalid PID, unavailable executables, and exhausted native query checks passed; the owned child exited and was joined.
- Native Windows limitation: this host has no WMIC, and its operating-system clock was not changed. Successful real WMIC fallback and actual host-clock stepping are not claimed.
- PID-identity sibling tests: **30/30**; native-Node source-closure test: **1/1**. All affected changed-file checks passed, including production/test types, lint, dead exports and source guards.
- Independent P0–P2 review: scoped-clean. No dependency, configuration, protocol, process-killing policy, or timestamp-format changes.

### Real subprocess clock-step proof (Windows)

The exact production probe was run on native Windows / Node 24.16.0 against two task-private, compiled .NET executable fixtures under its supported `SystemRoot` input. The primary executable sleeps 200 ms and fails; the fallback prints a valid creation timestamp after a chosen real delay. These are **protocol fixtures, not the host PowerShell or WMIC binaries**. `spawnSync` always delegates to the original native implementation, records its actual status/error and timeout, and steps only the parent process's `Date.now` after the first child returns. `performance.now`, production source, parsing and timeout enforcement are unchanged. No OS clock change or subprocess return-value stub is used.

Budget: **1,000 ms**; injected clock step: **±1 hour**.

| Case | Baseline | Fixed production |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Forward, 100 ms fallback work | Skips fallback; unknown after 255 ms | Launches fallback with 765 ms remaining; valid fixture identity after 392 ms |
| Backward, 1,400 ms fallback work | Grants 3,600,769 ms; succeeds after 1,671 ms, beyond the caller budget | Grants 768 ms; native child ends with `ETIMEDOUT`, unknown after 1,009 ms |

All four paired outcomes matched the expected behavior. Synchronous children joined, and the process-local clock/spawn hooks were restored. Fixed owner SHA-256: `7e6df825bb173629528ced517a5ba83aa6290e98e31874508f687ed2a289ee34`.

This proves the changed production fallback decision and real Windows child timeout boundary under injected clock steps. Native PowerShell identity/CIM behavior is covered separately above; **successful native WMIC remains unverified because WMIC is not installed**.

Both hosted native Windows jobs passed for signed head `50d8eb0bdd731c799096cf8d0113106249c514b2`, including all 19 owner cases and the native-Node import case: [Windows test-1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34922566746/job/104233875876), [Windows test-2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34922566746/job/104233876051).

Required CI is not green: the Linux `models-manual-policy.integration.test.ts:120` default-reset assertion failed. A single focused run on unchanged CI main base `dd3383345724424da5139473addcf247f0c9afbd`, without this PR, reproduced the authenticated timeout (the unauthenticated case passed). This is evidence of a separate baseline failure, not a CI waiver or a claim that both cases fail deterministically. No blind rerun or unrelated model-policy change was made in this PR.

Original fix and contributor credit: **tzy-17**. The follow-up expands the regression matrix without changing the production approach.

prs.title: fix(meeting): own a fresh root admission for agent consults
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #142610.

Every spoken question in a Google Meet agent-mode session fails with a misleading
`Gateway is draining; new tasks are not accepted` error, even though the gateway is
healthy. `consultMeetingAgent()` in `src/meeting-bot/agent-consult.ts` calls
`consultRealtimeVoiceAgent()` directly, without acquiring its own root-work
admission. Because the consult runs inside the same async chain that handled the
`googlemeet.create` request, it inherits that request's AsyncLocalStorage
root-work context — a context that is already `released` by the time a
participant actually asks a question minutes later. `enqueueCommandInLane()`
then rejects the consult via `isGatewaySubordinateWorkAdmissionClosed()`,
which returns `true` for a released inherited root.

The browser Talk path (`src/gateway/talk-client-agent-consult.ts`) already
handles this correctly by acquiring an independent root admission with
`runOutsideGatewayRootWorkAdmission(tryBeginGatewayRootWorkAdmission)` before
running the consult, and releasing it in a `finally`. The meeting path omitted
this step.

## Fix

`consultMeetingAgent()` now acquires its own root-work admission outside the
inherited (possibly-released) context before calling
`consultRealtimeVoiceAgent()`, mirroring the Talk path exactly, and releases it
once the consult settles. If admission is refused (a genuine drain/suspension),
it now throws `GatewayDrainingError` from an accurate state instead of from a
stale one.

## Evidence

Added a regression test that reproduces the real bug shape: it opens a root
admission (simulating the `googlemeet.create` request), schedules the consult
call as an async descendant of that root's callback (so it inherits the store
via Node's AsyncLocalStorage propagation, exactly like a transcript-triggered
callback registered during meeting creation), releases the root (simulating the
finished creation request), and only then lets the consult proceed. It asserts
that `isGatewaySubordinateWorkAdmissionClosed()` is `false` at the point the
consult actually runs — i.e. a fresh, open admission was acquired instead of the
stale released one.

Confirmed the test fails without the fix, for the intended reason:

```
$ git checkout HEAD~1 -- src/meeting-bot/agent-consult.ts
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/meeting-bot/agent-consult.test.ts

 × |unit| ... > consults successfully under a fresh admission after the meeting's creation-request root released
   → expected true to be false // Object.is equality
 Tests  1 failed | 5 passed (6)
```

And passes with the fix restored:

```
$ git checkout HEAD -- src/meeting-bot/agent-consult.ts
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/meeting-bot/agent-consult.test.ts

 ✓ |unit| ... > consults successfully under a fresh admission after the meeting's creation-request root released
 Tests  6 passed (6)
```

Also ran the acceptance-criteria suites named in triage, all green:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/meeting-bot/agent-consult.test.ts \
    src/process/gateway-work-admission.test.ts src/process/command-queue.test.ts \
    src/gateway/talk-client-gateway-control.agent-consult.test.ts

 RUN  v5.0.0 ...
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
 RUN  v5.0.0 ...
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  23 passed (23)
 RUN  v5.0.0 ...
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  70 passed (70)
[test] passed 3 Vitest shards in 24.75s
```

(The runner splits the four files across three shards; `gateway-work-admission.test.ts`
and `command-queue.test.ts` land in the same shard, so that shard's 70 already
includes the admission file's tests. Total: 6 + 23 + 70 = 99 tests, all passing.)

Typecheck and lint on the changed files:

```
$ pnpm tsgo:core                                   # passes clean
$ node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs --changed-paths-json '[...]'  # exit 0
$ node_modules/.bin/oxlint src/meeting-bot/agent-consult.ts src/meeting-bot/agent-consult.test.ts   # no findings
$ npx oxfmt --check src/meeting-bot/agent-consult.ts src/meeting-bot/agent-consult.test.ts          # correctly formatted
```

`pnpm check:changed`'s max-lines ratchet step fails against this fork's stale
`origin/main` (last synced at #114884, far behind `upstream/main` at #142632) —
reproduced identically on an unmodified checkout with no relation to this diff,
and passes cleanly with `--base upstream/main`.

## Real-meeting proof (community-supplied)

This sandbox still has no Google Meet OAuth credentials or live meeting to join, so it
cannot generate first-party live-meeting proof (see the 2026-09-09 comment on this PR).

The reporter of #142610, @jai-assistant, independently arrived at a functionally
identical fix and ran this exact change in production since 2026-09-08. They posted
real Google Meet before/after evidence and root-cause diagnostics in a
[PR comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/142692#issuecomment-5671310635):

- Before the patch: 27/27 spoken consults failed with `Gateway is draining; new tasks
  are not accepted`, each rejected in 5-19 ms.
- After the patch: 47 consults, 0 failures, across a continuous 21-minute session,
  still running six days later.
- Instrumentation of `isGatewaySubordinateWorkAdmissionClosed()` during the failure
  showed `reason=rootWorkReleased origin=ws:googlemeet.create refs=0`, matching this
  PR's diagnosis of a consult inheriting an already-released creation-request root.

This is third-party evidence from the reporter's own environment, not proof generated
in this session.

agent.

prs.title: fix(telegram): include duration in voice and audio uploads
prs.body:
Closes #142548

## What Problem This Solves

Telegram users can see 0:00 on OGG/Opus voice messages larger than 1 MiB, even though the audio plays. M4A audio uploads can return the same zero duration.

## Why This Change Was Made

In my tests Telegram inferred the duration for smaller uploads, but returned zero for OGG/Opus and M4A files above 1 MiB when OpenClaw left out the optional `duration` field. OpenClaw's buffer probe could not fill the gap because it fed ffprobe through a pipe. These containers can store duration metadata at the end of the file, and a pipe can't seek there.

`probeAudioDurationMs` in `src/media/media-probe.ts` writes the buffer to OpenClaw's private temp directory and passes it to the existing `probeMediaFile`. ffprobe gets a seekable file descriptor with `-protocol_whitelist fd`, so playlist-like bytes can't open nested files or URLs. Only OGG/Opus, MP3 and MP4/M4A MIME types are probed. Everything else skips probing. A probe or filesystem failure leaves `duration` out and delivery continues.

The shared Telegram sender in `extensions/telegram/src/outbound-media.ts` probes once per media item and passes the rounded duration to `sendVoice` and `sendAudio`. Durable sends and streaming replies both go through it.

The helper is exported from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/media-runtime`, which Telegram already imports. That barrel is deprecated, so the export location needs a decision from the Plugin SDK owner. Moving it to a private local-only subpath is a small follow-up once that's decided.

## User Impact

Telegram receives an explicit duration for voice and audio uploads, so long voice notes show their real length instead of 0:00. The waveform of the tested long voice message stayed flat. This change fixes the time display only.

## Evidence

Live Telegram observations (recorded on the pre-rebase head 9d77ebd0f2, same sender change). Screenshots are in #142548.

- On OpenClaw 2026.9.2 a 310.0065-second, 1,933,848-byte OGG/Opus voice message displayed 0:00. With the patch the sender passed `duration=310` and Telegram displayed 5:10.
- A 2,546,108-byte M4A upload without a duration returned 0. The patched `sendAudio` path returned 310 for a 310-second M4A of 2,545,899 bytes.
- Bot API controls without a duration: 1,048,514-byte OGG/Opus (62 bytes under 1 MiB) returned 235 seconds, 1,048,606 bytes (30 bytes over) returned 0. 289, 290 and 291-second OGG/Opus files under 640 KB and a 2,480,631-byte MP3 returned correct durations.

Fix commit 591c02aece, rebased on main 2ae25faa86:

- Real helper with system ffprobe 9.0.2 on generated files: 310 s OGG/Opus returned 310007 ms. A 310 s M4A with the `moov` atom after `mdat` returned 310000 ms. A 7.4 s MP3 returned 7400 ms. An HLS playlist pointing at a local file returned no duration both as `audio/ogg` and as `application/vnd.apple.mpegurl`.
- `src/media/media-probe.test.ts`: 31 tests pass. New cases check that ffprobe gets a regular-file descriptor, that playlist MIME skips ffprobe, and that a failed probe returns no duration.
- `extensions/telegram/src/send.recovery.telegram-http.test.ts`: 51 tests pass against the HTTP Telegram fixture. Four new cases cover `sendVoice` and `sendAudio` for durable and streaming delivery. With the sender change reverted, all four fail.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main`: typecheck for core, core tests, extensions, extension tests and scripts, Plugin SDK exports and surface budget, plugin boundaries, format and the other guards pass. The dead-export scan fails on 34 unrelated exports under `ui/src/pages/config` and `ui/src/components`, none in files this PR touches.
- Telegram Test Server E2E has not run. The `telegram-e2e-userbot` doctor fails with "Could not load the QA broker through the Convex CLI" because I don't have access to the team broker.

CI fix in a separate commit, 44e444100d (tests only, +14/-2): `checks-node-changed-compact-large-9` failed on `src/agents/tools/message-tool.internal-source-reply.integration.test.ts` with "Runtime config is not prepared". The same suite fails 9/10 on plain main 2ae25faa86, so it is not caused by this PR. Since #169714, `getRuntimeConfig()` needs a published runtime snapshot, and `withOpenClawTestState` resets that state on `applyEnv`. That PR updated the sibling message-tool tests but not this one. The suite and `message-tool.cron.test-support.ts` now publish the config after state setup, the way a booted Gateway does, and clear it after each test. 10/10 pass locally, and oxlint, oxfmt and the core test typecheck are clean.

The other red check, `checks-node-changed-compact-large-35` ([job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38303377720/job/114991957841)), is `update-managed-service-handoff-lifecycle.test.ts > rechecks the revoked requester after helper readiness and parent exit`, and it is not caused by this PR. In a Linux container (`node:24-bookworm`) running `scripts/ci-run-node-test-shard.mts` on just that file, it fails 3/3 on the merge base 2ae25faa86, 3/3 on this head and 3/3 on main d7be70250a; the rest of the file passes. The helper's sentinel write is refused with "undergoing offline maintenance", so the test reads `null`. CI only selects that file here because the `src/media/*` changes pull in the protected runtime tests. Filed as #170301.

Production code is +54/-11 (net +43). Tests are +61/-2. SDK budget tooling is +4/-2 for one new public export and one callable export. The growth is the temp-file probe, the duration field in the shared sender, and the SDK export.

No dependency, configuration, database or protocol change. Related PR #65999 was closed without merging. It used a custom OGG parser in one delivery path.

prs.title: fix(diagnostics): stuck-session recovery never runs on hosts with late heartbeat ticks
prs.body:
Fixes #142200.

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where automatic stuck-session recovery stops running for the lifetime of a Gateway process on virtualized hosts, so a session that hangs is warned about repeatedly but never recovered.

The diagnostic heartbeat treats its own lateness as a sign the event loop is congested. When a tick fires more than one second past its 30 second deadline, recovery decisions are deferred to the next healthy tick:

`src/logging/diagnostic.ts:1165`

```ts
const shouldDeferRecovery = heartbeatOverdueMs >= DEFAULT_LIVENESS_EVENT_LOOP_DELAY_WARN_MS;
```

```ts
if (!recovery || shouldDeferRecovery) {
  continue;
}
requestStuckSessionRecovery({ ... });
```

That tolerates 3.3 percent slop on a 30 second timer. The reporter measured a WSL2 host waking a sleeping timer 1120 to 1681 milliseconds late on 32 consecutive ticks while the true event-loop delay stayed at 10 to 13 milliseconds and the Gateway sat at 2.2 percent CPU. Every tick deferred, so the next healthy heartbeat the deferral waits for never arrived:

```
13:16:26.368Z WARN liveness heartbeat delayed: overdue=1483ms elapsed=31483ms; deferring recovery decisions
13:16:57.914Z WARN liveness heartbeat delayed: overdue=1546ms elapsed=31546ms; deferring recovery decisions
13:17:29.472Z WARN liveness heartbeat delayed: overdue=1558ms elapsed=31558ms; deferring recovery decisions
```

`logSessionAttention` still fires, so the operator sees stuck-session warnings, but `requestStuckSessionRecovery` is unreachable.

## Why This Change Was Made

The deferral protects a real case and is kept. What is wrong is the signal it reads. Wakeup latency is a property of the host scheduler; whether queued progress is stuck behind a blocked loop is a property of the event loop, and the Gateway already runs a sampler that measures the second one. On the reporter's ticks that sampler read 10 to 13 milliseconds while the heartbeat called the same ticks congested.

**The verdict belongs to the monitor, not the heartbeat.** Only the sampler knows whether its own next sample is overdue, and that turns out to be the whole answer:

`src/gateway/server/event-loop-health.ts`

```ts
eventLoopDelayed: () =>
  nowMs() - lastSampleAt >= EVENT_LOOP_DELAY_WARN_MS ||
  (lastSnapshot?.reasons.includes("event_loop_delay") ?? false),
```

`lastSampleAt` advances on every sampler callback, including the early-return path where a quiet window commits no snapshot, so it is a liveness marker for the sampler itself. A stall starves that 20 millisecond callback, which means the retained observation predates the stall and still reads healthy. The interval since the last callback is itself a delay measurement, so the monitor can answer correctly without waiting for a new observation to commit.

The Gateway passes that verdict for recovery and keeps the persistent filter for warnings, which are different questions:

```ts
readEventLoopDelayed: readinessEventLoopHealth.eventLoopDelayed,
```

`persistentDegradationSnapshot()` withholds anything under 60 seconds of continuous degradation (`event-loop-health.ts:14`, `:207-213`), which is right for an operator warning and wrong for a recovery decision, because a shorter genuine stall still holds queued progress.

Session ages continue to be measured against `recoveryObservationNow = now - heartbeatOverdueMs`, which is untouched, so timer jitter still cannot push a run past its threshold early.

Two earlier revisions of this PR got the mechanism wrong and are worth naming, since the current shape is a response to both. A counter capping consecutive deferrals gave chronic lateness a standing exemption. Comparing observation identity across ticks only proved that something had been published since the last heartbeat, which across a 30 second interval is about thirty commits, so a pre-stall observation still passed. Reading the pending sample interval has neither hole, adds no constant, and removes the third "no evidence" state entirely.

Because the callback is now a plain `() => boolean`, no freshness or identity semantics leak to SDK hosts implementing it. There is no longer a wrong way to return the value.

An earlier revision of this PR also carried a standalone fallback that read completed histogram samples when no verdict was supplied. That had the same ordering hole, with no way to detect its own pending sample, so it is removed rather than rebuilt. `startDiagnosticHeartbeat` is exported through `src/plugin-sdk/logging-core.ts`, and callers that omit the verdict now defer on a late tick, which is exactly main's behavior today. Only the Gateway changes.

No configuration option is added.

## User Impact

On hosts with chronic timer lateness, mainly WSL2 and other VMs, stuck sessions are recovered automatically again instead of only being warned about. A genuinely blocked event loop still defers recovery, including a stall shorter than the warning filter's minute and a stall that starved the sampler itself. The repeated warning now says which of the two it observed:

```
liveness heartbeat delayed: overdue=1483ms elapsed=31483ms; event loop stayed responsive, keeping recovery decisions
```

## Evidence

Production change is +40/-5 across three files, of which the Gateway wiring is one line.

The contract is proven at its owner, against the real monitor rather than a fake:

```ts
harness.samples(50);
expect(harness.monitor.snapshot()).toMatchObject({ degraded: false, reasons: [] });
expect(harness.monitor.eventLoopDelayed()).toBe(false);
harness.elapseWithoutSampling(1_200);
expect(harness.monitor.snapshot()).toMatchObject({ degraded: false, reasons: [] });
expect(harness.monitor.eventLoopDelayed()).toBe(true);
```

Healthy sampling, then the heartbeat-before-sampler window, asserting the snapshot still reads healthy while the verdict does not. Reducing the verdict to snapshot-only, the pre-fix semantics, fails it:

```
× reports a delayed loop once its own sample is overdue, before any new observation
  AssertionError: expected false to be true
  Tests  1 failed | 20 passed (21)
```

Reverting `src/logging/diagnostic.ts` to main, so the deferral reads lateness again:

```
× keeps recovery running when ticks are late but the event loop stayed responsive
  Error: missing recoverStuckSession call
```

A companion test asserts ten consecutive keeping-up samples stay `false`, so the guard fails in both directions rather than only one.

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/logging                              9 files, 110 passed
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server/event-loop-health.test.ts,
  question.recovery.test.ts                                                    49 passed
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway (recovery lane)             36 files, 697 passed
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json                                  clean
oxlint / oxfmt on all five touched files                                         clean
```

Proof gap worth stating plainly: this is fake-timer coverage of the heartbeat decision plus real-monitor coverage of the contract it depends on, not a runtime trace on an affected host. I have no WSL2 or VM host and cannot manufacture chronic host wakeup lateness here, so producing that trace would mean fabricating it. For anyone who does have such a host: run the Gateway with diagnostics enabled, leave a session `processing` past `stuckSessionWarnMs`, and grep for `liveness heartbeat delayed`. Before this change every line ends `deferring recovery decisions` and recovery is never requested; after it, lines end `event loop stayed responsive, keeping recovery decisions` and recovery is requested.

AI-assisted: yes. I traced the source path by hand and ran every command above myself.
