prs.title: fix(line): channel access token and secret cannot be secret references
prs.body:
Closes #133625

## What Problem This Solves

`channels.line.channelAccessToken` and `channels.line.channelSecret` reject the structured secret reference that `channels.telegram.botToken` and the credentials of eleven other channels accept, so a LINE deployment has to keep its bot credentials as plaintext in `openclaw.json`. Same reference shape, same config, two different answers.

Three things had to be true at once for that to work, and LINE had none of them:

- `extensions/line/src/config-schema.ts:28` declared both credentials as `z.string()`, so the schema rejected a reference before anything else ran.
- `extensions/line/secret-contract-api.ts` was an explicit stub — `// Line does not expose secret-contract surfaces.` — so even a reference that validated would never be collected for resolution. Four other channels ship the same stub (iMessage, Signal, WhatsApp, Zalo User), and for them it is accurate: none of the four declares a credential field in its config schema, because their auth lives in a linked-device store. LINE declares four (`channelAccessToken`, `channelSecret`, `tokenFile`, `secretFile`) and shipped the stub anyway.
- `resolveLineCredential` read the raw config value with `?.trim()`, so a reference object would have thrown rather than degraded.

The operator-visible result is that a LINE deployment cannot keep its bot credentials in the shared secret store, a file provider, or an external manager, and cannot bind them to an egress host — while a Telegram or Slack deployment beside it can.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix joins LINE to the contract that already exists rather than adding a LINE-specific credential path.

**Schema.** Both credentials become `registerSensitiveConfigSchema(SecretInputSchema.optional())`, the same declaration Telegram, Discord, Slack, Matrix and eight others use. Registering the schema is what makes host config projections redact the value, so this also stops LINE credentials from being echoed back in config reads.

**Contract.** `extensions/line/src/secret-contract.ts` publishes both credentials at the channel and account scopes, which is four target paths, and collects runtime assignments, so core resolves the reference and writes the literal back before the plugin reads it. The activity predicates encode LINE's own precedence rather than copying Telegram's:

- LINE reads the inline credential *before* its credential file, so an enabled account always consumes its own inline value. Telegram reads `tokenFile` first and therefore deactivates `botToken` when a file is configured; that condition would be wrong here.
- Only the default account falls back to channel-level credentials, and only while it supplies neither the inline value nor its own file.
- `resolveChannelAccountSurface` omits the default account when the accounts map names only other accounts, but LINE still resolves a default account from channel-level credentials in exactly that config. The contract adds that consumer back, otherwise a deployment with a channel-level reference plus one named account would leave its primary account permanently unresolved.

**Reader.** `resolveLineCredential` now reads through `resolveSecretInputString(..., mode: "inspect")`. A reference the runtime has not resolved returns `configured_unavailable` and stops there instead of falling through to the credential file or the environment: falling through would authenticate with a different credential than the operator named. `configured_unavailable` is the status `hasConfiguredUnavailableCredentialStatus` already feeds to channel status, gateway health, outbound target selection and the security audit, so the degraded state surfaces through the paths that exist rather than a new one.

**Setup wizard.** Two of its declarations were written while the schema was narrow, and neither survives a credential that can be a reference:

- `set: { value: "resolved" }` wrote the value the wizard had resolved a reference *to*, so choosing "Use external secret provider" stored the plaintext. Writing the reference itself was not possible before, which is why the declaration was there; it is now `set: { clearFields: [...] }`, matching Slack. Plaintext entry is unchanged, because that prompt returns the same string in both halves.
- `accountConfigured` asked whether the account as a whole was configured, which needs both credentials to resolve. Once a credential can be a reference, one reference the provider has not answered marks the other credential as missing too, and the wizard asks the operator to retype a value that works. It now answers per credential from what that credential resolved to: a resolved value, or a reference the operator named on purpose, can be kept; a credential file that cannot be read cannot. Whether the config names a value at all stays with `defineTokenCredential`, so a named file still suppresses the environment-variable offer and the operator's file is never dropped without a word.

One thing this deliberately does not do.

The default-account match uses `normalizeOptionalAccountId`, which leaves an id the router cannot read as `undefined`, because that is the answer the reader's own lookup gives: `resolveAccountEntry` does not match `"!!!"` for `"default"` either. The shared owner builder still normalizes non-optionally, so an `accounts` map naming only an unreadable id produces two config paths under one owner id (`line:default`), and a failure on the unreachable one isolates the reachable default account with it. That collapse is in `createChannelAccountSecretOwner`, not here, and matching it in LINE would put the wrong answer back.

One behavior note: a credential written as `$NAME` or `${NAME}` is now collected as an environment reference, which is how every other channel treats that spelling. The two spellings are matched by `^\$\{([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,127})\}$` and `^\$([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,127})$`; a LINE channel access token is a ~170-character mixed-case string, so no real credential can collide with it. The docs describe the object form, which is the spelling the reader and the collector agree on.

This PR touches `src/secrets/`, which CODEOWNERS assigns to `@openclaw/openclaw-secops`, with two files and no production code: `runtime-line-credential-inheritance.test.ts` and `runtime-line.test-support.ts`. The second follows the shape already there for Discord, Matrix, Telegram, Zalo and Nextcloud Talk, and the first uses it to run the real `prepareSecretsRuntimeSnapshot` against LINE's contract artifact rather than a hand-written double. Everything that runs in production is under `extensions/line/`.

No dependency, lockfile, or CHANGELOG changes.

## User Impact

A LINE operator can now keep both credentials outside `openclaw.json`:

```jsonc
{
  "secrets": { "providers": { "default": { "source": "store" } } },
  "channels": {
    "line": {
      "channelAccessToken": { "source": "store", "provider": "default", "id": "LINE_TOKEN" },
      "channelSecret": { "source": "store", "provider": "default", "id": "LINE_SECRET" }
    }
  }
}
```

Existing plaintext, `tokenFile`/`secretFile`, and `LINE_CHANNEL_ACCESS_TOKEN`/`LINE_CHANNEL_SECRET` configurations keep working unchanged, and their precedence is unchanged.

A configured reference owns its credential: when the runtime cannot resolve it at startup the account stops rather than quietly authenticating with `tokenFile`/`secretFile` or the environment variable the operator did not name. A reference that stops resolving later is a different case, and the Evidence below walks all three of them. `openclaw channels status` shows the account stopped with the reason and `openclaw doctor` points at that account's references rather than only the one that failed, with the retry command, instead of the account looking unconfigured. Rotating a stored value needs no config edit: `openclaw secrets reload` re-resolves it and restarts the LINE channel.

Guided setup answers per credential as a consequence, which reference support requires and which an operator on a plaintext config sees today:

- An account that holds one credential and not the other is no longer asked to retype the one it holds. A config with a channel access token and no signing secret used to prompt for both.
- A credential the runtime cannot resolve right now is judged by what it is. A reference the provider has not answered is still the operator's choice and can be kept; a credential file that cannot be read leaves nothing to keep, and the wizard asks for a credential, as it does today on `main`.

## Evidence

Run on a desktop LINE test channel against a real gateway built from this branch, with both credentials moved into the shared secret store and the config carrying only references. Three sittings are quoted below and every block says which one it belongs to. The blocks down to the audit pair come from the startup sitting, where each half restarts the gateway because the config changes between them; its platform verifications and tunnel rows carry matching timestamps. The rotation block comes from a separate sitting on one long-lived gateway, run earlier the same evening on the same build. The wizard and check blocks are neither: they are test runs, labelled with the commands that produced them.

```
$ openclaw --version
OpenClaw 2026.9.2 (5ccb173)
```

**Store, not config.** The credentials live in the store; the config names them:

```
$ openclaw secrets store list
LINE_STORE_SECRET [secret] (write-only); allowed hosts: none
LINE_STORE_TOKEN [secret] (write-only); allowed hosts: none

$ jq '.channels.line.accounts.default | {channelAccessToken, channelSecret}' openclaw.json
{
  "channelAccessToken": { "source": "store", "provider": "default", "id": "LINE_STORE_TOKEN" },
  "channelSecret": { "source": "store", "provider": "default", "id": "LINE_STORE_SECRET" }
}
```

**The command from the issue now succeeds**, and what lands in the config is the reference rather than a value resolved from it:

```
$ echo '{"channels":{"line":{"channelAccessToken":{"source":"store","provider":"default","id":"LINE_STORE_TOKEN"}}}}' | openclaw config patch --stdin
Config warnings: plugins.entries.codex: plugin disabled (bundled (disabled by default)) but config is present
Applied 1 config update(s). Restart the gateway to apply.

$ jq '.channels.line' openclaw.json
{
  "channelAccessToken": { "source": "store", "provider": "default", "id": "LINE_STORE_TOKEN" }
}
```

On `origin/main` that input cannot validate at all: `extensions/line/src/config-schema.ts` declares `channelAccessToken: z.string().optional()`, so an object is rejected before anything reads it.

**The account starts on the resolved credentials.** The startup probe reads the bot's display name back from the Messaging API using the resolved token:

```
2026-09-07T21:44:44.584+08:00 [line] [default] starting LINE provider (openclaw)
2026-09-07T21:44:44.592+08:00 line: registered webhook handler at /line/webhook

$ openclaw channels status
- LINE default: enabled, configured, running, connected, mode:webhook, token:***, signing:config
```

**LINE's own platform signs a request that the resolved signing secret validates.** This is the channel's webhook verification, so LINE computes the signature and reports the status it observed at our endpoint:

```
$ curl -X POST https://api.line.me/v2/bot/channel/webhook/test -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...'
{"success":true,"timestamp":"2026-09-07T13:44:53.826530Z","statusCode":200,"reason":"OK","detail":"200"}
```

**Negative half: the same config with the signing-secret reference pointed at a store key that does not exist, on a gateway restarted to pick it up.** Nothing else changed.

```
[secrets] [SECRETS_OWNER_UNAVAILABLE] Secret owner account:line:default is configured-unavailable;
          paths: channels.line.accounts.default.channelAccessToken,
                 channels.line.accounts.default.channelSecret
[secrets] [SECRETS_DEGRADED] cold account:line:default: secret reference was not found.
          Retry: openclaw secrets reload.
[line] channel startup failed: Secret owner account:line:default is configured but unavailable
       (secret reference was not found).

$ openclaw channels status
- LINE default: enabled, configured, reason:Secret owner account:line:default is configured but unavailable (secret reference was not found)., error:Secret owner account:line:default is configured but unavailable (secret reference was not found)., stopped
Warnings:
- line default: Channel runtime is blocked and needs operator action. (resolve the reported channel error, then restart the channel)

$ curl -X POST https://api.line.me/v2/bot/channel/webhook/test -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...'
{"success":false,"timestamp":"2026-09-07T13:45:34.726475Z","statusCode":403,"reason":"ERROR_STATUS_CODE","detail":"403"}
```

One unresolved reference degrades the account that owns it, so both of its config paths are named. `openclaw doctor` says the same against that gateway:

```
Secret runtime degradation
- cold account:line:default
  (channels.line.accounts.default.channelAccessToken,
   channels.line.accounts.default.channelSecret): secret reference was
   not found
  Retry: openclaw secrets reload
```

**Restoring the reference restores the channel**, with nothing else changed back:

```
$ openclaw channels status
- LINE default: enabled, configured, running, connected, mode:webhook, token:***, signing:config

$ curl -X POST https://api.line.me/v2/bot/channel/webhook/test -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...'
{"success":true,"timestamp":"2026-09-07T13:51:55.285903Z","statusCode":200,"reason":"OK","detail":"200"}
```

The tunnel in front of the gateway recorded all three of those deliveries, which is the whole A/B at the wire: same platform, same endpoint, same signature shape, and the only thing that differed between them was whether the signing secret could be resolved.

```
$ curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:4040/api/requests/http'          # newest first
21:51:55  POST /line/webhook -> 200 OK         reference restored
21:45:34  POST /line/webhook -> 403 Forbidden  reference pointed at a missing store key
21:44:53  POST /line/webhook -> 200 OK         reference resolved

all three: User-Agent LineBotWebhook/2.0, X-Line-Signature 44 chars
```

**Outbound uses the resolved access token.** Sent through OpenClaw rather than the raw API, and delivered to a real LINE account:

```
$ openclaw message send --channel line --target U4a… -m "…" --json
"deliveryStatus": "sent",
"payloadOutcomes": [ { "index": 0, "status": "sent", "resultCount": 1 } ]
```

**The audit can see LINE credentials for the first time.** Same build, two configs that differ only in whether those two fields hold references or literals:

```
# config with SecretRefs
Secrets audit: findings. plaintext=2, unresolved=0, shadowed=0, storeResidue=0, legacy=0.
- [PLAINTEXT_FOUND] gateway.auth.token is stored as plaintext.
- [PLAINTEXT_FOUND] models.providers.openrouter.apiKey is stored as plaintext.

# same build, credentials written inline
Secrets audit: findings. plaintext=4, unresolved=0, shadowed=0, storeResidue=0, legacy=0.
- [PLAINTEXT_FOUND] gateway.auth.token is stored as plaintext.
- [PLAINTEXT_FOUND] models.providers.openrouter.apiKey is stored as plaintext.
- [PLAINTEXT_FOUND] channels.line.accounts.default.channelAccessToken is stored as plaintext.
- [PLAINTEXT_FOUND] channels.line.accounts.default.channelSecret is stored as plaintext.
```

On `origin/main` the last two lines cannot appear at all: `extensions/line/secret-contract-api.ts` publishes `readonly []`, so the registry holds no LINE paths to audit.

**Rotating the stored value needs no config edit, and the new value is the one that gets used.** The store entry was changed twice on a running gateway; the config file was not touched:

```
$ openclaw secrets store set LINE_STORE_SECRET --value-file <a secret LINE will not accept>
Stored LINE_STORE_SECRET (secret).
A gateway is running. Run `openclaw secrets reload` for config-referenced values to take effect.

$ openclaw secrets reload
Secrets reloaded.

$ openclaw channels status
- LINE default: enabled, configured, running, connected, mode:webhook, token:***, signing:config

$ curl -X POST https://api.line.me/v2/bot/channel/webhook/test -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...'
{"success":false,"timestamp":"2026-09-07T13:34:20.193275Z","statusCode":401,"reason":"ERROR_STATUS_CODE","detail":"401"}

$ openclaw secrets store set LINE_STORE_SECRET --value-file <the real one>
$ openclaw secrets reload
$ curl -X POST https://api.line.me/v2/bot/channel/webhook/test -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...'
{"success":true,"timestamp":"2026-09-07T13:34:30.880093Z","statusCode":200,"reason":"OK","detail":"200"}

$ jq '.channels.line.accounts.default.channelSecret' openclaw.json   # unchanged throughout
{ "source": "store", "provider": "default", "id": "LINE_STORE_SECRET" }
```

The account stays up across the rotation because the reference still resolves; what changes is the value it resolves to, which is why LINE's signature check reports `401` rather than the `403` an unresolvable reference produces.

Removing the store entry outright, on the same running gateway, takes the third path the runtime has for a reference. This reload does not restart the channel at all, unlike the two rotations above it: the account keeps serving on the last value it resolved and the runtime says so, rather than dropping a live channel because a provider went away.

```
$ openclaw secrets store rm LINE_STORE_SECRET
Removed 1 team store entry.

$ openclaw secrets reload
Secrets reloaded with 1 warning(s).

[secrets] [SECRETS_OWNER_UNAVAILABLE] Secret owner account:line:default is using last-known-good;
          paths: channels.line.accounts.default.channelAccessToken,
                 channels.line.accounts.default.channelSecret
[secrets] [SECRETS_DEGRADED] stale account:line:default: secret reference was not found.
          Retry: openclaw secrets reload.

# and when the value comes back
[secrets] [SECRETS_RELOADER_RECOVERED] Secret resolution recovered; runtime remained on
          last-known-good during the outage.
```

So a LINE account now follows the same three states every other referenced credential has: `cold` and stopped when the reference cannot resolve at startup, `stale` and serving the last known good value when it stops resolving later, and recovered when it comes back. None of that is new machinery; LINE simply had no way to reach it.

**Guided setup.** The eight cases this PR adds are what hold the wizard's answer in place; seven of them fail if the answer is put back the way it was. Replacing the override with the whole-account question `main` asks reddens four of them; replacing it with the first attempt at the credential-file fix reddens the two that watch an unreadable file; removing it entirely reddens four:

```
$ vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-line.config.ts extensions/line/src/setup-surface.test.ts
      Tests  18 passed (18)

# with accountConfigured replaced by main's Boolean(token && secret)
 × answers each credential from what that credential resolved to
 × keeps a plaintext credential while the other one is a reference it cannot resolve
 × does not ask for the credential the account already has while the other is missing
 × treats a configured reference as configured while it stays unresolved
      Tests  4 failed | 14 passed (18)

# with the override moved back onto hasConfiguredValue
 × treats a credential file it cannot read as nothing to keep
 × asks for the credential behind an unreadable file even when the env var is set
      Tests  2 failed | 16 passed (18)

# with the override removed
 × answers each credential from what that credential resolved to
 × treats a credential file it cannot read as nothing to keep
 × asks for the credential behind an unreadable file even when the env var is set
 × asks for a token instead of offering to keep one behind an unreadable file
      Tests  4 failed | 14 passed (18)
```

**Checks.** All of the following ran on Windows at `4a7d6c0b92c`, on a branch rebased onto `233dabe750a`. One commit follows it, and it rewrites a single sentence in `docs/channels/line.md`; the format check below was re-run after it:

```
$ vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-line.config.ts extensions/line
 Test Files  2 failed | 53 passed (55)
      Tests  57 failed | 807 passed | 1 skipped (865)
```

Every failure is in `bot-message-context.test.ts` (45) and `bot-mention-context.test.ts` (12), from SQLite `EBUSY` unlinks and 120s timeouts that this branch does not touch. Running those two files alone in a pristine worktree checked out at this branch's base gives the same result, and the failing test names are identical in both directions:

```
$ vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-line.config.ts \
    extensions/line/src/bot-message-context.test.ts extensions/line/src/bot-mention-context.test.ts
 Test Files  2 failed (2)
      Tests  57 failed | 2 passed (59)

$ comm -3 branch-failures.txt baseline-failures.txt
(no output; 56 distinct names on each side)
```

The rest:

```
vitest --config test/vitest/vitest.secrets.config.ts src/secrets/{target-registry.docs,
        runtime-line-credential-inheritance,runtime.coverage}.test.ts   92 passed

tsgo -p tsconfig.extensions.json --noEmit                     0 errors
tsgo -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --noEmit  0 errors
pnpm lint:extensions                                          pass
oxfmt --check <all 16 changed .ts and .md files>              pass  (at 5ccb173f807)
pnpm check:assertion-safety  --base origin/main               3980 files, no new assertions
pnpm check:max-lines-ratchet --base origin/main               pass
pnpm config:channels:check                                    pass
```

**Not exercised.** A message typed by a person in the LINE client: the Windows LINE app ignores synthetic mouse and keyboard input, so the inbound half here is LINE's own platform verification rather than a user-authored message. That path is unchanged by this PR, and both credentials it depends on are exercised above.

prs.title: fix: side-chat questions send on Shift+Enter and do not wrap
prs.body:
Closes #141091
Related: #45591

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Side chat questions submitting on Shift+Enter instead of retaining paragraphs. Long questions stayed on one horizontally scrolling line, and submitted paragraph breaks could collapse.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use a one-row textarea with the existing composer sizing and submission lifecycle. Shift+Enter inserts a newline; Enter and Ask send once. Keep the shared height cap and 400-character limit.

History, empty-state content, and starter buttons share the existing scroll area above the composer. This keeps Ask visible when a long draft fills a narrow panel. Completed, pending, and failed questions preserve paragraph breaks.

## User Impact

Users can draft, review, and send multiline Side chat questions without interrupting the main draft. Long text wraps, scrolls inside the bounded editor, and shrinks after deletion or sending. Retry, reconnect, session drafts, and the main composer retain their existing behavior.

## Evidence

The repository's production-bundle Control UI fixture ran in Chromium 151.0.7922.34 with Playwright 1.62.1 and a synthetic Gateway at 1200×800 and 560×800, plus a 400×800 resize. Responses and session content are synthetic.

- Baseline `b827d2035651fb80be322ba3b1740ad13b2aa0e3`: Shift+Enter sent only the first paragraph and cleared the draft at both widths. Long text did not wrap.
- Production candidate `f38d2317ef077a6ce8fe5b6ea936e8db38490a08`: four browser cases pass, including exact Enter/Ask requests, pending/error/retry/reconnect, native character limits, focus, prefill, resizing, reattachment, session drafts, and main-composer submission.
- Independent acceptance first found that long narrow drafts hid Ask. The content scroll repair and an always-on viewport assertion now cover that failure. Fresh independent acceptance passes; long-draft Ask and starter submissions are exercised directly.
- Final head `50b1dd41067259b3eb1d37c5ecb90a951a10b59e` adds only two existing-test corrections after that production proof: metadata checks no longer hard-code the removed history floor, and the quote test targets the main composer by its accessible name. Three rail-layout cases and both quote-destination cases pass.
- 48 owner/lifecycle tests pass. Formatting, stylesheet lint, and focused static lint pass. Hosted checks are tracked on the [PR checks page](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/141101/checks).
- Composition uses recorded controlled browser events, including both Enter variants with composing state. This is not a real operating-system input-method or live-model test.

Fresh media below was inspected locally, then all 14 linked files were reopened anonymously and verified against those inspected bytes. The earlier inaccessible-media review history and the contributor's paragraph-rendering correction remain preserved.

Thanks @KJ21-ENG for the original repair and paragraph-rendering follow-up. All five contributor commits are retained.

<details>
<summary>Requested AI discussion transcript (task-relevant excerpts)</summary>

The reporter explicitly requested that this PR include the relevant discussion and a recording. These are excerpts from the visible conversation, not a full raw session export. Tool logs, environment details, and unrelated context are omitted.

**User:** “The problem is, as you can see in the video, that in the side panel text box, there is no concept of Shift+Enter/Return to go to a new line. When we are typing some lengthy text, it remains on a single line, so it's very hard for the user to write text in such an environment. That's not the case with the main text box of the main interface.”

**Assistant:** “Yes—I think this is worth raising as a UX bug, rather than a new feature. The side-chat input should support writing paragraphs and long prompts, consistently with the main composer.”

**Assistant (expected behavior):** “Shift+Enter/Return inserts a newline without sending. Long text wraps and the input grows, with internal scrolling after a reasonable height.”

**User:** “I would like you to go ahead and raise a PR with all the requirements and rules of OpenClaw…” The user also requested a relevant discussion transcript and a recording attached through GitHub's new attachment support.

**Implementation-session summary, not a verbatim transcript:** Current-source inspection found a native single-line input. Browser reproduction showed unintended submission on Shift+Enter. The repair reuses existing composer sizing instead of introducing another sizing system. Browser and owner/sibling tests validated paragraph entry and sending; the evidence above states the test boundary.

</details>

prs.title: fix(daemon): keep Windows service launchers intact when a rewrite fails
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #141002

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where users updating the Windows service (Scheduled Task or Startup login item) would have their existing `gateway.cmd` / `gateway.vbs` launcher truncated when the rewrite fails partway (e.g. disk full), even though the registered task or login entry still points at that file — the next service start or login then finds an 11-byte `@echo off` stub and `readScheduledTaskCommand` returns `null`.
- **Related:** #140760 addresses the same publication pattern for Linux/macOS service env files; this PR is the independent Windows CMD/VBS owner and does not touch other platforms or request a multi-file service transaction.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** a failed publication leaves the previous complete launcher in place; the replacement only takes over the path after its bytes have been fully staged. Covered write sites: the shared stage/install task script (CMD), the hidden-task launcher (VBS), and the Startup-folder fallback entry (CMD/VBS).
- **Out of scope:** Linux/macOS service publication, the restart-helper/temporary launcher writers (they already create fresh `wx` paths), and any multi-file transaction across script + task registration.
- **Highest-risk area:** launcher file modes and directory side effects of the new staged write.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** publication reuses the repo's canonical `replaceFileAtomic` helper with `preserveExistingMode` and the directory's existing mode, and regression tests assert prior bytes, prior mode, no `.tmp` leftovers, no Scheduler activation on failure, and a later successful rewrite. No in-place copy fallback is enabled, so a locked destination fails closed instead of tearing the file again.

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** after any failed launcher rewrite (partial write or failed rename), the previously installed launcher still contains its full previous content, its mode is unchanged, and command readback keeps returning the old command; a later install with the fault cleared republishes successfully.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `src/daemon/schtasks-layout.ts` (`publishWindowsLauncherScript`), `src/daemon/schtasks-install.ts` (three call sites), and the fault-injection regressions in `src/daemon/schtasks.install.test.ts` and `src/daemon/schtasks.startup-fallback.test.ts` (marker `#141002`).

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** real `stageScheduledTask`/`installScheduledTask` owners against a temp `USERPROFILE` filesystem, exercised both through the repo test fixtures and through a standalone reproduction script (no test runner) that drives the same owners with fault injection at the real filesystem write/rename boundary, plus one fully kernel-level fault (read-only launcher directory → real `EACCES`, zero mocking). The pinned `@openclaw/fs-safe` 0.8.3 `replaceFileAtomic(preserveExistingMode)` behavior was also verified directly against the installed package.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # 1. Regression tests on the unpatched owner (before evidence): new cases fail with the truncation from the report
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/daemon/schtasks.install.test.ts src/daemon/schtasks.startup-fallback.test.ts
  # 2. Same suites after the patch (all pass), plus the full daemon shard
  ```

prs.title: fix(mac): preserve companion exec timeouts
prs.body:
Closes #139706

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running long commands through the macOS companion would hit an unexplained failure after about 20 seconds, even when the requested command timeout was much longer. The Gateway reported the companion as unavailable and could not return the command's real result.

## Why This Change Was Made

The companion request already carries the caller's command timeout, so the socket response deadline now follows it with a 5-second grace period. The transport also distinguishes pre-send unavailability, post-send response loss, and response timeout; submitted commands remain fail-closed and are never replayed locally. A zero command timeout disables the transport deadline as well.

## User Impact

Long-running macOS companion commands can now wait for their requested lifetime and return their actual result. A late response is reported as `TIMEOUT`, while a lost response is reported as an unknown outcome instead of being mislabeled as an unreachable companion. Safe fallback remains available only when the request was never submitted.

## Evidence

- Before fix, base `9e5bb4a3ecd`: the real UDS regression suite passed while its `timeout` case observed `null` after a signed request had started a child; the direct probe returned: `{"result":null}`
- After fix, commit `eb8b824922a`: the same 50 ms transport probe with a 30 s command timeout returned: `{"result":{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"TIMEOUT","reason":"timeout","message":"TIMEOUT: macOS app exec host response timed out; execution outcome is unknown"}}}`
- Response-loss probe changed from `{"result":null}` before the fix to typed `UNKNOWN / response-lost` after the fix.
- Real UDS transport tests: **21 passed**, including child-started timeout, response-loss, malformed-response, zero-timeout, signing, and cancellation cases.
- Node-host system-run tests: **87 passed**; enforced response-loss path confirms `runCommand` was not called (no local replay).
- `pnpm test:changed`: passed.
- `pnpm check`: passed.
- `pnpm check:changed`: passed.
- `pnpm build`: passed.
- Autoreview: `scoped-clean`, no accepted/actionable P0/P1 findings.
- No screenshot is applicable; this is a transport/runtime behavior change with no UI surface.

## Rebase onto `main` (`e8684576989`)

Main still uses a fixed 20 s socket deadline (`exec-host.ts`, `params.timeoutMs ?? 20_000`) and maps every transport failure to `COMPANION_APP_UNAVAILABLE`. Conflicts were re-expressed on main's current node-host code:

- `src/node-host/invoke.ts`: main removed `runViaMacAppExecHost` and moved the macOS app dispatch into `invoke-system-run.ts`. Main's version is kept; the response deadline is now derived inside `requestExecHostViaSocket` from `request.timeoutMs` (+5 s grace, `0` disables it), so no call-site timeout is needed. The previously exported `resolveExecHostResponseTimeoutMs` is inlined (it would otherwise be a test-only export); `exec-host.test.ts` covers the same three cases through the real call.
- `src/node-host/invoke-system-run.ts`: `sendSystemRunDenied` now takes `(opts, execution, message, reason)`; `timeout` → `TIMEOUT` and `response-lost` → `UNKNOWN` are mapped there.
- `invoke-system-run.test.ts` / `invoke-system-run.socket.test.ts`: the two new cases are rewritten on main's `runMac` / `invokeResult` / `expectExecDeniedEvent` helpers; the socket test asserts the exact `UNKNOWN` result and the `response-lost` denial reason.
- `src/infra/exec-host.native.test-support.ts`: the macOS native transport proof expected `null` after a dropped response; it now expects the typed `UNKNOWN` / `response-lost` result.

The numbers above are from the previous base; CI on this head is the gate for the re-run. The native proof runs on macOS only.

prs.title: fix(infra): decode OEM console code pages in Windows subprocess output
prs.body:
Related: #135856, #136203

Not a fix for #135856. That report is `doctor --fix` refusing maintenance, and this pull request no longer changes Doctor or Scheduled Task inventory.

The Spanish and German `schtasks /FO LIST` parser was dropped. Current main reads task inventory from typed COM (`Schedule.Service`) through `listScheduledTasks`, and #151608 superseded the localized LIST-parser part of this pull request.

## What Problem This Solves

Windows subprocess output on a Spanish or German console comes back with U+FFFD in place of accented characters. Those consoles default to OEM code page 850. `chcp` reports 850, the console encoding probe only consulted the ANSI code-page map, and Node's `TextDecoder` has no label for the OEM `cp###` pages, so the bytes were decoded as UTF-8.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `chcp` probe now falls back to the existing OEM code-page map that the `.cmd` launcher already uses. Legacy decoding goes through iconv-lite for the `cp###` labels ICU lacks. `decodeWindowsOutputBuffer` and `createWindowsOutputDecoder` share that decoder. Valid UTF-8 is still tried first, and UTF-16 BOM handling is unchanged. The system ANSI probe is unchanged. Main's locale-independent task inventory is left as it is.

`src/infra/windows-encoding.ts` is on the PR wrapper inventory, so iconv-lite is pinned in that extracted dependency context. Without the pin, wrapper boot could not load the module.

## User Impact

Windows command output on the OEM console pages in that map, including 850, decodes accented text instead of replacement characters. English and UTF-8 consoles are unchanged. Deep Scheduled Task scanning stays on main's COM inventory.

## Evidence

No native localized Windows run was done. The previous Linux stand-in exercised the `schtasks /FO LIST` parser, and that path has been removed, so it is not proof for this scope.

Focused tests on the decoder head (Node 24.21.0):

prs.title: fix(slack): inherit root action gates in account overrides
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes partial Slack account-level `actions` overrides discarding channel-level restrictions for gates the account did not name.

With this configuration

```json
{
  "channels": {
    "slack": {
      "actions": { "messages": false, "pins": false },
      "accounts": {
        "work": { "botToken": "xoxb-...", "actions": { "reactions": true } }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

`work` resolved to `{ "reactions": true }`. Missing gates default to enabled, so discovery advertised disabled message and pin actions, and the runtime gate let them proceed to later checks. Target policy and API authorization still apply.

## User Impact

Account overrides now change only named gates. `actions: {}` previously reset every gate to enabled and now inherits channel-level gates. Anyone relying on replacement must explicitly enable the desired account gates. Root-only and account-only settings resolve as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The five-file delta adds `actions` to the nested merge list in `extensions/slack/src/accounts.ts`, three tests and one sentence in `docs/channels/slack/access-control.md`. The schema already accepts partial objects. Both consumers are unchanged.

The docs add a previously undocumented contract. Replacement predates refactor `ff759f991e6f`, but the inspected history establishes neither its introduction nor an intended reset contract. Earlier introduction-date and affected-release-range claims are withdrawn.

## Decision Needed

A maintainer must decide whether partial or empty account `actions` should inherit unset keys or replace the whole block. Acceptance remains pending.

## Evidence

On October 12, head `ec516390d97512019f058caafcda267b35d00317` merged cleanly against main `4f1b5766b6b9d166d15c6adc214f6f7983133aa6` in a merge check. No code changed and no tests were rerun.

Prior evidence records main `2d6f7a3052a0` merged with upstream test deletions retained, 28 tests in 74.17 seconds, changed-file checks in 1103.52 seconds and no actionable review findings through P2. Those records were not independently reconstructed today. Exact-head [CI 38024921612](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38024921612) passed, including `openclaw/ci-gate` and `security-fast`. Its published-driver job was skipped.

### Historical behavior checks

Earlier published results compare `fbae6ae9573f54f1504f40476ee2c9af0a5c635a` with baseline `cf0f8f90a7b6317a5a618ac5d5a7e69e01c050d2`. They were not rerun or independently reconstructed today.

- The account regression expects `work` to resolve to `{ messages: false, pins: false, reactions: true }` and the default account to retain the root object.
- With all root gates false and only account reactions enabled, discovery lists exactly `send`, `react`, and `reactions`.
- The runtime regression rejects `listPins` with "Slack pins are disabled" before any API call, while a `react` control runs.

The recorded baseline failed all three regressions. A discovery-only change left account and runtime checks failing. The runtime test uses a sibling file to respect the line limit.

Built CLI results with the example config and placeholder tokens were

| Check for account `work` | Baseline | Fixed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Capability discovery | exit 0, all 15 actions | exit 0, `send`, `broadcast`, `react`, `reactions`, `member-info`, `emoji-list` |
| `message pins --channel slack --account work` | exit 1, "Slack read target channel is not allowed." | exit 1, "Slack pins are disabled." |
| `message react --channel slack --account work` | exit 1, "Slack read target channel is not allowed." | same exit and error |

The unchanged reaction error proves gate passage, not delivery. The recorded default-account control without an override failed at the pins gate on both builds.

Historical records report 165 focused tests, 170 files/3124 extension tests, 145 files/2739 source tests, and passing type, lint, format, docs and assertion-safety checks, not current-head reruns.

### Supplementary forward upgrade on October 11

The PR declares `2026.9.9`. October 11's stable baseline was `2026.10.1`. Candidate [`b682ad79204c`](https://github.com/marmar9615-cloud/openclaw/commit/b682ad79204c585b345e1628746679812df81a00) applies the exact five-file delta to published [`2026.10.5-beta.1`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.10.5-beta.1), parent `f283c3c71226c2e1d9ca06b11972f8bdb3969bd8`. This proves release-line integration, not an exact-head forward upgrade. No release or extra PR was published.

[Run 38155906533](https://github.com/marmar9615-cloud/openclaw/actions/runs/38155906533), harness [`53f5600b88877`](https://github.com/marmar9615-cloud/openclaw/blob/53f5600b88877ac7d81610cd5f0b4773a7b6ed0c/proof.mjs), passed 47 checks, 28 tests in 52.040 seconds and changed-file checks in 918.444 seconds. Packaging passed. Source and harness reviews found no actionable P0 through P2 findings.

Both fixtures used published core and official Slack `2026.10.1`, all root gates false, and `work` set to `{ reactions: true }` or `{}`. Normal core plus external Slack retained the `@openclaw/slack@latest` selector. A sealed local registry supplied the matching companion without fabricated ownership.

Captured command and result excerpts are

```text
$ openclaw update --channel beta --tag /app/package/candidate.tgz --yes --no-restart --json
both fixtures exit=0, status="ok", run.status="succeeded"
before.version="2026.10.1", after.version="2026.10.5-beta.1"
slack plugin status="updated", sync.errors=[], integrityDrifts=[]

$ openclaw channels capabilities --channel slack --account work --json --timeout 1000
before update, both fixtures exit=0, all 15 actions
after update, partial exit=0, ["send","broadcast","react","reactions"]
after update, empty exit=0, ["send","broadcast"]
```

Installed core matched `b682ad79204c585b345e1628746679812df81a00`. External Slack loaded at `2026.10.5-beta.1` with matching SHA-512 integrity in both install records. Account actions, `channels.slack`, `gateway` and `plugins` were unchanged. Whole-file equality is false. Only empty webhook migration arrays for `telegram`, `feishu` and `nextcloud-talk`, `agents.entries.main`, `meta.lastTouchedVersion`, `wizard.lastRun*` and requested `update.channel` changed.

No live actions were sent. Offline probes returned expected connection-refused errors. These checks cover update completion and discovery, not live delivery or managed Gateway activation. Restart was skipped. Dummy plaintext credentials caused plugin status `warning`. Automatic database restoration was unavailable because an unknown writer changed databases after capture. Snapshots remained and cleanup was deferred. Rollback, complete data-resource recovery and production health were not proven.

Recorded SHA-256 identities follow. The [transcript, command records, plugin indexes and config snapshots](https://github.com/marmar9615-cloud/openclaw/actions/runs/38155906533/artifacts/11709788486) expire November 10, 2026.

| Item | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| Exact source delta | `40103994e51b960236893dbede3245cadbc168172524a9dfee6390e2664c80a9` |
| Candidate core | `f4c232fab8b16189ecea85d24fef545bdaab14ec70fba4a0704b646dbb4e76aa` |
| External Slack | `b82815544cd80c9aaa14b87590fb6f33c20419d4632ba11cb607ca839202bc2b` |
| Registry manifest | `ef974ec5c6325aeb58cbd015c71dd45cb6cfdd90f4acca7727dc6910b53e9d80` |

Earlier attempts [38155267259](https://github.com/marmar9615-cloud/openclaw/actions/runs/38155267259) and [38155468679](https://github.com/marmar9615-cloud/openclaw/actions/runs/38155468679) stopped on harness environment problems before updater fixtures ran. The latter had passed the 28 focused tests.

### Exact-head downgrade failed

[Run 38151741290](https://github.com/marmar9615-cloud/openclaw/actions/runs/38151741290) built and installed the exact PR head with `--bundle-plugin slack`. This custom `2026.9.9` package contained matching Slack source, unlike stock core. Its SHA-256 was `8f59b0067b4f6d39b4cf780f9e41c34bab27da713f3644525984357cc290e8d2`.

The baseline used published core `2026.10.1`, commit `e178c39e9aae3fa440735217f9aef9574f286677`, and official Slack `2026.10.1`. Action configs matched the cases above. The update command omitted `--channel beta`. Candidate action lists matched the forward results. Explicit account actions and the Slack, Gateway and plugin sections were preserved.

Both updater fixtures failed with exit 1. This was a downgrade/replacement from `2026.10.1` to `2026.9.9`, not forward-upgrade proof. Installation, candidate checks, startup canary, swap and configuration repair succeeded, but plugin handling reported `Plugin "slack" has no authoritative package-owner metadata`. Backup retention and recovery were unverified, the updater returned `state-migrated-no-rollback`, and a later cleanup import failed. The internal plugin index was not captured, so the deeper cause remains unestablished. Whole-file configuration preservation is not claimed.

These package proofs ran in isolated CI containers without repository or environment secrets or live Slack actions. The [transcript, commands, identities and configs](https://github.com/marmar9615-cloud/openclaw/actions/runs/38151741290/artifacts/11707372026) expire November 10, 2026. The forward result neither erases this failure nor establishes its cause.

prs.title: fix(cli): reject blank channels capabilities selectors
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes `openclaw channels capabilities` treating an explicitly blank selector as omitted, which could widen a channel report or skip a target permission audit.

## User Impact

Blank or whitespace-only `--channel`, `--agent`, and `--target` values now fail with exit 1 and a message naming the flag, consistent with the existing `--account` guard. Omitting selectors preserves the existing defaults. Scripts that pass empty variables must omit those flags when they want the default scope. No configuration migration is required.

Maintainer acceptance of this behavior change remains pending. The evidence below does not imply product approval.

## Why This Change Was Made

Capabilities reuses the existing `parseChannelSelector` owner. Account validation remains at its option parser, while the agent/target guards run after config validation and before secret resolution, discovery, and probes. The selector matrix stays at the cheaper command boundary, with one process smoke test for nonzero exit and JSON rendering.

Related PRs are #133781 and #136412.

## Evidence

- On October 12, 2026 the head was still `451a32c657f`, and a merge check against upstream main `4f1b5766b6b` reported a clean merge with no conflicts. No code changed, and no tests or proof were rerun for this check.
- Current head is `451a32c657fb1ac7f2fc167294f364c93819decf`. [Durable built-CLI command/output transcript](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/137233#issuecomment-6111025779) records all 10 blank/whitespace rejection cases and four omission controls passing on the installed `2026.9.9` package. It includes channel, agent, target with and without a channel, and the existing account guard. The canonical custom package includes Slack and Discord from the same commit.

Capability commands ran offline. Expected health-probe errors are not live-connectivity proof. The workflow's separate PR #137250 job failed. It does not invalidate this selector job.

The single-worker process-test command took 30.17 seconds. No product code was executed locally for this evidence update.
- Existing code reviews reported no actionable findings. Both earlier code-review conversations are resolved. This update publishes evidence without changing the reviewed head or rerunning valid proof.

Earlier published validation records seven failing command regressions on baseline `cf0f8f90a7b6317a5a618ac5d5a7e69e01c050d2`, followed by 26 passes at `19d8f01de3a0f3d1d1f57306dce151485defad29`. It also records a later local `check:changed` failure on an environment-variable budget mismatch of 456 versus 455, reproduced at the preceding head. prs.title: fix(acp): scope-check read locations before auto-approval
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An ACP agent connected to OpenClaw can read files outside the working directory without the operator ever seeing a permission prompt. It presents an in-cwd path as the tool input and puts the real target in `toolCall.locations`, which the read approval path never scope-checks.

The `read` branch of `classifyAcpToolApproval` builds its path candidates with `includeLocations: false`, so `toolCall.locations` is dropped before the scope check runs. A read whose `rawInput.path` sits inside cwd but whose declared `locations` point outside cwd classifies as `readonly_scoped` and auto-approves.

`resolvePermissionRequest` (`src/acp/client-helpers.ts:115`) passes `params.toolCall` straight through from the connected agent, and `RequestPermissionRequest.toolCall` is a `ToolCallUpdate`, which carries `locations?: ToolCallLocation[]`. Any connected agent can set it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The scope check now runs over `rawPaths` plus `readLocationPaths(toolCall.locations)`. `readLocationPaths` already existed in the file. `rawPaths.length > 0` still gates the grant, so a locations-only request with no real path source still denies, and the change can only ever deny more, never approve something that was previously blocked.

The sibling `SAFE_SEARCH_TOOL_IDS` branch ten lines down already passes `includeLocations: true` and has two tests pinning that an escaping location denies. The read branch was given the opposite requirement to pin, "does not auto-approve reads from locations-only metadata", and the author satisfied it by dropping locations from the candidate list entirely, which threw away the deny side along with it. No test combined an in-cwd `rawInput.path` with an out-of-cwd location, so the gap stayed invisible.

## User Impact

A read that declares a location outside the working directory now prompts the operator instead of auto-approving. Reads that stay inside cwd are unaffected.

Unattended ACP clients have no TTY, so that prompt already returns false and the request rejects or cancels. Mixed-scope reads that previously auto-approved in those setups will stop after this change. That is the same deny path search already uses for an escaping location.

## Evidence

Live trace against a real ACP agent, not a unit test. The peer is a separate process speaking NDJSON JSON-RPC on stdio; the client side is the real `runAcpClientInteractive` into `createAcpClient`, `spawn`, `ClientSideConnection`, `resolvePermissionRequest`. It runs on a pty so the operator prompt takes its interactive branch instead of the non-interactive fallback. cwd is the checkout root, `rawInput.path` is `src/acp/client.ts` and sits inside it, `locations[0]` is `/etc/passwd` and does not.

The agent sends the identical frame in both runs:

```
[agent send] {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":9001,"method":"session/request_permission","params":{"sessionId":"sess-acp-trace","toolCall":{"toolCallId":"call-1","title":"read: src/acp/client.ts","kind":"read","status":"pending","rawInput":{"path":"src/acp/client.ts"},"locations":[{"path":"/etc/passwd"}]},"options":[{"optionId":"allow-once","name":"Allow once","kind":"allow_once"},{"optionId":"reject-once","name":"Reject","kind":"reject_once"}]}}
```

Before, nothing is asked and the client answers for the operator:

```
[tool] read: src/acp/client.ts (pending)
[permission auto-approved] read (readonly_scoped)
[agent recv] {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":9001,"result":{"outcome":{"outcome":"selected","optionId":"allow-once"}}}
```

After, the prompt fires and typing `n` puts a reject on the wire (the doubled `n` is pty echo):

```
[tool] read: src/acp/client.ts (pending)

[permission requested] read: src/acp/client.ts (read) [other]

[permission] Allow "read: src/acp/client.ts (read)"? (y/N) nn

[permission denied] read
[agent recv] {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":9001,"result":{"outcome":{"outcome":"selected","optionId":"reject-once"}}}
```

Same build, `locations[0]` moved to `src/acp/client-helpers.ts` inside cwd, still auto-approves, so this is not denying everything:

```
[permission auto-approved] read (readonly_scoped)
```

Tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.config.ts src/acp/approval-classifier.test.ts` is 30 passed. The new case fails before the change, returning `readonly_scoped` / `autoApprove: true` where `other` / `false` is expected.

AI-assisted. Fully tested.

prs.title: fix(macos): run bundle copy off the main thread during self-install
prs.body:
## Problem

When OpenClaw is launched under **App Translocation** (the `com.apple.quarantine` xattr is still present on `/Applications/OpenClaw.app`), `handleLaunch()` falls into the `.offerInstall` path and calls `install()` **synchronously on the main thread**.

`copyItem()` on a 2 GB+ bundle blocks `applicationDidFinishLaunching` for minutes:
- No menu bar icon appears, no window opens
- CPU sits at 200–286 % continuously
- The process **cannot be terminated with SIGTERM** because the main thread is stuck in a kernel `write()` syscall — only `kill -9` works
- macOS generates a diagnostic report showing ~2.1 GB written in 40 s

Root cause and stack trace are documented in #134736.

## Changes

1. **`install()` is now `async`** — `copyItem` runs in a `Task.detached(priority: .userInitiated)` so the main thread can finish launching and present UI. `replaceItemAt` / `moveItem` stay on the main actor. Partial-copy and backup deletes are awaited off the main thread before exit.

2. **`.offerInstall` uses the existing activation-aware `confirmInstall`** (`AppActivation.shared.presentAlert`). When the confirm alert is answered before `handleLaunch` returns, the result is `.installing` and startup waits. If the copy fails, the failure alert is shown and the temporary app continues: menu, dock, and gateway start from that copy, matching a declined install. If the copy succeeds but the relaunch helper cannot be spawned, that process still quits, because the Applications copy is already installed and the alert tells the user to open it. A deferred `--no-activate` confirmation still returns `.continueLaunch` and does not terminate a session that already started.

3. **Relaunch** keeps the current activation-aware helper (`open` with `-g` / `--no-activate` when activation is disallowed).

4. **Progress copy** uses `String(localized:)` and is inventoried in `apps/.i18n/native-source.json` (catalog / locale JSON left to the native locale refresh).

## Testing

- Nesting-guard unit tests were removed with the unused staging containment surface (`isPath(_:nestedIn:)` / `UnsafeCopyDestinationError`); ClawSweeper withdrew that finding as unused surface when staging is under Applications.
- `pnpm native:i18n:verify` passed on Linux. `pnpm native:i18n:check` still reports untranslated locale rows for the two new progress strings; those catalogs belong to the native locale refresh.
- No Swift toolchain was available in the Linux agent environment, and no macOS offer-install recording is attached (fresh install / replacement / failure on a real Mac remain unproven).

## Risk

- Normal activation no longer blocks `applicationDidFinishLaunching` on the multi-GB copy. The transient bundle does not start gateway, menu, or onboarding while copying; the progress window stays up until relaunch or a failure alert (after which the temporary app continues launching).
- `FileManager.copyItem` work runs in a detached task with a task-local `FileManager()`; awaited cleanup avoids abandoning multi-GB staging/backup deletes on quit.
- A deferred `--no-activate` approval does not terminate an already-started session.

Fixes #134736

prs.title: fix(security): block Vault and 1Password CLI controls from workspace .env
prs.body:
## Summary
Hardening for the workspace `.env` blocklist. The bundled Vault and 1Password SecretRef resolvers read `VAULT_ADDR`, `VAULT_NAMESPACE`, `VAULT_TOKEN`, `VAULT_TOKEN_FILE`, and `CLAW_1PASSWORD_OP` from the Gateway environment, but none of these keys are blocked from workspace `.env` loading. Because the workspace file is loaded before the trusted global `~/.openclaw/.env`, a value committed in a project's `.env` takes precedence over the one the user configured globally, which lets the project choose the Vault endpoint and namespace or the `op` executable used for SecretRef resolution.

## Root cause
`src/infra/dotenv.ts`, `BLOCKED_WORKSPACE_DOTENV_KEYS` and `shouldBlockWorkspaceStaticDotEnvKey`. The blocklist covers `OPENCLAW_*` (so `OPENCLAW_VAULT_*` is already blocked) and similar executable or endpoint controls such as `HOMEBREW_CURL_PATH` and `UV_PYTHON`, but the unprefixed Vault keys and the 1Password CLI path have no entry and match no blocked suffix or prefix:

```ts
// before
  "SYNOLOGY_NAS_HOST",
  "UV_PYTHON",
  "ZALO_API_URL",
]);
```

The Vault resolver (`extensions/vault/vault-secret-ref-resolver.js`) sends `X-Vault-Token` to whatever `VAULT_ADDR` it receives, and the 1Password resolver (`extensions/onepassword/onepassword-secret-ref-resolver.js`) runs `CLAW_1PASSWORD_OP` with `OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN` in its environment. Both keys are in the manifests' `passEnv`, so the workspace value flows straight through.

## Fix
Add the keys the bundled resolvers actually read to the static blocklist, following the `HOMEBREW_CURL_PATH` / `HOMEBREW_GIT_PATH` precedent (#146389):

```ts
// after
  "CLAWHUB_URL",
  "CLAW_1PASSWORD_OP",
  "COMSPEC",
  ...
  "UV_PYTHON",
  "VAULT_ADDR",
  "VAULT_NAMESPACE",
  "VAULT_TOKEN",
  "VAULT_TOKEN_FILE",
  "ZALO_API_URL",
]);
```

## Why this is the right boundary
The workspace `.env` filter is the single gate both the sync (`loadWorkspaceDotEnvFile`, used by `loadCliDotEnv` and `loadDotEnv`) and async (`loadDotEnvAsync`) loaders route through via `shouldBlockWorkspaceStaticDotEnvKey`, so one entry per key covers every loader. Only keys that code reads are added: a grep for `VAULT_` and `CLAW_1PASSWORD` across the repo finds exactly these five outside `OPENCLAW_*`. No `VAULT_` prefix was added because nothing else in the tree reads one. Values from the launching shell and from the trusted global `.env` keep working, which is the configuration path the Vault and 1Password docs describe.

## Verification
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/dotenv-workspace-blocklist.test.ts`: on pristine `upstream/main` 9a18261098 with the new keys added to the existing runtime-control list, 1 failed / 8 passed (`CLAW_1PASSWORD_OP should be blocked by workspace .env: expected 'INJECTED_CLAW_1PASSWORD_OP' to be undefined`); with this patch, 9 passed.
- oxlint, oxfmt, tsgo, and build were left to CI.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: a project `.env` overrides the globally configured `VAULT_ADDR` and sets `VAULT_NAMESPACE` and `CLAW_1PASSWORD_OP`, so SecretRef resolution goes to the project's choice of Vault endpoint and `op` executable.
Real environment tested: macOS, Node 26.9.0. A standalone driver chdirs into a project directory and calls the real `loadCliDotEnv` from `src/cli/dotenv.ts` (the CLI startup loader) with `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` pointing at a state dir whose global `.env` sets `VAULT_ADDR=http://127.0.0.1:18201` and `VAULT_TOKEN=user-vault-token`, plus a 1Password service-account token file. The project `.env` sets `VAULT_ADDR=http://127.0.0.1:18202`, `VAULT_NAMESPACE=repo-namespace`, and `CLAW_1PASSWORD_OP=<project>/bin/op` (a `#!/bin/sh` script). The driver then spawns the real unmodified `extensions/vault/vault-secret-ref-resolver.js` and `extensions/onepassword/onepassword-secret-ref-resolver.js` with the manifest `passEnv` keys from the loaded environment, and two local HTTP listeners stand in for Vault servers. Run on pristine `upstream/main` 9a18261098 and on this patch with identical inputs; only `src/infra/dotenv.ts` differs. No `op` CLI is installed on this machine. The temp fixture prefix is shortened to `<tmp>` below.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH=<checkout>/tsconfig.json node --import <checkout>/node_modules/tsx/dist/loader.mjs driver.mts`
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine upstream/main 9a18261098)
after CLI dotenv load: VAULT_ADDR=http://127.0.0.1:18202 VAULT_NAMESPACE=repo-namespace CLAW_1PASSWORD_OP=<tmp>/repo/bin/op
repo vault listener :18202 got GET /v1/secret/data/app/db X-Vault-Token=user-vault-token X-Vault-Namespace=repo-namespace
vault resolver: {"protocolVersion":1,"values":{"app/db/password":"repo-value"},"errors":{}}
1password resolver: {"protocolVersion":1,"values":{"op://vault/item/field":"repo-op-output\n"},"errors":{}}
repo op binary executed: yes (OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN=user-op-service-token)
# AFTER (this patch, identical inputs)
after CLI dotenv load: VAULT_ADDR=http://127.0.0.1:18201 VAULT_NAMESPACE=(unset) CLAW_1PASSWORD_OP=(unset)
trusted vault listener :18201 got GET /v1/secret/data/app/db X-Vault-Token=user-vault-token X-Vault-Namespace=(none)
vault resolver: {"protocolVersion":1,"values":{"app/db/password":"trusted-value"},"errors":{}}
1password resolver: 1Password SecretRef resolver failed.
repo op binary executed: no
```
Observed result after fix: the project `.env` no longer changes where the Vault resolver sends the user's token or which `op` executable the 1Password resolver runs; the globally configured `VAULT_ADDR` is used, and with no `op` on this machine the 1Password resolver falls back to its normal not-found failure instead of running the project script.
What was not tested: no live Vault server or real 1Password CLI; the full Gateway process was not started (the driver calls the same CLI dotenv loader and spawns the shipped resolver scripts directly); Windows was not exercised.

prs.title: fix(doctor): stop reporting a fully configured Telegram setup as first-time setup
prs.body:
Closes #124705

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators running Telegram with multiple accounts would see
`openclaw doctor` report the channel as unconfigured, even though every account already
lists its groups and the bots reply in those groups normally:

```
- channels.telegram: Telegram is in first-time setup mode. DMs use pairing mode, so new
  senders must start a chat and be approved before regular messages are accepted. Group
  messages stay blocked until you add allowed chats under channels.telegram.groups ...
```

The warning tells operators their group messages are blocked when they are not, and points
at `channels.telegram.groups` — a key that multi-account setups intentionally leave empty
because each account carries its own `groups`. Doctor is what people reach for when
something looks broken, so a permanent false alarm there costs trust in every other line
it prints.

## Why This Change Was Made

There are two layers here, and the first one reaches past Telegram.

**Layer 1 — doctor could not resolve any channel's accounts.**
`resolveDoctorChannelAccountIds` resolves the channel through `normalizeAnyChannelId`,
which only knows channels present in the plugin *registry*. Doctor inspects config without
starting channels, so that registry is empty and the function returned `undefined` for
every channel. That makes `hasImplicitActiveAccount` unconditionally `true`, which means
`suppressParentGroupAllowlistWarning` — added in #93434 for exactly this class of
parent-scope false positive — has been permanently `false` in production. Its tests pass
because they run where the registry is populated.

Doctor was already inconsistent with itself: `channel-doctor.ts` locates the Telegram
adapter through `resolveReadOnlyChannelPluginsForConfig` (config-driven, registry-free), so
the warning is produced, while `channel-capabilities.ts` needs the registry, so the data
that would suppress it is missing. `getDoctorChannelCapabilities` already sidesteps this by
consulting the bundled catalog first. Account resolution now falls back the same way
doctor already does elsewhere — the bundled catalog for bundled channels, and the
config-driven read-only plugin loader for configured external ones — so both halves of
doctor agree on which channels exist, third-party channels included.

**Layer 2 — the parent container scope is checked as if it were an account.**
`scanEmptyAllowlistPolicyWarnings` calls `checkAccount(channelConfig, "channels.telegram",
…, parent: undefined)`. Once `accounts` are in use that scope holds no `groups` of its own,
so Telegram's first-time guidance fires there while both account scopes stay silent. The
scanner's existing suppression signal reaches `collectEmptyAllowlistPolicyWarningsForAccount`
but not the channel-supplied `extraWarningsForAccount` hook, which is where that guidance
comes from. The parent scope now carries its active child accounts in the existing
`ChannelDoctorEmptyAllowlistAccountContext` as an optional `childAccounts` field, and
Telegram skips first-time guidance only when every active account defines `groups`.

The field is **additive**. The hook keeps being invoked on exactly the scopes it is invoked
on today, and a channel plugin that ignores `childAccounts` behaves exactly as before, so
no existing plugin — bundled or external — changes behavior without opting in.

`childAccounts` is withheld when `hasImplicitActiveAccount` is true — the same guard #93434
applied. A container-level `botToken`/`tokenFile`/`$TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` synthesizes an
implicit `default` runtime account that inherits this scope and has no scope of its own to
warn on, so its group routing really is unconfigured and the container keeps owning that
guidance. It is also withheld when there are no active accounts, so when present it is
always non-empty. Deciding this in the scanner rather than in the adapter keeps the
account-resolution data and the guard in one place.

Non-goals: setups with no `accounts` block keep the existing warning verbatim, accounts
that genuinely lack `groups` keep warning at their own scope, and no authorization or
routing behavior changes — this only affects what doctor prints.

**Blast radius, stated plainly.** Layer 1 is broader than the Telegram symptom that led
here. Because `resolveDoctorChannelAccountIds` previously returned `undefined` for every
channel, `suppressParentGroupAllowlistWarning` was dead for every channel. This change
makes that suppression live across all channels at once. It only fires when every active
account genuinely resolves a `groupAllowFrom` (or `allowFrom` under the fallback
capability), so operators lose no real warning — but reviewers should weigh it as a
cross-channel behavior change, not a Telegram-only one. `empty-allowlist-scan.test.ts`
covers a non-Telegram channel on both sides of that boundary.

## User Impact

Operators running multiple Telegram accounts get a clean `openclaw doctor` run instead of a
standing false alarm, and real first-time setups still get the guidance they need, reported
at the account scope that actually needs fixing. Beyond Telegram, doctor can now resolve
channel accounts at all during a normal run, which is what #93434's suppression needed to
work in the first place.

## Evidence

**Measured on the real CLI, not just tests.** Built the repo and ran `node openclaw.mjs
doctor` against a live 6-account Telegram config. Temporary instrumentation confirmed the
root cause before the fix:

```
TMPDIAG2 channelId=null
TMPDIAG  telegram accountIds=undefined implicit=true active=6
```

Each layer was then reverted independently and the CLI rebuilt, which shows both are
required:

| Applied | `first-time setup` warnings in real `doctor` output |
|---|---|
| neither | 1 |
| layer 1 only | 1 |
| both | **0** |

No other Telegram warnings changed; the remaining ones are unrelated (dead-lettered ingress
events).

**Red/green, production change reverted per layer.** Reverting only
`src/commands/doctor/channel-capabilities.ts`:

```
× resolves account ids through the bundled catalog when no channel is registered
AssertionError: expected undefined to deeply equal { configured: [ 'default' ], …(1) }
```

Reverting only `extensions/telegram/src/doctor.ts`:

```
× skips parent-scope first-time guidance when every account configures groups
AssertionError: expected [ Array(1) ] to deeply equal []
```

Reverting only `src/commands/doctor/shared/empty-allowlist-scan.ts`:

```
× exposes active child accounts to the parent container scope only
AssertionError: Target cannot be null or undefined.
```

**Test lanes:**

| Lane | Result |
|---|---|
| commands lane (all doctor tests) | 319 files, 4117 passed, 4 skipped |
| `test:channels` | 100 files, 1122 passed |
| `test:contracts:plugins` | 42 files, 1039 passed |
| `test:contracts:channels` | 4 shards, all passed |
| `test:extension telegram` | 212 chunks, 3593 passed, 0 failed |
| `pnpm check` | green except `assertion SAFETY comment ratchet` |

The one `pnpm check` failure is pre-existing and unrelated: it reports
`src/gateway/server.auth.control-ui.pairing.suite.ts: 6 < 11` (a baseline larger than the
real count). Stashing this change and rerunning produces byte-identical output, so it
reproduces on `main` untouched.

New coverage pins both layers: account ids resolve through the bundled catalog when no
channel is registered, resolve a configured external plugin through the read-only loader,
and still return `undefined` when no loader can identify the channel;
first-time guidance is skipped only when every active account configures `groups`, and is
preserved when one account lacks them, when there is no `accounts` block, when
`childAccounts` is withheld for an implicit runtime account, and at account scope.

*Prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code).*

prs.title: fix(gateway): carry logical reasoning:false into route-variant sessions.list projection
prs.body:
## What this fixes

Closes #170528.

`sessions.list` row `thinkingLevels` disagreed with `models.list` and `agents.list` for the same session and model when the merged catalog entry set `reasoning: false`. The row reported the full effort list (off, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, ultra); the others correctly reported only off + ultra.

## Root cause

`resolveGatewaySessionThinkingProjectionInternal` selects the route-specific entry through `selectModelCatalogRuntimeEntry`, then projects `runtimeCatalog = [catalogEntry]` into `resolveGatewayModelThinkingFacts`. The raw route variant does not carry configured overrides (e.g. `reasoning: false`) that the merged logical entry owns. `resolveThinkingProfile` then sees `params.configuredReasoning ?? candidate.configuredReasoning ?? candidate.reasoning` as `undefined` for a `reasoning: false` model, so the `(category === false)` collapse to `{ off }` (plus the harness `ultra`) is skipped and the full provider effort ladder is returned.

`models.list` re-projects the variant with `projectModelCatalogEntryForRoute` and applies the configured override; `agents.list` uses the merged entry directly. Both are correct. The sessions list path was the only one that projected from the raw variant without carrying the configured override.

## Repair

Carry the logical entry's `reasoning` flag into `resolveGatewayModelThinkingFacts` as `configuredReasoning` when the logical entry explicitly disables reasoning. The merged catalog is the authoritative source for the user's configured intent, and the route variant is only the transport-selected row.

```ts
// The selected physical route variant does not carry configured overrides
// (e.g. reasoning: false) that the merged logical entry owns. Carry the
// logical configuredReasoning so the thinking profile matches the merged
// entry, not just the variant. (Closes #170528.)
const configuredReasoning = logicalEntry?.reasoning === false ? false : undefined;
```

The carry-over is gated on `reasoning === false` so it only fires when the user has explicitly disabled reasoning on the merged entry. `reasoning === true` and `reasoning === undefined` continue to fall through to the existing candidate-derived behavior.

## Evidence

Repro on 2026.10.1 against `opencode-go/muse-spark-1.3-contributor` (reasoning: false in `models.providers.opencode-go.models[]`):

| RPC | thinkingLevels |
| --- | --- |
| `sessions.list` row | off, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, ultra |
| `models.list {sessionKey}` entry | off, ultra |
| `agents.list` agent | off, ultra |

After the fix the sessions.list row reports `off, ultra` and matches the other two RPCs.

## Validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/session-utils-model.acp-owner.test.ts`: 9/9 passed (7 existing + 2 new: the regression for #170528 and a negative control that asserts no carry-over when the merged entry omits reasoning).
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` (incremental): clean.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs src --files src/gateway/session-utils-model.acp-owner.test.ts`: all 15 shards passed.
- `oxlint --type-aware src/gateway/session-utils-model.ts src/gateway/session-utils-model.acp-owner.test.ts`: 0 warnings, 0 errors.

## Scope

- `src/gateway/session-utils-model.ts`: +6/-0 (one short variable + spread).
- `src/gateway/session-utils-model.acp-owner.test.ts`: +94/-0 (two new tests).
