prs.title: fix(codex): avoid repeated host compaction after manual compact
prs.body:
Related: #126171

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated host compaction on the next chat turn after successful manual Codex compaction when OpenClaw's transcript mirror remains above its byte budget.

## User Impact

Explicit compaction applies the existing host byte guard before native Codex compaction. Below-budget sessions and sessions with valid byte-progress accounting remain native-only. A committed host summary stays committed if native compaction fails; the manual failure remains visible and clients receive the host update once.

**Maintainer decision remains open:** accept host-first manual compaction latency. Historical operator testing measured about 15m26s for the first host summary plus 30s native time; this PR does not claim to make that first summary faster. There are no configuration, schema, retention, or migration changes. The released synchronous SessionManager SDK and process-local incognito contracts remain supported.

## Why This Change Was Made

Codex owns its native history; native compaction does not rewrite OpenClaw's SQLite transcript mirror. Manual and ordinary-turn paths share one host accounting owner, with atomic boundary/count/latch persistence and current writer authority. Native-only accounting retains the host byte latch; a host rewrite below budget explicitly clears it.

The October 13 refresh resolves 12 text conflicts by merging main `f6c9a769e0f24780696a5aaf0e90dabf748adbcc` into the existing PR history. It retains upstream #168051 latch semantics, #169622 worker-backed source/currentness checks, #170199 actor ownership, and committed compaction details. It removes the superseded PR-only write-view helper because main's native persistence owner now carries that rollback protection.

The [latest review's P2 navigation finding](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158044#issuecomment-5830889301) is fixed: compaction captures the existing navigation assertion, checks it at worker admission and before receipt adoption, and preserves a genuinely newer published view. The dedicated accounting transaction retains the same exception while still checking binding, writer, ownership, lifecycle, and caller authority. No new state owner or public SDK export is introduced.

## Evidence

Product head: `a33bc638124dd72f88e6289e79dbff76417dc68c`. Previous head `7eb59d0bf6f3c442c628a41cd68b44fbaa4f4efb` remains first parent; history is not rewritten.

Code anchors for this revision: [manual byte/accounting owner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a33bc638124dd72f88e6289e79dbff76417dc68c/src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact.accounting.ts#L16), [navigation capture and receipt adoption](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a33bc638124dd72f88e6289e79dbff76417dc68c/src/agents/sessions/session-manager-compaction.ts#L96), [dedicated-owner newer-view exception](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a33bc638124dd72f88e6289e79dbff76417dc68c/src/agents/sessions/session-manager-persistence.ts#L140), and [real-worker navigation regression](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a33bc638124dd72f88e6289e79dbff76417dc68c/src/agents/sessions/session-manager-async-message.test.ts#L586).

At publication GitHub reports **MERGEABLE / BLOCKED**, with **35** later main commits behind the branch but no merge conflict. New-head CI is still running; the block is not being treated as a code conflict or a passing review. Maintainers can edit the branch. The security-review publisher workflow [completed successfully](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38343023552), but deliberately marks `openclaw/security-sensitive-review` and `openclaw/ci-gate` red: `Security review is awaiting maintainer approval.` This is an approval gate, not a failing product test.

All current runs used temporary synthetic state and private frozen dependencies, Node 24.18.0 / pnpm 12.9.0 on macOS. No running installation, Gateway, real database/configuration, or external channel was used.

| Check | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Scoped integration coverage | **243 distinct passing cases / 15 files** across the runs below; combined coverage, not one monolithic invocation |
| Final affected batch | **128 passed / 7 files**, process wall **148.07s** |
| Navigation and newer-view owner suite | **21 passed**, process wall **36.35s**; the five navigation/publication cases cost 40–54ms each in that run |
| Deliberate defect controls | Five independent mutations all fail at the intended boundary; restored candidate passes all **8 selected cases**, process wall **56.46s** |
| Last test-only type correction | Both newer-view cases pass again, process wall **14.22s**; raw database rows are narrowed with the existing record guard, without casts |
| Production / test types | Production core passed (51.90s); all five selected test graphs passed (sessions 8.6s, agents-other 47.4s, gateway-server 56.1s, messaging 47.7s, agents-root 45.1s compiler time) |
| Static checks | Scoped Oxfmt/Oxlint, 3-file MDX compilation, whitespace/conflict checks, line-cap/max-lines/assertion/database-worker/database-dialect/timeout/mock-export ratchets pass |
| Independent review | Codex P0–P2 autoreview: scoped-clean on the complete candidate delta plus unchanged owner context. The final record-type narrowing and unused test import removal also received independent scoped review. This is static review, not runtime proof |

The current tests exercise the queued manual entry, real host compaction owner and SQLite workers, slash-command handling, Gateway RPC, admission/cancellation, canonical path aliases, incognito storage, committed-host/native-failure publication, and latch refresh/rearming. Model and native-harness outputs are synthetic; these are runtime/storage boundary tests, **not a new live Codex or Weixin end-to-end run**.

Initial failures were identified and corrected: old delegate/hydration fixtures lacked the newly required runtime-config snapshot (the delegate also resets its module graph, so preparation must use the post-reset instance); an actor callback signature and a raw-JSON test type needed adaptation. The line-cap check required moving existing entry/routing fixture factories into their existing test-support module, without deleting coverage. These integration/fixture failures are not claimed as upstream product regressions.

<details>
<summary>The 12 conflicted files and resolution</summary>

- `docs/reference/database-schemas/worker-access.md`: retain the current worker/actor owner documentation and the manual boundary/accounting contract.
- `src/agents/sessions/agent-session-compaction.ts` and `.test.ts`: publish committed details once, preserve provider/server-endpoint compaction and cancellation fencing.
- `src/agents/sessions/session-manager-entries.ts`, `session-manager-metadata.ts`, and `session-manager-persistence.ts`: retain main's actor/worker split, currentness and navigation assertions, and acknowledged-commit handling.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.ts`: share accounting with manual compaction while preserving native-only latch retention.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-compact.ts`: use current prepared session reads and skip accounting already committed by the host owner.
- `src/config/sessions/session-entry-projection.ts`: retain main unchanged (`undefined` retains, `null` clears the latch).
- `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.compaction-boundary.test.ts`: preserve both upstream writer/transaction coverage and manual accounting regressions.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-compact.ts` and `src/gateway/server.sessions.compaction.test.ts`: preserve native/server semantics, stale-owner checks, negative-estimate coverage, and one committed-host notification even after native failure.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Reproducible commands, negative controls, and observed failure signatures</summary>

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/sessions/session-manager-async-message.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact.delegate.test.ts src/agents/sessions/agent-session-compaction.test.ts src/agents/sessions/agent-session-compaction.admission.test.ts src/agents/sessions/agent-session-compaction.degraded-reload.test.ts src/agents/sessions/session-manager.test.ts src/agents/sessions/session-manager-hydration.test.ts src/agents/session-tool-result-guard.transcript-events.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-accessor.compaction-boundary.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/commands-compact.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/commands-compact.lifecycle.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/commands-compact.runtime.test.ts src/gateway/server.sessions.compaction.test.ts src/gateway/server.sessions.compaction-accounting.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
# After repairing the runtime-snapshot fixtures, rerun the affected files and
# the command/storage shards that had not run after the earlier shard failure:
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact.delegate.test.ts src/agents/sessions/session-manager-hydration.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-accessor.compaction-boundary.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/commands-compact.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/commands-compact.lifecycle.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/commands-compact.runtime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm tsgo:core
node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs --ci-graphs-json '["core-test-agents-sessions","core-test-agents-other","core-test-gateway-server","core-test-messaging"]'
node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs --ci-graphs-json '["core-test-agents-root"]'
```

The second command initially passed 27 Gateway cases and 103 infra cases but failed the ten unprepared-snapshot fixture cases; it is not claimed as an entirely passing invocation. The next command passed 128 cases after those fixtures were corrected. Unaffected passing results are retained rather than rerun for appearances.

Each control below changed only the named production condition in the isolated worktree, ran the specified existing test filter, then restored the exact source bytes. These are deliberate defect controls, not a claim that the whole historical head was rerun.

| Removed/changed protection | Test file / `-t` filter | Actual result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Omit navigation assertion passed to `persistWorkerRecord` | `session-manager-async-message.test.ts` / `fences local navigation` | 2 fail, 1 pass; refusal happens only **after commit** instead of before commit; exit 1, 29.09s |
| Omit navigation check before receipt adoption | Same file/filter | 1 fail, 2 pass; expected committed-view failure is absent (`Received: undefined`); exit 1, 27.95s |
| Restore unconditional navigation check after dedicated compaction commit | Same file / `keeps a newer published view when an awaited compaction receipt` | Dedicated-owner case fails; generic worker control passes; exit 1, 27.98s |
| Restore `undefined` instead of explicit host latch clearing | `compact.delegate.test.ts` / `clears (the byte latch\|stale byte suppression)` | Both cases fail: stale latch remains instead of `undefined`; exit 1, 36.92s |
| Always clear latch after accounting, including native-only token compaction | `agent-runner-memory.test.ts` / `preserves host byte suppression when native token-pressure compaction succeeds` | Durable latch-preservation assertion fails; exit 1, 32.10s |

Final restored-source command (8 pass):

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/sessions/session-manager-async-message.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact.delegate.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.test.ts -t 'fences local navigation|keeps a newer published view when an awaited compaction|clears (the byte latch|stale byte)|preserves host byte suppression' --maxWorkers=1
```

The new host-summary-under-budget case cost 2.354s in the full delegate run; native latch preservation was under one second in the full owner run. No new sleeps, polling, longer timeouts, production test seams, or serial test configuration were added. Hosted CI timing for this revision is not yet available.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Preserved historical live/hosted evidence and limits</summary>

On macOS over official v2026.9.6, earlier operator testing reduced host bytes from **21,224,992 to 311,754**, persisted the checkpoint, completed native compaction, kept a second manual request native-only, and allowed ordinary chat afterward. Initial host compaction took about **15m26s + 30s native**. This is historical evidence, not a current-head provider run or a latency fix.

Historical product head `2bc49c17c57dd739f460fb7e7af702195f315bba` passed [secretless fork validation](https://github.com/scotthuang/openclaw/actions/runs/36552997054) through evidence commit `c202912da226699ab07c11fd3a38618b42d8739f`: 77 tests, production/test types, scoped static checks, and runtime build. Earlier broader [226-test/build](https://github.com/scotthuang/openclaw/actions/runs/36550491648) and [four type-lane](https://github.com/scotthuang/openclaw/actions/runs/36550966843) results remain pinned to their historical revisions. They do not certify this refresh.

The native contract was personally rechecked in sibling Codex source at `be9060ff9620e170a05a6353ab293efb7c704248`: `ThreadCompactStartParams` identifies a native thread; `thread_processor.rs::thread_compact_start` submits `Op::Compact`; `core/compact.rs` rewrites native history, not the OpenClaw transcript database.

Current-head CI/review and maintainer acceptance of host-first latency remain separate. No CI rerun/dispatch, production restart, real model/channel request, or PR merge was performed.

</details>

prs.title: fix(sessions): reclaim expired cron history placeholders
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Isolated cron runs can leave canonical retained-history placeholders after their live session entry is gone. Those intentionally empty SQLite rows are outside the readable session-entry model, so ordinary pruning cannot enumerate them; one observed production store accumulated 1,733 placeholders anchoring 19,206 transcript events.

## Why This Change Was Made

This patch extends `openclaw sessions cleanup` with one narrow eligibility contract:

- only canonical cron retained-history placeholders qualify;
- `cron.sessionRetention` owns the age boundary;
- malformed, unidentified, live, referenced, or admitted sessions are preserved;
- transcript state is archived before deletion;
- cleanup covers exactly the logical agents the caller selected, even when several agents share one SQLite store;
- candidates are revalidated under lifecycle admission and the SQLite write transaction;
- committed transcript archives are published after lifecycle and writer locks are released;
- placeholders are swept before disk-budget eviction, so reachable history is not evicted first.

The implementation reports preview/apply counts through the existing cleanup summary. It does not add a second cleanup policy or an unidentified-row deletion mode.

Owner scoping is recorded where it is produced rather than re-derived downstream. When `--all-agents` collapses several configured agents onto one physical database, `dedupeSessionStoreTargetsBySqliteTarget` now records the collapsed logical owners on the surviving target (`SessionStoreTarget.sharedOwnerAgentIds`), and the tombstone sweep scans that owner set. Single-agent selections never go through that dedupe, so `--agent <id>` and the default selection stay scoped to exactly one owner.

## User Impact

Cron-heavy installations can reclaim otherwise unreachable session-store debris through the existing cleanup command without weakening the canonical-key safety boundary or risking live/referenced sessions. `--all-agents` reclaims every selected agent's expired cron history in a shared store instead of silently reclaiming only the physical store owner's, and a single-agent run still touches only that agent.

## Evidence

Historical validation on head `8c0cccfa70bc3989929df42e6579096539863214` (not the current refreshed head):

- focused cleanup, retention, targets, archive-store, session-accessor, runtime, and serialization suites: **144/144 passing** across 20 files;
- adjacent `--all-agents` target consumers (doctor session SQLite / shared-store / transcripts, maintenance schema preflight, default-agent store, CLI route args, status-health-sessions, gateway session startup migration): **313 passing, 2 skipped, 0 failing** across 9 files;
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:scripts`: passing;
- focused type-aware Oxlint over every changed core and script file: passing;
- `pnpm check:changed`: every branch-owned lane passes (conflict markers, max-lines ratchet, assertion-safety ratchet, changelog attributions, doctor deprecation registry, wildcard re-export guards, duplicate-scan coverage, coercion helpers, dependency pins, formatting, deprecated API usage, wrapper shadowing, package patch guard, dead-export scan, core tsgo graph boundary, script erasability, typechecks, targeted lint, import cycles, database-first legacy-store guard, and the remaining repo guards). Two lanes fail and both are provably inherited from `main` at this head: `typecheck core tests` reports six errors, all in `src/gateway/server.channels-start-outcomes.test.ts`, whose blob is `9166d13ec73c950184a438b5a49d21adeba7b4dd` on both this head and `origin/main`; and `plugin boundaries` reports the purely date-driven "5 compatibility record(s) are due for removal" from `src/plugins/compat/registry-records.ts`, `src/plugins/compat/registry.ts`, and `scripts/plugin-boundary-report.ts`, all byte-identical to `origin/main`, which `scripts/check-changed.mts` documents in place — "After 2026-07-24, lapsed compatibility windows intentionally fail this gate until their scheduled deletion PRs land."

### Production LOC and stored data model

The owner-set repair adds no second cleanup path: the target-to-owner-set mapping moved into the sweep's own entry point, which left `cleanup-service.ts` 4 net lines smaller than before the repair. Round-local production delta is +10 net, 8 of which are the required invariant comments at the ownership boundary.

The branch's remaining ~+406 production lines are feature growth, not a bug-fix diff: 344 of them are the single new `cleanup-tombstones.ts` module carrying candidate listing, lifecycle-admission revalidation, in-transaction revalidation, archive materialization, post-lock archive publication, and cache invalidation. `src/cron/session-reaper.ts` is net -26. The reducible piece is the double revalidation, which is what makes the delete safe under concurrency; the tradeoff is flagged rather than silently trimmed.

No SQLite schema change is involved: the module issues no DDL, adds no table, column, or index, and does not touch a schema version; its writes are `DELETE`s plus existing archive rows through existing Kysely helpers. `shouldRunSqliteSessionSchemaBaselineCheck` does not select this branch's paths, so `check:changed` never schedules the SQLite schema baseline lane for it.

### Real behavior proof

`scripts/proof-117074-tombstone-shared-owners.ts` drives the real `runSessionsCleanup()` against real on-disk SQLite agent databases in a temporary `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, through real target resolution, lifecycle admission, write transactions, and archive publication. Nothing between the entrypoint and the assertions is stubbed.

```text
[1] --all-agents over an exact shared .sqlite locator
  ok   dedupe collapses both agents to one physical target = 1
  ok   selected target owner = "main"
  ok   swept remnants across selected owners = 2
  ok   main placeholder removed = 0
  ok   ops placeholder removed = 0
  ok   main transcript archived = 1
  ok   ops transcript archived = 1
[2] --agent main over the same shared store keeps ops isolated
  ok   swept exactly the requested owner = 1
  ok   ops placeholder preserved = 1
  ok   ops not archived = 0
[3] --all-agents over per-agent stores sweeps each store once
  ok   per-agent stores stay distinct targets = 2
  ok   swept one remnant per store = 2

assertions: 22, failures: 0
All runtime assertions passed.
```

On the previous head the same proof reports `assertions: 22, failures: 4` — `swept remnants across selected owners: expected 2, got 1`, plus the surviving `ops` node, transcript, and missing archive. Scenarios 2 and 3 pass on both heads, so the change is scoped to the multi-owner selection.

Two unit regressions pin the contract at the sweep boundary (`cleanup-tombstones.test.ts`): a full selected owner set sweeps every owner of a shared store, and a subset selection leaves an unselected third agent's placeholder, windows, and transcript untouched.

The focused suite also uses one main-owned explicit shared SQLite store containing canonical `main` and `ops` placeholders. Enforcing cleanup as either logical agent opens the physical database as `main`, removes and archives only the selected agent(s), and leaves unselected agents' node, window, and transcript state intact. The completed-sweep case verifies the archive row has a numeric `published_at` and the archive file exists before the command returns.

Exact-head real-store CLI proof used a temporary SQLite agent store containing one 48-hour-old canonical cron placeholder with one transcript event:

```text
before={"nodes":1,"windows":1,"events":1}
command=openclaw sessions cleanup --agent main --enforce --json --store <redacted-store>
tombstoneRemnants={"candidates":1,"removedNodes":1,"sweptTranscriptStates":1,"olderThanMs":86400000}
wouldMutate=true
after={"nodes":0,"windows":0,"events":0,"archives":1}
```

The temporary store was moved to trash after verification.

**Proof boundary:** the multi-owner path is proven through the real cleanup service, target resolution, lifecycle admission, write transactions, archive publication, and real SQLite stores. This is the owner of the CLI cleanup behavior; a live operator Gateway run is not intrinsically required to prove it. This is not a claim that an operator Gateway or production database was modified.

### Current head and round history

Current signed head: [`9adc742d334`](https://github.com/zeroaltitude/openclaw/commit/9adc742d334965245b6126ba363d272b87e35f75). The older test counts and inherited failures above remain historical, not current results; round 25 below carries the current ones.

Eleven rounds landed since the September 8 refresh:

1. **`2882b1b5be0` — bounded reference work across tombstone batches.** Candidate revalidation no longer enumerates the full store twice per candidate: the sweep primes reference analysis once for a batch of up to 32 candidates and answers each later boundary from that pass, while a connection-local token (`PRAGMA data_version` plus a TEMP-trigger generation counter) proves no insert, update, or external commit landed since. Both candidate revalidation boundaries are retained; a token change re-reads the store. The single-candidate `instr` probe became exact `IN` membership over the candidate set.

2. **`e63ac16d66f` — reference-preservation repair.** The `IN` prefilter was narrower than the reference parser it prefilters for, which is the regression ClawSweeper raised as [P1]. `collectSessionStateIdsForEntry` trims every id it collects, and an entry parses only when its `sessionId` equals `current_session_id`, so a row whose current id carries leading or trailing whitespace owns the trimmed id — and equality rejected that row before the parser could see it, in both the batch priming scan and the final deletion check. A `trim(current_session_id, …)` membership branch reproducing exactly the code points `String.prototype.trim` removes restores the conservative semantics; both reads share one query builder, so one branch covers both.

3. **`23f7d41a4bd` — concurrent-write latency measured.** `scripts/proof-117074-concurrent-write-latency.ts` drives the real sweep over a seeded 3,096-row mixed store (3,000 live sessions, a seventh of them carrying optional reference fields, plus 96 expired cron placeholders) while a separate OS process performs Gateway-turn-shaped session work through the real accessor at ~120 operations per second. No production file changed.

```text
    candidate scan over the whole store: 9.82ms
    quiet sweep: 70373.94ms total, 733.06ms per candidate, 3 reference batches
    transcript-archive worker threads: 192 spawned, 70023ms of worker lifetime (99.5% of the sweep, off the main thread)
    before sweep: n=729 rate=121.5/s mean=3.14ms p50=2.31ms p95=4.3ms p99=26.35ms max=28.61ms
    during sweep: n=8186 rate=116.06/s mean=3.42ms p50=2.38ms p95=9.76ms p99=27.59ms max=63.79ms
    sweep: 70530.58ms with a writer vs 70373.94ms quiet (1x), 734.69ms per candidate
    with a writer: 0/192 questions served, 192 fell back to a fresh read
    32 reference questions: unbatched 163.11ms (5.1ms each) vs batched 6.23ms (0.19ms each)
```

A continuously written store invalidates the memo completely — 0 of 192 reference questions served, in every run — so the optimization delivers nothing while writes keep landing. It cannot thrash: invalidation deletes the batch, so a batch primes at most once and every later question in it takes the unbatched read. That bounds the degraded case at the pre-batch cost plus one scan per 32-candidate batch, about 12 ms per candidate against a per-candidate sweep cost of 648–888 ms, because ~99.5% of the sweep's wall clock is transcript-archive worker threads running off the main thread. With `resolveBatchedReferencedSessionIds` forced to decline at source, the harness fails exactly the two assertions that pin the memo, EXIT 1. Caveat: run from source under `tsx`, so archive-worker boot is inflated and the reference share of a built runtime's smaller total would be correspondingly larger, still order 1–2%.

4. **`2770adddc6c` — the store writer is released across archive encoding.** The sweep took store writer admission once per candidate and awaited archive materialization inside that hold. The store writer queue is process-local and FIFO (`runQueuedStoreWrite` drains it with `await task.fn()`), so unrelated session writes in the same process — including the Gateway that invoked `sessions.cleanup` — waited for a transcript being encoded on a worker thread. The reclaim now follows the scheduling `session-history-eviction.ts` and `session-accessor.sqlite-lifecycle.ts` already use: a short `session.maintenance.tombstone-prepare` section revalidates and plans, the writer is released for materialization under reclamation admission, and a short `session.maintenance.tombstone-commit` section re-reads the placeholder and its references inside the deletion transaction before deleting. Lifecycle admission is held across the release and nothing decided before it is trusted after it, so the delete still requires two independent revalidations.

A same-process writer scenario was added to the harness. It runs the Gateway-shaped writer on the sweep's own event loop and reads the real `openclaw.session.write` diagnostics channel, which reports how long each write held the lane and how long it waited for it. Same host, same store, same scale, with and without the fix:

```text
before the fix (head 23f7d41a4bd)
    during sweep: n=4140 rate=58.09/s mean=11.96ms p50=2.49ms p95=19.92ms p99=361.1ms max=444.5ms
    session.maintenance.tombstone-sweep: n=96 mean=370.98ms p95=436ms max=448ms held
    unrelated same-process writes: n=4140 max queue wait=442ms
    (before sweep: rate=123.33/s p95=4.85ms max=31.51ms)

after the fix (head 2770adddc6c)
    during sweep: n=8060 rate=115.48/s mean=3.29ms p50=2.31ms p95=6.51ms p99=27.37ms max=77.89ms
    session.maintenance.tombstone-prepare: n=96 mean=5.54ms p95=8ms max=12ms held
    session.maintenance.tombstone-commit:  n=96 mean=13.34ms p95=27ms max=34ms held
    unrelated same-process writes: n=8060 max queue wait=0ms
    (before sweep: rate=113.33/s p95=6.6ms max=202.05ms)

assertions: 23, failures: 0
All runtime assertions passed.
```

The unfixed head fails three of those assertions rather than merely reporting worse numbers, so the harness is a regression gate and not only a measurement.

Gates at this head: 13 session, cleanup, cron, reclamation, eviction, and store-writer-queue suites were requested and 13 executed — 215 passed, EXIT 0 (81 / 34 / 31 / 22 / 17 / 8 / 8 / 7 / 2 / 2 / 1 / 1 / 1 per file; the 81 is `.each` expansion of 17 literal cases). `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:scripts`, the type-aware scripts and core oxlint lanes, `format:check`, `deadcode:unused-files` (0 entries on both scans), `config:schema:check`, `plugin-sdk:surface:check`, `check:no-conflict-markers`, and `git diff --check` all exit 0. Both proof harnesses exit 0 (23 assertions and 22 assertions, 0 failures).

5. **`5ba3e0d5b80` — upstream `main` integrated.** A merge of `origin/main` only; no branch production file changed in it. This is the head ClawSweeper reviewed as Revision 44 with no findings.

6. **`525a2013c7f` — second `main` integration, and the reference batch rekeyed to the database path.** Upstream's worker-coordinated transcript-archive publish can release and reopen the cached `DatabaseSync` for a path mid-sweep. The batch was keyed by the connection object in a `WeakMap`, so every such dispatch orphaned it and the next candidate fell back to a full re-scan — confirmed empirically by identical archive-publish dispatch counts on a working and a broken tree, with a connection-cache `MISS (fresh open)` immediately following every dispatch only where the batch was lost. Keying `activeBatches` by path fixes that. It also introduced the defect below.

7. **`e552c861ff0` — the reference batch is bound to its originating connection.** Path keying answered *how a batch is found* but left *whether it may be believed* unanswered. Both halves of the validity token — `PRAGMA data_version` and the TEMP-trigger generation counter — are connection-local in the strict sense: on a replacement handle they restart from that handle's own baseline rather than advancing, so a reading taken after an external commit is indistinguishable from one taken before it. Because the sweep releases its store writer across archive materialization and an unborrowed handle can be evicted in that window, both final reference checks could accept a stale memo and delete a generation a live session still references. The batch now carries the handle its token came from plus the priming closure; a replacement **rebuilds** the memo through the live connection (so the remaining candidates keep their single pass) instead of inheriting a proof that cannot describe it, and falls back to a store read if the rebuild cannot be established. `session-accessor.sqlite-reference-batch.test.ts` covers the close/reopen late-reference case: on the unfixed tree it fails with `- Set { "victim" } / + Set {}`, and passes 4/4 with the fix.

8. **`a2b4a1a6e1d` — the proof harnesses join their database owners before removing fixture roots.** `closeOpenClawAgentDatabasesForTest()` only *starts* asynchronous resource closure, so the `rmSync` that followed it took the shared-state database out from under reclamation workers that still needed it to release their durable leases. Both harnesses reported every assertion passing and then looped on ENOENT until a wall clock killed them, which made their exit status useless as a verdict. Each harness now collects its fixture roots and releases them through `cleanupSessionStateForTest`, the existing awaited lifecycle owner, before any root is removed; the concurrent-writer child releases its own leases and its parent joins the child's exit rather than killing it. The drain runs once, after the last scenario, because it is process-wide: draining between scenarios left every later scenario measuring a cold store and blew the latency harness's busy-timeout ceilings (7247 ms and 12395 ms against a 5000 ms bound, versus 1603 ms and 204 ms with a single end-of-run drain). Measured at this head: `proof-117074-tombstone-shared-owners.ts` 22 assertions / 0 failures / **0 ENOENT lines / EXIT 0**, against a pre-fix control on the same tree of 22 assertions / 0 failures / **284419 ENOENT lines / EXIT 124**; `proof-117074-concurrent-write-latency.ts` 23 assertions / 0 failures / 0 ENOENT lines / EXIT 0. The same round cleared four branch-owned CI lanes: an unused exported type (`SessionReferenceOwnerSink`, now module-local) that failed `check-dependencies`, two `node:sqlite` row assertions that needed `// SAFETY:` invariants for `check:assertion-safety`, and an `oxfmt --check` violation in the latency harness that was failing both `check-lint` and `check-docs`.

9. **`2390dc75a78` — the latency harness fails when its writer process exits badly.** Revision 47 found the join added above incomplete: the exit promise resolved regardless of exit code or signal, and the child published its report *before* awaiting its own drain, so a drain exception or the 30-second kill backstop still let the harness print a passing result. That is the original defect's own shape — a verdict outrunning its shutdown. The child now drains first and publishes afterwards, so a readable report is evidence the drain *succeeded*; the parent keeps the exit outcome and throws on a nonzero code, a signal, or the backstop firing, with the child's captured output attached. Negative control: with the child forced to `process.exitCode = 3` the harness throws `writer process did not shut down cleanly: code=3 signal=null`, never prints `All runtime assertions passed`, and exits 1. At this head the harness reports 23 assertions / 0 failures / 0 ENOENT lines / EXIT 0, with busy-timeout ceilings observed at 137.77 ms and 83.17 ms against the 5000 ms bound.

10. **`83b5b6d460f` — the cleanup suite drains its fixture databases, and its scan-budget fixture stops manufacturing an external commit (this round).** Two coupled defects, and fixing only the first moves the failure rather than removing it. (a) `closeOpenClawAgentDatabasesForTest()` in `afterEach` only *starts* asynchronous resource retirement, so the registered temp-dir hook could remove the fixture databases while reclamation workers still held their durable leases; the suite's 17 assertions passed and the shard then exited 1 on `AggregateError: Failed to reset global singleton lifecycle state` caused by `ENOENT ... /state/openclaw.sqlite`. `afterEach` now awaits `cleanupSessionStateForTest({ stateDir: tempDir })`, the existing awaited lifecycle owner, and Vitest's reverse-order `afterEach` scheduling settles it before the tracker's removal. (b) With drainage correct, `keeps the reference work SQLite performs flat as the backlog grows` then fails at `expected 33 to be less than or equal to 3` in the whole-file run too, not just under a `-t` filter. Instrumented cause: every entry write ends in `kickSessionEntryMaintenanceAfterWrite`, which queues a coalesced `setImmediate` maintenance pass; that pass reclaims with `forceInProcess: false`, so `runSqliteSessionReclamation` dispatches a Worker that opens the store on its own connection and commits. Probing `PRAGMA data_version` across each sweep phase shows the sweeping connection observing `dv 2 → 3` with the TEMP generation unchanged, one candidate after the seeding's maintenance pass lands. From that connection the commit is indistinguishable from an external writer creating a reference, so `revalidateSessionReferenceBatch` correctly drops the batch and the remaining candidates take the unbatched read — one batched pass plus 11 × 3 fallback statements is exactly the 33 observed. The order dependence has the same source: a whole-file run satisfies the maintenance age gate in an earlier test (one dispatch for the entire file) while the scan-budget test alone dispatches 30. The two scaling fixtures now seed through a local helper that passes the existing `skipMaintenance` option, so the fixture's own background maintenance cannot commit inside the window whose database work is being measured; every other test seeds exactly as before. **No production file changed, and reference invalidation is not weakened** — the batch still drops on any real external commit, and `re-reads references for a later candidate when a late owner appears mid-batch` still covers that path at full strength. Negative controls, each reverting one half: reverting only the awaited drainage gives 17 passed then the same `AggregateError` / `ENOENT` at EXIT 1; reverting only `skipMaintenance` gives `1 failed | 16 passed` with `AssertionError: expected 33 to be less than or equal to 3` at EXIT 1, in the full suite as well as under `-t`. At this head: the file passes 17/17 with the shard at EXIT 0 where it previously exited 1 on teardown; each measurement test passes alone under `-t` (`1 passed | 16 skipped`); and the acceptance scope (`cleanup-tombstones`, `cleanup-service.order`, `session-accessor.sqlite-reference-batch`) is 22 passed at EXIT 0.

11. **`9adc742d334` — the reclaim's undo restores the conversation, not just the rows that owned it (this round).** Addresses revision 58's [P1] and three of its four [P2]s, plus three breakages the branch carried that a source-only review could not see because **the branch did not compile at `164d9b405ab`** (`pnpm tsgo:core` reported five errors there; one was the review's own database-path [P2], the rest arrived in the 2026-10-08 `main` merge with no conflict marker — `runExclusiveSessionLifecycleMutation` gained a leading operation argument, and `readSqliteDataVersion` moved to `infra/sqlite-schema-facts.js`, which also broke the latency harness).

    [P1]: the post-delete snapshot held only `session_nodes` and `session_windows`, but `transcript_events` cascades off `session_windows` (`openclaw-agent-schema.sql:575`) along with eight other tables, and two more cascade off `transcript_events` — so restoring the metadata put a placeholder back with its conversation permanently gone while the sweep counted the candidate as restored. The new `cleanup-tombstones-snapshot.ts` captures the full cascade by walking `PRAGMA foreign_key_list` outward from `session_windows`, so a table added later is captured without anyone updating that file and a cascade the walk cannot follow by name throws rather than silently restoring less than the delete removed. Restoration now runs through the lifecycle mutation owner, the writer lane and a write transaction instead of bare inserts on a long-lived handle, and each restored generation is marked for the transcript index owner's reconcile (its projection table carries no foreign key and its FTS5 table has a delete-only trigger, so replaying projection rows would desynchronize it). Both directions measured on the existing restore test: with the fix, `transcript_events` = 1 with its seeded text intact and `transcript_event_identities` = 1; without the cascade capture those three assertions fail while every pre-existing assertion in the same test still passes.

    [P2] handle reuse: `batchDatabase` was opened once and reused across awaited archive materialization and publication, either of which can release and reopen the cached connection; every synchronous group now re-acquires the current handle. [P2] proof seeding: both harnesses deleted the readable entry outside an entry transaction, which `writeSessionEntrySnapshots` refuses; both now seed through `runOpenClawAgentWriteTransaction` and run to completion (22 and 23 assertions, 0 failures). [P2] off-thread database work is **not** addressed — it is enforced by `check:database-worker-ratchet` (main-thread SQLite T1 796 -> 804, eight call sites in `cleanup-tombstones.ts`), this round adds none of them, and `runExclusiveSqliteSessionWrite`'s `writer: "worker"` is an admission-queue choice rather than a thread dispatch, so the ask is a module redesign and a maintainer question is open on the PR.

    Also this round: the branch's own *"admits an unrelated same-process write"* test was measuring the wrong thing — run as a control with no sweep and nothing held, a plain `replaceSessionEntry` reports `pending` after 500 `setImmediate` turns, so the probe called an unobstructed write blocked; it is now a wall-clock budget asserting the write completes before the parked sweep is released. `check:line-cap-ratchet` (which the previous environment could never run, because git 2.34 lacks `cat-file --batch -z`) reported a real violation at `session-accessor.sqlite-lifecycle-state.ts` 700 -> 712 counted lines; narrowed reference reads and the batched analysis moved to `session-accessor.sqlite-reference-scan.ts`. The *"keeps the reference work SQLite performs flat"* test was removed at the reviewer's request: its 6.5x per-candidate allowance accepts the per-candidate scanning it was written to forbid, so it could not discriminate, and it shipped a `DBG_SCAN` debug branch; its sibling holds a tight 1.5x ratio and still guards the quadratic-revalidation regression.

    Gates at this head: `pnpm check:changed` 35 / 37 lanes green. The two reds are the worker ratchet above and `lint:core`, whose eight `max-lines` offenders are each byte-identical to `origin/main`. `config:schema:check`, `plugin-sdk:surface:check`, `deadcode:unused-files` (Knip production and full-tree, 0 entries each), `git diff --check`, `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test` and `tsgo:scripts` all clean — the three tsgo lanes were red at the reviewed head. Focused vitest: 11 files, 99 tests, 0 failures. Both proof harnesses exit 0.

**Status of the merge risks.** The writer-admission defect is fixed and measured above, including a negative control that fails on the unfixed head. Contended latency is measured on both axes: across processes (a second OS process at ~120 ops/s, p95 4.3 → 9.8 ms) and within one process (the axis a separate process structurally cannot observe, p95 6.6 → 6.5 ms, queue wait 0 ms). No representative-scale latency *improvement* is claimed for the contended case; the claim is that the degradation is bounded and off the critical path.

**Integration status, current as of this edit.** `525a2013c7f` merged then-current `origin/main` and resolved the three conflicted files recorded in the round-10 comment (`session-canonical-key.ts`, `targets-dedupe.test.ts`, `combined-store-gateway.test.ts`), and GitHub reported `mergeable: true` at `e552c861ff0`. That is no longer true: the fork's `main` is **1,863 commits behind `upstream/main`** as measured at this edit, GitHub reports `mergeable: false` / `mergeable_state: dirty` for head `9adc742d334`, and because no merge ref is produced the heavy `pull_request` matrix is not dispatched here at all — so the lightweight lanes are the only CI signal on this PR. The branch has only ever been fast-forwarded; the conflict is upstream drift, not a rewrite. Syncing the fork is not ours to do, so re-integrating and validating the resolved tree remains the outstanding merge-risk item.

No green-CI claim is made here: read the live check list on the PR rather than this paragraph, which cannot stay current.

prs.title: fix: respect disabled reasoning in session runtime routes
prs.body:
Closes #170528. Thanks @EmeraldPi for reporting the disagreement between session and model thinking metadata.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `sessions.list` offers native reasoning efforts for a model configured with `reasoning: false` when runtime selection substitutes a different catalog route.

## User Impact

Clients consuming session rows now receive only `off` and harness-level `ultra` for these models, rather than unsupported native reasoning choices. Models configured with reasoning enabled are unchanged. No configuration or schema changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the logical model's configured reasoning policy into the existing thinking owner while retaining the runtime route as the physical capability donor. The same resolved profile governs levels, defaults, and effective stored effort.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

## Evidence

Built, isolated Gateway at current main `ac8de4fd9562646ad7a41dfdec59fb35df06be4f` versus this fix. The operator config declares `openai/gpt-5.4` with `reasoning: false` on its ChatGPT Responses route and selects the OpenClaw runtime, whose Responses variant supports reasoning. Sessions were created using the shipped `gateway call sessions.create` CLI and read using `gateway call sessions.list`; no injected catalog or fault is used in this RPC proof.

Observed excerpts:

```text
sessions.list / reasoning:false model
  main: thinkingOptions=[off,minimal,low,medium,high,xhigh,ultra]; thinkingDefault=medium
  fix:  thinkingOptions=[off,ultra]; thinkingDefault=off
sessions.list / reasoning:true gpt-5-mini control
  main: thinkingOptions=[off,minimal,low,medium,high,ultra]; thinkingDefault=medium
  fix:  thinkingOptions=[off,minimal,low,medium,high,ultra]; thinkingDefault=medium
```

The distinct-route regression fails on main (extra native levels) and passes with the fix, including effective stored-effort clamping. Focused verification: 30 tests passed across `session-utils-model.thinking-default.test.ts` and `server.sessions.agent-model-catalog.test.ts`; changed-file Oxfmt and Oxlint passed.

Live provider control on the built candidate: the OpenClaw harness completed a `gpt-5-mini` turn with low reasoning and returned `P170528_OK` (4.0 seconds, 64 reasoning tokens).

Checked the real Control UI reasoning picker as well. In this fixture it already refreshes to an Off/Ultra picker on main; the candidate retains that presentation. The observed defect and correction are at `sessions.list`, not a claimed visual picker change.

Before:
![Main Control UI reasoning picker](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/db81c3e3-f8bd-4b70-bd60-1cf3ea172526)

After:
![Fixed Control UI reasoning picker](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0e63f2be-c993-42ef-b142-d920938243a9)

Simplification: reuses the existing thinking owner with one additional argument; no new state, projection layer, or compatibility path. Delta against the merge base: production +1/-0, tests +40/-0. The table protects disabled reasoning and the enabled control; no distinct boundary cases were removed.

Merge danger: two-way door; a revert fully restores previous projection behavior and no persistent state is migrated. Blast radius: session metadata consumers for models with logical reasoning policy differing from the chosen runtime route.

prs.title: fix(zalouser): sanitize outbound tool traces
prs.body:
## Merge Brief

- **Problem / value:** Zalo Personal's custom monitor callback bypasses its standard adapter, so a `message_sending` hook can reintroduce internal tool traces immediately before transport. This patch keeps recipient text and captions clean while preserving configured Markdown-table rendering.
- **Relevance:** Independent P1/security report #90684 tracks this leakage class. Merged #112621 sanitizes the standard adapter only; current `main` still leaves this distinct callback seam open.
- **Smallest complete fix / review map:** Keep configured table conversion in `delivery.preparePayload`, where durable final delivery sees it, and sanitize only the effective post-hook payload in the custom callback. Scope is 4 files, `+76/-20`: two small helpers, two focused regressions, and the boundary wiring.
- **Risk / proof:** Risk is limited to ordering between two existing transforms. Exact head `41e305a4a4f4fd73973bac5858b07766db1791f9`; full Zalouser `317/317`; production/test type graphs, changed-scope format/lint/diff checks, and the deterministic pre-PR gate are green. ClawSweeper Revision 30's durable-table P1 is covered by the new regression.
- **External proof limit:** Authenticated recipient-visible transport is `blocked_external` because no safe configured account/recipient route exists. Exact-head tests reach both lifecycle boundaries; no live send is claimed.
- **Non-goals:** Standard adapter, sanitizer parser dialects, Zalo Bot, authentication, configuration schema, and protocol changes.
- **Maintainer ask:** Please apply `no-stale` while authenticated recipient proof is coordinated; the assigned-PR age clock otherwise ignores substantive updates.

## What Problem This Solves

Zalo Personal's custom inbound-reply path in `monitor.ts` can deliver a post-hook payload without passing through the standard outbound adapter. That leaves one route for compact tool-failure lines or tool XML to reach recipients. The repair must also preserve `channels.zalouser.markdown.tables` for final replies handled by durable delivery. Related: #90684.

## User Impact

Recipients get intended assistant text and media without internal tool-trace scaffolding, while existing table preferences such as `markdown.tables: "bullets"` continue to apply to durable final replies. Ordinary prose, captions, chunking, and media delivery remain unchanged; users have no migration step.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `delivery.preparePayload` owns configured table conversion before the lifecycle can return through durable delivery.
- The private custom callback owns sanitization after `message_sending`, so a supported hook cannot reintroduce internal traces.
- Merged #112621 covers the standard adapter only; this remains a narrow, distinct callback repair.

## Evidence

- Exact signed candidate head: `41e305a4a4f4fd73973bac5858b07766db1791f9` on frozen maintenance base `b464d49019995ec229595bdcbba9d3b61ff035f7`.
- `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/zalouser`: `33` files and `317/317` tests passing, including configured bullet-table preparation before durable delivery and post-hook trace sanitization at custom delivery.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`: passing.
- Changed Zalouser scope passes type-aware Oxlint, Oxfmt, and `git diff --check`. Repository-wide extension lint's only failure is unchanged frozen-base debt in `extensions/amazon-bedrock/stream.runtime.test.ts` (`max-lines`).
- Deterministic `openclaw-pre-pr.sh` gate: passed for frozen base `b464d49019995ec229595bdcbba9d3b61ff035f7`, exact head `41e305a4a4f4fd73973bac5858b07766db1791f9`, and merge tree `1d2e0ad6dc09fd07dfa21423c38602b80e92ae9d`.
- Current-`main` negative control: the custom monitor callback still resolves and delivers the post-hook payload directly. This head restores pre-durable table preparation and sanitizes immediately before custom text/caption resolution.
- Remaining proof state is `blocked_external`, not a claimed live pass: authenticated recipient-visible proof still requires a safe Zalo Personal account and recipient route.

AI-assisted change, manually reviewed and validated.

prs.title: fix(ui): hide realtime Talk tail block while session is idle
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In a session mixing typed messages and realtime Talk (voice), typed messages sent after a Talk session ends rendered above the earlier voice turns in the Control UI transcript. The render order did not match actual chronology.

## Why This Change Was Made

Finalized voice turns are persisted into session history with real chronological positions. The live Talk block is a tail row. Once a caption's saved history id arrives, that caption must leave the tail so history owns its slot and it is not pinned below newer typed messages.

An earlier revision hid the entire tail whenever Talk reported idle. A normal gateway-relay close reports idle without clearing the conversation or waiting for saved rows to reach `props.messages`. That gate deleted unmatched captions (for example `transcriptId` `voice:call:1` absent from loaded history) even though they were the only rendered copy. Live-caption retirement, introduced so a caption disappears only when its matching saved row arrives, is restored: idle is not a persistence receipt. Unmatched captions, including ones with no transcript id, stay visible across idle closure and retire only on history replacement.

## User Impact

- Saved voice turns stay in history order and are not duplicated at the transcript tail after Talk goes idle, so later typed messages no longer render above those saved turns.
- Unmatched voice captions remain visible after Talk becomes idle until their saved history rows arrive. Closing Talk does not erase the only record of what was said.
- During an active Talk session, live and not-yet-saved captions still stream at the tail. Already-saved captions still leave the tail as soon as their history ids arrive.

## Evidence

Head `cebc660b683da1a7e6d452e1fc97aa5caff52d48` on `upstream/main` (`2c7872bdad12ebef2a87e42566aa69cd405a543d`).

`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/pages/chat/chat-view.realtime-talk.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-transcript-voice-reconciliation.test.ts --reporter=verbose`

```
 ✓  ui  ui/src/pages/chat/chat-view.realtime-talk.test.ts > realtime Talk tail block gating > hides the realtime Talk tail while idle once saved captions are in history
 ✓  ui  ui/src/pages/chat/chat-view.realtime-talk.test.ts > realtime Talk tail block gating > keeps an unmatched voice caption visible after Talk becomes idle
 ✓  ui  ui/src/pages/chat/chat-view.realtime-talk.test.ts > realtime Talk tail block gating > hides saved idle captions from the tail while an unmatched caption stays visible
 ✓  ui  ui/src/pages/chat/chat-view.realtime-talk.test.ts > realtime Talk tail block gating > retires an unmatched idle caption only when its saved history row arrives
 ✓  ui  ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-transcript-voice-reconciliation.test.ts > voice transcript membership > skips the voice membership scan for absent captions
```

prs.title: fix(security): prevent unsafe approval patterns from hanging command authorization
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Exec approval, cron, and plugin model argPattern values can use nested alternation or adjacent overlapping repeats such as a*a*...b or (a|b)*(b|c)*z. Those patterns hang the JavaScript regex engine (catastrophic backtracking) and can freeze command authorization. A zero-minimum separator (?, {0,n}, or *) can be omitted, so a*x?a* and a*x*a* are still adjacent on that path. The shared safe-regex compiler must reject those shapes, including complete branch unions, without banning required separators (a*xa*), disjoint optionals (a*x?b*), JWT-style {10,}.{10,} redact patterns, or safe Unicode class pairs used by group mentions.

Non-alternating grouped sequences such as (ab)*(cb)* must keep their complete languages. Reducing a group to its last token made (ab)* and (cb)* look like b vs b, so a safe pattern that should match abcb was rejected. Wrapping groups still flatten inner unions so ((a|b))*((b|c))* stays rejected.

Equal character-class twins such as corp-[A-Z]+[A-Z]+ are valid custom redaction patterns. Tightening adjacent-repeat checks on the shared compiler would drop those patterns from redactSensitiveText. Shared compileSafeRegex keeps those twins. Exec stays fail-closed so they cannot hang command authorization.

Braced Unicode \u{hex} is a code point only when flags include u or v. Without those flags, \u{2} is identity u plus {2}, so ^(\u{2}|u)+$ is overlapping (uu|u)+ and must be rejected.

Disjoint mixed alternatives of equal consumed length such as ab|[c]d must stay accepted. An unconditional mixed-structure fallback treated corp-(ab|[c]d)+ as overlapping even though both branches consume two characters and are disjoint. That dropped custom redaction and let Doctor delete ^(ab|[c]d)+$. Shared analysis now compares equal-length atom sequences. Exec stays fail-closed on unsafe overlap such as (aa|a.)+ and (a+)+.

The mixed extractor must not treat every simple token as one consumed character. No-flag \141 is octal a and \x61 is hex a, so ^(\141\x61|aaaa)+$ is overlapping (aa|aaaa)+. Splitting \141 into \1, 4, 1 made 4 versus a look disjoint and let that ReDoS reach native matching. Decode complete escapes, or mark unknown-width atoms unproven, before positional disjointness.

Safe capturing wrappers such as ((ab)|(cd))+ must stay accepted. Both branches are fixed-width and disjoint. Treating group tokens as unknown overlap dropped corp-((ab)|(cd))+ from custom redaction and let Doctor delete ^((ab)|(cd))+$. Unwrap those groups. Conservative uncertainty is not grounds for deletion.

Decoded scalars must keep literal identity when overlap probing re-parses them as regex source. \x24 is `$`, not an end-anchor, so ^(\x24a|[$]a)+$ must reject. `\.` is a literal dot, not a wildcard, so corp-(\.a|[b]a)+ must stay accepted and still mask. Legacy octal first digit 4-7 consumes at most two digits, so \400 is \40 plus literal 0 and ^(\400| 0)+$ must reject.

Two-digit and three-digit numeric escapes are backreferences when that capture exists. The two-digit high-octal rule treated \40 as space even with 40 capturing groups, so ^ + 39 empty groups + (a)(\40b|abab)+$ compared space-plus-b with abab and accepted. Native JavaScript repeats overlapping ab|abab. Count captures before decoding decimal escapes, or keep potentially valid backreferences unproven. Same for three-digit \141 when capture 141 exists.

Escaped dollars in alternatives are literals. corp-(a\$|b[!])+ is a safe disjoint two-char pair. Stripping the final `$` from a\$ left a dangling escape, so atom extraction failed and the fallback rejected. Redaction then stopped masking corp-a$b!, and Doctor deleted the equivalent approval. Strip only actual anchor tokens.

Safe nested alternatives such as corp-((ab|cd)e|(fg|hi)j)+ have disjoint fixed-width languages (abe, cde, fgj, hij). Atom extraction used to return null at the inner `|` and the overlap fallback marked the outer `+` unsafe. Custom redaction then dropped the pattern, and Doctor deleted the equivalent anchored approval. Expand inner group alternatives into finite sequences so those languages stay accepted.

Unequal-length alternatives are not ReDoS by length alone. ^(a|[b]c)+$ safely matches abc because the first characters are disjoint, so repetition is unambiguous. An unconditional unequal-length return labeled that rule unsafe, so exec denied it and Doctor deleted it. Check prefix disjointness first. Prefix overlap such as (a|aa)+ still rejects.

Property escapes are flag-dependent. Without u or v, \p{L} is identity p plus {L}, so ^(\p{L}a|p\{L\}ap\{L\}a)+$ is overlapping (p{L}a|p{L}ap{L}a)+. Tokenizing \p{L} as one Unicode atom and probing it with u compared a versus { and accepted that hang. Decode property escapes with the actual flags before positional comparison.

Analysis budget exhaustion is not the same as an unsafe pattern. The 32-atom cap used to abort extraction for ^([a] + 32 b's | [c] + 32 d's)+$ even though the first characters are disjoint. Keep truncated prefixes so proven-disjoint languages stay accepted. Equal-length truncated prefixes that already overlap, such as 33 versus 66 copies of [a]a{32}, are proven overlap and must reject.

Decoded non-ASCII scalars must keep that identity in the selected probe mode. Flag selection removes u, so emitting \u{e9} made ^(\u00E9a|[é]a)+$ look disjoint. Emit \xNN or \uXXXX instead.

The 16-sequence expansion cap is unproven, not overlap. ^((a|b|c|d|e|f|g|h|i|j|k|l|m|n|o|p|q)x|zx)+$ is disjoint fixed-width. Returning unsafe at that cap dropped custom redaction and let Doctor delete the stored rule. Returning no-overlap at that cap is also wrong: ^((a|...|q)x|axax)+$ never compared ax with axax, so repeating ax plus a failing suffix reached native matching. Collapse single-atom unions so the 17-way |x versus zx rule stays accepted and the axax prefix language still rejects. Leftover overflow is not permission to execute.

Incomplete equal prefixes are not proven overlap. p=[a] plus 31 a's, then p+b versus p+c, is fixed-width disjoint. Both truncated to the same 32 atoms. Unconditional true deleted that stored rule and dropped custom redaction. Keep a stored continuation atom so b versus c stays disjoint, while 33 versus 66 overlapping [a]a{32} prefixes still reject.

Shared Unicode atoms must be compared as languages. A class containing U+0100 versus a U+0100 literal (each followed by ASCII a, then repeated) share that code point, but the finite probe set never visits it, so first positions looked disjoint and redaction compiled it. Probe characters named by each atom. Disjoint [猫]|[犬] stays accepted on the shared compiler. Exec's stricter unprobed fallback does not protect redaction.

Overlap probes must inherit the s flag. ^(.a|\na\na)+$ with s lets dot consume newline, so the branches overlap. Comparing them without s declared them disjoint.

Exec approvals keep a stricter unprobed-Unicode fail-closed helper that is not part of the public plugin SDK. Runtime still refuses those conservative patterns. Doctor --fix must not delete a stored manual rule that the shared compiler accepts. Only unsafe or invalid entries are removed. Detect must not create or migrate shared approval state.

The same persisted allowlist is also evaluated by the native macOS app. Node and JavaScriptCore share compileExecArgPattern.

Ref #90014

## Evidence


Latest head [`01fb611710d`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/01fb611710dc053b65805ba24663fea7d02a7036). Isolated worktree `/tmp/oc-82950`. Shared compiler keeps disjoint overflow `^((aa|bb|...|qq)|zz)+$` and mixed class `^([0\p{Script=Greek}]|[1])+$` with `u`. Exec still refuses those (Doctor-conservative). Overlapping `\p{L}` vs `[0\p{Script=Greek}]` still rejects. Native `ExecArgPatternSafetyJS.generated.swift` regenerated. `pnpm check:exec-arg-pattern:swift` exits 0.


Live production proof on isolated OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR (not ~/.openclaw). Called production compileSafeRegexDetailed, compileSafeRegexForExec, compileExecArgPattern, matchAllowlist, redactSensitiveText, collectRejectedExecArgPatterns, and repairRejectedExecArgPatterns.

```console

STATE_DIR /var/folders/7_/3g02szlx2h3_4pdqp0knlw740000gn/T/oc-82950-state-iJFEBC
COMPILE

seventeen-way shared=accepted exec=accepted execArg=accepted
truncated-disjoint-32 shared=accepted exec=accepted execArg=accepted
greek-letter-u shared=unsafe-nested-repetition exec=unsafe-nested-repetition
truncated-overlap shared=unsafe-nested-repetition
e-acute shared=unsafe-nested-repetition
nested-plus shared=unsafe-nested-repetition
ALLOWLIST two-char-overflow refused
ALLOWLIST seventeen matched
ALLOWLIST truncated-disjoint-32 matched
REDACT two-char-overflow id=corp-axaxax
REDACT seventeen id=corp-ax***
REDACT truncated-disjoint-32 id=corp-aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaabaaaaaa…aaac
REDACT greek-letter id=corp-αaαa
DOCTOR removed 2 /bin/unsafe,/bin/two-char-overflow
DOCTOR remaining /bin/seventeen-way /bin/truncated-disjoint /bin/truncated-disjoint-32 /bin/long-disjoint /bin/safe
```

Two-character expansion overflow stays refused and visible in redaction. Incomplete 32-repeat prefixes with disjoint suffixes still mask and stay stored. Letter versus Script=Greek under u stays refused. 17-way, truncated 31, long disjoint, and nested plus keep their prior outcomes.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Shared compilation no longer treats incomplete equal prefixes as proven overlap, no longer treats expansion overflow as safe, and no longer declares unobserved Unicode property languages disjoint.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS 26.6.2 arm64, Node v26.8.2, OpenClaw worktree on fix/exec-approval-redos-guard at b8d332b9bbe, isolated OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/var/folders/7_/3g02szlx2h3_4pdqp0knlw740000gn/T/oc-82950-state-iJFEBC (not ~/.openclaw).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Set OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR to a fresh temp directory. Called production compileSafeRegexDetailed, compileSafeRegexForExec, compileExecArgPattern, matchAllowlist, and redactSensitiveText on the three remaining cases plus the keep set (17-way, truncated 31, é, truncated 33 versus 66, s flag, nested plus). Seeded persisted exec approvals through production saveExecApprovals, then ran production collectRejectedExecArgPatterns and repairRejectedExecArgPatterns. Command: node --import tsx /tmp/proof-82950-rev83.mjs from the patched worktree.
- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output from the isolated production run:

  ```console
  STATE_DIR .../oc-82950-state-iJFEBC
  two-char-overflow shared=unsafe-nested-repetition exec=unsafe-nested-repetition
  seventeen-way shared=accepted exec=accepted
  truncated-disjoint-32 shared=accepted exec=accepted
  greek-letter-u shared=unsafe-nested-repetition exec=unsafe-nested-repetition
  truncated-overlap shared=unsafe-nested-repetition
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** Two-character expansion overflow no longer authorizes `axax`. Incomplete 32-repeat prefixes with disjoint `b`/`c` suffixes stay stored and still mask. Unprobed Letter versus Script=Greek overlap no longer compiles as disjoint under `u`. Nested plus, é overlap, and truncated 33 versus 66 still refuse.
- **What was not tested:** Live click-through in the shipping menu-bar app against a private production allowlist. A published npm release upgrade on a user machine. Current native JavaScriptCore matching of this HEAD.

prs.title: fix(slack): keep workspace identity in October delivery receipts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Slack deliveries losing their workspace identity when a send result is converted into a receipt.

## User Impact

Workspace-qualified sends retain a receipt for the actual destination and thread, including multipart messages and attachments.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the workspace attested by the sending client into receipt targets and reuse the same receipt construction in action and outbound paths. Thread planning stays pure so a failed send does not consume a single-use reply thread.

This is PR 1 of a seven-part October beta compatibility review. Its base is `kimiyu_openclaw_2026-10-01-beta1-reviewed` and its diff contains original fix `0697fc9a1ee8b63d2d152b617d2bc48e6618f42e` and follow-ups `8385716ecbac16b659b540f2f29e5105e0f0f392` and `f06970c397cbeca1a9fe1c900ad116cf39c8b872`. The first review base is `v2026.10.1-beta.1` plus four carried ports. The seven fixes were previously pushed directly to a candidate branch; this PR makes the existing patch available for normal CI and independent review. Historical pushes and author-run checks do not count as completed PR review or CI.

## Evidence

### Current review-stack head

Current head: `f06970c397cbeca1a9fe1c900ad116cf39c8b872`; base: `433c9a3ab1a166d97e0c32df165b0436d0ad04c1`. Both part1 follow-ups (actual question-card destination decoding and the introduced static type-cycle repair) were merged through the stack using normal commits. Original candidate/internal pin/live bots remain unchanged. Historical runtime/CI evidence is bound to its recorded SHA; newest-head CI and ClawSweeper conclusions are assessed separately.

### Introduced CI type-cycle repair

The synchronized stack's architecture job exposed a two-file static type cycle: `send-results.ts` imported `SlackSendResult` from `send.ts`, while the sender imported the receipt helper. The repository Madge policy includes type edges; this additional cycle came from this receipt refactor and was not covered by the inherited-failure exception.

`f06970c397cbeca1a9fe1c900ad116cf39c8b872` moves the byte-identical `SlackSendResult` definition into the common receipt/result owner. The sender consumes it there and preserves its existing type export. Runtime function bodies, including `sendMessageSlack`, are unchanged; no new module, option, schema or dependency is added.

```text
Baseline433: Madge1 cycle (875-member existing component)
Prior synchronized CI: same baseline component + Slack send/results2-node cycle
Afterf069 repair: exactly the same baseline component; Slack cycle absent
Receipt/outbound controls: 5 passed; serial native wrapper25.24s
Native changed checks: exit0 (format, production/test types, lint and guards)
Fresh P2 autoreview: scoped-clean; unchanged result definition/export verified
```

The Madge command still exits1 for the independently reproduced inherited component. This is not called green. The requesting maintainer authorizes proven existing/unrelated failures as nonblocking; the new cycle was repaired rather than waived. New exact-head hosted CI/re-review remains pending.

### ClawSweeper question-card follow-up

Addressed the P2 consumer regression in the [completed review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/170416#issuecomment-6135265069). New receipt targets are workspace-qualified; question finalization had passed that whole string as `chat.update.channel` and reused the requested workspace. The finalizer now decodes the **actual delivered target** with the existing Slack parser. Its workspace wins over the requested route; bare legacy receipts retain the prior fallback. The registration ID retains the qualified destination and the actual accepted question-card message ID.

Inspectable boundary proof (synthetic transport; not live Slack): the test takes the actual `toSlackOutboundResult` output through `afterDeliverPayload` and the registered finalizer. It observes the production `updateMessageSlack` arguments and removal of question controls.

```text
Original head0697fc9a1ee8, receipt delivered in T999, requested route T123:
Expected: channelId C123, teamId T999
Received: channelId team:T999:channel:C123, teamId T123
Tests: 1 failed, 4 passed

Repair8385716ecbac, native serial test wrapper:
PASS finalizes the delivered card with workspace undefined and removes its controls
PASS finalizes the delivered card with workspace T999 and removes its controls
PASS finalizes the actual card through multipart/durable reconciliation
3 test files passed; 16 tests passed; wrapper wall8.70s
```

Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/slack/src/question-finalization.test.ts extensions/slack/src/send.enterprise.test.ts extensions/slack/src/outbound-adapter.send-receipts.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Native changed checks against0697 passed, including formatting, production/test types, lint and guards. Fresh P2 autoreview found no actionable defect in the supplied source; it explicitly did not verify live Slack. The follow-up has not been deployed or merged. New exact-head hosted CI and ClawSweeper remain pending.


Fresh combined-source validation at `09156d64a267aaeef7b0bc31d6ae225d9858caf3`: `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base 433c9a3ab1a166d97e0c32df165b0436d0ad04c1 --head 09156d64a267aaeef7b0bc31d6ae225d9858caf3 --timed` completed successfully on Node 24.16.0, including formatting, core and extension production/test types, lint, dead-export and runtime/database guards. This validates the combined source, not each intermediate head or hosted CI. A fresh combined P2 autoreview reported no actionable finding within the supplied source evidence; it does not replace ClawSweeper or maintainer approval.

ClawSweeper completed the original-head review; its concrete P2 finalization defect is addressed above. The first normal exact-head CI attempt had the inherited audit failure below. Current-head CI/re-review must be read separately.

Author-run proof for this patch: the original receipt boundary regression failed before the change; 103 related tests passed after it. Coverage includes workspace qualification, multipart IDs, outbound/action receipts and thread behavior.

The final combined source has passed a focused staging core acceptance of 12/12 and two model-menu controls. That does not establish all release-suite coverage or the individual intermediate heads. No production deployment is included. The original full release-suite coverage limits remain; the first public CI audit failed as attributed below, and prior-head acceptance does not prove this undeployed finalizer follow-up.


### Known inherited CI failure on the recorded earlier head

The [exact-head CI audit](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38325451054/job/115063262086) failed on three production dependency advisories: `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.30.1` and `@modelcontextprotocol/client@2.0.0` ([GHSA-6qxp-vccf-f47h](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6qxp-vccf-f47h)), and `source-map-js@1.2.1` ([GHSA-68fv-2mgg-jv7q](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-68fv-2mgg-jv7q)).

These are inherited from the selected public beta, not caused by this fix. All package manifests, the lockfile, workspace configuration and audit implementation are unchanged from `v2026.10.1-beta.1` through the PR base and head. The actual CI merge commit `a4e9a64a397de613f18808066abdd48ea913efb0` has the expected base/head parents and exactly the PR-head tree. The same three audit findings were inspected in all seven stack jobs. Upstream already tracked fixes in #165902 and #166217.

The requesting maintainer explicitly accepts these proven inherited CI failures as non-blocking for this compatibility review. This is an attributed exception, not green CI or approval of the code. The downstream `openclaw/ci-gate` failed and fail-fast cancelled sibling jobs; those cancelled jobs remain incomplete hosted coverage. Normal code/security review and any defects caused by this patch still require resolution. No dependency update, scanner suppression or CI rerun is included.

<details>
<summary>October review stack</summary>

- Part 1: #170416 — fix(slack): keep workspace identity in October delivery receipts
- Part 2: #170417 — fix(codex): retain native tools in default October cron turns
- Part 3: #170418 — fix(codex): allow scheduled read-only app calls under ask
- Part 4: #170419 — fix(codex): avoid timing out valid October automation runs
- Part 5: #170420 — fix(codex): refresh app access for default October scheduled jobs
- Part 6: #170421 — fix(models): clarify partial model availability in October menus
- Part 7: #170422 — fix(slack): recognize same-workspace source channel aliases

Merge in dependency order into `kimiyu_openclaw_2026-10-01-beta1-reviewed`; later PRs are based on the preceding review branch. The final original head is `09156d64a267aaeef7b0bc31d6ae225d9858caf3`.

</details>

prs.title: fix(tlon): prevent stopped channels reconnecting after authentication
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a stopped Tlon account reopens its event stream when an already-running reconnect authentication finishes.

## User Impact

User impact: disabling a Tlon account keeps its event stream stopped, even if reconnect authentication is in flight. Normal reconnects continue working. No configuration or database migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing reconnect AbortController for the stream request. Guards at the HTTP dispatch boundary prevent channel creation/activation and SSE requests after shutdown; a separate response-arrival guard releases a late response before publishing its stream. Redundant checks around authentication and connection are removed. Shutdown can still unsubscribe and delete its channel.

Includes the current SSE framing fix from #170125 and retains its transport coverage. Thanks to @zhangguiping-xydt for the report and original fix. No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

## Evidence

An isolated **built Gateway**, with its bundled Tlon plugin pointed at a local Urbit-compatible HTTP server, ran the same operator sequence on current-main baseline and this candidate: connect, drop SSE, hold reconnect login, disable `channels.tlon.enabled` through config reload, observe channel DELETE, then release login. No private credentials or production Gateway were used.

```text
Baseline (bf58e95ee3f, includes #170125):
  login-held
  channel-delete
  account-stopped
  login-released
  GET /~/channel/...
  stream-open
  streamsAfterStop=1

Candidate:
  login-held
  channel-delete
  account-stopped
  login-released
  streamsAfterStop=0, requestsAfterStop=[]

Uninterrupted reconnect control:
  login-held
  login-released
  GET /~/channel/...
  stream-open
  streams=2
```

Focused checks: all four SSE/channel-operation test files pass (47 tests; 40.99 seconds Vitest wall time, 42.79 seconds including wrapper). This includes CRLF/multiline framing, both shutdown APIs during authentication, and shutdown while stream/channel-creation headers are pending. Changed-file formatting and lint pass. The fixture is synthetic HTTP, not a live Urbit ship.

The two added authentication regression cases fail on baseline source with an extra HTTP request (expected 3 requests, received 4; expected 5, received 6), and pass on the candidate. The Gateway candidate trace records **no channel PUT or SSE GET after stop**, not merely no published stream.

On exact head `2d2d6bc37c939b6bdf57931ea72d9a15d011ce54`, a credential-isolated real OpenAI `gpt-5-mini` agent turn completed successfully (`stopReason=stop`, visible assistant reply). This is a provider smoke check, not a live Urbit claim. [Hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38342748605) passed, including `openclaw/ci-gate`; ClawSweeper reviewed that exact head with no findings.

Simplification removes nine net production lines from the original proposal. Against the merge base: production +14/-3 (net +11), tests +63/-0. Remaining growth carries shutdown authority into the existing HTTP request owners; no new controller or lifecycle abstraction.

Merge risk: two-way door; reverting restores the old reconnect behavior without persistent-state changes. Blast radius is Tlon SSE reconnect and channel startup/shutdown only.
