prs.title: fix(openshell): exclude nested .git from mirror sync
prs.body:
## Summary
The OpenShell docs say workspace synchronization excludes `.git`, `hooks`, and `git-hooks` in both directions so repository credentials, history, and trusted hook code stay on the Gateway host (`docs/gateway/openshell.md`, "Security hardening"). The mirror only applied that list to the workspace root. A nested repository such as `sub/.git` (its `config` and `hooks/`) was mirrored from the sandbox onto the host and staged from the host into the sandbox upload. When the sandbox deleted the parent directory, the host's nested `.git` was deleted as well.

This is a docs mismatch and hardening fix: nested `.git` now gets the same treatment as the root `.git`.

## Root cause
`extensions/openshell/src/mirror.ts`, `reconcileMirrorDirectory` filters entries with `excludeDirs`, but the recursion through `reconcileMirrorPath` drops the list, so every level below the root runs with no exclusions:

```ts
// before
const preservedEntries = await reconcileMirrorDirectory({
  sourceDir,
  targetDir: params.targetPath,
  replace: params.replace,
});
```

Both `replaceDirectoryContents` (sandbox to host) and `stageDirectoryContents` (host to sandbox upload) route through this one function, so both directions were affected.

## Fix
`reconcileMirrorDirectory` passes `.git` down the recursion when the caller excludes it, and counts excluded target entries as preserved so a remote delete or file replacement does not remove the directory that holds them:

```ts
// after
const nestedExcludeDirs = params.excludeDirs?.filter((dir) =>
  NESTED_MIRROR_EXCLUDE_DIRS.has(normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(dir)),
);
...
excludeDirs: nestedExcludeDirs,
...
let preservedEntries = targetEntries.some(isExcluded);
```

Depth semantics follow what each entry names:
- `.git` is repository metadata wherever a repository lives, so it matches by name at every depth.
- `hooks` and `git-hooks` name the workspace hook directories. Workspace hooks load only from `<workspace>/hooks` (`src/hooks/workspace.ts`), and the original exclusion (#54657) targeted that root directory. They stay root-scoped, so ordinary nested source folders such as `src/hooks` keep syncing. Matching them at every depth would silently stop syncing common application code.

The docs paragraph now states these semantics explicitly.

## Why this is the right boundary
`reconcileMirrorDirectory` is the single shared walker for both sync directions, so one change covers download and upload staging. Workspace-root matching stays case-insensitive. Nested names match `.git` exactly, without trimming or case normalization, so ordinary names such as ` .git ` remain synchronized. Callers that do not pass `.git` in `excludeDirs` see no change. The workdir validation in `backend.ts` (`validateMirrorWorkdir`) still checks only the first path segment. That check rejects exec workdirs inside root excluded directories and does not copy files, so I left it unchanged.

## Verification
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openshell/src/mirror.test.ts`: with `mirror.ts` reverted to `upstream/main` 9a18261098 the two new cases fail (`Tests 2 failed | 12 passed (14)`); with the patch, `Tests 14 passed (14)`, file duration 6.54s. After the warning commit, `Tests 15 passed (15)` on head 66bcec0576.
- New cases: a sandbox file colliding with a host directory holding `.git` keeps the directory and warns once with the path, nested `.git/hooks` is not copied to the host, a nested `hooks` source folder still syncs, a host nested `.git` survives the sandbox deleting its parent, and nested `.git/config` is not staged for upload.
- Follow-up verification below adds a real extension `tsgo` check on the earlier head. Local lint and `tsgo` were not re-run for the rebase and warning commit; hosted CI covers them.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: OpenShell mirror sync copied nested repository metadata (`sub/.git/config`, `sub/.git/hooks/pre-commit`) in both directions and deleted a host nested `.git` when the sandbox removed or replaced its parent, although the docs say `.git` is excluded in both directions. When a sandbox file collides with a host directory that holds `.git`, the host directory is now kept and a warning names the skipped path, so the mismatch is no longer silent.
Real environment tested: macOS, Node 26.9.0, head `66bcec0576b4867f191f8406c4f8a99c25c4049b` rebased on `origin/main` `ebc4e6de603c5c1ce55086f13565e21feb1c297d`. The real exported `replaceDirectoryContents` and `stageDirectoryContents` were driven with `DEFAULT_OPEN_SHELL_MIRROR_EXCLUDE_DIRS` against real temporary directories on disk, first with `mirror.ts` from `origin/main` `ebc4e6de60` and then with this head. No sandbox CLI or SSH transport was involved; the on-disk filesystem, the production mirror walker, and the production subsystem logger stayed real.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `tsx drive-proof.mts base|patch`, a standalone driver that seeds `sub/.git/hooks/pre-commit`, `sub/.git/config`, `sub/src/hooks/useThing.ts`, and `sub/README.md`, runs sandbox-to-host `replaceDirectoryContents` and host-to-sandbox `stageDirectoryContents`, then runs a replace where the sandbox has a plain file `sub` and the host has `sub/.git/HEAD` plus `sub/notes.txt`, and prints whether each path exists. Same driver and inputs for both runs; only `mirror.ts` was swapped. Temp paths shortened to `$TMPDIR`.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (origin/main ebc4e6de60)
sandbox -> host (replaceDirectoryContents)
  host/sub/.git/hooks/pre-commit: present
  host/sub/.git/config: present
  host/sub/src/hooks/useThing.ts: present
  host/sub/README.md: present
host -> sandbox upload stage (stageDirectoryContents)
  stage/sub/.git/hooks/pre-commit: present
  stage/sub/.git/config: present
  stage/sub/src/hooks/useThing.ts: present
  stage/sub/README.md: present
sandbox file sub vs host directory sub/.git (replaceDirectoryContents)
  host/sub type: file
  host/sub/.git/HEAD: absent
  host/sub/notes.txt: absent
# AFTER (head 66bcec0576, identical inputs)
sandbox -> host (replaceDirectoryContents)
  host/sub/.git/hooks/pre-commit: absent
  host/sub/.git/config: absent
  host/sub/src/hooks/useThing.ts: present
  host/sub/README.md: present
host -> sandbox upload stage (stageDirectoryContents)
  stage/sub/.git/hooks/pre-commit: absent
  stage/sub/.git/config: absent
  stage/sub/src/hooks/useThing.ts: present
  stage/sub/README.md: present
[openshell] mirror kept host directory $TMPDIR/oc-proof-QsGqjB/host2/sub because it contains preserved host entries; skipped the sandbox file at that path.
sandbox file sub vs host directory sub/.git (replaceDirectoryContents)
  host/sub type: directory
  host/sub/.git/HEAD: present
  host/sub/notes.txt: absent
```
Observed result after fix: nested `.git` content no longer crosses the mirror in either direction. Ordinary nested files, including a nested `src/hooks` folder, still sync. When the sandbox has a file where the host has a directory holding `.git`, main replaced the directory and lost the host Git metadata; this head keeps the directory and its `.git`, removes the other stale host entries, and emits one warning naming the skipped path.
What was not tested: no live OpenShell gateway or sandbox round trip over SSH (`pnpm test:e2e:openshell` needs Docker and a local OpenShell gateway); Windows case-insensitive paths were not exercised beyond the existing lowercase matcher.

## File vs preserved directory decision
Maintainer question: if the sandbox has a plain file `sub` and the host has `sub/` containing `.git`, should the mirror replace or preserve? This PR preserves and now warns. Reasoning: main already applies the same rule to host entries the mirror cannot represent (symlinks, FIFOs, sockets): "A remote file cannot replace a directory containing preserved host entries." Host `.git` is now one of those preserved entries, so the same rule applies, and the sandbox cannot delete host repository metadata by replacing its parent with a file. The new `log.warn` in `reconcileMirrorPath` names the kept host directory and says the sandbox file was skipped, so the divergence is visible. The docs paragraph states this behavior. If maintainers prefer source-wins replacement, that is a one-branch change in `reconcileMirrorPath`, but it would let the sandbox delete host Git metadata, which is what this PR is meant to stop.

## Exact-name follow-up verification
Contributor commits and credit are retained. No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

On candidate `9eab39c8a0d756d7b12ae9d6e76ecd6eb03cea14` (runtime and test sources unchanged from `5b48d963db77f677ead9a30679eefbd98cbbffc7`), a secretless Linux/Node 24 container exercised the production `replaceDirectoryContents` and `stageDirectoryContents` entry points used by `backend.ts:995` and `backend.ts:1048`. The baseline used the mirror owner from current main `e7546f2e40cc1d75d3a253fae40243be0eea8548`. Both used the same real-filesystem driver and a real `git init` at `sub/repo`.

| Control | Main | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nested `sub/repo/.git` mirrored/staged | yes | no |
| Submodule-style `.git` file mirrored/staged | yes | no |
| Root `.git` mirrored/staged | no | no |
| Normal-file checksums identical in both directions | yes | yes |
| Ordinary nested ` .git ` file copied | yes | yes |

SHA-256 listings were identical at source, download target, and upload stage on both versions:
```text
d7379507842868a936d38e05b250f8409cd5773edf03515312477243ccd85ed2  README
d614708341dc1c9880a1c3b44c47864dc9756bbfd0a0c1206e733ca4552e8b30  sub/ .git 
ee40a44130b3386b475b0a3ed6a811f9bd3c5c343eb69c00eb45a5272be02b2c  sub/linked/normal.txt
7f5996bcec7b8b4992b8bb5de78bb7696e6e7698393eaddf78a157149817ca14  sub/repo/normal.txt
```

Ancestor replacement control: with a source plain file `sub` and target directory `sub/.git`, main replaced the directory with the file. Candidate preserved the target directory and Git metadata, did not copy the replacement file, and left the source file unchanged. This deliberately preserves host Git metadata; no ordinary files were lost in this control.

- Original PR tests against main's mirror owner: 2 failures, 12 passes (nested metadata unexpectedly present).
- Spaced-name regression against contributor head `d4a16dc8607`: 2 failures, 12 passes (`ENOENT` reading `sub/ .git `).
- Candidate: all 14 tests pass, 4.66-second Vitest duration, 6.22-second wrapper wall time. Existing cases extended; no new process fixture or test added.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`: passed.
- Real OpenAI call through the candidate AI runtime: `gpt-5-mini`, reasoning low, max output 4096; returned `MIRROR_GATE_OK` with stop reason `stop` (14 input, 52 output tokens).

Limit: this is the real filesystem owner, not a Gateway/SSH/OpenShell service round trip. That requires an installed OpenShell CLI, reachable OpenShell gateway, and supported compute runtime. This isolated environment has no OpenShell CLI, gateway registration, or Docker daemon; sharing the host Docker socket or running privileged is not allowed. OpenShell supports local gateways without a paid account, but no isolated local gateway deployment is available here. The repository's `test:e2e:openshell` requires those same prerequisites.

Final-head documentation repair: replaced whitespace-bearing inline code with explicit prose because Markdown formatting removes the delimiter-adjacent spaces. Scoped `oxfmt --check` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions` passed; the live provider gate also passed again on final head. The prior head’s `check-lint` and `check-docs` formatting failures were caused by this PR and are repaired, not claimed as inherited.

prs.title: fix: release Doctor inspection resources and rejected locks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes retained plugin source directories after repeated Doctor/startup inspections, and a stranded filesystem lock when its post-acquisition handoff guard rejects ownership.

Related: #170439.

## User Impact

Repeated in-process preflight operations release their inspection resources. A rejected lock acquisition releases the acquired lock before rethrowing, so later operations can acquire it normally. Public SDK signatures, stored formats, schema, permissions, and update behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Fresh preflight caches now belong to the creating preflight operation. Superseded and failed reads retire there; the final cache transfers only after surrounding cleanup succeeds. Doctor carries that ownership in its existing disposable stack, ordinary CLI validation releases it on exit, and Gateway startup transfers it to the process cache owner. Ambient borrowed caches and metadata-only discovery behavior stay with their existing owners. The old unowned snapshot-reader export is removed and all callers migrate together.

The file-lock owner releases the underlying acquired handle when the handoff assertion throws. The restrictive guard on public release remains: it protects a borrowed resource at a real effect boundary. No new checks, generations, or synchronization protocols are introduced; no validation checks are removed in this lifecycle-only change, so there are no newly accepted check-removal edge cases.

The CLI transcript fallback item is already fixed by #170439 (`efd2af593300`): its helper releases a consumed write when the outer authority check rejects. Its existing regression covers that boundary; this PR does not duplicate the repair.

## Evidence

- Focused file-lock suite: 16/16 passed, including real sidecar removal and immediate reacquisition after rejected handoff (68.35 seconds including runner startup on the loaded development host).
- The same file-lock tests on base `e78a253059eb` fail only the new rejected-handoff regression: the lock sidecar remains present when cleanup should have removed it. The 15 existing tests pass (194.35 seconds command wall time on the loaded host).
- New preflight regression exercises external Doctor contract captures through real Doctor/startup operations, successful disposal, and rejected startup: all 3 passed locally (356.98 seconds including transforms on the loaded development host; test bodies 77.82/16.21/10.51 seconds). The fixture retires its caller-owned invocation cache separately from the fresh inspection caches under test.
- On the unchanged base, startup and rejected startup both fail at the capture-directory removal assertion: the directories still exist. The Doctor baseline case hit its 120-second timeout and is not counted as direct negative proof. The baseline command took 920.98 seconds including cold worker compilation; candidate Doctor/startup cases all pass locally and in CI.
- All six changed test files (66 cases), including the renamed-export mock consumer, pass on final head `c558b50e53d1` in [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38337574363). The lifecycle/startup batch passed 49 tests in 31.24 seconds; CLI guard batch passed 35 tests in 13.96 seconds; Doctor persistence batch passed 87 tests in 105.42 seconds; file-lock passed 16 tests in 1.64 seconds. CLI guard regression covers terminal retirement and preservation after Gateway adoption.
- Independent Codex autoreview: scoped-clean, no actionable findings (two rounds).
- Basic lint, hosted type-aware lint, production/test types, and source contracts passed. SDK API diff reports no entrypoint or export changes; SDK surface budget and runtime API guardrails passed (plugin contract suite: 23 files, 251 tests, 32.69 seconds). Final-head T1 and dialect ratchets passed: repository T1 stays 455→455; touched-owner T1 stays 0→0.
- [Published-driver × candidate update cell passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38336355954/job/115102599686): published 2026.10.2 updated to `0661bbc2831e`, returned readyz=200, verified the running version and preserved durable/incognito sessions. The only later commit corrects tests, so this is the final production implementation. CI supplied this proof; no remote lease or local Docker was needed.
- Madge on final head reports 0 cycles. The initial dependency scan's nine Knip findings match [scheduled main CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38334375513/job/115091147890) exactly in untouched files; main repaired them in #170499 (`12be6f68b5e1`), whose dependency check passed.
- Production diff: +115/−38 (153 changed lines), below the revised 400-line budget.

One frozen shared-harness v2.1 pair compared base `e78a253059eb` with final head `c558b50e53d1`, using Node 24.21.0 and SQLite 3.53.4. Both complete workloads passed all 13 turns plus control-plane, cron, compaction, and shutdown checks. Distributions below cover the ten warmed turns; one pair follows the current relaxed testing policy.

prs.title: fix(sessions): preserve requester identity at execution admission
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Related: #150705.

Delegated work can lose the original requester’s identity, and steering can mix two people’s requests under the active turn’s authority. This change preserves the requester and prepares the applicable destination policy when each new execution is admitted.

## User Impact

A message from a different requester waits for its own turn in the same conversation. The runtime acknowledges the actual queue decision and says that the active work has not changed. If queue overflow removes the message before the final acknowledgment check, the runtime reports that outcome. A queued stop request does not mean the active work stopped. Same-requester steering retains the existing compatibility and current-owner checks; explicit incompatible `sessions_send(mode="steer")` refuses with followup guidance.

Already admitted work retains its prepared policy while queued or running. Human input awaiting admission uses current policy when admitted; a new delegation resolves current applicable policy for the original requester at its destination. Accepted asynchronous work must survive normal source completion. Intentional delegation to a more capable agent remains supported under destination authorization. Shared conversation history remains shared.

## Why This Change Was Made

Requester facts travel through existing reply, accepted-input, recovery, worker, and transport owners. Cancellation, revocation, and superseded-owner checks remain effective. Telegram DM and X guest configuration resolve through their channel owners. The deprecated public SDK prepared-policy adapter retains its original request/queued-turn lifetime for external integrations and is not inherited into a new delegation. No universal source-capability ceiling, configuration option, database schema version, or request-hash format is added.

## Correction Candidate and Line Churn

**Current correction: `fcc42266d1af203f00f79d5136e4eea5e0dbe433`.** The branch includes pinned main `7f98077b2e30dd5b0c2aa271b9934f6414a106dc`, including the reviewed profile-authority, asset, archive-fixture, and publication-recovery repairs described below. Tree `84fadb6907a2d162614a20eb8c19bf4c349dbfe1` contains **245 files, +8,098 / −2,943 (net +5,155; churn 11,041)**. Frozen binary diff SHA-256: `fe0f7e999516a71a577ef886fc7f70d09f78dcda78fa35e742a6b1f32273b48b`. Final canonical runtime preparation passes (69.285s); the working tree is clean. Current-head CI settled red with one substantive SSE-history failure plus the aggregate gate; current-head hosted review meets the requested ratings (4/5/4) with no code findings. Prior-head results remain qualified below.

| Area | Files | Added | Removed | Net | Churn |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Production | 123 | +2,304 | −833 | +1,471 | 3,137 |
| Tests and support | 114 | +5,719 | −2,071 | +3,648 | 7,790 |
| Docs | 4 | +72 | −36 | +36 | 108 |
| Tooling and guard inventories | 4 | +3 | −3 | +0 | 6 |
| **Current total** | **245** | **+8,098** | **−2,943** | **+5,155** | **11,041** |

The corrections remove an import-cycle edge through the existing recorder owner; bound compatibility-registry declarations without changing the runtime records or exact code union; preserve hydrated reply routing; and repair real admission/configuration prerequisites in test fixtures. Consumed historical input receipts use their existing legacy shape without requester metadata; pending input still requires exact custody and payload hashes. Shared fixture extractions preserve suite order and assertions. Moved and reformatted lines count toward churn. No timeout, permission, assertion, or budget relaxation is used to conceal a failure.

## Evidence and Remaining Gates

**Current `fcc42266` CI settled red: 129 successful, 22 skipped, one substantive failure plus the aggregate gate.** [Run 38341751165](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38341751165) tests merge `c954cc95c2467bd0314e05709190cc49e464ec44`, main parent `bf58e95ee3f583c338f48225ad9c5b3479e7d8d7`. All seven UI shards pass; the archive group passes 144/144, suggestions 169/169, and orphan recovery 201/201. These outcomes do not establish causes for the earlier unreproduced failures. The new failure is `sessions-history-http.test.ts` / “bounds retained SSE history without truncating full history or live updates”: the SSE stream ends before the next event. Its production owners and target test are byte-identical to the tested main parent. One local replay of the actual merge and original ten-file HTTP group passes 281 cases with three platform skips (185.518s; target 2.250s). The unchanged-assertion observation run passes 20/20 (135.157s); all target read phases complete and no authority/sharing/identity failure branch fires. Source tracing rules out the proposed stale-sharing window for the existing transcript append: its receipt preserves the sharing projection and the final read remains available. No speculative ordering or guard change was made. A Blacksmith Testbox control then uses a private clean checkout of the exact merge on Linux x64 / Node 24.19.0: all 284 cases pass (143.00s Vitest / 144.92s wrapper; 237.788s including setup), target 1.577s. [Linux control run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38343320428); task-owned lease `tbx_01m4snxkk6re5p1vva0b5z6epd` was stopped and verified completed. Vitest owns cross-file scheduling; no passing control proves a fix. The original close branch and concurrent activity remain unknown. Relevant owner bytes matching main do not alone prove an inherited cause. All local instrumentation is restored; no source change was justified by this bounded investigation.

**Previous `115d4df4` CI settled red: 121 successful, 22 skipped, six failed jobs (five substantive plus aggregate).** [Run 38338351989](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38338351989) tests merge `fe0c1bb029ff484f515005f0c1969f5d224d657e`, main parent `877301a3af040d90690018379958073b28777ef3`. Original logs are retained once. The previous profile-authority failures cleared. Current attribution and remaining work:

- **Generated Workboard assets:** clean-main check reproduces the stale manifest (6.523s). Canonical regeneration changes only the two entry/style hash pointers. Fresh review is clean; committed asset check passes (14.769s). The exact +2/−2 correction is published on main as `054c048df0f3b7dbf44aa929658a638bc5d9ba6f` and incorporated in the current branch. No PR was merged.
- **Archive refresh:** unchanged main's actual 28-file envelope passes 144/144 (255.208s). A bounded real-descriptor diagnostic establishes premature archived fixture state, but causes a title assertion failure rather than CI's wrong `archived:false` request; exact CI timing causality remains unproven. The local alternative passes the full 10/10 archive suite on `ac8de4fd` (104.538s) and selected UI test types (265.214s). That unpublished alternative is superseded by upstream `ff136c3cc5cde2e150e5f9324f59260b00380e45` (#170521), included in main `19d6990b10`: it holds the patch before the click, waits for the real archive request, then publishes the descriptor and resolves the held patch through the canonical commit before awaiting the unchanged toast. All assertions remain; no production or appearance change. The local passes are not relabeled as exact-CI causality or as a replay of the upstream bytes.

Existing settings and transcript bytes remain owned by their current stores. There is no requester-metadata backfill or schema-version change in this PR. Consumed historical receipts may use their established legacy shape; pending input still binds exact custody and payload. Recovery without authenticated requester custody refuses explicitly rather than inferring identity from display text. The deprecated public SDK prepared-policy adapter keeps its documented original-request lifetime, and new delegation resolves policy afresh.

Shared conversation history remains shared. Queue notices describe the last authoritative admission/queue check; subsequent queue changes can race transport delivery under the existing queue owner. Live proof uses one leased Telegram user plus an authenticated Gateway operator and a controlled provider. Two Telegram accounts, native slash-stop, and nondeterministic provider behavior are not claimed by that campaign.

The PR remains open under validation. No PR has been merged or enabled for auto-merge.

Release publication admission repeatedly spends time searching for deltas while preparing a temporary local source pack.

prs.title: improve: reduce model catalog allocations after configuration reloads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After a neutral configuration reload, listing models and reading retained chat metadata can repeatedly copy the whole configuration for every model.

## User Impact

Model selection and chat metadata do less allocation work after a reload while retaining the same models, authentication decisions, and readiness checks. No schema change, migration, configuration option, or operator action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The managed reload publishes an equal-but-distinct runtime config object. Passing the prepared owner's original object into each model decision repeatedly reconstructs its source projection. The existing catalog projector now captures the runtime/source pair once and carries it through catalog preparation and retained metadata reads. This uses the existing capture owner and introduces no additional cache.

The original request stamps, observation identity, current-owner checks, live authentication store, authentication deadlines, and personal model pins retain their existing owners. Tests exercise the registered `models.list` handler and metadata preparation after an actual managed neutral publication.

## Evidence

For a synthetic 32-model catalog, a single matched measurement produced:

| Operation | Full-config clones before → after | Wall time before → after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Registered `models.list` | 97 → 3 | 14.10 → 10.11 ms |
| Metadata preparation | 97 → 3 | 15.94 → 8.06 ms |
| 32 retained metadata reads | 1,024 → 0 | 68.59 → 47.97 ms |

The clone counts establish the bounded allocation improvement. These are single timing samples on an isolated Node 24.19.0 runner, not a whole-Gateway latency claim. Small-case timings were mixed, and whole-command peak RSS was essentially unchanged. The temporary benchmark is not added to the test suite.

The original regression fails with 4 and 97 projections exceeding the preparation bound for one and 32 models. The candidate passes with one projection per preparation and none during retained reads, while preserving returned values and owner retirement.

The final focused run passed **56 tests across eight files in 62.13 seconds command wall**, using `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` with `--maxWorkers=1`. Coverage includes native readiness and revocation, owner/config stamps, authentication deadlines, personal pins, published results, plugin runtime, and configured runtime choices. The two new regression bodies took 454 ms and 141 ms. The two updated configured-index/authentication cases took 456 ms and 99 ms. Their fixture now observes the actual index owner and live auth store; restoring the original per-row construction still fails the index bound with **5 > 1**. Hosted CI measured 0.395 seconds across the two new regression bodies and 1.126 seconds for the updated index/authentication pair; these exclude setup and shard overhead.

The full changed gate passed core types, all **27 test type-check groups**, four-file lint with zero warnings/errors, formatting, dead exports, schema/legacy-store guards, import cycles, and the remaining structural checks in **1,263.66 seconds**. All 31 recorded source/toolchain inputs matched before and after execution. Incorporation onto main `632b150d462f` preserves those inputs and all four reviewed file contents. Fresh independent P0–P2 review is clean.

The [first hosted CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36501379881) passed all Node test shards. Its remaining browser shard exceeded the 25-minute job limit after two chat position-rail tests timed out at 120 seconds each. The required gate is red; the investigation below did not establish a product fix.

A bounded replay of the same merged source passed **81 files / 354 tests in 394.803 seconds command wall** (392.55 seconds Vitest) on an isolated Node 24.19.0 runner with four-CPU affinity and three workers. The native Vitest result cache was cleared and all 81 files matched the original cold shard order before execution. The original failing reader-dark and 80-message LTR layout cases passed in 20.114 and 22.352 seconds. Test source, assertions, and the 120-second test limit were unchanged.

Across 155 matching cases, the hosted median non-rail duration was 7.27 times the replay duration. The original job retained no quota, memory, steal-time, or timeout-capture evidence sufficient to explain this broad slowdown; the isolated machine is not fully equivalent to that runner. A passing replay does not prove a fix. No UI repair or hosted rerun was made, and the failed required gate remains unresolved.

prs.title: fix(outbound): failed media spool removals leave artifacts behind without a warning
prs.body:
Closes #153498
Related: #153483 (the same "swallowed cleanup error" pattern for the Gateway restart intent, fixed separately in #160805).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when the delivery queue can't delete a spooled media copy during release or orphan pruning (for example because of a permission or I/O error), the error is thrown away by an empty `catch {}`. The artifact stays on disk with **no log line** explaining why.

## User Impact

User impact: operators now get one `outbound/deliver` warning naming the spool artifact and the error whenever a removal fails unexpectedly. That makes leftover media in `delivery-queue-media/` explainable.

Nothing else changes:
- `releaseSpoolArtifacts` still never throws, and it keeps releasing the remaining artifacts after one fails.
- Artifacts that are **already gone** (released or pruned earlier) stay silent, so there's no new log noise.
- Queue settlement and reference-aware pruning are untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

```diff
   try {
     await openSpoolStore(stateDir).remove(relative);
-  } catch {}
+  } catch (err) {
+    // Already-released artifacts are expected; anything else would leave media behind silently.
+    if (!(err instanceof FsSafeError && err.code === "not-found")) {
+      log.warn(`failed to remove delivery queue media artifact ${relative}: ${String(err)}`);
+    }
+  }
```

`fileStore().remove()` throws `FsSafeError` with code `not-found` for a missing file. I verified this directly against `@openclaw/fs-safe`. That case is expected, so it stays quiet. The `FsSafeError` / `not-found` check is the same one used in `subagent-attachment-cleanup.ts`. The logger is the existing `outbound/deliver` subsystem shared by the delivery-queue modules.

As ClawSweeper noted on the issue, the periodic pruner can already retry unreferenced artifacts, so this is a **diagnostic** fix. Retention behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

### Real removal failure (no injected error, logger not mocked)

This runs the real `releaseSpoolArtifacts` with the real `outbound/deliver` logger against a fresh, isolated state directory. It uses three spool files:
- `000…001.ogg` has the macOS user-immutable flag (`chflags uchg`), so the **operating system itself** refuses to unlink it.
- `000…002.ogg` is a normal file.
- `000…003.ogg` was already released, so it's missing.

```text
--- before: merge base ad7669535c3 (empty catch)
[proof] spool: 000…001.ogg (immutable), 000…002.ogg (normal), 000…003.ogg (already released)
[proof] releaseSpoolArtifacts resolved (did not throw)
[proof] after release: 000…001.ogg exists=true, 000…002.ogg exists=false

--- after: this PR 48474f34260
[proof] spool: 000…001.ogg (immutable), 000…002.ogg (normal), 000…003.ogg (already released)
[outbound/deliver] failed to remove delivery queue media artifact 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001.ogg: FsSafeError: path could not be removed
[proof] releaseSpoolArtifacts resolved (did not throw)
[proof] after release: 000…001.ogg exists=true, 000…002.ogg exists=false
```

In both runs the stuck file stays behind, the normal file is still removed (cleanup continues), and the call resolves. The only difference is that the real failure is now reported. The already-released file produces no warning.

<details>
<summary>Proof script</summary>

```ts
// node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs proof.mts   (OC_REPO=<checkout>)
const stateDir = fs.realpathSync(fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "oc-spool-proof-")));
const { resolveDeliveryQueueMediaDir } = await import(`${repo}/src/config/paths.ts`);
const { releaseSpoolArtifacts } = await import(`${repo}/src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-media-spool.ts`);
const spoolRoot = resolveDeliveryQueueMediaDir(stateDir);
fs.mkdirSync(spoolRoot, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
fs.writeFileSync(stuck, "audio-bytes");
fs.writeFileSync(removable, "audio-bytes");
execFileSync("chflags", ["uchg", stuck]); // OS-level unlink refusal (EPERM)
await releaseSpoolArtifacts([stuck, removable, alreadyGone], stateDir);
execFileSync("chflags", ["nouchg", stuck]); // cleanup
```

</details>

### How to reproduce in a test

Release two spooled artifacts where removing the first one fails:

```ts
storeSpy.onRemove = (rel) => { if (rel === ARTIFACT_A) throw new Error("EACCES: permission denied"); };
await releaseSpoolArtifacts([stuck, removable], stateDir); // main: resolves, logs nothing
```

The test injects the failure at the `fileStore().remove` seam and uses the real filesystem for everything else.

### Regression tests

`src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-media-spool.test.ts` adds two cases under **ownership helpers**.

| Test | Asserts |
|---|---|
| warns when a spool artifact cannot be removed and keeps releasing the rest | release still resolves, the second artifact is removed, and exactly one warning contains `failed to remove delivery queue media artifact <name>: Error: EACCES` |
| stays quiet when a released artifact is already gone | no warning for the `not-found` case |

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-media-spool.test.ts
```

| | Result |
|---|---|
| without the fix | ❌ `expected "vi.fn()" to be called once, but got 0 times` |
| with the fix | ✅ 16 passed (16) |

Measured cost: `pnpm test src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-media-spool.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` took **47.6 s wall** with a cold transform cache. Vitest reports 42.3 s, of which 87% is transform and about 4.7 s is test execution for the whole file. The two new cases take about 10 ms together.

### Checks

- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` (tsgo core + core tests, oxlint, oxfmt, line-cap / max-lines ratchets): ✅ pass
- Codex autoreview (branch mode, P1): `scoped-clean`

### CI note

The remaining red checks on this head are not caused by this change:

- `openclaw/ci-gate` is red only because `check-additional-extension-package-boundary` hit its `timeout-minutes: 20` limit (it ran 20m49s and is reported as *cancelled*). Every step inside that job had already passed, ending with `extension package boundary check passed` / `[ok] test:extensions:package-boundary:canary`, and this PR touches no extension package. [job log](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36499983322/job/109188971133)
- `checks-node-changed-compact-large-21-1` failed one unrelated Gateway test, `src/gateway/server.chat-first-turn-binding.test.ts` ("binds a first native chat.send before streaming…"), with `Startup failed: required secrets are unavailable … Shared-state worker opening path changed` (`STATE_DATABASE_READ_ADMISSION_INVALIDATED`). That is a transient state-database admission race; this PR only touches the media spool helper. The same test passes locally on this head: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.chat-first-turn-binding.test.ts` gives 1 passed (1). [job log](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36499983322/job/109188974626)

prs.title: fix(gateway): failures clearing the restart intent are silently ignored
prs.body:
Closes #153483
Related: #153498 (the same "swallowed cleanup error" pattern in the delivery-queue media spool, fixed separately in #160806). Earlier restart work in #153510 and #71465 changed restart admission and drain but didn't touch this cleanup path.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when the Gateway can't clear its pending restart-intent row (for example because the state database is read-only, locked, or unreadable), the error is thrown away by an empty `catch {}`. The stale row stays behind with **nothing in the logs** to explain it.

## User Impact

User impact: operators now see a `restart` subsystem warning, `failed to clear gateway restart intent: <error>`, when cleanup fails. It matches the warning that already exists for a failed intent **write**, so a leftover restart intent is visible during triage.

Restart behavior itself is unchanged. The call stays non-throwing, so callers such as the `onRecorded` cleanup callback behave exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

```diff
-  } catch {}
+  } catch (err) {
+    restartLog.warn(`failed to clear gateway restart intent: ${String(err)}`);
+  }
```

`writeGatewayRestartIntentSync` already logs its failures through `restartLog`. `clearGatewayRestartIntentSync` is its counterpart, so it now reports the same way.

I deliberately did **not** change restart admission. The issue's "unwanted restart" consequence hasn't been demonstrated (ClawSweeper's review of the issue notes this too), so this PR only fixes the proven problem: the missing diagnostic.

## Evidence

### Real runtime trace (logger not mocked)

This runs the real `clearGatewayRestartIntentSync` with the real `restart` subsystem logger in a fresh, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, where the state database has been replaced by a file that isn't a SQLite database. Paths are redacted to `<state>`.

```text
--- before: merge base ad7669535c3 (empty catch)
[proof] state db replaced with a non-SQLite file: <state>/state/openclaw.sqlite
[proof] clearGatewayRestartIntentSync returned; threw=false

--- after: this PR 8377bb315cc
[proof] state db replaced with a non-SQLite file: <state>/state/openclaw.sqlite
[restart] failed to clear gateway restart intent: Error: file is not a database
[proof] clearGatewayRestartIntentSync returned; threw=false
```

Before the fix, the cleanup failure leaves no trace. After it, the same failure produces one `restart` warning, and the call still returns normally.

<details>
<summary>Proof script</summary>

```ts
// node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs proof.mts   (OC_REPO=<checkout>)
const stateDir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "oc-restart-intent-proof-"));
const env = { ...process.env, OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR: stateDir };
const { resolveOpenClawStateSqlitePath } = await import(`${repo}/src/state/openclaw-state-db.paths.ts`);
const { clearGatewayRestartIntentSync } = await import(`${repo}/src/infra/restart-intent.ts`);
const databasePath = resolveOpenClawStateSqlitePath(env);
fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(databasePath), { recursive: true });
fs.writeFileSync(databasePath, "not a sqlite database");
clearGatewayRestartIntentSync(env);
```

</details>

### How to reproduce in a test

Point the state directory at a file that isn't a SQLite database, then clear the intent:

```ts
fs.writeFileSync(resolveOpenClawStateSqlitePath(env), "not a sqlite database");
clearGatewayRestartIntentSync(env); // main: silently returns, nothing logged
```

This test uses real SQLite and the real state-DB transaction path, not a mocked transaction.

### Regression test

`src/infra/restart-intent.test.ts` adds **"warns instead of staying silent when clearing the intent fails"**. It asserts that the call does not throw and that it emits exactly one `restart` warning matching `/^failed to clear gateway restart intent: /`. The test observes only the `restart` subsystem logger. Everything else in the file keeps using the real logger.

```sh

```

|---|---|
| without the fix | ❌ `expected "vi.fn()" to be called once, but got 0 times` |

prs.title: fix: schedule local continuations with unauthenticated MCP integrations
prs.body:
Related: #156379

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes continuation scheduling being blocked when an unrelated configured MCP integration is not authenticated.

## User Impact

Agent-created continuations capture the currently executable, authorized subset and report excluded integrations in `warnings`. Explicit unavailable or unknown tool selectors fail before saving instead of silently disappearing. Trusted runtime aliases retain their canonical executable identities. Later login does not expand a saved tool ceiling; current permissions and approvals still apply. No configuration, storage schema, or protocol version changes.

**Intentional upgrade behavior:** older finite lists could silently drop unavailable names. New creates and explicit tool-policy edits reject those names, including named requirements alongside `*`; remove unavailable selectors or restore access. Existing stored caps are not rewritten.

This authority-sensitive PR remains a draft for owner/security review. Required CI/review gates are not waived; no merge or deployment is requested.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing creator-authority snapshot and cap owners. Keep the materializer's policy/approval-filtered tools, carry its exclusions into scheduling results, and replace earlier interactive configured-tool bindings with the fresh scheduled snapshot. Unexpected discovery failures and exact-run grant/lifecycle checks still fail closed. Host-issued shell aliases keep their existing executable identity and lifetime checks when provider normalization wraps them.

Thanks @jalehman for the report and the requested bounded-subset behavior.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @jalehman](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/92b42ef6-a8ac-4c05-b647-e509948f96cf)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/68653d35-34c2-412d-95c3-60634ea86479)

## Evidence

- **[Verified real-Gateway proof and inline reproducibility artifact](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160793#issuecomment-5881721192).** Baseline `fb503c9e1f25d8c3877881e55e83d4378eda3676` rejects local continuation creation for unrelated OAuth. Exact head `685ddfc5f86d242c115c96b988975421ad962d2c` passes all 16 cases: bounded save + warning, real shell/file effects, finite aliases, unknown/required selectors, healthy MCP, read-only caller, creator revocation, and unchanged saved ceilings after OAuth plus fresh discovery. Both snapshots use isolated built Gateways and managed Codex 0.158.0. Model/MCP peers are synthetic; Gateway, auth, storage, dispatch and effects are real.
- **341 targeted and sibling tests pass** across 13 files (137 feature-focused tests plus 204 normalizer/host/plugin-lifetime controls). Core and extension production types, relevant agent/plugin/extension test types, changed-file lint/formatting, line-growth and assertion-safety ratchets, and diff checks pass. The current environment budget passes **476/476**, without a budget edit in this PR.
- Full exact-head candidate build passed in Crabbox. Fresh independent autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Current PR is draft; `openclaw/ci-gate` is skipped, not asserted green. Owner/security review remains before merge.

**Proof limit:** post-login ceiling checks explicitly restart only the owned Gateway to force fresh authenticated discovery and verify persistence. This does not claim immediate warm-cache invalidation or live-vendor inference. The saved job’s attempted excluded MCP call is verified against the native unsupported-call response and zero peer tool calls, with a successful authenticated new-job control.

<details>
<summary>Measured test cost and implementation scope</summary>

Canonical `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run <file> --maxWorkers=1`, measured on the final head; wall time includes runner/cache/import overhead. CI seconds are unavailable while the PR is draft.

| Changed test file | Tests | Wall seconds |
|---|---:|---:|
| `cron-tool-creator-cap.test.ts` | 17 | 1.80 |
| `cron-tool.test.ts` | 71 | 13.16 |
| `cron-tool.authority-exclusions.test.ts` | 8 | 24.19 |
| `cron-tool.output-contract.test.ts` | 7 | 28.09 |
| `cron-creator-authority-context.test.ts` | 12 | 13.32 |
| `run-attempt.configured-mcp-authority.test.ts` | 9 | 42.16 |
| `tools.scheduled-projection.test.ts` | 7 | 11.68 |

The attempt-level tests exercise the actual capture composition and stale-binding replacement; the alias suite exercises real normalization and plugin admission, including nested/retired views and replaced executors. Pure name-matching tests would miss those boundaries. Upstream test pruning was preserved during conflict resolution.

Against rebase base `d4be6500114cff6fcbf72f323fc520861a06c6c9`: production **+150/-40 (net +110)**; tests **+422/-50 (net +372)**; docs **+16**. Growth is the returned exclusions, explicit selector validation, fresh finite-MCP capture and admission-preserving alias metadata transfer. The blanket diagnostic rejection, stale interactive-MCP union and duplicate output-schema shape are removed. Existing cap/grant/lifecycle owners remain authoritative; no storage/config/protocol change or budget increase.

</details>

prs.title: fix(ui): keep saved attempts from splitting conversation turns
prs.body:
Related: #156625. Second focused replacement, stacked on #160782. **Draft only; landing remains paused.**

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: interrupted and cancelled attempts can appear after newer answers and split messages that belong to the same conversation turn.

## User Impact

Saved attempts stay in the existing composer queue, clearly separate from runnable inputs. Users can inspect and copy available content, open available attachments, search loaded previews, and browse Earlier/Latest without changing their draft or executing anything. **This slice intentionally has no saved-row Send or Discard actions.**

## Why This Change Was Made

Inactive custody is not a new transcript turn. The existing transcript and queue renderers now present it in the right place, with pane-scoped explicit inspection. Active custody and native outbox recovery retain their existing owners. Forwarded recommendations and embedded content use the shared renderer's read-only mode rather than exposing installation or execution controls.

Search covers loaded previews and current transcript recovery, not a new full-payload index. Inspection reads are display data, not resubmission authority. No Gateway schema, scheduling, permission, or persistence changes are introduced.

## Evidence

- Original chronology/grouping assertions fail before the cutover and pass afterward. A separate stale-run correlation regression fails before the active-custody guard; same-ID and same-run active inputs cannot reappear as saved attempts.
- Dependency integration passed **600 consumer tests** and **212 ordinary rich-content sibling tests**. The admission dependency update passed a 462-case recheck; subsequent profile/source-refresh repairs passed 106 targeted profile/reader cases, the final **22-case inspection suite**, and the real Chromium copy fixture. These runs overlap. Production UI and test types, lint, styles, i18n verification, UI build, and independent P1 review pass.
- Real Chromium against the full source app and a synthetic Gateway verifies explicit loading/error/retry, complete-content copy, managed attachment resolution and sidebar content, preview search, and actual Earlier/Latest clicks on empty results. Inspection makes **no send/abort request or draft/outbox mutation**. Ordinary interactive ClawHub/canvas/MCP behavior remains covered by sibling tests.
- Wrong-source, still-capped, unavailable, stale client/session/agent/viewer, reconnect, source replacement, and closed or aborted inspection reads are rejected. Cosmetic profile changes and fresh display projections of the same accepted input preserve open inspection; reproduced regressions protect both cases. Source replacement and custody-state changes still retire the old read. Read-only, suggestion, and provider-review viewers can inspect without gaining content actions.
- This is controlled browser and owner-boundary proof, not live-provider/channel proof. CI timing is not yet available. The existing startup-CSS advisory remains below its hard ceiling; no budget changed.

<details>
<summary>Measured test cost</summary>

Repository wrapper, one worker, wall seconds for changed files: pending-inputs pagination 8.48; pending-inputs 13.17; system-notice 9.29; input ordering 8.69; live-final 6.38; chat-view 12.93; saved-inputs 3.39; saved-inputs browser 7.24. Import/transform time is included. The 14-file consumer batch took 13.22 seconds; rich-content siblings took 6.15 seconds.

</details>

### After

## What Problem This Solves

## User Impact

Users can recover or discard the complete browser-held message using its existing controls. Active Gateway custody and canonical delivery still take precedence. No automatic resend, new recovery action, persistence change, or queue-policy change is introduced.

The display selector keeps native held/failed recovery ahead of a matching interrupted server copy. Submission admission now checks the complete existing active snapshot as well as the browsed retained page; all callers use that same admission owner. prs.title: fix: prevent pre-reset history from entering plugin context rebuilds
prs.body:
Related: #160613

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the missing host contract that lets context-engine plugins reimport pre-reset history when rebuilding context after a same-identity session reset.

## User Impact

Context-engine plugin authors can obtain canonical reset-eligible message IDs and payloads, then persist their prepared import under host-owned final acceptance. Raw and visible archive/search history remain unchanged; host compaction is not treated as reset eligibility.

Consumers must adopt the new `api.runtime.agent.session.readTranscriptAdmission` / `acceptTranscriptAdmission` methods for bootstrap and rebuild. This is the host-side dependency, not a change to Lossless storage or its summary DAG. The new snapshot contract supports durable SQLite sessions; incognito keeps its existing commit path. No schema migration or SDK subpath is added.

**Callback constraint:** acceptance and durable turn commit hold the agent database writer queue until plugin persistence settles. Prepare expensive work outside the callback; commit briefly to plugin-owned storage only, await every effect, and do not invoke host session mutations or nested acceptance there. This is lifecycle serialization, not a distributed transaction across databases.

**Draft compatibility blocker:** the new default queue hold can deadlock an existing v1 commitTurn callback that awaits a host session write. A versioned opt-in preserving v1 scheduling is proposed and awaits the required protocol decision; this PR is not merge-ready. The proof also observed duplicate current-prompt input on both versions. It was traced to an unchanged provider-loop assembly call that omits the current-turn fence; initial assembly/bootstrap are fenced. This separate pre-existing limitation is documented in the proof comment and is not claimed fixed here.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the canonical branch/reset/tool-group selector and history-worker owner to combine eligible entries with durable transcript/reset identity. One-use, plugin-scoped acceptance rechecks the captured facts under the existing writer queue, closing the read/persist race. Reset, branch/rewrite, session replacement and append invalidate detached work; ordinary reader-cache retirement does not.

Durable outbox replay uses the same acceptance owner. Retired ready turns retain their payload as blocked evidence rather than entering a fresh context. Transient projection unavailability remains pending, not permanently stale. Reset notifications are documented as idempotent current-snapshot reconciliation hints so delayed or duplicate hooks cannot archive a newer consumer conversation.

## Evidence

- Before edits, a real SQLite lifecycle reproduction returned 11 generic visible messages against canonical clear=1 / preserve-tail=7.
- Final focused regression run: **69 tests passed** across snapshot/acceptance, canonical context selection, plugin revocation, outbox replay and host-parameter projection (5 shards, 93.05s).
- `pnpm build`; `pnpm tsgo:core`; all core-test typecheck shards; `pnpm tsgo:extensions:all`; scoped lint; SDK export/surface checks; transcript-reader, session-accessor, SQLite transaction and Kysely guards: passed.
- Public SDK surface remains 158 entrypoints / 4591 exports / 2695 callable exports. Independent autoreview: no actionable P0–P2 findings after repairs.
- **Known inherited gate failure:** `pnpm check:changed` stops at environment-variable budget 477 > 476. The unchanged baseline index at `fb503c9e1f25d8c3877881e55e83d4378eda3676` reproduces the same failure. This change adds no environment variables and does not raise the budget.
- [Real Gateway / external SQLite consumer before-after proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160781#issuecomment-5880568221): clear import 11→1, preserve-tail 11→7, paired tools retained, stale reset/branch/rewrite acceptance refused, delayed old turn blocked, and cold persistence verified on exact head. Inference alone was synthetic. The comment includes sanitized machine-readable evidence, commands, per-file test costs and explicit limits. Signed-only artifact links remain withheld under the requested publication constraint.

- @jalehman

prs.title: fix: session cleanup times out before the Gateway finishes
prs.body:
Related: #170474

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw sessions cleanup` reports a timeout when Gateway maintenance takes longer than ten seconds, even though the cleanup may still complete.

## User Impact

Delegated session cleanup can wait up to two minutes for its result, including cleanup across multiple agent stores. No configuration or migration is required. This does not make maintenance itself faster; a stalled request can now take longer to report a timeout.

## Why This Change Was Made

Give the delegated `sessions.cleanup` call a bounded 120-second deadline, leaving headroom above the roughly 27 seconds reported in the issue. The shared Gateway request default, explicit-store cleanup and local dry runs retain their existing behavior. The regression exercises the command through the real Gateway client and WebSocket protocol, using a controlled clock to return a valid aggregate result after eleven seconds.

## Evidence

- On base `e61083f8f116b50e742a64e219c6a26342e67fcd`, the actual CLI command `pnpm openclaw sessions cleanup --all-agents --json` exited 1 with `gateway timeout after 10000ms`. The isolated protocol peer completed after 11,002 ms with the connection already closed.
- On final commit `4ec9243d374df177139132c8fad22186d2ce642f`, the same shipped CLI exited 0 with the aggregate result after 11,005 ms; the connection remained open until the response arrived. `pnpm build:runtime` passed (4m 27s), with the build stamp matching this commit and clean inputs.
- Focused regression: 1 passed; test body 364 ms. The original real-time wire regression failed on the base with a dispatched-request timeout and passed with the fix.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, targeted oxlint, oxfmt and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Independent review of the final change: no P0-P2 findings; issue timeline and open PRs checked for duplicates.
- The combined run of the new regression and unchanged existing cleanup test file produced 11 passes / 3 failures, due to Windows/POSIX absolute-path expectations and a dry-run table expectation. That run is not a full-suite pass.

The delayed peer is a synthetic, isolated Gateway protocol fixture; it proves the shipped CLI waiting contract, not the throughput or mutations of a large real session database. No external model calls or user data were used.


<details>
<summary>Captured shipped CLI output and protocol trace (redacted)</summary>

Both runs used `pnpm openclaw sessions cleanup --all-agents --json`, the repository's supported shipped CLI entry point, against the same isolated protocol peer. The peer completes exactly one cleanup request after an eleven-second delay. Addresses, local paths, request IDs and connection IDs are omitted. Tokens were never recorded in these logs.

Base: `e61083f8f116b50e742a64e219c6a26342e67fcd`, exit code **1**.

```text
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs "sessions" "cleanup" "--all-agents" "--json"
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "gateway timeout after 10000ms ... [endpoint and config path redacted] ... The request was already sent to the gateway, so the operation may have been applied even though no response arrived; its outcome is unknown."
  }
}
OpenClaw took too long to respond.
Your request may have completed. Check its result before trying again.
[ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code 1.
```

Base protocol events (captured UTC timestamps):

```json
{"time":"2026-10-13T03:15:31.603Z","event":"request","method":"sessions.cleanup","params":{"allAgents":true,"enforce":false,"fixMissing":false,"fixDmScope":false}}
{"time":"2026-10-13T03:15:41.557Z","event":"closed","code":1005}
{"time":"2026-10-13T03:15:42.607Z","event":"cleanup-completed","elapsedMs":11002,"connectionOpen":false,"result":{"allAgents":true,"mode":"warn","dryRun":false,"stores":[]}}
```

Final head: `4ec9243d374df177139132c8fad22186d2ce642f`, exit code **0**.

```text
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs "sessions" "cleanup" "--all-agents" "--json"
{
  "allAgents": true,
  "mode": "warn",
  "dryRun": false,
  "stores": []
}
```

Final-head protocol events:

```json
{"time":"2026-10-13T03:36:32.526Z","event":"request","method":"sessions.cleanup","params":{"allAgents":true,"enforce":false,"fixMissing":false,"fixDmScope":false}}
{"time":"2026-10-13T03:36:43.533Z","event":"cleanup-completed","elapsedMs":11005,"connectionOpen":true,"result":{"allAgents":true,"mode":"warn","dryRun":false,"stores":[]}}
{"time":"2026-10-13T03:36:43.538Z","event":"closed","code":1005}
```

Final runtime build stamp:

```json
{"head":"4ec9243d374df177139132c8fad22186d2ce642f","inputsClean":true}
```

The final response arrived before connection close, and the shipped CLI printed the exact aggregate result. The fixture used real elapsed time; only the committed regression test uses a controlled clock. These runs establish the deadline behavior, not actual store-cleanup performance.

</details>

prs.title: fix: prevent compacted context from expanding after engine recovery
prs.body:
Related: #148569

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes compacted context expanding again on the next turn when a configured context engine recovers after process quarantine.

## User Impact

Queued and standalone context-engine compaction now operate on the configured engine's frontier, just as the next ordinary turn does. An unavailable or failing engine reports compaction failure instead of silently reducing only legacy history. Native-harness-owned compaction and native no-ops remain independent. No configuration or storage-schema migration is required. Existing configurations with an unavailable plugin now report compaction failure rather than legacy success; repair the plugin or explicitly select/disable it in favor of `legacy`. This intentional failure-path change requires maintainer acceptance before merge.

## Why This Change Was Made

The registry now pins fresh compaction selection without changing process quarantine or replaying a started operation through another engine. Pinned instances keep their actual plugin policy owner. Existing source retention, cancellation, watchdog, writer fences, maintenance, and disposal remain authoritative.

Native routes run before allocating an unrelated context engine. The obsolete CLI dual-path compaction guard and native context-engine projection were removed. Process-scoped subagent lifecycle fallback and fresh-turn retry are retained.

## Evidence

- **[Executed real-Gateway before/after proof on the exact final head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160772#issuecomment-5880363335):** baseline `fb503c9e1f25d8c3877881e55e83d4378eda3676` versus candidate `d9e6fedb4cb2a6065bd2576cfa492d83ae7095aa`. Historical messages assembled fall from **14 to 2**; removed history stays absent while current/recent context and the persisted frontier survive. Process quarantine stays unchanged.
- Independent frozen installs/full builds, ordinary CLI/RPC and actual advertised tool dispatch, healthy and failed-compaction/no-replay controls. Inference and the independently persisted plugin are synthetic; Gateway, auth, lifecycle and SQLite worker are real. Exact commands, complete fixtures, run links, hashes and limitations are posted with the proof. All owned Testboxes are stopped.
- **244 tests / 10 files passed**, including queued-to-next-turn regression, selection failures, caller cancellation, retained resources, deferred maintenance and native compaction controls.
- **Full selected changed checks passed** against integrated main `968a08c6d0eee2835f87b034d7dde37660a591cc`: production/test types, source/scripts lint, formatting, dead exports, schema, import cycles and repository guards. Fresh independent P0–P2 autoreview was scoped-clean.
- Actual merge conflicts were limited to upstream #160766 test consolidation. Its deletions are preserved and the fresh-selection assertion moved to the canonical auth-preparation test. The three runtime repair files stayed byte-identical; final-head Gateway proof was nevertheless rerun.
- Runtime code: **+21 net lines**; tests/support: **+301**. Growth provides registry-owned pinned selection and diagnostics; redundant CLI native allocation/projection and its duplicate guard were removed. No new configuration option, public SDK surface or storage schema.

<details>
<summary>Test cost and limits</summary>

New selection controls: 7 tests, 6.57 s single-file wall time. New queued-frontier regression: approximately 1 s test time; 51.16 s cold single-file wall time includes the shared subprocess compiler (about 49 s), not per-test Gateway boot or sleeps. The existing queued/CLI suites retain their shared fixtures. Focused commands use the repository's supported `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <file> --maxWorkers=1` route for this linked worktree. These file-cost measurements predate the test-conflict integration. CI is skipped while this PR remains draft; no hosted CI duration is claimed.

The initial pinned-base aggregate stopped at an inherited environment-name budget mismatch (477/476), reproduced on the unchanged baseline. After the required main integration, the full run passed at 476/476 without increasing that budget.

No operator Gateway, configuration, quarantine, or durable user data was changed. CI remains skipped while draft. Maintainer acceptance and unavailable-plugin upgrade qualification remain pre-merge conditions; this proof does not waive them. No merge or deployment is requested.

</details>

prs.title: fix(agentsapi): ignore saved cron tool lists at harness dispatch
prs.body:
## Why
Agents API cron turns can fail before inference because the saved Gateway tool list does not include the native shell, file, and search tools. Agents API cannot enforce that per-job list across its native tool surface. The fix belongs to its harness, without changing cron behavior for other backends.

## What changed
Agents API declares that its cron attempts use current agent tool policy. Shared harness dispatch consumes that declaration after choosing the actual backend and removes only `toolsAllow` from a copy of that attempt, before policy checks, host capabilities, and tool authority are prepared. Other backends and fallback attempts retain their original parameters.

Current configured restrictions, disabled tools, execution restrictions, and scheduled ownership remain enforced. Agents API still rejects a Gateway-only execution pin that its native shell cannot honor.

There are no changes to the cron service, job creation, stored job data, automation tools, or message grants. Cron continues to capture/store lists normally; Agents API ignores them at harness dispatch. Earlier scheduler checks still apply, so this addresses the reported native preflight failure rather than removing every upstream use of a cron list.

## Validation
- Revised implementation pushed before checks and review, as requested.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, and `git diff HEAD^ HEAD --check`: passed.
- Independent Auto Review of the narrowed implementation: no actionable P0/P1 findings. This is source review, not runtime proof.
- Unit tests, formatters, and live tests were not run, per the requested workflow. No Gateway was changed or restarted.

prs.body:
**Contributor:** Vyctor Brzezowski

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/78cbd373-7500-4ea2-8a32-a670b5cb8ff7)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes losing an unsent draft or changing its saved model when switching between a normal model and a native CLI target.

## User Impact

The same composer, prompt and attachments survive successful switches in both directions. Rejected navigation keeps the previous selection and model preferences. The agent subtitle stays unchanged. Native CLIs still use their own account and configuration; this does not create an OpenClaw chat.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing handoff owner carries the admitted target through navigation, and the model choice commits only after navigation succeeds. Cleanup cancels only its exact prepared entry. Agent, placement and privacy changes stay locked during the short admitted transition, while ordinary host discovery remains cancellable. Cached route data cannot consume the new handoff before its loader receives it.

## Evidence

- Reproduced draft loss on successful CLI selection using the frozen preceding PR; compared the same viewport, prompt and theme with this PR. The textarea remains mounted, and the corrected state keeps both prompt and picker.
- Rejected/stale navigation and abandoned prepared-entry failures were reproduced before repair and pass afterward. A separate regression reproduced an agent change during admitted navigation and now keeps the draft owner stable.
- The full browser flow found a repeat-selection defect: normal → CLI → normal → CLI performed three targeted reads instead of two. A mounted-page regression using the real router and registered loader reproduces the failure and verifies two reads after repair, with edited draft and textarea identity retained.
- Final cached-route repair: 59 page/route/selection tests passed in 5.37 seconds. Mounted-page file: 17 tests, 6.60 seconds wall; new real-router regression approximately 461 ms. Earlier handoff/account/runtime/persistence sibling coverage: 286 tests in 17.86 seconds.
- UI production types, UI-pages test types, scoped lint and formatting passed. Exact cached-route delta independently reviewed scoped-clean through P2. Equivalent admission cases are consolidated at the draft owner rather than duplicated.
- Captures use the actual Control UI with a mocked Gateway. The registered E2E runner remains blocked by loopback HTTP 502 preflight; no live Claude launch is claimed.
- Verification isolated only the known PR160210 duplicate-export build prerequisite and restored it byte-for-byte. No prerequisite change is included.

### Visual proof

Before: the preceding admission-only PR after an available native selection. After: this PR retains the prompt and shared picker. Destination presentation remains the next stacked PR.

prs.title: fix(doctor): update status keeps missing-transcript warnings after sessions cleanup removed the rows
prs.body:
Closes #160561

Related: #156551, #106551, #134765, #111168

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw update status` shows `transcript_missing` migration warnings forever, even after `openclaw sessions cleanup --fix-missing` has removed the session rows that referenced the missing transcripts.

## User Impact

User impact: once operators prune dangling sessions with the supported cleanup command, those stale warnings stop appearing. Every other migration warning, including a `transcript_missing` warning whose row still exists, stays visible. Manifests, rollback coverage and raw reports are unchanged. No migration or configuration change is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Warnings from completed session SQLite migrations are read back from their manifests, which is intentional: they are durable reports and rollback coverage.
- For `transcript_missing` only, the reader now checks the target's live store, read-only, and omits the warning when that exact normalized, agent-owned session key has no row left. There's nothing left to repair: the transcript was already missing when the migration ran, and the operator has removed the row.
- The check is conservative. Main-alias, bare and non-normalized keys (which canonical-key repair may have renamed) keep their warning. So does any store that is missing, corrupt, locked or without a schema.
- This follows the constraint in #156551. No archive reference or original is retired, and nothing is written.
- Only the one-shot `update status` CLI calls this reader, so the synchronous read does not run on a Gateway thread.

## Evidence

**Real host (Raspberry Pi 5, OpenClaw 2026.9.6),** with this change back-ported to the installed build:

- The migration completed 2026-09-11 and recorded 4 `transcript_missing` issues for one agent.
- After `openclaw sessions cleanup --agent <id> --fix-missing` (31 → 23 rows), `openclaw doctor --session-sqlite inspect` reported 0 issues and `integrityCheck: ok`.
- `openclaw update status --json` `migrationWarnings`: **4 before, 0 after**, with no `migrationWarningsError`.
- The manifest's SHA-256 was unchanged before and after.

**Tests:**
- The new `src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite-warnings.test.ts` covers:
  - a pruned row hidden and a surviving row shown;
  - an unreadable store shown;
  - main-alias and non-normalized keys shown;
  - mixed-case live keys;
  - other codes unaffected;
  - the manifest byte-for-byte unchanged.
- The new tests fail on `main` and pass with the fix. A mutation check confirmed that the case-sensitivity and main-alias guards are covered.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` on the new file, `status.recovery.test.ts` and `doctor-session-transcripts.sqlite.test.ts`: 43/43 passed.

**Static checks:**
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs` for the changed paths: 26/26 passed.
- `run-oxlint.mjs` on the changed files: 0 warnings. `lint:kysely`, `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check`: clean.

**Known gap:** `pnpm check:changed` stops at the env-var budget check, which is already over budget on `origin/main` (6b9da9dc028). This change adds no env vars.


## Data-model compatibility

The change is read-only and does not change the stored data model.

- **No schema or storage change.** It adds no table, column, index, migration, backfill or repair step.
- **No writes.** The reader opens the agent store only through `withOpenClawAgentDatabaseReadOnly` and runs one `SELECT session_key FROM session_nodes`. Migration manifests are only read.
- **Manifests are untouched.** The new test asserts the manifest is byte-for-byte unchanged, and the real-host run above recorded the same SHA-256 before and after.
- **Old and new data both work.** The filter applies only to `transcript_missing` issues in manifests that `update status` already reads. It works on manifests written by earlier releases. If a store is missing, unreadable, locked, corrupt or has no schema, the reader falls back to today's output and shows the warning.
- **Upgrade and downgrade.** Nothing needs migrating either way. An older build reading the same manifests shows the warnings exactly as `main` does now.

Retention, permissions and update behavior are otherwise unchanged. The file sits under `doctor-session-sqlite-*`, but this change only touches how warnings are presented.

prs.title: fix(sandbox): sandbox image builds fail on transient apt download errors
prs.body:
Closes #52665

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `scripts/sandbox-setup.sh`, `scripts/sandbox-common-setup.sh`, and `scripts/sandbox-browser-setup.sh` fail when a Debian mirror briefly returns errors or drops connections while apt downloads package lists or packages.

## User Impact

User impact: sandbox image builds now recover from short mirror or network hiccups instead of failing, and they still fail loudly when a required package cannot be installed. No image contract, package list, or cache mount changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the retry-only replacement requested in #85833: no `--fix-missing`, so required packages are never silently skipped.

- `apt-get update` exits 0 even when every index fetch fails (warnings only). The build then fails later with a misleading `Unable to locate package`, or quietly installs from stale lists left in the apt cache mount. `--error-on=any` makes index fetch failures fail the update step.
- The update step runs in the same bounded 3-attempt loop already used by `scripts/docker/install-sh-smoke/Dockerfile`, and still exits 1 after the last attempt.
- `-o Acquire::Retries=5` on update and install raises per-file retries above bookworm apt's default of 3, with apt's built-in backoff. Install is not looped, so a truly missing package fails immediately.
- Applied to the base, common, and browser sandbox Dockerfiles. The common image's Node step also gets `|| exit 1` on its apt installs.
- `src/docker-build-cache.test.ts` asserts the retry flags, the bounded loop, and the absence of `--fix-missing` for all three sandbox Dockerfiles.

## Evidence

Local Docker 29.8.1 (BuildKit) on linux/amd64, Debian bookworm-slim base pinned by the repo.

**Full default builds, package presence**

`scripts/sandbox-common-setup.sh` (which also builds the base image) and `scripts/sandbox-browser-setup.sh` both succeeded.

<details><summary>dpkg-query output</summary>

    build-essential	12.9
    ca-certificates	20250419~deb12u1
    cargo	0.66.0+ds1-1
    coreutils	9.1-1
    curl	7.88.1-10+deb12u15
    file	1:5.44-3
    git	1:2.39.5-0+deb12u3
    golang-go:amd64	2:1.19~1
    grep	3.8-5
    jq	1.6-2.1+deb12u2
    libasound2-dev:amd64	1.2.8-1+b1
    nodejs	24.21.0-1nodesource1
    pkg-config:amd64	1.8.1-1

    rustc	1.63.0+dfsg1-2

    wget	1.21.3-1+deb12u1
    (node v24.21.0, pnpm 12.5.0, bun 1.4.2, Homebrew present; final user: sandbox)

    $ docker run --rm openclaw-sandbox-browser:bookworm-slim dpkg-query -W bash ca-certificates chromium curl fonts-liberation fonts-noto-cjk fonts-noto-color-emoji git jq novnc python3 websockify x11vnc xvfb
    (all 14 present, chromium 154.0.8037.57-1~deb12u1)

</details>

**Still fails when a package is absent**

`PACKAGES="jq openclaw-nonexistent-package"` fails in about 2.6 s and produces no image:

    E: Unable to locate package openclaw-nonexistent-package
    ERROR: process "/bin/sh -c set -eu; for attempt in 1 2 3; do ... apt-get -o Acquire::Retries=5 install -y --no-install-recommends ${PACKAGES}" did not complete successfully: exit code: 100

**Simulated transient failures**

A local HTTP proxy returned 503 for the first N requests per URL (`docker build --network host --build-arg http_proxy=...`, `PACKAGES=tree`, apt cache mounts pruned before each run). Upstream = `Dockerfile.common` from current main.

| Injected failure | upstream main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 7× 503 on each `InRelease` | exit 1: `W: Some index files failed to download...` then `E: Unable to locate package tree` | exit 0: apt tries each index 6 times, then `apt-get update failed (attempt 1)`, second pass succeeds, `Setting up tree` |
| 4× 503 on the `.deb` | exit 1: `E: Unable to fetch some archives, maybe run apt-get update or try with --fix-missing?` | exit 0: `Get:1 ... tree 2.1.0-1`, `Setting up tree` |
| 100× 503 on the `.deb` (outage) | n/a | exit 1: `E: Failed to fetch ... 503`, no image produced (fail-closed) |

With warm apt list caches, upstream also exited 0 after every index fetch failed, installing from stale cached lists. This PR fails and retries in that case too.

**Tests**

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/docker-build-cache.test.ts`: 8/8 passed. The new assertions fail against the current upstream Dockerfiles.
- `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` are clean on the touched files.
- `pnpm check` passes except two unrelated ratchets that compared against a stale fork `origin/main`. Both pass with `--base upstream/main`.

**Known gap:** the NodeSource setup script runs its own internal `apt-get update`, which this change does not wrap.
