prs.title: fix(browser): keep remote tabs usable when health checks time out
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A named tab in an externally managed CDP browser can become unusable when a short health probe times out, even though tab enumeration and the browser session still work. This includes network CDP profiles and documented `attachOnly` CDP endpoints on loopback.

## User Impact

For a named tab on an externally managed CDP profile, OpenClaw resolves the tab before using reachability as an error diagnostic. A missing tab still reports "tab not found". The first enumeration uses a handshake-scale budget (at most 5 seconds, subject to the configured handshake minimum); a recovery enumeration retains the full action-level budget. A slow healthy browser can recover while an unavailable one consumes at most one full action-timeout enumeration. A stopped local *managed* browser retains its historical-target "not running" behavior. Lookup does not launch or replace a browser.

## Evidence

- Before fix: on OpenClaw 2026.9.6, a remote tab list showed the live tab while a subsequent snapshot returned "profile is not running". In 30 CDP probes, 3 exceeded the short health budget.
- Production-context regressions cover a present named remote tab with a failed health probe, a missing tab, first-failure/second-success recovery with the full second budget, and an unavailable remote profile with only one full-budget enumeration. A new regression covers an `attachOnly` loopback CDP tab with a failed health probe. The historical-target suite confirms a stopped managed browser is not launched and still reports "not running".
- Focused tests on this head: **44/44 passed** across remote Playwright, CDP fallback/attach-only, and historical-target suites in 6.06 s. The changed fallback suite alone: **14/14 passed in 2.66 s** (`pnpm exec vitest run extensions/browser/src/browser/server-context.remote-profile-tab-ops.fallback.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=dot`). `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint` (0 warnings/errors), and `git diff --check` passed. The local host lacks `tsgo`; exact-head CI supplies typecheck coverage.
- **Real-browser boundary proof on predecessor head `6d577728`:** An isolated Chromium with Debian libraries extracted into `/tmp` (no host package installation) was exercised through `createBrowserRouteContext` with a CDP profile classified as remote. A real page was enumerated, named-tab resolution and `focusTab` succeeded with the short health probe forced false and never called. An unavailable CDP port produced `BrowserProfileUnavailableError`. No tab IDs, page URLs, credentials, or private endpoints were printed. The current head leaves this non-loopback action path unchanged and adds the attached-loopback classification; that new path has production-context regression proof but not a separate real-browser trace.

  ```text
  LIVE_CDP_TRACE remoteProfile=true realPage=true healthProbeForcedFalse=true healthProbeCalls=0 namedTabResolved=true focusTab=pass elapsedMs=7
  LIVE_CDP_TRACE unavailableProfileError=true firstBudgetMs=5000 recoveryBudgetMs=5000 elapsedMs=3022
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  2 passed (2)
  Duration  6.00s
  ```
- A separate direct-source attempt against the configured production relay timed out during enumeration, although the installed Gateway could enumerate tabs; that attempt is **not** positive production-relay proof. The live Chromium proof was a one-off local test, not added to per-PR CI. The isolated browser and task-owned scratch were stopped and removed afterward.
- Local independent autoreview was attempted: Codex is not installed; Claude returned a 429 weekly-quota error before reviewing. Neither attempt produced a verdict. ClawSweeper's exact-head review found **no actionable code findings** and accepted the real-browser proof, but requests the browser maintainer's decision on the latency tradeoff below.
- Exact-head CI is **red because one job was canceled at the workflow's 20-minute limit**, not because a test assertion failed: `check-additional-extension-package-boundary` ran from 20:17:20 to 20:37:37 UTC. Its log completed all 125/125 plugin compilations and then ended with `The operation was canceled`; the aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` consequently failed. All other selected jobs passed or were skipped. The workflow fixes `check-additional-shard` at `timeout-minutes: 20`. No rerun or branch refresh was used to manufacture green CI; this gate needs maintainer CI-budget handling.

## Maintainer decision

A disconnected external CDP profile can take one handshake-scale first attempt plus one full action timeout (60 seconds by default) to report unavailable. The full recovery budget is intentional: shortening it would again reject a slow but healthy browser. **Recommendation:** accept this bounded delay in favor of correct tab recovery, or specify a different product latency budget. No configuration migration or user action is required. This does not repair genuinely expired or disconnected CDP sessions.

prs.title: fix(auto-reply): channel messages vanish from session history when required preflight compaction fails
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/86592

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a channel message (Telegram, Discord, and other channels on the reply pipeline) disappears from the session history when required preflight compaction fails before the agent starts.

## User Impact

User impact: after a "Context is too large and auto-compaction could not recover this turn" reply, the message that triggered it stays in the conversation, so the next turn (and restart recovery, history replay, and later compaction) still sees what the user asked. Nothing changes for turns that succeed.

## Why This Change Was Made

On the direct reply path, required preflight compaction runs before the user turn is admitted to the transcript. When compaction throws, the runner returns the failure reply and the user turn is never written. The Gateway `chat.send` handler already covers this case at its own boundary (it persists the user turn when the run returns an error), but channel inbound has no such fallback.

The fix sits at the reply runner, where admission is owned. When preflight compaction fails with the error that produces the "Context is too large" reply, the runner writes only the user-turn transcript entry through the turn's existing recorder, guarded by the current session id, and rethrows the original error. The run's live authority (abort signal, the admitted operator authority, and the run lifecycle generation) is revalidated inside that guarded write, after message resolution and the queued SQLite write have been awaited and immediately before the fresh insert, following the AGENTS.md rule to revalidate authority right before side effects. It uses the transcript append's existing synchronous `beforeFreshMessageCommit` hook, which the recorder's `persistApproved()` now accepts next to `expectedSessionId`, so no await runs inside the write transaction. Any other preflight error, or authority revoked at any point before the insert, writes nothing. It does not take a restart-recovery claim, so a failed turn is not resumed after a restart, and the write is idempotent by the source turn key. This follows the direction in the issue's ClawSweeper review (keep the accepted user turn durable at its owning boundary while preserving session and duplicate checks), but keeps the current order of preflight before admission instead of admitting early, which the review noted is unsafe across session rotation.

Scope is the direct reply path that reproduces. The Gateway `agent` method keeps a preflight-failed input as an interrupted pending input, which `docs/concepts/session-tool.md` documents, so it is unchanged. The permanent "no real conversation messages" wedge from the original report did not reproduce on current main (the next turn compacts and runs), and the queued-followup path and direct ACP are not changed here.

## Evidence

Tested at `e8f5b2cc4ac` (base `upstream/main` `733ceac1a7e`). The channel before/after below was captured at `b5fe749d25e` and the Telegram authority runs at `1cce3cc6ab3`; the later commits only narrow when the write happens. `e8f5b2cc4ac` moves the authority check from before `persistApproved()` into the guarded append; the regression below covers that interval directly.

A Gateway built from each tree (with the QA channel) ran with isolated state on loopback. Inbound messages came through the bundled QA channel plugin from a small synthetic channel bus, so they take the channel reply path. The model was a local OpenAI-compatible mock behind a proxy that reports token usage and returns HTTP 500 while a flag is set. TURN-ONE and TURN-TWO succeed; with the flag set, TURN-THREE needs required preflight compaction, whose summarization gets HTTP 500; the flag is cleared and TURN-FOUR follows. History comes from `chat.history` over Gateway RPC; the last block checks the mock's request log for which user turns the model saw on TURN-FOUR.

Before (base `733ceac1a7e`):

```text
== channel conversation (synthetic bus)
inbound m1 "TURN-ONE hello"
outbound m2 "This…"  (streamed reply; the bus logs the first chunk)
inbound m4 "TURN-TWO background filler0 filler1 filler2 filler3 filler4 "
outbound m5 "This…"  (streamed reply; the bus logs the first chunk)
inbound m7 "TURN-THREE please answer this filler0 filler1 filler2 filler"
outbound m8 "⚠️ Context is too large and auto-compaction could not recover this turn. Try again, use /compact, or use /new to start a fresh session."
inbound m9 "TURN-FOUR did you get my previous message?"
outbound m10 "This…"  (streamed reply; the bus logs the first chunk)
== gateway log (preflight)
[compaction] Full summarization failed: Turn prefix summarization failed: 500 injected failure
== transcript user turns
session totalTokens=76562 contextTokens=128000
sessionKey=agent:main:main
user      TURN-ONE
assistant This is a mock assistant reply with some selectable text for the repro
user      TURN-TWO
```

prs.title: fix(gateway): service startup refusal recommends an override it ignores after a downgrade
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/152791

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after a downgrade, the managed Gateway service refuses to start and tells the operator to set `OPENCLAW_ALLOW_OLDER_BINARY_DESTRUCTIVE_ACTIONS=1`, but service-mode startup deliberately ignores that variable, so following the instruction changes nothing (reported in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/152791).

## User Impact

User impact: an operator whose older OpenClaw binary is refused by the service now sees the supported recovery path (restore a verified pre-update backup with its matching release, with a link to the downgrade guide) and a plain statement that the override does not apply to gateway service startup, instead of a workaround that cannot work.

The startup guard itself is unchanged: service-mode startup still refuses (exit 78) an older binary against config written by a newer one, with or without the variable.

## Why This Change Was Made

The issue carries a maintainer-decision question: correct the misleading service-mode instruction while keeping the guard, or let the override admit an older Gateway against newer-written state. This PR takes the first choice only, which is the review bot's recommendation on the issue and matches the existing contract:

- The CLI tests already require service-mode startup to refuse and revoke the override even when it is set.
- The troubleshooting guide (https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/troubleshooting/updates-and-rollbacks) says not to override the guard to run older code against migrated state, and points intentional downgrades to https://docs.openclaw.ai/install/updating/rollback-and-recovery#downgrade.

It deliberately does not make the override admit an older Gateway in service mode; that would need a defined config and database downgrade contract from maintainers.

The linked issue is intentionally left open by this PR. It stays open for the maintainer decision on whether an older Gateway should ever be allowed to start in service mode against newer-written state; this PR only fixes the misleading instruction and is useful under either outcome.

Implementation: `resolveFutureConfigActionBlock` gains an `allowOverride` option. When a caller refuses the override, the guard ignores the variable and the refusal carries the downgrade hint instead of recommending it. The Gateway startup guard passes `allowOverride: false` in service mode, replacing its previous approach of deleting the variable from a cloned environment, so the decision to ignore the override and the message about it come from one place. Foreground `gateway run`, `gateway --force` and daemon lifecycle commands keep honoring the override and keep the existing hint.

## Evidence

Tested at `a2eb1cf6aba` (base `upstream/main` `988be486074`).

Built CLI in an isolated profile and HOME with a scrubbed environment. The config is stamped `meta.lastTouchedVersion: 2026.9.99` while the binary is 2026.9.6; the service marker is set the way the managed service unit sets it. Before ran on a built `upstream/main` `c136ec63146`; the guard files are identical between that commit and the branch base.

Command on both sides:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_SERVICE_MARKER=openclaw OPENCLAW_ALLOW_OLDER_BINARY_DESTRUCTIVE_ACTIONS=1 openclaw gateway run --port 41811
```

Before (base `c136ec63146`):

```text
Refusing to start the gateway service because this OpenClaw binary (2026.9.6) is older than the config last written by OpenClaw 2026.9.99.
Run the newer openclaw binary on PATH, or reinstall the intended gateway service from the newer install.
Set OPENCLAW_ALLOW_OLDER_BINARY_DESTRUCTIVE_ACTIONS=1 only for an intentional downgrade or recovery action.
exit=78
```

After (this PR):

```text
Refusing to start the gateway service because this OpenClaw binary (2026.9.6) is older than the config last written by OpenClaw 2026.9.99.
Run the newer openclaw binary on PATH, or reinstall the intended gateway service from the newer install.
For an intentional downgrade, restore a verified pre-update backup with its matching OpenClaw release: https://docs.openclaw.ai/install/updating/rollback-and-recovery#downgrade
OPENCLAW_ALLOW_OLDER_BINARY_DESTRUCTIVE_ACTIONS does not apply to gateway service startup.
exit=78
```

Control on this PR (foreground, no service marker): without the variable the refusal still recommends it (exit 1); with it the Gateway starts and `/healthz` returns 200, so the foreground override is unchanged.

Observed result: service-mode startup is still refused with exit 78, and the refusal no longer recommends the ignored variable.

Full captures: [before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20260928-issue-152791/before.txt), [after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20260928-issue-152791/after.txt), [control](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20260928-issue-152791/control.txt).

Not covered: a real systemd or launchd unit was not installed; service mode was entered through the same service marker the unit sets. The downgrade recovery itself (backup restore) is not exercised; only the guidance changed.

Tests:

- `src/config/future-version-guard.test.ts`: new case, a caller that disallows the override is refused even with the variable set, and the refusal does not recommend it. Fails on the base.
- `src/cli/gateway-cli/pre-bootstrap.process.test.ts`: the existing "future service-mode backup" child-process case now also asserts the refusal text. Fails on the base; no new test case or process boot.
- Also passed: `src/cli/run-main.exit.test.ts`, `src/cli/gateway-cli/run.option-collisions.test.ts`, `src/cli/daemon-cli/lifecycle-core.config-guard.test.ts` (337 tests across the five files), `oxfmt --check`, and `pnpm check:changed` (typecheck, lint, dead-code and guard lanes).
- Ran the `autoreview` skill on the branch: no findings.

| Test file | `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` wall | CI seconds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/config/future-version-guard.test.ts` | 2.2 s (whole file) | under 0.1 s for all 5 tests, new case 0 ms ([job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36418809499/job/108916892062)) |
| `src/cli/gateway-cli/pre-bootstrap.process.test.ts` | 84.5 s (whole file, unchanged by this PR: two added assertions in an existing case) | 94.5 s for the file, changed case 2.1 s ([job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36418809499/job/108916892118)) |

CI failures on this head (run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36418809499), unrelated to this change:

- `checks-node-changed-1`: `src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry.requester-wake.e2e.test.ts` timed out waiting for delivered subagent cleanup.
- `checks-node-changed-compact-large-15`: `src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.test.ts` (Gmail hot reload SecretRef case) hit the 120 s test timeout.
- `checks-node-changed-compact-large-24-1`: `src/gateway/server.chat.gateway-server-chat.test.ts` got agent run status `timeout` instead of `ok`.
- `checks-node-changed-compact-large-33`: `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.isolated-session-mirror.test.ts` hit a promise timeout.
- `openclaw/ci-gate`: aggregates the four jobs above.

All four are timeouts in subagent, Gateway chat, reload and heartbeat code that this diff does not touch; the only behavior change applies when a caller passes `allowOverride: false`, which only the service-mode startup guard does. The three non-E2E files pass on this branch locally (257 tests). The E2E file could not be run locally because its setup needs a runtime artifact publication step that the local host refuses. I found no earlier failure of these four tests in recent scheduled `main` runs, so I cannot link one; they read as timing flakes on this run.

prs.title: fix(ui): reconcile System theme on foreground restore
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

With **System** appearance selected, returning to a backgrounded Control UI can leave the page showing the opposite color scheme until another media-query event arrives. The theme owner currently accepts background observations but does not reconcile appearance when the document becomes visible or returns from the back-forward cache.

This remains reproducible after rebasing onto `162dea17b03112d48c0f5c6f4b73f0da7a025233`, using a controlled root-document lifecycle sequence.

## User Impact

System appearance is reconciled immediately on foreground restoration, without waiting for a Gateway reconnect or a preference change. Temporary background observations no longer replace its last admitted mode. Explicit Light/Dark choices remain independent.

**Limit:** this verifies a reproducible lifecycle defect, not elimination of every physical iOS 26 Home Screen flash. A transient observed while still visible can still be displayed; restoration uses the browser's fresh value rather than a debounce or a guessed settling delay.

**Unverified first-frame risk:** a genuine OS appearance change while the page is hidden is deferred until foreground reconciliation. If the browser presents the old page or a saved snapshot before that handler updates presentation, a visible old-to-new transition can still occur. If reconciliation happens before the first visible paint, it need not flash. The current tests verify DOM state after the handler, not the first restored frame. The blanket hidden-state freeze therefore needs real-device evaluation; this is not a demonstrated fix for the original iOS flash.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep one System-mode snapshot in the existing theme owner, shared by presentation and resolved-mode consumers. Refresh it while visible and reconcile it on visible `visibilitychange` / persisted `pageshow`. Palette completion and preference/catalog publications use the same snapshot.

Preserves catalog single-mode precedence, palette generation fences, legacy media-query listener cleanup, and the recent navigation-only preference optimization. No timers, user-agent branches, persistence changes, or Gateway changes.

Production delta: **+30 net lines** for the owner-held observation and lifecycle registration/cleanup; regression tests are separate. The previous independent presentation/getter sampling is removed rather than adding a second theme manager.

## Evidence

- Rebased baseline: **10 failing / 4 passing** in the new 14-case owner regression; the same tests all pass with the fix.
- Focused suite: **53 passing tests** across System lifecycle, presentation/navigation, theme resolution, and catalog behavior.
- Baseline and fixed Control UI production builds pass.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`: passes formatting, lint, UI production and selected test typechecks, i18n and repository guards.
- New-test cost: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/app/bootstrap-theme.system.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **1.86 s wrapper wall**, 1.08 s Vitest duration, 14 passing cases. No timers, sleeps, polling, or per-test Gateway boots. CI timing is not yet available.
- Actual built UI in **WebKit 26.6**, mobile 390×844: visible Dark → delivered Light → hidden → raw Dark without delivery → visible. Baseline remains Light; fixed UI is Dark synchronously, before another task or media event. Screenshots use synthetic chat content, not private phone logs.
- AutoReview, local candidate against the pinned base, P0–P2: **scoped-clean**.

### Controlled WebKit reproduction

Both captures are immediately after foreground return, with **System selected and a Dark root query**. This is the actual built UI with synthetic chat content and controlled lifecycle inputs—not physical iOS suspension.

| Before: stale Light | After: reconciled Dark |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before — System retains stale Light after foreground return](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/489c50f5-edd4-42b2-ab7e-9e15be6f790c) | ![After — System restores Dark on foreground return](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bcee9c35-72c2-45c6-9207-9f615ef5e7b8) |

Thanks to @hxy91819 (Mason) for reporting the problem and providing reproduction observations.

prs.title: fix(sessions): retain trusted parent scope for spawned children
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes scope-aware plugin access being rejected in spawned child sessions because the host loses the authorized parent's exact identity and trusted requester provenance.

## User Impact

Plugins can validate delegated parent scope without mistaking a child's synthetic launch authority for owner access. False or missing owner status remains fail-closed, and resetting a child preserves its original grant rather than granting access to a new parent generation.

This PR contains only the host-side fix. Plugin-specific scope resolution and native runtime child-tool bridges are outside its scope. There is no configuration or database migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Capture trusted owner status, parent session ID, and parent lifecycle revision at hidden and visible spawn creation; revalidate parent identity before hidden-child commit; carry the trusted flag through direct and signed Gateway creation; reserve the host-owned fields against plugin slot writes; preserve them across reset and rollover.

The patch is ported onto main's newer worker-backed/physical-store spawn preparation. Small behavior-preserving extractions of the visible-spawn schema, rollover policy/test group, and parent-row construction/selection keep existing oversized files within the repository's no-growth line-cap gates. No tests were removed and no limits were suppressed.

## Evidence

- **Red on main:** three recursive-spawn production-boundary cases fail on `6e0e17d27e54304256280295881fde4868aaf3ce` because child rows lack `parentSessionId` and `spawnedBySenderIsOwner`. For this comparison, production files were restored to main and the fixture used main's existing tool-construction contract (without the newly propagated expected-parent ID).
- **Still needed:** re-fetched main at `a08f2aa4ed7d3bbc8e60e334433af45e928de1c8`; none of the touched source files changed and the authority fields remain absent.
- **Green with fix:** 193 tests across eight files, including all 21 recursive production-boundary cases, plus 16 reply-rollover cases (207 unrelated cases filtered). The production cases cover owner true/false/absent and spoofed model arguments; creation coverage rejects replaced parents and same-ID lifecycle rotation. Gateway creation covers in-process, signed, public/spoofed, revoked, and mismatched callers.
- Core typecheck and all core-test typecheck shards passed. Changed-file oxlint, formatting, line-cap/max-lines/assertion ratchets, docs MDX sanity, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh independent autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 issue. Final tests ran against immutable source and passed the test runner's source-integrity checks.
- No full repository build or full test suite was run; verification was scoped to the changed contract. No running Gateway was rebuilt or restarted. CI results are pending.

### Measured test cost

Node 24.19, one Vitest worker. The eight-file run took **111.91 s wall** including worker compilation and **111.70 s** in the repository test runner; the separate `session.test.ts -t rollover` run took **43.84 s wall** (16 cases, 22.51 s Vitest duration). Commands used `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/test-projects.mts <files> --maxWorkers=1`, the direct implementation of `pnpm test`, to avoid package-manager lockfile rewrites during compiled-worker validation.

Per-file summed testcase durations from the eight-file run (not per-file process startup time):

| Test file | Passed | Testcase time |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `gateway/agent-runtime-identity-token.test.ts` | 28 | 2.54 s |
| `gateway/server.sessions.create.resolved-model.test.ts` | 11 | 10.29 s |
| `gateway/server.sessions.reset-cleanup.test.ts` | 22 | 8.38 s |
| `agents/subagents/spawn/subagent-spawn-session-patch.test.ts` | 4 | 2.31 s |
| `auto-reply/reply/get-reply.fast-path.test.ts` | 25 | 3.21 s |
| `agents/openclaw-tools.registration.test.ts` | 55 | 10.00 s |
| `agents/tools/in-process-gateway.test.ts` | 27 | 0.07 s |
| `agents/subagents/spawn/subagent-spawn.production-boundary.test.ts` | 21 | 22.84 s |

The existing Gateway/production suites exercise real creation, token transport, lifecycle, and cleanup composition that a helper-only test cannot prove. This patch adds no per-test Gateway boots or real timer waits. CI wall seconds will be available in the check runs.

prs.title: improve: stop repeating warnings before external content
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

External tool results repeat the same warning paragraph before already source-tagged, fenced content.

## User Impact

New external-content results start with the existing boundary envelope instead of repeated warning prose. Source labels, randomized markers, sanitization, tool policy, and approval enforcement remain intact. Existing transcripts are not rewritten, and no configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the paragraph at its producer—not in the UI—and delete the obsolete warning selection and budget branches across bundled callers. The shipped Plugin SDK `includeWarning` argument remains an ignored, deprecated boolean for source compatibility until the next major; internal callers no longer pass it. Attachment guidance now owns its explicit newline before the content envelope.

### Intentional output change and security tradeoff

This implements Peter's explicit request in the linked original discussion to remove the repeated paragraph from model-facing external content and land the change, not merely hide it in the UI. Full producer removal is intentional; retaining the paragraph behind the legacy SDK option would retain the removed output path.

For external plugin authors, this is an intentional **output-behavior change**: setting the released includeWarning option to true no longer prepends a paragraph. The deprecated field preserves TypeScript source compatibility only, not warning-bearing output. The upgrade path is to remove that option and consume the existing marker/source envelope; this is now documented in the prompt-injection guide. No new toggle is introduced.

Removing that natural-language cue is the requested product tradeoff. Marker/sanitizer regressions prove structural framing and sanitization, **not equivalent model-level injection resistance**; that effect remains unmeasured. Source metadata, randomized boundaries, special-token/forged-marker sanitization, tool policy, sandboxing, and approval enforcement remain unchanged. We do not treat the removed paragraph, or the remaining markers, as authorization enforcement.

The stale channel-context comment and adjacent threat-model descriptions were corrected in the documentation-only follow-up. The review's explicit-opt-in suggestion is intentionally not adopted for the full-removal scope above; no adversarial model evaluation is claimed.

## Evidence

- On base `bf939715e3775e5ca9f7bf38fa5a7e103d2afbb1`, the direct `web_fetch` result and spill-file regressions failed because the warning preceded the marker. Both pass after the change.
- 621 focused tests pass: 308 local tests across the sanitizer, fetch, attachment/PDF, network-error, and tool-loop consumers, plus 313 Browser/Firecrawl/Tavily tests on Blacksmith Testbox. Existing forged-marker and model-special-token cases remain covered.
- A real loopback HTTP fetch through `createWebFetchTool().execute` returned marker-first short and truncated results (203 and 698 characters under an 800-character budget), sanitized forged markers and model tokens, and produced a verified marker-first spill file. This is tool-boundary proof, not a live-model injection-resistance evaluation.
- Lead verification additionally caught the existing large-fetch test still requiring warning prose. Its old assertion failed (30 passed, 1 failed); it now requires marker-first output, with all 31 cases passing via node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/web-tools.fetch.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 (2.08 s wrapper wall time, 1.19 s Vitest). This brings focused coverage to 652 passing tests; production code is unchanged from the reviewed implementation.
- Lead personally checked the sibling Codex source at e766f7598993ce37cf61b9c26c80cc2ba3a4f2d7: codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/dynamic.rs:113-161 and codex-rs/protocol/src/models.rs:1658-1673,1940-2048. Tool-output text remains function-call output; its role does not depend on the removed prose. No claim of measured model-level injection-resistance equivalence.
- Independent autoreview accepted the producer removal. Its final pass identified the stale index copy of the attachment separator repair; the already-reviewed working-tree fix is now committed.
- Core, extension, and extension-test typechecks pass remotely; focused `agents-tools` and `other` test-project typechecks pass locally. Changed-file typed lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.

- Landing CI found an additional stale fixture: the imported-history test used the live producer to create a historical warning-bearing message, so the fixture stopped containing a warning. The [failed CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36402403387/job/108863852901) and local reproduction both showed 31 passing / 1 failing case. The fixture now supplies the historical paragraph explicitly, retaining the assertion that stored history is not rewritten. No UI or production code changed. Imported-history plus source-preview sibling tests pass (56 tests; wrapper 2.69 s, Vitest 1.89 s), bringing combined focused coverage to 708; targeted typed lint and formatting pass.

### CI follow-up

The refreshed head incorporates the actual inherited-fixture repairs instead of rerunning the old failures unchanged:

- The shared ACP dispatch mock fix is already on main in ea6bf83e821f4808e081f8ff1ffa30b34414edd7.
- Canonical skill-source and dispatcher-routing fixture repairs are already on main in [#160349](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160349). The superseded standalone skill reproduction was stopped during artifact preparation; it did not execute the test and is not counted as proof.
- The remaining ACP command mock correction is the reviewed one-file prerequisite [#160365](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160365), included as an ancestor of this refreshed head. Its direct main push was refused by branch protection; it follows the required PR route. Its final command suite passed all 73 existing tests.
- All five warning-removal commits are patch-identical after the base refresh (git range-diff). No warning prose was restored and no runtime safeguard was changed to accommodate CI.

The original model-catalog failure remains explicitly unqualified: one 60-second fixture timeout was followed by an empty-config diagnostic and a catalog-not-ready error in the next case. No causal path from warning removal has been identified, but this is not called a harmless flake or a proven repair. A bounded replay of the original scheduling inputs is being collected independently. Current-head GitHub gates remain mandatory.

**Validation gap:** the broader remote `check:changed` stopped at the pre-existing `ui-other` test-root budget (721 roots versus 720), before typechecking. This PR adds no test files and does not change the guard, shard definitions, tsconfigs, lockfile, or UI inventory. Scoped types and plugin tests passed separately. The remote batch also rejected an unsupported test-shard selector; the two intended canonical project typechecks were then run successfully with the corrected wrapper command.

<details>
<summary>Measured test cost</summary>

`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` wall time with prepared dependencies:

| File | Tests | Wall time |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `src/security/external-content.test.ts` | 85 | 1.96 s |
| `src/security/channel-metadata.test.ts` | 3 | 2.08 s |
| `src/agents/tools/web-fetch-output-contract.test.ts` | 23 | 6.79 s |
| `src/agents/tools/web-fetch.provider-fallback.test.ts` | 11 | 6.81 s |
| `src/media-understanding/file-attachment-outcomes.test.ts` | 24 | 1.50 s |

Individual test execution stays below one second per changed file; fetch wrapper/import preparation accounts for most of its wall time. PR CI job timing was not available at publication.

</details>

prs.title: fix(ui): native CLI selection strands the new-session composer
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the new-session composer losing its model picker and shifting layout after selecting a native CLI, including when no machine can run that CLI.

## User Impact

The existing composer, avatar, agent name, and “Pick where…” header stay in place. An unavailable CLI leaves the current model and draft untouched, with Retry in the picker. Users can switch from Claude Code or Codex back to a chat model without visiting /new or losing their prompt.

Native choices still launch the machine’s CLI in a terminal; this does not turn them into chat-model routes. Attachments, mentions, Incognito, Draft, and unsupported placement are not silently forwarded or converted.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve the existing native destination before committing selection, retain the shared model and Where pickers, and transfer the draft through the existing owner-fenced handoff instead of resetting it. Real route changes keep their isolation. The composer component itself is unchanged.

There is no new availability probe on picker open, search, or ordinary model selection. Successful navigation reuses the prepared target rather than repeating its lookup. Native startup permissions and CLI arguments are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Video proof — 38 seconds

Continuous recording of this PR head in the actual Control UI at 1280×800, with deterministic mocked Gateway data. It shows the unavailable choice, Retry, Claude Code/Codex selection, return to a chat model, and picker search. The prompt and exact header/composer/textarea bounds are asserted through the flow; three explicit CLI attempts produce three targeted lookups.

No live model or CLI is launched. Startup is 6×; interactions and pending states are shown at 1×. The capture applies only the upstream build prerequisite described below; the PR source is unchanged.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/da8bffba-c18d-4fde-bc30-9af570213f49

### Before and after

Actual Control UI with deterministic mocked Gateway data, matched text and viewport. The same build prerequisite was applied to both captures; these are implementation screenshots, not concept mocks.

**Before**

![Unavailable CLI removes recovery controls and shifts the composer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/10b3a60b-5daf-4248-bb7a-2a8b16999959)

**After**

![Failed CLI selection keeps the current model, prompt, and composer in place](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a2396cb5-4226-4326-acaf-6578e2e6530d)

<details>
<summary>Picker recovery, available CLI, and narrow viewport</summary>

![Retry stays inside the CLI picker row](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fcebfd53-326e-465b-ae07-73b31c0abfa3)

![Available native CLI uses the existing composer and Where picker](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e169b194-0475-4b0e-a864-3b6fa8d95689)

![The same composer remains stable at a narrow emulated browser viewport](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/81eac348-ce92-46ba-9e54-d50c137c980e)

</details>

- Reproduced the missing picker on main baseline cf6899819d15; rechecked main 2b8c65c47fd2 and the same removal remained.
- Actual Control UI with a mocked Gateway: identical header/composer/textarea rectangles and the same textarea element across failure, retry, Claude Code, Codex, and return to chat, at 1280px dark and 390px light. Direct unavailable URLs, multiple hosts, and reload retained correct identity and target semantics.
- Three explicit CLI selection/retry attempts produced exactly three targeted catalog requests; opening/reopening the picker and choosing a chat model added none.
- 252 changed-file unit cases are covered, plus 11 page-ownership tests. After the review correction, all 66 affected selection, runtime-choice, and Fast Mode tests passed. UI production and UI-test type graphs, scoped lint, i18n verification, formatting, conflict/line-cap/assertion checks passed.
- 21 browser regressions covered on [Blacksmith Testbox](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36391445375), lease tbx_01m3kechcchtq8w8q8qn12espd: 18 unchanged cases passed initially; all three native-destination cases passed after the focused fixture/recovery correction. The existing disconnect fixture was missing the node role required by the production event reader; it now sends a valid node event. The task-owned lease is completed. Local registered E2E execution was refused by loopback preflight; its proxy policy was not disabled.
- Independent autoreview completed scoped-clean through P2. Its earlier rapid-switch finding was reproduced by a failing regression and fixed by locking only the admitted route handoff; availability lookups remain interruptible by another choice. The regression also verifies that a blocked submit adds no layout-shifting notice.

**Build prerequisite:** The pinned PR base contains a duplicate clipboard-helper export, now fixed upstream by [#160210](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160210) at 7fac9b18dc9f. Builds, screenshots, and this video used only that isolated build-only removal; it is excluded from this PR. Before the final atomic-handoff correction, the UI build completed in 8.65s and verified 1,060 sidecars. That build’s advisory startup-size report was 177 bytes above the committed ceiling. A clean-base size comparison has not been rerun; no size baseline or enforcement was changed.

<details>
<summary>Focused test cost</summary>

One-worker test execution times (Vitest per-file measurements; process startup excluded):

| File | Cases | Test time |

| chat-attachment-handoff | 14 | 7ms |

| composer | 44 | 361ms |

| draft-native-terminal-start | 16 | 460ms |
| draft-persistence | 26 | 1.58s |
| model-control | 30 | 1.50s |
| route | 16 | 3ms |
| where-chip | 75 | 295ms |

The isolated persistence wrapper took 4.10s wall. The existing catalog-reconnect browser file took 34.96s; its registered reconnect/start boundaries require a browser. The corrected native-destination subset took 9.55s test time / 26.71s Vitest wall. New assertions reuse existing browser cases rather than adding per-test servers or sleeps.

</details>

prs.title: fix(ui): preserve reading position when switching sessions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes chats jumping to the wrong reading position or briefly bouncing when switching sessions, including when an expanded progress card changes the viewport.

## User Impact

First-open conversations start at the bottom; returning readers keep their message and offset. **Scroll to latest** retains its explicit destination. Fast previews remain immediate and inert until route admission. No settings, persistence-format, Gateway, or deployment changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Old numeric offsets were not stable bookmarks after virtual rows were rebuilt. The existing restoration owner now uses message anchors and committed measurements before presentation, including the first viewport-size commit.

Retained previews become visible before the route changes. Transcript positioning and existing progress-card presentation now follow that visual boundary, while reads and other route-owned work keep their original admission gates. The empty progress-loading spacer is removed. Main’s bounded initial overscan remains intact.

## Evidence

Published head `8716dcb603f06138ec35ffa8fa9a78d79b777152` has verified tree `c4c03226970b757ed983c06999da3863475260a5` (local repair commit `0edeb0776bae5fb689b22bfd9fa2106ade2db5d5`). This incorporates main `0a1ef3088a7e` to resolve the actual conflict while preserving its presentation/measurement changes.

### Before

First visible return in the earlier failing candidate: checkpoint 81 flashes before correction.

![Before: first visible return flashes checkpoint 81](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0322947c-1e05-45c9-a39c-b5f4bdb53de4)

### After

The same first-visible boundary immediately preserves checkpoint 78.

![After: first visible return immediately preserves checkpoint 78](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4fcb73a8-8987-4c1a-8dcb-d9e197293694)

### Session-switch video

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/690c5599-32df-4d54-ac1e-360ce4c2e56c

The ordinary-switch capture uses reviewed tree `d24193635350b9be5f4bdaa11fd6d04c0668b96c`. Its no-card path is unchanged by the final, separately tested expanded-progress presentation repair. The before image is an earlier failing candidate recorded with the same fixture and crop, not a main-branch capture. [Detailed capture provenance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160271#issuecomment-5877039434). The video does not claim to demonstrate expanded-progress behavior.

- **288 focused unit tests** passed: 208 transcript/scroll tests across 9 files and 80 progress/composer/controller tests across 4 files.
- **20 Chromium checks** passed: 16 native end-follow/ownership checks and 4 bundled actual-UI scenarios covering eviction, near-end reading, compact/reduced motion, and hidden expanded progress. Transition observations select the visibly presented pane, including the inert preview—not only the route-active pane.
- Red-before/green-after proof covers initial geometry, viewport-readiness notification, hidden end destinations, visible-preview reader/Latest positioning, missing preview progress chrome, and deleted bookmarks in empty/fitting history. The initial-end departure case is an additional preservation control, not a claimed failing reproduction.
- UI production and affected test type graphs, type-aware lint, formatting, styles, line-cap/assertion guards, i18n, and dead-export checks passed.
- Fresh independent **P0–P2 review: scoped-clean** on the complete candidate.
- Production build, 1,066 precompressed sidecars, and the canonical base-relative asset gate passed: startup JS **362,829 B gzip / 372,347 B limit**, startup CSS unchanged at **50,655 B**. The inherited CSS advisory remains below its hard ceiling; no budget was changed.
- **Updated-head CI and ClawSweeper:** awaiting results for this source update. Earlier green results on `2ffb1959dd89` are historical, not proof of this revision. No merge or deployment is requested or performed.

Proof uses the actual UI with synthetic Gateway responses in isolated Chromium, including native screen recordings. It is not live-Team or native Safari proof.

<details>
<summary>Test cost, fixture correction, and earlier local failure</summary>

Single-worker local measurements: 208 transcript tests took 13.74 s across their existing two shards; 80 progress/composer tests took 5.31 s; the 16 native browser checks took 4.87 s. The four bundled cases took 29.88 s including the build, with 18.554 s of test-body time. Browser geometry and inert-preview ordering require the real rendering boundary; the suite shares its server/browser. Hosted per-file timing is pending the updated-head run.

The native end-follow fixture now waits for the viewport owner’s actual dimensions and padding commit before measuring steady-state changes. Faster row measurement exposed its previous early baseline, adding an unrelated 27 px to those measurements. All existing assertions and tolerances are preserved.

One earlier local run timed out in the existing Swarm `notes` metadata test. Bounded same-order replay (128/128) and isolated replay (18/18) passed; the later 80-test progress run also passed. No deterministic cause was established, and no timeout or assertion was weakened. Passing replays are not claimed as a fix.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Enabled plugins can contribute MCP servers to the agent runtime while `openclaw mcp list`, diagnostics and login only see manually configured servers.

prs.title: fix(sessions): prevent search failures during session updates
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: message search intermittently reports unavailable during ordinary session activity, and the command palette leaves empty filters and hints beneath that failure.

## User Impact

Search now tolerates ordinary title/usage updates, including activity in excluded background sessions. Genuine database errors, changed access, and session-lifecycle changes are still checked and reported; a failed search never becomes a false “No results found.” The palette retains a compact error message and **Retry**, preserving the query, focus, and foreground draft.

No permission, schema, retention, or stored-data changes. This PR has not been deployed to the reported Gateway.

## Why This Change Was Made

The backend treated any pending session-row refresh as a changed search scope. Two harmless updates could consume both transcript-search attempts, even though the authorized session keys and lifecycle identities were unchanged.

Each attempt now joins one existing projection refresh before the original owner, readiness, scope, and generation checks. New dirty work after that refresh still consumes the existing retry budget. The final synchronous authorization/presentation check remains in place. This fixes the cause instead of suppressing its error.

Reported and requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/4af9f266-90c5-42af-880f-21bf9666678e)

## Evidence

- Retained live Gateway logs around the report contain sessions.search → “UNAVAILABLE: Session search scope changed while reading; retry the request”. The same error recurs later. No private log payloads are published here.
- Two registered-handler regressions reproduce that exact failure before the fix, using real SQLite/FTS worker reads and committed metadata updates on matched and excluded sessions. With the fix, both return the expected hit and current title with **one** transcript read.
- **12 backend tests pass**, covering ordinary updates; repeated real key-set, lifecycle, and refresh-settlement churn; visibility revocation; physical shared-store ownership; archived-hit preparation; and real FTS rejection. The five added cases take 3.33 s of test execution. Full file: 14.61 s test execution, 47.89 s Vitest duration, 50.60 s wall including 28.01 s cold worker compilation. Real projection/worker/SQLite composition is needed to reproduce this timing boundary.
- Final production and Gateway-methods test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, and diff checks pass. The earlier broader changed-check run also recorded passing repository guards and all selected test typecheck graphs.
- Fresh independent P0/P1 review is clean after replacing the initial proposed unbounded refresh loop with a single refresh per existing attempt. A new regression preserves the error when fresh work arrives as that refresh settles.
- The unchanged UI portion previously passed **82 palette tests** and Chromium checks at 1200×800 and 390×844: same-query Retry, focus restoration, and foreground-draft preservation. Its before/after images below demonstrate the retained failure fallback, not the backend concurrency fix.

<details>

The first UI changed-check run stopped at a native TypeScript compiler nil-pointer panic in checkCollisionWithRequireExportsInGeneratedCode. A controlled baseline run and the byte-identical restored candidate both passed afterward. No compiler/dependency change or suppression was made; that one-off panic remains unexplained. Remaining checks were run separately, not represented as a green initial aggregate.

</details>

prs.title: fix(acpx): resolve npm next to the node binary in ACP wrappers
prs.body:
Related to #160095.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: ACPX agent launches fail with `spawn EINVAL` on Windows hosts where npm is installed next to the node binary, whenever the captured adapter entry is unavailable and the wrapper falls back to the pinned package runner.

## User Impact

User impact: the pinned-package fallback actually runs on Windows installer layouts instead of dying with `spawn EINVAL` before npm is invoked. This is the path taken whenever the captured adapter is missing, which happens after plugin capture cleanup (see #160095) and whenever no local adapter is installed. No user action or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The generated wrapper looked for npm only under `<node>/../lib/node_modules`, which is the nvm-style layout. Windows installer layouts keep npm in a sibling `node_modules`, so the lookup returned nothing and the wrapper fell through to spawning `npx.cmd`. Modern Node rejects spawning a `.cmd` without a shell with a synchronous `spawn EINVAL`, so the fallback never reached npm.

Checking the sibling layout as well keeps the fallback on `process.execPath` plus `npm-cli.js`, which needs neither a shell nor argument re-quoting. This mirrors the lookup core already uses in `src/process/windows-command.ts`, and it deliberately avoids `shell: true` and the `cmd.exe` wrapper: this script is self-contained and spawns through `node:child_process` directly, so it cannot import core.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof (Windows, installed npm and installed adapter)

The generated wrapper was driven with a real ACP `initialize` JSON-RPC request. No stub package manager and no fake adapter: the installed `npm` 11.13.0 launched the installed `@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp` 1.12.0. Paths below are redacted.

Before capture removal, the captured adapter entry is used:

```
=== BEFORE capture removal ===
captured adapter responded: false "CAPTURED_ADAPTER_PATH_WAS_USED"
```

After deleting the capture directory, the same wrapper, with no other change, launches the pinned package through the real npm and returns a real protocol response:

```
=== AFTER capture removal (real npm launches real codex-acp) ===
captured adapter after cleanup: missing
initialize response received: true
protocolVersion: 1
agentInfo: {"name":"@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp","title":"Codex","version":"1.12.0"}
```

The same run against `main`'s `resolveNpmCliPath()` produces the failure this PR fixes, with the fallback never reaching npm:

```
=== AFTER capture removal ===
initialize response received: false
reason: closed:1
stdout: ""
stderr: "Error: spawn EINVAL
    at ChildProcess.spawn (node:internal/child_process:441:11)
    at spawn (node:child_process:796:9)
    at file:///<path>/state/acpx/codex-acp-wrapper.mjs:322:15
  errno: -4071,
  code: 'EINVAL',
  syscall: 'spawn' }"
```

### Regression test

The committed test builds a node shim whose npm exists **only** in the sibling layout, with the prefix `lib/` layout deliberately absent, so it isolates the lookup from the host's real npm.

RED on current `main` (`cf6899819d1`):

```
Error: spawn EINVAL
  code: 'EINVAL'
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 23 skipped (24)
```

GREEN with the change:

```
✓ falls back through npm when npm sits next to the node binary
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  24 passed (24)
```

The already-merged capture-reclaim regression for both adapters stays green with this change:

```
✓ launches codex after its captured adapter is removed
✓ launches claude after its captured adapter is removed
```

### Checks

Measured one-worker wall time for the changed test file: **15.08s** for 24 tests (1 file), on this host.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm test extensions/acpx/src/codex-auth-bridge.test.ts` (single worker) | 24 passed, 15.08s |
| `pnpm test extensions/acpx/src/codex-auth-bridge.migration.test.ts` | 5 passed |
| `pnpm test extensions/acpx/src/runtime-argv.process.test.ts` | 8 passed, 1 skipped |
| `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig extensions/tsconfig.json extensions/acpx` | 0 warnings, 0 errors |
| `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` | passed |
| `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` (2 changed files) | clean |
| `openclaw/ci-gate` on this PR | pass |

All validation ran on Windows, the affected platform. `pnpm test:extension acpx` (full extension suite) was not run to completion here: it exceeded a 10-minute budget on this host. The acpx test files that CI shards cover (`codex-auth-bridge`, `codex-auth-bridge.migration`, `runtime-argv`) pass locally and in CI.

prs.title: improve: reduce Online sidebar refresh cost on busy teams
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The sidebar's Online block spends unnecessary server CPU and browser rendering work as a busy team accumulates people and sessions.

## User Impact

Online keeps the same appearance, complete access-scoped Open/Running counts, sorting, filtering, and person links, with smaller refresh responses and cheaper large-roster rendering. No migration or configuration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Add `includeOwnerSessionCounts: "only"` to the existing `sessions.list` owner. Boolean `true` keeps its existing behavior; the new mode omits unused session rows and the owner facet without changing filters or pre-pagination counts.
- Avoid repeated allocations and unnecessary projected-run lookups for inactive rows. The request-local candidate index is used only for roster scans; selected-session reads and event publication retain direct lookups. Independent run owners and queued-state checks remain authoritative.
- Skip offscreen rendering work only above 50 online people. Rows stay mounted; focused rows and open person-card anchors remain uncontained, including scaled touch targets. No virtualization, persistence, or refresh-policy rewrite.

## Evidence

[Rendered UI proof — appearance preserved](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160220#issuecomment-5864927237).

Synthetic measurements on pinned baseline `2d39f2f738a89c27e0852943486af5c3971c4098`, then repeated optimization rounds. Gateway figures include the registered handler and JSON serialization, not WebSocket transport; each latency range is two 50-request block medians.

| Workload | Before | Final candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| 50 people / 1,000 sessions, count refresh | 2.52–2.93 ms | 1.47–2.24 ms |
| 500 people / 10,000 sessions, count refresh | 30.50–36.25 ms | 13.07–16.34 ms |
| 50-person response | 13,878 bytes | 4,407 bytes |
| 500-person response | 120,029 bytes | 38,158 bytes |
| 500-person production-UI stressed scroll, median frame | 41.9–48.4 ms | 18.5–26.0 ms |

- Fifty distinct synthetic viewers: a simultaneous 50-request count-only burst over 1,000 sessions completed in 65 ms; all per-viewer counts matched independent access-scoped oracles. At 10,000 sessions the latest burst was 860 ms: this is headroom evidence, not a production-capacity claim.
- No observed warm-read SQLite statements or worker dispatches. No cross-request count cache added.
- Real production UI / mocked Gateway: three samples each at 11/50/200/500 people; two-client event bursts, selected-chat startup priority, pending/trailing refresh, hidden visibility, reconnect, disposal and late replies passed. Desktop and emulated touch focus/card bounds passed at 85%, 100%, and 125% text scale with 500 people.
- Count accuracy/pagination/ownership/queue tests, active-run and keyed-presentation siblings, UI observer/event tests, core/UI typing, all 25 test-type graphs, changed-file type-aware lint, stylelint, formatting, protocol generation/check, and independent P0–P2 review passed. The test-type batch hit its outer time limit; remaining and affected graphs were completed explicitly. Native app builds were not run; generated Swift/Kotlin protocol parity was checked.
- Whole-core lint found one unchanged baseline error in `chat-attachments.ts` (716 counted lines / 700). It is already fixed on main by #160159. This branch merges cleanly with current main; no unrelated repair was copied into this PR.
- The new synchronous regression guards measured 14 ms and 4 ms. The reproducible 50-viewer benchmark is opt-in and remains skipped in normal CI; its measured test body was 8.93 s (35.49 s wrapper wall including compiler preparation).

Reproduce the checked-in opt-in variant:

```bash
OPENCLAW_BENCH_SESSION_VIEWERS=1 OPENCLAW_BENCH_OWNER_SESSION_COUNTS=only pnpm test src/gateway/session-list-viewers.perf.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
# Use OPENCLAW_BENCH_OWNER_SESSION_COUNTS=1 for the normal page plus counts.
```

Shared-host measurements varied between runs; earlier faster samples are not substituted for the final confirmation. The 50-person renderer was already smooth. Large filter re-expansion still reached 122–147 ms at 500 people; this does not introduce a full virtualizer. No live Team Gateway load, native-device capacity test, CI dispatch, merge, or deployment was performed.

Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski; @steipete cc'd for landing review.

prs.title: fix(browser): Windows Chrome setup fails after saved-profile Store enrollment
prs.body:
Related: #152057 (already merged; this is a narrow follow-up).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: automatic Windows Chrome setup refuses a saved extension profile after that profile explicitly requested Chrome Web Store installation.

## User Impact

User impact: selector-free inspect, verify, and install can recover the existing local profile without replacing its Store request. No new flags, configuration, permissions, or protocol changes. Chrome still owns extension approval.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Windows owner includes the browser profile in Store ownership. Inspecting the default `chrome` context can therefore report a context conflict and a foreign Store even when the saved `work` profile owns both. That observation now permits only bounded, serial read-only discovery. Selection still requires a validated current descriptor and a missing or owned Store request, followed by same-generation confirmation before relay access or the single C#-guarded mutation. Truly foreign, unknown, busy, and changed observations remain fail-closed.

## Evidence

- Reproduced through the registered setup CLI on base `6bfe76fcd7d31f64629c6889ce34e54368221d51`: all three new Store-requested cases failed while the other 25 cases passed. After the repair, all 35 Windows-selection cases pass, including foreign-Store refusal at candidate and confirmation stages before install/verify.
- 76 sibling tests pass: POSIX saved-profile migration, canonical CLI/setup, real authenticated relay, Windows adapter, and management transport. Total focused coverage: 111 passing tests.
- Independent P0–P2 autoreview: scoped-clean. Full changed-scope checks passed, including extension production/test typechecks, typed lint, dead-export/import-cycle checks, formatting and owner-boundary guards (plus six Doctor contract tests). Frozen reviewed head: `6cff547216bd3229446d7cc32a7dae667182ef51`; hosted exact-head CI remains required.
- Test cost: `pnpm test extensions/browser/src/cli/browser-cli-extension.windows-setup.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 7.20s runner wall, 5.99s Vitest wall, less than 1s test execution (35 cases). CI seconds will be added once available.
- Dependency behavior personally checked against `openclaw/openclaw-windows-node@92afaa430ee2bb5fb16e455ee8c9e41f246565f1` (`ManagementContract`, `WindowsRegistrationPlatform`, and `RegistrationService`). These local tests inject OS/C# boundary facts; they are **not native Windows acceptance**. The existing Windows lane owns exact-consumer native proof. No Windows producer or proof-script changes are included.

Worked on by: @steipete and @fuller-stack-dev

prs.title: fix: stop background authentication warning spam while signed out
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated background warnings and lost scheduled retries when the provider is signed out.

## User Impact

Heartbeat checks and scheduled jobs remain quiet during authentication failures while preserving failed run history and pending work. Direct requests still show sign-in guidance, and scheduled retries can resume after authentication is restored.

## Why This Change Was Made

Check the serving Codex account before each native OpenAI attempt, including reused connections, so a missing login is identified before thread handoff. If the cached account is missing, ask native auth to refresh it once before blocking; explicit custom providers keep their own authentication behavior.

Carry the classified failure through heartbeat completion into cron. Authentication failures retain the existing retry/backoff path without disabling recurring or one-shot jobs, and do not consume the retry budget for subsequent non-authentication errors. Cron retains ownership of its scheduled occurrence to avoid duplicate recovery work.

## Evidence

- Independent source review completed; recovery and retry-ownership findings addressed.
- Focused regression tests cover logout, cached OAuth recovery, preserved threads, accountless providers, quiet repeated failures, interactive guidance, and scheduled retry recovery.
- Formatting and test execution are pending. This PR was published before those checks at the author's request.
- No deployed or live channel-delivery validation has been performed for this patch.

prs.title: feat: add Lobster Packs and shared LobsterDex rendering
prs.body:
Related: #160081

## What Problem This Solves

Creators cannot add original characters to the LobsterDex, and plugins cannot reuse its existing collection and renderer through the public Control UI SDK.

## User Impact

Lobster Packs can contribute custom SVG characters and animated PNG sprite atlases from day one. Native Control UI plugins can browse built-in and custom definitions, read the browser's inventory, record encounters, and ask core to render a character's pose.

Installing or previewing a pack does not collect its characters. Existing built-in IDs and collection records remain intact; removing a pack keeps encounter history. Inventory remains browser-local. OpenClaw Pet is an intended consumer, but this PR does not modify that separate application or add a native desktop rendering bridge.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing plugin manifest and metadata lifecycle own contributions. Core validates and captures package-local artwork, exposes enabled definitions through `lobsterdex.catalog`, and serves artwork through authenticated Gateway routes. The shared renderer owns sizing, animation, reduced motion, and disposal for both the Dex and native plugin components.

This adds an optional capability to the existing `openclaw/plugin-sdk/control-ui` host. It introduces no new SDK subpath, renderer scripts inside packs, or collection store. The private, source-checkout-only Reef Lobsters example uses the normal plugin install flow. Published OpenClaw 2026.9.6 does not support this manifest field. The example no longer advertises that release: before publishing a derived pack, assign and test the actual first supporting `openclaw.compat.pluginApi` and `openclaw.install.minHostVersion`, and record the actual build version. Maintainer adoption of this public contract and its first supporting release remain pending. ClawHub discovery is the companion [ClawHub PR #3837](https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/pull/3837).

## Evidence

Implementation head: `8913849269417db0603730d2f8bb5bc45309874a`. The review repair adds a real installed-pack test and makes the example private/source-only; core implementation is unchanged from `57723b491a033b70393c5fd46e9836363bb6937b`. **Full `pnpm build` passed in 16m 28.7s** from an isolated temporary snapshot after the original checkout twice reported file metadata changing during compilation. The build used `cdb9840486c82b6123e86ed035cd8478fd41f436`; the previous implementation head differs only in a test-helper import cleanup, with identical production sources and a passing final mocked E2E replay.

- **67 backend tests passed**: manifest/asset validation, enabled-plugin catalog, authenticated HTTP route, method registration, and category acceptance. Metadata and HTTP tests were rerun after lint fixes: **28 passed**. Original focused run: 73.52s wall across three bounded shards; post-lint affected run: 76.30s including worker rebuild.
- **17 collection/catalog/SDK unit tests passed**, including legacy records, detached snapshots, connection invalidation, subscriptions, encounter timestamps, and revoked host access. File-run walls: 2.76s catalog, 10.09s SDK, 7.63s existing Dex/view.
- **8 Chromium component tests passed** (2.42s), covering built-in/custom rendering, animation, reduced motion, unavailable art, authenticated resource paths, credential fallback, and blob revocation.
- **Mocked-Gateway production UI end-to-end test passed**: 3.140s test body, 32.59s runner including the production bundle. A real native Control UI consumer uses the public host API; the HTTP fixture requires the bearer credential and `/reef-console` resource prefix. It verifies pack appearance, pose playback, reduced motion, no collection on preview, shared encounter history, reload persistence, and history after removal.
- Full build includes 95 local plugin builds, 53 built control-plane module checks, SDK declaration/export checks, and the production UI budget check. Generated public declarations include both `host.lobsterdex` and `mountClawmoji`.
- UI typecheck, scoped type-aware lint, SDK export/surface checks, i18n verification, line-cap ratchet, and documentation link audit passed (14,693 links; zero broken).
- Fresh independent review found an authenticated artwork-loading defect, which was fixed and re-reviewed with no remaining actionable findings. The PNG example was also inspected and its dimensions/chunk checksums verified.

**Real installed-pack proof passed:** `ui/src/e2e/lobsterdex-packs.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`, 1 test (32.364s body; 70.73s Vitest total). It packs the actual private example, installs the tarball with `plugins install npm-pack:<candidate.tgz> --force --accept-capabilities`, confirms a separate persisted installation, and uses an isolated real Gateway. No Gateway RPC, plugin delivery, or artwork HTTP interception is used.

- Real `lobsterdex.catalog` returns Coral and Tide from the installed manifest.
- Both artwork routes reject unauthenticated requests with **401**, return **200** with bearer authentication and the correct SVG/PNG MIME type, and produce SHA-256 hashes equal to both the installed files and source artwork.
- The real dashboard handoff renders both images through core under the `/reef-console` base path.
- Actual CLI disable plus restart of the test Gateway produces an **empty catalog**, removes the pack from the browser, and makes both authenticated artwork requests return **404**.
- Test-lane ownership regression: **41 tests passed** (55.18s). Final focused type-aware lint, formatting, and line-cap ratchet passed. Fresh independent review found no remaining actionable findings.

Reproduce from this supporting source checkout using the repository's supported E2E wrapper:

```sh
OPENCLAW_CAPTURE_UI_PROOF=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/lobsterdex-packs.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts
```

</details>

This closes the installed-package proof gap on the supporting source checkout. It does not establish compatibility with a published release, production publication, native OpenClaw Pet desktop integration, or hot-reload behavior. The existing mocked consumer scenario separately covers SDK inventory/encounters and legacy stored-state preservation. Earlier ClawHub zero-warning validation applied to the previous example metadata; the current private example intentionally omits release declarations and is not publishable as-is. No package release or production deployment was performed.

prs.title: feat(ui): run current-session actions from the command palette
prs.body:
Closes #160073

## What Problem This Solves

The command palette can't act on the open conversation: typing "archive" or "rename" only finds sessions whose titles contain those words, so renaming, pinning, forking, or deleting the current chat means leaving the keyboard for the header or sidebar menu.

## User Impact

User impact: while a chat is open, ⌘K / Ctrl+K lists **Current session** commands (Pin/Unpin, Rename, Mark as read/unread, Archive/Restore, Fork, Delete), so "archive" + Enter archives the current chat and "rename" + Enter starts editing its title. Only commands the chat header menu would enable appear, and they behave the same way: archive offers Undo, delete asks for confirmation, and rename edits the header title inline. With an empty palette they come after navigation, so Enter still opens New session.

## Why This Change Was Made

The active chat pane already registers itself with the palette for slash commands. It now also passes its header session actions in that registration. The palette closes first, so its dialog returns focus before Rename or the delete confirmation needs it. Then the pane rechecks the action against its current state and runs it through the header menu's existing code. The availability rules moved out of the session menu into a small shared module (`session-commands.ts`) that the menu and the palette both use, so they can't drift apart. Compact panes, like the one on Home, have no header, so they leave out Rename. Imported catalog transcripts, inactive or hidden panes, onboarding, and offline states offer nothing.

## Evidence

**Before (main):** "archive" only matches session titles. **After:** the Current session command leads and is selected, so Enter runs it.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![before: archive query on main](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jerrison/openclaw/196aedcaed79b2daa78a65e9d29c23c862b13bad/pr-assets/palette-session-commands/before-archive.png) | ![after: Archive session under Current session](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jerrison/openclaw/196aedcaed79b2daa78a65e9d29c23c862b13bad/pr-assets/palette-session-commands/after-archive.png) |

**Empty palette** lists the group after navigation. **Rename** closes the palette and focuses the header title with its text selected. **Archive** from the palette in the E2E harness shows the normal Undo toast and archived notice (the title was renamed in the same run).

| Empty palette | Rename | Archive |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![empty palette with Current session group](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jerrison/openclaw/196aedcaed79b2daa78a65e9d29c23c862b13bad/pr-assets/palette-session-commands/after-empty-scrolled.png) | ![header title editing after Rename](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jerrison/openclaw/196aedcaed79b2daa78a65e9d29c23c862b13bad/pr-assets/palette-session-commands/after-rename-editing.png) | ![Session archived with Undo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jerrison/openclaw/196aedcaed79b2daa78a65e9d29c23c862b13bad/pr-assets/palette-session-commands/e2e-archived.png) |

- **New tests.** `command-palette-session-commands.test.ts` covers ordering, Enter selection, running only after the dialog closes, and no chat target (4 tests, 2.7 s wall with `--maxWorkers=1`). `chat-pane-palette-session-commands.test.ts` covers header-menu parity, the main-session and compact guards, seven "offers nothing" states, archive with Undo, rename, and the recheck at run time (16 tests, 2.6 s). A shell-routing case in `app-host-lifecycle.test.ts` adds 1 test (1.9 s file). `command-palette-session-commands.e2e.test.ts` walks the full palette → shell → pane → `sessions.patch` flow for rename and archive (1 test, 0.7 s).
- **Checks.** `pnpm check:changed` passed: typecheck lanes, lint, format, i18n verify, knip, and the line-cap ratchet. Docs format and markdownlint are clean.
- **Nearby suites.** 137 related UI files, covering the palette, header and sidebar session menus, shell, and session-management E2E: 985 unit, 32 browser, and 428 of 429 E2E tests passed. The one failure was `session-owner-assignment.e2e.test.ts` (a submenu hover poll) under heavy local load; it passed 12/12 twice in isolation on both this branch and `main`.
- **CI follow-up.** The first CI run found a Madge import cycle, which counts type-only imports: `session-commands.ts` imported menu types from the module that imports it. Fixed in 70fd3741b9 by declaring those narrow types locally. `pnpm check:architecture` now passes locally. The other failure on that run, `test/scripts/ci-workflow-planning.test.ts` (`.ci-harness/scripts/ci-static-step.sh: No such file or directory`), also fails on unrelated PRs such as the `codex/chat-lifecycle-cleanup` CI run. It is a CI harness problem, not this change. On the 70fd3741b9 run, the only failure (apart from the aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate`) was `checks-node-compact-small-4`: `test/scripts/ci-node-test-plan.test.ts` › "keeps precise tooling selection through hosted overflow refusal" expected `exceeds 90 jobs (96 planned)` but got `95 planned`. This PR doesn't touch CI planning or `test/scripts`, and the same assertion fails on unrelated PRs, such as the CI runs for [`sunlit/fix/anthropic-session-catalog-json-cap`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36376004235) and [`feat/chat-reply-attribution-excerpt`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36375516217).
- **Manual checks.** In `pnpm dev:ui:mock` with Playwright, the palette's session commands matched the header menu on three sessions (child, pinnable, and history). Opening and closing the palette 10 times left no modals behind, with no page errors. Archive through the dev mock fails the same way on `main` via the header menu and ⌘⇧A ("Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'sessionId')"). That's a gap in the dev mock, so the archive proof above uses the E2E harness.

<details><summary>Notes</summary>

- New English strings: `palette.categories.currentSession` ("Current session") and `sessionsView.deleteSession` ("Delete session…"). Other labels reuse existing session-menu keys.
- The palette-registration contract now requires `sessionCommands` (null when the pane is inactive). The chat pane is its only sender.
- This PR was written with an AI coding agent and reviewed with the repo's `autoreview` skill (Codex, P2 threshold: no findings).

</details>
