prs.title: fix(ios): stop failed QR setup from connecting and losing retry state
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: iOS Gateway setup can continue connecting after required local preparation or credential saving fails, replacing the useful error and leaving users without a safe retry.

## User Impact

Failed scan, paste, and setup-link actions stop before connecting and keep a useful error visible. Try Again reuses the unapplied setup held in memory; expired codes offer Scan New Code. Endpoint, credential values, and credential ownership change together only after preparation and saving succeed.

**Not merge-ready — native onboarding paste with a bootstrap-bearing code now proves two persistent returned save errors stop connection, followed by successful retry after explicit fault removal. Settings/opened-link coverage, preparation faults, paired-state preservation, crash/Share recovery and retained-state upgrade remain open.** Target-specific cleanup may already have occurred before a later save failure; this fix does not promise rollback of target data. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

A shared setup operation gates field updates, navigation, and connection behind successful preparation and persistence. Failures retain their retry candidate and keep automatic reconnect paused. Cleanup belongs to the exact attempt so an older cancelled action cannot release a newer action’s pause.

The approved scope now includes the necessary QR-02 recovery work to avoid destructive pairing replacement before durable save. Global reset, scanner redesign, Cloudflare integration and unrelated connection races remain outside this PR.

## Evidence

### Native bootstrap-code persistent-failure/retry evidence — published head 0dd38ea

Colin returned a local Mac evidence bundle for exact commit **0dd38ea32c58785a02214d07a53d9a0624ce2308**, tree **325d7ce532ed1e00ce2a9257000ce12197b2d625**. The archive and all 32 listed file checksums were verified; instrumentation, fixture, test logs, exported summaries and all three screenshots were inspected. These results belong to the published source plus the disclosed task-only instrumentation, **not the unpublished QR-02 repair**. No GitHub workflow was dispatched for this validation.

- **Onboarding paste / Apply → Try Again → Try Again passes:** payload contains a bootstrapToken, not token-only setup. First save and the next retry both return injected Security status -25308 at GenericPasswordKeychainStore.saveStringResult. Each captured fixture state has zero connections and zero requests. After explicitly clearing the fault, the third save reaches the real save implementation and succeeds; the fixture records one node and one operator connect and the native app displays “You're connected.” The rendered UI test passed **1/1**, with **62.838 s** test execution.
- **Supporting native suites:** published **416/416 passed**, zero skips. Original baseline **410/411** on its first run; the failed GatewayOperatorFleetTests assertion (“auth pauses survive reconciliation until connection inputs change”) passed on a same-products full-suite replay (**3/3**). That replay is not a proven fix or the QR regression's red result; the failure's root cause is not established by this bundle.
- **Limits:** the loopback fixture accepts connections without validating credentials; this demonstrates native client failure gating/retry, not production authentication or absence of wrong-secret transmission after recovery. Fault injection returns an error before the Security mutation, not a physical Keychain outage. The debug attempt counter and “Clear Injected Fault” control change the captured failure-card layout, so these are instrumented-flow screenshots, not pristine production-layout proof. No matched before-version run of this persistent/bootstrap scenario is included. Full xcresults remain on the tester's Mac; the supplied command logs and exported summaries were reviewed here, not re-executed.
- **Still open:** Settings, opened-link/reset order, preparation failures, expiry/cancellation/view exit, ordinary manual compatibility, pre-existing paired data/outbox preservation, retained-state upgrade, Share-process races and restart/crash cleanup. The packet intentionally left the recovery candidate unbound. The returned matrix records only the onboarding F02/F03 and instrumented V01 slice as passed; it does not establish full acceptance or close the preservation/cancellation review findings.

Both images below show the **same published revision**; they are failure/recovery states, not a before-code/after-code comparison. Synthetic loopback data only.

**Before clearing the injected fault — second failed save, no fixture connection**

![Published 0dd38ea onboarding after a second injected write failure; debug-only attempt count and fault-clear control](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6a71a05b-8b0b-4c33-891c-26b65e488cb7)

**After clearing the fault and tapping Try Again — connected**

![Published 0dd38ea onboarding successful retry after explicitly clearing the injected write fault](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8a5c8a25-dc69-4f90-8f78-13bcb801f427)

### Earlier portable caller proof (historical, limited as described)

Validation ran locally on Linux with Swift 6.3.3 in Swift 6 language mode, using a network-disabled container. No GitHub workflow was manually dispatched for proof.

| Local source-exact caller harness | Before: b3f4c0aa540b | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Settings/onboarding post-scan, paste, and staged-link callers × four injected failures | 24/24 violate the failure contract | 24/24 pass |
| Healthy setup controls | 6/6 pass | 6/6 pass |
| Retry through the actual caller after clearing each injected fault | New retry path absent | 24/24 pass |

The baseline onboarding callers pass A’s fixture credentials into B’s save/connection calls after preparation fails. The candidate attempts no credential save after preparation failure and no connection after preparation or save failure. All six healthy controls still connect to B with B’s bootstrap credential.

The harness extracts method/type bodies byte-for-byte from the pinned baseline and candidate and verifies full-file/block hashes. It executes the actual Swift caller, auth-selection, preparation, application, and retry logic with explicitly substituted SwiftUI state containers and native I/O boundaries. **This is method-level behavioral proof, not a native app, SwiftUI lifecycle/rendering, physical Keychain/SQLite fault, camera, or wire-level test.**

- Five audited GatewaySetupApplicationTests pass using their actual source in an isolated proof module with the same declared platform substitutes. Test execution: 0.001 seconds; final parent compile/run/verification: 6 seconds with a warm build cache (initial parent run: 11 seconds). Native CI cost has not been measured.
- Strengthening the existing expiry test exposed an invalid-address message for expired retained codes. That assertion failed before the diagnostic-order fix and passes after it.
- Swift parser check passed for all eight changed Swift files. This is not a full Apple-framework typecheck.
- Pinned SwiftFormat 0.63.0: 0/8 files require formatting.
- Pinned SwiftLint 0.65.1 under the repository configuration: 0 violations across eight files.
- Staged-link reset ordering was restored to quiesce the existing session before offline preparation. Nine initial/retry ordering assertions failed before that correction and pass after it.
- Independent final source review: no accepted/actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Repository changed-path checks and git diff whitespace checks passed.
- Inspected native before/after and retry screenshots are now embedded in the [native evidence comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160049#issuecomment-5872505298) and the representative pair was attached in the requesting chat. This covers onboarding paste in light/default text, not every setup context.

### CI correction and review follow-through (`0dd38ea`)

The red `native-i18n` job on `e591cb1` failed because the source-owned inventory omitted the new setup/retry strings. The exact published source reproduced the same failure locally. Running the repository inventory generator changed only `apps/.i18n/native-source.json` (+11/-2); the same `native:i18n:verify` command then passed (4,095 entries, plus Android/Apple source safety checks). No translated/platform-generated artifacts, unfinished recovery code or workflow changes were included. No CI rerun or workflow dispatch was requested; this is a local red-to-green result, not a claim that all new-head CI is green.

Review disposition:

- **Existing-pairing preservation (Codex/ClawSweeper P1): accepted, still open on the published branch.** The repair must keep the same target's credentials, main/share device auth, TLS and queued work until durable commit, and settle committed cleanup after restart. The local recovery candidate, including shared-process Share-extension admission, is not yet published and remains under handoff review; native recovery execution is still outstanding.
- **Canceled async preparation (Copilot): accepted, still open until the recovery change is published and verified.** Generation checks after an await alone are insufficient; preparation and committed cleanup require owner-bound lifetime/settlement checks.
- **Duplicate welcome failure UI mentioned in the Copilot overview:** not reproduced by source tracing. `.welcome` is a separate branch from the Form error section, and `OnboardingWelcomeStep` uses failure-card **else** status text. No speculative UI change was made.
- **Production-boundary/native coverage:** still required. Prior `96a40df` token-only screenshots do not prove bootstrap replacement, cancellation, Share-process coordination or retained-state upgrade. These findings are not closed by the inventory fix or portable test counts.

### Manual-Connect scope correction (`e591cb1`)

A review found the save-failure stop had inadvertently changed ordinary manual Connect in Settings and onboarding. The two-file correction restores its baseline best-effort save behavior and the existing empty-instance guard; QR/setup callers remain gated by GatewaySetupApplication and skip a redundant second save. No extra permanent helper/test abstraction was added.

Local source-exact actual-caller proof reproduced both manual save-failure regressions at `96a40df`, with healthy controls passing and all four baseline cases passing. After correction, all four manual cases pass, retain target-bound credentials, and avoid bootstrap cleanup. The original 54 QR/setup/retry cases and five application tests also pass. Full QR proof compile/run/verification: 5 seconds warm. All eight changed Swift files pass parsing, pinned formatting and configured lint; whitespace checks pass. These are Linux boundary-double checks, not a native execution of this delta. Independent scoped review of the correction found no actionable P0–P2 regression.

The historical screenshots and Mac summaries in the `96a40df` section remain prior-head evidence. The newer `0dd38ea` native pass above supersedes the old-head execution gap for its stated onboarding and focused-suite scope only; ordinary manual Connect under save failure remains unrun natively.

### Native Mac evidence at prior head `96a40df`

Colin supplied a checksum-verified evidence bundle for baseline `b3f4c0aa540be135b722bec27922f105611b598d` and candidate `96a40dfabaedc98f239378ee2003fbbd3d0dc59d`. The screenshot images, instrumentation/UI-test/fixture sources, fault logs, fixture results, and exported native XCTest summaries were inspected. See the [native evidence and screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160049#issuecomment-5872505298).

- Exported native focused-test summaries: before **30/30**, after **35/35**, zero skips/failures. Native UI test: **1/1** on each revision. Mac runner reports pristine builds passing; full build logs and xcresults are retained by the runner, not independently re-executed here. Xcode 27.0 / Swift 6.4, iPhone 17 simulator / iOS 27.0.
- Real onboarding paste/Apply with a **one-shot returned Keychain save error**: baseline continues; candidate shows a usable error and has zero fixture connections/requests at the failure checkpoint. Real Try Again reuses the retained request and reaches the connected screen with operator/node fixture connects.
- **Important limits:** token-only payload, no `bootstrapToken`, so bootstrap preparation was not exercised. Baseline saves again before connecting; the one-shot fault does not establish connection without persistence. The fixture accepts connections without checking credentials, so role/traffic observations are not authentication or cross-target-secret proof. This is native app/simulator evidence with an injected storage result and synthetic loopback Gateway, not a physical Keychain outage or production Gateway test.

### Save-failure decision and compatibility boundary

**Chosen QR/setup behavior: keep the guarded connection.** A scan, pasted setup code or opened setup link must not connect when its required credential save reports failure. This does not change ordinary manual Connect: its existing target-bound in-memory credentials may still be used when a best-effort storage rewrite fails. The accidental extension of the guard into that manual path has been removed. This records the scoped implementation behavior, **not native validation, acceptance of destructive replacement, or merge approval**.

Source tracing at this PR head establishes:

- No Keychain item format, Gateway registry format, storage schema, or upgrade migration is changed. Normal registered-Gateway reconnect still uses the existing controller path, rather than the new setup application gate. This is source evidence, not a native upgrade test.
- Failed setup retains the unapplied request only while the setup screen remains open. Try Again repeats preparation and saving before connection. Expired requests require a fresh code; leaving or replacing setup discards the pending request.
- Bootstrap replacement is not rollback-safe: preparation can remove the target Gateway’s cached data, stored credentials, device-auth tokens, and TLS trust before a subsequent save fails. It also updates selection/auto-connect defaults. This PR does **not** promise that the previous target pairing or its live connection remains usable after that partial preparation.
- The local caller harness demonstrates retention of a different Gateway A’s synthetic stored credentials while B setup fails. It does not establish native Keychain preservation, same-target re-pair recovery, live connection continuity, or an upgrade from an installed earlier app.

### Approved recovery scope — implementation in progress

The unchanged bootstrap-preparation owner can clear the same target's existing credentials, device-auth tokens and TLS state before the new credential save succeeds. A later save failure can therefore leave an already paired target unusable. Surfacing an error/retry does not establish rollback or resolve this risk.

**Colin approved the scope expansion on September 28:** preserve the previous pairing until the replacement is durably committed, including the necessary QR-02 recovery work in this PR. Destructive replacement has not been accepted. Best-effort restoration into an unavailable Keychain is not a preservation guarantee. Implementation is in progress; this approval is not evidence of a completed fix or permission to merge. The recovery implementation and native paired-state/recovery proof remain outstanding.

### Native evidence still required before merge

The P1/P2 native-proof risks remain **open**. Required checks on an isolated native iOS build:

- [ ] Upgrade an installation already paired to Gateway A without resetting its storage; verify ordinary saved-Gateway reconnect.
- [ ] Exercise fresh setup success, a controlled credential-save failure, and successful Try Again through the rendered Settings and onboarding flows. Verify no connection after failed saving and no misleading success transition.
- [ ] With A already paired, attempt B setup with saving failure; read back A’s credentials/trust/state and verify A can still be selected and reconnected. Separately exercise replacement of an already paired target: a failed new save must preserve its old pairing and queued work, and successful retry must commit the replacement without using stale auth. Do not substitute best-effort rollback for preservation.
- [ ] Check expiry, leaving/reopening setup, and retry recovery after the storage fault is removed. Record the actual selection and auto-connect behavior.
- [x] Capture, inspect, sanitize and deliver a representative native onboarding before/after pair in the requesting chat and this PR. The linked evidence comment also includes retry success; PR image rendering was checked. Other materially different contexts remain part of the incomplete entrypoint coverage.

The native Mac pass is partial, not full acceptance. Remaining work: Settings/opened-link success/failure/retry, bootstrap preparation faults and staged-link reset order, persistent failure/recovery on already-paired targets, paired A/B and same-target recovery, expiry/view lifetime, cross-process/crash settlement, and paired-state baseline-to-recovery-candidate upgrade without reset. Physical camera and a previously released signed-build upgrade are conditional on authorized hardware/artifacts. No GitHub workflow is authorized or dispatched for proof. The PR is currently marked ready for review, but remains **not merge-ready**; its readiness setting was not changed. Source inspection or portable tests do not satisfy the remaining native gates.

prs.title: fix(gateway): failed visible tasks leave a stranded child session for write-only operators
prs.body:
Related: #159862
Stacked on #159940. Review only commit `e77c394fd72`; the earlier commits belong to #159940 and drop out once it lands, and the later ones are a `main` merge and an empty CI retrigger.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a visible `sessions_spawn` task fails to start for an operator with `operator.write` but no `operator.admin`, the failed child session is left behind and the model is told `Session cleanup unconfirmed`.

## User Impact

User impact: a failed visible task leaves no child behind for any caller that could create it, and the model gets the start error directly (for example `send blocked by session policy`). Callers with `operator.admin` see the same outcome as before, reported as a tool error instead of a structured error result.

## Why This Change Was Made

The tool's cleanup runs `sessions.delete`, which needs `operator.admin`. In-process tool calls are intersected with the caller's operator authority, so a write-only caller could create the child but never remove it.

Now `sessions.create` owns rollback of the child it created. When a spawn-owned visible child (`via: "spawn"` with a completion owner) has an initial task that never started, the same request deletes it through the shared `deleteGatewaySession` owner and returns the start error. That delete:

- runs under the create request's own session authority, revalidated just before the delete, so no scope is widened and a caller whose authority closed keeps the child for recovery;
- is fenced to the exact session id and lifecycle revision this request committed, so a reset or replacement in between keeps the newer child;
- keeps `emitLifecycleHooks: false`, matching the old tool cleanup, so hook behavior does not change.

If the rollback declines, `sessions.create` returns the old successful result with `runStarted: false`, and the tool's existing cleanup and message apply. Other `sessions.create` callers, including worker spawns without a completion owner, Control UI placement, and deferred worktree setup, keep the documented "child survives a rejected first send" contract. The protocol doc now describes the spawn exception.

## Evidence

**Real Gateway, write-only client.** The new `src/gateway/server.visible-spawn-start-failure.product-proof.test.ts` starts a real Gateway server and a real WebSocket client declaring `operator.approvals, operator.questions, operator.read, operator.write`, with a fake OpenAI Responses provider whose parent turn calls `sessions_spawn { task, visible: true }`. A `session.sendPolicy` deny rule on the dashboard prefix makes the child's first send fail. The client sends `chat.send`, waits with `agent.wait`, then reads `sessions.list`. Redacted output:

Before (this change reverted, #159940 head):

```json
{
  "spawnToolOutput": "{ \"status\": \"error\", \"error\": \"send blocked by session policy. Session cleanup unconfirmed. Inspect the child session before retrying.\", \"childSessionKey\": \"agent:main:dashboard:<uuid>\" }",
  "dashboardChildren": ["agent:main:dashboard:<uuid>"]
}
```

After:

```json
{
  "spawnToolOutput": "{ \"status\": \"error\", \"tool\": \"sessions_spawn\", \"error\": \"send blocked by session policy\" }",
  "dashboardChildren": []
}
```

**Real handler chain.** `src/gateway/server.sessions.visible-spawn-failure.test.ts` runs the registered tool through in-process dispatch as an admin Control UI client and as a paired write-only operator profile (the incident's shape). Both now report the start error and leave only the parent session. A third case resets a child and then asks the rollback to delete the original incarnation: the session id is unchanged, the lifecycle revision differs, and the child is kept. These tests fail without the `sessions-create.ts` change, and the fence case fails if the lifecycle-revision fence is dropped.

**Checks.** The visible-spawn, product-proof, child-custody, worktree-spawn, and visible-spawn-fallback Gateway suites pass (80 tests), as does `sessions-spawn-tool.test.ts`. `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` pass, and oxlint and oxfmt are clean. An independent review found no blocking issues. Its should-fix findings (protocol doc, and revalidating only session authority rather than creation-time selections) are addressed.

**Test cost.** Measured locally with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run <file> --maxWorkers=1`, and from the test times in CI run [36420025695](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36420025695), where all three files passed.

| `src/gateway/server.sessions.visible-spawn-failure.test.ts` (two cases added) | 3 | 32.8s | 23.1s (shard `agentic-control-plane-agent-chat`) |

**CI note.** The first run failed `check-test-types` on `test/scripts/ci-static-check-evidence.test.ts`, which `main` broke at 02:27 UTC and fixed at 03:08 UTC. After merging `main`, run 36420025695 had five timeouts in areas this diff does not reach: a Control UI sidebar e2e test, a Telegram history test, a `chat.send` history test, Gateway node shutdown, and a subagent requester-wake e2e test that mocks the Gateway. `main` was green at the same base, and GitHub refuses job reruns here, so an empty commit retriggers CI.

prs.title: fix(ui): show page reorder grips only for keyboard focus
prs.body:
Fixes #160006

## What Problem This Solves

Every row in the sidebar's top block of pages (Agents, Dashboards, Systems, Automations, Plugins, plugin pages and pinned sessions) has a grip button at its trailing edge. With a mouse it shows on hover or when the row is active ("Reorder Agents", opening **Move up** / **Move down**). On touch screens it is always visible. When it is invisible it still keeps a 24px slot, so the page link and its highlight stop short of the sidebar edge.

Mouse and touch users already reorder these rows by dragging, which is the obvious gesture. The grip gives them a second, less direct control for the same thing and uses horizontal space the sidebar doesn't have. Keyboard and screen-reader users can't drag, so the menu has to stay for them.

## User Impact

- Mouse and touch: page rows no longer show the grip on hover, when active, or on touch. The page link and its hover/active highlight now use the full row width (233px instead of 209px at 1440×900). Drag-and-drop is unchanged.
- Keyboard: Tab to a page row and the grip appears at the trailing edge. Tab again to reach it, then Enter opens **Move up** / **Move down**, as before. Focus stays on the moved item.
- Screen readers: the "Reorder <page>" button stays in the accessibility tree and in the tab order. It is only hidden visually.
- Stored session-section headers ("Reorder Beta" and similar) are unchanged. Their grip still shows on hover or focus, and on touch screens.

No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

`renderSidebarReorderMenu` now puts a `sidebar-reorder-menu--${kind}` modifier on the dropdown. Only `--entry` (the page block) changes. In `ui/src/styles/sidebar-reorder.css`:

- `wa-dropdown` is `display: contents`, so the trigger button is the element that gets a box. For entries it is absolutely positioned at the row's trailing edge, so it never takes row space.
- While the row has no `:focus-visible` descendant and the menu isn't open, the trigger uses the same clip recipe as `.sr-only` (1px, `clip-path: inset(50%)`). Pointer hover never reveals it, and a mouse click on the link doesn't match `:focus-visible`, so it stays hidden.
- When focus comes from the keyboard (`.sidebar-zone-entry:has(:focus-visible)`) or the menu is open, the trigger shows over the empty trailing end of the page link. The link keeps its width, so nothing shifts.
- Pinned sessions in the same block already show their pin/archive/menu actions at the trailing edge. For them the grip reveals in its own flex slot, as it did before, so it doesn't cover those actions. It only takes that slot while keyboard focus is in the row.
- The hover-opacity rule now only targets `.sidebar-reorder-menu--section`, so section headers behave exactly as before.

The docs (`docs/web/control-ui/sessions-and-sidebar.md`) now say that page and pinned-session grips are keyboard/screen-reader only and that section-header grips still show on hover, focus and touch.

## Evidence

**Testbox** (`node scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs run --provider blacksmith-testbox --timing-json`).

Head `49ef180f34e`, after the stylelint fix. The second commit moves `position: relative` into the existing `.sidebar-zone-entry` rule, which fixes `no-duplicate-selectors`:

| Check | Result | Run |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pnpm lint:ui:styles` (stylelint, as in `check-lint`) | passed | [36373743317](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36373743317), total 137.9 s (same run as the two rows below) |
| `oxfmt --check` (0.68.0) on the 5 touched files | clean | same run |
| `ui/src/e2e/sidebar-plugin-order.e2e.test.ts` + `ui/src/pages/workboard/workboard-sidebar.e2e.test.ts` | 2 files, 3 tests passed: keyboard-only case 1019 ms, reorder/reload 2626 ms, workboard widths 3069 ms | same run |

Head `efb32e36767`, first commit. The only difference from the current head is where the one CSS declaration sits:

| Check | Result | Run |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `oxfmt --check` (0.68.0) on the 5 touched files | clean | [36365240527](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36365240527), total 207.4 s (same run as the two rows below) |
| `pnpm tsgo:ui` | passed | same run |
| `ui/src/e2e/sidebar-plugin-order.e2e.test.ts` + `ui/src/pages/workboard/workboard-sidebar.e2e.test.ts` | 2 files, 3 tests passed: new keyboard-only case 879 ms, existing reorder/reload case 3487 ms, workboard widths 4254 ms | same run |
| `node --import tsx scripts/run-oxlint-shards.mts --only=core --split-core --core-stripe=N/5 --threads=1`, N = 1..5 | 0 warnings, 0 errors in every stripe | [36365308755](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36365308755), total 563.4 s |
| `pnpm ui:check-performance:base 11c32c43137` | startup CSS gzip 50488 B -> 50488 B (+0 B). Startup JS 372372 B is over the 371581 B enforcement limit, so the script exits 1 | [36365400992](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36365400992), total 146.3 s |

About the startup-JS result: the only script change is one class-name template in `sidebar-reorder.ts`. Current main is already over the committed startup-JS baseline, and CI treats that budget as advisory. I did not get a separate main-only JS number: a plain `pnpm ui:check-performance` on the merge base failed because there was no build.

**New e2e case** (`shows page reorder grips only for keyboard focus`):
- Pointer hover on "Agents": the trigger is 1px and clipped, the link fills the row, and the "Reorder Agents" button is still in the accessibility tree.
- Shift+Tab / Tab back onto the Agents link: the link matches `:focus-visible` and the trigger is 24px wide. The link width doesn't change.
- Tab to the trigger, Enter, **Move down**: the entry moves in the persisted order.
- Hover on a stored section header: its trigger opacity is 1.

The existing plugin-order case now does **Move down** with the keyboard instead of a mouse click on the grip. The workboard layout case now checks that page links fill the row and that the trigger takes no width.

**Mock Control UI** (`control-ui-mock-dev.ts`, Playwright Chromium, 1440×900 on the dev box). "Before" is the merge base `11c32c43137`. Agents row measurements:

| State | Before: link / row / grip | After: link / row / grip |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pointer hover | 209 / 233 / 24 px (visible) | 233 / 233 / 1 px (clipped) |
| Keyboard focus on link | 209 / 233 / 24 px | 233 / 233 / 24 px (overlaid, no shift) |

I also checked a pinned session ("Home server migration") with keyboard focus. The grip takes its own slot after the pin/archive/menu actions and doesn't cover them.

### Screenshots

Sidebar top block at 1440×900, before (merge base) and after:

| State | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pointer hovering "Agents", light | ![before hover light](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vyctorbrzezowski/openclaw/assets/pr-160017/before-hover-light.png) | ![after hover light](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vyctorbrzezowski/openclaw/assets/pr-160017/after-hover-light.png) |
| Pointer hovering "Agents", dark | ![before hover dark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vyctorbrzezowski/openclaw/assets/pr-160017/before-hover-dark.png) | ![after hover dark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vyctorbrzezowski/openclaw/assets/pr-160017/after-hover-dark.png) |
| Keyboard focus on "Agents", light | ![before keyboard light](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vyctorbrzezowski/openclaw/assets/pr-160017/before-keyboard-light.png) | ![after keyboard light](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vyctorbrzezowski/openclaw/assets/pr-160017/after-keyboard-light.png) |
| Keyboard focus on "Agents", dark | ![before keyboard dark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vyctorbrzezowski/openclaw/assets/pr-160017/before-keyboard-dark.png) | ![after keyboard dark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vyctorbrzezowski/openclaw/assets/pr-160017/after-keyboard-dark.png) |

## Risk and coverage

Low. The change is CSS scoped to `.sidebar-reorder-menu--entry` plus one modifier class. It changes no reorder logic, persistence or drag handling. The main tradeoff is on touch screens: page rows there now rely on drag only, and the menu stays reachable with a keyboard or screen reader. Visibility depends on `:has(:focus-visible)`, which the UI already uses widely. Only Chromium was exercised, not Firefox or Safari.

prs.title: fix(test): reserve compatibility HTTP listeners through startup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes intermittent `EADDRINUSE` failures while the OpenAI-compatible HTTP test fixture starts its Gateway.

## User Impact

Models and embeddings tests keep their endpoint reserved throughout startup. Product behavior is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared fixture previously retained a cooperative file claim while leaving the TCP endpoint available. It now uses the existing bound-listener reservation and lets the Gateway adopt that socket. All five callers use the fixture-owned port. Cleanup preserves Gateway ownership until shutdown completes.

## Evidence

- Original failure: [models HTTP CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36353255245/job/108716688020).
- [Blacksmith proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36359649226): a real competing bind in the existing disabled-models case reproduces `GatewayLockError/EADDRINUSE` with the old helper (396 passed / 1 failed in the original shard; 11 passed / 1 failed standalone). The reserved-listener fixture rejects the competing bind, returns the expected HTTP 404, and releases the port after shutdown. The historical competing process is not identified.
- 20/20 complete models-file runs, three original 12-file shard runs with 397 tests each, 43 embeddings tests, and 40 listener/allocation sibling tests passed.
- Measured standalone walls: models 26.96 seconds; embeddings 44.65 seconds. These existing suites exercise real Gateway/HTTP boundaries; the regression adds no Gateway boot.
- Final type-only cleanup received another complete models-file run, full selected checks against the verified base, and fresh independent P0–P2 review. All passed.
- No production changes, retries, longer deadlines, or weaker assertions.
- Current-head PR CI: [run 36362304204](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36362304204) passed (810s workflow elapsed). Selected test-job walls: checks-node-changed-compact-large-24: 117s, checks-node-changed-boundary: 110s. Job walls include setup and cleanup; standalone file timings are reported above.

prs.title: fix: image requests fail when Responses returns a native image
prs.body:
Related: #159869

## What Problem This Solves

Embedded agents can return an empty reply when an OpenAI-compatible Responses provider generates a native image.

## User Impact

The generated image is saved to OpenClaw's media store and included in the normal reply. The existing `image_generate` tool remains available as a workaround on unpatched versions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Responses stream handled text, reasoning, and function calls, but ignored completed `image_generation_call` output. This change materializes a completed image through the embedded runner's media store and records only a media reference in the assistant answer. It preserves output ordering and avoids duplicate saves when both item-completion and terminal events carry the image. Invalid or oversized image data fails rather than entering the transcript. The size guard uses decoded bytes, including the base64 padding boundary.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on OpenClaw 2026.9.6 with an embedded runtime: the provider returned three completed HTTP 200 image streams while the Gateway recorded no reply payload or tool call. A direct `image_generate` invocation sent an image through the same channel, isolating the failure before delivery.
- Patched embedded runtime smoke, 2026-09-27 (dev only): installed the patch into the OpenClaw 2026.9.6 Gateway image, reprovisioned one dev runtime, and confirmed the observed container image ID matched the patched image. In a fresh Telegram session, sent the plain prompt `Send me an image of a green square on a white background.` No explicit tool invocation was requested. Telegram displayed a native photo of a green square on white at 20:29 UTC, and the chat preview showed `Photo`. This was visually checked in Telegram Web. The runtime used `openai/gpt-6-sol` through CLIProxyAPI and the embedded OpenClaw transport. No Telegram relay changes were made.
- Redacted run trace: `20:28:40Z` Gateway logged a 57-character Telegram inbound message; `20:28:41Z` embedded agent logged its Code Mode tool catalog; `20:29Z` Telegram Web displayed the generated photo in the same chat. The pre-fix plain prompt had produced `Agent couldn't generate a response.`
- Final image smoke: after rebuilding the patched 2026.9.6 Gateway image with the decoded-size fix, a second fresh plain prompt delivered a native blue-circle photo. The observed dev runtime image ID matched that final build. After CLIProxyAPI was separately updated to stock v8.0.2, a third fresh plain prompt delivered a native yellow-star photo through the same patched Gateway. Both photos were checked visually in Telegram Web. This confirms the repair across both proxy versions; the proxy update alone did not fix the pre-patch failure.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` passed on current upstream `main` with the boundary fix.
- Focused Responses image, terminal-recovery, and stream-parity suites passed: 62 tests, including a regression that fails before the deferred-text ordering fix and passes after it. The new test confirms text precedes a done-only image in the reply. `pnpm test packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-stream-generated-image.test.ts packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-stream-terminal-recovery.test.ts packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-stream-parity.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` took 3.35 seconds wall time (Vitest duration 1.85 seconds). The media-core base64 suite passed, including one- and two-padding decoded-size boundaries.

- Telegram Test Server userbot proof is pending. The repository doctor could not load the QA broker through any existing Convex launcher (`convex`, `bunx convex`, or `npx convex` unavailable), and no broker credential pair is present in this workspace. The dev Telegram Web photo proof above is separate and does not claim Test Server coverage.

### Reproduce without a provider account

Feed the Responses stream parser a completed `image_generation_call` with base64 `result` in both `response.output_item.done` and `response.completed`. Before this change, the assistant output has no image or media reference. The new regression fixture covers this exact sequence.

prs.title: fix(link-detect): preserve intentional punctuation-ending paths
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Pasted links fetch the wrong page (or 404) when sentence punctuation trails them: `wow https://example.com/a!` was matched as the whole non-whitespace run, so the fetch went to `/a!` — a URL nobody typed on purpose. At the same time, real routes that legitimately end in punctuation must not be silently rewritten, and query/fragment values must survive byte-for-byte.

This PR resolves #158460's open review question ("may link understanding change the destination of a bare punctuation-ending path, or must it offer a literal?") by doing both: prose punctuation is trimmed in the path region, and an authored literal route is available via the angle-bracket autolink form.

## What Changed

### Smart punctuation trimming
`trimTrailingProsePunctuation()`:
- Collects the longest suffix of prose punctuation (`, . ; : ? ! " ' …`) and unbalanced closers inside the path region and trims it as one run when it follows word content — so stacked prose delimiters like `https://example.com/a).` resolve to `/a` instead of stopping at the `)`.
- Preserves query/fragment regions entirely — nothing at or after the first `?`/`#` is ever trimmed, so `?ids=1,2,` is fetched exactly as authored.
- Trims closing marks (`) ] } >`) only when unbalanced inside the path region, so `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foo_(bar)` keeps its suffix, and a link wrapped in prose parentheses `(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foo_(bar))` loses only the outer one.

### Literal route: the angle-bracket autolink form
```markdown
<https://example.com/Hello!>   // fetched exactly as written, brackets never reach the URL
see https://example.com/a!     // trims to /a in prose context
```
`stripMarkdownLinks` now keeps `<...>` autolink spans (mdast reports them as link nodes) so the literal destination reaches the token scan verbatim; explicit `[text](url)` markdown links remain stripped and unfetched, so display-only citations still never trigger fetches — including `[doc](<url>)` forms, whose angle brackets live inside the removed span.

## Evidence

- 49 tests pass in `src/link-understanding/detect.test.ts` (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/link-understanding/`): prose-punctuation trimming incl. the stacked `a).` case, balanced vs unbalanced closers, verbatim query/fragment preservation, angle-bracket literal routes, SSRF filtering of the literal form, and dedup between literal and trimmed bare forms.
- Guarded-fetch trace on head c2d0445859 through `extractLinksFromMessage` + `fetchWithSsrFGuard` (STRICT mode, same params as `runner.ts`), public example URLs only:

```text
"Check out https://example.com, for details"
  extracted: ["https://example.com"]
  fetch https://example.com -> HTTP 200, 558 bytes, finalUrl https://example.com
main-style raw token https://example.com, -> ERROR getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND example.com,

"wow <https://example.com/Hello!>"
  extracted: ["https://example.com/Hello!"]
  fetch https://example.com/Hello! -> finalUrl https://example.com/Hello! (requested verbatim; example.com has no such route)

"see https://example.com/a)."
  extracted: ["https://example.com/a"]

"read (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foo_(bar))"
  extracted: ["https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foo_(bar)"]
```

  The first pair is the production-path before/after: on main the comma-tailed token fails DNS entirely; with the trim the guarded fetch returns HTTP 200 and page bytes. The angle-bracket case proves the literal route requests `/Hello!` whole — the compatibility escape the review asked for.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:test:root` pass locally; branch is rebased onto current `main` (which contains the `test(ci): fix static evidence fixture contracts` lane fix) and formatted with `oxfmt`.


## Final-head proof (29020e1193) — trailing-slash and non-ASCII trimming

ClawSweeper revision 8 asked for a redacted final-head observation of the two
newly-changed trim roots. Trace through `extractLinksFromMessage` (which returns
only SSRF-allowed URLs, i.e. exactly what reaches `fetchWithSsrFGuard`) on head
`29020e1193`, public example URLs only:

```text
"see https://example.com/, then go"     -> ["https://example.com/"]     (trailing slash + comma trimmed)
"(read https://example.com/)"           -> ["https://example.com/"]     (paren-balanced root, slash kept, ")" trimmed)
"visit https://example.com/page/."      -> ["https://example.com/page/"](trailing slash kept, final "." trimmed)
"check https://example.com/a/, done"    -> ["https://example.com/a/"]
"see https://example.com/café, then go" -> ["https://example.com/café"] (non-ASCII root; guard now \\p{L})
"visit https://example.com/élève."      -> ["https://example.com/élève"]
"link https://example.com/日本,"         -> ["https://example.com/日本"]
"literal <https://example.com/Hello!> kept" -> ["https://example.com/Hello!"] (angle-bracket escape, verbatim)
"bare https://example.com/Hello! now trimmed" -> ["https://example.com/Hello"] (P1 compat surface, see below)
```

The non-ASCII predecessor guard was previously ASCII-only, so an accented or
non-Latin path root kept its prose comma/period onto the fetched path (ClawSweeper
P2). It is now `/[\p{L}\p{N}_/]/u`, and the cases above are pinned by regression
tests (31 tests in `detect.test.ts`).

## Open maintainer decision (P1) — bare punctuation-ending destinations

The last line above is the compatibility surface the review flags: a bare URL that
genuinely ends in punctuation (`https://example.com/Hello!`) now fetches `/Hello`.
Existing messages cannot retroactively adopt the `<…>` literal form, so this is a
user-visible policy choice, not something source review can authorize:

- **Trim prose punctuation by default (this PR's behavior)** — matches GitHub GFM
  autolink trimming and fixes the common "trailing comma 404" case; authors who
  mean a literal punctuation-ending path use `<url>`.
- **Preserve the existing default** — keep bare punctuation-ending destinations
  literal and gate normalization behind a maintainer-approved opt-in.

Requesting a maintainer call on which default is correct for link understanding
before merge; the code, tests, and angle-bracket escape support either outcome.

prs.title: fix(config): allowlisted sender stays blocked when a long numeric id is unquoted
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an allowlisted sender stays blocked, with no error, when their long numeric id (for example a 19-digit Zalo user id) is entered without quotes.

## User Impact

Entering a bare number that would be saved as a different number is now refused, naming the digits typed and what they would become, instead of silently saving a different id. Quoted ids and every number that is stored as written are unchanged. Configs saved earlier with such an id keep loading and the Gateway still starts; validation now warns on each affected id list entry so the operator can quote the original id.

## Why This Change Was Made

Integers above `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` are rounded while the value is parsed, so `1471383327500481391` becomes `1471383327500481300` before any schema check runs. The typed digits only exist in the input text, so the guard checks that text next to the existing finite-number check on every config input path: `config set` (value, strict JSON and batch), `config patch`, the system agent's config edits, and the gateway `config.patch` method. It scans the input the way the JSON5 parser does (strings with escapes and line continuations, comments ending at any JSON5 line terminator, identifiers), reads every number form (sign, fraction, exponent, hex, with the sign applied separately as JSON5 does) exactly, and refuses one only when it is an integer whose saved text would denote a different value. A number saved as the value written, such as 2^54, `1.5e300` or the rounded id typed back, is still accepted in any field. It is not applied to writes of the whole config, so a config saved before this change can still be edited.

For configs already on disk, the channel validation rules warn instead of rejecting, the same choice the existing dmPolicy/allowFrom warning makes to avoid breaking existing configs on upgrade. The warning only covers numeric entries of channel lists, which are all id lists in the bundled channels (`allowFrom`, `groupAllowFrom`, `users`, `approvers`, ...). No schema, Plugin SDK or generated metadata changes.

## Evidence

Real `openclaw` CLI run from source against a temporary state dir:

| Case | Before (main) | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `config set channels.zalo.allowFrom '[1471383327500481391]'` | "Updated", saved `[1471383327500481300]` | refused: `1471383327500481391 would be saved as a different number (1471383327500481300); quote it as a string`, nothing saved |
| `config set channels.zalo.allowFrom '[1471383327500481391e0]'` | "Updated", saved `[1471383327500481300]` | refused the same way, nothing saved |
| same with `'["1471383327500481391"]'` | saved | saved |
| `config set channels.zalo.mediaMaxMb 18014398509481984` (2^54, stored exactly) | saved | saved |
| `config set channels.zalo.mediaMaxMb 1.5e300` (saved as the value written) | saved | saved |
| `config set channels.zalo.allowFrom '[// note<CR>1471383327500481391]'` (comment ended by a carriage return) | "Updated", saved `[1471383327500481300]` | refused, nothing saved |
| `config set channels.zalo.mediaMaxMb +0x40000000000000` (2^54 in signed hex) | saved | saved `18014398509481984` |
| existing file with the bare id in `allowFrom` and in `mediaMaxMb`: `config validate` | valid, silent | valid, 1 warning on `channels.zalo.allowFrom.0` only ("may have been rounded") |
| existing file: `config set channels.zalo.dmPolicy allowlist` | saved | saved (warning printed) |
| existing file: `gateway run` | starts | gets past config loading into startup (logs `starting HTTP server...`, health monitor started) |

Tests (new ones fail on main, pass here):
- `src/cli/config-cli-path.test.ts`: rounded scalar, array and strict-JSON values, and exponent, fraction, signed and hex forms of the same id, rejected with the original text, including after a `//` comment ended by `` or U+2028; digits inside a string continued over LF, CRLF or U+2028 and `±0x40000000000000` are kept; quoted ids, 2^54, `1.5e300`, `0.1`, an already-rounded value typed as written, a negative Telegram-style id and a long number inside a comment are kept.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/config.test.ts`: `config.patch` with a bare 19-digit id is rejected and nothing is written.
- `src/config/validation.channel-metadata.test.ts`: a config holding rounded ids at channel and account scope still validates, with a warning at each id entry (including an exact 2^54, worded as "may have been rounded") and none for a non-id number.

Test cost: run with `scripts/test-projects.mts <file> --maxWorkers=1` on Windows: `config-cli-path.test.ts` and `config.test.ts` together 526s wall, `validation.channel-metadata.test.ts` alone about 3 min; the new tests take under 30ms each except the validation one (about 2.5s, most of it the shared plugin-metadata load). The 2 `config.openFile` tests in `config.test.ts` that fail here fail on this Windows machine on main as well.

Not run: the full repo suite.

## User Impact

The shared thread-configuration owner makes this choice from the current executable tool bridge. Start, resume, fork, and supervised Continue carry the same policy; configuration fingerprints refresh reused threads when availability changes. Retained tool declarations do not incorrectly imply that their executor is available. Authored native settings remain distinguishable from materialized defaults.

Without a callable `ask_user`, native questions retain their configured availability and mode requirements. Native async questions, MCP elicitations, and restricted-tool policy are unchanged. No new configuration or migration is required. Relevant Codex handler, registration, configuration, and authored-setting contracts were inspected directly.

## Evidence

Live QA used the real OpenAI provider and an existing conversation from before the upgrade. The pre-update transcript and stored answer passed exact continuity checks. Actual managed Codex 0.155.1 was probed with isolated synthetic configuration and no provider request. prs.title: fix(android): native Talk beeps every few seconds while the user is silent
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/150179

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Android native Talk (the device speech recognition path, for example `talk.realtime.mode: "stt-tts"`) plays the speech service's start sound roughly every 3 seconds while the user is silent, and on some devices a failure sound too, so an idle Talk session beeps continuously.

## User Impact

User impact: an idle native Talk session listens quietly. On Android 13 and later, silence no longer restarts recognition, so there are no repeated start or failure sounds; speaking after a long pause still sends the turn, and listening resumes after the reply. Devices below Android 13, and the speech-interrupt listener during playback, keep today's behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Continuous native Talk used one plain `SpeechRecognizer` session per utterance. With no speech, the service ends that session after about 3 s with no-match / speech-timeout, `onError` schedules a restart, and every `startListening()` makes the service play its start earcon. The public API cannot mute the earcon, so the fix has to stop the restarts. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/150175 fixed the related "never replies" defect on this path and listed this idle beep as not covered.

Push-to-talk in the same `TalkModeManager` already keeps one recognition session open across pauses: its recognition ladder tries a segmented session fed by an app-owned audio source (API 33+), then a silence-segmented session, then the plain restarting session. This change lets continuous Talk use that same ladder instead of a second recognition lifecycle:

- `startListeningInternal` starts continuous listening through the shared ladder; the speech-interrupt listener stays a plain session.
- Segment results accumulate through the push-to-talk segment list and merger, replacing the single `lastTranscript` value; the silence monitor still decides when a turn ends, so responsiveness is unchanged.
- A segmented session that closes within 1.5 s without hearing anything demotes later sessions one rung, so a recognition service that does not support segmented sessions falls back to today's behavior (the same rule the Voice Wake change in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/154873 uses for its own lifecycle).
- `retireRecognizer()` now also closes the app-owned audio source, so the microphone is released before reply playback, on stop and on push-to-talk takeover (three separate close calls became this one); `startListeningInternal` takes the capture lock so a concurrent stop cannot leave an open source behind.
- `onEndOfSpeech` stays a no-op, as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/150175 made it.

## Evidence

Real device, before and after, through the same entry point: a physical Xiaomi Redmi Note 11 (Android 13, Google speech services) paired to an isolated local Gateway (fresh HOME and profile, keyless scripted model, `talk.realtime.mode: "stt-tts"`), Chat screen, Start Talk, then nobody speaks. Before is `playDebug` from main `39caa592efb`, After is this branch; the Gateway build and config are the same for both. The phone's ringer is set to normal with system and notification volume raised so the earcons are audible, and a USB microphone in front of the phone records the room.

Screen recording with the room audio, Before then After (68 s; the strip under each screen is a scrolling spectrum of the microphone):

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/110355b2-a88c-4b7c-a276-8f8527d8f04f

If the player does not load: [the same MP4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20260927-issue-150179/android-talk-idle-before-after.mp4).

The room microphone for the first 44 s after Start Talk: Before, a start earcon followed by a failure earcon about every 3.3 s; After, only room noise (peak level -14 dB vs -37 dB).

![Room microphone spectrogram, 44 s after Start Talk with nobody speaking. Before: a start and a failure earcon about every 3.3 s. After: nothing but room noise.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20260927-issue-150179/android-talk-idle-room-spectrogram.png)

logcat (`-v threadtime`) from the same runs, counted in a fixed 30 s window that starts 6 s after the recognizer start triggered by the tap:

| 30 s of silence | Before (main) | After (this branch) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `RecognitionService#logStartListening` (restarts) | 9 | 0 |
| `Playing beep ...:raw/open` | 9 | 0 |
| `Playing beep ...:raw/failure` | 9 | 0 |
| `NO_SPEECH_DETECTED` errors | 9 | 0 |

Before, the same cycle repeats for the whole capture (start, start earcon, no speech after about 2.5 s, failure earcon, restart):

```text
23:16:46.365 I RecognitionServiceImpl: RecognitionService#logStartListening: callingApp: ai.openclaw.app.debug, locale: en-US
23:16:46.758 I AudioPlayer: Playing beep com.google.android.tts:raw/open (size 8626 bytes)
23:16:49.293 W RecognitionClient: #onError space agsa_transcription_NO_SPEECH_DETECTED code -1!
23:16:49.322 I AudioPlayer: Playing beep com.google.android.tts:raw/failure (size 14000 bytes)
23:16:49.938 I RecognitionServiceImpl: RecognitionService#logStartListening: callingApp: ai.openclaw.app.debug, locale: en-US
23:16:50.150 I AudioPlayer: Playing beep com.google.android.tts:raw/open (size 8626 bytes)
```

After, the only recognizer start in the capture is the one at the tap, and it plays no earcon. An earlier pair of runs with the phone in vibrate mode logged the same counts (the earcons were then played muted).

Spoken turn after a long pause, on this branch: Start Talk, 20 s of silence, then "What time is it right now?" from a speaker next to the phone. One session spanned the silence, `onStartOfSpeech` fired, the utterance reached the model, the reply came back and the app requested `talk.speak` (unavailable in this keyless setup), then listening resumed with a single new start. No earcon played during the capture.

Tests (`apps/android`), with JDK 17:

- `./gradlew :app:ktlintCheck :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest :app:testThirdPartyDebugUnitTest --tests '*TalkModeManager*'`: 112/112 in each flavor.
- New in `TalkModeManagerTest.kt`: `nativeTalkSegmentsOfOneUtteranceBecomeOneTurn` and `nativeTalkOnApi33OpensOneSegmentedSessionAndDemotesItWhenItClosesUnheard` fail on main with the production change reverted; `nativeTalkBelowApi33KeepsRestartingPlainSessions` pins the unchanged below-33 behavior.
- Measured cost (Robolectric, warm Gradle daemon): 0.07 s, 0.05 s and 0.82 s for the three new cases; the whole `TalkModeManagerTest` class runs 112 tests in 13.1 s.
- `pnpm native:i18n:check` and `git diff --check` pass.

Not covered: a recognition service that accepts the segmented session but still ends it after a few seconds of silence would keep restarting as today (a session that lived longer than 1.5 s does not demote). Only one device model was measured.

prs.title: feat(browser): extract page text from existing Chrome sessions
prs.body:
Closes #159610

## What Problem This Solves

Agents connected to an already signed-in Chrome session cannot use the browser's page-text action: `text` is rejected for `existing-session` profiles, forcing a snapshot or caller-written extraction script for ordinary reading.

## User Impact

`browser` with `action="text"` now reads bounded page prose from the `user` profile and other Chrome MCP existing-session profiles, including when caller-provided JavaScript evaluation is disabled. It accepts an optional native CSS selector, otherwise selects the first `article`, `main`, or `body`, and reports truncation with the resolved target and URL.

The existing-session selector uses native CSS only; Playwright selector extensions and shadow-root traversal are not supported. This reads the current document and does not add scrolling, feed parsing, or automatic expansion of collapsed content. No configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing text route now dispatches through the selected browser owner: Playwright for managed profiles, and the document-bound Chrome MCP adapter for existing sessions. The fixed internal reader checks the current document URL against the browser navigation policy, then checks the bound document and admitted URL again before reading text. Missing selectors wait under a shared, cancellable deadline and release the profile operation lock between attempts.

Results retain the existing 40,000-character ceiling and external-content wrapping. Unicode-safe truncation avoids splitting a surrogate pair in the new adapter. The capability flag, host-bound plugin schema test, shared tool fixture, and browser guidance now advertise text support. Existing tool text cases were moved into a focused sibling test file to preserve coverage without growing the oversized general browser-tool suite.

## Evidence

- **Before/after:** the new real-browser route test returns HTTP 501 when run with the baseline route and existing-session limit restored; the candidate returns bounded page text.
- **Real Chromium + packaged Chrome MCP:** all four tests in the existing opt-in Chromium suite passed. The added case exercises the registered `/text` route with `evaluateEnabled=false`, article/main/body fallback, first CSS match, hidden descendants, Chinese/emoji text, invalid selectors, and continued use of a snapshot button reference after reading.
- **Focused tests:** 284 cases passed across the route, tool, and real Chromium suites. After extracting the tool text cases into their own file, all 262 tool cases passed again. The final fixture-typing corrections were revalidated with all 17 affected route/tool cases passing.
- **Local static checks:** the implementation passed the complete changed-file lane, including production and test types, formatting, lint, unused exports, dependency guards, and runtime import cycles. The final capability-expectation and fixture updates also passed focused formatting and lint.
- **Plugin capability regression:** the host-bound existing-session schema must now expose `text` while still omitting unsupported actions. All 292 plugin/schema/tool cases and both dashboard cases passed with the aligned shared fixture.
- **Boundary tests:** the fixed extraction script is executed against a small document fixture to prove literal selector handling, length limits, delayed content, blocked URLs, document/URL changes during admission, and cancellation without reading prose.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and local validation commands</summary>

Against base `7f43b351149930f7db5b4545ad4df4693fe168fc`, preserve the new Chromium test and temporarily restore `routes/agent.debug.ts` plus `routes/existing-session-limits.ts` to their base versions. Run the new case with:

```sh
OPENCLAW_BROWSER_MCP_E2E=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome-mcp.chromium.test.ts -t 'reads bounded page text' --maxWorkers=1
```

Observed baseline: `501`, with the existing-session text unsupported message. The candidate's new real-browser case passed in 2.4 seconds on this host.

Candidate validation (the changed-file checks also passed with `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base 7f43b351149930f7db5b4545ad4df4693fe168fc --` followed by the implementation's 15 changed paths):

```sh
OPENCLAW_BROWSER_MCP_E2E=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.text.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.text.existing-session.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome-mcp.chromium.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.text.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.text.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.text.existing-session.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

The message context popover can report 100% occupancy from cumulative billed token usage even when the current prompt occupies only 9% of the context window. Reloading history also discarded the provider's saved prompt-context snapshot.

Explicitly unavailable context omits the percentage; messages without a snapshot retain the legacy calculation, and grouped messages show the largest known prompt. No migration or configuration change is required.

Live QA reproduced 22,887 prompt tokens alongside 1,089,037 cumulative cache-read tokens. The corrected saved answer shows 9% after two reloads, with its billing totals and original timestamp unchanged. Copy, Reply and the neighboring Unicode draft also survived. prs.title: fix(imessage): group messages anchored only by chat_guid are silently dropped
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

iMessage group messages are silently dropped when the bridge delivers them with a valid `chat_guid` (or `chat_identifier`) but no positive `chat_id`. This is a P2 message-delivery regression: the inbound gate at `extensions/imessage/src/monitor/inbound-processing.ts` used `if (isGroup && !chatId) return { kind: "drop", reason: "group without chat_id" }`, where `!chatId` is true for `chat_id === 0`, `undefined`, or `NaN`. Direct messages are unaffected, so the failure mode is "group chats go dark while DMs keep working" — exactly the symptom reported by bridges that only emit a guid-style anchor for group threads.

The contradiction that makes this a real bug rather than a deliberate guard: `extensions/imessage/src/monitor/conversation-repair.ts` treats a non-empty `chat_guid` as a *usable anchor* (`isIMessageAnchorless` returns false), so it never repairs these conversations. But the inbound gate treated the same payload as unanchored and dropped it. Two owners of the "is this group anchored?" question answered it differently, and the dropped messages never surfaced an error to the operator.

A follow-up review finding: conversation selection already rejected non-positive `chat_id` values, but `formatIMessageGroupTarget` delegated to `formatIMessageChatTarget`, which accepts `-1`. For `chat_id: -1` plus a valid GUID, inbound routing selected the GUID conversation while the outbound sender addressed `chat_id:-1`.

## User Impact

- **Who is affected:** Operators running iMessage bridges (e.g. Beeper-style bridges, BlueBubbles, or any sync client) whose group payloads expose `chat_guid`/`chat_identifier` but surface `chat_id` as `0`, a negative sentinel, or omit it.
- **Symptom before the fix:** Group messages from those bridges produce no reply, no error log, and no dispatch decision — they vanish between `resolveIMessageInboundDecision` and the conversation binder. DMs to the same account work normally, which makes the bug hard to diagnose. A negative `chat_id` plus GUID would also admit the group but send the reply to the unusable numeric id.
- **Symptom after the fix:** The same group messages dispatch normally, are routed under a stable `chat_guid`-anchored conversation id, and replies are addressed to `chat_guid:<guid>` so the outbound sender can resolve them back to the real thread. Conversation selection and reply targeting now share one positive-`chat_id` rule. When a group truly has no anchor of any kind, it is still dropped, but the drop reason is now `"group without usable anchor"` (accurate) instead of `"group without chat_id"` (misleading).

## Why This Change Was Made

The inbound gate and the conversation-repair owner need to agree on what counts as a usable group anchor. Today they don't, and the inbound gate is the stricter one — so strict that it drops payloads the repair owner considers already-anchored. Rather than loosening the repair owner (which risks double-repairing real anchorless groups), this change makes the inbound gate use the same anchor notion as repair: prefer a **positive** `chat_id`, fall back to `chat_guid`, then `chat_identifier`. Reply formatting now uses that same positive-id rule so the outbound send cannot address a different chat than the selected conversation.

Concretely:

- `hasPositiveIMessageChatId` is the single positive-`chat_id` rule used by both `resolveIMessageGroupAnchorId` and `formatIMessageGroupTarget`.
- `resolveIMessageGroupAnchorId({ chatId, chatGuid, chatIdentifier })` (in `conversation-id.ts`) centralizes the `positive chat_id > chat_guid > chat_identifier` precedence and mirrors the "usable anchor" semantics already owned by `monitor/conversation-repair.ts`.
- `formatIMessageGroupTarget` formats the reply target from whichever anchor survived. A negative sentinel such as `chat_id: -1` is not treated as a usable numeric target.
- `inbound-processing.ts` resolves `groupIdCandidate` through `resolveIMessageGroupAnchorId`, gates on `!groupIdCandidate` (not `!chatId`), and routes peer/session/reply metadata through that same anchor.
- `docs/channels/imessage/access-control.md` documents the GUID/identifier fallback, including negative sentinel ids.

The change is intentionally narrow: it does not alter DM routing, echo detection, reaction handling, or the repair owner's logic.

## Evidence

### Bug reproduction (source-level)

Before this change, the group gate was:

```
if (isGroup && !chatId) {
  return { kind: "drop", reason: "group without chat_id" };
}
```

`!chatId` is `true` for `chat_id === 0` (a common "missing" sentinel from bridges), for `undefined`, and for `NaN`. Meanwhile the repair owner considers the same payload anchored if `chat_guid` or `chat_identifier` is present.

The reply-target mismatch on the previous revision: `resolveIMessageGroupAnchorId` rejected `chat_id: -1` and selected the GUID, but `formatIMessageGroupTarget` called `formatIMessageChatTarget(-1)` and returned `chat_id:-1`. `send.ts` then put `chat_id: -1` on the imsg send request.

### Real behavior proof (production modules, after fix)

Ran the **real production modules** (`resolveIMessageGroupAnchorId`, `formatIMessageGroupTarget`, `parseIMessageTarget`) with Node via `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs`. Identifiers are redacted. This is the same target-selection and send-param construction used by the imsg monitor and outbound sender.

```
=== GUID-only group chat_id=0 ===
input {"chatId":0,"chatGuid":"iMessage;+;chat349","chatIdentifier":"chat349"}
conversation anchor iMessage;+;chat349
old reply target (formatIMessageChatTarget only) (empty)
new reply target (formatIMessageGroupTarget) chat_guid:iMessage;+;chat349
parsed outbound target {"kind":"chat_guid","chatGuid":"iMessage;+;chat349"}
imsg send params {"chat_guid":"iMessage;+;chat349"}
aligned true

=== GUID-only group chat_id=-1 ===
input {"chatId":-1,"chatGuid":"iMessage;+;chat349","chatIdentifier":"chat349"}
conversation anchor iMessage;+;chat349
old reply target (formatIMessageChatTarget only) chat_id:-1
new reply target (formatIMessageGroupTarget) chat_guid:iMessage;+;chat349
parsed outbound target {"kind":"chat_guid","chatGuid":"iMessage;+;chat349"}
imsg send params {"chat_guid":"iMessage;+;chat349"}
aligned true

=== positive chat_id still preferred ===
input {"chatId":42,"chatGuid":"iMessage;+;chat42","chatIdentifier":"chat42"}
conversation anchor 42
old reply target (formatIMessageChatTarget only) chat_id:42
new reply target (formatIMessageGroupTarget) chat_id:42
parsed outbound target {"kind":"chat_id","chatId":42}
imsg send params {"chat_id":42}
aligned true
```

The `chat_id: -1` case is the review finding: the old formatter would have sent `chat_id:-1`; the new formatter and the parsed imsg send params both use `chat_guid:iMessage;+;chat349`, matching the conversation anchor.

Inbound + outbound production path (Vitest, real modules, mock imsg RPC client — no live Apple Messages account on this host):

- `resolveIMessageInboundDecision` for `chat_id: -1` + GUID → `{ kind: "dispatch", groupId: "iMessage;+;chat349" }`
- `buildIMessageInboundContext` → `imessageTo` / `ctxPayload.To` = `chat_guid:iMessage;+;chat349`
- `sendMessageIMessage("chat_guid:iMessage;+;chat349", "hello group")` → RPC `send` params `{ chat_guid: "iMessage;+;chat349", text: "hello group" }`, and **not** `{ chat_id: -1 }`

A live signed-in `imsg` receive-and-reply from an Apple Messages account is not available in this environment. The trace above is the production decision, reply-target, parse, and outbound send-request chain that the bridge monitor and sender use.

### Regression tests

- `extensions/imessage/src/targets.test.ts` — `formatIMessageGroupTarget({ chatId: -1, chatGuid })` → `chat_guid:...`
- `extensions/imessage/src/conversation-id.test.ts` — `resolveIMessageGroupAnchorId({ chatId: -1, chatGuid })` → GUID
- `extensions/imessage/src/monitor/inbound-processing.test.ts` — negative `chat_id` + GUID dispatches; reply context uses `chat_guid:`
- `extensions/imessage/src/send.test.ts` — production sender issues `chat_guid` on the imsg RPC and never `chat_id: -1`

### Local validation

- `extensions/imessage/src/conversation-id.test.ts` + `targets.test.ts` — focused cases passed (imessage shard)
- `extensions/imessage/src/monitor/inbound-processing.test.ts` — including the new negative-`chat_id` dispatch and reply-target cases (extension-database-workers shard)
- `extensions/imessage/src/send.test.ts` — `sends group replies to chat_guid when the inbound chat_id is negative` passed

This branch is updated with the latest `openclaw/openclaw` `main`.

prs.title: fix(daemon): retry a transient SQLITE_IOERR owner-lease read after schtasks /End
prs.body:
Closes #159222

## What Problem This Solves

On Windows, `openclaw gateway restart`/`stop` fail with `Error: disk I/O error` (SQLITE_IOERR_TRUNCATE) when the Scheduled Task gateway is still unmapping its WAL/SHM files at the moment the CLI reads the owner lease right after `schtasks /End`, leaving the gateway stopped.

## User Impact

User impact: `openclaw gateway restart`/`stop` on a Windows Scheduled Task install now survive a brief post-kill SQLite I/O blip instead of aborting and leaving the gateway offline until a manual `schtasks /Run`.

## Why This Change Was Made

`stopScheduledTask`/`restartRegisteredScheduledTask` run `schtasks /End` (a hard kill, no graceful shutdown) and then immediately call `terminateScheduledTaskGatewayListeners` → `resolveScheduledTaskGatewayOwnership` → `readGatewayOwnerLease`, which opens a fresh read-only connection to the WAL-mode state DB (`src/daemon/schtasks-process.ts`). The dying process can still be releasing its SQLite locks and unmapping `openclaw.sqlite-shm` when that read lands, so Windows' win32 VFS occasionally returns `SQLITE_IOERR_TRUNCATE` (errcode 1546) 80–700 ms later — exactly the timing and stack trace reported in the issue.

This adds `isSqliteIoError` next to the existing `isSqliteLockError`/`isSqliteCorruptionError` classifiers in `src/infra/sqlite-error-diagnostics.ts` (same primary-result-code pattern already used for `SQLITE_BUSY`/`SQLITE_LOCKED` retries elsewhere in the codebase), and wraps just this one lease read in a small bounded retry (`readGatewayOwnerLeaseWithTransientRetry`, 4 retries at 150 ms) in `src/daemon/schtasks-process.ts`. All existing ownership/authority checks (task-supervisor identity, live-process verification, unattributed-owner refusal) are unchanged — only the transient I/O error on this one read is retried; a persistent I/O error still surfaces after the retry budget.

## Update Behavior

`terminateScheduledTaskGatewayListeners` (the function whose lease read this PR retries) is not only reached from the CLI stop/restart path above — `openclaw update`'s own Scheduled Task installer calls it too. `src/daemon/schtasks-install-files.ts`'s snapshot `restore()` path (line 124) runs `/Change /DISABLE`, `/End`, then, if the just-activated replacement task was still `running`, calls `terminateScheduledTaskGatewayListeners(env)` before restoring the prior task registration. That is the same post-`/End` lease read, on the same timing window, so the same transient `SQLITE_IOERR_TRUNCATE` could previously abort an in-progress update rollback with the task left disabled and the old registration unrestored.

This is a same-version, in-process reliability fix, not a schema/config migration: it touches no persisted state, needs no version-gated activation marker, and there is no "old parent updater vs. new candidate" split to reason about — the installer's rollback and the CLI's stop/restart both run whichever version's code is currently executing, so the retry applies uniformly the moment this fix ships. A persistent (non-transient) I/O error still surfaces exactly as before, so no failure mode is being newly swallowed.

I could not produce a published-driver × candidate cell for this. The Docker update-survivor lanes in `docs/help/testing-updates-plugins.md` (`projects-doctor`, `taskflow-restoration`, `channel-owner-policy`, `legacy-operator-state`) pin a Linux `openclaw@2026.9.4` baseline and exercise config/schema/plugin state; none of them installs or replaces a Windows Scheduled Task, so that matrix has no cell that covers this code path, and this sandbox has no Windows host to run `schtasks.exe` directly.

## Evidence

Added a regression test that reproduces the exact failure from the issue: `readGatewayOwnerLease` throws `{ code: "ERR_SQLITE_ERROR", errcode: 1546 }` (SQLITE_IOERR_TRUNCATE) once, then succeeds, while `terminateScheduledTaskGatewayListeners` runs on a mocked Windows Scheduled Task gateway.

Confirmed the test fails without the fix (`git checkout HEAD~1 -- src/daemon/schtasks-process.ts src/infra/sqlite-error-diagnostics.ts`, rerun, `git checkout HEAD -- ...` to restore):

```
FAIL src/daemon/schtasks-owner-publication.test.ts > retries the owner-lease read after a transient SQLITE_IOERR from schtasks /End teardown (#159222)
AssertionError: promise rejected "Error: disk I/O error { …(2) }" instead of resolving
Caused by: Error: disk I/O error
Serialized Error: { code: 'ERR_SQLITE_ERROR', errcode: 1546 }
```

With the fix, the full acceptance-criteria suite passes:

```
$ pnpm test src/daemon/schtasks-owner-publication.test.ts src/daemon/schtasks.stop.test.ts src/daemon/schtasks.startup-fallback.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
...
 ✓ |daemon| src/daemon/schtasks-owner-publication.test.ts > retries the owner-lease read after a transient SQLITE_IOERR from schtasks /End teardown (#159222) 10ms
...
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  131 passed (131)
```

Also ran, both clean on the touched files:
- `pnpm tsgo:core` (production typecheck, no errors)
- `npx oxlint src/daemon/schtasks-process.ts src/infra/sqlite-error-diagnostics.ts src/daemon/schtasks-owner-publication.test.ts` (no findings)
