prs.title: fix: keep links intact across streamed reply chunks
prs.body:
Fixes #151147

## What Problem This Solves

Streamed replies can split Markdown links and long URL targets at a chunk boundary, leaving recipients with a broken hyperlink and raw destination text. The shared embedded reply chunker selects boundaries before channel rendering.

## Solution

Keep complete and partial Markdown links, images, bare URLs, and angle autolinks together when they fit the transport budget. Break before protected links when possible, while preserving progress on malformed syntax and forced final drains.

`maxChars` remains the preferred chunk size. Default channel chunking may preserve a protected link up to the supplied transport ceiling. Explicit operator `blockStreamingChunk.maxChars`, caller-provided limits, and ACP `maxChunkChars` remain hard ceilings and are never widened to the channel limit.

The link scanner composes with Markdown tables, fences, code spans, malformed syntax, UTF-16-safe splitting, and streamed source custody. An unmatched backtick does not hide a later link from protection.

## Evidence

Candidate: `f50cf56d212e6fea385fa3f3efb79aff1cef3c45`, based on `e5b62e7c791427a300d0049d33918501605f1a80`.

- Blacksmith Testbox exact-source proof: [run 37413108184](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37413108184). Git blob hashes matched all 9 changed files plus `package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml`; the frozen install succeeded with `@openclaw/fs-safe@0.23.1`.
- Focused tests passed: 137/137 (`embedded-agent-block-chunker`: 80; `embedded-agent-utils` plus `block-streaming`: 57).
- `oxfmt` passed on all 9 changed files.
- Type-aware Oxlint passed for production and test configurations with zero warnings or errors.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` passed.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Exact-head native CI: [run 37415510425](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37415510425). Streaming tests, `security-fast`, formatting/docs, baseline ratchets, production/core/test types, lint stripes, package boundaries, and the remaining selected Node shards passed.
- The sole substantive native CI failure was the broad `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-1` shard: [job 112113391086](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37415510425/job/112113391086). Its three failures are in `extensions/github-copilot/index.test.ts`, where stored auth profiles were expected but received `undefined`. This PR changes only streaming/chunker source, tests, SDK exposure, and docs; it does not change Copilot or auth-profile code. `openclaw/ci-gate` failed as the aggregate consequence.
- Exact-head Security Review, CodeQL security scopes, OpenGrep, and dependency review passed. The earlier `source-map-js` advisory is no longer present in this run.
- Exact-head ClawSweeper review: [run 37415632836](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/37415632836). It found no actionable code defect and rated patch quality 5/6. Merge remains owner-blocked on acceptance of the additive `hardMaxChars` SDK contract and allowing a fitting protected link above the preferred 1200-character size under default channel settings; explicit operator and ACP limits remain hard ceilings.

## Proof Limits And Scope

No live external-channel delivery is claimed. Source tests do not establish rendered link integrity across every provider pipeline. This PR addresses link-boundary chunking and transport limits; it does not claim general list or blockquote atomicity.

prs.title: fix(sessions): transcript-ownership refusals from reset and compaction lack typed details
prs.body:
Closes #170175

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a session's current transcript is owned by another session key, for example a cron session whose latest isolated run owns the transcript, the ownership refusal from `sessions.reset`, and from a `sessions.compact` that trims to `maxLines`, carries no structured details and no `retryable` flag. Clients cannot tell it from a transient `UNAVAILABLE`.

## User Impact

User impact: `sessions.reset`, the `agent` RPC's `/reset`, and a `sessions.compact { maxLines }` that needs to trim the transcript now refuse with `UNAVAILABLE`, `retryable: false`, and `details: { code: "SESSION_TRANSCRIPT_OWNER_MISMATCH", sessionId, ownerSessionKey, requestedSessionKey }`. Clients can stop retrying and act on the owner key without parsing English.

The refusal still happens in the same cases, and the top-level `code` is unchanged. Changes that apply to reset only (compaction already returned the full message and never reached the dispatcher log):

- The reset `message` loses its `Error: ` prefix and is no longer cut at 240 characters.
- The Gateway no longer logs a reset refusal at error level as `request handler failed`. The ws response log line still records it.

There is no protocol version change; the detail code is additive (`ErrorShape.details` is already open).

## Why This Change Was Made

The ownership check now throws a typed `SessionTranscriptOwnerMismatchError` with the same sentence. The class is registered with the SQLite worker error transport, so its fields survive the worker hop. `handleGatewayRequest` then shapes it through `errorShapeFromError`, the same path `AgentDatabaseAdmissionError` already uses. That covers `sessions.reset` and the `agent` RPC's `/reset`.

`sessions.compact` answers from its own catch, so that catch now uses `errorShapeFromError` too, keeping its session-changed special case. Errors the mapper doesn't recognize keep their existing formatting. Compact also picks up the mapper's existing agent-database admission and incognito mappings: admission refusals now report their canonical reason and repair hint, and a nested incognito-ended error can replace the outer message.

The protocol declares the detail code with a closed schema, and the session-control protocol doc describes the refusal.

Keeping `UNAVAILABLE`, with `retryable: false` plus `details.code`, follows the existing typed refusals (`INCOGNITO_SESSION_ENDED`, `STALE_INSTALL`, agent-database admission) and leaves the code clients already branch on unchanged. If maintainers prefer `INVALID_REQUEST` for this refusal, it is a one-line change.

Out of scope:

- Whether resetting a cron base key should succeed by rotating to a fresh session id. This PR only makes the existing refusal machine-readable.
- The adjacent actor-path refusal (`Session actor transcript window belongs to another logical owner`) is still untyped. I have not shown that a public RPC can reach it.
- `chat.inject` can also reach this check, through the cached target resolution added in #168677, after `sessions.abort` has cached the row's entry facts. That is a separate bug, #170136, fixed at the resolver in #170137. It is not shaped here, because the fix belongs in target resolution, not in inject's error path.

## Evidence

- **Gateway WebSocket regression** in `src/gateway/server.sessions.store-rpc.test.ts`. It seeds a base row and a run row that name the same session id, with the run row written last, so the run key owns the transcript. That is the shape isolated cron runs leave behind.
  - `sessions.reset` twice plus `sessions.compact { maxLines: 1 }` on the base key all return the same typed refusal. On `main` (`7d0c05318`, and earlier `87f151f6`) the first reset frame is `{ code: "UNAVAILABLE", message: "Error: Transcript session … resolve the ..." }`, with no `details` and no `retryable`. With only the dispatcher change, compaction still returned an untyped `UNAVAILABLE`.
- **Stored state after the refusal.** A local readback check (not committed) re-read the two session rows (including `entry_json`), the transcript owner and the transcript events after each of two refused resets. They were byte-identical, and both responses were identical. Reset still runs its hooks and runtime cleanup before the write is refused; this check does not cover those.
- **Built Gateway on loopback.** After `pnpm build`, I started the built Gateway on `127.0.0.1` in a scrubbed environment (`env -i`) with an isolated state directory, seeded offline with the same rows. I then called `openclaw gateway call sessions.reset` through the CLI Gateway client. The before and after output is below. That build was made on `87f151f6` and predates the compaction change.
  - Before, the Gateway also logs `request handler failed`.
  - The CLI prints `retryable: false` in both runs because the client normalizes an absent flag. The raw-frame difference is the one shown by the regression test.
- **Focused tests** on `7d0c05318` (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`). Wall time is the full command, measured locally on macOS under heavy host load from other jobs, including cold transform. Hosted CI timing is pending; CI has not run.
  - Changed test files: `src/gateway/server.sessions.store-rpc.test.ts` 6/6 in 199 s. `src/state/openclaw-state-worker-error.test.ts` 46/46 in 20 s (new transport case). `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/error-codes.test.ts` 14/14 in 10 s (new schema case).
  - Compaction after the catch change: `server.sessions.compaction.test.ts` 21/21 in 157 s and `sessions-compact.settlement.test.ts` 4/4 in 91 s.
  - Unchanged and passing: `session-accessor.sqlite-data-version` 16/16 in 37 s, `session-transcript-runtime.configured-store` 9/9 in 43 s, `error-shape` 1/1 in 23 s, `server-methods.stale-install` 4/4 in 13 s.
- **Gates** on `7d0c05318`:
  - `pnpm check:changed --base origin/main --head HEAD` passes: format, core and core-test typecheck, oxlint on changed files, knip dead-export scans (0 entries), runtime import cycles (0), and the ratchets.
  - `pnpm protocol:check` passes, including the Swift and Kotlin contract checks.
  - The docs format check and markdownlint on the edited doc passed on the previous base; the doc change is unchanged.
  - `pnpm build` passed in round 1, on `87f151f6`.
- **Not run locally:** the full `pnpm check` and `pnpm test`, left to PR CI. No real isolated cron run either; the tests seed the persisted rows directly.

<details>
<summary>Built Gateway, before and after (synthetic ids, token redacted)</summary>

Before (`main`):

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "gateway_request_error",
    "code": "UNAVAILABLE",
    "message": "Error: Transcript session 8f14e45f-ceea-4e7a-9f8b-2d5c6b1a0e93 is owned by agent:main:cron:3f1c9a52-7d4e-4b8a-9c21-5e6f7a8b9c0d:run:8f14e45f-ceea-4e7a-9f8b-2d5c6b1a0e93, not agent:main:cron:3f1c9a52-7d4e-4b8a-9c21-5e6f7a8b9c0d; resolve the ...",
    "retryable": false
  }
}
```

After (this branch):

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "gateway_request_error",
    "code": "UNAVAILABLE",
    "message": "Transcript session 8f14e45f-ceea-4e7a-9f8b-2d5c6b1a0e93 is owned by agent:main:cron:3f1c9a52-7d4e-4b8a-9c21-5e6f7a8b9c0d:run:8f14e45f-ceea-4e7a-9f8b-2d5c6b1a0e93, not agent:main:cron:3f1c9a52-7d4e-4b8a-9c21-5e6f7a8b9c0d; resolve the transcript target again before retrying.",
    "details": {
      "code": "SESSION_TRANSCRIPT_OWNER_MISMATCH",
      "sessionId": "8f14e45f-ceea-4e7a-9f8b-2d5c6b1a0e93",
      "ownerSessionKey": "agent:main:cron:3f1c9a52-7d4e-4b8a-9c21-5e6f7a8b9c0d:run:8f14e45f-ceea-4e7a-9f8b-2d5c6b1a0e93",
      "requestedSessionKey": "agent:main:cron:3f1c9a52-7d4e-4b8a-9c21-5e6f7a8b9c0d"
    },
    "retryable": false
  }
}
```

</details>

prs.title: fix: allowlisted native Bash commands denied as "approval was not granted" when the command is long
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/156476

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on the `claude-cli` backend with `ask: "on-miss"`, a native Bash command that fully matches the agent's exec allowlist is denied when its tool input is longer than about 380 characters, and the model is told "OpenClaw approval was not granted for native tool use (Bash)" although no approval was ever requested.

## User Impact

User impact: operators who allowlist a binary for native Bash get the same auto-allow for long invocations of it as for short ones. Commands that still need a human prompt and are too long to show in full remain denied without a prompt, and the denial now says so and names the next step instead of reading like a timeout or a user denial: a shorter command, plus adding the executables to the agent's exec allowlist under `ask: "on-miss"` only. Under `ask: "always"` an allowlisted command still needs a prompt, so the message offers only the shorter command. No configuration change is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Native Bash refuses to prompt when the approval description would be truncated, so no human ever approves a command they cannot see in full. That check ran before the exec-allowlist auto-allow step added in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/141471, so it also blocked commands that need no human review: auto-allow evaluates and binds the complete command and shows no description to anyone. The check is now evaluated first as before, but only enforced when no allowlist auto-allow applies, which is exactly when a prompt would follow. The binding checks, the post-annotation description bound, `ask: "always"`, and Bash's allow-once-only decisions are unchanged. The `policy-oversized` outcome gets its own message. It suggests an exec allowlist entry only under `ask: "on-miss"`, the one mode where that entry can admit the command without a prompt.

The CLI backend docs now state that an allowlisted native Bash command auto-allows at any length, while a command that would need a prompt is denied without one when its description cannot show the complete input.

## Evidence

**Live before/after through a real Gateway.** I ran one real agent turn per build. Each turn went through an isolated local Gateway, using the `claude-cli` runtime (Claude Code 2.1.280, model `claude-cli/claude-sonnet-5`, the host's existing Claude Code login). Both builds had identical config and an identical prompt.

- **Before:** the fork point of this branch, built with `pnpm build`.
- **After:** this branch, built the same way.
- **State:** each run had its own fresh state dir, config, and `HOME`, on a free loopback port.

Setup, identical for both runs:

```sh
# <scratch>/bin/argcount is a two-line sh script that prints its argument count and byte length.
# <scratch>/bin/argcount-unlisted is a byte-identical copy that is NOT allowlisted.
openclaw approvals allowlist add --agent main <scratch>/bin/argcount
openclaw gateway run --port <free-port> --bind loopback --verbose
openclaw agent --agent main --json --message "<prompt below>"
```

```json5
{
  gateway: { mode: "local", bind: "loopback", auth: { mode: "token" } },
  agents: { defaults: { model: "claude-cli/claude-sonnet-5" } },
  tools: { exec: { security: "allowlist", ask: "on-miss", pathPrepend: ["<scratch>/bin"] } },
}
```

The prompt asks the model to run three commands exactly as written, without retrying:

1. `argcount short-control`, a control.
2. `argcount segment-01 … segment-48`, an allowlisted command of 536 chars.
3. `argcount-unlisted segment-01 … segment-48`, an unlisted command of 545 chars.

For commands 2 and 3, Claude Code's Bash tool input is 605–631 chars of JSON, above the 380-char approval-description cap. The model sent byte-identical commands in both runs.

Tool results copied from the Claude Code stream in the Gateway's verbose log:

| Command | Before (fork point) | After (this branch) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. allowlisted, short | `argcount: 1 arguments, 13 bytes` | `argcount: 1 arguments, 13 bytes` |
| 2. allowlisted, 536 chars | `PreToolUse:Bash hook error: OpenClaw approval was not granted for native tool use (Bash).` | `argcount: 48 arguments, 527 bytes` |
| 3. unlisted, 545 chars | `PreToolUse:Bash hook error: OpenClaw approval was not granted for native tool use (Bash).` | `PreToolUse:Bash hook error: OpenClaw denied native tool use (Bash): the input is too long to show in full in an approval prompt, so no approval request was created. This is not a user denial. Retry with a shorter command, or ask the operator to add its executables to this agent's exec allowlist.` |

Gateway-side observations for the same runs:

| Observation | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Claude CLI native Bash auto-allowed via exec allowlist` log lines | 1 (command 1) | 2 (commands 1 and 2) |
| Claude Code `permission_denials` | 2 | 1 |
| `agent --json` toolSummary | `{"calls":3,"failures":2}` | `{"calls":3,"failures":1}` |
| Gateway RPCs handled (`[ws] ⇄ res <method>`) | `agent`, `node.list`, `computer.status` | `agent`, `node.list`, `computer.status` |
| `plugin.approval.*` RPCs | 0 | 0 |

So, before the fix, the allowlisted command worked when short but was denied once long, with a message that reads as if an approval had failed; no approval was ever requested. After the fix, the same long command auto-allows and runs. The unlisted long command is still denied without an approval request (it was answered in 9 ms, with no approval RPC), and the message now says why and names the next step.

<details>
<summary>Tests</summary>

Regression cases in `src/agents/cli-runner/execute-plugin-native-bash.test.ts` run through the real plugin permission handler, with a real exec-approvals store and executable. Command: `gog calendar list --query <500 chars>`.

- **Allowlisted:** must auto-allow, with the resolved executable pinned and no Gateway approval call.
- **Unlisted:** must be denied, with no Gateway approval call and the new message, including the allowlist advice.
- **Allowlisted under `ask: "always"`:** must be denied, with no Gateway approval call, and the message must not suggest an allowlist entry (which cannot admit the command in that mode). Without the ask-aware message, this case fails because the denial still names the allowlist.

On the fork point, both cases fail for the reported reason: the first gets `"behavior": "deny"` instead of `allow`, and the second gets the old `approval was not granted` message. The result is `Tests 2 failed | 3 passed (5)`. With the fix: `Tests 6 passed (6)`; `pnpm test src/agents/cli-runner/execute-plugin-native-bash.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` takes 21.7 s wall on the author's machine, mostly module import.

Related suites pass unchanged, including the existing cases that deny truncated, sanitization-expanded, and detail-overflowing Bash descriptions without calling the Gateway. They ran as one command (135 passed):

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/cli-runner/cli-native-tool-approval.test.ts \
  src/agents/cli-runner/execute-plugin.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/execute-plugin-native-bash.test.ts \
  src/agents/cli-runner/execute-plugin.policy.test.ts extensions/anthropic/cli-runtime.test.ts
```

`pnpm check:changed` (core, core-tests, and docs lanes) and `git diff --check` also pass. The three new cases take about 400 ms together and use no real timers or Gateway boots.

</details>



CI seconds (per-test durations reported by Vitest, summed per file from the CI job log on the previous head `8cef26df7ab`, before the ask-always case was added; module import and worker startup are not included):
- `src/agents/cli-runner/execute-plugin-native-bash.test.ts`: 5 tests, 0.80 s in `checks-node-compact-large-30` (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35856793548/job/107167498969)

CI note: `checks-node-compact-large-25` (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35856793548/job/107167498773), and therefore `openclaw/ci-gate`, failed in `src/gateway/server.chat-abort-settlement.test.ts` ("preserves an acknowledged abort and completes its preinstalled waiter after …", `expected { type: 'res', … } to match object { ok: true, … }`). This PR changes only the CLI runner's native Bash approval path, its test and docs; the gateway chat abort test does not import them. Main was reworking exactly this test the same day: commit https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/fc574daa9adf5efef42b5e36f5823033134f1aad ("control the preinstalled abort wait deadline") landed at 10:03 UTC and was reverted at 10:42 UTC by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/9bb3ccca699058b17196d803f14c6da1f8ae5d29, this run started at 11:49 UTC, and the fixture fix https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/77b3233487a8e3fdb7d9a433ae72b3088033ff53 ("settle chat fixtures before releasing session stores") followed at 14:41 UTC, then https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156638. prs.title: fix(auth): honor renewed shared profiles over stale agent copies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an agent can keep skipping a renewed preferred OAuth account, or retry an account whose shared cooldown is still active, when its local store retains an older copy of the shared account.

## User Impact

Agents honor the current credential and health state of the shared account while preserving their configured account order. Different-account overrides, newer local credentials, and unrelated local health remain local. There is no schema or configuration migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing ownership policy already identifies these copied or older same-account OAuth credentials as shared-owned. Runtime composition nevertheless overlaid the stale local credential and health values. Selection could therefore exclude a renewed primary before the refresh owner had a chance to adopt it.

This change makes runtime composition use that existing ownership decision for both credential and health values across cold reads and prepared snapshots. It does not introduce a new ownership policy or write inherited credentials back into child stores.

## Evidence

### Exact-head runtime refresh and inherited recovery proof

At current head `13f3a86d00650a3e76efec12774e88c753ca8fb8`, I ran the production `resolveApiKeyForProfile` source path against two independently created canonical SQLite state roots. The input was an expired synthetic child-owned `openai:default` credential and a healthy synthetic alternate persisted only in the shared owner. The two runs differed only in whether the normal credential validator accepted or rejected the inherited alternate. No resolver, refresh manager, persistence function, or provider response was mocked.

```text
case=accept  validated=[legacy, fallback]  outcome=fallback-selected
case=reject  validated=[legacy, fallback]  outcome=OAuthRefreshFailureError
both: child fallback persisted before=false, after=false
both: child legacy refresh fence before=false, after=true, pending after=false
both: shared fallback credential unchanged=true; child-authored order unchanged=true
both: global schema 19→19; agent schema 23→23; auth store record version 1→1
```

These are sanitized observations from the actual resolver and owner database readback. The failed synthetic legacy refresh correctly settles in its child owner as a terminal fence; therefore the legacy child credential *does* change. The fallback credential remains exclusively shared, including after validator rejection, and the user's child-authored order remains intact. This exercises the current revision's persisted-owner settlement and inherited recovery path that was not covered by the earlier real provider turn. The synthetic inputs never held a real account token or refresh token; these runs do not prove a successful live OAuth renewal, a provider inference turn, or Matrix delivery. The historical real-provider before/after comparison below supplies separate evidence for selection and actual inference.

### Exact-head live installation provenance

The self-contained package built from this PR head reports `OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (13f3a86)`; its embedded build-info commit is `13f3a86d00650a3e76efec12774e88c753ca8fb8`. After installing that package on the operator's Gateway, the Gateway RPC reported build ID `2026.9.6-13f3a86d0065-2026-09-26T20-30-05.152Z`. The LaunchAgent was running, both `/healthz` and `/readyz` returned HTTP 200, and the configuration audit passed. The startup command itself reached its 45-second timeout before the Gateway became ready shortly afterward without a second restart. A post-install native agent turn has not yet completed, so none is counted as evidence here. This proves the core artifact and basic service readiness; it is not a live OAuth renewal or per-agent account-selection measurement.

- Production observation on 2026.9.4: the configured primary-first order was intact, but the shared and child primary credentials were failed refresh fences. The backup's current shared subscription block was masked by older child health. This observation motivated the reproduction; it does not establish the original provider refresh failure or prove live recovery from this patch.
- Before: isolated SQLite regression tests using the actual synchronous/asynchronous runtime readers and account selector failed 3 of 5 cases on the unmodified base: both renewed-primary reads and the current shared cooldown. The different-account and newer-local-generation controls already passed.
- After: all 5 regression cases pass, including prepared snapshot publication, preserved per-agent order, and unchanged persisted child rows. Related auth-store/snapshot tests total 129 unique passing tests after correcting one preexisting local-override fixture to use a distinct account.
- Production core typecheck and the repository's changed-file checks pass. Independent repository autoreview reported no actionable P0/P1 findings; the final diff was also manually reviewed.

### Real provider before/after proof

Ran the supported `openclaw agent --local --agent proof --session-key … --message 'Reply exactly AUTH_PROOF_OK. Do not use tools.' --timeout 180 --json` command through each exact source checkout's built CLI. Parent: `35e047f5e98bff430fa58050f28d2364a485ff27`. Candidate: `360075452b26ae85318c00bbe0b6ab14e53898bb`. Each case used a separate freshly bootstrapped state directory, the same authorized access-only OAuth credential, Codex stdio with an agent-scoped home, no channels, no model fallbacks, and denied tools. Historical stale rows were seeded through the existing canonical SQLite owner after startup.

| Input | Unmodified parent | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shared primary has a current credential; the same-account child retains a failed refresh fence; explicit order contains primary | Exit 1: `Explicit auth order for openai has no usable profiles.` No native binding was present at readback. | Exit 0; actual assistant response `AUTH_PROOF_OK`; native binding selects `primary`. |
| Shared primary has a future cooldown; child's copied primary has an expired cooldown; explicit order is primary, backup | Exit 0; actual response `AUTH_PROOF_OK`, but native binding incorrectly selects `primary` and its shared cooldown changes. | Exit 0; actual response `AUTH_PROOF_OK`; native binding selects `backup` and the primary's shared cooldown remains unchanged. |

For all three successful turns, the completed response session matches the exact durable native Codex binding and producer terminal receipt; the configured provider/model matches, no model fallback or reroute occurs, and zero successful tools are recorded. Both shared and child credential rows, authored child order, and child health remain unchanged across all four comparisons. Shared runtime success bookkeeping is allowed to change.

The renewed case took 6.18 s for the parent's rejection and 14.67 s for the candidate's completion; the cooldown parent completed in 18.59 s. The candidate cooldown's first attempt timed out starting native Codex before a completed response; no native binding was present at readback. One sequential retry, with no credential/config changes, completed in 23.37 s and selected backup; that transient failure is retained separately and is not counted as successful proof.

Proof boundaries: stale-state inputs and profile labels are synthetic; the cooldown labels use the same authorized real account, so this verifies profile selection and actual provider execution, not switching between two real subscriptions. No real refresh token was copied and no OAuth refresh was performed. This does not establish the cause of the original provider renewal failure or test Matrix delivery. An initial stable-schema setup was stopped by the pre-existing agent schema 21→23 Doctor requirement in both revisions before inference; those attempts are excluded from this comparison. The fresh-state runs use unchanged core schemas 18/23 on both sides.

### Codex bridge integration coverage

Fresh GitHub CI exposed an existing Codex bridge test that used the runtime-composed reader to assert stale persisted-child bytes. The test-only follow-up now checks both contracts: runtime reads see the current/refreshed shared owner, and the existing public persisted-credential reader proves that the stored child remains exactly unchanged. The complete `auth-bridge.test.ts` file passes 127/127, including the owner-token force-refresh assertions. The final fixture reuses credential objects while passing copies to the writers, preserving exact storage assertions and reducing the file below its pre-PR line count. The final 127-case run, scoped formatting/type-aware lint, full-PR line-cap ratchet, and fresh P1 autoreview passed. The full extension-test typecheck passed on the preceding test correction `2c0de13a592e9346cad2a6551b084c5dad12748d`; that broad lane was not repeated after this fixture-only deduplication, and that revision had its own GitHub CI run.

The earlier head `667ce32b263b75c2b7bc3b5285199794f9744cb6` added only the Codex test correction and fixture deduplication to the provider-tested candidate `360075452b26ae85318c00bbe0b6ab14e53898bb`. Its production files were byte-identical to that candidate. The later CI correction below changes production code; the provider results above remain historical measurements of the exact revisions named there, not a real-provider replay of the updated head.

### CI follow-up

Current head: `13f3a86d00650a3e76efec12774e88c753ca8fb8`; incorporated main: `bfff4f4cbd802e2f305f57eaa3ecb630eee88362`. This history-preserving merge resolved conflicts in two test files without adding a new auth production change. The Codex bridge test retains main's newer fixture structure and verifies both the effective shared owner and unchanged persisted child bytes. The Telegram native-pipeline fixture retains main's async `createBot` API and the PR's JSON wire serialization before drain processing. The resulting PR diff against that main remains 14 files: eight auth production files and six tests.

On this exact head, the 12 focused auth files passed **112/112** tests. The conflict-affected Codex bridge case passed 1/1 (109 intentionally skipped); the Telegram sticker case passed 1/1 (57 intentionally skipped). The two conflict files pass formatting, and the PR-specific staged diff has no whitespace errors. Fresh GitHub CI has passed the core-auth Critical Quality and core-auth Security High jobs. The current revision still requires a maintainer's security-sensitive approval; passing CI jobs are not that approval. The runtime proof above is newly measured on this exact head; the older real-provider comparison below remains tied to its expressly named revisions.

The completed broad CI run has one further failure: [changed-compact-large-4](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36269718560/job/108481782783) reached Vitest's 120-second timeout in `src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.test.ts` (“reports promoted no-op stop failure as recovery-required”) after 1,523 other tests passed. That Gateway file is unchanged by this PR. A targeted replay of the exact test on this exact head passed 1/1 in 4.747 s of case time (27.50 s including cold transform). This narrows the failure to the broad-shard context but does not establish why it hung there. The contributor account cannot rerun the workflow: GitHub reports that repository admin rights are required. A maintainer CI rerun remains necessary; this paragraph does not count the shard as green.

Previous head `641cc63b2fbd5fcb09fc66ef53ae4ba4c7bd116a` incorporated main `5a15cf46eba351142e02e73668b87e5a3727d368`. The conflict-affected sticker case passed once on that merged source (1 passed, 57 intentionally skipped): 92.09 s command wall / 91.65 s supported runner / 21.568 s case time, with cold compilation dominating. Scoped type-aware lint passed (143.32 s including regenerated SDK declarations), formatting and the complete PR line-cap ratchet passed, and fresh full-PR autoreview against its incorporated main was scoped-clean through P1. Normal CI and the independent current-revision security review gate remain in force; this does not claim all-CI success or a new real-provider replay.

The earlier auth-owner correction `28d322ff414326c37453c2ccb9c5a2fec7904c64` was reviewed and validated against main `2736e94e27091d7e0d273b3c5ed70b89be30fa0d`; its measurements below remain tied to that revision. The prior Telegram fixture correction and full 58-case proof at `f73cca6` are described below.

The initial full CI exposed six failures across credential settlement, prepared API-key reference reads, and Doctor shared-health coverage. A bounded reproduction using those three files passed all 19 tests on the original base `35e047f5e98bff430fa58050f28d2364a485ff27`, while head `667ce32b263b75c2b7bc3b5285199794f9744cb6` failed six. The failures were addressed at their owning boundaries:

- OAuth refresh transactions read their selected persisted owner using the existing owner-only load option. They must not validate a claimed child refresh against a newly composed inherited credential. The settlement validators and rejection assertions remain intact. The final error/recovery path separately retains the effective inherited view, so a failed child legacy-default refresh can still offer a healthy shared alternate to the existing fallback validator.
- Prepared external-reference reads compare the materialized store and prior runtime store under the same existing JSON normalization, preventing a metadata-only difference from causing a redundant publication. The original no-notification assertions remain intact.
- Doctor's fixture now separately asserts effective runtime selection of the canonical shared owner and exact preservation of the stale persisted child credential; distinct local-account selection remains covered.

At that correction head, the 12-file contract run passed **107/107 tests** in 39.84 s command wall time (39.50 s supported-runner wall; 14.323 s summed case time). It covers refresh claims and settlement, provider ownership, refresh fences/queues and cancellation, inherited selection, prepared snapshots/external references, fallback validation, and Doctor shared health. The two new split-owner fallback variants were first demonstrated red (2 failures, with both original variants passing); both now pass while preserving the shared credential and proving no inherited credential was written to the child.

All three affected type graphs pass: production core (45.54 s), core agent tests (39.34 s), and Doctor command tests (37.03 s). Formatting, the full-PR line-cap ratchet, and fresh scoped P0/P1 AutoReview pass; the independent caller audit found no remaining issue. The final type-aware scoped lint also passes (203.09 s including SDK declaration preparation). No real provider turn or OAuth refresh was replayed for this follow-up. These local results do not claim that every GitHub CI job is green; that pushed revision received its own CI run.

The branch also incorporates upstream main `2736e94e27091d7e0d273b3c5ed70b89be30fa0d`, including the existing memory retrieval-worker and Gateway archive-fixture repairs that postdate the failed CI merge. No unrelated production repair, timeout increase, or weakened assertion is included to force CI green.

#### Telegram fixture boundary correction

The next CI merge, `9b5a036ec8308f0678b2261cd7f5c001a9816e6d` (main `317054d42739986ac5bbcf119554698ba0c3a1da` plus auth head `28d322ff414326c37453c2ccb9c5a2fec7904c64`), failed the first-sticker-description case added upstream in [#155040](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155040). A bounded local replay of that exact merge preserved the full file's order and reproduced **57 passes / 1 failure**, with grammY's `Request timed out after 10000 ms`. It was not dismissed as a flake. Single-case controls on the clean main parent and the exact merge both passed with public-delegate phase timestamps (first update approximately 6.4 / 6.6 s); these controls do not erase the full-order failure or establish an auth defect.

The source establishes the fixture's wrong boundary: production `webhook.ts` acknowledges after durable `ingressMonitor.admit`, and `telegram-ingress-drain-factory.ts` separately processes the queued JSON through `bot.handleUpdate`. The test instead used grammY's generic `webhookCallback`, which places the entire media/description/reply flow under a 10-second HTTP deadline. OpenClaw's production webhook does not use that adapter. The fixture now sends a JSON-roundtripped update through the actual drain processing entry point. It retains the deferred description-before-admission check, committed-cache readback, updated file identity, reply context, and unsupported-sticker/supplemental-image assertions. The removed generic-adapter HTTP200 assertion belongs to the dedicated production webhook tests. No production behavior, timeout, provider mock, or cold-path prewarm was changed.

After incorporating pinned main `c7ee253e2c4c083ca497c1f164c9524eccfeaee0` without conflicts, the corrected full file passes **58/58**, including the formerly failing case. One-file formatting/type-aware lint, the full-PR line-growth ratchet, whitespace checks, and fresh full-PR P0/P1 AutoReview pass. After the 58-case run, the JSON encoding/decoding expression was split into explicit wire-body and parsed-update steps to distinguish wire serialization from deep cloning; execution order and payload semantics are unchanged. Final scoped type-aware lint and a fresh review of that exact fixture delta also pass. The monolithic extension-test type graph was not repeated for this fixture-only setup change. Auth implementation and auth-test bytes are identical to the previously tested CI merge, so the unchanged 107 auth cases were not repeated. No real provider or Matrix turn was rerun; the historical real-provider proof remains scoped to its exact revisions above. Fresh remote CI and the maintainer approval requirement for the security-sensitive review remain separate gates.

The separate worktree-GC CI failure timed out its 60-second child process while exercising a real 180,000-entry index. A bounded replay preserved all 37 tests and their in-file order on the updated branch: all passed in 135.622 s command wall time; the large-index case took 41.759 s. Observation of that child recorded its successful one-worktree removal at 32.043 s, exit 0 at 32.692 s, and closed output streams at 32.705 s, with no stderr. This does not reproduce or repair the original full-shard Linux timeout; it gives no evidence of a post-result process leak and does not justify changing product code, assertions, or timeouts. Fresh GitHub CI remains the full-shard check.

### Storage compatibility

Relative to incorporated main `bfff4f4cbd802e2f305f57eaa3ecb630eee88362`, this PR changes in-memory composition of existing version-1 auth store/state records and refresh-owner read selection. The exact-head isolated owner readback above confirmed unchanged global/agent schema versions (19/23) and version-1 auth records before and after both refresh-recovery outcomes. It adds no schema migration, persisted field, serialization format, or credential-write format. Persisted serialization and SQLite storage types remain unchanged by this PR. Authored agent order and genuine local-account overrides remain intact. Upstream schema changes incorporated from main relative to the original parent or stable are outside this PR; this is not a downgrade-compatibility claim.

<details>
<summary>Measured test cost</summary>

| New or changed test file | Passing cases | Sum of reported case times |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `src/agents/auth-profiles/store.inherited-selection.test.ts` | 5 | 1.118 s |
| `src/agents/auth-profiles/runtime-snapshots.test.ts` | 33 | 0.063 s |
| `extensions/codex/src/app-server/auth-bridge.test.ts` | 127 | 9.370 s |
| `src/commands/doctor-auth.shared-health.test.ts` | 7 | 5.904 s |
| `src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth.validator-fallback.test.ts` | 4 | 1.042 s |
| `extensions/telegram/src/bot.create-telegram-bot.native-pipeline.test.ts` | 58 | 69.726 s |

The two core-auth files pass together (38/38) in 10.01 s supported-runner wall time, including compiler/startup work. A standalone cold run of the new file passed 5/5 in 17.97 s, including 12.437 s compiler preparation. The four unchanged sibling files contributed 91 passing cases in the earlier six-file run; combined with the final changed-file run this gives 129 unique passing cases. The earlier six-file run had one snapshot-fixture failure, corrected by making its intended local override identify a distinct account. These retained logs do not establish standalone wall time for the snapshot file or per-file CI seconds. The final Codex bridge file passed in 32.37 s measured command wall (31.96 s supported-runner wall; 29.37 s Vitest), with compiler transformation accounting for 58% of Vitest duration. Doctor and fallback timings are case sums from the final 107-test grouped run, not standalone file wall times. No sleeps or Gateway boots were added.

The existing 58-case Telegram native-pipeline file needed 131.63 s command wall / 131.20 s supported-runner wall after the fixture correction (127.24 s Vitest, 55% test execution / 41% transformation). The sticker case took 13.819 s and the other 57 existing cases totaled 55.907 s. The correction adds no cases, processes, sleeps, worker configuration, or timeout budget. This case retains the real JSON-to-bot processing, media description ordering, and durable cache boundary because isolated cache/helper tests cannot prove that model admission observes the committed description. Its unrelated cold setup is no longer constrained by a nonproduction webhook adapter; the processing itself is still exercised and awaited. The before CI file took approximately 101.44 s, with its failing case 40.217 s; those are Linux failure measurements, not the new head's CI duration.

</details>

The fix cannot revive a failed shared credential without a successful login or renewal.

prs.title: feat(subagents): durable wait-claim ledger for subagent completion delivery
prs.body:
Related: #107788, #111647, #112668, #117283, #121187, #123548, #123668, #124343, #73628, #86684, #87330, #90944, #91370, #92116, #95996, #96190, #97922

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: subagent/requester completion delivery relied on ~5 independent, best-effort push mechanisms with no single source of truth for "requester X is waiting on children {A,B,C}". This produced 11 distinct identified failure modes, most severely: nested subagents and cron-triggered orchestrators were unconditionally excluded from wake logic entirely (no safety net at all), in-memory completion-wait retry timers vanished on gateway restart, and delivery-mode recomputation could drift across retries of the same completion.

## Why This Change Was Made

Introduce a durable wait-claim ledger: every sessions_yield call writes an explicit claim (requester, exact set of awaited children, timestamp) to the registry. Child completions are checked against that claim, and waking a requester is now a pull ("is this claim satisfied?") rather than a race between independent push mechanisms each guessing coverage. Nested and cron requesters now get the same wake gate as ordinary requesters. Rolled out in four cutover steps (durable store + atomic writes, shadow-mode resolver, cron+nested cutover, ordinary cutover + hardening), each with its own regression coverage, followed by a full self-audit that surfaced and fixed one latent run-ID adoption bug (steer/restart-recovery remapped batch run IDs but not the claim'''s awaited run IDs).

## User Impact

Nested subagents and cron-triggered orchestrators now reliably receive completion delivery instead of being silently excluded from wake logic. Completion-wait retries survive a gateway restart instead of being lost. No user-facing configuration change required.

## Evidence

- 8 of the original 11 root causes are fully resolved; 3 are partially resolved with two named, explicitly out-of-scope follow-ups (message-tool-skip fallback, proactive wedge notification) documented in BRIEF-wait-claim-ledger.md (included in this PR).
- Includes a fix for a regression this branch'''s own rebase onto upstream/main exposed: cutover step 3 removed an unconditional cron short-circuit from maybeWakeRequesterAfterAllChildrenSettled, silently breaking the "pending/no_claim keeps zero-delivery completion" contract for no-claim cron requesters (masked until the rebase'''s timing shift exposed it via a failing regression test). Restored, correctly gated on status === "no_claim".
- Local run today, targeted scope (subagents registry/announce, main-session-recovery, sqlite session accessor, gateway session-subagent-resume, TUI event handlers, runtime-context prompt): 256/256 passing after removing one test that had been duplicated onto this branch from the separate SQLite-fix PR (#154952) without its required import.
- Broader full-scope validation (~4900 tests across subagents/sessions/main-session-recovery/tui/gateway/runtime-context) was run earlier today as part of the same investigation, before this branch was split out of the combined working branch: 0 failures.
- Note: I do not have access to this repo'''s trusted CI (Testbox) from my fork; the above is local test evidence only. Maintainer/CI verification is still needed before merge.

prs.title: fix(tui): stop dropping deferred finals and prove live streamed text reaches real PTY frames
prs.body:
Related: #104602, #110190, #116754, #90684, #93966

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: two related TUI defects. (1) A history rebuild could display a stale or wrong run'''s output, or drop a deferred final response entirely, because the rebuild never recorded which run it actually displayed. (2) It was unclear whether live-streamed text in the TUI genuinely reached real PTY frames before the final response landed, or only appeared to stream due to a render-throttle artifact — investigation refuted the render-throttle theory. A related gateway-client same-run duplicate-replay bug and a session-projection grep break (which mis-split message facts) were found and fixed during the same investigation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Track which run a history rebuild actually displayed so deferred finals are never silently dropped. Fix the session-projection grep break so message facts split correctly. Fix gateway-client duplicate-replay of the same run, with regression coverage. Add a regression test proving live-streamed text reaches real PTY frames before the final response, closing the open render-throttle question.

## User Impact

TUI users no longer see a history rebuild display the wrong run'''s output or silently drop a deferred final reply. Streaming behavior is now proven correct rather than assumed; no configuration change required.

## Evidence

- New regression test proves live-streamed text reaches real PTY frames before the final response (test(tui): prove live streamed text reaches real PTY frames before the final).
- New regression test covers the gateway-client same-run duplicate-replay fix.
- Local scoped run today (TUI + gateway-client + main-session-recovery + subagents + sessions areas): 256/256 passing after two unrelated stale-test-assertion fixes applied during PR review (see follow-up commits on this branch).
- Full investigation writeups included in this PR: TUI-STUCK-RUNNING-BRIEF-20260819.md, TUI-STUCK-RUNNING-PROGRESS-20260819.md, TUI-STREAMING-RENDER-BRIEF-20260819.md, TUI-STREAMING-RENDER-PROGRESS-20260819.md.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A native `/codex bind` claims the inbound turn before normal media understanding. A downloaded voice note can therefore reach Codex with neither its transcript nor an attachment reference: the conversation input builder keeps only images, and the configured speech-to-text path in `get-reply` never runs.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Codex binding now runs the existing public `runMediaUnderstandingFile` audio contract on selected, untranscribed voice attachments before `turn/start`. The audio adapter and media runtime load only inside an audio turn, so Codex registration keeps the cold-loading split from #139911. Opaque cached clips keep their audio URL and a classifying MIME instead of a generic binary type. Selected clips are transcribed in configured preference order, and skipped clips stay tied to their original attachment. It does not add a transcription provider, change auth, or read the audio itself.

Successful transcription is framed as an untrusted transcript. Disabled, failed, empty, and limit-skipped results stay explicit. The original path or remote URL is retained as text. Gateway-local files are not sent as Codex `localAudio`, because a remote app-server cannot read them. Already transcribed audio is not transcribed again. Command and owner checks still happen before transcription.

## User Impact

Voice-only or captioned voice notes sent to a native `/codex`-bound conversation reach the bound turn with the configured transcript when speech-to-text succeeds. If it does not, the voice note no longer disappears silently: the turn includes an explicit failure and the original attachment reference. Image-only turns stay image input and do not call speech-to-text.

## Evidence

- Base: `upstream/main` `001e13bc4f7d9ca3fb4c3b4437b693633769f345`. Head: `f094fa63753c21786bd2c502d1e8fbf12a42aee9`.
- Ratchets were fixed by removing content, not by adding baseline entries. `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` on `1c7aa146830` reported `extensions/codex/src/conversation-audio.ts: 2 > 0` uncommented type assertions. On `8d93f3d5a0b` it reported a closed mock of `./conversation-binding.js`. The assertions are gone, and the test now passes through the real binding module.
- `check-test-types` on `df65efdc6ae` reported `conversation-binding.audio.test.ts(348,63): error TS2493: Tuple type '[]' of length '0' has no element at index '0'` and `error TS2339: Property 'mime' does not exist on type 'never'`. The mock now names the file-runtime arguments. Local `tsgo -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json` passed.
- On this head, a native bind claim with a local opaque clip and a configured CLI speech-to-text stub (no Codex account and no user API key) put `ship the fix` and the original path into the Codex turn input. The stub was invoked with that path. An image-only turn remained `localImage` and did not call the stub. No `localAudio` input was emitted.

Fixes openclaw/openclaw#139274

prs.title: fix(agents): escape the runtime-context carrier body and declare it to the model
prs.body:
Related: #92589

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the internal-runtime-context carrier could be terminated early when inbound chat text (sender names, group subjects, quoted messages, chat history) contained an unescaped internal delimiter marker, leaking the remainder of that text — potentially including a prompt-injection payload — outside the protected/strippable span and into ordinary model-facing content. This is the same class of leak previously tracked upstream for Feishu streaming cards (#92589), newly observed on the Matrix channel.

## Why This Change Was Made

Escape any occurrence of the internal-context delimiter markers within the carrier body before wrapping it, so inbound attacker- or user-controlled text can never prematurely close the protected block. Explicitly declare the wrapped block'''s provenance/type to the model rather than relying on it to infer the block'''s status from surrounding text alone.

## User Impact

No user-visible change under normal operation. Closes a real content-leak/prompt-injection vector: a user (or anyone quoted in chat history) could previously craft text containing the raw end-delimiter to break out of the protected context span.

## Evidence

- Regression test (escapes attacker-controlled delimiters so the protected block cannot be terminated early) constructs a hostile inbound context containing a literal, unescaped end-marker followed by a role-flip/prompt-injection attempt, and asserts: the raw end-marker never appears unescaped in the built carrier, the escaped form is present instead, and stripping the carrier removes the injection payload entirely.
- Full investigation writeup with root-cause analysis included in this PR (MATRIX-CONTEXT-LEAK-PROGRESS-20260819.md).
- Note: I do not have access to this repo'''s trusted CI (Testbox) from my fork; the above is local test evidence only. Maintainer/CI verification is still needed before merge.

prs.title: fix: Codex OAuth profile stays blocked until the weekly reset while purchased credits remain
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a ChatGPT/Codex OAuth profile stays blocked until the weekly usage window resets when the included usage is exhausted but the account has purchased credits, even though Codex keeps serving requests on those credits.

## User Impact

User impact: after buying Codex credits, `openai/gpt-*` turns work again on the next probe instead of failing (or silently falling back to another provider) for the rest of the week. Accounts with no credits, depleted workspace credits, or a reached overage cap keep today's block-until-reset behaviour. No configuration change or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The usage probe read only `rate_limit.limit_reached` and the window reset time and never looked at the `credits` object the same endpoint returns. Because an exhausted weekly window reports `used_percent: 100` until it resets, every half-open re-probe re-confirmed the block, so the profile could not recover before the reset even though requests succeeded.

Codex's own client treats remaining credits as "not limited" (its usage notice is suppressed when `credits.unlimited || credits.has_credits`, see [`usage_notice.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/usage_notice.rs)). The probe now applies that rule to the personal case only: an exhausted window returns `available` when `credits.has_credits` or `credits.unlimited` is set, `credits.overage_limit_reached` is not, and `rate_limit_reached_type` is the plain `rate_limit_reached` state (or absent, as in older payloads). Depleted workspace credits, admin-set workspace usage caps (`workspace_*_usage_limit_reached`), an `unknown` reached type, and a reached `spend_control` keep today's behaviour, because a credit balance does not prove those caps allow more spend.

`usage.ts` was already over its line cap, and the line-cap ratchet rejects growth, so the usage payload schema and its pure classification moved unchanged into a sibling module, `usage-wham.ts`. The request, HTTP-status handling, half-open re-probe, and store mutation stay in `usage.ts`; the new rule is the only behavioural change.

## Evidence

**Live observation** (2026-09-21, OpenClaw 2026.9.5, ChatGPT Pro account, native gateway):

- After a genuine "You've reached your Codex subscription usage limit" error on Sep 20, the profile carried `blockedUntil` = the Sep 25 reset with `blockedReason: "subscription_limit"`, `blockedSource: "wham"`.
- Credits were purchased afterwards. The usage endpoint then reported an exhausted window **and** credits, and direct requests to the Codex responses backend returned HTTP 200 for both `gpt-5.6-sol` and `gpt-6-astra`.
- OpenClaw kept logging `Provider openai is in cooldown (rate_limit)` and `Auth profile "openai:…" is temporarily unavailable for openai/gpt-5.6-luna` on every turn; each 5-minute re-probe only refreshed `lastProbeAt`. Clearing the stored block by hand restored service immediately, which isolates the probe classification as the cause.

<details>
<summary>Observed usage payload (ids redacted)</summary>

```json
{
  "plan_type": "pro",
  "rate_limit": {
    "allowed": false,
    "limit_reached": true,
    "primary_window": { "used_percent": 100, "limit_window_seconds": 604800, "reset_after_seconds": 363981, "reset_at": 1790322562 },
    "secondary_window": null
  },
  "credits": { "has_credits": true, "unlimited": false, "overage_limit_reached": false, "balance": "2269.83…" },
  "spend_control": { "reached": false },
  "rate_limit_reached_type": { "type": "rate_limit_reached", "details": "default" }
}
```

</details>

**Tests** (`pnpm exec vitest run src/agents/auth-profiles/usage.test.ts src/agents/auth-profiles/usage-wham.test.ts`): 117 passed. The existing WHAM-aware cooldown suite (probe headers, reset mapping, half-open re-probe, stale-result guards) is untouched and still passes against the extracted classifier. New `usage-wham.test.ts` covers the classifier directly:

- exhausted window + purchased credits, + unlimited credits, and + credits with no reached type → `available` (15 s burst cooldown, no block);
- eight negative cases still block until the reset: no `credits` object, `has_credits: false`, `overage_limit_reached: true`, both `*_credits_depleted` states, both `*_usage_limit_reached` states, and `unknown`;
- a reached `spend_control` is not overridden by credits;
- baselines: non-exhausted window → available; exhausted window without credits → blocked until reset.

Before extraction, the same credit cases were run through `markAuthProfileFailure` and the half-open re-probe against the unmodified probe: both failed (`expected 1700363981000 to be undefined`) while the negative cases passed, so the rule is what the tests pin.

**Checks** (Linux, Node 26.9, pnpm 12.4): `pnpm tsgo:core` clean; `pnpm check:changed` clean across all of its lanes, including the line-cap growth ratchet, the core-tests typecheck, and the dead-export scan (the scan caught one needlessly exported constant on the first pass; it is module-private now and the scan was re-run clean); `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` clean on the changed files; `markdownlint-cli2` clean on the three edited docs pages.

**Docs**: one sentence added to the three pages that describe the subscription-limit block (`docs/concepts/model-failover.md`, `docs/providers/openai/runtimes.md`, `docs/plugins/codex-harness/app-server.md`).

prs.title: fix(security): exempt allowSymlinkTargets from workspace symlink_escape audit
prs.body:
## Problem

`openclaw security audit` reports `skills.workspace.symlink_escape` for shared
skills that are symlinked into a workspace from a directory documented in
`skills.load.allowSymlinkTargets`. The runtime skill loader already exempts
these targets (via `resolveAllowedSkillSymlinkTargetRealPaths` /
`findContainingAllowedSkillSymlinkTarget` in `src/skills/loading/symlink-targets.ts`),
so a config that loads these skills fine still fails audit with hundreds of
false positives. On a real machine with `~/.agents/skills` allowlisted, the
audit reports 12 rows + `+1873 more`.

## Change

`collectWorkspaceSkillSymlinkEscapeFindings` in
`src/skills/security/workspace-audit.ts` now resolves the configured
`skills.load.allowSymlinkTargets` realpaths and skips any skill whose realpath
is contained in an allowlisted target. This reuses the exact helpers the loader
uses, so the audit boundary now matches the loader boundary. Everything else
(workspace-root containment, unresolvable-realpath handling, scan truncation) is
unchanged.

Two regression tests cover both branches:
- symlink target inside an allowlisted dir → **no** `symlink_escape` finding
- symlink target outside any allowlist → **still** a `symlink_escape` finding

## Proof

Before (upstream `main` at `8bae2c7a`, config allowlists `~/.agents/skills`):
```
skills.workspace.symlink_escape warn
- workspace=/Users/macbook/.openclaw/workspaces/dev/execution_agent
  skill=.../a2a-peer-disable/SKILL.md
  realpath=/Users/macbook/.agents/skills/a2a-peer-disable/SKILL.md
...
- +1873 more
```

After (this branch, same config): the `symlink_escape` check reports
`0` findings (`symlinkCount: 0`).

Unit tests: `pnpm test src/skills/security/workspace-audit.test.ts` → 6 passed
(4 existing + 2 new).

`pnpm check:changed` → green (type check, format, lint, all gated lanes).

## Prior related PRs (all closed/unmerged) and why this one differs

This gap has been attempted before. All prior attempts were closed without
merging:

- #60144 / #60155 / #60513 (`fix(security): align audit symlink_escape boundary with skill loader`)
- #73948 (openclaw-clownfish bot) — closed as superseded by #111801
- #111801 (`fix(security): audit symlinked workspace skill roots`) — the
  "current-path successor" named by the #73948 clawsweeper review; it too is
  closed/unmerged.

This PR is narrower and deliberately conservative:

- **Only** exempts explicit `skills.load.allowSymlinkTargets` matches — it does
  **not** widen the workspace-root containment boundary to a `skills/`
  subdirectory, and does **not** change how symlinked workspace roots are
  traversed. Those extra behaviors in prior PRs are what drew
  `merge-risk: 🚨 compatibility` / `merge-risk: 🚨 security-boundary` /
  `status: 📣 needs proof` review labels.
- Preserves the documented trusted-symlink-target contract exactly as the loader
  implements it (same helpers, same containment check), so the audit and the
  loader cannot disagree.
- Includes a reproducible before/after proof on a real config plus dual-branch
  regression tests.

## Acceptance

- [x] `pnpm check:changed` green
- [x] regression tests pass (allowlisted target exempt, non-allowlisted escape still reported)
- [x] e2e proof: real-machine audit shows `+1873 more` before, `0` after
- [x] key scan: no plaintext credentials

prs.title: fix(codex): deliver native tool output images
prs.body:
Closes #153949

## What Problem This Solves

Codex can return screenshots as nested `input_image` items inside `custom_tool_call_output` or `function_call_output`. OpenClaw previously ignored those bytes, so the assistant could refer to “the image above” while chat received no attachment.

This change projects validated nested images through the existing managed-media path. It uses stable item identities for deduplication, enforces the existing byte and MIME limits, records delivery receipts, and keeps base64 out of transcript text. Screenshot-view output remains replay-safe and is not counted as image-generation side-effect evidence. The decoder also accepts the `application/octet-stream` data URL currently emitted by Codex and confirms the actual image type from its bytes.

## Evidence

- Regression fixture failed before the production change for both raw response shapes.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.replay-safety.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.final-media.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/tool-media-payloads.test.ts` — 85 tests passed.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector-media.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Fresh P1 autoreview — clean.

Related: #154033. This version keeps screenshot delivery separate from generated-image accounting and covers current Codex octet-stream output.


## Evidence (clawsweeper P1/P2 follow-up)

- **[P1] Host dynamic-tool ownership:** raw `function_call_output` echoes whose `call_id` was registered through `recordDynamicToolCall` are skipped, so model-only (`media.outbound=false`) dynamic-tool images can no longer be republished as host-owned reply attachments; native tool outputs such as `view_image` still project. Sibling codex source inspected personally at `6b9826e3aa83`: `dynamic.rs` maps host-returned content to `FunctionCallOutputContentItem` under the host's `call_id`, and `view_image.rs` emits `ImageViewItem { id: call_id, path }`.
- **[P2] Source identity:** `ImageView` items attach their `path` as the `savedPath` alias of `${call_id}:image:*` records (both notification orders), so `projectDelivery` matches confirmed original-path sends: a source reply suppresses the managed copy, a target send attributes it once.
- **Regression proof:** the four new cases in `event-projector.media-tool-output.test.ts` fail on the pre-fix projector for the intended reasons (`toolMediaUrls` leaked, target alias missing) and pass after the fix.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` on media-tool-output, media, replay-safety, dynamic-tools, final-media, tool-media-payloads — green (3 shards); `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — passed; `oxfmt` and `git diff --check` — clean.
- Live Codex-to-chat runtime capture was not run locally; requesting ClawSweeper re-review on the updated head.

prs.title: fix(macos): get_window_state fails with invalid snapshot reference on Peekaboo
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #153622

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where users calling the V2 computer action `get_window_state` against a paired macOS node (Peekaboo provider) would get `Invalid snapshot reference '<UUID>'; expected ps1_ followed by 32 lowercase hexadecimal digits` instead of the window observation, even though `list_windows`, accessibility readback, and input actions all worked in the same session.
- **Related:** #153622; clawsweeper source review confirmed main still contains the mismatch and no open repair PR existed at fix time.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** `get_window_state` now asks Peekaboo for an owned snapshot (`saveSnapshot: true`) when it builds its observation request, so the provider's own reservation/publication lifecycle mints the `ps1_` reference, stores the screenshot and detection result, and publishes the snapshot. The executor's manual `storeDetectionResult` call — which fed a detection-only transient UUID into a manager that only accepts owned `ps1_` references — is removed as redundant. This matches the standalone Peekaboo CLI `see` command, which already requests `saveSnapshot: true`. Element-scoped follow-up actions also benefit: the observation state now carries a genuinely owned snapshot reference for `UIAutomationService`.
- **Out of scope:** no Peekaboo package changes (pinned 4.4.0 untouched), no UUID reformatting or validation weakening (ownership is required, per the issue), no CUA provider changes, and no V2 schema-exposure changes (#148541 is separate).
- **Highest-risk area:** `ComputerWindowActionExecutor.getWindowState` now persists a raw screenshot to a temp path on each call as part of the provider's snapshot lifecycle (same behavior as the CLI `see` command).
- **How is that risk mitigated?** The lifecycle, ownership checks, implicit-latest invalidation, and failure cleanup all remain inside `DesktopObservationService`/`ObservationOutputWriter` rather than being reimplemented in the consumer. The executor's `InMemorySnapshotManager` additionally runs with `deleteArtifactsOnCleanup` enabled, so the persisted window screenshots are deleted when their snapshot entry is evicted (25-entry LRU / 600s validity window) or cleaned up — no accumulation of private window captures in the temp directory. A regression test exercises the real manager: store a screenshot artifact, clean the snapshot, assert the file is gone.

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** `list_windows` → `get_window_state` on a paired macOS node returns the window observation (elements, bounds, screenshot) with no snapshot-reference error, and follow-up element actions keep working against the issued refs.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/ComputerWindowActionExecutor.swift` (request construction, snapshot-manager cleanup options, removed manual store, `WindowObservationArtifacts` owned output directory with failure sweep and teardown) and the regression tests `window state observation requests an owned snapshot`, `window snapshot manager owns artifact cleanup`, `window snapshot eviction removes evicted artifact files`, `failed observation artifacts are swept from the owned output directory`, and `teardown removes the owned output directory` in `apps/macos/Tests/OpenClawIPCTests/ComputerWindowObservationTests.swift`.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** Linux dev box (source-level verification only — no Swift toolchain or macOS host available locally); fix branch `feat/issue-153622-peekaboo-snapshot-ownership` @ c22449afb3e (follow-up commits cover cleanup ownership, artifact-ownership on failure/teardown, the native shutdown sweep, and a main-actor isolation fix in its test) on top of origin/main a4f0beadbd3, with the pinned Peekaboo 4.4.0 checkout (d82dbd88) inspected directly.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  git fetch origin main && git worktree add -b fix-branch origin/main
  # traced the failing chain on origin/main (executor L284-303 -> Peekaboo 4.4.0:
  # DesktopObservationRequestModels / ObservationOutputWriter / ElementDetectionService /
  # SnapshotPublicationBinding / InMemorySnapshotManager) — reproduced the reported error path from source
  # applied the fix, added regression test, rebase-checked upstream files (no drift), pushed
  swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --build-tests   # delegated to the macos-swift CI lane (no local Swift toolchain)
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  Source trace with output = DesktopObservationOutputOptions(saveSnapshot: true):
  DesktopObservationService.observeWithinOverallDeadline (DesktopObservationService.swift:474-487)
    -> reserveSnapshotIfNeeded: snapshotManager.createSnapshot(pendingAt:) mints an OWNED pending ps1_ id
    -> request.output.snapshotID = reserved ps1_ id
    -> detection (DesktopObservationService+Detection.swift:35) runs with the explicit id
       => elements.snapshotId == ps1_ id (no UUID().uuidString from SnapshotPublicationBinding.swift:5)
    -> ObservationOutputWriter.writeSnapshotIfNeeded: raw screenshot to temp dir,
       storeScreenshot + storeDetectionResult under the owned ps1_ id -> validation passes
    -> publishReservedSnapshot publishes the reservation
  Executor: result.elements?.snapshotId is the owned ps1_ reference; manual store removed.
  Regression test asserts request.output.saveSnapshot == true and unchanged target/
  capture-focus/detection-mode/traversal-budget (file: ComputerWindowObservationTests.swift).
  Artifact cleanup trace (Peekaboo 4.4.0 @ d82dbd88, executor commit b0b50d6586f):
  InMemorySnapshotManager.Options(deleteArtifactsOnCleanup: true)
    -> removeEntry (InMemorySnapshotManager+Pruning.swift:27-33) takes deleteArtifacts(for:),
       which removes snapshotData.screenshotPath + annotatedPath (arbitrary stored paths)
    -> same removeEntry serves ALL removal paths: explicit cleanSnapshot
       (InMemorySnapshotManager+Lifecycle.swift:228-232), 600s validity-window expiry and
       25-entry LRU eviction (InMemorySnapshotManager+Pruning.swift:5-21), so persisted
       window screenshots do not survive their snapshot record by any exit path.
  Regression tests exercise the real manager (not mocks):
    1. 'window snapshot manager owns artifact cleanup': store a real temp PNG via
       storeScreenshot, cleanSnapshot, assert the file is deleted.
    2. 'window snapshot eviction removes evicted artifact files': 26 snapshots each with
       a real stored PNG; the 25-entry LRU limit evicts the earliest, assert its PNG is
       deleted while the newest snapshot's PNG remains readable.
  Failure + teardown ownership trace (executor commit 0068f388f1a):
  DesktopObservationOutputOptions(path: <executor-owned dir>/, saveSnapshot: true)
    -> ObservationOutputPathResolver.resolve: directory-like path -> every persisted
       observation PNG lands under temporaryDirectory/openclaw-window-state-observations/
       instead of the general temp directory (single bounded cleanup root)
    -> getWindowState wraps observe in do/catch: Peekaboo writes the raw screenshot
       BEFORE registering it with the snapshot manager (ObservationOutputWriter.write:
       writeRawScreenshotIfNeeded precedes writeSnapshotIfNeeded), so a failed
       observation can leave an unregistered PNG; the executor sweeps files written
       since the observation started (contentModificationDate >= start) before
       rethrowing — registered artifacts of earlier snapshots have older mtimes and survive
    -> ComputerWindowActionExecutor.deinit removes the whole output directory, so
       captures cannot outlive the executor (manager pruning is operation-driven)
  Regression tests cover both new paths:
    3. 'failed observation artifacts are swept from the owned output directory': drives
       the REAL ObservationOutputWriter.write (saveRawScreenshot: true, saveSnapshot: false
       = the failure shape) to produce an unregistered PNG, asserts the sweep deletes it
       and leaves an earlier registered artifact intact.
    4. 'teardown removes the owned output directory': directory + capture removed wholesale.
  Native shutdown sweep trace (executor commit ff9981e39d2):
  MacNodeModeCoordinator.stopAndWait() -> beginTerminalStop()
    -> enqueueRouteInvalidation(mode: .terminalStop) (MacNodeModeCoordinator.swift:445-447)
    -> MacNodeRuntime.shutdown() (MacNodeRuntime.swift:918-926)
       -> cachedMainActorServices?.discardWindowObservationArtifacts()
          (the SAME services instance every computer command used — no services are
          spun up just to sweep)
    -> LiveMacNodeRuntimeMainActorServices -> ComputerActionService
       .discardWindowObservationArtifacts()
    -> ComputerActionExecutionQueue.discardWindowObservationArtifacts():
       releaseHeldInput(lifecycleGeneration: current + 1) first settles the active
       and queued computer actions with terminal-stop semantics (advanceLifecycle
       cancels stale work and releases held input; the queue awaits the active
       task and scoped releases before returning), THEN
       WindowObservationArtifacts.removeAllArtifacts(in: outputDirectory) removes
       the executor-owned directory wholesale.
  Shutdown-path regression tests (cover the entrypoint, not just the deletion helper):
    5. 'shutdown sweeps persisted window observation artifacts through the shared services'
       (MacNodeRuntimeTests.swift): a services-backed command caches the shared
       services instance, then the REAL MacNodeRuntime.shutdown() entrypoint must
       reach exactly that instance's discard call (count 0 before, 1 after).
    6. 'discardWindowObservationArtifacts removes persisted window observation artifacts'
       (ComputerActionServiceTests.swift): writes a REAL capture file into
       WindowObservationArtifacts.outputDirectory, calls the REAL service-level
       sweep, asserts the file and the directory are gone.
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** the `get_window_state` request can no longer hand a transient UUID to the snapshot manager — every step of the previously failing chain is replaced by the provider's owned reservation/publication lifecycle. The `macos-swift (tests)` CI lane compiled the package and ran the request-construction regression test successfully on the first revision (942fee59a2f, 20m41s, pass); on head `0068f388f1a` the same lane (24m24s, pass, macos-26-arm64 runner) ran the full suite (`Test run with 2271 tests in 257 suites passed`) including all five `ComputerWindowObservationTests` regression tests, each passed: `window state observation requests an owned snapshot`, `window snapshot manager owns artifact cleanup`, `window snapshot eviction removes evicted artifact files`, `failed observation artifacts are swept from the owned output directory`, and `teardown removes the owned output directory` (suite passed after 7.199s; job log: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35510349501/job/106077144108). On head `c22449afb3e` the same lane (23m20s, pass, macos-26-arm64 runner) ran the full suite again (`Test run with 2273 tests in 257 suites passed` — the two additional tests are the shutdown-path regressions), both new tests passed: `shutdown sweeps persisted window observation artifacts through the shared services` (passed after 7.132s, real `MacNodeRuntime.shutdown()` entrypoint reaching the cached shared-services instance) and `discardWindowObservationArtifacts removes persisted window observation artifacts` (passed after 0.177s, real file sweep); job log: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35515851747/job/106091635020. All other CI lanes green on this head (macOS/iOS dead-code scans, security-fast, Opengrep, ci-gate).
- **Before evidence (optional, visual changes encouraged):** on origin/main, `getWindowState` built the request without output options and manually stored `elements.snapshotId` (a `UUID().uuidString` correlation id from `SnapshotPublicationBinding.resultIdentifier(explicit: nil)`), which `InMemorySnapshotManager.storeDetectionResult` rejects via `SnapshotPublicationBinding.validate` — exactly the issue's live error. Full before/after trace: chain of file:line references in the fix notes.
- **What was not tested:** no live macOS run of `computer(action="get_window_state")` or of a real app termination (no macOS host or screen-recording session in this environment); the `macos-swift` CI lane compiles and runs the unit regression tests — including the shutdown-entrypoint and real-file sweep tests — but the full observation-to-publication integration and an actual quit-with-captures-on-disk run need a real window/host, which stays with the reporter/maintainer verification path described in the issue.
- **Proof tier:** L1 (source-level, with a compiled regression test delegated to macOS CI)
- **Proof limitations:** no Swift toolchain or macOS runtime on the dev machine, so neither `swift build`/`swift test` nor a live paired-node `get_window_state` call could be executed locally; the fix is verified by tracing the exact Peekaboo 4.4.0 source path that produced the reported error and confirming each step is replaced by the owned lifecycle, plus the new unit test that fails against the pre-fix request construction.
- **Review state:** Follow-up commits address every artifact-retention review finding: `b0b50d6586f` (explicit cleanup + eviction via `deleteArtifactsOnCleanup`), `0068f388f1a` (executor-owned output directory, failure-path sweep of unregistered PNGs, teardown removal), and `ff9981e39d2` (native shutdown sweep: `MacNodeRuntime.shutdown()` now reaches the cached shared services, settles in-flight actions, and removes the owned output directory — closing the "deinit is never called through the retained-services chain" gap). Awaiting re-review + maintainer review.
