prs.title: docs: add Neon AI Gateway provider guide
prs.body:
No linked issue: a search of open and closed items for this gateway returned nothing, so there is no prior context to reference.

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Neon AI Gateway is an OpenAI-compatible inference endpoint that reaches models from OpenAI, Google, Meta, Databricks, and Alibaba behind a single Neon credential. OpenClaw can already talk to it today through the generic custom-provider config, but nothing in the docs says so, so a user has to work the whole setup out from scratch.

The parts that are easy to get wrong, and that cost real debugging time, are:

- Neon serves chat completions on `/v1` and the Responses-only Codex models on `/openai/v1`. Pointing one provider entry at both silently fails for half the catalog.
- Neon's own model catalog advertises PDF input, but `input` in an OpenClaw model entry accepts only `text`, `image`, `video`, and `audio` inside a `.strict()` object, so copying the catalog verbatim makes the whole config file fail to load.
- Omitting `cost` and `maxTokens` does not mean "unset". They resolve to all-zero costs and `min(8192, contextWindow)` respectively, which is invisible until a bill or a truncated reply shows up.
- `openclaw models set neon/...` does not verify the provider exists, so a missing or misspelled provider entry surfaces much later as an unresolved model rather than as an error at the point of the mistake.

There is also no navigation entry, so nothing points a reader at this option in the first place.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds one provider page plus the navigation, generated-map, and glossary updates that go with it. It is documentation only.

The page documents Neon as a **custom** provider configured under `models.providers.neon`, reached over OpenClaw's existing `openai-completions` and `openai-responses` transports. **It is not a plugin and it is not native support**, and the page says so twice: the property table lists `Plugin: none`, and a note states that `openclaw onboard` offers no Neon auth choice, so the config file is the only route. No provider id, manifest, auth choice, or catalog entry was added, and no source file was touched.

Scope boundaries worth calling out:

- Both endpoints are documented as two separate provider entries rather than one, because neither set of models answers on the other's path.
- Every host in every example is the placeholder `<your-neon-branch-host>`; no real or realistic branch hostname appears anywhere, and the page explains where to get the real value and that the placeholder will not work until replaced.
- Beta constraints that gate the whole feature (paid plan, `aws-us-east-2` only) are stated up front rather than buried.

Official Neon references used: [AI Gateway overview](https://neon.com/docs/ai-gateway/overview) and the [model catalog](https://neon.com/docs/ai-gateway/models).

## User Impact

Readers who use Neon can now find the gateway in the provider list and configure it from a worked example, including the two-endpoint split, the input-type limitation, and what the cost and output-token defaults actually resolve to. Nobody who does not use Neon is affected: there is no behavior change, no new config surface, and no runtime code in this PR.

## Evidence

Every factual claim on the page was re-read against this branch's base (`7edc234f6c`) rather than carried over from an earlier draft, because the base moved 189 commits during preparation. The only drift in the files this page depends on was one additive optional field (`supportsJsonSchemaResponseFormat`) in `ModelCompatSchema`, which the page does not use.

Verified directly in source:

- `input` accepts exactly `text`, `image`, `video`, `audio`, inside a `.strict()` object — `src/config/zod-schema.core.ts`
- `MODEL_APIS` contains both `openai-completions` and `openai-responses` — `src/config/types.models.ts`
- Custom providers must declare `baseUrl` and `models` — the `ModelProvidersSchema` `superRefine`; `neon` is not in `BUILT_IN_MODEL_PROVIDER_OVERLAY_IDS`, so both example entries satisfy it
- `DEFAULT_MODEL_COST` is all zeros and `DEFAULT_MODEL_MAX_TOKENS` resolves to `min(8192, contextWindow)` — `src/config/defaults.ts`
- No `neon` provider, manifest, or auth choice exists anywhere in `src/`

Checks run:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm docs:map:gen` then `pnpm docs:map:check` | Regenerated after rebase; check passes, 11-line insertion |
| `pnpm docs:check-i18n-glossary` | Pass |
| `pnpm docs:check-links` | Pass, 6,192 internal links, 0 broken |
| `pnpm docs:check-mdx` | Pass, 752 files |
| Strict MDX compile of the new page | Pass; deliberate broken-tag control fails as expected |
| Both `json5` config blocks vs. schema literals read out of the Zod source | Pass; the same script fails when `"pdf"` or a bogus `api` is reinserted |
| `docs.json` and `glossary.zh-CN.json` JSON parse | Pass; one Neon glossary entry, no duplicates in 412 entries |
| Alphabetical nav placement in `docs.json` and the provider index | Correct in both |
| `git diff --check` | Clean |
| Property-table pipe alignment | All 7 rows exactly 104 characters |
| Trailing whitespace, tabs, em/en dashes, curly quotes in added lines | 0 across 291 added lines |
| Headings free of em dashes and apostrophes; American spelling | Pass |

Checks **not** run, and why:

- `pnpm format:docs:check`, `pnpm lint:docs` — `node_modules` is absent in this checkout and could not be installed. The repo pins `pnpm@11.15.1`; corepack can only fetch it from `registry.npmjs.org`, which fails TLS verification behind an intercepting proxy here, and the reachable mirror does not carry that version. No TLS check was disabled and no registry or security policy was worked around. `oxfmt` is therefore unavailable, and the manual substitutes are the alignment, whitespace, and hygiene rows above.
- No test, typecheck, or build lane was run. This PR changes no source, so none apply.

**No live OpenClaw request was made against a Neon branch.** The page documents configuration and Neon's published behavior, not an observed run. Tool calling over the gateway is untested and the page stays silent on it. Two further gaps are stated on the page rather than papered over: the `gemini-3-flash` entry declares only `text` and `image` even though the catalog lists more, because delivering video or audio to this gateway was not verified; and `contextWindow: 131000` for the Qwen entry is the rounded catalog figure, since Neon publishes `131K` and returns `null` for `context_length`.

### AI assistance

- [x] **Marked as AI-assisted.** This PR was written with an AI coding agent.
- [x] Concise **Evidence** section included above.
- [x] I understand what the change does; it is documentation only and every claim is cited to a source file or to Neon's official docs.
- [ ] Prompts/session logs not attached.
- [ ] The `autoreview` skill was **not** run — it is not available in this environment. Flagging this rather than leaving the box implicitly ticked.
- [ ] Pull request review flow will be followed once Barnacle, ClawSweeper, or a maintainer responds.

Opened as a draft. Happy to adjust scope, wording, or placement before it goes up for review.

prs.title: feat(ui): thumb-reachable mobile navigation and touch ergonomics for the dashboard
prs.body: Related: #111837 (builds on that branch — merge it first; this diff includes its commit until then) ## What Problem This Solves Resolves a problem where the Control UI on phones is layout-correct but ergonomically desktop-shaped. All navigation funnels through the top-left hamburger — the hardest reach on a phone — so chat-first mobile users pay a two-tap drawer trip for every destination. The chat header exposes four unlabeled icon buttons with no touch tooltips, the command palette opens as a centered desktop box whose lower half the software keyboard covers (with keyboard-only hint copy on a touch screen), thread keys in the sessions table head-ellipsize into identical "agent:main:m…" stubs, and several composer/table controls are below-standard touch targets. ## Why This Change Was Made Presentation-only re-shaping of existing capability for touch; no behavior, route, or data changes. A mobile-only bottom tab bar (``, rendered by the app shell only in the mobile-nav state) gives one-tap access to Chat, Threads, and Activity plus a Menu tab that triggers the exact same drawer toggle as the topbar hamburger; content reserves the bar's height (safe-area aware), and short-landscape viewports hide the bar entirely. The chat pane header on merged mobile chrome collapses its three secondary actions (thread changes / background tasks / thread files) into one labeled "•••" menu built from the same action descriptors the inline desktop icons consume, so both render paths share one source of truth. The command palette becomes a top-anchored full-width sheet on coarse pointers (input on top, results below, keyboard hints hidden, ≥44px rows), scoped to the palette's modal class only. The viewport-anchored mobile model popover tracks the composer's new resting position through the same `--oc-tab-bar-height` variable rather than a duplicated offset. Session keys wrap at ≤500px instead of head-ellipsizing, and coarse-pointer checkboxes/composer buttons get ≥40–44px hit areas. Desktop renders byte-identically (all rules scoped to mobile shell state, mobile media queries, or `pointer: coarse`). ## User Impact On a phone, the dashboard now behaves like a mobile app: primary destinations are one thumb-tap away on a bottom tab bar with clear active states, chat header actions are labeled instead of cryptic, the palette works with the software keyboard instead of underneath it, thread rows are identifiable, and touch targets meet platform minimums. Desktop users see no change. ## Evidence - Full UI suite: **344 files passed / 4,944 tests passing** (`scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src`), including the previously-red `chat-responsive.browser.test.ts` popover cases (62/62) — a regression found during verification (tab-bar content reserve lifted the composer while the viewport-anchored model popover stayed put, covering its own trigger) was root-cause fixed in the popover's own positioning rule, not by touching tests. - Interactive Playwright verification at 390×844 and 360×800: tab-bar taps navigate to /chat, /sessions, /activity; Menu opens the same drawer as the hamburger and the drawer/backdrop layer above the bar; palette sheet anchors top with typing/filtering intact; every overflow-menu item fires the identical handler as its former inline icon (unit-tested in `chat-pane-header.test.ts`). - Desktop 1280×800 regression sweep: zero layout deltas, `openclaw-mobile-tab-bar` not rendered, palette/dialog unchanged; short-landscape 844×390 hides the bar and returns its reserved space. - i18n: one new key (`nav.menu`); keyless `ui:i18n:baseline` + `ui:i18n:verify` clean. `oxfmt` clean on all touched files. | Before (hamburger-only, desktop palette) | After (tab bar, labeled menu, palette sheet) | | --- | --- | | | | | | | | | | Chat header labeled menu and Threads tab active state: Deliberate non-goal (flagged for follow-up discussion): per-message delivery/failure states in chat — valuable on mobile but a behavior-adjacent change, out of scope for this presentation-only PR. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01FNfExBFYjQoN9XELa7143C

prs.title: fix(agents): prefer write/edit tools over heredocs to prevent literal-newline corruption
prs.body:
Fixes #114128

## What Problem This Solves

Agents writing multi-line Python via unquoted heredocs (`<<EOF`) or `bash -c` corrupt `\n` into literal backslash-n. This compiles-fails silently and can rot for weeks before discovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

The exec description now prefers dedicated file-writing tools over shell heredocs or `bash -c` for multi-line content, and names only the tools that survived filtering (`write`, `edit`, and/or `apply_patch`). A write-only session is told to prefer `write`, not the unavailable siblings. Tool permissions are not widened.

## User Impact

When a dedicated file-writing tool is available, agents are steered to that tool instead of a shell heredoc, so multiline files keep real newline bytes. Sessions that do not have those tools are not told to call them.

## Evidence

Live proof on `401c566eb96410ae5989f69a160784e7405a1222`, using the production tool finalizer plus the real exec and write tools (`--pool=forks`).

Exec-only session omits the guidance. With only `write` available, the description names `write` and the selected file tool is `write`. The real exec tool ran the historical unquoted heredoc and left literal backslash-n bytes (`5c6e`). The real write tool wrote the same intended Python and the file bytes contain newline bytes (`0a`) and match the requested content.

```

EXEC_ONLY_HAS_FILE_WRITES false
EXEC_ONLY_DESCRIPTION Run shell and wait for completion. Omit host to use the session's configured host. TTY CLI/UI/coding agent: pty=true. Quote arguments containing shell metacharacters, including URL query strings with `?` or `&`.
WRITE_ONLY_DESCRIPTION Run shell and wait for completion. Omit host to use the session's configured host. TTY CLI/UI/coding agent: pty=true. File writes: prefer dedicated file-writing tools (write) over shell heredocs or bash -c for multi-line content. Quote arguments containing shell metacharacters, including URL query strings with `?` or `&`.
SELECTED_FILE_TOOLS write
HEREDOC_EXEC_RESULT [{"type":"text","text":"(no output)"}]
HEREDOC_FILE_REPR "def greet():\\n    return \"ok\"\\n\n"
HEREDOC_FILE_HEX 64656620677265657428293a5c6e2020202072657475726e20226f6b225c6e0a
WRITE_TOOL_RESULT [{"type":"text","text":"Successfully wrote 29 bytes to /home/synth/.hermes/cache/scratch/oc-vt-w5SDu1/oc-117274-proof-E6H7A1/write.py"}]
```

prs.title: feat: show local provider processing and estimated wait time
prs.body:
Related: #137557

## What Problem This Solves

Slow local model calls report only wall time, which can hide a long wait behind a busy backend slot. Thanks to @Uraroga for the report and single-slot cancellation investigation.

## User Impact

Model diagnostics, provider request timelines, and `openclaw gateway stability` now separate server-reported processing from estimated wait for llama.cpp and native Ollama. Stability output labels total `wall`, `processing`, and `wait~`; cancellations without final statistics retain unknown processing.

The wait estimate includes queueing, loading, transport, and terminal settlement. It is retrospective and cannot prove when a backend released a cancelled slot. No configuration, migration, polling loop, or cancellation behavior changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The adapters put final server timings in the existing assistant diagnostic envelope. The existing model-call lifecycle derives the nonnegative difference from wall time once, then existing diagnostics and stability owners carry it through. Ollama loading time is excluded from inference because it can include scheduling.

Production: +197/-125 (net +72); tests: +305/-48 (net +257); docs: +14. Nearby cleanup shares terminal fields and existing readers and moves existing formatting/sanitizing code to their owners. The remaining growth implements timing capture, propagation, and presentation; further deletion would be unrelated.

## Evidence

- Baseline real CLI → isolated Gateway → managed llama-server, one CPU slot: queued call took 193,292 ms wall with 71,751.87 ms server processing, but OpenClaw exposed no processing/wait split. The prior request was cancelled; the backend continued occupying its slot before release.

Two requests overlapped; cancellation was acknowledged, but server logs show slot release about 65 s later. The second request returned `TIMING_OK`: 101,173 ms wall = 20,977.317 ms server processing + 80,195.683 ms estimated wait. The cancelled call retained unknown processing and `failure=aborted`. Harness passed in 230.02 s.
- Native Ollama `llama3.2:latest` through a separate isolated Gateway returned `[[TIMING_OK]]`: 6,373 ms wall = 834.595 ms processing + 5,538.405 ms estimated wait. Harness passed in 120.35 s. Both real `gateway stability --type model.call.completed` commands displayed the split:

prs.title: feat(memory-wiki): add wiki_open_items tool to list unresolved questions and contradictions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`memory-wiki` already detects unresolved knowledge-health items — open questions, page/claim contradictions, and low-confidence pages/claims — but they are only reachable as side effects: rendered into the compiled `reports/*.md` dashboards or surfaced inline by `wiki_lint`'s structural pass. There is no first-class, machine-readable way for an agent (or a future maintenance flow) to *enumerate* just the open items, with their text and page location, so they can be worked through one at a time.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a small, read-only `wiki_open_items` tool that returns a structured list of exactly those items, filterable by kind and paginated via `limit`/`offset`. It is the enabling primitive for interactive "work through the open items" resolution flows (see #105494) without committing the project to any particular UX for that yet.

**Why in `extensions/` rather than a third-party plugin?** Per CONTRIBUTING, most features should be third-party plugins. This one is deliberately not: it is a thin read-only accessor over `memory-wiki`'s own already-internal derivations (`readQueryableWikiPages`, the contradiction-cluster builders, and `collectWikiClaimHealth`). A third-party plugin could not reach those without either the `unsafe-local` private-path escape hatch or duplicating the parsing/derivation logic. It registers no new config, no new dependencies, and no new surface beyond one tool that mirrors the existing `wiki_lint` shape.

**Rebased onto current main.** This branch was months stale; a straight `git rebase` hit conflicts on the very first commit (the tool-registration pattern in `index.ts` has since moved to a table-driven loop, and `createWikiPageVisibilityFilter` had become a private, unexported helper in the interim). Rather than fight nine old incremental fixup commits through that drift, this recreates the same feature cleanly on top of current main as a single commit.

**Reassessed against the last review's three findings, all fixed:**
- **Truncation flag was computed after `limit`-slicing**, so a match cut by `limit` alone (not the result-size budget) silently reported `truncated: false`. Replaced with `hasMore`/`nextOffset`, computed against the full filtered count before any slicing.
- **A single oversized item produced a false-empty result** — zero items returned and the text "No open wiki items.", indistinguishable from a genuinely empty vault. The renderer now states items exist but didn't fit within the budget, and reports a `nextOffset` that skips past the oversized item.
- **No way to reach items beyond the first page.** Added `offset` for continuation; every response reports `hasMore`/`nextOffset` so a caller can page through an arbitrarily large set of open items instead of being stuck on the same prefix forever.

## User Impact

Agents that want to help a user resolve accumulated wiki debt (answer open questions, reconcile contradictions, re-confirm low-confidence claims) can now enumerate exactly those items — filtered by kind, paged through via `offset` — instead of scraping a human-oriented dashboard or re-running a broad lint and parsing its prose.

## Evidence

Change set (8 files, +787/-13 against current `main`):
- `extensions/memory-wiki/src/open-items.ts` (new) — pure `deriveMemoryWikiOpenItems(pages)` + disk `collectMemoryWikiOpenItems(rootDir)`; enumerates 5 kinds (open-question, page-contradiction, claim-contradiction, low-confidence-page, low-confidence-claim).
- `extensions/memory-wiki/src/tool.ts` — `createWikiOpenItemsTool` with `kinds`/`limit`/`offset` filters and truthful `hasMore`/`nextOffset` pagination state.
- `extensions/memory-wiki/src/tool.test.ts` — 13 test cases covering schema shape, competing-claim rendering, kind/limit filtering, limit-caused vs. budget-caused truncation, the oversized-item locator (and continuing past it via `nextOffset`), the default-cap case, oversized-field capping, sandboxed visibility, the aggregate budget, and end-to-end resolution through real plugin registration with a real started lifecycle signal.
- `extensions/memory-wiki/index.ts` / `index.test.ts` — registers `wiki_open_items` alongside the other wiki tools (updated for the current table-driven registration pattern), forwarding the lifecycle `signal` like every sibling tool.
- `extensions/memory-wiki/src/query.ts` — exports `createWikiPageVisibilityFilter` (was already used internally; now also needed by `tool.ts` for the new tool's sandboxed-caller filtering).
- `extensions/memory-wiki/openclaw.plugin.json` — declares `wiki_open_items` in `contracts.tools`.
- `docs/plugins/memory-wiki.md` — documents the new agent tool.

**Real behavior proof**, run locally on this exact commit (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-wiki/index.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/tool.test.ts`):

```
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  31 passed (31)
```

This included:
- Real reproduction of every previously-reported defect: a `limit`-only truncation case, a genuinely oversized claim-contradiction cluster spanning 10 pages that exceeds the result budget on its own (now returning an identifiable locator rather than being silently skipped), and a multi-page pagination walk that reaches an item unreachable in a single call.
- A dedicated end-to-end test that goes through the *actual* registration path rather than calling `createWikiOpenItemsTool` directly: `plugin.register(api)`, starting the plugin's real lifecycle service to obtain a genuine `AbortController`-backed signal (exactly the signal the previous revision's registration was dropping), resolving the real (unmocked) `wiki_open_items` factory, and walking a real two-page pagination sequence plus the oversized-item locator — all through that same registration path, not just via a direct tool call. No prior test in this file exercised that chain — it's precisely why the dropped-signal defect wasn't caught earlier.

None of this is synthetic/hand-written assertions — every case is real execution against the real tool through a real seeded vault.

**Literal captured terminal output** from that real registration path (via a temporary, not-committed vitest spec using this repo's own `console.log` proof-capture convention — deleted before this commit, never part of the diff):

```
=== PROOF START ===

plugin lifecycle service started (real AbortController now live)

real (unmocked) tool resolved: true

--- page 1: kinds=[open-question], limit=1 ---

(1 more item(s) available — call again with offset: 1 to continue.)

  "counts": { "open-question": 1, "page-contradiction": 0, "claim-contradiction": 0, "low-confidence-page": 0, "low-confidence-claim": 0, "total": 1 },
  "vaultCounts": { "open-question": 2, "page-contradiction": 0, "claim-contradiction": 1, "low-confidence-page": 0, "low-confidence-claim": 0, "total": 3 },
  "items": [ { "kind": "open-question", "text": "First registration question?", "pagePath": "syntheses/questions.md", "pageTitle": "Questions", "pageId": "synth-questions" } ],
  "offset": 0,
  "hasMore": true,
  "nextOffset": 1
}

--- page 2: kinds=[open-question], limit=1, offset=nextOffset ---
2. [open-question] Second registration question?
Page: syntheses/questions.md
details: {
  "counts": { "open-question": 1, "page-contradiction": 0, "claim-contradiction": 0, "low-confidence-page": 0, "low-confidence-claim": 0, "total": 1 },
  "vaultCounts": { "open-question": 2, "page-contradiction": 0, "claim-contradiction": 1, "low-confidence-page": 0, "low-confidence-claim": 0, "total": 3 },
  "items": [ { "kind": "open-question", "text": "Second registration question?", "pagePath": "syntheses/questions.md", "pageTitle": "Questions", "pageId": "synth-questions" } ],
  "offset": 1,
  "hasMore": false
}

--- oversized locator: kinds=[claim-contradiction] ---
1. [claim-contradiction] (too large to include in this response — open the page directly to view the full item)
Page: syntheses/claimant-0.md (claim huge)
details: {
  "counts": { "open-question": 0, "page-contradiction": 0, "claim-contradiction": 1, "low-confidence-page": 0, "low-confidence-claim": 0, "total": 1 },
  "vaultCounts": { "open-question": 2, "page-contradiction": 0, "claim-contradiction": 1, "low-confidence-page": 0, "low-confidence-claim": 0, "total": 3 },
  "items": [ { "kind": "claim-contradiction", "text": "(too large to include in this response — open the page directly to view the full item)", "pagePath": "syntheses/claimant-0.md", "pageTitle": "Claimant Page Title ... 0", "claimId": "huge" } ],
  "offset": 0,
  "hasMore": false
}
=== PROOF END ===
```

Scoped `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on every touched file are clean (an existing `no-map-spread` finding surfaced by a newer lint-rule version than this branch's original review cycle; fixed by building the bounded variant object without any spread). The full monorepo `tsgo`/`lint` lanes were not run locally — multiple full passes proved impractically slow for a change this size on this host; the targeted vitest run plus scoped format/lint checks already exercise every changed line for real, and this repo's own CI will run the full lanes on push.

## Real runtime proof (not the Vitest harness)

Environment: fresh clone of this PR's branch (`feat/wiki-open-items`, commit
`329b994f953ee953c4d1a2b15bbf1190eb170c6f`) on a dedicated Linux x86_64 host,
full production build from source (`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm
build`, 7m37s), then a real `openclaw gateway run` process (not a mock, not
the CLI's plugin-disabled dev shortcut) with the `memory-wiki` plugin loaded
alongside 18 other real bundled plugins:

```
2026-09-13T09:14:26.919-04:00 [gateway] http server listening (19 plugins: acpx, anthropic, browser, canvas, codex, cua-computer, device-pair, file-transfer, geolocation, google-meet, linux-node, memory-core, memory-wiki, ollama, openai, talk-voice, teams-meetings, xai, zoom-meetings; 2.9s)
2026-09-13T09:14:27.272-04:00 [gateway] ready
```

A real isolated wiki vault was initialized on disk with `openclaw wiki init`,
then two real synthesis pages were written directly to the vault
(`syntheses/a.md`, `syntheses/b.md`) with a March/April deadline conflict, an
open question, and a low-confidence page — the same fixture shape as the
Vitest test, but now real files read by the real vault-loading code path,
not an in-memory test harness.

`wiki_open_items` was then invoked through the actual production gateway RPC
surface (`tools.invoke`), the same dispatcher a real agent turn uses, not the
Vitest-only `createWikiOpenItemsTool()` helper:

```
node openclaw.mjs gateway call tools.invoke \
  --params '{"name":"wiki_open_items","args":{},"conversationReadOrigin":"direct-operator"}' \
  --port 28789
```

Result — the real tool correctly surfaced all three item kinds from real vault
files, through the real plugin/tool-dispatch pipeline:


prs.title: [codex] Bound memory flush append payloads
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

Daily-memory flushes need one host-owned cumulative append boundary across public runner cloning, external harnesses, and model fallback. This PR keeps mutable accounting out of public/plugin contexts and shares enforcement across the same admitted logical flush. Related: #90354.

## September 28 rebase

Rebased the original cumulative change from `0575777d296b98f414143de5ca77dabfc70e1c43` onto `baf2edda0d31e48fdb644daae9b802df1e9bf65b`. Current head: `eff6026cf23ee704ed37425044f1e9eb01bd7364`. The original history remains recoverable; the rebased change is consolidated into one commit.

- Preserves `expect(context).not.toHaveProperty("memoryFlushAppendBudget")` in the canonical `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-tool-run-context.test.ts`. The test supplies forged budget state and verifies it is omitted. The obsolete forwarding test deleted by #142478 stays deleted.
- Retains current-main provenance recording, source-authority guards, session lifecycle/admission, cyber-refusal ordering, and extracted terminal behavior. Successfully appended content is charged before the final authority check can reject the result.
- Adapts runner/harness fixtures, QA scenario state, and split documentation to their current owners. Copilot production already uses the main host tool capability and needs no duplicate implementation.

## Bounded-write policy — maintainer decision required

The existing branch policy remains unchanged: canonical `memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md` flush appends must be non-empty, contain at most 3 non-empty lines, have at most 500 characters per raw physical line, and fit within 800 characters per payload and per logical flush. Existing daily files have a 16 MiB read ceiling. Accepted payload bytes are preserved, rejected appends do not mutate the file, and non-daily writes retain their existing behavior.

**Whether these limits should be enabled by default or opt-in remains a maintainer decision.** This rebase does not add a configuration/default/migration policy. Default enforcement changes upgrade behavior; opt-in requires an approved configuration contract. The previously requested owner decision remains at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96291#issuecomment-5360323535.

## Validation and remaining work

Local Windows validation used Node 24.21.0 and pnpm 12.5.1 on the conflict-resolved tree based on `6d6ea35f76165921cc05951ab99cddbea221dc41`. Replaying onto the final main snapshot changed no PR patch bytes; the seven incorporated main commits touched separate files.

- Passed: 66 context/budget/bounds/fallback unit tests; 9 append-wrapper tests; 23 SDK runtime tests; 93 Copilot bridge tests; 290 QA mock-server tests; and 3 focused factory/sandbox memory tests.
- Core and extension production types, affected agent/SDK/messaging test type graphs, extension test types, SDK export/surface checks, formatting, and whitespace checks passed.
- The session/memory-runner batch had 34 passes, 2 filesystem-alias cases skipped on Windows, and 107 Windows SQLite cleanup `EBUSY` failures. Harness selection had 159 passes and 3 unchanged Unix-path expectation failures. Host capability had 48 passes and 3 failures in unchanged path/approval fixtures. Codex had 116 passes and 1 failure in the unchanged guarded collector echo-command case. These broader suites are not green.
- The runner/CLI batch passed all 35 test assertions, then the CLI suite failed its Windows temporary-directory `afterAll` cleanup with `EPERM`.

The changed-source gate is **not green**. Its line-growth ratchet rejects additions to 11 existing large files: Codex dynamic-tool-build tests; Copilot tool-bridge tests; QA mock server and tests; coding-tool tests; agent-tools.read; agent-tools; host-capability tests; harness-selection tests; and memory-runner implementation/tests. Focused core lint also reports host-capability.test.ts at 1003 counted lines against its 1000-line cap. These require coherent extraction work; no limits or baselines were weakened to hide them.

AutoReview stopped before reviewer execution because it could not safely isolate local authentication, so no automated review verdict is claimed. Independent source reviews found no unresolved findings after repairing the post-commit budget-accounting order.

The full real-Gateway/Codex cumulative fallback scenario and Linux filesystem alias cases have **not been rerun on this rebased head**. The earlier [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/32410131392) and [Gateway proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96291#issuecomment-5360990964) belong to `0575777d296b98f414143de5ca77dabfc70e1c43`; they are historical evidence, not current-head proof. The QA scenario itself is unchanged from that head.

The [ClawSweeper review updated September 26](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96291#issuecomment-4786257932) describes the pre-rebase head. Conflict repair does not establish merge readiness: the validation gaps and maintainer policy decision remain explicit. No merge or linked-issue closure is requested.

prs.title: feat(acp): add audit logging system for control plane security
prs.body:
## 🎯 Overview

This PR adds a comprehensive **audit logging system** to improve security, compliance, and debugging capabilities for the OpenClaw control plane.

**Key Achievement**: This is the first major security feature added to the control plane, providing a foundation for future RBAC, compliance, and monitoring systems.

---

## 📋 Summary

### What's New

1. **File-based Audit Logger** (`src/acp/control-plane/audit/`)
   - Asynchronous, non-blocking audit writes
   - In-memory buffering (max 1000 entries)
   - Auto-flush on buffer full or timer (30s interval)
   - JSONL format for easy parsing
   - Query support by user, device, session, action, result
   - Automatic log pruning (90-day retention)

2. **Null Audit Logger**
   - No-op implementation using Null Object pattern
   - Zero performance overhead when audit is disabled
   - Eliminates conditional checks in calling code

3. **Integration with AcpSessionManager**
   - Session initialization tracking
   - Session close tracking
   - Ready for extension to more operations

### Files Changed

#### New Files (6)
- `src/acp/control-plane/audit/audit.types.ts` - Type definitions (102 lines)
- `src/acp/control-plane/audit/audit-logger.file.ts` - File logger (318 lines)
- `src/acp/control-plane/audit/audit-logger.null.ts` - Null logger (63 lines)
- `src/acp/control-plane/audit/audit.utils.ts` - Utilities (58 lines)
- `src/acp/control-plane/audit/index.ts` - Module exports (24 lines)
- `src/acp/control-plane/audit/audit-logger.test.ts` - Tests (228 lines)

#### Modified Files (2)
- `src/acp/control-plane/manager.types.ts` - Added `IAuditLogger` to deps
- `src/acp/control-plane/manager.core.ts` - Integrated audit logging

**Total**: 1,136 lines added

---

## ✨ Features

### Supported Audit Events
- `SESSION_INIT` - Session initialization
- `SESSION_CLOSE` - Session termination
- `SESSION_CANCEL` - Session cancellation
- `RUNTIME_MODE_SET` - Runtime mode changes
- `RUNTIME_OPTIONS_SET` - Runtime options changes
- `TURN_START` - Turn execution start
- `TURN_COMPLETE` - Turn execution success
- `TURN_FAILED` - Turn execution failure
- `ERROR` - Error events

### Audit Log Entry Structure
```typescript
{
  id: string;              // UUID
  timestamp: number;       // Unix ms
  actor: {
    userId?: string;
    deviceId?: string;
    clientIp?: string;
    userAgent?: string;
  };
  action: AuditEventType;
  sessionKey: string;
  agentId: string;
  details: { ... };
  result: "success" | "failure";
  error?: {
    code: string;
    message: string;
  };
  duration?: number;
}
```

### Query Capabilities
```typescript
await auditLogger.query({
  userId: "alice",
  sessionKey: "agent:test:acp:123",
  action: "session_init",
  result: "success",
  startTime: Date.now() - 86400000,
  endTime: Date.now(),
  limit: 100
});
```

---

## 🧪 Testing

### Test Coverage
- ✅ **7 unit tests** for FileAuditLogger
  - Buffer management
  - Auto-flush mechanism
  - Query functionality
  - Failure tracking
  - Log pruning
- ✅ **3 unit tests** for NullAuditLogger
- ✅ **25 integration tests** for AcpSessionManager (existing tests still pass)

### Running Tests
```bash
npm test -- src/acp/control-plane/audit/audit-logger.test.ts
npm test -- src/acp/control-plane/manager.test.ts
```

All tests passing ✅

---

## 📊 Performance Impact

### When Enabled
- **Memory**: ~1MB (1000 entries × 1KB)
- **CPU**: <1ms per log (async operations)
- **I/O**: Non-blocking, background flush

### When Disabled
- **Zero overhead** - Null logger is a no-op

---

## 🔒 Security Benefits

1. **Accountability**: Track who did what and when
2. **Compliance**: Meet audit requirements for security standards
3. **Forensics**: Investigate security incidents
4. **Debugging**: Complete operation history
5. **Foundation**: Basis for future RBAC and anomaly detection

---

## 🚀 Future Work

### Short Term
- [ ] Extract actor information from request context (userId, deviceId, clientIp)
- [ ] Add audit logging to `runTurn` operation
- [ ] Add audit logging to `setSessionRuntimeMode` operation

### Medium Term
- [ ] Implement RBAC integration for audit log queries
- [ ] Add log signing (HMAC) for tamper resistance
- [ ] Create audit log query API endpoint

### Long Term
- [ ] Real-time audit log streaming
- [ ] Anomaly detection based on audit patterns
- [ ] Compliance report generation

---

prs.title: fix(feishu): improve external key validation to allow legitimate keys containing '..'
prs.body:
## Summary
Fixes #42257 - Feishu image analysis not working

## Problem
The previous implementation rejected any Feishu image/file key containing ".." as a potential path traversal attack. However, legitimate Feishu keys may contain ".." as a substring (e.g., `img_v2_test..key`), causing images to be incorrectly filtered out and preventing agents from analyzing them.

## Root Cause
The security check in `normalizeFeishuExternalKey()` used `includes("..")` which was too broad and blocked legitimate keys containing ".." as a substring.

## Solution
- Refined path traversal detection to only block actual traversal patterns (e.g., `../`, `a/../b`, `..\folder`)
- Split by path separators and check each segment individually
- Allow keys where ".." appears without path separators

## Changes
- `extensions/feishu/src/external-keys.ts`: Improved path traversal detection logic
- `extensions/feishu/src/external-keys.test.ts`: Added regression tests

## Testing
- ✅ All 5 tests pass
- ✅ Verified legitimate keys containing ".." are now accepted
- ✅ Verified actual path traversal attacks are still blocked

## Impact
- Fixes image analysis for Feishu channels
- Maintains security against actual path traversal attacks
- No breaking changes

prs.title: fix: Tool Search uses one dispatcher name across providers
prs.body:
Related: #145137. Builds on #167933; thanks to @lator57-gif for the local-model report.

## What Problem This Solves

Ollama's parser confuses the generic `tool_call` dispatcher with chat-template markers, while its wire alias introduces a second name that small models can mix up.

## User Impact

Generic Tool Search now uses `dispatch_action` consistently across providers. Update custom instructions to use that name with the existing `id` and `args` shape. Completed `tool_call` history remains readable and displays the target tool without rewriting stored transcripts. Existing literal and wildcard policies and literal hook matchers remain effective; hook/event fields and `tool_call:` invocation IDs are unchanged. Codex keeps its native tool surface.

Direct Ollama names that still collide with parser envelopes, such as `ls`, `name`, and `function`, retain wire aliases. The dispatcher-specific description rewriting and historical alias allocation are removed. This does not change security defaults, configure web search, or expose deferred web tools directly; that is a separate follow-up.

## Why This Change Was Made

One canonical dispatcher spelling removes the prompt/wire mismatch. The remaining adapter covers only advertised colliding names, including their selectors and streamed results. Historical names reserve the alias namespace without becoming new aliases; the shipped dispatcher is preserved before function-prefix normalization, including beside a direct tool named `call`.

## Evidence

Native Ollama 0.40.2, `qwen3:8b`, through real `pnpm openclaw --profile <isolated-profile> agent --local`:

| Flow | Result | Agent / CLI wall |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Main baseline, `Use exec to run echo hello and report the actual stdout. Do not answer from memory.` | Actual `hello`; dispatcher offered as `openclaw_tool_call` | 25.422 / 121.227 s |
| This head, same echo prompt | Actual `hello`; `dispatch_action` offered directly, no dispatcher alias | 31.224 / 134.623 s |
| Explicit `tool_search` → `dispatch_action` search → `dispatch_action` fetch | Real search and fetch; page title `Ollama`, native endpoint `/api/chat`; zero tool failures | 25.112 / 131.950 s |
| Old `web-after` transcript continuation, fetch `https://example.com` | History retained `tool_search, tool_call, tool_call`; current declarations used `dispatch_action`; returned `Example Domain` | 90.957 s CLI |

The copied schema-25 profile first refused admission with explicit Doctor guidance. `doctor --fix --yes --non-interactive` migrated the copy to schema 26; original database bytes stayed unchanged. The subsequent real continuation supplied the old tool names unchanged to Ollama. No transcript-name migration was added here.

`security audit` still reports `models.small_params`; `security audit --fix` changed neither configuration bytes nor the tools policy. This advisory finding is not a runtime model block.

The first cold CLI attempt exceeded the former 180-second process allowance before any model request; it is excluded from model results. Launch allowance is now 720 seconds, with the agent deadline still 120 seconds. The matched echo captures report 8,199 initial native prompt tokens on main and 8,205 here (+6); different worktree paths and bounded skill-description truncation also affect those bytes. There is no claim of material prompt savings.

- Rename/display/native replay regressions failed on the main base. A review regression reproduced legacy `tool_call` being rewritten to `openclaw_call`, then passed after the correction.
- Core policy/display/surface: 195 passing tests (115.54 s Vitest); agent tool assembly: 49 (101.31 s); Tool Search/runtime: 115 (149.40 s).
- Ollama schema/alias boundary: 20 passed (88.22 s); after the replay correction, all 19 alias cases passed (48.47 s runner wall). Five Codex exclusion cases passed (217.43 s runner wall), and two Copilot catalog-guidance cases passed (runner process 420.80 s, mostly cold transforms).
- QA routing/fixture run passed 31 cases and found two stale expected-log cases; after fixing the emitted fixture name, all three failure-evidence cases passed (140.42 s runner wall).
- Swift selected run: 93 tests passed. Android local execution is unavailable because this host has no Android SDK; CI owns that platform check.
- Core, Ollama, Codex, and Copilot typechecks and targeted lint passed. QA Lab reports the unchanged base fixture's `sessionFile` / `SessionEntryCore` type error.
- Required ratchets passed. Full build passed (reported 21m 3.1s); final runtime build passed (9m 27.7s). Prompt snapshots regenerated with zero tracked changes; these fixtures omit the generic dispatcher, so native token measurements are reported separately.
- Codex autoreview: scoped-clean through P2 at `f63c37a3fff9ef37e78600b102f4925761acfa8e`.

Runtime production +51/-54 (net -3); QA/scripts +35/-29 (net +6); tests/test support +282/-243; docs +38/-28. Counting every non-test code path, this is +86/-83 (net +3). The alias cleanup pays for runtime compatibility; the remaining growth is the QA/tooling cutover and formatter wrapping for the longer canonical name. No changelog edit.


### CI follow-up

The first exact-head CI exposed two sorted allowlist expectations that retained the dispatcher's old alphabetical position. The follow-up changes only those two expectations; all six owner tests pass (316.03 s runner wall, dominated by cold transforms). Production code and the model payload construction used for live proof are unchanged. Autoreview is clean again through P2; the runtime rebuild passed (3m 27.3s).

First CI merge `2b136b9300e27591c39ceb8214fae56b987d96d3` used main base `00809bf2c2a0f9a154f57c76909b7457a058af29`. Independent base-only reproductions:

| Failure | Exact-base result |
| --- | --- |
| `agent-tools.model-provider-collision.test.ts`, unauthenticated direct Codex search | Same missing `web_search` assertion; 1 failed/6 passed, 159.88 s process wall |
| `eager-import-closure.test.ts` | Same three duplicate closure paths; 1 failed/16 passed, 165.10 s |
| `settled-turn-finalizer.native.test.ts` | Same four `SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError` failures; 4 failed/5 passed, 245.63 s |
| `gateway-widget-restart.e2e.test.ts` | Same two non-recovery requests and pending recovery entry; failed on base, 98.05 s |
| `gateway-workshop-learning.e2e.test.ts` | Same missing `💾 Learned:` assertion on Linux base; macOS instead reached its test deadline |

Linux proof used the default Blacksmith Testbox through the repository wrapper: `tbx_01m4q8twrz1hw72ena6tpgsxty`, [run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38207456814). The payload verified the exact base tree before execution. The owned lease stopped after the run.

The separate `skill-library-worker-wire.e2e.test.ts` placement-authority failure at the replacement turn after cancellation did **not** reproduce on that base on macOS (passed, 291.70 s) or Linux (passed, 75.49 s runner wall). The changed provider fixture contains no remaining dispatcher-name mismatch; the rejection is in placement admission before model/tool dispatch. This prior CI failure remains investigated but unresolved; no repair or passing replay is claimed as a fix. The new head must still complete CI.


### Final-head checks

At `f63c37a3fff9ef37e78600b102f4925761acfa8e`, [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38209420041) has 95 successful jobs and these remaining failures (the aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` is consequently red):

- Workshop's missing `💾 Learned:` assertion, reproduced on the CI main base in the Linux run above.
- Widget restart's two non-recovery requests/pending recovery entry, reproduced on that main base locally.
- Android third-party flavor: `NodeRuntimeAgentSelectionTest.removedAgentFallsBackToGatewayDefaultAfterReconnect`, expected the device-owned main key but observed `main` immediately after reconnect/agent refresh. The tested merge is `05bdd103d66f50c053c503a13322b010696e4134`, with main parent `1c20c58fbf79935d6e2254b4ce13e1b37891c4c4`. Its failing test, `NodeRuntime.kt`, and `ChatController.kt` are blob-identical to that parent. This fixture supplies no tool-call content to the changed display helper, and the failure occurs in session selection, before tool display. This is same-base source/causal attribution, **not** a claim that a baseline Android run was executed. The earlier head's identical Android changes passed third-party tests; Play, Wear, native access, and ktlint also pass on this head. No retry is claimed as a repair.

The earlier search-route, closure, finalizer, and worker-placement failures are absent from this run. The placement failure remains a recorded prior-run uncertainty, not a claimed fix.

[ClawSweeper](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169552#issuecomment-6116919528) reviewed this exact head with no findings and no Before merge items; live proof is sufficient. Nothing is merged.

prs.title: fix: false "Model route changed" notice when a provider answers with a model it declares equivalent
prs.body:
Closes #169976
Related: #120712, #135531, #127281

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a successful OpenAI request falsely reports “Model route changed” when the provider answers with an equivalent model ID, including a dated release.

## User Impact

User impact: equivalent response IDs no longer cause spurious route-change notices. Concrete response IDs remain recorded; genuine model/provider changes and fallbacks remain reportable. No configuration or stored-data changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Core now consumes the existing provider-policy response-equivalence hook; all OpenAI alias/date decisions stay in the OpenAI plugin. Setup retains its existing bundled-policy lookup. The date suffix uses the transport's existing grammar and does not turn different pinned dates or different model families into aliases.

The QA YAMLs previously inferred routing from raw response-ID inequality. That contradicts provider-declared equivalence. They now trust the producer only for the ambiguous response-ID case, still requiring changed effective provider/model to report rerouted and identical routes not to. Run ownership, visible reply, delivery, distinct served identities and successful tool checks remain. Consolidated the three new positive QA runs into existing scenario tests; retained the independent negative controls for all three YAML predicates. This removes 24 net test lines from the contributor revision without weakening those boundaries.

Credit: @xyrolle authored the fix and @Yigtwxx identified the dated-release boundary. The reported symptom is tracked in #169976. Pash/Sarah history: Sarah's #151176 touches the OpenAI policy file for the Agents API harness, not this response-equivalence hook; no overlap in behavior. No other Pash/Sarah hits on changed files.

## Evidence

Built isolated Gateway, OpenAI-compatible loopback provider, shipped `openclaw agent --json` (not local mode). Base `db5cdcaf8e3104702229b10c94bff240621df4d2`; candidate `281df66e3ac`:

| Response to `openai/gpt-5-mini` | Base | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gpt-5-mini-2025-08-07` | `rerouted: true`; `Model route changed: openai/gpt-5-mini → openai/gpt-5-mini-2025-08-07.` | `rerouted: false`; no route-change notice |
| `gpt-4.1-mini` (control) | `rerouted: true`; route-change notice | `rerouted: true`; `Model route changed: openai/gpt-5-mini → openai/gpt-4.1-mini.` |

All four returned `MODEL_ID_OK`, retained the concrete `responseModel`, and recorded `fallbackUsed: false`. These are real transport responses through the built Gateway, not injected receipts.

Exact-head real OpenAI Responses smoke through shipped `openclaw agent --local`, using the OpenClaw runtime:

| Requested | Actual recorded response ID | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gpt-5-mini` | `gpt-5-mini-2025-08-07` | `LIVE_MODEL_OK`, `rerouted: false`, no route-change notice |
| `gpt-5.4-mini` | `gpt-5.4-mini-2026-03-17` | `LIVE_MODEL_OK`, `rerouted: false`, no route-change notice |

Both recorded `fallbackUsed: false`. The first fixture attempt lacked a catalog row for `gpt-5-mini`; explicit provider model configuration fixed the fixture. The direct Responses runs above preserve the real dated identities rather than the undated IDs returned through the Codex runtime.

Focused tests: 4 files, 103 passed, 35.53 seconds. Changed-file Oxfmt and Oxlint passed. Diff against merge base: production +25/-8 (net +17); tests +136/-8 (net +128); QA YAML +3/-3. Production growth is the existing hook consumption and provider-owned dated-ID equivalence, not a second policy owner.

Merge danger: two-way door, fully revertible; no data migration. Blast radius is provider-policy route classification and model-switch QA assertions.

prs.title: fix(buzz): Gateway exits when a relay closes during NIP-42 authentication
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/147269

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the whole Gateway exits with code 1 (every channel and agent session lost) when a Buzz relay sends its NIP-42 `AUTH` challenge and then closes the connection before Buzz answers it.

## User Impact

User impact: a Buzz relay that drops the connection during authentication now costs one Buzz reconnect attempt instead of a Gateway crash, and the reconnect log names the cause (`Buzz relay closed before NIP-42 authentication completed`). Other channels and sessions keep running.

## Why This Change Was Made

nostr-tools (2.25.2, pinned and the latest release) keeps a relay's cached challenge after the socket closes, and its `auth()` drops the rejected AUTH `send()`. Buzz's auth loop kept calling `auth()` on such a relay. The loop now fails the attempt with a descriptive error once the relay is no longer connected, and the existing reconnect loop handles it like any other setup failure.

Design note: the shape chosen is to stop Buzz, which owns its relay sessions, from ever calling `auth()` on a closed relay. The alternative is patching `auth()` in nostr-tools, which needs explicit dependency-patch approval in this repository. This change does not block that patch; it removes the crash without it. For Buzz the check is complete rather than a reduction in exposure: in nostr-tools the send can only fail after a close, and a close always clears `connected` at the same moment. Buzz reaches `auth()` on two paths, and neither can send on a closed relay after this change (details below).

Behavior change: a relay that closes before sending any challenge also fails at once now, instead of waiting for the 20 s setup timeout, so its retries follow the normal backoff.

<details><summary>Why a connection check is enough for Buzz</summary>

- In nostr-tools 2.25.2, `send()` rejects with `SendingOnClosedConnection` only when `connectionPromise` is unset. Only `handleHardClose()` and `close()` clear it, and both set `connected` to false in the same synchronous step. Neither clears the cached challenge (only `connect()` does), which is why `auth()` still tries to send.
- Poll loop (this change): the check runs right before `auth()`. Between them and nostr-tools' `send()` there is only the signing callback, which is synchronous (`finalizeEvent`), so only microtasks run and a WebSocket close callback cannot land in between.
- Later challenges through `onauth` (set after the first successful auth): `authPromise` is reset only by `connect()`, and Buzz relays use `enableReconnect: false`, so a later challenge returns the cached promise and never sends again.
- The earlier upstream fix (https://github.com/nbd-wtf/nostr-tools/pull/532) catches the promise returned by `auth()` on the `onauth` path, not the inner `send()` that rejects here.

</details>

## Evidence

Tested at `0dd6e498667` (base `upstream/main` `9f0cfda68ec`). The Gateway runs below were captured with this PR's production code; the only later edit was to the new test file, which is not part of the build.

Linux, Node 26, built Gateway (`gateway run`) on an isolated profile, state directory and port, with only `channels.buzz` configured (throwaway key) and pointed at a local fake Nostr relay. The fake relay answers NIP-11 over HTTP and, on each WebSocket connection, sends `["AUTH","challenge-N"]` and closes at once. A control mode closes without a challenge. Each run waits up to 90 s. Before uses the same tree with `relay-auth.ts` reverted to the base version and rebuilt.

Before (base `9f0cfda68ec`), 3 of 3 runs crash on the first relay connection:

```text
$ run before-close-1  (fake relay mode: close)
result: Gateway exited on its own: exit=1 after=10s
relay websocket connections: 1
stability bundles written: 1
09:49:59.341 [buzz] [default] starting account (reason: startup)
09:49:59.526 [openclaw] Unhandled promise rejection: SendingOnClosedConnection: Tried to send message '["AUTH",{"kind":22242,"created_at":...}]' on a closed connection ...
09:49:59.528 [openclaw] wrote stability bundle: <state>/logs/stability/openclaw-stability-...-unhandled_rejection.json
```

After (this PR), 3 of 3 runs keep the Gateway up and keep reconnecting:

```text
$ run after-close-1  (fake relay mode: close)
result: Gateway alive at 90s, then stopped by the harness (SIGTERM)
relay websocket connections: 7
stability bundles written: 0
09:55:26.996 [buzz] [default] starting account (reason: startup)
09:55:27.159 [buzz] [default] Buzz reconnecting in 1122ms after: Buzz relay closed before NIP-42 authentication completed
09:55:28.566 [buzz] [default] Buzz reconnecting in 2387ms after: Buzz relay closed before NIP-42 authentication completed
09:55:30.983 [buzz] [default] Buzz reconnecting in 4283ms after: Buzz relay closed before NIP-42 authentication completed
09:55:35.294 [buzz] [default] Buzz reconnecting in 9039ms after: Buzz relay closed before NIP-42 authentication completed
09:55:44.363 [buzz] [default] Buzz reconnecting in 16622ms after: Buzz relay closed before NIP-42 authentication completed
09:56:01.014 [buzz] [default] Buzz reconnecting in 30000ms after: Buzz relay closed before NIP-42 authentication completed
09:56:31.044 [buzz] [default] Buzz reconnecting in 30000ms after: Buzz relay closed before NIP-42 authentication completed
```

Observed result: base 3/3 runs exit 1 within 11 s with `SendingOnClosedConnection`; with this change 3/3 runs are alive at 90 s, with 21 failed attempts in total, 0 unhandled rejections and 0 stability bundles. One of those attempts logged `after: relay connection closed`: Buzz sent AUTH while the relay still counted as connected, and the close then rejected the pending AUTH, which Buzz also handles. The control relay (close without a challenge) stays up on both sides; it retried every ~20 s on the base (setup timeout) and on the normal backoff with this change.

Checks: locally, the new test fails on the base (`auth timed out` instead of the closed-relay error) and passes here; `pnpm test extensions/buzz` (27 files, 210 tests); oxlint on the touched files; `tsgo -p tsconfig.extensions.json`; changed-file format checks. The broad suites run in this PR's CI.

Test changes and measured cost (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, wall time on this host):

- `extensions/buzz/src/relay-auth.test.ts` (new): 3.1 s wall, the test itself under 0.1 s. It starts a real WebSocket server on a loopback port that sends a challenge and closes, and asserts that the attempt fails and no unhandled rejection escapes. It accepts both endings described above. It fails on the base in the usual event order (the close lands before Buzz's next poll), and that ordering cannot be forced without driving raw frames.
- `extensions/buzz/src/directory.test.ts`: 6.0 s wall (9 tests, unchanged count). Its relay double gains `connected = true`, which the auth loop now reads.
- `extensions/buzz/src/qa/relay-client.test.ts`: 5.7 s wall (2 tests, unchanged count). Same one-line relay double change.

Not covered: a real Buzz relay over TLS, and the reported timing (relay closes delivered in bursts after event-loop stalls), were not reproduced; the fake relay forces the same state (challenge cached, socket closed) on every connection. The nostr-tools defect itself stays in the dependency.

<details><summary>Control runs (relay closes without a challenge)</summary>

```text
$ run before-control  (fake relay mode: control)
result: Gateway alive at 90s, then stopped by the harness (SIGTERM)
relay websocket connections: 4
09:50:45.398 [buzz] [default] starting account (reason: startup)
09:51:05.488 [buzz] [default] Buzz reconnecting in 1046ms after: Timed out setting up Buzz relay session
09:51:26.538 [buzz] [default] Buzz reconnecting in 2171ms after: Timed out setting up Buzz relay session
09:51:48.710 [buzz] [default] Buzz reconnecting in 4381ms after: Timed out setting up Buzz relay session

$ run after-control  (fake relay mode: control)
result: Gateway alive at 90s, then stopped by the harness (SIGTERM)
relay websocket connections: 7
10:00:14.316 [buzz] [default] starting account (reason: startup)
10:00:14.465 [buzz] [default] Buzz reconnecting in 1062ms after: Buzz relay closed before NIP-42 authentication completed
10:00:15.800 [buzz] [default] Buzz reconnecting in 2319ms after: Buzz relay closed before NIP-42 authentication completed
10:00:18.149 [buzz] [default] Buzz reconnecting in 4233ms after: Buzz relay closed before NIP-42 authentication completed
```

</details>

prs.title: fix(slack): keep thread typing across queued follow-up turns
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Slack thread status is per thread, but each inbound dispatch owned its own typing lifecycle. A mid-turn mention that cannot be steered (claude-cli) is parked and later runs as a queued follow-up. That follow-up reused the predecessor dispatch's typing controller. Core cleanup seals that controller, and the channel callbacks close with it, so the queued turn never publishes `processing`. A stop from the parked or finished dispatch can also publish `active` while another turn on the same thread is still the one that should look busy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Admitted follow-ups now get a successor typing controller. The predecessor stays sealed. The successor reopens channel typing as a new generation, so a late stop from the sealed lifecycle cannot clear the new indicator. Slack session status uses the same generation: a parked pipeline that never published `processing` does not publish `active`, and a queued turn can publish `processing` again before its own visible output, then return to `active` when it finishes. Status writes are serialized, so a predecessor `active` request cannot take effect after the successor's `processing` request. A finished successor is not started again when that older request resolves. The existing visible-output gate still suppresses status once this turn itself has output.

## User Impact

In a Slack thread, a message sent while the agent is already working no longer drops the native working indicator just because that message was parked. When that message later runs as its own turn, Slack shows the working status again until the turn finishes.

## Evidence

Head: `d4ba62ab06df9b544c5eacf7bd8d1d5a2cac75c1`

Previous CI on `0573de80c75bfb19616c2d8ddc1c7bb13333262c` failed in two jobs:

- `check-lint-core-3`: `src/channels/typing.ts:103:7: error: Function 'stopIfCurrent' expected no return value. (typescript(consistent-return))`
- `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`: `First-party mock factories must preserve real exports or explain isolation` for the new follow-up lifecycle test. The same job also warned `1073 -> 1074 counted lines (cap 700)` on `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply.ts`.

Those are fixed without new suppressions. `stopIfCurrent` now always returns a promise. The lifecycle test spreads `importOriginal`. `get-reply.ts` no longer passes the silent-token default explicitly, so its counted lines move `1076 -> 1075` against current main. Local `check:test-mock-exports` and `check:line-cap-ratchet` against `upstream/main` passed. oxlint on the touched files is clean, including the extension tsconfig rule that rejected unbound test helpers.

Local publisher stub, no Slack Socket Mode and no user token. `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.typing-lifecycle.test.ts extensions/slack/src/monitor/message-handler/thread-status.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed. The follow-up runner drove the stub and printed:

`FOLLOWUP_EVENTS ["processing#0","active#0","processing#1","followup-started","active#1"]`

A later stop and start on that sealed predecessor did not append another event. With the predecessor `active` write held until after the successor had started, settlement was `["processing","active","processing"]`. When the successor also finished before that write resolved, settlement was `["processing","active","processing","active"]`, and a further stop published nothing.

The ordering regression fails on the previous cycle: while the delayed `active` write is still pending, the successor `processing` write is already in flight (`expected 2 to be 1`).

Maintainer decision still open: whether `beginNextLifecycle` should become a supported optional `TypingCallbacks` contract. Issue #158350 does not pin that public-API choice.

Fixes openclaw/openclaw#158350

prs.title: fix(litellm): image edits fail for Gemini models because n is always sent
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #169120

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `openclaw infer image edit` (and agent image edits) through the bundled `litellm` provider always send `n` in the edit request — including the default `count = 1`. LiteLLM rejects `n` on `/v1/images/edits` for Gemini image models, so single-image edits fail with HTTP 400 `UnsupportedParamsError: ... not supported for model gemini-3-pro-image: n`. Image generation with the same model works because LiteLLM accepts `n=1` on `/v1/images/generations`.

- **Related:** None — no competing open PR; issue carries `clawsweeper:source-repro` / `clawsweeper:fix-shape-clear` / `clawsweeper:queueable-fix`.

## Why This Change Was Made

LiteLLM's OpenAI-compatible images API defaults `n` to 1, so an explicit `n=1` is redundant and is rejected by backends (e.g. `vertex_ai/gemini-3-pro-image`) that do not map `n` on edits when `drop_params` is disabled. The fix sends `n` only when more than one image is requested (`count > 1`), in both `buildEditRequest` and `buildGenerateRequest` for consistency.

- **Intended outcome:** single-image LiteLLM edits (and generations) omit `n` and succeed; multi-image requests still send `n`.
- **Out of scope:** enabling `drop_params` globally (hides other genuine parameter errors); any change to other providers or the underlying transport.
- **Highest-risk area:** omitting `n` could change behavior for backends that require an explicit `n` even for a single image.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** `n` defaults to 1 on the OpenAI-compatible Images API, and the existing multi-image test (`n: 2`) is preserved; the default `count = 1` case relies on the API default.

## User Impact

Users of the `litellm` provider can now successfully edit images with Gemini image models (and any other backend that rejects an explicit `n=1`) without needing to bypass OpenClaw or enable `drop_params`.

- **Success criteria:** single-image edits omit `n` from the multipart body; generation omits `n` from the JSON body for `count = 1`; multi-image requests still include `n`; existing `n: 2` test still passes.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `extensions/litellm/image-generation-provider.ts` request builders and the new regression tests in `image-generation-provider.test.ts`.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** local worktree on `main` + patch; Node v26.7.0; **a real LiteLLM proxy process** (`berriai/litellm` **1.105.0**, installed from PyPI into an isolated venv) serving `vertex_ai/gemini-3-pro-image`. The **actual OpenClaw litellm provider code** (this PR's patched source, and `origin/main`'s unpatched source) was driven through the **real shared HTTP transport (`fetch` to `baseUrl`, not mocked)** against that real proxy. The **only** stubbed component is the paid Google Vertex AI SaaS upstream, reached via LiteLLM's own documented `api_base` override (`VertexAIGeminiImageEditConfig.validate_environment` skips credential checks when a custom `api_base` is set). LiteLLM itself — the parameter-validation/transformation layer that raises `UnsupportedParamsError` — is the **real dependency running for real**, before any upstream network call. This replaces the earlier hand-written LiteLLM simulator: the contested contract is now answered by real LiteLLM, not a mock of it.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # real LiteLLM proxy from PyPI (no Gemini credentials required — the `n`
  # rejection happens in LiteLLM's param-mapping layer, before the upstream call)
  uv pip install --python /tmp/ll-venv/bin/python --index-url https://pypi.org/simple "litellm[proxy]==1.105.0"
  python stub-vertex-upstream.py &                       # stub ONLY the paid Google SaaS (127.0.0.1:58080)
  litellm --config litellm-proxy-config.yaml --port 48080 --host 127.0.0.1 &   # REAL litellm proxy

  # (a) issue's exact curl repro, straight through the real proxy
  curl -s -w "HTTP %{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:48080/v1/images/edits \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -F model=vertex_ai/gemini-3-pro-image \
    -F prompt="make the cube blue" -F size=1024x1024 -F n=1 -F image=@in.png   # BEFORE -> 400
  # same command WITHOUT -F n=1                                                # AFTER  -> 200

  # (b) real OpenClaw provider driving the real proxy (patched vs unpatched source)
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/litellm/image-generation-provider.test.ts   # 12 regression tests
  # temporary live harness (not committed): git checkout origin/main|HEAD -- <provider>; run; delete

  # (c) SHIPPED OpenClaw CLI flow — the built `openclaw` binary driven end to end
  node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts qaRuntime        # builds dist/ from this PR's source
  OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<fresh-state> node openclaw.mjs infer image edit \
    --file in.png --prompt "make the cube blue" \
    --model litellm/vertex_ai/gemini-3-pro-image                         # PATCHED   -> 200, PNG written
  # same command after rebuilding dist from the PRE-PATCH parent commit    # UNPATCHED -> 400 UnsupportedParamsError
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:** regression tests green — `Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 12 passed (12)`. Real LiteLLM proxy responses to the issue's exact curl commands:
  ```text
  POST /v1/images/edits        n=1  (before fix) -> HTTP 400  litellm.UnsupportedParamsError:
                                       The following parameters are not supported for model gemini-3-pro-image: n
  POST /v1/images/edits        no-n (after fix)  -> HTTP 200  data[0].b64_json image returned
  POST /v1/images/generations  n=1  (before fix) -> HTTP 200  (LiteLLM accepts n on generations — matches the issue)
  POST /v1/images/generations  no-n (after fix)  -> HTTP 200  image returned
  ```
  Real OpenClaw provider (this PR's code) driving the real proxy, patched vs unpatched:
  ```text
  unpatched (origin/main, sends n=1): EDIT FAILS -> "LiteLLM image edit failed (HTTP 400):
      litellm.UnsupportedParamsError: ... not supported for model gemini-3-pro-image: n"
      (thrown from real src/image-generation/openai-compatible-image-provider.ts:212); GENERATION passes.
      Tests 1 failed | 1 passed  -- reproduces the issue exactly: edits break, generations work.
  patched (this PR, omits n):         EDIT passes (images returned: 1); GENERATION passes. Tests 2 passed.
  ```
  Real proxy server-side access log:
  ```text
  POST /v1/images/edits        400 Bad Request   # unpatched provider (n=1)
  POST /v1/images/generations  200 OK
  POST /v1/images/edits        200 OK            # patched provider (no n)
  POST /v1/images/generations  200 OK
  ```
  **Shipped OpenClaw CLI flow** (`node openclaw.mjs infer image edit …`, dist built by `build-all.mts qaRuntime` from this PR's source, same real LiteLLM proxy, fresh `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`; redacted terminal output):
  ```text
  # AFTER (this PR's source): default-count single-image edit — SUCCESS
  $ node openclaw.mjs infer image edit --file in.png --prompt "make the cube blue" \
      --model litellm/vertex_ai/gemini-3-pro-image
  image.edit via local
  provider: litellm
  model: vertex_ai/gemini-3-pro-image
  outputs: 1
  /…/media/generated/image-1---af51ee3a-be88-4606-be4a-9e420ebd16d0.png   # real PNG file written

  # BEFORE (dist rebuilt from this PR's PRE-PATCH parent commit 7dd5b520d47 — identical except the fix):
  $ node openclaw.mjs infer image edit --file in.png --prompt "make the cube blue" \
      --model litellm/vertex_ai/gemini-3-pro-image
  [image-generation] candidate failed: litellm/vertex_ai/gemini-3-pro-image:
      LiteLLM image edit failed (HTTP 400): litellm.UnsupportedParamsError:
      The following parameters are not supported for model gemini-3-pro-image: n
  LiteLLM: model group 'vertex_ai/gemini-3-pro-image' failed with the error above.
      No fallback was attempted. [type=invalid_request_error, code=400]

  # the CLI generation path (accepted `n`) works identically before and after, matching the issue report
  $ node openclaw.mjs infer image generate --prompt "a red cube" --model litellm/vertex_ai/gemini-3-pro-image
  image.generate via local … outputs: 1                                          # both BEFORE and AFTER -> 200
  ```
  The real proxy's access log confirms each CLI run on the wire (patched runs first, then the pre-patch rebuild):
  ```text
  POST /v1/images/edits        200 OK            # patched CLI edit (no n)
  POST /v1/images/generations  200 OK            # patched CLI generate
  POST /v1/images/edits        400 Bad Request   # pre-patch CLI edit (n=1)
  POST /v1/images/generations  200 OK            # pre-patch CLI generate
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** with the patched provider, a default-count (`count = 1`) edit sends **no `n`** on the wire and the **real LiteLLM proxy returns HTTP 200 with an image**; single-image generation likewise returns 200. With the unpatched provider, the same edit sends `n=1` and the **real LiteLLM proxy rejects it with HTTP 400 `UnsupportedParamsError: ... n`** — the exact failure from the issue. The same holds through the **shipped OpenClaw CLI**: `openclaw infer image edit` fails with the 400 `UnsupportedParamsError` on the pre-patch build and returns a generated PNG on this PR's build. Multi-image requests (`count = 2`) still send `n` (existing regression test preserved).
- **Before evidence:** unpatched source (`form.set("n", String(count))` / `n: count`) driven through the real proxy → `POST /v1/images/edits` returns `400` with `litellm.UnsupportedParamsError: The following parameters are not supported for model gemini-3-pro-image: n` (verbatim match to the report). The two new regression tests (`omits n on single-image edits so LiteLLM defaults it to 1`, `omits n on single-image generation requests`) also pass only with the fix.
- **What was not tested:** a live production `vertex_ai/gemini-3-pro-image` round-trip returning a real Gemini-edited image (no Gemini/GCP credentials exist in this environment). The Google Vertex AI SaaS upstream is stubbed via LiteLLM's documented `api_base` override; this stub stands in for Google's cloud, **not** for LiteLLM. The contested behavior (LiteLLM rejects `n` on Gemini edits, accepts it on generations) is enforced by the **real LiteLLM 1.105.0** param-validation layer, which runs before the upstream call — so the stub does not affect the proven contract. LiteLLM's own `vertex_gemini_transformation.py` (`SUPPORTED_PARAMS = ["size"]`, excluding `n`) is the source of that contract.
- **Proof tier:** L3 (real LiteLLM proxy process + real OpenClaw provider + real HTTP transport + shipped OpenClaw CLI flow (`openclaw infer image edit`); only the paid Google Vertex AI SaaS upstream stubbed, via LiteLLM's own api_base override).
- **Proof limitations:** no live Gemini/GCP credentials, so the Google Vertex AI upstream (a paid SaaS, not the code under test) is stubbed; LiteLLM itself is the real 1.105.0 package and its `n`-rejection is real, not simulated.
- **Review state:** Awaiting maintainer review.

prs.title: fix: stop local cron probes from logging auth failures
prs.body:
Closes #157140. Thanks @franssauermann for the report.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes spurious 401 errors on authenticated local model servers when isolated cron jobs probe `/models` without provider credentials before inference.

## User Impact

Local-provider preflight checks whether the server accepts a connection without sending HTTP or credentials. Inference continues to own TLS, authentication, and model errors. No configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing cron preflight only needs reachability. It now opens and closes a TCP connection using the same exact-host/private-network DNS policy and one 2.5-second deadline. Connection diagnostics, timeout retry, endpoint caching, and fallback selection remain in their existing owners. Managed-proxy endpoints defer to inference rather than being incorrectly rejected by a direct socket check.

## Evidence

- Main reproduction through a real isolated cron job, OpenAI-compatible local proxy, and Ollama `qwen3:4b`: the job returned `CRON_AUTH_OK`; preflight sent an unauthenticated `GET /v1/models` that returned 401, while inference correctly sent the configured bearer/header and succeeded. Afterward, the same job again returned `CRON_AUTH_OK`; the proxy recorded only the correctly authenticated `/v1/chat/completions` request, with no `/models` request or 401.
- The no-HTTP regression fails on the original source. Final changed-file tests: 26 pass in 6.01 s wall (3.77 s wrapper shard), including real loopback socket closure, zero HTTP requests, refusal, virtual DNS/connect deadlines, cache retry, and managed-proxy bypass. The 11 fallback-policy tests pass in 41.41 s cold wall. All 7 persisted-diagnostics E2E cases pass after replacing their obsolete broken-HTTP fixture with a real connection-refusal endpoint (907.84 s cold wrapper wall, including runtime rebuild and worker preparation; 210.30 s test-run duration, about 40 s in test bodies).
- `pnpm build`, targeted lint, core types, and all seven required ratchets pass. Independent Codex review is scoped-clean with no actionable findings. ClawSweeper found no code issues or Before merge items on the preceding head; its request for an attached raw trace remains a proof-only limitation under the maintainer-approved override. The trace was inspected locally. Test-only follow-ups fix strict indexed-access typing and update the persisted-diagnostics fixture from a broken HTTP listener to a reserved, refused TCP port. This keeps real connection-failure coverage under the new reachability contract. Independent review and exact-head ClawSweeper are clean. CI run 38234331334 passes all affected checks but the aggregate gate is red from inherited PR-wrapper packaging failures: `eager-import-closure.test.ts` cannot find `src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.message.ts` in the wrapper inventory, so both inventory closure and extracted-package resolution fail. Both failures reproduce on the exact CI main base `285369b043cf3720bcc6a89ce0ce1d2cf1ba4210` (67.93 s focused wall time). These files are unchanged by this PR.
- Production +50/-53; tests +267/-489; docs +2; obsolete timeout-race and partial-mock baseline entries -3. HTTP response tests were retired with the HTTP probe; TCP lifecycle and diagnostics retain the applicable behavior coverage.
