prs.title: fix(sessions): avoid first-turn refusals from retired Usage executors
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a new session's first turn being refused with `Agent database execution admission is closed` when Usage writer preparation retains an executor that retires before consumption.

## User Impact

An existing store's Usage refresh acquires its current executor at writer admission. Session replacement and the first turn can proceed against the original physical store. A replacement file, revoked refresh authority, or cancellation still refuses the write. No operator action or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cache retained an execution reference before awaited work. Capture of an existing-store executor now happens inside the existing writer reservation, after checking the refresh authority, with the originally observed physical identity pinned. Missing stores still retain their creation witness before yielding; existing writers are still prepared before the scan, preserving the cold scan/prune fix in #170308. Incognito and maintenance paths are unchanged. There are no retries or changes to timeouts, schema, durability, retention, FIFO ordering, or authority.

Source attribution: the early cache-writer capture originated in #163287 (`4a66195396d4`) and survived the process-local reservation change in #169974 and existing-store preparation in #170308. The native failure also reproduced on #170464's warmed parent, so reverting #170464 does not repair it. This is source attribution plus a current-main deterministic negative control, not a claimed historical first-red bisect.

## Evidence

The new regression forces retirement before Usage acquisition, then verifies session replacement and independently reads the committed session and rollup. It fails on unpatched main `f9af58c66f79` with the exact admission-closed error (333 ms case; 50.89 s wrapper). Companion cases retain refusal and unchanged file bytes after physical replacement or authority revocation.

- `pnpm test src/infra/session-cost-usage-cache.admission.test.ts src/infra/session-cost-usage-cache.worker.test.ts src/state/openclaw-agent-execution.idle.test.ts src/state/openclaw-agent-execution.close-wedge.test.ts src/gateway/server.sessions.create.auth-policy.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 51/51 passed, 194.75 s wrapper. Includes the original Gateway initial-turn case and cancellation, pending-open, FIFO, missing-store creation, drainage, idle retention, and native-close recovery contracts. The three new cases took 1.178, 1.544, and 1.056 s.
- Core production types and the owning infra test graph passed. Changed-file typed lint, boundary lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed. The changed-check plan was inspected; broad checks are delegated to PR CI under the narrow-local proof policy.
- Isolated P2 review: scoped-clean, no actionable findings.

CI seconds are not available at PR creation. The first implementation used a creation constraint for an existing file and failed three pending-open assertions; using the existing file constraint restored them without changing those tests. The new replacement control initially expected the wrong refusal text and now asserts the owner's exact existing-only identity error. No failing run is relabeled green.

## Scope

prs.title: fix(mattermost): agent buttons render as plain text
prs.body:
Closes #168081

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Mattermost agents send unclickable text when they follow the advertised typed-callback button example, including Claude CLI-backed turns.

## User Impact

Mattermost accounts with `capabilities: ["inlineButtons"]` receive clickable choices. Disabled accounts receive no button hint. Rendering semantics and account configuration are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Mattermost channel adapter teaches its supported plain `value` shape using the existing account inspector. Core respects the optional typed `agentPrompt.customInlineButtonHint` contract instead of naming vendors. Slack uses the same contract, replacing its core exception. Ordinary, compaction, and CLI prompt preparation consume the same channel-owned guidance. There is no separate Mattermost prompt module.

Thanks to @ericcurtin for the original fix and @hannnnn-l for the report. Pash's overlapping Slack change concerns Markdown formatting; its instructions are unchanged, with a captured Slack control. No Sarah overlap was found in the changed owners.

## Evidence

Built base `d70a7e7300cd` and final candidate `9cab0322ca5d` in secretless Docker. Both embedded and **Claude CLI-backed** isolated Gateways received a Mattermost WebSocket message. A scripted model copied the example from the system prompt it received. The CLI fixture implements Claude's live stdio initialization/hooks and uses the real bundled MCP `message` tool, not a direct post helper.

| Observation | Base | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Enabled prompt example | `"action":{"type":"callback","value":"yes"}` | `"value":"yes"` |
| Actual `POST /api/v4/posts` | Text `Choose Yes` followed by `- Yes`; no attachments | Same accessible text plus `props.attachments[0].actions[0]` with `{"id":"yes","type":"button","name":"Yes"}` |
| API click | No action exists | `POST /api/v4/posts/<post>/actions/yes`; signed callback returns HTTP 200 |
| Agent input after click | Not possible | `[Button click: user @proofuser selected "Yes"]` |
| Agent reply | Not possible | Actual post: `Selection received: Yes.` |
| Buttons-disabled account | No enabled example; text-only post | No button hint; text-only post |

The embedded Slack **Messaging section is byte-identical** across base/candidate. CLI Slack suppresses the generic callback/OFF advice on both refs; the candidate also receives Slack's plugin-owned message guidance. Other prompt sections contain lane-specific state/workspace identifiers and are not asserted identical.

The preview image publishes only `linux/amd64`, while this runner is arm64. This uses the allowed Mattermost REST/WebSocket contract server rather than an emulated preview/database stack. It exercises shipped Gateway startup, ingress, model prompt assembly, message-tool/MCP dispatch, HTTP post payloads, signed callbacks, and selection readback. Mattermost UI rendering itself was not exercised.

- Final `pnpm build`, embedded roundtrip, CLI/MCP roundtrip, and disabled/Slack controls passed.
- Real-provider gate on the final candidate: `gpt-5-mini` returned `READY`, exit 0, without fallback. A Codex one-shot client cleanup warning was also logged.
- Prompt-focused tests: 74 passed across the CLI prompt, core prompt, and Mattermost hint files in 54.93s. After integrating main's profile-authority repair, both previously failing files passed locally: four cron manual-tool-authority cases and two pinned skill-library cases. Changed-file Oxfmt and Oxlint passed.
- Against merge base `db5cdcaf8e31`: production +50/-19 (net +31), tests +74/-7 (net +67), docs +5. The remaining growth carries the generic typed contract through all prompt owners; the vendor branch and standalone module are removed.
- Exact-head [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38341089751): `ci-gate` succeeded, no failed or cancelled jobs. ClawSweeper is ready on `9cab0322ca5d`; no CI override is required.

The previous CI reds were in cron operator authority and pinned skill-library session creation. This head incorporates main's authority repair; all six cases now pass locally, and the complete button proof was rerun afterward. No override of those failures is requested.

An earlier run also encountered the cron snapshot-count regression from #170463: `run.cron-model-override-forwarding.test.ts`, “persists the model and harness before execution (pre-run write fails: true),” expected three snapshots but received two. prs.title: feat(tui): add keyword slash command discovery in terminal editor
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Users frequently want to discover and execute actions like checking session costs, token usage, switching models, or resetting sessions without having to memorize exact slash command names or syntax.

## User Impact

User impact: Users typing slash commands with keyword synonyms (such as `/pricing`, `/token`, `/spend` -> `/usage`, `/switch`, `/llm` -> `/model`, `/restart` -> `/reset`) now discover and receive suggestions for the canonical underlying commands, preserving existing editor ergonomics and Tab file completion.

## Proposed Changes

1. **Scoped Slash Keyword Discovery**:
   - Implements `matchSlashKeywords` in `src/tui/commands-intent.ts` with weighted tag rankings for common operational keywords.
   - Strictly scoped to slash-prefixed input (`textBeforeCursor.startsWith("/")`) to guarantee ordinary conversational drafting and Tab-based file autocompletion are 100% preserved.

2. **Combined Autocomplete Integration**:
   - In `createTuiAutocompleteProvider` (`src/tui/tui-autocomplete.ts`), keyword matches augment standard slash suggestions.
   - Conforms strictly to `@earendil-works/pi-tui`'s `CombinedAutocompleteProvider` contract by passing bare command values (`value: m.command`), preventing double-slash (`//`) prefix artifacts upon selection.

3. **Decoupled Screen Clearing**:
   - Screen clearing is strictly decoupled from session reset to prevent any unintended session state modifications.

4. **Automated Test Coverage**:
   - Focused unit and integration tests in `src/tui/commands-intent.test.ts` exercising tag ranking, available command filtering, bare command completion application, and ordinary draft preservation.

prs.title: fix(agents): private subagent results are lost when the requester runs on a CLI backend
prs.body:
Related: #121661

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a hidden subagent spawned with `completionTarget: "parent"` finishes, but the user never hears about the result when the requester session runs on a CLI backend such as `claude-cli`.

## User Impact

User impact: requesters on CLI backends can relay private subagent results with the `message` tool, as the private-completion prompt already tells them to. That completion turn gets `message` only, still subject to operator, sandbox, inherited, and subagent policy. It does not get native CLI tools or the rest of the requester's tools. Embedded runtimes, announce-mode completions, and untrusted handoffs behave as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

A private parent completion runs the requester turn with delivery disabled. Since #149073 its prompt says the final reply stays internal and any user-facing update must go through a permitted messaging tool. Embedded requesters keep their tools for this turn. CLI completion handoffs never retain the requester tool surface, and the message-only grant was minted only for `message_tool_only` handoffs. On CLI the turn therefore ran with zero tools: the model answered `NO_REPLY` or wrote the tool call as plain text, and the result was dropped.

This change reuses the existing message-only grant for that case. A trusted handoff on a CLI runtime with `deliver === false` and `automatic` reply mode (the pair the private-completion path sends; its Gateway admission requires `deliver === false`) goes through the same `completion-handoff` policy check as message-tool-only handoffs and gets `toolsAllow: ["message"]`.

The grant needs the CLI runtime decision before the completion policy is resolved. `attempt-execution.ts` is over its line cap and the ratchet blocks growth, so the unchanged CLI runtime selection moved into `attempt-cli-runtime.ts` instead of up the same file. The CLI test file is over its cap too, so the CLI completion-handoff table test reads case fields directly instead of destructuring them, and that file does not grow either.

This is the narrow message-only slice proposed in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/121661#issuecomment-5840016202. It does not touch announce-mode wakes or restore the full requester tool surface on CLI; both stay open in #121661.

Risks and notes:

- One turn type goes from no tools to `message`. That turn's prompt carries frozen child output, so a prompt-injected child result could make the requester send a message to its source conversation or another permitted target. Message-tool-only handoffs and embedded private completions already have the same exposure. Explicit denies (operator, sandbox, inherited, subagent) still win, and `disableMessageTool` still turns it off.
- Destination scope (maintainer decision): this PR mints the existing completion-handoff message grant, not a new one. `message_tool_only` handoffs on `main` already give CLI requesters the same grant with the same destinations: anything the requester's policy permits, not only the source conversation, because the current-conversation fence covers read-capable actions, not `send` (`send` maps to `NO_CONVERSATION_READ` in `src/channels/plugins/message-action-dispatch.ts`). My recommendation is to accept that bounded grant, since operator denies, channel action gates, and revoked grants all stop the send at the final effect (see Evidence). If maintainers want private completions limited to the source conversation, that limit should cover both completion paths at their shared owner, so it belongs in a follow-up rather than in this PR alone.
- The discriminator is `deliver === false` plus `sourceReplyDeliveryMode: "automatic"` on a trusted `subagent_announce` handoff. Today only the private parent handoff produces that pair; a future path sending it would get the same message-only grant.
- The completion turn still starts a fresh CLI session (`cli session reset: reason=mcp`) because its MCP tool set differs from the conversation's. That already happened with zero tools; fresh-session and history-reseed behavior on such turns is discussed in #135364, #157823, and #154716. The requester's own CLI session binding is not touched: the next ordinary turn resumes it.

## Evidence

### Final-effect proof at `5b18b47d73600a17ce322e47cbfdf39ae09cc030`

The head adds one test commit on top of `dd2ed0476b0`; the production change is unchanged.

`test/cli-private-completion-message.integration.test.ts` drives the whole chain: a real Gateway, the private parent completion, the real CLI runner and its MCP loopback grant, the `message` tool, and the Telegram plugin's transport. Only Claude's decisions and Telegram's responses are synthetic. A protocol child stands in for Claude: it reads the MCP config the runner generated and calls the real loopback server with the minted grant. A fixture Bot API records every outbound send. Each case spawns a hidden child with `completionTarget: "parent"` from a `claude-cli` requester bound to a Telegram chat, then observes the requester's completion turn:

| Case | Completion turn | `message` call | Sends to Telegram with the child result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Allowed | MCP tools: exactly `message` | `ok`, message 702 to the requester chat | **1** |
| Operator `tools.deny: ["message"]` | no MCP server | none | **0** |
| `channels.telegram.actions.sendMessage: false` | MCP tools: exactly `message` | `isError`: "Telegram sendMessage is disabled." | **0** |
| Grant revoked between `tools/list` and `tools/call` | MCP tools: exactly `message` | HTTP 401 from the loopback server | **0** |

In every case the completion turn ran, and the requester's own reply reached the same chat, so the transport was reachable.

- Negative control: with only `attempt-execution.ts` reverted to `main` (`85afbe9e3c1`), the allowed, gated, and revoked cases fail. The completion turn starts with no MCP server (`{"kind":"completion","mcp":false,"calls":[]}`), and Telegram receives only the requester's reply. The deny case passes either way.
- Cost: `pnpm test test/cli-private-completion-message.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` takes 88.0 s command wall (75.7 s in Vitest): 27.0 s for the first case including warm-up, then 11–12 s per case. The test needs the host SQLite broker, so it is registered in the database-worker project. It is also listed as release-only, so CI runs it when it changes rather than on every pull request.
- Checks for this commit: the test-root type graph `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.other.json`, oxlint on the new test, type-aware oxlint on `scripts/lib/ci-proof-test-inventory.mts`, the inventory and Vitest ownership tests (490 passed), `oxfmt --check`, `git diff --check`, and the line-cap and max-lines ratchets against `85afbe9e3c1`.

### Earlier checks

Rebased onto `main` at 85afbe9e3c1. The conflicts came from #160786 and the agents cleanup passes; the production change is unchanged. #160786 keeps requester tools for settled `sessions_yield` continuations and does not cover this path: on current `main` a CLI private parent completion still runs tool-free (see the RED control below).

Focused checks on the rebased head `dd2ed0476b0`, run locally on Node 26.9.0:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/command/attempt-execution.cli.test.ts`: 83/83 passed, including the 8 new cases. `main` has since pruned this file, so the earlier 178-test count no longer applies.
- RED control on the rebased head: with only the new grant disabled, `bounds CLI subagent completion handoff tools for a private parent completion` is the single failure; the other 21 handoff cases pass.
- `attempt-execution.test.ts`, `attempt-execution.shared.test.ts`, `attempt-execution.error-propagation.test.ts`, and `attempt-callbacks.test.ts` pass.
- `tsgo:core` and the `tsgo` core-test graph `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-other.json` (which covers the changed tests) pass. Type-aware oxlint on the changed files is clean.
- `oxfmt --check`, `git diff --check`, and the line-cap and max-lines ratchets against `main` are clean.
- New cases: a CLI private completion gets `["message"]` with `disableTools: false`. These stay tool-free on CLI: a delivered automatic completion, and private completions with `disableMessageTool`, an operator `deny: ["message"]`, a runtime allowlist without `message`, an untrusted handoff, or a nested subagent requester. An embedded private completion still keeps the requester tools.

Live on OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (`eb377ac`) with a `claude-cli` requester and the same logic applied as a local patch to the 2026.9.6 build:

- Before: completion turns for `completionTarget: "parent"` children exposed 0 tools. Over two days 5 of 5 private results never reached the user.
- After: the completion turn exposed exactly `mcp__openclaw__message`, made one real `message(action=send)` call that returned `ok: true`, then ended with `NO_REPLY`. The next ordinary turn resumed the requester's CLI session.

```text
cli session reset: provider=claude-cli reason=mcp
cli exec: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 ... useResume=false ... reuse=invalidated:mcp historyPrompt=none
# tool list in the completion turn's Claude Code transcript
tools=1 ['mcp__openclaw__message']
tool_use mcp__openclaw__message action=send -> {"ok": true, ...}
cli exec: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 ... useResume=true ... reuse=reusable historyPrompt=none
```

The live patch used `deliver !== true` plus an explicit subagent-session guard. This PR uses `deliver === false` and relies on the subagent `message` deny instead. In the Gateway path `deliver` is always a boolean, and nested requesters are denied `message` by policy (see the nested case), so both variants grant the same turns. The live run covered a top-level requester only.

Checks and review:

- On the original head `904ddf78bd9`, `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` (lanes: core, core tests) passed: line-cap ratchet, `tsgo:core`, all `tsgo:core:test` graphs, oxlint on the changed files, Knip unused-export scans (0 entries), and import cycles (0).
- The nested-requester case was confirmed with temporary local logging (removed before commit): the handoff is trusted and the grant is requested, but the subagent `message` deny rejects it. The test assertion alone cannot tell that apart from an untrusted handoff.
- `autoreview` on the original head against `main` at P2: `scoped-clean`, no findings. Codex was unavailable here (authentication error), so the Claude engine ran it, as the skill allows.

CI on `dd2ed0476b0` failed six tests in five shards. None of them is in this PR's files. `src/gateway/session-activity-summaries.test.ts` › "readmits a relocated store and fences a delayed result" fails the same way on `main`'s hourly CI ([run 36697144647](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36697144647)). The other five are timing and locking failures in gateway-server and Codex tests: `database is locked`, a WebSocket wait timeout, a missed `waitFor` call, a reset-concurrency assertion, and a Codex settle-after-abort assertion. Following the repository's CI policy, I did not rerun them.

Not rerun on the rebased head: Knip, import cycles, and the other `tsgo:core:test` graphs. Not run locally at all: `pnpm build`, the full `pnpm check`, and the full `pnpm test`. Those are left to CI.

prs.title: fix: cap requester-settle history (token tax)
prs.body:
## Summary
- Cap embedded history for `inputProvenance.sourceTool === "subagent_settle"` so settle wakes keep the same requester session (delivery + yield adoption) without replaying a fat Telegram transcript.
- `resolveHistoryLimitForAttempt` now returns a `SettleHistoryLimit` (`{ limit: 4, keepFirstUser: true }` by default) so `limitHistoryTurns` keeps the **originating user request** plus the most recent `limit - 1` turns. This preserves parent requirements and output constraints while trimming transcript replay.
- Keep **normal workspace bootstrap** on settle; `bootstrapContextMode: "lightweight"` is no longer passed, so AGENTS.md / SOUL.md / USER.md instructions remain available.
- Soften settle wake guidance so main verifies child evidence and replies instead of restarting filesystem surgery in the settle turn.

## What Problem This Solves
Requester-settle wakes reuse the parent session (required for delivery routing and yield adoption) but currently feed the full DM transcript into the settle turn. On long Telegram sessions that balloons to ~90 messages / ~300k history tokens and ~900k total tokens for a turn that only needs to verify child evidence and reply. Isolating settle into a new session would break yield adoption, so the fix keeps same-session settle and caps history for `subagent_settle` provenance only. The first implementation only capped the tail; this revision keeps the originating user turn so parent requirements are not evicted.

## Evidence
### Unit / regression
Local validation on commit `0d615933`:

```text
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/test-projects.mts \
    src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/history.test.ts \
    src/agents/embedded-agent-runner.limithistoryturns.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  49 passed (49)   # includes settle-cap + keep-first-user cases

$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/test-projects.mts \
    src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce.requester-settle-dispatch.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  16 passed (16)

$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/test-projects.mts \
    src/cron/service/ops.native-attempt.test.ts \
    src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.code-mode-continuation.test.ts \
    src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.spawn-workspace.context-injection.test.ts
 Test Files  4 passed (4)
      Tests  36 passed (36)
```

A unit-level transcript with 20 user turns (`q0…q19`) trimmed by the settle limit retains `q0` (the originating request) plus the latest tail, while ordinary non-settle paths keep the configured `dmHistoryLimit` unchanged.

### Real behavior proof
`scripts/proof-settle-history-cap.mts` exercises the actual production history-limit helpers (`resolveHistoryLimitForAttempt` + `limitHistoryTurns`) and the production `estimateTokens` heuristic on a synthetic long DM transcript. It does not use mocks and does not touch a live gateway or provider.

Run:

```text
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/proof-settle-history-cap.mts
```

Result on Node v24.16.0:

```text
# Proof: settle history cap reduces input without dropping the original request

Synthetic long DM session: 80 turns + tool results + original request + settle wake.

| Scenario | Kept messages | Kept user turns | Est. input tokens | First user text preserved |
|---|---:|---:|---:|:---|
| Baseline (current main, no settle cap) | 216 | 82 | 124,657 | yes |
| Candidate (settle cap, keep first user turn) | 10 | 5 | 4,755 | yes |

## Inspectable output

{
  "node": "v24.16.0",
  "syntheticTurns": 80,
  "baseline": {
    "name": "Baseline (current main, no settle cap)",
    "limit": "unlimited",
    "totalMessages": 216,
    "keptMessages": 216,
    "userTurnsKept": 82,
    "estimatedInputTokens": 124657,
    "firstUserText": "Review and refactor the statement-pipeline cdk stack. Keep all existing behavior"
  },
  "candidate": {
    "name": "Candidate (settle cap, keep first user turn)",
    "limit": "settle cap 4 keepFirstUser",
    "totalMessages": 216,
    "keptMessages": 10,
    "userTurnsKept": 5,
    "estimatedInputTokens": 4755,
    "firstUserText": "Review and refactor the statement-pipeline cdk stack. Keep all existing behavior"
  },
  "reductionPercent": 96.19,
  "originalRequestPreserved": true
}

## Limits
Controlled local execution of production history-limit helpers only; no live gateway, provider,
or remote session store. Token estimates use the production estimateTokens heuristic, not a
provider tokenizer. Timings are not measured because this is a pure context-size proof.
```

## Test plan
- [x] `history.test.ts` + `limithistoryturns.test.ts` settle-cap + keep-first-user coverage
- [x] `requester-settle-dispatch.test.ts`
- [x] Embedded-run and cron affected shards (previously failed on mocked history.js)
- [x] `scripts/proof-settle-history-cap.mts` real-behavior proof
- [ ] Confirm settle still delivers on the requester session and yield adoption still works after upgrade
- [ ] Spot-check Langfuse/S3 root usage: settle turns should drop from ~900k toward wake+evidence scale

prs.title: ci(i18n): add non-publishing native locale refresh
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where maintainers cannot refresh secret-backed native translations for review without also creating and arming an auto-merge generated PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds an explicit non-publishing dispatch mode that runs the existing bounded locale matrix and validation, then uploads an allowlisted binary patch artifact. The default publishing path remains unchanged. A separate preflight-only mode proves an exact branch workflow definition without using translation or publishing secrets.

Secret-backed non-publishing runs execute only from the trusted `main` workflow. The operator supplies an exact source SHA; that SHA must be the current head of one open, non-draft PR targeting `main` with GitHub's current review decision `APPROVED`. Each locale worker revalidates the exact PR head and current approval immediately before the translation-secret step. Branch-selected workflow dispatch remains preflight-only and cannot reach translation or publication secrets.

## User Impact

No direct user-facing change. Maintainers gain a review-only native translation refresh path that cannot push, open a PR, or enable auto-merge, while unreviewed branch code cannot receive the translation credential.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/native-app-locale-refresh-workflow.test.ts` — 1 passed on exact head after rebase
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- .github/workflows/native-app-locale-refresh.yml test/scripts/native-app-locale-refresh-workflow.test.ts` — changed-surface format, type, lint, dependency, coercion, and dead-export gates passed
- `pnpm format:check --no-error-on-unmatched-pattern -- .github/workflows/native-app-locale-refresh.yml test/scripts/native-app-locale-refresh-workflow.test.ts` — passed after rebase
- `git diff --check` — passed after rebase
- Autoreview — clean; no accepted/actionable findings (confidence 0.87)
- Security boundary: non-publishing translation requires `github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'`; `source_sha` is exact, PR-bound, currently approved, and revalidated directly before the secret-bearing step. Arbitrary branch dispatch is limited to `preflight_only`.
- Production LOC: 0. Workflow policy: +198/-12. Guard tests: +101.

prs.title: feat(discord): AI auto-naming for threads via channels.discord.thread.autoName
prs.body:
Closes #160865

## What Problem This Solves

Discord threads often keep a generic creation-time name even after a conversation has made the topic clear. Renaming them manually or asking the agent to do it adds work to each thread.

## Why This Change Was Made

`channels.discord.thread.autoName` adds an opt-in message threshold for newly created threads. At the threshold, the Discord plugin sends a bounded recent user/agent transcript through the existing isolated conversation-label generator, sanitizes its title to Discord's 100-character limit, and attempts one rename. The generator starts with the configured utility model and can fall back to the agent's primary model; it does not read the thread session.

The plugin persists a one-time claim per account/thread, checks **Manage Threads** before and after generation, and limits its own rename attempts to two per parent channel in ten minutes. It skips further attempts when that budget is exhausted or Discord returns a permission or rate-limit response. A manually renamed thread is left alone.

The channel config schema has two new leaf paths (channel-wide and account override), so the intentional config-surface count rises from 3726 to 3728. Generated channel metadata and the docs baseline are updated with the schema.

## User Impact

```json5
{
  channels: {
    discord: {
      thread: { autoName: 5 },
      accounts: { work: { thread: { autoName: 8 } } },
    },
  },
}
```

`false` or `0` disables auto-naming (the default), `true` uses five user/agent messages, and a positive integer sets the threshold. An account value overrides the channel-wide value. Each new thread gets at most one attempt, including after a Gateway restart.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test:extension discord`: 268 files, 3,755 tests passed.
- Focused config, title-generation, and auto-naming Vitest files: 79 tests passed. These mock Discord API calls and cover parsing, account overrides, title cleanup and truncation, gateway listeners, one-time state, a manual-rename race, parent rate window, permission loss, and 429 handling.
- `pnpm lint:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm docs:check-config-examples`, `pnpm config:docs:check`, and `git diff --check` passed.

No live Discord account was used; the new behavior was exercised at the mocked gateway and REST boundary.

prs.title: fix(usage): Claude Code subscription usage missing for agents running on claude-cli
prs.body:
Related: #143419, #156296 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: agents that run through Claude Code (`claude-cli`) never show the subscription usage they actually consume. `usage.status` either has no Claude row or shows an error for a different Anthropic credential. ## User Impact Usage now follows the route an agent runs on. When agents run through Claude Code under the Gateway host's own login, `usage.status` reports a separate **Claude Code** row with that subscription's 5-hour and weekly windows and reset times. The row reaches the Control UI Usage page, chat `/status`, and Gateway clients. The **Anthropic** row is unchanged: an API key still shows spend and cost, a setup-token still shows its own result or error, and nothing is substituted between the two. The row appears after the first Claude Code turn following a Gateway start. It carries when it was reported (`observedAt`), shown as `as of 12m ago` in `/status` and `Observed 12m ago` on the Control UI usage cards, so a reader can tell when it may be out of date. ## Why This Change Was Made Anthropic has two billing surfaces, and OpenClaw can use both at once: - **Pay-per-use API** (API key): spend and cost, no subscription windows. - **Subscription through Claude Code** (`claude auth login`): the 5-hour and weekly windows. OpenClaw currently reports both as one "Claude" row and only asks the Anthropic credential for usage. For the Claude Code route that cannot work: - The usage request deliberately never uses Claude Code's login, because refreshing it would break Claude's own session (#129052). - A saved setup-token is refused with `scope requirement user:profile` (#143419). - An API key has no subscription windows at all. - Since `b9b2f455`, Claude Code runs never borrow a generic saved Anthropic credential. So whatever the Anthropic row reports can belong to a different account, or a different billing surface, than the one the agent is using. Claude Code already reports its own windows on every turn. Its stream-json output carries a `rate_limit_event` whose `rate_limit_info.unifiedWindows` has `five_hour` and `seven_day` utilization and reset times, and OpenClaw currently discards it. This change: - reads that record where the Claude stream is parsed; - keeps the latest windows in Gateway memory under a Claude Code identity; - reports them as their own **Claude Code** row whenever Claude usage is requested, beside the Anthropic row and never merged into it. **Recording is limited to the Gateway host's own Claude login.** It is skipped for: - paired-node turns; - turns under an OpenClaw auth profile (pinned, set on the agent's model, or picked automatically); - turns with a credential, auth endpoint, or provider switch in the child environment. Any `ANTHROPIC_*` variable counts except model selectors, OpenClaw's Admin API usage and API-key rotation keys, and Vertex project settings (inert without `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX`, which counts). Claude Code tokens and switches such as Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry, Mantle, or a gateway count too; names are matched case-insensitively; - turns with a `--settings` or `--managed-settings` backend argument; - turns with a different or skill-provided `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. Each of those can be another account. A record that carries only some windows updates just those. The store clears with the model-auth status usage cache, which runs on any model-auth change. **Where the row shows.** - **`/status`** shows the Claude Code row only for a Claude Code session on the host login, and reads it from the in-memory store without a network request. Two checks must pass. First, the runner notes on every Claude Code turn whether the recording rule admitted it, using the turn's real environment, arguments, skills, and account; the session's latest turn must have been admitted. Second, the run's own account resolver (`resolveCliExecutionAuthProfileId`) is asked with the session's pin, the agent's configured `@profile`, and the session's Claude Code binding, so a profile chosen since that turn also excludes it. Every other session keeps the usage line it had before, and the Claude Code row never stands in for its provider. - **The Models page** gives Claude Code its own usage-only card. Claude Code manages that login, so the card offers no credential actions: saving an API key there would have created a `claude-cli` profile that later Claude Code runs pick up. **Cache expiry.** A cached usage summary no longer serves a window after that window's reset time. The usage cache refreshes at the earliest reset in the summary instead of waiting for the 60 s TTL, and stale serves drop windows that have reset. A summary cached before Claude Code first reported its windows is also refreshed on the next read, so the row does not wait out the TTL after a Gateway start. This applies to every provider's windows, since a window past its reset is stale regardless of source. **Placement.** #129485 parsed the same record in core for turn-log diagnostics. It was closed because its target error was not an OpenClaw bug. This change uses the record for the documented usage surface. If maintainers prefer the Anthropic plugin to own the parser and row once #156296 moves Claude usage fetching there, both can move with it. **Known limits:** - The Claude Code row reflects the last recorded turn. Claude use outside this Gateway, or a `claude /login` switch, is picked up on the next turn or when model auth changes. The row's `observedAt` (the oldest time among its windows) makes that visible instead of presenting the windows as current. - The composer popover lists providers from auth profiles (`models.authStatus`). Matching a session to the Claude Code row there is a UI follow-up; this PR reports the row through `usage.status`. - A separate `openclaw status --usage` process does not see Gateway memory. - A user with a working Anthropic subscription OAuth login and Claude Code on the same account sees the same windows in both rows. Each row is still correct for its own route. No config, schema, or storage changes. One additive, optional field: `ProviderUsageSnapshot.observedAt` (epoch ms), set only on usage observed from runtime output rather than fetched. ## Evidence **Live proof** on a head-built dist and an isolated Gateway (`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and port isolated). Config: `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5` with `agentRuntime: claude-cli`, Claude Code 2.1.280 with its native subscription login, no Anthropic credential in OpenClaw. - **Before any turn:** `usage.status` returned `"providers": []`. - **One turn:** a single `openclaw agent` turn ran (`cli turn: provider=claude-cli model=claude-haiku-4-5 …`). - **After the usage cache refreshed,** `usage.status` returned: ```json { "provider": "claude-cli", "displayName": "Claude Code", "windows": [ { "label": "5h", "usedPercent": 56, "resetAt": 1790340000000 }, { "label": "Week", "usedPercent": 67, "resetAt": 1790784000000 } ] } ``` The trace showed `56.00000000000001` from `0.56 * 100`. The head rounds to two decimals, and a test covers it. **Control UI proof** (September 26). Same isolated setup for both: a fresh state directory, the Usage page opened first, one real `openclaw agent` turn through Claude Code, then the Usage page again. Headless Chromium 1187, dark theme, 1280×900 at 2×. Nothing private is shown; the session is the throwaway `ccusage-proof`. - **Before**, upstream base `516b1f8c4a6`, captured more than 60 s after the turn so the usage cache had expired: the page ends at Sessions. No provider section and no Claude Code row. - **After**, this head `127147da3e7`, captured on the first page load after the turn: the Claude Code card with its 5-hour and weekly windows, reset times, and `Observed just now`. The page had been opened before the turn, so this load also exercises the first-observation cache refresh below. | Before (base `516b1f8c4a6`) | After (head `127147da3e7`) | | --- | --- | | | | **Models page proof** (same isolated setup, one real Claude Code turn, Settings → Models). Before, the Anthropic card said "Not configured" yet showed Claude Code's windows as its own. After, Claude Code has its own usage-only card, and the Anthropic card reports its own (empty) usage with its usual actions. | Before: Anthropic card (`127147da3e7`) | After: Anthropic card (`fa180453a67`) | | --- | --- | | | | **Live `/status`** on the same Gateway and session after the turn (sent through `chat.send`): ``` Auth: native (claude-cli) Usage: 5h 92% left ⏱3h 19m · Week 83% left ⏱4d 4h · as of just now ``` **Wire shape** (Claude Code 2.1.280, identifiers removed), used as the parser fixture: `{"type":"rate_limit_event","rate_limit_info":{"status":"allowed","resetsAt":1790305200,"rateLimitType":"five_hour","overageStatus":"rejected","overageDisabledReason":"out_of_credits","isUsingOverage":false,"unifiedWindows":{"five_hour":{"utilization":0.03,"resetsAt":1790305200},"seven_day":{"utilization":0.48,"resetsAt":1790784000}}}}` **Tests:** - **Record mapping:** fraction → percent (rounded), seconds → ms, reset times that overflow to `Infinity` or leave the Date range are dropped, malformed sibling windows, events without `unifiedWindows`. - **Stream parser:** emits the windows and still observes the session id; ignored outside the Claude dialect. - **Runner entry point** (`executePreparedCliRun` with a Claude stream on stdout): records under the host login, not under an OpenClaw-selected profile or a configured backend credential override. The recording rule also rejects other backends, paired nodes, account and endpoint variables (including lowercase spellings), settings arguments, and a different or skill-provided `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. It keeps recording for model selectors, OpenClaw's own Admin and key-rotation variables, and feature switches. - **`/status`** (`buildStatusText`): a host-login Claude Code session shows `Usage: 5h 80% left` from the store with no usage request; a session whose latest turn the runner kept off the host login (for example, a backend credential) does not show the row; a session whose run uses a stored Claude token profile shows the Anthropic row instead; a session whose agent model pins an API-key `@profile` does not show the Claude Code row. The runner test also checks the per-session verdict it notes. The selection helper passes the session pin, the configured `@profile`, and the Claude Code binding to the run's resolver. The `/status` tests fail without their fixes. - **Models page:** the Claude Code card is usage-only (no buttons, status badge, or credential line), and the Anthropic card keeps its own usage. The view test fails without the fix. - **Store:** expiry at reset, partial records keep the other windows and report the oldest `observedAt`, no recording of windows without a reset time or with one beyond the longest quota period (8 days), clear. - **Formatting:** `/status` summary and the usage report label observed rows `as of …`. - **Control UI usage card:** an observed row shows `Observed 12m ago` with the exact time on hover; a fetched row shows no age line. - **Loader:** - no Anthropic credential gives the Claude Code row; - the Anthropic row is kept unchanged beside the Claude Code row for a setup-token scope refusal, a timeout, an Admin API row, and fetched subscription windows; - no Claude Code row when Claude usage was not requested. - **Usage cache:** a cached window stops being served at its reset time and triggers a refresh before the TTL. A usage summary cached before the first Claude Code turn refreshes on the next read once that turn records windows. A newer reading of a window already shown waits for the normal TTL. The new test fails without the fix. - **Usage cache timing:** a window that resets while its refresh is still loading expires at its reset, and a timed-out refresh reports the timeout when every retained window has reset. Both fail without the fix. - **Observed store:** its window-set version changes only when a provider gains a window: the first observation, a new label, or the first window after a reset. **Test cost** (`pnpm test --maxWorkers=1`, vitest-reported, cold transform included): | File | Duration | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | `provider-usage.observed.test.ts` | ≈0.3 s | | | `cli-runner/observed-usage.test.ts` | ≈9.6 s | 78% module transform of the runner harness; the three cases take ≈40 ms | | `cli-output-records.test.ts` | ≈0.8 s | | | `cli-output-stream.test.ts` | ≈0.5 s | | | `provider-usage.load.test.ts` | ≈24 s | 90% module transform; the new cases are ≈0.2 s together | | `usage.status-cache.test.ts` | three new cases | no timers | | `commands-status-claude-code-usage.test.ts` | ≈28 s | 74% module transform of `/status`; the four cases take ≈6 s. A new sibling file because `commands-status.test.ts` is at its line cap | | `status-usage-entry.test.ts` | ≈8.7 s | 73% module transform; the cases take <0.1 s | No sleeps or process boots. **Rebase (September 26):** rebased onto main `5be36d37cb7` as `53f2ce20d0b`. The only conflict was the upstream rewrite of the provider filter in `provider-usage.load.ts` (#158210); the Claude Code row block is unchanged and now precedes the new filter. `git range-diff` shows no other content change, so the proof above (captured on `127147da3e7`) applies to this head. The focused suites were re-run on the rebased head: 161 tests passed. **September 26, `2036029ad1d`:** rebased onto main `e518bd7310c` (263 commits, no conflicts; `git range-diff` shows the earlier commits unchanged). The last three commits address ClawSweeper Revisions 6 and 7 and two rounds of our own adversarial review (responses below). All 20 test files the PR touches, plus the session-override suites the refactor reaches, pass: 382 tests. `pnpm build` passed. The live proofs above were captured on `fa180453a67`; the only change since is the `/status` session check below, which a host-login turn satisfies. **Checks:** `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passed (format, lint, core and core-test typecheck, UI typecheck, boundaries, line-cap ratchet, dead-export scan). `pnpm ui:i18n:baseline` reports no raw-copy drift. The Control UI usage and model-provider page suites pass (544 jsdom tests).
Review responses (ClawSweeper, September 25) - **[P1] Bind observed windows to the setup-token account.** Resolved by design. Claude Code's windows are no longer substituted into the Anthropic row under any condition. They are reported as the Claude Code row, which is the login that produced them. The Anthropic row, including a setup-token scope error, is left exactly as the Anthropic credential reports it. - **[P2] Expire cached observed windows at their reset time.** Fixed. The usage cache refreshes at the earliest window reset, and stale serves omit windows past their reset.
Review responses (ClawSweeper, second review) - **[P2] Validate `resetsAt` after the millisecond conversion.** Fixed. The parser keeps a reset time only when `resetsAt * 1000` is finite and within the Date range. The store also refuses a reset time more than 8 days after the observation (the longest subscription window is 7 days), so a finite but far-future value cannot pin a window either. Tests cover both. - **Login switch on the host.** The Claude Code row now carries `observedAt`, the time its windows were reported, and `/status` shows it as `as of …`. A `claude auth login` switch still shows the previous login's windows until Claude Code's next turn, but the row no longer presents them as current. Docs say so.
Review responses (ClawSweeper, third review) - **[P2] Show the observation age on the Control UI Usage card.** Fixed. The shared usage card renderer (`ui/src/components/provider-usage.ts`), used by the Usage page and both Models settings surfaces, now renders `Observed ` under the windows whenever a snapshot carries `observedAt`, with the exact timestamp as a tooltip. Fetched snapshots are unchanged. A new English string `usage.providerUsage.observed` goes through the standard locale workflow. Covered by a card test for both states.
Review responses (ClawSweeper, fourth review) - **[P2] Refresh cached usage when the first Claude Code windows arrive.** Fixed in `127147da3e7`. The observed store keeps a window-set version that changes only when a provider gains a window it did not have. Each cached usage summary records the version it was loaded against, read before the load starts, and a mismatch makes it stale. The next read refreshes as with an expired entry, and the Claude Code row appears as soon as that refresh finishes instead of after the 60 s TTL. Newer readings of windows already shown keep the normal cadence, so a busy agent does not re-query every usage provider after each turn. Covered by a `usage.status` cache test for the sequence "empty summary → first observation → row", which fails without the fix, and by a store test for when the version changes. - **Control UI before-and-after screenshots.** Added under Evidence: base versus head on the same isolated setup after a real Claude Code turn. - **Login switch and security-sensitive approval.** These remain maintainer decisions. The row shows its observation age everywhere it is rendered, and the Docs describe the login-switch behavior.
Review responses (ClawSweeper Revision 6, plus our own review) - **[P2] Exclude configured Claude auth overrides before recording host usage.** Fixed in `3a469d30f3b`. Recording now fails closed: any `ANTHROPIC_*` variable in the child environment disables it except model selectors, OpenClaw's Admin API usage and API-key rotation keys, and Vertex project settings. Claude Code's own tokens, auth endpoints, and provider switches (checked against the Claude Code 2.1.280 binary) disable it too, matched case-insensitively. A runner-level test covers a configured backend `env` that re-adds `ANTHROPIC_OAUTH_TOKEN`. - **Security: configured credential mislabeled as host usage.** Same fix. - **Our own review** found more, all fixed with tests that fail without the fix: - The Models page merged the Claude Code row into the Anthropic card, replacing Anthropic's own usage. It is now a separate usage-only card. - `/status` only loaded usage for OAuth/token auth labels, so a host-login session (`native (claude-cli)`) never showed the row. It judged the account by the session pin alone. It now uses the run's own resolver, including the agent's configured `@profile`. - A skill-set `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` passed the config-directory comparison. Recording now fails closed on it. - The usage cache could re-query every provider on every read for a window reported past its reset, and a timed-out refresh could publish an empty entry. Both fixed: reset refresh uses the load start time, and the timeout is kept when nothing valid remains. - **Login switch and security-sensitive approval.** Still maintainer decisions. The row shows its observation age everywhere it is rendered.
Review responses (ClawSweeper Revision 7) - **[P2] Check backend account overrides before showing host quota.** Fixed. `/status` cannot see a session's backend environment, settings arguments, config directory, or skill environment, so it no longer guesses. The runner already evaluates the recording rule on every Claude Code turn from the turn's real environment and arguments. It now also notes that verdict per session, and `/status` shows the host login's windows only when the session's latest Claude Code turn was admitted and the run's account resolver still selects no profile. A session with a backend credential override is therefore never shown the host's quota. The notes are process-local, bounded, and cleared with the observed windows. `/status`, helper, store, and runner tests cover it; the `/status` and helper tests fail without the fix. - **Security: quota attributed to the wrong Claude account.** Same fix. - **Before-and-after UI images.** They are hosted as commit-pinned `raw.githubusercontent.com` URLs on this fork's `pr-157753-proof` branch and return `200 image/png`; the review's media manifest could not fetch them. - **Login switch and security-sensitive approval.** Maintainer decisions, unchanged.

prs.title: feat(android): bind Access Retry to its captured owner
prs.body:
## What problem does this solve?

Let a user retry a TLS gateway's Access action without allowing stale UI work to borrow a newer profile, grant, or Sign-out acknowledgement. Failed raw discovery must report to the action that owns it, including failures before a new route gains a durable association.

## Why this approach?

This tenth slice of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147305 depends on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156248. Retry starts with a captured action/entry/acknowledgement owner and acquires its registration in the same guarded commit. Failure reporting checks the captured owner and current revocation after callback reentry, before publishing.

The two-file delta is 1,083 changed lines: production +135/-1, tests +947/-0. This deliberate size exception keeps acquisition, acknowledgement handoff, reentrant failure handling, and their regression schedules in one capability. It introduces no app activation, cleartext admission, or shared-browser reuse; Retry accepts TLS routes only at this prefix.

## Evidence and remaining gates

- Add fourteen existing regression methods, bringing the prefix to 76 Controller methods. Cover cold/queued Retry, saved-entry replacement, Sign-out completion publication, acquired route replacement, failed origin replacement, callback reentry, and preservation of another origin's action.
- Existing gates, dispatcher choices, expected failure handling, and owned cancellation/join cleanup are preserved. Normal scoped commit hooks and `git diff --check` pass.
- Standalone compilation/runtime are pending. The original aggregate's 150-method results are historical evidence, not a passing result for this intermediate source.
- Automated source review remains held by the existing fixture filename classification. No blocked input is retried and no substitute clearance is claimed.
- Native persistence and complete fresh-install/same-signer install-over profile, selection, custom-header, settings, and pairing proof remain final-composition gates. This PR stays draft and is not merge-ready.

prs.title: feat(perplexity): add optional Agent API research tool
prs.body:
## Summary

- add an opt-in `perplexity_research` tool backed by Perplexity Agent API
- expose `low`, `medium`, `high`, and `xhigh` effort plus optional freshness
- keep the existing Perplexity `web_search` provider and default Search API path unchanged
- require a direct Perplexity API key for the Agent API tool while preserving OpenRouter behavior for `web_search`

## What Problem This Solves

The bundled plugin currently exposes Perplexity only through the standard `web_search` contract. Agent API adds a distinct capability: cited synthesis and deeper research. Registering it as an optional tool lets interested users enable that capability without changing behavior or cost for users who only selected Perplexity as their native search provider.

Closes #155137.

## Evidence

- focused Perplexity extension suite passes `57/57`
- full plugin contract suite passes `1145/1145`
- full test TypeScript gate passes
- formatter, type-aware lint, generated plugin inventory, SDK export, and `git diff --check` gates pass
## September 23 Exact-Head Refresh

Exact candidate: `a40cddb7a7683aac2dd1861bdeaee2f5d25fbaec`  
Frozen base: `5e5f9c27559776303d962aa37f8c09f676e640d4`  
Merge tree: `4bfd4ec1902de120b83aa08ac1c0c46cfbd88cb2`

- Focused Perplexity provider suite passes `65/65` on this exact head.
- The changed test file passes `65/65` with one worker in `2.78s` Vitest duration / `3.11s` wall time on October 7.
- Canonical pre-PR receipt passes all selected deterministic gates, including complete type, lint, dead-export, dependency, boundary, cycle, and repository-ratchet checks.
- Fresh independent `gpt-5.6-sol` review found no actionable P0-P2 defect.
- Explicit global search timeouts remain authoritative; the research default is 300 seconds only when no explicit timeout is configured.
- `webSearch.apiKey` is declared as an independent capability-owned secret input; OpenRouter credentials remain rejected for Agent API research.

## Dependency

prs.title: feat: connect MCP apps and embedded UI through principal-bound Gateway grants
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Remote MCP clients and ChatGPT's embedded browser need a public transport to a user's private Gateway. This adds the disabled-by-default `mcp-relay` plugin and a service-owned Gateway ingress, using an outbound relay connection without exposing an inbound port or sharing the Gateway token/password.

Each app grant now belongs to the approving principal: the owner on single-user Gateways, or the signed-in person on verified-profile Gateways. The new **Connected apps** tab supports optional **Sign in with your Gateway**, pairing codes, grant inspection, and revocation. Users select read/write access by default or their full permitted role, including administration when explicitly selected.

## Authority and update behavior

- One principal binding serves both MCP operations and the embedded Control UI. Effective access is the saved ceiling intersected with the principal's current authority; session visibility and role restrictions remain Gateway-owned.
- Signed embedded browsers are tokenless. They receive no reusable device credential. Grant revocation closes UI transports and fences MCP work; role changes retire a binding, and the next request can reopen under current authority.
- Grant creation, usage, and revocation share the existing write queue so an in-flight pairing cannot restore a revoked grant. Active grant IDs cannot replace their existing authority; rejecting a duplicate preserves the pairing code for a fresh ID.
- Assembled Control UI WebSocket messages are limited to 25 MiB, and HTTP bodies are capped at 100 MiB before enqueueing. The outgoing relay queue is capped at 32 MiB; overload fails the affected UI stream, and a fully saturated connection may reconnect if the terminal error cannot be sent.
- Consent derives the principal from the authenticated Gateway caller. Relay approval messages contain the required principal kind and label, never the profile ID. The fixed plugin redirect leads to normal Control UI authentication, and completion returns only to the configured relay origin.
- The plugin stores its identity, pairing codes, and principal grants through the Gateway runtime’s durable keyed-store owner. This new plugin has no legacy state migration. Verified-profile Gateways refuse owner access and direct users to pair as themselves. CLI owner pairing remains available on single-user Gateways.
- Users can inspect and revoke their own grants; administrators can manage all grants. Self-service writes use `operator.write`, with an additional admin check for another principal's grant or owner pairing.

The relay can see and modify content in transit; this is not end-to-end encrypted against it. Full access can include administration and approvals, so the consent screen and docs call out that choice. The relay owns OAuth single-use requests and the 30-day absolute refresh-token lifetime for person sign-in grants.

## Evidence

The unshipped ingress API now has one current principal-bound factory/open-options contract. The core and bundled plugin cut over together; obsolete factory compatibility exports and unions are removed.

- 312 passing cases across 26 focused files, including all nine MCP relay files and the real ingress integration suite (7/7). The composition exercises current role authority, session visibility, grant revocation, and MCP/UI recovery. The unsupported-auth cache, grant-write/revocation ordering, queued-upload, saturated-control-frame, and active-grant-ID regressions failed against the old behavior and passed with their fixes.
- Core, extension production/test, all 28 affected core test graphs, and UI typechecks passed. Changed-file type-aware lint and formatting passed.
- Dead-export scans passed without PR-owned orphans. Assertion ratchet passed with no required owned baseline shrinks. Runtime import-cycle and madge checks both report zero cycles.
- Docs, plugin inventory/sync, config schema/channel/docs generators, SDK export/surface checks, and the complete PR whitespace check passed.
- Exact-head `pnpm build:ci-artifacts` passed in 147.77 s, followed by `pnpm plugins:assets:build --check` in 7.27 s; generated assets match their manifests.
- Managed Codex integrated branch autoreview against `f864918135b6` completed both passes through P2 with no accepted/actionable findings on the final head.
- Existing synthetic Control UI proof covers native-tab navigation, default pairing, Full consent, configured-origin continuation despite a foreign query hint, and mobile role-limited rendering. The deslop UI comparison retained identical appearance.

Standalone `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` wall times include runner and compiler preparation. Fresh rows cover the final plugin/ingress source; retained rows cover unchanged core/UI inputs:

| File | Cases | Wall seconds | Proof |
|---|---:|---:|---|

The integration fixture now opens its V2 keyed store through the runtime store owner. Logging assertions retain the sanitized operation/method failure message. No authorization checks, timeouts, or assertions were weakened to make tests pass. CI seconds for the final head are pending.

Earlier owner-only revisions had live ChatGPT/production-relay smoke coverage. The sign-in/Team flow was tested with synthetic relay I/O and real isolated Gateway ingress, not a live OAuth provider or production Gateway. Relay-side OAuth expiry enforcement was not independently exercised. The coordinator Gateway was not restarted or reconfigured.

## Screenshots

Before: the Connected apps page was unavailable.

![Before: Connected apps unavailable](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4c8831ec-a957-46f0-b4ba-f3c6e8082b9b)

After: caller-bound consent with the app, return host, approving person, selected ceiling, and explicit administration warning. All capture data is synthetic.

![After: Connected apps consent](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/edaf7a47-fc02-480e-9f12-570cdbaca8ac)

Release-note context: optional MCP relay integration with principal-bound grants, tokenless embedded Control UI, Gateway sign-in consent, and a Connected apps management tab. Pairing codes remain supported; owner pairing defaults to read/write access on single-user Gateways.

prs.title: fix(perplexity): preserve synthesized search after Sonar shutdown
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: direct Perplexity `web_search` model/base-URL overrides would stop producing synthesized answers when Sonar Chat Completions reaches end of support on September 27, 2026.

## User Impact

User impact: existing direct Sonar overrides keep returning one synthesized, cited answer through Agent API. Native Perplexity Search API users and OpenRouter/custom chat-completions users keep their current transports and response shapes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Perplexity now maps the legacy Sonar models to Agent API presets. This change adds a direct-Perplexity `agent_api` transport, applies the official `sonar` → `fast`, `sonar-pro` → `low`, `sonar-reasoning-pro` → `medium`, and `sonar-deep-research` → `high` mappings, moves freshness into the Agent API web-search tool filters, and parses typed Agent API output. Non-Sonar direct model IDs are passed through with web search enabled.

The default Search API path remains `POST /search`. OpenRouter and non-Perplexity base URLs remain on `/chat/completions`; this PR does not force Agent API semantics onto those compatible endpoints.

This is complementary to #126889, which documents Perplexity as an OpenClaw model provider and MCP integration. It does not duplicate that provider/MCP work.

## Evidence

- Exact reviewed head: `e09761d552395208689a4235cabaeb4ddf0c6804`.
- Frozen maintenance base: `5e5f9c27559776303d962aa37f8c09f676e640d4`; deterministic merge tree: `15ff068c0325818d1375238e8d282792ffae233f`.
- Focused Perplexity provider suite: 60/60 passed, including all non-success statuses, cache behavior, Anthropic `max_output_tokens`, preset mappings, and mandatory direct-model web-search instructions.
- The changed test file was remeasured with one worker on October 7: 60/60 passed in `2.78s` Vitest duration / `3.30s` wall time.
- Canonical pre-PR wrapper passed every selected gate, including core/extension types, dead exports, lint, boundaries, runtime cycles, and repository ratchets.
- Independent exact-head Sol review found no actionable P0–P2 defects and verified the current Perplexity Agent API contract.
- Negative/sibling coverage: native Search API routing remains unchanged; OpenRouter/custom endpoints still use Chat Completions; structured-only filters remain absent from both synthesized-answer schemas.
- Exact-head paid live-provider proof is still `blocked_external`: it requires a Perplexity API credential and external API spend. The older live smoke is not reused as proof for this head.

prs.title: refactor(ui): simplify settings, plugins, and overlay ownership
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Recent Control UI migrations left duplicated settings state machines, view adapters, and speculative callback bookkeeping that make ordinary maintenance harder.

## User Impact

No intended visual change, feature removal, or Lit/Solid shipping cutover. Existing tags, classes, text, config keys, protocol shapes, credential checks, and normal draft/reconnect behavior remain. The uncommon callback/catalog scenarios below are explicitly best effort. No migration or operator action is required; the standalone Phase E memory backend is untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

Consolidate health reads for Meeting Capture and Session Storage under one parameterized owner, reuse local preference rows and plugin capability/artwork composition, remove no-op JSX wrappers, and share identical CSS declarations. Form controls use one scalar edit owner and parse JSON once. Overlay closure takes one snapshot of the existing tree instead of repeatedly admitting callback-created branches.

Production-only net reduction: **551 lines** (tests, fixtures, support, generated files and declarations excluded; includes both new shared helpers). This is the campaign's 500–999-line honest-sweep exception, not a claim of reaching 1,000.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Overlay hide listeners that synchronously create/reparent additional overlays: [#169128](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169128) introduced migration/browser contract machinery, with no cited human actual-use incident for this forced interleaving. Existing branches still honor child vetoes; a newly created peer may survive until the next ordinary dismissal.
- Root-style retention callbacks that synchronously move/dispose their own surface: the same migration's production callbacks retain styles only. Removed repeated registration/root probes and compensating cleanup; an exotic reentrant callback may retain styles until normal disposal. Ordinary root movement remains supported.
- Reopening during forced overlay retirement: the same migration's synthetic callback case is not a production caller or human report. Removed intent/reopen arbitration; requests during synchronous retirement are rejected, and a subsequent fresh activation works.
- Invisible equal-valued server theme events or a theme round trip during import: [#117292](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/117292) links [#117291](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/117291), which explicitly describes delayed mocked-Gateway/Testbox responses, not a human actual-use incident. Removed activation-intent/server-selection revisions; imported palettes are saved and may activate when the displayed theme still matches the starting choice. Newer imports, Clear/URL, navigation/connection disposal and config-write interlocks still retire stale work.
- Config change or explicit retry while MCP discovery is already pending: [#167906](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167906) records measured request sharing and synthetic tests, not a human incident requiring event-object invalidation. Removed pending-map replacement; consumers share the in-flight result and may see an older catalog until the next refresh. Connection/session identity, session-creation invalidation and Gateway launch authorization remain.
- Selection manually delivered to an already-disconnected plugin dropdown: [#168758](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168758) introduced a retired callback snapshot without a human actual-use report; its test explicitly removes the menu before dispatch. Removed that snapshot effect; current menus read current field/value and retain disabled/config-owner checks. An exceptionally late retired event is best effort.
- A config patch callback unexpectedly throwing after valid JSON: [#169046](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169046) retained a second parse inside a broad catch, without a human incident requiring silent callback failure. Parse/validate once and commit that candidate; invalid drafts and ordinary rejected patches still retain their recovery behavior, while an unexpected callback exception now surfaces instead of being silently treated as invalid JSON.

## Evidence

Identical-rendering refactor: CSS computed-style parity passed for every property across 32 profiles × 29 synthetic elements (desktop/mobile, light/dark, LTR/RTL and input states). No visual design changes are intended, so before/after screenshots are not applicable.

Focused existing boundary proofs, using isolated HOME/OpenClaw/XDG state and repository Vitest wrappers with `--maxWorkers=1`:

- Config/settings final packet: 85 unit tests plus 33 browser tests passed; wrapper 130.24s. Earlier Meeting Capture/Session Storage packet: 41 tests, 41.81s wrapper / 27.86s Vitest. Custom-theme retained lifecycle: 10 tests, 17.53s Vitest. New Session placement/icons: 23 tests passed.
- Plugin/model setup/provider views: 119 tests across 10 files, 132.64s wrapper / 101.34s Vitest; catalog Chromium 12 tests; settings editor 19 tests, 34.04s wrapper / 10.95s Vitest.
- MCP catalog: 11 tests passed, 39.58s Vitest / approximately 90s wrapper.
- Overlay lifecycle and closed-shadow boundaries: 53 Chromium tests (7.29s Vitest) and 53 WebKit tests (11.73s Vitest).
- Scalar/JSON form boundaries: 56 tests across five Chromium suites passed, 31.05s wrapper / 8.87s Vitest. Aggregate changed-file compiler, graph, i18n and ratchet checks passed; lint/format/style checks completed through the same owner's targeted recovery plan after fixing its findings. Final focused lint on the corrected health/plugin modules is clean, without warnings or suppressions.
- Final callback-boundary proof: all 6 existing mocked-Gateway plugin skill-route E2Es passed (145.82s Vitest), including installed/catalog request payloads, navigation, failure recovery and reconnect. Their production UI build passed (4,521 transformed modules, 84s build). Health reproof: 41 tests, 29.76s wrapper / 17.17s Vitest; plugin page reproof: 15 tests, 43.92s wrapper / 32.07s Vitest. Private-export correction: 8 overview tests plus 12 Chromium catalog/layout tests, 56.40s wrapper.
- UI production typecheck passed (`node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.ui.json`, isolated environment), including the final correction. All ten selected dependent test-type graphs passed. Final runtime cycles: zero. Final Madge component cycles: zero. Final lint-suppressions: 3 tests passed, 82.32s wrapper / 55.36s Vitest. Focused CSS lint/format and whitespace checks passed. Independent P0–P2 autoreview completed scoped-clean on the full candidate and both correction packets, with no accepted/actionable findings.

Only tests pinning the removed speculative mechanisms were removed; kept contracts were not skipped, retried, or weakened. Local findings were fixed: one test-format issue, two now-private overview exports, and two shared-health lint errors. The event callback's intentional displayed-package snapshot is explicit. Both the initial parallel full-tree Knip scan and the bounded serial recovery hit their existing 600s timeout; this is incomplete local proof, not a clean result. Production and script export scans pass with zero entries. No timeout was increased or skip flag added. The selected hosted gates do not establish that the full-tree Knip scan ran, so that gap remains explicit. One mistyped test filename and an isolated browser-cache omission stopped before collection; corrected commands passed. One review preparation refused a changing tree while lint was running; the final correction then reviewed scoped-clean after lint exited. No live Gateway/user state was used. Hosted CI on the exact pushed head is the broad gate; no claim of live backend or full-application visual proof.

### Hosted CI attribution and accepted gaps

Exact head: `0eca65bbe2afad595f039423cbc8e9ec17a887d4`; ready-state [run 38336312204](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38336312204). All selected jobs except UI E2E shards 1/9 and 7/9 passed; `openclaw/ci-gate` fails as their aggregate. The classifier compares shard names rather than selected cases and labels these NEW; case-level investigation follows instead of treating that as baseline proof.

- Shard 1/9, job 115097365510: `browser-dictation-status.e2e.test.ts:542`, null control bounding box. Classified inherited/intermittent using the maintainer-authorized selector-audit route below, with non-reproduction explicitly recorded, not a claim that the failure reproduced on main.
- Shard 7/9, job 115097365496: archive refresh case receives `archived=false` instead of `true`. The same key/polarity failure occurs on [PR #170521 run 38336358758, job 115097721162](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38336358758/job/115097721162), at `58578f459b47fbda869006cd7654aa0d14583d63`. That revision changes build tooling, not the archive test or archive/menu owners. Its later `50a55c866d6a625f2e16a983c882014ef0846600` repairs the premature archived descriptor in the fixture, after the failing run.
- Same shard 7/9: `update-run.e2e.test.ts:225`, 30-second wait for the completed report. Scheduled main [run 38334375513, job 115091146620](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38334375513/job/115091146620) fails the identical case/locator in shard 8/9. This failure is inherited, not a shard-name-only comparison.
- Cancelled draft `PR context and evidence` job 115097031747 was superseded by the same-head ready-event job 115097073479, which passed. Cancellation is not a baseline failure.

Diagnostic local replay of the three failing cases passed 3/3 (183.28s); complete-file replay on the PR head passed 24/24 (359.64s). Pinned main `cd1daee9ae927927d49b4940129ae0c0e9587791` passes 23/24 and fails the identical update report locator (313.57s). Dictation and archive pass in that macOS run; passing replay is not a repair or causal exoneration. A Linux Testbox reservation reported warmup complete, but direct status showed queued/no host; it was stopped rather than waiting or changing providers and ran no test payload. No hosted job was rerun, dispatched, or repushed merely for green.

Subsequent local Docker proof completed inside the maintainer's 45-minute budget: the unchanged dictation file passed **13/13 at this exact head (297.12s)** and **13/13 at merge base `2eb8ab3696773bd335060d1d9a15c9d6851f1b7b` (321.21s)**. Both used the repo-pinned official Playwright 1.63.0 noble image, digest `bc6ab0d6d44ff4826e4cb8c1e6d801e185bfc42bb0753f8e2a30efc70db054c7`, Linux x64 / Node 24.20.0, independent installs and isolated HOME/OpenClaw/XDG state. No host home, state, or credentials were mounted.

Because neither run reproduced the intermittent CI null box, attribution uses the authorized selector audit rather than pretending replay repaired it. Read-only instrumentation in the exported test copy recorded **zero matches** for all changed selectors on the dictating composer, phase, buttons, and every ancestor through `html`; the branch/assertions remain unchanged. `components.css` touches only agent-tool panel selectors. `new-session.css` touches only New Session roots/project/menu inputs, absent from this Chat subtree. `layout.css` touches sidebar-shell/catalog/menu labels and gateway-status elements, not these controls/ancestors; sidebar/status declarations merely move to immediately adjacent identical rules with unchanged specificity and values. Settings/Workshop selectors are absent too. No changed selector targets `.agent-chat__dictation-phase`, `.agent-chat__input`, their buttons, or their Chat/shell ancestors. The targeted diagnostic case also passes; 12 other cases were filtered, not newly skipped. The original CI interleaving remains unreproduced, an accepted gap under the selector-audit ruling.

The single additional full-tree Knip scan requested by the maintainer again hit its unchanged 600s budget (605s with settlement), with no findings emitted, under observed host load 72.74/68.39/69.60. This remains incomplete proof, not green. The PR's CI selection did not run dependencies; newer scheduled main's Knip job reports unrelated infra/skills/dropdown exports, not this diff. The maintainer accepted the remaining full-tree gap; no suppression, timeout change, CI rerun, dispatch, or repush was added.

<details>
<summary>Coverage ledger: recent three-day, fourteen-day, then largest-first sweep</summary>

- Config/New Session: consolidated duplicate health-read state machines and local preference rendering; simplified custom-theme activation edges and placement projection. Kept background upload/write authority, ordinary rapid locale/preference edits, reconnect recovery, external numeric validation and config loading/dirty interlocks.
- Remaining components: simplified overlay branch admission/root retention/retirement, scalar edit identity and JSON parsing. Kept normal focused drafts, union source identity, redaction/schema validation, rejection rollback, native animation/focus, gallery navigation, bounded prefetch and narration resource cleanup.
- Plugins/model setup/providers: consolidated action adapters, capability composition and artwork props; removed retired dropdown callback snapshot. Rejected a modal-shell extraction because it added lines without a better owner. Kept credentials, sign-in/wizard recovery, current detail selection, lazy icon boundaries and config mutation settlement.
- App/lib: removed MCP invalidation identity while keeping measured request sharing. Kept durable server preferences, authenticated profile scoping, normal pending edit reconciliation, markdown DOM migration foundation, projections, readiness, keyboard tabs and measured widget-theme caching.
- Styles: merged exact declaration clusters in six stylesheets with computed parity. Kept selectors whose media scope, nesting, specificity or later cascade differs. No chat stylesheet, Solid primitive, generated locale, backend/schema, or PR tooling changes.

The complete file/line coverage ledger follows (line locations refer to pre-change source).

## Config and New Session

- `pages/config/custom-theme-import-owner.ts:30-80,120-147,194-205`:
  ordered activation-intent objects and server-selection revisions track
  invisible/equal-valued theme selection edges during import. REMOVE that
  custody machinery; capture the displayed theme and compare at completion.
  [#117292](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/117292) points to
  [#117291](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/117291), whose report
  explicitly describes delayed mocked-Gateway Testbox responses, not an
  actual-use human incident. KEEP one current-import identity, Clear/URL/newer
  import retirement, route/Gateway disposal, and current displayed theme check.
  Invisible same-theme server events or a theme round trip during a pending
  import are best effort: the palette is saved and may activate if the current
  displayed theme matches the starting choice. Two tests solely pinning that
  removed invisible-edge protocol are deleted; ten ordinary import lifecycle
  contracts remain and pass. Full-config loading/dirty interlock stays because
  anonymous preference writes still use config.patch.
- `pages/config/view-appearance{,-preferences,-lobster,-background}.tsx`:
  #169046 introduced redundant single-child fragments and expression wrappers
