prs.title: feat(webui): add configurable local trusted extension surface
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds a configurable local WebUI extensions surface for trusted browser-side add-ons.

Extensions are discovered from a local directory, validated as folders with an `extension.json` manifest, and served through the gateway under scoped `/extensions/...` and `/api/extensions/...` routes. The host bridge authenticates requests and keeps API tokens out of the iframe.

## Why

This lets nanobot host small local browser apps without exposing credentials or creating a generic third-party app sandbox. The extension directory remains local to the gateway and can be configured per deployment.

## Changes

- add configurable extension root via `tools.webui_extensions_path`
- discover and validate extension manifests
- serve static extension assets from the gateway
- expose authenticated extension APIs through the WebUI host bridge
- add extension catalog / settings integration in the WebUI
- keep invalid or broken extensions from breaking the whole catalog

## Testing

- `cd webui && npm test -- --run src/tests/extension-client.test.ts src/tests/extensions-catalog.test.tsx`

## Notes

- The feature is local and trusted, not a sandboxed remote app model.
- The UI remains empty unless the configured extension root contains valid extensions.

prs.title: fix(transcription): convert non-WAV audio to 16kHz mono WAV before upload
prs.body:
## Problem

`OpenAITranscriptionProvider` and `GroqTranscriptionProvider` upload the audio file verbatim. OpenAI Cloud and Groq accept any common format, but **self-hosted Whisper backends behind `OPENAI_TRANSCRIPTION_BASE_URL` (notably whisper.cpp's `/inference` endpoint) accept only 16 kHz mono WAV** and return HTTP 400 for everything else.

Voice messages from Telegram, WhatsApp and Feishu all arrive as OGG/Opus, so any local-Whisper deployment is effectively broken without an external pre-processing step.

### Reproduce

```bash
# Run any whisper.cpp server, e.g.
./whisper-server -m ggml-large-v3.bin --port 8200

# Configure nanobot to use it
export OPENAI_TRANSCRIPTION_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8200/inference
export OPENAI_API_KEY=anything

# Send a Telegram voice message → 400 Bad Request, transcription returns ""
```

## Fix

Add a module-level helper `_ensure_whisper_compatible_audio()` that calls `ffmpeg` to normalise non-WAV input to 16 kHz mono WAV:

- `.wav` input is passed through untouched (zero overhead for the common case).
- If `ffmpeg` is missing on `PATH`, the original path is returned with a warning log — cloud backends still work, local backends keep their current 400 behaviour (no regression).
- If `ffmpeg` returns non-zero, the same fall-back kicks in.

Both providers call the helper before opening the upload stream and unlink the tempfile in `finally`.

## Tests

`tests/providers/test_transcription_format_convert.py` covers:

- WAV passthrough (no tempfile created)
- Missing `ffmpeg` returns the original path
- `ffmpeg` non-zero exit returns the original path
- Real round-trip through libopus, gated on `ffmpeg` being installed

All four pass on Python 3.14.4 with the project's `pyproject.toml` install.

## Backwards compatibility

- Cloud backends (OpenAI, Groq): identical behaviour — they accept WAV just as well as OGG, and the conversion is silently bypassed for `.wav` input.
- Local backends without `ffmpeg`: identical behaviour — original path is uploaded with a warning log.
- Local backends with `ffmpeg`: previously broken (HTTP 400), now work.

`ffmpeg` is treated as a runtime dependency only when needed; it's already a hard dependency for several other channels (Feishu voice download, WhatsApp media handling) and ships in nearly every Linux base image.

## Relation to #3513

#3513 ("unify transcription providers and add local Whisper support") refactors this module to introduce a `local` provider and remove the duplication between `OpenAITranscriptionProvider` and `GroqTranscriptionProvider`. It does **not** address audio-format conversion — even after #3513 lands, whisper.cpp users will still hit the 400 problem.

This PR is therefore complementary. Once #3513 is merged, the `_ensure_whisper_compatible_audio()` helper can be moved into the unified `WhisperTranscriptionProvider` with a one-line refit.

---

Bug discovered and patch authored together with my AI assistant Ren (Claude Opus 4.7). I'm submitting; the analysis is hers.

prs.title: feat(images): reuse named connections and image request settings
prs.body:
## Problem

Image settings list only fixed provider names. Users cannot select a named connection created in Models. Image-only request parameters must be placed in shared provider settings.

## Changes

- Select an image provider by its saved connection ID. Named custom connections use the OpenAI Images API. A chat endpoint does not imply image support.
- Reuse the saved key, URL, and proxy. Keep built-in adapters and the legacy `custom` connection.
- Add image-only headers and body parameters. Empty fields inherit provider settings. Secret values stay masked.
- Clear image-only overrides when the provider changes. Do not replace a missing connection with another provider.
- Reuse the existing parameter editor and request validation. Include all ten locales and failed-save recovery.

## Runtime integration

#6172 has merged into `main`. This branch now includes that main commit, `105b7722037bcae7fdd204d757690403ace22467`.

The application runtime owns image-tool registration and live reload. This PR supplies named connections and image request settings to that path. Provider discovery uses the same rules for the settings list, startup, and reload. No image-specific state or control-message branch is added to `AgentLoop`.

The final diff also reuses the shared editor and validation from #6159. It preserves the Codex Images API and `gpt-image-2` default from #6177.

## Compatibility

Existing saved configurations and high-level SDK, CLI, and WebUI entrypoints need no migration. Missing image-only fields retain the prior behavior. Reload reads the explicit gateway config path. A failed load retains the working tool. Clients created before reload retain their request settings.

This PR adds no further low-level constructor change beyond #6172. Direct `AgentLoop` callers must use the application composition described there.

Older releases do not support named custom image connections or the new image-only fields. Before a downgrade, select a provider supported by that release and check required request settings. See `docs/image-generation.md`.

Chat prompts, history, and tool schemas are unchanged. Updating image request settings does not change tool definitions or their order. Enabling or disabling a tool still changes its availability.

## Verification

After the main sync, at `9080bbdc9` (the current `fd27d9794` has the same complete file tree; only commit history was made linear):

- 497 focused backend tests passed. Coverage includes image adapters, download safety, SDK and CLI setup, live reload, settings routes, and WebSocket handling.
- 148 frontend tests passed for capabilities, model settings, provider settings, and localization.
- Ruff, strict BasedPyright for the four changed implementation files, WebUI lint, and the production build passed.
- [Current-head CI](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/38254406316) passed on `fd27d9794`, including Linux, Windows, Docker, and WebUI checks.
- The serialized tool definitions under the same existing config match the previous accepted version byte for byte. Reload tests also check definition order and client isolation.

Earlier isolated browser checks remain applicable to the unchanged image settings and parameter editor. They covered save, refresh, provider switching, clearing overrides, retry, cancel, light/dark themes, and a 390px viewport. They were not rerun as browser E2E during this main sync.

No live image service or physical mobile device was tested. Custom endpoints must implement the OpenAI Images API.

The dependency and compatibility checks are complete. The PR is ready for review.

prs.title: fix(providers): stream Codex image generation responses
prs.body:
Codex image generation requests SSE using buffered `AsyncClient.post()`, so HTTPX reads the response body before the existing parser can stop at a completed response. A disconnect or an open body after `response.completed` can therefore discard an already generated image. Follow-up to #4332.

Use `client.stream()` with the existing HTTP configuration and image parser. Preserve injected-client ownership, close streamed responses and owned clients, and read HTTP error bodies before reporting their details. Transport failures before completion still propagate.

Validation:

- Python 3.11 and 3.14: 187 image-generation and agent/session tests passed on each.
- The real-HTTPX regression fails with buffered POST and passes with streaming; coverage includes terminal events, disconnect/open/EOF, HTTP errors, client ownership and cancellation.
- 11 offline HTTP checks, including 3 real loopback HTTP/1.1 cases.
- Full Ruff, strict BasedPyright on the changed provider module, and `git diff --check` pass.

Live Codex and Windows behavior were not exercised locally; full-repository tests and type checking are left to CI.

prs.title: feat(provider): support OpenRouter native image generation API
prs.body:
## Reason for the Change

OpenRouter now provides image generation through its native Images API. Nanobot needs to use this API so OpenRouter image generation remains compatible with the current service and can expose more image-generation providers and models through the existing `generate_image` workflow.

## Summary

Update the OpenRouter image-generation client to use OpenRouter's native image API instead of the previous chat-completions image flow.

The implementation:

- Sends generation requests to `POST /api/v1/images`.
- Looks up model capabilities through `GET /api/v1/images/models`.
- Sends `aspect_ratio` and `resolution` only when the selected model advertises the requested values.
- Sends reference images using OpenRouter's native `input_references` format.
- Decodes `data[].b64_json` responses into nanobot image data URLs.
- Preserves a valid response `media_type` when one is returned.
- Keeps provider configuration and the existing `generate_image` tool interface unchanged.

The implementation was tested with these OpenRouter models:

- `openai/gpt-image-2.5-flare`
- `meta/muse-image`
- `bytedance-seed/seedream-5-0-lite`
- `bytedance-seed/seedream-4.5`
- `black-forest-labs/flux.2-pro`
- `x-ai/grok-imagine-image-quality`

## Testing

- `pytest tests/providers/test_image_generation.py -q`
  - Result: 99 passed in 0.82s

The suite covers:
- Native `POST /api/v1/images` requests.
- `GET /api/v1/images/models` capability discovery.
- Supported and unsupported aspect-ratio and resolution values.
- `extraBody` overrides.
- Native reference-image inputs.
- Base64 response decoding and returned media types.
- Capability-lookup failures and responses without images.
- Missing OpenRouter API keys.

## Compatibility and Rollout

Existing OpenRouter provider credentials, image-generation settings, and the `generate_image` tool remain unchanged. Models that do not advertise a requested aspect ratio or resolution receive a request without that optional field, allowing the model to use its default behavior.

prs.title: feat(channels): add WhatsApp Agent Platform channel
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds `whatsapp_agent`, an additive channel that connects nanobot to the **official** [WhatsApp Agent Platform](https://faq.whatsapp.com/1050934623978152) API (`https://api.whatsapp.com/agent/v1`, see the [Developer Manual](https://www.whatsapp.com/developer/WhatsApp-Agent-Platform-Developer-Manual.pdf)).

The existing `whatsapp` channel stays as-is. The two are different products, and both can run at once under different names.

| | `whatsapp_agent` (this PR) | `whatsapp` |
|---|---|---|
| Connection | Official agent API token | Linked device via Neonize (QR) |
| Inbound | Long-poll `GET /updates` | Device client |
| Reach | Only the agent's creator | Chats and groups the device can see |
| Groups | Not supported by the platform | Supported |
| End-to-end encryption | **No** — Meta processes agent chats | Yes, like a linked device |
| Availability | Limited countries / per account | Wherever WhatsApp can link a device |
| Account risk | Officially supported interface | Unofficial protocol |

**Benefits:** an officially sanctioned interface with no linked-device session, a much smaller blast radius (one conversation, no groups), no optional Python dependencies, and a token-based setup that needs no inbound URL or QR flow. **Tradeoffs:** no group support, no end-to-end encryption, and the rollout is limited by country and account.

## What it includes

- Authenticated long-polling with a durable cursor, dedup, and restart recovery.
- Read receipts and typing indicator, refreshed inside the 25-second window.
- Text replies split at 4096 characters, sent in order, with the first chunk quoting the inbound message.
- Inbound and outbound media (image, audio, video, document, sticker, generic binary) with MIME/size validation and digest verification.
- Voice-note transcription through the existing shared provider config.
- Per-method rolling-window pacing, protocol-aware retries, and secret handling.
- WebUI setup surface with locales for all 10 supported languages.

## Design decisions worth reviewing

- **Durable cursor.** The cursor, dedup window, and creator identifier live in one atomically replaced state file. A wamid is recorded *before* its message is handled, so a crash re-reads the batch without answering twice, and `next_offset` is only accepted after the batch is processed.
- **No backlog replay.** The first poll omits `offset`, which resolves the head. Passing `offset=0` would replay up to 30 days of history into an auto-replying agent.
- **Token rotation resets the cursor,** because `next_offset` is only valid for the agent that issued it.
- **Retry policy.** Only confirmed non-delivery is retried (`429`, `503`/`131016`). HTTP `500` and read timeouts leave the outcome unknown, so they are **not** retried unless `retryAmbiguousSends` is set — a duplicate is more disruptive than a missed reply, and a repeated chunk would be especially bad. This is routed through the existing `should_retry_send_error()` hook rather than the manager's default retry.
- **Progress traffic is off by default.** Every poll, send, receipt, and media call has its own 12–15/minute budget, and progress messages would spend the send budget the real reply needs.
- **Single poller.** The API permits one poll per agent. A duplicate gateway produces `409`, which is logged clearly.
- **Reactions are receive-only,** matching the API, and an empty emoji is read as a removal.

## Security

- The token is only ever placed in the `Authorization` header. It is never logged, and the state file stores a SHA-256 fingerprint rather than the value.
- Media URLs returned by the API pass through the shared `validate_url_target` SSRF guard before any request; all requests disable redirects and hit the fixed API base.
- Inbound media is size-capped and verified against the reported digest (Base64) before it reaches the agent.

## Tests

```
uv run pytest nanobot/channels/whatsapp_agent/tests tests/channels \
  tests/webui/test_settings_routes.py nanobot/channels/whatsapp -q
# 491 passed

uv run ruff check nanobot/ tests/channels          # clean
uv run basedpyright                                # 0 errors (strict, whole repo)

cd webui && npx vitest run                         # 2661 passed
cd webui && npm run lint && npm run build           # clean
```

80 new package tests cover message/status parsing, status-only batches, int64 offsets, `204` offset reuse, first-poll head resolution, cursor persistence, dedup across a replay, restart recovery, token-rotation reset, token redaction, chunked/ordered sends, retry classification, rate-limit pacing, media size/digest/SSRF handling, and duplicate pollers.

Two unrelated failures in `tests/webui/test_transcription_ws.py` reproduce on a clean checkout of `main` and are not touched by this PR.

## Notes for reviewers

- **Live verification.** The round trip was confirmed against the production API with a real agent token: authentication (`GET /updates` -> `204`), a real inbound message parsed into the agent pipeline, durable cursor persistence, dedup on batch replay (0 duplicates), a real outbound send, and a `delivered` receipt for the sent wamid. Media handling (upload, download, digest verification, transcription) follows the Developer Manual but was **not** exercised end-to-end, since that requires sending and receiving actual attachments.
- Two behaviours differed from the manual in practice, and the implementation already handles both conservatively. A `to` that is not the agent's creator returned `500` / `code 2` rather than the documented `403` / `131005`; because `500` is classified as ambiguous, that request is not retried. An over-length `text.body` returned `400` / `code 100` with `message` set to the bare field name `body`; because the length heuristic keys off the field-name form, it is not misreported as an invalid token.
- `docs/guides/whatsapp-agent-platform.md` is the new guide; `docs/chat-apps.md` and the existing WhatsApp guide cross-reference it.

prs.body:
Image generation currently adds provider-specific constructor parameters and cached state to `AgentLoop`, and applies settings changes through a dedicated inbound control message. Applications now assemble `ImageGenerationTool` with its provider configuration and register it in the shared `ToolRegistry` before creating the loop. The default loader preserves caller-supplied tools, including their configured instances.

The gateway supplies an image reload callback to the WebUI settings runtime, following the existing MCP callback path. Reload reads the gateway's explicit config path and replaces or removes the tool through the registry. Failed config reads preserve the live tool and report that a restart is required. Session-discard control remains with the loop's session management; the image control message, acknowledgement future, and intermediate control dispatcher are removed.

Direct `AgentLoop` callers that supplied `image_generation_provider_config(s)` should pre-register the configured tool in their caller-owned registry, using `register_image_generation_tool(config, registry, workspace=...)` or `ImageGenerationTool` directly. The high-level SDK, saved config, and WebUI mutation interfaces retain their existing contracts.

prs.title: fix(feishu): restore assistant creation and pairing recovery
prs.body:
## Summary

- Restore **Add another assistant** after a Feishu assistant is configured. Reuse the existing QR flow with `mode=create`. Keep existing assistants and their credentials unchanged.
- Record pairing reply delivery separately from sender approval. Show a recoverable failure when a reply cannot be sent, instead of only showing empty code slots. A new private message retries the same unexpired code. Keep code entry available if a delivery receipt could not be saved.
- Send Feishu pairing replies as plain text. Report an uninitialized client as a send failure. Do not require rich-text/card permissions for pairing.
- Report saved Feishu credentials as **Configured**, not **Connected**, in field-only validation.
- Add localized recovery copy and update the Feishu setup guide.
- Show a recovered pairing request even if its failure notice was dismissed. A failed approval stays idle until the user retries; polling does not submit it again.

## Cause

PR #5356 removed the create-another-assistant action. The server still supports this operation.

Pairing generated a pending code before sending it. A send failure left the pending request visible, but no delivery outcome reached WebUI. The screenshot alone does not identify the user's specific Feishu API error. This change fixes the observable failure path and reduces pairing's message-format dependencies; it does not bypass platform permissions.

## Verification

- Python: 263 tests passed across the Feishu suite, pairing store, base channel, and settings system. Two existing optional-dependency guards skipped tests.
- Frontend: 160 tests passed across QR flows, channel settings, pairing UI, and localization. The two new recovery tests reproduced both failures before the review fix.
- WebUI production build, frontend lint, scoped Ruff, and scoped strict basedpyright passed.
- Browser checks used the actual components with isolated synthetic data: existing assistants → QR creation → cancel → retry → simulated authorization → another assistant; failure recovery and code entry at 375px; Chinese/English and light/dark states.
- A Feishu handler test exercises failed send → plain-text retry → approval, including a named assistant and cross-assistant isolation. Delivery callbacks cannot revive expired/approved requests or replace a successful receipt with a failed concurrent retry.
- Review verification reran 130 related Python tests. An isolated compatibility probe used the actual pre-change store implementation to create records, read them through the current settings DTO, add delivery status, and then approve/delete them with the old implementation. Existing approvals remained intact.
- The browser review used the current popup with simulated responses. At 375px in Chinese, one failed approval stayed idle and the Retry button completed the second attempt. All ten locales include the Retry label.
- Integration checks after updating the branch to the current main: 163 focused frontend tests and 130 related Python tests passed. The earlier CI failure was in an existing Linear cancellation test. It now waits for the input to become enabled after the cancellation effect, without changing production behavior or weakening the assertion.

The browser authorization callback and Feishu transport were simulated. No live Feishu authorization or user account configuration was changed. This is not a claim that the reported user's live environment has passed E2E testing.

## Compatibility and scope

**Breaking changes: none.** `delivery_status` is optional. Old pending records and old gateways retain code entry. Pairing codes, TTLs, approval rules, config paths, and assistant identities are unchanged. Direct code generators that do not track delivery remain compatible. No new API operation or capability is required.

Repository guide: updated in this PR. Release notes and published website instructions: follow up with the release; no external site changes here. No deployment, release, or merge is included.

prs.title: fix(webui): keep settings restarts out of chat history
prs.body:
## Problem

The settings Restart button sends a silent `/restart` command. Without a current chat, it uses the connection's default routing ID. Saving that command, workspace scope or reply could create an empty topic.

## Change

Treat this authenticated settings request as a transient control. Keep the existing allowlist and workspace checks, correlated reply, ACK and retry deduplication. Do not save a chat, change its workspace, append display history or broadcast a user message for this request.

The gateway sets the internal marker only for an exact silent restart from a trusted WebUI connection. A turn-ID prefix alone is not sufficient. No new endpoint, client capability or agent-loop branch is needed.

Keep restart progress in each participating browser tab. Another tab can consume the shared reload marker without leaving the initiating tab stuck on “Restarting...”.

## Compatibility

Keep the existing wire protocol. Typed `/restart` and session commands keep their behavior. Existing canonical records and display transcripts are not migrated, deleted or hidden. Users can inspect and remove old empty topics. Prompts and tool schemas do not change.

## Verification

- After merging main `1e5ab8e95`, 418 backend tests passed across restart controls, command dispatch, workspace permissions, WebSocket ingress and HTTP routes. They cover repeated default IDs, unchanged history, canonical-only and display-only history, fresh-manager sidebar discovery, ACK retry, allowlist rejection and untrusted clients.
- 363 UI tests passed across App layout, composer, workspace selection and the WebSocket client. They include another tab clearing the restart marker before or after disconnect and integration with the permission-switching change in #6175.
- Earlier real gateway/browser checks restarted twice with multiple tabs connected. Both initiating tabs recovered without a page reload. No canonical record or display transcript was created.
- Current-head CI covers the Python matrix, WebUI and Docker build.

No live model or messaging channel was called. Physical mobile/PWA testing was not performed. This fixes the settings Restart action, not every possible cause of a new topic.

## Change

issues.body:
### Problem

The hermes v4 model-callable surface (schema `hermes.shared_metrics.v4.schema.json`, lines 4637-4650) currently lists 14 `kanban_*` tools. The hermes CLI (`hermes_cli/kanban.py`) already implements four useful workflow operations as subcommands, but none of them are bridged to the model tool surface. From inside a model session the following workflow operations cannot be performed at all:

- `kanban_update` -- reassign / re-priority / re-title / re-body. CLI analogs: `_cmd_reassign` (line 608) and `_cmd_set_model` (line 581).
- `kanban_archive` -- move a card out of the active list. CLI analog: `_cmd_archive` (line 1122).
- `kanban_dependency_add` / `kanban_dependency_remove` -- symmetric graph ops. CLI analogs: `_cmd_link` (line 707) / `_cmd_unlink` (line 728). The model surface today exposes only the one-shot `kanban_link` (no symmetric remove, no add that walks the runtime gate).
- `kanban_notify_subscribe` -- programmatic subscription of a card to a Matrix / Telegram room. CLI analog: `_cmd_notify_subscribe` (line 1155).

Each entry above is a CLI subcommand that already routes through `kbc.connect_closing()` and `kb.*`, so the runtime path is proven. Only the model-bridge enum entry is missing -- no new business logic is required.

### Use cases (real, observed)

1. Mid-flight reassignment (2026-10-13, card `t_ca0107ac`): an in-flight card needed to be reassigned when its original worker profile entered a circular-dependency crash. Without `kanban_update` (reassign), the only available path was to close the original card and create a replacement, polluting the audit trail. Recorded in the cross-link `t_63ae55b7 -> t_956c471c`.
2. Card subscription handoff: a card can be subscribed to a Matrix room via `hermes kanban notify-subscribe`, but the model cannot do this from its own session. Subscribing today requires a shell step, which a worker without terminal access (e.g. a delegated subagent) cannot perform.
3. Card graph reshuffling: when an assignee changes mid-flight the dependency graph often needs to be re-shuffled. Today the only way to remove a link is to recreate the child card, again polluting the audit.

### Proposed fix

Add four new entries to the `kanban_*` enum in `hermes.shared_metrics.v4.schema.json` and register their handlers in `hermes-agent/hermes_cli/kanban.py`. Most are one-line wrappers around existing CLI subcommands:

```python
# in hermes_cli/kanban.py, alongside the existing handler table
"archive": _cmd_archive,
"notify-subscribe": _cmd_notify_subscribe,
```

The four tools (`kanban_update`, `kanban_archive`, `kanban_dependency_add`, `kanban_dependency_remove`, `kanban_notify_subscribe`) can be added to the schema enum with the same shape as the existing entries. The `kanban_update` tool needs a thin wrapper around `_cmd_reassign` and `_cmd_set_model` so it covers reassign, priority, title, and body in one call.

### Backwards compatibility

- All four additions are additive. No existing tool changes.
- The new entries are toolset-gated; the existing `kanban` toolset is already enabled by default for the relevant profile types per `hermes tools --summary`.
- A side-patch / side-adapter approach can be vendored if the upstream merge is too slow; happy to coordinate via a separate channel.

### Related

- Diagnosis: card `t_ca0107ac` (operator-only, no PR).
- Schema SSOT: `hermes_cli/observability/schemas/hermes.shared_metrics.v4.schema.json` (lines 4637-4650 list the current 14 `kanban_*` tools; the four proposed additions are absent).
- CLI SSOT: `hermes_cli/kanban.py` (subcommand handlers at lines 573, 581, 608, 707, 728, 1122, 1155).

### Bug Description

I have a main agent that I have delegate multiple tasks to subagents. In the meantime I also guide the main agent through another separate task that runs tandem to the subagents. When conversing with the main agent, I sometimes have to interrupt it to correct it or myself. But this also interrupts every task delegated to subagents, and I have to ask the main agent to resume these tasks — which sometimes is not possible and the subagents have to redo from scratch.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a new session
2. Ask main agent to delegate certain tasks to subagent
3. Start conversing with main agent while subagent works in the background
4. Interrupt or stop main agent turn

Main agent interactions should not affect any background or subagent tasks unless specifically instructed to do so.

Interrupting main agent also immediately interrupts subagent tasks. The task are canceled, not put on hold or paused, so subagents are not able to "resume" them. issues.body:
## Bug Description

Desktop replays `approval.pending` as soon as a WebSocket emits `gateway.ready`, using the cached active runtime ID. If the connection was down long enough for the backend to reclaim that runtime, this request runs before `session.resume` rebinds the stored conversation and fails with JSON-RPC error `4001` (`session not found`). The unnecessary request can recur on subsequent reconnects.

The defect is still present on `main` at `63d0b94120027d487c9a5235b9ec64b696af1b26`.

## Upgrade-First Investigation (2026-10-13)

Before changing source code, I backed up the installation and ran the official `hermes update --yes`. This upgraded `v0.21.5+7251.ge473f5a` to `v0.21.7+279.g63d0b94`, the latest upstream `main` revision when investigated and filed. I also rebuilt and installed Desktop, restarted the gateway, and verified the running revision. The upgraded source tree was clean at this stage, with no local source patch.

The initial post-upgrade smoke test restored conversations and completed chat turns without new stale-session errors during its short observation window. I then tested the reconnect ordering specifically against the unpatched upgraded code at `63d0b94`. Across three simulated reconnects, the focused regression still made six `approval.pending` queries: three against retired runtime IDs at `gateway.ready`, followed by three against rebound IDs. That demonstrated the remaining defect before this patch was applied.

There are two distinct parts of the diagnosis:

- **Already fixed upstream:** [commit `1dfef400a7`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/commit/1dfef400a790f7fc6bda5b270d1683480c3e15bb) fixes heartbeat timeout decisions for hidden/minimized Desktop windows whose timers are throttled. The old code could close a healthy socket even after a ping had been acknowledged. This commit is included in `63d0b94`; the upgrade brought in that fix. A deterministic throttled-timer test failed on the old `e473f5a` code and passed on the upgraded code.
- **Addressed by PR #137641:** after an actual disconnect and runtime reclamation, `gateway.ready` still queries approvals using the cached runtime before session rebind. The patch removes this early query while retaining existing pending-approval restoration after rebind and on `session.info`. It does not change the heartbeat implementation.

With the patch, the same three-reconnect regression makes only three queries, all for rebound IDs, and restores their pending approvals. The separate Electron test passes after a 25-second simulated outage, with a fresh runtime and no stale approval rejection. These are controlled reconnect regressions; they do not establish that spontaneous heartbeat disconnects continued after upgrading, or that physical sleep/wake has been validated.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start Desktop with a local backend and complete one chat turn, leaving the conversation mounted.
2. Interrupt its WebSocket connection for more than the backend's default 20-second orphan grace period. A deterministic reproduction can close the socket and temporarily close reconnect attempts, while leaving the backend running.
3. Allow the socket to reconnect after 25 seconds.
4. Observe the request ordering: `gateway.ready` triggers `approval.pending` for the old runtime before the stored conversation is resumed under its current runtime ID.
5. Repeat the reconnect to observe another request against a retired runtime.

## Expected Behavior

Socket readiness alone should not trigger a session-scoped approval query. Restore pending approvals after a successful session rebind, and continue handling `session.info` refreshes.

## Actual Behavior

The client queries an expired runtime and receives `4001`. The stale-session guard cannot prevent this first query because the new connection has not yet established that the cached ID is gone.

## Root Cause and Proposed Fix

[`approvalReplaySessionId`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/63d0b94120027d487c9a5235b9ec64b696af1b26/apps/desktop/src/lib/gateway-events.ts) returns `activeSessionId` for `gateway.ready`. [`useGatewayEventHandler`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/63d0b94120027d487c9a5235b9ec64b696af1b26/apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-message-stream/gateway-event/index.ts) immediately passes it to `replayPendingApproval`.

Remove that early replay trigger and its now-unused argument. Existing `session.activate` / `session.resume` snapshot restoration and `session.info` approval replay remain in place; no approval policy or backend lifecycle change is needed.

## Reproduction Evidence

- A focused regression exercising the real replay helper, prompt store, request routing and stale-session guard over three reconnects queried six IDs before the fix, including three retired IDs. With the fix it queries only the three rebound IDs and restores their pending approvals.
- An Electron regression uses a real backend, isolated `HOME` / `HERMES_HOME` / user data, and a loopback mock model. After a 25-second outage it confirms a new runtime ID, preserved transcript, delivery of a follow-up message, and zero rejected approval queries. It passes with the fix.
- Tested on macOS 15.7.7, arm64, Python 3.14.7. Physical system sleep and other operating systems have not been tested.

## Related Work

Searched existing issues and PRs across open and closed states. #101531 addresses reattaching mounted warm sessions after reconnect, and #100639 concerns polling of stale runtimes. This report isolates the separate early query issued from `gateway.ready`, before rebind completes.

## Debug Report

The reproduction uses synthetic test conversations and a local mock provider. No personal configuration, credentials, conversation content or raw user logs are included.

- [x] I am submitting a corresponding fix and regression tests.

issues.body:
## Summary

Two related gaps in the Slack adapter when `allow_bots` admits peer bots (e.g. `allow_bots: mentions` plus a bot user in `SLACK_ALLOWED_USERS`):

### 1. Bot senders can control the gateway (security)

`_build_message_event` never sets `MessageEvent.allow_gateway_control`, so it keeps its default `True` for bot/app authors too. An admitted peer bot can:

- run gateway commands: `/yolo` (turns command approvals off for the session), `/approve`, `/restart`, `/update`, …
- answer a blocking approval prompt with a bare plaintext approval word (`yes`, `ok`, 👍), via `run_busy` → `_plaintext_approval_words`.

This lets any agent posting through an allowlisted bot bypass the human-in-the-loop approval gate without the model being involved at all. Reproduced live: a peer bot posting `@hermes /yolo` in a thread disabled approvals for that session.

The adapter already computes `is_bot=self._event_declares_bot_sender(event)` for the source, and plugin injection already uses `allow_gateway_control=False` for untrusted text.

**Fix:** in `_build_message_event`, pass `allow_gateway_control=not source.is_bot`. Bot posts then arrive as plain conversation; only human senders can steer the gateway.

### 2. Peer bots (and trailing mentions) force a reply, so `[SILENT]` becomes the ⚠️ fallback

`_slack_reply_expected` returns `True` for any message that mentions the bot. Under `allow_bots: mentions` *every* admitted bot post mentions it, so a peer agent's FYI can never be met with silence; the gateway substitutes the "returned only a silence marker" warning. Separately, a human follow-up that addresses someone else with a *trailing* mention (`that's a bug, see that @alice`) returns `None` (only a leading mention counts), which also forces the fallback.

**Fix:**
- `sender_is_bot` → `False` (silence allowed; the bot can still reply).
- When the message does not mention the bot, a mention of someone else **anywhere** (`<@U…>` or a literal `@handle`, for agent personas that are not Slack users; emails excluded) → `False`.
- Human messages that mention the bot, and plain follow-ups, keep the visible fallback (#110952).

Tested locally: `tests/gateway/test_slack_*.py` + `test_gateway_silence_tokens.py` pass (283), with four new `test_slack_reply_expected.py` cases (trailing peer mention, plain `@handle`, email not a mention, bot sender mentioning the bot). Happy to open a PR with the diff.

issues.body:
## Summary

`tool_call` naming a tool that is **already directly callable this session** is refused with:

> `'terminal' is a directly-listed tool, not a deferred one. Call it directly instead of via tool_call.`

(`tools/tool_search_validation.py` → `not_deferrable_error`, the directly-listed branch). The message is accurate and the model recovers by re-issuing the call directly — but the intent was unambiguous, so the bridge could dispatch it as a local call instead of erroring and costing a round-trip.

## Impact

Low / robustness. One wasted iteration per occurrence — observed 3x in a 24 h window across autonomous (cron) sessions, and more likely in long runs where the model cycles through a deferred catalog and reaches for `tool_call` out of habit while a directly-listed name is in the same batch.

## Repro

1. A session with the deferred-tool catalog loaded (so `tool_call` is present in the tool list).
2. Call `tool_call` with `{"calls":[{"name":"terminal","arguments":{...}}]}` where `terminal` is also directly listed.
3. Refusal; the model then retries with a direct call, which works.

## Related but distinct

- #108663 — the same wording is served for a toolset *disabled* on the platform, where the tool genuinely is not callable in any form. That one is a wrong-advice bug.
- #130153 — the inverse case: a deferred tool named bare says it "does not exist" instead of pointing at `tool_call`.

## Suggestion

In the directly-listed branch, dispatch as a local call (same path a direct call takes, so policy, hooks and approvals are unchanged); or, if the refusal stays, include the exact direct-call JSON in the error the way the "takes exactly one entry" refusal already does, so the retry costs no reasoning step. Either way the docstring's two-mistake split is preserved — the bare-MCP-suffix branch is unaffected.

issues.body:
### Bug Description

With `telegram.observe_unmentioned_group_messages: true`, a group-chat turn that carries an image (a photo, or a reply to an image) is persisted with the **wrapped** API message (`[Observed Telegram group context ...]` + backlog + `[Current addressed message ...]`) instead of the bare message. Each later image turn embeds the previous wrapped row twice, so the stored user turn doubles in size with every image turn.

In one group session the stored user turn reached 1.8M characters in three days. Auto-compaction then cannot help: it shrinks replay history, but the bloat rides in the current (protected) user turn. Two ineffective attempts trip the anti-thrash guard and the user sees:

```
⚠️ Context is over the compression threshold (~704,609 tokens >= 425,000) but compression is currently blocked (ineffective). The model may stop responding. Run /new to start a fresh session or /compress to retry immediately.
```

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Telegram group in `TELEGRAM_GROUP_ALLOWED_CHATS`, with `telegram.require_mention: true`, `telegram.observe_unmentioned_group_messages: true` and bot privacy mode off. Main model is vision-capable (native image routing), here `openai-codex`.
2. Post a few untagged messages so observed rows exist.
3. Mention the bot with a photo, or reply to an image while mentioning it. Repeat a few times, with some observed chatter in between.
4. Inspect `state.db`:

```sql
SELECT id, observed, active, compacted, length(content),
       (length(content) - length(replace(content, '[Observed Telegram group context', ''))) / 32 AS observed_headers
FROM messages
WHERE session_id = ? AND instr(content, '[Observed Telegram group context') > 0
ORDER BY id;
```

### Expected Behavior

The observed block is API-only. The persisted user row holds only the bare addressed message (the `persist_user_message = ctx.message` branch in `_run_conversation_with_approval`), as it already does for text-only turns. The size of one turn's observed context is bounded by the observed rows, and compaction can bring the session back under threshold.

### Actual Behavior

Every user row that contains the observed header is an image turn. Text-only turns in the same session are persisted bare. All header rows have `observed=0`:

| Row | Persisted at (UTC) | Length (chars) | `[Observed ...]` headers | `[Current addressed ...]` headers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2843 | 2026-10-10 11:54 | 51,311 | 1 | 1 |
| 2856 | 2026-10-10 11:55 | 102,904 | 2 | 2 |
| 4094 | 2026-10-13 04:21 | 225,507 | 4 | 4 |
| 4105 | 2026-10-13 04:22 | 451,160 | 8 | 8 |
| 4115 | 2026-10-13 04:24 | 902,526 | 16 | 16 |
| 4191 | 2026-10-13 05:00 | 1,806,298 | 32 | 32 |

Row 4191 has ~100k lines but only 1,274 unique lines. All of the session's observed rows together hold only ~66k characters.

Compaction log for the session:

```
context compression started: messages=76 tokens=~737,962
context compression done: messages=76->11 rough_tokens=~570,342 awaiting_real_usage=true
context compression started: messages=13 tokens=~710,346
context compression done: messages=13->10 rough_tokens=~567,171 awaiting_real_usage=true
```

The session then holds `compression_ineffective_count = 2` and `last_activity_description = "compression blocked (ineffective)"`. The provider keeps billing ~705k input tokens per call (`in=704937 ... in=710358` across one turn's 15 API calls), even though the active replayable rows hold only ~60k characters.

Each turn also logs `Repaired 12xx message-alternation violation(s) while restoring session ...`, and the count grows by one per turn.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram observed group context, turn persistence), Agent (context compression)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

Telegram

### Operating System

Linux arm64 (official Docker image `nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest`, s6, `gateway run`)

### Python Version

3.14.7

### Hermes Version

v0.21.6 (`hermes --version`: `Hermes Agent v0.21.6 (2026.9.24) · upstream 818c13be`). v0.21.7 release notes mention nothing related.

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

Partially traced; I have not confirmed the exact line.

- `gateway/run_turn_runner.py` `_run_conversation_with_approval` builds `api_message = _wrap_current_message_with_observed_context(self._native_image_run_message(), observed_group_context)` and sets `persist_user_message = ctx.message` when observed context is present.
- With an image, `_native_image_run_message()` returns a content-part **list**. `_wrap_current_message_with_observed_context` then prefixes the first text part.
- The rows above show that on this list path the wrapped text is what gets persisted. The bare `persist_user_message` override does not take effect. On the string path (text-only turns) it does.
- Once a wrapped row is in history, the next wrapped turn contains it twice, which gives the 2^n growth in header counts. Which path duplicates it is not confirmed. Candidates are the alternation repair merging consecutive user turns, and the observed-row collection in `_build_gateway_agent_history`.

Related but different: #48677 (in-place persist override dropped observed context from the API call), #47415 (observed photos stringified).

### Proposed Fix (optional)

- Apply `persist_user_message` for multimodal (list) current messages too, so the persisted row never contains the observed wrapper.
- Defensively, strip any `[Observed ... context]` … `[Current addressed message ...]` prefix from user rows when building replay history, so already-poisoned sessions recover without `/new`.
- Consider capping or flagging an over-threshold current user turn, so compaction reports "current turn too large" instead of repeatedly failing as "ineffective".

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

No

issues.title: Matrix: gateway never requests missing inbound room keys - messages from a device that withheld its Megolm session are dropped forever

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/plugins
labels.description: Plugin system and bundled plugins

labels.name: platform/matrix
labels.description: Matrix adapter (E2EE)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low — cosmetic, nice to have

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

issues.body:
## Summary

When an inbound `m.room.encrypted` event cannot be decrypted because the sender's Megolm session was never shared with the bot, the event is dropped with one log line and nothing else happens. The gateway never sends an `m.room_key_request`, so the key is never recovered — including after the sender's client is switched to share with unverified devices, which is the only recovery an operator has.

We hit this live: 1:1 E2EE room, one sender device withheld its session (`m.unverified` — the bot device is unverified, as it always is here, see #86018), 17 messages over ~2 hours were lost silently, while a second device of the same sender (different client, sharing normally) decrypted fine throughout.

## Environment

- hermes-agent `0.21.5` (`code_sha 749220ef`), Python 3.13.5, mautrix `0.21.1`
- Matrix 1:1 room, E2EE enabled (`MATRIX_ENCRYPTION`), no interactive verification of the bot device
- Sender side: ordinary clients; only one of the sender's devices withheld

## Symptoms

- mautrix logs `Failed to decrypt megolm event: no session with given ID <SESSION_1> found` per event; the same lines reappear for the same events after every gateway restart.
- The adapter's message handler is never invoked, so the bot simply stays silent — nothing surfaces to the user or as ERROR.
- Outbound is fine: the bot keeps sending encrypted, and shares for its own sessions succeed (e.g. a fresh share after a device-list change).

## Root cause

1. `plugins/platforms/matrix/adapter.py` (`main`): `olm = OlmMachine(client, crypto_store, crypto_state)` (line 1242), `olm.share_keys_min_trust = TrustState.UNVERIFIED` / `olm.send_keys_min_trust = TrustState.UNVERIFIED` (1243-1244), `client.crypto = olm` (1259).
2. That `OlmMachine` already contains the complete request machinery: it inherits `KeyRequestingMachine` (`request_room_key`, `_receive_forwarded_room_key`) and processes `m.forwarded_room_key` to-device events (`mautrix/crypto/machine.py`). But `request_room_key` is never called anywhere in the repo — `grep -rn request_room_key` outside `.venv` returns 0 hits.
3. Assigning `client.crypto` makes mautrix register its `DecryptionDispatcher` for `m.room.encrypted` (`mautrix/client/encryption_manager.py`). On `SessionNotFound` that dispatcher logs and returns — the event is neither dispatched nor does anything ask the sender for the key.
4. mautrix's reference implementation sits one layer above, in the bridge: `mautrix/bridge/matrix.py::_handle_encrypted_wait` → `crypto.request_room_key(room_id, sender_key, session_id, from_devices={sender: [device_id]})` → `wait_for_session(...)` → re-decrypt → dispatch. Hermes drives the `OlmMachine` directly and has no equivalent, so a withheld or lost inbound session is unrecoverable.
5. The trust thresholds configured at 1243-1244 govern what the bot *shares*; they are not the cause here. The withholding happens in the sender's client, outside the bot's control — which is exactly why the request path matters: it is the only way to recover once the sender's client is willing to share.

## Evidence from the affected deployment (ids redacted)

- `crypto.db` → `crypto_megolm_inbound_session`: the session of the sender's other device is present (decrypts fine), the withheld session id is absent. `crypto_olm_session` for the withholding device **exists**, with `last_decrypted` equal to the Olm session creation time. So the Olm channel to that device is up and healthy — only the group session is missing: an `m.room_key_request` would have had a working, already-established channel to travel on.
- Timeline: E2EE enabled 10:14, first undecryptable event 10:33, 17 total until 11:56, no key and no forwarded key ever received.
- After the sender's client was switched to share with unverified devices, new messages were still undecryptable: a client only shares on session creation, so nothing arrives without a request. (Meanwhile the bot created and shared a fresh outbound session at 12:25 without problems — the send path is unaffected.)

```
12:24:45 WARNING Failed to decrypt megolm event: no session with given ID <SESSION_1> found   # <-- requested a session, no handler, nothing further
```

## Candidate fix (~60 lines, adapter-local)

Install a `DecryptionDispatcher` subclass right after `client.crypto = olm`, which requests the missing key in the background and re-dispatches the event once it arrives — the same shape as the bridge reference above:

```python
def _install_key_requesting_dispatcher(client: Any) -> None:
    """Let the decryption dispatcher ask senders for missing Megolm keys.

    mautrix's OlmMachine never requests a room key on its own - only the
    high-level bridge does (mautrix/bridge/matrix.py, _handle_encrypted_wait).
    The gateway drives the OlmMachine directly, so without this a message whose
    session was never shared stays unreadable forever.
    """
    from mautrix.client import DecryptionDispatcher
    from mautrix.errors import DecryptionError, SessionNotFound
    from mautrix.util import background_task

    class _KeyRequestingDecryptionDispatcher(DecryptionDispatcher):
        async def handle(self, evt: Any) -> None:
            try:
                decrypted = await self.client.crypto.decrypt_megolm_event(evt)
            except SessionNotFound as err:
                self.client.crypto_log.warning(
                    "Matrix: missing session %s for %s - requesting room key from %s/%s",
                    err.session_id, evt.event_id, evt.sender, evt.content.device_id)
                background_task.create(self._request_and_retry(evt, err))
                return
            except DecryptionError as exc:
                self.client.crypto_log.warning("Failed to decrypt %s: %s", evt.event_id, exc)
                return
            self.client.dispatch_event(decrypted, evt.source)

        async def _request_and_retry(self, evt: Any, err: Any) -> None:
            crypto = self.client.crypto
            try:
                got = await crypto.request_room_key(
                    evt.room_id, evt.content.sender_key, evt.content.session_id,
                    from_devices={evt.sender: [evt.content.device_id]}, timeout=25)
            except Exception as exc:
                logger.warning("Matrix: room key request for %s failed: %s", err.session_id, exc)
                return
            if not got:
                logger.warning("Matrix: no room key for session %s - %s/%s did not share it",
                               err.session_id, evt.sender, evt.content.device_id)
                return
            try:
                decrypted = await crypto.decrypt_megolm_event(evt)
            except DecryptionError as exc:
                logger.warning("Matrix: %s still undecryptable after key request: %s",
                               evt.event_id, exc)
                return
            logger.info("Matrix: room key %s received - %s decrypted and dispatched",
                        err.session_id, evt.event_id)
            self.client.dispatch_event(decrypted, evt.source)

    client.remove_dispatcher(DecryptionDispatcher)
    client.add_dispatcher(_KeyRequestingDecryptionDispatcher)
```

## Non-goals

- No change to the sharing trust policy, no new key material exposed: the bot only asks for sessions it was supposed to receive.
- No historical/backup recovery.
- No change to outbound key delivery — #99624 and #101220 cover that direction.
- No new config knob unless the maintainers want one.

## Verification status

- Root cause: verified by reading current `main` plus the live evidence above.
- Fix: applied to a local 0.21.5 deployment via an idempotent patch script; `ast.parse` + `py_compile` clean; all mautrix APIs used were checked to exist in 0.21.1 (`OlmMachine.__mro__` includes `KeyRequestingMachine`; `request_room_key(room_id, sender_key, session_id, from_devices, timeout) -> bool`; `Client.crypto_log`; `background_task.create`).
- Runtime verification (does the sender's client answer the request and is the event dispatched?) is pending a gateway restart. I will update this body with the outcome either way — body edits, not follow-up comments.

## Related / prior art

- #77099 (closed) — the mirror-image gap: Hermes *rejecting* the owner's key requests, because `default_allow_key_share` serves only the bot's own user. Same class of hole, opposite direction; folded into #102278.
- #102278 (open) — opt-in cross-user key sharing for E2EE recovery (bot shares its own keys with allowlisted users).
- #99624 (open) — retries the *current outbound* Megolm key to devices omitted during the initial share; listed there as an explicit non-goal: "no room-key request handling".
- #101220 (open) — harden E2EE key delivery (persist one-time keys before upload, single crypto-store owner, re-share missed keys to allowlisted users).
- #71067 (open) — inbound messages silently dropped, caused by a fresh crypto store reporting rooms as unencrypted: different failure, same "bot silently deaf" symptom.
- #86018 (open) — SAS device verification; currently the only place in the tree that touches `request_room_key`.

## Questions

1. Is a PR of this shape welcome (a `DecryptionDispatcher` subclass installed right after `client.crypto = olm`), or would you prefer an explicit hook in the crypto setup that the adapter implements?
2. Unconditional, or behind a config knob (e.g. `matrix.e2ee_key_request_timeout`, `0` = off)?
3. Timeout/retry policy: the mautrix bridge waits 22 s for the key. Is a similar bound (one request, no unbounded waiting) in line with what you expect?
4. Should this stay narrow to the missing-session case, or also cover other "session gone" causes (e.g. after a device reset, cf. #89469)?

---

*Drafted with assistance from an AI agent (Hermes Agent, Nous Research) on behalf of the reporter, who operates this deployment. All room ids, user ids, device ids and event ids above are redacted.*

issues.body:
## Summary

On Windows, when the chat `/update` command (i.e. `hermes update --gateway`) runs against a checkout with local uncommitted changes, the updater autostashes them and then asks:

    Restore local changes now? [y/N]

On Windows that prompt can never reach the user, **and** the intended "gateways are paused" short-circuit never fires — so the update always waits the full 300-second timeout and silently applies the default `'n'`.

Two mechanisms combine to cause this:

1. The relay that forwards the prompt to the chat (`_forward_update_prompt` in `gateway/run_notifications.py`, ~L502) is part of the **gateway process** — but the update flow **pauses the gateway before the prompt is asked** (`→ Stopping Windows gateway process(es) before updating...` / `✓ Paused gateway profile(s): default`). There is nothing left to relay the prompt.
2. `_gateway_prompt()` in `hermes_cli/update_cmd.py` (~L379) has a deliberate short-circuit for exactly this case — its inline comment says "the gateway that would relay it is stopped for the update" — but the check is `update_cmd_posix_pause.gateways_paused()` (~L393), which only reads the POSIX pause state (`_RUN["posix_stopped"]`, set only in `update_cmd_posix_pause.py` ~L610/L670). On Windows the pause path is `update_cmd_windows.py`, which uses its own token (`resume_needed`, `profiles`, …) and never arms that state:

   `hermes_cli/update_cmd.py` ~L1780:
   `return _m()._pause_windows_gateways_for_update() or _posix_pause.arm_pause(...)`
   — on Windows the first call succeeds, the `or` short-circuits, and `arm_pause()` never runs.

Net effect: `_gateway_prompt()` believes a relay exists, writes `.update_prompt.json` (no consumer — the gateway is paused), and waits the full 300 s before returning the default. The user is never given a chance to answer, and every such update wastes 5 minutes.

## Environment

- Windows 10 (x64), source install (git checkout)
- Triggered via the chat `/update` command (gateway mode)
- Precondition: local uncommitted changes in the checkout (autostash kicks in) — any local source customization triggers it
- Reproduced consistently on one machine: every dirty-checkout update over a two-week window, across Hermes v0.21.5 → v0.21.7 (latest: `71d34bad`, 2026-10-13)

## Steps to reproduce

1. On Windows, have the source checkout with local uncommitted changes.
2. Run `/update` from the chat (or any update path that pauses the gateway first).
3. Check `~/.hermes/logs/update.log`: the prompt line appears and the full 300 s timeout runs; nothing appears in the chat:

    → Stopping Windows gateway process(es) before updating...
      ✓ Paused gateway profile(s): default
    → Local changes detected — stashing before update...
    Saved working directory and index state On main: hermes-update-autostash-...
    ...
    ⚠ Local changes were stashed before updating.
    Restore local changes now? [y/N]
      (no response after 300s, using default: 'n')
    Skipped restoring local changes.
    Your changes are still preserved in git stash.

Note the missing line: on POSIX, the paused-gateway short-circuit makes `_gateway_prompt()` print `→ Restore local changes now? → 'n' (gateways are paused for the update)` and return immediately — no wait, no prompt file.

## Root cause (code references)

- `hermes_cli/update_cmd.py`: `_gateway_prompt()` ~L379 (short-circuit at ~L393); `prompt_for_restore` ~L1423 (always true in gateway mode, ~L1426).
- `hermes_cli/update_cmd_posix_pause.py`: `gateways_paused()` ~L87 — `_RUN.get("posix_stopped") and _RUN.get("resume_needed")`; `posix_stopped` is only ever set in this module (~L610 / ~L670).
- `hermes_cli/update_cmd_windows.py`: the Windows pause path sets its own token and never touches `posix_stopped`; due to the `or` at `update_cmd.py` ~L1780, `_posix_pause.arm_pause()` is never called on Windows.
- `gateway/run_notifications.py`: `_forward_update_prompt` ~L502 — the relay that would consume `.update_prompt.json`; it only runs while the gateway process is alive.

## Impact

- Every dirty-checkout update on Windows wastes 300 s in a wait nobody can answer.
- The "restore local changes" question is effectively unreachable on Windows: it always resolves to the default, so "forward the prompt to the messenger instead of silently skipping it" degrades to "always silently skip".
- No data loss — the stash is preserved and the update completes.

## Related (not duplicates)

- #81482 — same 300-second symptom, different root cause: there the gateway **is** alive and the relay runs, but a soft `SendResult(success=False)` is treated as success and the text fallback is skipped. The fix in PR #81485 targets that path only; it does not cover the "no relay at all" case described here.
- #92303 — same prompt text, Windows, but the unattended **bare CLI** path (blocks on `input()` indefinitely); unrelated to `--gateway`.

## Expected behavior

On Windows with the gateways paused by this run, the prompt should short-circuit to the default immediately — printing the `(gateways are paused for the update)` line, like POSIX does — instead of writing an unconsumed `.update_prompt.json` and waiting the full 300 s.

## Suggested fix direction

Surface "this run already paused the gateways" to `_gateway_prompt()` on Windows too — e.g. have the Windows pause path (or the shared `or` at `update_cmd.py` ~L1780) record the paused state that `gateways_paused()` checks, so the prompt short-circuits to the default instead of waiting.

issues.body:
This is a consolidation proposal, not a new bug — the symptoms are tracked in #68128
(WhatsApp bridge) and #135179 (dashboard actions). Posting it because the repo currently
has **six open PRs** re-implementing the same fallback with three different exception
filters, two of them already marked duplicate, and the remaining choice is a per-site
policy question, not a code question.

## Call sites (audit at commit 562fda904c)

| Detached spawn (function names) | Fallback today | Fixed by |
|---|---|---|
| `gateway_windows.py::_spawn_detached` | ✅ hand-rolled | — |
| `gateway.py` respawn script (template string) | ✅ hand-rolled, stamps breakaway-state env | — |
| `main_desktop.py` desktop launch | ✅ (spawns without-breakaway directly) | — |
| `plugins/platforms/whatsapp/adapter.py` bridge spawn (`connect`) | ❌ retried identically forever | #65990 (drop flag unconditionally), #87777, #125117, #132463 (fallback variants) |
| `web_server_gateway.py::_spawn_hermes_action` | ❌ HTTP 500 WinError 5 | #135751, #135856 |
| `gateway/slash_commands.py::_spawn_detached_update` (`update --gateway` child) | ❌ same failure class | #125117 (also touches this file; no tracking issue) |

## Diagnosis, one sentence

The fallback contract ("callers catch OSError and fall back to
`windows_detach_flags_without_breakaway`") is documented on `windows_detach_flags()`, but
call sites spawn through `windows_detach_popen_kwargs()`, which neither mentions nor
implements it — so each site independently remembers or forgets eight lines.

## Proposal

Move the try/fallback the existing PRs already implement into one helper in
`_subprocess_compat.py`, so a forgetful call site cannot exist. The logic is #135751's and
#87777's; this only changes where it lives:

```python
def popen_detached(args, *, breakaway: bool = True, on_attempt=None, **kwargs) -> subprocess.Popen:
    """Popen detached from the console/Ctrl+C group (start_new_session on POSIX).

    Windows: when ``breakaway`` is true, tries CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB first and
    retries once without it if CreateProcess answers ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED.
    ``on_attempt(with_breakaway)`` runs before each attempt (e.g. to stamp env).
    """
    if not IS_WINDOWS:
        return subprocess.Popen(args, **{"start_new_session": True, **kwargs})
    extra = kwargs.pop("creationflags", 0)
    for with_breakaway in ([True] if breakaway else []) + [False]:
        flags = windows_detach_flags() if with_breakaway else windows_detach_flags_without_breakaway()
        if on_attempt is not None:
            on_attempt(with_breakaway)
        try:
            return subprocess.Popen(args, creationflags=flags | extra, **kwargs)
        except PermissionError as e:
            if not with_breakaway or getattr(e, "winerror", None) != 5:
                raise
            logger.warning("Detached spawn with CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB got access denied; "
                           "retrying without breakaway (child will stay in the parent's job)")
```

Sketch, untested. Design notes:

- `breakaway=False` is the knob that expresses the open per-site question (e.g. #65990's
  position for the bridge) without baking a policy in — the bridge and the self-update
  child have different lifetime needs.
- `on_attempt` exists so the env-stamping sites (`gateway.py` respawn, `_spawn_detached`)
  can migrate; if that hook is unwelcome, they stay hand-rolled and allowlisted.
- The retry logs the observation, not a diagnosis: winerror 5 also covers ACLs/AV blocks,
  and in those cases the second attempt fails identically into the original error path.
- The acceptance property that matters: **no code outside the compat module passes
  `CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB` to a spawn** — enforceable with a test that fails on any
  use of `windows_detach_flags()`/`windows_detach_popen_kwargs()` outside an allowlist.
  Without that, the helper is just a seventh convention.

## Why try/fallback rather than predicting the job

A field data point from a job-restricted deployment (Windows 11, build 10.0.26200):
`QueryInformationJobObject(NULL, ...)` on the affected host reports the immediate job as
`LimitFlags 0x3000` (`KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE | SILENT_BREAKAWAY_OK`), yet a live
`CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB` spawn was denied with winerror 5 — while a self-assign probe
under an identical 0x3000 job **accepts** the flag on the same build, and a plain
0x2000 job denies it. Readings of the immediate job do not determine what a nested chain
will do; CreateProcess is the only complete oracle, which is exactly why the fallback
belongs in one place instead of a pre-flight check or a predicted policy.

Happy to send a PR — or, just as gladly, for any of the six existing PRs to absorb this;
whichever you prefer.

Related: #68128, #135179, PRs #65990 / #87777 / #125117 / #132463 / #135751 / #135856.

---

— Theodore M Estrada (thermes5000@gmail.com)
