prs.title: fix(tools): a tool's SystemExit is a tool error, not a Hermes exit
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Three tool boundaries caught only `Exception`: `ToolRegistry.dispatch` (plugin and built-in tools; its docstring says every exception comes back as `{"error": ...}`), `MemoryManager.handle_tool_call` (memory-provider tools), and the sequential executor's `except` around every sequential dispatch (`agent/tool_executor.py::_run_sequential_call`), which is the boundary for context-engine tools and for a plugin `tool_execution` middleware on that path. `SystemExit` is not an `Exception`, so a plugin tool, a memory-provider or context-engine tool, or a library inside one that calls `sys.exit()` (argparse or click rejecting arguments the model passed, a client signalling an auth failure that way) got past them:

- A single call, or a batch that runs sequentially: the executor re-raised the exception on the agent thread and `AIAgent.run_conversation` re-raised it again. The model never got a tool result and the turn ended with the exception.
- A parallel-safe batch: the turn survived, but the model got `Error executing tool '<name>': thread did not return a result` instead of the error.
- On the gateway the turn runs through `loop.run_in_executor`. The `SystemExit` came back into the event loop, and asyncio re-raises a `SystemExit` out of a running loop, so the gateway's loop stopped and every other session on it with it.

This PR contains `SystemExit` at those three boundaries and returns it as a tool error, the boundary plugin hooks got in #117563 (for #117303). Other `BaseException`s (`KeyboardInterrupt`, `GeneratorExit`, `CancelledError`) still propagate, and inline and delegate tools still re-raise, as before.

**Why a tool's `SystemExit` is a tool failure, while Hermes' own exits are unaffected.** A handler's job is to return a result. A `sys.exit()` inside one is a library's way of saying that this call failed (argparse exits with 2 on bad arguments), not a request from the user or from Hermes to stop. The gateway's turn boundary deliberately re-raises `SystemExit` to keep shutdown semantics (b7936c892d, #86651), but at that point it cannot tell a tool's exit from a real shutdown; the tool boundary can. Nothing in these handler chains raises `SystemExit` on purpose (every `sys.exit()` / `raise SystemExit` under `agent/` and `tools/` is a `__main__` entry point or code run as a subprocess), and on the gateway, turns and their tools run on executor threads while Python raises a signal handler's exception on the main thread. `hermes -z` deliberately re-raises a `SystemExit` that escapes the agent itself (`hermes_cli/oneshot.py`: "Control-flow exceptions (Ctrl-C / sys.exit inside the agent) re-raise to the parent"). This PR doesn't touch that path, and a new guard test pins it: `_run_agent` raising `SystemExit(3)` still makes `run_oneshot` raise `SystemExit` with code 3.

## Related Issue

Related: #117303 / #117563 (the same boundary for plugin hooks). Open #123055 makes the same `except` change to `MemoryManager.handle_tool_call` as part of containing `SystemExit` in memory-provider probes; whichever lands second drops that hunk.

Not covered here: `hermes_cli/middleware.py` itself still catches only `Exception`, so a plugin `tool_execution` middleware that exits is contained on the sequential path (by the executor change above) but, in a parallel batch, still ends as "thread did not return a result"; inline tools and `delegate_task` re-raise by design. Giving `hermes_cli/middleware.py` the #117563 treatment would be a follow-up.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `tools/registry.py`: `dispatch` catches `(Exception, SystemExit)`; the docstring says which exceptions still propagate.
- `agent/memory_manager.py`: `handle_tool_call` catches `(Exception, SystemExit)` and now logs the traceback (`exc_info=True`, which the code-health ratchet requires of a changed catch-all boundary). Every memory-provider tool failure now logs its traceback at ERROR.
- `agent/tool_executor.py`: `_run_sequential_call` catches `(Exception, SystemExit)`; dispatches without an `error_result` (inline tools, `delegate_task`) still re-raise; `_SequentialDispatch.error_result` is typed to take a `BaseException`.
- `tests/tools/test_registry_dispatch_system_exit.py` (new): sync and async handlers, string and int exit codes, return a tool error and log it; the async bridge still runs the next async tool; `KeyboardInterrupt` and `GeneratorExit` propagate.
- `tests/agent/test_tool_system_exit.py` (new): real `AIAgent.run_conversation` turns where a registry tool (single call, and a parallel-safe two-call batch) or a context-engine tool raises `SystemExit`; each completes and the model's next request carries the error as that call's tool result. Memory-provider `SystemExit` becomes a tool error with its message; `KeyboardInterrupt` propagates.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_oneshot_exit_contract.py`: guard test that `hermes -z` still exits when the agent itself raises `SystemExit`.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_registry_dispatch_system_exit.py tests/agent/test_tool_system_exit.py tests/hermes_cli/test_oneshot_exit_contract.py`
2. Against `main` (tests kept, sources reverted): 8 of the 12 new tests fail, namely every tool-`SystemExit` case (the single-call and context-engine turns end with `SystemExit`; the parallel batch gets "thread did not return a result"). The other 4 (`KeyboardInterrupt`/`GeneratorExit` propagation, memory-provider `KeyboardInterrupt`, the `hermes -z` guard) pass on both and pin what must not change. With this PR all 14 tests in the three files pass.
3. Each part is needed: with only `tools/registry.py` reverted, the 4 registry cases and both registry-tool turns fail; with only `agent/memory_manager.py` reverted, the memory-provider case fails; with only `agent/tool_executor.py` reverted, the context-engine turn fails.
4. Gateway effect on `main`, checked with the real `GatewayRunner._run_agent` and an agent whose `run_conversation` raises `SystemExit` (what a tool's exit does on `main`): `asyncio.run` raised `SystemExit` and an unrelated task on the same loop got 1 of its 40 ticks, in 5 of 5 runs. That harness is not part of this PR.

- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)

- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass. Not literally: `scripts/run_tests.sh` on this change before it was rebased onto current `main` gave 5,518 files, 56,820 passed, 427 failed, 1,463 skipped on macOS 26.6. Every failing file also fails on a clean `main` checkout on this machine, except 15 that passed when re-run on this branch (load flakes). After the rebase, the files in How to Test plus the related registry, memory-provider, sequential-timeout and async-bridge tests (124 tests) and `python scripts/check` pass.
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes (the blocking lint and code-health checks CI runs)

prs.title: feat(state): persist message version provenance across compaction
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

An edited message can keep its logical `message_uid`, then be compacted before an external transcript reader sees the edit. At that point both the original and edited rows are marked compacted. A reader cannot safely distinguish a copy from a new authored version using the UID, timestamps, content, or compaction flags.

Add an opaque `message_version_uid` and a session-scoped version ledger. Ordinary edits get a new version; explicit compaction/rotation copies retain theirs, even when their model-facing text changes. The ledger cursor survives physical row replacement and advances for in-place edits. Consumers can recognize copies without discarding unseen edits.

## Related Issue

Consumer integration is tracked separately.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- Schema v32 adds the version column, bounded independent legacy backfill, and `message_versions` arrival ledger. Legacy provenance is not guessed.
- Shared persistence helpers preserve versions for explicit copies and unchanged reissues; canonical payload rewrites mint new versions transactionally. Rollback restores caller stamps.
- Conversation restore, transcript repair, import, compression handoff and concurrent tail clones carry the version. Merges discard the prior version.
- Desktop/TUI scalar writers keep their retained dictionaries aligned with the stored version, including prompt expansion and queue merges.
- Provider serialization strips the field; it is internal persistence metadata. No provider prompt text or wire schemas change.
- The context-engine documentation defines copy declarations, version boundaries, cursor scope and legacy limitations.

## How to Test

Run from the checkout:

```sh
HERMES_TEST_FILE_RETRIES=0 scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 \
  tests/hermes_state/test_message_versions.py \
  tests/hermes_state/test_message_uid.py \
  tests/agent/test_context_engine_message_uid.py \
  tests/hermes_state/test_compression_watermark_commit.py \
  tests/hermes_state/test_replace_messages_archives_suffix_only.py \
  tests/agent/test_in_place_commit_rollback.py \
  tests/tui_gateway/test_submit_row_session_target.py \
  tests/tui_gateway/test_model_switch_marker_role.py
python scripts/check --base origin/main
```

Result at `211a93f0b83b249ecf7dd23600cd35e95688c4b1`: **87 tests passed**; **12 repository checks passed**, zero blocking/advisory findings. Local merge-base review is clean. All test state is synthetic/disposable; no installed Agent, live store or deployment was changed.

## Regression proof

Baseline: `427d605d4985c2d49a795493ef6c5d66413057d1`.

Exact focused command before and after the production change:

```sh
HERMES_TEST_FILE_RETRIES=0 scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/hermes_state/test_message_versions.py
```

The two lifecycle invariants fail on the baseline at the intended version assertions (`assert None != None`): `test_edit_compaction_versions_survive_reopen_and_concurrent_clones` requires the original and edited message to have distinct versions, and `test_rewrites_merges_and_failed_transactions_do_not_reuse_a_committed_version` requires an in-place edit to advance the version. Both pass with the implementation. The tests exercise real `SessionDB` and the real in-flight request restatement, including compaction before any consumer observation, replacement, rotation, reopen/import, stale/owned writers, merge and rollback.

Additional scalar-writer regression: `HERMES_TEST_FILE_RETRIES=0 scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/tui_gateway/test_submit_row_session_target.py` failed before scalar propagation at the expanded-submit and model-switch assertions (`None` versus the persisted version); all nine tests now pass.

## Risk and rollback

Additive schema and metadata change. Version cursors belong to one database and owning session; deleting that session deletes its ledger. Historical backfill assigns independent versions, so it cannot reconstruct old copies. Old writers that omit versions remain usable but cannot promise copy provenance. Reverting the code leaves unused additive columns/table; do not destructively downgrade a live database.

## Checklist

- [x] Read the Contributing Guide; conventional commit; searched existing PR coverage.
- [x] Focused change with regression tests and documentation.
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes.
- [x] Tested on macOS with the repository-managed Python test environment.
- [ ] Full Python suite (CI).
- [x] No new dependencies, config keys, tools, provider schemas or platform-specific APIs.

prs.title: email: support multi-header Authentication-Results (iCloud) via multiple pinned authserv-ids
prs.body:
## Problem

iCloud Mail does not stamp one `Authentication-Results` header. It stamps one per check, each with its own authserv-id (`bimi.icloud.com`, `arc.icloud.com`, `dmarc.icloud.com`, `dkim-verifier.icloud.com`, `spf.icloud.com`). `EMAIL_AUTHSERV_ID` / `platforms.email.authserv_id` accepted a single id. A single pin only saw one of those headers, so the DMARC/SPF/DKIM verdict was split across headers and legitimate mail from allowed senders was dropped as unauthenticated.

## Approach

- `authserv_id` is now a comma-separated list. Entries are stripped, lowercased, and empties dropped.
- For each pinned id, only the topmost matching header is used. Later duplicates are ignored.
- The result clauses from the selected headers are merged. The existing DMARC / SPF / DKIM alignment logic then runs on the merged set.
- Selection reads only the contiguous topmost run of pinned headers. It stops at the first non-pinned or malformed header.
- It fails closed. No pin, no matching header, or an unbalanced quote or comment means the mail is rejected.
- A single id behaves as before, apart from the contiguous-run rule above.

## Security reasoning

- A forged duplicate of a pinned id placed below the real header is ignored (topmost-only per id).
- A forged pinned-id header sitting under a foreign topmost header is ignored (contiguous run only).
- Headers with unpinned ids are ignored. A genuine `spf.icloud.com` pass cannot rescue a failing `dmarc.icloud.com` when only the latter is pinned. Parent or child domains of a pinned id do not match.
- There is no "any header with `dmarc=pass`" shortcut. That approach is spoofable, because the sender can add headers.
- Limitation: if a real pinned header is absent and a sender adds one inside the pinned run, position cannot tell them apart. This relies on the receiving MTA stripping inbound results that claim its own ids, which is the existing trust assumption for authserv-id pinning.

## Tests

`TestMultiHeaderAuthenticationResults` in `tests/gateway/test_email.py` has 8 tests:
- iCloud multi-header pass
- SPF/DKIM-only pass
- forged duplicate rejected
- forged unpinned id rejected
- single id on iCloud fails
- whitespace/case tolerant pin list
- unpinned genuine headers do not count
- Gmail single header still works

A naive any-header implementation fails the forged tests. The existing `test_only_topmost_exact_authserv_id_is_trusted` still passes.

Results from my environment:
- `tests/gateway/test_email.py`: 51 passed, 20 failed. The same 20 fail on `main` with the home-I/O guard (`TEST BUG: file I/O against the REAL hermes home`), so they come from my sandbox and not this change. Before the change it was 43 passed and 20 failed.
- `ruff check` is clean on the changed Python files.
- I did not complete a full-repo run.

## Docs

`website/docs/user-guide/messaging/email.md` now covers:
- multi-id behavior (topmost per id, merged clauses, fail-closed)
- an iCloud example in both env and `config.yaml`
- a security note on not trusting `dmarc=pass` from an arbitrary header
- the updated env var table and drop-log hint text

The docs were not built or link-checked.

prs.title: plugin-catalog: bump hermes-dreaming to 2.6.1 (per-chat fact stores; all holographic languages; forget sweep)
prs.body:
Bumps the pinned `sha`, `version` and the pinned doc/image URLs of `plugin-catalog/hermes-dreaming.yaml` to
[2.6.1](https://github.com/itpartypattaya/hermes-dreaming/releases/tag/v2.6.1)
([CHANGELOG](https://github.com/itpartypattaya/hermes-dreaming/blob/d711eec58a92173d3461d30596163b8cf62b712b/CHANGELOG.md)).
This PR first pinned 2.4.0 and now carries 2.4.0, 2.5.0–2.5.3, 2.6.0 and 2.6.1. No change to the manifest shape, capabilities (still no
tools, hooks, middleware or env vars), the tier or the maintainer; The disclosure gains that the scripts read the holographic plugin's `scope` / `cron_writes` (2.5.3) and, only when `chat_stores` is set, the per-chat databases next to the store (2.6.0).

**2.6.1** fixes what an audit of 2.4.0–2.6.0 found: the forget-sweep gate no longer waits for a running nightly pass (a long pass got the gate killed under its timeout and Hermes delivered a false watchdog alert), an unusual `plugins:` shape in config.yaml reads as unset instead of ending the night, and `install.py --check` warns when the sweep job is missing. No change to the disclosure.

**2.6.0** adds per-chat fact stores (`chat_stores`, off by default) for holographic `scope: user / chat / thread`: `read` lists every per-chat database as counts (SQL — no text, no ids), `promote_from` makes the facts of listed chats candidates, each corroborated only by its own chat; their ids are `<store>#<id>`, the agent writes them only through `memory`, and their tombstones are swept like the shared store's. Reviewed by Codex before release (9 findings, 8 fixed with tests, one by design: trusted chats keep their trust).

**2.5.3** makes a silent failure visible: with holographic `scope: user / chat / thread` facts live in per-user / per-chat files the dream does not read (it would carry one chat's facts into memory every chat sees) and a cron job writes nothing, so the extraction stored nothing without a word; `cron_writes: false` likewise. The report, the diary and `install.py --check` now name the reason and the extraction gate stays asleep.

**2.5.2** fixes what a second review (of 2.5.1) found: the 2.5.1 "since <date> means durable" rule hid ranges («с 15.11 по 17.11»), times and unrelated clauses — now only that phrase is taken out; dashed deadlines and doctor visits are events again; chaining shared n-grams is linear. Same bench and live numbers.

**2.5.1** fixes what an external review of 2.5.0 found, each with a test: a capitalised Turkish month crashed the pass (`KeyError`); a dated profession or anything "since <date>" was taken for a one-off event and never promoted; a deadline now needs a whole date (and no longer backtracks on long numbers); Japanese particle pairs, the English words "solo" / "fare" as foreign stopwords, quadratic n-gram chaining and "Jane 14" as a January date are fixed. The benches, the blind sets and the live household data give the same numbers.

**What 2.5.0 adds — every language the holographic store reads** (0.11.0 reads 18,
[PR #137119](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/137119)). The dream compared words with its own
code, written for Russian and English: a Chinese, Japanese or Thai sentence was one token, so nothing in those
languages was ever corroborated, and a dated appointment was a one-off event only in Russian, English and Thai.
- Chinese, Japanese, Korean and Thai are compared by character n-grams, counted by the stretch of text they
  cover (a name alone is not a mention); Latin languages by stems without diacritics, with function words, months
  and weekdays of nine more languages kept out of the evidence.
- Dated one-off events, deadlines and numbers are read in 15 languages (`14 de noviembre`, `14 Kasım'da`,
  `11月14日`, `11월 14일`, `奶奶11/23上午`); two date bugs fixed (month markers matched by word starts, English
  dates matched by any month-like word).
- Blind sets written by agents that never saw the code (15 languages), first run: a message finds its fact
  56 → 72 % (ja / zh / ko from 0 to 46–54 %, th to 88 %), false mentions down in every Latin language; a one-off
  event is recognised in 6 → 53 of 90 cases. On the maintainer's live household data (Russian / English) the pass
  decides exactly as before.

**What 2.4.0 adds — working with holographic 0.8.0** (fact history and forgetting,
[PR #137119](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/137119)).
- The pass reads only current facts and reports `stats.fact_history`. A human's reply "no longer true" / "that was
  wrong" / "forget it" maps to `fact_store` `end` / `correct` / `forget`, never the agent's own judgement; a conflict
  whose older statement is itself a store fact becomes `change` with that id instead of a second fact.
- **Forget sweep.** `holographic` 0.8.0 erases a forgotten fact from its own file, but the dream keeps copies: the
  payload, refusal list, cooldowns, the diary and its archive, and the output of its own cron jobs. A no-agent job
  (`dream-forget-sweep.py`, every 15 min, no model) reads the store's `forgotten` table — ids only, no text — and
  removes those copies, rescanning every tombstone on each run. Diary lines now carry `[#id]` tags; older lines are
  matched by a preview-hash index. A pass that runs while a fact is forgotten is scrubbed before it is published.
- The installer warns when holographic 0.2–0.7 is installed: those versions refuse every `fact_store` write from a
  cron session, so the extraction job silently stored nothing.

CI of the plugin repository: unittest on Python 3.9 / 3.11 / 3.13, with and without PyYAML — green
([run](https://github.com/itpartypattaya/hermes-dreaming/actions/runs/38347300363)). `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py` passes on the entry; `hermes plugins validate` passes and the
security scan verdict is `safe`.

prs.title: fix(tools): coerce anyOf-typed args for string-coercing bridges (terminal notify)
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes the `terminal` tool's `notify` argument being refused on gateway surfaces whose bridge coerces JSON values (observed on Discord + desktop). The tool schema declares `notify` as `anyOf: [boolean, array<string>]` with **no top-level `type`**, and the shared coercion layer (`tools/arg_coercion.py`) skipped every property without `type` — so a bridge delivering `notify="true"` reached `_handle_terminal` as a string and hit the refusal, even though the unadvertised `notify_on_complete=true` (plain bool schema) worked.

This fixes the **class**, not the instance: `_union_branch_types()` resolves a type-less `anyOf`/`oneOf` property to its branch types (schema order) and lets the existing per-type coercion try each branch. A string value is left untouched when any branch accepts `string`, so already-valid strings are never reinterpreted.

`_handle_terminal` is hardened too: non-string/empty entries in a `notify` list are dropped (an empty-but-usable list keeps today's silent behavior), and the refusal message now names the received type and `repr` for future diagnosis.

## Related Issue

No existing issue found for this symptom; happy to file one if maintainers prefer it tracked separately.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✅ Tests

## Changes Made

- `tools/arg_coercion.py` — `_union_branch_types()`; `coerce_tool_args` now derives expected types for type-less union properties.
- `tools/terminal_tool.py` — `_handle_terminal`: list-entry filtering + diagnostic refusal message (semantics unchanged: bool→`notify_on_complete`, list→`watch_patterns`, explicit `notify` still wins over legacy aliases, heartbeat behavior untouched).
- `tests/tools/test_terminal_notify_coercion.py` (new) — exercises the **real dispatch** via `model_tools.handle_function_call`: `True`/`"true"`/`" True "`/`"false"`, list, JSON-string list, junk (`"yess"`, `"[1, 2]"`, dict) refused with `repr`, and `heartbeat`/`background`/`pty`/`persist_on_release` string forms.
- `tests/agent/test_tool_arg_coercion.py` — contract test: an `anyOf` union coerces; a union containing `string` does not reinterpret strings.

## How to test

```bash
python -m pm.build_env --source . --out .venv --group dev --group test
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tools/test_terminal_notify_coercion.py \
    tests/agent/test_tool_arg_coercion.py tests/tools/test_process_heartbeat.py \
    tests/tools/test_watch_patterns.py tests/tools/test_todo_tool_type_coercion.py -q
# 84 passed; the 2 failures in tests/tools/test_terminal_watcher_arming.py reproduce
# identically on the base commit (pre-existing, environment-dependent, unrelated).
```

Manual reproduction of the bug: from a session whose platform bridge coerces args (Discord gateway), call `terminal(background=true, notify=true)` → refusal "notify must be true/false … or a list of strings"; with this fix the same call arms completion notification (verified against `notify_on_complete=true`, which always worked through the legacy alias).

## Platforms tested

- **Linux** (gateway surfaces: Discord bridge + desktop app) — bug reproduced and fix exercised here.
- macOS/WSL2: not exercised locally; the change is platform-neutral arg validation with no file/process I/O.

## Notes for review

- The coercion applies to every `anyOf`/`oneOf` property whose branches are all simple non-string types — behavior only changes when parsing is unambiguous; on parse failure the original value passes through untouched.
- Nullable MCP unions (`anyOf[integer, null]`) now coerce numeric strings (`"42"`→42) in addition to `"null"`. This is the intended generalization of the existing per-type coercion.
- `"yes"`/`"si"`/`"1"` are deliberately NOT treated as booleans: the shared boolean coercion has an existing test pinning that behavior globally; the observed failure mode was `"true"`, not synonyms.

prs.title: feat(webapp): serve Desktop renderer in browsers
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds `hermes webapp`, an authenticated browser-hosted mode for the **actual Hermes Desktop renderer**. This is not the Web Dashboard: it serves the chat-first Desktop workspace and installs a browser implementation of `window.hermesDesktop` backed by the host running Hermes.

The implementation keeps the existing authority boundaries instead of cloning Desktop UI or adding a parallel backend:

- the renderer is built separately to `apps/desktop/dist-webapp` from the pinned repository workspace;
- the existing FastAPI authentication/session-token and one-time WebSocket-ticket controls gate the surface;
- host files, Git, previews, uploads, profiles, terminal, gateway, and Bot routing reuse existing profile-scoped APIs;
- native-only Electron capabilities are absent or fail explicitly rather than being falsely emulated;
- non-loopback binds remain fail-closed behind configured authentication.

### Lineage and overlap

- Browser bridge/build lineage is carried forward from @adybag14-cyber's #85604; the arbitrary-shell design that originally blocked that PR is not reused.
- The explicit `hermes webapp` product boundary is carried forward from @seagpt's #61171.
- Related browser/Desktop UX work was reviewed in #60829.
- Current main's connection-owner Bot routing (#92731, salvaging #90006) remains authoritative; this PR does not add a second connection resolver.

- Rebased onto main's whole-codebase decomposition (#102117, `d3630f853239e8c41ce7201e09fbdf39bcbc5431`). Webapp behavior follows the topical modules introduced by main, with host-terminal and profile-lifecycle policy in focused owners. All 28 original commits retain their author metadata and full messages, including contributor trailers. The earlier #78628/#78630 proposals and cited shards were reviewed before that main update; no code from unmerged PRs was copied.

Both source contributors are preserved with `Co-authored-by` trailers.

## Related Issue

No single issue. Related work: #85604, #61171, and #60829. This PR does not close those threads.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [x] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [x] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/webapp.py`, CLI parser/lifecycle code, and docs: add `hermes webapp`, isolated renderer builds, process identity, `--status`/`--stop`, and loopback-by-default launch behavior.
- `apps/desktop/src/lib/browser-desktop-bridge*.ts`: implement the browser preload contract for authenticated REST/gateway calls, uploads, files, Git, previews, clipboard, microphone, profiles, and Bot registry routes.
- `hermes_cli/web_server_chat.py`, `hermes_cli/web_host_terminal.py`, and the `chat_ws`, `files`, and `uploads` routers: add authenticated Webapp routing, profile-scoped upload staging, and host-terminal setup through the topical owners. The shared `/api/pty` transport remains in the chat router.
- Desktop preview/files/layout/terminal surfaces: website links open in a separate browser tab by default in Webapp; Electron retains its embedded browser with local or remote gateways. Explicit URL previews retain the sandboxed iframe and **Open in browser** recovery action. Other browser adaptations include deliberate native-only degradation, configured-layout persistence, and refresh-safe terminal history.
- Webapp downloads and media: implement the browser save bridge using authenticated download URLs and a HEAD check before handing off to the browser. Audio/video use authenticated HTTP streams with Range support. URLs retain the active profile and proxy base path; Electron keeps its native save dialog and media protocol. Existing managed-file access rules and size limits still apply.
- Profile lifecycle: persist a fresh incarnation per create/import, preserve it across rename, carry it through sessions/workers, and use the same cross-process lifecycle lease for legacy marker backfill, `SessionDB` pathname binding/schema initialization, and attachment writes so delete/recreate cannot cross a checked generation boundary. Partial-delete retries durably recover the token. Publication and retirement coordination lives in `hermes_cli/profile_lifecycle.py`; gateway retirement/fence policy lives in `tui_gateway/profile_lifecycle.py`.
- Upload and attachment handling: reuse the incoming upload spool, check its actual length, and carry captured installation/profile/incarnation ownership through browser picks, drops, edits, drafts, and retries. Already-staged files attach through the owning backend and retain the copy into the container-visible attachment cache.
- Clipboard publication: extract native clipboard images outside lifecycle/session locks, then validate the captured session and profile generation before publishing the image.
- Session display and recovery: derive human/runtime provenance from the backend's canonical classifier and carry it through REST/RPC hydration and reconciliation. Runtime journal boundaries preserve partial replies, tool/reasoning structure, human corrections, and stream ownership across reloads and reused stream IDs; completed replies retire the journal tail. Older gateways retain the existing fallback, with durable row IDs compared before text normalization.
- Detached turn continuity: a brief browser disconnect retains the running session and worker for a bounded reconnect grace period. Resume, activation, and prompt submission check profile generation and disconnect ownership before reattaching.
- Shared policy: use one typed Git REST mapping, the existing upload-generation resolver and desktop control-plane process classifier, an explicit staging destination for private profile initialization, and shared attachment response/error helpers. Profile checks access their lifecycle owner directly.
- Tests and smoke coverage: add browser bridge, uploads, Webapp command/lifecycle, same-name recreation ABA, deterministic barriers at attachment write/DB connect/legacy backfill, fail-closed lease-timeout behavior, concurrent cross-process marker publication, named-launch profiles, partial-delete retry, generation-scoped resume, fallback enumeration, real Chromium host-terminal/layout checks, concurrent clipboard extraction, staged-file ownership, canonical display provenance, and runtime journal recovery.

### Recent browser UX and reliability hardening

- Mobile controls: 44px touch targets for message actions, **Copy**/**More** access, native text selection, and a compact tab picker. Tapping outside the sidebar dismisses it without incidentally focusing the composer.
- Keyboard and media focus: keep the composer visible with visual-viewport fallback and a resize hint; preserve native video/audio controls and prevent queued focus retries from stealing focus after media interaction.
- Ticket and file ownership: carry profile incarnation through tickets and retain the checked ownership boundary through leased, pinned file opens. Profile asset/configuration writes and named-profile mirrors preserve the captured incarnation.
- Private launch containment: on macOS, private auto-open falls back to the operator's manual link instead of putting a bearer in process arguments. Launch-ticket redemption fails closed there; authenticated child-window tickets remain separate.
- Session and platform reliability: harden PTY worker/viewer ownership and reconnect/dead-shell cleanup, roll appearance back to confirmed state without overriding newer peer/profile changes, and correct SQLite lock tracking/read-only inspection and Docker runtime fingerprinting.

## How to Test

1. Build the browser renderer:
   ```bash
   hermes webapp --build-only --force-build
   ```
2. Start locally:
   ```bash
   hermes webapp --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9119
   ```
3. Verify Desktop sessions/files/Git/previews/terminal, create and delete a profile, refresh, and confirm the deleted profile remains absent from `/api/profiles`, Bot roster/routes, and the profile filesystem.
4. Click a website link in Webapp: it should open in a separate browser tab without creating a preview pane. In Electron, a normal click should still open its embedded browser, including when connected to a remote gateway.
5. Explicitly choose **Open in app** from a link context menu to use an embedded preview. Sites that reject embedding should retain the **Open in browser** recovery action.
6. Download a file from a chat attachment, play and seek an inline video/audio attachment, and try **Open video file** for an unsupported format. Missing files should show a download error while keeping the chat open.
7. For remote use, configure dashboard authentication first, then launch with an explicit non-loopback bind.
8. At a narrow/mobile viewport, select message text, use **Copy**/**More**, switch tabs, and dismiss the sidebar by tapping outside it. Sidebar dismissal and video/audio controls should not unexpectedly focus the composer. Open and close the software keyboard and check composer visibility; repeat media interaction while a focus retry is pending.
9. Disconnect/reconnect a running session and terminal, switch profiles, and retry after same-name profile recreation. Stale profile/ticket ownership must fail closed. For private macOS launch, follow the manual-link fallback.

### Verification

#### Current head: `043389d0839d3b33e970d4b52dac9c0fdd1c6e73`

- Since `651a108534`, this head adds the iOS Safari Webapp fixes and the review fixes, with [review replies](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/93508#issuecomment-5988688321):
  - 0fc97b49f7 keeps the composer visible when iOS zooms a focused field.
  - c68d68ffb1 leaves a long-press on message text to the browser.
  - 54651c8cc9 keeps a dismissed keyboard down after Send.
  - c6d8b30c7d fixes two-window appearance settlement (F7/F8).
  - 2b569213e3 has every window still on a profile re-read a raced appearance save, so the fix also holds when the window that saved has switched profile or gateway.
  - 043389d083 adds a 52-case cross-window appearance transport smoke, built on andrexibiza's review fixture (co-authored), and gives both appearance smokes a free port.
  - 8ac8d77a61 lets `--skip-build` work on a read-only install.
  - 76f707aa1b and 2f46c42e71 update two stale tests that would have failed hosted CI.
- The three iOS fixes were verified in iOS 26.5 Safari (Xcode simulator, touch input and the software keyboard) at those commits.
- On this head:
  - Desktop typecheck passed, and eslint reported 0 errors on the changed files.
  - The theme tests passed **269/269**.
  - The full Desktop vitest suite had **14,305 passed and 19 failed**. All 19 also fail at `2f46c42e71`; they are Electron packaging/updater and script tests that need the build environment.
  - In real Chromium on macOS, with a substituted config backend, the new transport smoke passed **52/52** and the two-page appearance smoke passed **28/28**, run concurrently. The review's two-page fixture passed **12/12**.
  - No Python changed after `2f46c42e71`, where the Webapp, dashboard-launch, host-attach, document-policy and export-boundary files gave **62 passed** on Windows 11 and **61 passed with one Windows-only skip** on macOS, with `ruff check` clean.
  - The broader 905-test Python and 1,298-test renderer selections were not rerun on this head.
- Still unverified: physical iPhone/Android keyboards and dictation, native Electron multi-window, WebKit for the appearance races, and native Windows UI. Hosted workflows need maintainer approval before they run; local checks are not green CI.

#### Historical validation

##### Earlier verification at `2f46c42e7143af5746d9535c8c128a3bedc478f3`

prs.title: fix(desktop): keep a bot-hosting non-primary local in the bot relay peer set
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`relayEligibleRoutes()` (from #108111) drops the non-primary local connection whenever Electron identifies one unambiguous remote primary — regardless of whether that "This device" hosts bots. On a laptop whose bots live on the local connection while a remote gateway is primary, the local routes leave the relay peer set, `syncRelayRosters()` then sees a sole connection and pushes `{agents: []}` to the remote gateway, and `message_agent` can no longer reach any local bot (#137618). The exclusion was written for viewer-only laptops (#108088) whose local has no bots at all, and the #108111 review already called for a "no roster agents on it" clause.

The route inventory is identity-only (connectionId/mode/primary/profile), so the renderer cannot distinguish a bot-hosting local from a bot-less one — but Electron already enumerates the Bot Mode title (`bot_title` from `/api/profiles\)) into `profileMetadata` on every roster row, and `buildRegistryProfileRoutes` simply discarded it when projecting routes. This PR projects that title onto local routes as an additive `bot?: true` marker and keys the local exclusion on it: a non-primary local that hosts at least one titled Bot stays in the peer set; a bot-less one is still excluded, so the #108088 spawn/keep-alive fix is preserved. Older shells that never set `bot` keep the current behavior.

## Related Issue

Fixes #137618

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/electron/plugin-profile-routes.ts` — `buildRegistryProfileRoutes` marks a local route with `bot: true` when the enumerated profile carries a non-empty Bot Mode title; `RegistryProfileRouteAgent` accepts the already-present `profileMetadata`.
- `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/relay.ts` — `relayEligibleRoutes` keeps the non-primary local in the peer set when any of its routes is marked `bot`.
- `apps/desktop/src/global.d.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/types.ts` — the additive `bot?: true` field on the route DTO.
- Tests: projection coverage in `electron/plugin-profile-routes.test.ts` (titled → marked, untitled/empty title → not marked, remote titles ignored) and a relay regression in `src/plugins/hermes-bots/relay.test.ts` (remote primary + local with a titled Bot → both gateways poll agents and receive each other's roster rows; the existing bot-less exclusion test still passes unchanged).

## How to Test

1. `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run src/plugins/hermes-bots/relay.test.ts --project ui` — 40 passed (includes the new #137618 regression).
2. `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run electron/plugin-profile-routes.test.ts --project electron` — 22 passed (includes the two new projection tests).
3. `cd apps/desktop && npm run typecheck` — should pass (all four tsc projects).

Manual scenario from the issue (needs two machines): laptop with a titled Bot on "This device" + remote gateway set primary → after this change the remote gateway's `bot_relay/roster.json` lists the local bot again and `message_agent` reaches it; a viewer-only laptop (no titled local profile) is still skipped exactly as before.

prs.title: fix(agent): parse vLLM max_model_len=max_total_tokens output-cap rejection
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

vLLM rejects an oversized `max_tokens` with:

```
max_tokens=393216 cannot be greater than max_model_len=max_total_tokens=262144. Please request fewer output tokens.
```

Nothing in `parse_available_output_tokens_from_error` / `is_output_cap_error` matched this wording, so `_recover_context_length` fell through to the prompt-too-long branch, compressed, retried with the *same* `max_tokens`, got the same 400 and ended in "Cannot compress further".

This PR classifies it as an output-cap error and returns the window (`262144`). `_clamp_output_cap` already subtracts the input estimate, so the retry lands on a cap that fits. The new signal and regex are scoped to `max_total_tokens`, so unrelated validation errors such as `temperature cannot be greater than 2` are not matched.

### Relationship to other open PRs

Not a competitor to #128176 / #129737 (bare `cannot be greater than N` / `max_model_len=N`): their patterns allow an optional `max_model_len=` prefix followed directly by digits, so they do **not** match vLLM's `max_model_len=max_total_tokens=N`. Checked with their regexes against the exact message above. Overlaps with the older #102502 / #102527 on the same issue, which are `CONFLICTING` against current `main`; this one is rebased on `63d0b941` and adds negative-control tests. Happy to fold this into any of them, or rebase on whichever lands first.

## Related Issue

Fixes #102494

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `agent/model_metadata.py`: add the `max_total_tokens` regex to `parse_available_output_tokens_from_error`, and the `("cannot be greater than", "max_total_tokens")` group to `_OUTPUT_CAP_SIGNALS` and `_PARSEABLE_OUTPUT_CAP_SIGNALS`. Folds the `available_tokens` / `available tokens` patterns into one equivalent regex so the file does not grow (file-length ratchet).
- `tests/agent/test_output_cap_parsing.py`: `TestParseVllmMaxTotalTokensOutputCap` (parse, classify, case/wrapper tolerance) plus two negative controls (unrelated `cannot be greater than`, genuine vLLM input overflow).

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_output_cap_parsing.py tests/agent/test_overflow_overhead_aware_tokens.py tests/agent/test_overflow_partial_terminal.py tests/agent/test_model_metadata.py` -> 155 passed.
2. Revert the `agent/model_metadata.py` change: the three positive tests fail, the two negative controls still pass.
3. `python scripts/check` -> 12 checks ok.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide
- [x] Conventional Commits
- [x] I searched for existing PRs (see above)
- [x] Only changes related to this fix
- [ ] Full `pytest tests/ -q` run: **not run**, targeted suites only (4 files above)
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes
- [x] Added tests
- [x] Tested on: macOS (Darwin 25.6, Apple Silicon). Parser tested with the verbatim error string; not run against a live vLLM server.

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] Docs / config / AGENTS.md / tool schemas / cross-platform: N/A

Adds a community catalog entry for **AdWhispr** (`plugin-catalog/adwhispr.yaml`), pinned to https://github.com/adwhispr/adwhispr-hermes-plugin at `80fd0e8fd93fe6207e6e9dd288811be9fe695bc2`. I am the owner and author of that repository.

The plugin connects Hermes to the hosted AdWhispr MCP for competitor ad research (brands verified to be advertising now, longest-running Meta and TikTok ads, Instagram content, Google keyword data), ad cloning (finished images and AI videos, with a free script approval before any credit is charged) and campaign execution on Meta, Google, TikTok, X and ChatGPT Ads. It bundles 24 workflow skills.

## Related Issue

None. New catalog entry.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

- `plugin-catalog/adwhispr.yaml`: new `tier: community` entry, full 40-character SHA pin, image pinned to the same commit.

## How to Test

1. `hermes plugins validate --install-deps <checkout of adwhispr/adwhispr-hermes-plugin at 80fd0e8>` passes (manifest OK, server trust: adwhispr untrusted, security scan: safe, portable plugin). The plugin repo's CI runs this on every push.
2. `hermes plugins install adwhispr/adwhispr-hermes-plugin --no-enable && hermes plugins enable adwhispr`, start a session, and the first AdWhispr tool call opens the browser sign-in (OAuth 2.1 + PKCE, dynamic client registration).
3. Ask "who is advertising in the meal kit space right now?" to exercise a read-only research call.

- **Auth:** pinned `mcp-remote@0.1.49` over npx stdio, the same bridge as the `adspirer` entry. No credentials in the repo; needs Node.js 20.18.1+.

prs.title: fix(agent): parse direct comparison output cap error formats (#128171)
prs.body:
Closes #128171.

## Summary

`parse_available_output_tokens_from_error()` and `is_output_cap_error()` in `agent/model_metadata.py` recognize output-cap phrasings from DashScope, Anthropic, OpenRouter, Azure, and Scaleway, but miss common OpenAI-compatible provider formats where the cap is stated as a direct comparison (such as AgnesAI and vLLM without context window echo).

When an endpoint returns e.g. `max_tokens exceeds the limit of 65536` or `'max_tokens': 65536 is greater than the maximum of 4096 - 'max_tokens'` or `max_tokens cannot be greater than max_model_len=8192`:
1. Neither parser pattern matches (the catch-all tail pattern `=\s*(\d+)\s*$` requires the digits to sit at the very end of the string, which fails on trailing request IDs or parameter references).
2. The gate signals in `_PARSEABLE_OUTPUT_CAP_SIGNALS` and `_OUTPUT_CAP_SIGNALS` reject the messages.
3. As a result, automatic output-cap clamping never triggers; the turn dies as an unhandled context-overflow failure, and the session enters an unnecessary compression and reset loop.

This change:
1. Adds regex patterns for common direct comparison phrasings:
   - `(?:exceeds|exceed)\s+the\s+limit\s+of\s*(\d+)`
   - `(?:is\s+)?greater than the maximum of\s*(\d+)`
   - `cannot be greater than\s*(?:max_model_len\s*=\s*)?(\d+)`
2. Adds corresponding phrase signals to `_OUTPUT_CAP_SIGNALS` and `_PARSEABLE_OUTPUT_CAP_SIGNALS` so both `is_output_cap_error()` and `parse_available_output_tokens_from_error()` recognize these errors properly.

## Verification

- Added 8 test cases in `TestParseDirectComparisonOutputCaps` in `tests/agent/test_output_cap_parsing.py` covering:
  - `max_tokens exceeds the limit of 65536 (request id: ...)`
  - `HTTP 400: max_tokens exceeds the limit of 32768`
  - `max_tokens cannot exceed the limit of 16384`
  - `'max_tokens': 65536 is greater than the maximum of 4096 - 'max_tokens'`
  - `max_tokens is greater than the maximum of 8192`
  - `max_tokens cannot be greater than max_model_len=8192`
  - `max_tokens cannot be greater than max_model_len=8192 (request id: ...)`
  - `max_tokens cannot be greater than 4096`
  - `is_output_cap_error()` classification on each variation.
- Verified fail-before: with the patch reverted, all 4 direct comparison classes fail to parse (`None`) and return `False` for `is_output_cap_error()`.
- Full suite passes: 36 tests passed in `tests/agent/test_output_cap_parsing.py` (0 failures).
- Neighbor suite passes: 110 passed in `tests/agent/test_model_metadata.py`.
- Linter clean: `ruff check agent/model_metadata.py tests/agent/test_output_cap_parsing.py` (0 errors).

prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds `hermes kanban comment <id> --body-file PATH` (`-` reads stdin) so multiline comments do not need to be embedded in a shell argument. UTF-8 BOM files are accepted, matching `create`. The existing database writer still strips surrounding whitespace.

## Related Issue

Part of #137599 — **comment input only**, not a full issue closure.

- Already on main: `create --body-file`.
- Delivered here: file/stdin comment input, invalid-input refusal, preservation of author/max-len and inline invocation behavior.
- Remaining: task body editing from files. #61702 already implements file-backed task-spec amendment; this PR does not compete with that contract. #118638 adds a separate inline `--body` alias for comments, which is not added here.

This is CLI ergonomics, not a command-execution vulnerability claim: ordinary quoted command substitution does not recursively execute backticks from the substituted file.

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature

## Changes Made

- `kanban_parser.py`: optional positional comment text plus file input; comment-only intermixed parsing preserves `comment <id> --author NAME "text"` on Python 3.11.
- `kanban.py`: load file/stdin before writing; reject conflicting sources, empty text, unreadable files and invalid UTF-8. Conversational `/kanban comment` refuses file input before reading, retaining inline comments.
- Behavioral tests drive the real parser, command dispatch and temporary SQLite board. Documentation includes the new CLI form.

## How to Test

`scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_comment_body_file.py -q --file-retries 0`

- Base `63d0b94120027d487c9a5235b9ec64b696af1b26`: real RED, parser refuses `--body-file` (exit 2).
- Focused GREEN on native Windows: **4 passed**. Covers file/BOM, stdin, multiline/backtick/Unicode content, existing inline option order, author and max-len, missing/unreadable/empty/invalid inputs, source conflict, and slash-path refusal with no comments written. Follow-up regressions cover literal `--` delimiters, file-only trailing delimiters, padded bodies before max-len, and refusal of ambiguous `--body`/`--b` abbreviations.
- Wider six-file final-head run: **38 passed, 2 failed, 2 skipped**. Both failures also reproduce on pristine base: dispatcher tests use a Windows `FakeProc` without `poll`. An earlier full-launcher exit-status subprocess timeout also reproduced on base, then passed on subsequent runs; it is recorded as unstable, not silently dismissed. The console-engine suite plus focused tests additionally passed **16 tests**.
- Separate-process real parser/dispatch → SQLite → separate-process readback passed for file, stdin and existing inline comments on `f1015b9eb39241c00c7397638d6ecfd430f32b71`. This exercises Kanban directly, not the full Hermes launcher.
- Ten non-ruff `scripts/check` guards passed. Ruff/code-health checks remain unavailable because the pinned ruff executable is not installed; no dependencies were installed. Full suite not run.
- Final-head verification is complete for the focused scope; the broader baseline failures and unavailable lint checks above remain disclosed. This PR remains Draft.

- [x] Behavioral regression and caller-boundary tests added
- [x] Tested on native Windows
- [x] Relevant documentation updated
- [ ] Full test suite passes (not run)

prs.title: fix(langfuse): close failed api traces
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Failed provider requests can currently be visible in Hermes logs while missing from Langfuse as usable failed traces. The reproduced case is a custom DeepSeek-compatible provider returning HTTP 402 before any streamed response is delivered: `pre_api_request` starts the Langfuse trace/generation, `api_request_error` records the failed attempt, but the terminal billing/error branch returns directly from `agent/conversation_loop.py` and never reaches the normal `agent/turn_finalizer.py` `on_session_end` emission.

This PR makes failed provider calls visible as errored Langfuse generations and ensures terminal API-error returns close the turn trace. The success-path trace flow and existing generation fields are preserved.

Related open PRs: #81874 and #81732 cover adjacent Langfuse failure-marking work. This PR includes the request-error hook wiring needed on current `main` and adds the core-loop lifecycle fix for terminal provider exceptions that skip `finalize_turn`.

## Related Issue

Related to #81731 and the Langfuse failed-observation reports in #81874 / #81732.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)

## Changes Made

- `plugins/observability/langfuse/__init__.py`
  - Add `api_request_error` handling for failed provider calls.
  - End the matching generation with `level="ERROR"` and a redacted `status_message`.
  - Include failure metadata: status code, retry counts, retryability, classifier reason, duration, error type, and safe summary.
  - Flush immediately after ending a failed generation.
- `plugins/observability/langfuse/plugin.yaml`
  - Declare the `api_request_error` hook.
- `agent/conversation_loop.py`
  - Emit `on_session_end` before direct terminal API-error returns so Langfuse can close the root turn trace even when `finalize_turn` is skipped.
- `tests/plugins/test_langfuse_plugin.py`
  - Add hook registration/no-op coverage and regression coverage for failed generations.
- `tests/run_agent/test_run_agent.py`
  - Add a DeepSeek-style HTTP 402 billing regression test asserting `api_request_error` and `on_session_end` share the same `api_request_id`.

## How to Test

1. Automated checks run locally:
   - `python3 -m pytest tests/plugins/test_langfuse_plugin.py tests/run_agent/test_run_agent.py::TestRunConversation::test_terminal_api_error_emits_session_end_hook tests/run_agent/test_31273_402_not_retried.py`
   - Result: `31 passed`
   - `git diff --check origin/main..HEAD`
2. Manual repro path:
   - Enable `observability/langfuse` with valid Langfuse credentials.
   - Configure a custom DeepSeek-compatible provider with a key/account that returns HTTP 402.
   - Send a chat turn. Expected: Hermes still returns the billing error to the caller, and Langfuse receives an errored generation plus a closed root turn trace for that failed request.

prs.title: fix(cli): start dashboard MCP discovery only after the listen socket is bound
prs.body:
## What

`cmd_dashboard` (both `hermes dashboard` and the headless `hermes serve` backend) kicked off background MCP discovery *before* calling `start_server`. Any failed bind — port already held by another dashboard, auth-gate fail-closed exit, anything that dies before uvicorn owns the socket — had therefore already spawned every configured stdio MCP server and opened a session on every HTTP MCP server, then exited without closing any of them.

On its own that's just leaked churn. Under a KeepAlive supervisor (a launchd LaunchAgent, a systemd unit) it becomes a fresh MCP session every `ThrottleInterval` seconds for as long as the bind keeps failing. In the field (companion to #89793) that ran for ~45 h and got a shared `n8n-mcp` container rate-limited (429) for **every** client on the host — Claude Code, Codex, other Hermes profiles — because the limiter keys on source IP.

`start_server` already has an explicit "the socket is now live" point: after `await server.startup()` it reads the bound port and prints the READY sentinel. This PR:

- adds an `on_listening: Optional[Callable[[], None]]` parameter to `start_server`, invoked exactly once on the event loop right after that point (skipped when startup bails via `should_exit`; exceptions are logged and swallowed so a bad hook can't take the server down);
- has `cmd_dashboard` start MCP discovery from that hook instead of up-front. Nothing else about discovery changes — same `start_background_mcp_discovery`, same thread name, still a background thread that can't block startup.

Net effect: a dashboard that never binds never reaches outside the process.

## How to test

Repro (any OS): with `mcp_servers` configured (an HTTP one makes it easy to watch), start one dashboard, then start a second on the same port:

```
hermes dashboard --no-open --skip-build --port 9119 &
hermes dashboard --no-open --skip-build --port 9119   # exits 1: address already in use
```

Before: the second process logs `MCP server '…' registered N tool(s)` / `POST http://…/mcp` in `logs/agent.log` and `starting MCP server` lines in `logs/mcp-stderr.log` before dying. After: exit 1 with zero MCP requests and zero stdio spawns (verified on macOS by diffing counts in both logs across the attempt).

Happy path is unchanged: with a free port the log shows the bind, then `MCP server '…' registered …`.

Tests:
- `tests/test_web_server.py`: hook fires after `startup()` (ordering asserted), is skipped when startup sets `should_exit`, and a raising hook doesn't stop the server.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_dashboard_web_dist_validation.py`: `cmd_dashboard` no longer calls `start_background_mcp_discovery` before/while entering `start_server`, and the `on_listening` it passes is what starts it (thread name `dashboard-mcp-discovery`).

Existing tests that stub `web_server.start_server` with `lambda **k:` are unaffected (new kwarg).

## Platforms

Tested on macOS 26 (Darwin 25.5). No platform-specific code; the hook sits in the shared POSIX/Windows `_serve()` path.

Related: #89793 (launchd-supervised dashboards were being kill+respawned by `hermes update`, which is what turned this into a loop), #44143.

prs.title: fix(cli): kickstart launchd-supervised dashboards on update instead of respawning
prs.body:
## What

`hermes update` (and the Desktop update handoff that runs it) kills every running `hermes dashboard` / `hermes serve` and respawns the ones it can't attribute to a systemd unit from their captured argv (#40449). On macOS a dashboard supervised by a user **LaunchAgent plist** (`KeepAlive`) is invisible to that check, so update SIGTERMs launchd's child *and* spawns a manual, detached duplicate with the same `--port`.

launchd's KeepAlive relaunch then races the duplicate for the port. Whichever loses crash-loops every `ThrottleInterval` seconds forever. On my machine: `runs = 10974`, ~45 h of `[Errno 48] error while attempting to bind on address ('0.0.0.0', 9119)` every 15 s — and because the dashboard starts MCP discovery before it binds, every attempt opened a fresh MCP session on every configured server, which got a shared `n8n-mcp` container rate-limited (429) for every other client on the host.

This PR mirrors the existing systemd handling (#68934) for launchd:

- **`_get_launchd_service_for_pid(pid)`** (darwin-only, in `hermes_cli/main.py` next to the systemd helpers): maps the PID — or an ancestor, for `sh -c … hermes dashboard` wrapper plists — to a label via `launchctl list`, then confirms with `launchctl print gui|user/<uid>/<label>` that the job's `type` is `LaunchAgent`/`LaunchDaemon`. `Submitted` application jobs (Terminal.app, VS Code, Hermes.app — every process started from an app window has one as an ancestor) return `None`, so hand-started dashboards keep today's respawn path.
- **`_try_restart_launchd_service(domain, label)`**: `launchctl kickstart domain/label` after the SIGTERM (no-op if KeepAlive already relaunched it, otherwise starts it now).
- **`_kill_stale_dashboard_processes`**: launchd-owned PIDs are never argv-respawned. Update path → kickstart (deduped per job). `--stop` path → still a plain stop, plus a hint that a KeepAlive job will come back and the `launchctl bootout` to keep it down.

Related: #44143 (Desktop update starts an extra dashboard next to a launchd-managed one — this is the update-side half of that), #44106 (first-class LaunchAgent lifecycle for the dashboard; this makes update safe for the hand-written plists people use today).

## How to test

Repro (macOS):
1. `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.example.hermes-dashboard.plist` running `hermes dashboard --no-open --skip-build --host 0.0.0.0 --port 9119` with `KeepAlive` true, `ThrottleInterval` 15; `launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u) …`.
2. `hermes update` (or from a venv python: `from hermes_cli import main as m; m._kill_stale_dashboard_processes(restart_managed=True)`).
3. Before: `✓ restarted: … hermes dashboard … --port 9119` (a detached duplicate) and then `launchctl print gui/$(id -u)/com.example.hermes-dashboard` shows `runs` climbing every 15 s with `dashboard.launchd.err` full of `Errno 48`.
   After: `✓ restarted launchd job gui/501/com.example.hermes-dashboard`, `lsof -nP -iTCP:9119 -sTCP:LISTEN` shows exactly one listener (launchd's), `runs` stays put.

Tests: `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_update_stale_dashboard.py` — new `TestLaunchdSupervisedBackendRestart` (kickstart / no respawn / dedupe per job / kickstart failure → hint, no duplicate / `--stop` hint) and `TestGetLaunchdServiceForPid` (stubbed `launchctl`/`ps`: direct job PID, shell-wrapped child, app-terminal ancestor → None, unknown PID, missing launchctl). Existing tests stub launchd detection to `None` in the autouse fixture so macOS runners never shell out for fake PIDs.

## Platforms

Tested on macOS 26 (Darwin 25.5). Linux/Windows: helpers are `sys.platform == "darwin"` guarded and return `None` immediately, so the existing systemd / taskkill paths are unchanged.

prs.body: Session-scoped model and reasoning choices survive idle reaping on the desktop/TUI gateway and restarts on the messaging gateway. `config.get key:'model'` reports the session's effective model and provider, including a deferred choice. Persist an explicit session-override marker for accepted session-scoped changes, preserve it on resume, and persist the messaging gateway's reasoning override alongside its existing model override. Global, one-turn and rejected selections do not create a durable session pin. Conversation boundaries clear the corresponding overrides. Existing unpinned Bot Mode rows continue to follow the profile. The current upstream integration carries both reasoning and `yolo` during route repoints and reads the primary session runtime while a temporary voice route is active. Upstream's live-session authority check remains intact: detached session RPCs return 4001 and require resume before they can write either profile or session state. Failed persisted reads/writes retain diagnostic information rather than silently falling through. ## Validation Against upstream `63d0b94120027d487c9a5235b9ec64b696af1b26`, head `5e45bf84076bd3102f839a110117f9699bd31f05`: - 37 behavioral tests pass across persistence, scope guards, lazy/unroutable resume, reasoning commands, voice runtime reads and route repoints. - Two generated-contract tests pass. - All 12 canonical `scripts/check --base upstream/main` checks pass; health reports zero blocking or advisory findings with no new waivers. - Idle reaping/restarts and authority guards are exercised through deterministic tests; no live user profile or provider session was used. The full repository suite was not rerun. ## Folded PRs Three open PRs are folded into this one. Their commits are cherry-picked or salvaged, so authorship is preserved. | PR | Author | Contribution | |---|---|---| | #83503 | @Kyzcreig | gateway `/reasoning` persistence across restarts (landed in full) | | #27504 | @Qwinty | the same gateway fix on an older base. Folded into the #83503 commit as co-author | | #103531 | @BrunoBza | lazy and unroutable-provider resume restores the stored runtime | #105998 (@User0856) targets the same bot-chat reasoning symptom by writing the member profile config. This PR fixes it with the durable row override, so #105998 is superseded. > Automated posting by agentic team with human oversight. ## Infographic

prs.title: fix(desktop): show summary reasoning from message.complete when no streamed reasoning exists
prs.body:
Show the sanitized readable reasoning summary carried by `message.complete` in desktop live chat when no reasoning part streamed. Previously the same turn showed its summary only after history hydration or reload.

Forward the completion summary through the existing event handler and add exactly one reasoning part on either settlement path. Streamed reasoning stays authoritative; missing, invalid and whitespace-only summaries remain absent. The current integration preserves upstream's `responseReused` argument and adds coverage proving reused final text is not duplicated when the fallback summary is attached.

This changes the desktop consumer and its types only. It does not expose encrypted or raw reasoning sidecars or change provider, persistence or gateway event behavior.

## Validation

prs.title: security: guard .hermes.md as project-context instruction file; add protected_instruction_allowlist_dirs
prs.body:
## What

`.hermes.md` / `HERMES.md` is loaded as project context at **priority 1** and has **no write guard**, while every other project-context instruction file does.

The prompt builder enumerates project-context types first-match-wins:

```
# agent/prompt_builder.py (upstream main)
# Project-context types in priority order: the first type with any non-empty file wins, later types are
# shadowed. ...
_CONTEXT_FILE_CANDIDATES = {
    "hermes_md": _hermes_md_candidates,   # .hermes.md / HERMES.md — nearest match walking parents to the git root
    "agents_md": _agents_md_candidates,   # AGENTS.md chain, git root -> cwd
    "claude_md": _claude_md_candidates,   # CLAUDE.md, cwd
    "cursorrules": _cursorrules_candidates,
}
```

So `.hermes.md` **shadows every `AGENTS.md` in the tree** — and `_find_hermes_md` walks parents up to the git root, so a match planted high in the tree wins from anywhere below it.

The write gate protects this set:

```python
# tools/file_tools_write_guards.py (upstream main, line 189)
_PROTECTED_INSTRUCTION_BASENAMES = frozenset({
    "agents.md", "claude.md", "soul.md", ".cursorrules"})
```

`.hermes.md` is in neither that set nor the config globs, nor the immediate-parent `.hermes` rule (which matches a file whose *parent directory* is named `.hermes`, not a file named `.hermes.md`).

## Why it matters

The gate's own rationale is that instruction files are a prompt-injection **persistence** vector, and that basenames match in ANY directory "because project-context instruction files are loaded from cwd trees — an AGENTS.md anywhere the agent might later run from is a live target". `.hermes.md` is exactly such a file, and a *higher*-priority one: it is the single instruction file an injected agent can rewrite with **no approval dialog at all**, from the position that outranks the guarded one.

## Repro

In a project directory:

```
cp AGENTS.md .hermes.md      # no approval prompt
# a subsequent targeted patch on .hermes.md -> no approval prompt
# the same writes against AGENTS.md prompt every time
```

Measured 2026-10-12 against a fork checkout of upstream main.

## The change

1. **Add `.hermes.md` and `hermes.md` to `_PROTECTED_INSTRUCTION_BASENAMES`.** Both spellings, because `_find_hermes_md` probes both; matching is case-insensitive, so this covers the loader exactly.

2. **Implement `security.protected_instruction_allowlist_dirs`** — an operator-declared list of absolute directory prefixes whose whole subtree is exempt from the gate, checked BEFORE the basename match.

Part 2 rides with part 1 because closing the guard also closes the only dialog-free path operators have for project instruction files. The exemption is the supported way to keep one: it is config-only (`config.yaml` is hard-blocked from agent writes, so an exemption is always a human declaration, never a self-grant), it is `realpath`'d on **both** sides so a symlinked directory or a symlinked target cannot evade it, it matches on a path boundary (`/work` does not exempt `/workshop`), and the gate stays ON everywhere else.

```yaml
security:
  protected_instruction_files: true
  protected_instruction_extra_patterns: []
  protected_instruction_allowlist_dirs: []   # e.g. ["/opt/sandbox"]
```

## Tests

`tests/tools/test_file_write_safety.py` + `tests/tools/test_protected_instruction_cli_channel.py`.

Two-arm run on the pushed tip, same invocation both arms:

```
BASE (unmodified):  1 failed, 73 passed, 6 skipped
GREEN (this branch): 1 failed, 85 passed, 6 skipped
```

The one failure is identical in both arms and is an artifact of running the suite inside a git worktree of a live install (the test resolves a real hermes-home path); it is unrelated to this change.

The added tests cover: `.hermes.md`/`HERMES.md` now prompt on every protected-name path shape (deny / once / yolo / case-variant / traversal / multi-file patch); the allowlist exempts each protected basename inside the declared tree; the gate stays on outside it; a symlinked allowlist entry still matches; a sibling prefix (`/work` vs `/workshop`) is not exempt; and the real config reader surfaces the key end-to-end.

prs.title: fix(state): reap orphan message rows and merge both FTS5 indexes in state.db auto-maintenance
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`messages.session_id` references `sessions(id)` and the schema declares no `ON DELETE CASCADE`, so a session row removed while foreign-key enforcement was OFF (a legacy importer, an older writer that never issued `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON`, a bulk cleanup) strands that session's whole transcript in `messages` **and in both FTS5 shadow indexes** (`messages_fts` + `messages_fts_trigram`) forever. The session-level retention policy can never age it out: it deletes sessions, and there is no session left to grow old.

The trigram index leaks hardest. `messages_fts_trigram_delete`'s `WHEN` clause requires the message's session row to still exist — exactly false for an orphan — so it never fires and the orphan's segments stay in the trigram index permanently. The FTS merge only ever ran inside `vacuum()`, which the freelist-ratio gate skips precisely on a dense store: the one case where the merge is the only reclaim available.

This PR makes the standing state.db auto-maintenance own both gaps:

- **`SessionMaintenanceMixin.reap_orphan_messages()`** — deletes `messages` rows whose `session_id` names no session, purging the trigram index **explicitly** (the FTS5 `'delete'` command, bounded to the rows the index actually holds via `messages_fts_trigram_docsize`) before the `DELETE` fires the standard `messages_fts` trigger. A store with no trigram index (older CJK-less store) is handled: the purge is skipped and the reap still runs.
- **`maybe_auto_prune_and_vacuum()`** — after pruning, it reaps orphan messages (before the merge, so the merged index does not carry their segments) and merges **both** FTS5 indexes on every run, independent of the VACUUM gates. Reaped rows count toward the VACUUM admission.
- **`_record_state_db_maintenance()`** — one row per run, in `state_meta['last_state_db_maintenance']` (cheap to read back) and appended to `<home>/logs/state-db-maintenance.jsonl` (per-run history): the counters the run produced plus the store geometry after it. Never raises — a bookkeeping failure must not fail maintenance.

## Related Issue

No issue filed; found while investigating the unbounded growth of a long-lived production `state.db` (the trigram index alone held ~42 % of the file, and nothing ever reaped the orphan rows feeding it).

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_state_maintenance.py` — add `reap_orphan_messages()`; wire the orphan reap + `optimize_fts()` into `maybe_auto_prune_and_vacuum()`; add `_record_state_db_maintenance()`; document the new result keys on the method.
- `tests/hermes_state/test_state_db_reap_orphans_fts_optimize.py` (new) — 3 tests: orphans are reaped while a live session's rows are spared (both FTS indexes drop the orphans, and the no-op reap returns 0), both indexes are optimized even when `vacuum=False`, and one recorded row per run that agrees with the jsonl history line.
- `tests/hermes_state/test_startup_maintenance_lease.py` — lease-renewal count 4 → 6: the two new long steps renew the armed watchdog lease.

## How to Test

1. `pytest tests/hermes_state/test_state_db_reap_orphans_fts_optimize.py tests/hermes_state/test_startup_maintenance_lease.py -q` — all pass.
2. Reproduce the leak pre-fix: the three new tests are red on the base commit (`reap_orphan_messages` does not exist, no `fts_indexes_optimized` key, no `last_state_db_maintenance` row). The orphan test builds the orphan the only way one can be born on a store that enforces foreign keys — with `PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF` — and proves both FTS indexes drop the rows.
3. On a real store, one `maybe_auto_prune_and_vacuum()` run with the fix records `state_meta['last_state_db_maintenance']` and appends a matching `logs/state-db-maintenance.jsonl` line; `fts_indexes_optimized` is ≥ 2 even when the run declines to VACUUM.

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate (none found for orphan reaping or FTS optimize in `state.db` maintenance)
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)

prs.title: fix(approvals): `hermes approvals test` must see a pattern-key standing approval
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`hermes approvals test` renders a false `ask-approval` for a command the runtime would
auto-approve, whenever the standing approval is expressed as a PATTERN KEY.

Step 6 of the dry-run tester (`hermes_cli/approvals_test.py`) decided "permanently
approved" with `approval_floors._command_matches_permanent_allowlist(command)`, which
compares the command TEXT or a shell-style glob. The runtime gate consents by PATTERN KEY:
`approval._is_permanently_approved(pattern_key)` under cron/-q deny mode and
`approval.is_approved(session_key, pattern_key)` in the human gate. Every `[a]lways`
choice persists a key, and the entries already in `~/.hermes/config.yaml` are keys — so the
CLI reports `ask-approval` for a standing approval the runtime honours.

Why it matters: this CLI is the surface an operator or a lane uses to CHECK whether a
standing approval is in effect. A false `ask-approval` reads as "the approval you granted is
not working", which pushes the reader toward re-granting it, widening it, or routing around
the guard — the exact failure mode the approval layer exists to prevent.

The fix is the shape the issue describes: step 6 detects the pattern first (the same
`detect_dangerous_command` call step 7 already made) and reports allow when the command's
key is permanently approved, keeping the existing text/glob check for manual entries. The
evaluation ORDER is unchanged.

## Related Issue

No upstream issue exists for this: it was measured on a live install and is reported here
with the full repro in "How to Test". The defect and its proof are self-contained in this
PR.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/approvals_test.py` — step 6 now consults the pattern-key set
  (`approval._is_permanently_approved(pattern_key)`) as well as the text/glob allowlist;
  `detect_dangerous_command` is hoisted to step 6 and reused by step 7. Module docstring
  updated to match.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_approvals_test.py` — new `TestPermanentAllowlistConsentKinds`
  class (5 rows) covering BOTH entry kinds.

## How to Test

Repro on `main`, fresh processes, both `HERMES_HOME` settings:

```
command_allowlist: []                       -> runtime _is_permanently_approved(key)=false
                                               runtime is_approved(session,key)=false
                                               approvals_test helper           =false
command_allowlist: [<the pattern key>]      -> runtime _is_permanently_approved(key)=TRUE
                                               runtime is_approved(session,key)=TRUE
                                               approvals_test helper           =false   <-- stale
```

`approvals-test-matrix.json` is byte-identical with and without the key present.

Worked example (`git push --force-with-lease origin <own-branch>`, pattern key
`git force push (rewrites remote history)`) — parity probe over BOTH runtime predicates:

| allowlist | runtime human gate allows | runtime cron deny-mode allows | CLI verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `[]` | false | false | ask-approval |
| `[<pattern key>]` | true | true | **allow** (was `ask-approval`) |
| `[recursive delete]` | false | false | ask-approval |
| `[podman *]` | true (text/glob floor) | true | allow |

1. `hermes approvals test -- <command>` with the command's pattern key in
   `command_allowlist` now prints `allow` (exit 0) instead of `ask-approval` (exit 2).
2. A manual `podman *`-style glob entry still allows a matching command.
3. A key for a DIFFERENT pattern, and a glob that does not match, still report
   `ask-approval`.

Tests: the key row is red on the base (`1 failed / 19 passed`) and green after
(`20 passed`). The 9-file approval suite shows an identical 27-failure set before and
after (all 27 pre-existing in this environment), 293 passed after vs 288 before.
