prs.title: fix(artifacts): let zoomed image, SVG and Mermaid previews pan to every edge
prs.body:
## Problem

User report: after zooming an image in the preview panel (e.g. to 160%), the left part of the image can no longer be reached.

The image, SVG and Mermaid renderers all zoomed with `transform: scale()` and a center origin inside an `overflow-auto` container. A transform does not extend the scrollable area to the left or top, so that part of the content could never be scrolled into view. At 300%, a wide image lost 584px on the left and 226px at the top; a tall image lost 1651px at the top. The zoom badge also lived inside the scroller, so it scrolled away with the content.

## Changes

- New `renderers/zoomPan.ts` (pure sizing and anchor math, with unit tests) and `renderers/ZoomPanViewport.tsx` (`useZoomPan`, `useInjectedSvgSize`, the viewport and the reset badge), shared by the three renderers.
- Zoom changes the content's layout size (fit width × scale), and the content is centered with auto margins. Oversized content overflows only to the right and bottom, where it can be scrolled to.
- Ctrl/Cmd + wheel and trackpad pinch zoom around the pointer. Each step is multiplicative (about 10% per wheel notch). The Mermaid +/− buttons zoom around the viewport center.
- When content overflows the panel, it can be dragged with the mouse (grab cursor). Presses on the scrollbars are left to the browser.
- The zoom badge and Mermaid controls are pinned over the viewport instead of scrolling with the content.
- `ArtifactRenderer` keys the three renderers by `artifact.id`. Switching to another artifact opens it at 100%; refreshing or saving the same artifact keeps the zoom. This also clears the old sticky "Failed to load image" state when switching images.
- The 100% layout is unchanged: fit to the panel width, never upscale small images, tall content scrolls vertically. The viewport reserves the scrollbar gutter (`scrollbar-gutter: stable`) so the computed fit width cannot oscillate as the scrollbar appears and disappears. As a result, the fit width is 6px narrower.
- SVGs with declared width/height (including pt units from Graphviz) now keep their aspect ratio. Before, a 1200×800 SVG was squeezed into a 600×800 box.

No IPC, storage, runtime or OpenClaw changes. Renderer-only.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run src/renderer/components/artifacts src/renderer/components/library`: 51 files and 558 tests pass, including 19 new tests in `zoomPan.test.ts`.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` and ESLint (CI rules) on all touched files pass.
- Standalone renderer harness in headless Chromium, comparing old and new components across 10 content types (wide, tall, small and huge images, five SVG variants, Mermaid) zoomed to about 300%. The old version left unreachable content in 9 of 10 cases; the new version reaches all four edges in every case.
- Same harness, with real input:
  - Ctrl+wheel keeps the point under the pointer fixed.
  - A drag of (-100, -100) scrolls by exactly (100, 100).
  - Zooming out to 10%, the reset badge and resizing the panel while zoomed all behave correctly, with no console errors.
  - Switching artifacts while zoomed goes back to 100% and scroll (0, 0); a same-id refresh keeps the zoom with no stretched frames.
- Manually tested in `npm run electron:dev` by the reporter's team.

## Screenshots

Before/after at 160%, scrolled fully to the left: before, the left 164px (the TL/BL corners) cannot be reached; after, the left edge is fully visible. (Comparison image to be attached.)

prs.title: feat(agent): polish agent header and add double-click task rename
prs.body:
## Summary
Three UI changes to the agent and sidebar surfaces:

1. **Remove the legacy emoji avatar path.** Since 2026.5.9 every stored agent icon is normalized to a designed SVG avatar at startup and on write, so the emoji/text rendering branch is no longer reachable. This removes it end to end.
2. **Agent header polish.** The name and description fields in agent create/settings are ghost inputs (plain text at rest, a pill on hover, a focus ring while editing), and the avatar picker shows an edit badge. The working directory chip in the prompt input uses a line folder icon drawn on the same grid as the agent avatars.
3. **Double-click a task title to rename it** in the sidebar.

## Changes Made
**Legacy avatar removal**
- `src/shared/agent/avatar.ts`: drop `isDesignedAgentAvatarIcon` and the `agent-avatar:` legacy-format branch in `parseAgentAvatarIcon`.
- `src/renderer/components/agent/AgentAvatarIcon.tsx`: always render an SVG avatar. Unparseable values fall back to `DefaultAgentAvatar`. Removes the `legacyClassName`, `fallbackText` and `useDefaultWhenEmpty` props and adds `inheritColor` (tint with the parent's text color, used by the prompt input agent chip).
- Call sites updated: `AgentsView`, `AgentCreateModal`, `AgentSettingsPanel`, `AgentAvatarPicker`, `AgentTreeNode`, `SubagentSpawnCard`, `CoworkPromptInput` (which also drops its `DefaultAgentIcon` special case).
- `src/main/libs/openclawAgentModels.ts`: `buildAgentEntry` no longer writes `identity.emoji`. It writes `identity: { name }` only when the agent has a name.

**Agent header**
- New `src/renderer/components/agent/agentHeaderStyles.ts`: shared class names for the header layout and ghost inputs (`field-sizing: content`), used by `AgentCreateModal` and `AgentSettingsPanel`.
- `AgentAvatarPicker`: always-visible pencil badge, `aria-expanded`, `focus-visible` ring.
- New `src/renderer/components/icons/WorkingDirectoryIcon.tsx`, replacing the solid heroicons `FolderIcon` in `CoworkPromptInput`.

**Double-click rename**
- `src/renderer/components/agentSidebar/AgentTaskRow.tsx`: double-clicking the title opens the rename editor and reports `task_rename_double_click`. Only the first click of a double click selects the task, so it does not open twice. In batch mode, clicks still toggle selection and double-click does nothing. The menu's Rename and the double click share `startRename`.
- `specs/features/usage-analytics/2026-06-22-usage-analytics-design.md`: documents the new `task_rename_double_click` action.

## Electron-specific behavior
- **OpenClaw config:** agent entries in `openclaw.json` no longer carry `identity.emoji`. Since 2026.5.9 stored icons are normalized to SVG values, which were already skipped here, so the generated config should be unchanged for current data.
- No IPC, storage schema, preload or windowing changes.

## Visible behavior changes
- `SubagentSpawnCard` and the picker grid used to render nothing or a text fallback for an empty icon. They now show the default avatar.
- The sidebar agent row and the prompt input agent chip no longer fall back to the first letter of the agent name.

## Type of Change
- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [x] Code refactoring
- [x] Documentation update
- [ ] Performance improvement
- [ ] Other (please describe):

## Testing
- [x] Tested locally
- [ ] Added new tests
- [x] Updated existing tests
- [ ] Manual testing performed

- `src/shared/agent/avatar.test.ts`: updated for the removed export, and adds cases showing that `🤖` normalizes to the default avatar and that a 2-part `agent-avatar:` value is rejected.
- `npm test`: 607 files passed, 18 skipped (6532 tests passed, 154 skipped).
- `npm run compile:electron` and `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`: clean.
- ESLint with CI rules (`--max-warnings 0`) on the 13 touched TS/TSX files: clean.
- No remaining references to `isDesignedAgentAvatarIcon`, `legacyClassName` or `LegacyAgentAvatarIconFormat`.

Not yet manually verified in the app: the double-click rename (including batch mode), the ghost input hover/focus states, and the avatar picker badge. Screenshots to follow.

issues.title: Web turns on a channel-bound session are delivered to the channel, bypassing the account's chat access policy (and without any web UI warning)
issues.body:
### Summary
When a non-gateway turn (web UI / cron / webhook / `sessions_send`) runs on a **channel-bound** session, Moltis downgrades it to public context (no tools / no private context — intended) **and also delivers the reply to that channel chat**. Two problems:

1. **Access-policy bypass:** delivery happens even when the target chat is *not* permitted by the account's policy (e.g. `group_policy = "allowlist"` with the group absent from `group_allowlist`). The allowlist gates inbound, but not this outbound path.
2. **No warning in the web UI:** a bound channel session looks like an ordinary private chat; nothing indicates that whatever you type will be posted to the real chat.

### Environment
- Moltis `20260913.02` (`org.opencontainers.image.revision=6aa48819a77856e73d53021b5fa591f93798a88d`)
- Self-hosted Docker container
- Channel account: `<channel_type>=<account_id>` (e.g. `whatsapp:<account>`), `dm_policy="disabled"`, `group_policy="allowlist"`, `group_allowlist=["<other-group>@g.us"]`
- Affected session: `<channel_type>:<account_id>:<group-chat-id>` — a group **not** in the allowlist

### Steps to reproduce
1. Have a group chat that has an existing bot session (e.g. from earlier interaction) and ensure that group is **not** in `group_allowlist`.
2. In the web UI, open that chat's session (URL like `/chats/<channel_type>/<account_id>/<chat_id>`).
3. Type any message and send.
4. Observe the assistant's reply is **delivered to the group**, and the run had `tools_count: 0`.

### Expected
- A turn into a chat the account policy forbids should not deliver to that chat (or at minimum be blocked/warned).
- The web UI should clearly indicate the session is channel-bound and where the reply will be sent.

### Actual
- Reply delivered to the non-allowlisted group; no warning; privacy leak (sensitive personal content posted to a group chat).

### Evidence
Log (`session=<channel_type>:<account_id>:<group-chat-id>`, web-originated, `client_seq=Some(n)`):

```
moltis_chat::service::chat_impl::channel_security:
  "session is bound to a channel; running this turn without tools or private context. Clear the binding to restore full access."
moltis_agents::runner::streaming: "starting streaming agent loop ... tools_count:0"
```

Stored user message metadata: `channel: { sender_id: "web", private_context: false }`.

(The assistant reply was then persisted and delivered to the chat.)

### Root cause
- `crates/chat/src/service/chat_impl/channel_security.rs` → `apply_channel_bound_public_context()`:
  - applies the public ceiling via `apply_public_context_ceiling()` (sets `_tool_audience="public"`, `_tool_policy.deny=["*"]`, `channel.private_context=false`), and
  - when the session is the active session for the chat, sets `params["_channel_reply_target"] = target`, which causes `crates/chat/src/channels.rs` → `deliver_channel_replies()` to send the reply to the chat via `ChannelOutbound`.
- The outbound send (`crates/<channel>/src/outbound.rs`; `deliver_reply_to_target` in `crates/chat/src/channels.rs`) performs **no account/chat access-policy check**.

Related minor issue: `deliver_channel_replies_inner()` derives `is_channel_session` from only `telegram:`/`msteams:`/`discord:` prefixes, so deliveries for other channels aren't logged at INFO — making this class of delivery invisible in logs.

### Suggested fixes
- **Gate outbound delivery on the account/chat access policy**: skip (or refuse/warn) delivery to a chat that `group_policy`/`group_allowlist` (or the DM equivalent) disallows.
- **Web UI**: show a prominent indicator/banner on channel-bound sessions ("Replies will be sent to this chat") and/or require confirmation before sending.
- Include the remaining channel prefixes in `is_channel_session` delivery logging for observability.

### Notes
- The binding is intentional and durable ("a chat's own session cannot be released"). Clearing it via `sessions.patch { channelBinding: null }` (or the DB) stops the delivery.
- Observed accidentally twice on the same group.

prs.title: Chat ↔ sub-agent parity: persona, system_prompt_suffix, delegate_only, preset model
prs.body:
## Summary

Today several preset fields only affect `spawn_agent` sub-runs, not direct chat with the same agent. This makes coordinator/worker setups and “talk to the agent as itself” diverge.

This PR aligns the two paths:

1. **Sub-agent persona** — `build_sub_agent_prompt` loads the target workspace `IDENTITY.md` / `SOUL.md` / `AGENTS.md` / `GUIDELINES.md` so a spawned agent gets the same written persona as direct chat.
2. **`system_prompt_suffix`** — appended in live chat turns, `raw_prompt`, and `full_context` (same Role / composite suffix content as spawn).
3. **`delegate_only`** — direct chat uses the same shared delegate toolset as spawn (`DELEGATE_ONLY_TOOLS`).
4. **Model resolve** — chat model order becomes explicit → session → **preset** → default / history, so a preset `model` is a real default when the session has none.

Docs comments on the preset schema note that suffix / `delegate_only` apply to chat and sub-agents.

**Base pin:** `1f6d28ea750d6654d52d5899b8be67727ebf7a19` (rebase onto latest `main` before merge). May also need [#1280](https://github.com/moltis-org/moltis/pull/1280) if that change is not already in the base (touches `spawn_agent` tool wiring). Independent of the follow-up `spawn.allow` PR.

**Compatibility:** additive for existing configs. No new required fields. Presets without suffix / `delegate_only` / `model` behave as before.

## Test plan

- [ ] `cargo test -p moltis-tools` — workspace persona injection in spawn (`test_workspace_persona_injected_*`)
- [ ] `cargo test -p moltis-chat` — `append_preset_system_prompt_suffix_*`, `resolve_chat_model_id_*`, `delegate_only_keeps_shared_delegate_toolset`
- [ ] Manual: agent with non-empty `system_prompt_suffix` → `chat.raw_prompt` / reply reflects it
- [ ] Manual: `delegate_only = true` → tool list matches spawn delegate set
- [ ] Manual: session without model, preset with model → chat uses preset model

prs.title: Preset spawn.allow: allowlist for spawn_agent targets
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds optional `agents.presets.<id>.spawn.allow` so a caller can only `spawn_agent` into listed presets (org-chart / coordinator graphs). Enforcement is in `resolve_preset` before provider work; the tool schema / description lists only allowed targets for the calling agent.

**Depends on:** [#1301](https://github.com/moltis-org/moltis/pull/1301) (chat ↔ sub-agent parity / patch `0002`) — **required**. This branch is stacked on that PR. Also [#1280](https://github.com/moltis-org/moltis/pull/1280) if that is still unmerged on the target base.

**Base pin:** `1f6d28ea750d6654d52d5899b8be67727ebf7a19` **with #1301 already applied**. Do not review against bare pin without parity — the hunks expect parity helpers and related `spawn_agent` / chat context changes.

**Compatibility (important):**

| `spawn.allow` value | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| **Absent / `None`** | **Unrestricted** (legacy default — existing configs unchanged) |
| `Some([])` / empty list | Deny all spawn targets |
| Non-empty `Some([…])` | Allowlist only those preset ids |

RPC: `agents.preset.update` accepts `spawn_allow` (`null` clears to unrestricted); `preset.get` exposes `fields.spawn_allow`. Markdown agent defs: YAML frontmatter `spawn_allow` (CSV; empty string = deny all). Docs: `docs/src/session-tools.md`.

## Test plan

- [ ] `cargo test -p moltis-tools` — `test_resolve_preset_rejects_target_outside_spawn_allow`, `test_resolve_preset_empty_spawn_allow_rejects_all`, `test_resolve_preset_absent_spawn_allow_unrestricted`, `test_spawn_allow_bound_schema_*`, `test_execute_rejects_disallowed_preset_before_provider`
- [ ] `cargo test -p moltis-config` — schema / agent_defs round-trip for `spawn_allow` (incl. empty list vs absent)
- [ ] Manual: caller with `spawn.allow = ["writer"]` → spawn `writer` ok, other preset → visible `spawn_agent denied`
- [ ] Manual: field absent → any known preset still spawnable (unrestricted)

issues.title: [Bug]: Hub restart leaves desired-running Local runtimes stopped and silently skips cron jobs
issues.body:
## Summary

Hub with the Local process provisioner does not restore desired-running user runtimes after the Hub process restarts. Enabled cron jobs inside those runtimes silently miss their scheduled executions until an authenticated request starts the runtime again.

The Hub can be healthy and reachable while the user runtime, its channel connections and its cron scheduler are not running.

## Environment and verification scope

- Observed on QwenPaw 2.2.0, Linux, Hub with Local runtimes.
- Also inspected v2.2.1, v2.2.2-beta.4, and main at 753cb6dc4f1b7440dcd2d3869360d2a5677bd168: no startup restoration of desired-running user runtimes was found. These newer versions were inspected statically, not reproduced in production.
- Runtime desired state is running; cron jobs are enabled with an explicit timezone.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start Hub and a user's Local runtime.
2. Create an enabled recurring cron job scheduled a few minutes ahead; confirm its next execution time.
3. Restart the Hub process before the scheduled time.
4. Do not open that user's chat or make an authenticated request through the personal runtime proxy.
5. Wait past the scheduled time.
6. Open the user's chat / access the personal runtime API.

## Actual behavior

- The Local runtime does not restart with Hub, so its cron scheduler never triggers the job.
- Accessing the user's personal runtime starts it later.
- The scheduler registers the next future execution; the missed recurring job is not automatically replayed.
- An enabled task and a healthy Hub do not indicate that its execution runtime is actually running.

In the affected deployment, all three enabled daily jobs missed execution after a Hub restart. They had triggered the previous day, and their schedule configurations had not changed.

## Expected behavior

On Hub startup, reconcile runtimes whose persisted desired_state is running and restore their execution processes without requiring user traffic. Explicitly stopped or administrator-disabled runtimes should remain stopped.

Recovery should use existing lifecycle locking, capacity checks and provisioner operations; leave healthy runtimes alone; and isolate failures so one tenant does not block recovery of other tenants. Failed recovery should remain visible to administrators.

Missed-job notification / replay policy would be a separate improvement. Increasing misfire_grace_seconds alone cannot help when the runtime itself is not running.

## Relevant code

- src/qwenpaw/hub/control_app.py: the application lifespan has no desired-running runtime restoration. ensure_personal_runtime() starts a stopped runtime on request.
- src/qwenpaw/hub/service.py: close() closes provisioners and records stopped observed states.
- src/qwenpaw/hub/local_provisioner.py: close() terminates the child processes it owns.
- src/qwenpaw/app/crons/manager.py: startup loads job specs and registers a fresh process-local scheduler.

Source inspected: https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/blob/753cb6dc4f1b7440dcd2d3869360d2a5677bd168/src/qwenpaw/hub/control_app.py

## Local mitigation tested

We added desired-running runtime restoration to the Hub lifespan using the existing lifecycle service. Local tests cover stopped vs. desired-running runtimes, healthy-runtime idempotency, an administrator stop during recovery, and one failed tenant not blocking another.

After deploying that mitigation and performing a controlled Hub restart, both desired-running Local runtimes started automatically before any personal-runtime API request. The affected agent's channels and all three enabled cron schedules were restored; the disabled job remained disabled and all job configurations were unchanged.

issues.title: Feature: Add i18n support for protected execution contract prompt
issues.body:
## Background

QwenPaw already has an i18n mechanism for the scroll context management prompt (`SCROLL_SYSTEM_PROMPT_TEMPLATES` dict with `"zh"` and `"en"` keys in `agents/context/scroll/prompt.py`, selected via the `language` field in agent config). This works well — when `language: zh` is set, the scroll system prompt (retrieval headline, recall_history, context map, etc.) is correctly rendered in Chinese.

## Problem

The **protected execution contract** (`runtime/protected_prompt.py` → `PROTECTED_EXECUTION_CONTRACT_PROMPT`) is hardcoded in English only. It's injected via `ProtectedExecutionContractContributor` in `runtime/prompt_contributors.py` without any language parameter.

This means even when `language: zh` is configured, the agent's system prompt contains a mix of:
- ✅ Chinese: scroll prompt (headline/recall/map/discipline), AGENTS.md/SOUL.md/PROFILE.md
- ❌ English: protected execution contract (Match the request / Clarify before acting / Stay within authorization / Untrusted content / Finishing the job / Tool-use enforcement)

Other sections like the framework info block (About/GitHub/OS/Working directory) and agent-skills description are also English-only, but the protected execution contract is the most impactful one since it defines core behavioral constraints.

## Proposal

Extend the existing i18n pattern to `protected_prompt.py`:

1. Add `PROTECTED_EXECUTION_CONTRACT_PROMPT_ZH` (and other languages as needed)
2. Add a `PROTECTED_EXECUTION_CONTRACT_TEMPLATES` dict similar to `SCROLL_SYSTEM_PROMPT_TEMPLATES`
3. Update `ProtectedExecutionContractContributor.contribute_sync()` to accept and use the `language` parameter from agent config

This would be a natural extension of the i18n infrastructure already in place for scroll prompts, and would give non-English users a fully localized system prompt experience.

## Environment

- QwenPaw deployed via platform.agentscope.io
- `language: zh` set in agent config
- Observed English protected execution contract in system prompt despite Chinese language setting

issues.title: [Bug]: qwenpaw-creator - Project deletion always fails on Windows once the project's own log file has been written (WinError 5 renaming the project directory that contains an open creator.log)
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.2.1 (Windows), plugin `qwenpaw-creator` **v2.0.1**

- **OS:** Windows Server 2022 (10.0.20348), Python 3.12 (uv-managed CPython)
- **Install method:** QwenPaw installed under the user profile (`C:\Users\<user>\.qwenpaw\...`), plugin from the QwenPaw app store
- **Note:** `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\FileSystem\LongPathsEnabled = 1` on this machine, so this report is **not** the MAX_PATH issue of #8163.

## Description

On Windows, deleting a Creator project **always fails** once anything has written to that project's own log file:

```
DELETE /api/qwenpaw-creator/projects/<project-id>  →  HTTP 503 STORAGE_INTEGRITY_ERROR
ProjectStoreError: Cannot delete Project: <project-id>
```

Cause: the plugin routes log records into a **per-project** log file that lives **inside the project directory**:

```
<data-root>/project-<id>/observability/logs/creator.log
```

`utils/logger.py::_CreatorRoutingFileHandler` keeps one `_SecureTimedRotatingFileHandler(..., delay=False)` **per project, open for the lifetime of the process** (it is only released by `close_creator_project_logging(project_id)`).

Project deletion starts by atomically renaming the whole project directory onto a tombstone path:

```python
# services/project_files/store.py::ProjectStore.delete()  (lines 546-556)
tombstone = self.root / f".deleted-{safe_id}-{uuid4().hex}"
try:
    atomic_replace_path(project_root, tombstone)   # line 553 → atomic_store.py:125 → os.replace
    _fsync_directory(self.root)
except OSError as exc:
    raise ProjectStoreError(f"Cannot delete Project: {safe_id}") from exc   # line 556
```

**Windows refuses to rename a directory that contains an open file**, so the rename fails with `PermissionError: [WinError 5] Access is denied` and deletion is impossible for that project.

The ordering in the API makes this unrecoverable inside a process:

```python
# api/project_routes.py::delete_project()
await asyncio.to_thread(services.projects.delete, project_id, cascade=cascade)   # line 590  → fails here
...
services.poller.close(project_id)                                # line 599  (never reached on failure)
close_creator_project_logging(project_id)                        # line 602  (never reached on failure)
```

The handler that pins the directory is released **after** the rename that needs it released — and on failure the code raises before reaching it. So as soon as a project has produced one project-scoped log record (opening the project / its detail page / polling is enough), that project can never be deleted again in that process, no matter how often the user retries. `atomic_replace_path` already retries `PermissionError` 50 × 20 ms on Windows, so this is not a transient lock.

**Workaround that actually works** (verified by the reporter, after 4 failed attempts):

1. Restart the **QwenPaw process** (not just re-open the Creator app — re-entering the app while the old process is still serving does nothing, the handle is still held).
2. Re-enter the Creator app so the plugin's file runtime initializes.
3. Delete the project(s) **from the list, without opening the project first** (opening it re-creates that project's log handler).

**Related PR(s):** none. (#8163 / PR #8167 addressed a different Windows defect — the Review decision journal publish on long paths — this is an independent file-handle/lifetime defect.)

**Security considerations:** none. Local file-handle lifetime only; no auth, config or network surface.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

(Plugin `qwenpaw-creator`: `backend/services/project_files/store.py`, `backend/api/project_routes.py`, `backend/utils/logger.py`)

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.2.1
- **Plugin version:** qwenpaw-creator 2.0.1
- **OS:** Windows Server 2022, 10.0.20348
- **Install method:** per-user install under `C:\Users\<user>\.qwenpaw` + plugin from the app store
- **Python version:** 3.12

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On Windows, create a Creator project.
2. Open the project (or just view its detail page) so at least one record is written to `project-<id>/observability/logs/creator.log`.
3. Try to delete the project from the project list.

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** the request fails with 503 `STORAGE_INTEGRITY_ERROR` / `Cannot delete Project: <id>`. Every retry fails identically. The project can never be deleted until the QwenPaw process is restarted (and the project is not touched again before the delete).
  Observed on 4 consecutive attempts in the same process (timestamps from `qwenpaw.log`, 2026-10-13): `10:03:52`, `10:04:03`, `10:40:46`, `10:40:52` — all `status=503 code=STORAGE_INTEGRITY_ERROR method=DELETE`.
- **Expected:** the project is deleted, or at minimum the API reports a non-retryable, actionable error. Deletion must not depend on whether the project's log has ever been written.

## Logs / Screenshots

`project-<id>/observability/logs/creator.log` (the project-level log, written by the very handler that blocks the rename):

```
2026-10-13 10:04:03 | ERROR | qwenpaw.creator.api.errors | dependencies.py:185 | Creator request failed
  ... status=503 code=STORAGE_INTEGRITY_ERROR method=DELETE
  path=/api/qwenpaw-creator/projects/<project-id> details={}
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../plugins/qwenpaw-creator/backend/services/project_files/store.py", line 553, in delete
    atomic_replace_path(project_root, tombstone)
  File ".../plugins/qwenpaw-creator/backend/services/runtime_files/atomic_store.py", line 125, in atomic_replace_path
    os.replace(source, target)
PermissionError: [WinError 5] 拒绝访问。:
  'C:\Users\<user>\.qwenpaw\creator-runtime\project-<id>'
  -> 'C:\Users\<user>\.qwenpaw\creator-runtime\.deleted-project-<id>-0f0a55e5b3074592861f469ccfbbc58e'

The above exception was the direct cause of the following exception:
  File ".../backend/api/project_routes.py", line 590, in delete_project
    await asyncio.to_thread(
  File ".../backend/services/project_files/store.py", line 556, in delete
    raise ProjectStoreError(
plugin_qwenpaw_creator.services.project_files.store.ProjectStoreError: Cannot delete Project: <project-id>
```

Which file is actually held (probe: rename the candidate file, then rename it straight back — nothing is modified):

```
LOCKED      project-<id-1>/observability/logs/creator.log      -> PermissionError: [WinError 32] The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process
LOCKED      project-<id-2>/observability/logs/creator.log      -> PermissionError: [WinError 32]
NOT-LOCKED  project-<id-1>/project.json
NOT-LOCKED  project-<id-2>/project.json
NOT-LOCKED  project-<id-2>/observability/logs/creator.log.2026-10-12   (rotated sibling)
```

After the workaround, the same API call succeeds and the background tree cleanup completes (no tombstone left on disk):

```
2026-10-13 10:42:46 | INFO | ...project_files.recovery | recovery.py:278 | recovery complete: 2 projects scanned, 0 integrity errors
2026-10-13 10:42:49 | INFO | ...plugin.qwenpaw_creator | main.py:229 | QwenPaw Creator file runtime ready at <data-root>
2026-10-13 10:43:03 | INFO | store | store.py:580 | project deleted: project-<id-2>
2026-10-13 10:43:12 | INFO | store | store.py:580 | project deleted: project-<id-1>
```

(For reference, the two affected projects held 970 files / 413.9 MB and 217 files / 21.4 MB.)

## Additional Notes

**Why it happens, precisely:** `_CreatorRoutingFileHandler` resolves a log target per record (project-scoped records go to `<project>/observability/logs/creator.log`) and caches one `TimedRotatingFileHandler(delay=False)` per target in `self._targets`. `delay=False` means the stream is opened on creation and kept open; python's handler opens the file without `FILE_SHARE_DELETE`, so the directory entry cannot be renamed while it is open. On Windows a rename of a directory containing an open file fails with `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` (WinError 5) — note it is *not* reported as "file in use" (WinError 32), which is what makes this look mysterious in the UI.

**Suggested fixes (any one of 1/2 removes the deadlock; 3 removes the class of bug):**

1. **Release before renaming.** In `api/project_routes.py::delete_project`, close the project's log handler (and the poller) *before* calling `services.projects.delete(...)`: move `close_creator_project_logging(project_id)` (currently line 602) and `services.poller.close(project_id)` ahead of the delete call at line 590. The delete path becomes: stop log routing → stop poller → rename → cleanup.
2. **Make the rename resilient.** In `ProjectStore.delete`, or in the route, catch the `OSError` from `atomic_replace_path`, release the project's log handler, and retry the rename once; if it still fails, fall back to publishing a "deleted" tombstone manifest instead of leaving the project permanently un-deletable. Today a single held handle makes the project undeletable for the life of the process with a `retryable`-looking 503.
3. **Don't keep a deletable object open.** Write per-project logs **outside** the project directory (e.g. `<data-root>/observability/projects/<project_id>/creator.log`) so no log handle can ever pin the directory that deletion must rename. (The plugin already stores system logs outside project directories: `<data-root>/observability/logs/creator.log`.)

**Test suggestion:** a regression test that writes a project-scoped log record (creating the handler) and then deletes the project, asserting the delete succeeds — that fails deterministically on Windows with the current code order.

issues.title: [Feature]: Make skill-pool download a cancellable background job (progress + explicit cancel)
issues.body:
Follow-up from the review of #8055.

`POST /pool/download` currently waits for the whole copy before responding.
#8055 removes the event-loop freeze by moving the copy to a worker thread,
but the request itself is still synchronous, so a large skill still trips
the client's 30 s timeout and the UI still reports a failure for a download
that is actually progressing.

The end state we want:

* The download runs as a server-side job; the request returns immediately
  with a job id.
* Progress is pollable (files copied / total, current skill).
* Explicit cancellation that **reaches the worker** — aborting the HTTP
  request does not stop an already-running copy, so cancel needs to be a
  real signal to the thread doing the work.
* The frontend stops treating 30 s as a failure and shows pending state
  until the job reports done or cancelled.

Scope note: this changes the API contract and the UX, which is why it was
not folded into #8055.

Related: #8013

issues.title: [Bug]: Console 聊天间歇性静默空完成——回合约 1 秒结束、output 为空、模型从未被调用，前端无任何回复
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version / Environment

- QwenPaw **2.2.0**（Docker，Linux x86_64，Python 3.11，NAS 部署）
- 故障渠道：**Web 控制台（console channel）** 内嵌在 PawApp 里的聊天面板（不是 feishu 等其他渠道）
- 故障 agent：`qwenpaw-data`（由 PawApp 模板 `pawapp:qwenpaw-data` 创建），模型 `octopus/keyong`（OpenAI 兼容网关，实测稳定 5/5）
- 会话：`pawapp:qwenpaw-data`，上下文约 70K–105K tokens

## Description / 现象

在 console 聊天里发送消息，**间歇性得不到任何回复**。抓 SSE 流可见失败回合长这样：

- 事件只有三个：`created` → `in_progress` → `completed`，`output: []`
- 约 **1 秒**完成（正常回合 2.5–12 秒）
- `turn_usage`：`completion_tokens: 0`，`provider_id: ""`，`model_name: ""` —— **模型从未被调用**
- 全程无任何错误日志：runtime 无 unhandled error、无 ConfigurationException、无 429、无 HTTP 错误
- 服务端日志签名（可 grep）：`console stream done: event_count=3 has_response=True`

用户体验：消息发出去，界面既不出回复也不报错，唯一的信号是“什么都没发生”。

## Steps to Reproduce / 复现实测

```http
POST /api/agents/qwenpaw-data/console/chat
X-Agent-Id: qwenpaw-data
Content-Type: application/json

{"session_id":"pawapp:qwenpaw-data","user_id":"default","channel":"console",
 "input":[{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"诊断测试1：请只回复一个字：好"}]}]}
```

连发 10 次（每次间隔约 3 秒，payload 仅序号不同）：

| # | 时间 | 耗时 | output | completion_tokens | provider | 结果 |
|---|------|------|--------|-------------------|----------|------|
| 1 | 23:35:44 | 1.34s | 0 | 0 | '' | 空输出 |
| 2 | 23:35:48 | 0.91s | 0 | 0 | '' | 空输出 |
| 3 | 23:35:52 | 1.08s | 0 | 0 | '' | 空输出 |
| 4 | 23:35:56 | 1.22s | 0 | 0 | '' | 空输出 |
| 5 | 23:36:01 | 11.88s | 1 | 2 | octopus | 正常（回复“好好”） |
| 6–10 | 23:36:15–23:36:54 | 2.5–9.2s | 1 | 2 | octopus | 正常 |

失败率 4/10。模式：**长时间空闲后的前几个回合集中失败，之后同样 payload 全部成功**。当晚三次观察一致：23:01 与 23:03 用户两条真实消息零回复 → 23:20 复现失败一次 → 23:22 同样内容成功 → 23:35 四连败后全成功。

## Actual vs Expected

- Actual：有效用户消息被静默吞掉，回合空完成，前端无回复、无错误提示。
- Expected：要么正常回复，要么给出可见错误；任何情况下 `completed` 的 response 不应是空 output 且无任何日志。

## 已排除的可能（都不是根因）

1. **模型不可用**：绕过 agent 直调 `octopus/keyong` 的 `/chat/completions`，5/5 成功（1.5–5.4s）。
2. **任务卡死占场**（409）：TaskTracker reconnect 挂上来返回空流（idle）；chat 记录 status=idle。
3. **插件 hook 短路**：`qwenpaw-data` 插件未注册任何 SHORT_CIRCUIT/SKIP_AGENT hook；全部已装插件的 hook 也均不短路上两阶段。
4. **ConfigurationException**：日志无 `runtime: configuration required`。
5. **no-text debounce 吞消息**：`_content_has_text()` 对文本 content 返回 True，不会进缓冲分支。
6. **QwenPaw Data 后端/Neo4j**：context service access log 无卡住请求，execute_sql/datasources/bolt 全部 200。
7. **飞书主链路**：同期 feishu 会话（default agent）回复完全正常。

## 代码路径与疑似点（供定位，未确认根因）

调用链：

```
POST /console/chat
→ TaskTracker.attach_or_start
→ ConsoleChannel.stream_one        (app/channels/console/channel.py:358)
→ Workspace.stream_query           (app/workspace/workspace.py:414)
→ Runtime.run（8 阶段）             (runtime/runtime.py:50)
→ AgentExecutor.run                (runtime/executor.py:37)
→ agent.reply_stream → _reply_impl  (agentscope/agent/_agent.py:915)
```

“零事件空完成”在 `_reply_impl` 里有两条退出路径会产生完全相同的现象：

- `inputs` 为空列表 → `_handle_incoming_messages` 的 `if msgs:` 不成立 → 上下文不追加 → `_next_action` 首轮即 `Exit` → 唯一 yield 的 `exit_msg` 又被 `reply_stream`（`yield_final_msg=False`）过滤 → 客户端收到空 `completed`；
- 或首轮 `_next_action` 直接判 Exit（上下一条末条是 assistant 消息时）。

两种都等价于一个结论：**用户消息没有进入 agent 的 input_msgs**。可疑丢失点（按链路顺序）：

- `app/channels/console/channel.py` `stream_one` 的 debounce / merged / `build_agent_request_from_native` 路径；
- `runtime/runtime.py` `_build_context`：`input_msgs=_request_input_to_msgs(request.input)`；
- `runtime/message_convert.py` 的请求→Msg 转换；
- scroll 上下文系统（`persisted_ids` / `seen_*` 去重）与新回合输入合并的竞态——注意每轮日志都有 `builder: built agent ... model=octopus/keyong tools=31`，即 runtime 完整构建后直接空完成，agent 本身已就绪。

另一个附带问题（可独立修）：失败回合的 `completed` 完全静默——`_commit_turn_usage` 记了一条 provider 为空的 usage，但没有任何 WARNING/ERROR。建议对“无 content 事件的空 completed”至少打一条 WARNING，否则用户侧根本无法排查。

## Logs / 证据样本

失败回合（23:35:44–45，grep `pawapp:qwenpaw-data`）：

```
23:35:44 | INFO | runtime/builder.py:538 | builder: built agent for session=pawapp:qwenpaw-data agent=qwenpaw-data model=octopus/keyong tools=31
23:35:45 | INFO | app/channels/base.py:1962 | Usage for session pawapp:qwenpaw-data: {'provider_id': '', 'model_name': '', 'prompt_tokens': 70801, 'completion_tokens': 0, ...}
23:35:45 | INFO | app/channels/console/channel.py:494 | console stream done: event_count=3 has_response=True
```

用户侧对话记录（dialog jsonl）：23:01:04、23:03:43 两条 user 消息后无任何 assistant 消息。

复现脚本与原始数据（本地，未随 issue 附）：`scripts/_debug/pawapp_repro.py`、`scripts/state/pawapp_repro_result.jsonl`。

## Additional Notes

- 与 open issue **#7549**（Ark trailing assistant 400）不同：那例有明确 400 报错，本例零错误、模型未调用。
- 与 **#5856**（compaction 丢 tool_call 结构）不同症；但本例失败回合 `prompt_tokens≈70.8K` 恒定、scroll 每轮 compact，供参考。
- 临时规避：重发同一消息通常可触发（不是每次都需要多重试，观察到的模式是空闲后前几发性失败）。

---

### English summary (for maintainers)

Intermittent silent failure in the console (web) chat: a valid user message sometimes produces an "empty completion" — SSE shows only created/in_progress/completed with `output: []` in ~1s, `turn_usage` has `completion_tokens=0` and empty `provider_id`/`model_name`, i.e. the model is never called, and nothing is logged as an error. Reproduced 4/10 consecutive POSTs to `/api/agents/<id>/console/chat` (first attempts after idle fail, later identical requests succeed). Model, task tracker, plugin hooks, configuration errors, debounce and the data backend were all verified healthy. Suspect the user message is lost before reaching the agent's `input_msgs` (console `stream_one` → `Runtime._build_context` → `_request_input_to_msgs`, or a race with the scroll context system), so `_reply_impl` exits with zero events. Suggest also logging a WARNING when a response completes with no content events — right now the failure is completely silent.

issues.title: [Bug]: Installing a skill from GitHub silently corrupts its binary files — all non-UTF-8 bytes are replaced with U+FFFD (images/fonts unreadable)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.2.1 (Docker). 

## Description

Installing a skill **from GitHub** via `qwenpaw skills install https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/tree/<branch>/<skill-dir>` silently corrupts every binary file in the skill: all non-UTF-8 bytes are replaced with U+FFFD (`�`). Images (PNG/JPEG), fonts, PDFs, ZIPs etc. become unreadable, while text files stay intact. No warning is emitted and the security scan still reports the skill as safe.

Byte-level reproduction shows the installed file is *exactly* `original_bytes.decode("utf-8", errors="replace").encode("utf-8")`.

Root cause: the GitHub fetch path treats every file as text.

- `agents/skill_system/hub.py` → `_github_read_file()` (main: ~L1278) returns `str`; it reads files via `_http_text_get(download_url)` (which ends in `payload.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")` inside `_http_get`, main: L653) or via `base64.b64decode(...).decode("utf-8", errors="replace")`.
- `_github_collect_tree_files()` (main: ~L1312) accumulates files into a `dict[str, str]` bundle that is later written to disk — binary content cannot survive.

Note: the ZIP-based providers (LobeHub / ModelScope / QwenPaw archive) apply a `_is_probably_text_blob()` guard and *skip* non-text files with a warning — so skills that ship assets silently lose those files there. The GitHub path does not even skip; it corrupts. Both behaviors look unintended for skills that ship binary assets.

**Related PR(s):** #783 (merged 2026-03-06, "Fix import failure caused by non-UTF-8 bytes in the skill folder") — appears to be the origin of the current behavior: it changed `_http_get()` from `.decode("utf-8")` to `.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")`, and `_github_read_file()`'s base64 branch likewise. That stopped imports from *failing* on non-UTF-8 files, but it also silently replaces invalid bytes in **every** file — which is how binary files get corrupted today. A proper fix should preserve bytes for non-text blobs (or at minimum skip/warn instead of corrupting).

**Security considerations:** data integrity only (silent file corruption on disk); no auth/secret exposure.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Skills
- [x] CLI

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.2.1 (affected code also in `main` @ `59f2849c`)
- **OS:** Linux (Debian 12 container, x86_64) — the bug is platform-independent
- **Install method:** Docker (CLI `qwenpaw skills install`)
- **Python version:** 3.11

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a repository containing a skill folder with a binary asset, e.g. `skills/demo/SKILL.md` + `skills/demo/assets/logo.png` (any valid PNG).
2. Run: `qwenpaw skills install https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/tree/main/skills/demo --agent-id <agent-id> --enable`
3. Compare the installed `assets/logo.png` against the repository copy (size / md5), or open it — `PIL.Image.open` raises `UnidentifiedImageError`.

Real-case observation (skill with 31 PNGs — all 31 corrupted; text files byte-identical):

```
original : 719,220 bytes  md5 79cd1265bc835092ee66c3f7cf08f3e0
installed: 1,300,327 bytes md5 9f765880327b357e6d802c1fca8c26cc
check    : installed == original.decode("utf-8", errors="replace").encode("utf-8")  → True (byte-exact)
detail   : +293,002 U+FFFD chars in that one file; assets dir 5.0 MB → 8.9 MB
another  : command-1.png — 169,778 bytes → 66,412 U+FFFD;  text .tsv unchanged
```

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** binary files are silently corrupted on install (non-UTF-8 bytes → U+FFFD); images can't be opened; scanner reports "safe"; no warning anywhere.
- **Expected:** binary files preserved byte-for-byte (skills commonly ship screenshots/images/fonts). At the very least, non-text files should not be corrupted silently.

## Logs / Screenshots

```
$ qwenpaw skills install https://github.com/... --agent-id ... --enable
✓ Installed skill 'demo' to agent '...'.
✓ Skill enabled.
[scanner] Scan of 'demo' completed in 0.02s – 0 finding(s), safe=True

$ python3 -c "from PIL import Image; Image.open('.../assets/logo.png')"
PIL.UnidentifiedImageError: cannot identify image file '.../assets/logo.png'
```

## Additional Notes

- Suggested fix: preserve raw bytes for non-text blobs through the bundle pipeline — e.g. allow `bytes` values in the files dict (`dict[str, str | bytes]`) and write them as bytes, deciding via `_is_probably_text_blob()`. A regression test with a tiny PNG fixture would catch this class of bug.
- Workaround used while reporting: repaired the installed copies from the source repository after installation.
- Happy to test a patch / open a PR if useful.

issues.title: [Bug]: Allow configurable console basename for reverse-proxy subpath deployments

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## Description

The Web Console hardcodes its router basename to `/console`, which means it cannot be served under an arbitrary subpath (e.g., `/qwenpaw/`) behind a reverse proxy. This blocks a common self-hosted deployment pattern: multiplexing multiple services on a single domain, where each service lives under its own path prefix.

The only way to serve the console under a custom subpath today is to patch `CONSOLE_BASENAME` in the source and rebuild the frontend, which forks the user from upstream releases.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install QwenPaw and start it: `qwenpaw app`
2. Put a reverse proxy (Caddy, Nginx, Traefik) in front of it
3. Configure the proxy to serve QwenPaw under `/qwenpaw/` instead of `/` or `/console/`
4. Navigate to `https://your-host/qwenpaw/`

## Actual Behavior

The SPA loads but renders blank. Browser console shows:

```
Failed to load module script: Expected a JavaScript-or-Wasm module script but the server
responded with a MIME type of "text/html".
```

The root cause is in `console/src/utils/navigationMode.ts`:

```typescript
const CONSOLE_BASENAME = "/console";

export function getRouterBasename(pathname: string): string | undefined {
    return /^\/console(?:\/|$)/.test(pathname) ? CONSOLE_BASENAME : undefined;
}
```

When the browser URL is `/qwenpaw/`, the regex doesn't match, `getRouterBasename()` returns `undefined`, and React Router boots without a basename. It then tries to match `/qwenpaw/` as a route, fails, and renders nothing.

## Expected Behavior

The router basename should be configurable at build time, so users can deploy the console under any subpath without patching the source. For example:

```bash
VITE_CONSOLE_BASENAME=/qwenpaw npm run build
```

And the resulting bundle should detect that `/qwenpaw` is the basename, route all SPA navigation relative to it, and emit asset URLs prefixed with `/qwenpaw/assets/`.

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** QwenPaw, version 2.2.1
- **Install method:** uv / pip / Docker
- **Deployment:** Reverse proxy (Caddy) in front of `qwenpaw app`
- **OS:** macOS 15 (also affects Linux/Docker deployments)

## Proposed Fix

Make `CONSOLE_BASENAME` read from an environment variable at build time, with `/console` as the fallback for backward compatibility:

```typescript
const CONSOLE_BASENAME =
    import.meta.env.VITE_CONSOLE_BASENAME || "/console";

export function getRouterBasename(pathname: string): string | undefined {
    const escaped = CONSOLE_BASENAME.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, "\\$&");
    return new RegExp(`^${escaped}(?:/|$)`).test(pathname)
        ? CONSOLE_BASENAME
        : undefined;
}
```

This preserves the current default (`/console`) so existing deployments are unaffected. Users who need a custom subpath set `VITE_CONSOLE_BASENAME` before running `npm run build`.

## Additional Context

- This is a common pattern for self-hosted apps. Grafana (`root_url`), Jellyfin (base URL), and Vaultwarden (`DOMAIN`) all support configurable subpaths.
- The related issue #2171 already notes that the console build can be polluted by generic shell variables like `BASE_URL`. Namespacing the new variable with `VITE_` avoids that class of bug.
- Discussion thread with full reverse-proxy setup details: [link to your article or a gist]

## Activity

- [x] I searched for existing issues and didn't find a duplicate
- [x] I'm willing to submit a PR if the maintainers agree on the approach

issues.title: A message sent on one device is invisible on the other until the whole turn finishes
issues.body:
# A message sent on one device is invisible on the other until the whole turn finishes

## Problem

When a user message is sent — from the web console, or from a mobile app — it is only persisted to the chat history at **run end**. While the run is in flight:

- `GET /api/chats` (history) does not contain the user's own message;
- the run's SSE stream does not contain it either — the stream starts with the assistant's output.

## Reproduction

1. Have QwenPaw running with at least one agent.
2. Open the web console on device A and the mobile app on device B, logged into the same workspace (or open the console on two devices).
3. On device A, send a message that starts a long run (e.g. a coding task that takes minutes).
4. Watch device B:
   - the chat view shows no user message at all — the assistant appears to "start a turn from nowhere";
   - the message only appears on device B **after the run finishes** and device B refetches history.

Same failure mode in reverse: a message sent from the mobile app is invisible on the console until the turn completes.

## Expected

The user's own message should be visible to all connected clients **as soon as the run starts**, not after it ends — the turn should read as "user asked → assistant answering" on every screen from the first second.

## Root cause (server-side)

The console run stream only forwards provider/assistant output; the user message that triggered the run is written to the chat store when the run completes. There is no channel that carries the user message to live observers mid-run. The web console currently papers over this with a **local optimistic echo** — which only fixes the one screen that sent the message, not every other observer of the same run.

## Impact

- Multi-device setups (console + mobile app, or two consoles) experience "I sent a message and it doesn't exist on the other screen" for the full duration of the turn.
- Any API consumer of the run stream (integrations, automation, dashboards) cannot correlate a run with the request that started it until the run ends.

## Proposed direction

Emit the user's message as an out-of-band frame at the **start of each new run's stream** (shape-compatible with the existing `turn_usage` / `replay_end` out-of-band frames, which unknown-frame-tolerant clients already ignore), so that:

- the frame is produced once per run and enters the run buffer like any other frame;
- reconnect/replay of a live run includes it (a late joiner sees the user turn without waiting for run end);
- clients that render history-only are unaffected (unknown frames are ignored).

Design details, per-client handler contracts and compatibility analysis: see the companion design doc (`方案.md`) in this folder, and the in-flight server patch on `feat/harmony-app` (commit `781e7378`).

issues.title: [Feature]: Firecrawl as a web_search provider
issues.body:
Hey, I'm Juampi from the Firecrawl team.

## Summary

Add Firecrawl as a third `web_search` provider next to the two existing ones. I'd build and maintain it.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Problem / Motivation

The `SearchProvider` abstraction from #7081 makes a new backend small. Today users who want Firecrawl have to go through ClawHub skills or a custom MCP config. Firecrawl search also works without an API key on a keyless free tier that is capped per IP (https://docs.firecrawl.dev/billing), and a key raises the limits, so it fits the same optional-key shape as the provider added in #7081.

## Proposed Solution

Follow the layout from #7081: a `FirecrawlProvider` in `websearch/` that posts to `https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/search` through the existing `_post` helper, the provider option in the Console modal and router config, an optional `api_key` credential slot, and unit tests. No new dependency. The current default stays the default. Requests carry an `origin: "qwenpaw"` field so Firecrawl can tell where they come from.

A possible follow-up, only if you want it: an opt-in `web_fetch` fallback to Firecrawl for pages the direct fetch can't read. I'd keep that as a separate PR.

## Alternatives Considered

A Firecrawl MCP client template next to the existing one. The provider needs no MCP setup, so it is simpler for users.

## Additional Context

I have the change built and tested, and I'm opening the PR next to this issue. Happy to change anything from the layout in #7081. @rayrayraykk @cuiyuebing

issues.title: console perf: large backdrop-filter radii (12-28px) on glass surfaces + per-frame decorative costs keep the GPU busy (most visible on iGPU) — suggest an official "reduced effects" tier
issues.body:
## Problem

Opening the console keeps the GPU busy for no visible reason — sustained GPU utilization just from having the page open, rising further while a chat is streaming. We traced the load to **design-level GPU costs that exist on every machine**: large `backdrop-filter` radii on full-width glass surfaces (recomputed every frame whenever the backdrop changes), plus continuously running decorative animations. The load is hardware-agnostic in origin; it is simply **most visible on integrated graphics**, which has far less headroom for sustained fill-rate work (heat, fan, battery drain, input lag show up there first).

**Environment:** Linux Docker deployment; console accessed from a browser on an Intel/AMD iGPU laptop. (The code-level costs below apply regardless of GPU class.)

## Upstream pieces that are already solid (verified against source)

We read the console source before writing this — several things are already done right, and we want to be explicit about it so the ask stays scoped:

- `RunningGlow` (the rotating glow on the session avatar): the orbit is a pure `transform: rotate` (compositor-only), **paused by default**, and gated by `active && inView && !document.hidden && !reduced-motion`. Well engineered.
- The ambient glow under it is an 8px element with `blur(12px)` at low opacity — cheap.
- As designed, the orbit runs while the page is visible and the component is in view. On discrete GPU that's an acceptable decorative cost.

## Evidence (current codebase)

1. **Backdrop-filter radii are consistently large, on large surfaces.** Blur cost scales with radius², and for `backdrop-filter` it is paid **per frame** whenever what's behind the layer changes (scrolling, chat streaming):

   | Location | Radii |
   |---|---|
   | `console/src/os/useOsStyles.ts` (L285 / L405 / L487 / L828 / L1075 / L1190) | 22 / 14 / 28 / 26 / 20 / 24 px |
   | `console/src/pages/Hub/components/HubShell.module.less` | 20 px |
   | `console/src/components/PageHeader/index.module.less` | 16 px |
   | `console/src/layouts/sidebarSessionList.module.less` | 12 px |
   | `console/src/components/RenderableCodeBlock/index.module.less` | 12 px |

   These are full-width / full-height glass layers (page chrome, header, sidebar, code blocks). On a pure radius² basis, 22px → 6px is **up to ~13× less per-frame work** — a geometric upper bound, not a measurement; the realized saving also depends on affected area, backdrop-change rate, and the browser's filter implementation (a controlled micro-benchmark is in PR #8137). The same cap applied across the list is still a low-risk, behavior-free win because the visual difference at 12–28px is subtle for readability.
2. **Streaming multiplies it.** During a chat, message text grows per token: markdown re-layout, per-message enter animations, and the ever-changing backdrop behind every glass layer all run at frame rate. This is the "the console gets warm just by watching a reply" part — the component-level breakdown is in a follow-up.
3. **Measured decorative-work cost (a different layer — the 3D graph, not the glass blur).** During an earlier event-loop-freeze investigation we measured the WebGL draw-call rate of the console's 3D graph view (3d-force-graph) with a counter wrapping the WebGL context's draw methods, sampled per second. Scenario: the graph tab is kept alive after navigating away; its internal rAF render loop is not visibility-gated, so draw calls held at **2,340/s** even while hidden — gating the loop on visibility brought it to **0/s** while hidden. This is a separate cost layer from the glass blur in item 1 (the upstream `MemoryGraphView` has the same ungated rAF pattern); both contribute to the sustained load. It shows the continuous decorative work is real, measurable, and of the order of thousands of GPU submissions per second.

## Impact

- Sustained background GPU load → heat/fan/battery on laptops, throttling on iGPU; visible even at "idle" page open.
- iGPU users are hit disproportionately (same root cost, less headroom).
- Long streaming sessions (the console's core use case) compound every factor above simultaneously.

## Proposal

1. **Global radius audit:** cap glass `backdrop-filter` radii at ~6–8px across the console (values above → table). Pure CSS change, no behavior risk.
2. **An official "reduced effects" setting** (Settings → Appearance & language, alongside theme), at minimum covering a glass-radius tier and a decorative-animation toggle. Suggested semantics:
   - **Full** (default): current behavior;
   - **Reduced:** glass radii capped (~6px), animations kept;
   - **Off:** no blur, decorative animations stopped;
   - **Follow system** default, respecting `prefers-reduced-motion`.
   We are happy to send a PR for this — our downstream plugin already ships exactly this tier (see below), so the implementation is proven.
3. **Streaming throttling (follow-up, separate PR):** degrade per-message enter animations and/or batch markdown re-renders per chunk while a reply is streaming.

## Downstream status (for context)

Our downstream plugin already ships a user-facing console-effects tier (default "light": glass radii capped at 6px, animations kept; "off": everything stopped), implemented with CSS overrides (`data-wb-fx`). If upstream ships an official tier, we will switch to it. This issue is about the universal upstream benefit — every console user, not just iGPU ones.

## How to observe

1. Open the console (any session list visible); watch GPU usage in the browser's task manager (or `intel_gpu_top` / `nvidia-smi` on the host).
2. Note the sustained baseline while idle; then start a chat reply and watch it climb.
3. (For the radius part) DevTools → render → "Paint flashing"/GPU panel: the glass layers are recomposited on every backdrop change.

---

## 问题

打开 console 就没有理由地持续占着 GPU——页面只开不动就有持续占用，聊天流式输出时进一步升高。我们把占用追到了**所有机器上都存在的设计层 GPU 成本**：大面积玻璃层上使用过大的 `backdrop-filter` 半径（backdrop 一变就每帧重算），外加持续运行的装饰动画。这个成本与硬件无关，只是在**核显（iGPU）上最明显**——核显持续 fill-rate 余量小，发热/风扇/掉电/输入延迟最先在那里显现。

**环境**：Linux Docker 部署，Intel/AMD 核显笔记本浏览器访问 console（下述代码层成本与 GPU 类别无关）。

## 上游已做得好的部分（源码核实过，先讲清楚，把请求范围收住）

- `RunningGlow`（会话头像上的旋转光环）：orbit 是纯 `transform: rotate`（只走合成器）、**默认 paused**、由 `active && inView && !document.hidden && !reduced-motion` 门控——工程化良好。
- 其下方 ambient 光晕是 8px 元素 + `blur(12px)` 低透明度——便宜。
- 按设计，页面可见且组件在视野内时 orbit 就是要转的。独显上这属于可接受的装饰成本。

## 证据（当前代码库）

1. **backdrop-filter 半径普遍过大，且在大面积层上。** 模糊成本 ∝ 半径²，且对 `backdrop-filter` 而言，只要层后面有变化（滚动、聊天流式）就**每帧支付**：

   | 位置 | 半径 |
   |---|---|
   | `console/src/os/useOsStyles.ts`（L285 / L405 / L487 / L828 / L1075 / L1190） | 22 / 14 / 28 / 26 / 20 / 24 px |
   | `console/src/pages/Hub/components/HubShell.module.less` | 20 px |
   | `console/src/components/PageHeader/index.module.less` | 16 px |
   | `console/src/layouts/sidebarSessionList.module.less` | 12 px |
   | `console/src/components/RenderableCodeBlock/index.module.less` | 12 px |

   这些是整宽/整高的玻璃层（页面框架、页头、侧栏、代码块）。纯按半径²算，22px→6px 每帧工作量**至多省约 13×**——这是几何上界而非实测；实际收益还取决于受影响面积、backdrop 变化速率与浏览器滤镜实现（受控微基准见 PR #8137）。全表统一封顶仍是零行为风险的纯 CSS 收益（12–28px 之间可读性视觉差异很微妙）。
2. **流式把它成倍放大。** 聊天中消息逐 token 增长：markdown 重排、每条消息入场动画、每个玻璃层背后持续变化的 backdrop 全部以帧率运行——这就是"光看着回复就热"的部分（组件级细分留 follow-up）。
3. **装饰工作成本有实测（另一个层——3D 图谱，不是玻璃模糊）。** 之前一次事件循环冻结调查中，我们给 WebGL 上下文的绘制方法包了计数器，按秒采样 3D 图谱视图（3d-force-graph）的 WebGL draw-call 速率。场景：图谱页签切走后由 keep-alive 保活，其内部 rAF 渲染循环不受可见性门控，隐藏状态下绘制调用仍恒定 **2,340 次/秒**——按可见性门控后隐藏时降到 **0 次/秒**。这是与第 1 点玻璃模糊**相互独立**的成本层（上游 `MemoryGraphView` 同样存在无门控 rAF 模式），两者共同构成持续占用；它说明持续装饰工作是真实的、可测量的，量级达每秒数千次 GPU 提交。

## 影响

- 持续后台 GPU 占用 → 笔记本发热/风扇/耗电，核显还会触发降频；页面"空开"即可见。
- 核显用户受不成比例的影响（同一根因，余量更小）。
- 长流式会话（console 核心使用场景）同时叠加以上全部因素。

## 提案

1. **全量半径审计**：全 console 玻璃层 `backdrop-filter` 半径封顶 ~6–8px（见上表）。纯 CSS 改动，无行为风险。
2. **官方"降低特效"设置项**（设置 → 外观与语言，与主题并列），至少覆盖玻璃半径档 + 装饰动画开关。建议语义：
   - **完整**（默认）：现状；
   - **降低**：玻璃半径封顶（~6px），动画保留；
   - **关闭**：无模糊，装饰动画全停；
   - 默认**跟随系统**，尊重 `prefers-reduced-motion`。
   我们愿意为此提 PR——下游插件已经上线了完全相同的档位（见下），实现是验证过的。
3. **流式节流（follow-up，单独 PR）**：流式回复期间降级消息入场动画和/或按 chunk 批量提交 markdown 重渲染。

## 下游现状（供参考）

我们的下游插件已上线用户可切的 console 特效档（默认"降低"：玻璃半径封顶 6px、动画保留；"关闭"：全停），用 CSS 覆盖实现（`data-wb-fx`）。上游出官方档后我们会切过去。本 issue 关注的是上游普适收益——每个 console 用户，不只是核显用户。

## 如何观察

1. 打开 console（能看到会话列表即可），在浏览器任务管理器（或宿主机 `intel_gpu_top` / `nvidia-smi`）看 GPU 占用。
2. 记下空开时的持续基线；再发起一条聊天回复，看它爬升。
3.（半径部分）DevTools → render → Paint flashing/GPU 面板：玻璃层在每次 backdrop 变化时都会重合成。

issues.body:
Title
[Feature] Model pool has no delete/remove action — only enable/disable, so deprecated models can't be purged

Question or topic
The model pool / model-management UI only offers an enable/disable toggle. There is no way to permanently delete a model entry from a provider, so deprecated or broken models stay in the list forever (they can only be greyed out). Please either add a delete action, or document how to remove entries via API.

Context
QwenPaw version: 2.2.2b4
Channel: Console (web UI, default port 8088)
Skill / use case: Custom OpenAI-compatible provider backed by a local relay (base_url: http://127.0.0.1:20128/v1), with model auto-discovery enabled (discovery_strategy: openai_models, model_sync_mode: startup).
Impact: The provider returned several upstream models that were later deprecated upstream. They now fail at call time (e.g. HTTP 410 ModelDeprecated: Model mimo-v2.5-free has been deprecated). Because the UI can only disable them, they stay in the pool and there is no discoverable way to clean them up without hand-editing provider JSON.
Expected
A way to delete a model entry from a provider (a trash/remove action in the model pool or the model-management modal), so deprecated models can be permanently removed and won't be re-added by the next discovery sync.

Actual
The pool list only exposes a selection toggle (enabled/disabled). The only icon that looks like "remove" is in the model selector dropdown and actually calls updateModelPool(..., {selected: false}) — i.e. it deselects, not deletes. It is also hidden behind a "manage" button (its useState(false) flag starts as false), so most users never see it.

What I found in the source (may save maintainers time)
A real delete endpoint already exists and works: DELETE /api/models/{provider_id}/models/{model_id:path} → providers.py, remove_model_endpoint, which calls ProviderManager.delete_model_from_provider → Provider.delete_model (provider.py), adding the id to removed_model_ids and dropping it from extra_models / discovered_models.
There is simply no UI wired to it. In the console bundles (RemoteModelManageModal-*.js, index-*.js) the only model-pool mutations are updateModelPool (enable/disable) and addModel. No deleteModel call exists.
So this looks like a missing-UI gap rather than a backend limitation.

Tried so far
Read the frontend console bundles: searched for removeModel / deleteModel / updateModelPool — the "remove" control is a deselect, not a delete.
Confirmed the backend DELETE /api/models/{provider}/models/{model} route exists (providers.py, remove_model_endpoint).
Verified the running service responds normally (GET /api/models/{provider_id}/pool → 200).
Workaround: calling the DELETE API by hand, or editing working.secret/providers/custom/<id>.json — neither is discoverable from the UI.

issues.title: [Bug] qwenpaw-creator startup hook aborts: os.kill(pid, 0) raises SystemError (not caught by except OSError) when runtime-owner.json holds a stale pid
issues.body:
### Summary

QwenPaw Desktop **fails to start** when `creator-runtime/runtime-owner.json` contains a **stale pid**.
The `qwenpaw-creator` plugin's startup hook calls `os.kill(pid, 0)` as a liveness probe; on Windows this can raise
`SystemError: <class 'OSError'> returned a result with an exception set` (underlying `OSError: [WinError 6] 句柄无效 / invalid handle`),
which is **not** caught by the existing `except OSError:` handler. The exception escapes, the whole startup hook fails,
and the Creator runtime never becomes ready. The app is unusable until the file is manually deleted.

### Environment

- QwenPaw Desktop **2.2.2-beta.4** (Windows 10 AMD64)
- Plugin `qwenpaw-creator` **2.0.1**
- Python **3.12.10** (bundled backend)

### Steps to reproduce (in the field)

1. Let the Creator runtime start successfully once — it writes `creator-runtime/runtime-owner.json`, e.g.
   `{"pid": 2924, "startedAtEpoch": 1791374773.9167662}`.
2. Shut QwenPaw down **without deleting that file** (it is never removed on shutdown).
3. Kill/exit the process whose pid is recorded (normal case after a restart).
4. Start QwenPaw again.

### Expected

QwenPaw starts; stale pid is treated as "no live peer".

### Actual

Startup hook fails, Creator runtime never reaches "ready":

```
2026-10-12 19:08:43 | ERROR | qwenpaw\app\_app.py:627 | ✗ Failed to execute startup hook
    'pawapp_qwenpaw-creator_1744292470816' from plugin 'qwenpaw-creator':
    <class 'OSError'> returned a result with an exception set
OSError: [WinError 6] 句柄无效。

The above exception was the direct cause of the following exception:

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "qwenpaw\app\_app.py", line 620, in _background_startup
  File "...\plugins\qwenpaw-creator\backend\main.py", line 175, in _startup
    services = creator_file_services(data_root)
  File "...\backend\services\project_files\facade.py", line 849, in creator_file_services
    services = CreatorFileServices.create(resolved)
  File "...\backend\services\project_files\facade.py", line 240, in create
    if _warn_on_second_backend(projects.root):
  File "...\backend\services\project_files\facade.py", line 199, in _warn_on_second_backend
    os.kill(pid, 0)
SystemError: <class 'OSError'> returned a result with an exception set
```

The same error was observed on **2026-10-10 20:05** and twice on **2026-10-12 (19:08, 19:10)**.

### Root cause

`plugins/qwenpaw-creator/backend/services/project_files/facade.py` (~line 180-215):

```python
def _warn_on_second_backend(root: Path) -> bool:
    marker = root / "runtime-owner.json"
    try:
        previous = json.loads(marker.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        pid = int(previous.get("pid") or 0)
    except (OSError, ValueError, TypeError):
        pid = 0
    peer_alive = False
    if pid and pid != os.getpid():
        try:
            os.kill(pid, 0)          # <-- raises SystemError on Windows here
        except OSError:              # <-- does NOT catch SystemError
            pass
        else:
            peer_alive = True
            logger.error("another QwenPaw Creator backend ...")
    ...
    # marker is written back only AFTER the probe
```

Two problems compound:

1. **Wrong exception type is caught.** On Windows, a failed `os.kill(pid, 0)` did not surface as a plain `OSError`
   here but as `SystemError: <class 'OSError'> returned a result with an exception set`
   (underlying `OSError: [WinError 6] 句柄无效`). `SystemError` is not a subclass of `OSError`, so it escapes.
2. **The marker write-back sits after the probe**, so once the probe raises, the stale pid is **never refreshed** —
   the file stays frozen at the old pid and **every subsequent restart hits the same failure**.
   (In our logs the marker was frozen at a pid written 5 days earlier.)

Note on reproducibility: we could **not** deterministically reproduce it with an arbitrary nonexistent pid —
on the same machine `os.kill(999999, 0)` and `os.kill(<the stale pid>, 0)` currently return a **catchable**
`OSError(winerror=87, ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER)`. The `WinError 6` (ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE) in the field suggests the
failing call took a different path (handle/pid state at that moment). Regardless, the traceback above is the raw evidence.

### Suggested fix

```python
    peer_alive = False
    if pid and pid != os.getpid():
        try:
            os.kill(pid, 0)
        except OSError:
            pass
        except Exception:            # Windows may raise SystemError instead
            logger.debug("liveness probe for pid=%s failed", pid, exc_info=True)
        else:
            peer_alive = True
            logger.error(...)
```

Additionally recommended:

- Prefer a Windows-safe liveness check instead of `os.kill(pid, 0)`
  (e.g. `OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION)` + `GetExitCodeProcess`, or `WaitForSingleObject`),
  because on Windows `os.kill` is not documented as a "signal 0 = probe" operation.
- Move the marker write-back so it always runs (e.g. `try/finally`), so a probe failure cannot freeze a stale pid forever.
- Do not let this *advisory* probe abort the entire plugin startup hook — it is explicitly documented as
  "Advisory (zero-lock) detection ... warns loudly instead of blocking".

### Workaround

Delete (or clear) the marker before starting; it is recreated automatically on the next successful start:

```
%USERPROFILE%\.copaw\creator-runtime\runtime-owner.json
```

### Additional notes

- The trace in `creator-runtime/observability/traces/creator-trace-*.jsonl` shows
  `creator.runtime.starting` with **no matching `creator.runtime.started`** for the failed attempts,
  and a successful `creator.runtime.started` immediately after the marker was removed.
- Happy to provide full logs.

issues.title: [Feature]: web_search built-in tavily provider has no API-key config surface — paid quota unusable (内置 tavily provider 无法配置自有 API key)

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
## Summary

The built-in `web_search` tool's tavily provider always uses keyless anonymous REST (request header `X-Tavily-Access-Mode: keyless`), and **there is no configuration surface to supply a user's own Tavily API key**. Users with a paid Tavily subscription can neither consume their own quota nor avoid the anonymous channel's rate limits.

中文：内置 `web_search` 的 tavily provider 固定走 keyless 匿名 REST（请求头 `X-Tavily-Access-Mode: keyless`），没有任何配置入口填入用户自己的 Tavily API key。持有订阅的用户既无法消耗自有额度，还随时受匿名通道限流。理解 keyless 是"开箱即用"的产品决策，本单无意要求改变默认；诉求只是**给有 key 的用户一扇门**。

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (agents/tools — `websearch` providers & factory)
- [x] Console (frontend web UI — provider dropdown has no key field)
- [ ] Channels
- [ ] Skills
- [x] CLI (`qwenpaw` config surfaces for `web_search.config`)

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.2.1
- **OS:** macOS 15 (arm64), Python 3.12, pip install
- Tavily account: Researcher plan (1000 credits/month)

## Problem Details / Reproduction

1. Inspect outbound requests from `web_search`: every call carries `X-Tavily-Access-Mode: keyless`; the account's own quota consumption stays at zero.
2. Look for a place to configure a key: `web_search.config` schema exposes only the provider choice (`tavily` / `anysearch`); the Console dropdown likewise. Neither has an `api_key`/credential field anywhere.
3. Result: a user holding a valid Tavily key has no supported way to make the built-in provider use it.
4. Keyless is not a theoretical risk: our logs contain a real **HTTP 432** (quota-class error) failure from the anonymous path.

This is a feature gap rather than a crash — the symptom is "I have a key but nowhere to put it", with no warning anywhere. It belongs to the same natural evolution as #8139 and #7711 (adding new web_search providers).

## Current Workaround & Its Cost

We patched venv site-packages directly (with the operator's explicit authorization): added an authed provider that reads the key reference from QwenPaw's **existing credential store**, POSTs to `api.tavily.com/search` authenticated, and on any 432/429/401/network error **automatically falls back to keyless** — plus wiring changes in `factory.py` default and the Console dropdown options. End-to-end verified: authed path genuinely used; fallback path PASS.

Costs we are paying, which upstream fixes would eliminate:

1. `qwenpaw update` overwrites the patch — explicit technical debt we must re-apply after every upgrade.
2. During rollout we hit a related papercut: AgentConfigWatcher hot-reloads JSON configs only; Python code changes do not take effect, and the running process kept reporting `Unknown web_search provider` with **no hint that a restart was required**.

## Suggested Implementation

1. Add an `api_key_ref` field to `web_search.config` pointing into the framework's existing credential store (we verified tool-layer code can read it; implementation cost is low and it avoids plaintext keys in `agent.json`); expose a key input in the Console form accordingly.
2. Implement **authed→keyless automatic fallback** officially: degrade with a log line when quota is exhausted/rate-limited. This is the most valuable part of our hand-rolled solution and we suggest adopting it as-is.
3. (Bonus) At startup or config change, if tool-layer module mtime is newer than process start time, emit `WARN: restart required` — prevents the "changed it but nothing happened and nobody knows why" class of confusion.

Severity: **feature-gap level**. All implementation details from our prototype are available on request. Thanks!

---

### 中文版全文

**问题**：内置 tavily provider 无 API key 配置入口，付费额度用不上，只能吃匿名通道的限流与低质量结果（日志有真实 HTTP 432 记录）。**复现**：任何位置尝试配置 key → 无处可填 → 出站请求仍为 keyless。**临时解决及代价**：直改 site-packages 实现 authed + keyless 自动回退（已端到端验证），但升级即被覆盖，属技术债；且暴露"改代码不重启不生效、框架无任何提示"的关联问题。**建议**：① `web_search.config.api_key_ref` 指向既有 credentials 库 + Console 表单露出密钥输入；② 官方吸收 authed→keyless 自动降级；③ 工具层模块 mtime 晚于进程启动时打 WARN "restart required"。原型实现细节可提供，欢迎评论区索取。谢谢！

prs.title: fix: finish tool streams without yielding during GeneratorExit
prs.body:
## Description

Tool errors and interruptions can leave AgentScope's `Toolkit.call_tool()` suspended before its final `ToolResponse`. When QwenPaw stops consuming that generator, finalization enters AgentScope's yielding `finally` block and logs `RuntimeError: async generator ignored GeneratorExit` as an unhandled task exception. Returning immediately after a successful `ToolResponse` also skips middleware work after the stream.

Drain tool streams to exhaustion while retaining the first terminal result. The batch-tool path likewise preserves an interrupted result while consuming the remaining toolkit output. Handle `GeneratorExit` separately in `Runtime.run()` so closing a response stream saves partial state and runs cleanup without trying to emit an error envelope.

Reproduced against upstream main `753cb6dc4`; this is not specific to research mode.

**Security Considerations:** No permission or authentication changes.

No test files are included in this minimal patch.

## Evidence

On unmodified upstream main, the local regression cases fail because tool streams are not exhausted; error/interruption paths log `async generator ignored GeneratorExit`. Explicitly awaiting `Runtime.run(...).aclose()` also raises that exact exception.

prs.title: fix(creator): close project logging before directory delete
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Windows, deleting a Creator project fails with `503 STORAGE_INTEGRITY_ERROR` / `WinError 5` once that project's `creator.log` has been opened. `delete_project` renamed the project directory via `atomic_replace_path` / `os.replace` **before** releasing the per-project log handler (`close_creator_project_logging`) and the poller. Windows refuses to rename a directory that contains an open file, and on failure the close never ran — so the project stayed undeletable for the life of the process.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8206

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (Creator plugin)
- [x] Tests

## Checklist

- [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` as relevant) and they pass
- [x] Ready for review

## What Changed

In `plugins/apps/qwenpaw-creator/backend/api/project_routes.py::delete_project`, close the poller and per-project logging **before** calling `services.projects.delete`, so the open `creator.log` handle is released ahead of the directory rename.

## Evidence

Portable regression test simulates the Windows denial: while the project log path is still in `_FILE_HANDLER._targets`, `atomic_replace_path` raises `PermissionError(5, "Access is denied")`.

**Before the fix** (test fails with 503):

```
AssertionError: ... STORAGE_INTEGRITY_ERROR ... Cannot delete Project: ...
assert 503 == 204
PermissionError: [Errno 5] Access is denied
```

**After the fix:**

```
tests/api/test_delete_closes_logging_before_rename.py + tests/api/test_projects.py
10 passed
```

```bash
pytest tests/api/test_delete_closes_logging_before_rename.py tests/api/test_projects.py
```

prs.title: fix(observability): Langfuse tool observation never records tool output
prs.body: ## Description Fixes Langfuse `tool.*` observations never recording `output`: tool spans were exported with `input` and `metadata` only, on 100% of normal (non-interrupted) tool calls. Root cause is an interaction between two components: 1. `ToolCoordinatorMiddleware._drain` returns as soon as it receives the final `ToolResponse` (and on ERROR/INTERRUPTED chunks), so it never resumes the `on_acting` generator chain afterwards. 2. `LangfuseToolSpanMiddleware.on_acting` wrote the observation output *after* its `async for event in next_handler()` loop. Since the generator is left suspended at `yield event` and later closed with `GeneratorExit`, that code never ran — while `tool_span`'s `finally: observation.end()` still ran during cleanup, which is why the span showed up with input but no output. The fix records the output at the moment the `ToolResponse` is captured, i.e. *before* yielding it, with a `try/finally` fallback for early generator close. The `finally` stays inside the `async with tool_span(...)` block so `observation.update()` always happens before `observation.end()`. More generally, any `on_acting` middleware code placed after its final `yield` is not guaranteed to execute because consumers may stop iterating once the terminal event is seen. This may be worth documenting in `MiddlewareBase.on_acting`; happy to follow up if desired. **Related Issue:** Fixes (#7963) **Security Considerations:** None. ## Type of Change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Breaking change - [ ] Documentation - [ ] Refactoring ## Component(s) Affected - [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models) - [ ] Console (frontend web UI) - [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.) - [ ] Skills - [ ] CLI - [ ] Documentation (website) - [x] Tests - [ ] CI/CD - [ ] Scripts / Deploy ## Checklist - [ ] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes - [ ] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks - [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass - [ ] Documentation updated (if needed) - [x] Ready for review ## Testing 1. Unit: `pytest tests/unit/observability/test_langfuse_integration.py -v` — 14 passed, including two new regression tests: - `test_records_output_on_normal_drain`: output recorded exactly once on a fully drained consumer, and `update` strictly before `end`. - `test_records_output_when_consumer_stops_at_tool_response`: simulates `_drain` short-circuiting after the final `ToolResponse` (consumer breaks out of the loop, generator closed via `aclose()`) — the exact production path that lost the output. 2.
