- **Revision:** `eaea62766b`. The locally built debug binary reports `zeroclaw 0.8.5 (v0.8.5-535-geaea62766b)`.
- **Environment:** macOS arm64. One isolated daemon, with `HOME`, `ZEROCLAW_CONFIG_DIR` and the RPC socket in a scratch directory, and nothing read from or written to the real `~/.zeroclaw`. The gateway listens on `127.0.0.1:43617`, WSS on `127.0.0.1:49781` and enrollment on `127.0.0.1:49782`. The config is the setup above: the `reader` profile, and `[users.alice]` with uid 59999, which no account on the host holds.
- **Client:** the WSS client certificate was enrolled with `zerocode --enroll`, after checking the client's SAS against the one on the daemon console. A small JSON-RPC client then connected over mTLS with that certificate and presented the token in `initialize`. Codes and tokens are omitted below.
- **Observed:**
  1. `zeroclaw gateway get-paircode --new --user alice` printed a code and "This code pairs as user:alice: the device that redeems it gets that roster user's permissions, not the operator's."
  2. `POST /pair` returned `200` with `"principal_id": "user:alice"`.
  3. `config.toml` holds the token's hash once, under `[gateway.paired_token_users]` mapped to `"alice"`, and `gateway.paired_tokens` is absent.
  4. With the bound token, `GET /api/devices` returned `401`, `GET /api/config` returned `200`, and `PATCH /api/config` returned `403` ("Principal lacks the config grant required for this method").

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: a roster user can now hold a pairing token, a second credential next to their peer uid. Only the operator can mint one (a loopback peer plus the owner-only admin token), the redeeming client cannot choose or strip the binding, the token carries only the user's permission profiles through the shared resolver, and every operator-authority route refuses it. The new persisted map holds token hashes and principal ids, written in the same atomic save as the token list, and a damaged entry makes its token fail closed at load. The map is stored in plain text; see the open question above.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. Existing tokens are unbound and behave as before; the new field defaults empty.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes:
  - the gateway-managed `gateway.paired_token_users`;
  - `zeroclaw gateway get-paircode --new --user <name>`;
  - a `user` query parameter on `POST /admin/paircode/new`;
  - `principal_id` in the `/pair`, `/api/pair`, `/admin/paircode*` and dashboard rotation responses, on each device in `GET /api/devices`, and in the CLI's `--json` output.

  No schema version change.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: none. An operator opts in by minting a code with `--user`.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** revert the merge. An older binary ignores `gateway.paired_token_users`, so bound tokens stop authenticating there instead of turning into operator tokens, and the affected users re-pair. Entries left in the file work again after a later upgrade, so delete the table when downgrading if the bound devices should stay revoked.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** none. The feature is inert until a code is minted with `--user`.
- **Observable failure symptoms:**
  - `RPC principal bound` events with `auth_provider = native` and a `user:` principal id;
  - `RPC authorization denied` events for bound principals;
  - the load-time warning `gateway.paired_token_users has entries that are not a token hash mapped to one valid roster principal id`;
  - `401` for a bound token on the dashboard and other operator routes.

Phase 3: The Gateway. Separate the web surface from the agent core so the gateway is optional and can restart independently.

Source of truth: [#7432 - v0.9.0 gateway](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432#v090-gateway), including existing issues/PRs, missing work, sequencing, and acceptance evidence.

Deliverables: agree the full core IPC contract first; finish the supported local IPC server; ship standalone zeroclaw-gw; migrate vendor webhook behavior into channel plugins; and have Tauri package and manage both processes.

Existing OIDC, principal-isolation, and ZeroRelay work must integrate with this boundary. WATI is already retired. Feature acceptance and normal review/CI/release holds still apply.

prs.title: feat(zerocode): show message times in the transcript
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The ZeroCode transcript never showed when anything happened. When an automated prompt, a refused queued message and a long tool call overlap in one session, there was no way to tell the order or the durations from the screen. A time on every message proved to be too much (an earlier revision of this PR did that). The transcript now shows time context in two places only:
    - a dim, centered divider (`── Today 01:00 ──`, `── Yesterday 22:20 ──`, or a date) before a prompt that starts the transcript, comes 15 minutes or more after the previous activity, or starts a new day. A quick back-and-forth gets no dividers.
    - a dim footer (`─── 01:00 → 01:31 · 31m 40s`) under a turn that ran for a minute or more. Short turns get none.
  - `session/messages` entries gain an optional `created_at` (RFC 3339) wherever the store has one: ACP full loads, ACP cursor pages, and the Chat backend via `load_with_timestamps`. It is skipped when absent and `#[serde(default)]` on the client, so either side can be older.
  - **Store fix underneath.** Checkpointed ACP turns write all their visible rows at finalization with one timestamp, so a turn's prompt read as the time the turn **ended**. A divider or footer built on that would be wrong by the whole length of the turn. The checkpoint row now records `started_at` (a nullable column, added on upgrade), and finalization and crash recovery stamp the turn's prompt row with it. The other rows of the turn keep the finalization time, which is the turn's end: exactly what the footer needs.
  - Live turns: entries are stamped on receipt, and the footer is placed when the turn settles. A later terminal frame for the same turn does not move it. A history load taken mid-turn hands the footer to the live settle.
  - A reloaded turn that ends in a recovery marker gets no footer, because recovery stamps its rows when it runs, which can be hours after the turn stopped.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - Individual tool calls and replies in ACP history still share the turn's finish time. Giving each its own time would need a time on every checkpoint journal event; it isn't needed for dividers and footers.
  - No toggle. The only existing display toggle is thoughts; a timestamp toggle would need a new action, keybinding and help text.
  - The Chat-backend path (gateway SQLite) is affected by #11420, which rewrites every row's `created_at` on each turn. This PR passes through what that store holds.
- **Blast radius:** the ACP store's write path for checkpointed turns (only the prompt row's `created_at`) and one additive column on `acp_turn_checkpoints`; the `session/messages` wire shape (additive, optional); ZeroCode transcript layout (divider and footer rows drawn outside each entry's line range, with the tail re-render accounting for them).
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11620. Related #11420.

### What this does, simply

ZeroCode now shows a small grey date-and-time line when you come back to a conversation after a break or on a new day, and a small grey line under any turn that took more than a minute, saying when it started, when it finished and how long it took. Quick exchanges look exactly as before. Under the hood, the daemon's database used to record every message of a turn as happening when the turn finished; this PR records when the prompt was sent, so those lines are right after a reload too.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `tui` (ZeroCode over the daemon socket)
- **Setup / preconditions:** a daemon and ZeroCode built from this branch; any agent.
- **Steps to run:** send a prompt that runs a tool and takes over a minute. Then send a quick follow-up. Wait 15 minutes (or reload a session from yesterday) and send another. Switch away from the session and back to force a `session/messages` reload.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** a `── Today HH:MM ──` divider above the first prompt; a `─── start → end · duration` footer under the long turn; nothing around the quick follow-up; a new divider after the gap. The same marks after the reload. A session from an older daemon shows no marks rather than wrong ones.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** no times anywhere.

### How I tested

All builds and tests ran through `scripts/zc-cargo` on the remote build host.

- `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on the touched files: clean.
- `zc-cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-infra -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `zc-cargo test -p zerocode`: `test result: FAILED. 1433 passed; 1 failed; 2 ignored`. The one failure, `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint`, fails the same way on unmodified `master` on the same host.
- `zc-cargo test -p zeroclaw-infra --lib`: `test result: ok. 314 passed; 0 failed`.
- `zc-cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib`: `5627 passed; 4 failed` at the earlier head. The 4 (`relay::local_dial_tests` x2, `new_session_methods_are_denied_without_their_grants`, `peer_turn_cost_scope_through_execute_boundary_attributes_recipient_and_shares_budget`) fail the same way on unmodified `master` on the same host. The runtime diff is unchanged since.

Each new test fails with its fix reverted and passes with it restored:

- Store: `finalized_turn_prompt_keeps_turn_start_time_and_reply_keeps_finalization_time`, `recovered_turn_prompt_keeps_turn_start_time` (fail when the prompt keeps the finalization time); `turn_checkpoint_start_column_is_added_to_an_existing_database` (fails without the migration).
- RPC: `conversation_message_entries_carry_each_source_message_time` (fails when the projection drops times).
- Rules (`chat::entry_time`): `dividers_mark_the_first_prompt_gaps_and_day_changes_only` (fails when every prompt divides), `a_day_change_divides_even_after_a_short_gap` (fails without the day check), `footers_follow_finished_turns_of_a_minute_or_more` (fails without the one-minute floor), plus label and parsing tests.
- Transcript: `transcript_shows_gap_dividers_and_long_turn_footers_not_message_times` and `a_live_turn_gets_its_footer_when_it_settles` (fail when the layout drops the footer row, when a settle doesn't invalidate the tail, or when a later frame may move the end); `a_history_load_taken_mid_turn_hands_the_footer_to_the_live_settle` (fails when a moved footer doesn't force a full rebuild); `a_footer_on_a_divided_entry_keeps_one_divider` (fails when the tail re-render ignores the divider row); `a_recovered_turn_gets_no_footer_from_its_recovery_time`.

`rpc::dispatch::tests::cursor_pages_equal_legacy_projection_for_valid_tool_groups` was updated: cursor pages now carry times, so its full-load reference uses the timed projection.

- **CI checks relied on:** the Rust lanes for the three crates.
- **Known CI coverage gap:** no end-to-end daemon+TUI run in CI for this.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The divider and footer rows were checked in a live ZeroCode pane against a scratch daemon (seeded history plus a live turn), by reading the terminal's text.
- **Visual interface evidence:** I'm verifying this in the experiment build.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** none.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. Times are display-only and never reach the model.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. The new wire field is optional both ways. The new column is nullable and added on open; an older binary ignores it (its inserts name their columns). A checkpoint begun by an older binary has no start time, and its prompt keeps the finalization time as before.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` the PR's commits. The added `acp_turn_checkpoints.started_at` column is harmless to the reverted code and needs no down-migration.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** no dividers or footers (old daemon or missing `created_at`), or a footer whose start is later than expected (start time not recorded).

prs.title: feat(tools): add opt-in subprocess memory watchdog
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Add `runtime_profiles.<alias>.shell_max_memory_mb`, measured in MiB and disabled by default, for native shell and skill subprocesses.
  - Sample the command's resident memory plus its visible descendants. Stop the owned command group or Windows Job Object when a sample exceeds the threshold, and return a failed `ToolResult` with the threshold and observed memory.
  - Share the existing capped-output execution path between shell and skill tools. Stop the command on monitoring failure, preserve capped partial output with truncation markers, and bound cleanup waiting after timeout or failure.
  - Check zero RSS readings through the operating system's process API. Accept a confirmed zero for the same observed process identity and skip descendants confirmed to have exited after the snapshot. Unreadable live processes and incomplete responses remain monitoring errors.
  - Carry the threshold through the existing runtime-profile policy. Explicit child policies cannot raise or disable a finite parent threshold.
- **Scope boundary:** No `RLIMIT_AS`, default memory cap, hard allocation ceiling, cgroup implementation, or guarantee against host OOM. Detached or reparented processes can escape sampling. Docker keeps its existing container memory controls.
- **Blast radius:** Native shell and skill execution, runtime-profile policy construction, explicit child-policy validation, and Windows process ownership. Existing tool admission, environment filtering, and sandbox authorization remain in place.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #6916. The original strict OOM-prevention requirements remain open. #7937 introduced the earlier implementation, which #8417 reverted; this PR uses resident-memory sampling instead of restoring it.
- **Runtime placement:** The bounded native shell/skill RSS scope was approved by @tidux and recorded in merged #11436. Its catalogue list still needs the Spanish, French, Japanese and Simplified Chinese files, as requested in [the implementation review](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11456#pullrequestreview-5419663657). That record correction is separate from implementation review.

### What this does, simply

The shell and skill tools let an agent run programs on your machine. Their timeout and output cap limit how long a command runs and how much text ZeroClaw stores, but they do not limit the memory used by the program itself.

This adds an optional watcher. You choose a memory threshold in the agent's runtime profile. While its command runs, ZeroClaw samples the physical memory used by that command and its visible children. If the total crosses the threshold, ZeroClaw stops the owned command group and tells the agent why it failed. A zero reading is checked directly with the operating system so an unavailable measurement is not mistaken for no memory use. A child that exits between the snapshot and that check no longer causes an otherwise healthy command to be stopped. If output was capped before a command failed, its partial output says it was truncated.

The watcher is off unless configured. It reacts after observing memory use, so a command can exceed the threshold between samples. It does not reserve memory, impose a kernel allocation ceiling, or guarantee that an out-of-memory event cannot happen. Virtual-address reservations alone do not count, avoiding the earlier virtual-memory-limit approach.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

Both tool entry points need the same child ownership, bounded output capture, timeout, and memory-failure handling. Sharing the existing shell runner avoids implementing those lifecycles twice. The new sampler uses the existing `sysinfo` dependency; Windows containment and failed-spawn cleanup reuse the existing `process-wrap` dependency and service guard.

The essential new work is per-command process ancestry and RSS sampling, plus platform-specific ownership on Windows. Three small native readers resolve zero readings without adding another process cache or dependency. They compare the returned process identity at the existing whole-second precision; this does not eliminate every descendant PID-reuse race. There is no global process cache, new dependency, polling scheduler, or sandbox backend. Sampling runs about every 100 ms plus observation time. Its metadata work scales with host process count and concurrent monitored commands; disabled monitoring starts no sampler. Shared resident pages may count more than once.

Monitoring follows the root command's lifetime. On Windows, dropping the enabled command's owner explicitly terminates its Job Object before closing the handle, stopping remaining job descendants even after root completion. Non-native runtimes, Docker sandboxes, and unsupported operating systems reject an enabled watchdog before spawning; Docker deployments should use their existing container memory limits.

The bounded runtime placement exception is recorded by merged #11436.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. Focused tests spawn real subprocesses and exercise resident allocation, descendant aggregation, virtual reservation, and tool-result conversion without requiring a provider or changing a live agent's configuration.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [Current-head CI](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38010558146) is pending on `73db3b5cae818a5d45d9f5676f69643d8ee48007`, which integrates master and preserves its terminal-detachment fix in the shared shell runner. On preceding repair head `a42774653cd4f1458707854863228f3e5d6594ef`, [required CI](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38007168838) passed, including Linux Test, Parallel Runtime Test, Lint, Format, Windows compilation and task-owner recovery. Linux execution covers the departure regression and Linux error classification. On earlier head `99386e6fb737b46e2aa08648bc047469e6b34dcd`, [required CI](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38000719997/attempts/2) passed. The [macOS platform job](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38000741090/job/114058025862) passed all 11 earlier watchdog tests, the shell diagnostic and container rejection, and all three truncation tests. The [Windows platform job](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38000741090/job/114058025868) passed all 10 earlier watchdog tests, including owned-descendant cleanup after root exit.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Execution of the new departure regression on Windows remains pending. The preceding full macOS job failed six tests outside the watchdog's changed mechanisms; no clean-master macOS execution baseline was run. The preceding full Windows job failed nine tests that also fail in the [clean-master Windows run](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/37880263821/job/113658218149). Existing fixes in #11361, #11362, #11363, #11365, #11366 and #11630 cover those nine failures, with the corresponding tests passing in their Windows merge-ref runs. Those fixes are not included here, and the full Windows suite is not being reported as green.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

The integrated head `73db3b5cae818a5d45d9f5676f69643d8ee48007` passes the focused macOS watchdog, terminal-detachment and descendant-cleanup checks:

```text
cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -E 'test(tools::subprocess_memory::tests) | test(shell_child_cannot_open_owners_controlling_terminal) | test(shell_reaps_descendants_after_timeout_or_cancellation)' --test-threads=1
Summary: 14 tests run, 14 passed.

cargo fmt --all -- --check
Passed.

bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
Comment hygiene gate passed.

git diff --check
Passed.
```

The departure repair at `a42774653cd4f1458707854863228f3e5d6594ef` passes the focused macOS watchdog suite, formatting, diff integrity and comment hygiene:

```text
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib tools::subprocess_memory::tests -- --test-threads=1
12 passed; 0 failed on macOS, including descendant departure and live read-failure controls.

cargo fmt --all
Passed.
```

The following results are from earlier implementation and repair candidates:

```text
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib tools::subprocess_memory::tests -- --test-threads=1
11 passed; 0 failed on the repaired candidate.

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib tools::shell::tests::shell_marks
3 passed; 0 failed, including capped stdout/stderr on timeout.

cargo fmt --all
Passed on the repaired candidate.

Earlier implementation validation:
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config --lib -- from_profiles_ ensure_no_escalation_
27 passed; 0 failed.

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- tools::subprocess_memory:: tools::shell::tests:: tools::skill_tool::tests::
110 passed; 0 failed; completed in 2.86 seconds after compilation.

cargo fmt -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime
Passed.

bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
Comment hygiene gate passed.

git diff --check
Passed.
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Source comparison confirms that shell and skill tools use the same runner, enabled monitoring is rejected before unsupported execution, and bounded delegates retain their parent-owned tool policy. No real-account or live-agent exercise was needed for the subprocess contract.
- **Build warning:** The macOS linker reported that the debug test executable's `__eh_frame` section exceeds its 16 MiB compact-unwind encoding limit. All selected tests completed. Existing clean-master validation also records this linker warning; no new source warning was reported.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. This changes subprocess enforcement rather than visual presentation. The shell regression observes the returned failed tool result and memory diagnostic.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** The commits in this PR; native subprocess execution and `ToolResult`, exercised by `tools::subprocess_memory::tests`, `tools::shell::tests`, `tools::skill_tool::tests`, and the config policy tests.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** `shell_memory_failure_surfaces_resident_cause` checks that the failed tool result identifies the resident-memory threshold.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** The process fixtures distinguish touched resident pages from a large untouched virtual reservation, aggregate two descendants, and preserve completion when monitoring is disabled or memory stays below the threshold. Focused regressions distinguish successful zero measurements from failed reads and identity changes, and confirm truncation markers on both captured streams after a timeout. The departure regression discovers a live child, deliberately kills and reaps it before the native fallback, and confirms that sampling continues; its live-process read-denial control remains an error. The integrated master regressions confirm the child cannot open its owner's controlling terminal and descendants stop after timeout or cancellation. Policy tests parse the setting and reject child escalation.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No duplicate local full-workspace run. The focused macOS suite checks the changed process path; fresh required CI supplies Linux execution and Windows compilation. Broader platform failures remain visible above.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes. Memory failure adds a localized diagnostic to the existing tool result. Its threshold and RSS values are numeric, and it grants no authority. Existing command output remains untrusted and capped.
- **Risk and mitigation:** A configured watchdog can stop a legitimate memory-heavy command. Shared pages can inflate the total, and polling can miss short spikes. Only owned process groups or Job Objects are signaled; sampled descendant PIDs are never termination targets. Samples remain in memory for the invocation and are not persisted.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for existing configuration. The new setting defaults to `0`. Sharing the shell runner also bounds skill output during collection and applies owned-process cleanup on skill timeout or cancellation.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes. Adds `runtime_profiles.<alias>.shell_max_memory_mb`.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- **Upgrade steps:** None for existing users. To opt in, set `shell_max_memory_mb` in the runtime profile selected by the agent. Use `0` to disable it. For Docker runtime limits, use `runtime.docker.memory_limit_mb` instead of this native watchdog.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Set the selected runtime profile's `shell_max_memory_mb` to `0` and recreate the affected agent/session. Revert the merge commit to remove the implementation and shared skill-runner change entirely.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `runtime_profiles.<alias>.shell_max_memory_mb = 0` disables sampling.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Failed tool results containing `resident-memory threshold`, `resident-memory monitoring failed`, or the unsupported-native-runtime diagnostic. Legitimate commands terminating early indicate a threshold that is too low or a monitoring failure.

## Supersede Attribution

N/A. This does not supersede an open PR or incorporate contributor code from the reverted implementation.

prs.title: feat(runtime): let the operator override an exceeded cost limit
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - `cost.allow_override` was documented but read by nothing, so an exceeded shared limit always failed the turn and the only way on was a daemon restart. With it on, the main tool loop now pauses before a provider call that would exceed the shared daily or monthly limit and asks through the turn's approval channel (`tool_name = cost_limit_override`, exported as `COST_LIMIT_OVERRIDE_APPROVAL`). Deny, no answer within 10 minutes, or a channel that cannot ask stops the turn exactly as before.
  - Approval calls `CostTracker::grant_override`, which records the override for the current UTC day or month on state shared by every derived tracker, so one answer covers every session and delegation of the daemon. `check_budget` skips that limit (and its warning) while the stored period matches, so it expires on its own at rollover. Per-hop and per-agent ceilings still bind, and `grant_override` refuses when `allow_override` is off.
  - The grant is written to `state/cost-overrides.json` beside the ledger (temp file plus rename, best effort) and loaded when the tracker starts, so a daemon restart keeps it until rollover. An unreadable file means no override, and a stored grant is ignored while `allow_override` is off.
  - A turn waiting on its own prompt also watches for a grant from another session (a `watch` channel on the tracker). When one arrives it drops its request and continues. `RpcApprovalChannel` sends a new `session/update` type, `approval_withdrawn` (`request_id`), for any approval that ends without an answer from its client, and ZeroCode takes that prompt down. Before this, approving in one session left the same prompt up in the other, and that turn stopped at the 10-minute timeout although the limit was already lifted.
  - `RpcApprovalChannel` and `AskUserApprovalBridge` now implement `request_approval_attributed_with_timeout`. The trait default wrapped `request_approval_attributed`, whose own 120 s deadline fired first, so the 10-minute wait would have been cut short.
  - ZeroCode renders a `cost_limit_override` approval as a centred, bold red notice with Override and Stop buttons instead of the tool card. Only Override or Stop (key or click) closes it.
- **Scope boundary:** no warning at `warn_at_percent` (#10950) and no notice for a turn that stops with no override possible; both need a daemon-to-client budget event this PR does not add. `cost.enforcement.mode` stays unread. Applying `config/set` limit changes to the live tracker is #11587.
- **Blast radius:** turns that hit a shared limit with `allow_override = true` now wait for an answer instead of failing, on any channel that answers approvals (ZeroCode, ACP, Telegram inline buttons). The approval bridge's timeout plumbing is used only by callers that pass a budget; tool approvals are unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11585
- **Labels:** (set after open)

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw can stop the agent when spending passes a daily or monthly limit. There was a setting meant to let you go past the limit, but nothing used it: once the limit tripped, every message failed, and the only way to continue was to raise the limit and restart, which closes every open session.

Now, with that setting on, the agent pauses when it reaches the limit and ZeroCode shows a red box asking whether to keep going. Say yes and the same task carries on, and the limit stays lifted until the day (or month) ends, even if the app or daemon restarts. If several sessions were waiting at the limit, one yes lets all of them continue. Say no, or leave it for ten minutes, and the task stops as it does today. Chat apps that cannot show the question, and scheduled jobs, still stop at the limit.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface` `tui` (ZeroCode Code tab over RPC)
- **Setup / preconditions:** `[cost] enabled = true`, `allow_override = true`, `daily_limit_usd` just above today's recorded spend.
- **Steps to run:** in ZeroCode, run a prompt that makes a few model calls until spend passes the limit. When the red notice appears, click Override. Then open a second session and send a prompt. Separately: get two sessions waiting on the notice at once and Override in one; and restart the daemon after an Override and send a prompt.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the first turn pauses on the red notice and continues after Override; the second session is not asked again; with two waiting, the other notice closes and its turn continues; after a restart nobody is asked again that day. With Stop instead, the turn ends with the budget error.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the turn fails with `Budget exceeded: ... Cannot make further API calls until the budget resets.`, there is no prompt, and every later turn fails until a restart.

### How I tested

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check   # rustfmt --edition 2024 on the changed files
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib cost::tracker
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib budget_override
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib approval_
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- budget_override_tests rpc::approval_channel
cargo test -p zerocode --bins -- approval parse_approval cost_limit
cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode cost_limit
cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode approval
scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Rust test and clippy jobs for the four crates; Docs Style for `docs/book/src/ops/cost-tracking.md`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** no end-to-end test drives a real provider turn into the gate; the gate tests call it under a scoped tracker with a scripted channel.
- **Commands run and tail output:** on `225c52bb636f` (rebased on master `f12da7462a0f`): clippy `-D warnings` clean on the four crates; `cost::tracker` 50 passed; runtime `budget_override_tests rpc::approval_channel` 17 passed; zerocode `approval parse_approval cost_limit` 13 passed; comment hygiene gate passed. With each fix disabled, `override_survives_a_restart_and_stops_counting_when_disallowed` and `approval_in_another_session_releases_a_waiting_prompt` fail. Earlier run at `58a7050d`: clippy `Finished`, no warnings. `cost::tracker` 47 passed, `budget_override` 3 passed, `approval_` 106 passed, zerocode `cost_limit` 2 passed, zerocode `approval` 9 passed, docs gate 0 errors.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Coverage: tracker override (day lifts, rollover expiry, derived trackers share it, per-hop and per-agent ceilings still bind, day does not lift month, refused when not allowed); gate (approve continues and does not ask twice, deny and runtime timeout stop, no prompt without `allow_override` or a channel); RPC channel honours a 600 s budget through `dyn Channel`; ZeroCode notice render and button clicks; restart persistence, unreadable file, cross-session release, `approval_withdrawn` sent only for unanswered prompts and cleared only for the matching id. I ran the override live in the experiment build; the two follow-up bugs above came from that run.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact final-interface output pending; the render test asserts the title, summary, both buttons and the red button fill through `render_with_plan_placement` at 100x30.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `225c52bb636f` on master `f12da7462a0f`; tests on a remote macOS arm64 builder. Live: experiment build https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261013T015950Z-b89c9e407c42 (commit https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/commit/b89c9e407c4279bbfb05f9d0e0cdec7e34b6e561).
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** to be added from the dogfood smoke before Ready.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** full crate suites not run locally; CI runs them.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No (one new file, `state/cost-overrides.json`, in the existing cost state directory)
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No

prs.title: fix(tools): probe the saved provider alias after a model-routing update
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Build the post-save provider probe from the alias in the effective reloaded configuration, including decryption and the normal environment-override precedence for credentials, endpoint, runtime options, and model.
  - Enter the probe from the post-save alias boundary even when the disk entry has no model, so a supported environment-only model override cannot bypass validation.
  - Select the probed model from the effective configuration alone and stop before dispatch when it resolves none, so an environment override that explicitly clears the alias model (an empty `ZEROCLAW_*__model` value) can never be replaced by the saved model the reloaded runtime will not serve.
  - Select the alias credential only from the effective reloaded configuration. Missing, empty, or whitespace-only credentials take the existing no-credential skip. Removing a saved key or a current environment credential cannot revive a key from the startup snapshot; current environment-only credentials still reach the probe without being persisted.
  - Treat provider-construction and environment-override reconstruction failures as unsuccessful tool results instead of passing them through the chat-error retry heuristic; keep the intentional secrets-decryption compatibility skip distinct.
  - Sanitize probe failures before returning or logging them, name the effective model the probe actually validated in those diagnostics, and roll back atomically after a fatal probe by restoring an updated alias's prior entry or removing a newly created alias before persisting.
  - Move effective-config reconstruction, including secret resolution, into a blocking worker so the post-save probe does not block a Tokio worker thread.
- **Scope boundary:** This does not change provider request behavior, the existing request-error retry classification, model-routing configuration syntax, or environment-override precedence. A secrets-decryption failure still skips the probe; making that compatibility path separately observable remains outside this PR. An alias whose effective model or effective credential is absent (never set, removed from saved configuration or the environment, or explicitly cleared by the environment) is still saved with the probe skipped, as before; rejecting such an update is a separate policy decision.
- **Blast radius:** The `model_routing_config` tool's post-save validation, error reporting, and rollback path only. Operators with invalid aliases or malformed effective overrides now receive a sanitized validation failure that was previously reported as success.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #9592. Related #8858.
- **Labels:** `bug`, `tool`, `distinguished contributor`, `risk:medium`, `size:XL`, `domain:security`

## Current exact-head validation (2026-09-30)

- **Head:** `bf21f5cc08e8ce92efb0d13cfcf6fa239b360124`
- **Repair since `ec7d374ac51418b04b3bae5fc52c201b28312a2f`:** One commit, `fix(tools): honor removed probe credentials`, removes startup-snapshot credential fallback and updates the affected tests. The aggregate change remains confined to `crates/zeroclaw-tools/src/model_routing_config.rs`.
- **Required CI:** [`CI Required Gate` passed on this head](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/36604152566/job/109534960557). The advisory Windows job was skipped on this head; the Windows results below belong to the historical September 10 head.
- **Repair coverage:** The saved-key-removal test constructs a tool with a key, removes it through `upsert_agent` with `api_key: null`, then calls `set_default` on the same tool. It asserts zero provider requests and checks that the key remains absent while the model and temperature update persist. The current environment-only credential test matches the request's Authorization header, requires one request, and checks that the environment key stays off disk. Startup-only credentials now take the no-credential skip; construction-failure coverage uses a current environment credential.
- **Review validation:** I inspected the repair and its regression assertions and checked hosted CI. I did not rerun local Cargo commands or make a live-provider request for this head. The local outputs below are historical evidence.

## Historical validation record

> The records below predate the current head. Their commands and results apply only to the named historical revisions. The September 29 repair supersedes the earlier startup-credential fallback behavior and its positive control.

### Head `ec7d374ac51418b04b3bae5fc52c201b28312a2f` (2026-09-10)

- **Head:** `ec7d374ac51418b04b3bae5fc52c201b28312a2f`
- **Base integrated:** `origin/master` at `46479bdca74bedb5c71e30afab657ccaac77dab4` (clean merge; master did not touch `model_routing_config.rs`, and the aggregate base-to-head patch is still that one file)
- **Delta since the reviewed head `fbabd89b7c81532654ca939dc74ab370fab12314`:** one `master` merge and two commits. The functional commit answers the 2026-09-09 zeroclaw-reviewer blocker on the explicitly cleared API-key override; the second is the rustfmt fixup for one assertion in the new test. `crates/zeroclaw-tools/src/model_routing_config.rs:855-858` now records the alias credential path and keeps `None` when that path is environment-owned, so the runtime-snapshot fallback applies only to a genuinely unoverridden path.
- **Required CI:**
  - Hosted CI on this head (`ec7d374ac51418b04b3bae5fc52c201b28312a2f`): `CI Required Gate` SUCCESS, run 34553249805. `Advisory Windows nextest (scoped, plugin-host=false)` failed (non-required); its actual test results are summarized below.
  - Historical: `CI Required Gate` passed on the previous exact head `fbabd89b7c81532654ca939dc74ab370fab12314` in [run 34181632115](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/34181632115).
  - The [non-required Windows job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/34553249805/job/103125841193) ran 9,422 tests: 9,418 passed, four failed, and 16 were skipped. The failures were the `../../web/dist` packaging assertion, `process_line_session_new_creates_session_on_two_megabyte_stack` (stack overflow), and the two PowerShell pipeline tests in `tools::shell` and `tools::skill_tool` (60-second timeouts). These failures are outside the changed model-routing path. Both explicit-clear regressions, the retained-key control, and the effective-model diagnostic and composed rollback tests passed in this job.
- **Local validation on this exact head:**

```text
cargo fmt --all --check
  clean

bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
  Comment hygiene gate passed.

./scripts/ci/rust_quality_gate.sh --strict
  fmt clean
  cargo clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets --features ci-all -- -D warnings
    Finished `dev` profile, no Clippy diagnostics
  provider dispatch gate clean

cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets
  Finished

RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-default-features
  Finished

cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-tools
  Summary [8.748s] 1730 tests run: 1730 passed (1 leaky), 0 skipped

cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-tools --all-features -E 'test(model_routing_config)'
  Summary [0.479s] 24 tests run: 24 passed, 1716 skipped

cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-run
  Finished `test` profile

cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-fail-fast
  Summary [76.282s] 15614 tests run: 15613 passed (5 leaky), 1 failed, 24 skipped
  FAIL zeroclaw-providers grok_cli::tests::unix_fake_child::timeout_kills_leader_and_descendant
```

  The single workspace failure is the known local-only macOS process-kill race in `grok_cli`. It cannot see this change: `git diff origin/master HEAD -- crates/zeroclaw-providers` is empty on this head, and `zeroclaw-providers` does not depend on `zeroclaw-tools`. It also reproduces serially on this machine (`cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-providers --test-threads=1 -E 'test(timeout_kills_leader_and_descendant)'` fails at 2.02s, the wall-clock boundary the test asserts), so I am reporting it rather than claiming a pass. Hosted CI is the authority for that crate.

  Fail-before/pass-after evidence for the credential fix, produced by deleting the `None if effective.prop_is_env_overridden(&api_key_path) => None` arm on the working tree, running the model-routing suite, then restoring the tracked file and rerunning:

```text
before (guard arm removed)
  Summary [0.727s] 24 tests run: 22 passed, 2 failed, 1706 skipped
  FAIL probe_model_keeps_an_explicitly_cleared_credential_clear
  FAIL set_default_does_not_probe_with_the_snapshot_key_after_an_explicit_empty_override
    the boot snapshot credential must not be probed once the environment cleared the
    effective one; got 1 request(s)

after (tracked file restored)
  Summary [0.834s] 24 tests run: 24 passed, 1706 skipped
```

  The third new case, `set_default_still_probes_with_the_snapshot_key_when_the_path_is_not_overridden`, passes in both directions by design: it pins the unoverridden fallback so the new guard cannot swallow it. Docs gates were not run because the aggregate base-to-head patch touches no file under `docs/`.

- **Remaining external/non-blocking gaps:** No live probe against a paid provider; every request-level assertion runs against Wiremock. The explicit-empty regressions set process environment variables to the empty string. They passed locally on macOS and in the exact-head Windows job above, closing the empty-value platform uncertainty despite that job's unrelated failures. The retryable-failure log record carries the effective model, but no test asserts the log attribute. When the environment layer itself cannot be rebuilt, the fatal message still names the saved model because no effective model exists at that point. The workspace `grok_cli` timeout test could not be made to pass on this machine and is reported as failing above.
- **Visual evidence:** N/A; no rendered interface changed.

### Head `fbabd89b7c81532654ca939dc74ab370fab12314` (2026-09-08)

- Base integrated: `origin/master` at `ab72fe5d7fd0c1ab8e9cbc226c2b783eb4914332` (clean merge; the aggregate base-to-head patch was already confined to `model_routing_config.rs`).
- Required CI: [`CI Required Gate` run 34181632115](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/34181632115) passed at that head.
- That head answered the 2026-09-04 and 2026-09-07 reviews: the explicit-empty *model* override, effective-model diagnostics, a two-string message cleanup, the composed unavailable-model regression, and narrowing effective-model selection to the effective configuration alone. Each production fix carried an outer-boundary `set_default` regression that failed when the pre-fix expression was restored and passed with the fix.
- Local gate set on that head: `cargo fmt --all --check` clean, `bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh` passed, `./scripts/ci/rust_quality_gate.sh --strict` passed, both `cargo check` variants finished, `cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-tools` 1727 passed, and the full workspace run reported 15455 passed with 4 load-sensitive failures that all passed when rerun serially.

### Head `969ff52f239703cc1ddb15bd3dfa1e043bb96fbe` (2026-08-30)

- Base integrated: `origin/master` at `559c543a0fe8ee47418345e1a87ce77dfbb39177`.
- Required CI: [Quality Gate run 33294368004](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/33294368004) passed at that head; every check context was complete with no failures.
- Carried-forward focused validation: eighteen model-routing tests passed in ten consecutive normal parallel runs, all 18 passed with all features, and strict Clippy passed on the prior reviewed implementation.

### Head `a7fda8c7a476981c302ed1895a8ed950649ffc7e` (test-isolation repair)

- Hosted CI was green on that exact head; the repair delta was confined to shared test locking and panic-safe environment restoration in the model-routing test module.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A` — deterministic config, construction, wiremock dispatch, sanitization, persisted rollback, and test-isolation coverage exercise the boundary without a live provider credential.

### How I tested

The current-head review relies on hosted CI and inspection of the repaired request and persistence assertions. Local command outputs above belong to their named historical heads.

- `set_default_does_not_probe_after_upsert_agent_removes_the_saved_key` covers saved-key removal after tool construction, zero dispatched requests, and persistence of the key-free update.
- `set_default_probes_with_current_environment_only_credentials` covers a credential introduced through the environment after tool construction, the exact Authorization header, one dispatched request, and no credential persistence.
- Retained explicit-empty model and credential tests cover environment clears. The former snapshot-fallback positive control now requires a skip when the current effective configuration has no key.

The focused implementation suite was first tested locally at `7590d14f051cfbfd706cdd06d01019980ab8d50a`, covering updated and newly created aliases, credential/endpoint/runtime-option/model precedence, the environment-only model entry point, reconstruction and construction error classification, returned-error sanitization, and persisted rollback.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The required hosted gate covers repository policy, the broader workspace/platform matrix, and the default-parallel test boundary. The historical focused local tests and strict workspace lint exercised the earlier tool/config/provider behavior; they were not rerun locally for this repair.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No successful live-provider request was made because it would require a real credential and network dependency. The Wiremock tests inspect the actual dispatched request without external traffic. A secrets-decryption failure remains an intentional non-fatal skip and is not separately surfaced. The historical local macOS `grok_cli` failure is recorded above; it was not rerun for this head.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Historical outputs are included above with their revisions; current-head hosted CI is linked separately.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Traced `set_default` from its persisted write through decryption, full environment overrides, alias-aware provider construction, effective-credential and effective-model selection (including both explicit-clear branches), sanitized failure output, and persisted rollback. Inspected the outer-boundary assertions for saved-key removal and current environment-only credentials, including request counts, the Authorization header, and persisted configuration.
- **Visual interface changed?** `N/A` — no rendered text, layout, or interaction changed.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** The docs gates were not run because no file under `docs/` changed.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? `No`
- New external network calls? `Yes` — the existing post-save alias probe is now also reached when the effective model comes only from a supported environment override. This adds no new destination class or request shape; it uses the effective alias endpoint and credentials, and failures are sanitized before operator output or logging. An absent effective model or credential, including a removed saved key or an explicit environment clear, results in no request at all.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? `Yes`
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? `No`
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? `No`
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: The probe clones the private saved configuration and transfers that owned clone to a blocking worker for decryption and environment overrides. The clone is not persisted, and probe failure text is passed through the existing provider error sanitizer before it reaches tool output, `ToolResult.error`, or logs. The credential fix narrows what the probe may send: an absent effective credential is never repopulated from the startup snapshot, whether it was removed from saved configuration, removed from the environment, or explicitly cleared.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? `Yes` — invalid provider aliases and malformed effective overrides now fail and roll back instead of being silently accepted.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? `No`
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? `No`

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** After merge, revert the landed PR commit with `git revert <landed-pr-commit-sha>`.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `model_routing_config` reports a sanitized probe failure for a valid effective alias, fails to send the environment-effective model, dispatches a saved model after an environment clear or a stale snapshot credential after credential removal or clearing, uses an unexpected endpoint/runtime option, or fails to restore/remove the alias after a rejected update. Check tool failure logs for `model_routing_config` and rerun the focused `model_routing_config` suite.

prs.title: feat(tools): defer built-in schemas through tool_search
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:** Add default-off `RuntimeProfileConfig.deferred_builtin_tools`. Keep permitted workspace and basic memory tools visible, advertise other admitted built-ins through compact discovery, and retrieve full schemas with the existing `tool_search` protocol. Apply exposure separately from callable-name recognition, argument recovery, and native streaming suppression.
- **Scope boundary:** Schema exposure only. Keep executable instances, tool permissions, approval rules, caller and principal restrictions, MCP activation, tool listing, and context-history recovery under their existing owners.
- **Blast radius:** Config, scoped tool assembly, shared native requests, Agent and lower-level text prompts, independent delegates, and channel startup prompts. Executable built-ins remain in `ScopedToolRegistry`; `ActivatedToolSet` records built-in schema metadata and selection only.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #5808.
- **Runtime placement:** The bounded schema-deferral exception landed in #11436, approved by @tidux. The implementation remains within that recorded scope.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw tells the model what tools it can use and how to call them. Today, it sends every enabled built-in tool's full description and argument format before the model knows which tools it needs. That catalog consumes part of each request's context budget. Trimming conversation history cannot remove it from the protected system prompt.

This adds an optional way to send less of that catalog upfront. Permitted shell, file read/write/edit, and basic memory recall/store tools stay fully described. Other permitted built-ins appear in a short list. The model asks `tool_search` for a full definition when it needs one. Native tool-calling providers receive selected definitions on subsequent requests; text providers receive them in the search result.

Tools remain callable under the same permissions and approval rules. Looking up a definition does not grant access, and knowing a permitted tool's name still lets the model call it directly. The option defaults off. When search is unavailable, native requests restore permitted built-in definitions. Text prompts restore them within the configured prompt budget, including same-agent SOP steps that reuse the parent prompt. Full definitions remain when they fit; the existing identity/safety and timestamp priorities apply when they do not. Custom instructions appended before a model call retain their existing treatment outside the base prompt's cap.

When a step permits search but excludes other tools, its compact catalogue lists only that step's permitted built-ins. A scoped catalogue refresh only filters complete surviving blocks that fit in their existing space. It removes truncated blocks and leaves omitted catalogues omitted, preserving prompt assembly's budget decision. Both projections change only the provider-request copy, leaving the parent prompt and shared selection unchanged. Independent delegates use their target's permitted catalogue for both native and text providers. Each cross-agent SOP step uses its admitted configuration, including its prompt cap.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

This reuses MCP's discovery protocol and existing conversation selection handle, without placing built-in executables in MCP's activation map or adding a second discovery tool. The integration spans existing assembly, prompt, request, parsing, and streaming consumers because hiding a schema must not hide a callable name or let protocol text leak into streamed answers. Keeping only the native-request filter would leave text providers unchanged and break structured argument recovery.

The large diff includes inline proof of policy filtering, narrowing, memory rebinding, eager fallback, native/text requests, direct calls, mixed batches, and streaming. No dependency, new execution subsystem, ownership-tier inventory, or history-trimming redesign is added. Internal schemas still support parsing; the optimization concerns definitions sent to providers, not schema-allocation costs inside the process.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. Captured requests at the production Agent boundary and focused discovery/registry tests establish the schema-exposure contract without a credentialed provider.

### How I tested

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: exit 0.
- Eager fallback cap repair: `cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -E 'test(builtin_search_fallback_preserves_strict_policy_and_scoped_replay) | test(run_tool_call_loop_enforces_sop_step_tool_scope) | test(strict_non_native_prompt_policy_hides_text_tool_protocol_inputs) | test(cross_agent_step_) | test(scoped_protocol_refresh_keeps_hook_appended_text)'`: exit 0, `10 tests run: 10 passed, 5719 skipped`. Production SOP request capture covers a finite cap that truncates definitions, a finite cap that retains full permitted definitions, explicit unlimited zero, and configless scoped cap transport. It checks the Unicode character ceiling, timestamp orientation, continued denied execution, unchanged parent history and shared selection. The existing projection fixture covers repeated no-hook refresh and fresh requests with appended custom instructions; it preserves those instructions outside the base cap. Cross-agent isolation, tool scope, model-switch isolation and strict text-policy checks pass. The existing macOS compact-unwind linker warning remains. Initial fixture compilation failed on borrowed temporaries; a later assertion rejected a harmless trailing newline after orientation. Both fixture issues were corrected before this final full selection passed; production code was unchanged by those corrections.
- Prompt-limit repair: `cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -E 'test(builtin_search_fallback_preserves_strict_policy_and_scoped_replay) | test(run_tool_call_loop_enforces_sop_step_tool_scope) | test(strict_non_native_prompt_policy_hides_text_tool_protocol_inputs)'`: exit 0, 3 passed. The existing projection test now uses rendered catalogues and real capped prompts in native/text modes. It checks that partial or omitted catalogues are not restored, complete replacements cannot grow by Unicode character count, repeated refresh preserves history, and context and timestamp orientation survive. Production SOP request capture and strict text-policy checks also pass.
- Catalogue-scope repair: `cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-tools --lib -E 'test(turn_prompt_defers_builtin_definition_until_search_selection) | test(run_tool_call_loop_enforces_sop_step_tool_scope) | test(builtin_search_fallback_preserves_strict_policy_and_scoped_replay) | test(builtin_prompt_is_compact_filtered_and_omits_selected_schemas) | test(builtin_catalog_refresh_updates_only_surviving_deferred_names) | test(strict_non_native_prompt_policy_hides_text_tool_protocol_inputs) | test(independent_prompt_respects_text_tool_policy_for_deferred_section) | test(agent::turn::tool_specs::tests)'`: exit 0, 10 passed. Production SOP request capture covers search allowed and excluded in native and text modes, continued execution denials, and unchanged parent history and shared selection. Existing projection tests cover repeated scoped refresh, duplicate and truncated catalogues, preserved unrelated sections and timestamp orientation, and strict text suppression.
- Scoped fallback repair validation: `cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -E 'test(agent::turn::provider_call::) | test(agent::turn::tool_specs::tests) | test(turn_prompt_defers_builtin_definition_until_search_selection) | test(independent_full_target_receives_full_prompt_and_executes_uncovered_tool) | test(independent_prompt_respects_text_tool_policy_for_deferred_section) | test(independent_delegate_denies_prompt_required_skill_tools_without_approval_route) | test(run_tool_call_loop_enforces_sop_step_tool_scope) | test(builtin_search_fallback_preserves_strict_policy_and_scoped_replay) | test(strict_non_native_prompt_policy_hides_text_tool_protocol_inputs)'`: 38 checks passed; the SOP scope test initially expected the native denial message in text mode. After correcting only that assertion, `cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -E 'test(run_tool_call_loop_enforces_sop_step_tool_scope)'` passed, exit 0. Together these cover all 39 selected checks. The production SOP test captures native and text requests, verifies permitted definitions when search is excluded, preserves execution denials and parent history, and leaves shared selection unchanged. The focused scoped-refresh replay test prevents duplicate protocol/schema blocks and verifies strict text non-injection and unrelated prompt sections. Production code was unchanged between these two runs.
- Discovery repair validation before master integration: `cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -E 'test(agent::turn::tool_specs::tests) | test(turn_prompt_defers_builtin_definition_until_search_selection) | test(independent_full_target_receives_full_prompt_and_executes_uncovered_tool) | test(independent_prompt_respects_text_tool_policy_for_deferred_section) | test(independent_delegate_denies_prompt_required_skill_tools_without_approval_route)'`: exit 0, 7 passed and 5,473 skipped. The production independent-delegate test covers native and text discovery while retaining approval behavior. The rebuilt loop prompt and iteration-spec tests cover eager permitted definitions when search is excluded, continued exclusions, and unchanged shared selection state. Strict text-tool suppression also passes.

prs.title: fix(security): apply configured firejail_args to the Firejail wrapper
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `FirejailSandbox` used to be a unit struct, and `wrap_invocation` built a fixed argument list. Configured `firejail_args` never reached the firejail command line, even though the risk-profile schema accepts them and `security status` feeds them into the sandbox config. The struct now holds validated extra arguments. `create_selected_sandbox` builds it through `FirejailSandbox::with_args(&sandbox.firejail_args)` on both the explicit-backend path and the auto-detect path. The arguments go after the wrapper's own flags and hardening flags, and before the wrapped invocation, so firejail reads them as its own options and not as arguments to the target command.
  - Validation follows the maintainer decision on #11594. An entry is rejected if it is empty, has leading or trailing whitespace, is `--`, isn't a single `--option` / `--option=value` (for example `none` or `-q`), or names an option that would undo the wrapper. The rejected options are `--profile` (the wrapper sets `--noprofile`), `--include`, `--ignore` (it can drop the wrapper's flags), `--private` / `--private=…` (the wrapper sets `--private=home`; `--private-tmp`, `--private-etc=…` and similar are still allowed), `--allow-debuggers`, `--join`, `--join-or-start`, `--join-network`, `--join-filesystem`, `--chroot` / `--chroot=…` (chroot mode clears Firejail's `--noroot` and skips the private home setup, undoing the wrapper's `--noroot` and `--private=home`), `--seccomp-error-action=log` (logging executes the syscall instead of preserving seccomp denial), and every `--keep-dev-*` option (`--keep-dev-shm`, `--keep-dev-ntsync`, `--keep-dev-tpm`), which Firejail documents as re-exposing host devices or the host `/dev/shm` even with the `--private-dev` the wrapper requires. Option names may contain dots (`--seccomp.block-secondary`, `--caps.drop=…`): each dot-separated segment must start with a letter or digit, so `--seccomp.`, `--.x` and `--a..b` are still rejected. The name grammar and the conflict check are separate steps.
  - If Firejail is selected but its arguments are rejected, the sandbox becomes `RejectedFirejailArgsSandbox`. It refuses every command (`wrap_command` / `check_initialization` return `InvalidInput` with the reason), the same way `FailedSeatbeltSandbox` does. It does not fall back to running without the arguments or to `NoopSandbox`, since either would present the configured hardening as active when it isn't.
  - `sandbox_posture`, which feeds `security status`, now describes the active Firejail backend as "Firejail selected, but firejail_args were rejected; commands are blocked (…reason…)". Before, it described a configuration that wouldn't be applied.
- **Scope boundary:** This PR doesn't touch #11538 / #11539 (the hard-coded `--private=home` / `--nowheel` launch failures) or the docs change in #11591. It doesn't edit the schema doc comment or the generated `config.md`. `firejail_args` still has no effect when another backend is active (Landlock, Bubblewrap, and so on), which matches its documented meaning ("when sandbox_backend resolves to firejail").
- **Blast radius:** Linux, and only when Firejail is the selected sandbox backend. With empty `firejail_args` (the default and all presets) the firejail command line is byte-for-byte the same as before; a test covers this. A profile that has non-empty `firejail_args` gets them applied now. If they're invalid, its shell commands are refused with the reason and no longer run without them.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11594

### What this does, simply

A risk profile can list extra Firejail options in `firejail_args` (for example `--net=none`), but ZeroClaw silently ignored them while still reporting them back. Now they're actually passed to firejail. Options that would break or weaken ZeroClaw's own Firejail setup, or that aren't Firejail options at all, are rejected with a clear message. In that case commands are blocked, not run as if the hardening applied, and the sandbox status says so.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The new behavior is in command construction and backend selection, which the unit tests cover without needing firejail installed. A live Firejail smoke test would add signal, but I couldn't run one here (see below).

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The Rust test and lint jobs run the `zeroclaw-runtime` unit tests, which include the new `security::firejail` and `security::detect` tests.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Nothing exercises a real firejail binary. The non-Linux `cfg` branches (where firejail isn't compiled) were only checked by reading them: I don't have a macOS/Windows target installed, so CI's cross-platform jobs are the check for those.
- **Commands run and tail output** (Linux x86_64):
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- security::firejail security::detect`
    ```
    test security::firejail::tests::firejail_wrap_passes_configured_args_before_the_wrapped_command ... ok
    test security::firejail::tests::firejail_wrap_without_configured_args_is_unchanged ... ok
    test security::firejail::tests::firejail_accepts_single_options_with_and_without_values ... ok
    test security::firejail::tests::firejail_rejects_args_that_are_not_options_or_undo_the_wrapper ... ok
    test security::firejail::tests::firejail_with_args_reports_rejected_args_before_probing ... ok
    test security::detect::tests::selected_firejail_with_rejected_args_blocks_commands_instead_of_dropping_them ... ok
    test security::detect::tests::firejail_posture_reports_rejected_args ... ok
    test result: ok. 43 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5663 filtered out; finished in 0.03s
    ```
  - `cargo fmt -p zeroclaw-runtime -- --check`: clean
  - `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings`: no findings in `security/firejail.rs` or `security/detect.rs`. The crate still fails clippy on lints that already exist on master with this box's newer toolchain: deprecated `fetch_update` in `rpc/upload.rs` and `rpc/dispatch.rs`, and `needless_borrows_for_generic_args` in `agent/turn/stream_guard.rs`. This PR doesn't touch those files.
  - Follow-up commit 806fc4b (review fixes: option-name validation, Fluent text, comment hygiene): `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- security:: i18n::` → `test result: ok. 405 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored`; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean; `bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh` → passed; `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` → no findings in `security/`.
  - Follow-up commit aca1e8ad (review fixes: reject `--keep-dev-*`, accept dotted option names). With only the validator change reverted, the two new tests fail:
    ```
    test security::firejail::tests::firejail_rejects_args_that_reexpose_host_devices_despite_private_dev ... FAILED
    test security::firejail::tests::firejail_accepts_dotted_options_and_passes_them_before_the_wrapped_command ... FAILED
    test result: FAILED. 19 passed; 2 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5688 filtered out
    ```
    With it: `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib security::firejail` → `test result: ok. 21 passed; 0 failed` (including `firejail_rejects_malformed_dotted_option_names`), and `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib security::` → `test result: ok. 365 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored`. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean. `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings`: no findings in `security/`; it still stops on the same pre-existing toolchain lints listed above.
